Postquam heterodoxias reprobavit Apostolus, jam summam orthodoxias exhibet partim in genere, partim in specie, tum quantum ad legem, cuj9 usum genuinum asserit; tum quantum ad Evangelium, cujus praxin salutarem suo exemplo docet. Finem parangelias in genere dicit charitatem, non au- tem Evangelii, uti pervertit Grotius. Nam lex & ad charitatem Dei & proximi directa est tanquam fi- nem internum, & summatim utraque tabula absol- vitur Dei & proximi dilectione; priori tabula di- lectionem Dei, posteriori dilectionem proximi nobis præscribente. In Evangelio charitas Dei er- ga nos sistitur, non autem charitas hominis erga Deum præcipitur. Frequens & facilis est Grotio confusio legis & Evangelii more Sociniano & Ar- miniano. Non negamus tamen parangelian complecti hic quoque Evangelium.

Ek katharas kardias kai syneidēseōs agathēs, kai pisteōs anypo- kritou) Dat nobis & Paulus brevem genealogian sed peruti- lem. Ex fide minima ficta emeth emunah, cujus mentio 2. Tim.II. 5. nascitur bona conscientia, id est abstinentia a pec- catis, Act. XXIII.1. infra 19. III. 9. 2. Tim. I. 3. Ebr. IX. 14. X. 22. XIII.18. 1. Pet. III.16.21. Hinc puritas cordis, id est, inte- rior, Act. 15, 9. Hinc porro dilectio, quæ & pax 2. Tim.II.22.

Nulla hic genealogia. Ex fide non modo purifi- catio cordis est, quæ consistit in emundatione a pec- catis per sanguinem Christi, 1. Joh. I. 7. sed etiam bona conscientia nascitur, cum nempe fidem con- sequitur sanctificatio, quæ etiam purificationis isti9 est consequens. Nam per fidem purgatur con- scientia ab operibus mortuis per sanguinem Christi agni illius immaculati, ut serviamus Deo viventi, Ebr. IX. 14. & efficax est fides per charitatem, Gal. V.

v. 6. Bona vero conscientia, quæ ex fide nascitur, non est ipsa abstinentia a peccatis, sed tranquillitas cordis ob remissionem peccatorum vel justificatio- nem, Rom. V. 1. quam sequitur studium sanctitatis & abstinentia a peccatis, ne conscientiæ tranquillitas turbetur. Tria illa proskeimena dilectionis sunt, quæ justificationem consequitur: Primo quod ex corde puro hominis justificati redundet, utpote cu- jus cor mundatum per Christi sanguinem, tum in sacramento baptismi, quod suscipitur in remissio- nem peccatorum, Act. II. 38. quo abluimur a pec- catis, c. 22, 6. & a mala conscientia liberamur; tum per aspersionem sanguinis Christi, quæ fit præconio Verbi, 1. Petr. I. 2. 22. Lex postulat, tum ut cor pu- rum sit ab omni peccato, tum ut sincerum sit, non fallax. Pri9 quod attinet, nemo de se dicere potest: Purum est cor meum, Prov. XX. 8. idcirco opus fide est, quo non imputentur peccata, Rom. IV. 6. Poste- rius autem ex illa non imputatione sequitur, & cu- c eadem connexum est, Ps. XXXII. 1. 2. Ideo à justi- ficatis requiritur, ut cor habeant sincerum, non hypocriticum. Deinde oritur dilectio è conscientia bona, ut certi de remissione peccatorum & con- scientiæ purificatione Deum & proximum dilige- re, prout par est, animo prompto & sincero con- tendamus, ac Deum quidem ex toto corde, proxi- mum vero ut nosmetipsos. Tertio è fide non ficta: utpote quæ & puritatis cordis & bonitatis atque tranquillitatis conscientiæ causa est. Nam qui in- tegro animo in Deum crediderit, nequaquam tulerit à vera charitate disjungi, quæ omnes consuevit eun- dem in modum complecti, ut hic Theophylactus. Fi- des ἀνυπόκριτος edit etiam charitatem ἀνυπόκρι- τον. Qualis est genitrix, talis est fœtus. Fides ficta, inquit Haymo, est, quæ confitetur in ore, sed non te- netur in corde neque exornatur operibus. Fides ita- que (si sincera sit) Chrysostomo autore in hunc lo- cum, quod verum est, indicat, & ex sincera fide chari- tas gignitur. Qui enim veraciter in Deum credit, nunquam ab ea desistere poterit. Fides autem illa ἀνυπόκριτος qualis sit, B. Lutherus in Summa des Christlichen Lebens Tom. VI. Altenb. fol. 39. do- cet: Dass der Glaube müsse zukommen/ und solcher Glaube/ der nicht Heucheley sey/ und gemenget mit Zuversicht eigener Heiligkeit. Denn wo der nicht ist/ da wird das Hertze nicht vor GOtt rein/ noch das Gewissen bestehct / wenn das scharffe Gericht und Rechnung wird angehen.

v. 6. Ὧν τινες ἀστοχήσαντες) Aberrantes, infra VI. v. 21. 2. Tim. II. 18. Ἐξετράπησαν ματαιολογίαν) Diverterunt, ut infra V. 15. 2. Tim. IV. 4. התפכו ματαιολογία dissertatio infrugifera. Qui talibus utuntur, ματαιολόγοι Tit. I. 10.

Qui à fide ac charitate aberrarunt, diverterunt ad vaniloquia. Vanum est, quantacunque verbo- rum pompa ornetur, quod aberrat à fide ac chari- tate. Metaphora est in voce ἀστοχήσαντες, aberrantes à scopo, petita à malis jaculatoribus, notante Chry- sostomo, Theophylacto, & Oecumenio. Ut sagittantes scopum suum habent propositum, à quo, si qui, cum periti haberi velint, aberrent, ab omnibus ir- ridentur, imprimis in ludis publicis. Sic quosdam dicit à charitate, ejusque individuo comite, ac du- ce, fide non ficta velut à scopo turpissime errasse non citra ignominiam. Ἐξετράπησαν exposuit Vulgata, conversi sunt. Rectius vertitur deflexe- runt. Εἰς ματαιολογίαν ad vaniloquium, ad studia, doctrinas & sermones inanes, μύθους scilicet & γε- νεαλογίας. Notat hic Erasmus Scholasticos, quos nequicquam excusat Estius, quum fateri necessum habeat, peccatum interdum à nonnullis fuisse vel curiositate nimia vel superfluitate. Vid. B. Meisne- rus in Scholis Academicis de vitiosa disputandi ra- tione Scholasticorum.

v. 7. Θέλοντες εἶναι νομοδιδάσκαλοι) De Cerintho Tertul- lianus: Legem etiam proponit, scilicet ad excludendum Evangelium & vindicandum Judaismum. Ephesi multi semper fuerant Judæi: Horum quidam Christianismum in speciem amplexi, multum de Judaïsmo retinebant: Inter fabulas Judaicas erat etiam colloquium legis cum Deo an- te mundum conditum: Volebantque mundum conditum propter legem. Vide Rabbinum Israëlem de anima. Νομο- διδάσκαλοι חפשי תורה, Luc. V. 17. Act. V. 34. Μὴ νοοῦντες μήτε ἃ λέγουσι, μήτε περὶ τίνων διαβεβαιοῦνται) Non vident, quid dicant. Legem ajunt observatu necessa- riam, & eam non observant. Affirmant multa, quæ ex nullo habent certo sensu aut revelatione. Διαβεβαιοῦσθαι est pro certo affirmare, Tit. III. 8. מכל.

Dum explicat, quinam tales aberrantes sint, cau- sas aberrationis simul involvit Apostolus, nimirum tum fastum & presumptionem, quod præ aliis ve- lint haberi legis Interpretes, quales erant tempore Christi νομικοὶ legisperiti, Christum ipsum ex lege probare non verentes, & illi, de quibus Apostolus Rom. II. 19. Unde Theophylactus: Per ambitionem ipsi sibi ignorantia istius & erroris erant autores, tum inscitiam scriptura, unde nesciant, sive quæ asserunt, utpote δευτερώσεις de necessitate ac usu legis, variisque traditionibus, quod ad conclusiones spectat, ad quas referunt Chrysostomus & Theophy- lactus, quæ de scopo ac duratione legis secus doce- bant. Hyperius & alii, quod justificationis doctrinam non recte tradebant, legem cum Evangelio con- fundebant: Sive de quibus asseverant, quæ ad prin- cipia conclusionum referenda videntur, unde βε- βαίωσις petebatur assertionum, ut Haymo, Danæus, & B. Gerhardus accipiunt. Nam qui circa legem neque ea intelligit, quæ asserit, neque ea, quibus assertionibus suis fidem facere vult, adeoque & in conclusionibus & in probationibus nullam habet veram notitiam & intelligentiam, ille quantum- cunque se venditet legisperitum ac Doctorem, à scopo legis & veritate aberrat, ac p. c. ad matæo- logiam deflectit. Honoris ergo causa jam legis usum explicat.

v. 8. Οἴδαμεν δὲ, ὅτι καλὸς ὁ νόμος, ἐάν τις αὐτῷ νομίμως χρῆται) Lex hunc usum semper habuit, & nunc quoque habet, ostendat scelera & flagitia DEO displicere. Vide Rom. VII. 12. כמשפט Νομίμως.

Nos vero, inquit Apostolus, scimus, opponens suam aliorumque verorum Doctorum scientiam falsorum doctorum ignorantiæ. Admittit autem κατ' ἀνθυποφορὰν, prævertens objectionem, quasi doctrinâ Apostolica lex ipsa arguatur ceu non bo- na, quia lex nihil faciat ad justificationem ac salu- tem consequendam. Novimus omnino, non enim opus est, ut ab istis νομοδιδασκάλοις id primum di- scamus, quod lex bona sit, tum quia à bono Deo profecta, tum quia de bono nos informat, quid faciendum & quomodo malum fugiendum, tum quia ad bonum nos, si præstetur, deducit, Rom. VII.

v. 12. Sed bona est, si quis illa νομίμως legitimè uta- tur: Bona semper in se est, nec per abusum intrin- sece redditur non bona, sed ut bona nobis sit & in bonum cedat, usus ejus legitimus requiritur, quem

Deus intendit. Ita ergo Apostolus tangit finem legis, qui triplex est, primo, quod nos convincat de peccato ejusque reatu, adeoque pædagogus nobis sit ad Christum, per quem liberamur à peccato, deinde quod à peccato liberatos dirigat in charita- te ex corde puro, conscientia bona, & fide non fi- cta, ne gratia exhibita excidamus. Denique quod infidelibus incumbat ad pœna, ac facinorosos coër- ceat. Primus usus solet vocari Pædagogicus; alter Pædeuticus: Tertius Politicus, quem forensem po- tius dixerimus, ut forum tum divinum tum huma- num respiciatur. Legitime, inquit Theophylactus, ille utitur lege, qui per legem ad Christum deducitur. Lex namque, quæ justificandi careat potestate, ad Christum remittit, idque lex ipsa exigit, ut quis se utatur legiti- me, hoc est, quemadmodum ipsa lex jubet, quæ sibi Christum præponit. Non autem νομίμως utebantur lege Adversarii usum legis à Deo intentum magna partam negligentes. Nam nec peccata recte æsti- mabant è lege, per Pharisæicas corruptelas occupa- ti, adeoque justitiam propriam erigentes, Christu, qui est τέλος νόμε, prout par erat, non suscipiebant: nec in usu pædeutico vel directoriο legis νομίμως versari poterant, magis circa inanes δευτερώσεις & ceremonias, quam moralia occupati: Et quia fide vera excidebant per legis & Evangelii mixturam, gratiæq; meræ abnegatione, lex ipsos maledictio- ne feriebat, utpote vera, quæ in solo Christo est, justitia destitutos. De tertio usu imprimis differit peculiariter, quia secundus in summaria comple- xione doctrinæ Christianæ charitatis nomine, quæ est pleroma legis Rom. XIII. 8. 9. 10: jam v. 5. com- prehensus est. Primum autem exemplo suo mon- strat in praxi, cum se primarium peccatorem profi- tetur, & unice divinae gratiae, & Salvatoris Christi redemptioni salutem acceptam refert.

Eidos touto, hoti dikaio nomos ou keitai) eidos pro oida יֹדֵעַ. Frequens enim Ebraeis participium ponere pro verbo prae- senti, quo carent. Latinus legit eidotes. Sensus est: Si posteri Abrahami, Isaaci, & Jacobi fuissent, quales illi majores eo- rum fuerant, lege Mosis opus non fuisset. Aegyptius incola- tus & inde nata contagia eam fecerunt necessariam. Lex illa Dei per Mosen data magna sui parte effectus habet commu- nes cum aliis civilibus populorum legibus. Philo de alle- goriis: 'Entelletai de touto all' ouchi toi kat' eikona kai ten idean gegonoti. Ekeinos men gar kai dicha proptropes ten areten echei automathos. Deinde: Toi men en teleioi kai kat' eikona pro- stattes, e apagoreuein oudeis dei. Oudenos gar o teleios deitai. Xenocratis dictum de Philosophis refert Laertius: Monos poiein hekousios, ha poiousin akontes hoi loipoi dia ton nomon. Id Servius ad illud VII. Aeneidos: Sponte sua veterisque Dei se more tenentem, Sic extulit: Xenocrates qui cum primus Philosophiae scholam aperuisset, (quod antea in porticibus Philosophi tractarent) & interrogatus esset, quid praestare possit discipulis? respondit, ut id voluntate faciant, quod alii jure cogantur: Tacitus Annal. III. Vetustissimi mortalium nulla adhuc mala libidine, sine pre- tio, scelere, eoque sine poena aut coërcitionibus agebant: neque praemiis opus erat, cum honesta suopte ingenio peterentur, & ubi nihil contra morem cuperent, nihil per metum vetabantur. Idem de Germania: Plusque ibi boni mores valent, quam alibi bonae leges. Clemens Strom. IV. ut Socrates citat: Nomou heneka agathon ouk an genoito. Idem Strom. V. Toi teleioi ouk en symbolaiois politikois, oud' en apagoreusei nomou, all' ex idiopragias kai tes pros ton Theon agapes he dikaiosyne. Plato de legibus IX. Aischron men de tina tropon, nomothetein panta hoposa nyn mellomen teithe drai en toioutei polei, hen phamen oi- kesesthai te eu kai pases orthotetos pros epitedeusin aretes, ubi & alia ad hanc rem. Laudatur & Aristotelis dictum: Hoti ek philosophias touto auto perigegoine, to anepitaktos poiein, ha tines dia ton apo ton nomon phobon poiousi. Cornelia apud Propertium: Mi natura dedit leges a sanguine ductas, Ne possem melior judicis esse metu. Dio Chrysostomus dissertatione LXXVI. ei gar hapantes esan agathoi, delonoti ton engraphon (nomon) hemin ouk an edei, ubi & plura huc pertinentia. Epicurus non longe hinc abit: Hoi nomoi charin ton sophon keintai, ouch hopos me adikosin, all' hopos me adikontai.

Sensum illum Grotii nemo divinando assequi potuisset. Abraham, Isaac & Jacobus legem omni- no eandem habuere, quam Moses duabus tabulis postea divino jussu consignavit. Nam Decalogus legem Protoplastis natura insculpta exhibet: quae etsi obscurata per lapsum fuit, non tamen penitus erasa. De forensi lege ac ceremoniali alia ratio est, illa ob politiam Judaicam data, haec magnam parte ob Messiam praefigurandum sancita. Neutra alios proprie populos concernebat, quam Judaicum. De hisce autem in praesenti non agitur. Moralis legis ratio exponitur: Quod illa justo non incumbat. Justus per naturam fuit ante lapsum Adam. Per gratiam post lapsum sunt, qui cum Adamo in Mes- siam credunt. Ea in parte non differunt posteri Pa- triarcharum a Patriarchis. Ex aequo enim justifica- tur & servantur, quotquot credunt in Christum, Act. XV. 11. Atque ita justum intelligit Ambrosius, qui accepta remissione justificatus est. Illos ergo non premit lex, non incumbit iis, nec ratione maledi- ctionis, nec ratione coactionis, rigoris, vel etia neces- sitatis observationis ad salutem. Non negat legere- gulae & directionis ratione, ac more renatis neces- sariam, quod contrarium esset Verbo: Neq; dicit o tithetai, sed ou keitai, quo significatur imprimis onus maledictionis, quod incumbit legis conteptoribus, aliisque, prolixe recensitis. Bernhard. Non dicitur, inquit, justis cessat, non habent legem aut justi sunt sine lege; sed justis non est lex posita: Sed voluntariis eo liberaliter data, quo suaviter inspirata. Fren.

inquit Theophylactus, equo lascivienti & efferato, non ductu facili imponuntur. Recte ergo B. Hun- nius: Apostolicum, inquit, pronunciatum non sim- pliciter, sed secundum quid accipiendum est: Con- stat enim, etiam justo Adamo legem fuisse positam an- te lapsum, Gen. II. Constat piis & renatis legem ideo positam esse, ut in illam ceu speculum intuentes naturæ suæ deformitatem liquidius adspiciant, & pro- fundius agnoscant: & ut in statu novæ obedientiæ le- gis ductum ceu præscriptam formam ac normam se- quantur, secundum quam Deo sua præbent ac præ- stent officia: Et hactenus quidem etiam justo lex est posita. Ratione vero tertii finis (qui est coërcere in officio præfractos, & disciplinam externam inter ho- mines conservare) lex justo posita non est.

Recenset eos, quibus coërcendis lex data sit, quosque premat onere maledictionis. Ἀνόμους Vul- gata, B. Luther. Piscator reddidere injustos. Beza legis còmtemptores, alii exleges. Ἀσεβεῖς aliis impii sunt, qui adversus primam legis tabulam peccant. Nomen ἁμαρτωλοὶ non tantum de seditiosis, sed etiam aliis insignibus peccatoribus occurrit, Luc. III. v. 31. XV. 1. Gen. XIII. 13. 1. Sam. XV. 13. Βέβηλοι qui publice & nullo pudore peccant. Distinctionem ta- men B. Hunnii Grotianæ præferendam censemus; qui præmitti observat, quæ totum genus sceleratorũ complectuntur, quos injustos, inobsequentes, impios & peccatores nominat, non eo, quo natura sumus omnes, gradu atque modo, sed plane κατ' ἐξοχὴν, cum datur opera ejusmodi crassis peccatis, & externis, quæ & in oculos occurrunt, & rationis judicio da- mnantur. Ideoque & ea, quæ in specie recensentur peccata, cum lege Dei pugnantia, non esse, (hoc qui- dem in loco) de interna legis prævaricatione seu pec- catis intra cordis latebras conclusis intelligenda, sed de manifestis, quæ nemo, nisi mente captus, peccata esse negat. Illos vero transgressores juxta seriem præ- ceptorum secundæ tabulæ distribui. Primo enim loco ponit eos, qui partim quarti, partim quinti præcepti repagula confringunt, ut sunt πατραλοῖαι parricidæ, & μητραλοῖαι matricidæ, qui lucem iis adimunt, quorum beneficio ipsis lucem hanc adspicere datum est, nempe genitoribus & parentibus suis. Atque ibi supremo gradu peccant contra præceptum quartum: Honora patrem & matrem tuam, similiter contra quintum præceptum: Non occides. Qui quanto sup- plicio digni sint, inde liquet, quod lex eos, qui paren- tibus duntaxat maledicunt, aut percutiunt tantum, non etiam necant, morte plectendos, Exod. XXI. Lev. XX. His porro proxime accensentur, qui sim- pliciter quintum præceptum violant, homicidæ, quos itidem lex e medio tolli præcepit, Gen. IX. & Exod. XXI. His subjunguntur, qui contra sexum præce- ptum illicitis sese, nefariisque libidinibus contami- nant: Ut sunt scortatores, qui cum solutis personis rem habent; Deinde masculorum concubitores, qui cum masculis infandam libidinem exercent, scelere contra naturam, quod Sodomiticum appellatur. Et hos lex Dei jubet exterminari, quippe lucis usura prorsus indignos, Levit. XX. Ab his transitum facit Apostolus ad septimi præcepti peccata, ex quorum cumulo id, quod primarium, & atrocissimum est, perstringit, plagium videlicet, cum quis alteri non as, non aurum, non ferrum, non vestes, non pecora, non domos aut agros, sed homines, adeoque id, quod in rebus humanis omnium habet pretiosissimum, uxo- rem, liberosve, seu per vim seu dolo abducit & eripit. Quibus itidem extremam mortis sententiam dictat lex Mosaica Exod. XXI. Tandem eos etiam in hunc atrum & infaustum catalogum refert, qui octavi præcepti violatione peccant. Tales sunt mendaces, qui ut noceant proximo, aut inter eos, qui pacifice vive- bant, dissidia serant, excogitatis mendaciis, & falsis testimoniis octavo præcepto vetitis, concordiam illorum disturbare, & infestis contentionibus imo digladiationibus illos inter sese committere moliun- tur. Horum in præcepto octavo nefarie violando so- cii sunt perjuri, qui datam fidem perjurii scelere violare nihil exhorrescunt.

v. 11. Καὶ εἴτι ἕτερον τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδασκαλίᾳ ἀντίκειται, κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς δόξης τοῦ μακαρίου Θεοῦ) Est συνεκδοχὴ, non enim lex omnia coërcet, quæ Evangelium improbat, sed graviora. Vide, quæ diximus in Annot. ad c. IV. libri I. de Jure Belli ac Pacis. Doctrina Philosophorum & Rabbinorum partim sana, partim morbida, quæ in Evangelio tota sana, infra VI. 3. 2. Tim. I. 13. IV. 3. Tit. I. 9. II. 1. Est אָמְנָה שְׁלֵמָה ut loquuntur Ebræi. Evangelium dicitur τῆς δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ ex effectu, quia Deus inde maximam gloriam consequitur, 2. Cor. IV. 6. 15. Eph. I. 6. 12. 14. Philipp. I. 11. Vocatur au- tem hic & infra VI. 15. Deus μακάριος, ut exprimatur E- bræum יָשִׁיר, Deus sibi sufficiens erat ad beatitudinem, non indigebat nostri. Fecit ergo, quicquid fecit, nostri causa. Syrus hic posuit מברכא εὐλογητοῦ. Etiam Græci de diis suis dicunt μάκαρες, sed falso.

Recurrit error ille geminus Grotii, quod lex non coërceat peccata omnia, sed graviora, & quod Evangelii etiam sit peccata coërcere. Isto legis per- fectioni derogatur, hoc natura Evangelii everti- tur, quod est concio gratiæ, non iræ, uti contra lex iram operatur, Rom. IV. 15. Per τὴν ὑγιαίνουσην διδασκαλίαν generaliter doctrina cœlestis, non ve- ro Evangelium intelligitur : Quæ ita vocatur vel per Metaphoram, quod non laboret errorum mor- bis; vel per Metonymiam, quod veram animæ sa- nitatem afferat: quum Evangelium peculiariter sana illa doctrina vocetur, quæ conscientias legis terroribus sauciatas sanat, Christum Salvatorem & Medicum ipsis monstrando, ut hic B. Gerhardus.

Non male hic Antinomis respondet Crocius : Sen- sus est, inquit, legem adversari omnibus, quæ cum pura salutis doctrina pugnant. Antinomi hoc ver- bum Apostoli adversus legem torquebant, concluden- tes, peccata Evangelio argui, proinde legis usum nul- lum esse hodie. Vere torquent: Non enim sequitur, sce- lera tum nominata, tum alia innominata Evangelio adversantur. Ergo Evangelium ea directe arguit. Adversantur, quia legem Evangelium non abolet sed stabilit: scelera repugnant fructibus fidei, quam tradit Evangelium. Dum medicinam offert, indire- cte convincit nos ægritudinis. At directe agnitio mor- bi ex lege. Ideo ejus usus necessarius. Plenior est B. Hunnii responsio : Evangelio autem adversantur enumerata scelera, non quod sit Evangelii speciali- ter sic appellati munus, arguere & damnare pecca- ta : Sed primum quia enormibus istis peccatis ho- minum impiorum de novo crucifigitur Christus, qui totius Evangelica predicationis cor & caput est : Deinde quia peccatis hisce, quæ in catalogo suo recenset Apostolus, conscientia sic vastatur, ut fidei, (quam scimus ad Evangelii doctrinam pertinere, & ex ea nasci) nullus possit esse locus. Tertio quia iisdem atrocibus delictis impediuntur Evangelicæ fidei justitiæque fructus, ut homo nec Deo nec Ev- angelio digne ambulet, sed sit ad omne opus bonum reprobus. Denique quia faciunt illa hominem ab- errare à fine patefacti Evangelii, qui est, ut liberati à peccatis serviamus Deo in sanctitate & justitia Luc. 1. & simus populus peculiaris, sectator bono- rum operum, Tit. 2. Porro distinctionem receptam hic immutat Grotius. Nam hæc xατὰ τὸ Εὐαγγέ- λιον τῆς δόξης τῦ μακαρίε Θεῦ ad v. 11. spectant, ubi Vulgata præmisit ad supplendum sensum voces il- las: QUÆ SIT secundum Evangelium. De quo Theophylactus: Hunc orationis, inquit, contextum ita construito: Sanæ doctrinæ, quæ secundum Evan- gelium constat. Dicit secundum Evangelium, non secundum legem, ut ostendat, se nec legem tolle- re, nec illi contraria docere, quin potius suavem esse consensum inter legem & Evangelium, quum lex adversetur omnibus, quæ pugnant cum Ev- angelio. Evangelium autem gloriæ dicitur, non modo quod gloriam Dei patefaciat, eidemque ce- lebrandæ inserviat, sed etiam, quod medium sit, gloriam Dei consequendi, ut eadem æternum fruamur, quia est potentia Dei ad salutem omni cre- denti, Rom. 1, 16.

Ὅ ἐπισεύθην ἐγὼ) Loquendi genus Græcum, quale Rom. 3, 2. 1. Cor. 9, 17. Tit. 1, 3.

Vers. 12.

Καὶ χάριν ἔχω τῷ ἐνδυναμώσαντί με Χρισῷ τῷ Κυρίῳ) Non possum rem tantam exequi sine eximia ejus ope. Ἐνδυναμῶντί με מעזני 2. Sam. 22, 33. aut הזק Psalm. 19, 2. vide Act. 9, 22. 1. Tim. 4, 17. Ebr. 11, 34.

Ὅτι πισόν με ἡγήσατο) Ut magnum à Deo auxilium consequamur, non satis est à Deo vocari, sed opus est fidem præstemus in eo, ad quod vocati sumus: Sicut Paulus fecit 1. Cor. 4, 2. c. 7. 25.

Θέμενος εἰς διακονίαν) Postquam me adhibuisset mi- nisterio. Nam θέμενος hic est plus quam perfectæ si- gnificationis. Διακονία per excellentiam Apostolatus Act. 1, 17. 25. Rom. 11, 13. 2. Cor. 4, 1. c. 5. 8.

Recte hæc de donis ministrantibus, non sanctifi- cantibus accipiuntur de assistentia & confortatio- ne in officii partibus, in quibus fidelem CHRI- STUS invenit Apostolum. Nam πισὸν non fidem justificantem, sed fidelitatem muneris infert hic & 1. Corinth. 4, 12. Ubi vero probè Estius: Jam quod dicit, quia fidelem me existimavit, non sic accipiendum, quasi DEUS Paulum fidelem invenerit, non autem fecerit, (quod lectori parum attento Chrysostomus ejusque sequaces videri possunt sensisse) sed minus dicendo plus voluit intelligi. Nam homines quidem iis credunt rerum suarum dispensationem, quos fideles existimant, etsi non fa- ciunt. DEUS autem neminem judicat fidelem, quem non faciat. Idque significare voluisse Aposto- lum probat ipsa gratiarum actio. Nulla enim gra- tia Deo debetur, quod hominem, qui fidelis est, talem judicet (est enim hoc judicium in Deo necessarium) sed quod talem faciat.

Vers. 13.

Τὸν πρότερον ὄντα βλάσφημον καὶ διώκτην, καὶ ὑβρισὴν Ostendit magnitudinem beneficii è statu suo priore. Adeo βλάσφημος fuerat, ut etiam alios cogeret βλασφη- μεῖν Act. 26, 11. Erat & persecutor, ut apparet Act. 9, 4. 5. c. 22, 4. c. 26, 11. 1. Cor. 15, 9. & contumeliosus, ut appa- ret Act. 8, 3. c. 9, 2. De voce ὑβρίζον vide Matth. 22, 6.

Ἀλλ’ ἠλεήθην, ὅτι ἀγνοῶν ἐποίησα ἐν ἀπιστίᾳ) Non cau- sam adfert, cur ipsi ignosci debuerit, sed cur Deus ipsi po- tius, quam aliis ignoverit. Sunt שְׁגָגוֹת ἀγνοίαι pec- cata, sed in genere peccatorum minus gravia, quam ea quæ fiunt בְּיָד רָמָה, ut est Num. 15, 30. Vide Luc. 12, 40. ἐν ἀπιστίᾳ tempus designat, cum adhuc incredulus, inquit, essem. Ἠλεήθην dicitur ea forma, qua modo ἐπιστεύθην רֻחַמְתִּי in Pual, vide Act. 23, 1.

Ita Papistis velificari videtur Grotius, cum cau- sam reddi dicit, cur Paulo potius, quam aliis Deus ignoverit, quemadmodum Becanus ex hoc loco ve- niale peccatum, quod excausa vocat, colligit, quod aliquo modo dignum sit venia, quia non ex malitia, sed ex ignorantia sit commissum: Et Bellarminus di- sputat libr. I. de grat. & statu pecc. cap. 3. & 11. in hujusmodi veniali peccato esse aliquid, quod im- minuat peccatum. Ex adverso Salmero, ut & Tho- mas & glossa ordinaria censet, non imminuere hæc sed exaggerere peccatum, quasi dicat, Deus vidit me per incredulitatem excæcatum, ut mala mea non agnoscerem, ideo mera sua misericordia me prævenit. Conferens locum Gen. 8, 21. Sed optime Estius: Videtur dicendum, quod fecisse per ignorantiam re- spectu misericordiæ ac veniæ à Deo impetrandæ in prædictis sententiis neque allegatur proprie ad exagge- rationem peccati, neque ad ejus extenuationem, præser- tim cum omnibus peccatis aliquo modo commune sit, quod ex ignorantia fiant, quemadmodum docetur in 2. sent. d. 22. sed affertur ut ratio objecti maxime convenientis, circa quod Deus misericordiam suam exerceat. Nam objectum seu materia misericordiæ est miseria. Unde quanto miseria major, tanto ma- gis nata est misericordiam movere. Quod igitur A- postolus dicit, tale est: Ideo misericordiam consecutus sum, quia magna erat miseria mea, hæc nimirum quod tanta mala facerem per ignorantiam & incre- dulitatem, instar ægroti, qui per insaniam medicum cædit, quemadmodum pulchre explicat Augustinus Serm. VIII. de verb. Apost.

Vers. 14.

Ὑπερεπλεόνασε δὲ ἡ χάρις τῦ Κυρίυ ἡμῶν) Multum cre- vit in me Christi gratia, id est, dona spiritualia. Ὑπερε- πλεόνασε בְּמְאֹד מְאֹד פָּרַץ. Sic illi ὑπερπερίσσευσεν ἡ χάρις, Rom. 5, 20. Amat enim Paulus tales voces, ut alibi jam notavimus.

Μετὰ πίστεως κὰ ἀγάπης τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησῦ) Quantum in me, inquit, crevit fides & dilectio tam Dei quam proximi propter Christum. Cyprianus ad Donatum: Nostrum tan- tum sitiat pectus & pateat: quantum illuc fidei afferimus, tantum gratiæ inundantis haurimus. Notant veteres hic conjungi liberum arbitrium cum gratia, sed ita ut gratiæ non tantum priores sint partes sed & superiores.

Hæc de libero arbitrio non conveniunt textui. Nihil enim de libero arbitrio. Gratiæ omnia tri- buit Apostolus. Et quidem fsuperabundanti, quæ in remissione peccatorum, & vocatione Apostoli admiranda ratione se exeruit. Superabundavit, inquit Chrysostomus, id est, excessit misericordia mo- dum; quippe ista non miserentis, sed amantis sunt, ac desiderantis, & nimia vi dilectionis affecti. Ad- ditur ergo, μετὰ πίστεως κὶ ἀγάπης, non quod per fidei & dilectionis meritum vel opus gratia abun- darit; gratia enim non est gratia, ullo modo, nisi sit gratuita omni modo, ut habet Augustini regula è Rom. 11, 6. Sed quod gratia una cum fide, ac dile- ctione, quæ est in Christo Jesu superabundarit, hoc est, quod non tantum gratia remissionis pec- catorum, sed etiam donationis vel operationis fi- dei & dilectionis in Apostolo, quæ per Spiritum sanctum excitatur in nobis, superabundanter sese exeruerit, vel si malis reddere PER: quod per ipsam fidei & dilectionis gratiosam donationem in eo, qui fidei adversarius, & fidelium non amator, sed persecutor insignis fuerit, gratia

Divina sese superabundanter exhibuerit ac de- monstrarit in Christo Jesu, hoc est, quam acquisi- vit Christus, qui mihi est ejus conciliator, non lex.

Vers. 15.

Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος, καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος) Eadem verba habes infra c. 4, 9. Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος etiam infra c. 3, 1. & 2. Tim. 2, 11. & Tit. 3, 8. Ebræi dicunt אמת הדבר. Non tantum vera est hæc, quam dicam sententia, sed & digna, quæ fiat plurimi. Sic ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιον dixit Dio- dorus Siculus. Ἀποδοχῆς ἀξιῶσαι Dionysius Halicar- nassensis in Rhetoricis. Pari sensu ἀποδεκτὸς habebimus infra c. 2, 3.

Ab exemplo gratiæ Domini sibi exhibitæ, hypo- thesin ad thesin transferens ad generalem gratiæ CHRISTI deprædicationem, vel summam potius Evangelicæ concionis gratiæ progreditur, quo o- mnes peccatores inde fidem ac solatium haurire possint. Quem finem non diffitetur in Calvini schola Crocius: Non satis est, inquit, Apostolo, id quod æmuli adversus muneris autoritatem objicie- bant, ad augendam ministerio fidem transferre. Transfert porro ad omnium quorumvis maximorum peccatorum resipiscentium solidam utilitatem, Chri- sti adventus & Divinæ misericordiæ erga se declara- tæ exemplo, ut intelligant, quod adversarii ipsi da- bant probro, id Ecclesiæ utile esse. Dum enim ex immani bellua CHRISTUS Pastorem fecit, mani- festum gratiæ specimen edidit, unde maximi quique peccatores certam fiduciam concipiant: Nullis enim gravissimis aditum ad salutem præcludi. Quod si intenditur à Paulo, necessum est, non particula- rem, sed universalem esse gratiam Dei salutife- ram. Exhibet autem Apostolus hic 1. Evange- lii elogium ac certitudinem, quod sermo sit non in- certus aut dubius, sed πιστὸς fidelis, id est, verissi- mus ac certissimus, cui fides tuto adhibeatur, ac πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος, dignus, qui omni receptione admittatur, quemque fideli apprehensione omnes merito suum faciant, sibique applicent. Πάσης, inquit, ἀποδοχῆς, ut omnibus modis suscipien- dum, omni religione venerandum ac fide omni ex parte dignissimum innuatur Verbum Evangelii. Nonnulli videntur legisse χρηστὸς humanus, ut Ambrosiaster, sed Codd. omnes cum Syro & Vulgato habent πιστός. Quod etiam Græci ac La- tini alii retinuere. In Ebræo נאמן אדני dictum Domini respondere ajunt, etiam B. Gerhardus. Quod autem huic sententiæ hoc elogium tribuat, non ea mente accipiendum, ac si alia in scriptu- ris minus certa essent: Sed quod hic summam Evangelii, atque articulum fidei maxime princi- palem, & cujus interest omnium, quicunque fi- dem salvificam vel concipere, vel conceptam adversus tentationes quasvis fovere debeant, proponat, quo pacto etiam docetur, quod ad fidem, quæ huic Verbo relative respondet, quum Verbum & fides relata sint, requiratur ἀποδοχὴ seu receptio Verbi & Christi, qui per Verbum Evangelii fide suspiciendus exhibetur, Johan. 1, 12. ceu proprium Evangelii objectum. Addit etiam Chrysostomus hanc elogii istius cau- sam, quod sermo ille nostræ rationi incredibilis videatur, ideoque contra omni receptione fidei dignus definiatur. Incredibile, inquit, videbatur: Siquidem homo, qui omnem vitam priorem fru- stra & inaniter consumpsisset, duxissetque per mala opera, postmodum ex fide sola salvandus diceretur. Denique opponitur ita fabulis & mateologiæ τῶν ἑτεροδόξων, quæ nihil certi, nihil acceptione digni habebant. Judæi jactabant traditionem & cabalam, quam legi scriptæ æquabant. Sed hic est vera & cælestis cabala à Deo per Verbum Pro- phetarum & Apostolorum accepta omni acce- ptione superior, omni acceptatione dignissima. Quo respicere Apostolum Paulus Fagius obser- vat: Verbum, קבל inquit, non simpliciter respicere significat, sed pro certo ac indubitato aliquid reti- cere, acquiescere ac fidem habere. Hinc derivatur vox Cabala, qua intelligunt Ebræi, quicquid authen- ticum, certum, & indubitatum est. Hinc autem nata est Cabala, quod olim à Patribus sacra myste- ria, maxime quæ de regno Christi ore ad os per suc- cessionem tradebantur, quæ alius ab alio accipiebat, unde ab accipiendo Cabala dicebatur, &c. Ad Ca- balisticam illam rationem allusit Apostolus 1. Tim. 1. ubi & voce Cabala usus est. Sic enim scribit: Fide- lis sermo, & omni acceptione sive Cabala dignus, quia Christus Jesus venit in hunc mundum, peccatores salvos facere, quasi dicat: Si quis cupiat audire ca- balam, ego certam, veram & indubitatam indica- bo. Ea autem est, quod Christus Jesus venit in hunc mundum, ut peccatores salvos faceret. Hoc ve- rum dogma Cabalisticum est, de quo plane nihil ambigendum. Cohærent sane illa: Sermo fidus & omni acceptione dignus. Nam quia fidus, di- gnus etiam acceptione est; Sed peculiariter hoc posterius additur, ut natura fidei, quemadmodum diximus, explicetur.

Ὅτι Χριστὸς Ἰησῦς ἦλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον) id est, Dei do- no hominibus apparuit, Joh. 1, 9. c. 3, 2. c. 6, 14. c. 9, 39. c. 11, 27. c. 12, 46. c. 18, 37.

Ἁμαρτωλὺς σῶσαι) Matth. 9, 13. Marc. 2, 17. Luc. 5, 32. Rom. 5, 8.

Addit jam secundo Apostolus Evangelii summa- rium, quod consistit in adventus vel incarnationis Christi veritate, ejusdemque fine, salvatione pecca- torum. Jesum Christum dicit venisse, ut innuat, Messiam promissum, hoc est, unctum illum Domi- ni, qui χριστὸς Græcis, exhibitum esse: Eundem- que non alium esse, quam JESUM, qui hoc no- men consequutus est in circumcisione, Luc. 2, 20. Sicut hisce duabus vocibus fidei summam ita com- plexus est S. Johannes: Hæc scripta sunt, ut cre- datis Jesum esse Christum Dei Filium, & 1. Joh. 5, 1. Qui credit, quod JESUS sit CHRISTUS, ex DEO genitus est. Quum vero JESUS CHRISTUS Filius DEI sit, Filii DEI adventum in hunc mundum hic designat; qui etsi semper in mundo fuit, quia mundus per ipsum factus est, venisse tamen in mundum dicitur, quum in assumpta humana natura in mundo esse, & in carne manife- stari voluit, 1. Timoth. 3, 16. cum Verbum caro fa- ctum est, & habitavit in nobis, Johan. 1, 14. cum Filius DEI æternus carnis & sanguinis nostri par- ticeps factus est, & semen Abrahæ assumpsit, Ebr. 2, 14. & 16. Exiit enim à Patre, & in mundum venit nascendo, quemadmodum vicissim mundum reliquit & profectus est ad Patrem moriendo & ascendendo in cœlum, Joh. 16, 28. Finis incar- nationis est, ut peccatores salvaret. Quos? Non Angelos, sed homines; non justos, non enim inve- nit justos, ac ne unum quidem Psal. 14, vers. 3. sed peccato obnoxios, ac mortis & damnationis æternæ reos. Omnes enim declinarant, simul inutiles facti erant, Roman. 3, 12. Totus mundus erat DEO ὑπόδικος, vers. 19. Omnes erant sub incredulitate conclusi, cap. 11. vers. 32. sub peccato, Galat. 3. vers. 22. ut salvaret ἁμαρτωλὺς peccato- res, qui corrupto naturæ habitu, qui internis cogitatis, dictis, factisque DEO repugnabant. Non quosdam, sed indefinite, omnes, nemine exce- pto, nemine excluso. Omnium enim Deus mi- sereri voluit, Rom. 11, 32. toti mundo Filium suum unigenitum dedit, Joh. 3, 16. Salvatorem mundi, 1. Johan. 4, 16. Non venit ut perderet, sed ut salva- ret peccatores. Non enim misit DEUS Filium su- um, ut judicaret mundum, sed ut salvaretur mundus per ipsum, Joh. 3, 17. Non tantum ut liberaret, & absolveret peccatores a peccato & poena peccati, morte, & condemnatione æterna, sed ut salutem ac vitam, & salutem æternam ipsis compararet ac donaret. Ut salvaret, nempe auferendo ma- lum, & conferendo bonum, auferendo per satisfa- ctionem, conferendo per meritum, quod utrum- que præstare intendat per vocationem ad salutis partæ communionem, per justificationem, qua pec- cata remittuntur, & justitia ejus nobis imputatur per fidem: necnon per glorificationem, qua plene liberati a peccato ejusque pœna ad salutem & vi- tam æternam provehimur. Non ait, ut servare incipiat, & illi porro seipsos servent, sed ut servet, scilicet plane & perfecte. Non ut animam servet, sed ut homines peccatores, adeoque corpus & a- nimam servet. Non ait, ut ad tempus servet, sed absolute, ut servet, scilicet in æternum.

Ὧν πρῶτός εἰμι ἐγώ) Hoc non est sententiæ, sed obiter ei additum. Est au- tem dictum ὑπερβολικῶς ex summa modestia, qualis & 1. Corinth. 15. vers. 9.

Applicat hanc universalem Christi redemptio- nem ad sese in individuo, suoque exemplo docet, quod quisque sibi eam applicare, ac vera fide ap- prehendere debeat. Ideo quemadmodum hypo- thesin ad thesin transtulerat: Ita nunc a thesi ad hy- pothesin, & exemplum suum regreditur. Non er- go hoc obiter additur, sed ex instituto, ut pariter ex- emplo ejus salvare nos velle non perdere CHRI- STUM concludamus, etsi maximi peccatores si- mus. Non enim venit, ut peccatorum tantum certum genus, sed ut peccatores quosvis quibus- cunque peccatis obnoxios servaret. Primum se agnoscebat Apostolus non ratione temporis, ut somniavit quidam hæreticus apud Thomam in h. l. quasi Adami primi peccatoris anima in Paulum migravit; sed ratione prævaricationis: Quo de Augustinus in Psalm. 70. Nunquid ante illum non erant peccatores? Quid est ergo primus ego? An- tecedens omnes non tempore, sed malignitate. Quæ non per hyperbolen, aut ex modestia dicta, sed ex vera humilitate, animique contritione ac sensu, quod peccatum ita animo suo obversaretur, ita eum an- geret, ac si vel maximus esset inter omnes peccato- res. Imo vero, inquit Danæus, ex serio intimoque a- nimi sensu loquitur, & quali a nobis infidelitas omnis, maximeque obstinata apprehendi debet cum pavore ac horrore conscientiæ. Qua confessione sibi abro- gat omne meritum, dignitatem, præparationem & dispositionem ad gratiam, nosque docet, quantis- cunque onusti simus peccatis, non desperare, sed hunc Salvatorem peccatorum ejusque salutem o- mnibus partam vera fide apprehendere. Si dixe- rit quispiam, inquit Chrysostomus, Regem omnibus culpas velle dimittere, non ita verbis fides adhibebi- tur, sicuti si videant eum, qui plus omnibus, gravius- que deliquit, venia fuisse donatum. Nulla enim jam ambiguitas remanere poterit, quum omnibus igno- scere velle existimetur Rex, qui eum absolverit, qui erat præ cæteris peccatoribus insignis, hoc & Paulus ait: Quum inquit, vellet Deus certiores homines fa- cere, quod omnia illis peccata donavit, elegit eum, qui plus omnibus deliquerat, cui scelera cuncta dimitte- ret. Me enim potito venia, nemini jam de se dubi- tare permittitur, quemadmodum etiam habet con- suetudo loquendi: Si huic ignovit Deus, neminem puniet, ut per id ostendatur, ipsum venia quidem di- gnum non fuisse, verum eam aliorum pro salute me- ruisse. Nullus igitur ambigat, inquit, nullus de se desperet, quandoquidem ipse salvatus sum.

Vers. 16.

Ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἠλεήθην, ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ πρώτῳ ἐνδείξηται Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τὴν πᾶσαν μακροθυμίαν) Christus Dei ima- go. Deus cum ignoscit & causas habere solet προκα- ταρκτικὰς, qualis illa de qua supra 13. & præterea τελι- κὰς, id est, aliquem usum, quem sibi proponit. Vide quæ diximus ad Luc. 7, 47. Sic Midrasch in Psal. 51. ait, ideo permissum labi Davidem, ut alios solari posset. Πρῶτος vero hic est positum pro πρότερον, ut Joh. 1, 15. in me Christus priusquam in aliis qui à me erant con- vertendi; ostendit summam suam lenitatem. Quidam Codices hic habent, ἐν ἐμοὶ πρώτῳ sensu eodem. Πᾶσαν hic interpretor summam, ut modo πάσης ἀποδοχῆς. Sic Herodoto ἐλπὶς πᾶσα, spes maxima. Hanc lenita- tem μακροθυμίαν etiam Petrus vocat 2. Petr. 3, 15.

Non comparat se Apostolus cum post conver- tendis, sed cum peccatoribus maximis, & quemad- modum insignissimum se inter eos ex seria cordis contritione professus est: ita imprimis sibi mise- ricordiam exhibitam, summamque longanimita- tem sibi à Jesu, quem persequutus erat, Actor. 9, 5. præ aliis demonstratam esse deprædicat, ut alii et- iam eandem expectare habeant. Quod Theodo- retus ita declaravit: Quemadmodum, inquit, medi- cus, cum in una domo multi simul ægrotant, & omnes de salute desperant, si unum pessime affectum acce- perit, & datis ei medicamentis ad perfectissimam sani- tatem deduxerit, facit ut alii omnes sint bono animo ac fiduciam concipiant: Ita Dominus Christus ani- marum medicus, cum factus esset homo pro salute pec- catorum, me, qui eram iniquissimus & omnium sce- leratissimus non solum à prioribus liberavit maculis, sed maximis etiam donis obruit, omnibus hominibus per me ostendens summam patientiam & clementiam. Ut nemo eorum, qui maxima scelera perpetraverint, ad me respiciens de salute desperet. Non ergo opus est, ex superlativo facere comparativum, & ex inde- finita, quæ universali respondet, particularem re- strictam ad tempora, conversionem Paulinam se- quuta, nedum ad eos, qui per Paulum convertendi erant. JESUS CHRISTUS heri, hodie, idem & in secula, Ebr. 13, 8. Recte etiam emphasis ob- servata Chrysostomo in voce OMNEM: Non dixit, inquit, ut in me ostenderet patientiam, sed omnem patientiam, ac si apertius diceret: Nullus est, in quo major habenda sit patientia, neque inveniri facile potest peccator, qui tanta abundantia miserationis in- digeat. Omnem, inquit, in me ostendit patien- tiam, non partem, quemadmodum in his, qui mo- dica deliquerunt.

Πρὸς ὑποτύπωσιν τῶν μελλόντων πιστεύειν ἐπ' αὐτῷ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον) ὑποτύπωσις ut & τύπος sunt prima pictu- rarum vel operum lineamenta. Præformatio sumi- tur hic pro exemplo. Nam exemplo Pauli, qui post tam sæva facta, dona Spiritus erat consequutus, ac proinde & jus ad vitam æternam (nam dona illa vitæ æternæ erant arrhabo) etiam illi ex gentibus qui pra- ve vixerant, audebant sperare vitam æternam, post- quam eandem, quam Paulus profitebatur, vitam rece- pissent.

Alii non prima lineamenta, sed illustrem & vi- vam rei demonstrationem intelligunt per ὑποτύ- πωσιν. Exemplum etiam Pauli talem demon- strationem præbet. Hypotyposis, inquit Flacius, Græca vox non qualecunque, sed illustre exem- plum, & veluti vivam præfigurationem, aut ad- umbrationem ante oculos propositam significat.

Non autem illis tantum, qui è gentibus, nedum qui per Paulum credituri erant, sed omnibus, qui credunt. Nam & Judæi & è gentibus alii per ex- emplum hoc illustre Pauli gratiam sperare habue- runt, dummodo credituri erant. Οἱ μέλλοντες πιστεύειν non sunt, quibus absoluto beneplacito DEUS est fidem concessurus, sed qui Verbo Ev- angelii fideli & omni acceptione digno fidem ha- bituri sunt, quam nemini denegare Deus vult, modo obicem ipsi conversionem intendenti non ponamus, 1. Timoth. 2, 4. 2. Petr. 3, 9. Actor. 7, 51. quam non ἀμέσως sed per auditum Verbi, non per irresistibilem gratiam, sed quæ per se actu qui- dem primo efficax sit ad conversionem, nec tamen operetur modo irresistibili, aut efficaciam in actu secundo exerat in repugnantibus actuali malitia, aut impedientibus Spiritus sancti operationem.

Vers. 17.

Τῷ δὲ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων) Regi omnium temporum : עתיק יומי Dan. 9, 17. Ἀφθάρτῳ) vide Rom. 1, 23. & ibi dicta: & Sapient. 12, 1. Ἀοράτῳ) Ebr. 11, 27. Proprium id Deo. Habitat enim lucem inaccessam, infra c. 6, 16. Deus per se non conspicitur. At conspicitur in operibus, Rom. 1, 20. apertissime vero in Filio 2. Cor. 4. Ebr. 1, 3. Μόνῳ σοφῷ Θεῷ) Sic & Rom. 16, 27. non quod non aliis is titulus aliquo sensu tribuatur, sed quia hoc quicquid est, à Deo venit. Sic & Judas v. 25. Eadem loquutio infra c. 6, 6. At in Manuscripto est σοφῷ, ita ut illud μόνῳ ad ἀοράτῳ referatur. Et sic quidem Lati- ni legerunt. Τιμὴ, δόξα) Usurpant nostri scriptores ἀσυνδέτως etiam in duabus vocibus. Εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων) Sic & Gal. 1, 5. & Philipp. 2, 20. & 2. Tim. 4, 18. Ebr. 13, 21. 1. Petr. 4, 11. cap. 5, v. 11. Apoc. 1, 6. c. 5, 13. c. 7, 12.

A commemoratione superabundantis gratiæ Di- vinæ convertit se Apostolus ad gratiarum actio- nem pro omni Divina patientia, & longanimita- te: Illa vero directa, juxta Theodoretum, est ad sacrosanctam Trinitatem; juxta Chrysostomum ad Deum Patrem: non excluso tamen Filio & Spiri- tu sancto, juxta alios ad ipsummet CHRISTUM JESUM; quæ sententia maxime consentanea videtur. Nam Christi gratiam superabundan- tem deprædicarat, ipsi donum fidei & charitatis tribuerat, vers. 14. ## 1:1 Argument
PART II. OF CHAPTER I. An exhortation concerning keeping the faith and a good conscience.

Latin:

PARS II. CAPITIS I. Adhortatio de servanda fide, bonaque conscientia.

## 1:18
Verse 18.

This charge I commit to you: A very effective word. For no faith is holier than the faith of a deposit. Therefore, those who deny a deposit are infamous among all nations. See also below ch. 6:20, 2 Tim. 1:14. Thus Exod. 19:7, וַיָּשֶׂם לִפְנֵיהֶם אֵת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִים. In the Greek it is 'he set before them all these words.' Child Timothy: He could not have spoken more effectively.

Blessed Hunnius rightly warns here that by the word 'charge' (or denunciation) in this place (according to the subject matter and the connection of these words with those immediately preceding) is understood the Gospel specifically so called, and that by a phrase not unusual in the Holy Scriptures, Psalm 19 and 119 and in other places, where the properties and marks added there demonstrate the word 'charge' to be the doctrine of the Gospel. In which meaning the 'charge' which is said in Moses not to be above us, etc., is expounded concerning the word of faith, that is, concerning the Gospel, Rom. 10. This, therefore, is the charge, this is the word, this is the doctrine which he wishes to be most commended to his Timothy. Which deposit, the holy Apostle again warning, Timothy ought to keep most holily, 1 Tim. 6:20, 2 Tim. 2:4. Crocius prefers to draw this command toward the following. But it is more convenient to refer it to the preceding, because he had already warned about faith and love, and therefore he commands that the deposit of doctrine be kept so that faith and a good conscience may be preserved, for if that is lost, neither faith nor a good conscience has any place. Calvin, a great interpreter to Crocius, Bullinger, Aretius, Hyperius, Musculus, Cornelius à Lapide, and among the ancients, Theodoret, also refer it to the preceding.

According to the prophecies going before on thee) on thee עליך. Remember that you were made an Evangelist, the Spirit of God exciting us and others to this. For so it was accustomed to be done then: Acts 1:24, ch. 13:2. Ambrose, or whoever it is that is read under his name on this passage: For Timothy was predestined when he was taken by the Apostle for this purpose, that he might be ordained. Then, since nothing human was happening, the priests were made by prophecy. Oecumenius: For by the revelation of the Spirit he was chosen by Paul as a disciple, and was circumcised, and was ordained bishop. Theophylact: In ancient times the priests were made by prophecy, that is, by the Holy Spirit.

That you might war in them the good warfare) in them, that is, according to them; excited by them. For in the prophecies concerning him there had been those words, to war the good warfare; the whole life of man is a warfare, Job 7:1, especially the life of a Christian, 2 Cor. 10:4. But especially that of an Evangelical pastor, 1 Cor. 9:7, 2 Tim. 2:24, Phil. 2:5, Philem. 1, 2. Thus the ministry of the Levites is called צבא warfare.

He makes mention of a prophecy of this kind also in ch. 4, v. 14. Theodoret: Prophecy, he says, kindles charity by the remembrance of a benefactor. For he says, you have not attained a human calling, but through Divine revelation you have received the order. It is likely, however, that he was not only appointed to the office of teaching by revelation, but that he had also obtained his calling from the beginning by some such reason. For which cause he did not say prophecy, but prophecies. The entire commentary of Theophylact has it thus: Since the dignity of a teacher and priest is great, it must be confirmed by the judgment of God, so that he who is more worthy may undertake that office. And therefore among the ancients, priests were created by the prediction and command of the Prophets (that is, by the Holy Spirit). For prophecy is also a proper or present speaking. Thus also Timothy was elected into the priesthood, concerning whom he testifies that prophecies had been published. Or perhaps even then, when he was assumed into the priesthood and circumcised, and finally promoted to holy orders, having obtained all such dignity from prophecy and the revelation of the Spirit. He adds, therefore: I advise and warn you, that you should walk according to the prophecies preceding concerning you, that is, that having contemplated these, and as if taught by them what you must do, you should proceed to do everything according to their dignity, so that you may in no way be a disgrace and ignominy to them. The reason why the prophecies are designated in the plural, the blessed Hunnius brings forward as follows: For it was signified to Timothy, either by his religious grandmother Lois, or his most pious mother Eunice (whose faith and holiness are celebrated in 2 Tim. 1), or by some other person through the Holy Spirit, what an excellent herald of the Gospel he would be, and an elect instrument of God, and a strenuous soldier of Jesus Christ. Having recalled these prophetic predictions to his mind, he adds a spur, so that he may strive to respond again and again to the Divine oracles brought forth concerning him, and in them or according to them fight the good fight, that is, show himself such a soldier as they had predicted he would be: who, namely, standing in the battle line against Satan and the ministers of his diabolical impiety, may fight manfully and carry away from them a victory joined with the perpetual uses of many. Concerning which Theodoret again says: For it behooves you to show yourself worthy of the election, and to put an end to the prophecies, and to undertake the battle bravely against the opposing demons. For it behooves a teacher to be his own first teacher, and it behooves a commander to be a good soldier. Similarly Theophylact: He mentions the militia, however, to argue that, although a fierce war is waged against all, it is waged most fiercely against him who instructs others to live rightly, and therefore he must be more vigilant. Nor is it necessary that he should show himself more languid, but excited and vigilant.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

Ταύτην παραγγελίαν παρατίθεμαί σοι) Verbum valde efficax. Nulla enim fides sanctior fide depositi. Ideo infames sunt apud omnes gentes qui depositum abnegant. Vide & infra c. 6, 20. 2. Tim. 1, 14. Sic Exod. 19, 7. וַיָּשֶׂם לִפְנֵיהֶם אֵת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִים In Græco est παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους. Τέκνον Τιμόθεε) Non potuit loqui efficacius.

Recte hic B. Hunnius monet præcepti (vel denunciationis) vocabulo hoc loco (secundum subjectam materiam & horum verborum à proxime præcedentibus connexionem) intelligi Evangelium specifice sic dictum, idque phrasi sacris literis non insolita, Psalm. 19. & 119. & aliis in locis, ubi præcepti vocem doctrinam Evangelii additæ ibi notæ proprietatesque demonstrant. Quo significatu præceptum, quod in Mose dicitur, non esse supra nos &c. de verbo fidei, hoc est, de Evangelio exponitur, Rom. 10. Hoc igitur est præceptum, hic sermo, hæc doctrina, quam Timotheo suo vult esse quam commendatissimam. Quam παρακαταθήκην, monente iterum S. Apostolo, asservare debebat quam sanctissime Timotheus, 1. Timoth. 6, 20. 2. Timoth. 2, 4. Crocius mavult ad sequentia hoc mandatum pertrahere. Sed convenientius est ad præcedentia referri, quia de fide & dilectione jam monuerat, ideoque ut servetur fides & bona conscientia, doctrinæ depositum servari jubet, quo deperdito nec fides, nec bona conscientia locum habet. Ad præcedentia etiam referunt Calvinus, magnus Crocio Interpres, Bullingerus, Aretius, Hyperius, Musculus, Cornelius à Lapide, & è veteribus Theodoretius.

Κατὰ τὰς προαγούσας ἐπί σε προφητείας) ἐπί σε עליך. Memento factum te Evangelistam, Spiritu Dei nos & alios id excitante. Ita enim tunc fieri solebat: Act. 1, 24. c. 13, 2. Ambrosius aut quisquis est qui sub ejus nomine legitur in hunc locum: Prædestinatus est enim Timotheus, quando ad hoc ab Apostolo assumptus est, ut ordinaretur. Τότε δὲ ἐπεὶ οὐδὲν ἀνθρώπινον ἐγίνετο, κὶ ἀπὸ προφητείας ἐγίνοντο οἱ ἱερεῖς. Oecumenius: Κατὰ γὰρ Πνεύματος ἀποκάλυψιν καὶ ἡρέθη παρὰ τῷ Παύλῳ εἰς μαθητὴν καὶ περιετμήθη, καὶ ἐπίσκοπος ἐχειροτονήθη. Theophylactus: Τὸ παλαιὸν ἀπὸ προφητείας ἐγίνοντο οἱ ἱερεῖς, τουτέστιν ἀπὸ Πνεύματος ἁγίου.

Ἵνα στρατεύῃ ἐν αὐταῖς τὴν καλὴν στρατείαν) ἐν αὐταῖς, id est, secundum illas; per illas excitatus. Nam in prophetiis, de ipso illa verba fuerant, στρατεύειν τὴν καλὴν στρατείαν, omnis vita hominis militia Job. 7, 1. imprimis hominis Christiani 2. Cor. 10, 4. Maxime vero pastoris Evangelici, 1. Corinth. 9, 7. 2. Tim. 2, 24. Philipp. 2, 5. Philem. 1. 2. Sic Levitarum ministerium dicitur צבא στρατεία.

Meminit hujusmodi prophetiæ & cap. 4, v. 14. Theodoretus: Prophetia, inquit, recordatione in benefactorem charitatem accendit. Non enim inquit, humanam es assecutus vocationem, sed per Divinam revelationem suscepisti ordinem. Verisimile est autem non solum ex revelatione fuisse eum docendi muneri præfectum, sed etiam aliqua ejusmodi ratione vocationem ab initio fuisse consecutum. Qua de causa non dixit prophetiam, sed prophetias. Theophylacti commentarius integer ita habet: Præceptoris & Sacerdotis cum magna sit dignitas, Dei judicio confirmanda hæc fuerit, ut, qui dignior sit, id munus suscipiat. Eoque apud veteres Prophetarum vaticinio, & jussu Sacerdotes (hoc est per Spiritum sanctum) mox creabantur. Est enim & Prophetia proprium vel præsentia dicere. Sic ita& est & Timotheus in Sacerdotem electus, de quo & editas prophetias fuisse testatur. Vel tum forte, cum fuit ad sacerdotium ille assum- ptus & circumcisus, & ad sacros ordines demum provectus, perinde dignitatem omnem hujusmodi ex prophetia & Spiritus revelatione adeptus. Subdit igitur: Consulo tibi & moneo, ut secundum præce- dentes in te prophetias incedas, hoc est, ut has con- templatus, & quasi ab illis edoctus, quid tibi agen- dum sit, pergas pro illarum dignitate omnia facere, ut nequaquam his probro & ignominiæ sis. Cau- sam, quod prophetiæ in plurali designantur, B. Hunnius hanc adducit: Nam vel religiosæ ipsius aviæ Loidi, vel pientissimæ matri Eunicæ (qua- rum fides & sanctimonia celebratur 2. Timoth. 1.) vel alteri alicui per Spiritum sanctum de Timo- theo significatum est, quam ille sit futurus eximius Evangelii præco, & organum electum DEI, & strenuus miles JESU CHRISTI. Quibus vati- dicis prædictionibus ad animum ei revocatis ceu calcar addit, ut Divinis oraculis de se proditis etiam atque etiam respondere contendat, & in eis vel secundum ea militet bonam militiam, hoc est talem se præstet militem, qualem illa futurum prænunciarint: qui scilicet in acie stans adversus Satanam, ejusque Diabolica impietatis administros mascule depugnet, & ab illis victoriam deportet cum plurimorum perpetuis usibus conjunctam. Quo de iterum Theodoretus: Oportet enim te ostendere dignum electione, & finem prophetiis im- ponere, & adversus adversarios Dæmones pugnam fortiter suscipere. Oportet enim Doctorem esse primo suum Doctorem, & oportet Imperatorem bonum esse militem. Similiter Theophylactus: Militiæ autem meminit, ut arguat, etsi acre omni- bus bellum infertur, ei tamen inferri acerrimum, qui alios instruat ad recte vivendum, eoque esse huic & magis invigilandum. Neque ut se langui- diorem præstet, necesse est, sed excitum & vigi- lantem.

## 1:19
Verse 19.

Having faith and a good conscience) See above verse 5. ἔχων for κατέχων, simple for compound. You have κατέχων in Luke 8:15 and 1 Cor. 11:2.

This spiritual warfare, according to the interpretation of the blessed Hunnius, he shows cannot be legitimately completed unless faith in Christ is preserved holily and chastely: as it is like a shield in that panoply of the Christian soldier, entirely suited for crushing the darts of the Devil. Again, he warns that faith cannot be guarded unless a good conscience is kept, and one abstains from all those things which cloud the serenity of the conscience. Therefore he joins faith and conscience, and demonstrates that they are so coupled in an indivisible bond that if the latter fails, the former immediately threatens ruin. The paraphrase of Theophylact is as follows: Do not, he says, think it will be enough for you that you were promoted to that priestly office through the Spirit and prophecy, unless an indubitable faith is also provided by you, so that you may be able to bring forth words rightly, and have a good conscience, that is, an irreproachable life, from which this straighter conscience arises, so that you may even be able to preside over others. For just as it is necessary for one who wishes to lead an army to have previously acted as an excellent soldier, so also it is necessary for a teacher to be endowed with these virtues which he is later to demand from his disciples.

Which some having thrust away concerning the faith have made shipwreck) Just as fire needs fuel, so faith needs good works, otherwise it is easily extinguished. For those who wish to do evil seek everything to persuade themselves that those things which are said about eternal rewards and punishments are not true, or at least that God does not deal with men by such a law. Faith is like a ship: a pure life is like the rudder. The rudder having been cast away, it is no wonder if the ship, struck against the rocks, is broken. Words like ἀπωθεῖσθαι, taken from navigation as from shipwrecks, are very frequent. Faith here is to be understood as that true faith, of which also 2 Tim. 3:10 speaks. ἀπωθεῖσθαι is שׁלַח or נָעַל, to remove from oneself, as in Rom. 11:1, 2 and ch. 13:12, according to some codices. Περὶ here is 'as regards' the faith. So also 2 Tim. 2:18. See also below ch. 3:4. Clement, Strom. II, dealing with those who are denoted here, having produced this passage, adds: That they defiled the conscience which came from God with unbelief.

Life is not compared quite conveniently to a rudder, so that faith becomes the ship. For faith is rather like a rudder in life, Isa. 57, last verse. Furthermore, when a good conscience is repelled, Theophylact explains the shipwreck of faith that follows thus: For when life has become more impure, certain perverse dogmas emerge from it. Indeed, those who have led an unclean and sordid life, so that they may not be tormented by fear of the future, rashly persuade themselves that all things which are handed down by us are false. Whence it happens that he who has driven away faith, having involved everything in opinions, must necessarily perish by shipwreck concerning the faith. Therefore Estius: The Apostle does not mean that once a good conscience is lost, faith is immediately lost, but that it usually happens that he who, having received faith, does not live according to it, loses the faith itself. But it must be observed that by faith here is not understood dogmatic or historical faith, as they call it, but saving faith, which does not consist with sins against conscience. Thus the error of the Calvinists is also refuted, that faith cannot fail. For since a shipwreck of faith occurs, who would doubt that faith can fail? The metaphor, says Crocius, is taken from sailors. For as those who make shipwreck lose their ship; so those who make shipwreck of the faith lose the right faith: which ship, in order to be safe in this vast sea of the world's errors and crimes, needs an anchor, a good conscience, which being loosened, those who give their sails to the blasts of arrogance and contention, and are carried away by the waves of evil desires, recede from the straight path, strike against the rocks of perfidy, and miserably perish.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

Ἔχων πίσιν καὶ ἀγαθὴν συνείδησιν) Vide supra vers. 5. ἔχων pro κατέχων, simplex pro composito. Κατέχων habes Luc. 8, 15. & 1. Cor. 11, 2.

Hanc spiritualem militiam, interprete B. Hun- nio, ostendit legitime perfici non posse, nisi fide in Christum sancte casteque conservata: utpote quæ ceu scutum est in illa Christiani militis πανοπλίᾳ, ad elidenda jacula Diaboli prorsus accommodum. Rursum fidem custodiri non posse monet, nisi bona servetur conscientia, & abstineatur ab iis omni- bus, quæ conscientiæ serenitatem obnubilant. Id- circo fidem & conscientiam conjungit, & indivi- so nexu sic copulata esse demonstrat, ut fatiscente hac illico ruinam minetur & illa. Paraphrasis Theophylacti sic habet: Haudquaquam, inquit, existimes sat tibi fore, quod per Spiritum fueris, & prophetiam ad sacerdotale id munus provectus, nisi & fides per te indubitata præstetur, ut verba promere recte queas, & conscientiam bonam, hoc est vitam irreprehensibilem habeas, à qua oritur rectior hæc conscientia, ita ut aliis etiam præesse queas. Nam quemadmodum qui exercitum du- ctare velit, ut optimum militem antea egerit ne- cesse est, sic & Præceptorem his esse virtutibus præ- ditum, quas postmodum sit à discipulis exacturus.

Ἧς τινες ἀπωσάμενοι περὶ τὴν πίσιν ἐναυάγησαν) Sicut ignis pabulo indiget, ita fides bonis operibus, alio- qui facile exstinguitur. Nam qui male agere volunt, omnia quærunt ut sibi persuadeant ea, quæ de præmiis ac pœnis æternis dicuntur, non esse vera, aut certe non tali lege Deum agere cum hominibus. Fides est, ut navis: Vita pura velut gubernaculum. Guberna- culo abjecto, non mirum si navis in scopulos impacta frangitur. Ἀπωγεῖσθαι ut à navigatione ita à naufragiis sumptæ valde sunt frequentes. Fides hic intelligenda vera illa, de qua & 2. Tim. 3, 10. ἀπωθεῖσθαι שׁלַח aut נָעַל à se amovere, ut Rom. 11, 1. 2. & c. 13, 12. secun- dum quosdam Codices. Περὶ hic est quod ad fidem at- tinet. Sic & 2. Tim. 2, 18. Vide & infra c. 3, 4. Cle- mens Strom. II. de his qui hic denotantur, agens, pro- ducto hoc loco addit : Ὅτι τὴν θεόθεν ἧκουσαν συνείδησιν ἀπιστίᾳ κατημίαναν.

Vita non satis commode gubernaculo compara- tur, ut navis fit fides. Nam fides potius gubernacu- li instar est in vita, Esa. 57. v. ult. De cætero cum repellitur bona conscientia, fidei naufragium fe- qui sic explicat Theophylactus: Nam cum fuerit vita impurior, ex ea & dogmata quædam perversa emergunt. Siquidem qui immundam & sordidam duxerint vitam, ne in futurum formidine crucien- tur, temere sibi hoc suadent, falsa omnia credi, quæ à nobis traduntur. Quo fit, ut qui fidem abēgerit, opinionibus cuncta involverit circa fidem nau- fragio pereat necesse est. Ideo Estius: Non sentit Apostolus, amissâ bona conscientia continuo fi- dem amitti, sed plerumque fieri, ut, qui accepta fi- de non secundum eam vivit, & ipsam amittat fi- dem. Sed observandum, quod hic per fidem non intelligatur fides dogmatica, vel historica, quam vocant, sed fides salvifica, quæ cum peccatis contra conscientiam non consistit. Refellitur etiam ita error Calvinianorum, quod fides defi- cere non possit. Nam quia naufragium fit fidei, deficere fidem quis dubitet? Metaphora, inquit Crocius, à navigantibus petita. Ut enim qui nau- fragium faciunt, perdunt navim; sic qui naufra- gium fidei faciunt, amittunt fidem rectam: quæ navis in tuto sit in hoc vasto mundi errorum & scele- rum pelago, opus est anchora, bona conscientia, quæ soluta, qui flatibus arrogantiæ & contentionis vela dant, abreptique malarum cupiditatum fluctibus à via recta recedunt, impingunt in perfidiæ scopulos, & misere pereunt.

## 1:20
Verse 20.

Of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander.) He does not only say this can happen, but also shows it has happened. See what a shipwreck Hymenaeus made, who denied that the resurrection would be at the end of the ages, 2 Tim. 2:17, surely one of those against whom chapter 15 of the first to the Corinthians is directed. Alexander is that coppersmith of whom Paul complains also in 2 Tim. 2:14. He lived at Ephesus, as we learn in Acts 19:33, where see what is said.

That Hymenaeus made shipwreck of the faith, and having become an apostate and a heretic, turned many away from the truth: teaching that the resurrection had already taken place: which heresy is also thought to have been Alexander's. He, having fallen into heresy on account of the pursuit of pleasures, which B. Gerhard notes the very name implies: because Hymenaeus to the Greeks is the God of weddings, and a wedding song. Regarding Alexander, Baronius suspects that he is the one who calmed the tumult stirred up at Ephesus, Acts 19:33. But Estius rightly refutes that. For he was the town clerk; but who would believe that a Jewish man was the town clerk of Ephesus?

Whom I have delivered unto Satan) namely to be tormented by diseases, as we explained in 1 Cor. 5:5. The author of the responses to the orthodox: When through the long-suffering of those who are insulted there is no correction, then the severity of long-suffering is more useful to those who are incorrigible.

That they may be taught not to blaspheme) Just as in 1 Cor. 5:5 it is said for the destruction of the flesh for the extirpation of carnal affections, for amendment, not for perdition, says Tertullian in 'De Pudicitia': that they may be amended, in the book 'De Fuga in Persecutione'. And he rightly said 'to blaspheme'. For those who fall away from true doctrine are accustomed, lest they be thought to do so in vain, to speak evil of it, as those men said that the dogma of the resurrection was foolish and alien to all reason. See Acts 17:32. Tertullian in 'De Testimonio Animae', concerning the resurrection, of which we are considered presumptuous.

What we have said here is to be compared to 1 Corinthians 5:5. Theophylact asks here: But how, someone will say, were they delivered to Satan? And he answers: Whoever was contumacious and less obedient was sent out of the Church, and was cast out from the rest of the flock, and being naked and deserted, was soon delivered to the wolves as prey. For just as once a cloud covered the tabernacle, so the Spirit covers the Church of Christ. Whoever, therefore, has been cast out of the Church and deprived of the Holy Spirit, this wretch will be very easy to capture. So great is the censure of being repelled from the company and communion of others. For God will soon afflict such a person with diseases and press them with evils for the sake of chastising those liable to sins. Tertullian in Apology, chapter 39, calls this excommunication a divine censure. Cyprian, epistle 62, a spiritual sword. Jerome, epistle 1, a spiritual dagger. Epistle 13, an iron rod. The intention of the excommunicating Church is that he may return to a sound mind.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

Ὧν ἐστι Ὑμέναιος καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος.) Non tantum dicit hoc fieri posse, sed & factum ostendit. Vide quantum naufragium fecerit Hymenæus, qui resurrectionem in fine seculorum futuram negavit, 2. Tim. 2, 17. nimirum unus illorum adversus quos directum est caput 15. prioris ad Corinthios. Alexander est faber ille ærarius, de quo Pau- lus queritur etiam 2. Tim. 2, 14. Ephesi is habitabat, ut discimus Actor. 19, 33. ubi dicta vide.

Hymenæus ille fidei naufragium fecit, & apostata atque hæreticus factus multos à veritate avertit: docens resurrectionem jam esse factam: quæ hære- sis etiam Alexandri fuisse putatur. Ille ob volu- ptatum sectationem in hæresin lapsus, quod ipsum nomen innuere B. Gerhardus monet: quia Hyme- næus Græcis est Deus nuptiarum, & carmen nu- ptiale. De Alexandro suspicatur Baronius, quod sit is, qui tumultum Ephesi excitatum sedavit, Act. 19,33. Sed id refellit merito Estius. Is enim fuit scriba civitatis; Quis autem credat, homi- nem Judæum fuisse scribam civitatis Ephesi?

Οὓς παρέδωκα τῷ Σατανᾷ) nempe morbis cruciandos, ut 1. Cor. 5, 5. explicavimus. Scriptor responsionum ad orthodoxos: Ὅτε διὰ τῆς μακροθυμίας τῶν ὑβριζομέ- νων οὐ γίνεται διόρθωσις, τότε ἡ ἀποτομία τῆς μακροθυμίας τοῖς ἀδιορθώτοις ἐστὶ χρησιμωτέρα.

Ἵνα παιδευθῶσι μὴ βλασφημεῖν) Sicut 1. Cor. 5, 5. dici- tur εἰς ὄλεθρον σαρκὸς ad affectuum carnalium extirpa- tionem, in emendationem, non in perditionem, ait Tertullianus de pudicitia: ut emendentur, in libro de fuga in persecutione. Et recte dixit βλασφημεῖν. Nam solent qui à vera doctrina deficiunt, ne id frustra facere putentur, ei maledicere, ut isti resurrectionis dogma stul- tum & ab omni ratione alienum esse dicebant. Vide Act. 17, 32. Tertullianus testimonio animæ, de resurrectione, cujus nos præsumptores deputamur.

Conferenda hic quæ diximus ad 1. Corinth. 5, 5. Quærit hic Theophylactus: Verum quomodo, aliquis dicet, Satanæ tradebantur? Et respondet: Qui con- tumax esset & minus obediens, extra Ecclesiam emit- tebatur, ejiciebaturque à cætero grege, & nudus mox & desertus lupis dedebatur in prædam. Nam quem- admodum olim nubes tabernaculum obducebat: Sic Christi Ecclesiam Spiritus. Quicunque ergo ex Ec- clesia fuerit ejectus, & Spiritu sancto privatus, erit hic miser perfacilis in capturam. Tanti est ab alio- rum consortio & communione repelli, censura. Istius- modi namque mox Deus & peccatis obnoxios casti- gandi gratia & morbis afficit & malis urgebit. Tertull. in Apol. cap. 39. hanc excommunicationem Divi- nam vocat censuram. Cyprianus epist. LXII. gla- dium spiritualem. Hieronymus epist. I. spiritualem mucronem. Epist. XIII. virgam ferream. Intentio Ecclesiæ excommunicantis est, ut ad sanam men- tem redeat.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.

He exhorts to prayers for all, especially for the magistrate, because God wishes all to be saved: And Christ the Mediator gave Himself for all: And he teaches how men and women ought to conduct themselves in prayers and public assemblies.

There are two parts: I. An exhortation to prayers, to verse 7. II. Instruction of men concerning the requirements of prayers, and of women concerning true adornment, piety, and subjection, to verse 15. B. Gerhard establishes three parts: concerning the object of prayers, or for whom one must pray, to verse 7. Concerning the place and manner of prayers, verse 8. And concerning the adornment of women in prayers and their duty.

PART I. Exhortation to prayers. Verse 1.

Παρακαλῶ ὖν πρῶτον πάντων) Just as Roman Emperors were accustomed to give mandates to governors, so Paul gives mandates to bishops in Timothy. That ὖν depends on the preceding 1. Ταύτην παραγγελίαν παρατίθεμαί σοι. This first, he says, I prescribe. For he will prescribe other things in turn.

Ποιεῖσθαι δεήσεις) δεήσεις are supplications for averting evils. See Acts 1:14, Philippians 4:6. תחנת.

Προσευχὰς) προσευχαὶ are prayers for obtaining good things for ourselves. See Ephesians 1:16, chapter 6:18. תפלות. You will find these two names and others by which the names of prayers are distinguished in the book concerning the death of Moses.

Εντεύξεις) ἐντεύξεις are prayers for others. See Romans 8:26. פגעים.

Εὐχαριστίας) Thanksgivings, for goods already received, which ought to be joined to prayers, Philippians 4:6. תודות.

That Timothy the Bishop was superior to the Presbyters in power of order and jurisdiction is rashly assumed. It is not evident from the scriptures. Nor were there such Bishops at that time, who were introduced long after by human authority. The particle ὖν, although it depends on the preceding, does not however pertain to the παραγγελία in chapter 1, 18. The Apostle had exhorted to the guarding of the deposit of heavenly doctrine, and to the preserving of faith and a good conscience against any assaults whatsoever; but because these are not in our power, he infers that before all things there is need of prayers, both for averting evils and for obtaining goods. He had warned about true religion, which ought to be of the greatest concern to a Minister of the word: Now he reminds us of public prayers in particular, which are necessary in the Church alongside the purer doctrine or the deposit of the Divine Word, and ought to be most highly commended by the ministers of the Word above all else. First of all, says Theophylact (this is right), Divine [services] are to be performed daily. For the Priest, as the common Father of the whole world, stands at the holy altar to look out for all, and in the likeness of God, to whom he is dedicated. Some wish the occasion for the present exhortation to have been given by a question raised among the faithful, and a certain defect detected in the prayers. But nothing certain is known about these. Furthermore, the Apostle distributes prayers into different classes, when by them we either seek Divine grace, whether praying for ourselves, both for declining evils and for obtaining goods; or for others, or we give thanks for grace received or Divine gifts, both for our own sake and also for the sake of others. Some, however, with Theophylact, take all the terms as synonyms: But it is better to distinguish them with Theodoret, St. Augustine, and B. Luther.

Ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων) Even for those not yet believing. The writer on the calling of the Gentiles, chapter 1, verse 12. Therefore, the Apostle Paul, writing to Timothy, says: I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, thanksgivings, be made for all men, for Kings, and for all that are in authority: That we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; who gave himself a ransom for all. Concerning this Apostolic rule of doctrine, by which the universal Church is imbued, lest we wander into a different understanding by our own judgment, let us inquire what the universal Church itself thinks: because nothing will be able to be doubtful in a precept, if obedience agrees in study. The Apostle therefore commanded, or rather the Lord, who was speaking through the Apostle, that supplications and prayers, thanksgivings, be made for all men, for Kings, and for those who are in authority. Which law of supplication the devotion of all Priests and all the faithful holds so concordantly, that there is no part of the world in which prayers of this kind are not celebrated by Christian people. The Church therefore supplicates everywhere to God, not only for the saints and those already regenerated in Christ, but also for all infidels and enemies of the cross of Christ, for all idolaters, for all who persecute Christ in his members, for the Jews whose blindness the light of the Gospel does not shine upon, for heretics, for schismatics, who are alienated from the unity of faith and charity. But what do you ask for them, except that, having abandoned their errors, they may be converted to God, receive faith, receive charity, and, liberated from the darkness of ignorance, may come to the knowledge of the truth. Because they cannot perform this for themselves, oppressed by the weight of evil custom and bound by the chains of the Devil, nor are they able to overcome their deceptions, to which they have so pertinaciously clung, that as much as truth is to be loved, so much they also bind falsehood, the merciful and just Lord wishes that supplication be made for all men to him, so that when we see countless numbers rescued from such profound evils, we may not doubt that God has granted what he was prayed to grant: And giving thanks for those who have been saved, we may hope that those who are not yet illuminated are also to be rescued from the power of darkness by the same work of Divine grace, so that they may be transferred into the kingdom of God, before they depart from this life. Philo on the high priest of the Jews: Οὐ μόνον ὑπὲρ ἁπάντων ἀνθρώπων γένους, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑπὲρ τῶν τῆς Φύσεως με- ρῶν, γῆς, ὕδατος, ἀέρος, καὶ πυρὸς, τάς τε εὐχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐυ- χαριςίας ποιεῖται. There are certain prayers for all: There are also others for the faithful only, as John 17, 9.

Latin:

CAPUT II. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Adhortatur ad preces pro omnibus, imprimis pro magistratu, quod Deus velit omnes sal- vari: Ac Christus Mediator se pro omnibus tradiderit: Et quales se viri, ac mulieres in precibus ac congressibus publicis gerere debeant, docet.

Duæ sunt partes: I. Adhortatio ad preces, ad v. 7. II. Informatio virorum de requisitis precum, & mulierum de vero ornatu, pietate, ac subjectione, ad vers. 15. B. Gerhardus tres partes constituit de precum objecto, vel pro quibus orandum, ad vers. 7. De precum loco & modo, v. 8. & de mulierum in pre- cibus ornatu earumque officio.

PARS I. Adhortatio ad preces. Vers. 1.

Παρακαλῶ ὖν πρῶτον πάντων) Sicut Imperatores Ro- mani mandata dare Præsidibus solebant: Ita Paulus in Timotheo mandata dat Episcopis. Illud ὖν pendet ex præcedentibus 1. Ταύτην παραγγελίαν παρατίθεμαί σοι. Hoc primum, inquit, præscribo. Nam præscribet de- inceps & alia.

Ποιεῖσθαι δεήσεις) δεήσεις sunt deprecationes ad mala a- vertenda. Vide Act. 1, 14. Phil. 4, 6. תחנת.

Προσευχὰς) προσευχαὶ sunt preces, ad bona nobis ob- tinenda. Vide Eph. 1, 16. c. 6, 18. תפלות. Hæc duo nomina & alia quibus precum nomina distinguuntur re- peries in libro de morte Mosis.

Εντεύξεις) ἐντεύξεις sunt preces pro aliis. Vide Rom. 8, 26. פגעים.

Εὐχαριστίας) Gratiarum actiones, pro bonis jam ac- ceptis, quæ precibus adjungi debent, Phil. 4, 6. תודות.

Timotheum Episcopum Presbyteris ordinis ac jurisdictionis potestate superiorem fuisse, temere supponitur. Non patet è scripturis. Nec tum erant ejusmodi Episcopi, qui introducti longe post humana autoritate. Particula ὖν etsi à præ- cedentibus pendeat, non tamen παραγγελία cap. 1, 18. huc pertinet. Adhortatus erat Apostolus ad custodiendum doctrinæ cœlestis depositum, & ad fidem & ad conscientiam bonam adversus insultus quosvis servandam; quia vero hæc non sunt in no- stra potestate, infert, ante omnia precibus opus es- se, tum ad mala avertenda, tum ad bona impetran- da. Monuerat de vera religione, quæ Ministro verbi maxime curæ esset debet: Jam de precibus imprimis publicis commonefacit, quæ juxta cum puriori doctrina vel deposito Verbi Divini in Ec- clefia necessariæ sunt, & ministris Verbi ante omnia debent esse quam commendatissimæ. Omnium primum, inquit Theophylactus (hoc est jure) Divina quotidie peragenda. Sacerdos namque tanquam communis orbis terrarum Pater sancto al- tari adstat omnibus prospecturus, & Dei ad instar, cui est dedicatus. Adhortationi præsenti occasionem datam quidam volunt à quæstione inter fideles mota, & defectu quodam in orationibus depre- henso. Sed de his nihil certi constat. Cæterum preces in diversas classes distribuit Apostolus, quum illis vel expetimus Divinam gratiam, sive pro nobis orantes, tum pro malis declinandis tum pro bonis obtinendis; sive pro aliis, vel gratias a- gimus pro accepta gratiâ vel muneribus Divinis, tum nostri, tum aliorum etiam causa. Nonnulli tamen voces omnes cum Theophylacto pro Syno- nymis habent: Sed præstat easdem cum Theodore- to, S. Augustino & B. Luthero distinguere.

Ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων) Etiam pro nondum creden- tibus. Scriptor de vocatione gentium cap. 1. vers. 12. Scribentis itaque ad Timotheum paulus Apostolus ait: Obsecro igitur primum omnium fieri obsecrationes, postulatio- nes, gratiarum actiones pro omnibus hominibus, pro Regibus, & omnibus qui in sublimitate sunt: Ut quietam & tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate & castitate. Hoc enim bo- num est & acceptum coram Salvatore nostro Deo, qui omnes homines vult salvos fieri, & in agnitionem veritatis venire. Unus enim Deus & unus Mediator Dei & hominum homo Christus Jesus, qui dedit redemptionem semetipsum pro omni- bus. De hac ergo doctrina Apostolica regula, qua Ecclesia uni- versalis imbuitur, ne in diversum intellectum nostro evagare- mur arbitrio, quid ipsa Ecclesia universalis sentiat, requira- mus: quia nihil dubium esse poterit in præcepto, si obedientia concordet in studio. Præcepit itaque Apostolus, imo per Aposto- lum Dominus, qui loquebatur, fieri obsecrationes & postulatio- nes, gratiarum actiones pro omnibus hominibus, pro Regibus, ac pro his qui in sublimitate sunt. Quam legem supplicationis ita omnium Sacerdotum & omnium fidelium devotio concorditer tenet, ut nulla pars mundi sit, in qua bujusmodi orationes non celebrentur à populu Christianis. Supplicat ergo ubique Ecclesia Deo, non solum pro sanctis & in Christo jam regeneratis, sed et- iam pro omnibus infidelibus & inimicis crucis Christi, pro omni- bus idolorum cultoribus, pro omnibus qui Christum in mem- bris ejus persequuntur, pro Judæis quorum cæcitati lumen Ev- angelii non refulget, pro hæreticis, pro schismaticis, qui ab unita- te fidei & charitatis alieni sunt.
