II. 8. Præterea cum hæres succedat in possessio- nem bonorum ei, cujus hæres est; An Christus hæ- res omnium est, quod Patri successerit, an verò quod una cum Patre sit Dominus rerum omnium? Dictum est antea, hæredem hic significari possessorem, non exclusis tamen respectibus iis, quos emphasis isti- us vocis importat. Possidet autem Filius DEI non post Patrem, ut sit in rebus humanis, sed unà cum Patre, quod recte hic notat Schlichtingius, quod observandum adversus reliquos Socinia- nos: qui DEUM ipsum jam non ex persona sua Ecclesiam gubernare, sed CHRISTUM po- tius in ea exercere divina judicia, præeunte F. Socino Rel. Christ. Or. V. just. pag. 95. tra- dunt, quod succedaneus fuerit CHRISTUS in administratione rerum: quem etiam vicarium & præfectum indigitare solent. Verum enim verò rectius Schlichtingius : uti dixi, unà cum Patre possidere omnia CHRISTUM: quia non ab- dicavit sese Pater à rerum dominio, & possessio- ne, dum Christo id concessit, sed Christum in thronum regiminis sui evexit, ejusque consor- tem effecit; nec ideo ipse DEUS ex persona sua haud gubernat Ecclesiam, quod Christo ean- dem gubernandam dederit, quia una eademque est gubernatio, unus idemque actus gubernatio- nis DEI & CHRISTI, ut unus idemque Do- minus est, non verò plures Domini. Particeps enim factus est Christus divinæ virtutis & Maje- statis, qua gubernantur omnia, eadem regit & gu- bernat omnia.

IV. Territorium denique atque terminus hu- jus hæreditatis & possessionis voce πάντων ex- primitur. Quam aliqui restringunt ad personas, omnium scilicet hominum & Angelorum, & il- lorum tum viventium, tum mortuorum : alii ad res referunt, ita tamen, ut & personæ sub ampli- tudine rerum comprehendantur, ideoque Chry- sostomus & Theophylactus Dominatorem totius mundi explicant, alii adhuc magis extendunt, ut non tantum rerum creatarum possessionem, sed omnium etiam ἀυχημάτων divinorum hære- dem factum innui velint, quorum participem factum esse Scriptura docet: Ideoque hæredem esse universorum triplici respectu: (1) latè & universim, idque cùm κατ' ἔσω, quia tota pleni- tudo divinitatis in ipso habitat corporaliter, Co- loss. II. vers. 9. tum κατ' ἔξω, quia omnes omni- nò creaturæ ei subjectæ sunt, Psalm. VIII, 7. seq. (2) strictè & separatim respectu omnium ho- minum, quorum hæreditatem consecutus sit CHRISTUS, tum ut eos sua passione & morte redimeret, tum ut regnum gratiæ, erectum ex toto mundo, sive omnibus hominibus, sibi col- ligeret, Psalm. II. vers. 8. & Pf. LXXII. vers. 8. (3) strictissimè & specialissimè, respectu creden- tium, & electorum, de qua hæreditate Christus gloriatur Psalm. XVI. vers. 5. Conf. Johan. VI. vers. 37. 39. 40. XVII. vers. 2. Quanquam verò rectissimè hæc dicantur secundum fidei analo- giam, præsenti tamen loco ea omnia ex æquo indigitari haud arbitramur. Sed eum solum hic innui sensum, quà universim omnia intelligun- tur, super quæ constitutus est in cœlo & in ter- ra, quod præcipuè patescit tum (1) è vocis uni- versalis propria significatione, quæ complectitur sub ambitu suo universa, tum (2) è relatione ad Patrem, quæ voce hæredis hic innuitur, quod ut Pater est omnium Dominus, ita est Filius hæ- res constitutus super omnia. Est autem Pater Dominus omnium absolutè & citra exceptio- nem ullius creaturæ: tum (3) è verbis subjun- ctis: per quem & secula fecit: quia hæres eorum omnium constitutus est ratione humanæ natu- ræ, quorum Autor & Conditor est ratione di- vinæ naturæ: tum (4) è propositionis explicatio- ne, ac confirmatione, in subsequentibus facta, à throno & sceptro Regali Christi, à Domino abso- luto in cœlo & in terra, à sessione ad dextram DEI, à gloriosa coronatione & constitutione su- per omnia opera manuum DEI è Psalm. XLV. CII. CX. ut CII. &c. tum denique (5) è locorum similium collatione, ubi de hæreditate, ad quam CHRISTUS evectus est, agitur, quæ complecti- tur quidem sub sese Ecclesiam per universam terram collectam, Psalm. II. vers. 8. XVI. vers. 5. 6. 7. & LXX. vers. 8. sed latius extenditur etiam extra pomœria Ecclesiæ, imo supra omnes crea- turas, Psalm. VIII. vers. 6. 1. Corinth. XV. v. 27. Ebr. II. vers. 8. Est enim dominium absolutum & Catholicum, quod CHRISTUS gerit juxta cum Patre, ac Spiritu Sancto ut verus natura DEUS: Idem autem dominium, quod Christus ut DEUS tenuit ab orbe condito, CHRISTUS ut homo accepit in exaltatione, quia ut unus tantum est Dominus, CHRISTUS θεάνθρωπος, DEUS & homo, unus Rector, ita unicum est dominium, unicus Rectoratus omnium, 1. Cor. IIX. vers. 6. Ephes. IV. vers. 5. 1. Tim. II. vers. 6. Apocal. XVII. vers. 14. cap. XIX. vers. 16. Ideò CHRISTO homini dicuntur omnia tradita in manus, Johan. III. vers. 35. & Matth. XI. vers. 27. non excepto, nisi eo, qui subjecit ei omnia, da- ta est ei omnis potestas in cælo & in terra, Matth. XIIX. vers. 18. quæ est περίφρασις divinæ po- testatis immensæ & infinitæ super omnia, Gene- sis XIV. vers. 12. XXIV. vers. 3. 7. Esdr. I. v. 2. 12. V. vers. 11. VI. v. 9. 10. VII. v. 12. 21. 23. Dan. VI. vers. 27. Matth. XI. vers. 25. Luc. X. v. 21. Actor. XVII. vers. 24. Quod hic observandum venit contra Socinianos, qui CHRISTUM hæredem & possessorem, atque Dominum tantum Eccle- siæ, & eorum, quæ ad Ecclesiam pertinent, non autem omnium quæcunque sunt creaturarum Dominum esse admittunt. Vide Smalzium de divinit. Christi p. 114. Subdolè autem Sociniani docent, addo & contradictoriè, Christum non esse constitutum omnium Dominum, uti Pater est, sed tantùm Ecclesiæ & eorum, quæ ad Ecclesiam pertinent: quia nihil est, quin ad Ecclesiam ali- quem habeat respectum, vel ut ejus usui cedat, vel ne ejusdem saluti adversum sit, & noceat, cum omnia administrentur ea ratione, ut tùm in laudem nominis divini, tùm in salutem Eccle- siæ vergant. Itaque hoc pacto nihil omninò ex- cipietur à Dominio CHRISTI. Adde, quod CHRISTUS ἁπλῶς universaliter pronunciat, quæcunque facit Pater, eadem similiter & Filium facere, Johan. V. vers. 19. & Apostolus mox sub- juncturus sit, CHRISTUM omnia portare verbo virtutis suæ, vers. 3. hujus capitis ad Ebræos primi. Idcircò fatetur Schlichtingius, omnia hic intelligi, quorum Pater est Dominus: Cum Pater sit omni- um rerum Dominus, ideò etiam Christus unicus ejus Filius omnium rerum hæres & Dominus eva- sit. Addit insuper CHRISTUM & solum omnium planè rerum hæreditate gaudere, & sum- mo in omnes tam Angelos, quam homines imperio ac dominatu pollere.

Hæc autem hæreditas CHRISTI, quà super omnia constitutus est, non communis, sed pro- pria est, non fidelibus & electis quibusvis con- veniens, sed soli Christo: quandoquidem hæc sit ipsius propria hoc in loco περίφρασις, nec de ul- lo ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ dici queat, eum ita constitui hæredem omnium, ut hic de CHRISTO di- citur, id est, ut istius unici summique Dominii DEI consors sit, unusque cum eo Dominus. Divisum enim imperium Jehovah cum nemine habet, nec ulli suam concedit gloriam. Quo circa toto genere diversa est hæreditas fidelium & ipsius CHRISTI, nec nisi κατά τι dicuntur fideles Christi cohæredes, Roman. IIX. 17. nempe non ratione omnium, quæ Christus possidet, sed determinatè ratione gloriæ vitæ æternæ, ad quam evehendi sunt fideles post passiones hujus vi- tæ, ita tamen, ut hæc quoque gloria respectu Christi & Electorum non gradu tantum discri- minetur, sed infinitis parasangis distet: quia Christi gloria est æterna & immensa gloria, Joh. XVII. vers. 5. & ipsius DEI Patris gloria, Apoc. V. vers. 12. 13. Electorum autem gloria est fini- ta, & à gloria DEI Patris immensum distat. Quod discrimen indicat quoque inter alia CHRISTUS, cum dicit, se electis daturum sedere super so- lium suum, quemadmodum ipse consedit super thronum Patris sui, distinguens thronum Patris à throno suo, & se tantum occupasse thronum Patris asserens, Electos autem non ad Patris, sed ad suum tantum thronum ipsis præparatum evehere. Conf. Apocal. VII. vers. 17. ubi agnus in medio throni sedere dicitur, hoc est, in throno DEI, ad dextram Majestatis, Ebr. XII. vers. 2. ceu Dominus gloriæ, 1. Corinth. II. vers. 8. Do- minus dominantium, Apocal. XVII. vers. 14. XIX. vers. 16. Dominus super omnia opera manuum Dei, Psalm. IIX. vers. 7. Quod nemini Electorum, imo nec Angelorum quidem vel Arch-Angelo- rum convenit. Cui enim Angelorum dixit un- quam, sede ad dextram meam? Ebr. I. 13.

Δι’ ὗ καὶ τὂς αἰῶνας ἐποίησε.

Videtur δι’ ὗ hic recte accipi posse pro δι’ ὅν, nam sic ut διὰ cum accusativo interdum est per, ut alibi ostendi- mus, & amplius probatur per locum Apocalypseos c. IV. v. 11. XII. v. 11. XIII. v. 14. Ita διὰ in Genitivo inter- dum valet propter. Vide Bezam Roman. VI. v. 4. sic δι’ ὗν pro quapropter poni solet. Et aoristus ille ἐποίησε hic commodissime vertitur per plusquamperfectum condide- rat. Ideo autem hæc interpretatio hoc loco maximè mihi se probat, quia ad Ebræos scribens videtur respicere ad di- ctum vetus Ebræorum: propter Messiam conditum esse mundum. Idem Ebræi עלמים quod valet αἰῶνας pro mundo ponunt per metonymiam quandam. Hinc DEUS רב עלמים fic כולי עלמא Chaldæis, totus mundus, sic infra XI. vers. 3. πίσει νοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τὂς αἰῶνας, id est mundum. Quid mirum est esse Dominum omnium, cujus causa condita fuere omnia.

Altera pars descriptionis personæ CHRISTI concernens divinam naturam, his verbis propo- nitur, δι’ ὗ καὶ τὂς αἰῶνας ἐποίησε, in quibus oc- currit (1) Nexus & cohærentia cum priori parte in vocula καὶ, quæ hic tum αἰτιολογικῶς accipi potest, ut causam conjungat præcedentis mem- bri. Quod enim CHRISTUS ut Homo hæres constitutus est omnium, inde est, quod idem CHRISTUS ut DEUS sit Creator omnium: tum αὐξητικῶς: ut vim augendi habeat, quod admit- tit Schlichtingius, docetque res ipsa, q. d. Chri- stum non tantum hæredem esse constitutum o- mnium, sed & auctorem esse omnium, vel non tan- tum possidere omnia jure hæreditatis, & vi divinæ constitutionis, sed & jure creationis, & proprie- tatis originariæ, non obtinere saltim supremum rerum dominium, qua novissimis temporibus evectus est super omnia, sed jam ante secula ex- titisse, & conditorem seculorum omnium esse, adeoque inde à seculo Dominum fuisse super omnia. Non autem è copula id colligendum, quod ejusdem naturæ respectu hæres constitutus sit omnium, & secula condiderit, quia notissimum est copulandi particulam distinctissima, & distin- ctissimo respectu attributa sæpe conjungere, nec quicquam hinc inferri potest, quàm eidem suppo- sito aut personæ utrumque assignari, & conveni- re, non verò eidem naturæ.

(2) Sensus & materia dicendi his verbis pro- posita, quod nempe per Christum secula sint condita. Notantur ergo tria, (1) Per quem sint condita, δι' 8. Filium D E J respici nullum dubi- um est. Voculam διὰ designare ministerialem & organicam causam creationis primæ, Ariani quon- dam contendebant; hodiè Sociniani mediam & prima subordinatam causam secundæ creationis in- nui volunt, quod facit Schlichtingius h. in l. p. 18. quod hac præpositione inferatur differentia Filii à Patre: Quod Filius non creet à seipso ut Pater, sed Pater per Filium. Verum nullius momenti est illa probatio. Quandoquidem (1) præpositio διὰ non adhibeatur tantum de causa media & instrumentali, sed etiam de causa prima & prin- cipali, Roman. VI. vers. 4. 1. Cor. I. vers. 9. Rom. XI. vers. 36. &c. nec ad nudum præpositionis hujus usum, sed ad objectum potius, de quo agitur, respiciendum sit. Adhæc (2) si primam creationem respicias, nulla fuit adhibita causa me- dia sive instrumentalis: quia nec in creationis hi- storia ullius causæ instrumentalis, vel alterius ge- neris quocunque nomine mentio fiat, sed solus Deus creasse omnia refertur, nec præterea us- piam in scripturis tale quid legitur de organo creationis; adhæc excluduntur quoque omnes extra Deum à creationis opere, Job. IX. v. 8. Es. XLIV. v. 24. XLV. 6. Denique virtus creandi infinita ei, qui extra DEUM est, communicari non potest, sine qua creatio perfici nequit. Ta- ceo, quod CHRISTUS non sit causa creatio- nis primæ media, sed prima, idem cum Patre Creator, idem opifex rerum omnium, Es. XLIV. vers. 24. Prov. VIII. vers. 22. Johan. I. vers. 3. 10. Coloss. I. vers. 16. quod cumprimis è demonstra- tione Apostoli nostri vers. 10. hujus 1. Cap. ad Ebr. facta è Psalm. CII. vers. 26. manifestum erit postea. Si de creatione secunda vel reparatione intelligatur, quanquam de ea intelligi haud de- beat, certum tamen est, Filium non esse causam secundam ut salutis nostræ, ita reparationis, & regenerationis, sed causam primam, quia est is, præter quem non est salus, Actor. IV. vers. 12. quod est unius summi D E I, Es. XLIII. vers. 11. Conf. Es. XLV. vers. 22. cum Rom. XIV. vers. 11. Phil. II. vers. 10. & vivificat nos pariter, sicut Pater, Johan. V. vers. 21. αὐτοκρατορικῶς, καὶ ἀυτεξυ- σίως, ut ἀρχηγὸς τῆς ζωῆς καὶ σωτηρίας, Act. III. vers. 15. Ebr. II. vers. 10. fidei dux & consum- mator, Ebr. XII. vers. 2. & auctor æternæ salutis omnibus, Ebr. V. vers. 9. Jehovah justitia nostra, salutis & securitatis auctor, Jerem. XXIII. vers. 5.6. Salvator & magnus DEUS, Tit. II. vers. 13. 14. Salvator & Dominus, per quem omnia, 1. Corinth. IIX. vers. 6. Salvator & solus DEUS, Jud. vers. ult. Adde (3) quod Apostolus seipsum satis explicet, quod intelligat, per Filium creata esse secula, non quidem ut per causam instrumen- talem vel secundam, sed tanquam virtutem DEI substantialem, & characterem ὑποστάσεως DEI Patris, & splendorem gloriæ ejus, qui omnia por- tat verbo providentiæ suæ. Alii ita explicant, ut per Filium judicare dicatur Pater, quia judicem genuit, sic etiam per Filium creasse dicitur, quia eum genuit opificem. Simplicissimè cum scri- pturis dicitur Pater condidisse omnia per Fili- um, ut per Verbum hypostaticum, Gen. I. vers. 2. 1. Johan. I. vers. 3. ut sapientiam architectonicam, Prov. IIX. vers. 30. virtutem & potentiam infini- tam, Luc. I. vers. 35. 1. Corinth. I. vers. 24. & dex- tram DEI omnipotentem, Pf. LXXII. 11. ut ergo dextra DEI non est instrumentum vel medium DEI, sed virtutem infinitam DEI, quæ ipse DEUS est, designat, ita nec Filius est causa media, & instru- mentalis creationis, licet dicatur per Filium omnia condita esse à Deo. (4) Notatur autem hoc pacto saltim ordo in SS. Trinitate, quod Filius sit à Patre ratione personæ, per quem Pater crea- vit omnia : tametsi ratione essentiæ Filius sit unum cum Patre, Joh. X. 30. Joh. V. 7.

Grotii glossa, quod δι᾿ ὕ pro δι ὃν dictum sit, h. e. propter ipsum, non modo nova est, sed à communi etiam præpositionis in ista constructio- ne significatu recedit citra necessitatem : adhæc Rabbinico potius, quam Biblico fundamento inni- titur. Ubi enim propter Messiam in Scripturis mundus dicitur conditus? & qua ratione vel An- geli, vel creaturæ irrationales & inanimatæ atti- nent Filium DEI ceu unctum in Mediatorem, vel Sacerdotem, Regem ac Prophetam. Nam istorum causa unctus minimè est, sed propter hominem; multò minus illa propter Messiam vel unctum Do- mini condita sunt, quum ne homo quidem pro- pter Messiam creatus sit.

II. Secula, quæ dicuntur condita. Per τὺς αἰῶ- νας non solum intelliguntur tempora, vel secula universa, ut est absolute, vel indefinite positum, quemadmodum tempora seculiria dicuntur reve- lationes temporum, Roman. XVI. vers. 25. 2. Tim. I. vers. 9. Tit. I. vers. 2. χρόνοι αἰώνιοι, & αἰῶνες, Coloss. I. vers. 26. sed & omnia temporalia, vel quæ tempore mensurantur, in tempore creata sunt, & subsistunt. Nam vox αἰῶν bifariam accipi- tur, (1) de duratione ac tempore; (2) de rebus, quæ in tempore creata sunt, & existunt, vel pro rebus creatis & factis in seculo, quæcunque un- quam usquam extiterunt, extant, aut extabunt, ut vox עוֹלָם apud Ebræos, & seculum vel tem- pus, & res in seculo existentes significat, mundum & quæ in mundo sunt. Notat Flacius in Clav. part. II. cap. 287. regulam: quod Scriptores No- vi Testamenti aliquas Ebræas voces πολυσήμυς reddituri sæpe una significatione pro alia utantur, eoque referri potest præsens vox αἰώνων. Nam & Ebr. עוֹלָם & secula mundum significare, notissimum est, ideo αἰῶνες secula redduntur pro mundo; Eodem prorsus modo dixit Apostolus cap. XI. 3. aptata esse secula Verbo: seu, per Verbum DEI mundum conditum esse.

Enjedinus per αἰῶνας intelligi vult Ecclesiam novam: Schlichtingius secula per Christum facta dicit, non quod omnia, quæ unquam extiterunt secula per eum condita, sed quod aliqua, nem- pe nova, & à prioribus diversa, iisque longe feliciora. Quod factum esse pronunciat, quia DEUS per Christum plane novam, & à priori longe diversam rerum ac mundi fabricam indu- xerit, & respexisse hîc divinum autorem ad Græ- cam Bibliorum translationem, in qua Christus Es. IX. vers. 6. Pater vel Autor futuri seculi no- minatur, quatenus DEUS per eum futura quæ- dam, eaque valdè felicia secula conditurus erat, ut puta non ea tantum, quæ post mundi finem extabunt, sed etiam illa, quæ à Christi regno, & totius mundi per eum factà reformatione fluere cœperunt.

Verum enim vero neuter assequitur mentem Apostoli, qui non de Ecclesiæ novæ constitutio- ne, vel mundi per CHRISTUM reformatio- ne: aut cœlestis beatitudinis origine hic disserit, sed CHRISTUM rerum omnium hæredem omni- um quoque opificem & autorem esse testatur. Itaque vocem αἰῶν hic non de Ecclesiâ, vel seculis Novi Testam. aut vitæ æternæ, quod vo- lunt prædicti hæretici, sed de mundo universo vel omnibus seculis accipi debere confirmamus his documentis. (1) Vox αἰώνων indefinite po- nitur, ideoque universaliter secula omnia sunt intelligenda, non verò aliqua saltem. Non enim articulus hic restringit vocem ad certa secula, quem sæpissime apponi, ubi yox indefinite po- sita universaliter accipienda est, probatione haud eget; (2) quia αἰῶνες nuspiam absolutè dicun- tur de Ecclesia. Reponit Enjedinus cap. II. v. 5. hujus Epist. CHRISTO mundum futurum sub- jectum dici, & cap. V. verf. 6. virtutes futuri seculi gustari de prægustu vitæ æternæ: Sed prio- ri loco non habetur vox αἰώνων, verum οἰκουμέ- νης, posteriori verò non Ecclesia, sed vita æter- na & beatitudo cælestis venit nomine αἰῶνῶ, in singulari, & quidem non absolute, sed cum adjecta determinatione τοῦ μέλλοντος futuri se- culi. (3) Quia crescit hic oratio Apostoli faten- te Schlichtingio: Minus autem est dignitatis in eo, quod CHRISTUS dicatur aliqua secu- la utut felicissima condidisse, quam quod hæres omnium, quæcunque sunt in cælo & in terra, & Dominus sit super omnia opera manuum DEI absolutus & catholicus. (4) Imo causa hic red- ditur, ob quam jure ad hæreditatem evectus sit à DEO CHRISTUS: quia nempe secula per eum condita sint: Nulla autem erit συνέχεια cau- sæ hujus, si aliqua tantum secula fecisse dicatur, unde non nisi eorum hæreditas ad ipsum jure devoluta videbitur, quorum ipse est Autor & opifex. (5) Ea sine dubio per Filium condi- ta sunt, quæ ipse portat verbo virtutis suæ: cum non tantum ejusdem sit condere, & conservare, sive ferre omnia, sed & Apostolus hic immedia- te subjungat, CHRISTUM omnia ferre vel sustentare verbo suo potenti, quemadmodum dixerat, per CHRISTUM esse creata, vel condita secula. Atqui omnia CHRISTUS portat & sustentat, non aliqua tantum dicente Apostolo. (6) Id per secula intelligit Aposto- lus in προθέσει, quæ esse condita dixit vers. 2. quod in ἐκθέσει, & enarratione propositionis innuit, cum cælum & terram esse à CHRISTO condi- ta docet vers. 10. Hic verò non Ecclesiam no- vam, vel etiam vitam æternam sive futurum se- culum, sed ipsam cæli terræque præsentis ma- chinam indigitari manifestissimum est. (7) Ac- cedit locus parallelus è cap. XI. vers. 3. πίστει νοῦ- μεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας ῥήματι Θεοῦ. Nam uti τοὺς αἰῶνας secula aptata ibi dicit Apostolus, ita præsenti loco τοὺς αἰῶνας secula condita do- cet à DEO. At indubiè aptata secula dicuntur de creatione mundi, neutiquam vero de refor- matione Ecclesiæ. (8) Per CHRISTUM plane novam, & à priori longe diversam rerum ac mundi faciem inductam esse, nuspiam Scriptu- ra docet, sed commentum est cerebri Sociniani illa totius mundi per CHRISTUM facta refor- matio. CHRISTUM autem esse rerum omnium auctorem & opificem, non modo Apostolus in- fra ostendit è Psalm. CII. vers. 26. sed & universa Scripturæ consensus est. (9) Si hic per secula intelligenda non tantum secula beata alterius vi- tæ, sed quotquot à CHRISTI regno fluere cœ- perunt, utique non aliqua saltem, sed omnia se- cula universim designantur. Nam regnum Chri- sti cœpit inde ab origine mundi, Ebr. XIII. vers. 8. Apocal. XIII. vers. 8. (10) Si Christus secula condidit beata, hoc est, æternam vitam, quum eadem sit non solum fidelium in Novo Test. sed omnium quotquot ab orbe condito fuêre fideles, oportet etiam fideles inde ab origine seculi ad re- gnum Christi pertinere; imò cum ad beata secula non admittantur, nisi qui fuerint consortes re- gni Christi in hoc seculo, teste universa Scriptu- ra Sacra, necessum est, regnum Christi cum ipsa mundi origine cepisse. (11) Si per Christum bea- ta secula condita, id est, vita æterna præparata est, fatente Schlichtingio, Christum ante tempo- ra secularia, vel ab origine seculi extitisse opor- tet: quia vita beata ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμυ præpa- rata est electis, Matth. XXV. 34. & nos electi su- mus in ipso, Ephes. I. 4. & data est nobis gratia in Christo Jesu πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων, 2. Tim. I. 9. ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, 2. Thess. II. 13. (12) Tandem, quem dabi- mus certiorem Interpretem, quam ipsum Spiri- tum S. qui Joh. I. 3. per Verbum, DEI Filium, con- dita dicit omnia, & v. 10. mundum per Verbum factum esse testatur, & Col. I. 16. omnia per ipsum esse creata docet : perinde ut hic per Filium DEI condita esse secula pronunciat. Agnoscit hanc locorum analogiam Schlichtingius: Idem, inquit, sensus erit, si seculorum voce mundum intelligamus. Nam & ipse D. Autor infra eadem significatione vocem hanc usurpavit, adeo, ut si rem ipsam spectes, nihil aliud hic D. Autor, quàm quod Johannes dixit, mundum per sermonem esse factum, aut Pau- lus, omnia per Christum esse condita. Johannes au- tem cum mundum per ipsum factum esse dicit, vel omnia condita per ipsum, quæcunque con- dita, ut & Paulus non tantum aliqua intelligunt, aut Ecclesiam novam, multò minus vitam æter- nam indigitant, sed universum mundum, omnia, quæcunque creata sunt, adeo, ut sine ipso nihil factum sit, quod factum est, omnia, quæ in cælo & in terra sunt, visibilia & invisibilia. Concludi- mus itaque, ea omnia quoque voce αἰώνων hic denotari. Quod denique agnoscere etiam viden- tur Racovienses, qui reddunt in Germana ver- sione τὺς αἰῶνας die Welt. Quæ hic probandæ suæ depravationi adducunt veritatis hostes, di- luemus circa ultimum membrum: Id tantum hic adjicimus, non omninò certum esse, hic respice- re voluisse Apostolum ad LXX. translationem Es. IX. vers. 6. voce αἰώνων: quia ibi vox compo- sita μέλλοντος αἰῶνος, hic nomen simplex αἰώνων commemoratur; ibi Pater futuri seculi Christus vocandus dicitur, hic per Christum secula condita, ne dicam, quod illic in Ebræo & originali textu אבי עד neutraliter & ἁπλῶע reddi possit, ut vi- detur intellexisse Chaldæus interpres, reddens h. m. גברא קים לעלמא vir permanens in æternum, ut ille אל גבור DEUS fortis dicatur esse Pater æternus, vereque ejus exprimatur æternitas: quo de loco pluribus egimus dissertat. Rostochiens. pag. 63. seqq.

III. Actus Creationis seculorum exprimitur voce ἐποίησεν, fecit, quæ hic pro subjecta mate- ria, de prima rerum creatione intelligenda venit, non verò, ut Sociniani contendunt, de reforma- tione. Quanquam enim haud negamus fieri quan- doque in Scripturis dici, quod ratione qualita- tum quarundam fit aliud, & novam veluti for- mam induit, vel de factione ratione qualitatis, ac conditionis alicujus, non ratione ipsius natu- ræ, quodque præterea reparatio nostra in Christo dicatur creatio, (quod frustra hîc probat Schlich- tingius) neutiquam tamen hinc inferri potest, eandem hîc loci obtineri significationem. Pro- cedit enim argumentum à particulari.

Quin o- mnino hic creationem primam intelligi, ostendi- mus, (1) Quia de rerum omnium creatione ser- monem esse jam evicimus. Non est autem facta reformatio à Christo rerum omnium, sed tantum generis humani, cujus tanquam præcipuæ mundi partis reformationem si dicat Schlichtingius, esse omnium rerum vel mundi conditionem, partem cum toto perverse confundet, nec Apostolo sa- tisfaciet, quem citra Synecdochen omnia intelli- gere ostensum. (2) Quia reformatio humani ge- neris, & seculorum creatio maximè diversa sunt: nec ulli Epistolam hanc sine præcepta opinione legenti hoc in mentem poterat venire, cum secu- la condita dicuntur per Christum, indigitatam esse reformationem generis humani. Is autem pro- cul dubio est alienus sensus, qui neutiquam è ver- bis ipsis elicitur, sed ibidem infertur; Sensus ge- nuinus Spiritus S. nemini obscurus est verba ejus- dem legenti. (3) Adhæc contextus haud admit- tit, hæc intelligi de reparatione nostra, vel præ- paratione æternæ gloriæ, quum his versibus pro- œmialibus Apostolus proponat ea, de quibus con- stitutum est in hac Epistola velut ex professo age- re; non est ergò verisimile, ipsum hic reparatio- nis nostræ mentionem facere voluisse, quam de- mum v. seq. indicat purificatione peccatorum no- strorum commemorata, postquam scil. fundamen- ti loco substrata erat doctrina de persona Christi, & natura ejus utraque cum humana, tum divina. Ideoque idem bis dictum esset in propositione Apostolica, si per secula condita humanum genus reparatum à Christo intelligeretur, quod hic ad- mittere non est necesse. Imo ita ordo rerum in- verteretur, (quem tamen observatum esse vult Schlichtingius) si reparatio nostra præmittere- tur purificationi peccatorum nostrorum per sanguinem Christi factæ, & evectioni ejusdem ad dexteram DEI, quia reparationem istam de- mùm post exaltationem ad dextram DEI perfe- ctam esse ait Schlichtingius. (4) Quid per ποίη- σιν hanc intellectum velit Apostolus, docet ἐξή- γησις & demonstratio ejusdem v. 10. subjuncta, ubi non novæ terræ, novique cæli, sed universi hujus fundationem & creationem vindicat Filio DEI, eundemque conditorem & creatorem esse cœli & terræ, λευκάδι φωνῇ docet, atque evin- cit. (5) Ubicunque in Scripturis creatio secunda, vel reparatio indigitatur, non simplicis rerum facturæ, vel productionis, aut creationis men- tio fit, sed cum adjuncta ejusmodi declaratione, ut liquidò constet, intelligi secundam creatio- nem. Ubi autem absolutè res omnes productæ dicuntur à DEO, vel creatio mundi commemo- ratur, primam creationem intelligendam esse, certum est. Id vel loca illa docent, quæ allegat Schlichtingius, Psalm. C. vers. 3. Ipse fecit nos, & non ipsi nos, additur populum suum, & oves pascuæ ejus. Ephes. II. vers. 10. Creati in Christo Jesu ad bona opera. Ita 2. Corinth. V. vers. 17. qui in CHRISTO est, creatura dicitur cum adjecto καινὴ nova, & adjuncta novitatis decla- ratione Es. LI. vers. 16. plantatio cæli, & fun- datio terræ dicitur, non ipsa restitutio è Babylo- nica captivitate, sed Ecclesiæ collectio, regenera- tio, & populi Domini per verbum creatio, ut subjuncta explicatio docet: quia plantare dicit tur Deus cælum, fundare terram, dum verbum suum in ore Prophetæ ponit, & Zioni dicit (hoc est reipsa talem præstat Ziona populum Israe- liticum, uti dicere DEI est facere, & tum dici, quid Scriptura ait, cum reipsa præstatur) po- pulus meus, es tu. Ideoque Prophetæ etiam ad- scribitur hæc cæli plantatio & terræ funda- tio, non saltim ratione prædictionis, vel quod ea verbis suis & vaticiniis prædixerit, sed ratione prædicationis verbi divini, & ministerialis ad plantandum cœlum & terram fundandam con- cursus: quia Deus per ministerium Doctorum verbi plantat cœlum, fundat terram, qui hinc Θεῦ σύνεργοι dicuntur 1. Cor. III. 11. Gal. IV. 19. Phil. V. v. 10. qui sunt plantæ Domini Es. LXI. vers. 3. qui- bus repletur Paradisus cœlestis Ap. II. vers. 7. & possident terram in æternum Es. LX. vers. 21. ideoque licet per terram & cœlum l. c. intelligere vel regnum gratiæ, sive Ecclesiam in his terris, vel regnum gloriæ, sive novum cœlum, novamque terram Es. LXVI. 22. Schlichtingius laudat Mu- sculi, aliorumque ad Christum hæc referentium interpretationem, cui Pater verba sua in os ipsius dederit, ut cœlum novum & terram novam con- deret, sed de Propheta sermonem esse, manifeste docet series verborum. Quem consolatur & eri- git Dominus in officio pollicitatione gratiosæ assistentiæ, & fructus præclari muneris sui. My- stico autem sensu ad Christum hoc referri debere, & quidem illam seculorum creationem istis Prophetæ verbis designatam esse nullo argumen- to docet adversarius, imo Filius DEI est is, qui Prophetæ hæc verba in os ejus ponit, ut è col- latione cap. præced. vers. 6. liquet. Id autem è verbis ipsis omnino perspicuum est, non respici primam creationem. Quod pariter de cæteris Scripturæ locis, quæ forte secundam creationem sistunt accipiendum, quod nomen semetipsum satis explicat. Hic autem nulla vel determina- tio adjecta, vel explicatio subjuncta, unde vel minimo judicio constet, de reparatione sermo- nem esse. Adde (6) quod nunquam è Scri- pturis proferre possint adversarii locum paral- lelum, ubi secula condita vel parata, aut simile quid dicatur de reformatione, quam dicit per Christum factam. Et quod hac locutione prima creatio insinuetur, documento est si- milis locus Ebr. XI. vers. 3. ubi aptata dicuntur secula. Ideoque prævia quidem Scriptura nos de prima creatione, ἄτερ γραφῆς autem de se- cunda Sociniani hanc phrasin accipiunt. Deni- que conferimus hic denuo alia Novi Testam. loca huic parallela, quæ hanc ποίησιν, qua Deus per Christum omnia condidit, de prima hujus universi creatione interpretantur Johann. I. vers. 3. 10. & Coloss. I. vers. 16.

Nec ullius ponderis est, quod per Filium di- cantur secula condita, ex quo infert Schlichtin- gius: de veteri creatione sermonem non esse, quæ nunquam dicatur per causam aliquam me- diam fuisse peracta. Nam intermediam causam voce ista designari nimis frivolum, ut ante nota- vimus, & jam pridem adversus Arianos obser- varunt veteres Ecclesiæ Doctores. Athanasius serm. III. contra Arium, Cyrillus lib. I. in Johan. cap. 3. & Basilius lib. de Spiritu sancto cap. IIX. & X. quum & Patri 1. Cor. I. 9. Gal. I. vers. 1. Ebr. XI. vers. 10. & Spiritui S. tribuatur Rom. V. v. 5. Ordinem autem & distinctionem Patris à Filio insinuari admittimus, ut Basilius pluribus docuit l. c. c. 1. id tantum significari: Patrem esse prin- cipium sine principio, Filium esse principium de principio, ex quo fiat, ut quæ Pater facit, recte dicatur, non solum per se, sed etiam per Filium facere, quia Filius à Patre accepit & originem & Naturam, & Vim faciendi. Dimissa vero notio- ne causæ intermediæ veterem creationem PER Verbum, PER Sapientiam, PER Virtutem DEI, ut & PER Spiritum ejus factam uspiam dici, si negat Adversarius, Solem nunc lucere ne- gat. PER Sapientiam, dicit Salomo, fundavit Dominus terram cap. III. 19. PER VIRTU- TEM suam terram fecit, per Sapientiam suam stabilitivit orbem, Jer. X. vers. 12. Conf.' cap. LI. vers. 15. Per magnam virtutem suam cælum & terram fecit, & per excelsum brachium suum, Jerem. XXXII. vers. 7. Per Verbum Domini cæli firmati sunt, & per Spiritum oris ejus omnis ex- ercitus eorum, Psalm. XXXIII. vers. 6. Quo pacto etiam Chaldæus Interpres Es. XLIV. vers. 14. red- dit. Ego Dominus creator omnium extendens cælos verbo meo, fundavi terram in virtute mea. Et in Nov. Testam. per verbum hypostaticum omnia creata dicuntur, Johan. I. vers. 3. Mundus per ipsum conditus est, vers. 10. DEUS PER Christum omnia creavit, Ephes. III. vers. 9. & Coloss. I. vers. 16. Omnia per ipsum creata sunt. Quod autem D. Johannes non de reformatione mundi, ut vult Schlichtingius, sed de prima crea- tione agat c. I. 3. & 10. nec alludat tantum ad veterem creationem, cum per Verbum omnia crea- ta esse dicit, & lucis mentionem injicit, sed osten- dat, Verbum quod in principio rerum omnium apud DEUM extitit, quodque DEUS ipse est, condidisse omnia e nihilo, totumque hoc universum creasse, & scopus & verborum evi- dentia, & contextus luculenter docent. Et qui alluderet mentione lucis, quæ primo omnium condita erat, cum hic Filium DEI lucem Ma- gnam indigitet, quem non e creaturarum nu- mero esse ait, sed potius rerum omnium crea- torem, cum nihil sine ipso conditum, quod con- ditum. Paulus vero cum distribuit κατὰ μερισμὸν ea omnia, quæ condita sunt per imaginem Dei invisibilis Col. I. vers. 16. ea quæ in cælis & quæ in terris sunt, visibilia & invisibilia, thronos, po- testates, dominationes, &c. eaque omnia & sin- gula per ipsum, & ad ipsum condita dicit: qua fronte id trahit Schlichtingius ad reformatio- nem, vel reparationem? Quid enim? num & Angeli & potestates, throni, dominatus reformati sunt & reparati per Christum? Num omnia, quæ in cælo, & quæ in terra sunt nova facta sunt per Christum, visibilia & invisibilia? Sed hic for- tasse dicturus est Schlichtingius cum Sacino & Schmalzio Præceptoribus suis, politias Angelo- rum reformatas esse, & pristinas eorum dignita- tes mutatas, ut aliæ nunc sint ab illis quas antea, quam Christus in cælum ascenderet, habuere in Ex. 157. Error. pag. 12. & l. de divin. Filii. c. XVI. pag. 98. imo & dæmones creatos per Christum dici posse, quatenus Christus omnem illorum potestatem ita reformavit, ut nunc etiam Christo subditi sint & pareant in Ex. Error. 157. Err. 133. pag. 53. Verum nova est hæc Theologia, Scripturæ S. prorsus incognita de reformatione Angelorum & Diabolorum per Christum facta, de creatio- ne eorundem per Christum post ascensionem in cælum, quam unice ad elidendum Scriptu- ræ testimonium luculentissimum nuper excogi- tarunt Sociniani. Nuspiam de reformatione Angelorum & dæmonum legere est in Scriptu- ra: nuspiam creatio nova ad Angelos vel dæ- mones extenditur, & cur non pisces, volucres, aves, & quæcunque sunt in mundo, reformata, noviterque creata dicit Schmalzius per Chri- stum, quum eadem omnia Christo nunc subje- cta sint per exaltationem ejus ad dexteram Dei Psalm. IIX. vers. 7. Ebr. II. vers. 8. si subjectio illa reformatio est, & nova creatio? In Christo nova sunt omnia, dicente Apostolo 1. Cor. V. v. 17. sed non universaliter omnia quæ sunt in cælo & interna, sed quæ in Christo sunt, ideo se ipsum expli- cat: si quis est in Christo, est nova creatura. Con- fert præterea Schlichtingius verba Esaiæ supra ci- tata c. LI, 16. quod cæli plantatio, & terræ funda- tio Christo adscribenda sit, quatenus per eum novum cœlum, vel nova terra, vel novus DEI populus condendus erat, unde nova secula con- secuta sint. Verum si admitteretur etiam de Chri- sto sive quoad literam, sive mystico sensu eadem ex- plicare debere, quod tamen ob certas causas ad- mittendum non esse, antea ostensum, unde con- stat, apud Apostolum secula condita per Chri- stum idem esse, quod cœlum novum & terram novam apud Prophetam : Unde, novum cœ- lum, novam terram idem quod novum popu- lum, vel novam Ecclesiam potius, quam cœle- stem Hierosolymam? Assumit hæc Schlichtin- gius pro indubiis, nec ullo Scripturæ fundamen- to confirmat, ideoque ea facilitate negari pos- sunt, qua adseruntur.

Restat, ut Enjedini rationes, quæ majoris vi- dentur momenti, refellamus: sunt autem hæ: (1) quod dicatur mundus conditus per Filium (ut nos dicimus) incarnatum sive per Hominem Chri- stum. At fuit Homo Christus aliquot centenis an- nis mundo visibili creato posterior. (2) quod prius dicatur DEUS locutus per Filium, postea per eum condidisse mundum. At cum per homi- nem Christum locutus est, mundi machina jam pridem erat condita. Denique ait: Propositum Apostoli est Filium DEI supra omnes creaturas extollere, & ejus excellentiam deprædicare. Quid vero opus est DEUM æternum creaturis suis ex- cellentiorem esse demonstrare, cum id omnibus sit notum? Sed in promptu est ad easdem è verbo DEI responsio: Ad primam quidem; Per Fi- lium incarnatum dicitur mundus conditus: quia non est alius DEI Filius ante incarnationem, per quem mundus creatus est, Joh. I. vers. 10. Col. I. vers. 16. alius post incarnationem: Sed idem DEI Filius, eadem persona, ideoque recte tribuitur mundi creatio Filio DEI incar- nato, vel etiam Homini Christo, ob personæ identitatem, uti Christus Homo sese prius fuisse, quam Abraham erat Joh. IIX. vers. 59. asserit, non ratione naturæ, quam in tempore assumsit ex Patribus, vel secundum carnem, sed qua est æternus & benedictus in secula DEUS, Rom. IX. vers. 5. Posterior ergo est creato mundo ratione naturæ humanæ: qui prior est mundo & autor mundi ratione divinæ naturæ. Secunda ratio lu- brico nititur fundamento. Non enim ea, quæ prius dicuntur, priora ordinis, temporis, vel na- turæ esse necessum est: Nec ait Apostolus, novis- simis temporibus demum condidisse DEUM per Christum secula, sed Eundem, per quem no- vissimis temporibus locutus est, conditorem esse seculorum testatur. Identitas est hîc personæ, non temporis. Ordinem autem eum in hisce prædi- catis, Loquela DEI per Christum facta, Ejus- dem ad hæreditatem omnium admissione, seculo- rum denique creatione per Christum itidem fa- cta observatum, ut creatio seculorum illis po- sterior sit tempore, nec edocet Adversarius. Notissimum vero est, sæpe ea posteriori loco dici, prout intentio dicentis, & orationis se- ries exigit, quæ priora cæteris tempore vel na- tura. Intendit autem hic Apostolus divinam Christi naturam describere, quam ideo subjun- git descriptioni humanæ naturæ; quia vers. sequ. pluribus eandem explicare aggressus est, & quod notavimus antea, orationem intendere magis magisque voluit. Magnum est; DEUM per Filium locutum esse Ebræis novissimis tempori- bus. Sed majus id esse Ebræis videri poterat, quod per eum Filium, qui hæres est constitutus omnium in cælo & in terra: Maximum deni- que, quod per Eum, qui omnium, quæ in cælo & in terra, autor & Conditor est. Tertia Enje- dini ratio majorem quidem veri speciem præ se fert, in recessu tamen nihil omnino veri subest. Quia nec insolens est Scripturis componi Deum cum creaturis, iisdemque longe doceri eminen- tiorem, quum ne quidem aliter summam DEI eminentiam & sublimitatem animo concipere & apprehendere, vel cogitando assequi possimus, quam comparatione facta cum creaturis, quas infinitis superat & excedit rationibus, nec de- clamare solum consuevit Scriptura DEI Maje- statem comparatione creaturarum, sed demonstra- re quoque & asserere, quod absurdum videtur Enjedino, uti & Socino resp. ad Wujeck. pag. 86. DEUM infinitis modis præstantiorem esse crea- turis, quas infinitis superat & excedit rationi- bus, DEUM non esse sicut hominem, & id ge- nus alia, Num. XXIII. vers. 19. Es. LV. vers. 9. Job. IX. vers. 8. cap. XXXIII.vers.12. XXXIIX. vers. 18. sequ. cap. XLI. vers. 2. Quod vel e Psalm. CII. hic ab Apostolo vers. 11. adducto discere poterat adversarius, ubi confertur Deus summus cum creaturis vers. 27. Quid quod fre- quentissime DEUS cum idolis gentium, quæ nil nisi Dæmonia sunt, & nihil, conferatur, & sese illis infinito intervallo præstantiorem esse multis argumentis contendat, 1. Reg. XIIX. vers. 24. Psalm. XCVI. vers. 15. & CXV. vers. 4. sequ. Es. XLII. vers. 8. cap. XLIII. vers. 9. XLV. vers. 20. Jerem. X.vers.10.&c. Dehinc advertendum: quod Filius DEI conferatur cum creaturis, iis- que eminentior esse doceatur, qua de re dubium erat Ebræis motum ab hostibus Deitatis Chri- sti. Non ergo demonstrat Apostolus eum, quem summum Deum agnoscebant omnes, esse supe- riorem Angelis aliisque creaturis, sed Filium DEI, quem summum DEUM esse inficiaban- tur hæretici, nec satis agnoverant Ebræi, esse supremum DEUM Angelorum Dominum, cæli terræque creatorem: idque juxta Scripturas Vet. Testam. quarum autoritatem Ebræi suscipiebant, & venerabantur.

## 1:2
verse 2, Psalm 103:19, Isa. 63:15, Joel 3:17. Cf. 1 Kings 8:49, chapter 22:19, Isa. 6:1, and from the designation of the Divine seat, that he sits on the throne of GOD and in the midst of the throne, Apocal. 3:21, chapter 5:6, at the right hand of the throne of the majesty of God, Heb. 8:1, on the throne of glory, Matth. 19:28, chapter 25:31. For such as the throne is, such is the session. But that throne is of the highest, infinite, and most omnipresent majesty, the throne of GOD, Heb. 12:2, the throne of the Father, Apocal. 3:21, the eternal throne, Heb. 1:8, and from the attributes and effects of this exaltation to the right hand of GOD, that he rules wisely and in justice, Isa. 32:1, Jerem. 23:6, that he graciously and powerfully presides over his Church, and protects and defends it, Ephes. 1:22, chapter 5:23, Psalm 45:5. Psalm 72:4, that he feeds his people, Ezech. 34:23, Apoc. 7:16, and gives them pastors and Doctors, Ephes. 4:11, that he grants repentance and remission of sins, Acts 5:11, that he rules from sea to sea, Psalm 72:8, rules in the midst of his enemies, Psalm 110:2, 5, 6, destroys and crushes his enemies, Psalm 2:9, Psalm 45:9, subjects all things to his feet, 1 Corinth. 15:27, that he judges the world, Isa. 11:3, 4, Acts 17:3, Roman. 14:11, Philipp. 2:11, brings the hidden things of men into the light, 1 Corinth. 4:5, renders to each according to his works, Apocal. 22:12, Rom. 2:6, that finally he both saves and condemns, Matth. 25, etc. All of which are such that from them both the Calvinists and the Papists alike prove the supreme Deity of CHRIST against the Socinians. Whence it is necessary that they infer not a finite, but an infinite and truly immense and Divine power: and from the names which CHRIST obtains from thence, that he is Lord over his people, Mich. 5:2, head of the Church, Ephes. 1:22, chapter 5:23, Lord of the living and the dead, Roman. 14:9, of Angels and Principalities, Ephes. 1:21, Lord over all the works of the hands of God, Psalm 8:7, Lord of Lords, Apocal. 19:16, Lord of glory, 1 Corinth. 2:8. But as CHRIST is only one Lord, and one head, God and man: so also there must be only one Lord of CHRIST, God and man. Which certainly must be infinite, just as indeed from those sayings the supreme Deity of Christ is shown even by the Calvinists themselves against the Socinians: and finally from the glory and honor befitting CHRIST on account of this session at the right hand of Majesty. For that honor is not inferior to the honor of God; nor is Divine and religious honor twofold, one supreme, another intermediate or subordinate: But there is only one Divine honor, only one religious adoration, Conf. Dan. 7. verse 14. Roman. 14. verse 11. Philipp. 2, 14. Apocal. 5, 12.

It remains IV. that we explain that προσδιορισμὸν in the highest. From what has been said, however, it is evident that it ought not to be taken locally or by reason of place; but figuratively or by reason of manner; because neither the right hand of God, nor the sitting at the right hand of God is local, or in a certain place, but the right hand is immense, and the sitting is a Divine government extending itself to all things. Therefore it can be concluded in no place. These heights are those which in Luke 2, 14 are called the highest, on account of which GOD himself is called the highest Luke 1, 35. whence the dawn from on high has visited us Luke 1. verse 78. which were celebrated in song through Hosanna, Matt. XXI. verse 9. Mark XI. verse 10. Luke XIX. verse 38. whence the Apostles were endued with power, Luke XXIV. verse 49. Which are ὑπὲρ ἄνω πάντων, John III. verse 31. Eph. I. verse 21. They are called ὕψηλα not because they are within any dimension or boundary, but because they are above every one, Job IX. verses 7, 8. And therefore μεγαλωσύνη ἐν ὑψίλοις or ὑψίστοις is μεγαλωσύνη ὑψισὴ the highest and interminable Majesty: And CHRIST is said to sit in the highest or in the heavens by reason of his glory and exalted and heavenly Majesty. For the Holy Spirit defines that height and the right hand of GOD not by the sublimity of a place, but by the ineffable loftiness of glory and heavenly Majesty, as Athanasius, Cyril, Augustine, Philip, and indeed even Calvin interpret; just as the throne is in the heavens and the highest, Heb. VIII. verse 1, which throne, however, is not material or local or finite, because it is eternal, Psalm XLV. verse 7, and the throne of GOD himself, Rev. III. verse 21, Heb. XII. v. 1. But shall we attribute a local or finite throne to GOD? Shall we believe that GOD the Father, whom we profess to be in the heavens, Matt. VI. verse 9, is therefore in a place? Constantine the Presbyter of Antioch, according to the opinion of Chrysostom: What is in the highest? Does he enclose God in a place? Far be it. But just as by saying at the right hand, he did not figure him, but showed him to be in the same honor as the Father: So by saying him in the highest, he did not enclose him there, but showed that which is the highest of all, and which transcends all: This is, he arrived at the paternal throne itself. How therefore the Father is in the highest, so also is he himself. For to be seated signifies nothing else than to be in the same honor. And Theophylact: He does not say that he sits, as if GOD were circumscribed by some place, but to show the Son equal to the Father in honor and glory. For he arrived at the paternal throne, and as the Father sits sublime, so also the Son ascends the highest things. Whence, as Cornelius à Lapide observes, some express by this name μεγαλωσύνην, namely magnitude, magnificence, Divine and Paternal majesty designated here, and they understand in the Greek the article τῆς as if he were saying, μεγαλωσύνης τῆς ἐν ὑψηλοῖς, by translating of the most high majesty, which is not other, as he himself says, than that of GOD the Father. Wherefore Grotius trifles with the Calvinists, when he asserts that CHRIST is in the highest heaven, just as David was established in a certain eminent place on earth. That is not said of David in Psalm LXXXIX. verse 28. Nor is the subject there David, but CHRIST, nor is the predicate understood of a place, but of a state of eminence. But CHRIST is in heaven in such a way that he is above all heavens, and fills all things in heaven and on earth, Eph. IV. 10, Matt. XXVIII. 18.

Which further shine forth from the Apostolic comparison. For thus far the Apostle has described the exaltation of CHRIST absolutely through his session at the right hand of the Majesty on high. But now he describes the same comparatively also in verse 4, in that he has been made so much more excellent than the Angels, as he has inherited a more excellent name than they. Where these five points occur to be weighed: 1. According to which nature has he been made more excellent? 2. Why is he compared here with the Angels? 3. What is that διαφορώτερον name? 4.

When did he obtain it? and 5. how has he been made more sublime than the Angels, and inherited a more excellent name than them?

Regarding the former, the matter is settled from the preceding. For according to the same nature by which he sits at the right hand of Majesty, according to the same he has also been made more sublime, and has obtained a more excellent name. Which both the συνέχεια here teaches, and the ἀναλογία of the parallel passage, Phil. II. verse 19, διὸ καὶ ἀυτὸν ὁ Θεὸς ὑπερύψωσε, καὶ ἐχαρίσατο ἀυτῷ ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα; and also the passage Eph. 1. verses 21, 22, ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ ἀυτõ ἐν τοῖς ἐπȣρανίοις ὑπεράνω πάσης ἀρχῆς, καὶ παντὸς ὀνόματG: and finally the thing itself; because that sitting imports dominion, and from dominion the Lord is named; and therefore when he was raised to supreme dominion, he was constituted Lord of all, Acts II. verse 34, chapter X. verse 36, for which reason David confesses CHRIST sitting at the right hand of the Lord to be his Lord, who is likewise the Lord of all the faithful, and besides he says that he rules in the midst of his enemies, Psalm CX. verses 1, 2. Now it has been shown before that CHRIST sits at the right hand of Majesty according to his human nature: And therefore he has also been made more sublime, and has obtained a more excellent name according to his human nature. Although, says Leo the Great, Epist. 38, in CHRIST there is one and the same person of Deity and Humanity, yet we understand the exaltation, and the name above every name, to pertain to that form which was to be enriched with the increase of such great glorification. Regarding the word γενόμενG, Blessed Dorscheus has this to say in this place. It is manifest that Γίνομαι is put for I am or I exist, and partly also for I become. Regarding the former, see John I. verse 6, Luke XXIV. verse 19. Regarding the latter, Matt. XI. verses 20, 21, 23, 26, chapter XVII. verse 2, chapter XXI. verse 42, chapter XXVI. verse 24, John I. 3, chapter X. verse 12. If you take it in the first way, that CHRIST is said to be γενόμενG, the sense is this: being so much more sublime than the Angels, by how much, etc. If in the second sense, this will be the Apostolic sentiment: having been made so much more sublime than the Angels, both agreeable to the text and the analogy of faith. Speaking absolutely, the Son of GOD was always more sublime and better than all the Angels, because he always existed with GOD the Father even ἐν ἀρχῇ, by which all things were made, and the Angels themselves were produced, John I. v. 3, as he through whom the Angelic αἰῶνες were also made, Heb. I. 2. Who is the brightness of glory and the character ὑποστάσεως not Angelic or finite, but divine and infinite, who carries all things, and therefore the Angels themselves. He was also made better than the Angels both through ἕνωσιν, or ἐπίληψιν σαρκὸς καὶ αἵματG and of the seed of Abraham, below chapter II. verses 14 and 16, through καταρτισμὸν σώματG ἐμψύχȣ, below chapter X. Compare Phil. II. verse 6, 1. 1 Tim. III. ver. 16, then through the ὑπερύψωσιν and session at the right hand, in respect of which in Acts II. ver. 36 he is said to have been made Lord and CHRIST by reason of the plenary usurpation of the Majesty received. But this latter sense is without doubt more suitable to the present passage, which the Vulgate, B. Luther, and other interpreters also embrace, because it is not taught in these words who the Son of GOD was at the beginning of the Creation, but what manner of person He was made after the purification of sins, and through the session at the right hand of God.

As for the second, the comparison with the Angels is instituted:

1. So that it may be taught how greatly our nature, that is, the human nature, has been exalted in CHRIST, and so that the dignity of the nature which the Son of God assumed from their own lineage may be set before the eyes of the Hebrews by this συγκρίσει (comparison). For without doubt the Angels are the most noble of all creatures, but the Devils are the most abject after the apostasy. Since, therefore, our nature through diabolical seduction was not only cast down very far below the Angels, but was also thrown into the kingdom of darkness and the society of the Devils: that the same nature has been so greatly honored in CHRIST that it leaves the Angels far behind it, having been made far more sublime than them, and having obtained a far more eminent name; this indeed redounds to the highest honor, consolation, and joy for the human race. CHRIST was abject according to his human nature below the Angels in the state of humiliation. Now, therefore, it is taught how greatly he has been exalted above the Angels, when he sat down at the right hand of majesty.

2. Because the Son of God appeared not for the sake of the Angels, but for our sake; he assumed not the Angels, but the seed of Abraham, that is, human nature from the seed of Abraham, so that he might make expiation for our sins by himself: which grace the Apostle had determined to explain. Therefore, he here proclaims the dignity which has been conferred upon human nature in CHRIST, according to which he is ὁμοούσιοι (of the same substance) with us, before the Angels and above the Angels.

As for the third: We admit that that name διαφορώτερον is rightly explained as a more excellent name, and we acknowledge that by τὸ ὄνομα (the name) one should not understand a bare name, whence it is in vain to seek some name, whether proper or appellative, which is designated here, since the name is taken for the thing itself, just as for the Hebrews to be called is to be. Therefore, what some think, that the name Jehovah is understood, or others, with Cornelius à Lapide, that the name of the Son of God is understood, does not sufficiently agree.

Add that CHRIST inherited this name according to his human nature, that he obtained it after his humiliation and the expiation of our sins, that he received it when he was exalted, when he sat down at the right hand of GOD, when he was made more sublime than the Angels. But CHRIST did not inherit the name Jehovah and the name of the Son of GOD according to his human nature: for that belongs to him not by reason of his human nature, but his Divine nature: nor can the human nature of CHRIST, or CHRIST according to his human nature, be called Jehovah or the Son of GOD in the nominative case: nor was the man CHRIST made Jehovah or the Son of GOD after his humiliation, but by personal union, and in the very conception and birth, the holy thing which was born of Mary was called the Son of GOD, Luke 1:35, and the branch of David, Jehovah, Jeremiah 23:6.

He was not made Jehovah and the Son of God after the purification of our sins, because he had to be the Son of man, the Son of God, and Jehovah himself in order to expiate our sins, Isaiah 43:24, 25.

The man CHRIST did not obtain that name and dignity, so as to be called Jehovah and the Son of God in the concrete, only when he was exalted, but from the very first moment of the incarnation, when the Word was made flesh, John 1:14.

Nor indeed can it be said that he then obtained that name in a more perfect way in his exaltation.

For the name Jehovah does not admit of more and less; nor did he become the Son of God in a more perfect way, which is a Socinian fiction already refuted elsewhere, especially in our Anti-Crellius.

If you say that the Apostle himself explains this name διαφορώτερον as the name of the Son of God, when he adds: For to which of the Angels did he ever say: You are my Son? verse 5. I answer that this proof, taken from Psalm 2:7, is by no means brought forward by the Apostle to confirm this last member of the proposition, that he was made more excellent than the Angels, and obtained a more excellent name than them.

The Apostle does not begin his demonstration with a καθ᾽ ὕστερον πρότερον [putting the latter first], but proves first that which was primary in the προθέσει [proposition], concerning the declaration of the eminence of the person of our Teacher and Priest, namely that he himself is the Son of God, the Creator of the ages, the brightness of his glory and the express image of God's person, upholding all things by the word of his power: which first of the members, having been completed in verse 4, he begins in verse 5 to demonstrate from the προθέσει [proposition] that the eternal Son of GOD, begotten before the ages, who is the substantial image of God, to be worshipped by the Angels themselves, is GOD himself Jehovah, the creator and preserver of all things, proving this most solidly from Psalm II, verse 7; 2 Samuel VII, verse 14; Psalm XCVII, verse 8; Psalm XLV, verse 7; Psalm CII, verse 7.

With this demonstration of the first member concerning the eminence of the person with respect to the Divine nature completed, he finally undertakes in verse 13 to demonstrate the eminence of the person of our Teacher and High Priest by reason of his human nature, namely that according to it he has been constituted heir of all things, that he sits at the right hand of majesty, that he has been made better than the Angels, that he has obtained a more excellent name, which he confirms first from Psalm CX, verse 1. For to which of the Angels did he ever say, sit at my right hand? Afterwards, from Psalm VIII, verse 5, concerning the Son of man constituted over all the works of God's hands, and thus over the Angels themselves, inasmuch as all things are subject to him, so that nothing is left ἀνυπότακτον [unsubjected], chapter II, 6 et seqq.

What, therefore, is understood by that more excellent name? It is acknowledged that a mere name is not meant. For by the reception of a name alone, no one would be better than the Angels. Schlichtingius denies that dignity is denoted, because this comparison would be tautological. For what, he says, is it to be made more excellent than the Angels, other than to have obtained greater dignity than them? But why could not a more eminent excellence be concluded from a name that brings with it the greatest dignity, such as the name or title of the One Sitting at the right hand of GOD: or the name above every name, or Lord of all? Why could it not be inferred from greater dignity and glory, without tautology, that he has been made τῶν κρείττων [better]? Grotius indeed names it a greater title, but wishes it to be understood that a certain and lasting right is designated at the same time, because he obtained the more excellent name by inheritance.

More correctly, that more sublime name is understood as the glory and majesty more excellent than the Angels. For the name of GOD is the glory and majesty of GOD according to the usage of Scripture, of which Christ was made a partaker according to his human nature, because in him dwells the whole fullness of the Godhead bodily, Coloss. II. verse 9. and his glory was seen as the glory of the Only-begotten Son of GOD, John I. verse 14. crowned with honor and glory, Psalm VIII. v. 6. Heb. II. verse 7. Which glory, since it is eternal, which he had as the Son of GOD before the world was created, John 13. verse 13. and thus is infinite and immense, and is the glory of GOD himself, because from eternity there was nothing but GOD, there was nothing finite, therefore CHRIST is said to be about to come in the glory of GOD the Father, Matt. XXV. verse 31. and to be in the glory of God the Father, Philipp. II. verse 11. he is in infinite ways more sublime in dignity and glory than the Angels, just as the finite and the infinite differ infinitely.

It is a name above every name, in which the knees of all must bow, Philipp. II. verses 9 and 10, just as he has been exalted above everything that can be named, in this age and in the future, Ephes. I. verse 22.

Thus he has obtained a more excellent name above all Angels, that is, a more sublime dignity; which would not be a name above every name, unless the dignity and glory were truly Divine. For otherwise there would be given yet another name, another dignity, and a glory of GOD of an infinitely more eminent degree. Concerning which Theodoret says in Psalm XXI: If the assumed nature is joined with the assuming Divinity, it has also been made a participant and consort of the same glory and honor. And in Heb. I: The humanity itself after the resurrection has obtained Divine glory. Likewise to Ephes. 1: That the nature assumed from us is a participant of the same honor with him who assumed it, so that no difference of adoration is seen, but through the nature which is perceived, the Divinity which is not perceived is adored, this indeed surpasses every miracle. Διαφορώτερον for more excellent also occurs in Heb. 8. verse 6, and in Arrian and other exotic writers.

As to the fourth: When was he made better than the Angels, and inherited a more excellent name than the Angels? The Apostle says with a resounding voice that this was done after the expiation of our sins, when he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty. Although CHRIST was made a participant of the Divine Majesty and glory according to his human nature by virtue of the personal union, nevertheless a voluntary κένωσις or emptying intervened, in the state of humiliation, for the sake of the expiation of our sins, therefore it was necessary that, that expiation having been accomplished, CHRIST should be exalted, and admitted to the plenary usurpation of Divine glory, for which cause he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high: and therefore he is said to have been made better than the Angels, having been made lower than the Angels for a short time, and to have obtained a more excellent name than they, after he had made purification of our sins by himself: See Phil. 2, 6. seqq.

Whence Eusebius Emissenus in his homily for the Friday after Easter: He who according to his Divinity always had power over all things together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now also according to his humanity has received power over all things, so that that man, who recently suffered, may rule over heaven and earth.

And Theophylactus from Chrysostom in Matt. chap. XXVIII: Because human nature, previously condemned, is now joined to GOD the Word personally, but is also adored in heaven and by the Angels, he rightly says: All power is given to me in heaven and on earth. For human nature previously served, now in CHRIST it commands all things. Therefore Cornelius à Lapide, although he does not disapprove of the opinion of Gabriel Vasquez: To sit at the right hand of GOD, who is on high, denotes by metaphor the greatest honor which the humanity of CHRIST had: indeed, also the consortium of the same dignity in the same seat, and thus by reason of the hypostatic union with the Word, the humanity of CHRIST sat at the right hand of the Father from the beginning of its conception. He rightly adds: But because here and in the creed CHRIST is said to sit at the right hand of GOD after his death, resurrection, and ascension into heaven: Hence the humanity of CHRIST is best said to sit at the right hand of GOD after it ascended to the heavens, having been exalted above all creatures, so that it far transcends the Angels, Cherubim, and Seraphim.

As to the fifth, concerning the manner, in what way CHRIST was made κρείττων better than the Angels after the expiation of sins, in what way he obtained a more excellent name, this is to be understood not by reason of κοινωνίας simply or by reason of κτήσεως and possession of Divine glory and Majesty: For as man he received this communicated through the hypostatic union, and thus possessed it from the first moment of the incarnation; since the hypostatic union with the Divine nature cannot be imagined without a true and real communication of Divine glory: But by reason of χρήσεως, as regards the usurpation, and that a plenary one, as he had emptied himself in the state of humiliation, as the Apostle testifies, Philipp. II, where he speaks more fully of these things.

He is said to have inherited that name, because he did not obtain it by the merit of humiliation. For he merited nothing for himself, but everything for us, for whom he was born and given, Isa. IX. verse 6. For an inheritance is not obtained by merits: But by grace, to which merit is opposed, the name above every name was given to him, (ἐχαρίσατο) Philipp. 2. verse 9. and the human nature of CHRIST, accepted within the hypostasis of the Son of GOD, was made heir of all things, Heb. 1. verse 2. According to which it was said to the Son of GOD, ask of me, and I will give thee the nations for an inheritance, Psalm 2. verse 8. For inherited, in Greek it is κεκληρονόμηκεν, that is, he has obtained by lot, he has received by lot; by lot, that is, by inheritance. For an inheritance was divided among heirs by lots or by lot, hence it was called a hereditary lot.

There is, however, a catachresis in the word inherited. For it is not called an inheritance which is entered upon when a parent has died, nor is he an heir who succeeds him: But because he obtained that glory like an inheritance, and was constituted Lord of all like an heir, with an allusion made to the name of Son, to whom an inheritance belongs by right.

Therefore he is not said to be made κρείττων better or more excellent than the Angels as regards morals, but as regards glory and dignity: not as regards a bare declaration, as Cornelius à Lapide and Estius with Constantinus Presbyter and Theophylactus; but as regards the truth of the matter. Just as the evacuation or emptying was true and real: So also the exaltation and betterment must be believed to be real and true: Nor does this favor the Arians in any way, because it happened to him according to his human nature. For is not the admission to plenary lordship, to the perpetual and plenary usurpation of the Divine Majesty, something real? Nor is the inheritance of a more excellent name the possession of the name of the Son of GOD, either by nature; as Thomas wishes, whose commentary, in Estius's judgment, seems to have some offense; because theologians do not concede that a man was made God or the Son of God, just as they concede and teach that God and the Son of God was made man, which he also proves from Thomas III. p. 116. art. 7. or by union, as Cajetan explains: It is one thing to possess the name of the Son of God, another to inherit a name more excellent than the Angels. The divine nature of Christ, the Son of God, possesses the name not by union, but by eternal generation, even if the human nature is united to the divine nature, which union causes it not to be υἱὸς Son of God, but ὑπόθεσις, assumed into the hypostasis of the Son of God, or subsisting in the hypostasis of the Son of God: but the human nature of Christ obtained the more excellent name after the expiation, not by union, but by exaltation; which is the divine glory itself regarding its plenary usurpation. Nor therefore does Estius correctly explain it in this way: Christ claimed for himself the possession of the name of the Son of God as if by right of debt, when he began to be acknowledged by that name openly and everywhere among men.

Fourthly, that he not only weakens the passage of Ps. 2, 7 with a new version regarding emphasis, but also overturns its meaning through a perverse explanation. For the Greek κατὰ πόδας, as is done by others, undoubtedly has greater emphasis when rendered: You are my Son, today I have begotten you, than that Grotian one: O my Son, today I have begotten you. There the generation of the Father is given as the cause of the υἱότητος, here a bare address of the Son is held, and something is stated about him without such an αἰτιολογία. Regarding the meaning of the words of the Psalmist, Grotius is mistaken when he says that this Psalm was fulfilled in some way in David, which it has been shown in its place concerns none but CHRIST: He is mistaken when he invents a double meaning of the Psalm, when there is only a single meaning for one statement: He is mistaken when he says that it pertains to CHRIST only in a mystical or secret and more sublime sense, as he calls it, if indeed it treats of Christ in the literal sense, and this is even acknowledged by certain Hebrews, as was said in the cited passage.

PART II. OF CHAPTER I. Demonstration of the divine eminence of Christ. MEMBER I. Demonstration of the divine nature of Christ.

vers. 2. Psalm. 103. vers. 19. Esa. 63. vers. 15. Joel. 3. vers. 17. Conf. 1. Reg. 8. vers. 49. cap. 22. vers. 19. Esa. 6. vers. 1. tum è sedis Divinæ designatione, quod in throno DEI, & in medio throni sedeat Apocal. 3. vers. 21. cap. 5. vers. 6. ad dextram thro- ni majestatis Dei, Ebr. 8. vers. 1. in throno glo- riæ, Matth. 19. vers. 28. cap. 25. vers. 31. . Qualis enim thronus, talis sessio. At thronus ille est summæ, infinitæ, & omnipræsentissimæ maje- statis, thronus DEI, Ebr. 12. vers. 2. thronus Pa- tris, Apocal. 3. vers. 21. thronus æternus, Ebr. 1. v. 8. tum ex attributis & effectis hujus exaltationis ad dextram DEI, quod sapienter & in justitia re- gnet, Esa. 32. vers. 1. Jerem. 23. vers. 6. Ecclesiæ suæ gratiosæ & potenter præsit, eamque prote- gat ac defendat, Ephes. 1. vers. 22. cap. 5. vers. 23. Psalm. 45. vers. 5. Psalm. 72. vers. 4. quod popu- lum suum pascat, Ezech. 34. vers. 23. Apoc. 7. v. 16. eique pastores & Doctores det, Ephes. 4. vers. 11. quod pœnitentiam & remissionem peccatorum donet, Actor. 5. vers. 11. quod à mari ad mare dominetur, Psalm. 72. vers. 8. dominetur in me- dio inimicorum, Psalm. 110. vers. 2. 5. 6. inimi- cos suos destruat & conterat, Psalm. 2. vers. 9. Psalm. 45. vers. 9. omnia pedibus suis subjiciat, 1. Corinth. 15. vers. 27. quod orbem judicet, Esa. 11. vers. 3. 4. Actor. 17. vers. 3. Roman. 14. vers. 11. Philipp. 2. vers. 11. occulta hominum in apricum producat, 1. Corinth. 4. vers. 5. unicuique secun- dum opera sua reddat, Apocal. 22. vers. 12. Rom. 2. vers. 6. quod denique & salvat & condemnet Matth. 25. &c. Quæ omnia talia sunt, ut ex iisdem Deitatem CHRISTI supremam contra Socinianos Calviniani pariter & Pontificii pro- bent. Unde non finitam, sed infinitam & vere immensam ac Divinam virtutem ea inferre ne- cessum est: tum è nominibus, quæ CHRI- STUS inde obtinet, quod sit Dominus super populum suum, Mich. 5. vers. 2. caput Eccle- siæ, Ephes. 1. vers. 22. cap. 5. vers. 23. Dominus vivorum & mortuorum, Roman. 14. vers. 9. An- gelorum & Principatuum, Ephes. 1. vers. 21. Do- minus super omnia opera manuum Dei, Psalm. 8. vers. 7. Dominus Dominantium, Apocal. 19, 16. Dominus gloriæ, 1. Corinth. 2. vers. 8. Ut autem Dominus unus tantum est CHRISTUS, & unum caput, Deus & homo: Ita etiam unum tantum oportet esse Dominum CHRISTI Dei & homi- nis. Quod certe infinitum esse oportet, quem- admodum utique ex illis dictis etiam suprema Christi Deitas ab ipsis Calvinianis ostenditur ad- versus Socinianos: tum denique è gloria & honore CHRISTO competente ob hanc sessionem ad de- xtram Majestatis. Honor enim ille non est ho- nore Dei inferior; nec geminus est Divinus & re- ligiosus honor, alius summus alius intermedius vel subordinatus: Sed unus tantum est honor Divinus, una tantum religiosa adoratio, Conf. Dan. 7. vers. 14. Roman. 14. vers. 11. Philipp. 2, 14. Apocal. 5, 12.

Superest IV. ut προσδιορισμὸν illum ἐν ὑψη- λοῖς explicemus. Ex dictis autem constat, quod accipi non debeat τοπικῶς vel ratione loci; sed τροπικῶς vel ratione modi; quia nec dextra Dei, nec sessio ad dextram Dei localis est, aut in cer- to loco, sed dextra est immensa, & sessio est gu- bernatio Divina ad omnia sese extendens. Nul- lo ergo loco concludi potest. Sunt hæc ὑψηλὰ ea, quæ Luc. 2, 14. ὕψισα dicta, propter quæ DEUS ipse dicitur ὕψιστος Luc. 1, 35. unde nos visitavit ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψυς Luc. 1. vers. 78. quæ de- cantata sunt per Hosanna, Matth. XXI. vers. 9. Marc. XI. vers. 10. Luc. XIX. vers. 38. unde vir- tute induti sunt Apostoli SS. Luc. XXIV. vers. 49. Quæ sunt ὑπὲρ ἄνω πάντων, Johan. III. vers. 31. Ephes. I. vers. 21. Dicuntur ὕψηλα non quia sunt intra aliquam sive dimensionem sive finitionem, sed quia sunt supra omnem, Job. IX. vers. 7. 8. Ideoque μεγαλωσύνη ἐν ὑψίλοις vel ὑψίστοις est μεγαλωσύνη ὑψισὴ summa & interminabilis Ma- jestas: Et CHRISTUS in excelsis vel in cælis sedere dicitur ratione gloriæ & Majestatis excel- sæ, & cælestis. Altitudinem enim illam & de- xtram DEI Spiritus sanctus non loci sublimita- te, sed gloriæ & Majestatis cælestis inenarra- bili celsitudine definit, ut Athanasius, Cyrillus, Augustinus, Philippus, imo etiam Calvinus in- terpretantur; quemadmodum & thronus in cælis & excelsis est, Ebr. VIII. vers. 1. qui tamen thronus non materialis est aut localis aut finitus, quia æternus est, Psalm. XLV. vers. 7. & ipsius DEI thronus, Apocal. III. vers. 21. Ebr. XII. v. 1. Num autem DEO thronum localem aut finitum tribuemus? Num DEUM Patrem, quem profitemur in cælis esse, Matth. VI. vers. 9. ideo in loco esse credemus? Constantinus Presby- ter Antioch. ex sententia Chrysostomi: Quid est in excelsis? Deumne loco concludit? Ab- sit. Sed sicut dicens ad dextram, eum non figu- ravit, sed ostendit, eum in eodem esse honore, quo Pater: Ita eum dicens in excelsis, non eum illic inclusit, sed ostendit id, quod est o- mnium altissimum, & quod omnia transcen- dit: Hoc est, pervenit ad ipsum thronum pa- ternum. Quomodo ergo Pater est in excelsis, ita etiam ipse. Concessus enim nihil aliud significat, quam in eodem esse honore. Et Theophylactus: Non sedere hunc dicit, perinde ac si DEUS loco circumscribatur aliquo, sed ut Filium Pa- tri honore parem ostendat & gloria. Ad pater- num enim thronum pervenit, & ut Pater sedet sublimis, sic & Filius excelsa conscendit. Un- de, Cornelio à Lapide observante, nonnulli hoc nomine exprimunt μεγαλωσύνην magnitudinem nempe, magnificentiam, majestatem Divinam, & Paternam hic designari, ac subintelligunt in Græco articulum τῆς quasi dicat, μεγαλω- σύνης τῆς ἐν ὑψηλοῖς, vertendo majestatis ex- celsissimæ, quæ non est alia, ipso dicente, quam DEI Patris. Quapropter nugatur cum Cal- vinianis Grotius, cum CHRISTUM in cælo supremo esse, quemadmodum David in exi- mio quodam loco in terris constitutus fuit, asse- rit. Id de Davide Psalm. LXXXIX. vers. 28. non dicitur. Nec ibi vel subjectum David est, sed CHRISTUS, vel prædicatum de loco intelligitur, sed de eminentiæ statu. CHRI- STUS vero ita in cælo est, ut super omnes cælos sit, & omnia impleat in cælo & in terra, Ephes. IV. 10. Matth. XXVIII. 18.

Quæ è comparatione Apostolica ulterius e- lucescunt. Hactenus enim absolute exaltatio- nem CHRISTI descripsit Apostolus per con- sessum in dextra Majestatis in excelsis. Jam vero comparate etiam eandem describit vers. 4. quod tanto eminentior Angelis factus sit, quan- to excellentius nomen præ ipsis hæreditavit. Ubi hæc quinque occurrunt expendenda: 1. Se- cundum quam naturam eminentior factus sit? 2. Cur cum Angelis hic comparetur? 3. Quodnam sit illud nomen διαφορώτερον? 4.

Quando id consequutus sit? & 5. quomodo sublimior Angelis factus sit, & excellentius nomen præ illis hæreditavit?

De priori res expedita est è superioribus. Nam secundum quam naturam sedet ad dextram Majestatis, secundùm eandem etiam sublimior factus, & nomen excellentius consequutus est. Quod tum συνέχεια hic docet, tum ἀναλογία loci paralleli, Philipp. II. vers. 19. διὸ καὶ ἀυτὸν ὁ Θεὸς ὑπερύψωσε, καὶ ἐχαρίσατο ἀυτῷ ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα; nec non loci Eph. 1. vers. 21. 22. ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ ἀυτõ ἐν τοῖς ἐπȣρανίοις ὑπεράνω πάσης ἀρχῆς, καὶ παντὸς ὀνόματG: tum denique res ipsa; quia sessio illa importat dominium, à dominio autem denominatur Dominus; ideoque cum ad dominium summum evectus est, constitutus est Dominus omnium, Actor. II. vers. 34. cap. X. vers. 36. ob quam causam David CHRISTUM sedentem ad dextram Domini profitetur Dominum suum, qui perinde omnium fidelium Dominus est, ac præterea dominari eundem dicit in medio inimicorum suorum, Psalm. CX. vers. 1. 2. Jam secundum humanam naturam ad dextram Majestatis CHRISTUM sedere anteà ostensum: Ideoque etiam sublimior factus, & nomen excellentius consequutus est secundum humanam naturam. Licet Deitatis & Humanitatis, inquit Leo Magnus Epist. 38. in CHRISTO una prorsus eademque persona, exaltationem tamen, & nomen super omne nomen ad eam intelligimus pertinere formam, quæ ditanda erat tantæ glorificationis augmento. De verbo γενόμενG ita habet hoc loco B. Dorscheus. Γίνομαι pro sum vel existo, partim etiam pro fio poni, manifestum est. De priori vide Johan. I. vers. 6. Luc. XXIV. vers. 19. De posteriori Matth. XI. vers. 20. & 21. & 23. & 26. cap. XVII. vers. 2. cap. XXI. vers. 42. cap. XXVI. vers. 24. Johan. I. 3. cap. X. vers. 12. Si primo modo capias, quod CHRISTUS dicitur γενόμενG, sensus hic est: tanto sublimior existens Angelis, quanto &c. Si secundo sensu, hæc erit sententia Apostolica: tanto sublimior factus Angelis, utraque textui & analogiæ fidei consentanea. Erat absolute loquendo Filius DEI semper sublimior & melior omnibus Angelis, quia semper extitit apud DEUM Patrem etiam ἐν ἀρχῇ, qua facta sunt omnia, & ipsi etiam Angeli producti, Johan. I. v. 3. tanquam ille, per quem αἰῶνες Angelici etiam facti sunt, Ebr. I. 2. Qui est splendor gloriæ & character ὑποστάσεως non Angelicæ vel finitæ, sed divinæ & infinitæ, qui portat omnia, adeoquo ipsos etiam Angelos. Factus est etiam melior Angelis tum per ἕνωσιν, sive ἐπίληψιν σαρκὸς καὶ αἵματG & seminis Abrahæ, infra cap. II. vers. 14. & 16. per καταρτισμὸν σώματG ἐμψύχȣ, infra cap. X. Confer. Philipp. II. vers. 6. 1. Timoth. III. vers. 16. tum per ὑπερύψωσιν & sessionem ad dextram, cujus respectu Actor. II. vers. 36. dicitur Dominus & CHRISTUS factus ratione plenariæ usurpationis Majestatis acceptæ. Sed hic posterior sensus, sine dubio præsenti loco convenientior est, quem Vulgatus, B. Lutherus, aliique Interpretes etiam amplectuntur, quia non quis fuerit Filius DEI in initio Creationis, sed qualis factus sit post purificationem peccatorum, & per confessum ad dextram Dei his verbis docetur.

Quod ad alterum comparatio cum Angelis instituitur :

1. Ut quantopere nostra natura, hoc est, humana in CHRISTO exaltata sit, doceatur, & Ebræis naturæ, quam ex ipsorum prosapia affumpsit Filius Dei, dignitas hac συγκρίσει ob oculos ponatur. Sine dubio enim creaturæ omnium nobilissimæ sunt Angeli, abjectissimæ vero post apostasiam sunt Diaboli. Quum ergo nostra natura per seductionem Diabolicam non modo longissime infra Angelos abjecta, sed etiam in regnum tenebrarum & societatem Diabolorum dejecta fuerit : Eandem in CHRISTO tantopere honoratam esse, ut longis post se intervallis relinquat Angelos, longe sublimior illis facta, longe eminentius nomen consequuta sit; id vero summo honori, solatio, atque gaudio cedit humano generi. Abjectus fuit CHRISTUS secundum humanam naturam infra Angelos in statu exinanitionis. Jam ergo quantopere exaltatus sit supra Angelos docetur, cum consedit ad dextram majestatis.

2. Quia non Angelorum, sed nostri causa Filius Dei apparuit, non Angelos, sed semen Abrahæ, hoc est, naturam humanam ex semine Abrahæ assumpsit, ut nostrorum peccatorum expiationem per semetipsum faceret : Quam gratiam explicare constituerat Apostolus. Ideo hic dignitatem, quæ Humanæ naturæ in CHRISTO, secundum quam ὁμοούσιοι nobis est, collata est, præ Angelis & supra Angelos deprædicat.

Quod ad tertium: Nomen illud διαφορώτερον recte explicari de nomine excellentiori admittimus, neque per τὸ ὄνομα nudum nomen intelligendum esse agnoscimus, unde frustra nomen aliquod, sive proprium, sive appellativum quæritur, quod hic designetur, quum nomen pro re ipsa sumatur, uti Ebræis vocari est esse. Quod ergo nonnulli putant nomen Jehovah, alii nomen Filii Dei cum Cornelio à Lapide intelligi, haud satis convenit.

Adde quod CHRISTUS nomen hoc secundum humanam naturam hæreditavit, quod consequutus id sit post exinanitionem & expiationem peccatorum nostrorum, quod id acceperit, quando exaltatus est, quando consedit ad dextram DEI, quando sublimior factus est Angelis. At nomen Jehovah, & nomen Filii DEI non hæreditavit CHRISTUS secundum Humanam naturam : Id namque non ratione humanæ, sed Divinæ naturæ ei convenit : nec enim humana natura CHRISTI vel CHRISTUS secundum humanam naturam in casu recto dici potest Jehovah, aut Filius DEI: neque homo CHRISTUS Jehovah, aut Filius DEI factus est post exinanitionem, sed per unionem personalem, & in ipsa conceptione, ac nativitate, sanctum, quod ex Maria natum est, Filius DEI vocatum fuit, Luc. I. 35. & germen Davidis Jehovah, Jerem. XXIII. vers. 6.

Non factus est Jehovah & Filius Dei post purificationem peccatorum nostrorum, quia ideo Filius hominis, Filius Dei, & Jehovah ipse esse debuit, ut expiaret peccata nostra, Esa. XLIII. 24. 25.

Non consequutus est homo CHRISTUS id nominis, & dignitatis, ut vocaretur in concreto Jehovah, & Filius Dei demum, quando exal- tatus est, sed à primo statim incarnationis mo- mento, quando Verbum caro factum est, Johan. I. 14.

Nec vero dici potest, quod tum in exaltatio- ne nomen illud perfectiori modo consequutus sit.

Non enim nomen Jehovah magis & minus ad- mittit; nec Filius Dei modo perfectiori evasit, quod Socinianum commentum alias profligatum est, imprimis in Anti-Crellio nostro.

Si dicas Apostolum ipsum explicare hoc no- men διαφορώτερον de nomine Filii Dei, cum sub- jicit: Cui enim unquam Angelorum dixit: Filius meus es tu? vers. 5.
