Mich. 5. vers. 2. ὁμόθρονος, quia Rex in monte Zion possidens gentes & omnes fines terræ; ἰσοδύνα- μος & æque ut Pater ἀυτεξόσιος in confunden- dis legibus, vinculisque constringendis, perden- dis, excindendis quibusvis hostibus; ἰσότιμος, quia adversus ipsum, æque, ut Patrem, rebellione peccatur, in ipsum fiducia collocanda, ipse osculo fidei religioso amplectendus, ira ejus metuenda, ab ipso beatitudo speranda, ut è totius Psalmi conte- xtu liquet. Adde quod hic actus generationis Fi- lii Dei antecedat decretum divinum de Christo ungendo, & in regnum gratiæ, imo in orbis terra- rum hæreditatem introducendo, eique ceu funda- mentum substernatur, Psalm. 2, 7. 8. Id vero de- cretum æternum est. Unde oportet Filium Dei æternum, & Patri vere coæternum esse.

Septimo, confundit Grotius υἱότητα καὶ γέννησιν Christi cum ejusdem exaltatione, quæ in προθέσει Apostolica distinctissima. Secundum illam dici- tur Filius Dei splendor gloriæ Patris, & character substantiæ ejus, secundum hanc dicitur hæres omni- um, evectus ad dextram Majestatis, melior factus Angelis, & sublimiori nomine ditatus. Et annon tautologia hæc esset: Ego hodie genui te, id est, col- locavi te ad dextram meam, & omnia tibi subjeci. E. postula, & dabo tibi hæreditatem omnium, hoc est, omnia tibi subjiciam, & te collocabo ad dextram meam? Fuit sane in hoc decreto compellatus Fi- lius Dei, qui est genitus ab æterno, sed non qua est genitus ab æterno; & æterna ejus generatio al- legatur tanquam fundamentum, ex quo jure pete- re possit in ordine voluntariæ exinanitionis & œ- conomiæ ineffabilis, quod ante titulo occupat, & possidet, unde & cum actu Christus peteret, filia- tionem suam ablegat Joh. 17, 5.

Octavo, Actor. 13, 33. non explicatur locus Psal- mide excitatione CHRISTI à mortuis, sed doce- tur, Deum excitasse Filium suum Messiam è Patri- bus, quo de vaticinatus est David Psal. II.

Nono, particulam היום de temporibus infi- gnis lætitiæ adhiberi, è Jerem. 1, 10. 18. non constat. Ibi enim tempus præsens simpliciter notat diem vo- cationis Jeremiæ; sed hic ubi de Filio Dei è sub- stantia Patris genito ejusdem cum Patre essentiæ, potestatis, & gloriæ sermo est, non potest hodie temporale intelligi, quia de generatione agitur, quæ actus internus est & proinde æternus in Patre.

Aliter ergo היום intelligitur, cum de actu hominis, aliter cum de actu Divino, eoq; interno, ser- mo est. Hodie temporale ad Angelos, & alias crea- turas pertinet: in quo innumeri filii Dei constitu- ti sunt: Hoc vero HODIE supra Angelos & crea- turas est, & antevertit id omne tempus, in quo adver- sus Deum & Messiam tumultuari hostes poterant. Dum enim per orbem terrarum idololatria se con- taminat genus humanum, jam in Divino hodie de firmando regno Dei, & constituendo ejus capite decretum est, hoc est, ab æterno, & jam ante, ordine naturæ, generatio Filii Dei in illo היום facta est, quam præsupponit istud decretum, ut paulo ante observavimus.

Missa itaque Grotiana glossa textus συνέχεια docenda. Proposuerat autem, quod ad perso- nam CHRISTI, de duobus agere Aposto- lus:

Primo de Divina natura; Deinde de Huma- na natura præstantia vel eminentia. Illius ratio- ne tribuit ei primo nomen Filii DEI, per quem loquutus est DEUS Pater novissimis diebus ceu Doctorem Novi Testamenti, eundemque dixit ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης, καὶ χαρακτῆρα τῆς ὑπο- στάσεως αὐτοῦ. Dixit etiam eundem conditorem se- culorum, & conservatorem rerum omnium, adeo- que verum DEUM. Ea ergo ut penes Ebræ- os demonstret, testimoniis Veteris Testamenti utitur, disputans è concesso principio: quia illa iisdem erant authentica. Et Filium DEI esse Messiam, Doctorem, vel Prophetam Novi Testa- menti è Psalm. 2, 7. probat, quo de legibus à Deo & Messia nostro propositis, quarum vincula Re- ges & populi ac gentes perfringere nequicquam satagunt, temere adversus ipsum tumultuantes, facile, nisi se ipsi submittant, confundendi, atque exscindendi.

De doctrina etiam salutifera fide suspicienda à Regibus & Judicibus terræ, omnibusque, qui non perire ira ejus in via velint, sed fiducia in ipso servari, vaticinatus est Hieropsaltes. Eum ergo esse Filium DEI è Patris essentia ab æterno geni- tum docet Apostolus adducto hoc Psalmi testi- monio, Filium non per creationem, nec propter potestatis concessionem, ut Angeli: Sed multo eminentiori ratione, quæ conditionem & sor- tem omnium Angelorum longissime excedit. Cui enim Angelorum unquam dixit: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te? Quum vero supra An- gelos nihil eminentius sit præter DEUM, quan- tum ad naturam vel essentiam, Filium DEI Di- vinæ naturæ esse oportet, adeoque quum non nisi unus sit natura DEUS ejusdem naturæ & essentiæ cum Deo Patre: Vides, inquit Chrysosto- mus, quod nomen Filii significet τὴν γνησιότητα pro- prietatem & germanitatem. Et certe si non est pro- prius & germanus Filius, proprium autem & ger- manum nihil est aliud, quam ex ipso, quomodo ex ipso confirmat? Nam si est gratia Filius, non solum non est Angelis præstantior, sed etiam minor. Quo- modo? Quoniam homines quoque justi vocati sunt filii, & nomen filius, nisi sit filius proprius & germa- nus, non potest ostendere excellentiam. Et significans quod est quædam differentia creaturarum & opificis, vide, quid dicat: Cui enim dixit aliquando: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te.

Similiter Theophylactus: Nam cum Filium di- cimus, illud sane prætendimus, quod ex Patre sit ge- nitus. Quare si per gratiam esset Filii nomen ad- eptus, Angelis esset hic plane inferior. Illud vero, ego te hodie genui, nihil aliud exprimit, nisi quod à principio, & ex quo Pater est, Filium genuisse. Nam quemadmodum ego sum, inquit tempore præsenti id protulit, sic hodie dixit, quod Deo præcipue congruit, ut se sempiternum ostendat. Tempora siquidem etsi multiplicia sint, sunt tamen DEO præsentia. Sensum ergo non male reddidit Estius: Quis Angelorum tam excellentis est natura aut dignita- tis, cui dictum aliquando legatur à DEO: Tu es Filius meus? nimirum singulariter, ac peculiari- ter: Quomodo hoc à Patre dici solet Filio, quem de se genuit, maxime si sit unigenitus. Etenim si dives aliquis plures sibi adoptasset filios, sed uni- cum haberet filium naturalem, huic uni & soli di- ceret: Filius meus es tu, præsertim si & illud adderet, quia ego te genui. Quæ rectius se ha- bent, quam cum Genebrardus de temporali CHRISTI generatione exponit, aut alii de refur- rectione ex mortuis cum Socinianis, quod in Anti- Crellio profligavimus, utpote Sasboldus, Janse- nius aliique ex neotericis, notante nec omnino ab- nuente Estio; utut illi ad Athanasium, Theodore- tum, Euthymium, & Fulgentium; hi vero ad O- rigenem, Hilarium, & Chrysostomum provocent. Qui tamen omnes illa Filius meus es tu, de Filio Dei proprio & naturali intelligunt, etsi de poste- rioribus verbis varient. Sed citra causam: Quum iisdem reddatur τῆς χότης ratio, nec alio sensu hic ab Apostolo ea adducantur, utpote qui non occupatur in probanda vel temporali CHRISTI generatione, vel resurrectione ex mortuis, aut collo- catione ad dextram Dei, sed id demonstrare vult, quod CHRISTUS sit æternus DEI Filius ante sæcula genitus, utpote per quem Pater sæcula con- didit.

Similiter Augustinus, quem sequuntur alii, de æterna Filii Dei ex substantia Patris generatione, interpretatur; Siquidem æternitas apertissime ex- primatur per verbum hodie, quo præsens dies si- gnificatur, quia æternitas est unus dies, idemque semper præsens, ut non diffitetur Estius, & contra Socinianos probat Cornelius à Lapide: Melius & aptius, inquit, S. Augustinus in Psalm. II. & Chryso- stomus, Theophylactus, Anshelmus, D. Thomas, hic hunc locum accipiunt de æterna & Divina ge- neratione Filii DEI.

Unde HODIE significat præsentem durationem, quæ semper præsens est, indivisibilis & immobilis, amplectiturque omne tempus præteritum, præsens, & futurum, qualis est æternitas.

HODIE ergo, id est, in & ab æternitate, in qua unum est hodie, unum instans, unum nunc, unum stabile & perenne præsens.

Sequitur ergo, Psalm. II. ad literam non loqui de Davide in se, ut volunt Rabbini, nec etiam de Davide quatenus fuit typus CHRISTI, ut vult Jansenius, sed proprie, per se, & primo de Christo dictatum & scriptum esse: Soli enim CHRISTO convenit τὸ Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te. Et: Postula à me, & dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam & possessionem tuam terminos terræ, aliaque plura, quæ in Psalmo dicuntur.

Καὶ πάλιν) Id est alio loco. Sic πάλιν habes Matth. 4, 7. Rom. 15, 10. 11. 12. 1. Cor. 3, 20. Sic & infra II, 13. X, 30. Ita rursum posuit Virgilius III. Æneidos. Rur- sum in secessu &c. Est autem is locus 2. Sam. 7, 14.

Alterum hoc est testimonium de CHRISTO Dei Filio, quod nunc non de eodem solum, prout intra simplicissimum Divinæ essentiæ com- plexum ab æterno genitus est, agit: Sed simul prædicit ejusdem excitationem è corpore Davidis, quum de Filio DEI in carne exhibito disserere proposuerit, & JESUM esse illum Dei Filium ab æterno à Patre genitum demonstrare.

Ex hac ergo combinatione locorum, Davidis nempe, de æterna generatione Filii DEI, & pro- missionis Davidi datæ, quod quum ipse dormie- rit cum Patribus, Deus post ipsum semen, hoc est, Filium excitaturus sit e lumbis ejus, qui ipse Filius Dei futurus sit; patet, JESUM Davidis Filium, qui ex semine ejus est secundum carnem, Roman. 1. vers. 3. esse Filium illum DEI, de quo Pater dixit: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te, hoc est, unam esse personam Filium Davidis & Fi- lium DEI, adeoque æternum Filium Dei nasci debuisse in tempore è Davide, secundum carnem juxta promissionem Davidi factam, qui domum nomini Domini ædificaturus esset, cui thronum regni in æternum confirmare velit DEUS: quod de Filio Mariæ è prosapia Davidis, qui idem Filius DEI Altissimi, interpretatus est Gabriel, Luc. I. vers. 32. seqq.

Patet secundo locum illum 2. Samuel. 7. non agere de ullo alio, quam de CHRISTO, quia si de alio ageret, se non recte haberet demon- stratio, ab Apostolo inde petita.

Patet tertio, agere eundem non de Filio quo- dam DEI secundum gratiam, vel per adoptionem, sed de Filio DEI naturali, vel per æternam gene- rationem. Si autem de Salomone ageret, non posset intelligi naturalis Filius, aut adhiberi ad demonstrandam πρόθεσιν Apostolicam, de Chri- sti Doctoris & Sacerdotis nostri persona Divina, quod nempe sit æternus DEI Filius, per quem secula condita, splendor gloriæ & character hy- postaseos Patris, omnia portans verbo virtutis suæ. Quam non potest Psalmi locus de alio in- telligi, quam de naturali DEI Filio, ab æterno à Patre genito: tam non potest de alio Filio DEI, aut alio respectu paternitatis accipi locus ille, qui præ manibus est, vi demonstrationis A- postolicæ ex utroque loco petitæ, & conclusio- nis, quam infert Apostolus, utpote quæ secun- dum propositionem Apostolicam demonstranda erat.

Patet quarto, in confesso fuisse tum apud Ebræos, tam in vaticinio præsenti, quam in Psalm. II. de CHRISTO secundum literalem sensum agi; alioquin inde Apostolus demon- strationem instituere non potuisset penes Ebræ- os, qui assumit hoc tanquam ὁμολογύμενον, quod ista de CHRISTO dicta sint.

Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ εἰς Πατέρα, καὶ αὐτὸς ἔται μοι εἰς ὑὸν) Id est, ego ero ei vice Patris, & ipse mihi vice Filii. Utar eo, quomodo Patres filio utuntur, & eum prote- gam, quomodo patres filios solent. Et hæc verba de Græco desumpta Salomon, de quo dicto loco agitur, in sensu vulgari typus CHRISTI, non in omnibus (ostendunt id sequentia, quæ CHRISTO applicari nequeunt) sed eo quod sapientia præstitit, regnavit in pace, gentibus multis imperans, templum DEO stru- xit. Et hunc in modum ad Messiam aptat hæc verba Isaac Benarama.

Depravat Grotius sensum vaticinii non uno modo, quod DEUS dixit: Ero ei in Patrem vel Pater, & ipse erit mihi in Filium, hoc est, Filius, ex Ebraismo notissimo, id Grotius per- vertit, quod tantum vice Patris & vice Filii sit; ac porro hunc sensum reddit prorsus je- junum & alienum: Utar eo quomodo Patres filio utuntur, & eum protegam, quomodo Patres filios solent.

Quod 1. est contra apertam literam. Aliud est esse Patrem, aliud vice Patris; aliud est esse Filium, aliud vice Filii. Aliud uti aliquo ceu Pa- tres filio utuntur, aliud prorsus, esse filium, quem- admodum aliud omnino est, protegere aliquem instar Patris, & aliud esse Patrem alicujus.

2. Contra apertam vaticinii mentem. Longe enim magnificentiora sunt, quæ ibi DEUS præ- dicit de semine vel filio Davidis; Cui DEUS non protectionem tantum promittit, sed quem Filium sibi ὁμούσιον καὶ ὁμόθρονον fore prædi- cit; quia thronum & regnum æternum non ha- bet, nisi æternus & verus natura DEUS. 3. Contra apertam Apostoli assertionem; qui hoc prædicatum eminentius esse docet, quam ut ulli Angelorum conveniat. Num vero hoc Angelis non convenit, quod iis Deus utatur ceu filiis, eos protegat, imo sustentet, ceu filios.

4. Contra intentionem Apostolicam, quia pro- bare hic non protectionem, non usum Christi vice filii, sed Divinam uiornta Christi, quod verus & naturalis Dei Filius sit, intendit, per quem secula condidit, qui omnia sustentat, qui expiationem peccatorum nostrorum fecit.

5. Contra loci paralleli Psal. 2, 7. sententiam, quo agitur de Filio Dei ex essentia Patris genito & con- substantiali.

6. Contra συνέχειαν Apostolicam. Nam talis filius, quo Deus Pater tantum utitur ceu filio, quem- que tantum protegit, ut Patres solent filios, nec secu- lorum conditor, nec hæres & herus omnium, nec re- rum omnium conservator, nec expiator peccatorum nostrorum esse potest: nec sedere in dextra Maje- statis, nedum Filius Dei απαύγασμα της δόξης η χαρακτηρ της υποστάσεως αυτ8 esse potest.

7. Contra persona Filii Dei veritatem. Non enim Christus est tantum vice-Filius, sed vere est Filius Dei, Filius proprius, Rom. 8,32. Filius Unige- nitus, Joh. 3, 16. Filius μονογενὴς παρὰ τῶ Πατρός, Johan. 1, 18. Primogenitus, ut sequenti testimonio docebit Apostolus: Πρωτότοκος πάσης κτίσεως, Primogenitus ante omnem creaturam, Coloss. 1. v. 15. Rursus Deus Pater Christo non est tantum vice Patris, sed verus & proprius ejus Pater est, Johan. 5,19. qui genuit Filium in æterno illo hodie, Pf. 2,7. ceu imaginem sibi ομοόσιον ejusdem essentiæ & gloriæ, quod negare velle est Apostolo contradice- re, & ad castra Arianorum transire. Non usus tantum est Christo pro Filio, non protegit eum tantum, ceu Filium, sed per eum secula condidit, eumque hæredem omnium constituit, & ad dextram Majestatis suæ considere fecit, regnum æternum ei dedit.

8. Contra officium Christi, cujus hic fundamen- tum designat Apostolus: Non enim vel Doctoralis officii fundamentum est, quod Christus sit vicefilius quidam, sed quod sit Filius ille soligenitus à Patre, qui est in sinu Patris, & Deum, quem nemo unquam vidit enarravit nobis, Joh. 1, 18. non ψιλός ἄνθρω- -πος, ut Prophetæ erant in Veteri Testamento; vel offici Sacerdotalis, quod utatur eo Deus pro Filio, sed ejus rei, quod expiationem peccatorum no- strorum Christus fecerit per semetipsum, funda- mentum hoc posuit Apostolus, quod Christus non sit merus homo, ut Sacerdotes, qui in Veteri Te- stamento expiarunt peccata, sed æternus & consub- stantialis Dei Filius.

9. Contra statum exaltationis Christi. Non e- nim vicefilium ad dextram Majestatis in excelsis collocare, non vicefilio nomen, quod est supra o- mne nomen dare poterat. Dignitas illa tanta est, quæ in nullum, etsi eminentissimum, Ange- lum cadit; nec nisi soli Filio Dei Unigenito & na- turali convenit, quum inferat Divinæ Majestatis in propria persona possessæ plenariam usurpatio- nem, ac gloriam vere Divinam atque immensam, quæ nulli vice filio convenit, aut convenire pot- est, Esa. 42, 8.

Secundo fallitur Grotius, cum 2. Sam.7. de Salo- mone agi in sensu literali, quem vulgarem vocat, ty- po Christi, non in omnibus, sed eo, quod sapientia præstitit, regnavit in pace, gentibus multis imperavit, templum Deo struxit. Sequutus est ea parte Isaac

Benarama Judæum, quum sequi debuisset Spiritum sanctum, juxta cujus mentem vaticinium Davidi factum non de Salomone agit, sed de Christo: Non sensum geminum habet, sed, ut omnia scripturæ loca, unicum tantum: quia Spiritus sanctus non Apollinis more loquutus ambigue sensum diver- sum iisdem verbis occultavit, sed aperte in verbo suo loquitur, & unius oraculi non nisi unicum sen- sum esse voluit, quem nobis, ne in ambiguo versa- remur, luculentis verbis, ne ab intentione & men- te ejus aberremus, prodidit. Neque hic quic- quam occurrit, quod Christo non conveniat, sed soli Salomoni, aut quod Salomoni ut typo con- veniat; non de sapientia Salomonis, non de re- gno ejus pacifico, non de imperio in plures populos hic verbo egit, nedum in eo Salomonem typum Christi, hoc quidem oraculo, constituit: Nec de structura materialis templi Salomonei, sed structu- ra spiritualis templi nomini Domini erigendi à filio post Davidis fata excitando, vaticinium loqui- tur. Quæ omnia circa locum 2. Sam. 7. satis de- monstrata sunt.

Guilielmus Estius, & Cornelius à Lapide hic di- versas afferunt explicationes oraculi: Primum quod eodem agatur secundum literam & de Chri- sto & de Salomone, quam sententiam Cornelius à Lapide notat esse Lyrani, Burgensis, & Abulensis. Sed unius dicti plures esse sensus eosque literales, non magis admittendum est, quam unius rei plu- res esse formas essentiales. Et fatetur hic Estius, nullam esse scripturam, in quam plures simul histo- rici seu literales sensus concurrant. Nec dici potest, quædam de Salomone, quædam de Christo hic di- ci. Nam subjectum non diversum est, sed uni- cum tantum in illo vaticinio: Ideo quæ hic oc- currunt prædicata, de uno illo subjecto efferun- tur omnia. Si dicas, alterum subjectum exprimi, alterum subintelligi, adhuc statuendus erit ejus- dem dicti aut vocis, etiam semel tantum positæ geminus literalis sensus, nimirum alter è verbo i- pso redundans, alter vero tacitus, vel subintelle- ctus, quod est absurdum.

Secundo quod secundum literam agatur de Sa- lomone, secundum mysticum sensum de Christo: quam Eucherii, Thomæ, Angelomi, Cajetani, & Ri- beræ sententiam suam faciunt Estius & Cornelius. Sed ea probanda minime est.

Nam 1. fingitur ita adhuc dicti ejusdem geminus sensus, unus literalis, alter mysticus, quod repu- gnat simplicitati ac perspicuitati scripturæ.

2. Geminum introducitur subjectum, quum non nisi de unico subjecto, de semine Davidis agatur, post fata ejus excitando, quod est Christus, Jer. 23, 6. Unde ergo alterum subjectum invehetur textui, cujus nulla in eodem facta mentio? Sub typo in- telligi antitypum dicitur, non probatur. Typus quoad factum potest repræsentare antitypum, Salo- mo Christum: Sed de typo aliquid dici, & simul de antitypo intelligendum esse, nullo exemplo doce- bitur, nec id Spiritus sancti orationi convenit, ne- dum de Christo alicubi agi, subintelligi vero ex mente Spiritus sancti simul Salomonem.

3. Apostoli argumentum enervatur, quum non nisi è sensu literali firma argumenta & documen- ta ac demonstrationes petuntur.

4. Sensus oraculi evertitur, quòd de CHRI- STO unice agere suo loco docuimus.

5. Fatetur Cornelius à Lapide, de CHRISTO propriissime dici: Ero ipsi in Patrem, & ipse erit mihi in Filium. Fatetur CHRISTI regnum, id est, Ecclesiam, absolute esse æternam, ut hic dici- tur. Quedam, inquit, sunt, quæ magis compe- tant CHRISTO, quam Salomoni, ut quod hic dicitur: Ego ero illi in Patrem, & misericordiam meam non auferam ab eo, & fidelis erit domus tua, id est, stabilis erit familia & progenies tua Regalis, & stabiliam thronum regni ejus usque in sempitèr- num. Quæ verba licet quodammodo tenuiter & quasi per hyperbolen conveniant Salomoni, eo quod DEUS eum regno non dejecerit, sicut dejecit Sau- lem, sed regnum ejus per posteros continuavit & perpetuavit ad quatuor annorum centurias, scilicet usque ad captivitatem Babylonicam, in qua status Israelis concidit, fuitque populus Judæorum plane eversus, quæ æternitas quædam est. Plenius tamen & integrius hæc conveniunt CHRISTO. De CHRISTO enim propriissime dicitur: Ego ero illi in Patrem, &c. Cur ergo à sensu hoc pro- priissimo recedit citra causam?

6. Quod in contrarium pro Salomone è 2. Paralip. XXII. affertur, ad hoc oraculum non pertinet (cui respondet locus 2. Paralip. XVII. sed aliam refert visionem, adeoque ἀλλότριον est.

Tertio adferunt interpretationem de solo CHRISTO, quæ Lactantii est libr. IV. divin. In- stit. cap. 13. & Ruperti libr. II. in libr. Reg. cap. XXX. Sixti Senensis, Sasboldi, Catharini, Galeni, aliorumque nonnullorum, quæ omnino præfe- renda: pro qua hæc argumenta urgent:

1. Quod de eo agatur, qui post Davidem de- functum excitandus est, ut semen ejus, non ve- ro ad regnum evehendus, ut successor ejus.

2. Quod thronus illius stabiliendus sit in æter- num, quum regnum Salomonis quoad decem tribus in filio, & tandem plane in Zidekia de- fecerit.

3. Quod misericordia ejus auferenda non sit: Quod de Salomone non apparet, qui cultu Dei derelicto adeo graviter peccavit, ut de ejus sa- lute multi dubitent.

4. Quod Apostolus de nullo Angelorum hoc dictum esse affirmet, adeoque CHRISTUM inde Angelis majorem esse doceat. Quomodo ergo de Salomone, mero homine dictum? Ubi frustra ad typi rationem sese recipit Estius: Nun- quam hæc tam grandia & magnifica de Salomone dicerentur, nisi in eo veluti quodam typo & ima- gine CHRISTUS fuisset præfiguratus. Nam præ- terquam quod in eo principium petatur, quod tam grandia de Salomone, vel ullo typo CHRI- STI dicantur, quæ, de nullo Angelorum un- quam dicta, non in eo fuit typus CHRISTI Salomo, quod in filium assumptus est, nec in eo typi rationem constituit vel Estius vel Grotius, nec typi ratio hic locum habet. Esto in regno typus fuerit CHRISTI: At in adoptione in fi- lium prææternæ generationis CHRISTI vel na- turalis ejusdem υἱότητος typum constituere per- absurdum est, De ea autem ex instituto hic ab Apostolo agi, ἔνδηλον & ἀναντοῤῥήτως certum.

Adde (5) quod Esaias cap. IX. 5. inter alia elo- gia soli CHRISTO competentia etiam ea re- censeat, quæ hîc occurrunt. (6) Quodque ita in- terpretetur Gabriel Luc. I. 32. 33. (7) ut & S. Pe- trus Actor. II. 30. (8) nec non David ipse Psal. 89. &c. Vid. quæ ad 2. Sam. 7. & ad Psalm. 89. locum parallelum dicta, nec non ad Psal. 72, 7. seqq.

& confer imprimis quæ ad v. 19. 2. Sam. 7. obfer- vata. Quod ad rem præfentem, agnoscit B. Dor- scheus, etfi cum B. Glaffio ad Salomonem vaticinium illud simul referat respectum filiationis, qualis est in- ter Deum Patrem & Messiam longe sublimiorem ef- se, quam ut Angelis sit communicabilis : tantum ab- est, ut in Salomonem incidere possit. Itaque pergit, cum dicit: Ego vero ei in Patrem, non patrocinium & beneficium finitum indicatur, sed infinita gloria & Majestas: imo, inquam, hypostaticus genera- tionis activæ character vere divinus Deo Patri proprius, uti per illa, & ipse erit mihi in Fili m, character hypostaticus, quem Filius, ut talis per ge- nerationem passivam habet, uti est ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης, καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως τῦ Πατρὸς, interprete Apostolo, indicatur.

## 1:6
Verse 6.

When he again bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world) The Syrian rightly saw that there is a proposition here. For the direct construction would be: But again when he bringeth in. Next, it is to be noted that the word scripture is understood here, as in Galatians 3:16 and elsewhere. Furthermore, that phrase, where he bringeth in, is equivalent to where he describes him as being brought in, by the same figure by which Virgil said: Then he surrounds the Phaethontiades with bitter bark moss.

See also Gal. 3, 22. He signifies David by the firstborn in the lower sense, who is called by that name as being eminent among Kings, Ps. 89, 27. And that οἰκουμένην [means] the land of Judea, which also appears from the Greek inscription of that Psalm, namely XCVII: But in the more excellent sense, the firstborn is Christ, Rom. 8, 29. Col. 1, 15. 18. Rev. 1, 5. And οἰκουμένη is that supreme region which is inhabited by Angels, as our Author himself, looking back to these words of his, will presently say in II. 5. David Kimchi said that all the Psalms from XCIII to CI contain in themselves the mystery of the Messiah.

This is the third testimony of the Apostolic demonstration, from Ps. 97, 7, by which he proves that Christ is the Son of God, ὁμοούσιον [consubstantial], inasmuch as he is ἰσότιμον [equal in honor] to God the Father. For he would not be of the same glory with God the Father, unless he were of the same essence with him. Which argument Catholics everywhere urge as ἀμετακίνητον [unshakable] against the Arians.

He who is religiously adored by Angels and men, or is worshipped with the cult of adoration and Divine honor, is true God by nature. For by this oracle, with a comparison instituted with Ps. 89, 27, 28, the parallel of the preceding testimony, it is clearly taught both that Christ is the true and natural Son of God, as being the Firstborn of God, which to the Apostle is πρωτότοκος πάσης κτίσεως [firstborn of all creation] Col. 1, 15, and that he is of the same glory with the Father, as being no less to be adored by all the Angels than the Father. And the Apostle brings forward this testimony here all the more willingly because by it Christ is again introduced, that firstborn into the οἰκουμένην [world], who had previously been introduced through the prophecy of 2 Sam. 7 and the parallel passage in Ps. 89. For that sounded concerning Christ not by reason of his simple Deity, but as he was to be raised up from the seed of David.

And therefore it matters little whether it is explained as 'when he introduces again' with the Syriac, Vatablus, Hentenius, Sasboldus, and Grotius; or whether it is rendered 'when he introduces again'; which, however, is later and simpler without the transposition of words, and agrees more with the text. 'When he introduces the firstborn again into the world,' that is, when he speaks or prophesies again concerning his introduction into the world, or concerning his coming into these lands, to establish his kingdom, which happened at the incarnation.

Whence those Glosses of Ambrosius Catharinus are superfluous: [that] the apostate Angels sinned by the desire of the hypostatic union, which they envied for the human race, which desire they had removed, as soon as GOD had revealed this mystery to them: which revelation he calls the first introduction into the world, which was followed afterwards by a second, by which the Messiah was introduced into the world, and exhibited to the persevering Angels to be adored I, Disp. 233, chap. 1. The disputes of others and of other people according to Guilhelmus Estius, as to how it is said he was introduced again into the world, whether for the reason that he was first introduced into the world through eternal generation, or even in the creation of the Angels, and again in the incarnation, as Cornelius a Lapide wishes to be explained by Chrysostom, Ambrose, Theophylact, Oecumenius, and Cyril on the faith to the Queens, that he was introduced because, when begotten by the Father, he immediately filled these spaces in which the world was afterwards founded, which he calls a more suitable explanation, yet not the most suitable. But in truth it is neither sufficiently suitable, nor analogous to the faith, by which he compares the eternal generation with the advent of the incarnation regarding the filling of the world, nor was that the mind of those Fathers. Chrysostom indeed interprets the introduction as concerning the assumption of flesh; And furthermore he shows, he says, how much better he is than the Angels, namely as much as the Lord is to the servant, so that if anyone introduces someone into a house, he immediately orders those who are in charge of it to adore him. But Chrysostom says nothing about an introduction through eternal generation. Nor do other ancients say anything about it.

He is introduced, however, says Theophylact, in no other way than in the flesh. For just as GOD the Word was in the world, and the world was made through him, he makes the Father the one introducing the Son, so that he may render this Word acceptable. Gregory of Nyssa and likewise Cyril interpret this statement in such a way, and say that the Son, before he put on flesh, had nothing in common with this structure of the world, as one who was GOD and lacked flesh. But when he assumed flesh, then he became a participant in the world and an effect of created things, in so far as he had united this created flesh to himself, he is said to be introduced into this machinery of the world. And let all the Angels of GOD adore him, namely him who assumed the flesh.

He shows furthermore from these things how much he excelled, and how much the Lord is superior to the servant. Nor is he said to be introduced here otherwise than if someone had brought the Lords themselves into a house, whom the whole household would immediately receive with reverence.

But what explanation does Cornelius think is the most suitable? First, he says, CHRIST the man was brought into the world through the incarnation as passible and mortal: But again or secondly through the resurrection from death as glorious and impassible, or rather he will introduce him again on the day of judgment, so that he may judge the world, and then all the Angels, who first adored him at his birth, will again or secondly adore him publicly in glory. But what need is there to invent a double introduction, when the Apostle asserts that the firstborn is introduced again by the Holy Spirit, in another place of Scripture, that is to say?

Rightly B. Dorscheus: We interpret it more simply and without either transposition or ellipsis, if we say that the word is correctly placed for a notificative, just as it often is in the Holy Scriptures. Thus Heb. 10:5.

CHRIST εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον, that is, predicting and notifying that he is about to come into the world, says, sacrifice and offering you did not desire. The sense therefore is, when he indicates again (Scripture or the Holy Spirit) what GOD the Father decreed should be done in the introduction of his Son, he commands these things, etc. And what does either the resurrection have to do with this, or impassibility in the resurrection, about which the Apostle says not a word either in the proposition or in the demonstration of the proposition, or the day of judgment, of which there is likewise no trace here? There is also nothing about either in the cited place of the Psalm. Those things are therefore clearly irrelevant. For although he is called the Judge of the whole earth, that is not about the final judgment, but about the governance of the world, for which the daughters of Judah rejoice, with Zion, that is, the daughters of the Church with their mother Jerusalem, of which the eternal Church are as it were the daughters, Psalm 97, verse 8. Not to mention how ineptly Cornelius then says that CHRIST is to be adored by the Angels a second time, as he was adored first at his birth, as if he had never been adored after his birth, or is not adored now by the Angels! When on the contrary Estius says he was introduced again, when after his ascension into heaven and the mission of the Holy Spirit through the preaching of the Apostles he caused the world to receive him by faith and acknowledge him as its Lord: Who nevertheless afterwards prefers the sense of others, concerning the bringing of CHRIST from heaven, at the consummation of the age, so that he may judge the world; Which we have already warned do not fit here equally.

Estius says in the two prior testimonies that the Apostle dealt with the dignity of CHRIST manifested to the world through Apostolic preaching; now he speaks of a different time: But he proves neither, and neither fits the purpose of the Apostle.

He says that the energy of the word 'to introduce' appears more in this way, which for jurists is to induct or send into possession. But what does the juridical meaning have to do with this? And will CHRIST finally be sent into possession of the world only at the final judgment?

Does not a similar passage, Heb. 10:5, εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον, which Estius compared before, dealing with the advent of the incarnation, fit better? He says that Heb. 2:5 confirms the sense concerning the judgment: for he did not subject the world to come to the Angels. But here there is no parallelism either by reason of the words or by reason of the things: because there the world to come is designated, which is said to be subjected to CHRIST; here it is simply called οἰκουμένη, and there is no mention of its subjection, he is only said to be introduced into the world. And Estius finally acknowledges the convenience of our explanation: Furthermore, if to anyone the adverb 'again' seems here, as elsewhere, to serve for citing a new testimony, he will be able to explain the text in this way not unsuitably: And when he testifies again, that is, in another place of Scripture, that he introduces the firstborn, etc. Schlichting's commentary therefore collapses, which moreover is a copy of a twofold entry of CHRIST into heaven, the one before he undertook his office, the other through the ascension: it cannot be taught that οἰκουμένην, placed absolutely, denotes the blessed seats of the angels, nor does that meaning suit this passage of the Psalmist or the Apostolic text.

Grotius wishes τὸν πρωτότοκον to signify David in an inferior sense, from Psalm 89, verse 27, which he seems to apply to this passage, because he understands οἰκουμένην as the land of Judea in the same sense: but in a more excellent sense, he says that πρωτότοκον denotes CHRIST, and οἰκουμένην the supreme region, which is inhabited by the Angels, where there are again as many errors as there are clauses. For since 1. an introduction is said to be made in Psalm XCII, verse 6, by what reason, I ask, could that Psalm be adapted to David in any way? But he is called by Paul the firstborn, of whom that Psalm speaks: That it does not treat of David but of CHRIST has been solidly shown in the annotations on the Psalm. 2. Psalm LXXXIX, verse 27, we deny that David is noted by the name of Firstborn. That it treats of CHRIST there was shown during the explanation of that Psalm. 3. That by οἰκουμένην the Apostle designates the land of Judea, whatever senses may be feigned, is likewise most false. For thus it would have to be said that Paul intends this: that the sacred Psalmist is there treating of David being introduced into the land of Judea, because all the Angels are bound to worship him: What could be feigned more absurdly? 4. The Greek inscription of the Psalm is ἐπιβολιμαῖος: τῷ Δαβὶδ, ὅτε ἡ γῆ ἀυτῶ καθίσαται. For in the Hebrew the Psalm is ἀνεπίγραφος. That the title has fallen out of the Hebrew codices, as Bellarmine suspects, cannot be admitted, as it is repugnant to Divine providence; nor does it have a foundation, for which reason he himself distrusts that conjecture, whether that title was not rather added by the LXX Interpreters. But it was added, not because they opined that the present Psalm treats only of the land of Judea, but on the occasion of the land being restored to David, which his son Absalom had taken away, that is, when the kingdom, or the possession of the land, was being returned to him in turn. Which Bellarmine acknowledges: It does not seem, he says, that the Psalm should be understood literally concerning the restoration or constitution of the kingdom of David, for we read nothing of the sort in the Psalm, but it seems the holy Prophet, inspired by the Holy Spirit on the occasion of the land recovered by him, sang of the restoration and perfect constitution of the Church, which will be after the last judgment, when, with all persecutions removed and all enemies of CHRIST set under his feet, the Church will enjoy perpetual peace and tranquility, and CHRIST himself will reign peacefully over the whole creation. However, we have taught in the explanation of the Psalm that the Psalm pertains not to the final day and the kingdom of glory in the future age (which Franc. Gomarus wished to explain, likewise interpreting it of the judiciary introduction), but to the times of the New Testament and the kingdom of grace in this age to be administered by CHRIST the King throughout the whole world. 5. The Rabbis did not expound the present Psalm in the literal or lower sense, which Grotius calls it, concerning David, but some of them acknowledged that it prophesies of the kingdom of CHRIST: For they saw correctly that it could in no way be expounded concerning David. 6. By οἰκουμένην in a more eminent sense, it is understood here as heaven; from where will this be proven? Some expound the word οἰκουμένης in this place as heaven, we admit. But no one, so far as I know, is found who asserts that in a more eminent sense, that is, a mystical and not a literal sense, τὴν οἰκουμένην denotes heaven here. That could be admitted for the reason that in the ascension into heaven, if that is understood by the introduction into the οἰκουμένην, CHRIST occupied his kingdom, not so much in the heavens as on the earth. For even if he occupied heaven: that is not what is treated here, but the Apostle treats of that only later, demonstrating the session of CHRIST at the right hand of GOD. But he began his kingdom in the whole world after he ascended into heaven, of which kingdom the sacred Psalmist properly treats. It is better, however, to understand the words of the Apostle concerning the introduction into the world through his birth, which was done to the end that he might occupy the Royal throne of David and be King over the house of Jacob forever, Luke I. 32, 33. Whence he is called born King of the Jews, Matthew II. 1, born CHRIST the Lord, Luke II. 11, in which he was introduced into the present world and began to dwell among us, John I. 10, 14. Which sense we prefer, both because οἰκουμένη is named here absolutely, by which word the totality of things is understood, and because the word πάλιν, again, preceding the testimony, looks back to that by which the raising up of the seed of David or the birth of CHRIST the Son of GOD was designated, by reason of which this firstborn is introduced here again; and because he, that πρωτότοκος, had Royal Majesty and the dignity of glory of worship through his birth and from his birth, as far as right is concerned, to whom therefore the Angels served in the very birth, and otherwise in the days of his flesh, even if he freely emptied himself of this usurpation of majesty, being made lower than the Angels; and because by the force of the context and the thread of the Apostolic treatment, it is not yet a question here of the exaltation of CHRIST, but of his Divinity, that the Son of God is of the same essence with the Father, or is true GOD by nature, which is most clearly evident from the Psalm, which treats entirely of CHRIST. But the Apostle says that the Firstborn is introduced in the same, not taking that word πρωτότοκος from this Psalm, but from a comparison of it with Psalm LXXXIX. 27, 28, where he is introduced both as calling GOD his Father as the Firstborn, and as the highest among the Kings of the earth, whom he did not allege, since that Psalm is only a certain interpretation of the promise previously alleged from 2 Samuel VII; but the Apostle preferred to bring a new testimony, by which the firstborn is introduced again, so that he might recall to the Hebrews the parallelism between them, most known to them, of this XCVII Psalm, and by a comparison of the same, that this firstborn is the very highest GOD, of whom the sacred Psalmist treats there expressly, by which he is Jehovah and the Oecumenical King, verse 1. Ruler of the whole earth, verse 5, whose justice and glory all peoples acknowledge, whom all אלהים (that is, the angels, as they are called by this name primarily after GOD) are bound to worship, verse 7, for whose rule the whole Church rejoices, verse 8, of whom he himself says: Lord, you are the Most High in all the earth, you are greatly exalted above all the gods of the earth, verse 9. That Socinus posits a double subject, namely Jehovah and Adon the Lord, verse 5, in this Psalm (resp. contr. Bellarm. & Wiejeck. cap. 4. page 80), that is entirely repugnant to the text, in which it was confessed among the Hebrews that it treats of the Messiah, and from the kingdom among the nations, verse 1, for which the earth and the islands rejoice, it is evident that it is attributed particularly to the Messiah in Psalm LXXII and elsewhere throughout, who is also that Ruler and judge of the whole earth, verse 5. (Compare. Gen. XVIII. 25.) whose Majesty of Advent is illustrated by His appearance on Mount Sinai: for whose justice and government all peoples rejoice, Isa. XLV. 24. Jer. XXIII. 6. Ps. XCVIII. 2. Ps. XXII. 28. 32. in whose kingdom all who worship idols are put to shame, ver. 7. under whom light and justice arise, ver. 11. Compare Isa. XLII. 1. ch. LX. 1. ch. LXI. 11. ch. LXIII. 1. But that He of whom the Psalmist speaks is none other than Jehovah, the King and Ruler of the whole earth, the Lord most high in all regions exalted above all gods, keeping the souls of the Saints and delivering them, in whom the righteous ought to rejoice and celebrate His holiness. The entire sequence of the Psalm teaches whom, therefore, all Angels are bound to religiously venerate and adore as the one JEHOVAH GOD: whose immutable and eternal Deity, by the word הוה, the ecumenical dominion over all the earth, infinite power over the clouds, fire, lightnings, and the whole world, the active Divine presence, the glory of adoration due to Him alone by all creatures and by the Angels themselves, the incomprehensible height and immense redeeming power and illuminating grace, are graphically described here. Which, with a sonorous voice, proclaim the Messiah to be Jehovah, the most high God.

6. What Grotius brings together from the New Testament concerning the word πρωτότοκος does not equally pertain here. For properly, the eternal generation is looked to here, on account of which He Himself is called πρωτότοκος, Colossians 1, verse 15, of all creation, through which He is the natural Son of GOD, ὁμοούσιος to GOD the Father. That He is called the firstborn among brothers, Romans 8, and the firstborn from the dead, Apocalypse 3, does not apply here: nor is generation properly so-called understood there, according to which that Son and Firstborn is the brightness of the glory and the express image of the person of God. Therefore, He is not called the Firstborn in this place because others born after Him are of the same order: But because He was born first, before anything had proceeded from God, before the ages were founded, before every creature, and thus is absolutely and deservedly named πρωτότοκος, from Proverbs 8, verse 23, et seqq., Micah 5, verse 2, Colossians 1, verse 15, John 1, verse 1.

Καὶ προσκυνήτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες Ἄγγελοι Θεοῦ) In the Greek Psalm: Προσκυνήσατε αὐτῷ πάντες Ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ. But there it treats of GOD, here of the Messiah. True, this. But because it had long been accepted among the Hebrews that GOD would dwell in the Messiah in a singular way, and would be (as the Talmudists speak) pointable by the finger, therefore whatever was said concerning the honor of GOD was accustomed to be applied to the Messiah. The sense, however, of this passage is the same as 1 Peter III. 22.

Some think that Deuteronomy 32:32 is cited according to the LXX version, such as Theodoret, Euthymius, and Procopius in the Canticle of Moses, but nothing of the sort is held there in the Hebrew: nor even in the Latin, and without doubt those things crept into the LXX version from elsewhere. Undoubtedly, therefore, Psalm 97 is adduced, in which Cornelius à Lapide rashly suspects from a collation of the LXX that the word מלאכי (Angels) has fallen out, which opinion Estius himself refutes: For he says, not only in this place, but in many others, the LXX either truly or apparently differ from the Hebrew source, which therefore to wish to reform according to their version would be preposterous and an infinite task. He wishes, therefore, that by the name אלהים in the Psalm, both Angels and men are included, as many as excel others in power and dignity, and thus that there is no power so sublime that it ought not to bow itself and submit to the empire of the reigning Lord, therefore the LXX Interpreters whose interpretation St. Paul uses, deservedly restricted to the most excellent kind of created power, that is, to the Angels, since from a genus taken universally to a certain species, the argumentation is legitimate. Which sense the collation in the Psalm, verses 7 and 9, favors: Adore Him all you Gods: You are greatly exalted above all Gods. But because the Hieropsaltes treated distinctly of all peoples or regions acknowledging His glory, verse 6, here, however, for the confusion of those who serve τοῖς

אלילים (idols) serve, he says that they, the אלהים, namely the most excellent creatures and of most eminent dignity, the Angels of GOD, adore that Ecumenical King: from which the Apostle demonstrates that the same is the true and Most High GOD, and proves His most eminent glory above the Angels, it is established that the name Elohim is more correctly accepted concerning the Angels than in a more general sense in the Psalm, just as it was expounded by the LXX Interpreters and Paul. But when Grotius says: There it treats of GOD, here of the Messiah, he contradicts himself no less than Paul: Himself, because he had said that the Psalm treats of David in the literal sense. But what literal sense of David is there, where it treats of GOD? Paul, because he clearly testifies here that not GOD the Father, but the Firstborn, or the Son of GOD, is introduced. What he says is accepted among the Hebrews, Grotius proves by no testimony. The faithful Hebrews had been taught from the scriptures of the Old Testament, not that GOD would dwell in the Messiah, but that the Messiah would be GOD Jehovah Himself, Jeremiah 23, verse 6, which they could also have from this Psalm. Therefore, GOD is pointable by the finger in the Messiah, because the Messiah is GOD Himself manifested in the flesh, 1 Timothy 3, verse 16. If they applied those things which were said concerning the honor of GOD to the Messiah, being by nature a mere man, they sinned against the first commandment of the first table, and against the Divine protestation, Isaiah 42, verse 8: My glory I will not give to another. The application is not instituted here by the Apostle alone, but a demonstration is taken from the Psalm: which, therefore, must treat of CHRIST the Firstborn of God, and must have been so understood by the Hebrews: if this demonstration is to be considered firm among them. Cornelius à Lapide rightly says here that CHRIST, as He is man, is to be adored with latria, equally as CHRIST, as He is GOD. How, therefore, do the Jesuits deny that a communication of Majesty was made to the human nature of CHRIST? But it is not rightly inferred in the Eucharist that Christ the man present is to be worshipped with latria, by virtue of the decree of the Council of Trent, Session 13, chapters 5 and 6. For the decree is very bad, and it is very badly deduced there from this place. For even if CHRIST as man is to be adored, yet that is not decreed in this place by the Apostle, who is occupied in demonstrating the Deity of CHRIST, nor does it follow that the Eucharistic bread is worshipped with the cult of latria without idolatry; because the bread is not the body of CHRIST itself, or CHRIST Himself, but a communication or medium of the communication of the body of CHRIST, it is not transubstantiated into the body of Christ, but communicates and exhibits to us by the power of the institution of the Sacrament the body of CHRIST, 1 Corinthians 10, verse 16. But the divine nature of the Messiah is rightly proved from the adoration commanded to the angels, and especially from this Davidic Psalm, in which we have already shown that the Messiah is expressly described as that true and only JEHOVAH GOD, to whom alone adoration is due, to whom therefore the Hebrews are here referred. For this adoration is not civil, and of the second table, but religious, and of the first, namely, that which was attributed to graven images through idolatry, but is due to the one GOD, verse 7, such as Jehovah himself, his kingdom verse 1, his admirable mighty works in the kingdom of power verse 2 seqq., his divine presence verse 5, the glory of justice manifested verse 6, and the benefits of divine grace verse 8 seqq. in the kingdom of grace require.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

Ὅταν δὲ πάλιν εἰσαγάγῃ τὸν πρωτότοκον εἰς τὴν οἰκουμέ- νην) Esse hic propositionem, bene vidit Syrus. Recta enim constructio esset: Πάλιν δὲ ὅταν εἰσαγάγῃ. Dein- de notandum, subaudiri hic nomen γραφὴ, ut Galat. 3, 16. & alibi. Præterea illud, ubi introducit, valere, ubi describit introduci, eadem figura, qua Virgilius dixit: Tum Phaëtontiadas musco circumdat amara Corticis.

Vide & Gal. 3, 22. Τὸν πρωτότοκον sensu inferiore signi- ficat Davidem, qui eo nomine ut inter Reges eximius vo- catur, Psal. 89, 27. & illud οἰκουμένην terram Judæam, quod etiam ex Græca Psalmi illius nempe XCVII. inscriptio- ne apparet : Sensu autem excellentiore πρωτότοκος est Christus, Roman. 8, 29. Coloss. 1, 15. 18. Apoc. 1, 5. Et οἰκουμένη est regio illa suprema, quæ ab Angelis habitatur, ut ipse mox Scriptor noster ad hæc sua verba respiciens dicet II. 5. Psalmos omnes à XCIII. ad CI. in se continere mysterium Messiæ dixit David Kimchi.

Tertium hoc demonstrationis Apostolicæ te- stimonium est, è Psalm. 97, 7. quo probat, Chri- stum esse Dei Filium ὁμοούσιον, utpote Deo Patri ἰσότιμον. Non enim esset ejusdem cum Deo Patre gloriæ, nisi ejusdem cum ipso esset essentiæ. Quod argumentum tanquam ἀμετακίνητον contra Aria- nos passim urgent Catholici.

Qui religiose ab Angelis & hominibus adora- tur, vel cultu adorationis & honore Divino coli- tur, is verus est natura Deus. Hoc enim oraculo collatione cum Ps. 89. 27. 28. præcedentis testimo- nii parallelo, instituta luculenter docetur, tum quod Christus verus & naturalis Dei Filius sit, ut- pote Primogenitus Dei, quod Apostolo est πρωτό- τοκος πάσης κτίσεως Coloff. 1, 15. tum quod ejus- dem sit cum Patre gloriæ, utpote non minus ado- randus ab Angelis omnibus, quam Pater. Idque testimonium eo libentius hic adducit Apostolus, quod eodem iterum introducatur Christus pri- mogenitus ille in οἰκουμένην, qui antea introductus erat per vaticinium 2. Sam. 7. & locum parallelum Psalm. 89. Nam illud sonabat de Christo non ratione simplicis Deitatis, sed prout erat excitan- dus è semine Davidis.

Ideoque parum refert, sive explicetur iterum quando introducit cum Syro Vatablo, Hentenio, Sasboldo, Grotio; sive reddatur, cum vero ite- rum introducit; quod tamen posterius & sim- plicius est sine trajectione vocum, & magis con- gruit textui. Cum iterum introducit primogeni- tum in mundum, id est, cum iterum loquitur vel vaticinatur de introductione ejus in mundum, vel de ejus adventu in has terras, ad erigendum regnum suum, qui accidit in incarnatione.

Unde supervacaneæ sunt illæ Glossæ Ambro- sii Catharini: Angelos Apostatas peccasse appetitu unionis hypostaticae, quam inviderint generi hu- mano, quem appetitum exemerint, cum primum DEUS ipsis revelasset hoc mysterium: quam re- velationem vocat primam introductionem in or- bem, quam sequuta sit postea altera, qua Mes- sias introductus in orbem, & Angelis perseveran- tibus ad adorandum exhibitus sit; Quas nugas refellit Vasquez in 1. Parte Tom. I. Ir. Disp. 233. cap. 1. Alienae & aliorum disputationes apud Guilhelmum Estium, quomodo dicatur iterum introductus in mundum, an ea ratione, quod in mundum primum introductus sit per aeternam generationem, vel etiam in Angelorum creatione, & iterum in incarnatione, quomodo Cornelius a Lapide vult a Chrysostomo, Ambrosio, Theophy- lacto, Oecumenio & Cyrillo de fide ad Reginas exponi, quod introductus sit, quia cum geni- tus a Patre statim implevit spatia haec, in qui- bus postea orbis conditus est, quam aptiorem dicit explicationem, nondum tamen aptissimam. Sed revera nec satis apta est, nec fidei analoga, qua comparat aeternam generationem cum ad- ventu incarnationis quoad impletionem mundi, neque ea Patrum istorum mens fuit. Introdu- Etionem quidem de carnis susceptione interpreta- tur Chrysostomus; Et porro ostendit, inquit, quantum Angelis sit melior, nempe quantum Do- minus servo, ut si quis aliquo in domum introdu- cto, eos, qui illi praesunt, statim ipsum jubet adora- re. Nihil autem Chrysostomus de introductione per aeternam generationem. Nec de eo quic- quam alii veteres.

Introducitur autem, inquit Theophylactus, haudquaquam aliter, nisi in carne. Nam quem- admodum DEUS Verbum in mundo erat, & mundus per ipsum est factus, Patrem facit Filium introducentem, ut acceptabile reddat hoc Verbum. Gregorius vero Nyssenus & item Cyrillus ita id di- Etum interpretantur, & filium dicunt, priusquam carnem indueret, nihil habuisse cum hac mundi structura commune, utpote, qui DEUS esset, & carne careret. Ubi vero carnem assumpsit tunc mundi participem & creatarum rerum effectum, in quantum creatam hanc carnem sibi uniisset, in mundi hanc dici machinam introductum. Et ad- orent eum omnes Angeli DEI, eum scilicet, qui carnem assumpsit.

Ostendit praeterea ex his, quam ille praestaret, & quam Dominus servo sit potior. Nec secus hic di- citur introductus, quam si quis Dominos ipsos in domum invexerit, quos mox & familia omnis venerabunda excipiat.

Quamnam vero aptissimam putat Cornelius explicationem? Primum, inquit, inductus est CHRISTUS homo in orbem per incarnationem passibilis & mortalis: Iterum vero sive secundo per resurrectionem a morte gloriosus & impassibilis, vel potius iterum inducet in die judicii, ut judicet or- bem, tuncque Angeli omnes, qui primo adorave- runt eum in nativitate, iterum sive secundo ado- rabunt publice in gloria. Sed quid opus est, ge- minam introductionem fingere, quum non nisi iterum a Spiritu S. introduci, alio scilic. loco Scri- pturae, primogenitum, asserat Apostolus?

Recte B. Dorscheus: Simplicius & absque vel trajectione vel ellipsi interpretamur, si dicamus, verbum recte pro notificativo positum esse, quem- admodum saepius in S. Literis sit. Sic Ebr. 10, 5.

CHRISTUS εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον, id est, prædicens & notificans se venturum in mun- dum, dicit, sacrificium & oblationem noluisti. Sensus itaque est, cum iterum indicat (Scriptura vel SS.) quid decrevit DEUS Pater in intro- ductione Filii sui faciendum esse, hæc imperat, &c. Et quid huc vel resurrectio facit, vel impassibili- tas in resurrectione, de qua nullo verbo sive in propositione, sive in propositionis demonstra- tione Apostolus, vel dies judicii, quo de pari- ter nullum hic vestigium? De neutra etiam quicquam in Psalmi loco citato. Ea ergo pla- ne aliena. Nam quamvis Judex dicatur uni- versæ terræ, id tamen non de extremo judicio, sed de regimine mundi, ob quod gaudent filiæ Ju- dæ, cum Zione, id est, Ecclesiæ filiæ cum matre Hierosolyma, cujus æternæ Ecclesiæ veluti fi- liæ sunt Psalm. XCVII. vers. 8. ut taceam, quam inepte tum secundo ab Angelis adorandum CHRI- STUM dicat Cornelius, uti primo in nativitate adoratus, quasi nunquam post nativitatem ad- oratus sit, aut nunc non adoretur ab Angelis! Quum contra Estius rursus introductum dicat, quando post ascensum in cælos, & missionem Spiri- tus sancti per Apostolorum prædicationem effecit, ut mundus eum fide reciperet, & Dominum suum agnosceret: Qui tamen postea præfert aliorum sensum, de adductione CHRISTI de cælo, in con- summatione sæculi, ut mundum judicet; Quæ æ- que huc non quadrare, jam monuimus.

Dicit Estius in prioribus duobus testimoniis A- postolum de dignitate CHRISTI per prædicationem Apostolicam mundo manifestata egisse; jam de di- verso tempore loqui: Sed neutrum probat, neu- trum instituto Apostoli congruit.

Dicit vocis introducere ἐνέργειαν sic magis ap- parere, quæ JCtis est inducere seu mittere in pos- sessionem. Sed quid huc juridica significatio? Et num in judicio extremo demum mittetur CHRI- STUS in possessionem orbis?

Annon potius convenit locus similis Ebr. X. 5. εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον, quem antea contu- lit Estius, agens de adventu incarnationis? Dicit, sensum de judicio confirmare Ebr. II. 5. non enim Angelis subjecit orbem terræ futurum. Sed hic nullus est parallelismus neque ratione verborum neque ratione rerum: quia ibi orbis futurus de- signatur, qui subjiciendus dicitur CHRISTO; hic simpliciter οἰκουμένη nominatur, nec de sub- jectione ejus mentio sit, in orbem solum intro- duci dicitur. Et agnoscit tandem Estius nostræ explicationis convenientiam: Porro si cui magis videtur Adverbium, iterum, hic sicut alibi servire novo testimonio citando, poterit is hoc modo textum non inconcinne exponere: Et cum iterum, id est, alio scripturæ loco, testatur, se introducere primoge- nitum &c. Corruit ergo & Schlichtingii Com- mentum, quod præterea ἀντίγραφον est de ge- mino CHRISTI ingressu in cælum, altero an- tequam officium aggrederetur, altero per ascensio- nem: οἰκουμένην absolute positam angelorum beatas sedes notare doceri nequit, nec huic Psaltis loco aut Apostolico textui congruit ea significatio.

Grotius τὸν πρωτότοκον sensu inferiore signifi- care Davidem vult, è Psalm. LXXXIX. vers. 27. quod huic loco applicare videtur, quia οἰκουμέ- νην de terra Judæa eodem sensu intelligit: Sensu autem excellentiori πρωτότοκον CHRISTUM, & οἰκουμένην regionem supremam, quæ ab Angelis habitatur, notare ait, ubi iterum tot errata, quot commata. Nam quum 1. introductio fie- ri dicatur Psalm. XCII. vers. 6. qua obsecro ratione Davidi ullatenus Psalmus ille aptari poterit? Is autem vocatur à Paulo primoge- nitus, de quo Psalmus iste loquitur: Quem non de Davide sed de CHRISTO agere in an- not. ad Psalm. solide ostensum est. 2. Psalm. LXXXIX. vers. 27. Davidem nomine Primo- geniti notari negamus. De CHRISTO illic agi, circa explicationem istius Psalmi osten- sum fuit. 3. Per οἰκουμένην ab Apostolo terram Judæam, quicunque tandem sensus fingantur, designari, falsissimum itidem est. Nam sic di- cendum fuerit, Paulum id velle, Hieropsalten illic agere de Davide in terram Judæam intro- ducto, quod eundem omnes Angeli adorare tene- antur: Quid absurdius fingi poterat? 4. Græca Psalmi inscriptio ἐπιβολιμαῖος est: τῷ Δαβὶδ, ὅτε ἡ γῆ ἀυτῶ καθίσαται. In Ebræo enim Psalmus ἀνεπίγραφος est. Quod titu- lum excidisse Ebræis codicibus Bellarminus su- spicatur, admitti non potest, utpote repu- gnans Divinæ providentiæ; nec fundamentum habet, ideo illi conjecturæ diffidit ipse, annon potius additus ille titulus sit à LXX. Interpreti- bus. Additus autem est, non quod opinati sint agere de terra Judæa tantum præsentem Psal- mum, sed occasione terræ Davidi, quam Abso- lon filius abstulerat, restitutæ, hoc est, cum re- gnum ei, vel possessio terræ vicissim reddere- tur. Quod agnoscit Bellarminus: Non vide- tur, inquit, Psalmus ad literam intelligendus de restitutione aut constitutione regni Davidis, nihil enim ejusmodi in Psalmo legimus, sed videtur san- ctus Propheta occasione terræ à se recuperatæ Spi- ritu sancto afflatus cecinisse restitutionem & con- stitutionem perfectam Ecclesiæ, quæ futura est post ultimum judicium, quando remotis persecutioni- bus omnibus, & omnibus inimicis CHRISTI sub pedibus ejus constitutis Ecclesia pace perpetua & tranquillitate fruetur, & CHRISTUS ipse pacifice in universa creatura regnabit. Non au- tem ad diem novissimum & regnum gloriæ in fu- turo seculo, (quod voluit Franc. Gomarus de introductione judiciaria itidem explicans) sed ad tempora Novi Testamenti & regnum gratiæ in hoc seculo à CHRISTO Rege per orbem universum administrandum Psalmum pertinere in explicatione Psalmi docuimus. 5. Rabbini non exposuere Psalmum præsentem sensu litera- li aut humiliori, quem vocat Grotius, de Da- vide, sed agnovere nonnulli ex iisdem, quod va- ticinetur de regno CHRISTI: Probe enim viderunt, de Davide nullatenus exponi posse. 6. Per οἰκουμένην sensu eminentiori hic cœlum in- telligi unde probabitur? Exponunt nonnulli vocem οἰκουμένης hoc loco de cælo, fatemur. Sed nemo, quod sciam, invenitur, qui sensu eminen- tiori, hoc est, mystico, non vero sensu literali τὴν οἰκουμένην hic cœlum notare asserat. Illud ea ratione admitti possit, quod in ascensione in cœ- lum, si illa intelligatur per introductionem in οἰκουμένην, CHRISTUS regnum suum occupa- rit, non tam in cœlis, quam in terris. Nam etsi occupavit cælum: Id tamen hic non agitur, sed de eo postmodum demum tractat Apostolus, de- monstrans sessionem CHRISTI ad dextram DEI. At in toto terrarum orbe regnum suum cepit, post- quam ascendit in cœlum, de quo regno proprie agit Hieropsaltes. Præstat tamen de introductione in mundum, per nativitatem verba Apostoli intel- ligere, quæ vero ea fini facta est, ut Regium Davi- dis thronum occuparet, & Rex esset super domum Jacob in æternum, Luc. I. 32. 33. Unde Rex Ju- dæorum natus dicitur Matth. II. 1. CHRISTUS Dominus natus, Luc. II. 11. in qua in mundum præ- sentem introductus est, & habitare cœpit in nobis, Johan. I. 10. 14. Quem sensum præferimus, tum quod οἰκουμένη hic absolute nominetur, qua voce rerum universitas intelligitur, tum quod vox πάλιν iterum præcedens testimonium respiciat, quo ex- citatio germinis Davidis vel nativitas CHRISTI Filii DEI designata fuit, cujus ratione iterum in- troducitur hic primogenitus; tum quod Maje- statem Regiam, & dignitatem gloriæ adorationis per nativitatem & inde à nativitate, quantum ad jus, habuerit ille πρωτότοκος, 'cui in ipsa nativitate ideo inserviere Angeli, & alias in diebus carnis, etsi hac majestatis usurpatione sese libere evacua- rit, minoratus infra Angelos; tum quod vi con- textus, & fili Apostolicæ tractationis hic nondum agatur de exaltatione CHRISTI, sed de Divi- nitate ejus, quod Filius Dei ejusdem essentiæ sit cum Patre, vel verus natura DEUS, quod ex Psalmo, qui de CHRISTO totus agit, lucu- lentissime patet. In eodem autem introduci Pri- mogenitum ait Apostolus, vocem illam πρωτότο- κος non ex hoc Psalmo desumens, sed ex colla- tione ejusdem cum Psalmo XXCIX. 27. 28. ubi & ut Primogenitus DEUM Patrem suum vocans, & ut excelsus inter Reges terræ introducitur, quem non allegavit, quum promissionis antea allegatæ, è 2. Samul. VII. ille Psalmus tantum quædam sit interpretatio; sed novum testimonium, quo ite- rum introducatur primogenitus, adducere ma- luit Apostolus, ut Ebræis & hujus XCVII. Psal- mi parallelismum inter ipsos notissimum in me- moriam revocet, atque ejusdem collatione, hunc primogenitum esse ipsum celsissimum DEUM, de quo Hieropsaltes ibi ex professo, quo sit Jehovah & Rex Oecumenicus, vers. 1. Dominator universæ terræ, vers. 5. cujus justitiam & gloriam omnes po- puli agnoscant, quem omnes אלהים (id est, angeli utpote qui post DEUM πρώτως hoc no- mine nuncupantur) adorare teneantur, vers. 7. ob cujus regimen Ecclesiæ universæ lætentur, vers. 8. de quo ipse: Domine, tu Altissimus in omnibus terris, tu valde exaltatus supra omnes Deos terræ, vers. 9. Quod Socinus geminum subjectum, Jeho- vam nempe, & Adon Dominum vers. 5. statuit in hoc Psalmo, resp. contr. Bellarm. & Wiejeck. cap. 4. pagin. 80. id repugnat penitus textui, in quo de Messia agi penes Ebræos in confesso erat & è regno inter gentes vers. 1. ob quod terra & insulæ lætantur, patet, quod peculiariter Messiæ tribuitur Psal. LXXII. & alibi passim, qui etiam Dominator & judex ille universæ terræ est, vers. 5. (Confer. Gen. XVIII. 25.) cujus Adventus Ma- jestas ex apparitione ejusdem in Monte Sinai il- lustratur: ob cujus justitiam & regimen omnes populi lætantur, Esa. XLV. 24. Jerem. XXIII. 6. Psalm. XCVIII. 2. Psalm. XXII. 28. 32. in cujus regno omnes colentes idola confusi vers. 7. sub quo lux & justitia oritur, vers. 11. Confer Esa. XLII. 1. cap. LX. 1. cap. LXI. 11. cap. LXIII. 1. Hunc autem de quo Psaltes agit, non alium esse quam Jehovam, Regem & Dominatorem to- tius terræ, Dominum altissimum in omnibus re- gionibus exaltatum super omnes Deos custodien- tem animas Sanctorum easque liberantem, in quo justi lætari debeant ejusque sanctitatem celebrare. Tota Psalmi συνέχεια docet, quem proinde ceu Jehovam unum DEUM religiose venerari at- que adorare teneantur omnes Angeli : cujus immutabilis & æterna Deitas voce הוה Oecume- nicum dominium in omnem terram, infinita po- tentia in nubes, ignem, fulgura & orbem totum operosa, præsentia Divina, gloria adorationis ipsi u- ni debita ab omnibus creaturis, ipsisque Angelis altitudo incomprehensibilis & immensa potestas re- demptrix & gratia illuminatrix, graphice hic de- scripta. Quæ sonora voce proclamant Messiam esse Jehovam, Deum altissimum.

6. Quæ consert Grotius è Novo Testamento de voce πρωτότοκος, non ex æquo huc pertinent. Proprie enim hic respicitur generatio æterna, ob quam ipse πρωτότοκος dicitur, Coloss. 1. vers. 15. πάσης κτίσεως, per quam est naturalis DEI Fi- lius, DEO Patri ὁμοούσιος, Quod primogeni- tus inter fratres, Roman. 8. dicitur, & primogeni- tus è mortuis, Apocal. 3. huc non facit: nec istic proprie dicta generatio intelligitur, secundum quam ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ θεοῦ Filius ille & Primogenitus est. Non ergo Primogenitus hoc loco dicitur, quod alii post ipsum geniti ejusdem ordinis sint : Sed quod primum, antequam quicquam à Deo prodiisset, antequam secula conderentur, ipse genitus sit, ante omnem creaturam, adeoque absolute πρωτότοκος, merito nominetur è Pro- verb. 8. vers. 23. seqq. Mich. 5. vers. 2. Coloss. 1. vers. 15. Johan. 1. vers. 1.

Καὶ προσκυνήτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες Ἄγγελοι Θεοῦ) In Græco Psalmo : Προσκυνήσατε αὐτῷ πάντες Ἄγγελοι αὐ- τοῦ. At ibi de DEO agitur, hic de Messia. Verum hoc. Sed quia pridem receptum erat apud Ebræos, DE- UM singulari modo in Messia habitaturum, & fore (ut Thalmudici loquuntur) digito monstrabilem, ideo quæcunque de honore DEI dicebantur, eadem appli- cari solebant ad Messiam. Sensus autem, qui hujus lo- ci, idem & 1. Petr. III. 22.

Nonnulli Deut. 32, 32. juxta versionem LXX. citari putant, utpote Theodoretus, Euthymius, & Procopius in Cantic. Mosis, sed illic in Ebræo nihil tale habetur : neque etiam in Latino, & sine dubio aliunde ista in LXX. versionem ir- repsere. Indubie ergo Psalm. 97. adducitur, in quo verbum מלאכי Angeli excidisse temere Cor- nelius à Lapide è collatione LXX. suspicatur, quam sententiam refellit ipse Estius : Non enim, inquit, in hoc loco tantum, sed in multis aliis LXX. seu vere seu apparenter discrepant à fonte Ebræo, quem proinde reformare velle ad illorum versionem præposterum sit & infiniti negotii. Vult ergo nomine אלהים in Psalmo compre- hendi tam Angelos, quam homines, quotquot po- tentia atque dignitate supra alios eminent, adeoque nullam esse tam sublimem potentiam, quæ non incurvare se debeat, ac submittere Domini re- gnantis imperio, ideo LXX. Interppr. quorum in- terpretatione S. Paulus utitur, merito restrin- xisse ad excellentissimum genus creatæ potestatis, id est, ad Angelos, cum à genere universim sumpto ad certam speciem legitima sit argumen- tatio. Cui sensui collatio favet in Psalmo vers. 7. & 9. Adorate eum omnes Dii : Tu valde exaltatus es supra omnes Deos. Sed quia distin- cte Hiero-Psaltes de omnibus populis vel regio- nibus gloriam ejus agnoscentibus egit, vers. 6. hic vero ad confusionem eorum, qui τοῖς

אלילים serviunt, ipsos אלהים creaturas scilicet excellentissimas, & dignitatis eminentissimæ, Angelos DEI adorare illum Regem Oecume- cum ait : è quibus, eundem verum esse & Al- tissimum DEUM, demonstrat Apostolus, ejus- que eminentissimam supra Angelos gloriam pro- bat, rectius nomen Elohim de Angelis, quam sensu generaliori in psalmo accipi, prout à LXX. Interpretibus & Paulo id expositum est, sta- tuitur. Cum autem Grotius ait : Ibi de DEO, hic de Messia agi, non minus sibi, quam Pau- lo contradicit : Sibi quia de Davide Psalmum literali sensu agere dixerat. Qui autem de Da- vide sensus literalis est, ubi de DEO agitur ? Paulo, quia diferte hic testatur, non DEUM Patrem, sed Primogenitum, vel Filium DEI in- troduci. Quod receptum dicit ad Ebræos, nul- lo testimonio probat Grotius. Ebræi fideles è scripturis Veteris Testamenti edocti erant, non DEUM in Messia habitaturum, sed Messiam futurum DEUM Jehovam ipsum Jerem. 23. vers. 6. quod etiam ex hoc Psalmo habere po- terant. Digito ergo est demonstrabilis DEUS in Messia, quia Messias est ipse DEUS manife- status in carne, 1. Timoth. 3, vers. 16. Si ea, quæ de honore DEI dicta sunt, applicarunt ad Mes- siam natura merum hominem, peccarunt con- tra primæ tabulæ primum præceptum, & con- tra protestationem Divinam, Esa. 42. vers. 8. Gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Non applica- tio ab Apostolo hic solum instituitur, sed de- monstratio è Psalmo desumitur : quem proinde de CHRISTO Primogenito Dei agere, & ab Ebræis ita intellectum fuisse oportet : Si firma penes ipsos debeat censeri hæc demonstratio. Recte hic Cornelius à Lapide CHRISTUM, qua homo est, latria adorandum esse, æque ac CHRISTUM, qua DEUS est. Quomodo ergo negant Jesuitæ, communicationem Maje- statis humanæ CHRISTI naturæ factam ? Non autem recte infertur in Eucharistia, Chri- stum hominem præsentem latria colendum esse, vi decreti Concilii Tridentini Sess. 13. cap. 5. 6. Pessime enim decretum, pessime id ibidem ex hoc loco deductum. Nam etsi CHRISTUS qua homo adorandus sit ; non tamen id hoc loco decretum ab Apostolo, qui occupatur in demonstranda Deitate CHRISTI, neque consequens est, quod panis Eucharisticus citra idololatriam cultu latrias colatur ; quia panis non est ipsum corpus CHRISTI, aut CHRISTUS ipse, sed communicatio vel medium communica- tionis corporis CHRISTI, non transsubstantia- tur in corpus Christi, sed communicat & ex- hibet nobis vi institutionis Sacramenti CHRI- STI corpus, 1. Corinth. 10. vers. 16. Recte au- tem ex adoratione Messiæ Angelis præcepta divi- na ejus natura probatur, & imprimis ex hoc Psalmo Davidico, in quo Messiam ex professo, ut Jehovam verum illum & unicum DEUM, cui soli adoratio debetur, describi jam osten- dimus, ad quem proinde hic remittuntur E- bræi. Adoratio enim hæc non est civilis, & secundæ tabulæ, sed religiosa, & primæ talis scil. quæ sculptilibus per idololatriam tribuebatur u- ni DEO debita, vers. 7. qualem ipse Jehovah, ejus regnum vers. 1. ejus admiranda opera in re- gno potentiæ vers. 2. seqq. ejus divina præsentia vers. 5. manifestata justitiæ gloria vers. 6. & di- vinæ gratiæ beneficia vers. 8. seqq. in regno gra- tiæ requirunt.

## 1:7
Vers. 7. And to the angels he says) That is, concerning the Angels, which we have just noted to be an idiom of Luke. A similar locution is in Jerem. XIV. Who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire) And this is from the Greek LXX, except that this writer, citing the passage from memory, put πυρὸς φλόγα for πῦρ φλέγον, where Aquila has πῦρ λάβρον, Symmachus πυρίνην φλόγα. The sense of this passage is: There is nothing great in the name of Angels and ministers, since Scripture gives those names even to wind and flame. For we have said at Gen. III. 23. and Maimonides in Guide for the Perplexed II. 6, that all creatures which God uses out of the ordinary course come under that name. And just as wind and flame are called Angels: so conversely some Angels are Seraphim, that is, flames, and Cherubim, by which name winds seem to be signified of old. Compare Psalm XVIII. 11. and LIV. 3. because both efficacy and swiftness cannot be better expressed than through things known to us. But the series of the passage in the Psalm demands the former sense more, nor does that article τοὺς, which is believed to denote the subject, not the predicate, stand in the way. For both among the Attics and among our own writers that article often abounds. Vers. 8. And to the Son) He means this, that much more eminent titles are given to the Son. Now it was agreed among the Hebrews, as we have just touched upon, that Solomon in many things was a type of the Messiah, and that the titles which are given to him apply in a much more sublime sense to the Messiah. Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever, a rod of uprightness is the rod of thy kingdom. Vers. 9. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity, therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows) Clearly the same words as in the Greek of that Psalm, which is XLV in the Hebrews, XLIV in the Greeks, except that in the Greek it is for ever and ever without articles. And in the Manuscript in this place, for iniquity there is injustice, with the same sense. For ὁ Θεὸς in the Hebrew is אלהים, which name is indeed accustomed to be given to many, whether Angels or Judges: but when it is attributed to one, it befits God alone, because then it is a speech ἑλικτικὴ for אלהה אלהים, as we have said elsewhere. The sense therefore is: God himself is thy perpetual seat, that is, if we look to Solomon: Just as a seat holds men unshaken: So God will always sustain thee in the kingdom. But if we look to Christ: God himself will sustain thee in a kingdom that will never fail. By the royal sceptre in Solomon is understood metonymically the manner of government: In Christ, the word of the Gospel first published by him. Solomon loved justice and hated injustice, namely from his early age: therefore he was chosen by God as King above not only his fellow-citizens, but also his brothers, 1 Chron. XXVIII. v. 5. which is signified by anointing, 1 Kings I. v. 34. Jesus, while he lived a mortal life, taught nothing other than all things just and honest by word and example, refuting things contrary to these. Therefore, after death, having been raised, he obtained a dignity above all men, and indeed even above the Angels, which dignity is signified here in the human manner by the word anointing. Thus God made him Christ, Acts II. v. 36. take therefore as wherefore in Philipp. II. v. 9. Moreover, the Accusative ἔλαιον is placed in the Greek manner in the sense in which the Latins use the Ablative. And that is called oil of gladness which gives cause for supreme joy. See John XV. 11. XVII. 13. Others in the Psalm translated it as oil of splendor, others of adornment, of glory, of ointment. For fellows Symmachus put companions. Moreover, there are two nominatives אלהים אלהיך, that God whom thou worshippest. The Chaldean Paraphrast and many Rabbis interpret this passage concerning the Messiah.

The Apostle now undertakes a new demonstration, and the same one again through comparison with the Angels, for asserting the infinite Deity of CHRIST, which is fourth in order: which teaches from Psalm CIV. 4. in v. 7 that the Angels were created by God and are ministers of God. But he demonstrates from Psalm XLV. v. 7 that the Son of GOD is not a creature of GOD, but true GOD with the Father, not a minister of GOD, but co-throned with GOD the Father, whose throne is eternal, and who also according to his human nature was anointed with the oil of gladness, with the immense gifts of the Holy Spirit, which anointing would have no place if Christ were only a mere man. For how can a mere man be endowed and anointed with the infinite gifts of the Holy Spirit, or as it is said in John III. v. 34, the Holy Spirit be given to him not by measure, that is, in an immense and infinite manner. But those two former points are properly urged here, immediately referring to the divine nature, whence the argument is immovable: He who is called God by the Holy Spirit, and to whom, as God, an eternal throne is attributed, he must be God by nature in truth. But the antecedent is true concerning the Son of GOD. Therefore the consequent also. The assumption from the Psalm is certain: From which, therefore, not only those words by which he is called God, and his eternal throne is treated, but also other things added concerning the anointing are brought forward, so that it may be certain of which person of the most holy Trinity these things are said, or that they were said to the Son, to the Messiah, that anointed one of the Lord, so that it may be understood more fully. Chrysostom explained and applied these things at length and solidly against the heretics: See how and how clearly he divides creatures and Creator, ministers and Lord, and the true and proper heir and son and servants. But to the son he says: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever. Behold the sign of the kingdom. The rod of equity is the rod of thy kingdom. Behold again also another sign of the kingdom. Then again concerning him who is clothed in flesh: Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee. What is thy God? For since he has spoken a great thing, he again softens and mitigates it. Here he strikes both the Jews, and the followers of Paul of Samosata, and the Arians, and Marcellus and Sabellius, and Marcion. How? The Jews indeed, by showing two persons, God and man. The others, however, I mean the followers of Paul of Samosata, because he says these things concerning the eternal substance and uncreated essence. For to discern, and to distinguish from the opposite, he opposed this to that 'He made': Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever. Against the Arians, however, again this very thing, and that he is not a servant. If, however, he were a creature, he would be a servant. Against Marcellus, however, and others, that they are two persons divided by hypostasis. Against the Marcionites, however, [it is argued] that the divinity is not anointed, but the humanity. Then, 'above your fellows,' he says; who, however, are the fellows, if not men? This is, Christ received the Spirit not by measure. You see how he joins to the discourse concerning the uncreated nature also the discourse concerning the dispensation. What is clearer than this? You see how the creature is not the same as that which is begotten. For he would not have divided [them], and added 'He made' in opposition to distinguish that. But to the Son he said: 'Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever.' Whom Theophylact has likewise followed. Nor does Theodoret say otherwise: By these things, he says, he openly shows that the angels indeed have a created nature, but the Only-begotten [has] an uncreated and eternal one. For 'Your throne, O God,' he says, 'is for ever and ever.' And this testimony certainly convicts the blasphemy of Arius. For it shows the eternal throne of the Word, and by the dyad of persons it refutes the confusion of Sabellius. This very thing also stops the impudent mouth of the Jews. These things are clear from the consensus of antiquity and the Catholic Church.

But it is helpful, for the sake of fuller confirmation, to add here the argument for the Deity of Christ, as it was once asserted against the Socinians. It stands thus in this place. That God, whose throne is for ever and ever, is the true and eternal GOD. But Christ is that God, whose throne is for ever and ever. Therefore. The minor premise is clear from the context: πρὸς δὲ τὸν ὑιὸν, ὁ θρόνος σου, ὁ Θεὸς, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος. 'But to the Son, Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever,' and again verse 9, διὰ τοῦτο ἔχρισέ σε ὁ Θεὸς σου. The Vulgate renders it: 'Therefore God, your God, has anointed you, O GOD.' So also the Racovian [Catechism]. The German version: 'Drum hat dich, O GOTT, dein GOtt gesalbet.' Similarly B. Luther, Beza, Piscator, the recent Dutch Version, and others. The following points establish the major premise: (1) The name אלהים, which is found in Psalm 45:7, from whence the Apostolic citation is made, is never used in its proper sense except of that supreme and eternal God. (2) Nor is there any reason why, if it denotes the eternal God in verse 3 or even 8, it should not denote Him here. I say that no trace of a disparate meaning appears in the context.
