Thus above, Psalm 34, verse 9, and 1 Peter 2, verse 4, by 'taste' a spiritual eating is truly indicated, and with CHRIST, Hebrews 2, verse 9, 'taste' is attributed in respect to death, it is entirely indicated that He truly swallowed and ate death. And when in Matthew 27, verse 34, it is said that when CHRIST had tasted the vinegar mixed with gall, He did not want to drink, this is to be understood concerning the continuation; He did not want, that is, to drink further. Therefore, 'taste' is not opposed to drinking simply. Hence Chrysostom in this place, as we said above, says: What is it, 'and they tasted the heavenly gift'? Is this not to taste the remission of sins? Therefore, this taste is truly the criterion of the reborn.

Furthermore, participation of the Holy Spirit denotes a true and real perception and communication, as appears above in Hebrews 2, verses 3, 4; chapter 3, verses 1, 14; and below in chapter 12, verse 8; and 1 Corinthians 10, verse 17. Those, therefore, who become partakers of the Holy Spirit regarding His gracious indwelling and the communion of gifts, they are truly reborn. And such are those who commit this sin. Therefore. Moreover, they are said to be those who have fallen away. But he who never stood is by no means said to fall. Compare Romans 14, verse 4; 1 Corinthians 10, verse 12. Furthermore, it is manifest that this deals with those converted through repentance or true penitence; which does not befit hypocrites. For the Apostle speaks of RENEWAL to repentance. To which repentance, therefore, it is impossible for them to be RENEWED, one must confess that they had performed it before the fall. But that renewal to repentance is understood as true repentance, which is nothing without true faith. Heavenly gifts, the good Word of the Gospel, and the mighty works of the age to come cannot be tasted except through true faith: And those who are partakers of the Spirit in such a way that they taste those things, cannot lack true faith. By τὸν μέλλοντα αἰῶνα in the Holy Scriptures is understood the state of the other life, Matth. XII. verse 32. Mark X. verse 30. Luke XVIII. verse 30. chap. XX. verse 35. to which the state of the present age is opposed, 1. Corinth. I. verse 20. chap. II. verse 6. 9. chap. III. verse 17. 1. Timoth. IV. verse 10. That, however, is not tasted by hypocrites. Add that the Apostle makes express mention of ἁγιασμοῦ & the Spirit of grace in the parallel passage Heb. X. verse 29. Which do not fall except to the reborn and truly believing.

Of such subjects, therefore, it is said that if they fall away, it is impossible for such to be renewed to repentance, which must be rightly understood again. 1. The Apostle says παραπεσόντας not of any fall whatsoever, but of apostasy from the faith, in which they were enlightened, by which they tasted the heavenly gifts, the good Word of GOD, the mighty works of the age to come, by which they were made partakers of the gifts of the HOLY SPIRIT, and were sanctified, which fall is most grave. For that παράπτωσις (falling away) occurs, as the blessed Dorscheus rightly says, primarily concerning the elements and principles of the Divine oracles, chap. 5, verse 12; concerning this and solid spiritual food; concerning the λόγον δικαιοσύνης (word of righteousness), verses 13, 14; concerning the good Word of God, chap. VI, 5. Whence it appears that this sin is not so much moral as it is dogmatic, and indeed runs directly and immediately against the truth of heavenly doctrine, that is, against the illumination and taste of heavenly doctrine: But also, although it can be committed in a certain way against the revelation of the Divine law, if, namely, one who is sufficiently informed about the nature and use of the law should nevertheless deny it against his conscience, it is, however, primarily committed against the doctrine of the Gospel. For this is the principle of illumination; this is the good Word of God, verses 4 and 5. Finally, this sin is not committed concerning some question of secondary revealed truth, but either concerning the whole Divine doctrine, or certainly concerning the very foundation of salvation. For here the principle of illumination resides most of all; this the good Word of GOD comprehends. Nor is this a matter of simple apostasy from the faith, but one which is joined with the loss of those goods—the grace of illumination, other heavenly gifts, the good Word of God, and the προγεύσματος (foretaste) of the powers of the world to come, and the communion of the Holy Spirit—and with the repeated crucifixion of the Son of GOD, and the reviling of the same.

They are called Ἀνασταυρῶντες (crucifying again) because they had previously driven Him to the cross, that is, they had affixed the Son of GOD to the cross with their sins, inasmuch as He was delivered up for our sins, wounded and stricken for our iniquities, and numbered among the transgressors, He laid down His life for us on the cross as a sacrifice, and bore our sins on the wood of the cross. Falling away voluntarily from this, therefore, and denying the same, they crucify the Son of GOD anew with the most grievous sin of apostasy, as if renewing His sufferings, cross, and wounds. Just as those who drove CHRIST, the Son of GOD, to the cross did not acknowledge Him, denied Him, and indeed crucified Him for the reason that they did not want Him to be held and received as the Son of God, and because He professed Himself to be the Son of God: So these apostates crucify the Son of God anew, denying Him and the power of His cross; they crucify Him by infidelity, apostasy, and blasphemies, by which they traduce the Son of God who was crucified for us, so that they would be ready to drive Him to the cross itself, just as those who crucified Him did, if they had Him in their hands. They crucify Him not in effect, indeed, but in intent. And thus far Grotius is not wrong. They crucify, that is, they show that they believe Christ was an impostor, and therefore worthy of the cross: And that they do this ἑαυτοῖς (to themselves), that is, they do it within themselves, while they approve of the deed. And not without reason did the blessed Hülsemann observe in his Breviarium. chap. page 59, that the intention of destroying and suppressing the acknowledged Evangelical truth is signified by that phrase, namely, through the repeated crucifixion of the Son of God and the trampling underfoot of His blood, committed at least in spirit.

They are called παραδειγματίζοντες because they hold Him up for a show, as the Vulgate says, or triumph by ostentation, as Ambrose, book II, de poenit., chap. II, says; or expose Him to mockery, as Erasmus says; or defame Him, as others do from Matthew 1, verse 19, where the Vulgate translated it as 'to traduce.' For it denotes an impious reviling, an ambitious blasphemy joined with the pleasure of the mind. In the parallel passage, they are said to trample underfoot the Son of God, and to count the blood of the Testament, by which they were sanctified, as profane, to hold it as the blood of a criminal, as Grotius explains, and to blaspheme the Spirit of grace, Heb. 10:29. And therefore it is manifest that the discourse is about such apostates who traduce the person and office of Christ, and not only utterly reject and hold in contempt those things by which salvation was to be secured for them—the blood of Christ and the Spirit of grace—but also impiously revile and blaspheme them. Whence they sin not only against the Son of man, as did those who for the most part affixed Him to the cross, but also against the Holy Spirit, because they blaspheme the Spirit of grace and reject and trample underfoot all the means of salvation, and thus voluntarily deprive themselves of a return to repentance, grace, and salvation. For this requirement, that they do all these things ἑκουσίως (willfully), is not to be neglected from Heb. 10:29, that is, not forced by the violence of persecutions and tyrants, as if against their will, but of their own accord and with full will, concerning which see those who have treated expressly of the sin against the Holy Spirit. The blessed Meisner in his Anthropol., the blessed Feuerbornius in a special booklet, Dr. Joh. Adam Scherzer in his inaugural dissertation, and others. For that this is an invincible proof that the discourse here is about the sin against the Holy Spirit: That sin which is irremissible is the sin against the Holy Spirit, as Christ testifies, Matt. 12:32. But this sin, of which the Apostle is currently speaking, is irremissible. For he says that it is ἀδύνατον (impossible) for such a one to be renewed to repentance. But to whom it is impossible to be renewed to repentance, to him it is impossible to obtain the remission of that sin for which or from which it is impossible for him to be renewed to repentance, and therefore that sin is truly irremissible. 2. Ἀδύνατον therefore

It is not for the Apostle to explain with the Socinians what is difficult; but just as the force of the word implies that it is altogether impossible, so it is said that that sin is not forgiven, neither in this world, nor in the world to come, Matt. 12:32. See Socinism. prof. sect. VII. art. IV. contr. VII. page 715. Nor is the remission to be considered impossible only in a certain respect, namely, that such persons do not listen to the Gospel, but crucify CHRIST and hold Him in derision, as Phil. Melanchthon has in his Corpus doctrinae: because those things do not restrict the predicate, but pertain to the description of the subject, and tacitly provide the reason why the remission of such apostasy is impossible, or the renewal of such apostates to repentance, just as the growth of thorns and thistles is the reason why the τέλος of that land is a curse, and the conclusion necessarily follows, verse 8. That Ἀδύνατον does not mean the same as difficult, B. Dorscheus proves, both from the nature of the word and from the nature of the thing. Ἀδύνατον, he says, is used in five ways in the Scriptures: 1. That which is contrary to justice, Matt. 6:24, 1 Cor. 10:21, Acts 4:20, 2 Cor. 13:8. 2. That which is difficult and rarely happening, as Matt. 5:14, Mark 9:39. 3. That which is ἀβόλητον, Gen. 43:32, Mark 6:5. 4. That which is ἀδύνατον to nature, John 3:4, Matt. 7:18. 5. Finally, that which is simply impossible, John 19. And this fifth meaning of τᾶ ἀδυνάτε is the principal and proper one. Therefore, it rightly holds in this place until the contrary is proven, especially since in Matt. 12:32 this sin is expressly called irremissible. But from the nature of the thing, the irremissibility of this sin appears, because it denies, blasphemes, and attacks all the causes of the remission of sins, against which it is directly and immediately directed, which other sins do not do. Just as, for example, a sick man lying lethally ill, if he persistently and maliciously rejects and attacks the medicines of whose efficacy he is convinced, nay, tramples upon the physician, desires him to be removed, and most foully blasphemes him, he is rendered incurable by that very constitution of his. Therefore, this sin is irremissible not only because of final impenitence, but because of its formal reason from which final impenitence originates. Therefore, the cause of the irremissibility of this sin is not to be sought 1. in any absolute decree, or in a defect of the antecedent will, as if it were destining justifying and saving grace for these sinners. For that this [grace] has extended and does extend itself to these sinners before they put on the horrible form of this sin, is clear from the criteria of true renewal exhibited above. For those to whom true renewal belongs, they have been invited by the antecedent will of God to the complex of heavenly grace. 2. Nor in a defect of the merit of Christ; for sinners against the Holy Spirit are said to crucify the Son of God to themselves again. Whence it is clear that Christ was crucified for them. For re-crucifixion presupposes crucifixion. Nowhere is the Devil said to re-crucify Christ to himself, although he persecutes Christ, because Christ was never crucified for him. Nor 3. in a defect of serious calling. For that it extends itself as it were to those who subsequently commit the sin against the Holy Spirit, is clear from this argument: Those sinners who were enlightened, tasted the heavenly gift, the good Word of God, and the mighty works of the age to come, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit, to them a serious calling to repentance and life was not lacking. But that happened to these sinners. Therefore, the calling was not lacking.

Vain indeed is Grotius's restriction, that it is impossible for such to be renewed to repentance through the law of Moses; for there is nothing about that in the Apostle, who simply says this is impossible: Nor did renewal to repentance consist for anyone through the law of Moses: which is altogether impossible without faith had from the Gospel, Heb. 11:6. Nor does it appear that the law of Moses is valid here, where it is a matter of apostasy from the faith of the Gospel. Finally, in the parallel, the remedy is not removed only by the law of Moses, but by the Gospel, οὐκέτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία, Heb. 10:26, because there is no remedy left even from the sacrifice of Christ for the sin against the Holy Spirit, and thus it is simply irremissible. 3. Ἀδύνατον it is said, such πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν, to be renewed again. Therefore, it is necessary that they had been renewed before. For those of whom there is talk of being renewed again, it is necessary that they had been truly renewed before. Therefore, both the word πάλιν and the particle ἀνὰ are to be observed, by which both iterations are noted. The Calvinists therefore err when they deny that those of whom there is talk here were truly renewed or reborn, τῇ ὑποθέσει δουλεύοντες, because, namely, the reborn cannot fall from faith or lose the Holy Spirit, to which this passage is diametrically opposed. However, the active ἀνακαινίζειν is held in the Greek, not because the text is corrupt, since all copies agree, but because either a reciprocal pronoun is understood, as Erasmus wishes, to renew themselves again to repentance: Or, which is more approved by Estius, the verb to renew is referred to the Ministers of the Word, through whom God renews, converts, and saves. (4) The phrase ἀνακαινίζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν, to be renewed to repentance, is to be observed. Which supposes that those whose apostasy the Apostle notes here had previously performed repentance. But that those who truly performed repentance were also truly believers, there is no doubt. Which is again to be noted against the Calvinist hypothesis. Estius explains the opinion of the Fathers, who seem to take this passage concerning baptism which cannot be repeated, in such a way that they seem to look especially and properly to the effect of baptism, that is, to the renewal itself, to be received in that manner and with that ease with which it had been acquired through baptism, so that the sense is: a man once renewed by the sacrament of baptism, if he has relapsed into the oldness of sin, cannot by performing repentance again, such as he had performed before baptism, attain that newness which he had received in baptism. The error of the Novatians, who denied repentance to those who had fallen after baptism, even if some take it as if God himself closes the doors of his grace to them, with the blessed Fevvrbornius loc. cit. page 7. Others, however, explain it in such a way that they cut off only the hope of pardon to be granted by the Church, by reason of the certainty of future remission: See the blessed Chemnitius part I. Exam. Concil. Trid. on justifying faith, from the Tripartita book IX. Ambrose book I. on repentance, chapter II. proves it. Compare Joh. Forbesius à Corse Instr. Histor. Theol. book XIV. chapter 3.

Ἀνασταυρῶντας ἑαυτοῖς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ παραδειγματίζοντας) See how great a sin it is to defect from Christianity. For those who do that, by that very fact show that they believe Christ was an impostor, and therefore worthy of the cross and all ignominy. They are said to do this ἑαυτοῖς, that is, among themselves. And by an excellent figure they are said to do that which they approve as done. In a similar sense he teaches below in chapter 10:29 that by such men the Son of God is trampled underfoot, that is, most foully treated, and his blood, by which he ratified the covenant, is held as profane blood, that is, the blood of a criminal man. Concerning the meaning of the word παραδειγματίζειν see Matthew 1:19.

Latin:

5. Γευσαμένυς δυνάμεις μέλλοντος αἰῶνος, qui gustaverunt virtutes futuri sæculi, hoc est, qui beatitudinis cœlestis in altera vita non tan- tum aliquam speciem, sed ipsasmet virtutes, & bona ipsa cœlestia perceperunt, imo intimis veluti medullis exceperunt, ac si delicias illas de ligno vitæ, Apoc. 2. vers. 7. 17. manna ab- sconditum, & aquas vivas fluvii crystallini de throno DEI & Agni procedentes degustârint, iisdemque se refecerint Apoc. 22. v. 7. πρόγευσμα & προποτισμόν suavitatis bonorum cœlestium sentiendo & experiundo. Loquitur de iis, inquit B. Hunnius, qui fuerant illuminati agnitione Do- mini nostri JESU CHRISTI, qui est lux vera, ut intelligant, hanc de JESU CHRISTO doćtri- nam esse indubiam & cœlestem veritatem. De- inde quod gustaverint donum cœleste, id est, vive- re jam in illis cœperat CHRISTUS, & per fidem sancita in illorum cordibus fuerat spes hæreditatis Filiorum DEI. Præterea participes faćti erant Spiritus sanćti, quo erant conversi, regenerati, il- lustrati, & sanćtificati. Gustaverunt insuper bonum DEI Verbum, & virtutes futuri seculi, dum ex DEI Verbo divitias bonitatis Divinæ, & quendam quasi sensum & gustum æternæ vitæ re- gnique cœlestis perceperunt, obsignati scilicet Spiritu sanćto, tanquam arrha hæreditatis elećtorum. Flacius hæc ita exposuit: Denotat illos quatuor hisce proprietatibus, quod sint ii, qui primum vere fuerant illustrati per Verbum & Spiritum san- ćtum, hoc est, qui veram fidem in CHRISTUM habuerant, deinde qui etiam donum cæleste gusta- verant, quod de justificatione & pace cordis eam consequente intelligo : tertio qui Spiritum san- ćtum perceperant, quæ est donatio Spiritus sanćti cum suis gratiis aut donis, totaque illa regenera- tione : quarto loco ponit gustationem Verbi DEI, quæ est vera cognitio Verbi per Spiritum veraque consolatio & regimen cordis nostri, ex Verbo Dei perpetuo nobis proveniens. Virtutes futuri seculi sunt illud ineffabile piorum gaudium, ex Verbo & Spiritu sanćto nobis proveniens : qui vere est gu- stus quidam bonorum ac efficaciæ venturæ illius vi- tæ: quo quidem etiam CHRISTUS ipse alias hilarius exultavit, cum interdum etiam contra i- psimet olim & omnes pii dolores inferni sentiant. Hoc ille modo descripsit tum antecedentia istud tantum peccatum, tum etiam ipsas personas, quæ potissimum tam horribiliter corruere solcant, ut plane resurgere nequeant. Quæ singula si ex- pendamus, prout par est, (quanto minus, si universa) non possunt convenire hypocritis, aut iis, qui initium tantum fidei quoddam ha- bent, vel dona communia, ut Calviniani con- tendunt, sed vere renatis & fidelibus solum, qui si uspiam in sacris literis emphatice descripti funt, hic profećto designati sunt efficacissime. De illuminationis certe initio sine vera fide, levi gustu sine fruitione, de Spiritus sanćti donis non sanćtificantibus, & hypocritis communibus, de mundi renovati seu Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti quibusdam miraculis perceptis, hæc cum Pisca- tore, Tossano, Pareo explicare, est textum sole luculentiorem insigniter obscurare. Rećte ob- servat B. Dorscheus: Gustum notare objećti ve- ram perceptionem, conf. Psalm. XXXIV. vers. 9. Proverb. XXXI. vers. 18. 1. Petr. II. vers. 3. Ebr. II. vers. 9. Hinc cum de aliqua re gustus iste nota- tur, simul etiam notatur perceptio & vera sensio, Matth. XVI. vers. 18. Marc. IX. vers. 1. Luc. IX. vers. 27. Johan. VIII. vers. 52. ubi simul etiam ju- xta Ebræorum dicendi formam verbum sensus non nudam sensionem, sed & motus annexos annotat.

Unde cum gustasse illi prolabentes dicuntur bonum Dei Verbum &c. vera Evangelii agnitio, vera cum CHRISTO unio, vera dulcedinis vitæ æter- næ prægustatio intelligitur. Itaque male Zan- chius in Misc. pag. 286. Sohnius l. supra cit. pag. 776. & Rob. Sarisburiensis pagin. 51. distinguunt inter gustum & esum. Gustaverunt, inquiunt, non autem comederunt, deglutiverunt, nedum ventriculo retinuerunt. Unde concludunt, vere renatos non fuisse, nec ad manducationem spiritua- lem pervenisse. Non convenit usui Scripturæ distinctio. Nam in Sacris gustare idem est, quod comedere, conf. 1. Samuel. XIV. vers. 24. 27. 28. & 29. Sic supra Psalm. XXXIV. vers. 9. & 1. Petr. II. vers. 4. per gustum revera manducatio spiritua- lis indicatur & cum CHRISTO Ebr. II. vers. 9. gustus respectu mortis tribuitur, omnino indica- tur, ipsum vere mortem deglutivisse & comedisse. Et quando Matth. XXVII. vers. 34. dicitur, cum CHRISTUS gustasset acetum felle mixtum, nolu- isse bibere, de continuatione hoc intelligendum est, noluit scilicet bibere ulterius. Itaque gustus non opponitur bibitioni simpliciter. Hinc Chrysosto- mus hoc loco, ut supra diximus, quid est, inquit, & gustaverunt donum cæleste: Nonne hoc est re- missionem peccatorum gustare? Vere itaque κρι- τήριον Renatorum est iste gustus.

Porro μετοχὴ Spiritus sancti notat veram rea- lemque perceptionem & communicationem, uti ap- paret supra Ebr. II. vers. 3. 4. cap. III. vers. 1. 14. & infra cap. XII. vers. 8. & 1. Corinth. X. vers. 17. Qui itaque Spiritus sancti quoad gratiosam inhabi- tationem & χαρισμάτων communionem fiunt μέ- τοχοι, illi revera renati sunt. Tales autem sunt committentes hoc peccatum. Ergo. Adhæc di- cuntur illi παραπεσόντες. At qui nunquam ste- tit, cadere nequaquam dicitur. Confer. Rom. XIV. vers. 4. 1. Corinth. X. v. 12. Præterea de con- versis per μετάνοιαν vel veram pœnitentiam hic agi, manifestum est; quæ non convenit hypo- critis. Loquitur enim Apostolus de RENO- VATIONE ad pœnitentiam. Ad quam ergo pœnitentiam eos RENOVARI ἀδύνατον, eam illos prius ante lapsum egisse, fateri oportet. At illa renovatio ad pœnitentiam de vera pœ- nitentia intelligitur, quæ sine fide vera nulla est. Dona cælestia, bonum Evangelii Verbum, & virtutes seculi futuri non possunt nisi per fi- dem veram gustari: Et qui ita Spiritus partici- pes sunt, ut illa gustent, fide vera carere non pos- sunt. Per τὸν μέλλοντα αἰῶνα in sacris literis in- telligitur status alterius vitæ, Matth. XII. vers. 32. Marc. X. vers. 30. Luc. XVIII. vers. 30. cap. XX. vers. 35. cui status præsentis seculi opponitur, 1. Corinth. I. vers. 20. cap. II. vers. 6. 9. cap. III. vers. 17. 1. Timoth. IV. vers. 10. Ille autem non gusta- tur ab hypocritis. Adde quod ἁγιασμοῦ & Spi- ritus gratiæ disertam mentionem faciat Aposto- lus in parallelo loco Ebr. X. vers. 29. Quæ non cadunt nisi in renatos & vere credentes.

De talibus ergo subjectis dicitur, quod si la- bantur, impossibile sit, tales renovari ad pœni- tentiam, quod dextre iterum intelligendum. 1. παραπεσόντας dicit Apostolus non de quovis lapsu, sed de apostasia à fide, in qua illumina- ti, qua gustarunt dona cœlestia, bonum DEI Verbum, virtutes futuri seculi, qua partici- pes facti sunt donorum SPIRITUS SAN- CTI, & sanctificati, qui lapsus est gravissimus. Fit enim παράπτωσις illa, ut recte B. Dorscheus, potissimum circa elementa & principia oraculorum Divinorum, cap. 5. vers. 12. circa hoc & solidum cibum spiritualem, circa λόγον δικαιοσύνης vers. 13. 14. circa bonum Verbum Dei cap. VI. 5. Unde apparet, hoc peccatum non tam esse morale, quam dogmaticum, & quidem directe & immediate currere contra cælestis doctrinæ veritatem, hoc est, contra illuminationem & gustum doctrinæ cælestis : Sed & quamvis certa ratione, & contra revelationem legis Divinæ committi possit, si scilicet is sufficienter de natura & usu legis informatus, contra conscientiam tamen abnegaret, potissimum tamen committi contra doctrinam Evangelii. Hæc enim est principium illuminationis, hæc est bonum Dei Verbum, vers. 4. & 5. Denique hoc peccatum non committi circa quæstionem aliquam secundariæ veritatis revelatæ, sed vel circa totam doctrinam Divinam, vel certe circa ipsum fundamentum salutis. Hic enim potissimum illuminationis principium residet, hoc comprehendit bonum DEI Verbum. Nec de simplici hic agitur à fide apostasia, sed quæ conjuncta est, & cum illorum bonorum amissione, gratiæ illuminationis, donorum aliorum cælestium, boni Dei Verbi, & προγεύσματος virtutum futuri seculi, ac communionis Spiritus sancti, & cum iterata crucifixione Filii DEI, ac criminatione ejusdem.

Ἀνασταυρῶντες dicuntur, quod prius in crucem egerint, hoc est, peccatis suis cruci affixerint Filium DEI, utpote qui traditus est propter peccata nostra, vulneratus & percussus propter iniquitates nostras, & inter transgressores numeratus in cruce animam suam pro nobis posuit in sacrificium, ac peccata nostra tulit in ligno crucis. Ab hoc ergo deficientes voluntarie, eundemque abnegantes, noviter gravissimo apostasiæ peccato Filium DEI crucifigunt, passiones, crucem, ac vulnera ejus veluti renovando. Ut qui in crucem agebant CHRISTUM, Filium DEI non agnoscebant, abnegabant, imo ideo crucifigebant, quod nollent eum haberi ac suscipere pro Filio Dei, & quia se Filium Dei profitebatur : Ita denuo crucifigunt hi apostatæ Filium Dei, abnegantes eundem, & vim crucis ejus : crucifigunt infidelitate, apostasia & blasphemiis, quibus pro nobis crucifixum Dei Filium traducunt, ut vel in crucem ipsam, æque ac qui crucifixerunt eundem, acturi essent, si in manu sua haberent. Crucifigunt non effectu quidem, attamen affectu. Et hactenus non male Grotius. Crucifigunt, id est, ostendunt credere se Christum fuisse impostorem, ac proinde dignum cruce : Idque facere ἑαυτοῖς, id est, apud se id facere, dum factum approbant. Nec abs re B. Hülsemannus observavit in Breviar. cap. pag. 59. animum delendi & opprimendi agnitam veritatem Evangelicam ea phrasi significari, per iteratam nempe crucifixionem Filii Dei & sanguinis ejus conculcationem, animo saltem commissam.

Dicuntur παραδειγματίζοντες, quod ostentui habeant, ut Vulgata, vel ostentatione triumphent, ut Ambros. libr. II. de pœnit. cap. II. ludibrio exponant, ut Erasmus, vel infament, ut alii è Matth. 1. vers. 19. ubi reddidit Vulgatus traducere. Denotatur enim impia criminatio, ambitiosa & cum voluptate animi conjuncta blasphematio. In loco parallelo dicuntur pedibus conculcare Filium Dei, & sanguinem Testamenti prophanum ducere, quo sanctificati sunt, habere pro sanguine hominis facinorosi, ut explicat Grotius, & Spiritum gratiæ blasphemare, Ebr. 10, 29. Ideoque manifestum est, de talibus apostatis sermonem esse, qui personam & officium Christi traducunt, & ea, per quæ ipsis salus consta- re debebat, sanguinem Christi, & Spiritum gratiæ non modo penitus reprobent, & contemptui ha- beant, sed & impie criminentur, ac blasphement. Unde non solum in Filium hominis peccant, quem- admodum!illi, qui eundem cruci affixere plerique, sed etiam in Spiritum sanctum, quia Spiritum gra- tiæ blasphemant, & omnia media salutis repro- bant, ac pedibus conculcant, adeoque semetipsos reditu ad pœnitentiam, gratiam, & salutem volun- tarie privant. Nam hoc requisitum, quod hæc o- mnia ἑκουσίως faciant, non negligendum est ex Ebr. 10, 29. hoc est, non coacti vi persequutionum & tyrannorum, veluti inviti, sed sponte sua & plena voluntate, quo de vid. qui ex professo de peccatq in Spiritum S. tractarunt. B. Meisnerus in Anthro- pol. B. Fevverbornius peculiari opusculo, Dn. D. Joh. Adam. Scherzerus disputat. inaug. & alii. De peccato enim in Spiritum sanctum hic agi, docet hæc invieta ἀπόδειξις: Illud peccatum, quod irremissi- bile est, peccatum est in Spiritum sanctum, teste Christo, Matth. 12, 32. At hoc peccatum, de quo Apostolus inpræsentiarum agit, est irremissibile. Dicit enim, quod ἀδύνατον sit, talem renovari ad pœ- nitentiam. Cui autem impossibile est renovari ad pœnitentiam, illi impossibile est consequi remissi- onem illius peccati, ob quod vel ex quo ei ad pœ- nitentiam renovari impossibile, adeoque pecca- tum illud vere est irremissibile. 2. Ἀδύνατον ergo

Apostoli non est cum Socinianis explicandum, quod difficile sit; sed quemadmodum importat vis vocis, quod omnino id sit impossibile, ideo dicitur peccatum illud non remitti, neque in hoc, neque in futuro seculo Matth. 12, 32. Vid. Socinism. prof. se&. VII. art. IV. contr. VII. pagin. 715. neque tan- tum secundum quid impossibilis censenda remissio, quod usque nempe tales non auscultant Evangelio, sed crucifigunt CHRISTUM, & ludibrio habent, ut Phil. Melanchthon in corp. doctrinæ habet: quia illa non restringunt prædicatum, sed pertinent ad descriptionem subjecti, taciteque reddunt causam, cur impossibilis sit talis apostasiæ remissio, vel a- postatarum ejusmodi renovatio ad pœnitentiam, sicut proventus spinarum & tribulorum causa est, cur τέλος terræ istius sit maledictio, & necessario sequatur conclusio, vers. 8. Ἀδύνατον non esse i- dem, quod difficile, B. Dorscheus probat, tum ex na- tura vocabuli, tum ex natura rei. Ἀδύνατον, inquit, quinque modis in sacris dici, 1. illud quod est à justi- tia alienum, Matth. 6, 24. 1. Cor. 10, 21. Actor. 4, 20. 2. Corinth. 13, 8. 2. quod est difficile & raro contin- gens, ut Matth. 5, 14. Marc. 9, 39. 3. quod est ἀβό- λητον, Gen. 43, 32. Marc. 6, 5. 4. quod est ἀδύνατον naturæ Joh. 3, 4. Matth. 7, 18. 5. denique quod sim- pliciter est impossibile, Johan. 19. Atque hæc quinta τᾶ ἀδυνάτε significatio est principalis & propria. I- taque hoc loco tamdiu obtinet merito, donec contrari- um probetur, præsertim cum Matth. 12, 32. hoc pec- catum diserte irremissibile dicatur. Ex natura au- tem rei apparet hujus peccati irremissibilitas, quia abnegat, blasphemat, & oppugnat omnes causas re- missionis peccatorum, contra quas directe & imme- diate fertur, quod non faciunt peccata alia. Sicut, exempli gratia, ægrotus lethaliter decumbens, si medi- camenta, de quorum efficacia convictus est, pertina- citer & malitiose repellit, oppugnet, imo medicum conculcet, è medio sublatum cupiat, & fœdissime bla- sphemet, is ex illa ipsa sua constitutione incurabilis red- ditur. Itaq; hoc peccatum irremissibile est non tantum propter finalem impœnitentiam, sed propter formalem sum rationem, ex qua finalis impœnitentia proma- nat. Non itaque causa irremiffibilitatis hujus pecca- ti quærenda est 1. in absoluto aliquo decreto, pel in de- fectu voluntatis antecedentis ceu gratiam justifican- tem & salvantem his peccatoribus destinantis. Nam hanc ad hos peccatores sese extendisse & extendere an- tequam in horribilem hujus peccati figuram esse in- duerent, ex criteriis veræ renovationis supra exhibi- tis liquet. Quibus enim vera renovatio competit, illi antecedente Dei voluntate ad complexum gratiæ cœlestis invitati sunt. 2. Neque in defectu meriti Christi; Dicuntur enim peccatores in Spiritum S. Filium Dei sibi rursus crucifigere. Unde liquet, Christum pro ipsis crucifixum fuisse. Recrucifixio enim præsupponit crucifixionem. Nuspiam Diabo- lus dicitur recrucifigere Christum sibi, quamvis Chri- stum persequatur, quia ipsi Christus nunquam cruci- fixus fuit. Neque 3. in defectu seriæ vocationis. Il- lam enim ad eos quasi sese extendere, qui postmodum peccatum in Spiritum sanctum committunt, hoc ar- gumento liquet: Qui peccatores fuerunt illuminati, donum cœleste gustarunt, bonum Dei Verbum, ac vir- tutes futuri seculi, & participes facti fuerunt Spiritus sancti, illis non defuit seria ad pœnitentiam & vitam vocatio. Atqui id contigit istis peccatoribus. Ergo vocatio non defuit.

Vana vero est Grotii restrictio, quod impossibile sit, tales renovari ad pœnitentiam per legem Mosis; nam de illa nihil penes Apostolum, qui simpliciter hoc dicit impossibile: Neque per legem Mosis ul- li constitit renovatio ad pœnitentiam: quæ sine fide ex Evangelio habita impossibilis omnino est, Ebr. 11, 6. Nec quod lex Mosis hic valeat, ubi de apostasia à fide Evangelii est, apparet. Denique in parallelo non removetur tantum remedium per legem Mosis, sed per Evangelium, ὀυκέτι περὶ ἁμαρ- τιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία, Ebr. 10, 26. quod nec ab hostia Christi pro peccato in Spiritum sanctum re- liquum sit remedium, adeoque simpliciter illud sit irremissibile. 3. Ἀδύνατον dicitur, tales πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν, iterum renovari. Eos ergo oportet antea renovatos fuisse. De quibus enim iterum renovandis sermo est, illi antea vere renovati fue- rint oportet. Observanda ergo tum vox πάλιν, tum particula ἀνὰ, qua utraque iteratio notatur. Er- rant itaque Calviniani, cum eos, de quibus hic agi- tur, negant vere fuisse renovatos aut renatos, τῇ ὑποθέσει δουλεύοντες, quod nempe renati non pos- sint fide excidere, aut Spiritum sanctum amittere, cui hic locus καδδιάμετρον oppositus est. Habetur au- tem in Græco activum ἀνακαινίζειν, non quod tex- tus corruptus sit, siquidem exemplaria omnia consonent, sed quod vel subintelligatur Prono- men reciprocum, ut Erasmus vult, rursus renovare se ad pœnitentiam: Vel quod Estio magis probatur, verbum renovare ad Ministros Verbi referatur, per quos Deus renovat, convertit, salvat. (4) Ob- servanda phrasis ἀνακαινίζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν, renova- ri ad pœnitentiam. Quæ eos, quorum apostasiam hic notat Apostolus, antea pœnitentiam egisse, supponit. Qui autem vere pœnitentiam egere, il- los etiam vere fideles fuisse dubium nullum est. Quod iterum contra Calvinianam hypothesin no- tandum. Patrum sententiam, qui hunc locum de baptismo non iterabili videntur accipere, sic ex- plicat Estius, quod videantur potissimum ac proprie respicere ad effectum baptismi, id est, ad ipsam re- novationem, eo modo eaque facilitate, qua per ba- ptismum fuerat acquisita, recipiendam, ut sensus sit, hominem semel sacramento baptismi renova- tum, si relapsus fuerit in vetustatem peccati, non posse iterum acta pœnitentia, qualem ante bapti- smum egerat, eam consequi novitatem, quam in baptismo acceperat. Novatianorum errorem, qui prolapsis post baptismum pœnitentiam ne- gabant, etiamsi nonnulli sic accipiant, quasi Deus ipse iis gratiæ suæ fores præcludat, cum B. Fevvrbornio loc. cit. pag. 7. Alii tamen ita ex- plicant, quod ipsis tantum spem veniæ ab Ecclesia concedendæ, ratione certitudinis futuræ remissio- nis præsciderint: Vid. B. Chemnitius part. I. Ex- am. Concil. Trid. de fid. justif. è Tripartita l. IX. Ambrosius libr. I. de pœnit. cap. II. probat. Conf. Joh. Forbesius à Corse Instr. Histor. Theol. l. XIV. cap. 3.

Ἀνασταυρῶντας ἑαυτοῖς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ παραδειγμα- τίζοντας) Vide quantum sit peccatum, à Christianismo deficere. Nam qui id faciunt, eo ipso ostendunt, cre- dere se, Christum fuisse impostorem, ac proinde di- gnum' cruce, omnique ignominia. Dicuntur hoc fa- cere ἑαυτοῖς, id est, apud se. Et egregia figura dicun- tur facere id, quod approbant factum. Pari sensu infra docet cap. 10, 29. à talibus hominibus proculcari, id est, fœdissime tractari Dei Filium, & sanguinem ejus, quo fœdus sanxit, haberi pro sanguine profano, id est, fa- cinorosi hominis. De significatu vocis παραδειγματίζειν vide Matth. 1, 19.

## 6:7
Vers. 7.

Γῆ γὰρ ἡ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπ' αὐτῆς πολλάκις ἐρχόμενον ὑετὸν καὶ τίκτουσα βοτάνην εὔθετον ἐκείνοις δι' οὓς καὶ γεωργεῖται, μεταλαμβάνει εὐλογίας ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ) To drink is also said of the earth in Greek, when it is irrigated. Anacreon: Ἡ γῆ μέλαινα πίνει. And to the Hebrews רוה to be inebriated Psalm 65:11. Βοτάνη in this place is worth the same as the Hebrew דשא, as can be seen in Genesis 1:11, where in the Greek it is βοτάνη. It signifies, however, everything that is born from the earth, even crops. He called εὔθετον useful to those for whom it is cultivated, that is, to the masters of the land: See Luke 14:35. Such land has received a blessing from God, that is, it is called the land of God, as can be seen in Genesis 13:10, Ezekiel 28:3. ברך εὐλογεῖν signifies many things, but among others also to praise, to celebrate, as Psalm 12:15, Psalm 145:1, Genesis 9:26. To the earth corresponds man taken from the earth. To the rain, those gifts of which there was mention above. Thus βαπτίζειν πνέυματι, Mark 1:8. and prophecy is called a drop. The crops are the works of piety. The Lord whose fruits these are, is God. From him they are named, they are called children of God.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Γῆ γὰρ ἡ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπ' αὐτῆς πολλάκις ἐρχόμενον ὑετὸν καὶ τίκτουσα βοτάνην εὔθετον ἐκείνοις δι' οὓς καὶ γεωργεῖται, με- ταλαμβάνει εὐλογίας ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ) Bibere etiam Græcis terra dicitur, cum irrigatur. Anacreon: Ἡ γῆ μέλαινα πίνει. Et Ebræis רוה inebriari Psal. 65, 11. Βοτάνη hoc loco idem valet, quod Ebræum דשא, ut videre est Genes. 1, 11. ubi in Græco est βοτάνη. Significat autem o- mne id, quod ex terra nascitur, etiam fruges. Εὔθε- τον dixit utilem iis, propter quos colitur, id est, fundi Dominis: Vide Luc. 14, 35. Talis terra benedictionem accepit à Deo, id est, vocatur terra Dei, ut videre est Genes. 13, 10. Ezech. 28, 3. ברך εὐλογεῖν multa signi- ficat, sed inter alia etiam laudare, celebrare, ut Psal. 12, 15. Psalm. 145, 1. Genes. 9, 26. Terræ respondet ho- mo ex terra sumptus. Imbri dona illa, quorum supra fuit mentio. Sic βαπτίζειν πνέυματι, Marc. 1, 8. & pro- phetia stilla dicitur. Fruges sunt opera pietatis. Do- minus cujus isti fructus sunt, est Deus. Ab eo denomi- nantur, vocantur filii Dei.

## 6:8
Ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους) A rough forest comes up, and burrs and thistles, as it is in Virgil. See also Matt. 13, 7. He did not say here τίκτουσα as just now, but ἐκφέρουσα, casting out as if it were an abortion. An allusion to the passage in Gen. 3, 17. 18.

Ἀδόκιμος) Such land is displeasing to its Lord.

Καὶ κατάρας ἐγγὺς) It will shortly come to pass, if it remains such, that the Lord will curse such land. See Matt. 21, 19. Mark 11, 21. ἐγγὺς signifies that a thing will happen shortly, Matt. 24, 32. ch. 26, 18. Mark 13, 28. Luke 20, 30. ch. 21, 31. John 2, 13. ch. 6, 4. ch. 7, 2. ch. 11, 55. So also below ch. 8, 23.

Ἧς τὸ τέλος εἰς καῦσιν) This will be the outcome, that at length the Lord, weary of the expenses, will burn up the farm and the trees and the thorn-bushes, and have it for a wasteland. Similar is Luke 13, 6. and following. Add Matt. 3, 10. and ch. 13, 30. Moreover, this is a Metonymy. For it is said of the land, which properly belongs to those things that stand upon the land. Τέλος is the outcome of a thing, as Rom. 6, 21. 22. Phil. 3, 19. To the thorns and thistles corresponds the contempt of the Christian religion: to the master's curse, damnation, fire, the punishment of Gehenna.

The Vulgate rendered the word πιοῦσα as 'drinking', but in Greek it is an Aorist, having the meaning of the past, 'when it has drunk', as Estius himself warns, and Erasmus explains: The explanation of the words δι' οὓς by Faber and the Syriac, 'for whose sake', so that it may be referred to the Lords, is even more approved than the interpretation of the Vulgate, 'from whom', which the farmers it refers. He understands Εὐλογίαν as the more ample blessing which is provided by GOD, so that the herb which it has produced may arrive at the maturity of the crop, Mark 4:28. The Ἀπόλυσις, which is to be understood, is this: Thus faithful hearers, among whom the seed of the Divine Word bears fruit, are blessed by GOD and receive increases of gifts, Matt. 25:29, Mark 4:25. Estius renders this sense by antithesis: But if, after it has often drunk the rain coming upon it, instead of good and useful herb, it brings forth thorns and thistles for its cultivators; it is reprobated and deserted as ungrateful, and is destined for burning. For this seems to be the curse he understands. The CONSUMMATION of which, in Greek τέλος, the end is into COMBUSTION. This alone, he says, remains for it, that the fire be applied to the vicious and useless herbs which it has brought forth. Others interpret the combustion as that of the earth itself. For rustics are accustomed to burn up the darnel and other defects of the fields by the roots, just as Pliny mentions in book XVIII of his Natural History, chapter XXX, from the Georgics of Virgil, or to cut away unfruitful earth in the form of sods and destine it for the hearth. Similar are the comparisons which we read in the Gospel about the tree and the branch not bearing fruit, and therefore being cast into the fire, as Estius again not incorrectly says. This Ἀπόδοσις will be: Thus apostates, by whom the rain of the Word and of grace is drunk in vain, when they bring forth only thorns and thistles, will be cursed by GOD, Matt. 25, verse 30. How much more must this be held concerning such notable apostates, who after such great and so many manifold gifts voluntarily fall away, and traduce the Divine will, and crucify the Son of GOD himself again? B. Dorscheus explains this similitude thus: It is illustrated, he says, by the similitude of the earth, which is proposed as being of a twofold condition: One is fertile and fruitful, the other sterile and unfruitful. The former is described as being γῆ πιοῦσα τὸν ἐπ’ αὐτῆς πολλάκις ἐρχόμενον ὑετὸν, the earth drinking in the rains often falling upon it, bringing forth plants suitable for those by whom it is cultivated, and receiving a blessing from GOD. Where the causes of fruitfulness are: 1. The Divine blessing, 2. The dispensation of means, among which is also the suitable weather, 3. The farmers, who as ministering causes cultivate the earth. 4. The receptivity of the earth itself, which is therefore said to partake (μεταλαμβάνειν) and to drink (πιεῖν). The latter is described both by its effects and by its consequences. With respect to the former, it is said to bear thistles and thorns. With respect to the latter, it is said to be held as reprobate and cursed, which at length is to experience a conflagration instead of a harvest. The Ἀπόδοσις or the whole Apostolic comparison is this: Just as that earth finally attains the effect of the Divine blessing which is tractable under the hand of the farmers, and does not resist the plow and the harrow, which drinks the rains fallen from heaven, and does not allow them to flow away because of stoniness, and hence brings forth plants suitable and useful. On the contrary, however, that which is refractory and resists the cultivators, and which does not absorb the rains but rejects them, and thus instead of the desired plants brings forth thistles and thorns, is deservedly held as reprobate and cursed, which is finally to be subjected to fire. Thus those hearers of the Divine Word become partakers of the Divine blessing who admit the heavenly culture, retain the Divine seed, drink the rains of heavenly graces, and bring forth the desired fruits, and in this way strive toward perfection and maturity. On the contrary, however, those who are indeed under culture for some time, admit the seed, taste the rains of heavenly graces, but always only begin to grow and flourish, but do not continue to grow, nor rise to maturity, nay rather at length shake off the seed, and on the other hand generate thorns and thistles of malicious denial and blasphemous persecution, are most rightly held as reprobate and cursed, whom it is impossible to lead to fruitfulness, nay rather it is necessary that they be delivered to eternal destruction by the just final judgment of GOD.

PART III. Exhortation to constancy in faith, and immovable hope.

Latin:

Ἐκφέρουσα δὲ ἀκάνθας καὶ τριβόλους) Subit aspera sylva, lappaæque tribulique, ut est apud Vir- gilium. Vide & Matth. 13, 7. Non dixit hic τίκτουσα ut modo, sed ἐκφέρουσα, ejiciens velut abortus. Allusio ad locum Gen. 3, 17. 18.

Ἀδόκιμος) Displicet talis terra Domino suo.

Καὶ κατάρας ἐγγὺς) Brevi futurum est, si talis ma- net, ut Dominus terram talem execretur. Vide Matth. 21, 19. Marc. 11, 21. ἐγγὺς rem brevi futuram significat Matth. 24, 32. cap. 26, 18. Marc. 13, 28. Luc. 20, 30. cap. 21, 31. Johan. 2, 13. cap. 6, 4. cap. 7, 2. cap. 11, 55. Sic & infra c. 8, 23.

Ἧς τὸ τέλος εἰς καῦσιν) Hic erit exitus, ut tandem Dominus pertæsus sum- ptuum, villam & arbores, & senticeta exurat, habeat- que derelictui. Simile est Luc. 13, 6. & seqq. Adde Matth. 3, 10. & cap. 13, 30. Est autem hic Μετωνυμία. Nam de terra dicitur, quod proprie iis rebus convenit, quæ terræ superstant. Τέλος rei exitus, ut Roman. 6, 21. 22. Philipp. 3, 19. Sentibus & tribulis respondet contemptus Christianæ religionis: maledicto herili damnatio, incen- dio, pœna Gehennæ.

Vulgata vocem πιοῦσα reddidit bibens, sed in Græco est Aoristus, Præteriti significationem habens, cum biberit, monente ipsomet Estio, & exponente Erasmo: Magis etiam probatur Estio verborum δι' οὓς explicatio Fabri & Syri, propter quos, ut ad Dominos referatur, quam Vulgatæ interpretatio, à quibus, quæ agricolas respicit. Εὐλογίαν de ampliori benedictione in- telligit, quæ præstatur à DEO, ut herba, quam produxit, ad segetis maturitatem proveniat, Marc. 4, 28. Ἀπόλυσις, quæ subintelligenda, hæc est: Ita fideles auditores, apud quos semen Verbi Divini fructificat, à DEO benedicuntur, & incrementa donorum accipiunt, Matth. 25, 29. Marc. 4, 25. Antithesi hunc reddit Estius sen- sum: Si vero, postquam sæpe venientem super se bi- berit imbrem, pro herba bona & utili, spinas ac tribulos cultoribus suis afferat; tanquam ingrata reprobatur ac deseritur, atque incendio destina- tur. Hanc enim videtur intelligere maledictio- nem. Cujus CONSUMMATIO, Græce τέ- λος, finis in COMBUSTIONEM. Hoc so- lum, inquit, ei restat, ut vitiosis ac inutilibus her- bis, quas protulit, ignis subjiciatur. Alii combustio- nem interpretantur ipsius terræ. Solent enim ru- stici lolium, & cætera agrorum vitia, stirpitus ex- urere, quemadmodum ex Georgicis Virgilii comme- morat Plinius libr. XVIII. naturalis historiæ cap. XXX. aut terram infrugiferam cespitum forma ex- scindere, ac foco destinare. Similes sunt compa- rationes, quas in Evangelio legimus de arbore & palmite non ferente fructum, ideoque in ignem mittendo, ut iterum non inrecte Estius. Ἀπόδο- σις hæc erit: Sic apostatæ, quibus imber Ver- bi & gratiæ frustra bibitur, cum solum spinas ac tribulos proferunt, à DEO maledicentur, Matth. 25. vers. 30. Quanto magis id de tam insignibus apostatis, qui post tanta & tam mul- tiplicia dona voluntarie deficiunt, ac voluntatem Divinam traducunt, Filium ipsum DEI ite- rum crucifigunt, habendum? B. Dorscheus ita explicat hanc similitudinem: Illustratur, inquit, similitudine terræ, quæ geminæ conditionis proponi- tur: Una est fertilis & fæcunda, altera sterilis & infrugifera. Illa describitur, quod sit γῆ πιῦ- σα τὸν ἐπ’ αὐτῆς πολλάκις ἐρχόμενον ὑετὸν, pluvias sæpe super ipsam cadentes hauriens terra, pariens plantas commodas illis, per quos colitur, & bene- dictionem à DEO accipiens. Ubi sunt causæ fœ- cunditatis, 1. benedictio Divina, 2. Mediorum dispensatio, inter quæ & tempestas commoda, 3. agricolæ, qui veluti causæ ministrantes terram ex- colunt. 4. Ipsa terræ receptivitas, quæ propterea dicitur μεταλαμβάνειν & πιεῖν. Hæc describitur tum ab effectibus, tum à consequentibus. Respe- ctu illorum dicitur ferre carduos & tribulos. Re- spectu horum dicitur haberi reproba & maledicta, quæ tandem loco messis incendium expertura sit. Ἀπόδοσις vel tota comparatio Apostolica hæc est: Quemadmodum ea terra benedictionis Divinæ fi- naliter consequitur effectum, quæ sub manu agri- colarum tractabilis est, nec renititur aratro at- que occæ, quæ haurit pluvias cœlitus delapsas, non autem propter lapidositatem defluere patitur, atque hinc plantas commodas atque utiles profert. Econtra vero illa, quæ refragatur, resistitque cultoribus, quæque pluvias non sorbet, sed respuit, atque adeo loco plantarum desideratarum carduos & tri- bulos parit, pro reproba & maledicta merito ha- betur, quæ tandem incendio fit afficienda. Sic illi Verbi Divini auditores benedictionis Divinæ par- ticipes fiunt, qui culturam cœlestem admittunt, semen Divinum retinent, pluvias cælestium gra- tiarum hauriunt, & fructus desideratos profe- runt, atque hoc modo ad perfectionem atque ma- turitatem contendunt. Econtra vero illi, qui qui- dem aliquandiu sub cultura sunt, semen admit- tunt, pluvias cælestium gratiarum gustant, sem- per autem incipiunt tantum crescere & virescere, non autem crescere pergunt, neque ad maturita- tem assurgunt, imo vero semen demum excutiunt, ex adverso vero carduos & tribulos malitiosæ abne- gationis & blasphemæ persecutionis generant, rectis- sime pro reprobis & maledictis habentur, quos im- possibile sit ad frugem perduci, imo necesse sit justo demum judicio DEI æterno exitio tradi.

PARS III. Exhortatio ad constantiam in fide, & spem immotam.

## 6:9
Verse 9.

We are persuaded concerning you, beloved, the better things and those that belong to salvation, even if we speak thus) That is, although we have said these things, we hope nevertheless that you, that is, the greatest part of you, are not in such a state that you are about to fall away from Christianity, although there are some among you who have led the way by a bad example, and the rest have remitted something of their first alacrity. Πέποιθα here does not mean 'I am certain,' but 'I hope,' or 'I persuade myself,' as also in Romans 15:4. Plato also uses it thus, 'those that belong to salvation' (ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας), which cohere with salvation, that is, those things which do not entirely alienate you from salvation.

The Vulgate rendered it 'we are confident.' But Estius observes that the Greek verb is to be explained as 'we are persuaded,' and that this is something more than 'we are confident.' Which is to be noted against the Vulgate hypothesis of the Papists, that faith, which is called πεποίθησις, 2 Corinthians 3:4, Ephesians 3:12, is not knowledge, nor trust, but a bare assent. For persuasion cannot exist without knowledge of the thing of which we are persuaded, and it implies something more, as Estius admits, than trust or confidence. The Apostle tempers the austerity of the preceding words, by which he seemed to have noted the Hebrews because their progress did not correspond to the beginnings of the faith they had started. Better things, he says, I have persuaded myself concerning you, and such as promise salvation rather than destruction. This confidence and persuasion, however, is only from the judgment of charity and is probable: But in matters of faith, which rest upon the Divine revelation of Scripture, the judgment of truth and the persuasion and confidence is most certain. The former is conceived from the works of charity, which are the argument and sign of faith: But since because of hypocrisy falsity can underlie them, an infallible argument does not arise from thence. Augustine, in book III against Cresconius, chapter 74, reads 'inhering to salvation' for 'those that belong to salvation' (ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας). The Vulgate has 'nearer to salvation,' Erasmus 'joined with salvation,' as if he were saying, in the similitude which I have proposed, I have conceived in my mind the better part concerning you, namely the blessing of the good earth. ALTHOUGH WE SPEAK THUS, namely adding also the mention of the earth near to the curse, to which he opposed what he has already said, 'nearer to salvation.' Τὰ κρείττονα, as B. Dorscheus rightly observes, are not only in opposition to apostates who crucify CHRIST for themselves and expose Him to ignominy, who are like the earth bearing thorns and thistles, and thus reprobate, but also in comparison, namely with respect to the elements of Christian doctrine. Therefore, he asserts that those beloved ones, who are well known to him, not only do not depart from the heavenly truth and make themselves liable to the judgment of reprobation, but have already progressed to some extent even from the very elements of Christian doctrine, and are diligent on the way to perfection. In which sense the Apostle exhorts in 1 Corinthians 12:31 to pursue the χαρίσματα τὰ κρείττονα things that are better. Thus also ἐχόμενα τῆς σωτηρίας (things that accompany salvation) are not only spoken of in opposition to those who have brought upon themselves the impossibility of renewal unto repentance and salvation, who are called earth κα- θάρας ἐγγὺς (near to being cursed), whose end tends toward burning, but also in comparison. Namely, in such a way that they are not only in the structure of the foundation, but also τῶν ἐχο- μένων σωτηρίας, that is, of those things which, being joined to salvation, are to be built upon the foundation, or pertaining to salvation.

For God is not unjust to forget your work and labor of love, which you have shown toward His name, in that you have ministered to the saints, and do minister. Therefore, he says, I hope that you will attain salvation, because you have begun well. It is of justice to fulfill promises: wherefore GOD could in some way be called unjust if He did not stand by His promises. Understand ἔργου here as what is called ἔργον πίστεως (work of faith), 1 Thess. 1, verse 3, an open profession of Christianity. To this he adds, as also in the passage to the Thessalonians, κόπον ἀγάπης (labor of love), love joined with labors and troubles, although in the Manuscript, as also in the Latin, κόπυ is absent: Which you show, he says, in His name, that is, in the Christian religion, through which GOD is highly honored: Because you have ministered, he says, to the saints, that is, you have brought all aid to those bound or otherwise afflicted for CHRIST'S sake. See below ch. 10, 33. Let that Mnason, Acts 21, 16, be an example. He also adds 'and do minister,' and by that very thing shows that he is not speaking to those who have fallen, but to those who are still standing, although with the danger of slipping, especially to those who, for fear, had begun to abstain from public assemblies.

The Apostle has rendered the reason for his confidence concerning the Hebrews, and at the same time, by the commemoration of good works, he inflames them to a constant zeal for piety and charity. GOD seems to forget good works when no reward appears. Yet He would be unjust if He were to forget them, not because they are such by their own nature that a reward is owed to them by GOD; but because He would act against the faithfulness of His promise if He did not reward them. But from this, Estius wrongly gathers the merits of good works, because the goodness of GOD toward us is so great that He wills our works to be merits, which are His own gifts. For, not to mention that by 'work' is understood the profession of Christianity, the Apostle does not attribute the eulogy of merit either to our work or to our love. He only intends this: that GOD will not permit the faithful Hebrews, who are laborious in love, to slip so far as to deny the heavenly truth. Estius himself acknowledged that good works by their own nature are not such that a reward is owed to them, and therefore in the rewards of good works, the justice of equality or proportion does not reign, but the justice of truth or promise, and consequently merit, properly so called, which relies on the justice of equality or proportion, is banished. Rightly, therefore, the Blessed Dorfscheus says here: The justice of GOD is either that equity which causes that to each be given what by right belongs to him, and conversely the injustice opposed to it denotes that iniquity which perverts and infringes upon another's right, or justice designates that equity which inclines one more toward beneficence and kindness, and which is seen in the giving of those things to which the other has no right properly so called, yet there are some causes which incite one to give something to someone, so that if it were not given, one would be acting more iniquitously and harshly. That is the injustice of condignity, and is founded in the very perfection of the thing to be regarded, which is so great that the other is obligated, nor has any cause for not giving. This is of the promise, which, although the thing itself by its own perfection does not correspond to the rule of justice, yet from the promise itself an obligation to give arises. The Apostle speaks of the latter in this place. For although GOD, because of the sloth of the multitude of the Hebrews, might have causes why He would forget—that is, why He would have no regard (for this is what it is to forget, when it is attributed to GOD; otherwise, oblivion properly so called does not fall upon GOD)—for the works performed by them, yet out of that supreme kindness and promise, He deems it to pertain to His justice to remember and to deign to favor them with His glorious patronage. In this sense, δίκαιον (just) is also taken in Phil. 1, 7; 2 Thess. 1, 7. Although in the Vulgate version the name of labor, τῶ κόπω, is omitted, as also in Grotius's only Manuscript, and add also in the Syriac version, it is not, however, to be considered an addition with Estius. Since the most approved Greek codices do not omit it, and it occurs likewise in the parallel passage, 1 Thess. 1, verse 3.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

Πεπείσμεθα δὲ περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀγαπητοὶ, τὰ κρείσσονα καὶ ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας, εἰ καὶ ὕτω λαλῦμεν) Id est, quan- quam hæc diximus, speramus tamen vos, id est, maxi- mam partem vestram non esse eo loco, ut à Christiani- smo defecturi sitis, quanquam sunt è vobis, qui malo exemplo præivere, & cæteri aliquid remisere de prima alacritate. Πέποιθα hic non est certus sum, sed spero, aut mihi persuadeo, ut & Roman. 15, 4. Utitur sic & Plato, ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας, quæ cum salute cohæreant, id est ea, quæ vos non plane à salute a- lienent.

Vulgatus reddidit confidimus. Sed observat Estius, Græcum Verbum exponendum esse persuasi sumus, idque plus aliquid esse, quam confidimus. Quod contra Vulgatam Pontifi- ciorum hypothesin, quod fides, quæ πεποίθησις dicitur, 2. Corinth. 3, 4. Ephes. 3, 12. non sit noti- tia, nec fiducia, sed nudus assensus, observan- dum. Persuasio enim sine notitia esse nequit ejus rei, de qua persuasi sumus, & aliquid am- plius infert fatente Estio, quam fiduciam vel con- fidentiam. Temperat Apostolus austeritatem superiorum verborum, quibus Ebræos notasse videbatur, quod eorum progressus non respon- deret initiis cœptæ fidei. Meliora, inquit, mihi de vobis persuasi, quæque salutem promittant potius, quam exitium. Hæc tamen confidentia & per- suasio est tantum ex judicio charitatis & proba- bilis: At in rebus fidei, quæ Divina revela- tione scripturæ nituntur, judicium veritatis ac persuasio, & confidentia est quam certissima. Illa concipitur è charitatis operibus, quæ fidei argumentum sunt & signum: Sed quum ob hy- pocrisin subesse falsitas possit, non oritur inde argumentum infallibile. Ἐχόμενα σωτηρίας Au- gustinus libr. III. contra Crescon. cap. 74. hæren- tia saluti legit. Vulgatus habet viciniora saluti, Erasmo conjuncta cum salute quasi dicat, in si- militudine quam posui, meliorem partem de vobis animo concepi, benedictionem scilicet terræ bonæ. TAMETSI ITA LOQUIMUR, videlicet adjungentes etiam mentionem terræ maledictioni proximæ, cui opposuit, quod jam dixit, viciniora saluti. Τὰ κρείττονα, ut recte B. Dorscheus, non tantum in oppositione adversus apostatas CHRISTUM sibi crucifigentes, & igno- miniæ exponentes, qui similes sunt terræ, spinas ac tribulos ferenti, adeoque reprobæ, sed etiam in com- paratione, respectu scilicet elementorum doctrinæ Christianæ. Itaque asserit illos dilectos, sibique pro- be cognitos non tantum non discedere à veritate cœ- lesti, & reprobationis judicio sese facere obnoxios, sed etiam ab ipsis elementis doctrinæ Christianæ jam aliquo usque progressos, & in via ad perfe- ctionem sedulos esse. Quo sensu Apostolus horta- tur 1. Corinth. 12, 31. ad χαρίσματα τὰ κρείττονα consectanda. Sic & ἐχόμενα τῆς σωτηρίας non tantum dicuntur in oppositione adversus eos, qui si- bi contraxerunt impossibilitatem renovationis ad pœnitentiam & salutem, qui dicuntur terra κα- θάρας ἐγγὺς, cujus exitus tendit ad exustionem, sed etiam in comparatione. Ita scilicet, ut non tan- tum sint in structura fundamenti, sed etiam τῶν ἐχο- μένων σωτηρίας, hoc est, eorum, quæ fundamento sunt superstruenda saluti conjuncta, vel ad salutem pertinentia.

Οὐ γὰρ ἄδικος ὁ Θεὸς ἐπιλαθέσθαι τῦ ἔργυ ὑμῶν καὶ τῦ κόπυ τῆς ἀγάπης, ἧς ἐνεδείξασθε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῦ, διακονή- σαντες τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ διακονῦντες) Ideo, inquit, spero, vos salutem adepturos, quia bene cœpistis. Justitiæ est implere promissa: quare DEUS injustus aliquo modo dici posset, si non staret promissis. ἔργου hic intellige, quod ἔργον πίστεως dicitur, 1. Thessal. 1. vers. 3. apertam professionem Christianismi. Huic addit, ut & dicto ad Thessalonicenses loco κόπον ἀγάπης, dile- ctionem conjunctam cum laboribus & molestiis, quanquam in Manuscripto, ut & in Latino abest κόπυ: Quam ostenditis, inquit, in nomen ipsius, id est, in religionem Christianam, per quam DEUS summe honoratur: Quia ministrastis, inquit, san- ctis, id est, ob CHRISTUM vinctis, aut aliter afflictis omnem opem tulistis. Vide infra cap. 10, 33. Ex- emplo sit ille Mnason Actor. 21, 16. Addit & mini- stratis, eoque ipso ostendit, se non lapsis loqui, sed adhuc stantibus, quanquam cum labendi periculo, iis maxime, qui præ metu à publicis cœtibus abstinere cœperant.

Reddidit Apostolus causam suæ de Ebræis fi- duciæ, simulque bonorum operum commemo- ratione ad constans pietatis & charitatis studium eos inflammat. DEUS videtur bonorum ope- rum oblivisci, quando nulla apparet remunera- tio. Injustus autem esset, si eorum obliviscere- tur, non quod illa suapte natura talia sint, ut eis remuneratio debeatur à DEO; sed quia fa- ceret contra fidem suæ promissionis, si non re- muneraretur. Sed inde perperam colligit Estius bonorum operum merita, quod tanta sit DEI erga nos bonitas, ut nostra velit esse merita, quæ sunt ipsius dona. Nam ut non dicam, per opus intelligi professionem Christianismi, non tri- buit Apostolus vel operi, vel dilectioni nostræ elogium meriti. Solum id vult, quod DEUS Ebræos fideles, & in dilectione laboriosos non permissurus sit eo usque prolabi, ut veritatem cœlestem abnegent. Agnovit Estius ipse, bo- na opera natura sua non esse talia, ut eis debea- tur remuneratio, ideoque in præmiis bonorum operum non regnat justitia æqualitatis sive pro- portionis, sed justitia veritatis sive promissio- nis ac proinde exulat meritum proprie sic di- ctum, quod justitią æqualitatis sive proportio- nis nititur. Recte itaque hic Beat. Dorfscheus: Justitia DEI vel est ea æquitas, quæ facit, ut cui- que tribuatur id, quod illi jure competit, & con- tra injustitia illi opposita eam iniquitatem notat, quæ pervertit & infringit alienum jus, vel justi- tia eam designat æquitatem, quæ quis magis ad beneficentiam & benignitatem inclinat, quæque in iis rebus dandis cernitur, ad quas alter nullum jus proprie dictum habet, causæ tamen aliquæ sunt, quæ incitant ad dandum alicui aliquid, ad- eo, ut si id non daretur, iniquius duriusque age- retur. Illa injustitia condignitatis est, & in ipsa perfectione rei respiciendæ fundatur, quæ tanta est, ut alter obligatus sit, nec ullam habeat non dan- di causam. Hæc promissionis est, quæ quamvis res ipsa sui perfectione non respondeat justitiæ re- gulæ, tamen ex ipsa promissione dandi obligatio nascitur. De posteriori hoc loco loquitur Apostolus. Quamvis enim DEUS propter multitudinis Ebræorum socordiam causas habeat, cur oblivisceretur, hoc est, nullam rationem haberet (Hoc enim est oblivisci, quando DEO tribuitur, alias oblivio proprie sic dicta in DEUM non cadit) operum ab ipsis præstitorum, tamen ex summa ista benignitate & promissione meminisse, & glorioso suo patrocinio ista dignari, ad justitiam suam pertinere existimat. Hoc sensu δίκαιον sumitur etiam Phil. 1, 7. 2. Thessal. 1, 7. Quanquam in Vulgata versione omittatur τῶ κόπω laboris nomen, nec non in unico Grotii Manuscripto, adde & in Syriaca versione, non tamen cum Estio adjectitia censenda est. Siquidem Græci codices probatissimi eandem non omittant, locoque parallelo itidem ea occurrat 1. Thessal. 1. vers. 3.

## 6:11
Vers. 11.

Ἐπιθυμῶμεν δὲ ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι σπουδὴν (But we desire that each one of you show the same diligence). It is not enough for attaining salvation to know these things, but one must persevere. See with what prudence this Writer uses: now he terrifies; then again he raises up; having raised them up, he warns them again, and not only all together, but also each one individually, τὴν ἀυτήν σπουδήν (the same diligence), that is, the same zeal as you showed heretofore. For some had grown cold.

Πρὸς τὴν πληροφορίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἄχρι τέλους (Unto the full assurance of hope unto the end). πληροφορία here is not certainty, but fulfillment or consummation, in which sense we have πληροφορίαν in Colossians 2, 2 and 1 Thess. 1, 5. Πληροφορεῖν in 2 Timothy 4, v. 5, 17. Now he is said to fulfill hope who fulfills the condition under which the thing to be hoped for is proposed.

But why would πληροφορία not denote full certainty and confidence? Because its signification is more accepted in sacred writings, and it best agrees with the propriety of the word, since he is said to be πληροφορεῖσθαι (fully assured) who, just as a ship is carried along with full sails, so his confidence is carried toward that thing which is proposed to him in the word of promise, nor is that word taken otherwise in Coloss. 2, 2; 2 Thess. 1, 5, so that the sense may be: Although I persuade myself of all the best things concerning you, yet I cannot but exhort you to perseverance, most eagerly desiring that each one of you show the same zeal for good works until the end of life, for by this reason the confidence of your hope will be full, just as Estius himself and with him the Blessed Gerhard explains. For they judge that that ἄχρι τέλους (unto the end) is not to be referred to the nearer, namely to πληροφορίαν ἐλπίδος (full assurance of hope), but to the more remote, namely to ἔνδειξιν σπουδῆς (the showing of diligence), which the Apostle wishes to be persevering until death, Heb. 3, 6, 14. And Erasmus and Hentenius depart from the Vulgate version, which rendered it 'the fulfillment of hope.' For they are explained as 'unto the full certainty of hope.' Here B. Dorscheus noted Grotius at length, whose refutation it is helpful to repeat from his unpublished commentary: Grotius denies that πληροφορία in this passage, as elsewhere, denotes certainty, since it rather designates fulfillment or consummation, as also in Colossians 2:2, 1 Thessalonians 1:5, 2 Timothy 4:5 and 17; but nothing prevents it from being able to denote certainty here as well. For, first, that [certainty] is most correctly urged in the embracing of Divine promises. Then, the same was greatly desired among the Hebrews, inasmuch as sloth and a certain weariness of progressing in Divine matters dominated them, indeed a certain slipperiness and inconstancy, which caused them to relapse so often to the elements of the Christian religion. But the certainty obtained by them would validly fortify them against the danger of relapse. Finally, certainty also draws after itself the very zeal for consummation, which indeed requires the effect of the promises of tithes from GOD himself; nor is Coloss. 2, verse 2, πληροφορία anything other than most certain trust, or fiducial certainty. For πληροφορία τῆς συνέσεως is consummate intelligence, which is certainty itself. It is read in exactly the same sense also in 1 Thess. 1, 5 & 2 Tim. 4, 5 & 17. For when the Apostle says that his Gospel was communicated to the Thessalonians, not in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and in much πληροφορία, he implies nothing other than that his preaching had generated the fullest certainty and trust in the minds of the faithful through the power of the Holy Spirit. And when he exhorts Timothy and says: Τὴν διακονίαν πληροφόρησον, he requires entirely that he should undertake the ministry with a certain trust in heavenly blessing. This, therefore, is properly the sentiment of the Apostle; we desire most eagerly that, just as you have begun well, so with the same zeal each one of you, running in that stadium of the Christian faith until the end, may strive for the full certainty of hope, that is, that he may be confirmed more and more in his heart in the hope of the eternal inheritance.

Verse 11.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

Ἐπιθυμῶμεν δὲ ἕκαστον ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι σπουδὴν) Non satis est ad consequendam salutem ea nosse, sed perstandum est. Vide quanta prudentia Scriptor hic utatur, modo terret; Deinde rursus erigit, erectos iterum monet, nec universos tantum, sed & singulos, τὴν ἀυτήν σπουδήν, id est, par studium, quale ostendistis antehac. Quidam enim refrixerant.

Πρὸς τὴν πληροφορίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἄχρι τέλους) πληροφορία hic non est certitudo, sed impletio, sive consummatio, quo sensu πληροφορίαν habemus Colossens. 2, 2. & 1. Thessal. 1, 5. Πληροφορεῖν 2. Timoth. 4. v. 5. 17. Implere autem spem dicitur, qui conditionem implet, sub qua res speranda proposita est.

Cur vero πληροφορία non notaret plenam certitudinem & fiduciam, quia receptior ejus in sacris est significatio, & vocis proprietati maxime convenit, quum πληροφορεῖσθαι dicatur, qui, sicut navis plenis velis provehitur, sic fiducia sua eam in rem fertur, quæ ipsi in verbo promissionis est proposita, nec aliter accipitur ea vox Coloss. 2, 2. 2. Thessal. 1, 5. ut sensus sit: Quamvis optima quæque de vobis mihi persuadeam, tamen non possum non ad perseverantiam vos exhortari, cupidissime expetens, unumquemque vestrum eidem bonorum operum studium usque ad finem vitæ præstare, hac enim ratione plena erit spei vestræ fiducia, quemadmodum ipsemet Estius & cum eo B. Gerhardus exponit. Illud enim ἄχρι τέλους non ad propinquius, videlicet ad πληροφορίαν ἐλπίδος referendum censent, sed ad remotius, videlicet ad ἔνδειξιν σπουδῆς, quam Apostolus vult esse perseverantem usque ad mortem, Ebr. 3, 6. 14. Et discedunt Erasmus, & Hentenius à Vulgata versione, quæ reddidit expletionem spei. Exponuntur enim ad plenam spei certitudinem. Notavit hic Grotium prolixe B. Dorscheus, cujus elenchum repetere è comment. ἀνεκδότῳ juvat: Grotius negat πληροφορίαν hoc loco, ut alibi certitudinem notare, cum potius impletionem vel consummationem designet, sic & Colossens. 2, 2. 1. Thessal. 1, 5. 2. Tim. 4, 5. & 17. sed nihil repugnat, quo minus certitudinem etiam hic denotare possit. Nam primo illa in amplexu promissionum Divinarum rectissime urgetur. Deinde eadem in Ebræis desiderabatur maxime, utpote in quibus dominabatur socordia & tædium quoddam proficiendi in rebus Divinis, imo lubricitas quædam atque inconstantia, quæ fecit, ut toties ad elementa Christiana religionis relaberentur. Certitudo vero ab ipsis obtenta valide ipsos contra periculum relapsus communiret. Denique certitudo ipsum etiam studium consummationis post se trahit, quod quidem ratione promissionum Decimarum ab ipso DEO effectum requirit; nec Coloss. 2. vers. 2. πλη- ροφορία aliud est, quam fiducia certissima, vel cer- titudo fiducialis. Est enim πληροφορία τῆς συνέ- σεως consummata intelligentia, quæ est ipsa certitu- do. Eodem plane sensu etiam 1. Thessal. 1, 5. & 2. Timoth. 4, 5. & 17. legitur. Nam cum Apo- stolus dicit, Evangelium suum Thessalonicen- sibus communicatum esse, non in verbo so- lam, sed etiam in virtute, & Spiritu sancto & πληροφορίᾳ multâ, non aliud innuit, quam præ- dicationem suam per virtutem Spiritus sancti in animis fidelium plenissimam generavisse certitudinem atque fiduciam. Et cum Timotheum hortatur dicitque: Τὴν διακονίαν πληροφόρησον, hoc omnino requirit, ut certa quadam fiducia cælestis benedi- ctionis ministerium aggrediatur. Hæc ergo pro- prie est sententia Apostoli; desideramus cupi- dissime, ut quemadmodum bene cæpistis. Ita eo- dem studio unusquisque vestrum in stadio illo Chri- stianæ fidei usque ad finem decurrens ad plenam cer- titudinem spei contendat, hoc est, ut in corde suo magis magisque confirmetur in spe hæreditatis æter- næ.

Vers. 11.

## 6:12
That you may not become sluggish) I say this for this reason, he says, so that you may not slacken in that zeal of yours. νωθρὸς and παρειμένος are joined. Sirach 4, 32. In the glossary νωθρότης, more languid. In Hebrew עצל.

And imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises) Of the Patriarchs, as the following indicates. And κληρονομούντων is placed for κληρονομησάντων, the present for the past. For although Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob did not possess that promised land, nor did they see that huge posterity and kingdom in it, they nevertheless transmitted the most certain right to their descendants. But he who has the right seems in a way to have the thing itself, as has been set forth in law. Moreover, it is a ἓν διὰ δυοῖν when it is said πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας for through patient or constant faith in adversities. When the discourse is about us, ἐπαγγελία is usually said in the singular number: when about the Fathers, often ἐπαγγελίαι. For there were many promises, made at different times, through which, however, that one and great promise made to us concerning eternal life is shadowed forth, and was mystically contained in them.

We do not deny that these things are said concerning the promises made to Abraham and other Patriarchs; but we deny that bodily promises were made to them alone, and that these are being looked at in this place. The promise certainly made to Abraham concerning the blessing in CHRIST, the blessed seed, concerned spiritual and heavenly goods, Galat. 3, 16. Nor does the blessed Dorscheus speak ill here: In the promise (made to Abraham) one must distinguish the Divine blessing, which is the end, from that which is the means. The blessing which is the end is that in which we communicate with Abraham, concerning which the Apostle discourses at length in Gal. 3, 8 & seqq., which is the very promise of the Messiah and his benefits. The blessing which is the means has the very multiplication of the nation and of the Abrahamic race, which God the Best and Greatest granted, so that in the course of the Patriarchal posterity spreading far and wide, the Messiah might finally arise, and thus the blessing which is the end might follow. Nor is ἐπαγγελία always said in the singular number when the discourse is about us in the New Testament, but ἐπαγγελίαι occur in 2 Corinth. 7, 1, Heb. 8, 6, and vice versa, when the discourse is about the Fathers in the Old Testament, sometimes the singular number is used, Acts 13, 23, 22, ch. 29, 6, Galat. 3, 17, etc. But πίσις and μακροθυμία are rightly explained by hendiadys as patient or constant faith in adversities. Μακροθυμία

this, as the blessed Dorscheus observes, is not patience itself, otherwise numbered among the Christian virtues and distinct from them, but is an act of faith, explained in Romans 4, where it is said that he believed things impossible by nature, verse 17, believed against hope in hope, verse 18, was not weakened in faith, in view of a body almost incapable of generation, verse 19, did not hesitate concerning the promise of GOD with scrupulous incredulity, but was strengthened by faith, verse 20, and πληροφορηθεὶς verse 21. Therefore, μακροθυμία is that constancy and perseverance of faith which the Apostle calls ἐνδυνάμωσιν, which bravely crushed and repelled whatever objections were placed against it. Hence μακροθυμία is joined with faith, verse 12, not as a virtue distinct from faith, but as a degree of faith. For faith ought to be μακρόθυμος and ἐνδυναμωθεῖσα and πληροφορηθεῖσα, as shines forth in the example of Abraham, whose imitation is proposed to us. The nerve of the argument of the Papists is thus cut, that we inherit the promised goods not through faith alone, but also through long-suffering. Certainly, μακροθυμία is required, since we do not yet have the complement of the promises here, but it is not the cause of the inheritance, which is apprehended and obtained only by faith, and we are warned at least that faith must be μακροθυμῦσα καὶ ὑπομένουσα, in which sense indeed μακροθυμία is not a virtue, but the constancy of faith: Nor do we have Estius dissenting here: For he exhorts the Hebrews that, by the example of their ancestors, who believing the Divine promises without doubt, and patiently expecting the same, have attained and are attaining them: In the faith and expectation of heavenly promises, they should constantly persevere among the adversities of this storm.

Latin:

Ἵνα μὴ νωθροὶ γένησθε) Hoc ideo dico, inquit, ne quid remittatis de isto studio. Conjunguntur νωθρὸς & παρειμένος. Sirac. 4, 32. In glossario νωθρότης, langui- dior. Ebræis עצל.

Μιμηταὶ δὲ τῶν διὰ πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας κληρονο- μούντων τὰς ἐπαγγελίας) Patriarcharum, ut sequentia indicant. Et κληρονομούντων positum prò κληρονομησάν- των præsens pro Præterito. Nam quanquam Abraha- mus, Isaacus & Jacobus terram illam promissam non possederunt, neque viderunt ingentem illam posterita- tem & regnum in ea, jus tamen certissimum ad poste- ros transmiferunt. Qui autem jus habet, rem ipsam ha- bere quodammodo videtur, ut in jure est proditum. Est autem ἓν διὰ δυοῖν cum dicitur πίστεως καὶ μακροθυμίας pro per fidem patientem sive constantem in adversis. Cum de nobis sermo est, ἐπαγγελία singulari numero dici solet: cum de Patribus sæpe ἐπαγγελίαι. Complu- ra enim erant promissa, diversis facta temporibus, per quæ tamen illud unum & magnum promissum de vita æterna nobis factum adumbratur, & mystice in illis con- tinebatur.

De promissionibus Abrahæ, & aliis Patriarchis factis hæc dici non abnuimus; sed illis tantum factas corporales promissiones, easque hoc loco respici negamus. Promissio certe Abrahæ fa- cta de benedictione in CHRISTO semine benedi- cto spiritualia & cælestia bona concernebat, Galat. 3, 16. Neque male hic B. Dorscheus: In promissione (Abrahæ facta) distinguenda est bene- dictio Divina, quæ finis est, ab ea, qua medium est. Benedictio, quæ finis est, illa est, in qua cum Abrahamo communicamus, de qua Gal. 3, 8. & seqq. prolixe Apostolus disserit, quæ est ipsa promissio Messiæ, ejusque beneficiorum. Benedictio, qua me- dium est, habet ipsam multiplicationem gentis, & generis Abrahæi, quam Deus Optimus Maximus largitus est, ut in decursu posteritatis Patriarcha- lis longe lateque sese diffundentis tandem oriretur Messias, & sic benedictio, quæ finis est, sequeretur. Neque semper cum de nobis sermo est in No- vo Testamento ἐπαγγελία in singulari numero dicitur, sed ἐπαγγελίαι occurrunt 2. Corinth. 7, 1. Ebr. 8, 6. & vice versa, cum de Patribus sermo est in Veteri Testamento, quandoque singula- ris numerus adhibetur, Actor. 13, 23. 22. cap. 29, 6. Galat. 3, 17. &c. Recte autem per Hen- dyadep explicatur πίσις & μακροθυμία de fide patiente sive constante in adversis. Μακροθυμία

hæc, ut observat B. Dorscheus, non est ipsa pa- tientia, alias inter virtutes Christianas connumea- ta, & ab iisdem distincta, sed est actus fidei, ex- positus Roman. 4. qua dicitur credidisse natura im- possibilia, vers. 17. credidisse contra spem in spem, vers. 18. non debilitatus esse fide, intuitu corporis ad generationem fere inhabilis, vers. 19. circa pro- missionem DEI non scrupulosa incredulitate hæsi- tasse, sed corroboratus esse fide, vers. 20. & πλη- ροφορηθεὶς vers. 21. Itaque μακροθυμία est illa constantia & perseverantia fidei, quam Apostolus ἐνδυνάμωσιν vocat, quæ quasve objectiones sibi op- positas fortiter elisit & repulit. Hinc μακροθυμία cum fide conjungitur, vers. 12. non ut virtus à fide distincta, sed ut gradus fidei. Fides enim debet esse μακρόθυμος & ἐνδυναμωθεῖσα, & πληροφο- ρηθεῖσα, uti in exemplo Abrahæ, cujus imitatio nobis proposita est, lucet. Nervus ita inciditur argumento Papistarum, quod nos non per fi- dem solum, sed etiam per longanimitatem bona promissa hæreditemus.
