He proceeds well to render the reason for the other statement, namely that Christ is a Priest in the whole universe and therefore also in the highest heaven. For if he had had to perform his ministry on earth, that is, only on earth, there was no need for him to be made a Priest, which is predicted in the Psalm. ἦν among the Greeks, especially where ἂν is added, has the force of the potential mood, as if he were saying, ὀυκ ἂν εἴη.

Ὄντων τῶν ἱερέων τῶν προσφερόντων κατὰ νόμον τὰ δῶρα] In the Manuscript ἱερέων is missing. There were those who offered those things which are prescribed in the law. There was no need for the Messiah to be sent for that reason. In the word δῶρα, θυσίας is also understood κατὰ σύνεψιν. They were, namely, when that Psalm was written. For ὄντων is also put for the Imperfect. Thus Plautus: Coming just now with his wife, he takes pleasure. Pliny: Boars fight among themselves, hardening their ribs by the rubbing of trees, that is, after they have hardened them. Learned men have noted many such things.

The scope, connection, and sense of the Apostle is as follows: He wishes to prove the necessity of the eminence and the priestly function in the heavens of our High Priest, which the particle γὰρ teaches. He proves it thus: Since High Priests had to offer gifts and sacrifices, and therefore it was absolutely necessary that Christ, the true High Priest, should also have something to offer, namely the victim of his own body, he would not even be a High Priest if he were still on earth, where Aaronic Priests existed who were offering, unless, of course, having entered into heaven, he were the λειτουργὸς of the holy of holies and of the true tabernacle: as if he were concluding: If that is denied, the priesthood of Christ itself is denied; that is by no means to be denied. But if the entry of Christ into the holy of holies, that is, into heaven, is denied, the priesthood of Christ itself is denied. Therefore, the entry of Christ into the holy of holies, that is, into heaven, is by no means to be denied. The major [premise] shines by its own light: but the minor is confirmed, because, since it was the duty of the High Priests to offer a sacrifice in the holy place or in the first tabernacle, and having offered it to enter into the holy of holies, Christ also had to have a sacrifice which He might offer in the Church on these earths, which was no other than the victim of His own body, which He offered once, ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας, which the Apostle had taught in chapter 7, 27, when He laid down His soul as a sacrifice, Isa. 53. 10, and having offered it to enter into the holy of holies, that is, into heaven: which therefore if it were not done, He would not even be the true Priest Himself, prefigured by the Levitical Priests. For if He were still on earth, and had not died, or had not offered Himself through death as a sacrifice, He would not have entered through His ascension and exaltation into heaven. How then could He be considered the true High Priest, whom the Aaronic Priests prefigured, since they offered, or were bound to offer, their gifts and sacrifices according to the law: according to the law, I say, which required that the High Priest should so offer sacrifices in the holy place, that afterwards, the sacrifices having been offered, he should enter into the holy of holies. This figure the Apostle hints at here, intending to unfold it more fully later in the following chapter. It sufficed here to have taught in general that the holy of holies and the tabernacle were a figure and type, along with the sacrifices and the offering Priest, and his entry into heaven, which he proves in verse 5, teaching from Moses that the Aaronic Priests served only τῷ ὑποδείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ τῶν ἐπουρανίων, in order to attribute to Christ, the true High Priest, a more sublime λειτουργίαν τῶν ἐπουρανίων, inasmuch as by it, according to the Prophet, He had to become the Mediator of a better Testament. For the Apostle wished to demonstrate here above all else both things regarding the adumbration of the Levitical Priesthood and the imperfection of the Old Testament, the former of which he demonstrates from Moses, Exod. 25, 40, and the latter from the Prophets, namely Jerem. 31, 31 ff. That the former priesthood was only a ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σκιὰν of heavenly things, which we have uniquely in the priesthood of Christ the true High Priest: and that the former testament was by no means ἄμεμπτον, which He Himself, finding fault, testified through Jeremiah, so that He might explain both of those more abundantly in what follows, intending to provide solid food (στερεὰν τροφὴν) to His Hebrews concerning these mysteries in chapters IX and X.

Therefore, neither the Socinians, nor the Papists, nor the Calvinists will elicit anything from this Apostolic passage, even if they apply a thousand alembics: of whom the first group strive to carve out from this, against the mind and intention of the Holy Spirit, that Christ did not perform an offering on earth, nor was he truly a High Priest; the middle group, that Christ still offers an unbloody sacrifice in heaven through little sacrificing-priests in the mass; the last group, that Christ, by reason of his human nature, is not present on earth. For it is now in the open that those things are openly contrary to the mind and purpose of the Holy Spirit, who is rather concerned to teach that it was entirely necessary that Christ, the true High Priest, should offer the sacrifice of his body on earth in the sanctuary, which was done by all the priests in the Old Testament, in a pattern, figure, and shadow of the true High Priest, who afterwards [entered] into the holy of holies, that he might be there a minister of the holy things and of the true tabernacle, not indeed by sacrificing—for he had done this once when he offered himself as a sacrifice on the altar of the cross—but by interceding for us, which is consistent with the type of the old High Priest. As for the others, besides the fact that they invent without Scripture that Christ sacrifices in heaven, and that not immediately, but through little sacrificing-priests on earth celebrating the mass, of whom there is no trace either here or elsewhere in the Scriptures, it is evident from these things that they likewise stand diametrically opposed to this passage. First, because the Apostle testifies with a resounding voice that Christ offered himself only once: how, therefore, do those not contradict him who contend here with Estius that Christ still offers himself daily? Especially since, secondly, the Apostle establishes the distinction between the typical priests and the true High Priest in this, that they were accustomed to offer daily according to the law, but he, on the other hand, had to offer himself, and did offer himself, only once, once for all (cap. 7:27, cap. 9:25, 26, 28, cap. 10:10, 12, 14). Furthermore, thirdly, if an offering were still being made on earth by Christ the true Priest, he would not even be that Priest, since our High Priest had to enter heaven once the offering was completed, nor could he be considered the true High Priest, since the typical priests had to offer on earth according to the law, in such a way that, once the offering was completed, they would enter into the holy of holies. To say nothing, fourthly, of the fact that according to the Apostle an unbloody sacrifice is an object of contradiction, since no expiatory sacrifice has ever been performed without the shedding of blood. Estius himself indeed admits that the Apostle is completely silent here about that offering which they dream is made in the mass. It is probable, he says, that the Apostle is speaking of that offering by which he now continually represents to the Father in heaven himself, who once suffered and was offered on the cross. For the Apostle is completely silent about the other: because it is a mystery which he leaves to be understood by the faithful who are conscious of the mysteries. But to wish to prove from this passage that which the Apostle is completely silent about in this passage, is that not the height of rashness? However, the little argument which Estius brings forward to prove that Christ in heaven, through his ministers as his vicars, the priests, as the true Priest, offers a true sacrifice in the mass, is of no weight: because the universal proposition is that every High Priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices, and it is consistent that the whole of it should be explained concerning CHRIST, both as once mortal and now immortal: that gifts were unbloody sacrifices, but sacrifices were bloody: therefore, Christ, while mortal, indeed offered a gift, that is, the Eucharist at the last supper, and offered also a sacrifice, himself on the cross; but now, immortal, he offers the same Eucharistic gift from the rising of the sun to its setting through his vicars, the priests, and offers also a sacrifice, because he still presents and represents to the Father in heaven himself, once suspended, wounded, and killed on the cross for us. For what can you find in these things besides a begging of the question? Let us admit that the gifts of the priests were unbloody sacrifices, and the sacrifices were bloody: let us admit that both are indicated, let us admit that these are asserted in the present tense concerning Christ, both mortal and immortal: but what necessity will there be that we should immediately admit these Papal inventions as well? Namely: 1. That the Eucharist at the last supper was a gift which he offered while mortal, which was celebrated not as a gift offered to God, but as a Sacrament dispensed to the Apostles. For what was offered to God by Christ in the Eucharist by way of a gift? He did not give or offer to God, but distributed to the Apostles bread and wine, and under the blessed bread and wine his body and blood to be eaten and drunk. That those things were then offered to God as a sacrifice at the last supper is a brain-spun invention, completely contrary to the description of the holy supper. Furthermore, if the sacrifice offered there was propitiatory, as the Papists wish, how could it have been an unbloody sacrifice, since no propitiatory sacrifice is or ever has been unbloody? Indeed, how is the Eucharist unbloody, in which the blood of Christ is dispensed? But although Christ, while mortal, may be said to have offered both a gift and a sacrifice, did he not offer himself as a sacrifice by dying on the cross? So also he is rightly said to have offered a gift by pouring out prayers, which are a gift pleasing to God, such as the expression found in Heb. 5:7, 'offering up prayers and supplications.' Furthermore, now that Christ is immortal, although he presents and represents himself to the Father in heaven as the sacrifice made for us, this is nevertheless not offering a bloody sacrifice. For that representation is not a sacrificial offering, inasmuch as it was made once on the altar of the cross, nor does he appear there before the face of God as bloody, much less does he appear as killed, for in that he died to sin, he died once (Rom. 6:10). It is one thing for Christ to present himself in heaven, who was made a sacrifice for us in his passion and death: it is another thing for Christ to offer himself as a sacrifice in heaven: the former is consistent with Scripture, the latter is not. And although intercession in heaven could come under the name of an offering by analogy to the passage in Heb. 5:7, it could not, however, in any way be called a bloody sacrifice, even if it be admitted with Ambrose (Book X on Luke) that Christ even reserved the open wounds of his passion in his body. For it is one thing for Christ to present his wounds, and another for Christ to offer himself as a sacrifice. Did Christ, in his Easter appearance to the disciples and Thomas, present his wounds, John 20:27, and offer himself to God the Father as a sacrifice? Similarly, even if Christ, even as an immortal, were said to offer a gift, does it follow that this gift is a sacrificial mass, which is believed to be offered by mass-priests? That is certainly not the gift which is offered to God by Christ. But it is rather a gift which Christ provides to us in the Holy Supper for our confirmation in faith: nor is it an unbloody sacrifice, insofar as it is provided in the Holy Eucharist: because in no way is a sacrifice performed there, even if the body, which was once offered for us as a sacrifice, is provided there, because it is exhibited in the Holy Supper not as a sacrifice, but as food for all: nor is the body alone, but also the blood of Christ is drunk in the Holy Supper, and therefore it can be considered as a place of unbloody sacrifice all the less. If you ask, what gift then, what victim does the immortal Christ offer? I answer: He can be said to offer (in the sense that obtains in Hebrews 5:7, but not in the sense in which sacrifices are said to be offered, or in the sense of a simple presentation, but not of an expiatory oblation) himself in heaven, when he presents himself, who was made a victim for us on the cross, appearing before the face of God.

The prayers of the saints can also be said to be offered, as a gift pleasing to God, since these spiritual sacrifices or incense ascend through his own hands before God, Apoc. 8, 4. Moreover, there is no necessity that Christ be said to offer both a bloodless and a bloody sacrifice, as much in heaven as an immortal, as on earth as a mortal; since his Pontificate is completed by the oblation, which was performed on the altar of the cross, and by the intercession, which still exists in heaven: And the Apostle here intends only this, that Christ, as the true Pontiff, had need of the victim which he had to offer for the expiation of sins, so that, having offered it, he could for our sake enter into the holy of holies, and there be a λειτυργὸς for the sake of our salvation.

Finally, this opinion also favors the Calvinists in nothing, that Christ, if he were still on earth, would not be that true Priest: For it is denied that he is on earth κατά τι, namely for that reason by which the Levitical Priests, before their entry into the holy of holies, had to be occupied with slaughtering and offering sacrifices: Thus the Apostle denies that he is still on earth, and there offering himself as a sacrifice, and that he has not yet entered into heaven, and having posited that, he teaches that it is denied that Christ is the true Pontiff, as one to whose priestly office, in order for it to be complete, an entry into the holy of holies was absolutely required, whence Camero in myroth. observes on this passage that the action of the high Priest sacrificing outside the sanctuary and entering into the sanctuary was one and the same, and therefore the one could not rightly exist without the other, since the Priest offered outside the sanctuary for no other purpose than that he might enter into the sanctuary, nor was that expiation instituted for any other end, nor by any other law, than that having entered into the sanctuary he should present himself, after the sacrifice was performed, before the Lord, which had to be done for as long as the true Priest had not brought the true sacrifice into the sanctuary, since it had to be signified by this pact that the true Priest had not yet entered into the true sanctuary, namely heaven, Heb. 9, 18. Whence Camero concludes: Therefore, with Christ remaining on earth, the tabernacle would have stood, and consequently, also the λατρεία, and while that stood, Christ could not be a Priest, because two priesthoods cannot by right obtain at the same time. If therefore Christ had remained on earth, since he would thus have obtained the Levitical Priesthood, Christ himself would not even be a Priest. But now he has entered into heaven, and so the shadows have vanished. These things Camero in the cited place, where what he adds is also worthy of note: It is one thing to offer on earth, another to remain on earth after the oblation is performed. The Apostle does not say: If Christ had offered on earth, he would not have been a Priest: But (as is evident from the beginning of the chapter) the Apostle only intends this: If Christ had remained on earth, if he had not sat down at the right hand of the Father (for this is εἰ γὰρ ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς) he would not even have been a Priest, for he is not a Priest who has only begun, and not completed, the priestly action. Just as therefore if the high Priest had not entered into the holy of holies, he would not even have been a high Priest, I say; So if Christ had not sat down at the right hand of the Father, by the same reasoning he would not even have been a Priest, in function, I say. And because in Christ, who is the holy of holies, the office cannot be distinguished from the legitimate function of the office, from the fact that he would not be performing the office, it could rightly be inferred that the office itself would not belong to him. Since therefore these words of the Apostle do nothing to deny the presence of Christ according to his Human nature in these lands, it is now most manifest, after we have rendered the genuine sense of the words of the Apostle. Which we have also already observed in Socinismo proflig. poster. edition, page 346, in these very words: The force of the Apostolic assertion, if you weigh it correctly, is this, that Christ would not be that true Pontiff, prefigured in the Old Testament, if he still existed upon the earth, because he would not yet have performed his oblation, as one which he had to perform by his death, nor would he have entered into the holy of holies, or into heaven, through his own blood; he would not yet have made expiation for sins by himself, since he does not, as other Priests on earth, acting in this life, sacrifice and perform their priesthood, perform his Priesthood, but expose himself to death for us, and offer himself to God as a victim of sweet odor, and by that reason had to enter into the heavenly sanctuary through his own blood, so that he might there eternally intercede for us.

Others render this meaning of these words of the Apostle: He who must remain on earth, like the Levitical Priests, had to minister to the tabernacle, which is upon the earth. Thus also Christ would not even be a Priest, because he was not from the tribe of Levi, to whom alone that was fitting according to the law. Thus Rivetus Comm. in Ps. Prophets, page 471, in Psalm CX, noting: These words, if he were upon the earth, are to be understood from a comparison of the preceding and subsequent parts, so that they are not taken simply and absolutely, as if Christ living on earth could not perform a priesthood: But with relation and κατά τι, by reason of the quality of the priesthood and the sacrifice, as if he were saying, if he were a Priest on earth, that is, a minister of the tabernacle, which is upon the earth, he would not even be a Priest: The reason is evident, because since he was not from the tribe of Levi, or from the successors of Aaron, he could not serve that earthly tabernacle, and perform a priesthood in it. This reason is added in the text itself: Since there were those who offered gifts according to the law, who serve the copy of heavenly things. Christ certainly was not such a Priest, but he himself was that heavenly thing, upon which all others depend, whose copy the Levitical priesthood served. Christ therefore is not a Priest on earth, not as if he did not perform a sacrifice on earth, but because he did not have an earthly oblation after the manner of the Levitical Priests, which was only a figure and shadow of things to come. What the Calvinists wish to gain for the ἀπροσία of the Human nature after the ascension from the earth by admitting this explanation, they may see for themselves.

Some of our own understand by the words ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς [on earth] an earthly [thing], in this sense: If he (the Priest) were earthly, he would not even be a Priest, since there are Priests offering gifts according to the law, who could no less offer an earthly sacrifice. And they take what follows in v. 5 as a new reason. How would he be a Priest and antitype, if he offered an earthly sacrifice? Since every earthly sacrifice serves the shadow of heavenly things. But in that way they acknowledge that in the words, he would not even be a Priest, is understood that true Priest and antitype, which must be established entirely. And therefore there is only one reason, not different ones: in this way: If he were still on earth, he would not even be that true Priest prefigured by the Levitical Priests, since the Priests offered gifts according to the law, who served the shadow of heavenly things, and therefore it was necessary for him not to remain on earth after the manner of those serving the shadow, but to penetrate into heaven itself. It is added that according to this explanation, as the blessed D. König admits, one departs from the property of the letter, and that furthermore it is established that the phrase ἐπὶ γῆς εἶναι [to be on earth] here ought not to be denied so much of Christ the Priest himself, as of his sacrifice: provided they wish an opposition to be made in this special medium, that Christ offered a nobler victim, and on that account is a Priest nobler than the Levites, which with the Glossa Ordinaria and John Calvin the same blessed D. König [maintains] in his Vindiciae. Sacr. loc. 30. page 172. he asserts, with this reason added, that τὸ γῆς [the earth], including an earthly condition and used of persons, is construed with the preposition ἐκ [from], Isa. 41:24, John 3:31. Concerning things however, since ἐπὶ is found in Col. 3:2. But the common opinion hitherto has been that those words εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς were spoken about the Priest, not about the sacrifice. Finally, they gratuitously assume that λειτουργὸν τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς signifies nothing other than that Christ is the sacrificer of his own body, and that those words, τῶν ἁγίων καὶ σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς, are said exegetically. Something else has been established from our interpretation already set forth.

But Grotius's gloss on v. 4 cannot be approved: If you supply 'only' in 'on earth', he would have had to perform the ministry, there was no need for him to be made a Priest, there were those who offered those things which are prescribed in the law. There was no need for the Messiah to be sent for that reason. For thus 1. the particle 'only', which is not in the text, is rashly inserted. 2. The words εἰ ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς do not signify, if he had to perform the ministry on earth, but, if he were on earth. 3. The words εἰδ᾽ ἂν ἦν ἱερεὺς do not signify, there was no need for him to be made a Priest, much less was there no need for the Messiah to be sent: But that he (JESUS) himself would not even be a Priest. 4. The verb ὄντων is feigned by a new invention to refer here to the time of the Psalmist, not indeed to the time of Christ, so that a new sense may be extorted. 5. The Apostle was not acting to teach that there was a need for the Messiah to be sent, but he wishes to demonstrate that Christ, if he is to be considered a true High Priest, ought not to remain on earth, as the High Priests of the Old Testament were on earth and remained as long as they were performing the High Priesthood, but that it was necessary, after the sacrifice was performed on earth, for him to enter heaven, just as, after the sacrifice was performed, the High Priests of the Old Testament used to enter the holy of holies, with whom he now compares CHRIST here, and so if he were still on earth, says the Apostle, he would be a Priest, if indeed there were also in Christ's time Priests who offered gifts according to the law, until, with the veil torn at the death of Christ, the entrance into the holy of holies was open to all, not only to the High Priest, where there was no longer any place for that solemn entrance of the Priest into the sanctuary.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

Εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἐπὶ γῆς, ὀυδ’ ἂν ἦν ἱερεὺς] In Manuscripto: Εἰ μὲν ἦν. Bene progreditur ad causam reddendam dicti al- terius, nempe Christum in toto universo ac proinde etiam in summo cœlo esse Sacerdotem. Nam si in terris, supple tantum, obeundum ei fuisset ministerium, nihil opus erat eum fieri Sacerdotem, quod in Psalmo prædicitur. ἦν apud Græcos præsertim ubi ἂν additur, vim habet modi potentialis, quasi diceret, ὀυκ ἂν εἴη.

Ὄντων τῶν ἱερέων τῶν προσφερόντων κατὰ νόμον τὰ δῶρα] In Manuscripto deest ἱερέων. Erant, qui ista offerrent, quæ in lege præscripta sunt. Nihil opus erat ob id Messiam mit- ti. In voce δῶρα intelligi κατὰ σύνεψιν etiam θυσίας. E- rant, nempe cum Psalmus iste scriberetur. Nam ὄντων etiam pro Imperfecto ponitur. Sic Plautus: Cum uxore modo adveniens voluptatem capit. Plinius: Apri inter se dimicant, indurantes attritu arborum costas, id est, postquam induravere. Plura talia notarunt vi- ri docti.

Scopus, συνέχεια, & sensus Apostoli sic habet: Probare vult necessitatem eminentiæ, & functio- nem sacerdotalem in cœlis, Pontificis nostri, quod particula γὰρ docet. Eam ita probat: Quum Pon- tifices offerre debuerint munera & sacrificia, ad- eoque necessarium omnino fuerit, ut Christus ve- rus Pontifex haberet etiam, quod offerret, hosti- am nempe corporis sui, eum ne quidem fore Pon- tificem, si in terris adhuc esset, ubi existebant Sacer- dotes Aaronici, qui offerebant, nisi scilicet in cœ- lum ingressus λειτουργὸς sancti sanctorum & taber- naculi veri esset: quasi concluderet: Quo negato negatur ipsummet sacerdotium Christi, id mini- me negandum est. At negato ingressu Christi in sanctum sanctorum, hoc est, in cœlum, negatur ipsummet sacerdotium Christi. Ergo ingressus Christi in sanctum sanctorum, hoc est, in cœlum minime negandus est. Major sua luce radiat: Mi- nor vero confirmatur, quia, quum Pontificum fue- rit, hostiam offerre in sancto vel in tabernaculo priori, eaque oblata in sanctum sanctorum ingre- di, hostiam etiam habere debuit Christus, quam in Ecclesia in his terris offerret, quæ nulla alia fuit, quam victima corporis ipsius, quam semel obtulit, ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας, quod cap. 7, 27. docuerat Apo- stolus, cum animam suam posuit in sacrificium, Esa. 53. 10. eaque oblata ingredi in sanctum sanctorum, hoc est, in cœlum: Quod itaque si factum non sit, ne quidem verus Sacerdos ipse erit, præfiguratus à Sacerdotibus Leviticis. Nam si adhuc in terris esset, nec mortuus foret, vel obtulisset se per mortem in sacrificium, nec ingressus esset per ascensionem suam & exaltationem in cœlum. Quomodo ergo verus Pontifex haberi posset, quem præfigurarent Sacerdotes Aaronici, quum illi secundum legem dona & sacrificia sua obtulerint, vel offerre debue- rint: secundum legem, inquam, quæ requirebat, ut sic offerret sacrificia Pontifex in sancto, ut dein- ceps oblatis sacrificiis in sanctum sanctorum ingre- deretur. Quam figuram hic innuit Apostolus, post- modum plenius eandem cap. seq. evoluturus. Suf- ficiebat hic in genere docuisse, quod sanctum san- ctorum & tabernaculum figura & typus fuerit, cum sacrificiis & Sacerdote offerente, ejusque in- gressu in cœlum, quod vers. 5. probat, docens è Mose, quod Sacerdotes Aaronici solum τῷ ὑπο- δείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ inservierint τῶν ἐπουρανίων, ut in- ferret sublimiorem Christo, vero Pontifici, τῶν ἐπουρανίων nempe obtigisse λειτουργίαν, utpote quâ secundum Prophetam etiam melioris Testamenti Mediator fieri debuerit. Id enim utrumque de adumbratione Sacerdotii Levitici, & de imperfectione Testamenti Veteris ante omnia hic demonstrare voluit Apostolus, quorum alterum è Mose Exod. 25, 40. alterum è Prophetis, nominatim Jerem. 31, 31. seqq. demonstrat. Prius sacerdotium ὑπόδειγμα tantum καὶ σκιὰν fuisse cœlestium, quæ habemus unice in sacerdotio Christi veri Pontificis: Et prius testamentum haud fuisse ἄμεμπτον, quod μεμφό- μενος ipse testatus est per Jeremiam, ut utrumq; illud uberius explicaret in sequentibus, Ebræis suis porro στερεὰν τροφὴν de hisce mysteriis præ- biturus IX. & X. capp.

Non ergo vel Sociniani, vel Papistæ, vel Calvi- niani quicquam ex hoc Apostolico loco, etiamsi mille alembicos adhibeant, elicient: Quorum priores Christum in terris non peregisse oblatio- nem, nec Pontificem vere fuisse; medii Christum in cœlis per sacrificulos adhuc offerre sacrificium incruentum in missa, postremi Christum ratione Humanæ naturæ in terris præsentem non esse, hinc exsculpere contra mentem atque intentio- nem Spiritus sancti satagunt. Nam illos palam menti ac scopo Spiritus sancti contraria jam in aprico est, qui potius in eo est, ut doceat, omnino opus fuisse, ut Christus verus Pontifex in terris in sancto sacrificium corporis sui offerret, quod ab omnibus Sacerdotibus in Veteri Testamento fie- bat, ἐν ὑποδείγματι figura & umbra veri Pontificis, qui postea in sanctum sanctorum, ut illic λειτουργὸς esset τῶν ἁγίων καὶ σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς, non qui- dem sacrificando, hoc enim semel fecerat, cum se- ipsum in sacrificium obtulit in ara crucis, sed quod veteris Pontificis typo constat, intercedendo pro nobis. Istos vero, præterquam quod ἄτερ γρα- φῆς fingant, Christum in cœlis sacrificare, idque non immediate, sed per sacrificulos in terris, mis- sam celebrantes, de quibus nullum vestigium; sive hic sive alibi in Scripturis, huic loco itidem καδ- διάμετρον adversari ex hisce constat. Primum quod Apostolus semel tantum obtulisse Christum semetipsum sonora voce testetur: Quomodo er- go non contradicunt illi, qui Christum adhuc quo- tidie se offerre cum Estio hic contendunt? Impri- mis quum secundo Apostolus in eo discrimen con- stituat typicorum Sacerdotum, & veri Pontificis, quod illi quotidie offerre soliti sint secundum le- gem, hic vero non nisi ἐφάπαξ semel se offerre de- buerit, & obtulerit, cap. 7, 27. cap. 9, 25. 26. 28. cap. 10, 10. 12. 14. Adhæc tertio, si adhuc in terris ob- latio fieret à Christo vero Sacerdote, ne Sacerdos quidem ille esset, quum cœlum ingredi peracta oblatione debuerit Pontifex noster, nec verus Pontifex haberi possit, quum in terris secundum legem offerre debuerint typici Sacerdotes, ita ut peracta oblatione in sanctum sanctorum ingrede- rentur. Ut quarto taceamus, quod secundum A- postolum sacrificium incruentum ἀντικείμενον sit ἐν προσκειμένῳ, quum sacrificium expiatorium nullum sine sanguinis effusione peractum fuerit. Fatetur utique Estius ipse, Apostolum hic prorsus tacere de oblatione illa, quam in missa fieri somni- ant. Probabile est, inquit, Apostolum loqui de ea oblatione, qua seipsum quondam in cruce passum & oblatum continuo nunc repræsentat Patri in cœlis. Nam de altera Apostolus prorsus tacet: quia myste- rium est, quod intelligendum relinquit fidelibus my- steriorum consciis. Quo de vero prorsus tacet Apo- stolus hoc in loco, id ex hoc loco probare velle, an- non summæ temeritatis est? Nullius autem mo- menti est ratiuncula, quam affert Estius, ut probet, Christum in cœlis per ministros ad vicarios suos Sa- cerdotes, ceu verum Sacerdotem, verum offerre sa- crificium in missa: Quia propositio universalis est, omnem Pontificem ad offerendum munera & hostias constitui, consentaneum esse, ut & de CHRISTO, tam olim mortali, quam nunc immortali, tota ea ex- plicetur: Munera autem incruenta sacrificia fuisse, hostias vero cruenta: Christum igitur mor- talem obtulisse quidem munus, id est, Eucharistiam in cœna novissima, obtulisse & hostiam seipsum in cruce nunc vero immortalem offerre idem munus Eucha- risticum ab ortu solis usque ad occasum per vicarios suos Sacerdotes, offerre & hostiam, quia seipsum olim in cruce suspensum, vulneratum, & occisum adhuc pro nobis in cœlo fistat ac repræsentet Patri. Quid enim in hisce præter petitionem principii invenias? Admittamus munera Sacerdotum incruenta, ho- stias cruenta sacrificia fuisse: admittamus utraque indigitari, admittamus & de Christo mortali, & de immortali hæc in præsenti efferri: Quæ vero ne- cessitas erit, ut ista etiam commenta Papalia statim admittamus? Nimirum 1. Eucharistiam in cœna novissima munus fuisse, quod obtulerit mortalis, quæ non ut munus Deo oblatum, sed ut Sacramentum Apostolis dispensatum celebrata est. Quid enim Deo à Christo in Eucharistia oblatum est instar muneris? Non Deo dedit vel obtulit, sed Aposto- lis distribuit panem & vinum, & sub pane & vino benedicto corpus & sanguinem suum ad mandu- candum & bibendum. In sacrificium illa tum Deo oblata fuisse in cœna novissima cerebrinum est commentum, cœnæ sacræ descriptioni prorsus contrarium. Porro si sacrificium ibi oblatum pro- pitiatorium, quod volunt Papistæ, quomodo id in- cruentum sacrificium fuerit, quum nullum sacrifi- cium propitiatorium incruentum sit aut fuerit un- quam: Imo quomodo incruenta Eucharistia est, in qua sanguis Christi dispensatur? Christus vero mortalis etsi & munus & hostiam obtulisse dicatur, anne ut hostiam seipsum obtulit in cruce mori- endo: Ita & munus obtulisse recte dicitur preces fundendo, quæ munus Deo gratum sunt, qualis lo- quutio Ebr. 5, 7. habetur, δεήσεις τε καὶ ἱκετηρίας προσενέγκας. Porro jam immortalis Christus, quamvis se sacrificium pro nobis factum sistat, ac repræsentet Patri in cœlis, hoc tamen non est offerre hostiam cruentam. Illa enim repræsentatio non est sacrificialis oblatio, utpote quæ semel in ara crucis facta est, nec ibi apparet coram vultu Dei cruento, nedum ut occisus apparet, quod enim mortuus pec- cato, mortuus est semel, Rom. 6, 10. Aliud est præsen- tare se Christum in cœlis, qui pro nobis factus est in passione & morte sua sacrificium: Aliud est offerre sese Christum in sacrificium in cœlis: Prius Scripturæ consentaneum est, posterius non item. Et quamvis intercessio in cœlis venire posset oblationis nomine ex analogia loci Ebr. 5, 7. non tamen ea ullatenus sacrificium cruentum dici posset, utut cum Ambrosio l. X. in Luc. admittatur, ipsa etiam passionis suæ vul- nera patentia in suo corpore Christum reservasse. Aliud enim est vulnera præsentare Christum, aliud Christum offerre sese in sacrificium. Num Christus in apparitione sua Paschali cum discipulis & Tho- ma vulnera sua præsentavit, Joh. 20, 27. obtulit sese Deo Patri in sacrificium? Similiter etsi munus of- ferre Christus etiam immortalis diceretur, num ideo consequens est, quod munus illud sit sacrifi- um missaticum, quod per sacrificulos offerre credi- tur? Id certe munus non est, quod Deo à Christo offertur. Sed est donum potius, quod Christus no- bis in S. Cœna præbet ad nostri confirmationem in fide: nec sacrificium incruentum est, quatenus præ- betur in S. Eucharistia: quia nullo modo ibi sacri- ficium peragitur, etsi corpus, quod pro nobis in sacrificium quondam oblatum est, ibi præbeatur, quia non ut sacrificium, sed ut omnibus exhibetur in S. Cœna: nec corpus solum, sed etiam sanguis Christi bibitur in S. Cœna, ideoque ea incruenti sa- crificii loco eo minus haberi potest. Si petas, quod- nam ergo munus, quamnam hostiam Christus immor- talis offerat? Resp. Offerre dici potest (eo sensu, qui Ebr. 5, 7. obtinet, non vero quo dicuntur sa- crificia offerre, vel sensu simplicis præsentationis, non vero expiatoriæ oblationis) in cœlis semet- ipsum, cum se sistit, qui factus in cruce ho- stia pro nobis apparens coram vultu DEI.

Offerre etiam dici potest preces sanctorum, ce munus Deo gratum, quum hæc spiritualia sacrifi- cia vel odoramenta per manus ipsius ascendant co- ram Deo, Apoc. 8, 4. Cæterum nulla necessitas est ut Christum tam in cælis ceu immortalis, quam in terris, ut mortalis & sacrificium incruentum & cruentum offerre dicatur; quum Pontificatus ejus oblatione, quæ in ara crucis peracta, & intercessio- ne, quæ etiamnum in cælis sit, absolvatur: Et Apo- stolus id solum hic velit, quod hostia, quam offerre debuerit in expiationem peccatorum, opus ha- buerit Christus, ceu verus Pontifex, ut ea oblata nostri causa ingredi posset in sanctum sanctorum, ibique λειτυργὸς esse salutis nostræ gratia.

Denique nihil etiam Calvinianis favet hæc sen- tentia, quod Christus, si adhuc in terris esset, Sacer- dos ille verus non esset: Nam κατά τι in terris esse negatur, nempe ea ratione, qua ante ingressum in sanctum sanctorum mactandis & offerendis sacrifi- ciis occupari debebant Sacerdotes Aaronici: Sic eum in terris adhuc esse, ibiq; offerre sese in sacrifi- cium, nec dum ingressum in cœlum esse negat A- postolus, eoq; posito docet, negari Christum verum Pontificem esse, utpote ad cujus sacerdotale offi- cium, ut completum sit, requirebatur omnino in- gressus in sanctum sanctorum, unde Camero in myroth. ad h. l. observat actionem summi Sacerdotis im- molantis extra sanctuarium & ingredientis in san- ctuarium unam eandemq; fuisse, adeoque alteram sine altera jure esse non potuisse, siquidem non alio consilio Sacerdos obtulerit extra sanctuarium, qua ut ingrederetur in sacrarium, nec expiatio illa in a- lium finem instituta fuerit, neq; alia lege, quam ut ingressus in sanctuarium sisteret se, peracto sacrifi- cio, coram Domino, quod tantisper fieri oportuit, quantisper verus Sacerdos non intulit in sanctua- rium verum sacrificium, quoniam oportuit hoc pacto significari verum Sacerdotem nondum in- troiisse in verum sanctuarium, nempe cœlum, Ebr. 9, 18. Unde concludit Camero: Ergo Christo re- manente in terra stetisset tabernaculum, proindeque, & λατρεία, atq; illa stante Christus Sacerdos esse non po- tuit, quia duo sacerdotia de jure non possunt simul ob- tinere. Si ergo Christus mansisset in terra, quoniam sic obtinuisset Sacerdotium Leviticum, Christus ipse ne Sacerdos quidem foret. Jam vero ingressus est in cælum, itaq; umbræ evanuerunt. Hæc Camero lo- co citato, ubi notatu digna etiam sunt, quæ addit: Aliud est offerre in terra, aliud peracta oblatione ma- nere in terra. Apostolus non dicit: Si Christus ob- tulisset in terra, non fuisset Sacerdos: Sed (ut constat ex initio capitis) hoc tantum vult Apostolus: Si Chri- stus mansisset in terra, si non consedisset ad dextram Patris (hoc enim est εἰ γὰρ ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς) ne Sacerdos quidem fuisset, non est nempe Sacerdos, qui cœpit dun- taxat, non absolvit actionem Sacerdotalem. Quemad- modum igitur si summus Sacerdos non fuisset ingres- sus in sancta sanctorum, ne Sacerdos quidem fuisset summus, inquam; Ita si Christus non consedisset ad dextram Patris, pari ratione ne Sacerdos quidem fu- isset, functione, inquam. Et quia in Christo, qui san- ctus est sanctorum, non potest officium a legitima fun- ctione officii distingui, ex eo, quod non fungeretur offi- cio, recte inferri posset, ne officium quidem ei compete- re. Quum ergo nihil hæc Apostoli verba faciant pro neganda Christi secundum Humanam natu- ram præsentia in his terris, jam manifestissimum est, postquam sensum genuinum verborum Apo- stoli reddidimus. Quem etiam in Socinismo proflig. poster. edit. pag. 346. jam observavimus his omnino verbis: Vis assertionis Apostolicæ, si recte eandem expendas, hæc est, Christum non fore Pontifi- cem illum verum, in Veteri Testamento præfigura- tum, si super terram adhuc existeret, quia ita nondum peregisset oblationem suam, utpote quam morte sua peragere debebat, neq́; per sanguinẽ proprium ingred- sus fuisset in sanctum sanctorum, vel in cælum; non- dum expiationem peccatorum fecisset per semetipsum, siquidem non, ut alii Sacerdotes in terra, in hac vita agentes sacrificant, & sacerdotio suo funguntur, Sa- cerdotium suum peragere, sed in mortem sese pro no- bis exponere, atq́; Deo in victimam suavis odoris of- ferre, eaq́; ratione per proprium sanguinem in cæle- ste sanctuarium ingredi debuerit, ut ibi æternum pro nobis interpellaret.

Alii reddunt horum Apostoli verborum hanc sententiam: Qui in terra manere debet, ut Sacerdotes Levitici, ministrare debebat tabernaculo, quod est super terram. Ita & Christus ne esset quidem Sacerdos, quia non erat è tribu Levi, quibus id solis conveniebat se- cundum legem. Sic Rivetus Comm. in Ps. Proph. p. 471. in Psal. CX. notans: Hæc verba, si esset super ter- ram, ex collatione antecedentium & subsequentium ita esse intelligenda, ut non simpliciter accipiantur & absolute, quasi Christus in terra vivens non potuerit fungi sacerdotio: Sed cum relatione & κατά τι, ra- tione qualitatis sacerdotii & sacrificii, quasi diceret, si esset in terra Sacerdos, id est, minister tabernaculi, quod est, super terram, ne Sacerdos quidem esset: Ratio est evidens, quia cum non esset ex tribu Levi, aut ex suc- cessoribus Aaronis, non potuit tabernaculo illi terre- stri servire, & in eo fungi sacerdotio. Hæc ratio ad- ditur in ipso textu: Cum essent, qui offerrent secundum legem munera, qui exemplari serviunt cælestium. Christus certe talis Sacerdos non fuit, sed ipse res cæle- stis illa fuit, à qua aliæ omnes pendent, quorum exem- plari serviebat Leviticum sacerdotium. Christus ergo non est Sacerdos in terris, non quasi in terris sacrificium non peregerit, sed quia more Leviticorum Sacerdotum oblationem terrenam non habuit, quæ figura tantum & umbra futurorum fuit. Quid hac explicatione admissa lucrari pro ἀπροσία Humanæ naturæ post adscensionem è terris Calviniani velint, siquidem ipsimet viderint.

Nonnulli è nostris per verba ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς intelli- gunt ἐπίγειον terrenum, hoc sensu: Si terrenus esset (Sacerdos) ne quidem Sacerdos esset, quum sint Sa- cerdotes offerentes secundum legem dona, qui non minus terrenum offerre possent sacrificium. Et quæ sequuntur v. 5. pro nova ratione habent. Quomodo esset Sacerdos & antitypus, si offerret terre- num sacrificium? Cum omne terrenum sacrificium de- serviat umbræ rerum cælestium. Sed eo pacto agno- scunt, in verbis, ne quidem Sacerdos esset, intelligi Sacerdotem illum verum & antitypum, quod o- mnino statuendum. Ideoque una ratio tantum est, non diversæ: hoc modo: Si in terra adhuc esset, ne esset quidem verus ille Sacerdos per Sacerdotes Le- viticos præfiguratus, quum Sacerdotes obtulerint secundum legem dona, qui servierunt umbræ cæ- lestium, ideoq; ipsum oportuerit non manere in terra ad morẽ servientiũ umbræ, sed in ipsum cælu penetrare. Accedit, quod juxta istã explicationem, fatente B. D. König, à proprietate literæ recedatur, quodq; statuatur præterea phrasin ἐπὶ γῆς εἶναι hic non tã negari debere de ipso Christo Sacerdote, quã de sacrificio ejus: Siquidẽ velint oppositionẽ fieri in medio hoc speciali, quod Christus hostiã nobiliorẽ obtulerit, & ea propter Sacerdos Levitis nobilior, quod cũ glossa ordin. & Job. Calvino idem B. D. König in vind. Sacr. loc. 30. pag. 172. asserit, addita hac ra- tione, quod τὸ γῆς, includens conditionem terre- nam & de personis usurpatum construatur cum Præpositione ἐκ, Esa. 41, 24. Joh. 3, 31. De rebus autem cum ἐπὶ reperiatur Col. 3, 2. At illa εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς de Sacerdote dicta esse, non de sacrifi- cio, communis hactenus sententia fuit. Denique gra- tis illi assumunt λειτουργὸν τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς nihil aliud significare, quam Christum esse sacrificatorem proprii corporis, & illa, τῶν ἁγίων καὶ σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς ἐξηγητικῶς dici. Aliud ex interpretatione nostra jam exposita constitit.

Grotii autem glossa ad v. 4. probari non potest: Si in terris supple tantum, obeundum ei fuisset mini- sterium, nihil opus erat, eum fieri Sacerdotem, erant, qui ista offerrent, quæ in lege præscripta sunt. Ni- hil opus erat, ob id Messiam mitti. Nam ita 1. in- geritur temere particula tantum, quæ in textu non habetur. 2. Verba εἰ ἦν ἐπὶ γῆς non significant, si in terris ei obeundum fuisset ministerium, sed, si in ter- ris esset. 3. Verba εἰδ᾽ ἂν ἦν ἱερεὺς non signifi- cant, nihil opus erat, eum fieri Sacerdotem, nedum nihil opus erat, Messiam mitti: Sed ne esset quidem ipse (JESUS) Sacerdos. 4. Verbum ὄντων hic respicere tempus Psaltis, non vero tempus Christi novo commento fingitur, ut novus sensus extor- queatur. 5. Non id agebat Apostolus, ut doce- ret opus fuisse, ut Messias mitteretur, sed id de- monstrare vult, Christum, si verus Pontifex haberi debeat, non in terris manere, ut Pontifices Veteris Testamenti, quamdiu Pontificatu fungebantur, in terris erant, & manebant, debuisse, sed oportuisse, peracto in terris sacrificio, cœlum ingredi, quem- admodum, peracto sacrificio, in sanctum sancto- rum ingrediebantur Pontifices Veteris Testamen- ti, cum quibus hic CHRISTUM jam componit, adeoque si in terris adhuc esset, inquit Apostolus, Sacerdos, siquidem essent etiam Christi tempore Sacerdotes, qui secundum legem dona offerrent, donec, scisso in morte Christi velo, omnibus, non tantum Pontifici summo, pateret ingressus in san- ctum sanctorum, ubi amplius illi solenni Pontificis in sanctuarium ingressui locus non erat.

## 8:5
Ver. 5.

Οἵτινες ὑποδείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ λατρεύουσι τῶν ἐπουρανίων] He well gives the reason why a greater Priest had to be sent, because that worship was shadowy. The principal things are called bodies, but those things which have a signification of the principal things are called shadows, by a very clear metaphor, Coloss. 2:17. See also below chapter 10, verse 1. Δεῖγμα is a part taken from a thing, from which the quality of the thing may be understood. The Latins say specimen, and thus that Greek word is explained in the Glossary. Ὑπόδειγμα is something less, not a part of the thing, but something similar. See below chapter 9:23, James 5:10, 2 Peter 2:6. See also above chapter 4:11. The tent in the times of Moses, and indeed the temple after Solomon, were nothing other than shadows of the whole universe and of the government of GOD in the universe, of which the principal part is that region above the ether. See below chapter 9.

The reason is not given here why a greater Priest had to be sent, but why it was necessary for Christ the Priest to enter into heaven after the offering of his body, if indeed the Aaronic Priests offering sacrifices κατὰ τὸν νόμον were types of him: And they indeed performed their priesthood only on earth, as serving only a shadow of heavenly things, whereas Christ as the true High Priest had to perform his priesthood not only on earth, but by his entrance into heaven had to become the λειτουργὸς τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς. By ὑπόδειγμα the Vulgate understands an exemplar. But Estius warns that the Greek is a sub-showing, i.e., an obscure delineation, and that Theophylact explains it thus. Regarding the word σκιᾶς (shadow), he observes that the metaphor does not refer to the shadow which a body placed in the sun casts from itself, so that the shadow is opposed to the body, but that it is taken from painters, who first outline the image they wish to make with rough drawn lines. But how shall we understand this whole universe through heavenly things? Those things are called heavenly which are figured here, because the things which are in Christ, the true Priest, are truly heavenly mysteries, and not merely naked earthly figures, and things of that kind which pertained to the earth: The Priest there was earthly, here the Lord is heavenly from heaven; There the sacrifices were earthly, here Christ offered himself as a sacrifice, whom John professed to be not ἐκ τῆς γῆς, but ἐκ τῦ ὀρανῦ, John 3:31. There the High Priest entered into the holy place, which was on earth and earthly, here into the true holy place, that is, into heaven itself: Add that there also there were figures of heavenly goods, when, for example, spiritual purification was shadowed forth by Levitical purifications: Which, however, seem to be hinted at not so much here as in the following words about a better testament. Yet Theophylact joins all these things here, because the Priesthood and the Testament cohere, and the Priest and the Mediator of the New Testament concur in Christ, as the Apostle will now teach. But the Aaronic Priests did not shadow forth the government of God in the universe, just as neither the Mosaic tabernacle nor the Solomonic temple were a ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σκιὰ of the universe, and also of some created region above the ether, which Grotius invents with the Papists, the empyrean heaven, and with the Calvinists, who imagine some heaven above the firmament, I know not what (for they themselves do not know what it is, material or spiritual?): But they shadowed forth CHRIST, and his priesthood, which he partly performed on earth, and partly still performs in the heavens: Concerning which the Apostle treats here, not concerning the government of the universe, of which it is said, without scripture and in a manner unheard of among Christians, that the Aaronic priesthood was a type. In this place, says Theophylact, where CHRIST now enjoys the heavens, he argues for the excellence of the priesthood, since he calls the Old Testament indeed a certain figure and shadow, but ours are called heavenly, in which there is nothing earthly, but all things are spiritual, which are perfected by these mysteries. For in these both the Angels sing together in hymns, and the keys of the heavenly kingdom, and the remission of sins, and again the binding are present, and finally our conversation is in the heavens. Therefore the Priests of the law prefer the figures and shadows of these, that is, certain obscure arguments, and shadowy lines, which are revealed in the Old Testament through Moses.

Καθὼς κεχρημάτισαι Μωσῆς] Divinely instructed. Concerning the verb χρηματίζεσθαι see Matt. 2, 12. 22. Acts 10, 22. below chapter 11, 7. in which places you see the Passive formed in the Greek manner from the Active governing the Dative: So that it is permitted to explain καθὼς κεχρημάτισαι τῷ Μωσῇ by that locution which we have in Luke 2, 26. The Hebrews would say צוה in the Pual.

Μέλλων ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν σκηνὴν] Namely Exod. 25, 40. To which Stephen also refers in Acts 7, 44.

Ποιήσας πάντα κατὰ τὸν τύπον τὸν δειχθέντα σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει] These are the words of the LXX, except that πάντα is added. That example shown to Moses on the mountain was spiritual, its figure was corporeal. But that spiritual thing signified a thing much more spiritual, and the mountain the highest heaven. The ancient Hebrews also saw that this was the mystical sense of that place in Exodus. Philo in the book 'The Worse Attacks the Better': Ἡ δὲ Μωϋσέως σκηνὴ συμβολικῶς ὖσα ἀνθρώπε ἀρετὴ, κλήσεως ὀχ ὑπάρξεως ἀξιωθήσεται, μίμημα καὶ ἀπεικόνισμα τῆς θείας ἐκείνης ὑπάρχυσα. The same author in the book 'On Drunkenness' says: Σκηνὴν ἀρετῆς ἀσωμάτε σύμβολον. And in 'On the Life of Moses': Σκηνὴν ἧς ἔργον ἱερώτατον δημιεργῆι ἔδοξεν, ἧς τὴν κατασκευὴν θεσφάτοις λόγοις ἐπὶ τῶ ὄρες Μωϋσῆς ἀνεδιδάσκετο, τῶν μελλόντων ἀποτελεῖσθαι σωμάτων ἀσωμάτες ἰδέας τῇ ψυχῇ θεωρῶν, πρὸς ἃς ἔδει, καθάπερ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχετύπε γραφῆς καὶ νοητῶν παραδειγμάτων αἰσθητὰ μιμήματα ἀπεικονισθῆναι.

The Vulgate rendered it: As it was answered to Moses. But χρηματίζειν, as Estius warns, is not simply to answer, but to deliver or give an oracle, even if one has not been asked, chap. 11, 7. chap. 12, 25. Nor could Estius prove that which the Vulgate explained for the words μέλλων ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν σκηνὴν, when he was to finish the tabernacle: That it ought to be rendered, When he was about to finish the tabernacle, that is, about to make it, he rightly advises. Because the words which the Apostle cites were said to Moses before he had begun to make the tabernacle, as those by which the form of making the tabernacle was prescribed, Exod. 25, 40. In which place the word πάντα is not indeed held, as far as the letter goes, yet the sense is universal: see v. 9. and they shall make me a sanctuary according to all the likeness of the tabernacle which I will show you, and of all the vessels for its worship. Κατὰ τὸν τύπον, says this Apostle here from the LXX. To the interpreters, the Vulgate renders it exemplar, just as a little before it explained ὑπόδειγμα. But Estius observes that exemplar is not understood here as shadowy or prefigurative, but as proposed for imitation, and that this is the more proper meaning of exemplar. Most people establish the reason and strength of the argument in this, that God himself prescribed the type, according to which all things in the tabernacle ought to have been adorned and perfected, and did not permit it to human invention, which is also observed in the adorning of the temple, 2 Chron. 28, 19. which was done not without mystery, but so that it might be understood that something was signified by those things which were to be observed concerning the tabernacle and the temple. Grotius thinks that the prototype shown to Moses on the mountain was something spiritual, and that the same thing signified something more spiritual, which we do not reluctantly admit, provided it is rightly understood and the Apostle's argument is not weakened. For he is already dealing with the priesthood of Christ, and just as all things that pertained to the tabernacle had to be perfected according to the prescribed exemplar, on account of a certain spiritual signification; so he concludes that the priesthood, for whose sake the tabernacle was constructed, also had a mystical signification, and was only a shadow with respect to that which was shadowed forth by it. For that on account of which each thing is such, that thing is more such. Now, the tabernacle had to be adorned so accurately according to the Lord's prescription on account of the priesthood, for the sake of a spiritual signification. Therefore, much more was the priesthood to be instituted according to the Lord's prescription on account of a mystical signification. Pareus proves the consequence thus: In correlates there is a mutual path. The type refers to the archetype. Conversely, the archetype is represented by the type, because the type is made to the figure of the archetype. Since, therefore, the earthly tabernacle was fashioned by God's command according to the heavenly archetype, it is therefore rightly said to have been the exemplar and shadow of the heavenly archetype. But what else is proved by that reasoning than that the earthly tabernacle was a shadow of the archetype which God showed to Moses from heaven? But the Apostle does not intend to prove that, but that it was a shadow of the heavenly things which are held in the New Testament. Pareus therefore leaves the doubt, he does not dissolve it. Others wish the Apostle to draw the argument from the word תַּבְנִית of likeness. For because through that tabernacle and those things which were done in it, God wished to prefigure those things which pertain to the priesthood of CHRIST, he therefore prescribed its form as most convenient for signifying these things. Thus B. Gerhard with Estius. But thus it is supposed what was to be proved by the Apostle, namely, that through that tabernacle, and those things which were done in it, God wished to prefigure those things which pertain to the priesthood of CHRIST. B. Hunnius touched the core more closely: The difference, he says, between CHRIST and other priests consists principally in this, that Christ, indeed, ordained as a Priest according to the order of Melchizedek, is occupied with the substance of things once shadowed forth: While the priests of the Levitical order serve only an exemplar in the tabernacle, the idea of which the Lord showed to Moses on the mountain, and by this very showing of the exemplar he wished to declare that that earthly tabernacle would be as it were the image and shadow or exemplar of another. B. Dorscheus explains the Apostolic consequence thus: Whose priesthood's institutions were adorned according to the type shown to Moses from heaven on the mountain, and no priesthood to be perpetually administered in these lands ought to have succeeded. Whence neither was the Messiah's priesthood to be perpetually administered in these lands. But the institutions of the Levitical sacrifice were adorned according to the type shown from heaven on the mountain. Therefore, to them ought not to have succeeded, etc. The major proposition of this latter argument seems to be confirmed from this, because the type was shown to Moses from heaven on the mountain for this reason, when he was about to construct the tabernacle, so that by this very thing it might be indicated that, with the tabernacle or sanctuary finished and completed according to the type shown from heaven, the priesthood would be there where the archetype is. Nor would any priesthood to be perfected and perpetuated in these lands according to the heavenly type succeed. He observes, moreover, that the χρηματισμὸς which happened to Moses was not only concerning the tabernacle with respect to its form, but also with respect to its end, and indeed its principal and ultimate one. But this χρηματισμὸς is said to have happened to Moses when he wished ἐπιτελεῖν, that is, to begin, so that he might finish (for the χρηματισμὸς did not happen in the middle of the act of constituting the tabernacle, but before it was begun, chap. 26, 1.) the tabernacle, χρηματισμὸς, he himself commands all things to be made (thus the LXX insert τὰ πάντα according to the sense of v. 8, 9) according to the type shown on the mountain, which without doubt embraced not only the delineation of the tabernacle and of those things which ought to have been in it, but also insinuated the mysteries themselves by a certain reason. These things are from B. Dorscheus. But if neither these, nor the reason for the Apostolic inference previously rendered by us, which I see Cameron also hinted at, should satisfy, it must perhaps be said that by the word type here is signified not a bare figure or something shadowy, but the archetype itself, so called because of the similarity which the Hebrew word introduces, since the Apostle interchanges these words, when in the following chapter, verse 24, he calls the patterns of the things in the heavens ἀντίτυπα τῶν ἀληθινῶν, thus opposing the antitypes to the true things, so that the true thing is the type, namely the correlate or opposite to the antitype. If therefore in this place he understands by type the true things, the sense will be that Moses had to adorn everything so that they might be conformed to the true things, which were shown to him on the mountain by GOD. In which way the Apostle will intimate that there was a similarity and conformity of the earthly tabernacle with the type, that is, those heavenly things which were shown to Moses, and which had to be shadowed forth by the earthly tabernacle. Which is the explanation of Piscator: By the name of type or pattern is to be understood the archetype or that primary model of heavenly or spiritual things, which through the tabernacle and the ceremonies annexed to it, and accustomed to be celebrated in it, were as it were shadowed forth by antitypes. But those things are the very death of CHRIST upon the altar of the cross, and his entry into the sanctuary of heaven, which things, as appears from the present passage, were shown to Moses Divinely in the Spirit.

But since the word τύπꙋ in the words of God has as its correlate the tabernacle to be constructed by Moses, which was to be adorned according to the likeness and type shown to Moses: there seems to be no place for that explanation. Piscator himself certainly acknowledges that Moses was commanded by that oracle to confirm the entire structure of the tabernacle to the pattern which had been shown to him on the mountain. Therefore, it will perhaps be more correctly said that the expression δειχθέντα signifies not a simple showing, but one made with a declaration of its meaning, or at least that an explanation of the type was joined to that showing of the type, concerning the meaning of which Moses had been informed on the mountain. In the Talmud, Chagigah chapter II, it is read thus: R. Simeon said: At the hour when God commanded the Israelites to erect the tabernacle, He indicated to the angels of ministry that they too should make a tabernacle. When, therefore, the lower tabernacle was erected, a higher tabernacle was also erected for Metraton, or the Angel Metator, in which he offers the souls of the just to make expiation for Israel during the time of their captivity. And for this reason it is said אֶת־הַוּוֹי שָׁכַן in Exodus 40, as if to say, with the tabernacle, because another tabernacle was erected with it. These things are wrapped in Talmudic trifles. But they undoubtedly involve mysteries handed down by the Prophets of old. By the Angel Metator they understand him of whom it is written in Exodus 23:21, 'my name is in the midst of him,' who, as Elijah testifies in the Tisbi, is called the Prince of the Countenances, of whom the Talmudists write that power was given to him to sit and record the merits of the Israelites, whose name is Michael, who was also the tutor of Moses; see Buxtorf's Lexicon Talmudicum, p. 1191. And by Gematria they call שדי God Almighty, and established as the Ruler of all, and Lord of the whole house, to whom all things are subject, the Redeemer of the angels, in whom is that great name of God, the Angel of the face of God, nay, the very face of God, concerning which and other things see Buxtorf's History of the Ark of the Covenant, page 132, as the traces of the ancient theology of the Hebrews in chapter I of this epistle, nay, throughout the whole epistle, established among the Hebrews from the sacred Scriptures. That the Rabbis, according to their custom, wished to express Cabalistically in this way that this Redeemer offers the souls of the just—either by presenting them through his intercession to the grace of God, or by offering himself for them, taking their place, and satisfying for them to make expiation for all Israel, for their liberation from spiritual captivity, according to the ancient faith received from the Patriarchs and Prophets—we have no doubt. We have observed other things of that kind here and there. These things, therefore, seem to imply that the idea of the tabernacle was not only shown to Moses on the mountain, but was at the same time handed down, or exhibited, and represented. We judge it not unreasonable, and certainly consistent with the truth, that these things were handed down or even represented to such a servant of God, Moses, by God, who spoke with the Lord face to face, as a friend speaks with a friend, and who saw the Lord in His form, Num. 12:8. For it seems likely that God, when He conversed so familiarly with Moses and called him up to Himself on the mountain, did not show him only bare and shadowy types and figures, but primarily revealed the τὰ ἀληθινὰ, the τὰ ἐπεράνια, as the end and goal of such an elaborate structure, so that such a great Prophet of God might not be ignorant of them. Flacius observes that God did not merely show the idea of the work to Moses in idleness, which he was to imitate in the construction of the tabernacle; but that He wished to signify that the true tabernacle, and the holy of holies, and the true Priest, and that Lamb slain from eternity, and that abundant redemption or propitiation, which is to be sought perpetually by begging faith at the throne of grace, exist properly with Him. This, which God undoubtedly wished to signify, He also openly explained to Moses, so faithful a servant in all His house: which is now opened here to the Hebrews by the leader of the Apostles. But that heaven was signified by those things which were shown to Moses on the mountain, and by the tabernacle adorned after that likeness, we concede only as far as the holy of holies, which was a pattern of it: nor do we judge that those things brought forward from Philo concerning mighty works fit here. The allegories of Philo and the Hebrews are well known, rarely drawn from the Scriptures, most frequently imposed upon the Scriptures. And not only the form of the tabernacle, but also those things which were to be expiated in it, seem to have been shown to Moses. As Theophylact says: For since we perceive more keenly those things which we behold with our eyes than those which we learn by hearing, for that reason God revealed all things to Moses. And not only the form of the tabernacle, but also how it was to be sacrificed, and other rites and worship were to be performed.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

Οἵτινες ὑποδείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ λατρεύουσι τῶν ἐπουρανίων] Bene causam reddit, cur major Sacerdos mitti debuerit, quia ille cultus erat umbratilis. Res principales vocan- tur corpora, ea vero, quæ rerum principalium signifi- cationem habent, umbræ, perspicua admodum transla- tione, Coloss. 2, 17. Vide & infra cap. 10. vers. 1. Δεῖγμα est pars de re sumpta, unde rei qualitas intelligatur. Latini dicunt specimen, & sic vox illa Græca in Glossa- rio exponitur. Ὑπόδειγμα minus aliquid, non pars rei, sed simile quiddam. Vide infra cap. 9, 23. Jac. 5, 10. 2. Petr. 2, 6. Vide & supra cap. 4, 11. Tentorium Mo- sis temporibus, templum vero post Salomonem nihil aliud erant, quam umbræ totius universi & gubernationis DEI in universo, cujus pars præcipua est regio illa superætherea. Vide infra cap. 9.

Non hic causa redditur, cur major Sacerdos mit- ti debuerit, sed cur in cœlum ingredi oportuerit Chri- stum Sacerdotem post oblationem corporis sui, si- quidem Sacerdotes Aaronici sacrificia offerentes κατὰ τὸν νόμον typi fuerint ipsius: Et illi quidem in terris tantum defuncti sint sacerdotio suo, utpote inservientes solum umbræ rerum cœlestium, quum Christus ceu verus Pontifex non in terris tantum sacerdotio fungi, sed per ingressum in cœlum τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἀληθινῆς λειτουργὸς fieri debuerit. Per ὑπόδειγμα Vulgata intelligit exem- plar. Sed Estius monet, Græcum esse subosten- sionem, f. obscuram delineationem, atque ita ex- ponere Theophylactum. Circa vocem σκιᾶς um- bræ observat, metaphoram non respicere umbram, quam corpus in sole positum de se projicit, ut scili- cet umbra corpori opponatur, sed desumptam esse à pictoribus, qui imaginem, quam facere volunt, prius adumbrant rudibus ductis lineamentis. Quomodo autem per cœlestia totum hoc univer- sum intelligemus? Cœlestia dicuntur, quæ hic figurata sunt, quia quæ in Christo sunt, vero Sacer- dote, verè cœlestia sunt mysteria, non autem nudæ tantum terrenæ figuræ, & res ejusmodi, quæ ad terras pertinebant: Terrenus ibi Sacerdos erat, hic Dominus de cælo cœlestis; Ibi terrenæ ho- stia, hic Christus seipsum in hostiam obtulit, quem non ἐκ τῆς γῆς, sed ἐκ τῦ ὀρανῦ esse Johannes pro- fessus est, Joh. 3, 31. Ibi in sanctum, quod erat in terris & terrenum, ingressus est Pontifex, hic in sanctum verum, hoc est, in cælum ipsum: Adde quod ibi etiam cœlestium bonorum figuræ exti- terint, cum v. g. purificationibus Leviticis purifi- catio spiritualis adumbrata: Quæ tamen non tam hic, quam verbis sequentibus de meliori testamento innui videntur. Conjungit tamen ista hic omnia Theophylactus, quod cohæreant Sacerdotium & Testamentum ac Sacerdos & Mediator Novi Testamenti in Christo concurrant, uti jam doce- bit Apostolus. Non autem adumbrabant Sa- cerdotes Aaronici gubernationem Dei in univer- so, quemadmodum nec tabernaculum Mosaicum vel templum Salominicum ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σκιὰ universi, ac regionis etiam cujusdam creatæ super- æthereæ, quam Grotius comminiscitur cum Pa- pistis, cælum empyræum, & cum Calvinianis cœ- lum, supra firmamentum, nescio quod (nam & ipsi quodnam nesciunt, materialené, an spiritua- le?) fingentibus: Sed adumbrabant CHRISTUM , ejusque sacerdotium, quo in terris partim fun- ctus est, partim etiamnum in cœlis fungitur: De quo hic tractat Apostolus, non de guberna- tione universi, cujus typum fuisse sacerdotium Aaronicum ἄτερ γραφῆς, & ratione inter Chri- stianos inaudita dicitur. Hoc loco, inquit Theo- phylactus, quo CHRISTUS in cælis jam fruitur, sacerdotii arguit excellentiam, cum vetus quidem testamentum figuram quandam & umbram dicat, nostra vero cælestia dici, in quibus nihil est terrenum, sed spiritualia cuncta, quæ hisce mysteriis perficiun- tur. In his enim & Angeli concinunt hymnis, cæ- lestis & regni claves, & peccatorum remissio, rursum & colligatio insunt, & nostra deniq; in cælis est con- versatio. Horum itaq; figuras & umbras legis præ- ferunt Sacerdotes, id est, subobscura quædam ar- gumenta, & umbratiles lineas, quæ in Veteri sunt Testamento per Mosen patefacta.

Καθὼς κεχρημάτισαι Μωσῆς] Divinitus edoctus. De verbo χρηματίζεσθαι vide Matth. 2, 12. 22. Actor. 10, 22. infra cap. 11, 7. quibus in locis vides more Græco Passi- vum formari ab Activo Dativum regente: Ita, ut expli- care liceat καθὼς κεχρημάτισαι τῷ Μωσῇ ea loquutione, quam habemus Luc. 2, 26. Ebræi dicerent צוה in Pual.

Μέλλων ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν σκηνὴν] Nempe Exod. 25, 40. Quo respicit & Stephanus Act. 7, 44.

Ποιήσας πάντα κατὰ τὸν τύπον τὸν δειχθέντα σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει] Verba sunt LXX, nisi quod additum est πάντα. Exemplum illud in monte Mosi monstratum erat spiritua- le, corporeum ejus figura. At illud spirituale significa- vit rem multo magis spiritualem, & mons cœlum supre- mum. Hunc sensum esse loci istius in Exodo mysticum viderunt & veteres Ebræi. Philo libro pejorem insidiari meliori. Ἡ δὲ Μωϋσέως σκηνὴ συμβολικῶς ὖσα ἀνθρώπε ἀρετὴ, κλήσεως ὀχ ὑπάρξεως ἀξιωθήσεται, μίμημα καὶ ἀπεικόνισμα τῆς θείας ἐκείνης ὑπάρχυσα. Idem libro de ebrietate dicit: Σκηνὴν ἀρετῆς ἀσωμάτε σύμβολον. Et de vita Mosis: Σκηνὴν ἧς ἔργον ἱερώτατον δημιεργῆι ἔδο- ξεν, ἧς τὴν κατασκευὴν θεσφάτοις λόγοις ἐπὶ τῶ ὄρες Μωϋ- σῆς ἀνεδιδάσκετο, τῶν μελλόντων ἀποτελεῖσθαι σωμάτων ἀ- σωμάτες ἰδέας τῇ ψυχῇ θεωρῶν, πρὸς ἃς ἔδει, καθάπερ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχετύπε γραφῆς καὶ νοητῶν παραδειγμάτων αἰσθητὰ μιμήματα ἀπεικονισθῆναι.

Vulgata reddidit: Sicut responsum est Mosi. Sed χρηματίζειν monente Estio, non est simpliciter re- spondere, sed oraculum reddere seu dare, etiamsi in- terrogatus non fuerit, cap. 11, 7. cap. 12, 25. Nec id probare potuit Estius, quod Vulgata verba μέλλων ἐπιτελεῖν τὴν σκηνὴν exposuit, cum consummaret ta- bernaculum: Reddi debere, Cum esset consumma- turus tabernaculum, id est, facturus, recte monet. Quia verba, quæ citat Apostolus, dicta sunt Mosi, priusquam tabernaculum facere cœpisset, utpote qui- bus forma tabernaculi faciendi præscripta, Exod. 25, 40. In quo loco non quidem vox πάντα ha- betur, quoad τὸ ῥητὸν, sensus tamen universalis est: vi v. 9. facientq́; mihi sanctuarium juxta omnem si- militudinem tabernaculi, quod ostendam tibi, & o- mnium vasorum in cultum ejus. Κατὰ τὸν τύπον, inquit hic Apostolus è LXX. Interpretibus, Vulga- ta reddit exemplar, ut paulo ante ὑπόδειγμα ex- posuerit. Ast intelligi hic exemplar non umbra- ticum, aut præfigurativum, sed propositum ad imi- tandum, eamque magis propriam esse exemplaris significationem, observat Estius. Rationem & nervum argumenti in eo constituunt plerique, quod Deus ipse typum præscripserit, juxta quam debuerint omnia in tabernaculo adornari & per- fici, non vero id humanæ inventioni permiserit, quod etiam in templo adornando observatur, 2. Paral. 28, 19. quod non citra mysterium factum, sed ut aliquid significari illis, quæ circa tabernacu lum & templum observanda erant, intelligeretur. Grotius ita censet, prototypum in monte ostensum Mosi aliquid spirituale fuisse, idemq́; aliquid magis spirituale significasse, quod haud ægre admittimus, si modo recte intelligatur, neque argumentum A- postoli enervetur. Nam is de sacerdotio Christi jam agit, & uti omnia, quæ ad tabernaculum spe- ctabant, juxta exemplar præscriptum perfici debe- bant, ob spiritualem quandam significationem; ita etiam sacerdotium, cujus causa tabernaculum con- structum, mysticam habuisse significationem, & umbram tantum fuisse respectu ejus, quod eodem adumbratum est, colligit. Propter quod enim unumquodque tale est, illud magis tale est. Jam propter sacerdotium tam accurate tabernaculum secundum præscriptum Domini adornandum e- rat, significationis spiritualis causa. Multo ergo magis sacerdotium secundum præscriptum Domi- ni erat instituendum ob mysticam significationem. Pareus ita consequentiam probat: In correlatis est mutuum iter. Typus refert archetypum. Vicissim archetypum repræsentatur typo, quia typus est ad fi- guram archetypi factus. Quoniam igitur taber- naculum terrenum Dei jussu erat juxta archetypum cæleste effigiatum, ideo recte dicitur fuisse archetypi cælestis exemplar & umbra. Sed quid ea ratione aliud probatur, quam quod tabernaculum terre- num archetypi, quod de cælo ostendit Deus Mo- si, umbra fuerit. At Apostolus non id probare intendit, sed quod umbra fuerit rerum cælestium, quæ in Novo Testamento habentur. Relinquit ergo Pareus, non dissolvit dubium. Alii argu- mentum ducere Apostolum volunt ex voce תַּבְנִית similitudinis. Quia enim per illud tabernaculum & ea, quæ in illo gerebantur, Deus voluit præfigurare ea, quæ ad CHRISTI sacerdotium pertinent, ideo formam ejus præscripsit ad hæc significanda conve- nientissimam. Ita B. Gerhardus cum Estio. Sed ita supponitur, quod probandum erat ab Aposto- lo, nimirum, quod per illud tabernaculum, & ea, quæ in illo fiebant, Deus præfigurare voluerit ea, quæ ad sacerdotium CHRISTI pertinent. Pro- pius nervum attigit B. Hunnius: Discrimen, inquit, CHRISTI & Sacerdotum cæterorum in eo principaliter consistit, quod Christus quidem jux- ta ordinem Melchisedech ordinatus Sacerdos, circa rerum olim adumbratarum substantiam occupatus est: Cùm Sacerdotes Levitici ordinis exemplari tan- tum inserviant in tabernaculo, cujus ideam Domi- nus Mosi in monte commonstravit, & hac ipsa com- monstratione exemplaris declarare voluit, fore terre- num illud tabernaculum alterius cujusdam velut ima- ginem atque umbram sive exemplar. B. Dorscheus ita consequentiam Apostolicam explicat: Cujus sacerdotii instituta juxta typum in monte cælitus Mosi ostensum adornata fuerunt, & non debuit ali- quod sacerdotium in his terris perpetuo administran- dum succedere. Unde nec Messiæ sacerdotium in his terris perpetuo administrandum fuerat. At in- stituta sacrificii Levitici secundum typum in monte cælitus ostensum adornata fuerunt. Ergo illis non debuit succedere &c. Major propositio hujus poste- rioris argumenti ex eo confirmari videtur, quia Mosi propterea cum tabernaculum esset constructurus, ty- pus in monte cælitus ostensus fuit, ut hoc ipso indica- retur, tabernaculo vel sanctuario juxta typum cæli- tus ostensum confecto, consummato, ibi sacerdotium fore, ubi archetypus est. Neg; successurum aliquod juxta typum cælestem perficiendum & perpetuan- dum in his terris sacerdotium. Observat insuper χρηματισμὸν, qui Mosi contigit, non tantum de ta- bernaculo fuisse respectu formæ, sed etiam respectu fi- nis, & quidem principalis & ultimi. Dicitur au- tem iste χρηματισμὸς contigisse Mosi, cum vellet ἐπιτελεῖν, hoc est, inchoare, ut perficeret (non enim in medio actu constituendi tabernaculi χρηματισμὸς contigit, sed antequam inchoaretur cap. 26, 1.) τὴν σκηνὴν, χρηματισμὸς, ipse mandat facienda esse omnia (ita LXX. τὰ πάντα inserunt juxta sententiam v. 8. 9.) juxta typum in monte ostensum, qui procul du- bio non tantum delineationem tabernaculi, & eorum, quæ in eo esse debuerant, complexus est, sed & myste- ria ipsa certa ratione insinuavit. Hæc B. Dor- scheus. Quod si vero neque hæc, neque prius à nobis reddita ratio illationis Apostolicæ, quam etiam Cameronem video subinnuisse, satisfaciat, dicendum fortassis per typum hic non nudam fi- guram aut umbratile quid significari, sed ipsum archetypum ob similitudinem, quam vox Ebræa infert, ita dictum, siquidem Apostolus has voces permutet, cum cap. sequentis vers. 24. ἀντίτυπα τῶν ἀληθινῶν vocet τὰ ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὀυρανοῖς, opponens ita ἀντίτυπα τοῖς ἀληθινοῖς, ut τὸ ἀληθινὸν sit τύπος correlatum nempe vel op- positum τῷ ἀντιτύπῳ. Si ergo hoc loco per τύπον intelligat τὰ ἀληθινὰ, sensus erit, Mosen debuisse omnia adornare, ut conformia sint τοῖς ἀληθινοῖς, quæ ipsi exhibita in monte à DEO. Quo pacto innuet Apostolus similitu- dinem & conformitatem fuisse tabernaculi ter- reni cum τύπῳ, id est, cælestibus illis rebus, quæ monstratæ Mosi sint, & umbrari debue- rint per terrenum tabernaculum. Quæ Piscato- ris explicatio est: Nomine τύπȣ seu exemplaris intelligendus est archetypus seu primarium illud exemplar rerum cælestium sive spiritualium, quæ per tabernaculum & ceremonias ei annexas, atque in eo celebrari solitas, fuerunt tanquam per ἀντί- τυπα adumbratæ. Eæ autem res sunt ipsa mors CHRISTI super altare crucis, & ingressus ipsius sanctuarium cæli, quæ res, ut ex præsente loco apparet, Mosi Divinitus in Spiritu ostensæ fuerunt.

Sed quum vox τύπꙋ in verbis Dei pro correlato habeat tabernaculum à Mose construendum, quod juxta similitudinem & typum Mosi monstratum adornandum erat : nec illi explicationi locus esse videtur. Agnoscit certe Piscator ipse, quod Mo- ses illo oraculo jussus sit, totam tabernaculi stru- cturam confirmare exemplari, quod ei ostensum fuerat in monte. Id ergo rectius forte dicetur voce δειχθέντα exprimi ostensionem non simplicem, sed cum declaratione significationis factam, aut certe isti typi ostensioni conjunctam fuisse typi explica- tionem, de cujus significatione Moses in monte in- formatus fuerit. In Thalmud Chagigah cap. II. ita legitur: R. Simeon dixit : Ea hora, qua jussit Deus Israelitas erigere tabernaculum, indicavit Angelis ministerii, ut & ipsi facerent tabernaculum. Cum itaq; erigeretur tabernaculum inferius, erectum quo- que fuit superius tabernaculum Metratoni, seu An- geli Metatoris, in quo offert animas justorum ad ex- piationem faciendam pro Israele tempore captivitatis ipsorum. Et hac de causa dicitur אֶת־הַוּוֹי שָׁכַן Exod. XL. quasi diceret, cum tabernaculo, quia aliud tabernaculum erectum fuit cum eo. Sunt hæc involuta Talmudicis nugis. Sed mysteria tamen olim à Prophetis tradita sine dubio invol- vunt. Per Angelum Metatorem intelligunt eum, de quo Exod. 23, 21. nomen meum in medio ejus, qui teste Elia in Tisbi ipsius dicatur Princeps facierum, de quo Talmudici scribunt, quod data sit ei po- testas, ut sedeat, & conscribat merita Israelitarum, cujus nomen sit Michael, qui Præceptor etiam Mosis fuerit; Vid. Buxtorffii Lexic. Thalm. p. 1191. Et per Gematriam שדי Deum omnipotentem di- cunt, & constitutum Dominatorem omnium, & Dominum totius domus, cui omnia subjecta sint, Angelorum Redemptorem, in quo est nomen illud Dei magnum, Angelum faciei Dei, imo fa- ciem Dei ipsam, quæ & alia vide in histor. Arcæ fœderis Buxtorffii pag. 132. ceu vestigia veteris Theologiæ Ebræorum cap. I. hujus epistolæ, imo per totam epistolam penes Ebræos è Scripturis sacris stabilita. Quem Redemptorem offerre ani- mas justorum, sive intercessione sua eas sistendo Divinæ gratiæ, sive pro iisdem semetipsum offe- rendo, vicem ipsorum subeundo, pro eisdem satis- faciendo ad expiationem faciendam pro Israele u- niverso, ad liberationem à spirituali captivitate, se- cundum antiquam à Patriarchis & Prophetis acce- ptam fidem ita pro more suo Cabalistice exprime- re Rabbinos voluisse, nullum nobis est dubium. Observavimus ejus generis alia passim. Hæc er- go Mosi, tum exhibita ipsi est in monte idea taber- naculi, simul tradita, vel exhibita, ac repræsentata fuisse, subinnuere videntur. Vero certe consen- taneum id non abs re censemus, quod tradita vel etiam repræsentata tanto DEI servo Mosi à DEO fuerint, qui cum de facie ad faciem, ceu amicus cum amico, loquutus est Dominus, quique Do- minum vidit in forma sua, Num. 12, 8. Verisimile enim videtur, Deum Mosi, cum quo adeo familia- riter conversatus est, quemq; in montem ad se ac- cessivit, non nudos tantum & umbratiles typos & fi- guras monstrasse, sed imprimis patefecisse τὰ ἀλη- θινὰ, τὰ ἐπεράνια, ut finem & scopum tam operosæ structuræ, ne ignoraret tantus Dei Propheta. Fla- cius observat, quod Deus non otiose tantum ideam operis monstravit Mosi, quam in constructione ta- bernaculi imitaretur; sed quod voluerit significare apud se proprie esse illud verum tabernaculum, ac sanctum sanctorum, verumq; Sacerdotem, ac illum ab æterno mactatum agnum, & illam copiosam re- demptionem aut propitiationem, quæ perpetuo sit mendica fide ad thronum gratiæ quærenda.
