XXV, verse 16, which was placed in the interior cavity of the ark. But the urn could nowhere be more rightly placed before the testimony than if it were placed at such an exterior side. Ribera retorts that by that very fact neither the urn nor the rod were in the ark, even with respect to some exterior sinus, which are said to be placed before the Lord and before the testimony. For thus also the golden lampstand is said in Exod. XXVII to be before the Lord, and in chapter XXX it is commanded that incense be made before the testimony. So also in Num. XVII it is commanded concerning the rod that it be stored before the testimony, v. 25. But the tables of the law are nowhere said to be before the Lord, because they were not outside but between the ark. R. Those things which are said to be before the Lord or the testimony, some are said to have been before the Lord more remotely, some more closely and conjunctively to the ark. In the latter way the budding rod and the golden urn were before the Lord, and by that very fact are said to have been before the Lord or the testimony, because they were stored in a certain exterior sinus, which is not said of the tables of the law for that reason, because they were placed between the ark. Ribera retorts again that the length of the ark was small, namely two and a half cubits, and therefore the budding rod of Aaron could not be placed in it. Resp. Yet it is nowhere indicated what the length of the budding rod was, and that it was longer than two and a half cubits. Furthermore, Ribera brings forward yet another interpretation, both in this place and in lib. II, de templ. c. 2, p. 105. It may be said that 'in which' is placed for 'with which', so that the sense is: with which ark there were at the same time in the tabernacle the rod, and the urn, and the tables; or with Anselm, that these were next to the ark, which kind of reconciliation also pleased B. Gerhard: 'It is answered most simply,' he says, 'that the preposition ἐν does not always signify in, but is sometimes placed for apud, juxta, corresponding to the prefix ב, adducing examples Matt. XXI. 12, Mark XI. 15, John X. 23, Luke IX. 31, chap. XIII, 33, and observing that also sometimes the preposition IN, like ב, is used for 'with', Deut. VI, 7, 1 Sam. I. 24, Acts VII. 38, 2 Pet. I. 5.' Nor is Capellus alien to this interpretation in his observations on the epistle to the Hebrews, page 142, nor Calixtus in his exposition on chapter XVI of Exodus, v. 33, 34. But that sense can hardly be admitted here, since the Apostle is not accurately distinguishing what was next to the ark, or with the ark in the holy of holies, but what was placed in the ark, in the holy of holies, distinguishing those things which were in the ark and which were above the ark, which is said of the Cherubim, which certainly were also with the ark in the holy of holies, and next to or by the ark. What? Because the Apostle says of the urn and the rod likewise, as of the tables of the law, that they were in the ark: but were the tables of the law only next to or by were they in the ark or with the ark, but not truly deposited in the ark or within the ark? Or must a double sense of the preposition ἐν be admitted here at the same time, which does not seem very probable to Drusius himself, Comment. ad loc. difficil. Ex. cap. XXIX. pag. 189. It is clearly more correctly denied by the blessed D. König that it ever in one simple statement sustains one meaning and another and at the same time denotes both within and with or near; as indeed Buxtorf contends: Nor did he speak badly, when inquiring, about these ἐν ᾗ, in which they were, for in and with which, because, as Scripture speaks, they were before the testimony, that is, either placed contiguously and very near to the ark, or they adhered to it continuously through an appendage added to the ark, so that both that which was in the appendage of the ark, and that which was within the ark, could be said to be ἐν αὐτῇ, in it, especially by one who does not undertake an accurate description of some thing. Thus, of course, it was not necessary to attach a double different meaning to one word placed once, but also to argue that the Apostle gave an inaccurate description, who so accurately designated those things which were below and which were above the ark. But then that the urn of Manna and the rod of Aaron were within the ark with the tables of the law, Interpreters write, and that it is so held in the Cabala or a certain tradition of the Rabbis, Abarbanel noted on 1 Kings 8:19, to which man of much reading and observation something about such a tradition undoubtedly became known, Buxtorf judges: Which R. Levi Ben Gerson gathers from chapter 16 of Exodus, verses 33, 34. But from the fact that he says before the testimony, rather than before the ark, we learn that they were within the ark (the urn of Manna and the rod of Aaron). For if they had been outside it, he would have had to say before the ark, not before the testimony, which for him is, before the tables. To which is added, that they were in better custody in the ark (than outside it) etc. Because, namely, Numbers 17:10 (to which place R. Levi annotates this) it is said: Bring the rod of Aaron before the testimony into custody. Which reasons, as we leave them to the Rabbis: So nevertheless it is certain by their own testimonies and tradition, that those things were within the ark, although they differ among themselves in their opinions about it. Moreover, B. König uses almost the same reasons on page 715. But what finally about the place 1 Kings 8:19? Vatablus renders this meaning: In the ark, understand from the book of the law, there was nothing, except the two tables of the law, i.e., from the whole law nothing was contained in that ark except the precepts of the Decalogue. Similarly to that place R. Levi Ben Gerson: This does not deny that those things were there, which are commemorated in the law to have been deposited in it, such as the rod of Aaron, and the little urn of Manna: But he only denies that anything else was placed there from the law, except the Decalogue, because that contains the sum of the whole law. Which can be opposed to R. Lusitanus in the work of the blessed D. Müller in Judaism page 1364, who attacks the present place of the epistle to the Hebrews, as if it were contrary to the place 1 Kings 8:9. Nor is D. König alien to that explanation, when carefully elucidating the present place: yet he still brings forward and prefers another, that namely exclusive particles sometimes appropriately exclude only and not absolutely universally, as in the same book of Kings chapter 22, verse 20, so that the meaning may be: Only two tables were in the ark, as the more principal treasures, for the preservation of which the ark was especially crafted. But by occasion the urn and the rod were also added. Which interpretation has Thomas as its author. Neither explanation, however, is without difficulty: not that of the Rabbis, because there is nothing there in the text from which it can be gathered that one must understand from the book of the law, or about the whole law, and such an interpretation is clearly arbitrary: Nor this Thomistic one, because not only other more principal things are excluded, but it is taught that nothing else was in the ark than the two tables. For the Holy Spirit does not say that only of the more principal things, or for which the ark was made, were the two tables in the ark: But there was nothing in it, except only two stone tables: Whence one must still rest in the opinion, toward which Ambrosius Catharinus inclined in his booklet on the keys of Scripture, second key, and book 1, annotations on Cajetan. to rest, which is thus reported by the blessed König and Buxtorf in the aforementioned places in exactly the same words: There are others, who distinguish the times, and say, that all these things were within the ark at that time, of which Paul speaks, namely when the tabernacle was first constructed, and as long as that ark had to be carried with the tabernacle through the desert: For then, since they did not have a convenient place to put those things, since the tabernacle was unstable and wandering, they had deposited them in the ark with the tables of the law, to which this place properly belonged: but when later the temple had been built, that is, the stable dwelling of the tabernacle and the ark of the Lord, and space was given, in which there could be more capacious repositories, then only the law remained within the ark, the rest were disposed and kept in their place beside it. And that the Apostle to the Hebrews indeed speaks about the state of the ambulatory tabernacle: But the book of Kings about the stable temple, at which time things were reduced into a more convenient order. O how solid this reconciliation would be, if it rested on as firm a proof as it does on vain divination, exclaims the blessed König! But we believe that the Apostolic place compared with the place in Kings is entirely sufficient for us as a firm proof: For it is in the open, that the Apostle looks to the Mosaic times, and the tabernacle crafted by Moses: nor is it less clear, that in the place in Kings it is a matter of the time of Solomon, and the temple built by him: The distinction of times therefore is certain, nor is the reason for the diversity of the more ample and fixed temple with the less spacious and portable tabernacle, with which the ark was to be carried around through the desert, obscure. As for the objection that Moses could not have placed the urn and the rod inside the ark without a command, nor could it have been lawful to remove them from the ark in the time of Solomon without a new intervening ordinance of God, those points can be answered by what B. König has on page 715: that the ark was fashioned primarily for the preservation of the tablets; but that the urn and the rod were added only as an occasion arose. Now, this was done either without a special ordinance of God, or by virtue of a divine ordinance. If the latter, then it must be produced from the sacred Pandects; if the former, the same difficulty remains regarding the placing of those things into the ark, which is urged regarding their removal from the same. But although Buxtorff denies that Moses had a command concerning the placing of them inside the ark, B. König does not deny it. He intends, he says, to point the finger at it in a certain way, when in Numbers 17:10 he mentions concerning the rod of Aaron that it was placed before the Lord for safekeeping, and in Exodus 16:34 concerning the urn, that it was also placed before the testimony for safekeeping. Why so? To intimate that the rod and the urn were placed for so long before the federal tables, which themselves had also been kept for some time in a certain sacred and more secret place, until the ark was ready, as may be gathered from Exod. XL. verse 20, compared with Exod. XXXIV. verse 29, until the whole tabernacle had been erected, and then each individual item was received into the ark, and had been diligently replaced in its own place and order. But who would believe (these are his own words, p. 712) that when in other matters far inferior the tremendous edict of GOD prevailed, 'What I command you, that only do,' Deut. XII. verse 32, He would have failed in a matter of such great moment, and left the power of acting free to human discretion? And how can it be doubtful that David received a command from the Lord concerning it, how one ought to act with these things of such great moment, even if a command concerning them in particular does not exist in writing, since the Holy Spirit testifies generally in 1 Chron. the penultimate chapter that David gave to Solomon the description of the portico and the temple and the chambers in the inner sanctuaries, and of the house of propitiation, and also of all the courts he had thought of, etc., and of the priestly and Levitical divisions for all the works of the house of the Lord, and for ALL THE VESSELS of the ministry of the temple of the Lord. Concerning which and all other things, especially concerning the ark of the covenant, David says thus in verse 19: ALL came written BY THE HAND OF THE LORD to me, that I might understand ALL THE WORKS of the pattern. Concerning the sanctuary also to be built and the ark to be introduced, as also concerning the sacred vessels, there exists a special command of David of this tenor: Arise and build the sanctuary of the Lord God, that the ark of the covenant of the Lord may be brought in, and the consecrated vessels of the Lord into the house which is being built for our Lord, 1 Chron. XXII. last. To whom the pattern for all things was prescribed by the Lord, why should he not have received a command concerning the urn of Manna and the rod of Aaron, which were once ordered to be placed specifically before the Lord and before the testimony, Exod. XVI. verses 33, 34, and Num. XVII. 10, and according to that command ordered them to be placed in the sanctuary? He placed them, however, in such a way that only the tables of the law remained in the ark of the Lord: that these alone were in it, the Holy Spirit testifies with a resounding voice, 1 Kings VIII. verse 9. But that any of the Rabbis said that that urn and rod were placed in a crypt under the earth, and not at the time the temple was built, neither does Grotius teach, nor was it permitted to observe from Buxtorf or others. But the Rabbis trifle that the ark was hidden in the very holy of holies in a certain crypt hidden for that purpose immediately after the temple was built by Solomon; however, most say this was done in the time of Josiah, who ordered the rod of Aaron, the urn of Manna, and the oil of sacred anointing to be hidden together with the ark, R. David Kimchi on 2 Chron. XXXV. verse 3, as also the Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim, R. Bachai on the law, fol. 199, Abarbenel, etc. Others, having followed the author of the book of 2 Macc. c. 11 and Josephus Gorionides, book I, chapter 17, say the ark was hidden only in the time of Jeremiah, concerning which fiction see Rivetus on Ex. XXV, B. Müller's Judaism, p. 475, and he who dealt with these things especially at length, Johannes Buxtorf, l. c., p. 190 seqq.

As to the signified or antitypes: 1. That the censer brought in from the outer tent into the inner sanctuary signifies the body of Christ, which after the most grievous sufferings passed from the earth into the highest heaven, perhaps does not sufficiently fit. For the Apostle teaches that the censer, or rather the thurible, was in the holy of holies itself, not in the outer tent; and the burning coals were not only outside the holy of holies, but also in the holy place itself, so that the smoke might ascend before the Lord: but that the body of Christ is subjected to sufferings in heaven is ἀθεόλογον (theological nonsense). Let us admit, however, that the body of CHRIST is mystically the golden censer, as the incense which ascends before the Lord are prayers, Apoc. VIII. Thus the fire by which they are kindled is the love of CHRIST, whose flames and efficacy are found in the holy of holies itself, heaven, in most ardent intercession. 2. We do not deny that the rod of Aaron designates the ever-enduring Priesthood of CHRIST; although perhaps others not inappropriately refer it to the Kingly office of CHRIST, with others judging that the Political state was designated by the rod or scepter of Aaron, just as they wish the Ecclesiastical to be noted by the tables of the law, and the Economic by the Manna, all of which states God covers with the wings of His providence, just as the Cherubim overshadowed the ark with their wings. 3. We readily grant that the Manna corresponds to the heavenly pasture which the Lord gives us in His Word. By which we think the Prophetic office of CHRIST was foreshadowed from the comparison of John VI. 4. But the tables of the covenant do not signify the better precepts of Christ. For neither was CHRIST a lawgiver, nor were more perfect precepts delivered in the New Testament than in the law, which was in itself most perfect, and prescribing the love of GOD above all things, and of our neighbor as ourselves, so exactly that it could not be more exact. But it was signified by the tables of the covenant hidden in the ark that Christ had the law of the Lord in the middle or interior of His heart, according to that Psalm XL. v. 9: In the head of the book it is written of me, that I should do thy will, O my GOD, I have willed, and thy law in the middle of my heart. By which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ, Heb. X. verse 10. And therefore the fulfillment of the law done for us, and the obedience of CHRIST even unto death, even the death of the cross, Gal. IV. verse 5, Phil. II. verse 8, is signified. Just as 5. The Ark itself was a figure of the body of CHRIST or His Human nature, which was seen in heaven, Apoc. XII. 19, concerning which comparison elsewhere.

But were the remains of the broken tables stored in the ark? Although some of the Hebrews think so, especially the Ancients, as also Abarbenel, on 1 Kings VIII. verse 9, yet most deny it, such as R. David Kimchi on 1 Kings VIII. Here is the proof that the broken tables were not in the ark. Aben-Ezra on Exod. XXV. verse 56: We do not read that God commanded Moses to make an ark and to place the former tables into it. For God was not ignorant that Moses would break them, but it is said concerning the tables which Moses hewed, 'And you shall make for yourself a wooden ark,' Deut. X. verse 1.

Latin:

V. 4. Χρυσῦν ἔχουσα θυμιατήριον, καὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς δια- θήκης περικεκαλυμμένην πάντοθεν χρυσίῳ, ἐν ᾗ στάμνος χρυσῆ ἔχουσα τὸ μάννα, καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἡ βλαστήσασα, καὶ αἱ πλάκες τῆς διαθήκης] Hic est locus, qui eruditis plurimis suspectam fecit epistolam: alios vero multum torsit: quia θυμιατήριον fuisse ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τῇ ἐξωτέρᾳ satis constat ex Mo- se, Philone, Josepho, Rabbinis. Tum vero 1. Reg. VIII. 9. 2. Paral. V. 10. Joseph. VIII. 2, Satis aperte dicitur, in arca nihil fuisse aliud nisi duas πλάκας τῆς διαθήκης id est, τὸ δεκαλόγω, quod initium διαθήκης. Ego qui hanc epistolam maximi facio, nunquam adducar, ut ejus autoritatem dese- ram. Objectis autem optime puto hoc modo responde- ri: θυμιατήριον hic non est mensa, sed impositum mensæ ba- tillum: ἐσχάραν vocat Josephus III. 8. πυρεῖον LXX. Le- vit. XVI. 12. ubi in Ebræo המחתה, quam vocem Saadias Gaon vertit מנמרה. quod significat πυρεῖον prunarium, quo nomine ab Arabibus vocatur illud in cœlo sidus, ut nota- tum Scaligero. Hæc ἐσχάρα facile portabatur, ut idem ille Josephus nos docet. Ubi autem describitur Levitici XVI. commate 12. ritus ille expiationis anniversariæ, dicitur in Ebræo de summo Sacerdote: ולקח מלא־המחתה גחלי־אש מעל המזבח מלפני יהוה ומלא חפניו קטרת סמים דקה והביא מבית לפרכת: ונתן את־הקטרת על־האש לפני יהוה: Quæ LXX. sic vertunt Καὶ λήψεται τὸ πυρεῖον πλῆρες ἀνθρά- κων πυρὸς ἀπὸ τῶ θυσιαστηρίω τῶ ἀπέναντι Κυρίω, καὶ πλήσει τὰς χεῖρας θυμιάματος συνθέσεως λεπτῆς. Καὶ εἰσοίσει ἐσώτε- ρον τῶ καταπετάσματος. Καὶ ἐπιθήσει τὸ θυμίαμα ἐπὶ τὸ ἐναντίο Κυρίω. Quorum verborum hic est, ut arbitror, sensus: Su- met summus Sacerdos batillum cum prunis de ista mensa, quæ respicit arcam, manus autem suas implebit aromate opti- me facto: deinde cum istis, [nempe prius transponens batil- lum intra velum, deinde ipse intrans cum pugillis aromatum] intrabit intra velum interius: & de isto aromate imponet in prunas batilli apud arcam. Dicitur ἐσχάρα autem fuisse coram Deo isto Levitici loco, quia respiciebat arcam, ut aperte dicitur Exod. XXV. 5. Notus autem est mos Ebræ- orum, qui per συνεκδοχὴν signi pro re signata arcam ap- pellant Dei nomine. Ita Exod. XXX. 6. 8. quod dictum fu- erat coram propitiatorio, mox dicitur coram Domino. Jam non difficile est intellectu, cur dicat hic scriptor, inte- rius illud tentorium habuisse batillum, non quod ibi semper esset, sed quod semper arcam, quæ erat in adyto, respiceret, & in illo die maxime solemni expiationis in tentorium in- terius, id est, in adytum transferretur. Habere enim dici- mur id, quod in nostro est usu. Quod vero de urna & vir- ga ex libro Regum & aliunde objicitur, id puto sic opti- me dilui. Mosis tempore fuit in arca & urna illa cum Man- na, & Aaronis virga. Et ubi potius quam in arca, cum intra adytum Manna positum apertum sit, ex loco Exod. XVI. 33. Virgam vero positam apud ipsam legem, quæ & testi- monium dicitur, constat ex Num. XVII. 10. Et in arca po- sitam fuisse virgam dicit Gorionides. Et lapsu temporis, cum metus esset, ne virga cariem, Manna autem mucorem pateretur, ablata ea sunt ex arca, & custodita in loco ca- rente ventis & Solibus. Et cum templum Salomonis con- deretur, eadem de causa non reposita sunt illa in arca, sed in crypta subterranea, ut Rabbini veteres scribunt. Sunt au- tem hæc omnia ab hoc scriptore non inaniter posita. Nam illud batillum ex tentorio exteriore illatum in adytum si- gnificat corpus Christi, quod post gravissimas perpessio- nes, quæ igni comparari solent in sacris literis, ex terris transiit in cœlum supremum. Suffitus preces Christi signi- ficat, quas semper pro nobis facit, Apoc. V. 8. Virga au- tem Aaronis, quæ fructum protulit, [id enim est ἐβλάστησε, de quo historia est Num. XVII.] semper durans Christi sacer- dotium: Manna vero pastum cœlestem, quem nobis dat in Verbo suo: Tabulæ autem fœderis significant præcepta meliora Christi, ad diligendum Deum super omnia, & pro- ximum juxta nos ipsos. Dicit præterea divinus hic Scriptor batillum fuisse ex auro, quod dictum etiam à Josepho di- cto loco Antiq. III. 7. Arca ארון הברית nulli alii rei serviebat, quam ad asservanda ea, quæ erant in arca, ut Philo notat de vita Mosis, sicut & multarum gentium sacra cista condebantur, ut Clemens nos docet admonitione ad gentes de sacris Eleusiniis: de sacris verò Thebanis Seneca Hercu- le Oetæo: Non Cadmais Orgia ferre Tecum folita condita ciftis.

Hanc quoque arcam sive cistam obtectam ait fuisse auro, quod & Exod. XXV. 11. XXXIII. 3. legimus. Addit & ur- nam fuisse auream, quod ipsum habemus Exod. XVI. 33. Στάμνος urceus, urna in glossario. Apud Hesychium κάμνος, ὑδρία, κάλη. Aurum quia rubiginem non sentit, ut notat Philo de rerum divinarum hærede, significat perpetuam durationem eorum bonorum, quæ per ista aurea vel aura- ta significantur. Πλάκες לחת Exod. XXXI. 18. Hinc δι- πλακα θεσμὸν dixit Orphicorum scriptor. Tabulas intel- lige integras ac novas: quanquam & fractarum reliquias in arcam conditas quidam tradant.

Quod ad aureum θυμιατήριον, thuribulum et- iam intelligunt Theophylactus, Anshelmus, Tho- mas, Lyranus, & è Reformatis Ludovicus de Dieu, cujus rationes adducit & approbat hic B. Dorsche- us: Ex facto liquet, tum in sancto sanctorum ex in- strumentis sanctuarii præter arcam etiam fuisse thuribulum: tum idipsum thuribulum, etiamsi il- lico post excitatam nubem rursus ex sancto sancto- rum fuisset elatum, longe rectius dici posse, quod ha- beatur à sancto sanctorum, quam quod ab eo- dem altare thymiamatis habeatur. Quod enim nunquam inter velum comparuit, quomodo rectius habitum fuisse à sancto sanctorum dici poterit, quam illud instrumentum sacrum, quod quotannis aliquamdiu saltem inter velum fuit: tum nuspiam dicitur thuribulum illud post annuum istum usum statim è sancto sanctorum exportatum fuisse. Veri- similius est, ibi fuisse asservatum, donec rursum esset usurpandum. Et propterea fuisse aureum, utpote soli summo Sacerdoti in illo solenni ingressu usitatum, quam quotidiana in sanctuario suffumigia à Sacer- dotibus excitanda aureum thuribulum vix sustine- re posset. Nihil itaq; docet Paulus, quod non ex cir- cumstantiis facti manifeste eluceat. Nec obstat auto- ritas Josephi, qui tantum describit contenta taber- naculi exterioris. Cum hoc itaque aureo thuri- bulo ingressus est Pontifex sanctum sanctorum thus incendens, ut illius fumo ac nebula tegeren- tur sancta sanctorum, ne videri possent ab iis, qui erant in exteriori tabernaculo. Huic sententiæ opponit tale argumentum Tostatus: Si id in san- cto sanctorum asservatum fuit, sequitur, ter ad minimum uno expiationis die Pontificem in illud in- gressum fuisse, videl. primo, ut auferret thuribu- lum; secundo, quando cum eo thure & igne re- pleto redibat, ut adoleret incensum, & suffumiga- ret in sancto sanctorum; tertio, cum rursum illi egrediendum erat ad cineres & ignem exponen- dum, & regrediendum ad reponendum thuribu- lum, cum tamen semel tantum illi licuerit ingredi in sanctum sanctorum. Quod argumentum adeo movit Villalpandum, ut in Ez. I. IV. cap. 25. statuerit, Pontificem thuribulum hujusmodi in sancto sanctorum semper reliquisse post ingres- sum, quo incensum penitus ibi consumeretur, & anno sequente aliud intulisse, prius autem & ante annum ibi relictum tum reportasse. Alii urgent, quod Exod. XXV. 29. cap. XXVII. 16. legantur quidem facta thuribula, sed horum thuribulo- rum aliud fuisse in sancto sanctorum non lega- tur. Frigida autem est Grotii explicatio, interius illud tentorium dici habuisse batillum, non quod ibi semper esset, sed quod semper ar- cam, quæ erat in adito, respiceret: & in illo die expiationis in adytum inferretur: Nam hoc posteriori sensu etiam Pontificem habuisse diceretur, quia Pontifex ingrediebatur illud inte- rius tentorium vel sanctum sanctorum. Aliam explicationem afferunt Origenes homil. IX. in Levit. Augustinus quæst. CXXXIII. & CLXXIV. in Exod. Alph. Tostatus, in Exod. XXV. q. 6. &

in 1. Reg. VI. q. 16. Franc. Ribera in h. l. Estius Corn. à Lapide, Jac. Capellus, Franc. Junius, B. Gerhardus, alii, nimirum per θυμιατήριον illud in- telligendum esse aureum altare θυμιάματος, Exod. XXX. vers. 1. cap. XXXVII. vers. 25. quod sanctum sanctorum habuisse dicitur, quod altare, ut nonnulli ex ipsis declarant, illud sibi haberet obver- sum, & ob sui cultum erectum, unde etiam altare oraculi dictum sit, Levit. XVI. vers. 12. vel quod sanctum sanctorum non quidem habuerit in se, sed ante se, ita tamen, ut proximum planeque obver- sum illi esset, ut ex hoc altari fumus superne ingre- deretur ipsa τὰ ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων, ut in eo quotidia- no suffitu Deus in illis residens honoraretur. An- nuit huic sententiæ Schlichtingius cum Crellio, Alta- re significatur, in quo adolebantur incensa Deo, quod revera quidem in primo tabernaculo erat, sed quia secundo velo, quo posterius tabernaculum à priore dividebatur, adhærebat, & quia tabernaculo adeo vicinum erat, propterea secundo tabernaculo illud tri- buit Autor. Sed quomodo secundo tabernaculo ita tribui id posset, quod revera in primo constitu- tum erat, ut in ea recensione, qua distincte illa, quæ in primo, quæque in secundo, quæ ante ve- lum, quæ post velum constituta fuere, recen- seatur?

Junius monet, sacrarium instrumenta quædam foris, sed intra velum habuisse, nimirum altare suf- fitus, quod in ipso aditu ante conspectum Jehovæ habuit ante arcam testimonii è regione operculi propitiatorii, quod erat super arcam fœderis. Sed si intra velum fuisset, quomodo ergo non intra sanctum sanctorum? Adde quod aliud sit θυμια- τήριον, vel thuribulum, aliud θυσιαστήριον θυμιάμα- τος vel altare suffimenti, de quo Luc. I. vers. 11. quæ distincta fuisse ex Levit. XVI. vers. 12. Num. XVI. vers. 46 patet: quodque illud hic χρυσᾶν aureum dicatur sensu accurato, prout id à περιε- καλυμμένῳ πάντοθεν χρυσίῳ, circumtecto ab omni parte auro distinguitur, hoc vero altare thymia- matos non aureum totum fuerit, sed auro tan- tum circumtectum. Juvant tamen hanc sen- tentiam nonnihil, quæ observavit B. Gerhardus, utpote 1. quod Apostolus non dixerit, aureum illud thuribulum fuisse in tabernaculi parte po- steriori, sive sancto sanctorum, sed quod taberna- culum HABUERIT thuribulum, σκηνὴ ἔχουσα, videlicet proxime sibi admotum, ut usibus ejus inserviret. Adde quod habuerit quoad usum, ut Cornelius à Lapide, quod scilicet fumus ex illo in sanctum sanctorum ascenderit, ac penetra- rit, ejusque odoratum illic odoratus sit Domi- nus in arca propitiatorii, eodemque honorari quotidie voluerit, Lev. XVI. vers. 13. Factum erat, dicente B. Gerhardo, illud altare, ut deser- viret sancto sanctorum. Cùm enim soli Pon- tifici fas esset illuc ingredi, nec id, nisi semel in anno, ne ea pars tabernaculi, quæ sacratior erat, honore thuris careret, jussit Dominus juxta sta- tui altare, in quo thymiama adoleretur, cujus fumus è proximo sanctum sanctorum obnubila- ret. 2. Quod altare illud nihil aliud fuerit, quam magnum thuribulum, nec majus tamen, quam cubitum habens longitudinis & cubitum latitudinis, utpote cujus non alius esset usus, quam ut in eo ignis imponeretur, & odores incenderentur: Et quod θυμιατήριον non solum significet thuribulum, sed etiam locum aut aram, in qua sit suffitus, apud Josephum lib. iii. Antiq. c. 7. l. VI. de Bello Jud. c. 6. Et quæ fortasse maxi- mè moveant, quod Moses nullius aurei thuribu- li meminerit, quod ab altari thymiamatos distin- Qum fuerit: Apostolus vero alio nomine altare thymiamatos non introducat, ea, quæ in taber- naculo fuere, describens, quod tamen unum ex præcipuis erat in tabernaculo. 3. Quod aure- um vocetur altare Mosaica voce, Exod. XXXIX. 38. cap. XL. 26. etsi non ex auro solido conflatum, quia scilicet totum erat auro tectum, Exod. XXX. 3. cap. XXXVII. 26. Quo sensu etiam mensa, in quâ panes propositionis erant, vocatur aurea, 1. Reg. VII. 48. non quod ex auro erat facta (utrumque enim & altare thymiamatos & mensa ex lignis Sittim erat confectum) sed quia tota erat auro obducta. Aug. quæst. ult. in Exod. Altare incensi aliquan- do aureum dixit Scriptura, aliquando deauratum: Aureum utique appellans, quod erat inauratum. Accedit, quod aureum id vocetur ad differenti- am altaris holocaustorum, quod æneum fuit, Exod. XXVII. vers. 2. B. Dorscheus, ita in h. l. Cur dixit Paulus sancta sanctorum habere thuribulum aure- um, cum docuit Scriptura Exod. ult. altare incensi fuisse extra velum, id est, extra sanctum sanctorum. Altare hoc factum erat, ut deserviret sancto sancto- rum. Cum enim non possent Sacerdotes in illa in- gredi, nisi Pontifex, idque semel singulis annis, ne ea tabernaculi pars, quæ erat sacratior, & in qua erant arca & propitiatorium & Cherubim, honore thuris careret, factum est altare thymiamatis, ac sanctis sanctorum admotum, in quo aromata in- cenderentur, quorum fumus in sancta sanctorum ingrederetur. Non ergo in sanctis sanctorum erat altare incensi, ut existimat Oecumenius & August. quæst. 133. in Exod. sed prope adjunctum. Hinc altare oraculi dicitur 3. Reg. VI. vers. 22. sed & altare oraculi texit auro, & Levit. XVI. vers. 23. vo- catur altare, quod erat coram Domino, quia erat coram sanctis sanctorum, & ubi nos habemus altare oraculi in Ebræo est altare, quod erat ad oraculum, sive juxta oraculum, quod manifestius vertunt LXX. & fecit altare ante faciem oraculi. Potest etiam verti, ut vertit Hieronymus, altare oraculi, sive altare, quod erat oraculo, s. quod sancta sancto- rum in suos usus habebant.

E duabus hisce sententiis utra præferenda sit, ambiguum videri queat. Verisimilior tamen illa videtur, quæ non altare suffimenti auro ob- ductum, sed thuribulum aureum designari vult, cui prunæ cum suffimento erant imponendæ. Quum enim id jussus sit Pontifex, Lev. XVI. 12. assumpto thuribulo (λήψεται τὸ πυρεῖον, habent LXX. Interpretes: In Ebræo est מַחְתָּה recepta- culum, B. Lutherus reddit Nåpffen, item Kohl- pfannen Exod. XXVII. 3. cap. XXXIIX. 3. quod θυμιατήριον alias dicitur Exod. XXVI. vers. 19. Ezech. XIIX. vers. 11. Ebr. מִקְטֶרֶת) quod de pru- nis altaris impleverit, & hauriens manu compositum thymiama in incensum ultra velum intrare in sancta, ut positis super ignem aromatibus, nebu- la eorum & vapor operiat oraculum, quod erat supra testimonium, necessum fuit, ut pararetur thuribulum. Quod sine dubio aureum fuit: imo fuisse vel hoc loco docemur, quemadmodum etiam 2. Paral. XV. vers. 22. aurea thuribula commemorantur. Non itaque sine thuribu- lo cum thymiamate ad faciendum incensum in- ferre potuit summus Sacerdos, & ita inferre jus- sus fuit. Licet ergo nomine θυμιατηρίε id red- ditum non fuerit in recensione utensilium ad ta- bernaculum facientium, ac ne quidem illis alia πυρεῖα quam ærea commemorentur; ad ingres- sum tamen Pontificis in sanctum sanctorum pe- culiari πυρείῳ opus fuit, sanctum sanctorum, quod totum auro fulgebat, decente: quod aure- um fuisse, Apostolus ex Spiritus Sancti inspira- tione indicat, idque eum in finem in sancto san- ctorum asservatum. Peculiare aliquod fuisse thuribulum aureum in eum finem & usum de- stinatum, ut cum eo Sacerdos summus quotan- nis in die expiationum ingrediatur in sanctum sanctorum, nec Buxtorffio displicet, etsi id in eo asservatum neget. Sed quia eadem ratione Apostolus de thuribulo aureo ait, quod sanctum sanctorum id habuerit, qua id de arca fœderis, quæ utique in eo asservabatur, affirmat, idque cum in eo occupatur, ut quæ fuérint in san- cto, quæ in sancto sanctorum distincte expli- cat; vel cum Villalpando duo ejusmodi aurea thuribula statuenda alternatim adhibita, ut ne opus haberet Pontifex, nisi una vice quotan- nis ingredi in sanctum sanctorum: Vel cum B. D. Georg König in vindic. sacr. loc. CXIV. pag. 708. dicendum: Aliud esse intrare ad adolendum & ad sanguinem offerendum, aliud ad refarciendum, si quid fractum concisumque fuis- set, aut si erigenda, movendaque castra, aut si quid reponendum sive educendum. Illud solius fuisse Pon- tificis semel in anno peragere, hoc licuisse, quoties necessitas efflagitaverit, non pontifici soli, sed & aliis Sacerdotibus; quod probat ex Num. IV. vers. 5. ubi non soli Aaroni, sed & filiis ejusdem injun- gitur, quodnam in refingendo sancto sanctorum munus esse debeat. Cui præcipue favere videtur, quod unum tantum thuribulum aureum hic no- minetur, neque in Ebræorum antiquitate facile quicquam reperiatur, observante Buxtorffio de gemino aureo thuribulo alternatim adhibito: Qui vero id ad histor. arc. fœd. c. V. pag. 68. ex addi- tionibus Thalmudicis in Bava Bathra fol. 14. ad- junxit: Exigente necessitate ad aliquid in eo repa- randum licitum fuisse ingredi sanctum sanctorum legimus in Erurim fol. 118. Imo pag. 75. observa- vit, ex mente Ebræorum quater in die expiatio- num ingressum in sanctum sanctorum Pontificem: 1. cum thymiamterium cum prunis & aromatibus in illud intulit, illud ibi relinquens, donec cæteros etiam cultus peregerit. 2. Cum sanguine juvenci eo octies inter vectes arcæ spargendo. 3. Cum san- guine hirci mactati &c. 4. Sub vesperam ingre- ditur & effert inde acerram & thuribulum. Vid. Majemon. & Thal. Joma cap. VII. Abarbenel in Lev. XVI. Qui ingreditur, inquit, quarta vice, ad auferendum inde thuribulum & acerram, quæ ibi remanserunt à tempore, quo suffitum fecit. Lau- datur etiam ibi R. Levi Ben Gerson rationem reddens 1. cur hæc ibi tamdiu relicta fuerint? quia scil. non conveniebat, ut ista vasa inde effe- rat, antequam perfecta consumpta fuerint suffitus & ignis in thuribulo. 2. Cur Scriptura nullam exertam mentionem faciat efferendorum horum vasorum? Quia hoc non de præcipuo scopo fuit hujus diei, neque de necessitate expiationis. 3. Cur efferenda fuerint? Quia hoc pertinebat ad hono- rem illius loci, ne cinis per totum annum ibi relin- quatur usque ad sequentem diem expiationum, quo demum illum removeat Sacerdos summus. Quæ nos suo relinquimus loco. B. Dorsecheus qua- ter ingrediendum fuisse ex Levit. XVI. ita colli- git: 1. cum suffitus inter velum excitandus v. 12. 2. cum sanguis juvenci versus propitiatorium spar- gendus. 3. cum idem de sanguine hirci faciendum v. 14. 15. 4. denique cum totum sanctuarium expiandum v. 32. An vero plane nullo casu summus Sacerdos extra hunc diem intra velum sese conferre potue- rit, disquiri poterit, partim quia casus esse poter.st, quo consulendum fuerat os Domini, qui cum sum- mo Sacerdote se loquuturum promisit e superiori parte operculi propitiatorii e medio duorum Che- rubinorum, qui sunt super arcam illam testimonii, Exod. XV. vers. 22. ubi nihil obstare potuisse vi- detur, quo minus intra velum sese conferret sum- mus Sacerdos, & responsa divina acciperet. Ut enim ad 10. Thisri usque istam consultatio- nem cum Domino differat, ipsa urgens necessitas non permisit. Alter casus est, quo in librum san- ctuarii referenda fuerunt, quae ad ipsius ceu divini canonis complementum pertinuerunt, de quo supra ex Deut. & aliis Scripturae dictis actum est. Iterum enim istam inscriptionem ad 10. Thisri restringendam aut prorogandam fuisse nullate- nus manifestum est. Quod igitur Lev. XVI; 2. dicitur, ne ingrediatur summus Sacerdos quovis tempore in sanctum intra velum ante illud oper- culum propitiatorium, quod est super arcam, ne moriatur, de promiscuo & arbitrario aditu accipi- endum est, non autem ad necessitatem & divi- num officium extendendum. Interdum istiusmodi aditus, scil. expiatorius & conciliatorius ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ uno isto anni die fuit licitus. Id autem plane illicitum est, & contra divinum manda- tum tentatum fuisset, si vere esset, quod dicitur, B. Virginem in ipsis pueritiae annis summo Sacerdo- ti, ab eoque in sancto sanctorum occultatam & educatam fuisse, quod post aliquot Veteres Baro- nius in apparatu annal. asserere non erubuit, con- futatus a Casaubono, Montacutio, Jacobo Capello, Riveto de B. Virgine & aliis. Conf. Anti - Conr. cap. XXVI. 377.

Quod ad ea, quae in arca fœderis fuisse dicuntur, urnam nempe auream, Manna haben- tem, & Virgam Aaronis florentem, ut & tabulas Testamenti, difficultas, quae e 1. Reg. IIX. vers. 9. collatione movetur, felicius sane a Grotio expedi- tur quam a Ribera in h. l. Joh. Scanno in Symph. Proph. Stapul. & Jacobo Capello de sedis Rom. potest. libr. I. cap. III. pag. 10. qui eam nequic- quam solvunt, per relationem vocularum ἐν ᾗ, ad remotius nempe σκηνὴν, quia non quid in ta- bernaculo fuerit, sed quid in arca explicari col- latio v. 5. docet, quo illa, ὑπεράνω δὲ αὐτῆς Χερυ- βὶμ, non de tabernaculo, quasi super illud Cheru- bim fuerint, sed de arca intelligenda esse certum est. Alii tamen malunt arcam fœderis distin- cte considerare, vel determinate & proprie quoad ipsum corpus vel sinum medium, qui tectus fuit propitiatorio, vel late, prout totam structuram notat, comprehendentem non solum ipsum cor- pus arcae, sed etiam receptacula lateralia, qualia eam habuisse colligunt e Deut. XXXI. vers. 26. & 1. Sam. VI. vers. 8. in quibus urna & virga fue- rit, quae explicatio Lyrani & Bellarmini fuit, lib. I. de Verbo Dei cap. 17. probata B. Glassio part. III. Phil. S. p. 179. Sed quam in accurata fabri- cae arcae descriptione nulla lateralis ejusmodi re- ceptaculi mentio facta sit, Exod. XXV. neque lo- cis istis repositum quid dicatur in tali recepta- culo, vel appendiculo arcae adjecto, quod ad ar- cam pertinuerit, & cum ea σύνολον quoddam no- mine arcae nuncupatum fecerit, sed tantum מצד a latere arcae vel e regione arcae, prope arcam, juxta arcam liber legis repositus dicasur, Deu- teronomion in ipsa fœderis arca fuisse nemo fa- cile dixerit: rejicitur haec conciliatio a Ribera in comm. ad h. l. & a B. D. König. in vind. sacr. pag. 711.

Respondet Riberae B. Dorscheus: Ge- neratim quidem arcae structuram Exod. XXV. de- scribi, non autem delineari ipsam figuram & constitutionem, qua ipsa exornata & artificis ma- nu composita fuit: neque abhorrere ab ista deli- neatione, quam Exodus habet, si dicatur, arcam ha- buisse latera sinuosa, in quibus aliquid poterat repo- ni: Fuit certe arca in longitudine duorum cubito- rum cum dimidio & sesquicubiti latitudine, simili- terque sesquicubiti altitudine. Itaque majoris or- natus causa istos sinus habere poterat. Adde quod in aliquo ejusmodi arcæ sinu etiam liber san- ctuarii repositus fuerit, in quem successive scribe- batur, quod pro Canone Ecclesiæ Veteris Testamenti ad posteros transmittere Deus voluit, Deut. III. 26. De cujus asservatione vide Theol. Zachar. part. II. θ. 84. Certe Exod. XVI. 34. antequam tabu- læ legis essent exhibitæ, aut arca fœderis constructa, præcipitur de urna aurea, ut reponatur & colloce- tur ante conspectum Jehovæ asservanda per ætates, & dicitur Aaron eam collocasse coram testimonio ipso, quod testimonium Exod. XXV. vers. 16. est, quod in arcæ interiori concavo collocatum fuit. Nusquam autem rectius coram testimonio collo- cari poterat urna, quam si ad latus ejusmodi exte- rius collocabatur. Regerit Ribera, eo ipso non fuis- se in arca, etiam respectu sinus cujusdam exterioris, vel urnam vel virgam, quæ coram Domino & coram testimonio dicuntur collocatæ. Sic enim & candelabrum aureum Exod. XXVII. dici co- ram Domino, & cap. XXX. θυμίαμα faciendum præcipitur coram testimonio. Ita & Num. XVII. præcipitur de virga, ut reponatur ante testimoni- um v. 25. Nusquam autem tabulas legis dici esse coram Domino, quia non fuerant extra sed inter arcam. R. Quæ coram Domino vel testimonio esse dicuntur, quædam remotius, quædam propius & conjunctius arcæ coram Domino fuisse dici. Poste- riori modo virgam frondentem & urnam auream coram Domino fuisse, & eo ipso coram Domino vel testimonio fuisse dici, quia in sinu quodam exteriori repositæ fuerunt, quod propterea de tabulis legis non dicitur, quia inter arcam collocabantur. Regerit rursus Ribera, parvam fuisse arcæ longitudinem duorum scilicet cubitorum & dimidii, adeoque vir- gam Aaronis frondentem in ea collocari non potu- isse. Resp. Nusquam tamen indicari longitudinem virgæ frondentis, & quod duobus cubitis cum dimi- dio longior fuerit. Porro affert Ribera adhuc ali- am interpretationem, tum in h. l. tum l. II. de templ. c. 2. p. 105. Dici posse, in qua poni, pro cum qua poni, ut sit sensus, cum qua arca erant si- mul in tabernaculo virga, & urna, & tabulæ; vel cum Anshelmo, hæc fuisse juxta arcam, qualis conciliatio etiam placuit B. Gerhardo: Simplicis- sime, inquit, respondetur, præpositionem ἐν non sem- per significare in, sed quandoque poni pro apud, juxta, respondens præfixo ב, adducens exempla Matth. XXI. 12. Marc. XI. 15. Joh. X. 23. Luc. IX. 31. cap. XIII, 33. & observans, quod etiam quandoque præpositio IN, uti ב, pro cum usur- petur, Deut. VI, 7. 1. Sam. I. 24. Act. VII. 38. 2. Petr. I. 5. Neque alienus est ab hac interpre- tatione Capellus in observat. in epist. ad Ebr. pag. 142. nec Calixtus expos. in cap. XVI. Exod. v. 33. 34. Sed ille sensus hic ægre admitti potest, quum Apostolus non quid juxta arcam, vel cum arca in sancto sanctorum fuerit, sed quid in arca, in sancto sanctorum positum fuerit, ac- curate distinguens ea, quæ in arca & quæ supra arcam fuere, quod de Cherubim dicitur, quæ utique etiam cum arca in sancto sanctorum fue- re, & juxta vel apud arcam. Quid? quod de urna ac virga pariter, uti de tabulis legis dicat Apostolus, quod in arca fuerint: num autem tabulæ legis solum juxta vel apud arcam aut cum arca fuere, non vero in arca vel intra arcam repositæ erant? aut num gemi- nus sensus præpositionis ἐν hic simul admittendus, quod non admodum probabile ipsimet Drusio videtur Comment. ad loc. difficil. Ex. cap. XXIX. pag. 189. Rectius planè negatur à B. D. König IN usquam in una simplici enunciatione aliam atque aliam sustinere significationem ac simul notare & intra & cum vel prope; uti quidem Buxtorfius contendit: Neque malè dixit, sinqui- ente, de his ἐν ᾗ, in qua erant, pro in & cum qua, quia, ut Scriptura loquitur, coram testimonio erant, hoc est, vel contigue & proxime juxta arcam po- fitæ, vel continue per adjectam arcæ appendiculam ei adhærebant, ut tam id, quod in arcæ appendi- ce, quam quod intra arcam erat ἐν αὐτῇ, in illa fuisfe dici posfit, maximè ab eo, qui non accu- ratam alicujus rei descriptionem instituit. Ita scilicet non uni voci semel positæ geminam di- versam significationem affingere necesfum fuit, sed & Apostolum arguere inaccuratæ descriptio- nis, qui tam accurate ea, quæ infra & quæ supra arcam fuere, designavit. Tum verò intra arcam fuisfe cum tabulis legis urnam Manna & virgam Aaronis, Interpretes scribere, & ita haberi in Ca- bala seu traditione quadam Rabbinorum, Abar- banel ad 1. Reg. IIX. vers. 19. notavit, cui viro multæ lectionis & observationis de tali aliqua traditione procul dubio aliquid innotuisfe, Bux- torfius censet: Quod R. Levi Ben Gerson colli- git è cap. XVI. Exodi vers. 33. 34. Ex eo au- tem quod dicit coram testimonio potius, quam coram arca, discimus, quod intra arcam fuerint (urna Manna & virga Aaronis. Nam si ex- tra eam fuislent, dicendum ipsi fuisset coram ar- ca, non coram testimonio, quod ipsi est, coram tabulis. Quo accedit, quod in meliori custodia fuerint in arca (quam extra eam) &c. Quia scil. Num. XVII. vers. 10. (ad quem locum hæc annotat R. Levi) dicitur: Refer virgam Aa- ronis coram testimonio in custodiam. Quas ra- tiones, uti Rabbinis relinquimus: Ita tamen constat ipsorum etiam testimoniis & traditione, intra arcam illa fuisle, quamvis de eo inter se sen- tentiis discrepent. Cæterum iisdem ferme ra- tionibus utitur B. König pag. 715. Sed quid tandem ad locum 1. Reg. IIX. vers. 19.? Vata- blus hunc reddit sensum: In arca, subintellige ex libro legis, nihil erat, nisi duæ tabulæ legis, q. d. ex tota lege nihil in ea arca continebatur præter præcepta Decalogi. Similiter ad istum locum R. Levi Ben Gerson: Hoc non negat, ibi fuisfe ea, quæ commemorantur in lege in eam fuisse repo- sita, ut virgam Aaronis, & urnulam Mannæ: Sed negat tantum de lege, ibi quicquid aliud fuisfe collocatum, præter Decalogum, eo quod ille sum- mam contineat totius legis. Quæ opponi pof- sunt R. Lusitano apud B. D. Müllerum in Ju- daismo pag. 1364. epistolæ ad Ebræos præsen- tem locum exagitanti, quasi contrarietur loco 1. Reg. IIX. vers. 9. Neque alienus ab ea ex- plicatione est D. König, cum cura præsentem locum enucleans: aliam tamen adhuc affert & præfert, quod nempe exclusivæ particulæ inter- dum accommodè solum nec prorfus universaliter excludant, ut in eodem Regum libro cap. XXII. vers. 20. ut sensus sit: Duæ tantum tabulæ fuere in arca, tanquam principaliora κειμήλια, propter quorum conservationem arca potissimum erat fa- brefacta. Per occasionem vero urna & virga etiam superadditæ. Quæ interpretatio Tho- mam autorem habet. Neutra tamen explica- tio difficultate caret: non illa Rabbinorum, quia nihil ibi in textu, unde colligi possit, sub in- telligendum esse ex libro legis, vel de tota lege, & plane arbitrarium sit ejusmodi interpreta- mentum: Neque hæc Thomistica, quia non principaliora tantum alia excluduntur, sed ni- hil aliud, quam tabulas duas in arca fuisse do- cetur. Nec enim Spiritus Sanctus ait tantum è principalioribus rebus, aut propter quas fa- cta est arca, duæ tabulæ erant in arca: Sed ni- hil in ea erat, nisi tantum duæ tabulæ lapideæ: Unde adhuc in sententia, in quam inclinavit Ambrosius Catharinus in libell. de clavib. Script. clav. secunda & l. 1. annot. in Cajetan. acqui- escendum, quæ ita à B. Konigio, & Buxtorffio ll. cc. iisdem omnino verbis refertur: Sunt alii, qui tempora distinguunt, & dicunt, fuisse hæc omnia intra arcam tempore illo, de quo loquitur Paulus, nempe cum primum constructum fuit tabernaculum, & quamdiu arca illa cum taber- naculo deferri debuit per desertum: Tunc enim cum locum commodum non haberent ad ista collocanda, cum instabile & vagum esset tabernaculum, ea reposuisse in arca cum tabulis legis, ad quas propriè pertinebat hic locus: sed cum postea exstructum fuisset templum, id est, stabile tabernaculi & arcæ Domini domicilium, & spatium fuit datum, in quo potuerunt capa- ciora esse repositoria, tunc sola lex mansit intra arcam, reliqua juxta illam suo loco fuerunt dispo- sita & asservata. Et Apostolum ad Ebræos qui- dem loqui de statu tabernaculi ambulatorii: Li- brum Regum autem de stabili templo, quo tem- pore res in ordinem commodiorem erunt redactæ. O quam solida esset hæc conciliatio, si tam firma niteretur probatione, quam vana divina- tione, exclamat B. Königius! Verum probatio- nem firmam sufficere nobis Apostolicum locum cum loco Regum collatum omnino existima- mus: Nam in aprico est, Apostolum respicere tempora Mosaica, & tabernaculum à Mose fa- brefactum: nec minus liquidum est, in loco Regum agi de tempore Salomonis, & templo ab eo exstructo: Temporum ergo distinctio certa est, neque obscura est diversitatis templi am- plioris & fixi cum tabernaculi minus spatiofi ac portatilis, cum quo per desertum circumfe- renda esset arca, ratio. Quod autem obverti- tur, Nec sine mandato intra arcam reponere Mosen potuisse urnam & virgam, nec sine intercedente nova Dei ordinatione hæc ex arca licuisse surri- pere tempore Salomonis, ad ea reponi possunt, quæ B. König habet pag. 715. quod propter ta- bularum conservationem arca potissimum fuerit fabrefacta: Per occasionem vero tantum urna etiam & virga superaddita: Id autem vel citra ordinationem Dei peculiarem factum, vel vi ordinationis divinæ: Si hoc, ea ergo è sacris Pandectis producenda: Si illud, manet eadem difficultas quoad illationem earum rerum in ar- cam, quæ urgetur quoad translationem ex ea- dem. Sed quanquam Buxtorffius neget manda- tum habuisse de repositione earum intra arcam Mosen, non tamen B. König id inficiatus est: Intendit, inquit, eo quodammodo digitum Moses, quando Num. XVII. 10. de virga Aaronis comme- morat, quod sit posita coram Domino in custodiam & Exod. XVI. 34. de urna, quod etiam sit posita coram testimonio in custodiam: Cur sic? Ut in- nuat virgam & urnam tamdiu collocatas coram tabulis fœderalibus, quæ & ipsæ aliquandiu in loco quodam sacro & secretiore asservatæ fuerant, do- nec parata esset arca, ut colligere est ex Exod. XL. vers. 20. collata cum Exod. XXXIV. vers. 29. usq; dum erectum fuisset totum tabernaculum, & tum singula intra arcam recepta, ac suo loco & ordine diligenter fuisse reposita. Quis vero credat (verba ejusdem sunt pag. 712.) cum in aliis longe inferio- ribus edictum DEI tremendum obtinuerit, quod præcipio tibi, hoc tantum facito, Deut. XII. vers. 32. in re tanti momenti defecisse, & humano arbitra- tui liberum agendi potestatem reliquisse? Et quo- modo dubium esse potest accepisse Davidem de eo mandatum à Domino, quomodo cum hisce rebus tam magni momenti agendum esset, tam- etsi de illis in specie descriptum non extet man- datum, siquidem generatim testetur Spiritus San- ctus 1. Paral. cap. penult. dedisse Davidem Salo- moni descriptionem porticus & templi & cubiculo- rum in adytis, & domus propitiationis, nec non & omnium, quæ cogitaverat atriorum &c. discrimi- numque Sacerdotalium & Leviticorum in omnia opera domus Domini, & in UNIVERSA VASA ministerii templi Domini. De quibus & aliis omnibus, imprimis de arca fœderis ita inquit David vers. 19. OMNIA venerunt scripta MANU DOMINI ad me, ut intelligerem UNIVERSA OPERA exemplaris. De san- ctuario etiam construendo & arca introducen- da, ut & de vasis sacris peculiare extat manda- tum Davidis hujus tenoris: Consurgite & ædifi- cate sanctuarium Domini Dei, ut introducatur arca fœderis Domini, & vasa Domini consecrata in domum, quæ ædificatur, nostri Domini, 1. Paral. XXII. ult. Cui de omnibus præscriptum est ex- emplar à Domino, quidni de urna Manna & virga Aaronis, quæ olim peculiariter coram Do- mino & coram testimonio reponi jussa sunt, Exod. XVI. vers. 33. 34. & Num. XVII. 10. mandatum acceperit, ac juxta illud ea in sanctuario reponi jusserit? Reposuit autem ita, ut solæ tabulæ legis in arca Domini manserint: Quas solas in eadem fuisse, sonora voce testatur Spiritus Sanctus, 1. Reg. IIX. vers. 9. Qui vero è Rabbinis urnam illam & virgam in Crypta sub terra, nec tempo- re extructi templi repositam dixerint, nec Gro- tius docet, nec è Buxtorffio aliisve observare li- cuit. At arcam in ipso sancto sanctorum in cry- pta quadam abstrusa eum in finem statim ab ædi- ficato templo à Salomone constructa abscondi- tam nugantur Rabbini, hoc autem factum ple- rique dicunt tempore Josiæ, qui cum arca simul virgam Aaronis, urnam Mannæ, & oleum uncti- onis sacrum abscondi jusserit R. David Kimchi ad 2. Chron. XXXV. vers. 3. ut & Thalmud. Hie- rosolym. Sche Kalim, R. Bæchai in legem fol. 199. Abarbenel. &c. alii autorem lib. vill. Macc. c. 11. & Josephum Gorionidem l. I. cap. 17. sequuti, tem- pore Jeremiæ demum absconditam dicunt arcam, de quo commento vid. Rivetus ad Ex. XXV. B. Mülleri Judaism. pag. 475. & qui de hisce im- primis prolixe egit Johan. Buxtorffius l. c. pag. 190. seqq.

Quod ad significata vel antitypa 1. Batillum ex tentorio exteriore illatum in adytum significare corpus Christi, quod post gravissimas perpessio- nes ex terris transiit in cœlum supremum, forte non satis convenit. Nam batillum vel potius thuribulum in ipso sancto sanctorum fuisse, non in exteriori tentorio, Apostolus docet; & pru- næ ardentes erant non tantum extra sanctum sanctorum, sed etiam in ipso sancto, ut fumus ascenderet coram Domino: Corpus autem Chri- sti perpessionibus in cœlo subjici, ἀθεόλογον. Ad- mittamus tamen, corpus CHRISTI mystice esse thuribulum aureum, ut odoramenta, quæ ascen- dunt coram Domino, preces sunt Apocal. VIII. Ita ignis, quo accenduntur, est amor CHRISTI, cujus flammæ & efficacia in ipso sancto sancto- rum cœlo, in intercessione ardentissima depre- henduntur. 2. Virgam Aaronis semper durans CHRISTI Sacerdotium designare non abnui- mus; quamvis nec incommode fortassis alii, eam ad Regium CHRISTI officium referant, aliis per virgam seu sceptrum Aaronis statum Politi- cum designatum censentibus, uti per tabulas le- gis Ecclesiasticum, per Manna Oeconomicum no- tatum volunt, quos status omnes Deus alis pro- videntiæ suæ tegat, quemadmodum Cherubini cum alis suis arcam obumbrarunt. 3. Manna pastui cælesti, quem nobis dat in Verbo suo Do- minus, convenire facile largimur. Quo adum- bratum fuisse officium CHRISTI Propheticum è collatione Johan. VI. existimamus. 4. Tabulæ autem fœderis non significant præcepta Christi meliora. Nam nec CHRISTUS νομοθέτης fuit, nec perfectiora præcepta in Novo Testamento tradita, quam in lege, quæ per se perfectissima fuit, & dilectionem DEI super omnia, & pro- ximi juxta nos ipsos tam exacte præscribens, ut exactius non possit. Fuit autem per tabulas fœ- deris in arca reconditas significatum, quod le- gem Domini in medio vel interiori cordis sui habuerit Christus, juxta illud Psal. XL. v. 9. In capite libri scriptum est de me, ut facerem volun- tatem tuam, DEUS meus volui, & legem tuam in medio cordis mei. Quâ voluntate sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Jesu Christi, Ebr.X. vers. 10. Ideoque impletio legis pro nobis facta, & obedientia CHRISTI usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis, Gal. IV. vers. 5. Phil. II. vers. 8. significata. Quemadmodum 5. Arca ipsa fuit figura corporis CHRISTI vel Humanæ ejus naturæ, quæ visa est in cœlo Apoc. XII. 19. de qua collatione alias.

Anne autem tabularum fractarum reliquiæ in arca conditæ fuere? Etsi putent id Ebræorum nonnulli, Veteres inprimis, ut & Abarbenel, ad 1. Reg. IIX. vers. 9. plerique tamen negant, utpote R. David Kimchi ad 1. Reg. VIII. Hic ha- betur probatio, quod in arca fracta tabula non fu- erint. Aben-Ezra ad Exod. XXV. vers. 56. Non legimus, Deum Mosi præcepisse facere arcam, & in eam reponere tabulas priores. Haud enim igno- ravit Deus, Mosen illas fracturum, sed de tabu- lis, quas, Moses dolavit, dicitur, & facies tibi ar- cam ligneam, Deut. X. vers. 1.

## 9:5
Vers. 5. And above it the Cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy-seat, of which it is not now the time to speak in detail.] Cherubim of glory, that is, the form of the Cherubim, among whom the Majesty of God showed itself Exod. XXV. 22. Lev. XVI. 2. The Greeks everywhere construe Cherubim with a neuter article or Adjective, namely because the greater part of the form was taken from mute animals. The LXX and Philo use ἱλαστήριον for כפרת because כפר also signifies ἱλάσκειν, to propitiate. God, however, showed Himself propitious to the people by showing the sign of His presence, as we have already said, between the Cherubim, or which is the same thing, above the ark. But כפר in its native sense is to cover, as Gen. VI. 14, whence כפרת can be translated ἐπίθεμα, which word Josephus uses in Antiq. III, 6, and Philo, who also calls it πῶμα in his book on the life of Moses. It was a covering open at the top resting upon the ark, in the manner of a tablet, as R. Solomon says. Κατασκιάζειν which is συσκιάζειν Ex. XXXV. 20. XXXVII. 9. Σκιάζειν 1. Par. XXVIII. 18. because the wings of the Cherubim were spread over that covering of the ark, just as birds brood over their chicks: whence the proverbial shadow of the wings Ps. LVII. 2. He reserves the explanation of the mysteries lying hidden under this thing for another time, but because he either was prevented by death and did not perform this, or certainly this book did not reach us, we have said what we judge to be most probable regarding that matter, partly from Philo, partly from others at Matth. XXVII. 51. On Exodus 25:18 and on Ezekiel 1:5. In each Cherub there were four forms: of a man and a lion—the former signifying beneficence, the latter wrath—and of an eagle, which signifies speed, and of an ox, which signifies slowness. Thus those forms imply the same thing that God said to Moses, that He is swift to do good and slow to vengeance. Hence, what Philo says in many places does not depart from this, that by the Cherubim is understood God’s ἀγαθότητα (goodness) and ἐξουσίαν (authority) or δύναμιν ποιητικὴν (creative power) and βασιλικὴν (kingly) or ἐυἐργετιν (beneficent) and κολασήριον (punitive), as he speaks in his book On Those Who Sacrifice. Between these two faculties of God is the ἡ ἵλεως Θεῦ δύναμις (the propitious power of God), which Philo says in On the Life of Moses is shadowed forth by the ἱλασήριον (mercy seat): that is, clemency toward the fallen. This indeed appeared so excellently in Christ that for this reason Christ is called ἱλασήριον in Romans 3:25 and ἱλασμὸς in 1 John 2:2 and 4:10.

We have spoken of the Cherubim elsewhere. Avenarius in his Lexicon interprets כרוב in this way: It is the image of each face, which, with wings spread, is painted and appears as if it were a bird flying. It has a relationship with רכב, he was carried. Compare 2 Samuel 22 and Psalm 18:9, which, along with Mercer in Pagninus’s Lexicon, he has from Forster in his Lexicon: who, from a comparison of Ezekiel chapters 1 and 10, observes that the figure or likeness of the four animals, because they appear to be carried and to fly with wings, are called כרובים. Schindler in his Pentaglot Lexicon notes that כרוב is a figure comprehending all images, an image similar to a youth, who is called רבי by the Chaldeans: that כרובים are images of Angels and Angels having human form and wings. Similarly, Aben Ezra wishes to signify forms צורות in general: Philo Judaeus says that winged images are called Cherubim in the vernacular tongue, that is, much knowledge: In which manner by some כרוב is called as if it were כרב, like Rabbi, like wise, much knowledge. R. Levi Ben Gerson explains it as boys, as if רוכים growing from רכה to grow, to become great on account of the wonderful accretion which is detected in them. Talmud Chagigah folio 13. What is כרוב? R. Aschu said: כרביא as if an adolescent (a species of boy), for thus in Babylon they call a boy. Abarbenel, after having brought forward the opinions of the Talmudists and Aben Ezra, adds: It suffices in this place to know that the Cherubim had the form of little boys with wings. Thus the כ indeed is servile in its origin, but by usage it passed into a Radical, of which Buxtorf notes that more examples are found in this language. Regarding the cause and signification of the Cherubim, the opinion of the Hebrews is rightly demanded. Maimonides in More part 3, chapter 45: God commanded the figure of two Cherubim to be made above the ark to confirm the existence of Angels in the minds of men. But if there had been only one figure, that is, the form of only one Cherub, this would easily have provided a cause for error. For one could easily have thought that it was a figure of God to be worshipped, as idolaters do, or as if the Angel were only a single individual, and thus lead into multiple errors. Nothing is observed from the Rabbis concerning the same Cherub of the fourfold animal figure. Which Grotius makes the foundation of his mystical signification. Nor indeed were the Cherubim meant to represent divine properties, but rather angelic ones: such as humanity, holiness, and perpetuity, because boys, by their gentler form, exhibit sweet humanity and Φιλανθρωπίαν (philanthropy), and by their simple innocence, holiness, and by their blooming appearance, the perpetuity and ever-flourishing state of the Angels. It is so far from the case that the Rabbis designated the form of the Cherubim and the animals that they rather professed the same to be inexplicable to themselves: Concerning which Josephus in Antiquities book 8, chapter 2, says that no one can conjecture or declare what these Cherubic figures were in appearance. However, that Paul reserved the explanation of those mysteries figured in the apparatus of the tabernacle for another time does not appear from his words. For he says nothing other than that now, according to the reason of his present undertaking, there is no reason why he should speak of these things particularly and unfold them one by one. But he by no means commits himself to explain these things to them elsewhere by letter. What then does it matter to ask whether he performed it or not? Why he did not perform it, whether because he was prevented by death, or for some other cause; much less to conclude that he did perform it, but that this book has not reached us. If he had promised it by the instinct of the Holy Spirit, without doubt the Spirit of truth would have led him to perform it, nor would He have allowed the Canonical Scripture to perish, which is consistent for the whole Hebrew nation.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Ὑπεράνω δὲ αὐτῆς Χερυβὶμ δόξης, κατασκιάζοντα τὸ ἱλαστήριον, περὶ ὧν οὐκ ἔστι νῦν λέγειν κατὰ μέρος.] Χερυβὶμ δόξης, id est, forma Cherubinorum, inter quos Dei Majestas se ostendebat Exod. XXV. 22. Lev. XVI. 2. Græci Χερυβὶμ ubique construunt cum articulo aut Adjectivo neutro, nem- pe quia major pars formæ sumpta erat de mutis animanti- bus. Ἱλαστήριον ponunt LXX. & Philo pro כפרת quia כפר etiam ἱλάσκειν propitiare significat. Deus autem propitium se ostendebat populo, præsentiæ suæ signum ostendendo, ut jam diximus, inter Cherubinos, sive quod idem est super arcam. At כפר nativo sensu est tegere, ut Gen. VI. 14. unde כפרת verti potest ἐπίθεμα, qua voce utitur Josephus Antiq. III, 6. & Philo, qui & πῶμα vocat libro de vita Mosis. Erat tegmen superne patulum requiescens super arcam, more tabulæ, ut ait R. Salomo. Κατασκιάζειν quod συσκιάζειν est Ex. XXXV. 20. XXXVII. 9. Σκιάζειν 1. Par. XXVIII. 18. quia Cherubinorum alæ si erant expansæ super illud arcæ teg- men, sicut aves pullis incubant: unde proverbiale umbra alarum Ps. LVII. 2. Explicationem mysteriorum sub hac re latentium in aliud tempus reservat, sed quia hoc aut morte præventus non præstitit, aut certe liber iste ad nos non perve- nit, nos id quod maxime probabile arbitramur, ea de re di- ximus partim ex Philone, partim ex aliis ad Matth. XXVII. 51. ad Exod. XXV, 18. & ad Ezech. I, 5. Erant in unoquoq; Che- rubino formæ quatuor, hominis & leonis: illa beneficentiam, hæc iram significans: & aquilæ, quæ celeritatem, & bovis, quæ tarditatem significat. Ita formæ illæ idem innuunt, quod De- us Mosi dixit, se celerem esse ad benefacta, tardum ad ultio- nem. Unde non abit, quod Philo dicit multis in locis, per Cherubinos, intelligi Dei ἀγαθότητα & ἐξουσίαν sive δύναμιν ποιητικὴν κὶ βασιλικὴν sive ἐυἐργετιν & κολασήριον, ut loquitur libro de sacrificantibus. Inter has duas Dei facultates media est ἡ ἵλεως Θεῦ δύναμις, quam per ἱλασήριον adumbrari ait Philo de vita Mosis: id est, clementia erga lapsos. Hæc vero in Christo ita eximie apparuit, ut propterea Christus ἱλασή- ριον vocetur Rom. III, 25. & ἱλασμὸς, 1. Joh. II, 2. IV, 10.

De Cherubinis alias diximus. Avenarius in Lexic. כרוב interpretatur hoc modo: Est imago cujusque faciei, quæ expansis alis tanquam avis volare pingitur & apparet. Cognationem habet cum רכב, vectus est. Conf. 2. Sam. XXII. & Psal. XIIX, 9. quæ cum Mercero in Lexico Pagnini, à Forstero in Lexico habet: qui è collatione Cap. I. & X. Ezech. observat, quod figura seu similitudo quatuor animalium, quia alata vehi & volare ap- pareant, כרובים dicantur. Schindlerus in Lexic. Pentagl. כרוב notat figuram, omnes imagines comprehendentem, imaginem similem juveni, qui Chaldæis רבי dicitur: כרובים imagines esse An- gelorum & Angelos humanam formam & alas habentes. Similiter Aben Ezra vult in genere significare formas צורות: Philo Judæus dicit ima- gines volucres sermone vernaculo vocari Che- rubim, hoc est, multa scientia: Quo pacto nonnul- lis כרוב dicitur, quasi כרב, sicut Rabbi, sicut sapiens, multa scientia. R. Levi Ben Gerson ex- ponit pueros, quasi רוכים crescentes à רכה cre- scere, magnum fieri propter accretionem admi- randam, quæ in illis deprehenditur. Talmud Cha- gigah fol. 13. Quid est כרוב? R. Aschu dixit: כרביא quasi adolescens, (species pueri) sic enim in Ba- bylonia puerum vocant. Abarbenel post addu- ctas Thalmudicorum & Aben Esdræ sententias sub- jungit: Sufficit hoc loco scire, quod Cherubini habuerint formulam parvulorum puerorum cum alis. Ita כ quidem servile est origine sua, sed usu transiit in Radicalem, qualia plura in hac lingua inveniri notat Buxtorffius. De causa & significa- tione Cherubinorum recte exigitur sententia E- bræorum Maimonides in More part. III. cap. 45. Præcepit Deus supra arcam duorum Cherubino- rum figuram facere ad existentiam Angelorum in animis hominum confirmandam. Quod si una tan- tum figura fuisset, hoc est, unius tantum Cherubini forma, id facile errandi causam præbuisset. Existima- mare enim facile quis potuisset, ac si esset figura Dei colendi, sicut idololatræ faciunt, vel quasi Angelus unicum duntaxat esset individuum, atq; ita in multiplices errores inducere. De eodem Cherub quadruplicis animalis figuræ nihil è Rab- binis observatum. Quæ fundamentum suæ signi- ficationis mysticæ facit Grotius. Nec vero divinas proprietates repræsentare Cherubini debebant, sed Angelicas potius: quales sint humanitas, & sanctitas ac perennitas, quia pueri blandiori for- ma suavem humanitatem ac Φιλανθρωπίαν & sim- plici innocentia sanctitatem & florida sua specie perennitatem semperque florentem statum An- gelorum exhibent: Formam Cherubinorum & animalium tantum abest, ut Rabbini designarint, ut professi potius sint eandem sibi esse inexplica- bilem: Quo de Josephus in Antiqu. l. IIX. cap. 2. has Cherubicas figuras, quænam specie fuerint, ne- minem conjicere posse vel eloqui. Explicationem autem illorum mysteriorum in apparati taberna- culi figuratorum in aliud tempus reservasse Pau- lum è verbis ejus non apparet. Nihil enim aliud dicit, quam nunc secundum præsentis sui institu- ti rationem non esse, quod de his particulariter dicat, & singula evolvat. Minime autem recipit sese alias ipsis hæc per epistolam expositurum. Quid ergo attinet quærere, anne id præstiterit, necne? Cur id non præstiterit, an quia morte præventus fuit, an alia de causa; nedum statuere, quod præstiterit id, sed liber iste ad nos non per- venerit. Si Spiritus Sancti instinctu id promisisset, sine dubio Spiritus veritatis ipsum ad id præstan- dum egisset, neque passus tum fuisset Scripturam Canonicam Ebræorum genti universæ consecta- neam interire.

## 9:6
V. 6. Τούτων δὲ οὕτω κατεσκευασμένων] That is, when the structure of the outer and inner tent is thus.

Εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν διαπαντὸς εἰσίασιν ἱερεῖς τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες] They do not enter once, but daily, and there perform the worship, that is, they offer incense, set forth the bread, and light the lamp. Διαπαντὸς corresponds to the Hebrew תמיד, which you often have in the law. Take τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν as above at the beginning of this section. Ἐπιτελεῖν, as also συντελεῖν, is accustomed to be put for עשׂה or פעל, which is to do, to perform. And thus the Syrian rightly understood it here.

After the Apostle has brought forward the apparatus and vessels of the tabernacle, he now pursues the duties or works which were to be performed in it, both those in the former tabernacle, in which the Priests performed worship daily, and in the latter, which the High Priest entered only once every year, to whom alone this was appropriate. But these three things were not the only ones appropriate for the Priests to perform τὰς λατρείας, the worships or ministries; the Vulgate rendered it the offices of the sacrifices. Not only to offer incense, set forth the bread, and light the lamp, but also that they were obliged to offer propitiatory sacrifices and others, as is evident from Leviticus. Although these were offered in the courtyard, some nevertheless not without reason warn that the Apostle speaks of the former tabernacle in such a way that it also includes that part of the courtyard in which was the altar of burnt offering: since the Apostle's aim is that a distinction be maintained between the first and second tabernacle, which remains entirely, even if the place of the altar of burnt offering is joined to the former tabernacle. And although the slaughtering and burning of animals took place outside the veil, that part of the priests' duty, which consisted in bringing in the blood and sprinkling it against the veil of the sanctuary, and upon the horns of the altar of incense, was performed within the veil in the former tabernacle, Lev. IV, 3. 5. 6. 7.

Latin:

V. 6. Τούτων δὲ οὕτω κατεσκευασμένων] Id est, cum ita se habeat tentorii exterioris & interioris structura.

Εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν διαπαντὸς εἰσίασιν ἱερεῖς τὰς λα- τρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες] Non semel intrant, sed quotidie & ibi cultum peragunt, id est, suffitum faciunt, panes proponunt, lucernam accendunt. Διαπαντὸς respondet Ebræo תמיד, quod sæpe habes in lege. Τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν sume ut supra ini- tio hujus sectionis. Ἐπιτελεῖν ut & συντελεῖν solet poni pro עשׂה vel פעל, quod est facere, obire. Et ita hic recte accepit Syrus.

Postquam apparatum & vasa tabernaculi ad- duxit Apostolus, jam munia vel opera, quæ in eo expediunda erant, persequitur, tum quæ in priori tabernaculo, in quo Sacerdotes quotidie cultum peregerunt, tum in posteriori, quod non nisi semel quotannis ingressus est summus Sacerdos, cui uni hoc conveniebat. Non autem tantum hæc tria Sacerdotibus conveniebant, ut perficerent τὰς λατρείας, cultus seu ministeria, Vulgatus reddidit sacrificiorum officia. Non tantum suffitum face- re, panes proponere, & lucernam accendere, sed etiam sacrificia propitiatoria & alia offerre debue- re, ut ex Levitico constat. Quæ licet in atrio ob- lata sint, non abs re tamen monent nonnulli, Apostolum de priori tabernaculo ita loqui, ut et- iam comprehendat eam artii partem, in qua erat altare holocausti: quum scopus Apostoli sit, ut inter primum & secundum tabernaculum distin- ctio servetur, quæ omnino manet, etiamsi priori tabernaculo locus altaris holocausti adjungatur. Et quamvis mactatio & crematio animalium ex- tra velum fieret, ea tamen officii Sacerdotum pars, quæ consistebat in sanguine inferendo & spargendo contra velum sanctuarii, & super cor- nua altaris thymiamatis, intra velum in taberna- culo priori peracta est, Lev. IV, 3. 5. 6. 7.

## 9:7
Vers. 7.

Εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν] Which is also ἐσωτέρα, that is, into the inner sanctuary.

Ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς.

For the sake of the figure rather than the thing itself. For the greater part of the sacred rite was performed elsewhere. Ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ אחת בשנה Exod. XXX, 10. Lev. XVI, 34. That day was the tenth of the month Tisri.

Οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος.

Of the bull and the goat, Lev. XVI, 14. 15. With that blood that covering or ἱλαστήριον was sprinkled. Hence it appears, although it is said that the high priest entered once, that this is to be understood as meaning that he entered on only one day, not that he did not go out and enter again several times. For it was necessary for him to enter first for the sake of bringing in the censer: then for the incense: then for the blood of the bull first, then also of the goat. And so Moses Kotzi says he entered four times on that day: Correctly.

We previously observed that fourfold entry differently from Maimonides and Abarbanel, namely that the first time it was done by bringing in the censer with coals and spices, and thus making the incense; the second with the blood of the bullock; the third with the blood of the slaughtered goat; the fourth, however, to take away the vessel and the censer from there. Buxtorf, however, in his History of the Ark of the Covenant, ch. V, p. 76, denies that the high priest entered more than once on the day of atonements: And since the analogy of the Apostolic comparison regarding the single entry of Christ into heaven does not seem to permit anything else, nor does the opinion of Moses Kotzi, nor of other Rabbis, deserve assent here at all, of whom, however, Kotzi is less probable than the others. Whether one believes in a double golden censer with Villalpando, or with Buxtorf maintains both a single golden censer and a single annual entry with it, and that it was not indeed enclosed and kept in the holy of holies, but is said in that sense, that the holy of holies had it, that it served peculiarly for this use, so that the High Priest might offer incense with it in the holy of holies. Briefly, he had it in that manner not by reason of possession, but by reason of use.

Which he offers for himself and the ignorances of the people] he offers, that is, he carries inside the sanctuary קרב. For himself the blood of a calf, of a goat for the people. Although, however, on the day of expiation all sins were expiated for which there was not added in the law the penalty of death, or of excision, nevertheless this writer preferred to use the word ignorances, so that he might spare the honor of the Hebrew High Priest, who also offered and prayed for himself. But it ought not to be presumed that he had sinned otherwise than through ignorance. Otherwise, any sins are also accustomed to be called ignorances by way of euphemism, as can be seen in Tob. III, verse 3, Judith V, v. 22, Sirach LI, 26, 1 Macc. XIII, 39.

Three things are to be noted in these Grotian remarks: 1. That he explains προσφέρειν as to carry inside the sanctuary. Which false interpretation he owes to the Socinians. And yet to offer for ignorances is to offer, that is, to sacrifice for ignorances. But sacrifices were offered, and victims were made, not when they were brought into the sanctuary, but outside the sanctuary: which has been sufficiently shown in Socinismus Profligatus. 2. That he does not say all sins were expiated on the day of expiations, but only those for which there was not added in the law the penalty of death or of excision; in which Grotius again Socinianizes. On the contrary, the Holy Spirit teaches expressly that all iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins were expiated, Levit. XVI, 21. Which also the analogy with the antitype demands, Isa. LIII, 5, 6. Compare also Levit. XVI, v. 16, 30, 34, Chap. VI, 1, seqq. That he explained ignorances as sins through ignorance: which should rather be taken generally of any sins whatsoever, since there is ignorance in all sins. And therefore that word is accustomed to be used generally of sins, as Grotius himself acknowledged, not by way of euphemism, but because all sins proceed from ignorance and a certain error of the mind, even the more serious ones, Luke XXIII, 34, 1 Pet. I, verse 14. Concerning which the Scholastics dispute, with Thomas leading the way, that there is no sin which does not proceed from an error of practical judgment. But the Vulgate did not translate this conveniently here, which he offers for his and the people's ignorance: since in Greek it is not: for his and the people's ignorances, but for himself, and those of the people, etc., which he offers for himself, and the ignorances of the people, as the Syriac Interpreter rendered it.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν] Quæ & ἐσωτέρα, id est, in adytum.

Ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ Ἀρχιερεὺς.

Figuræ magis quam rei causa. Nam major pars sacri alibi fiebat. Ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ אחת בשנה Exod. XXX, 10. Lev. XVI, 34. Is dies erat decimus mensis Tisri.

Οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος.

Vituli & hirci, Lev. XVI, 14. 15. Eo sanguine adspergeba- tur tegmen illud sive ἱλαστήριον. Hinc apparet, quanquam di- citur summus Sacerdos semel intrasse, id intelligendum, quod uno tantum die intraverit, non quod non aliquoties exive- rit & rursus intraverit. Primum enim intrare eum oportuit batilli inferendi causa : deinde suffitus: deinde sanguinis vi- tulini primum, deinde & hircini. Itaque quater illo die eum intraffe ait Moses Kotzi: Recte.

Aliter illum quaternum ingressum è Maimoni- de & Abarbenele observavimus antea, nimirum prima vice factum, thymiaterium cum prunis & aromatibus inferendo, adeoque suffitum facien- do; alterum cum sanguine juvenci; tertium cum sanguine hirci mactati; quartum vero ad aufe- rendum inde acerram atque thuribulum. Bux- torfius tamen histor. arcæ fœd. cap. V. p. 76. ne- gat, plus vice simplici ingressum esse summum Pontificem die expiationum: Et quum analogia comparationis Apostolicæ quoad unicum Christi in cœlum ingressum haud videatur aliud permit- tere, neque Mofis Kotzi, neque aliorum Rabbino- rum sententia hic omnino assensum meretur, è quibus tamen Kotzi præ aliis minus probabilis est. Sive geminum cum Villalpando thuribulum aureum quis credat, sive cum Buxtorffio statuat & aureum thuribulum unicum, & unicum cum eo ingressum annuum, id vero non in sancto sancto- rum inclusum & asservatum fuisse, sed eo sensu dici, quod sanctum sanctorum id habuerit, quod illud huic usui peculiariter inservierit, ut eo Sacer- dos summus in sancto sanctorum adoleret. Brevi- ter habuit de eo modo non ratione τῆς κτήσεως, sed ratione τῆς χρήσεως.

Ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτῦ καὶ τῶν τῦ λαῦ ἀγνοημάτων] προσφέρει, id est, fert intra adytum קרב. Pro se vitulinum sanguinem, hircinum pro populo. Quanquam autem in die ἱλασμῶ expiabantur omnia peccata, quibus in lege non erat adjecta mortis pœna, aut ἐξολοθρεύσεως, tamen maluit hic scriptor uti voce ἀγνοημάτων, ut summi Sacerdotis Ebraici honori parceret, qui & pro se offerebat ac precabatur. Præ- sumi autem non debebat aliter peccasse, quam per ignoran- tiam. Alioqui solent etiam quævis peccata per χαριεντισμὸν dici ἀγνοήματα, ut videre est Tob. III. vers. 3. Judith. V. v. 22. Sicach. LI, 26. 1. Macc. XIII, 39.

Tria in his Grotianis notanda: 1. Quod προσ- φέρειν explicet ferre intra adytum. Quam ψευδερ- μηνείαν Socinianis debet. Atqui προσφέρειν ὑπὲρ ἀγνοημάτων est offerre, id est sacrificare pro igno- rantiis. Offerebantur autem sacrificia, & fiebant victimæ, non cum inferrentur in adytum, sed extra adytum: Quod in Socinismo Profligato sa- tis ostensum. 2. Quod non omnia peccata in die expiationum dicat expiata, sed tantum ea, quibus in lege non erat adjecta mortis pœna aut ἐξολοθρεύ- σεως; quo iterum Socinizat Grotius. Contra Spi- ritus Sanctus docet expresse, quod omnes עונות iniquitates filiorum Israël, & omnes פשעיהם præ- varicationes eorum in omnibus חטאתם peccatis eorum expiata sint, Levit. XVI, 21. Quod etiam analogia cum antitypo postulat, Esa. LIII, 5. 6. Conf. & Levit. XVI. v. 16. 30. 34. Cap. VI, 1. seqq, 3. Quod ἀγνοήματα de peccatis per ignorantiam exposuit: quæ generaliter potius accipienda de quibusvis peccatis, siquidem in omnibus peccatis ignorantia sit. Ideoque generaliter de peccatis ad- hiberi illa vox consuevit, ut Grotius ipse agnovit, non per χαριεντισμὸν, sed quod omnia peccata ex ignorantia, & errore quodam mentis proce- dant, etiam graviora, Luc.
