Testatorem, qui hoc loco vocatur Μεσίτης, & quidem inter Deum & homi- nes, utpote qui ex parte Dei accepit plenissimam testandi potestatem, quoniam in ipso omnis plenitu- do Deitatis inhabitabat, & omnes thesauri sapientiæ & scientiæ abscondebantur, ipsique omnis potestas in cælo & in terra data erat, imo omnia in manus ipsius data. Non itaque ad testamentum hoc con- currit ut testis, vel consiliarius, vel notarius, vel in- tercessor, qui ab aliquo legata precaretur in pote- state sua nullatenus posita, sed ut Dominus, Dicta- tor, fœderis Autor. 2. Testamenti naturam. Vo- catur ab Apostolo Novum Testamentum, de quo supra cap. VIII. ad vers. 6. & seq. latissime actum est. Novitas in eo posita est, quod typis at- que umbris remotis omnia clarissime exhibeat, im- pletumque

, primis cum Vetus Testamentum ita sancitum esset, ut mors non in ipso Testatore vel Mediatore, sed in aliquo adjuncto vel substituto perficeretur, atque ita ratibaberetur promissio: hoc mortem in ipso Testatore ostenderet. Unde notamus 3. Testamenti consummationem, quæ facta est θανάτου γενομένου. Non equidem ita cælestis Testatoris voluntas ambu- latoria fuit usque ad mortem, sicut de alio quocun- que Testatore dicitur. Nam quicquid hoc Testamen- to nobis donatum est, πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων datum est, 2. Tim. I. 9. adeoque voluntate immutabili constat, nihilominus morte obsignatum fuit, quia ab æterno ita decretum est. Pertinet enim & mors ad ὡρισμέ- νην βουλὴν, Actor. II. 23. & quia mors naturalis repu- gnabat conditioni Christi, imo & conditioni sacrifi- cii. Nam & naturæ Christi Humanæ ea fuit per- fectio, ut nunquam in eam incidere potuerint causæ mortem naturalem accersentes, & quæ morte na- turali interierunt, nunquam ad sacrificium apta habeantur, ideoque ex admirabili κενώσει divinæque consilio ita fuit ἔνδοξος, ut mortem violentam ad- miserit. Unde etiam sanguinem habere potuit, quo in sanctuarium ingrederetur. 4. Testamenti effe- ctum: Is geminus est, primus est remissio peccato- rum sive transgressionum fœderi primo repugnan- tium: Secundus est promissio æternæ hæreditatis. Postquam enim per ἀπολύτρωσιν morte Christi fa- ctam, Veteris Testamenti maledictio transgressiones ssequuta expiravit, per se sequitur ἐπαγγελία τῆς αἰω- νίου κληρονομίας, uti Apostolus loquitur. Quod & Gal. III. 13. 14. uberius explicat, ubi dicit, Christum nos redemisse à maledictione legis, cum ipse pro nobis maledictum fieret, ut ad gentes benedictio Abrahami emanaret in Christo Jesu, & nos promissionem Spi- ritus acciperemus. 5. Hæredes. Dicuntur illi κε- κλημένοι vocati sive nuncupati. Nominari enim & nuncupari in Testamentis debent hæredes Sunt au- tem hoc loco οἱ κεκλημένοι non ex absoluto decreto per irresistibilem gratiam vocati. Tales enim sacra scri- ptura ignorat. Neque sunt tantum homines Novi Testamenti, uti Schlichtingius existimat, cum ait: Vocatos esse illos, quibus tempore Novi Testamenti hæreditas æterna per Christi Evangelium est oblata, quique tantam Dei gratiam fide complectuntur. Nam etiam ante tempus Novi Testamenti vocatio- nem ad æternam hæreditatem contigisse Christus il- lustribus parabolis indicat Matth. XX. & XXII. & alibi: Sed sunt ex intentione Dei omnes homines, ex ordinatione Dei non malitiose gratiæ exhibitæ resi- stentes, atque ita eandem λαμβάνοντες. Intentionem explicat Paulus 2. Timoth. II. 4. ordinationem partim Actor. XIII. 46. & seqq. partim XVII. 30. & seqq.

Porrò redimere transgressiones dicitur, sub priori testamento manentes, à quibus sub illo liberari non poteramus, hoc est, nos redimere ab illis transgref- sionibus per mortis suæ interventum, quia pœnam pro illis nobis debitam in se suscepit, & pro nobis exantlavit. Non quæ tempore Veteris Testamenti commissæ sunt; nam non ab illis tantum liberavit, sed quæ Veteris Testamenti rigore manebant irre- missæ, vel à quibus non poterant in lege Mosis justi- ficari, Act. XIII. 39. sub quibus concluseramus, vi pacti legalis, quod iram tantum operabatur, & omnes sub peccato concludebat, Rom. III. 9. 19. 20. cap. IV. 15. cap. XI. 32. Gal. III. 22.

Alii intelligunt peccata in Veteri Testamento commissa, quæ peculiariter hic commemorata sint, quod de illis dubitari poterat, an per mortem Chri sti expiata, & propter eam olim remissa credenti- bus fuerint, cum tempus Messiæ exhibiti sint ante- gressa, ut sensus sit: Non sunt liberati Patres in Ve- Vet. Testamento per sacrificia sua carnalia & ex- terna, sed solum per fidem & expiationem venturi sacrificii Messiæ, quod per illa præfiguratum fu- it, Act. XV. 11. Ebr. XIII 8. Apoc. XIII. 8. Sed solidi- or est prior explicatio; quam prolixe asserit B. Dartheus, docens particulam ἐπὶ hic esse εἰς in vel contra primum testamentum: Fœdus, inquit, seu Testamentum primum sancitum erat cum conditione strictissimæ observantiæ legi debitæ. Contra hanc infinitiæs peccatum est jam inde ab orbe condito, & peccabitur ad consummationem usque seculi. Quan- do itaque transgressionum ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ fa- starum fit mentio, non alia possunt intelligi, quam quæ contra legem currunt, quæ sola in Veteri Testa- mento ea erat, quæ παραϐάσεις & violationes pati- ebatur. Itaque non ad tempus dicti Veteris Te- stamenti hæc verba sunt referenda, sed ad fœdus atque conditionem fœderi antiquo cohærentem, quæ ex ipso naturæ vinculo nobis imposita est. Sane illi ipsi κεκλημένοι sive municipati hæredes æternæ felici- tatis fruuntur illa ἀπολυτρώσει τῶν παραϐάσεων ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ. Ergo etiam transgressiones seu peccata, quæ sub Novo Testamento committuntur, sunt παραϐάσεις ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ non ratione tem poris, sed ratione objecti, quia impingunt in basin & fundamentum τῆς πρώτης διαθήκης, hoc est, legem moralem. Neque licet ἀπολύτρωσιν ad transgressio- nes tempore Veteris Testamenti commissas duntaxat restringere. Ubi enim esset ἀπολύτρωσις tempore Novi Testamenti perpetratarum transgressionum. Sic enim & λῆψις ἐπαγγελίας ad Novum Testamen- tum duntaxat restringeretur, si de tempore, & non de objecto potius h. l. sermo esset. Sed & absurda da- retur sententia, si ita explicaremus. Sensus enim esset: Propterea Christus Novi Testamenti Media- tor est, ut morte facta redemptionem transgressio- num suarum acciperent, qui tempore Veteris Testa- menti vixerunt. Econtra qui vocati sunt ad hære- ditatem æternam in Novo Testamento, acciperent promissionem æternæ beatitudinis. Qui sensus in- commodissimus est & ineptissimus. Quid enim ad vocatos in Novo Testamento pertinet transgressio- num remissio facta hominibus Veteris Testamenti tempore viventibus? Anne promissionem accipere possunt homines Novi Testamenti sine transgressio- num remissione? Anne etiam homines in Veteri Te- stamento remissionem transgressionum suarum nacti a promissione exclusi sunt? Simplicissimus ita sensus est, fructum mortis Christi hunc esse, quod redimat & liberet sua infinita pretiositate à transgressionibus, quarum genus humanum convinci poterat vi fœde- ris antiqui & rigorosi, in quo lex homini concreata, sed ingravescente malitia postea oppressa, restaura- ta, & repetita solemniter fuit. Ἐπὶ itaque pro εἰς recte hoc loco dicitur posita.

Frustra ergo post alios est Ribera, cum hoc loco n. 74. dicit: Apostoli mentem esse dicere, tantæ virtutis fuisse passionem Christi, ut ne sancti quidem, qui in Veteri Testamen- to fuerunt, salutem sine ipsa consequi potuerint, quo- niam peccata illis remitti non potuerunt, nisi per sanguinem Christi, qui fundendus erat in pretium redemptionis, cujus effusionem sacrificiis suis præfi- gurabant, & per eum delenda esse profitebantur. Unde peccata ita tunc remittebantur, ut sustineri à Deo viderentur, quia pretium eorum nondum erat exsolutum, sed expectabatur solvendum. Vera quidem sententia est, sed non quadrat ad scopum Apostolicum, cum ad tempus potius, quam ad ob- jectum Veteris Testamenti primum fructum mortis Christi restringit: Ex qua causa idem frustra scisci- tatur, cum ait: Sed cur non loquutus est etiam de peccatis eorum, qui vixerunt in lege naturæ, quan- doquidem nec illa remittebantur, nisi propter pas- sionem Christi futuram? Et respondet: Scribebat ad Ebræos, quibus metuebat, ne forte plus, quam erat, legi tribuentes, ad illam reverterentur, ideoque sem- per legis infirmitatem demonstrat. Deinde nihil opus erat de illis loqui. Nam si Ebræi, qui à Deo per Mosen acceperant legem & ritus sacrificiorum pro peccatis, emundari sacrificiis illis non potuerunt, sed per sanguinem Christi sanctificati sunt, multo minus, qui erant in lege natura potuissent suis sacri- ficiis emundari, quæ à Deo data non erant. Respon- sio est partim falsa, partim superflua. Falsa, dum ait: Metu relapsus Ebræorum ad venerationem legis nihil fuisse sine fructu redundante ex morte Christi ad eos, qui vixerunt ante promulgationem Veteris Testamenti, dicendum. Quid enim hoc ad exaggerationem legis pertinuisset, si dixisset Aposto- lus, vi mortis Christi liberatos esse à peccato, quot- quot ab origine mundi vixerunt. Deinde & illud falsum est, homines, qui vixerunt ante solenniter promulgatum Novum Testamentum, non habuisse sacrificia à Deo data. Est hic error eorum, qui sacrificia ad dictamen naturæ referunt, & existi- mant, ipsa naturali ratione suggerente, omnibus temporibus apud omnes homines debere esse sacrifi- cia continuata, contra quos disputatum est in Mys- Mist. c. 1. A. vera fide obtulit Abel Ebr. XI. 4. Ergo ex revelatione. Fides enim sine revelatione non est fides. Superflua autem est ista responsio, quia A- postolus loquitur de transgressionibus in templum, quas illa lex arguit, quæ sub Veteri Testamento con- firmata fuit. Fuit autem antea, & ab origine ho- minum. Quemadmodum enim Gal. III. 17. No- vum Testamentum dicitur in Abrahamo κεκυρωμέ- νον, quod postmodum per Mosen solenniter promul- gatum fuit. Frustra etiam Ribera hoc loco addit: De lege nova sive Christi nihil necesse erat dicere, quæ non habet sacrificium, nisi corporis & sanguinis Christi, & sacramenta, quæ ex passione & sanguine Christi vim habent sanctificandi. Quasi vero A- postolus de lege nova, quam vocant, hoc loco nihil di- ceret, cum vim ejus summam atque inexplicabilem proponit. Eundem errorem errat Schlichtingius, cum de tempore hunc locum interpretatur, & ait: Utitur Apostolus voce παραϐάσεων, id est, trans- gressionum, quæ gravia peccata notari solent, ut ostendat, qualia imprimis peccata in Novo Testa- mento remittantur, nempe gravia, quibus in Veteri Testamento nulla expiatio, sed tantum mortis pœna fuit constituta. Ideo addit: Quæ sub priori Testa- mento, subintellige, manebant, seu expiari non po- terant, quorum nulla tunc concessa fuit remissio. Vi- detur autem simul indicare voluisse, ista gravia pec- cata sub Veteri Testamento locum habuisse, seu com- mitti fuisse solita, cum Novum Testamentum una cum eorum reatu, & ipsa in iis, qui promissionibus illius ex animo credunt, penitus auferat. Ita Schlich- tingius, qui postea pergit rationem dare, cur Apo- stolus graviorum peccatorum tantum meminerit. Quod verò, inquit, transgressionum tantum seu graviorum scelerum expiatio commemoretur, id non propterea fit, quasi sub Novo Testamento non etiam expientur omnia leviora peccata: Sed vel perinde est, ac si dictum esset, etiam transgressionum earum &c. Solet enim interdum simpliciter loqui Scriptura, ut non excludat alia, sed includi doceat & illa, de quibus poterat esse major dubitatio, quæ- que si inclusa censeantur, multo magis id statuendum sit de cæteris. Sic inter alia David Psal. XXV. 8. pronunciat de Deo, ut textus Ebraicus habet, bonus & rectus Dominus, ideo docebit peccatores in via, id est, etiam peccatores, non tantum homines justos, seu, ut statim addit, mansuetos & humiles, de quibus id affirmat. Sic & Paulus impium à Deo justificari dicit, non quod hunc solum, sed quod etiam hunc justificet Roman. IV. Vel ideo tantum gravium pec- catorum meminit Autor, ut ostendat, ea imprimis sub Novo Testamento expiari, huncque proprium esse Novi Testamenti & expiationis Christi fructum. Sed si gravium peccatorum reatus sub Novo Testa- mento aufertur, multo magis id in levioribus fieri censendum est. Adde quod gravia illa peccata mul- to magis conscientiam turbare potuerint, quam le- viora delicta, quandoquidem istis tum aliqua expia- tio in lege fuerit concessa, ex qua suspicari saltem li- cebat, Deum pro sua immensa bonitate etiam aeterne mortis poenam ablutarum esse, illis vero plane nulla. Sic ille, qui 1. in eo hallucinatur, quod παραβά- σεων tantum gravia peccata notari dicat, cum id ne- que vis vocis neque usus postulet. Nam supra cap. II. 2. παράβασις & παρακοὴ conjunguntur, & quam- cunque inobedientiam non gravem tantum & enormem designant. 2. Errat, cum existimat, non ipsa, quae erant ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ, sed talia peccata ab A- postolo intelligi, quibus per mortem Christi contingat ἀπολύτρωσις, cum Apostolus diserte loquatur de transgressionibus ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ. Ergo nullo modo de talibus tantum, sed potius de ipsis pronun- tiat, quod à Christo habeant ἀπολύτρωσιν. 3. Pec- cat in eo, quod dicit, gravia peccata sub Veteri Te- stamento locum habuisse, seu committi fuisse solita, cum Novum Testamentum una cum eorum reatu & ipsa penitus auferat. Nam si de tempore sermo sit, & Novi & Veteris Testamenti tempore gravia peccata committuntur: Si vero de instituto utriusque Testa- menti loquamur, neutrum gravibus peccatis locum concedit, utrumque ea penitus auferri vult: Si vero de virtute contra peccata valente intelligamus, ve- rissimum est, eandem esse in Novo Testamento, non vero in Veteri: Id tamen etiam certum est, virtutem illam retrorsum sub Veteri Testamento fuisse dispen- satam. Unde 4. in eo quoque labitur, quod ait, sub Veteri Testamento gravia delicta mansisse, seu ex- piari non potuisse, nullamque tum concessam fuisse eorum remissionem, levioribus delictis tantum ali quam expiationem fuisse in lege concessam, ex qua suspicari licebat, Deum pro immensa sua bonitate etiam aeterne mortis poenam ablaturum esse. Nam etiamsi vi Veteris Testamenti peccatorum nulla facta fuerit remissio, sed tota hausta sit ex bonis Novi Te- stamenti praefiguratis, nihilo minus sub Veteri Testa- mento remissio contingebat; imo Vetus Testamen- tum ordinabatur, ut famularetur istis mysteriis ad- umbrandis, unde per fidem accipi remissio peccato- rum poterat. Manet itaque ἀπολύτρωσιν sive libe- rationem pretio soluto factam à transgressionibus ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ esse universalem, omniumque temporum, non vero duntaxat vel ad Vetus, vel ad Novum Testamentum restringendam. Omnis enim hominum omnium transgressio est ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ, quia in illa est tribunal justitiae divinae, hoc est, lex moralis, quae omnes homines autoritate divi- na concludit sub peccatum, ut omnibus contingat misericordia, Roman. XI. 32. Galat. III. 22. Atque catenus etiam lex paedagogus est ad Christum, qua- tenus ea transgressioens ita arguit, ut in se tamen nullam ἀπολύτρωσιν promittat, sed potius, ut alibi quaeramus, adigat, Gal. III. 24. Unde etiam adjecta dicitur & imposita παραβάσεων χάρις, Galat. III. 19. Syrus luculenter ita transfert: Idcircò ipse fact9 Mediator foederis novi, qui per mortem suam idem factus est Redemptor illis, qui transgressi fuerant foedus prius. Calvinus in h. l. commemorat vim & effectum mortis Christi, cum dicit, solutum esse pro peccatis pretium, quæ sub priori Testamento leri pecudum sanguine non poterant, quibus verbis Judæos à lege ad Christum traducere voluit. Nam si tanta est legis imbecillitas, ut, quæcunque expian- dis peccatis remedia adhibet, minimè præstent, quod figurant: Quis in ea tanquam in portu quiescat? Hoc inquam unum abunde eos stimulare debuit ad expetendam legis correctionem, quia fieri non pote- rat, quin perpetuo anxii essent. Contra ubi ad Chri- stum ventum est, quia in ipso obtinemus plenam re- demptionem, nihil est, quod nos amplius solicitet &c. Nec abnuit Osiander: Quam certum est, quod Chri- stus pro peccatis nostris sit mortuus, tam firmum etiam est fœdus gratiæ, seu Novum Testamentum: In quo omnibus in Christum credentibus offeruntur & donantur remissio peccatorum & vita æterna. Pri- mum enim Testamentum peccata nostra arguit: se- cundum Testamentum eadem condonat. Non enim prioris temporis, sed potius prioris pacti ratio ha- betur, ut ad caput præcedens observavimus.

Frustra ergo Grotius est, comparans sordes tem- porum Veteris Testamenti & populum Israël cum tempore Novi Testamenti & populo Christiano. Sa- lus autem dicitur hæreditas, quia ad illam creden- tes in filios Dei gratuito in regeneratione adoptan- tur, iisque non ex merito datur, sed ex gratia ejus, qui propter Christum Pater credentium factus est, Apoc. 21, 6. 7. Grotii observationem, quod ἀπο- λύτρωσις παραβάσεων sit ἀπὸ παραβάσεων fa- cile admittimus. Sed non recte explicat redem- tionem è transgressionibus de perpetrandis, cum de perpetratis intelligenda sit, non quod cessemus peccare, sed quod à peccatorum culpa & pœna, cui obnoxii eramus, liberati simus, qua ἀπολυ- τρώσῄ qui per fidem fruuntur, justificati nempe à Deo, & remissionem peccatorum consecuti, in pace sunt cum Deo, Rom. V. 1.

## 9:16
Verse 16.

For where there is a testament] In that better and more excellent sense, as we just said.

To be borne, that is, to be expected, how ἤνεγκε in Romans IX. 22. For expectation is a certain burden. Thus you have נשא in Deuteronomy XXIV. 15, Jeremiah XLIV. 14. Some testators, when there is no need, yet express it, as in Salvian against avarice III: When I shall have departed from human affairs, then you, my dearest, be my heir.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη] In sensu illo potiore & excellentiore, ut modo diximus.

Θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τῷ διατιθεμένῳ] Ferri, id est, ex- pectari, quomodo ἤνεγκε Rom. IX. 22. Est enim expecta- tio onus quoddam. Sic נשא habes Deut. XXIV. 15. Je- rem. XLIV. 14. Quidam testatores, quando non opus est, tamen id exprimunt, ut apud Salvianum contra ava- ritiam III. Quando ego ex rebus humanis exiero, tunc mihi tu ille, charissime, hæres esto.

## 9:17
Verse 17.

For a testament is of force after men are dead] This is what the Roman jurists say: A testament is confirmed by death. Ἐπὶ here has the mark of time: when those who have made a testament are dead. Thus the Greeks say ἐπὶ κυνὶ for the time of the dog star.

For it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth] For it is never valid while the testator lives, that is, it produces no effect in the meantime, as the Syrian rightly says here. For a testament is, as defined by Modestinus, the just expression of one's will concerning that which one wishes to be done after one's death. Whence also the will of the deceased is defined by Quintilian. There is no inheritance of a living person, l. 1. D. de hæred. vel Act. vendita l. I. D. pro hærede.

The scope of the Apostle is to demonstrate that we could not have obtained the promised inheritance except through the death of Christ. For he presupposes that Christ is the Mediator of the New Testament in such a way that He is also its Author and the Testator Himself. Ἐπὶ νεκροῖς is from death, a Hebrew phrase, according to which Christ is said to be from the dead, that is, to have risen from death or the state of the dead. Nevertheless, the New Testament was valid even before the death of Christ, as Estius rightly says, because of the foreknowledge and acceptance of the Father, who, looking upon the death of His Son, accepted it as having been accomplished. But if, however, on account of the promise of the ransom made to a man worthy of trust, the captive is sometimes released; why should the promise of the λύτρε to be paid in the fullness of time, made by Him who is Truth itself, not have been far more effective before the heavenly Father? He who therefore cuts his own vines when he denies that the heavenly inheritance was given to anyone before the death and glorification of Christ, [argues that it] was fitting. For if the New Testament was valid, why should the faithful of the Old Testament not have obtained the inheritance by the power of the same? Why would that not have been fitting? For those who were regenerated to the heavenly inheritance through the sacrament of circumcision, and made heirs of righteousness through faith in the Messiah, whose God is God not only in this life but also in the other; how could the inheritance of eternal life be denied to them after this life? Indeed, Christ teaches by the example of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that it was not denied, and convinces the Sadducees of it, Matt. XXII. 32. If the death of Christ was effective for the remission of sin and justification, why not also for the glorification of the faithful of the O.T.? If the foreseen death of Christ was so effective that by its power those whom GOD foresaw would believe in Christ were elected to salvation from eternity; why should it not also have been so effective that by its power those believing in Him were made partakers of eternal salvation immediately after death? Regarding the truth of the matter itself, see Acts XV. 11, Heb. XIII. 8, Rev. XIII. 8. Furthermore, regarding the doubt that occurs concerning this argumentation of the Apostle taken from the Testament, whether it might not be concluded by the same reasoning that it was necessary for the author of the old covenant also to die: since that too was by the LXX. Interpreters and Heb. VIII. called it a covenant, Estius does not poorly respond: The Old covenant was not called a testament by the counsel of the Holy Spirit because it was to be confirmed by the death of its Author; but because it was a covenant figurative of that covenant which was to be confirmed by the death of its Author. Nevertheless, it pleased [God] that it also be dedicated in blood, not of the author or mediator, but of brute animals: so that it might have some likeness of a testament properly so called, in that it would not be consummated without death, especially since it also was sometimes to be called διαθήκη by the Greeks, and testament by the Latins. This, therefore, is what follows: Since not even that old one was dedicated without blood. Theophylact paraphrases these words thus: Let not the death of Christ, he says, terrify you. For if He had not granted it to nature, how would we ourselves be made heirs? (For it is certain that a testament also has both force and firmness after the death of the Testator) Or in what way would we be worthy of this inheritance, if the enmities between us and God had not yet been removed.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

Διαθήκη γὰρ ἐπὶ νεκροῖς βεβαία] Hoc est, quod dicunt Romani Juris consulti: Testamentum morte confirmatur. Ἐπὶ hic temporis habet notam: ubi illi mortui sunt, qui testamentum fecere. Sic ἐπὶ κυνὶ tempore caniculæ dicunt Græci.

Ἐπεὶ μήποτε ἰσχύει, ὅτε ζῇ ὁ διαθέμενος] Nunquam enim valet, dum vivit testator, id est, nullum interim producit effectum, ut recte hic Syrus. Est enim testamen- tum, Modestino definiente, voluntatis justa sententia de eo, quod quis post mortem suam fieri velit. Unde & vo- luntas defuncti a Quintiliano definitur. Viventis nulla est hæreditas l. 1. D. de hæred. vel Act. vendita l. I. D. pro hærede.

Scopus Apostoli est demonstrare, quod promis- sam hæreditatem non nisi per mortem Christi consequi potuerimus. Præsupponit enim Christum ita Mediatorem esse Novi Testamenti, ut Autor etiam ejusdem sit & Testator ipse. Ἐπὶ νεκροῖς est à morte, phrasi Ebræa, juxta quam Christus dici- tur à mortuis, hoc est, ex morte sive statu mortuo- rum resurrexisse. Valuit tamen Novum Testamen- tum etiam ante mortem Christi, ut recte Estius, propter præscientiam & acceptationem Patris, qui mortem Filii sui aspiciens acceptavit ut fa- ctam. Quod si autem ob promissionem λύτρ& à viro fide digno factum quandoq; captivus dimit- titur; quidni longe magis apud Patrem cœlestem efficax fuit promissio λύτρε in plenitudine tempo- ris exolvendi, facta ab eo, qui est ipsa veritas: qui proinde propria vineta cædit, cum negat, hæredi- tatem cœlestem cuiquam dari ante mortem & glo- rificationem Christi, conveniens fuisse. Si enim valuit Novum Testamentum, quidni vi ejusdem hæreditatem consequuti fuerint fideles Vet. Testa- menti cur id non fuerit conveniens? Qui enim per sacramentum circumcisionis regeniti sunt ad hæ- reditatem cœlestem, & per fidem in Messiam, justi- tiæ hæredes facti, quorum Deus est Deus non in hac tantum vita, sed etiam in altera; quomodo illis post hanc vitam hæreditas negari potuit æternæ vitæ; imo non negatam fuisse Abrahami, Isaaci, & Jaco- bi exemplo Christus docet, ac Sadducæos de eo convincit Matth. XXII. 32. Si mors Christi effi- cax fuit ad peccati remissionem & justificationem, quidni etiam ad glorificationem fidelium V. T.? Si prævisa mors Christi tam fuit efficax, ut vi illius ab æterno fuerint electi ad salutem, quos DEUS ad Christum credituros prævidit; quidni etiam ita ef- ficax fuerit, ut vi illius credentes in ipsum statim post mortem æternæ salutis participes redderen- tur? De ipsa vero rei veritate vide Act. XV. 11. Ebr. XIII. 8. Apoc. XIII. 8. Cæterum ad dubium, quod circa hanc Apostoli à Testamento petitam argu- mentationem occurrit, annon pari ratione colligi possit, necessarium fuisse, ut & autor veteris pacti moreretur: Siquidem & illud à LXX. Interpretib9 & Ebr. IIX. vocatum est pactum, non male respon- det Estius: Vetus pactum non eo consilio Spiritus sancti vocatum fuisse testamentum, quod morte sui Auto- ris esset confirmandum; sed quia pactum erat figura- tivum ejus pacti, quod Autoris sui morte confirmari debuit. Placuit tamen illud etiam in sanguine de- dicari, non autoris aut mediatoris, sed brutorum ani- malium: ut haberet quondam similitudinem testa- menti proprie dicti, in eo quod non sine morte con- summaretur, maxime quoniam ipsum etiam ali- quando appellandum erat Græcis διαθήκη, testamen- tum Latinis. Hoc ergo est, quod sequitur: Quan- doquidem ne vetus quidem illud absq; sanguine dedicatum fuit. Theophylactus ita παραφράζει hæc verba: Haudquaquam, inquit, vos Christi mors terreat. Nam si naturæ ille non concessisset, quomodo ipsi hæredes efficeremur? (Constat enim & testamen- tum post Testatoris excessum & vim habere & firmi- tatem) Vel quo pacto digni hujusce essemus hæredi- tatis, si nondum fuissent nos inter & Deum sublatæ inimicitiæ.

## 9:18
Vers. 18. Ὅθεν ὐδὲ ἡ πρώτη χωρὶς αἵματος ἐγκεκαίνιςαι] Namely, so that the figure might approach more closely to the thing figured. Ἐγκαίνια or in the plural ἐγκαίνια is the dedication of some thing, Ezra VI. 16, 17, Nehem. XII. 27, Dan. III. 2. The same is ἀγκαίνισις Num. VII. 28, ἐγκαινισμὸς Num. VII. 10, 11, 2 Chron. VII. 9, Dan. III. 3, and in the inscription of Psalm 84, which is 30 for the Hebrews, 29 for the Greeks, 1 Macc. IV. 56, 59, 2 Macc. II. 9, 28. Quintilian: Nor should the first crime be considered an encaenium. The verb ἐγκαινίζειν חנך Deut. XX. 5, 1 Kings VIII. 64, 2 Chron. VII. 5, 1 Macc. IV. 36, 54, 57, V. 1. We also have where חדש is translated ἐγκαινίζειν, as 1 Sam. XI. 14, 2 Chron. XV. 8. You have this verb also below X. 20.

The word ἐγκεκαίνιςαι is rendered 'dedicated' by the Vulgate, but as Estius notes, it is 'initiated', 'sanctioned', 'confirmed', as the Syriac version has it, so that the sense may be: Let it not be a wonder what I said, that the New Testament could not be confirmed without the blood and death of the Mediator Christ: since not even that first and Old Testament, although it was not so properly a testament, was confirmed without blood. For in its sanctioning, victims were slain, whose blood would prefigure the blood of Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 18. Ὅθεν ὐδὲ ἡ πρώτη χωρὶς αἵματος ἐγκεκαίνιςαι] Nempe ut figura ad rem figuratam propius accederet. Ἐγκαίνια vel pluraliter ἐγκαίνια est rei alicujus dedicatio, Esdræ VI. 16. 17. Nehem. XII. 27. Dan. III. 2. Idem ἀγκαίνισις Num. VII. 28. ἐγκαινισμὸς Num. VII. 10. 11. 2. Paral. VII. 9. Dan. III. 3. & inscriptione Psalmi 84. qui Ebræis XXX. Græcis XXIX. 1. Macc. IV. 56. 59. 2. Macc. II. 9. 28. Quintilianus: Nec pro encænio ducen- dum scelus primum. Verbum ἐγκαινίζειν חנך Deut. XX. 5. 1. Reg. VIII. 64. 2. Paral. VII. 5. 1. Macc. IV. 36. 54. 57. V. 1. Habemus & ubi חדש vertitur ἐγκαινίζειν, ut 1. Sam. XI. 14. 2. Paral. XV. 8. Habes hoc verbum & in- fra X. 20.

Vox ἐγκεκαίνιςαι dedicatum est redditur à Vul- gata, sed Estio notante est, initiatum, sancitum, con- firmatum est, ut habet Syriaca versio, ut sensus sit: Non mirum sit quid dixi, Novum Testamentum sine sanguine & morte Mediatoris Christi non potuisse confirmari: quandoquidem nec primum illud & Ve- tus Testamentum, quamvis non ita proprie testamen- tum esset, sine sanguine fuit confirmatum. Nam in eo fanciendo cæsæ sunt victimæ, quarum sanguis præ- figuraret sanguinem Christi.

## 9:19
Vers. 19. Λαληθείσης γὰρ πάσης ἐντολῆς, κατὰ νόμον ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως παντὶ τῷ λαῷ] He understands those precepts which are in Exod. XX, XXI, XXII, XXIII. And λαλεῖν here is to recite from a book. Κατὰ νόμον according to God's command.

Theophylact notes another sense of the words κατὰ νόμον, by which a command according to the law denotes nothing other than a command comprehended by the law, which is more elegant.

Λαβὼν τὸ αἷμα τῶν μόσχων τράγων μετὰ ὕδατος καὶ ἐρίου κοκκίνου καὶ ὑσσώπου] In Exod. XXIV. 6 it is only said that the people were sprinkled with the blood of the victims. But we learn from another place, Lev. XIV. 49, 50, that it was customary for water to be mixed with the blood and for a sprinkling to be made from hyssop and scarlet wool. You also have the use of hyssop in sprinkling in Exod. XII. 22 and Ps. LI. 9. The mention of the goat outside the text of Moses is added here, because it is credible that besides the peace offerings, there were also sin offerings, in which class the goat is the most important victim, Lev. IV. 23, IX. 3, XVI. 15. We see that it was customary to join eucharistic victims and sin offerings in the cited place, Lev. IX. 3, 4.

And this conjunction of peace offerings and sin offerings was fitting for the thing signified. For the blood of the New Testament prefigured there was shed as much for the expiation of sins as for the salvation of men.

Αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον καὶ πάντα τὸν λαὸν ἐῤῥάντισε] By the people are understood those who were standing nearest from among the people, and in this matter were acting in the place of the whole people. We do not read in Moses or in the Talmudic writings that the book was sprinkled. And αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον can be referred to λαβών. For history expressly says that in Exod. XXIV. 7. Thus καὶ here will be redundant, as often happens after participles: because those participles have the force of a verb. For it is just as if he had said, he took, and he sprinkled. Peter alludes to this 1 Pet. I. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 19. Λαληθείσης γὰρ πάσης ἐντολῆς, κατὰ νόμον ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως παντὶ τῷ λαῷ] Intelligit præcepta illa, quæ sunt Exod. XX. XXI. XXII. XXIII. Et λαλεῖν, hic est de li- bro recitare. Κατὰ νόμον ex Dei jussu.

Notat Theophylactus & alium verborum κατὰ νόμον sensum, quo mandatum secundum legem no- tat non aliud, quam mandatum lege comprehen- fum, qui est concinnior.

Λαβὼν τὸ αἷμα τῶν μόσχων τράγων μετὰ ὕδατος καὶ ἐρίου κοκκίνου καὶ ὑσσώπου] Exod. XXIV. 6. tantum dici- tur sanguine victimarum respersum fuisse populum. Sed sanguini solitam misceri aquam & περιῤῥαντηρίαν fieri ex hyssopo & lana coccinea discimus ex altero loco Levit. XIV. 49. 50. De hyssopi usu in aspersione habes & Exod. XII. 22. & Psal. LI. 9. Hirci mentio extra textum Mosis hic addita, quia credibile est prætor victimas σωτηρίους acces- sisse & περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν in quo genere potissima victima hir- cus Levit. IV. 23. IX. 3. XVI. 15. Solere autem jungi vi- ctimas εὐχαριστηρίους & περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν, videmus dicto loco Levit. IX. 3. 4.

Et hæc conjunctio sacrificiorum pacificorum & pro peccato rei significatæ conveniebat. Sanguis enim Novi Testamenti illic præfiguratus, tam pro peccatorum expiatione, quam pro salute homi- num effusus est.

Αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον καὶ πάντα τὸν λαὸν ἐῤῥάντισε] Per populum intelligi eos, qui de populo proxime adstabant, & in hac re populi totius gerebant vices. Librum fuisse respersum nec in Mose nec in Thalmudicis legimus. Et potest αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον referri ad λαβών. Id enim ex- presse dicit historia Exod. XXIV. 7. Ita καὶ hic erit παρέλκον ut sæpe fieri solet post participia: quia illa par- ticipia vim habent verbi. Perinde enim est quasi di- xisset, ἔλαβε, καὶ ἐῤῥάντισεν. Huc alludit Petrus 1. I. 2.

## 9:20
Vers. 20.

Saying, 'This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded to you.' In the LXX: 'Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.' We have spoken of the most ancient custom of ratifying covenants with blood at Matthew XXVI. 28. Christ alludes to these words in that passage in Matthew, 'Which he commanded' (אשר כרת), Exodus XXIV. 8.

Nothing, however, prevents us from understanding that the book was also sprinkled, since the Apostle could have had that from divine inspiration. For neither was the water mentioned by Moses, although one may gather that it was necessary, because it would have been difficult to sprinkle blood widely upon the people unless the blood were mixed with water, so that it might be both more liquid for sprinkling and more abundant. These and other things, from which Guil. Baillius in Catech. Controv. tr. 1. q. 9. proves the authority of traditions from this passage, Ribera and Estius deduce from Moses himself. Blessed Dorotheus says in this place that the Apostle speaks nothing beyond Scripture when he explains the rite of consecration in verse 19. He says that the reading of the law preceded, and indeed of the whole of it. For 'when every commandment had been spoken,' he calls it 'a commandment according to the law,' that is, a commandment already written in the book of the law, Exodus XXIV, 4 and 7. He says that Moses read it, according to Exodus XXIV. 7. He says he read it to all the people, according to the cited passage. He says that he offered burnt offerings, among which there could have been goats, especially because a goat had to be sacrificed in the solemn expiation of the people and the annual purification, Leviticus XVI, 5. He says that young bulls were sacrificed, according to Exodus XXIV. 5. He says that the blood of goats and calves was kept, according to Exodus XXIV. 6. He says that water was taken, just as was customary in other sprinklings of blood, according to Leviticus XIV. 51, 52 and Numbers XIX. 6 and 18. He says that scarlet wool and hyssop were used for a sprinkler, as is the custom in such sprinklings. The Apostle says that the book itself was purified. There is no one who doubts that this is to be understood of the book of the law. And although it does not exist [in the text] that the book was also sprinkled with blood of the law; yet because he was present at the establishing of the old covenant, and all other things were sprinkled with blood, it can easily be understood that the book of the law also did not lack that sprinkling.

Moreover, from that mixture of water and blood, it is wrongly concluded that there is a mixture of water with wine in the Eucharist, which is contrary to the institution of Christ; it is more correctly said that the blood and water are signified, which flowed from the side of Christ, John 19, which signification Estius does not disapprove of, as the sacraments of both baptism on account of the water, and the holy supper on account of the blood. Theophylact wishes baptism to be signified. For he says, both blood and water constitute this, and it consists of these two.

The sprinkling, however, of both the book of the law and the people signified that neither could the law be fulfilled, nor the people be expiated from sins, without there being a need for the sprinkling of the blood of Christ, in whom alone we have both the πλήρωμα τῦ νόμ8 [fullness of the law] and the expiation of sins.

Hyssop, which is a humble herb and has the power of cleansing the chest, Thomas interprets typically as faith, which both subjects the mind to God and purifies the hearts, Acts 15:20. Wool and scarlet, which is of a red color, he interprets as charity. Others, as Estius notes, wish for the human nature of Christ to be signified by hyssop, in which both humility is shown and power lies hidden for cleansing the vices of our heart. By the scarlet wool, however, the flesh of Christ, which is white in itself like wool, is reddened by the blood of the passion like scarlet. But since by the blood of slaughtered animals the blood of Christ slaughtered for us is understood, and here an application is made, which ought to be done through the ministry of the Word as a sprinkling, scarlet wool not unsuitably signifies the ministry of the Word, through which we are sprinkled with the blood of Christ: For the Word, and the ministry of the Word, ought to be white with the justice and innocence of Christ, and red with his blood as a ministry of reconciliation: By hyssop, however, the efficacy of the Word and the ministry of the Word is noted, which, even if it seems humble and contemptible, is nevertheless the δύναμις [power] of God, the Gospel, for purifying hearts through faith, John 15:3, Acts 15:24. There was no place here for speaking properly of faith, which is on our part, concerning which in the following chapter, and its use was desired in the people by sprinkling, not in the means through which the sprinkling was done.

Theophylact does not interpret badly the tabernacle as the Church or believers: Or indeed, he says, this presents the figure of us, who are also the tabernacle. For he says: I will walk in them and will dwell in them. And elsewhere: But the great vessels of the house of God are some gold, some silver. We are therefore truly sprinkled with the blood of Christ, and have obtained sanctification, since we have also been washed in his death by baptism. It is gathered, however, from this whole action, that because the people said: All things which the Lord has spoken, we will do, Moses had to sprinkle the book of the law and the people with blood, as if to indicate, you will not obtain the promised inheritance by the Testament through your obedience, by which it is impossible to fulfill the law, but solely through the obedience of the Messiah, and that even unto a bloody death, which is figured by this blood of innocent victims. Moreover, just as in this sanction of the Old Testament the words of Moses τῦτο τὸ ἅιμα τῆς διαθήκης [this is the blood of the covenant] are to be understood properly of the blood of the victims, with which the people were sprinkled; so no less properly are the words of Christ to be understood in the sanction of the New Testament, this is my blood, that blood of the New Testament, which was shed for the remission of sins, Matthew 26:28. Just as the promise concerning the possession of the land of Canaan was confirmed to the people by the blood of the sacrifices, and the people in turn were bound to the observation of the commandments of God

So by the blood of Christ in the holy supper the promise concerning the remission of sins and eternal life is sealed to us: but we are admonished that we should exhibit obedience (for the sake of thanksgiving) to Christ our savior, as Osiander here.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

Λέγων τοῦτο τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης ἧς ἐνετείλατο πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεός] In LXX. Ἰδὼ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης, Κύριος πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ πάντων τῶν λόγων τούτων. De antiquissi- mo more fœdera sanciendi sanguine diximus ad Matth. XXVI. 28. Ad hæc verba alludis Christus illo apud Matthæum loco, Ἧς ἐνετείλατο אשר כרת, Exod. XXIV. 8.

Nihil tamen obstat, quo minus & librum con- spersum intelligamus, quum id habere potuerit Apostolus ex inspiratione Divina. Nam nec aqua Mosi commemorata est, quamvis ea opus fuisse colligere liceat, eo quod sanguinem late spargere in populum difficile fuerit, nisi sanguine com- misceretur aqua, ut & liquidior esset ad aspersio- nem & copiosior. Quæ & alia, ex quibus Guil. Baillius in catech. Controv. tr. 1. q. 9. ex hoc loco traditionum autoritatem probat, Ribera & Estius e Mose ipso deducunt. Nihil, inquit hoc loco B. Dorotheus, præter scripturam loquitur Aposto- lus, cum ritus consecrationis v. 19. exponit. Dicit lectionem legis antecessisse, & quidem universæ. λα- ληθείσης γὰρ πάσης ἐντολῆς vocat ἐντολὴν κατὰ νόμον hoc est, ἐντολὴν in libro legis jam scriptam Exod. XXIV, 4. & 7. Dicit Mosen legisse juxta Exod. XXIV. 7. Dicit omni populo legisse juxta locum citatum. Dicit obtulisse holocausta, inter quæ po- tuerunt esse hirci, præsertim quia hircus in solenni expiatione populi & anniversaria purificatione im- molandus fuit, Levit. XVI, 5. Dicit immolatos suis- se juvencos juxta Exod. XXIV. 5. Dicit sanguinem hircorum & vitulorum fuisse asservatum, juxta Exod. XXIV. 6. Dicit aquam fuisse assumptam, sicut ali- as in sanguinis aspersionibus fieri solebat juxta Levit. XIV. 51. 52. & Num. XIX. 6. & 18. Dicit lanam coc- cineam & hyssopum pro aspergillo fuisse adhibitam, uti moris est ejusmodi aspersionibus. Dicit Apostolus αὐτὸ τὸ βιβλίον purificatum esse. Quod de libro legis accipiendum esse, nemo est, qui dubitat. Etsi vero non extat, sanguine conspersum quoque fuisse librum legis; quia tamen in constituendo veteri fœdere ad- erat, & cætera omnia sanguine conspergebantur, fa- cile intelligi potest, librum legis quoque conspersione illa non caruisse.

Cæterum ex illa aquæ & sanguinis mixtione per- peram concluditur mixtura aquæ cum vino in Eu- charistia, qua institutioni Christi contrariatur, re- ctius dicitur sanguinem & aquam significari, quæ de latere Christi promanavit Joh. XIX. quam signi- ficationem non improbat Estius qua sacramenta tum baptismi ob aquam, tum sacræ cœnæ ob sangui- nem. Theophylactus baptismum significari vult. Hunc enim & sanguis & aqua, inquit, conficiunt, & ex duobus his constat.

Adspersio autem & libri legis & populi significa- bat, nec legem impleri posse, nec populum à pec- catis expiari, quin opus sit aspersione sanguinis Christi, in quo unice habem9 & πλήρωμα τῦ νόμ8, & expiationem peccatorum.

Hyssopum, quæ est herba humilis, & vim habet purgandi pectoris, Thomas typice interpretatur de fide, quæ & men- tem Deo subjicit & corda purificat, Act. XV. 20. Lanam & coccineam, quæ rubei est coloris, inter- pretatur charitatem. Alii, notante Estio, per hysso- pum significari volunt humanam Christi naturam, in qua & humilitas ostensa est, & virtus latet ad pur- ganda cordis nostri vitia. Per lanam vero cocci- neam Christi carnem, quæ per se candida, velut la- na, sanguine passionis velut cocco rubricatur. Sed quum sanguine animalium mactatorum sanguis Christi intelligatur pro nobis mactati, hic vero ap- plicatio fiat, quæ per ministerium Verbi fieri debe- at aspersio, lana coccinea ministerium Verbi non in- commode significat, per quod aspergimur sangui- ne Christi: Nam Verbum, & Verbi ministerium candere debet justitia & innocentia Christi, & ru- bere ejus sanguine ceu ministerium reconciliatio- nem: Per hyssopum vero notatur efficacia Verbi, & ministerii Verbi, quod & si humile & contempti- bile videatur, δύναμις tamen Dei Evangelium sit ad purificandum corda per fidem, Joh. XV. 3. Act. XV. 24. De fide, medio ex parte nostri hic proprie dicendi locus non erat, de qua cap. seq. ejusque usus in populo desiderabatur aspergendo, non in mediis, per quæ fiebat aspersio.

Per tabernaculum Ecclesiam vel credentes in- telligit non male Theophylactus: Vel hoc quidem, in- quit, nostri præfert figuram, qui & tabernaculum sumus. Ait namque: Inambulabo in eis & inhabi- tabo. Et alibi: Vasa autem magna domus Dei quæ- dam aurea sunt, quædam argentea. Sumus itaque nos vero Christi sanguine respersi, & sanctificationem adepti, quandoquidem & in ejus fuerimus morte baptismo abluti. Colligitur autem ex hac tota actio- ne, quia cum populus diceret: Omnia, quæ Domi- nus loquutus est, faciemus, Moses adspergere debuit librum legis & populum sanguine, quasi indicaret, non vestra obedientia, qua legem implere impos- sibile est, promissam Testamento hæreditatem ob- tinebitis, sed unicè obedientia Messiæ, eademque usq; ad mortem cruentam, quæ hoc innocentium victimarum sanguine figuratur. Cæterũ uti in hac sanctione Veteris Testamenti verba Mosis τῦτο τὸ ἅιμα τῆς διαθήκης proprie intelligenda sunt de san- guine victimarum, quo aspergebatur populus; Ita non minus proprie intelliganda sunt verba Christi in sanctione Novi Testamenti, hoc est sanguis me- us sanguis ille Novi Testamenti, qui effusus est in remissionem peccatorum, Matth. XXVI. 28. Sicut sanguine hostiarum confirmabatur populo promissio de possessione terræ Canaan, & populus vicissim ad observationem mandatorum Dei adstringebatur

Ita sanguine Christi in sacra cœna obsignatur nobis promissio de remissione peccatorum & vita æterna: nos verò admonemur, ut obedientiam (gratitudinis ergo) exhibeamus Christo servatori nostro, ut hic Osiander.

## 9:21
Verse 21. And the tabernacle also, and all the vessels of the ministry he sprinkled likewise with blood;] We read that the tabernacle was anointed by Moses with the vessels pertaining to it, Leviticus 8:10. We rightly gather that the sprinkling of blood was accustomed to be placed before the anointing from the fact that it follows there concerning the altar, which was sprinkled first, then anointed. Thus also the priestly garments were sprinkled with blood, Leviticus 8:30, concerning which matter Josephus 3.9 says thus: Κᾶν τῷ ἅιματος τῶν τεθυμένων. τὴν δὲ στολὴν τᾶ Ἀαρωνθ· κἀι ἀυτοὶ σὺν τοῖς παισὶν ἐῤῥαινεν ἀφαγνίσας, πηγαίοις τε ὕδασι καὶ μύρῳ ἵνα τῷ Θεῷ γίγνοι- το [And with the blood of the sacrificed. And the robe of Aaron; and he himself with his sons sprinkled it, having purified it with spring waters and myrrh, so that it might be for God], where you see the sprinkling likewise precedes, the anointing follows. Σκεύη τῆς λειτουργίας [vessels of the ministry] כלי השרת, Numbers 4:12.

Therefore, it is no longer a question here of the sprinkling done in the very dedication of the Old Testament, Exodus 24, nor of the sprinkling commanded to Eleazar, Numbers 19, or enjoined upon the High Priest, Leviticus 16: But of the sprinkling of the tabernacle and its vessels, described in Exodus 40 and Leviticus 8, because in that dedication the tabernacle had not yet been built, and this discourse is about the sprinkling performed by Moses, not by the High Priest and Eleazar: And although that sprinkling could have been gathered from similar places and held by tradition from the elders, also observed by Josephus, there can nevertheless be no doubt that the Apostle had the same from the Θεοπνευσίᾳ [divine inspiration], from which this whole epistle proceeded, 2 Timothy 3:16.

Latin:

Vers. 21. Καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν δὲ, καὶ πάντα τὰ σκέυη τῆς λει- τουργίας τῷ ἅιματι ὁμόιως ἐῤῥάντισε;] Unctum fuisse à Mo- se tabernaculum cum vasis eo pertinentibus legimus Le- vit. VIII. 10. Adspersionem vero sanguinis præmitti soli- tam unctioni recte colligimus ex eo, quod ibidem sequi- tur de altari asperso primum, deinde uncto. Sic & vestes sacerdotales aspersæ fuere sanguine Levit. VIII. 30. qua de re sic Josephus III. 9. Κᾶν τῷ ἅιματος τῶν τεθυμένων. τὴν δὲ στολὴν τᾶ Ἀαρωνθ· κἀι ἀυτοὶ σὺν τοῖς παισὶν ἐῤῥαινεν ἀφαγνίσας, πηγαίοις τε ὕδασι καὶ μύρῳ ἵνα τῷ Θεῷ γίγνοι- το, ubi vides pariter præcedere adspersionem, unctionem sequi. Σκεύη τῆς λειτουργίας כלי השרת, Num. IV. 12.

Non ergo hic amplius agitur de aspersione facta in ipsa Veteris Testamenti dedicatione, Exod. XXIV. nec de aspersione Eleazaro, Num. XIX. præcepta, aut Levit. XVI. Pontifici injuncta: Sed de taber- naculi & vasorum ejus adspersione, Exod. XL. & Lev. VIII descripta, quia in dedicatione illa non- dum erat extructum tabernaculum, & de aspersi- one à Mose, non à Pontifice & Eleazaro peracta hic sermo est: Quanquam vero colligi ea aspersio ex similibus locis, & ex traditione à majoribus haberi potuerit, observata etiam Josepho, dubium ta- men esse non potest, quin è Θεοπνευσίᾳ eandem habuerit Apostolus, è qua profecta est tota hæc epistola, 2. Tim. III. 16.

## 9:22
Vers. 22. Καὶ σχεδὸν ἐν ἅιματι πάντα καθαρίζεται] He says σχεδὸν (almost) prudently, because some purifications were performed by water alone, Exod. XIX. 10. Levit. XVI. 28. Num. XXXI. 23.

Some Greeks note that that particle σχεδὸν can be referred to the verb καθαρίζεται, in this sense: almost, that is, imperfectly, to be purified according to the law; but that sense of Grotius, which the Latin interpreters have followed, is more elegant and suitable, since not all things were to be cleansed by blood, but some by water, and some also by fire, Num. XXXI. 23. The Apostle adds these things, however, so that it might not seem strange to the Hebrews, and provide a scandal, that he teaches we are cleansed from sins through Christ crucified, and his blood poured out on the altar of the cross, 1. Cor. I. vers. 23.

Καὶ χωρὶς αἱματεκχυσίας ὀυ γίνεται ἄφεσις] It is a Hebrew proverb. It is cited in the Jerusalem Talmud under the name of Ben Uzziel: לאכפרא אלא בדם. It seems that this began to be used first in more serious crimes, so that by the blood of the animal, he who offered it signified that he, if God wished to act rigidly, had deserved death. Macrobius, quoting Trebatius, says that an animal sacrifice is that in which the soul alone is consecrated to God: and its causes are explained by Virgil in that verse: Hanc tibi Eryx meliorem animam pro morte Daretis.

Wherever you find נסלח in the law, you will find the mention of blood precedes it. There was, however, an exception here too, namely the case of the poor, such that they could not procure for themselves turtledoves or pigeons, Levit. V. 11.

Thus it is read in the Talmud Joma c. Schibach lamini: There is no remission of sin without blood, because it is written in Levit. XVII. vers. 11. The blood itself shall satisfy for the soul. For even pigeons at least had to be killed, and their blood poured out, so that it might be signified that sins are not remitted except on account of the blood of Christ, 1. Joh. I. 7. If you say that certain legal purifications were also performed by water, I respond that this deals with the remission of sins, for which no ceremony was instituted that did not require the shedding of blood. For propitiatory sacrifices were offered for sins, all of which were bloody, nor were any sins to be excepted from expiation, since for all without exception on the day of ex- sacrifices for expiations have been offered, and others have been ordained for more serious matters, as we have taught elsewhere. Rightly, however, the unbloody sacrifice of the Mass is refuted from this, to which the Papists ascribe propitiation (Conc. Trid. Sess. VI. cap. II. can. 2.), since without the shedding of blood there is no remission of sin, where there is no instance of Estius concerning Baptism. For baptism is not an expiatory sacrifice, but a sacrament applying the expiation of Christ, in which, however, the blood of Christ is not lacking, but pertains to the heavenly matter of the same.

PART III. OF CHAPTER IX. The reason is given for those things which were said concerning the liturgy and mediation of the New Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 22. Καὶ σχεδὸν ἐν ἅιματι πάντα καθαρίζεται] σχε- δὸν prudenter dicit, quia nonnullæ purificationes per aquam solam fiebant, Exod. XIX. 10. Levit. XVI. 28. Num. XXXI. 23.

Notant quidam Græci particulam illam σχε- δὸν referri posse ad verbum καθαρίζεται, hoc sen- su ferè, id est, imperfecte, secundum legem purifica- ri; sed concinnior & convenientior est sensus ille Grotii, quem Lat. Interpretes sequuti sunt, quum non omnia sanguine, sed quædam aqua, quædã eti- am igne mundanda fuerint, Num. XXXI. 23. Sub- jungit autem hæc ideo Apostolus, ne Ebræis mi- rum videatur, ac scandalum præbeat, quod per Christum crucifixum, & sanguinem ejus in ara crucis effusum nos à peccatis mundari doceat, 1. Cor. I. vers. 23.

Καὶ χωρὶς αἱματεκχυσίας ὀυ γίνεται ἄφεσις] Est Pro- verbium Ebraicum. Citatur in Thalmud Hierosolymi- tano sub nomine Benuzielis לאכפרא אלא בדם videtur id primum usurpari cœpisse in criminibus gravi- oribus, ut per pecudis sanguinem significaret is, qui eum offerebat, se, si rigide Deus agere vellet, mortem meruis- se. Macrobius ex Trebatio animalem hostiam esse dicit, in quo anima sola Deo sacretur: ejusque causas explicari à Virgilio illo versu: Hanc tibi Eryx meliorem animam pro morte Daretis.

Ubicunque est נסלח in lege reperies præcedere san- guinis mentionem. Erat tamen & hic quædam exceptio, nempe ita pauperum, ut nec turtures nec columbas sibi com- parare possent Levit. V. 11.

Ita legitur in Thalmud Joma c.Schibach lamini: Non est peccati remissio sine sanguine, quia scriptum est Levit. XVII. vers. 11. Sanguis ipse pro ani- ma satisfaciet. Nam vel columbas saltem occidi, eorumque sanguinem fundi oportebat, ut significa- retur, non remitti peccata, nisi propter sangui- nem Christi, 1. Joh. I. 7. Si dicas quasdam le- gales mundationes etiam per aquam factas esses Resp. hic agi de remissione peccatorum, ad quam nulla instituta erat ceremonia, quæ sanguinis effu- sionem non exigeret. Nam pro peccatis offere- bantur sacrificia propitiatoria, quæ omnia cruen- ta erant, nec ab expiatione peccata ulla excipien- da, quum pro omnibus sine exceptione in die ex- piationum oblata sint sacrificia, & alias pro gravio- ribus illa ordinata fuerint, ut alibi docuimus. Re- cte autem hinc refellitur incruentum missæ sacrifi- cium, cui Papistæ propitiationem adscribunt Conc. Trid. Sess. VI. cap. II. can. 2. quum sine sanguinis effusione non fiat peccati remissio, ubi nulla est Estii de Baptismo instantia. Nam baptismus non est sacrificium expiatorium, sed sacramentum ex- piationis Christi applicatorium, in quo tamen non deficit sanguis Christi, sed ad materiam ejusdem cœlestem pertinet.

PARS III. CAPITIS IX. Quæ eorum, quæ de λειτουργίᾳ & μεσιτείᾳ Novi Testamenti dicta, ratio traditur.

## 9:23
Verse 23. Ἀνάγκη ὖν τὰ μὲν ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὀυρα- νοῖς τέτοις καθαρίζεσθαι] We spoke above about the word ὑποδείγματος at VIII. 5. This refers to the tent and the exterior [part] which was a figure of the starry heaven, and especially to the interior [part] which was a figure of the highest or super-ethereal heaven, which itself also was sprinkled with the blood of the victim at the first dedication, before the High Priest solemnly entered into it.

Αὐτὰ δὲ τὰ ἐπεράνια] Those super-ethereal places. See 1 Cor. XV. 40, 48, 49; Eph. I. 3, 20; II. 6; III. 10; VI. 11; 2 Tim. IV. 18; above III. 1; VI. 4; VIII. 5.

Κρείττοσι θυσίαις παρὰ ταύτας] It is asked why he said θυσίαις in the plural, and then why he says καθαρίζεσθαι concerning that region in which there is nothing impure. He said θυσίαις because he understands not only the sufferings of Christ, but also those of them who follow him, together with prayers and works of mercy. That καθαρίζεσθαι, however, is a metonymy, such as it is necessary to use often when things partly similar and partly dissimilar are compared with one another. For because access was given into the sanctuary through the legal καθαρισμὸν, therefore, taking the effect for the cause, he said the highest heaven is to be cleansed for that which is applied through these things to be given into that heaven. And note here again κρείττω with παρὰ added, when it would have been sufficient to say κρείττοσι τέτων.

It is now explained what the Apostle had said concerning the liturgy and mediation of the New Testament: as regards the former, first that there was a need for a better sacrifice in the same, then that the entry into heaven had to be made to appear there before the face of God, not that Christ had to enter often, for thus he would have had to suffer and die often, which was done once: as regards the latter, that he is to appear at his second coming to complete the same without sin for the salvation of those who await him through faith: since it is the [office] of the Mediator of the New Testament to introduce those who are called κατὰ πρόθεσιν to the eternal inheritance, as is evident from the collation of verses 16 and 28. That [point] concerning the better sacrifice is deduced through the particle ὖν from the preceding: Therefore, says the Apostle, it was necessary indeed, according to the hypothesis of Divine ordination and command, for the copies of heavenly things to be cleansed by these ceremonial [rites], as being the blood of brute animals, but for the heavenly things themselves to be cleansed by better sacrifices than these, namely the peace-offering of obedience and the expiatory [sacrifice] of the passion and death of Christ; thus there is no need for an enallage of number, so that sacrifices are said to be put for sacrifice, because he compares him with the various victims of the Old Testament, which Estius posits: In that which the Apostle says 'better sacrifices,' when he speaks of the one sacrifice of Christ, there is an enallage of number, to which the preceding plural number invited. Through θυσίας, with Grotius, one should understand both the passions of Christ and of those who follow him, together with prayers and works of mercy, ὰ θεόλογον. For it is repugnant to the Scriptures that our hearts are expiated or purified by the passions of the saints and works of mercy, which ascribes that solely to the blood of Christ, 1 John I. 7; Heb. IX. 15. Nor should it be said with Barthol. Petrus that both the bloody sacrifice once offered and the unbloody [sacrifice] of the daily offering are indicated. For the unbloody propitiatory sacrifice is a σιδηρόξυλον. And the Apostle acknowledges no other than a single offering, and that a bloody one, Heb. VII. verses 26, 27; chap. IX. 28; chap. X. 10, 12, 14. And Estius says that the Apostle was silent about the sacrifice of the Mass, and he offers the cause of that matter at chap. VII. 8, 10.

However, the ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὀυρανοῖς are not called the exterior and interior tent with respect to the starry and super-ethereal heaven, because we deny that the starry heaven was figured here, and we acknowledge no super-ethereal one, and it is clear that cleansing does not befit either, but [they are] the exterior tabernacle with the vessels and instruments, concerning the purification of which it had been treated. But the Apostle commemorates nothing concerning the cleansing of the inner sanctuary. That tabernacle, however, with the furniture of the Levitical Divine worship, were types of heavenly things, that is, of the mystical tabernacle of the Church, and of the spiritual worship in the same, which are afterwards called τὰ ἐπουράνια. Thus the Greeks Chrysostom, Theophylact, Oecumenius, and among the Latins Primasius, Anselm, Haymo understand the militant Church and what is done in it, which there is no doubt were figured by those Levitical things, namely by the tabernacle and the instruments or furniture of the worship which was performed in it. The patterns of heavenly things, says Theophylact, he calls our Church. For mention was made above of how heaven represents the Church. Therefore, the Jewish rites had presented both the arguments and the figures of these. But the heavenly things themselves, that is, those which belong to the Church itself, are ours. It must be seen, however, how τὰ ἐπουράνια and κλῆσις ἐπουράνιος are accepted, Eph. VI. 12, Heb. III. 1. To note that the cleansing is an access into heaven is an unheard-of distortion. That word signifies cleansing not only by the force of its proper notion, but also by the force of the preceding verses 13, 14, 22; nor does that metonymical acceptance concerning access into the sanctuary or heaven occur anywhere. There is also a harsh catachresis in the gloss of Thomas, as if heavenly things are said to be cleansed insofar as men are cleansed from sins, by which they are hindered from the entrance of the heavenly kingdom. Therefore Estius himself rejects the explanation of Thomas along with Ribera, because it sounds too harsh that heaven is cleansed.

Schlichting and Crellius indeed attempt to soften these glosses, which Grotius made his own, as being too harsh, asserting that that heavenly sanctuary was cleansed by the sacrificial offering of Christ, first insofar as it was consecrated through it so that access to it might be opened to us, and be dedicated to our uses henceforth, so that in this sense, by a certain inverted, yet not unusual, manner of speaking, heaven is said to be cleansed, for the perfect cleansing of us, so that we might enjoy the right of heaven. Secondly, insofar as it seems to be polluted by the access of sinful men, who are called through the Evangelical doctrine to lay hold of the possession of the kingdom of heaven, not otherwise than that ancient tabernacle was considered to be polluted by the sins and uncleannesses of the people (in whose midst it was situated). But those at least betray the artifice of distortion more and more. For because access to heaven is opened to us in the first place, therefore cleansing is not to be attributed to heaven itself, but rather we have need of cleansing. And therefore this sense is truly inverted; but those Socinians did not teach where such a manner of speaking is customary. Secondly, heaven cannot be polluted by the access of sinners, because no sinner, as such, is admitted into heaven, nor is heaven situated in the midst of sinners, as the tabernacle was in the midst of the Israelite people polluted by sins. The comparison concerning the kingdom of heaven suffering violence, and being taken by the violent, Matt. 11:12, is here entirely foreign. Concerning the sense of that phrase, see in its own place. Finally, not so that access to the inner sanctuary might be open to the priests was this to be expiated, but because the most holy God had his seat there.

Estius refutes Ribera's speculation—that heaven, polluted by the sin of our first parents and subsequently by the sins of other men, is cleansed by the blood of Christ, by which the stench of sins ascending into heaven is removed—as follows: But against this speculation, although subtle, it can first be objected that the Apostle, opposing Christ to the Aaronic High Priest and declaring his offices from the antithesis of those things which were done in the Old Testament, always attributes to Christ and his blood a true and properly so-called cleansing and sanctification, by which, namely, that thing which is said to be cleansed is made truly clean according to conscience and before God. But the cleansing already explained is not true, but figuratively spoken, since it is admitted that heaven, if we speak of cleansing properly and according to the Apostle, cannot be cleansed. Furthermore, the Apostle would seem to depart from his purpose if he were to make a transition from the cleansing of men, about which he is perpetually discoursing, to the cleansing of heaven, such as is imagined here. Finally, neither does that subtlety escape the harshness of the expression by which it is said that heaven is cleansed, on account of which the opinion of Blessed Thomas was displeasing. Although that which Ribera says is most correct, that the Apostle in the following passage does not allude to the dedication of the tabernacle, but to the entry of the High Priest into the sanctuary to be expiated from the sins of the children of Israel. Truly, that expiation of the tabernacle did not so much signify the cleansing of heaven polluted by the sins of men, as the cleansing of the Church defiled by the sins of men, of whom it consists. Add to these that the Apostle, by 'heavenly things,' does not wish to be understood so much that heavenly place as the Church of the saints who are in the heavens. For we have already said that for the word 'heavenly things' is held in Greek, 'of those things which are in the heavens.' But no one would say that the Church which is in the heavens is polluted by the sins of men acting on earth. These are the words of Estius, who also adds another explanation: But if it pleases one that by 'heavenly things' the whole Church be understood, which by the Apostle in Galatians IV is called 'Jerusalem which is above, our mother,' and in Revelation XXI is said to 'descend from heaven,' because indeed by meditation and study it is always occupied with heavenly things, even in the part where it journeys on earth: this sense of this passage could be very conveniently rendered: The heavenly things themselves, that is, the whole Church, embracing both the triumphant and the militant, is cleansed, that is, it receives all its cleanliness and holiness continuously from the better sacrifice, which is Christ offered on the cross. For Christ does not so cleanse the Church with his blood that it ceases to be cleansed at some time, if it is cleansed, it is to impart cleanliness and holiness, but he always does this and is about to do it. But the exposition is simpler concerning the Church in these lands, which is occupied with heavenly things and is called the kingdom of heaven. Wherefore, through the sacrifices of Christ, both his obedience and his sufferings, the Church is said to be cleansed, and whatever is done in it, so that they may be acceptable to God.

Latin:

Vers. 23. Ἀνάγκη ὖν τὰ μὲν ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὀυρα- νοῖς τέτοις καθαρίζεσθαι] De voce ὑποδείγματος diximus supra VIII. 5. Refertur hoc ad tentorium & exterius quod cœli altriferi erat figura, & maxime ad interius quod figura erat cœli summi sive superætherei, quod & ipsum in prima dedicatione aspersum fuit sanguine vi- ctimali, priusquam eo solenniter intraret summus Sa- cerdos.

Αὐτὰ δὲ τὰ ἐπεράνια] Loca illa superætherea. Vide 1. Cor. XV. 40. 48. 49. Eph. I. 3. 20. II. 6. III. 10. VI. 11. 2. Tim. IV. 18. supra III. 1. VI. 4. VIII. 5.

Κρείττοσι θυσίαις παρὰ ταύτας] Quæritur cur θυ- σίαις dixerit in plurali, deinde cur καθαρίζεσθαι dicat de illa regione in qua nihil est impuri. Θυσίαις di- xit quia non tantum Christi perpessiones intelligit, sed & eorum, qui ipsum sectantur, una cum precibus & misericordiæ operibus. Illud autem καθαρίζεσθαι est Me- tonymia, qualem sæpe usurpari necesse est, ubi inter se comparantur res partim similes, partim dissimiles. Nam quia per legalem καθαρισμὸν aditus dabatur in sanctuari- um, ideo, effectum sumendo pro causa, καθαρίζεσθαι dixit cœlum summum pro eo, quod est adhibitum per ista in illud cœlum dari. Et nota hic iterum κρείττω addito παρὰ, cum satis fuisset dicere κρείττοσι τέτων.

Exponitur jam, quod de λειτουργίᾳ & μεσιτείᾳ Novi Testamenti dixerat Apostolus, quoad illam quidem, primo quod opus fuerit meliori hostia in eodem, tum quod ingressus in cœlum fieri debue- rit ad apparendum illic coram vultu Dei, non quod sæpe ingrediendum Christo fuerit, ita enim sæpe ipsi patiendum & moriendum fuisset, quod semel factum est: quoad hanc vero, quod ad ean- dem consumandam sine peccato appariturus in se- cundo adventu sit ad salutem eorum, qui ipsum per fidem expectant: Siquidem Mediatoris Novi Testam. ad hæreditatem æternam eos, qui vocati sunt κατὰ πρόθεσιν, introducere, ut è vers. 16. & 28. collatione constat. Illud autem de meliori hostia deducitur per particulam ὖν è superioribus: Igitur, inquit Apostolus, necesseum quidem fuit ex hypo- thesi Divinæ ordinationis & mandati, exemplaria cœlestium hisce ceremonialibus, utpote sanguine brutorum mundari, ipsa autem cœlestia meliori- bus hostiis, quam istis, nimirum victima pacifica obedientiæ, & expiatoria passionis & mortis Christi; Sic opus nõ est enallage numeri, ut hostiæ dicantur positæ pro hostia, eo quod eum cum variis Veteris Testamenti victimis comparet, quam Estius statu- it: In eo quod dicit Apostolus melioribus hostiis, cum de una Christi hostia loquatur, enallage numeri est, ad quam invitavit numerus pluralis præcedens. Per θυσίας cum Grotio intelligere & Christi, & eorum, qui sectantur ipsum, passiones, una cum precibus & operibus misericordiæ, ὰ θεόλογον. Passionibus enim sanctorum & operibus misericordiæ expiari vel purificari corda nostra, scripturæ repugnat, quæ unice id adscribit sanguini Christi, 1. Joh. I. 7. Ebr. IX. 15. Neq; cum Barthol. Petro dicendum & hostia cruentam semel oblatam, & incruentam quo- tidianæ oblationis indicari. Nam incruenta ho- ftia propitiatoria est σιδηρόξυλον. Et Apostolus non nisi unicam oblationem, eamque cruentam agnoscit, Ebr. VII. vers. 26. 27. cap. IX. 28. cap. X. 10. 12. 14. Et de sacrificio Missæ tacuisse Apo- stolum ait Estius, causamque ejus rei profert ad cap. VII. 8. 10.

Dicuntur autem ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς ὀυρα- νοῖς non tentorium exterius & interius respectu cœli astrifera & superætherei, quia cœlum astriferum hic figuratum fuisse negamus, superæthereum vero nullum agnoscimus, neutri etiam mundationem convenire in aprico est, sed tabernaculum exteri- us cum vasis & instrumentis, de quorum purifica- tione actum erat. De adyti vero mundatione ni- hil commemorat Apostolus. Illud vero taberna- culum cum supellectile cultus Divini Levitici typi fuere rerum cœlestium, hoc est, mystici tabernacu- li Ecclesiæ, & cultus in eadem spiritualis, quæ post- ea τὰ ἐπουράνια dicuntur. Ita Græci Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, Oecumenius, & è Latinis Primasius, Anshelmus, Haymo intelligunt Ecclesiam militan- tem & quæ in ea geruntur, quæ figurata illis Levi- ticis fuisse dubium nullum est, tabernaculo nempe & instrumentis vel supellectile cultus, qui in eo peragebatur. Cœlestium exemplaria, inquit Theo- phylactus, nostram Ecclesiam dicit. Habita est enim su- perius mentio, quemadmodum cœlum Ecclesiam præferat. Horum itaque & argumenta prætule- rant & figuras Judaici ritus. Ipsa autem cœlestia, id est, quo ipsius Ecclesiæ sunt, nostra. Videndum autem ita τὰ ἐπουράνια & κλῆσις ἐπουράνιος accipi- antur, Eph. VI. 12. Ebr. II. 1. Τὸ καθαρίζεσθαι no- tare aditum in cœlum στρεβλότης est inaudita. Mun- dationem significat illud verbum non tantum vi notionis propriæ, sed etiam vi antecedentium v. 13. 14. 22. neque uspiam ea Metonymica acceptio de aditu in sanctuarium vel cœlum occurrit. Dura etiam Catachresis est in Thomæ glossa, quasi mun dari dicantur cœlestia, quatenus homines mundan- tur à peccatis, quibus ab ingressu regni cœlestis im- pediuntur. Ideo reprobat Estius ipse Thomæ expli- cationem cum Ribera, quod durius sonet cœlum mundari.

Conatur quidem has glossas, quas Grotius suas fecit, Schlichtingius & Crellius, utpote duriores emollire, sanctuarium illud cœleste victimale obla- tione Christi emundatum asseri, primo quatenus per eam ita consecratum fuit, ut nobis ad illud accessus pateat, nostrisque usibus imposterum dicatum sit, ad- eo ut hoc sensu inversa quadam, nec tamen inusita- ta dicendi ratione cœlum emundari dicatur, pro nostri perfecta, ut cœli jure gaudere possemus, emun- datione. Deinde quatenus hominum peccatorum accessu, qui per Evangelicam doctrinam ad capes- sendam regni cœlorum possessionem vocantur, pollui videtur, non secus atque tabernaculum illud an- tiquum peccatis & immunditiis populi (in cujus medio situm erat) pollui censebatur. Sed illa sal- tim artificium στρεβλότητος magis magisque pro- dunt. Quod enim primo nobis accessus pateat ad cœlum, ideo non cœlo ipsi καθαρισμὸς tribu- endus, sed nos potius καθαρισμῷ opus habemus. Ideoque hic sensus vere inversus est ubi autem usi- tata sit talis dicendi ratio, nõ docuere illi Sociniani. Deinde accessu peccatorum pollui non potest cœ- lum, quia peccator nullus, qua talis, in cœlum ad- mittitur, nec in medio peccatorum situm est cœlũ, uti tabernaculum erat in medio populi Israëlitici peccatis polluti. Collatio de regno cœlorũ vim passo, & à violentis rapto Mat. 11, 12. hic prorsus alie- na est. De cuj9 phras. sensu suo loco videas. Deniq; non ut Sacerdotibus aditus pateret in adytum, hoc expiandum erat, sed quia Deus sanctissimus ibi sedem habebat.

Ribera speculationem, quod cœlum peccato primorum Parentum, ac deinceps aliorum homi- num peccatis pollutum Christi sanguine, quo pec- catorum fœtor in cœlum adscendens, tollitur, emundari, sic refutat Estius: Sed contra hanc speculationem etsi subtilem primum objici potest, quod Apostolus Christum opponens Pontifici Aaro- nico, illiusque officia declarans ex antithesi eorum, quæ fiebant in Veteri Testamento, semper Christo ac sanguini ejus veram ac proprie dictam mundatio- nem & sanctificationem tribuit, qua scilicet vere secundum conscientiam & coram Deo munda fiat ea res, quæ mundari dicitur. Atqui mundatio jam exposita non vera, sed figurate dicta est, cum sit in confesso, cœlum, si de mundatione proprie & secun- dum Apostolum loquamur, mundari non posse. De- inde videretur Apostolus ab instituto declinare, si a mundatione hominum, de qua perpetuo disse- ruit, transitum faceret ad mundationem cœli, qua- lis hic fingitur. Denique nec ista subtilitas evadit duritiem sermonis, qua dicitur cœlum mundari, propter quam displicebat sententia B. Thomæ. Quanquam illud rectissime, quod dicit Ribera, Apostolum in pericope sequenti non alludere ad dedicationem tabernaculi, sed ad introitum Ponti- ficis in sanctuarium a peccatis filiorum Israël ex- piandum. Verum illa tabernaculi expiatio non tam significabat mundationem cœli peccatis homi- num polluti, quam mundationem Ecclesiæ peccatis hominum, ex quibus constat, commaculatæ. His ad- de, quod Apostolus per cælestia non tam intelligi vult locum illum cælestem, quam Ecclesiam sancto- rum, qui sunt in cælis. Jam enim diximus pro vo- cabulo cælestium haberi Græce, eorum, quæ sunt in cælis. Nemo autem dixerit Ecclesiam, quæ in cælis est, pollui peccatis hominum agentium in terris. Hæc Estius, qui aliam etiam addit explicationem: Quod si per cælestia placeat totam Ecclesiam intelligi, quæ ab Apostolo, Gal. IV. vocatur Jerusalem, quæ sursum est, mater nostra, & Apoc. XXI. dicitur descende- re de cælo, quia nimirum meditatione & studio sem- per in cælis versatur, etiam qua parte peregrina- tur in terris: Percommode reddi poterat hujus lo- ci iste sensus: Ipsa cælestia, id est, tota Ecclesia, tam triumphantem quam militantem complectens, mun- datur, id est, munditiam ac sanctitatem suam omnem accipit continuo ab hostia meliori, qua est Christus in cruce oblatus. Non enim ita Christus Ecclesiam suo mundare sanguine, ut mundare aliquando desinat, si mundat est munditiam & sanctitatem impertiri, sed semper id facit ac facturus est. Sed simplicior est expositio de Ecclesia in his terris, quæ in cœlis versa- tur, & regnum cælorum appellatur. Quapropter per hostias Christi cum obedientia tum passionum ejus mundari dicitur Ecclesia, & quicquid in ea ge- ritur, ut accepta Deo sint.

## 9:24
Vers. 24. For Christ did not enter into holy places made by hands, antitypes of the true ones] Understand 'made by hands' as those which were made by the art of men, and therefore not by Divine power. See above IX, 11. 24. 'Antitypos' is a word of double meaning, for it is said of a figure, as here; and of the thing signified through a figure, as 1 Peter III. 21. In the Glossary, 'antitypon' is an example, a copy. The same sense is in Wisdom IX. 8. 'You said to build a temple on your holy mountain and an altar in the city of your dwelling, a copy of your holy tent, which you prepared from the beginning.' Philo on the life of Moses: 'The inner sanctuaries of the tent, which are symbolically intelligible.' So also Rabbi Israel says of the soul that the lower sanctuary was made to the likeness of the higher one. Therefore here 'antitypa' is the same as 'mimemata' to the Hebrew Sage, 'typoi' in Romans V. 14, 1 Corinthians X. 11. And 'alethina' here as above VIII. 2, which are 'noeta' to Philo.

But into heaven itself] Namely, the heaven, that is, the highest heaven. Thus he has said 'holy places' several times, and will say it for 'holy of holies.' For that is sufficiently understood from the nature of the thing.

Now to appear before the face of God for us] That is, 'in order to appear,' such a brevity of speech we also had above. 'Emphanisthenai' is to appear, to give oneself to be seen, as Matthew XXVII. 53. 'Phanerosthai' below 26. The Syrian here 'denithaze' as to make himself to be seen. He persists in the likeness. For the High Priest also is said to appear before God, where he stands before the ark. Thus Christ appears before the throne of Majesty, so that he may commend our affairs to God, above VII. 25.

On the word antitypos, Blessed Dorotheus: That the tabernacle made by hands is called 'antitypon' is said not in respect to the type, but to the 'prototypon' or 'archetypon.' For 'antitypa' are the same as 'hypodeigmata' in verse 23. But 'hypodeigma' and 'skia' (shadow) are joined in Hebrews V. Therefore 'antitypa' in this place are images expressed from the prototype. Therefore, it is not as if they were 'anti tou typou' (against the type), from the opposite of the type or image, just as the thing itself is opposed to its image, in the way we are accustomed to oppose type and antitype, but as if they were 'typoi anti tou pragmatos' (types against the thing), types or images placed opposite the thing itself. Wherefore it is the same as if 'hand-made holy places' had been called types simply, just as in 1 Corinthians X. 6 and 11 the things of the Old Testament are called types: Thus also in 1 Timothy II. 6, 'antilutron' is put for 'lutron' (ransom).

Furthermore, the Apostle teaches that there was need of a better sacrifice and sacrificial blood for Christ, the High Priest of the New Testament; because he ought not to have entered into the holy of holies made by hands, into which the High Priests of the Old Testament entered with the blood of animals; but into heaven itself, so that he might now appear before the face of God for us. But not for that reason, that he should offer himself as a sacrifice more often, by which the entry with his own blood would be repeated more often: but as the High Priest enters into the holy of holies every year with the blood of another; otherwise it would have been necessary for him to suffer more often and undergo death from the foundation of the world, by which he could expiate the sins of men from the creation of the world, who had no less need of their expiation than those who lived in the time of the Old Testament, or under the New Testament, and having expiated them with his blood and death, to enter into heaven with his own blood.

From which it is most clearly evident that προσφέ- ρειν v. 25. is not ἐμφανίζειν, to show himself in the sanctuary of heaven, as Grotius, following the Socinians, perverts it, because the Apostle accurately distinguishes these in v. 24. 25., to appear before the face of God for us, and to offer himself. Therefore these are not to be confused with one another. And he interchanges the oblation and the passion, verses 25. 26., as also death v. 27. and the oblation verse 28., where those Socinians, Crellius and Schlichtingius, [comment] thus on verse 26. He thinks Christ ought not to offer himself often. For otherwise it would have been necessary for him to suffer often, since the oblation of a living thing cannot be made without slaughter and suffering. Grotius also confuses τὸ ἐμφανισθῆναι verse 24. [with] Φανερῶσθαι, verse 26. For there it is a matter of the appearance of Christ in the heavens before the face of God, or intercession for us: here, however, it is a matter of the appearance on earth for the oblation, so that he might become a victim for us εἰς ἀθέτησιν ἁμαρτίας.
