For those ancestors also held to the resurrection, and their blessings of this kind were spiritual, because indeed spiritual things were figured to them by those corporal things, nor were these believed to be about to happen otherwise than in the Messiah and on account of the Messiah, for whose sake the most holy Patriarchs had in their promises, and embraced by faith, the kingdom, the priesthood, and even the land of Canaan itself, his birthplace and seat, in which he was to execute his office and carry out the redemption of the human race.

Latin:

Vers. 20. Πίστει περὶ μελλόντων εὐλόγησεν Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακὼβ καὶ τὸν Ἡσαῦ) Crediderat Deo res magnas posteris suis eventuras, Gen. XXVI. 24. Sed solenniter quasi testamentum conditurus Deo dirigente eas ita partitus est, ut Jacobo potiores assigna- ret, nempe de terra illa Abrahamo promissa. Ideoque Jacob hic quanquam natu minor præponitur: quomodo & Abra- ham Nachoro, Gen. XI. 26. In hac quoque re figura latet po- puli Judaici & Christiani, quam evolvit Paulus Rom. IX.

De Patriarchacum triga generatim antea egerat Apostolus: tum etiam speciatim de Abrahamo: Jam de Isaaco id è Gen. 27, 29. 30. observat, quod per fidem in Messiam, in quo omnis benedictio con- tingit, de futuris benedixerit Isaac filiis suis Jacobo & Esavo. Non enim benedictio ulla cum effectu fieri potest, nisi in Christo & per Christum, quem fide in- tuitum esse Isaacum in hac benedictione tribuenda testatur Apostolus. Nam promissa erat benedictio Messia ceu seminis illius benedicti in Isaaci poste- ritate, Gen. 21, 12. cap. 22, 18. & imprimis v. 26. 4. quam promissionem fide amplexus Isaacus semper in corde habuit, nec nisi per fidem in semen illud be- nedictum hanc filiorum benedictionem instituit. Theophylactus in verbis περὶ μελλόντων ponderat non modo certitudinem fidei de terra promissa: Quo pacto enim, inquit, qui in terra consedisset alie- na, tot bona filiis polliceretur optaretq;, nisi promissa daturum Deum fide indubitata sperasset? Sed etiam bona futura cœlestia, quorum illa figura erant. De futuris cum dicit, vel bona quæ in futurum non manent, demonstrat. Nam & resurrectionem tene- bant majores illi, & spiritualia erant eorum bene- dicta hujusmodi, quia nempe spiritualia illis cor- poralibus figurabantur, neq; hæc aliter, quam in Messia & propter Messiam credebantur obventu- ra, cujus causa regnum, sacerdotium, ipsam etiam terram Canaan ejusdem natalem locum & sedem, in qua munus suum exequi, & redemptionem generis humani peragere debebat, in promissis habebant, & fide complectebantur Patriarchæ sanctissimi.

## 11:21
Vers. 21. Πίστει Ἰακὼβ ἀποθνήσκων ἕκαστον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰωσὴφ εὐλόγησεν) 'Dying,' that is, about to die: the present for the immediate future, such locutions as we have brought forward at Matt. XXVI. 28. In this testament of Jacob also, with God directing, the younger was preferred to the older, to figure the same thing that we have said. And note that ἕκαστον is used even when the discourse is about only two. Jacob understood that the kingdom would arise in the line of Ephraim. Concerning the third Patriarch, Jacob, the Apostle teaches in the same way how he demonstrated his faith in the Messiah in the blessing of both sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, which shines forth most clearly from the words of the blessing, Gen. 48:16. For he explicitly names that Angel who redeemed (גאל) by right of kinship, himself from every evil, both spiritual and bodily, of both guilt and punishment, whom in the blessing he joins equally with God the Father, whence nothing is more certain than that the Son of God, our only Redeemer, is understood, in whom the Patriarch so testified his faith to the Father, that he acknowledged Him as his Redeemer, who as true God and true man, having interposed himself as a ransom (λύτρῳ), had redeemed or was about to redeem, in whose name every blessing is obtained, Is. 45:23 ff., Acts 4:12. Which he did while dying (ἀποθνήσκων), because he wished to die and depart in this faith, and he wished to commend it here, along with the blessing, as if in a Testament, not only to his sons, to whom he presents the Messiah under the name Shiloh (שילה) Gen. 49:10 and Salvation (ישועה) v. 18, but also to his grandsons, the Patriarch being full of faith and inspired by God (θεόπνευστος).

And he worshipped toward the top of his staff (Καὶ προσεκύνησε πρὸς τὸ ἄκρον τῆς ῥάβδου ἀυτῶ). Clearly our writer here follows the version of the LXX, Gen. 47:31. The Hebrew word which is read in this place in Genesis, and 48:2, מטה, can signify a staff just as well as a bed. For the vowel points, which vary the meaning, were not written in formerly: perhaps also the pronunciation was once the same in both meanings, as there are many words that are polysemous (πολύσημοι), but the distinction was discovered later by grammarians. He worshipped, however, namely God, which the Latin interpreter added in the said place, Gen. 47:31, and the same is to be supplied in 1 Kings 1:47. It seems, however, that Jacob, in order to have greater honor for God, had risen from his bed to pray (for he is said to have drawn his feet back into the bed later, Gen. 49:32) and sat upon it, leaning on his staff, which gesture has an excellent image of faith. For that upon which one leans is compared to a staff, 2 Kings 18:21, Is. 36:6, Ezek. 29:6. And therefore מטה is also translated as a support (στήριγμα), as in Ps. 105:16, Ezek. 4:16, 5:16, 7:11, 14:13.

That adoration at the top of Joseph's scepter, if it be said to have been done toward that, did not only refer to the sublimity of the Ephraimite scepter, but primarily, because faith having been placed in the Messiah, it looked toward the eminence of the kingdom of the Messiah, which Joseph clearly figured by his scepter and other things pertaining to the notable type of Christ. This Estius acknowledges along with others: He says, they explain the mystery best who say that Jacob in his son Joseph foresaw Christ signified, and in the rod of Joseph acknowledged the royal power of Christ. But what he adds, that he worshipped the very top or head of the rod, because the head of Christ is God, is a fault of the Latin Vulgate. For in the Greek it is not said that he worshipped the top of Joseph's rod, or τὸ ἄκρον ῥάβδου, but he is said to have worshipped upon the top (ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον), which, however, must be taken concerning civil veneration, if we follow the Vulgate, in which Joseph's dream about the bowing of the sun was fulfilled, Gen. 37:9. It is better, however, to understand it concerning religious adoration done at the top of the rod, or the worship of the Messiah, whom he acknowledged to be figured in the exalted Joseph: And because in the Hebrew it is said, and Israel bowed himself at the head of the bed, it is better to understand here the rod or staff of Jacob rather than of Joseph, so that the rough breathing (spiritus asper) is on 'his' (ἀυτῶ), which reading we said should be preferred with Augustine in the reconciliation of this place with the Mosaic one, Gen. 47:31, in his commentary on Genesis, where the Grotius suspicion of a changed reading is rash (concerning which the Critici Sacri should be consulted), since the infirmity of Jacob is noted in both, whether he is said to be leaning on a staff, or he bowed himself at the head of the bed, and the sum of the matter is that Jacob, certain about his remains being brought to the sepulcher of his ancestors, in the promised land, the fatherland of the Messiah, and about other divine promises, primarily about the blessed seed, venerated and worshipped God. Whether he did that bowed at the head of the bed, or at the top of his staff, it makes no difference to the signification of faith, which the Apostle intends to prove from this act. Nor indeed is there any reason why we should here take refuge with Grotius to Gen. 48 in his annotations on that place, who in this place acknowledges with us that Gen. 47:31 is being looked back upon. For although the Apostle speaks about the blessing given to the sons of Joseph (which is the argument of Blessed Luther in his commentary on Genesis), he does not, however, bring it forward alone as an argument for Jacob's faith, but he also joins that adoration of Israel, when he bowed his head over the top of his staff, as it was a certain document of Jacob's faith concerning the promises made to him, which he was certain would be fulfilled, and for that reason he desired to be buried in the land of Canaan, and was confirmed in it by the oath of Joseph, and likewise concerning the promise of the Messiah, whom he believed would come forth in that land, and finally concerning the blessed resurrection, which faith he testified by his desire to sleep with his fathers.

Latin:

Vers. 21. Πίστει Ἰακὼβ ἀποθνήσκων ἕκαστον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰωσὴφ εὐλό- γησεν) Ἀποθνήσκων, id est moriturus: præsens pro proxime futuro, quales loquutiones complures adduximus ad Matth. XXVI. 28. In hoc quoque Jacobi testamento, Deo dirigente, minor prælatus est majori, ad idem figurandum, quod dixi- mus. Et nota ἕκαστον dici etiam, ubi de duobus tantum sermo est. Intellexit Jacobus regnum in Ephraimi stirpe extiturum. De tertio Patriarcha Jacobo itidem docet Apo- stolus, quomodo fidem in Messiam demonstrarit in benedictione utriusque filii Josephi, Manassis & E- phraim, quæ è verbis benedictionis, Gen. XLIIX. 16. luculentissimè effulget. Nominat enim disertè Angelum illum, qui redemit גאל jure consanguini- tatis, ipsum ab omni malo spiritali, tum corporali, cum culpæ tum pœnæ, quem in benedictione ex æquo conjungit Deo Patri, unde nihil certius, quam quod intelligatur Filius Dei Redemptor noster uni- cus, in quem fidem suam ita testificatus est Patriar- cha, quod agnoverit eum proRedemptore suo, qui ceu verus Deus & verus homo sese λύτρῳ interposi- to, redemerit vel redempturus erat, in cujus nomi- ne obtineatur omnis benedictio, Es. XLV. 23. seqq. Act. IV. 12. Quod ἀποθνήσκων fecit, quia in hac fide mori ac decedere voluit, eamq; cum benedictione, velut in Testamento, non filiis tantum, quibus Messiam sistit sub nomine שילה Gen. XLIX. 10. & ישועה v. 18. sed & nepotibus hic loci commendare voluit Patriarcha fide plenus & θεόπνευστος.

Καὶ προσεκύνησε πρὸς τὸ ἄκρον τῆς ῥάβδου ἀυτῶ) Plane hic sequitur noster Scriptor versionem LXX. Gen. XLVII. 31. Vox Ebræa, quæ hoc loco in Genesi legitur, & XLVIII. 2. מטה tam baculum potest significare quam lectum. Nam puncta vocalia, quæ significationem variant, olim adscripta non fuere: forte etiam eadem olim fuit pro- nunciatio in significatu utroque, ut multæ sunt voces πολύσημοι, sed à Grammaticis postea reperta discrimina- tio. Adoravit autem, nempe Deum, quod Latinus Inter- pres addidit dicto loco, Gen. XLVII. 31. & idem supplen- dum 1. Reg. I. 47. Videtur autem Jacobus, quo majorem Deo honorem haberet, preces facturus ex lecto surrexisse (nam postea retulisse pedes suos in lectum dicitur, Gen. XLIX. 32.) & in eo consedisse, innixus fcipioni, qui gestus egregiam habet fidei imaginem. Nam cui quis innititur, id scipioni comparatur, 2. Reg. XVIII. 21. Es. XXXVI. 6. Ezech. XXIX. 6. Et ideo מטה etiam στήριγμα vertitur, ut Psal. CV. 16. Ezech. IV. 16. V. 16. VII. 11. XIV. 13.

Illa adoratio ad fastigium sceptri Josephi, si ad il- lud facta dicatur, non tantum sceptri Ephraimici sublimitatem referebat, sed imprimis, quia fide in Messiam facta, respiciebat eminentiam regni Messiæ, quam figurabat præclare Joseph sceptro suo, aliisq; ad typum insignem Christi pertinentibus. Quod agnoscit Estius cum aliis: Mysterium, inquit, optime explicant, qui dicunt Jacobum in Josepho filio suo Christum significatum prospexisse, & in virga Josephi Regiam Christi potestatem agnovisse. Sed quod ad- dit, ipsum virgæ fastigium seu caput adorasse, quia caput Christi Deus, è Latina Vulgata vitio est. In Græco enim non fastigium virgæ Josephi, vel τὸ ἄκρον ῥάβδου, sed ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον adorasse dicitur, quod tamen de civili veneratione accipiendum, si Vul- gatam sequamur, in qua impletum Josephi somni- um de inclinatione solis, Gen. XXXVII. 9. Præstat autem de religiosa adoratione ad fastigium virgæ facta, seu cultu Messiæ, quem in Josepho exaltato figurari agnoscebat: Et quia in Ebræo dicitur, & incurvabat se Israel ad caput lectuli, virgam vel baculum Jacobi potius quam Josephi, hic intelli- gere, ut spiritus asper ἀυτῶ sit, quam lectionem præferendam cum Augustino in conciliatione hujus loci cum Mosaico, Gen. XLVII. 31. in comment. ad Genesin diximus, ubi temeraria est suspicio mu- tatæ lectionis Grotiana, (quo de conferendus Criti- cus Sacer) quum infirmitas Jacobi notetur utro- que, sive innixus baculo dicatur, sive ad caput lectu- li se inclinavit & summa rei sit, Jacobum certum de exuviis suis sepulchro majorum, in terra promissa, Messia patria, inferendis, & de aliis divinis promissio- nibus, imprimis de semine benedicto Deum veneratum esse, & adorasse. Num id fecerit inclinatus ad caput lectuli, an ad fastigium scipionis, nihil interest ad fi- dei significationem, quam ex hoc actu probare in- tendit Apostolus. Nec vero est, quod cum Grotio hic nos recipiamus ad Gen. XLIIX. in annot. ad istum locum, qui hoc in loco nobiscum agnoscit re- spici Gen. XLVII. 31. Nam etsi Apostolus de bene- dictione filiis Josephi facta loquatur (quod argu- mentum est B. Lutheri in comm. ad Gen.) non ta- men eam solum in argumentum fidei Jacobææ ad- ducit, sed conjungit quoque adorationem illam Is- raëlis, cum inclinaret caput super fastigium baculi, utpote quæ documentum erat certum fidei Jacobi de promissionibus sibi factis, quas impletum iri certus erat, eoq; nomine in terra Canaan tumulari desiderabat, & Juramento Josephi de eo confir- mabatur, de promissione item Messiæ, quem in terra illa proditurum credebat, ac denique de beata resurrectione, quam fidem desiderio dor- miendi cum Patribus suis testabatur.

## 11:22
Verse 22. By faith Joseph when he was dying (Πίστει Ἰωσὴφ τελευτῶν). And here 'dying' (τελευτῶν) is to be taken as 'dying' (ἀποθνήσκων) just now. He made mention of the exodus of the children of Israel (Περὶ τῆς ἐξόδε τῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευσε). He was mindful that another land was promised to his descendants and those of his brothers, and therefore that they would someday go out of Egypt. And he gave commandment concerning his bones (Καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὑτῶ ἐνετείλατο). He gave commands concerning his bones being carried into the promised land, which was a sign that he did not doubt at all about the promised possession. The history is from Gen. 50:24, Josh. 24:32. See also Acts 7:16.

To that most famous trio of Patriarchs is now joined Joseph, who himself was also a Patriarch and Prophet, and he likewise celebrates the faith of the dying, in which he sweetly fell asleep, because the same τελευτῶν finishing his life, now near the end of life, Matth. II. 19. περὶ τῆς ἐξόδε ὑιῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευσεν, he recalled to the memory of his brothers the promise heard from his father Jacob concerning the exodus of the children of Israel from Egypt, which finally followed after 144 years, Gen. L. 25. καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὑτῶ ἐνετείλατο he gave a command concerning his bones, namely, that they be carried out of Egypt. Where a twofold document of faith in the Messiah is contained: inasmuch as he embraced by faith the leading out from Egypt into the promised land, in which the Messiah was to be born, and because he desired to be buried in the same with the faithful Fathers, in which the Messiah was also to be buried and resurrected, concerning whom Joseph was not poorly informed by the Patriarchs Isaac his grandfather and Jacob his father, as the Seed of the woman, the seed that would be the provider of every blessing, the Angel, the Lord, the Redeemer, Shiloh, and his passion and kingdom, Jesus, the salvation of the Lord, etc., who taught that true beatific wisdom also to others, even to the Princes of Egypt and the Elders themselves, Ps. CV. 22, which is the only solid wisdom, Jer. IX. 24, 1 Cor. I. 31. And Joseph saw without doubt, as a Prophet, in himself a notable type of Christ, which he bore both in the state of humiliation and of exaltation.

Latin:

Vers. 22. Πίστει Ἰωσὴφ τελευτῶν) Et hic τελευτῶν sumen- dum, ut modo ἀποθνήσκων. Περὶ τῆς ἐξόδε τῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευσε) Memor fuit aliam terram suis & fratrum posteris promissam, ac proinde eos aliquando ex Ægypto exituros. Καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὑτῶ ἐνετείλατο) Mandata dedit de ossibus suis in terram promissam deportandis, quod signum erat, eum de possessione promissa nihil dubitare. Historia ex Gen. L. 24. Jos. XXIV. 32. Vide & Act. VII. 16.

Trigæ illi celeberrimæ Patriarcharum jam jungitur Josephus, qui & ipse Patriarcha fuit ac Pro- pheta, ejusque itidem moribundi fidem, in qua suaviter obdormivit, celebrat, quod eadem τε- λευτῶν vitam finiens, vitæ fini jam proximus, Matth. II. 19. περὶ τῆς ἐξόδε ὑιῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευ- σεν, in memoriam fratribus suis revocavit promis- sionem à Patre Jacobo auditam de exitu filiorum Israel ex Ægypto, qui post 144. an. demum sequu- tus est, Gen. L. 25. καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὑτῶ ἐνετείλατο de ossibus suis ex Ægypto scilicet deportandis mandatum dederit. Ubi geminum continetur do- cumentum fidei in Messiam: utpote quod eductio- nem ex Ægypto in terram promissam, in qua prodi- turus erat Messias, fide complexus sit, quodq; in ea- dem tumulari cum Patribus fidelibus desiderarit, in qua etiam sepeliendus erat & resuscitandus Messi- as, de quo non proletarie informatus à Patriarchis Isaaco avo, & Jacobo Parente Josephus erat, ceu Semine mulieris, semine quod omnis benedictionis pa- rarium futurum, Angelo, Domino, Redemptore, Schi- lo, ejusque passione & regno, Jesu, salute Domini &c. qui veram illam sapientiam beatificam edocuit et- iam alios, ipsosmet quoq; Principes Ægypti & Se- niores Ps. CV. 22. quæ unice solida est sapientia, Jer. IX. 24. 1. Cor. I. 31. Et vidit sine dubio Josephus, ceu Propheta, in sese insignem Christi typum, quem & in exinanitionis & in exaltationis statu gessit.

## 11:23
Vers. 23. By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents) By the faith of the parents, whom he here calls πατέρας, using the masculine for the common, as Jurisconsults often do. The same expression is in Ps. XLV. 17. What the holy Scripture narrates about the mother of Moses in Exod. II, 21, Stephen teaches us must also be understood of the Father, Act. VII. 20, and the LXX themselves in Exodus: They covered him for three months. But when they could no longer hide him, etc. Therefore the Writer here rightly designates both parents. In Ezekiel the Jewish Tragedian, Moses speaks thus: There my mother who bore me hid me for three months. Because they saw the child was fair) An oracle having been previously received that one would arise from them who would be the author of liberty for the people, wherefore when the infant was born to them, in a wonderful manner beautiful טוב הוא ἀστεῖος, as the LXX there, ἀστεῖος τῷ Θεῷ, as Stephen, Act. VII. 19. good, as Aquila, beautiful as Symmachus, they did not doubt but that he was the very one to whom that oracle pertained: Much and pure childish grace, according to Josephus, who also has this: He believed that God would provide every security so that nothing of what was said would be false. Philo on the life of Moses: The child therefore, having been born, immediately showed a look more beautiful than that of a private person. And they did not fear the king's commandment) Great faith overcomes all fears. Understand the edict by which Jewish parents were ordered to produce their male infants so that they might be killed. For this also was included in the edict, which is briefly referred to in Exod. I. 22. Ezekiel the Tragedian: Then he proclaims to the race of the Hebrews

Casting the pleasing things into the deep-flowing river. Philo on the parents of Moses: 'so as even to disregard the proclamations of the Tyrant.'

From Joseph the Patriarch, the Apostle descends to the faithful parents of Moses, because Moses, recently born, was hidden by faith; which deed is joined to the preceding document concerning the departure of the Israelites from Egypt, and is attributed to faith by the Apostle. It is likely, since there is no faith without revelation or the word of God, that something had been revealed divinely to the pious parents of Moses concerning this son of theirs, whom the grace of God had endowed as an infant with singular beauty, which he did in confirmation of faith in the promised Messiah; whence they also did not fear the wrath of Pharaoh, because the Royal command was disregarded, and committing their little son to the waters, they were secure in the same faith concerning divine grace and preservation. Which, therefore, the Apostle deemed as documents of very remarkable faith not to be neglected here. To which pertains what Josephus, book II of the Jewish Antiquities, chapter V, cited here by Grotius, relates: that God stood by Amram, the father of Moses, in a dream and promised that a son would be born to him who in his own time would liberate the Hebrews from Egyptian servitude: that he himself told this very thing to his pregnant wife. Both applied faith to the oracle, and induced by that faith, after the woman had given birth so easily that she deceived the observers, they had nourished the little infant secretly with them for three months. B. Gerhard observes primarily the word ἀστεῖον, which is added here not without cause by Paul in celebrating the faith of the parents of Moses: From the beauty and elegance of the child, the parents understood by the impulse of the Holy Spirit that this son of theirs would be a peculiar instrument of God and the liberator of His people from Egypt, whence in Acts 7:20 it is added that he was ἀστεῖον τῷ Θεῷ, which the Syrian translates as 'pleasing to God,' as one who was about to work something singular through him. Although indeed mention is made only of the mother in this matter in Exodus 2:3, the father is not excluded, nor is there doubt that all things were done in such a great cause with the father's knowledge; and therefore the LXX attributed these things to both parents, whom the Apostle himself followed.

Latin:

Vers. 23. Πίστει Μωυσῆς γεννηθεὶς ἐκρύβη τρίμηνον ὑπὸ τῶν πατέρων αὑτῶ) Fide nempe parentum, quos hic πατέρας vo- cat, masculinum pro communi usurpans, ut sæpe Juriscon- sulti. Eadem loquutio Psal. XLV. 17. Quod sacra Scriptura de matre Mosis narrat Exod. II, 21. idem debere & de Patre intelligi docet nos Stephanus, Act. VII. 20. & ipsi LXX. in Exodo: Ἐσκέπασαν αὐτὸ μῆνας τρεῖς. Ἐπεὶ δὲ ἐκ ἐδύναντο αὐτὸ ἔτι κρύπτειν &c. Itaque recte hic Scriptor utrumque paren- tem designat. Apud Ezechielem Tragicum Judæum Moses sic loquitur: Ἐνταῦθα μήτηρ ἡ τεκῦσα ἔκρυπτέ με τρεῖς μῆνας. Διότι εἶδον ἀστεῖον τὸ παιδίον) Oraculo prius accepto ex ipsis oriturum, qui populo libertatis autor esset, quare cum infans ipsis natus esset mirum in modum pulcher טוב הוא ἀστεῖος, ut ibi LXX. ἀστεῖος τῷ Θεῷ, ut Stepha- nus Act. VII. 19. ἀγαθός, ut Aquila, καλὸς ut Symmachus, non dubitarunt, quin is ipse esset, ad quem id oraculum pertine- ret: Χάρις ἡ παιδικὴ πολλὴ κὶ ἄκρατος apud Josephum, qui & hoc habet: Τὸν δὲ Θεὸν ἡγεῖτο πᾶσαν ἐμπορίσειν ἀσφάλειαν ὑπὲρ τῶ μηδὲν ψεῦδος γενέσθαι τῶν εἰρημένων. Philo de vita Mosis: Γεννηθεὶς ὖν ὁ παῖς εὐθὺς ὄψιν ἐνέφηνεν ἀστειοτέραν ἢ κατ᾿ ἰδιώτην. Καὶ ἐκ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸ διάταγμα τῶ βασιλέως) Magna fides vincit metus omnes. Edictum intellige, quo jube- bantur parentes Judæi exhibere infantes mares, ut inter- ficerentur. Nam & hoc comprehensum fuit in edicto, quod breviter refertur Exod. I. 22. Ezechiel Tragicus: Ἔπειτα κηρύσσει μὲν Ἑβραίων γενᾷ

Τ᾿ ἀρεσικὰ ῥίπτον ποταμὸν εἰς βαθύῥῥοον. Philo de paren- tibus Mofis : ὧς καὶ τῶν τῦ Τυράννυ κηρυγμάτων ἀλογῆσαι.

A Jofepho Patriarcha ad parentes Mofis fideles descendit Apostolus, quod aliis Moses recens na- tus per fidem occultatus fuerit, quod factum jungi- tur præcedenti documento de exitu Israëlitarum ex Ægypto, & fidei tribuitur ab Apostolo, verisi- mile est, quum fides nulla sit sine revelatione vel verbo Dei revelatum fuisse piis Mosis parentibus divinitus aliquid de hoc filio suo, quem singulari pulchritudine divina gratia dotarat infantulum, quod in confirmationem fidei in Messiam pro- missum fecerit, unde etiam nec iram Pharaonis, ob mandatum Regium posthabitum, metuebant, & aquæ committentes filiolum, de divina gratia & conservatione securi erant eadem fide. Quæ proin- de perquam insignis fidei documenta hic minimè negligenda duxit Apostolus. Quo facit, quod Jose- phus l.II. Antiq.Judaic. cap. V. hic à Grotio laudatus perhibet, Deum Amramo Patri Mosis adstitisse per somnium ac promisisse nasciturum ei filium, qui suo tempore Ebræos ex Ægyptiaca servitute liberaret: Vivum id ipsum narrasse uxori gravidæ. Utrumque fidem oraculo adhibuisse, & ea fide inductos, post- quam mulier tam facile esset enixa, ut observatores falleret, infantulum per tres menses clam apud se nutrivisse. B. Gerhardus observat imprimis vocem ἀστεῖον quæ hic non sine causa additur à Paulo in fide parentum Mosis celebranda: Ex venustate & elegantia puelli speciati Spiritus sancti impulsu pa- rentes intelligebant, hunc filium suum fore peculiare Dei organum, & populi sui ex Ægypto liberatorem, unde Act. VII. 20. additur, quod fuerit ἀστεῖον τῷ Θεῷ, quod Syrus vertit gratus Deo, utpote qui singu- lare quippiam per eum sit operaturus. Quanquam ve- ro matris tantum mentio fiat in hac causa Exod. II. 3. non excluditur tamen Pater, neque dubium Pa- tre conscio omnia acta in tanta causa; ideoque LXX. ad utrumque parentem ea retulere, quos A- postolus ipse sequutus est.

## 11:24
Verse 24. By faith Moses, when he had become great, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter) He spurned the honor he had of being called the adopted son of Thermutis, the daughter of so great a King, Exodus 2:9, Acts 7:21. Ezechiel the Tragedian: 'As long as we had the time of the boy, he promised all things by royal pretexts and teachings, as if from his own bowels.' In Josephus, Thermuthis says: 'I deemed it a willing thing to make him a child, and the successor of your kingdom.' You have the same in Midrash Bereshith. Moreover, the infant Moses gave a presage of this generous spirit when he threw to the ground the diadem placed upon him by the King in jest, which Josephus narrates in Antiquities II.5. ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι, he refused to be called. For the Greeks also use ἀρνεῖσθαι for 'to repel,' as has been noted by the learned. Μέγας γενόμενος, ויגדל, Exodus 2:11, where the LXX says 'Moses having become great,' that is, when he had already reached the proper age of 40 years. Acts 7:23, just as Midrash Bereshith and other Hebrews [say]. Great is the faith that spurns principalities and joins itself to the despised.

Latin:

Vers. 24. Πίσει Μωϋσῆς μέγας γενόμενος ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι υἱὸς θυγατρὸς Φαραώ) Sprevit honorem quem habebat dici filium adoptivum Thermutidis filiæ tanti Regis, Exod. II. 9. Act. VII. 21. Ezechiel Tragicus: Ἕως μὲν ἗ν τὸν παιδὸς εἴχομεν χρόνον Προφᾶσι βασιλικαῖσι καὶ παιδεύμασιν Ἅπανθ᾽ ὑπισχνῆθ᾽, ὡς ἀπὸ σπλάγχνων ἑῶν. Apud Josephum Thermuthis dicit: Ἐκούσης μὲν ἠγησάμην παῖδα ποιήσασθαι, τῆς δὲ σῆς βασιλείας διάδοχον. Idem habes in Midrasch Berefchith. Hujus autem animi generosi præsa- gium dedit Moses infans, cum diadema sibi per jocum à Re- ge impositum abjecit in terram, quod narrat Josephus Antiq. II. 5. ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι recusavit dici. Nam & ἀρνεῖσθαι pro repellere usurpant Græci, ut notatum eruditis. Μέγας γενό- μενος, ויגדל, Exod. II. 11. ubi LXX. μέγας γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς, id est cum jam ad justam ætatem pervenisset anno- rum XL. Act. VII. 23. quomodo & Midrasch Berefchith & Ebræi alii. Magna fides, quæ principatus spernit & con- temptis se aggregat.

## 11:25
Verse 25. Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to have the temporary enjoyment of sin) for he could not retain that fortune, being now of an age capable of honors, unless he also supported those cruel edicts, which was a sin grave in itself, and much graver in one who knew the promises made to that people. Everything that is temporal is brief; that which passes to posterity is lasting. Κακυχεῖσθαι is a good Greek word, which this writer will also use below in verse 37 and chapter 13:7. Thucydides and others use it. You see the Gospel prefigured even then, with faith demonstrated through the endurance of the cross.

Latin:

Vers. 25. Μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος συγκακουχεῖσθαι τῷ λαῷ τῦ Θεῦ ἢ πρόσκαιρον ἔχειν ἁμαρτίας ἀπόλαυσιν) neque enim poterat fortunam illam retinere ætate jam honorum capace, nisi & edicta illa crudelia tueretur, quod erat peccatum per se grave, & multo gravius in eo, qui nosset promissa isti popu- lo facta. Breve est omne, quod temporale est, diuturnum quod ad posteros transit. Κακυχεῖσθαι vox bene Græca, quam & infra usurpabit hic Scriptor v. 37. & cap. XIII. 7. Utitur Thucydides & alii. Vides jam tum præfiguratum Evangelium, fide per crucis tolerantiam demonstrata.

## 11:26
Verse 26. Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt) He calls the 'reproach of Christ' here those insults which the Israelites were suffering at that time, which were a figure of those which Christ was about to suffer, and for Christ's sake, Christians, as Chrysostom rightly says here. For this is a contracted locution, and similar to that which we had above in [verse] 15. And the comparison proceeds well: For the Israelite people, just as the Son of God, is called the firstborn, Exodus 4:21, Jeremiah 31:6, so also is Christ, Habakkuk 3:13, because of the greatest benefits, which are signified by the name of ointment. Thus also the parents of that people are called 'Christs' [anointed ones], Psalm 105:15.

Now the Apostle turns himself to Moses himself, in whom the Hebrews greatly boasted, and who was a singular example of great faith, and first indeed he concludes his faith in the Messiah from the fact that he spurned the Royal court and grace and the treasures of Egypt, and did not hesitate to prefer to them the reproach of Christ. 'Having become great,' says the Apostle, because he was already 40 years old, Acts 7:23, 'refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,' by whom he had been adopted. By the very deed he rejected the Royal adoption, when, having left the court, he went out to visit his Hebrew brothers in their affliction, and did not return to the court again: choosing rather to be afflicted with the people of God than to have the temporal pleasure of sin, if he had communicated in the sins which were rampant in the court, or at least had disguised himself as a Hebrew and separated himself from the people of God. Here he departs from the Vulgate, which has 'temporal', Estius: It is not 'temporal', he says, but 'temporal' πρόσκαιρον, so that it may refer to pleasure. And his commentaries teach that the ancient Greeks also, Chrysostom and the others, read it thus. From whom the Syriac edition does not dissent. For it has it thus: And not for a short time to be delighted in sin. Paul also, 2 Cor. 4, referred the same word to the goods which men enjoy: The things which are seen, he says, are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal. And in truth the delight of sin is only temporal, because it passes away: But sin remains by reason of guilt and the sting of conscience. By ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, which the words properly sound and according to the letter the reproach of Christ, which Moses through faith in the Messiah was not ignorant that he himself would experience in the days of his flesh, and which was preached among the people of God, to whom he preferred to be joined rather than to enjoy the splendor of the court and the treasures of Egypt, we understand. For there is no reason why we should depart to impropriety and figures, having abandoned the proper sense: And that proper sense contributes most to the description of faith, in the explaining, illustrating, and proving of which by examples the Apostle is occupied, since the proper object of saving faith is the ὀνειδισμὸς τοῦ Χριστοῦ, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, Heb. 12:2, to whom the Apostle warns that Moses looked, and that the Hebrews ought to look by his example and that of other ancient believers, and the proper act of justifying faith is to embrace with true confidence whatever Christ endured for us of ὀνειδισμοῦ from the Devil likewise, and from the world, nay even from the wrath of God on account of the sin of the world received into himself, and to prefer that to all the treasures of the world, just as Moses by faith counted the ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ greater riches than even the Royal treasures of Egypt, for the sake of which he put those things behind him, and associated himself with the people of God, who held the reproach of Christ in value; since that is the symbol of all the faithful and of the people of God, which was the Apostle's, Gal. 6:14, God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the Apostle does not hesitate to prefer this one wisdom to the wisdom of all men, which is concerning Christ Jesus, and him crucified, 1 Cor. 2:3, and he wishes us to glory uniquely in this, that Christ is made unto us by God wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption, 1 Cor. 1:30, which glorying was without doubt proper and perpetual among the people of God of the faithful, to whom the promise of blessing in the seed of Abraham, and what God had manifested to the Patriarchs concerning him, was in fresh memory, nay in public proclamation, propagated through the παλαιοπαράδοξον tradition from the time of Joseph, who had departed from the living only a century before. Which sense is without ambiguity simpler and more convenient to the letter and the text than if, with others, by ὀνειδισμ τοῦ Χριστοῦ one understands the reproach by which the people of God was affected on account of Christ, because he professed that he was expecting Him from the promise of God; or concerning the reproach which the Egyptians were about to speak against Moses, when he renounced the royal adoption and professed himself to be an Israelite; or, with Theodoret and Thomas, that which Moses suffered from his brothers is called the reproach it was a type and figure of that which Christ was about to suffer: to which opinion Grotius acceded, but inventing a strained locution, as if Christ were said for Christian, without example, without necessity, and concerning the whole cause. Ribera's exposition is similar, but it regards the reproach of Christ only as an example, not as a merit, whereas on the contrary faith looks upon the reproach of Christ as a merit, and as a compensation for the reproach that was owed to us, or as satisfaction for the same, by which heavenly treasures are shared with us, whence by His grace we deservedly put behind and despise all the riches and treasures of the world. For Ribera says thus: That Moses, looking with a prophetic spirit upon the passion and reproaches of Christ, desired conformity to Him, and from that devotion of mind preferred to be affected by reproaches, that is, to suffer with Christ in a certain way, rather than to abound in honors and riches in the court of Pharaoh.

For he looked away to the reward) That reward promised to Abraham, Gen. XV. 1, that excellent land. Ἀποβλέπειν is to look away. A word frequent among good Greek writers. We have already had the word μισθαποδοσία a few times.

The reward promised to Abraham was far, nay, infinitely greater than that excellent land: I, says the Lord Himself, will be your reward. Which he undoubtedly looked to, as it was in that promise, apprehended by mere faith, that his blessedness consisted: For when he believed, he had faith in Him, it was imputed to him for righteousness, Gen. XV. 1, 6. This therefore is the μισθαποδοσία, the reward not of debt, as the Papists trifle—for who can merit God Himself?—but bringing it freely: From which God both received what He wills to be our reward, and it will be an eternal reward for the elect, especially in the other life: because then God will be all in all to us, 1 Cor. XV. 28. Thus Moses could easily despise the royal treasures of Egypt, who through faith looked upon the heavenly riches hidden in the reproach of Christ, and obtained by the death of Christ, and to be obtained by a faithful embrace of that reproach, which he was obtaining spiritually with the people of God in the kingdom of grace, but was awaiting eternally in the kingdom of glory in an ineffable and immense manner. Which riches are in God, Luke XII. 21. Rich in faith, James II. 3, to whom God Himself is here and eternally the reward: A reward truly great, because immense and infinite, to which there is no analogy or proportion, no condignity, of any sufferings, even if all the things of the present time were heaped together into one, Rom. VIII. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 26. Μείζονα πλῦτον ἡγησάμενος τῶν Αἰγύπτιου θη- σαυρῶν τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τῦ Χριστῦ) Ὀνειδισμὸν Christi hic vocat contumelias illas, quas tum Israëlitæ patiebantur, quæ figura erant earum, quas perpessurus erat Christus, & ob Christum Christiani, ut recte hic Chrysostomus. Est enim hæc loquutio contracta, & similis ei, quam supra habuimus 15. Et bene procedit comparatio : Nam & po- pulus Israëliticus, sicut filius Dei, primogenitus vocatur, Exod. IV. 21. Jer. XXXI. 6. ita & Christus Abac. III. 13. ob maxima beneficia, quæ unguenti nomine significantur. Sic & parentes ejus populi Χριστοὶ vocantur Ps. CV, 15.

Jam ad Mosen ipsum, in quo valde gloriabantur Ebræi, & qui exemplum singulare erat magnæ fidei, sese confert Apostolus, & primum quidem fidem ejus in Messiam inde concludit, quod Regiam aulam & gratiam, ac thesauros Ægypti spreverit, iisdemque opprobrium Christi præferre non dubitarit. Μέγας γενόμενος, inquit Apostolus, quia 40. ann. natus jam erat, Act. VII. 23. ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι υἱὸς θυγατρὸς Φαραὼ, renuit vocari filius filiæ Pharaonis à qua adoptatus erat. Facto ipso respuit adoptionem Regiam, cum relicta aula ad fratres suos Ebræos in afflictione visitandos egressus, nec ad aulam iterum reversus est: magis eligens affligi cum populo Dei, quam temporalem peccati jucunditatem habere, si peccatis, quæ in aula grassabantur, communicasset, vel saltim Ebræum sese dissimulasset, ac à populo Dei separasset. Recedit hic à Vulgata, quæ habet temporalis, Estius: Non est temporalis, inquit, sed temporalem πρόσκαιρον, ut ad jucunditatem referatur. Atque ita veteres etiam Græcos, Chrysostomum ac cæteros, legisse docent eorum commentarii. A quibus nec Syriaca dissentit editio. Sic enim habet: Et non modico tempore delectari in peccato. Paulus quoq; 2. Cor. IV. ad bona quibus homines fruuntur, eandem vocem retulit: Quæ videntur, inquit, temporalia sunt, quæ non videntur, æterna. Et revera delectatio peccati temporalis tantum est, quia transit: Peccatum autem manet ratione reatus & conscientiæ morsus. Per ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, quod propriè verba sonant & secundum literam opprobrium Christi, quod in diebus carnis ipsum experturum esse Moses per fidem in Messiam non ignorabat, quodq; in populo Dei prædicabatur, cui sociari, quam aulæ splendore & thesauris Ægypti frui malebat, intelligimus. Nam cur ad improprietatem & figuras, relicto proprio sensu abeamus, causa nulla est: Et facit ille sensus proprius maximè ad descriptionem fidei, in qua explicanda & exemplis illustranda ac comprobanda occupatur Apostolus, siquidem fidei salvificæ objectum proprium sit ὀνειδισμὸς τοῦ Χριστοῦ, qui ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῷ χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινε σταυρὸν, αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, Ebr. XII. 2. in quem respexisse Mosen, & Ebræos respicere ejus aliorumque veterum fidelium exemplo debere, monet Apostolus, actusque fidei justificantis proprius sit fiducia vera amplecti, quicquid Christus pro nobis sustulit ὀνειδισμοῦ à Diabolo pariter, & à mundo, imò etiam ab ira Dei ob peccatum mundi in se receptum, idque præferre omnib9 mundi thesauris, sicut Moses majores divitias duxit per fidem præ thesauris etiam Regiis Ægypti τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, cujus gratia illos posthabuit, & sese populo Dei, Christi opprobrium in pretio habenti, associavit; siquidem symbolum fidelium omnium ac populi Dei illud sit, quod Apostoli erat, Gal. VI. 14. Absit mihi gloriari, præterquam in cruce Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quemadmodum hanc unam sapientiam omnium hominum sapientiæ præferre non dubitat Apostolus, quæ est de Christo Jesu, eoque crucifixo, 1. Cor. II. 3. & in eo unicè nos vult gloriari, quod Christus nobis factus à Deo sapientia, justitia & sanctificatio & redemptio 1. Cor. I. 3. quæ gloriatio sine dubio in populo Dei fidelium propria fuit ac perpetua, quibus semper promissio benedictionis in semine Abrahami, & quæ Patriarchis Deus de illo manifestarat, in recenti memoria, imò in publico præconio erat, per παλαιοπαράδοξον traditionem inde à Josepho, qui ante seculum demum è vivis excesserat, propagata. Qui sensus procul ambiguo simplicior & literæ ac textui convenientior, quam si cum aliis per ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ probrum intelligatur, quo populus Dei afficiebatur propter Christum, quod profiteretur, se illum ex Dei promissione expectare; vel de im- properio, quod Ægyptii dicturi erant in Mosen, abdicantem a se Regiam adoptionem, & profiten- tem se esse Israëlitam; aut cum Theodoreto & Tho- ma, id quod Moses a fratribus passus est, imprope- rium Christi vocari dicatur, quia typus & figura fuit ejus, quod Christus erat passurus: Cui sen- tentiæ accessit Grotius, sed contractam loqutio- nem fingens, quasi Christus dicatur pro Chri- stiano, sine exemplo, sine necessitate, & circa omnem causam. Affinis est Ribera expositio, sed quæ respicit tantum opprobrium Christi, ut exemplum, non ut meritum, quum ex adverso fi- des intueatur Christi opprobrium qua meritum, & ejus, quod nobis debebatur, opprobrii compen- satio, vel pro eodem satisfactio est, quo nobis parti sunt cœlestes thesauri, unde ejus gratia merito posthabemus ac contemnimus omnes mundi divi- tias & thesauros. Ita enim Ribera: Quod Moses Spiritu Prophetico intuens Christi passionem & op- probria optaverit ejus conformitatem, atque ex ea animi devotione maluerit opprobriis affici, id est, Christo quodammodo compati, quam honoribus ac divitiis abundare in aula Pharaonis.

Ἀπέβλεπε γὰρ εἰς τὴν μισθαποδοσίαν) Mercedem illam Abrahamo promissam, Gen. XV. 1. terram illam excellen- tem. Ἀποβλέπειν est respicere. Vox frequens Scriptoribus bene Græcis. Vocem μισθαποδοσίας jam aliquoties ha- buimus.

Merces Abrahamo promissa longè, imò infini- ties major erat, quam terra illa excellens: Ego, in- quit Dominus ipse, ero merces tua. Quam sine du- bio respexit, utpote in qua promissione mera fide apprehensa consistebat ejus beatitudo: Dum enim credidit, ei fidem habuit, imputatum id ei est ad justitiam Gen. XV. 1. 6. Hæc ergo est μισθαποδοσία, mercedem non debiti, ut nugantur Papistæ: Ecquis enim mereri Deum ipsum potest? sed gratis infe- rens: Ex qua Deus & recepit, quod velit nostra mer- ces esse, & electis æterna merces, imprimis in altera vita, erit: quia tum Deus nobis erit omnia in omnibus, 1. Cor. XV. 28. Spernere ita facile potuit Moses thesauros Ægypti Regios, qui divitias cœ- lestes per fidem intuebatur in opprobrio Christi reconditas, & morte Christi partas, opprobriique illius fideli amplexu obtinendas, quas cum popu- lo Dei spiritualiter in regno gratiæ consequeba- tur, sed in regno gloriæ ineffabili & immensa ratio- ne æternum expectabat. Quæ divitiæ in Deo sunt, Luc. XII. 21. Divitibus fide propriæ, Jac. II. 3. qui- bus Deus ipse hic & æternum merces est: Merces verè magna, quia immensa & infinita, ad quam nulla est passionum, etsi omnes τὰ νῦν καιρᾶ in unum cumulentur, analogia aut proportio, nulla con- dignitas, Rom. VIII. 18.

## 11:27
Vers. 27. By faith he left Egypt) having faith in the oracle in the bush and so many others.

Not fearing the wrath of the king) The history is referred to, which is Exod. X. 28, 29. For when the King had said to Moses: Beware that you do not see my face again, for on whatever day you appear, you shall die; Moses answered: It shall be as you say, I will not see your face again. Such are the edicts of many kings, like that of the Corinthian King in Euripides' Medea: ---- I warn you, if the shining lamp of the god sees you and your children within the boundaries of the land, you shall die ---- Which Ennius had translated thus: If I find you at the second light, you shall die. ---- For he endured as seeing the invisible) He endured, that is, he was constant. See Job II. 9. And why was he constant? Because he held God, though invisible, so present in his mind, as if he were seeing Him. And this is an excellent description of faith. That [verse] never escaped him, 'as if he saw Him who is invisible'.

This is the second proof of Mosaic faith, that he left Egypt through faith, fearing nothing of the king's wrath: But it is treated here of that leaving of Egypt, not that by which he fled into Midian after killing the Egyptian, as it seemed to Theophylact, where he altogether feared the king's wrath, Exod. II. 14, but that by which, at God's command, he led the Israelites out of Egypt. Which leading out is attributed to faith in the Messiah for the reason that not only did the Son of God Himself promise to Moses in the burning bush that He would be the God of the Hebrews, who is the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, Exod. III. 18, but because that leading out had as its goal the land of Canaan, the fatherland of the Messiah, and in it the kingdom and priesthood proper to the people of God, a type and figure of the royal and priestly office of Christ until His advent, whom the Apostle taught in this epistle especially to be the body of those shadows, just as he demonstrated here that the introduction into the land of Canaan was a figure of the introduction into eternal rest. The constancy of Mosaic faith is rightly observed to be expressed by the word ἐκαρτέρησεν, which was not broken by the wrath or indignation of Pharaoh, or by the fear of the pursuit of the people, when he was being led out of Egypt, or even when he was already actually pursuing the people. For he held fast to the invisible as if he saw Him, which the blessed Luther rendered emphatically, 'er hielt an dem, den er nicht sahe, als sehe er ihn' [he held to Him whom he did not see, as if he saw Him], which is also an argument that faith is the evidence of things not seen, v. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 27. Πίστει κατέλιπεν Αἴγυπτον) fidem habens ora- culo in rubo & tot aliis.

Μὴ φοβηθεὶς τὸν θυμὸν τοῦ βασιλέως) Respicitur historia, quæ est Exod. X. 28. 29. Nam cum Rex dixisset Mosi: cave ne ultra faciem meam videas, nam quocunque die apparue- ris, morte morieris; respondit Moses: Erit ut dicis, non vi- debo ultra faciem tuam. Talia sunt multorum Regum edi- cta, quale illud Corinthii Regis in Medea Euripides: ---- Προυννέπω δέ σοι Εἰ σ' ἡπιοῦσα λαμπὰς ὄψεται Θεῦ Καὶ παῖδας ἐντὸς δὲ τερμόνων χθονὸς Θανῇ ---- Quod Ennius sic verterat: Si te secundo lumine bie offendero, Moriere. ---- Τὸν γὰρ ἀόρατον ὡς ὁρῶν ἐκαρτέρησε) Ἐκαρτέρησε החזק, id est, constans fuit. Vide Job. II. 9. Et cur constans fuit? Quia Deum inconspicuum ita præsentem habebat animo, quasi eum conspiceret. Et hæc egregia est fidei descriptio. Nunquam illi excidebat illud אשר אחרי

Alterum hoc fidei Mosaicae est documentum, quod Ægyptum per fidem reliquerit, nihil metuens iram Regis: Agitur autem hic de illa Ægypti reli- ctione, non qua in Midian profugit post interfe- ctum Ægyptium, ut Theophylacto visum, ubi omni- no Regis iram veritus est, Exod. II. 14. sed qua man- dante Deo, Israëlitas ex Ægypto educebat. Quæ eductio fidei in Messiam ideo tribuitur, quod non tantum ipse Filius Dei in rubo ardente Mosi promi- serit, se futurum Deum Ebræorum, qui Deus Abra- ham, Deus Isaac & Deus Jacob est, Exod. III. 18. sed quod eductio illa pro termino habuerit terram Ca- naan, Messiæ patriam, & in ea regnum sacerdotium populo Dei proprium, Regii & Sacerdotalis Christi muneris typum & figuram usq; ad ejus adventum, quem umbrarum istarum corpus esse Apostolus hac imprimis epistola docuit, quemadmodum per introductionem in terram Canaan figuratam esse introductionem in æternam quietem, itidem hic demonstravit Apostolus. Recte autem fidei Mo- saicæ constantiam expressam verbo ἐκαρτέρησεν observatur, quæ non fracta fuit ira vel indignatio- ne Pharaonis, aut metu insectationis populi, cum educeretur ex Ægypto, aut etiam cum actu jam persequeretur populum. Nam invisibilem ac si vi- deret ipsum, tenuit constans, quod emphatice red- didit B. Lutherus, er hielt an dem, den er nicht sahe, als sehe er ihn, quod etiam argumentum est, fidem esse ἔλεγχον τῶν μὴ βλεπομένων, v. 1.

## 11:28
Vers. 28. By faith he kept the Passover) that is, he celebrated the Passover, פָּסַח in Hebrew formulas, trusting in the promise, which is Exod. XII. 3. This Passover, however, with the things annexed to it, has a manifest figure of Christ, 1 Cor. V. 7.

Καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τῦ αἵματ[?] ) to sprinkle and to pour out correspond to the Hebrew זָרַק, which is to sprinkle, Exod. XXIV. 6. XXIX. 11. 16. & in Leviticus & elsewhere often. One must understand here by πρόσχυσις or sprinkling that which was done to the doorposts, which mystically signify our heart, just as that blood signifies the passion of Christ.

Ἵνα μὴ ὁ ὀλοθρεύων τὰ πρωτότοκα, θίγῃ αὐτῶν) the destroyer, namely the Angel, who is the destroyer in 1 Cor. X. 10, the destroyer, Wisd. XVIII. 22, 25. He is the one who in the book of Tobit & among the Rabbis is called אשמדי. The same is המשחית, Exod. XII. 23, where the Greeks have τὸν ὀλεθρεύοντα, & Jer. II. 30, where likewise in the Greek is ὁ ὀλεθρεύων. See what has been said by us at the place already indicated to the Corinthians, τὰ πρωτότοκα, namely the offspring. For it concerns cattle as much as men in Exod. XII. 12. To touch here is to strike נָגַע, Exod. XXI. 23, in which way also ἅπτεσθαι is taken, 1 Chron. XVI. 22, Ps. CV. 15, 1 John V. 18. Thus also we, through the blood of Christ, if we are rightly sprinkled with it, are delivered from him who has the power of death.

The third proof of the faith of Moses in the Messiah is the celebration of the Passover, in which especially the shedding of blood is commemorated, because both the slaughter of the paschal lamb was a notable figure of the Lamb of God to be slaughtered for us, John I. 29, 1 Cor. V. 7, Rev. XIII. 8, & the shedding of blood foreshadowed the effusion of the blood of Christ, by whose mighty work we escape the slaughter of the destroying Angel, obtaining through the blood of Christ the remission of sins, Matt. XXVI. 27, Eph. I. 7, Col. I. 14, Heb. II. 14. Thus therefore by faith Moses celebrated the Passover with the people of God, in that he apprehended by faith the slaughter of Christ for us figured in that Passover as that immaculate Lamb, 1 Pet. I. 19, & the shedding of blood made for us for the remission of sins. The Passover, named from the passing over of the Lord, was not only a memorial of the past passing over of the destroying Angel, by which those who were in the houses smeared with the blood of the paschal lamb were delivered, but also a type of the future redemption, which Christ was to accomplish by his own blood, by which, while our hearts are sprinkled, we are actually delivered from the power of Satan. The proper object therefore of faith is our Passover, Christ sacrificed for us, 1 Cor. V. 7, that Lamb of God, who redeemed us with his own blood, 1 Pet. I. 18, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 28. Πίσει πεποίηκε τὸ Πάσχα) id est ἐπασχάτισε, פָּסַח in formulis Ebraicis, fistas promisso, quod est Exod. XII. 3. Hoc autem Pascha cum rebus annexis manifestam habet Christi figuram 1. Cor. V. 7.

Καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τῦ αἵματ[?] ) προσχέειν & προσκκύειν respondent Ebræo זָרַק, quod est aspergere, Exod. XXIV. 6. XXIX. 11. 16. & in Levitico & alibi sæpe. Intelligenda hic πρόσχυσις sive sparsio facta ad postes, qui mysticè cor no- strum significant, sicut sanguis ille Agni passionem Christi.

Ἵνα μὴ ὁ ὀλοθρεύων τὰ πρωτότοκα, θίγῃ αὐτῶν) ὁ ὀλοθρεύων nempe Ἄγγελος, qui ὁ ὀλοθρευτὴς 1. Cor. X. 10. ὁ ὀλοθρεύων, Sap. XVIII. 22. 25. Is est, qui in libro Tobiæ & apud Rabi- nos dicitur אשמדי. Idem המשחית, Exod. XII. 23. ubi Græci τὸν ὀλεθρεύοντα, & Jer. II. 30. ubi itidem in Græco ὁ ὀλεθρεύων. Vide quæ dicta nobis ad indicatum jam ad Co- rinthios locum, τὰ πρωτότοκα, nempe γενήματα. Tam enim de pecudibus quam de hominibus agitur in Exod. XII. 12. Tangere hic est ferire נָגַע, Exod. XXI. 23. quomodo & ἅπτεσθαι sumitur, 1. Par. XVI. 22. Psal. CV. 15. 1. Joh. V. 18. Sic & nos per Christi sanguinem, si eo recte aspergamur, li- beramur ab eo, qui mortis habet imperium.

Tertium fidei Mosis in Messiam documentum est celebratio Paschatis, in qua cumprimis sanguinis profusio commemoratur, quia & mactatio agni paschalis erat insignis agni Dei pro nobis mactan- di figura, Joh. I. 29. 1. Cor. V. 7. Apoc. XIII. 8. & pro- fusio sanguinis adumbrabat effusionem sanguinis Christi, cujus virtute effugimus Angeli vastatoris cædem, consequentes per Christi sanguinem re- missionem peccatorum, Matth. XXVI. 27. Eph. I. 7. Col. I. 14. Ebr. II. 14. Ita ergo per fidem celebra- vit Pascha Moses, cum populo Dei, ut fide appre- henderit figuratam in isto Paschate Christi pro no- bis mactationem ceu Agni illius immaculati, 1. Petr. I. 19. & sanguinis effusionem factam pro no- bis in remissionem peccatorum. Pascha, à transitu Domini dictum, non tantum memoriale fuit præ- teriti transitus Angeli vastatoris, quo sanguine Agni paschalis illitis ædium postibus liberaban- tur, qui in illis erant, sed etiam typus futuræ re- demptionis, quam Christus sanguine suo peragere debuit, quo dum asperguntur corda nostra, actu nos à potestate Satanæ liberamur. Objectum ergo fidei proprium est Pascha nostrum Christus pro no- bis immolatus, 1. Cor. V. 7. Agnus ille Dei, qui san- guine suo nos redemit, 1. Petr. I. 18. 19.

## 11:29
Verse 29. By faith they passed through the Red Sea, as by dry land. He explains what is in Exod. XIV. 22. 'And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground.' He shows an example of faith not only in the leading men, but also in the multitude. For at the exhortations of Moses, which we read in Exod. XIV. 13, they entered into the sea, and unharmed they crossed a semicircle in the sea itself. That sea is here called ἐρυθρὰ θάλασσα, just as the LXX speak in Ps. CVI and CXXXV. But it is more correctly called Erythraea, not from redness, but from Erythra, just as the Greeks translated the name of Edom, who is the same as Esau: whose descendants held the shore of that sea, as we see in 1 Kings IX. 26. ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς. Thus Exod. XIV. 21. 'He made the sea as dry land.' In the Hebrew לחרבה:

The wave, curved into the likeness of a mountain, stood around. Ἧς πεῖραν λαβόντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι κατεπόθησαν) Drawn by the example, and thinking that it would be safe for them, because they saw it yielding safely to the Israelites, they were swallowed up, namely by the waves, Exod. XIV. 27. בלע. Καταπίνω in many places is valid, and is translated as καταποντίζω. Thus also the unbelieving are submerged in the greatest evils, while the pious escape.

These things now do not concern Moses only, but also all the faithful Israelites: who, following Moses as their leader, passed through the Red or Erythraean Sea by faith, ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς, that is, γῆς, as through dry land, having placed their faith in the Messiah, who appeared to them at the Red Sea, as the Author of the Old Testament, when they were in the greatest straits, shining before them in a pillar of cloud, and placing himself as a Protector between the Egyptian army and the army of Israel, of whom Moses says: 'Fear not, stand firm, and see what salvation the Lord is about to work for you,' Exod. XIV. 13, 20. This trust in the Messiah the Redeemer, who was about to liberate them from the power of the infernal enemy, just as he was now about to liberate them from the hand of the Egyptian tyrant, and through that liberation was about to seal that same [liberation] among them. We have therefore here again a proper object of faith, Christ the Redeemer and Savior of men, whom the Israelites believing in him then celebrated as such, Exod. XIV. 32, chap. XV. 2, and this bodily liberation prefigured the spiritual redemption of Christ, which the faithful Israelites embraced with true faith.

Latin:

Verf. 29. Πίστει διέβησαν τὴν ἐρυθρὰν θάλασσαν, ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς) Explicat quod est Exod. XIV. 22. ויבאו בני ישראל בתוך הים ביבשה Non tantùm in viris primoribus, sed & in multitudine ostendit exemplum fidei. Nam ad Mo- sis hortamenta, quæ legimus Exod. XIV. 13. ingressi sunt in mare, & illæsi semicirculum in ipso mari transiere. Id mare hic vocatur ἐρυθρὰ θάλασσα, quomodo in Psal. CVI. & CXXXV. loquuntur LXX. Sed rectius Ἐρυθραία dici- tur non à rubore, sed ab Erythra, quomodo Græci transtu- lere nomen Edomi, qui idem Esau: cujus posteri oram illius maris tenuere, ut videmus 1. Reg. IX. 26. ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς. Sic Exod. XIV. 21. ἐποίησε τὴν θάλασσαν ὡς ξηράν. In Ebræo לחרבה:

Curvata in montis speciem circumstetit unda Ἧς πεῖραν λαβόντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι κατεπόθησαν) Tracti exemplo, & putantes, sibi tutum fore, quod Israëlitıs tuto cedere videbant, absorpti sunt, nempe fluctibus, Exod. XIV. 27. בלע. Καταπίνω pluribus in locis valet, & vertitur καταποντίζω. Sic etiam increduli in summa mer- gentur mala, piis evadentibus.

Hæc jam non concernunt Mosen tantum, sed & Israëlitas omnes fideles : qui Mosen ducem sequuti per fidem transierunt mare rubrum vel Erythræ- um, ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς scilicet γῆς, ut per aridam terram, fide in Messiam collocata, qui ipsis ad mare ru- brum apparuit, ut Veteris Testamenti Autor, quum in summis essent angustiis, prælucens in co- lumna nubis, & sistens sese ceu Protectorem inter exercitum Ægyptium & exercitum Israëlīs, de quo Moses : Ne timeatis, state firmi, & videte, quam sa- lutem vobis facturus sit Dominus, Exod. XIV. 13. 20. Hæc fiducia in Messiam Redemptorem, qui ut li- beraturus ipsos à potestate hostis infernalis, sic à manu tyranni Ægyptiaci ipsos jam liberaturus, & per illam liberationem istam penes eosdem obsi- gnaturus erat. Habemus ergo hic iterum obje- ctum fidei proprium, Christum Redemptorem & Sàlvatorem hominum, quem ceu talem deinde celebrârunt Israëlītæ credentes in ipsum, Exod. XIV. 32. cap. XV. 2. & præfiguravit hæc corpora- lis liberatio spiritualem redemptionem Christi, quam vera fiue complexi sunt fideles Israëlītæ.

## 11:30
Verse 30. By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, having been compassed about for seven days. Construe Πίστει with κυκλωθέντα, explain it not as besieged but as circled. For the people had done this with arms and trumpets, the ark going before, having faith in the words of Joshua, Josh. VI. 1. But the walls fell down on the Sabbath day, as the Hebrews hand down. Thus in the times of Christ, which is the fulfillment of the Sabbath, idolatry fell down without any human force, at the sound of his word.

From the history of Joshua, the example of the faith of Joshua, the Levites, and the people is set forth in that first victory over Jericho, which they obtained through faith in the Messiah, as he who appeared to them in the form of a man, as the Prince of the host of the Lord, and their Savior, Josh. V; and he was the Author not only of this victory, but of all which they obtained over the Canaanites; because that Lord was with Joshua, as in that first expedition, Josh. VI. 27, so in all the following ones. See Josh. X. 8, and he fought for Israel, v. 41, etc. By whose power they occupied the land of Canaan, in which, having apprehended it by true faith, we convince the world, just as the Israelites conquered Jericho, 1 John V. 1, and we occupy the heavenly Canaan, Heb. III and IV.

Latin:

Verf. 30. Πίστει τὰ τείχη ἱεριχὼ ἔπεσε κυκλωθέντα ἐπὶ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας) Πίστει construe cum κυκλωθέντα, expone non obseffa sed circuita. Fecerat enim hoc populus cum armis & bucci- nis, arca præeunte, fidem habens Josuæ dictis Jos. VI. 1. Conciderunt autem mœnia die sabbathi, ut tradunt Ebræi. Sic Christi temporibus, quod implementum est Sabbathi, concidit idololatria sine ulla vi humana, ad sonum verbi ejus.

Ex historia Josuæ exemplum fidei Josuæ, Levi- tarum, & populi sistitur prima illa victoria de Je- richo, quam per fidem in Messiam obtinuere, ut- pote qui ipsius in forma viri, ceu Princeps exerci- tus Domini, & Sospitator ipsorum apparuit, Jos. V; nec hujus tantum victoriæ, sed omnium, quas de Chananæis obtinuere, Autor fuit; quia Domi- nus ille cum Josua fuit, ut in illa prima expeditio- ne, Jos. VI. 27. ita in sequentibus universis. Vid. Jos. X. 8. & pugnavit pro Israële v. 41. &c. Cujus virtute terram Canaan occuparunt, in quo vera fide apprehensa convincimus mundum, ut Israëli- tæ Jericho vicere, 1. Joh. V. 1. & occupamus cœle- stem Canaan, Ebr. III. & IV.

## 11:31
Verse 31. By faith Rahab the harlot perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace. And here Πίστει is to be construed with δεξαμένη, therefore she received and saved the spies, sent by Joshua, because she believed that there was one true God, who had performed such wondrous things in Egypt and in the desert places of Arabia, whose worshippers the Israelites were. After the examples of the Fathers, he added also the example of a woman and a foreigner and of a base life. For she practiced both an inn, and at the same time gain from her body, whence she is called זונה, that is, πόρνη. Concerning that custom see L. Palam §. si qua, D. de ritu nuptiarum; and L. qui adulterium, C. de adulteriis. She is called πόρνη, however, not because she remained such, but because she had been such before, just as in Matt. XXI. 31, the harlots are said to enter into the kingdom of heaven.

Μετ' εἰρήνης with safety, that is, she received them in such a way that she rendered them safe at the risk of her own life. A great faith indeed, and as James explains, joined with excellent works, such as the faith of Christians ought to be. Chrysostom rightly said that in Rahab there is a figure of those who were once idolaters, and as Scripture speaks, had committed whoredom with demons. For these, after faith, but not an idle one, are taken out of the destruction to which the unbelieving will be subject.

Specifically this example of Rahab the woman, and that a harlot, is brought forward as a testimony that women, even sinners, obtain salvation through faith, just as Rahab was not only saved from bodily destruction, nor did she perish with the unbelievers τοῖς ἀπειθήσασι, but she was also justified and eternally saved through faith. Who is called זונה in Josh. II. 1, that is, not an innkeeper, as Jonathan and the more recent Jews translate, but a harlot, which meaning that word always carries, Gen. XXXIV. 3, chap. XXXVIII. 15, Jud. XI. 1. Therefore she is named πόρνη by the LXX Interpreters as also by Paul here, and not least by James in chap. II. 5: Who not only gave faith to the words of the Lord, but also testified to her faith by a work of charity, when she received the spies with peace. For she acknowledged the God of the Israelites to be God above in heaven, and below on earth, and confessed the same by true faith, Josh. II. 11. That she was saved through faith in Christ, the Apostle testifies, and therefore he adds her here to the catalog of the faithful.

Latin:

Verf. 31. Πίστει Ῥαὰϐ ἡ πόρνη συναπώλετο τοῖς ἀπειθή- σασι, δεξαμένη τοὺς κατασκόπους μετ' εἰρήνης) Et hic πίστει construendum cum δεξαμένη, ideo excepit & sal- vos fecit exploratores; à Josua missos, quod crede- ret, unum esse Deum verum, qui in Ægypto & in Ara- biæ desertis locis res tam miras patrâsset, cujus cultores erant Israëlītæ. Post exempla Patrum addidit etiam exemplum fœminæ & extraneæ & turpis vitæ. Nam & cauponam exercebat, & simul corpore quæstum, unde זונה, id est πόρνη dicitur. De eo more vide L. Palam §. si qua, D. de ritu nuptiarum; & L. qui adulterium, C. de adulteriis. Vocatur autem πόρνη non quod talis manserit, sed quod talis ante fuiffet, quomodo Matth. XXI. 31. ἁι πόρναι dicuntur intrare in regnum cœleste.

Μετ' εἰρήνης cum incolumitate, id est, ita eos excepit, ut tutos eos præstaret cum capitis sui periculo. Fides sane magna, & ut Jacobus explicat, cum egregiis operibus conjuncta, qualis esse debet Christianorum fides. Recte dixit Chrysostomus in Raaba esse figuram eorum, qui olim idololatræ, & ut Scriptura loquitur, cum Dæmonibus scor- tati fuerant. Nam hi post fidem, sed non otiosam, eximen- tur exitio, cui subjacebunt increduli.

Specialiter hoc exemplum de Raaba fœmina eaque meretrice inducitur in testimonium, quod mulieres etiam peccatrices per fidem salutem adi- piscantur, quemadmodum Raab non tantum ser- vata est ab interitu corporali, nec periit cum incre- dulis τοῖς ἀπειθήσασι, sed etiam justificata est & æternum salvata per fidem. Quæ זונה dicitur Jos. II.1. hoc est non caupona, ut Jonathan & Judæi re- centiores vertunt, sed meretrix, quem sensum vox illa semper infert, Gen. XXXIV. 3. cap. XXXIIX. 15. Jud. XI. 1. Ideo πόρνη à LXX. Interpretibus ut & Paulo hic, nec non à Jacobo cap. II. 5. nomina- ta: Quæ non modo verbis Domini fidem adhibuit, sed fidem etiam testata est opere charitatis, cum exploratores suscepit cum pace. Agnovit enim Deum Israëlitrarum esse Deum supra in cælo, & in- fra in terra, eundemque professa est vera fide Jos. II. 11. Quam per fidem in Christum servatam esse testatur Apostolus, ideoque catalogo fidelium hic accenset.

## 11:32
Vers. 32. Καὶ τί ἔτι λέγω; What need is there for me to speak further about this matter? The whole Scripture is full of such examples. Ἐπιλείψει γάρ με διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος) Such is that: Before the day is done, Vesper will settle on Olympus, and similar things. Περὶ Γεδεὼν) Who had faith in the Angel, Jud. VI. Βαρὰκ τε, καὶ Σαμψὼν, καὶ Ἰεφθὰὲ) Who were all stirred by divine inspiration to rule and avenge the people, whence they are also called Prophets by Josephus. They obeyed this inspiration through faith. See Jud. IV. 14. XI. 29. XIII. 25. Angels had also appeared to the parents of Gideon and Samson, Jud. VI. 11. XIII. 3. 11. He does not, however, keep the order of times. For Barak was before Gideon, and Jephthah before Samson. So also 1 Sam. XII. 11 in the Greek τὸν Ἱεροβοὰλ (that is, Gideon) καὶ τὸν Βαρὰκ, for they read ברק, where now in the Hebrew it is בדן. He writes Ἰεφθὰὲ, just as the LXX do, namely, that is placed for the letter ת, as also in Νωὲ and other words. Concerning his vow and how it was fulfilled, we have stated our opinion at that passage in the book of Judges. In the same place you will find why neither Gideon nor Samson should be thought to have sinned against the law. Δαυίδ τε, καὶ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν Προφητῶν) To all of whom God signified His will through inspiration, through a voice, and sometimes through visions: And they, having faith, performed great deeds. David is named before Samuel, so that Samuel may then be better connected with the other Prophets.

He therefore touches upon other faithful ones at least by omission, whom he nevertheless declares to have been likewise of faith in the Messiah. Gideon, who, sent by the Angel, the Son of God, liberated Israel, placing his trust in the same, confirmed in that faith by a notable miracle, Jud. VI. 14. seqq. Barak, who testified to his faith in his Eucharistic hymn for the liberation of Israel, Jud. V. 2. Samson, of whose faith in the Messiah, of whom he himself was an excellent type, one may read in Jud. XIII. seqq. cap. XVI. 25. Jephthah, whose faith his prayer in Jud. XI. 21 and the victory reported in the name of the Lord teach. David, concerning whom, both in history and in the Psalms, and especially in the prophetic ones, most clear documents of faith in the Messiah exist; And Samuel, whom he joins to the Prophets, because the Prophets from Samuel onwards foretold the days of Christ, as Peter testifies, Acts III. 24, that through faith in His name we obtain remission of sins, cap. X. 43. To all those, therefore, the Holy Spirit here bears witness of faith in the Messiah, and that they obtained salvation in no other way than through this faith, which also shone forth in their works and deeds: just as also the deeds of many in subsequent times, without regard for the chronological order, which he also does not attend to here regarding the Heroes from the book of Judges, he brought forward, and generally in v. 39 concluded concerning all, that namely by faith they were righteous before God, and by faith they pleased Him, v. 5, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 32. Καὶ τί ἔτι λέγω; Quid opus est hac de re ut lo- quar amplius? Plena est talium exemplorum tota scriptura. Ἐπιλείψει γάρ με διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος) Tale illud: An- te diem sero componet Vesper olympo, & similia. Περὶ Γεδεὼν) Qui fidem habuit Angelo Jud. VI. Βαρὰκ τε, καὶ Σαμψὼν, καὶ Ἰεφθὰὲ) Qui omnes afflatu divino excitati sunt ad regendum vindicandumque popu- lum, unde & Prophetæ Josepho vocantur. Huic afflatui paruere per fidem. Vid. Jud. IV. 14. XI. 29. XIII. 25. Ge- deonis & Sampsonis parentibus etiam Angeli apparuerant, Jud. VI. 11. XIII. 3. 11. Non servat autem ordinem tempo- rum. Nam Barac ante Gedeonem fuit, & Jephthes ante Sampsonem. Sic & 1. Sam. XII. 1. in Græco τὸν Ἱεροβοὰλ (id est Gedeon) καὶ τὸν Βαρὰκ legerunt enim ברק, ubi nunc in Ebræo בדן. Scribit autem Ἰεφθὰὲ, quomodo & LXX. nempe, illud ponitur pro litera ת, ut & in Νωὲ & vocibus aliis. De hujus voto & quomodo impletum sit, diximus sententiam nostram ad locum illum in Judi- cum libro. Ibidem invenies, cur neque Gideon, neque Sampson credendi sint in legem peccasse. Δαυίδ τε, καὶ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν Προφητῶν) Quibus omnibus Deus voluntatem suam significavit per afflatum, per vocem, interdum & per visa: Et illi fidem habentes res magnas ges- sere. David ante Samuelem nominatur, ut Samuel deinde melius connectatur cum Prophetis aliis.

Alios itaque fideles per præteritionem saltem at- tingit, quos verò à fide in Messiam itidem præ- dicat. Gedeonem, qui ab Angelo Filio Dei mis- sus Israëlem liberavit in eundem fiduciam collo- cans, insigni miraculo in fide illa confirmatus, Jud. VI. 14. seqq. Barak, qui fidem testatus est hymno suo Eucharistico pro liberatione Israëlis Jud. V. 2. Simsonem, de cujus fide in Messiam, cu- jus ipse eximius erat typus Jud. XIII. seqq. cap. XVI. 25. legere est. Jephtbam cujus fidem ora- tio ejus Jud. XI. 21. & victoria in nomine Domi- ni reportata docet. Davidem, de quo cum in his- storia, tùm in Psalmis, imprimis vero Propheti- cis, fidei in Messiam extant luculentissima docu- menta; Et Samuelem, quem Prophetis jungit, quia Prophetæ inde à Samuele prænunciarunt dies Christi teste Petro, Act. III. 24. quod per fi- dem in nomine ejus remissionem peccatorum consequamur cap. X. 43. Omnibus ergo illis testi- monium perhibet hic Spiritus sanctus fidei in Messiam, nec aliter eos, quam per hanc fidem, quæ etiam in operibus & factis eorum eluxit, sa- lutem adeptos esse: quemadmodum & facta plu- rium in subsequentibus temporibus non habita ra- tione seriei temporum, quam etiam hic circa He- roes e libro Judicum non attendit, adduxit, & ge- neratim v. 39. de omnibus conclusit, quod nem- pe fide fuerint justi coram Deo, ipsique per fi- dem placuerint v. 5. 6.

## 11:33
Vers. 33. Who through faith subdued kingdoms) They conquered many kings named in Joshua XII. Barak the Canaanites: Gideon the Midianites: Jephthah the Ammonites: Samson and Samuel the Philistines: David the Philistines, Amalekites, Jebusites, Moabites, Edomites, Syrians, whose faith of David you have depicted in vivid colors in Psalms II, XIII, XX, XXI. Thus also we must conquer the Prince of this world through faith.

Wrought righteousness) They led an honest and praiseworthy life according to the standard of those times. Thus also 'to do justice' is taken in Ezek. XVIII. 5, Sirach XIV. 17, XX. 30. This fits Samuel and Jehoshaphat excellently. We must do the same, but according to the more sublime precepts of the Gospel.

Obtained promises) They achieved huge victories, according to God's promises. What is said generally here, the following explains more specifically; we shall obtain greater promises.

Stopped the mouths of lions) They are said to have done this, because they obtained from God that it should happen. The history of Dan. VI. 22 is referred to, where in the Greek: 'He sent His Angel, and shut the mouths of the lions.' Thus also we through faith escape the maw of the Devil, who as a roaring lion seeks to devour us, 1 Pet. V. 8.

Latin:

Vers. 33. Οἱ διὰ πίστεως κατηγωνίσαντο βασιλείας) Vicere Josuae Reges multos nominatos Josuae XII. Barac Cananaeos: Gideon Midianitas: Jephtah Ammonitas: Samson & Sa- muel Philistinos: David Philistinos, Amalekitas, Jebusaeos, Moabitas, Idumaeos, Syros, cujus Davidis fidem vivis colo- ribus depictam habes Psal, II. XIII. XX. XXI. Sic & nos per fidem vincere debemus mundi hujus Principem.

Εἰργάσαντο δικαιοσύνην) Vitam egere honestam ac lauda- bilem pro illorum temporum ratione. Ita etiam sumitur facere justitiam, Ezech. XVIII. 5. Sirach. XIV. 17. XX. 30. Congruit hoc eximie Samueli & Josaphato. Idem & nos facere debemus, sed secundum sublimiora Evangelii prae- cepta.

Ἐπέτυχον ἐπαγγελιῶν) Ingentes victorias consequuti sunt, secundum Dei promissa. Hoc generaliter dictum specia- lius explicant sequentia, majora promissa nos consequemur.

Ἔφραξαν στόματα λεόντων) Dicuntur id fecisse, quod a Deo obtinuere, ut fieret. Respicitur historia Dan. VI. 22. ubi in Graeco: Ἀπέστειλε τὸν Ἄγγελον αὑτοῦ, καὶ ἐνέφραξε τὰ στόματα λεόντων. Sic & nos per fidem evadimus rictum Diaboli, qui tanquam leo rugiens quaerit nos devorare, 1. Petr. V. 8.

## 11:34
Vers. 34. Quenched the power of fire) The same figure, that is, they obtained that the fire should lose its force, as if it were extinguished, which happened to Ananias, Mizaël, and Azarias, as can be seen in Dan. III. 49, 50, 92. Thus also we shall be saved from eternal fire.

Escaped the edges of the sword) To flee sharp swords. For that is פי־חרב. See above IV. 12. Thus David escaped the swords of Saul: Elijah and Micaiah those of Ahab: Elisha those of Joram: Jeremiah those of the Jewish nobles: Esther and Mordecai, and other Jews, those of Haman. Thus also we [escape] the wrath of God which is compared to a sword in Jerem. XII and elsewhere.

Were made strong out of weakness) The manuscript has ἐδυναμώθησαν. They recovered from diseases like Job, Hezekiah 2 Kings XX. Tobias can be added. And we have recovered from the evils of the soul.

Became strong in war) As Jonathan 1 Sam. XIII and XIV. The commanders of David's army 2 Sam. XXIII.

Turned to flight the armies of the aliens) Παρεμβολὴ often among the interpreters of the Old Testament and Greek writers of Jewish histories signifies not camps but armies, as 1 Sam. IV. 16, Gen. XXXII. 7, Sir. XLVIII. 24, and often in the Maccabees. Κλίνειν is a military term for 'to put to flight,' even in Livy, 'the battle line is turned.' Ἀλλότριοι here are זרים, men alien from the worship of God. Thus we must put to flight from us desires alien to God.

Latin:

Vers. 34. Ἔσβεσαν δύναμιν πυρὸς) Eadem figura, id est, obtinuere, ut ignis vim suam amitteret, quasi extinctus esset, quod evenit Ananiae, Mizaëli & Azariae, ut videre est Dan. III. 49. 50. 92. Sic & nos servabimur ab igne aeterno.

Ἔφυγον στόματα μαχαίρας) Effugere enses acutos. Id enim פי־חרב. Vide supra IV. 12. Sic David effugit en- ses Saulis: Elias & Michaeas Achabi: Elisaeus Jorami: Jere- mias procerum Judaeorum: Esther Mardachaeus, & Judaei alii Hamanis. Sic & nos iram Dei quae gladio comparatur Jerem. XII. & alibi.

Ἐνεδυναμώθησαν ἀπὸ ἀσθενείας) Manuscriptus ἐδυναμώ- θησαν. Revaluere a morbis ut Job, Ezechias 2. Reg. XX. Addi potest Tobias. Et nos a malis animi convaluimus.

Ἐγενήθησαν ἰσχυροὶ ἐν πολέμῳ) Ut Jonathan 1. Sam. XIII. & XIV. Davidis militiae Duces 2. Sam. XXIII.

Παρεμβολὰς ἔκλιναν ἀλλοτρίων) Παρεμβολὴ saepe apud In- terpretes Veteris Testamenti & Scriptores Judaicarum hi- storiarum Graecos, non castra sed exercitus significat, ut 1. Sam. IV. 16. Gen. XXXII. 7. Sir. XLVIII. 24. & in Mac- cabaicis saepe. Κλίνειν vox militaris in fugam agere, etiam apud Livium est, inclinatur acies, Ἀλλότριοι hic sunt זרים homines extranei a Dei cultu. Sic nos fugare debemus a nobis cupiditates a Deo alienas.

## 11:35
Vers. 35. Women received their dead by resurrection) It now comes closer to the figures of both the hope and the patience of Christians. Women received their children back from death to mortal life, 1 Kings XVII. 21, 2 Kings IV. 34, 35. But we, we shall receive ourselves into immortal life. Ἐξ ἀναστάσεως here is δι' ἀναστάσεως. A similar expression in Gal. III. 11.

And others were tortured) That τύμπανον is the rack, through which human skin is stretched just as ox-hide on a drum, we said at 2 Macc. VI. 19, and confirmed from the Scholiast of Aristophanes. Plutarch also mentions it in Dion, and Lucilius in a Greek epigram. Hence τυμπανίζειν 'to torture' in Plutarch on the flatterer. Those who are tortured to death are called ἀποτυμπανίζεσθαι in 1 Maccabees III, Lysias against Ageratus, and Aristotle in Rhetoric II. In which sense the Syrian also interprets that ἐτυμπανίσθησαν in this place. The histories of the mother and seven sons are not obscurely referred to here, which are in 1 Macc. VI, VII, and in the book ἀυτοκράτορος λογισμοῦ, which is usually ascribed to Josephus, and among the Talmudists.

Οὐ προσδεξάμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν) Not accepting the liberation from punishments offered to them under the condition of idolatry. Thus Eleazar, 2 Macc. VI. 30: 'being able to be freed from death, I endure hard bodily pains.'

Ἵνα κρείττονος ἀναστάσεως τύχωσιν) They endured these evils with this hope, that after their death Jewish affairs would be restored to a better state. Which was a certain figure of that resurrection which we believe, as stated at Dan. XII. 2. 36. 'Ανάστασις here is like תקומה, Lev. 26. 37. Moreover, we are said to attain what we attain in our descendants.

Latin:

Vers. 35. Ἔλαβον γυναῖκες ἐξ ἀναστάσεως τοὺς νεκροὺς αὑτῶν) Propius jam venit ad figuras & spei & patientiae Christia- norum. Recepere foeminae suos liberos ex morte ad vitam rursus mortalem, 1. Reg. XVII. 21. 2. Reg. IV. 34. 35. At nos, recipiemus nosmetipsos in vitam immortalem. Ἐξ ἀναστάσεως hic est δι' ἀναστάσεως. Similis loquutio Gal. III. 11.

Ἄλλοι δὲ ἐτυμπανίσθησαν) Τύμπανον esse fidiculas, per quas humana pellis ita extenditur, ut bubula in tympa- no, diximus ad 2. Macc. VI. 19. & firmavimus ex Aristo- phanis Scholiafte. Meminit & Plutarchus Dione, & in Epigrammate Graeco Lucilius. Hinc τυμπανίζειν tor- quere apud Plutarchum de adulatore. Ἀποτυμπανίζεσθαι dicuntur, qui ad mortem usque torquentur 1. Maccabai- corum III. Lysiae adversus Ageratum, Aristoteli Rhetori- corum II. Quo sensu etiam hoc loco illud ἐτυμπανίσθησαν Syrus interpretatur. Non obscure respiciuntur hic historiae matris ac septem filiorum, quae sunt 1. Macc. VI. VII. & in libro ἀυτοκράτορος λογισμοῦ, qui Josepho adscribi solet & apud Thalmudicos.

Οὐ προσδεξάμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν) Non acceptantes liberationem a poenis sibi oblatam sub conditione ido- lolatriae. Sic Eleazarus 2. Macc. VI. 30. δυνάμενος ἀπολυ- θῆναι τοῦ θανάτου σκληρὰς ὑποφέρω κατὰ σῶμα ἀλγηδόνας.

Ἵνα κρείττονος ἀναστάσεως τύχωσιν) Tolerarunt ista ma- la hac spe, fore ut post suam mortem res Judaicae in me- liorem statum restituerentur. Quae figura quaedam erat ejus resurrectionis, quam nos credimus, ut dictum ad Dan. XII. 2. 36. Ἀνάστασις hic quod תקומה, Lev. 26. 37. Dicimur autem consequi & quod in posteris conse- quimur.

## 11:36
