Illustr. and let the parallel passages in the Old Testament be compared at the same time, Isa. 8:11, 13, ch. 28:16, Dan. 2:34, Zech. 3:9, and in the New, Matt. 21:42, Mark 12:10, Luke 20:17, Acts 4:11, Rom. 9:33, as also Luke 2:34.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

Πρὸς ὃν προσερχόμενοι.] Vox hæc cultum obedientiam- que significat, vide Ebr. 4, 16. cap. 7, 25. c. 10, 1. 22. c. 11, 6. קָרַב.

Λίθον ζῶντα, ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον, παρὰ δὲ Θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν, ἔντιμον.] Illud ζῶντα significat ἀλληγορίαν, sicut modo vox λογικὸν, alibi πηρὸν, alibi πληθυόμενον aut πλου- ματικὸν & similia. Respiciuntur loca Psal. 118, 22. & Esa. 8, 14. & cap. 28, 16. de quibus diximus ad Matth. 21, 42. & Act. 4, 11. Homines hic intellige Judæos, sed præcipue eos, qui erant in synedrio. Ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον סוּסַר, sic & Matth. 21, 42. Marc. 12, 10. Luc. 20, 17. pro eodem est ἐξουθενηθεὶς Act. 4, 11. quod in Psalmo est, factum in lapidem angularem, id est, quo totum ædificium sustineretur. Id hic aliis verbis dixit sen- su eodem ex Esa. 28, 16. ἐκλεκτὸν בְּחִיר Ebræis, quomodo LXX. legere, dicto jam Esaiæ loco, ubi vulgo מָסָד. Syrus id גבא, quomodo hic vertitur, deinde יקר maximi factum à DEO.

Argumento ab Evangelii suavitate secundum B. Gerhardum aliud succedit jam à piorum dignita- te, quod sint domus Dei spiritualis, ac Sacerdotes Dei, adeoque omnem immunditiam deponere debeant. Postquam ad incrementum renatorum desiderium ac studium doctrinam Evangelicam hauriendi fide amplectendi & imbibendi veluti, necnon in succum & sanguinem convertendi re- quisivit; nunc opus etiam esse alia metaphora usus docet, nos extruendi in templum Domini, & spiritua- les hostias offerendi quotidie, ut proficiamus in Domino. Consecrati sumus in baptismo, & per Verbum Domini in templa mystica, quia qui Ver- bum Dei audit, ad eum Deus venit, & mansionem apud eum facit, Joh. 14, 23. & Christus habitat in nobis per fidem, Eph. 2, 17. quotquot in Christum baptizati sumus, Christum induimus, Gal. 3. v. 27. Sed necessum est, ut templum Domini non destru- amus per incredulitatem, sed maneamus domus Domini spiritualis per fidem, 1. Cor. 3, 16. 17. Ædifi- cati sumus fide super lapidem illum vivum, eidem superædificati, Marc. 16, 17. in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu, Ephes. 2. vers. 20. 22. 1. Corinth. 3. vers. 11. Sed opus est, ut per eundem Spiritum nos qui per fidem in Christum vitam ab ipso habemus super Petra illa subinde magis ac magis nos ædificemus.

Facti sumus Sacerdotes spirituales abluti sanguine Christi, Apoc. I. 5. oleo uncti Spiritus in baptismo & Verbo 1. Joh. II, 30. quapropter opus est, ut per Spiritum sanctum hostias spirituales in fide ju- giter offeramus, quae in Christo Jesu acceptae sunt Deo. Templum Domini mundum oportebat servari, non pollui, Levit. 15, 31. cap. 21, 12. Num. 19. vers. 13. Sacerdotes debebant munditiei & san- ctitati studere, Levit. 21, 8. Per fidem autem pu- rificantur corda nostra, Act. 15. vers. 9. ac sangui- ne Christi fide consperse mundantur conscien- tiae, Ebr. IX, 14. sine qua impossibile est placere Deo, Ebr. XII, 6. Quando Evangelii doctrinam, inquit Apostolus, interprete B. Gerhardo pag. 165. fide recepistis, jamdudum ad CHRISTUM accedere, ac instar vivorum lapidum super ipsum tanquam angularem lapidem aedificari caepistis. Equum igitur est, ut in hac vocatione vestra constanter perga- tis, ac quotidianis in fide profectibus ad Christum ac- cedentes ipsi tanquam vivi lapides magis magisq; su- per eum aedificemini, sicque in vita spirituali majore subinde incrementa capiatis. Ut ergo similitudi- ne extructionis super lapidem vivum profectum in fide vera, ut nempe per ipsam magis cum eo quasi conglutinentur & coalescant fideles, declarat: Ita comparatione Sacerdotum profectum fidelium in sanctitate illustrat, fideles Sacerdotibus, bona ope- ra sacrificiis comparans, quae spirituales Sacerdo- tes per fidem offerre debent.

Informat ita tum de Christo, qui est lapis vivus ab hominibus reprobatus in passione, qua nos re- demit, apud Deum vero electus & honorificatus in fundamenti Ecclesiae constitutione, qua super hunc electum lapidem totam Ecclesiam extruxit Matth. 16, 17. tum de Christianis, qui lapides vivi superaedificati Christo in domum spiritualem ex- truuntur, quique etiam sunt sacerdotium sanctum per Christum ad id uncti, & per Christum hostias ac- ceptabiles Deo offerentes.

Vox προσερχόμενοι redditur à Vulgata acceden- tes, Syrus reddit appropinquastis, innuit continuum accessionis actum, quae fit per fidem, Ebr. XI, 6. ad CHRISTUM, cujus suavitatem gustare di- cuntur: qui est lapis ille vivus, totam Ecclesiae do- mum sustentans, eique firmitatem praestans adver- sus ipsas inferorum portas, Matth. XVI. vers. 18. qui non solum vitam in se ipso habet, Johan. V. vers. 25. 1. Joh. V. vers. 20. imo vita ipsa est, sed etiam lapides super se extructos, hoc est fide si- bi adhaerentes vivificat, Johan. 6. vers. 88. cap. 5. vers. 28. 29. cap. 10. vers. 28. non solum ratione meriti, & acquisitionis, sed etiam ratione efficaciae & applicationis. Dicitur autem ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων ἀποδεδοκιμασμένῳ, quod etsi nonnulli ad omnes extendant reprobos, è Psalmo tamen CXVIII. vers. 22. collato cum Actor. IV. vers. 11. liquet, re- jectionem intelligi in passione CHRISTI fa- ctam à stolidis illis architectis, Sacerdotibus, Scribis & Pharisaeis, conf. hic vers. 7. de reprobis in genere, qui opponuntur aedificantibus sese su- per lapide vivo, & per incredulitatem offen- dunt, deinceps agetur, vers. 78. Porro παρὰ δὲ τῷ θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν dicit ἐξοχικῶς vivum hunc lapi- dem, quod proprie est apud Deum, non ut Vul- gata habet à DEO electum, hoc est, non dile- ctum modo, sed excellentem, quia, phrasi E- braea, electus est praestans, & excellens, 1. Timoth. 5, vers. 21. quod talia in electione libera praefer- ri soleant, Esa. 42, 1. Matth. 22. vers. 48. Ἔντιμον pretiosum, quod apud Deum ipsum sit gemma pretiosissima: super quam unicam gemmam to- tam ta cœlestis Hierosolyma, vere etiam gemmea, sed vigore, & virtute hujus gemmæ ædificata est, Apoc. 21. vers. 19. qui ut uni fundamento in- nituntur duodecim fundamenta, hoc est, Apo- stoli, Ephes. 2. vers. 20. Conf. Matth. 13. vers. 46. & Esa. 54. vers. 11. 12. Qui etsi apud homines reprobatus sit, penes DEUM tamen in pretio habitus. Honorificatus, inquit Lyranus in h. l. est hic lapis in miraculorum operatione, in resurre- ctione, in ascensione, in Spiritus sancti missione. Sed hic præcipue in fundamenti Ecclesiæ constitu- tione honoratus intelligatur. B. Lutherus: Vor Gottes Augen ist der Stein erwählet, und ein aus- erlesen köstlicher Stein, gilt so viel, daß er den Tod hinweg nimmet, Sünde bezahlet, und von der Höllen errettet, dazu das Himmelreich giebt. De di- cto Psalmi quod hic respiciatur, vid. Bibl. Illustr. & conferantur simul loca parallela in Veteri Te- stamento, Esa. 8. vers. 11. 13. cap. 28. vers. 16. Dan. 2. vers. 34. Zachar. 3, 9. & in Novo Matth. 21. vers. 42. Marc. 12, 10. Luc. 20, 17. Actor. 4. vers. 11. Rom. 9. vers. 33. ut & Luc. 2, 34.

## 2:5
Verse 5.

Καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε, οἶκος πνευματικός.] Both ζῶντες, which is repeated here, and πνευματικὸς, as just now θυσίας πνευματικὰς, are, as we have said, significant of the allegory. But the sense is the same as in Eph. 2:20. Among the Hebrews, the Levites were called the stones of the temple, but now individual Christians are stones: they all together are the temple or house of God, 1 Cor. 3:16-17, ch. 5:19, 2 Cor. 6:16, Eph. 2:21, Apoc. 3:12. In the Manuscript it is ἐποικοδομεῖσθε, namely upon Christ the principal stone, nor does the Latin read it otherwise.

It can be taken both in the Indicative and in the Imperative; Erasmus and Hentenius with the Syriac prefer the latter, Beda, Cajetanus, Hesselius, and Estius prefer the former with the Vulgate, who adds this reason with the Syriac: because Peter is engaged in this place in declaring and commending the dignity of Christians, which they share from Christ the author. Therefore, the powers of free will cannot be gathered from this place; the ministers are the builders of the Church, by whom the hearers are built up. Add that here not those to be regenerated but the regenerated are compelled, of whom Beda says: 'He does not want us to be dead stones, but living, so that he may insinuate the effort of good intention or action, by which, with God's grace preceding and accompanying, they ought always to exercise themselves.'

Six reasons can be given for the comparison of the faithful and the stone in a building: 1. From the super-edification, because as the remaining stones are built upon and lean upon the foundational stone: So we are built upon and lean upon Christ by faith, concerning which B. Luther says on this passage: The other stones in the building cannot stand without the foundation stone: Thus we all must stand upon Christ, and acknowledge him as a foundation stone. Therefore we may not boast that the stone must take anything from us, but we must receive benefit from him. For we do not carry him, but he carries us, and sin, death, and hell lie upon him, and everything that we have, so that all this, and whatever strikes us, cannot harm us when we are placed upon the foundation. For when we thus stand upon him, and rely upon him, we must also remain where he is. Just as natural stones must rely upon their foundation stone. 2. From hardness and firmness, which living stones have from the foundation stone, so that it may be able to withstand any attacks of enemies and storms of tempests, Matt. 7, ch. 16, 17. On the Rock, says Bernard, Sermon LXI on the Song of Songs, I am exalted, on the rock I am secure, on the rock I stand firmly, secure from the enemy, safe from a fall; the world trembles, the body presses, the devil lies in wait, I do not fall, for I am founded upon the firm rock. The pious, built up by faith upon Christ, become stony and of stone, that is, they receive strength and firmness from CHRIST. Through true faith, says John Ferus on chapter XVI of Matthew, we are joined to CHRIST, and thus in a way we too are a rock, if it is permitted to speak so. Salmero, disp. XIII on 1 Peter, introduces Peter speaking thus: I have been surnamed Peter, a rock, by CHRIST: And not only am I Peter, but you all are also Peters: Just as from Christ the King, Priest, Shepherd, and Teacher, all the faithful participate in his kingdom, priesthood, pastorate, and teaching office. 3. From the adaptation of stones: Just as a stone must be worked and polished for a building: So we must be adorned by the Holy Spirit, and polished through tribulations, concerning which things are brought forward from St. Ambrose. By blows and pressures, polished stones are fitted to their places, and are arranged by the hands of the craftsman to remain in the buildings that have been erected. 4. From the dimension of stones, which is done according to a plumb line. Whence St. Ignatius in his epistle to the Ephesians: Jesus Christ has founded us upon the rock, as chosen stones, which are fit for the building of GOD the Father, raised on high by Christ, who was crucified for us, using the plumb line of the Holy Spirit, drawn up in faith, and raised from the earth to heaven by love. 5. From the joining of stones. As one stone is glued to another, so it strengthens both itself and its companion and the whole structure. So also one faithful person is joined to another by charity, by which he strengthens and corroborates both himself and his neighbor, and the whole Church, Colossians 3, verse 14. 6. From mutual carrying: Just as the lower stone carries the upper one, and this one the lower and the collateral one: So, as Gregory says in Homily XIII on Ezekiel, in the holy Church each one both carries another, and is carried by another, Galatians 6, verse 2.

Now they are called living stones, the elect, both because they are rendered participants in spiritual life by Christ through faith in him, and because they were not hewn by the hands of men, or chosen for the building by human judgment, but were ordained for this structure by the eternal counsel of God, and because the excellence of the true temple is thus to be shown; which is not built, like that Jerusalem one, with material stones, but with spiritual living stones.

Moreover, the same are called οἶκος πνευματικὸς, because both individual believers are houses of the Lord spiritually, and the totality of the faithful, the Church, is the house of the living God, 1 Timothy 3, verse 15. Augustine in Psalm LXXXVI, as also Bede, refers to the spiritual house, i.e., you are built up upon Christ, that you may be the mystical house of God. But the Greek Codices consistently have οἶκος πνευματικός. For the spiritual house of God is both the universal temple of God, the Catholic Church, and the particular one, each believer, 1 Cor. 3, 16. The Syriac has: Be spiritual temples. Therefore, it is not necessary that we understand the whole Church here, as Cornelius à Lapide and Estius do. For although otherwise stones are not the house itself, in this spiritual building, however, individual believers are, and they are living stones with respect to the whole temple of the Church, and they are the mystical house or temple of God, as Grotius rightly says. For they are also called holy priests.

Ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον.] In the Manuscript εἰς ἱεράτευμα. ἱεράτευμα here signifies the order of Priests, which the passage Exodus 19:6 proves, and Onkelos there, and Revelation 1:6. In the passage of Exodus in Hebrew it is כהנים, in Greek ἱεράτευμα. Formerly they were priests from one part of the tribe; through Christ all are, Rom. 12:1, Phil. 2:17, ch. 4:18, Heb. 13:15, Rev. 1:6, ch. 5:10, ch. 20:6.

In the Old Testament, the priesthood was not only determined for certain persons, but those also had to be anointed with external oil, and they offered external sacrifices. In the New Testament, however, all the faithful are Priests anointed with the oil of the Holy Spirit, to offer spiritual sacrifices, and thus are truly holy. Estius rightly says: Those who are properly called Priests, namely those deputed to offer external sacrifices, are not all holy, that is, endowed with the internal holiness and purity of souls, even while they perform their priesthood, like Hophni and Phinehas, 1 Kings 2, and many others in the old law. But those who pertain to this priesthood of which Peter speaks, unless they are holy, cannot offer the sacrifices proper to their priesthood. But that in the New Testament, besides this spiritual priesthood, there is still another priesthood given, offering external sacrifices, which Estius here contends for with Cornelius à Lapide, can neither be taught from the sacred Scriptures, and is contrary to the Scriptures, which predicted that external sacrifices in the New Testament would cease, and testify that they have ceased, after the unique expiatory sacrifice of the New Testament, foreshadowed by those, succeeded, offered on the altar of the cross for the sins of the whole world: besides which, that there is need for another unbloody oblation detracts from the perfection of the sacrifice of Christ, who offered himself once, and by that one oblation perfected forever those who are sanctified, Heb. X, v. 12, 14. Cornelius à Lapide says that a faithful Layman is a Priest, but a mystical one, 1. because he is a member of the Church, which has true Priests, and of Christ, who is the high Priest; which latter we admit, the former we deny; 2. because by assisting, serving, nourishing, and cooperating with true Priests, he offers a true sacrifice to God in the mass: All of which is unwritten and a copy. 3. because he offers to God the calves of the lips, namely sacrifices of praise, penance, mortification, charity, and other virtues. Thus St. Athanasius explains in his homily on the seed, St. Hilary on Psalm CXVIII, Clement of Alexandria in his oration to the Gentiles, St. Ambrose on Psalm CXVIII, octonary 6; see Origen, Homily IX on Leviticus. Which is correct. 4. because he offers to GOD the passion and death of CHRIST, who made himself a living victim to God on the cross, especially while he receives the holy communion. For then it represents and announces the death of the Lord in reality, as Christ says in Luke 22, verse 19, and Paul in 1 Corinthians 11, 26. 5. Because in heaven He will offer Himself entirely as a sacrifice, as it were, for the perpetual praise of GOD, Apoc. 5, 10. Which we do not disapprove. 6. Because the holy faithful are most closely joined to GOD, as His friends, members of His household, children, and heirs. For thus the princes are called priests most closely joined to King David, 2 Kings (Samuel) 8, last verse. But by this last reason the diverse significations of the word priests are confused, since here only one signification, as always for a single word, can obtain.

Ἀνενέγκαι θυσίας πνευματικὰς.] That is, εἰς τὸ ἀνενέγκαι, in a manner of speaking frequent among us. Spiritual sacrifices, that is, those sacrifices of which the old ones were shadows. These sacrifices, however, are prayers, chastity of the body, and works of mercy. See what has been said by us at Matthew 2, 11, and at the passages of Paul already mentioned. Add that statement of Justin in the dialogue with Trypho: Ὅτι μὲν οὖν εὐχαὶ καὶ εὐχαρισίαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀξίων γινόμεναι, τελεῖαι μόναι καὶ εὐάρεστοί εἰσι τῷ Θεῷ θυσίαι.

Contained here is both a description of the Church, that believers, as living stones, are built by faith upon the living foundational stone Christ into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood to offer spiritual sacrifices, from which it is evident that the Church is properly the assembly of the faithful and the saints: then a silent exhortation to good works: or spiritual sacrifices, for the offering of which the faithful are consecrated in baptism, and anointed with the oil of the Holy Spirit. This is truly a worshipper of GOD, as Lactantius says, lib. VI. Inst. cap. 26, whose sacrifices are meekness of mind, and a life exhibits all these, sacrifices as often as he has done something good and pious.

• Εὐπροσδέκτες τῷ Θεῷ.] The mystical sense of the law of GOD ריח־ניחוח, Levit. I, 9. See what has been said by us Rom. XII, 1. cap. XV, 16. 31.

Διὰ ἰησῦ Χριστῦ.] According to the precept of Christ, as Heb. XIII, 15.

The mystical sense can be understood either regarding the mystical application of bodily sacrifices to spiritual ones, which however has a place not in expiatory sacrifices, but rather in others, e.g., Eucharistic ones, or regarding the different sense of the odor of rest, one in the bodily sacrifices of the Old Testament, another regarding the mystical sacrifices of the faithful: which indeed are not proper to the New Testament, but also had a place under the Old Testament. We deny this double sense, and we judge that the odor of rest brings about the reconciliation of God and the acceptance of sacrifices, which must be affirmed of both, when they are or were offered with true faith, without a duality of sense. Therefore, spiritual sacrifices are pleasing, but through faith in Christ, and thus through and because of Christ apprehended by faith, or his propitiatory sacrifice, which he himself offered to God εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, Ephes. 5, 2. That interpretation διαὰ Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ according to the precept of Christ can neither be proven from a parallel passage, Heb. 13, 15, nor does it suit this. For sacrifices are not pleasing to God according to the precept of Christ, but through Christ: the reason why they are acceptable to GOD is rendered here: to which that gloss does not at all correspond: Namely, they are pleasing and acceptable to God for this reason; not because they are perfect in themselves, but because Christ covers their imperfection with his perfect righteousness, and commends the same to God by his intercession, Apoc. 8, 3. 4. Concerning which Estius in h. l. Through Christ we offer spiritual sacrifices, in so far as he, as our Mediator and Priest, offers them to GOD the Father as if received from us, and commends them by his intercession. Other Scriptures favor this construction. For Heb. 13, it is said thus concerning Christ: Through him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God always, And Apoc. 8. There was given to him (the Angel) much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar. By which Angel Christ is signified. Estius reports there a triple sense, 1. Of Bede, who wishes to look to all these things premised, that through the grace of Christ we are both built up into a spiritual house, and participate in a holy priesthood, and offer sacrifices acceptable to God, 2. Of others, who refer it only to the part 'acceptable to God', 3. Of those who wish to refer it to the word 'offer': The sense of which construction he not undeservedly judges to be almost the same as the preceding. For he says, Christ offers our prayers and other good works to God the Father, because through his merit he makes them pleasing and acceptable to Him.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

Καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε, οἶκος πνευματι- κός.] Tam ζῶντες, quod hic repetitur, quam πνευματικὸς, ut jam mox θυσίας πνευματικὰς, sunt ut diximus signifi- cantia allegoriam. Est autem sensus idem, qui Ephes. II.. vers. 20. Apud Hebræos Levitæ dicebantur lapides templi, at nunc singuli Christiani lapides: Iidem cuncti templum sive domus Dei, 1. Corinth. 3, 16. 17. cap. 5, 19. 2. Cor. 6, 16. Eph. 2, 21. Apoc. 3, 12. In Manuscripto est ἐποικοδομεῖσθε, nempe super Christo lapide principali, nec aliter legit & La- tinus.

Accipi potest & in Indicativo & in Imperativo; hunc mavult Erasmus & Hentenius cum Syro, il- lum præfert cum Vulgata Beda, Cajetanus, Hesse- lius, Estius, qui rationem hanc addit cum Syro; quia versatur hoc loco Petrus in declaranda & com- mendanda dignitate Christianorum, quam à Chri- sto autore participant. Non ergo ex hoc loco vires liberi arbitrii possunt colligi, ædificantes mi- nistri sunt Ecclesiæ, à quibus ædificantur audito- res. Adde quod hic non regenerandi sed rege- niti compellentur, de quibus Beda: non vult nos mortuos lapides, sed vivos, ut conatum insinuet bona intentionis sive actionis, quo præveniente se ac comi- tante Dei gratia exercere semper debeant.

Comparationis fidelium & lapidis in fabrica sex dari possunt rationes, 1. à superædificatione, quia ut lapidi fundamentali reliqui superstruuntur & innituntur: Ita fide nos Christo superstruimur & innitimur, quo de B. Lutherus in hunc locum: Die andern Steine am Bau können nicht ste- hen, ohne auff den Grund-Stein: Also müs- sen wir alle auff Christo stehen, und ihn für einen Grund-Stein erkennen. Darum mögen wir uns nicht rühmen, daß der Stein von uns et- was müsse nehmen, sondern wir müssen von ihm Wohlthat empfahen. Denn wir tragen ihn nicht, sondern er träget uns, und liegt auff ihm Sünde, Tod und Hölle, und alles was wir haben, also, daß uns diß alles, und was uns an- stösset, nicht schaden kan, wann wir auff den Grund gesetzet sind. Denn wenn wir also auff ihn stehen, und uns auff ihn verlassen, so müs- sen wir auch bleiben, wo er ist. Gleichwie sich die natürlichen Steine müssen auff ihren Grund-Stein verlassen. 2. A duritie ac firmi- tudine, quam vivi lapides habent à lapide funda- mentali, ut quosvis hoftium impetus & tempesta- tum procellas sustinere possit Matth. 7. cap. 16, 17. In Petra, inquit Bernhardus Serm. LXI. in Cant. exaltatus, in petra securus, in petra firmiter sto, secu- rus ab hoste, tutus à casu, tremit mundus, premit cor- pus, diabolus insidiatur, non cado, fundatus enim sum supra firmam petram. Pii fide super Chri- stum extructi fiunt petrini ac lapidei, id est, robur ac firmitudinem à CHRISTO accipiunt. Per veram fidem, inquit Joh. Ferus in cap. XVI. Matth. CHRISTO conjungimur, & sic quodammodo & nos petra sumus, si sic licet loqui. Salmero disp. XIII. in 1. Petr. Petrum ita loquentem introducit: Ego à CHRISTO petra Petrus sum cognominatus: Et non tantum ego Petrus sum, sed & vos omnes Petri estis: Quemadmodum à Christo Rege, Sacerdote, Pastore & Doctore omnes fideles de regno ejus & sacerdotio & pastoratu atque doctoratu participant. 3. A lapidum adaptatione: Sicut lapis elaborandus poliendusque est ad fabricam: Ita adornandi su- mus à Spiritu sancto, & per tribulationes polien- di, de quo è S. Ambrosio afferuntur. Tunsionibus, pressuris, expoliti lapides suis aptantur locis, per ma- nus artificis disponuntur permansuri jactis ædificiis. 4. A lapidum dimensione, quæ juxta perpendicu- lum fit. Unde S. Ignatius in epist. ad Eph. Jesus Christus fundavit nos super petram, tanquam lapi- des electos, qui apti sunt ad ædificium DEI Patris elevati in altum à Christo, qui pro nobis crucifixus est, perpendiculo usi Spiritus sancti in fide subducti, & dilectione elevati à terra in cœlum. 5. A lapi- dum coagmentatione. Ut lapis unus conglutina- tur alteri, itaque se & socium & totam structuram firmat. Sic & fidelis unus alteri charitate com- paginatur, qua se & proximum, totamque Eccle- siam firmat & corroborat, Coloff. 3, vers. 14. 6. A mutua portatione: Sicut lapis inferior portat su- periorem, & hic inferiorem ac collateralem: Ita dicente Gregorio homil. XIII. in Ezech. in sacra Ecclesia unusquisque & portat alterum, & porta- tur ab altero, Galat. 6. vers. 2.

Lapides autem vivi dicuntur electi, tum quia à Christo per fidem in ipsum redduntur vitæ spiri- tualis participes, tum quia non sunt cæsi hominum manibus, aut humano arbitrio ad ædificium electi, sed æterno Dei consilio ad hanc fabricam sunt or- dinati, tum quia ita ostendenda præstantia veri templi; quod non ut illud Hierosolymitanum ma- terialibus, sed spiritual. vivis lapidibus exstruitur.

Vocantur autem iidem οἶκος πνευματικὸς, quia & singuli fideles domus sunt Domini spiritualis, & universitas fidelium Ecclesia est domus Dei vi- ventis, 1. Timoth. 3. vers. 15. Augustinus in Psalm. LXXXVI. ut & Beda refert ad domum spiritualem, q. d. super Christum ædificamini, ut sitis domus Dei mystica. Sed Græci Codices constanter ha- bent οἶκ® πνευματικός. Domus enim Dei spiritua- lis est tum universale Dei templum, Catholica Ec- clesia, tum particulare, fidelis quisque, 1. Cor. 3, 16. Syrus habet: Estote templa spiritualia. Non er- go necessum est, ut cum Cornelio à Lapide & Estio Ecclesiam totam hic intelligamus. Etsi enim alias lapides non sint ipsa domus, in hac tamen spiritua- li fabrica singuli fideles sunt, & lapides sunt vivi re- spectu totius templi Ecclesiæ, & domus sunt my- stica vel templum Dei, ut recte Grotius. Nam & Sacerdotes sancti iidem dicuntur.

Ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον.] In Manuscripto εἰς ἱεράτευμα. ἱερά τευμα hic significat ordinem Sacerdotum, quod evincit lo- cus Exod. 19, 6. & ibi Onkelos & Apoc. I, 6. in loco Exodi in Ebr. est כהנים, in Græco ἱεράτευμα. Olim ex una tribus parte erant Sacerdotes per Christum omnes, Rom. 12, 1. Phil. 2, 17. c. 4, 18. Ebr. 13, 15. Apoc. 1, 6. c. 5, 10. c. 20, 6.

In Veteri Testamento non tantum ad certas personas determinatum erat sacerdotium, sed illæ etiam ungendæ erant oleo externo, & offerebant externa sacrificia. In Novo Testamento autem omnes fideles sunt Sacerdotes uncti oleo Spiritus sancti, ad spirituales hostias offerendas, adeoque vere sancti. Recte Estius: Qui proprie Sacerdotes dicuntur, videlicet ad externa sacrificia offerenda deputati, non omnes sunt sancti, id est, interna animorum sanctimonia & puritate præditi, etiam dum suo funguntur sacerdotio, ut Ophri & Phinees, 1. Reg. 2. & alii multi in veteri lege. Qui vero ad hoc, de quo Petrus loquitur, sacerdotium pertinent, nisi sancti sint, hostias suo sacerdotio proprias offerre non possunt. Quod autem in Novo Testamento præter hoc sacerdotium spirituale aliud adhuc detur sacerdotium, externa offerens sacrificia, quod hic Estius cum Cornelio à Lapide contendit, neque è Scripturis sacris doceri potest, & contrarium est Scripturis, quæ sacrificia externa in Novo Testamento cessatura prædixere, ac cessasse testantur, postquam adumbratum per illa unicum Novi Testamenti sacrificium expiatorium successit in ara crucis pro peccatis totius mundi oblatum: præter quod alia oblatione incruenta opus esse, derogat perfectioni sacrificii Christi, qui semel se obtulit, & unica illa oblatione consummavit in perpetuum omnes, qui sanctificantur, Ebr. X. v. 12. 14. Cornelius à Lapide fidelem Laicum Sacerdotem esse, sed mysticum ait, 1. quia membrum est Ecclesiæ, quæ veros habet Sacerdotes, & Christi, qui est summus Sacerdos; quod posterius admittimus, prius inficiamur; 2. quia per veros Sacerdotes eis assistendo, serviendo, alendo, cooperando verum in missa Deo offert sacrificium: Quod totum est ἄγραφον & ἀντίγραφον. 3. quia offert Deo vitulos labiorum, puta hostias laudis, pœnitentiæ, mortificationis, charitatis, aliarumq́; virtutum. Ita explicant S. Athanasius homil. de semente, S. Hilarius in Psalm. CXVIII. Clemens Alexandr. orat. ad gent. S. Ambrosius in Psalm. CXVIII. octon. 6. vide Origenem homil. IX. in Levit. Quod recte se habet 4. quia offert DEO passionem & mortem CHRISTI, qui vivam in cruce se fecit victimam Deo, præsertim dum sumit sacram synaxin. Tunc enim re ipsa repræsentat & annuntiat mortem Domini, ut ait Christus Luc. 22. verf. 19. & Paulus 1. Corinth. 11, 16. 5. Quia in cœlo seipsum totum ad perpetuam DEI laudem in sacrificium quasi offeret, Apoc. V, 10. Quæ non improbamus. 6. Quia fideles sancti DEO sunt conjunctissimi, quasiejus amici, domestici, filii & hæredes. Sic enim Principes Davidi Regi conjunctissimi vocantur Sacerdotes 2. Reg. (Samuel.) 8. vers. ult. Qua vero postrema ratione diversæ vocis Sacerdotes significationes confunduntur, quum hic non nisi unica, ut semper unius vocis, obtinere possit significatio.

Ἀνενέγκαι θυσίας πνευματικὰς.] Id est, εἰς τὸ ἀνενέγκαι loquutione nostris frequente. Θυσίας πνευματικὰς, id est, ea sacrificia, quorum vetera umbræ fuere. Hæc autem sacrificia sunt preces, castitas corporis, opera misericordiæ. Vide quæ à nobis dicta ad Matth. II, 11. & ad dicta jam Pauli loca. Adde Justini illud in colloquio cum Tryphone: Ὅτι μὲν οὖν εὐχαὶ καὶ εὐχαρισίαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀξίων γινόμεναι, τελεῖαι μόναι καὶ εὐάρεστοί εἰσι τῷ Θεῷ θυσίαι.

Continetur hic tum Ecclesiæ descriptio, quod credentes, tanquam lapides vivi, ædificentur fide super lapidem vivum fundamentalem Christum domus spiritualis, sacerdotium sanctum ad offerendum hostias spirituales, unde constat, Ecclesiam proprie esse cœtum fideliũ & sanctorum: tum tacita adhortatio ad bona opera: seu spiritualia sacrificia, ad quæ offerenda fideles in baptismo consecrantur, & oleo Spiritus sancti unguntur. Hic est vere DEI cultor, Lactantio dicente l. VI. Inst. cap. 26. cujus sacrificia sunt mansuetudo animi, & vita innocens, & actus boni, quæ omnia qui exhibet, toties sacrificat, quoties bonum aliquid & pium fecerit.

• Εὐπροσδέκτες τῷ Θεῷ.] Sensus mysticus legis DEI ריח־ניחוח, Levit. I, 9. Vide, quæ à nobis dicta Rom. XII, 1. cap. XV, 16. 31.

Διὰ ἰησῦ Χριστῦ.] Secundum Christi præceptum, ut Ebr. XIII, 15.

Sensus mysticus intelligi potest vel quoad mysti- cam sacrificiorum corporalium ad spiritualia appli- cationem, quæ tamen non in sacrificiis expiatoriis, sed aliis potius, v. g. Eucharisticis locum habet, vel quoad sensum diversum odoris quietis, alium in sa- crificiis corporalibus Veteris Testamenti, alium quoad sacrificia mystica fidelium: quæ vero non Novo Testamento propria sunt, sed etiam sub Ve- teri Testamento locum habuere. Quem geminum sensum negamus, & odorem quietis reconciliatio- nem Dei, & acceptationem sacrificiorum inferre, quæ de utrisque, cum vera fide oblata sunt aut of- feruntur, affirmanda, citra sensus διτλότητα, cense- mus. Grata ergo spiritualia sacrificia, sed per fidem in Christum, adeoque per, & propter Christum fide apprehensum, vel sacrificium ejus propitiatorium, quod obtulit ipse Deo εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, Ephes. 5, 2. Interpretatio illa διαὰ Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ secundum præce- ptum Christi nec è loco parallelo probari potest, Ebr. 13, 15. neque huic convenit. Non enim secun- dum Christi præceptum grata sunt sacrificia Deo, sed per Christum: Causa, cur accepta DEO sint, hic redditur: cui glossa ista minime congruit: Ni- mirum ideo grata & accepta Deo sunt; non quia in se perfecta, sed quia Christus ipsorum imperfe- ctionem perfecta sua justitia tegit, eademque Deo intercessione sua commendat, Apoc. 8, 3. 4. Quo de Estius in h. l. Per Christum offerimus spirituales hostias, in quantum ille, tanquam Mediator & Sa- cerdos noster eas velut à nobis susceptas offert DEO Patri, suaque intercessione commendat. Huic con- structioni favent alia Scripturæ. Nam Ebr. 13. de Christo sic dicitur: Per ipsum ergo offeramus ho- stiam laudis Deo semper, Et Apoc. 8. Data sunt illi (Angelo) incensa multa, ut daret orationibus omni- um sanctorum super altare aureum. Per quem Ange- lum Christus significatur. Refert ibi Estius tripli- cem sensum, 1. Bedæ qui ad cuncta præmissa hæc spectare velit, quod per Christi gratiam & super- ædificemur in domum spiritualem, & sacerdotio sancto participemus, & hostias Deo acceptabiles offeramus, 2. aliorum, qui referunt ad solam par- tem acceptabiles Deo, 3. Eorum, qui referre vo- lunt ad verbum offerre: Cujus constructionis sen- sum pene eundem esse cum præcedenti non im- merito censet. Offert enim, inquit, Christus ora- tiones nostras ac cætera bona opera Deo Patri, quia per suum meritum grata ei facit & accepta.

## 2:6
Vers. 6.

Διότι περιέχει ἐν τῇ γραφῇ.] In the Manuscript ἐν γραφῇ, without the article, holy is understood, which is added Rom. 1, 2. or divinely inspired, as 2. Tim. 3, 16. περιέχει, that is, it is read. See 1. Maccab. 15, 2. 2. Macc. 9, 18. cap. 11, 16. 22. It is, however, a brief expression for περιέχει ἡ περιοχὴ. For the Hebrews are accustomed to understand nouns from the words. Περιοχὴ is some passage in Scripture, Act. 8, 32.

Ἰδὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ἀκρογωνιαῖον, ἐκλεκτὸν, ἔντιμον, καὶ ὁ πισεύων ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ, ὀὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.] Contracted from the Greek of Isa. 28, 16. ἰδὺ ἐγὼ ἐμβάλλω εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιὼν λίθον πολυτελῆ, ἐκλεκτὸν, ἀκρογωνιαῖον, ἔντιμον, εἰς τὰ θεμέλια αὐτῆς, καὶ ὁ πισεύων μὴ καταισχυνθῇ. Where it appears the LXX.

Interpreters did not read badly for כהן, בהור, but also for יהוש they read יבש, and Paul follows this reading also, Rom. 9, 33. The sense is literal according to the Prophet. If any wished to be saved from the ten tribes, they had to flee to Jerusalem as to a fortress, as we said at the place of the Prophet. But there is a more sublime sense in Christ, to whom all must flee who desire to be saved eternally.

With the commentary on the double sense having been otherwise refuted and the opinion of the Prophet vindicated in its own place, we only note here that it is no longer a question here of the ten tribes, but that both counsel and comfort are exhibited to the faithful, which is universal, and pertains to all times and all who are to be saved. For Christ is the Savior of the whole world 1. Joh. IV, 16. B. Gerhard has this concerning it in h. l. page 174. The Prophet prophesies in that chapter both about the destruction of the Israelite kingdom and about the devastation of the kingdom of Judah to be sent upon both because of the most grave sins, but lest they should think that on that account the promise concerning the Messiah would be void, or the Church would utterly perish, he therefore promises that he will send his Son at a defined time, who will be the foundational stone sustaining the whole building of the Church to be gathered from Jews and Gentiles. God also complains in the same place about the incredulity of the Jewish people refusing to depend on Divine promises, and about their vain trust, by which they relied on human and fig-tree defenses. Intending to bring a remedy for both evils, he proposes his infallible decree concerning the promised Son, the Messiah, to be sent into the flesh, in whom, as the foundational stone of the Church to be perpetually preserved, everyone who is to rest by true faith, he pronounces will not be confounded or put to shame. Estius proposes it thus: In Sion, that is, in the Church, which will have its origin on Mount Sion in Jerusalem, I will place Christ the Savior in the place of a foundation, as a corner stone, elect, precious. But it should be known why he is called angular or chief-corner, that by Hebrew phrase princes and leaders among peoples are called the angles of the peoples, as if their foundations and chief supports, as Jud. 20. 1. Reg. 14. Isa. 19. Soph. 1. and 3. CHRIST, therefore, is called the cornerstone of the Church, that is, its primary and principal foundation, because He is its prince and head, strengthening, supporting, and sustaining it by the governance of His Spirit. Furthermore, He is also the cornerstone for this reason, because just as a cornerstone in a building connects two walls together: so He joins in Himself the two peoples, Jewish and Gentile. Cf. Eph. 2:20. This citation by Peter, just as the Pauline one in Rom. 9, refutes the twofold sense of Grotius. For the literal sense, from which alone arguments are sought, has been handed down by these Apostles. Nor were only those who were to live under the New Testament commanded to take refuge in Christ: But just as the address is directed to men under the Old Testament: so it undoubtedly concerned them also in its proper and literal sense. Cf. Is. 65:23 ff. Ps. v. ult. In sum, all the promises of the Old Testament concerning salvation to be obtained through faith in Christ, to which all the Prophets bear witness, as St. Peter teaches, Acts 10:43, concern men of the Old Testament no less than those of the New. Therefore, they are deservedly cited in the New Testament in this way: because the Prophets of the Old Testament did not minister these things to themselves alone, but to us also, as our Apostle testifies, 1 Epist. 1:12, cf. 2 Pet. 3:2.

The words: HE WHO BELIEVES, SHALL NOT MAKE HASTE, as the Hebrew text has it, Estius explained thus: He who shall have believed what I say about the stone being placed in the foundations of Zion, and about salvation to be hoped for through Him, let him not hasten toward the promised thing, impatient of delay, as if it ought to be exhibited immediately, nor if it be deferred, [let him not] cast away his hope, but wait patiently. For he shall not be put to shame, nor shall he be frustrated in the salvation he awaits. But these things do not attain to the sense of the Prophet, neither as regards the subject, who believes, nor as regards the object of faith, nor as regards the predicate. For the subject is not he who believes with simple assent, but, as Peter interprets here and St. Paul in Rom. 9, 33, ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ, which the Vulgate explains as, he who shall have believed in him, and thus he who shall have placed his trust in that cornerstone, that is, Christ. The object of faith is not the mission of Christ, and salvation to be hoped for through him, but Christ himself, not as he was to be sent in time, but as he was placed as a foundation stone by the eternal decree of God revealed here through the Prophet, and by other oracles both of the Old Testament and of the New Testament to that end, that in that living stone, who was rejected by the builders in his passion, but after his resurrection was ordained and made the head of the corner, so that in that one person men might have salvation, just as St. Peter himself interpreted from a comparison of the Scriptures, Acts 4, 10: 11. 12. we all, whoever desire to be saved, may trust, and place our faith solely in that rock of salvation, certain that it is not otherwise than in that name, since no other has been given under heaven, that it is necessary to be saved through faith. Describing the object of such justifying faith, the faith of Abraham the father of believers, and of all those who follow in the footsteps of that faith, he assigned in Romans 4:24-25 that they should believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead, inasmuch as He was delivered for our sins and raised for our justification. The predicate is not: to hasten out of impatience at delay, but as the holy Apostles explained it again, and καταισχυνθῇ, HE SHALL NOT BE ASHAMED, from whose exposition we are taught that the consequent is put by the Prophet for the antecedent: for he who is ashamed hastens, lest he come into view, after the example of our first parents, who hastened to flee from the sight of God, being ashamed by the Divine summons and the conviction of their own conscience. He is not, however, shamefully confounded, nor does he, trembling or in haste, contemplate flight, but he persists intrepid, and can stand in the judgment of GOD, whoever believes in Christ the Savior alone, and adheres to Him and leans upon Him by true faith as upon the rock of salvation. Therefore that foundation stone is truly precious to those who believe. For what can be more precious than this non-confounding, by which, through a customary μείωσιν, the glory and boasting of the faithful is denoted, concerning which Paul says in Rom. 5:2, that through faith we stand in the grace of God, ἑστήκαμεν κ̀ καυχώμεθα ἐπ᾿ ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης τῶ θεῶ, and we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God. Concerning which the blessed Luther on this passage: Weil der heilige Geist saget, daß die nicht zu Schanden werden, die an Christum glauben, giebt er uns zu verstehen, was er im Sinne hat, nemlich daß er das Urtheil schon hat gehen lassen, und beschlossen, daß alle Welt müsse zu Schanden und schamroth werden. Yet he wishes to draw some out from the crowd, so that no one may escape shame, except he who believes in Christ. Thus Christ himself explains it in the last chapter of Mark: He who believes and is baptized will be saved, but he who does not believe will be condemned. B. Gerhardus, p. 177: "He who believes will not be in haste," that is, he will not have need to flee to other remedies, either out of anxiety or trepidation of heart, just as it is said conversely of those who follow another, Ps. 16:4: "They have multiplied their grievous labors, afterwards they have hastened." For those who seek their salvation elsewhere than in Christ, namely in their own works or in other invented Saviors, they fluctuate perpetually, as if uncertain of their salvation, and their end at last is confusion, Phil. 3:19. But those who believe in Christ, in whom alone God has placed our salvation, Acts IV, 12, they are not frustrated of the salvation expected, but most certainly attain it in its own time, Conf. Rom. X, 11. What those things have to do with the Petrine or the Pauline treatment, so that one should not hasten to the promised thing, does not appear, nor will anyone easily teach it. When Salmero duly noticed this, he thought the Prophetic oracle should be expounded thus: He who believes, let him not hasten, namely to obtain the eternal palm of life, because a long way still remains, but let him act patiently, and run to the way of the commandments, which is against the Lutherans, who think that by faith alone and that by itself all things are perfected and completed, which faith indeed is worthy of confusion and illusion. But in the Prophet there is nothing about hastening to the palm of eternal life, which is not prohibited, but rather commended to us by St. Peter 2. Epist. 3, 12. Nor does it conflict with patience, but is joined with it in the same place by the Apostle: Nothing is held there concerning the way of God’s commandments, and St. Peter, just as St. Paul, does not explain it as not hastening toward the goal, but as not fleeing to others than Christ, in whom alone trust is to be placed, and thus they establish the righteousness of Christ alone, and faith in Christ, by which we lean upon him as a living stone, and they promise to those who place their trust in him alone the true and everlasting glory and consistency before God, instead of shameful flight and confusion. Paul furthermore compares the passage of Isaiah, he who shall have believed in him shall not be confounded, Rom. X, 11. 12. with the oracle of Joel: He who shall have called upon the name of the Lord (Jesus, of whom the Apostle treats) (with true faith, or shall have believed in it, for the whole treatment of the Apostle tends to that), shall be saved. So far is it from being the case that placing one’s trust solely in Christ the Savior for the sake of salvation is a faith worthy of illusion and confusion, that, as the Apostle testifies, this one faith delivers us from eternal confusion and ignominy, and brings us eternal salvation and glory. Meanwhile, we do not deny that believers ought to run in the way of God’s commandments, but those good works done according to the commandments of God are the way to the kingdom, not the cause of reigning.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

Διότι περιέχει ἐν τῇ γραφῇ.] In Manuscripto ἐν γραφῇ, si- ne articulo subintellecto ἁγίᾳ, quod additur Rom. 1, 2. aut θεοπνεύσῳ, quomodo 2. Tim. 3, 16. περιέχει, id est, legitur. Vide 1. Maccab. 15, 2. 2. Macc. 9, 18. cap. 11, 16. 22. Est autem brevis locutio pro περιέχει ή̓ περιοχὴ. Nam Ebræi ex verbis nomina solent subintelligere. Περιοχὴ locus aliquis in Scri- ptura, Act. 8, 32.

Ἰδὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ἀκρογωνιαῖον, ἐκλεκτὸν, ἔντιμον, καὶ ὁ πισεύων ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ, ὀὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ.] Contractum ex Græco Esa. 28, 16. ἰδὺ ἐγὼ ἐμβάλλω εἰς τὰ θεμέλια Σιὼν λί- θον πολυτελῆ, ἐκλεκτὸν, ἀκρογωνιαῖον, ἔντιμον, εἰς τὰ θεμέ- λια αὐτῆς, καὶ ὁ πισεύων μὴ καταισχυνθῇ. Ubi apparet LXX.

Interpretes non male pro כהן legisse בהור, sed & pro יהוש legisse יבש & hanc lectionem sequitur etiam Pau- lus, Rom. 9, 33. Sensus κατὰ πόδας apud Prophetam est. Si qui salvi esse vellent ex decem tribubus, illis confugiendum Hierosolyma velut ad arcem, ut ad Prophetæ locum diximus. Sublimior vero sensus in Christo, ad quem confugere debent omnes, qui in æternum servari cupiunt.

Commento de gemino sensu alias profligato & sententia Prophetæ suo loco vindicata, id hic so- lum advertimus, non de decem tribubus hic amplius agi, sed fidelibus & consilium & solatium exhiberi, quod universale sit, & ad omnia tempora, omnes- que salvandos pertineat. Christus enim est Sal- vator totius mundi 1. Joh. IV, 16. B. Gerhardus de eo sic habet h. l. pag. 174. Vaticinatur Propheta in illo capite tum de regni Israëlitici excidio, tum de re- gni Juda vastatione propter peccata gravissima utrique immittendis, sed ne cogitarent propterea promissio- nem de Messia fore irritam, vel Ecclesiam penitus in- terituram, ideo promittit, se Filium suum tempore definito missurum, qui futurus sit fundamentalis lapis totum ædificium Ecclesiæ ex Judæis & gentibus colli- gendæ sustentans. Conqueritur etiam ibidem Deus de incredulitate populi Judaici renuentis pendere à Divinis promissionibus, ac de vana ejusdem fiducia, qua confidebat humanis & ficulneis præsidiis. Utrique malo remedium allaturus proponit infallibile suum decretum de Filio promisso Messia in carnem mit- tendo, in quem velut fundamentalem Ecclesiæ perpe- tuo conservandæ lapidem quisque vera fide recubitu- rus sit, eum non confusum vel pudefactum iri pro- nunciat. Estius id ita proponit: In Sion, hoc est, in Ecclesia, qua ortum habebit in monte Sion in Je- rusalem, ponam loco fundamenti Christum Salvato- rem, ut lapidem angularem, electum, pretiosum. An- gularis autem sive summ-angularis cur vocetur sci- endum, Ebræa phrasi Principes ac primores in popu- lis vocari angulos populorum, quasi fundamenta eo- rum, & sustentacula præcipua, ut Jud. 20. 1. Reg. 14. Esa. 19. Soph. 1. & 3. CHRISTUS igitur dicitur angularis Ecclesiæ lapis, id est, primarium ac princi- pale ejus fundamentum, quia princeps & caput ejus est, Spiritus sui gubernatione eam firmans, fulciens atque sustentans. Deinde etiam ob hoc lapis summ- angularis, quia sicut lapis angularis in ædificio duos inter se parietes connectit: Ita duos populos Judai- cum & gentilem ipse in se conjungit. Conf. Ephes. 2, 20. Duplicem Grotii sensum hæc Petri allega- tio, quemadmodum & Paulina Rom. 9. refellit. Nam ab his Apostolis sensus literalis, ex quo solo argumenta petuntur, traditus est. Nec ad Chri- stum tantum jussi sunt eodem confugere, qui sub Novo Testamento victuri erant: Sed uti compel- latio directa est ad homines sub Veteri Testamen- to: Ita illos sine dubio ea etiam proprio & literali sensu concernebat. Conf. Es. 65, 23. sqq. Psal. v. ult. Summa omnes promissiones Veteris Testamenti de salute per fidem in Christum consequenda, qua de omnes Prophetæ testantur, docente S. Petro, Act. 10, 43. non minus Veteris Testamenti quam Novi homines concernunt. Ideo merito ita in Novo Testamento etiam adducuntur: quia non sibi solum, sed nobis etiam ministrarunt Veteris Testamenti Prophetæ, teste Apostolo nostro, 1. epist. 1, 12. conf. 2. Petr. 3, 2.

Verba: QUI CREDIT, NON FESTINA- BIT, ut Ebræus textus habet, Estius ita exposuit: Qui crediderit, quæ dico de lapide in fundamentis Sion mittendo, & salute per eum speranda, ne fe- stinet ad rem promissam, impatiens moræ, quasi statim ea debeat exhiberi, neque si differatur, spem abjiciat, sed patienter expectet. Non enim pude- fiet, non frustrabitur salute expectata. Sed sensum Prophetæ hæc non assequuntur, neque qua subje- ctum, qui credit, neque qua objectum fidei, neque qua prædicatum. Nam subjectum non est, qui credit simplici assensu, sed interprete Petro hic & S. Paulo, Rom. 9, 23. ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ, quod exponit Vul- gatus, qui crediderit in eum, adeoque qui fiduciam in lapidem illum angularem, hoc est, Christum collocarit. Objectum fidei non est missio Christi, & salus per eum speranda, sed Christus ipse, non qua mittendus in tempore, sed qua positus in lapidem fun- damenti æterna Dei constitutione revelata hic per Prophetam, & alia tum Veteris Testamenti ora- cula, tum Novi Testamenti ea fini, ut lapidi illi vi- vo, qui ab architectis in passione sua reprobatus, at post resurrectionem in caput anguli ordinatus & factus, quo in illo uno homines salutem haberent, quemadmodum ipse S. Petrus e collatione Scriptu- rarum interpretatus est, Actor. 4, 10: 11. 12. omnes, quicunque salvari cupimus, confidamus, & unice in illa salutis petra fidem collocemus, certi; quod non nisi in illo nomine, quum aliud sub cœlo da- tum non sit, per fidem oporteat salvari: Cujusmo- di fidei justificæ objectum, fidem Abrahami Patris credentium, & eorum omnium, qui fidei istius ve- stigiis insistunt, describens, assignavit Roman. IV. v. 6. ultim. quod nempe in eum crediderit, ipsiq́; cre- dere debeant, qui Jesum Dominum nostrum è mor- tuis suscitavit, utpote qui traditus est propter peccata nostra, & resuscitatus propter justificationem nostram. Prædicatum non est; festinare ex impatientia mo- ræ, sed ut iterum S. Apostoli exposuere, & καταισχυν- θῆ, NON PUDEFIET, è quorum ἐκθέσει doce- mur, consequens positum esse à Propheta pro ante- cedente: Nam qui confunditur, festinat, ne in con- spectum veniat, exemplo Protoplastorum, qui fe- stinabant conspectum Dei effugere, utpote pude- facti citatione Divina, & convictione propriæ conscientiæ. Non autem turpiter confunditur, nec fugam tremebundus, aut festinabundus medi- tatur, sed intrepidus persistit, ac in judicio DEI consistere potest, quisquis solum in Christum Sal- vatorem credit, eique vera fide ceu petræ salutis adhærescit, atque innititur. Ideo lapis ille funda- mentalis iis, qui credunt, vere pretiosus est. Quid enim pretiosius esse potest hac non pudefactione, qua per μείωσιν usitatam gloria & gloriatio fidelium denotatur, de qua Paulus Rom. 5, 2. quod per fidem in gratia Dei ἑστήκαμεν κ̀ καυχώμεθα ἐπ᾿ ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης τῶ θεῶ consistamus & gloriemur in spe glo- riæ Dei. De quo B. Lutherus in hunc locum: Weil der heilige Geist saget, daß die nicht zu Schanden werden, die an Christum glauben, giebt er uns zu verstehen, was er im Sinne hat, nemlich daß er das Urtheil schon hat gehen lassen, und beschlossen, daß alle Welt müsse zu Schanden und schamroth wer- den. Doch will er etliche aus dem Hauffen ziehen, also, daß niemand der Schande möge entlauffen, denn der an Christum glaubet. Also leget es Christus selbst aus Marci am letzten: Wer da glaubet und getaufft wird, der wird selig, wer aber nicht glaubet, der wird verdammet werden. B. Gerhardus pag. 177. Qui credit, non festinabit, id est, non opus habebit ad alia remedia confugere vel ex anxietate, vel trepidatione cordis fugere, sicut ex ad- verso de illis, qui alienum sequuntur, dicitur Ps. 16, 4. Multiplicaverunt molestos labores suos, postea accele- raverunt. Qui enim alibi quam in Christo salutem suam quærunt, in propriis scilicet operibus, vel in aliis confictis Salvatoribus, illi perpetuo fluctuant, tan- quam de salute sua incerti, ac eorum tandem finis con- fusio Phil. 3, 19. Sed qui in Christum credunt, in quo solo Deus salutem nostram reposuit, Actor. IV, 12. illi non frustrantur expectata salute, sed eam suo tempo- re certissime consequuntur. Conf. Rom. X, 11. Quid illæ, ne festinet ad rem promissam, ad Petrinam, quid ad Paulinam tractationem faciant, non apparet, nec facile quisquam docebit. Quod cum probe animadvertit Salmero, ita exponendum oracu- lum Propheticum duxit: Qui credit, non festinet, scilicet ad palmam vitæ æternam obtinendam, quia longa adhuc restat via, sed patienter agat, & ad viam mandatorum currat, quod est contra Lutheranos, qui una fide eaque solo putant omnia perfecta & completa, quæ quidem fides digna est confusione & illusione. Sed in Propheta nihil de festinatione ad palmam vitæ æternæ, quæ non prohibetur, sed commendatur potius nobis à S. Petro 2. Epist. 3, 12. nec cum pa- tientia pugnat, sed conjungitur ibidem cum eadem ab Apostolo: Nihil etiam de via mandatorum Dei illic habetur, & S. Petrus, ut & S. Paulus non ex- plicant de non festinando ad metam, sed non con- fugiendo ad alia, quam ad Christum, in quem so- lum fiducia collocanda, adeoque solam Christi justitiam, & fidem in Christum, qua ei ceu lapidi vivo innitimur, statuminant, ac fiduciam in eum solum collocantibus promittunt, hos & ignomi- niosæ fugæ & confusionis veram ac perennem glo- riam ac consistentiam coram Deo. Paulus con- fert insuper locum Esaiæ, qui in eum crediderit, non confundetur, Rom. X, 11. 12. cum oraculo Joë- lis: Qui nomen Domini (Jesu, de quo agit Aposto- lus) invocaverit (vera fide, vel in illud crediderit, eo enim tendit tota tractatio Apostoli, salvus erit. Tantum ergo abest, ut unice fiduciam in Salvato- rem Christum salutis causa collocare fides sit illu- sione & confusione digna, ut teste Apostolo hæc una fides ab æterna confusione & ignominia libe- ret, ac æternam salutem & gloriam nobis afferat. Interim non inficiamur, credentes in via man- datorum Dei debere currere, sed bona illa ope- ra juxta mandata Dei facta via regni, non causa sunt regnandi.

## 2:7
Verse 7.

[Ὑμῖν ὔν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πισεύουσιν.] To you, therefore, who believe, is the honor. For he alludes to that which preceded, ἔντιμον.

Estius acknowledges that this is deduced partly from what preceded, and partly from the word ἔντιμον. From the former, with Bede, in this way: To you therefore who believe, there is honor. That honor, to be sure, that you may not be confounded by him at his coming. But as he himself says, if any man serve me, my Father will honor him. From the derived word, however, in this way: I said that that stone is ἔντιμον, that is, precious, honorable: But you, as living stones, are built upon him, and are joined to him through faith into a spiritual house: Therefore to you also who believe there is honor, namely in the judgment of God: Concerning which honor Paul also says in Rom. II. Glory and peace and honor to every one that worketh good. Thus also Blessed Gerhard from the context: Because those who believe in Christ are not put to shame, Peter infers from this: To you therefore who believe this stone is honor, that is, because by faith you are built upon this stone, therefore shame and ignominy are not to be feared by you, but honor and glory are to be expected. Blessed Luther rendered it precious in this sense: That he is precious both by reason of the estimation of the faithful, and by reason of effect and truth: To those who believe, he is precious; my heart must become glad when I place my confidence and comfort in him. Therefore he says, he is precious to you who believe; that is, you think much of him, for although he is precious and good in himself, he is of no use to me, and does not help me; therefore he must be precious to us, in such a way that he gives us much more precious goods, like a precious gemstone, which does not keep its goods to itself, but breaks them out, and gives all its power from itself, so that I thus have everything that he is. However, the sense is to be sought primarily from the customary meaning of the word τιμὴ, honor, in our judgment, but in such a way that we believe, with B. Luther leading the way, that both explanations can be joined in this manner: To you, however, who believe, honor, that is, glory, is esteemed, and truly precious, as one who truly brings glory to you, just as in contrast to the unbelievers, a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, because they strike against the same in such a way that they fall, which brings them not glory, but shame and perpetual confusion. Interlinear Gloss. in this place. He who believes in Christ will not be put to shame, that is, he will neither blush at his fall in the present, nor will he be empty of reward in the future.

But to the disobedient, the stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner and a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense. It is a construction like that: The city, which I am establishing, is yours. But the Manuscript, according to a more received phrasing, has λίθο̃ς. But I think that in the Syriac, all those things are absent, 'the stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner,' and, and are transferred here from Matt. 21:42, for they do not belong here. But those things which follow are well adapted to the unbelievers, and are in Isaiah 8:13. What is said there about God is here most excellently attributed to Christ. Those who strike against a hard stone are often accustomed to fall heavily and be wounded. The sense is the same in Matt. 21:44, where see the remarks.

The Syriac version cannot prejudice the authentic text; nor is it to be believed that Divine providence has watched more over the rivulets than over the fountain and the original text, which it had destined for the canon of the universal Church. Nor is that description of the stone in this place in vain. For it is taught that even to the unbelievers themselves, that living and elect stone was destined to be the head of the corner, and thus the foundation of faith and salvation, even though by their own fault it became a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense. As for the construction, however, that which pertains can be understood in the customary manner, in this way: But to the unbelievers, the stone which the builders rejected, it has become the head of the corner. Cf. Acts 10:36, 38; 1 John 2:24, 27. Or it must be said that it is a customary Hebraism, which the LXX Interpreters also imitated, Gen. 31:16, Num. 32:4, Josh. 1:3, 1 Kings 6:31, 2. Kings 1:4, to which Grotius's example goes: The city which I am establishing, is yours.

Moreover, Isa. 8:13 is equally said of Christ, and not indeed of God the Father, as it is cited here concerning Christ, and thus it is invincibly inferred from it that Christ is the true God, Jehovah. For he, of whom the Prophet prophesies that he will be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, is Jehovah, the true God, which is clear from the Prophet. But Christ is he of whom the Prophet prophesied that. Therefore, Christ is Jehovah, the true God.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Ὑμῖν ὔν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πισεύουσιν.] Vobis honori est lapis ille. Alludit enim ad id, quod præcessit ἔντιμον.

Illud deduci partim ex eo, quod præcessit, agno- scit Estius, partim ex voce ἔντιμον. Ex illo cum Beda hoc modo: Vobis igitur qui creditis, honor est. Ille nimirum honor, ut non confundamini ab eo in ad- ventu ejus. Sed sicut ipse ait, si quis mihi ministra- verit, honorificabit eum Pater meus. Ex voce autem derivata hoc modo: Dixi, lapidem illum esse ἔντιμον, id est, pretiosum, honorabilem: Atqui vos, tanquam lapides vivi super eo ædificamini, illique coadunamini per fidem in domum spiritualem: Igitur & vobis cre- dentibus honor, scilicet in judicio Dei: De quo honore etiam Paulus Rom. II. Gloria & pax & honor omni operanti bonum. Sic & B. Gerhardus è contextu: Quia illi, qui in Christum credunt, non pudefiunt, ex eo Petrus infert: Vobis igitur credentibus hic lapis est honor, id est, quia fide in hunc lapidem ædificamini, ideo non metuendus vobis pudor & ignominia, sed ex- spectandus honor & gloria. B. Lutherus pretiosum reddidit hoc sensu: Quod & ratione æstimationis fidelium, & ratione effectus ac veritatis pretiosus sit: Denen, die da glauben, ist er köstlich, da muß mein Hertz froh werden, wenn ich meine Zu- versicht und Trost auff ihn setze. Darum sa- get er, köstlich ist er euch, die ihr glaubet; das ist, ihr haltet viel von ihm, denn ob er gleich an ihm selbst köstlich und gut ist, ist er mir doch nicht nütze, und hilfft mich nicht, darum muß er uns köstlich seyn, also, daß er uns viel köstlichere Güter gebe, wie ein köstlich Edelgestein, der sei- ne Güter nicht bey ihm behält, sondern heraus bricht, und gibt alle seine Krafft von sich, daß ich also alles habe, was er ist. Sensus tamen potissi- mum ex usitata significatione vocis τιμὴ honor, nostro judicio, petendus, sed ita, ut censeamus, utramque B. Luthero präeunte, conjungi posse explicationem hoc modo: Vobis autem creden- tibus honor, id est, gloria æstimatur, ac vere pre- tiosus, utpote qui gloriam revera vobis affert, quem- admodum in ἀντιθέσει incredulis lapis offensionis, & petra scandali, quod in eundem ita impingunt, ut corruant, quod ipsis non gloriam, sed ignominiam & confusionem perpetuam affert. Glossa interlin. in h. l. Qui in Christum credit, non confundetur, hoc est, neq́; in præsenti de casu erubescet, neq́; in futuro vacuus erit præmio.

Ἀπειθῦσι δὲ λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ ὀικοδομῦντες, ὗτο̃ς ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας καὶ λίθο̃ς προσκόμματο̃ς, καὶ πέτρα σκανδάλε.] Est constructio, qualis illa: Urbem,quam statuo, vestra est. At Manuscriptus secundum locutionem receptiorem λίθο̃ς. Sed recte puto inSyriaco abesse illa omnia, λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ ὀικοδομῦντες, ὗτο̃ς ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφα- λὴν γωνίας, καὶ, & translata huc ex Matth. 21, 42. neque enim huc pertinent. Sed bene aptantur incredulis ea, quæ sequun- tur, & sunt apud Esaiam VIII, 13. Quod ibi de Deo dicitur, id Christo hic optime tribuitur. Qui in durum lapidem im- pingunt,graviter cadere sæpe & vulnerari solent. Sensus idem Matth. XXI, 44. ubi dicta vide.

Syriaca versio non potest præjudicare textui au- thentico; neque credendum est, Divinam provi- dentiam magis pro rivulis, quam pro fonte ac textu originario, quem in canonem Ecclesiæ universalis destinarat, vigilasse. Neque frustranea est illa la- pidis descriptio hoc in loco. Nam docetur ita etiam incredulis ipsis lapidem illum vivum & ele- ctum κεφαλὴν γωνίας destinatum esse, adeoque fundamentum fidei & salutis, tametsi culpa ipso- rum factus sit lapis offendiculi & petra scandali. Quoad constructionem autem subintelligi potest more consueto illud, quod attinet, h. m. Incredulis vero lapidem, quem reprobarunt ædificantes, ille factus est in caput anguli. Conf. Actor. 10, 36. 38. 1. Joh. 2, 24. 27. Vel dicendum, Ebraismum usita- tum esse, quem imitati etiam sunt LXX. Interpre- tes, Gen. 31, 16. Numer. 32, 4. Jos. 1, 3. 1. Reg. 6, 31. 2. Reg. 1, 4. quo abit exemplum Grotii: Urbem quam statuo, vestra est.

Cæterum Esa. 8, 13. æque id de Christo dicitur, non vero de Deo Patre,uti hic de Christo id addu- citur, adeoque ex eo Christum esse verum Deum, Jehovam, invicte colligitur. Nam is, de quo Pro- pheta vaticinatur, quod sit futurus lapis offendicu- li, & petra scandali, est Jehovah verus Deus, quod è Propheta liquet. Atqui Christus est is, de quo Propheta id vaticinatus est, teste Apostolo. Ergo Christus est Jehovah verus Deus.

## 2:8
Verse 8.

Who stumble at the word, being disobedient. It is the present for the future. Not wishing to believe in the Word of the Gospel, they will stumble most gravely, that is, they will bear the most grave punishments, by the destruction of the city and the temple, by captivities, by exiles, and finally by contempt among all. See James 5:1.

These do not immediately sound of punishment, much less precisely the destruction of the city and other things listed here, nor do they concern the Jews uniquely; but just as believers in general of all times are understood when promise is made to them not of confusion, but of honor and glory; so the disobedient or rather the unbelieving, which the Greek word imports, are designated as all in general, such as, however, the Jews were in the highest degree, for whose sake we do not doubt that these things were specially predicted, Rom. 9:32, 33. Yet that fault, that they strike against Christ the foundational stone, and are offended and scandalized in him, carries with it punishment, and that most eternal, for he who does not believe is already judged, because he does not believe in the name of the Only-begotten Son of God, John 3:15. He who does not believe is condemned, Mark 16:17, concerning which punishment see Matt. 21:44.

To which they were also appointed. For this, the unbelievers were destined by God, that they might strike most gravely, that is, that they might bear the hardest punishments of their unbelief. For τίθεσθαι, to set, is often to ordain, to destine, as John 15:16, Acts 13:47. Thus, he set them for wrath, 1 Thess. 5:9. The Syrian in this place has 'they are designated.' The Arab has 'they are constituted': namely, by the Divine decree, which is in Daniel and Malachi.

It is not a question, as we have said, of punishments here in the immediate sense. Because of the variety of words in the Latin text, since the Vulgate reads IN WHICH, Bede IN WHAT, as in the Greek, and the translation of the Latin, AND THEY DO NOT BELIEVE, diverse explanations have arisen, which Estius reports. The first is: And they do not believe (the Word of the Gospel) to which they were placed to be received by faith: To which Estius opposes that in the Greek it is ἀπειθοῦσι, and 'word' (λόγος) is of the masculine gender, but the relative is neuter. For which reason Estius also disapproves of the other sense of someone who refers the relative to the stone: for 'stone' (λίθος) is also masculine. Others explain 'to which', that is, that they might believe the Evangelical sermon, they were prepared and instructed through the Mosaic law, like Lyranus, Rickelius, Cajetanus, Erasmus, which sense Estius notes coincides with the first; nor can the particle 'in which' be referred to the Word 'believe', which does not precede in the Greek, since it is written ἀπειθοῦντες, 'disbelieving'. Therefore, fourthly, Estius explains it in this way: 'to which', that is, that they might stumble at the Word, and not believe, they were placed and ordained by God, namely, by His permitting it, on account of their preceding sins, and on account of His own glory, which He prepares for Himself from their just condemnation. He says that this sense seems genuine to him, and is brought forward by Didymus, Oecumenius, Gagnejus, Salmeron, Lorinus, and Franciscus Lucas. But although in a certain respect those things can be admitted regarding the judicial will, nevertheless that εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν is rightly referred to the preceding verse: ὑμῖν οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν, as also to the things above, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ, because even the infidels were placed for this, that they might believe, and that glory might be theirs, so that they too, as living stones, might be built upon the foundation through faith, and not be put to shame, namely, regarding God's counsel, intention, and antecedent will, as also regarding the calling through the Gospel. Others, however, through infidelity stumble at the Word. With which explanation of Holy Scripture, Luke 7:30, Matthew 23:36, 1 Timothy 2:4, Acts 13:46 easily agree, as do several others, as far as the matter itself is concerned, even if they differ in the manner of explaining it. In which manner also Cornelius à Lapide has interpreted it; that is to say, they were placed to believe in Christ, and yet they do not believe, because they do not wish to believe, bringing forward as being of the same mind Bede and Lyranus, which sense not even Calvin himself rejects: 'Commonly,' he says, 'they interpret that they were placed to believe, because the promise of salvation was destined for them. But the other sense can equally well fit, that they were ordained to incredulity.' And afterwards: 'But if, however, the former exposition is more pleasing, it is a vehement reproach: for thence Peter exaggerates the incredulity of the people chosen by God, because they rejected the salvation peculiarly ordained for them.'

If, however, anyone should contend at all that these things must be referred to what immediately precedes, it is still not necessary for us to concede that those unbelievers who stumble at the word of the Gospel are placed by God for that purpose, that is, predestined by GOD, in order that they might stumble, as Piscator contends. For this was not added by Peter. Therefore, this sense is rendered: To which wicked work they were directed, as Oecumenius explains, because by their own voluntary malice they were established in that wicked work. Salmero on this passage: This position, he says, is voluntary: they were placed by themselves. Who, asks the Calvinist Aretinus, placed them so that they were vessels of wrath fashioned for destruction? Certainly not GOD, who is the author of good and of order, not of evil or of disorder, but Satan placed such ones, and their innate malice. To which pertains that statement of Augustine on the predestination of GOD, chapter 2. Above all, it is a sin to say that GOD predestines anything except what is good. Likewise: Behold, the unhappy man is bound to death, not by the predestination of GOD, but by his own offense. For although predestination precedes offense in time, offense nevertheless precedes predestination in effect. And Fulgentius, book 1 to Monimus: GOD could never have predestined a man to that which He Himself determined both to forbid by commandment, and to wash away by mercy, and to punish by justice. GOD has not placed us into wrath, says the Apostle, 1 Thess. 5:9, but into the acquisition of salvation. Wherefore, the gloss of Beza, that some were created for this purpose, that they might stumble, is to be detested. But the fabrication of those who dared to insert the same into the Latin Bibles, published at Frankfurt am Main in the year '91 of the previous century, is execrable, in this way: To those who stumble at the word, being disobedient, for which they were also created. Hemmingius refutes Beza under the name of a certain new interpreter: Besides the fact, he says, that he translates ἐτέθησαν as 'WERE CREATED,' he does violence to this passage against the nature of the Greek word. For the Apostle said above that this stone, CHRIST, had been rejected by the builders, which would by no means have been true if this stone had not been placed before them. We now pass over the explanation of those who, referring the pronoun to λόγον, apply a grammatical rule here: that the neuter gender is sometimes used for the masculine when the discourse is about a person; and by λόγον they understand with Drusius the λόγον ὑποστατικὸν, or with the Syrian they interpret it in this way: Because they do not acquiesce to the Word, for which they were placed. See B. Glassius, Grammat. S. book III, tract I, can. XXI.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

Οἱ προσκόπτυσι τῷ λόγῳ ἀπειθῦντες.] Est præsens pro futuro. Nolentes Verbo Evangelii credere, gravissime impin- gent, id est, gravissimas pœnas ferent, excidio urbis ac tem- pli, captivitatibus, exiliis, contemptu denique apud omnes. Vide Jac. 5, 1.

Non pœnam hæc immediate sonant, nedum præ- cise excidium urbis & alia hic recensita, nec Judæos unice concernunt; Sed quemadmodum credentes in genere omnes omnium temporum intelligun- tur, cum illis promittitur non confusio, sed honor & gloria; ita inobedientes vel increduli potius,quod vox Graeca importat, omnes in universum desi- gnantur, quales tamen vel maxime Judaei fuere, quorum causa specialiter haec praedicta esse non dubitamus, Rom. 9, 32. 33. Culpa tamen illa, quod impingant in Christum lapidem fundamentalem, & offendantur ac scandalizentur in illo, secum tra- hit poenam, eamque maxime aeternam, Qui enim non credit, jam judicatus est, eo, quod non credat in nomen Filii Dei Unigeniti, Joh. 3, 15. Qui non cre- dit, condemnatur, Marc. XVI, 17. de qua poena Matth. XXI, 44.

Εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν.] In hoc a Deo increduli sunt desti- nati, ut gravissime impingant, id est, durissimas ferant incre- dulitatis suae poenas. Est enim τίθεσθαι שׂוּם saepe ordinare, destinare, ut Joh. 15, 16. Actor. 13, 47. Sic ἔθετο εἰς ὀργὴν, 1. Thessal. 5, 9. Syrus hoc loco סים, designati sunt. A- rabs נצו Constituti sunt: nempe decreto Divino, quod est apud Danielem & Malachiam.

Non agitur, ut diximus, hic de poenis, sensu im- mediato. Propter varietatem verborum in Latino textu, quum Vulgata legat IN QUO, Beda IN QUOD, ut in Graeco, & translationem Latini, NEC CREDUNT, diversae enatae sunt explica- tiones, quas refert Estius. Prima est: Nec credunt (Verbo Evangelii) ad quod fide suscipiendum positi sunt: Cui opponit Estius, quod in Graeco sit ἀπει- θοῦσι, & λόγος sit generis Masculini, Relativum au- tem neutrum. Quo nomine etiam alterum sen- sum cujusdam, qui relativum refert ad lapidem, im- probat Estius: nam & λίθος masculinum est. Alii exponunt ad quod, id est, ut crederent Evange- lico sermoni, praeparati erant & instructi per legem Mosaicam, ut Lyranus, Rickelius, Cajetanus, Era- smus, quem sensum cum primo coincidere monet Estius; nec particulam in quod referri posse ad Ver- bum credere, quod in Graeco non praecessit, quum habeatur ἀπειθοῦντες diffidentes. Proinde quarto Estius exponit hoc modo, ad quod, id est, ut offen- dant in Verbum, & non credant positi, & ordinati à Deo sint, videl. permittente, propter eorum peccata praecedentia, & propter gloriam suam, quam ex illu- rum justa condemnatione sibi parat. Quem sensum sibi videri germanum ait, afferrique à Didymo, Oe- cumenio, Gagnejo, Salmerone, Lorino, & Francisco Luca.Sed quanquam certo respectu ista quoad vo- luntatem judiciariam admitti possint, recte tamen illud εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν refertur ad versum praece- dentem: ὑμῖν οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν, ut & ad su- periora, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυν- θῇ, quod & infideles positi ad id sint, ut credant, & ut ipsis sit gloria, ut & ipsi ceu lapides vivi superaedifi- centur fundamento per fidem, nec confundantur, sci- licet quoad DEI consilium, intentionem, ac volun- tatem antecedentem, ut & quoad vocationem per Evangelium. Alii vero per infidelitatem impin- gunt in Verbum. Cum qua explicatione Scriptu- rae sacrae consentanea facile Luc. 7, 30. Matth. 23, 36. 1.Tim. 2, 4. Act. 13, 46. facile alii nonnulli con- gruunt, quantum ad rem ipsam, etsi modo expli- candi discrepent. Quo pacto & Cornelius à Lapide interpretatus est; q. d. Positi sunt ad credendum in Christum, nec tamen credunt, quia credere nolunt, ad- ducens sibi ὁμοψήφους Bedam & Lyranum, quem sensum nec ipse Calvinus reprobat: Vulgo, inquit, interpretantur, quod fuerint positi ad credendum, quia illis destinata erat salutis promissio. Sed alter sensus PEREQUE quadrare potest, quod ad incre- dulitatem ordinati fuerint. Et postea: Quod si ta- men prior expositio magis arridet, vehemens expro- bratio est: Nam inde Petrus incredulitatem populi à Deo electi exaggerat, quod salutem peculiariter sib i ordinatam respuerit.

Si vero omnino quis contendat, ad proxime antecedentia haec referenda esse, non tamen opus est, ut concedamus, positos ad id, ut of- fendant, esse à Deo, quemadmodum Piscator con- tendit, incredulos illos, qui ad sermonem Evan- gelii offendunt, ad hoc ipsum esse positos, id est, à DEO praedestinatos. Non enim hoc à Petro additum. Hic ergo sensus redditur: Ad quod nefandum opus toti sunt directi, ut Oecume- nius explicat, quod sua voluntaria malitia in il- lud nefarium opus sint constituti. Salmero in h. l. Est haec, inquit, positio voluntaria: positi sunt à seipsis. Quis illos, inquit Aretins Calvinista, sic posuit, ut essent vasa irae ad interitum coa- gmentata? Non certe DEUS, qui autor boni est, & ordinis, non mali aut ἀταξίας, sed Satan tales posuit, & innata malitia. Quo facit illud Au- gustini de praedest. DEI, cap. 2. Imprimis nefas est dicere, DEUM aliquid, nisi bonum, praedesti- nare. Item: Ecce homo infelix alligatur morti, non per DEI praedestinationem, sed per suam of- fensionem. Quamvis enim praedestinatio offensio- nem praecurrat tempore: Offensio tamen praedesti- nationem praecedit effectione: Et Fulgentii l. 1. ad Monim. Nunquam DEUS ad hoc hominem po- tuit praedestinare, quod ipse disposuit & praecepto prohibere, & misericordia diluere, & justitia pu- nire. Non posuit nos DEUS in iram, inquit Apostolus 1. Thessal. V. vers. 9. sed in acquisitio- nem salutis. Quapropter detestanda est Beza- nae glossa, quosdam ad hoc conditos, ut offenderent. Execrabile vero factitius est eorum, qui eandem Bibliis Latinis, Anno XCI. superioris seculi Francofurti ad Moenum editis, inserere ausi sunt, hoc modo: His, qui offendunt ad sermonem in- morigeri, ad quod etiam conditi fuerunt. Refel- lit Bezam sub nomine novi cujusdam interpre- tis Hemmingius: Praeter id, inquit, quod ἐτέθη- σαν vertit, CONDITI SUNT, contra vocis Graecanicae naturam, vim facit huic loco. Nam supra dixit Apostolus, hunc lapidem CHRISTUM fuisse ab aedificantibus reprobatum, quod nequa- quam verum fuisset, nisi hic lapis his fuisset abla- tis antèn. Mittimus jam illorum explicationem, qui ad λόγον referentes pronomen, hic applicant regulam Grammaticam: Neutrum genus pro Mas- sculino quandoque usurpari, quando de persona ser- mo est: & per λόγον intelligunt cum Drusio λό- γον ὑποστατικὸν, aut cum Syro interpretantur hoc modo: Quod non acquiescant Verbo, in quod po- siti sunt. Vid. B. Glassius Grammat. S. libr. III. tract. I. can. XXI.

## 2:9
Verse 9.

Ὑμεῖς δὲ γένος ἐκλεκτὸν.] See above c. 1, 1. You have the very words γένος ἐκλεκτὸν in Isaiah 43:20.

It is called an elect race not in a general sense, as any who are called to the kingdom of grace are called elect, Deut. 3:37, ch. 7:6, ch. 10:15, ch. 14:2, which also seems to have a place in Isaiah 43:20, but in a more special sense regarding those elect to the kingdom of glory, which the remaining titles confirm, or if they are taken as referring to the whole assembly of the Church, it is nevertheless certain that they are attributed to them by reason of the better part, just as in the Scriptures that bride of Christ, Cant. 4:10, Isa. 61:10, John 3:29, is called inwardly adorned and glorious, Psalm 45:14, all beautiful and without spot, Cant. 4:7, holy and blameless, Eph. 5:27, the body of Christ, 1 Cor. 12:24, Eph. 1:29, ch. 4:16, the spiritual house of God, 1 Tim. 3:15, Heb. 3:6, 1 Pet. 3:6, etc.

Βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα.] They are ἱεράτευμα, as above in verse 5.
