The Vulgate wrongly rendered: When they were waiting for the patience of God, since in the Greek it is singular, was waiting, and the nominative is μακροθυμία, which reading Cornelius acknowledges to be plain and appropriate, and here Estius puts the Vulgate after: It is clearly likely that an error crept into the Vulgate version, so that for that which the Interpreter translated from the Greek, the patience of God was waiting, it was written by the unlearned, they were waiting for the patience of God. And indeed in the Roman Missal corrected by Clement the Eighth in the epistle for the Friday of Easter week it is read the patience of God was waiting. In which way Jerome and Augustine read: likewise Idacius the Bishop in a book written against Varimedus, and indeed among the more recent ones Dionysius the Carthusian. His commentary also signifies not obscurely that Bede read it in that way. But the patience of God is said to wait, because God patiently waits, in the way the Apostle speaks of him here in the 2nd epistle c. III. He acts patiently for your sake. Otherwise to say that men wait for God's patience is neither customary in the scriptures nor does it have a convenient sense. Where he also refutes Erasmus: Erasmus wrongly translates it passively as 'was awaited,' although certain others have imitated this. For the Greek verb ἐκδέχεσθαι or ἀπεκδέχεσθαι or the simple δέχεσθαι, which Erasmus testifies is found in certain codices, even if it is middle in voice, is nevertheless always taken actively, as are many others of that kind.

How much less will Salmeron's opinion be able to be admitted in this place concerning the Gentiles saved by implicit faith, for whom Christ, coming to the underworld immediately after his death, supplied what was lacking in their faith, along with Anastasius of Antioch (who flourished at the time of the VI Synod) in his Odegos, asserting that Plato was saved and was among the first who had believed in Christ at his descent into the underworld, which Bellarmine refutes: or even that of Cajetan, that Christ, descending into the underworld, preached fruitfully to those who had been incredulous in the time of Noah, since they had trusted in the goodness of God, which Lorinus refutes here: How did they believe, who did not believe Noah preaching in the name of God? Which errors of the Papists are not far from the heresy of those who, in Philastrius, heresy 121, and Augustine, On Heresies, no. 79, asserted that the spirits of the impious were converted by the preaching of Christ descending into the underworld and were liberated from hell, which with Augustine and Epiphanius, heresy XLVI, Gregory Nazianzen, oration XIII, Gregory the Great, book VI, epistle 179, and Bede in this place of St. Peter, overthrow. He opposes to those incredulous ones the souls that were saved. He implies, therefore, that those others were damned, whom he also affirms to be shut up in hell, from which no liberation is given. Therefore Bellarmine, silently criticizing Salmeron, says: In Christ's descent into hell, he says, not one soul of the damned was liberated to gehenna.

Εἰς ἧν ὀλίγαι, τοῦτἔςιν ὀκτὼ ψυχαὶ διεσώθησαν δι' ὕδατό) Eight, that is, Noah, his wife, three sons, three daughters-in-law, Gen. VI. 18. See also 2 Pet. II. 5. Ψυχαὶ, that is, persons, as Acts II. 41, VII. 4.

Arias Montanus understands those eight souls in the ark as the spirits shut up in prison, because the ark was as it were a prison; but Peter distinguishes the spirits in prison and the eight souls in the ark; he says the former were unbelievers, and thus makes them, as condemned to prison, a type of the damned, but he establishes that the latter believed and, saved through the ark, are a type of the saved through baptism.

Δι ὕδατος.] That is, when they were in the waters. You have Διὰ for ἐν in Rom. IV. 12. See what we said there.

A more convenient passage for that meaning is 2 Pet. III. 5. The earth consists δι' ὕδατος, in the midst of the waters. The sense is, according to Blessed Gerhard, they were saved in water, that is, notwithstanding the water of the flood, just as 1 Tim. II. 15, the woman shall be saved διὰ τεκνογονίας, in the childbearing, that is, notwithstanding the same. So also Acts XIV. 22, διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων, we must enter into the kingdom of heaven through many tribulations; that is, tribulations cannot hinder salvation. See 2 Cor. VI. 8, Gal. IV. 13. Nevertheless, the more common meaning could be retained in this place, that those eight souls were saved δι ὕδατος, through water. For if they had remained on land, they would have perished. But they were saved not simply through water, but in the ark. For the ark floated upon the waters. Thus the analogy is more elegant. For we are saved δι ὕδατος, through water, not simply, but as we are washed in the Church from sins through baptism, and pass through the waters of baptism into the harbor of eternal life.

Latin:

Vers. 20. Ἀπειθήσασί ποτε, ὅτε ἅπαξ ἐξεδέχετο ἡ τῦ Θεῦ μακροθυμία ἐν ἡμέραις Νῶε, κατασκευαζομένης κιβωτῦ] Quales animi olim Noæ temporibus non obtemperarunt. Loquitur quasi iidem fuissent, & fuerant iidem Spiritus sive animi, non ἀριθμῷ, ut Aristoteles loquitur, sed ge- nere, id est, animi pariter Deo inutiles, illi scilicet, qui Noæ prædicationi non crediderunt. Homines à Deo planè ab- alienati Noæ non crediderunt, Christo crediderunt. Vide de loquendi modo non dissimili, quæ diximus libr. II. de Ju- re Belli & Pacis IX. 3. in textu & in annotatis. Expectavit e- os Dei patientia, quam diu struebatur arca per annos CXX. Vide Ebr. XI. 7. Vox ἀπεκδέχομαι non infrequens nostris scriptoribus. Vide Rom. VII. 9. VIII. 23. 1. Cor. I. 7. Gal. V. 5. Phil. III. 20. Ebr. IX. 28.

Commentarius hic verè novus, & inauditus est. Nam quod ad Hieronymum in Esaiam jam provo- cat, debuisset locum vel caput designare. Certi au- tē omnino fumus, tam mirabilem explicationem apud Hieronymum non reperiri. Affinis tamē vide- tur Socini glossa, unde fortè hæc desuta, amat enim Grotius in posterioribus Socinizare; in explicat. quorundam locorum Script. ita habet Socinus de h. l. p. 113. (quæ explicationes adjectæ sunt explica- tioni primæ part. 1. c. Joh. I. Factum est enim, ut li- cet is propter infirmitatem carnis necatus fuerit, & mortem gustaverit, divina tamen vi atq; potentia ad immortalem vitam postmodum sit restitutus. Per e- andem vero divinam vim atque potentiam, cum hinc ad Patrem profectus esset dimissis per universum orbē discipulis, & ministris suis, qui tantam ejus adversus mortem victoriam prædicarent, & palam testaren- tur, eorum etiam hominum mentibus & animis clare concionatus est, & veritatem patefecit, qui malitia, & ignorantia vi, quodam quasi carere, tan- quam ire Dei captivi detinebantur, & contumaces fuerant aliquando. Quod non secus accidit, atque cum ætate Noæ Dei lenitas, atque clementia hominum con- tumacium resipiscentiam expectaret, quos arca, quæ ab ipso Noe ex divino præscripto construebatur, ipso- rum officii, & divini quod imminebat supplicii, satis admonebat. Quam Socini glossam eodem ferè, quo Grotius interpolavit modo Schlichtingius, in comment. in h. l. Christus per Spiritum S. profectus est, quatenus illum à Patre acceptum, ipse in cælis ma- nens, sui loco misit. Prædicavit autem per eundem Spi- ritum, quatenus Apostolos suos illo instruxit, qui illo afflati & instructi Evangelium prædicarunt. Et por- ro: Per Spiritum Spiritibus prædicatur, id est, animis hominum, quorum carcer spiritualis est carcer. Neque enim alio in carcere Spiritus esse possunt, quam in spi- rituali: qui carcer quid aliud est, quam peccatum, & quæ peccatum consequitur damnatio? Addit: Eos, qui- bus Christus prædicavit, inobedientes aliquando, sci- licet in diebus Noë fuisse, quod iidem essent genere, itidem Spiritus in carcere, itidem peccatores damna- ti, non autem iidem numero. Affine etiã videri que- at Joh. Hesselij de Lovanio Commentum, qui exi- stimiat vocationem gentium per prædicationem A- postolicã à priori hic describi, quia gẽtes infideles à Prophetis describantur tanquam vincti, obtene- brati, vectibus ferreis, & portis æreis conclusi Esa. XLII. 7. c. XLIX. 7. In hac autem Grotiana inter- pretatione hæc potissimum desideram, 1. quod per Spiritum intelligat Spiritum S. quum oppositio car- nis & suppositum vel persona Christi satis doceat, nomen Spiritus potius de Divinitate Christi acci- piendum esse. 2. Quod de Christi Spiritu post ζωο- ποίησιν ipsius factum dicit Apostolus, ad Apostolorum tempora rejicit Grotius post ascensionem Christi. 3. Ordine sese consequuntur juxta S. Petrum passio & mors Christi, ejus vivificatio, & ad Spiritus in car- cere inferni profectio vel descensus ad inferos, resur- rectio, profectio vel ascensio in cælum, sessio ad dex- tram Dei & vi ejusdem subjectio Angelorum, quem- admodũ ista in symboli Apostolici articulo secun- do sese consequi notissimum est. 4. Gentium voca- tio nō excipit statim vivificationem Christi, sed se- quuta est post resurrectionem & ascensionem ejus in cælum. 5. Quod Christo vel Christi Spiritui tri- buitur à S. Petro, id Apostolis tribuit Grotius. 6. S. Petrus loquitur de Spiritibus in carcere, Grotius de animis hominum in corpore. Quod ubi minus con- gruere visum est Schlichtingio, ita carcerem non de corpore, sed de peccato, & de damnatione nova σχε- βλότητι interpretatus est. Nam & peccatum, inqui- ens, animi carcer est, nõ corporis & damnationis carce- re etiam extinctis corporibus, Spiritus attinetur. Sed ubi in S. literis peccatũ carcer animi dicitur? Rom. XI. 22. sub incredulitatem quidem Deus omnes con- clusisse dicitur. Sed peccatum φυλακὴν aut carcerem non dicit Apostolus. Et num qui extinctis corpori- bus damnationis carcere continebantur, ad pœniten- tiam & remissionem peccatorum vocati sunt præ- conio Apostolorum 7. Petrus loquitur de incredu- lis tempore Noæ, Grotius de incredulis tempore Novi Testamenti, similibus illis, qui tempore Noæ vixere. 8. Petrus de eorum Spiritibus, quibus Noah olim prædicavit, Grotius de diversis, fingens Petrum de diversis loqui, quasi iidem fuissent. Quod est affingere Petro orationẽ min9 congruam, ut moderatissime vocem 9. Petrus de Spiritibus eorum, qui in incredu- litate mansere: Grotius de illis, qui inutiles Deo & increduli fuere quidem aliquando (sub gentilismo nēpe) postea autem Christo crediderunt 10. Petrus de prædicatione illis facta, qui ob eam non creditam damnati, & in carcere infernali conclusi sunt, Gro- tius de præconio per fidem suscepto, illis facto, qui salvati sunt Christo credentes.

Enjedinus τελείαν ςιγμὴν, exemplari aliquo fre- tus, post dictionem aliquando fingit: Et cætera ver- ba per interpositam particulam SICUT disjungit, h.m. gentes olim fuisse immorigeras, sub Vet. Testam. & tempore Christi: Sicut in diebus Noæ. Sed illa SI- MILITUDINIS vox nuspiam in ullo codice ap- paret; nec admitti potest per relationem vocularũ ὅτε, πότε, quæ nullam interpunctionem perfectam patiuntur; sed incredulos aliquando fuisse Spiritus, quando scilicet expectabat eos Dei longanimitas, docent tẽpore Noæ. Quando semel, inquit Schlich- tingius, sic loqui solemus, cum aliquid aliquando eve- nisse narramus. In diebus Noæ: Exprimit, quando hæc Dei expectatio facta sit, nempe tum cum viveret Noæ. Manifestum ergo est, ab Enjedino & à Grotio in sensum prorsus alienum detorqueri Petrinam o- rationẽ. Ne dicam de collatione loci Mosaici, quæ hic à Grotio instituitur, alienissima & detorsione perversissima; qua de ad Genesin in comment. & Bibl. Illustr. actum.

Quod ad genuinam S. Apostoli mentem, expli- cant eandem nonnulli de profectione & prædicatione tempore Noæ facta à Spiritu Christi, quo pacto Be- da: Qui nostris temporibus in carne veniens iter viæ mundo prædicavit, ipse etiam ante diluvium eis, qui tunc increduli erant, & carnaliter vivebant, Spiritus veniens prædicavit. Ipse autem per Spiritum S. erat in Noe, cæterisque, qui tunc fuere, sanctis, & per eo- rum bonam conversationem pravis illius ævi homini- bus, ut ad meliora converterentur, prædicavit. Quem sensum tradiderat Augustin. epist. XCIX. ad Evo- dium, quod Christ9 prædicarit incredulis tempore Noæ non in carne, quia illo tempore nondum ve- nerat in carnem, sed in Spiritu: quod Spiritus in car- cere non sint in infernali carcere, sed animæ in carne, atque ignorantiæ tenebris in carcere velut conclusæ. Sequutus eandem expositionem est Thomas part. III. q. 53. artic. 2. & 3. Hugo, Autor gloffæ ordin. Ly- ranus, Carthufianus, Titelmannus, Joh. Benedictus; cui hactenus etiam cum B. Winckelmanno, ut & An- dradio libr. II. defens. Trid. accedit B. Gerhardus, qua hæc prædicatio tempore Noæ facta statuitur. Sensus, inquit, in hunc locum p. 466, hic est: Chri- stus in Spiritu, hoc est Divinitate sua, sive secundum na- turam divinam profectus prædicavit, per Noachum scilicet, præconem justitiæ, hominibus antediluvianis, quorum animæ sunt in inferni carcere, eorum scilicet, qui prædicationi huic fidem habere noluerunt.

Alii tamen plerique de profectione & κηρύξἒ Christi non Noæ tempore facta, sed postquam Christus mortificatus carne, & vivificatus iterum Spiritu fuit non hominibus antediluvianis, sed Spi- ritibus eorum, qui in carcere infernali fuere, inter- pretantur, adeoque de descensu Christi ad inferos ex- plicant. Quæ interpretatio præferenda videtur 1. quia subjectum est Christ9 θεάνθρωπος, non vero Fili9 Dei ἄσαρκος. 2. Agitur de Christo secundum carnem vel Humanam naturam mortificato, de quo etiam cap. IV. 1. χριστὲ ἐν παθόντος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν σαρκὶ, per Spiritum autem vivificato. Non ergo de iis, quæ sab isto gesta sunt Noæ rempore. 3. Christus ζωοποιηθεὶς πορευθεὶς dicitur prædicasse, at de λό- γῳ hæc dici nequeunt ante incarnationem. 4. Neq; ipsi cõvenit proprie profectio ante ἐνσάρκωσιν, cur autem à proprietate vocis discedendum sit, causa nulla est. 5. Uti πορευθεὶς dicitur εἰς ὀρανὸν, v. 22. Ita etiam πορευθεὶς ἐκήρυξε v. 19. Illic autem proprie dicta profectio intelligitur. 6. Series actuum & passionum Christi postulat, ut non de profectione tempore Noæ, sed post passionem Christi hæc ac- cipiamus, quia sequuntur ordine mortificatio, vi- vificatio, profectio ad Spiritus in carcere constitu- tos. Quomodo ergo regressus hic fieri potest quo- ad actus Christi ad tempora Noæ? 7. Profectus ad Spiritus dicitur, ipsisque prædicasse. Non ergo ho- mines antediluviani hic intelligi possunt adhuc su- perstites. Nuspiam enim Spirituum nomine homi- nes vivi intelliguntur, quoad substantiam spectati Joh. IV. 1. seqq. Πνεύματα vox, ut ex oppositione πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ constat, non homines seducto- res, sed Spiritum, quo agitantur, designat, vel certe non ratione substantiæ, sed doctrinæ spectantur. Ob- servat ipse B. Gerhardus p. 484. Nomen Spiritus de hominibus in carne viventibus accipi insolens esse.

8. Non tantum ad quos profectus sit, sed etiam quan- do, & ubi indicat S. Apostolus, nimirum τοῖς ἐν φυ- λακῇ, nonnulli codices addunt κατακεκλεισμένοις, quod quidem non admittimus ob codices proba- tiores, subintelligendum tamen esse res ipsa docet. Spiritus ergo illi, cum ipsis prædicavit Christus, jam in carcere conclusi erant infernali. Si dicas quomo- do illis pœnitentia prædicari potuit? Resp. Non prædi- cavit, ut pœniterent, sed quod non pœnituerint; non ut converterentur, sed ut de infidelitate & conde- mnationis merito convincerentur, sive verbis id fa- ctum, sive facto præsentatione suæ de Satana & pec- cato victoriæ, quam per infidelitatem cum à præ- cone justitiæ Noacho sisteretur, contempserant. Habemus hic iterum ὁμόψηφον B. Gerhardum, qui obvertentibus, prædicationem non satis commode dici in inferno factam, respondet: Intelligitur præ- dicatio non tam verbalis, sed realis, (sicut Ebr. XII. 24. loquela non verbalis, sed realis) qua Christus non ad conversionem & liberationem animabus impio- rum prædicavit, sicut in ministerio suo in his terris fe- cerat, sed ad ipsorum confutationem & confusionem, ut magno suo cum malo hunc præconem justitiæ, qui per Noachum olim ipsis prædicaverat, se sprevisse in- telligerent. Ut enim in judicio extremo impii in suis corporibus ipsum Judicem conspecturi sunt, & pœnas à facie Domini sensuri, 1. Thess. I. 9. Apoc. I, 7. ita quo- que animæ eorum extra corpora constitutæ ipsum ut gloriosum triumphatorem in inferno conspexerunt, & hac visione cruciatus in ipsis fuit auctus. Sensus igitur hic est, Christus divina virtute ad inferos de- scendit, & ibi apparuit Spiritibus ob incredulitatem damnatis, non ut eos inde liberaret, neque ut tempus resipiscendi illis concederet, Ebr. IX. 27. sed ut eis ostenderet, nunc se in carne venisse, & redemptionis pretium præstitisse, quod illi olim temporibus Noæ, cum de eo ipsis prædicaretur, præfracte contempsissent.

9. Qui ἐν φυλακῇ sese stitisse dicitur, ea fini πορευ- θεὶς, ut prædicaret quondam incredulis, quando eo- rum pœnitentiam expectavit Dei μακροθυμία, ille non prædicasse intelligitur πορευθεὶς aliquot ante secula, quando illi non ἐν φυλακῇ, sed in terris age- bant, & adhuc pœnitentiam agere poterant.

10. B. Gerhardus adducit ipse inter alia hujusmodi pro- bationem: Sicut in ascensione sua Christus suam gloriam & majestatem Spiritibus justorum ostendit: Sic in de- scensu & inferos suam gloriosam victoriam ad Majestatem Spiritibus damnatorum ostendit, illis quidem in glo- rificationem & exultationem, his vero in ignominiam & confusionem, 11. Huc facit locus parallelus, Eph. IV. 9. 10. qui descendit, idem est, qui ascendit super omnes cælos, ut impleret omnia. Nam & hic, πορευθεὶς profectus dicitur in carcerem in infernum descen- dendo, qui profectus in cœlum adscendendo, v. 19. 22.

12. Illi, quibus prædicavit Christus, ERANT in car- cere, cum prædicaret, quomodo Vulgatus & Ve- teres reddunt ERANT, non SUNT. Et Syr. Prædicavit animabus illis, quæ detinebantur in inferno. Si quis neget nomen Φυλακῆς de inferno accipi, cõvince- tur è cap. XX. 7. conf. v. 3. & Matth. V. 25. c. XVIII. 30. Luc. XII. 58. Unde Syrus hic reddidit in inferno. Si quis urgeat: Cur solis illis, qui tempore Noæ incre- duli fuerant, prædicasse dicatur, neque etiam aliis in inferno? Resp. non exclusive id accipiendum, imo ex parte totum intelligendum esse; peculiariter au- tem illos nominari, ut antediluvianos etiã in Chri- stum credere debuisse, ac propter incredulitatem damnatos esse doceretur, ac ratio typi diluvii quo- ad antitypum baptismum explicaretur. 13. Huic se- tentiæ annuunt plerique Patres, quod itidem agno- scit B. Gerhardus: Plerique ex Veteribus; inquit, hunc locum accipiunt de descensu Christi ad inferos hoc sen- su: Christus mortificatus est carne, quia corporis & animæ unio in morte fuit soluta, sed vivificatus Spiri- tu, quia per divinam ejus virtutem & potentiam a- nima corpori vicissim fuit unita, ac vita ei restituta 2. Cor. XIII. 4. in qua divina virtute secundum animã & secundum modum glorificati ac spiritualis corpo- ris, tanquam gloriosus triumphator profectus est & descendit ad Spiritus damnatos in carcere inferni constitutos, qui increduli aliquando fuerant, & pro- pter incredulitatem suam in hunc locum venerant, ipfisque prædicavit, hoc est, incredulitatem eorum redarguit, ac divinam suam Majestatem & victoriam manifestavit. Adduxit Athanasium in epist. ad E- pictet. Cyrillum de recta fid. ad Theodos. Ambro- sium in Eph. IV. Bellarm. l. IV. de Christo c. 13. Cle- mentem Alexandrinum l. VI. Strom. Athanasium libr. de incarnat. Cyrillum de recta fid. ad Regin. & l. XII. in Joh. c. 36. Hilarium in Ps. CXIIX. Ambro- sium in c. X. Rom. Ruffinum in exposit. Symboli. Quamvis vero illi modo & fine descensus ad inferos non conveniant: de descensu tamen ad inferos Petri verba pleriq; accipiunt. Justinus Martyr dial. cum Tryph. p. m. 132. affert nonnulla, quæ in exemplari- bus quibusdam extiterint, sed à Judæis resecta sint, quæ huc facere videntur. Ex Hieremia similiter di- ctis ista resecuerunt: Recordatus est Dominus Deus mortuorum suorum ex Israële, qui obdormierunt in terra aggeris (in tumulis scilicet & sepulchris) & de- scendit ad eos, ut evangelizaret eis salutare suum. Irenæus libr. III. adversus hæres. c. 23. Esaiam talia dicentem commemorat. Esaias ait, & commemoratus est Dominus sanctus Israël mortuorum suorum, quia dormierunt in terra sepultionis, & discendit ad eos evangelizare salutem, quæ est ab eo, ut eos salvaret. Sed illa nec in Esaia, nec in Jeremia sive in Ebræo, sive apud LXX. Interpretes inveniuntur. Docent tamen non quidem S. Petrum hæc inde accepisse, quod verisimile videtur Cornelio à Lapide, Justi- num tamen & Irenæum descensum Christi ad inferos, quem è verbis Petrinis hauserunt, è V. T. compro- bare voluisse, undecunque etiam ista acceperint.

Suffragantur etiam Pontificii, quod Christi de- scensus ad inferos hisce S. Petri verbis exhibeatur, quamvis ipsi in co errent, quod per carcerem lim- bum Patrum intelligi velint, quæ Bellarmini & Cor- nelii à Lapide, hic valde ineptientis, Paradisum la- troni promissum & traditum fuisse in æterna glori- am, Christumque ad inferos descendisse, ut plene subiret & lueret pœnas peccatorum nostrorum, & aliorum est sententia, vel purgatorium, quod Fr. Tur- rianus l. IV. pro epistol. Pontif. cap. 12. vel utrumq; quod Estig ad h. l. voluit. Nam in neutrum ἀπειθεῖς, hoc est, ἄπιϛοι increduli (vid. Joh. II. 26. Act. XIV. 2. Rom. VII. 8. Ebr. III. 8. 1. Petr. III. 1. 4.) ablegari possunt, quorum pœna est condemnatio in inferno æterna, uti ex adverso fidelium retributio gratuita est in cælo æterna vita Rom. VII. v. ult. Joh. III. 15. 16. 18. Marc. XVI. 16. Ideo Augustinus epist. XCIX. monet, Apostolum non facere mentionem S. Pa- trum, sed eorum, qui temporibus Noæ fuerunt in- creduli. Et cur tempus Noæ peculiariter nomina- ret, cum omnes Sanctos usque ad tempus descensus Christi in limbo ponant Papistæ? Quid? quod non solum Andradius illam explicationem reprobet, sed etiam Lorinus Salmeronem, Fevardentium, Ca- tharinum, Saa, Bellarminum, Suarezium & Valen- tium refellat, quod statuerint, Petrum id velle, quod eorum animæ, quas tempore diluvii pœnituit, nunciis latum sua redemptionis à Christo acceperint, doceat- que Petrum loqui de damnatis, qui diluvio peri- erunt, & incertum dicat, an Christus tunc aliquas a- nimas eduxerit è purgatorio, ac improbabile esse il- las animas tam diu in purgatorio fuisse, quod etiam Cornelio à Lapide minus credibile videtur, qua de re Bellarminus quoque cum Thoma suo vehemen- ter fluctuat l. IV. de Christo, cap. 16. §. Quartum. Christum prædicasse damnatis, arguendo eorum infi- delitatem agnoscit. Hægerus, Paez l. VII. de symb. cap. 20. Neque probari ullo modo potest hoc loco Calvini figmentum l. II. Instit. cap. 16. §. 9. & in Psy- chopannych. (cui tamen favere videtur paraphra- sis Osiandrina) de animabus post mortem non statim ad beatificam Dei visionem admissis, quod limbo Pa- trum analogum apparet.

Perperam Vulgata reddidit: Quando expecta- bant Dei patientiam, cum singulare in Græco sit ex- pectabat, & nominativus μακροθυμία, quam lecti- onem planam & appositam esse agnoscit Cornelius, & postponit hic Estius Vulgatam: Plane verisimile est, irrepsisse mendum in Vulgatam versionem, ut pro eo quod ex Græco transtulit Interpres, expectabas Dei patientia, scriptum sit ab indoctis, expectabant Dei patientiam. Ac profecto in Missali Romano per Clementem Octavum correcto in epistola feria sexta Paschalis legitur expectabat Dei patientia. Quo mo- do legunt Hieronymus & Augustinus: item Idacius Episcopus libro scripto contra Varimedum, imo & inter recentiores Dionysius Carthusianus. Bedam quoque eo modo legisse Commentarius ejus haud ob- scure significat. Dicitur autem patientia Dei expecta- re, quia Deus patienter expectat, quomodo de eo dicit hic Apostolus in 2. epist. c. III. Patienter agit propter vos. Alioqui dicere, quod homines expectant Dei pa- tientiam, nec usitatum est in scripturis, nec sensum habet commodum. Ubi etiam Erasmum refellit: Ma- le Erasmus passive vertit expectabatur, licet id alii quidam imitati sint. Nam Græcum verbum ἐκδέχε- σθαι sive ἀπεκδέχεσθαι sive simplex δέχεσθαι, quod E- rasmus in quibusdam codicibus haberi testatur, etsi voce medium sit, tamen active semper accipitur, ut multa e- jus generis alia.

Quanto minus admitti poterit Salmeronis in h. l. opinio de gentibus fide implicita salvatis, quibus suppleverit Christus statim a morte ad inferos veni- ens, quod fidei eorum deerat, cum Anastasio Antio- chene, (qui tempore VI. Synodi floruit) in ὁδηγῷ asserētis, Platonem salvatum & ex primis fuisse, qui in Christum credidissent, in descensu ejus ad infe- ros, quam refellit Bellarminus: aut etiam Cajetani, quod Christus, descendens ad inferos, illis, qui tem- pore Noæ increduli fuerant, fructuose prædicarit, quoniam in Dei bonitate confisi essent, quem Lorinus hic refutat: Quomodo credebant, qui Noacho Dei nomine prædicanti non credebant? Qui Pontificio- rum errores non multum absunt ab hæresi eorum, qui apud Philastrium hær. 121. August. de hær. n. 79. asseruere, Spiritus impiorum prædicatione Christi ad inferos descendentis cōversos, & ex inferno li- beratos esse, quam cum Aug. & Epiphan. hær. XLVI. profligant Greg. Nazianz. orat. XIII. Greg. M. l. VI. ep. 179. & Beda in h. l. S. Petr. incredulis illis opponit animas, quæ salvatæ sunt. Istos ergo damnatos esse innuit, innuit, quos in inferno conclusos etiam affirmat, è quo nulla datur liberatio. Ideo Bellarminus taci- te Salmeronem perstringens: In Christi ad inferos descensu, inquit, non est liberata ulla anima damna- torum ad gehennam.

Εἰς ἧν ὀλίγαι, τοῦτἔςιν ὀκτὼ ψυχαὶ διεσώθησαν δι' ὕδατό) Octo, id est, Noë, uxor, filii tres, tres nurus, Gen. VI. 18. Vide & 2. Petr. II. 5. Ψυχαὶ, id est, personæ, ut Act. II. 41. VII. 4.

Octo illas animas in arca de Spiritibus in carcere inclusis intelligit Ariasmontanus, quod arca velut carcer fuerit; sed Petrus distinguit Spiritus in car- cere, & octo animas in arca; illos incredulos fuisse ait, adeoque carceri adjudicatos typum damnato- rum facit, hos vero credidisse, ac per arcam serva- tos constituit typum salvatorum per baptismum.

Δι ὕδατος.] Id est, cum in aquis versarentur. Διὰ pro ἐν ha- bes Rom. IV. 12. Vide quæ ibi diximus.

Commodior est locus pro illa significatione 2. Petr. III. 5. Terra consistit δι' ὕδατος, in medio aquarum. Sensus est secundum B. Gerhardum, salvatæ sunt in aqua, id est, non obstante aqua dilu- vio, uti 1. Tim. II.15. salvabitur mulier διὰ τεκνογο- νίας, in filiorum generatione, hoc est, non obstante ea- dem. Sic & Act. XIV. 22. διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων in multis tribulationibus oportet nos ingredi in regnum cœlorum; id est, Tribulationes non possunt impedire salutem. Vide 2. Cor. VI. 8. Gal. IV. 13. Retineri tamen posset hoc loco usitatior significatio, quod δι ὕδατος per aquam servatæ sint octo animæ illæ. Nam si in terris mansissent, periissent. Per aquam autem non simpliciter, sed in arca servatæ sunt. Ar- ca enim aquis innatabat. Sic analogia concinnior est. Nam δι ὕδατος per aquam salvamur, non simpliciter, sed qua abluimur in Ecclesia à peccatis per baptismum, & per aquas baptismi trajicimus in portum æternæ vitæ.

## 3:21
Vers. 21. ὧ καὶ ἡμᾶς ἀντίτυπον νῦν σώζει βάπτισμα] That is, ὧ ἀντίστοιχον, as the Greeks say. The word ἀντίτυπον is common to both related things, that is, it is attributed as much to the figure, as Heb. IX. 14, as to the thing signified by the figure, as here in the glossary ἀντίτυπον is an exemplar, a copy, a likeness. But for the most part, when the Apostles name baptism, they simultaneously include the doctrine of baptism, concerning which see Heb. VI. 2, add Rom. VI. 3, 4, Eph. V. 5, Gal. III. 27, Col. II. 12. Philo, in his Life of Moses, says that the salvation obtained by Noah was a certain παλιγγενεσίας, a rebirth. In the best manuscript and others, there is ὅ here, so that it may be referred to ὕδωρ, not that the same thing is signified, but a similar one: which notes that ἀντίτυπον is placed adjectivally, and βάπτισμα is placed substantively.

As the usual reading, which the best Greek Codices confirm, is more approved, so it is also more suitable. For those things are forced, namely that ὅ is ὕδωρ, which water in reality, signified by that type or figure, that is, its very antitype, baptism, now saves us. Although that pronoun ὧ is indeed referred by some to the noun ὕδατος, to which, namely, the water corresponds, or the antitype baptism saves us: others, however, even our Blessed Gerhard, prefer to refer it to the whole sentence, in this sense: that baptism corresponds as an ἀντίτυπον to that preservation as a type of spiritual preservation, in which way the Syrian also accepted the text, rendering it thus: According to which type you also have been saved. The word ἀντίτυπος is correctly explained concerning the truth corresponding to the type, because the flood was a type of baptism, and that preservation in the flood was a figure of the salvation which we obtain in baptism. But it is wrongly [explained] by Piscator in this place and Chamier IV. Panstrat. l. 2. c. 5. §. 9. that preservation in the flood and the ark, and baptism are established as types. For thus an antitype would not have succeeded a type, but a type a type: and with Peter resisting, salvation will not be attributed to baptism; but only the signification of salvation. Indeed, Tossanus himself renders it Gegenbild. Pareus, however, expressly in Heb. IX. 24, understands by antitype here the thing signified by the type, baptism signified by the water of the flood. Aretius in this place: The flood, he says, insofar as it saved Noah with his own, is a figure of baptism. That transposition of words, which would have been clearer thus, ᾧ ἀντίτυπον βάπτισμα κὴ ἡμᾶς νῦν σώζει, has a not dissimilar example in 2 Pet. II. 19, ᾧ καλῶς ποιεῖτε προσέχοντες, for ᾧ προσέχοντες ὡς λύχνῳ &c. καλῶς ποιεῖτε. Although the Word ought not to be separated from baptism, for it is the washing of water in the Word, Eph. V. 26, yet the doctrine of baptism is not simultaneously included by the word baptism. Moreover, the water of the flood is compared to baptism, by which it saves us, because in it the unfaithful were indeed immersed and suffocated, but the faithful, swimming in the water, were preserved, because they were shut up in the ark of Noah, in which both our sins and the Devil with all his power are suffocated and perish. Which our Church prays in the prayer accustomed to be placed before the act of baptism: That God, who through the flood condemned the unfaithful world by a just judgment, but preserved Noah with his own according to his great mercy, and suffocated the hardened Pharaoh with all his own in the Red Sea, sanctified and instituted the waters for the salutary flood of sinners, may be willing to endow those who are baptized with true faith in the Holy Spirit, so that through that salutary flood whatever sin is innate to them from Adam, and committed by them, may be suffocated and perish in them, and that, separated from the assembly of the unfaithful, they may be preserved secure in the holy ark of the Christian Church. In which manner Gregory the Great, book IX, epistle 39: He who says that sins are not fundamentally remitted in baptism, let him say that the Egyptians did not truly die in the Red Sea. And Augustine, homily XCI. de tempore: When Christians are immersed for the third time in the salutary washing, then the Egyptians, that is, original sins or actual sins, are buried as if in the Red Sea. And Arator, book II, History of the Apostles.

--- All the weapons of the Demon. In these waters are submerged those by which that infant is reborn who was a captive.

St. Cyprian, Book IV, Epistle 7, to Magnus: In baptism, the Devil loses all the powers of his wickedness. Basil the Great on Psalm XXVII: τῇ λαμπέσῃ ψυχῇ ἀπὸ κατακλυσμῦ ἐνιδρυθεὶς ὁ Θεὸς οἱονεὶ θρόνον αὐτὴν ἑαυτῷ ἀπεργάζεται: God, being established in the soul shining after the flood (of baptism), makes it as it were a throne for Himself. Thus the water of the flood is established as a type of baptism, the ark as a type of the Church. Bede on this passage says the form of baptism is assimilated to the ark and the waters of the flood. Ambrose, On Those Who Are Initiated into the Mysteries, Chapter III: Do you see the water? Do you see the wood? Do you behold the dove, and do you doubt the mystery? It is water, therefore, in which the flesh is submerged, so that every sin may be washed away; every vice is buried there. It is the wood on which the Lord Jesus was affixed when He suffered for us. It is the dove in whose form the Holy Spirit descended, inspiring in you the peace of the soul and the tranquility of the mind. There are three most important members of the comparison: 1. Just as the water of the flood did not save Noah by itself, but through the medium of the wood: so the water of baptism does not save by itself, but through the medium of the wood of the cross or the passion of Christ endured upon it. All the power of baptism descends from the passion of Christ from the wood of the cross. Concerning which Augustine, Book XII, 5, Against Faustus, Chapter 14: Noah with his family is liberated through water and wood; just as the family of Christ is liberated through baptism signed by the passion of the cross. 2. The waters of the flood suffocated everything in which there was a living soul. Thus Baptism is the suffocation or mortification of our sins and of the old Adam. The Interlinear Gloss on this passage: By those who were submerged in the flood, the mortification of the flesh is signified: By those who were saved in the ark, the vivification of the Spirit is signified. 3. Just as the water of the flood vii. He preserved pious Noah by lifting up the ark, and carrying it for a whole year, so that it might be in safety, or to be placed in port: So also baptism lifts us up from the sea of the world into the deep, carries us, and places us in port. Which effect of water, since ships are preserved in it, is by no means accidental with respect to the ships. Thus also, by reason of the ships of the Church, preservation and salvation truly agree in the water of baptism by the institution of our God. Regarding the comparison of the ark with the Church, Augustine, in his book On the Unity of the Church, ch. 5, sets forth the opinion of the Church thus: It is doubtful to none of us that by the ark of Noah, saving the truth of the historical events, so that with the sinners destroyed the house of the righteous might be freed from the flood, the Church was also prefigured, which perhaps might seem a conjecture of human ingenuity, if the Apostle Peter did not say this in his epistle. And in book XV of The City of God, ch. 22. The ark of Noah is without doubt a figure of the city of God wandering in this age, that is, the Church, which is saved through the wood, on which hung the Mediator of God and men, the Man Jesus Christ. Outside the ark there was no salvation: Thus there is no salvation outside the Church. That which is outside the ark, says Augustine in book XII against Faustus, ch. 17, all flesh, which the earth sustained, was consumed by the flood, signifies that outside the society of the Church the water of baptism, although it be the same, not only does not avail for salvation, but rather avails for destruction.

Not serving that thing for which baths suffice. For what is the benefit of that baptism which brightens the flesh and the body only, as Justin says in his dialogue with Trypho. See what has been said by us on Matthew III. 16.

is a legal term, as can be seen in Theophilus under the title of the Institutes on the obligations of words and those following. And among other Greek interpreters of Roman law. In the glossary, I stipulate, but by metonymy, as is often the case in law, the name of stipulation also includes the response or promise. For also I am asked signifies I promise, I pledge in the same glossary. In baptism, the Bishop or some other person in his name used to ask thus, or what is the same, used to stipulate, Do you renounce Satan? The one to be baptized would answer, I renounce; being asked again, Do you pledge yourself to Christ? He would answer, I pledge myself. Tertullian calls this the pledge of salvation in his work on baptism. The same author in his work on the resurrection of the flesh: For the soul is sanctioned not by washing, but by response. Cyprian called it the interrogation of baptism in epistle LXXX. & LXXVI. wherefore it is said here for God, namely with the word 'made' understood. A pledge made to God from a pure conscience. See what is on Matthew XXVIII. 19.

They did not only return that response: But primarily also concerning the faith: while being asked whether they believe in Christ, with a good conscience, that is, seriously and from the heart, they answered that they believed and renounced, as Estius observes from Bede, and that this interrogation is aptly called an interrogation, that is, a stipulation, by which a contract is usually made between two, one asking and the other answering. Heinsius explains interrogation and examination, because an examination and proof of conscience was required by the Ancients from adults in baptism just as in the other sacrament of self-examination. Therefore, that baptism is a proof of a good conscience according to God, consisting not in the washing away of external filth, but in the proof of oneself and true faith in God, and on that occasion he conjectures that the ancients introduced their interrogation in Baptism, the summary of which was to believe in eternal life and the forgiveness of sins, as Cyprian has it in the epistle to Jovinus prefixed to the Council of Carthage: Therefore, says Heinsius, it is the same as interrogation, which, as it can be instituted by another, so it can and ought to be by adults who are baptized. For he asks who examines himself. Cornelius a Lapide brought forward a similar interpretation, but in another sense: Interrogation, i.e., proof and exploration, as if to say. Baptism makes us safe, because it causes us to have a conscience approved before God, that is, a good, pure, and clean one; according to that passage in Hebrews X. 22, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water, so that it is a metalepsis: As they are thought to be by Estius, who observes that the very effect of baptism is signified, which is the sprinkling or cleansing of hearts from an evil conscience, as Paul speaks in Hebrews X. For baptism makes a good conscience. For it remits past sins, so that a man's conscience need no longer fear and tremble on account of them: But rather boldly ask God for grace toward himself. Which interrogation has the force of a vehement assertion in the Hebrew phrase, Gen. XIII. 2, Ezek. XXII. 2. We acknowledge that it is a metalepsis, and that the consequent is put for the antecedent, which was already involved in the antithesis in this way: Baptism is not an external washing of the body's filth, but an interior washing of the soul's filth, whence arises the interrogation of a good conscience, so that we may also endure to be asked by God concerning our conscience, as being cleansed and tranquil and secure because of the certainty of Divine grace: and that we may be able to answer God promptly, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and washed from sins by the water of baptism, Heb. X. 22, and cleansed by the blood of Christ from dead works, Heb. IX. 14, that is, from sins, having a pure and peaceful conscience. Therefore the Greek Scholia do not explain the word itself, but express the sense: Interrogation, that is, a pledge, a security, a demonstration of a good conscience, and B. Luther interprets it as a covenant: because baptism confirms our conscience that we are in God's grace, and seals the covenant of grace, so that the baptized may confidently call upon God: And baptism is a covenant or stipulation, and a mutual obligation, by which God offers, applies, and seals His grace to man, and in turn the conscience, made more certain of the grace of God, testifies that it believes in God and binds itself to observe His will. In which manner Gagneius also explained it, and others among the Papists as a stipulation, a pact, a contract, that is, as interpreted by Cornelius a Lapide, as if to say, Baptism makes us safe, insofar as it is a stipulation and pact between God and the baptized. For God makes a covenant in baptism with the baptized, and by the covenant gives him a good conscience, namely the remission of sins, grace, righteousness, and the promise of eternal life. Furthermore, He promises that He will be his God, Father, Provider, and Protector: conversely, the baptized promises that he will be a faithful servant and son to God, and that he will begin a new life, will preserve the good conscience received from Him, until the last breath of life, and will obey His law and commandments in all things. For this reason, those who were formerly about to profess the Christian faith in baptism used to look up to heaven publicly, and raise their right hands on high, with an oath taken before witnesses: and the oath, signed by the hand of the baptized and sealed with his ring, was recorded in the registers: as Joseph Vicecomes teaches from the Fathers in book II of the rites of baptism, chapter 27. Somewhat more foreign is the interpretation of the Syriac: You have been saved through baptism, not by washing the body of filth, but by confessing God in a pure conscience: And that of Estius: The doctrine of the Apostle in this place is that external faith, expressed by an outward profession while one is being baptized, is that which makes us saved in baptism. Not that he removes this effect from the external ceremony of washing, but that he teaches what is the principal thing. For Scripture is accustomed to speak in this way when it commends one thing over another, as in Hosea 6: I desired mercy and not sacrifice. For Peter in his first epistle simply denies that the washing away of the filth of the body occurs in baptism: which is an effect of natural water, for it contributes nothing to the sacramental use of baptism. For water here is not to be regarded in regard to its physical use, but in regard to its sacramental duty. Therefore that comparative sense is foreign here. 2. E̓περώτημα is not internal faith itself, but overflows from faith. For he whose heart has been purified through faith, he at last can testify concerning a good conscience and confidently interrogate God, and answer God. 3. Exterior profession in baptism, whether proper to adults or to infants through godparents, originated in the Church indeed from this interrogation or stipulation designated by Peter, yet it is not that very ἐπερώτημα properly. 4. Since Estius makes faith the principal thing in baptism, he is forced to confess that baptism does not profit by the work performed. Meanwhile, unless it can be admitted by a convenient interpretation, what he adds: Nor does faith have its power from baptism, but baptism from faith at least as a disposition necessary in itself for the effect of baptism. For the Holy Spirit works faith through baptism as a washing of regeneration, Tit. III. 5, even if baptism obtains the power of saving from faith. Faith, however, is not a disposition to salvation, but a means of salvation: by which we are justified and saved not dispositively, but organically. And in this sense St. Augustine, tract. LXXX on John, says: whence, he asks, such great power of water, that it touches the body and washes the heart, unless by the Word acting: not because it is said, but because it is believed.

From which it is clear that Cornelius a Lapide falsely attributes to Blessed Luther and his followers that baptism does not save us by its own power, because it is a mere sign, but because it is a testimony of a good, that is, a faithful conscience, and seals its faith. For we do not attribute to baptism only the sealing of faith, but also the operation and regeneration of the same, through which faith arises in us: nor do we make baptism with the Calvinists a sign merely significant, but communicative, by which the grace of regeneration, faith, remission of sins, or justification and salvation is offered and conferred upon us. Therefore we truly say that baptism saves us, but that it is not merely a sign of salvation: that baptism is truly the washing not of the filth of the body, but of the soul: that baptism is truly the interrogation of a good conscience, which is the deposition of the filth of the soul, or confers the remission of sins, from which arises a good and tranquil conscience. We deny that the opinions of the Calvinists concerning interior and exterior baptism have any place here, because in baptism no exterior washing occurs, but only the washing of the filth of the soul, as St. Peter testifies: which the Papists, not alien to the Calvinist distinction, as is evident from Estius, openly contradict. Blessed Luther thinks it alludes to the Levitical washings, but denies that in baptism a washing of the body occurs, explaining it thus: 'Thereby you are not kept and saved, that you wash the filth from the flesh, that the body may be clean, as the Jews did. Such cleanliness is now worth nothing more, but the covenant of a good conscience with God, that is, that you feel within yourself a good, joyful conscience, which stands in covenant with God, and could say, He has promised this to me, He will keep it, for He cannot lie. When you therefore hang and cling to His Word, then you must be saved.' Baptism therefore saves not by reason of that external washing or the work performed, but by reason of this Divine promise, by which God, both by word and also by the sign joined to it, offers Himself to us as a propitious Father, and applies and pledges the benefits of His Son to us who believe. And this is what the Minister says: I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, that is, I strike a covenant with you, and I certainly pledge grace to you, and that not by any authority of my own, or even rashness, but also by the command and promise of God, and in His name and place, and that on account of the merit and intercession of Christ who suffered for you, as Flacius has it here.

Lord Dr. Sebastian Schmid explains ἐπερώτημα as the petition of the Minister or prayer in Colleg. Bibl. poster., whose entire opinion I am pleased to transcribe. What, therefore, he says, must be determined by us? Resp. 1. that mutual stipulation or obligation does not greatly please us, nor should the adversaries abuse it, and hide some condition of salvation, at least a sine qua non, in our stipulation, even if we take and interpret those of our own side in the best sense, as we indicated in the tract on circumcision p. 304 and following. We add 2. that the word ἐπερωτᾶν also signifies to ask. Hence that baptism is the seeking and acquisition of a good conscience toward God and before God. But we explain the meaning 3. further thus: Dr. Peter seems to look, through the name of ἐπερώτημα, of seeking, of petition, which a certain acquisition follows, to the formula of baptism, by which we baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. This formula is also precatory, by which he who baptizes seeks and asks something from God. For it is invoked, as we speak with Blessed Gerhard on Baptism §. 80, over the water of baptism the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, of the one true God, so that in the baptismal action commanded by Himself He may be present according to His promise, and the baptized may receive grace. Indeed by the power of the command (we speak with the same) and of the Divine institution, the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is invoked over the baptized, and water is joined in baptism. By the command and institution of this formula, the ecclesiastical prayers for the salvation and good conscience of the baptized, which are accustomed to be made by the Church in the act of baptism, are also used. To this formula of baptism 4. it also seems to be looked at through this, that mention of the whole Holy Trinity is made not obscurely. For it is a petition or seeking of a good conscience toward God the Father through the resurrection of Jesus Christ in the Holy Spirit, to be given through the purging of the conscience, Heb. 9:24. The Apostle therefore wishes to say that sacramental baptism does not consist in this, that its minister washes away the filth of the flesh and causes them to be laid aside, but that he may petition, seek, and acquire by the words of the formula of baptism in the invoked name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, a good conscience, as that which in baptism is purged through the blood of Christ applied by the operation of the Holy Spirit. And I do not know 6. whether the ministry of the baptizer could have been expressed by a more convenient term than τῶ ἐπερωτήματος, of the seeking, petition, or asking of a good conscience: to indicate that the minister of baptism acts precariously and effects what he does and effects all his effect by the power of the words of institution from God, as the principal cause, praying. This is Mr. Dr. Schmid. We acquiesce in the common explanation of the Fathers and our theologians, who understand it of the baptized, not the baptizer, just as the noun ἐπερώτημα or ἐρώτημα is not easily found for a seeking or petition, much less for an acquisition, but denotes a question or interrogation, which is the most common meaning of the verb ἐρωτᾶν; nor does the ministerial cause of baptism always employ prayer in the dispensation of the sacrament, which is complete without ecclesiastical prayers, provided only that baptism is performed in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit: nor is the ministry of the baptizer properly situated in invocation, much less in the petition or seeking of a good conscience, or in the entreaty for Divine benefits, but in the sprinkling of water in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; and in this sacred act the administering cause is subordinated to the principal, which does not appear in a petition.

Δι ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ χριστῦ] This pledge of a good conscience comes from faith in the resurrection of Christ, for from that we also have conceived the hope of resurrection.

By others it is referred, with the Syriac, not to ἐπερώτημα, but to the word σώζει. For baptism saves us through the resurrection of Christ, insofar as Christ was delivered for our sins, and was raised for our justification, Rom. IV. v. ult. It can, however, be conveniently referred to ἐπερώτημα. For baptism is the washing of sin, and the stipulation of a good conscience by the virtue of the merit of the passion and resurrection of Christ. Thus with B. Luther, Flacius: Furthermore, he says that this stipulation of a good conscience is made through the resurrection of Christ, under which also his passion and his whole merit or efficacy is understood. Insofar, therefore, as baptism applies the efficacy of baptism to us, to that extent it finally saves. And B. Gerhard: It is conveniently referred to what is nearer, and is joined with the immediately preceding noun ἐπερώτημα, with the participle γενόμενον understood, in the sense that that interrogation of a good conscience before God is made through the resurrection of Christ, which indeed is the foundation of faith apprehending the promise concerning the remission of sins and the grace of God offered in Christ, 1 Cor. XV. 17. If Christ has not risen, your faith is vain, for you are still in your sins. Therefore, by the contrary sense: If Christ has risen, our faith is firm, and we are no longer in our sins. A good conscience rests upon the resurrection of Christ, as it is a public testimony that satisfaction has been fully made for our sins, that we are perfectly reconciled to God, that death has been swallowed up into victory, and that all things which looked toward meriting our salvation have been perfectly consummated. Rightly Cornelius à Lapide: Through the resurrection of Jesus Christ: First, i.e., baptism has this power, namely of making the conscience good and holy, from the merit of the passion of Christ, the end and complement of which was the resurrection of the same, according to that Rom. IV. 25. Second, through the resurrection, because through it Christ conquered and swallowed up death, both his own and consequently ours, and opened the way into heaven for us, which is the second effect of baptism, namely that just as he gives us the life of grace: so likewise after it he gives the life of glory, and makes us heirs of eternal life; so Beda and Lyranus. Third, because the resurrection of Christ is the exemplary and final cause of our holiness, and of the new life which we receive and enter upon in baptism. So the Glossa, Hugo, and Thomas Anglicus. Finally, Paul and the Apostles are accustomed to attribute our justification and salvation to the resurrection, because that, as a clause and seal, sealed all the dogmas and sacraments of Christ. For if Christ has not risen, our faith and hope is empty, 1 Cor. XV. 15.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ὧ καὶ ἡμᾶς ἀντίτυπον νῦν σώζει βάπτισμα] Id est, ὧ ἀντίστοιχον, ut loquuntur Græci. Vox ἀντίτυπον est communis utrique relato, id est, tam figuræ tribuitur, ut Ebr. IX. 14. quam rei per figuram significatæ, ut hic in glos- sario ἀντίτυπον exemplar, exemplar, instar. Plerumque au- tem Apostoli cum baptisina nuncupant, simul comprehen- dunt doctrinam baptisini, de qua vide Ebr. VI. 2. adde Rom. VI. 3.4. Eph.V.5. Gal. III.27. Col. II. 12. salutem Noæ par- tam quandam παλιγγενεσίας fuisse imaginem ait Philo de Mosis vita. In Manuscripto optimo & aliis hic est ὅ, ut nempe id referatur ad ὕδωρ, non ut idem significetur, sed si- mile: quod notat illud ἀντίτυπον positum ἐπιθετικῶς, & βάπτισμα positum προθετικῶς.

Uti probatior est usitata lectio, quam confir- mant optimi Codices Græci, sic etiam convenien- tior. Nam coacta illa sunt, ὅ scilicet ὕδωρ, quæ aqua in re, illo typo seu figura significata, hoc est, ipsum ejus antitypon baptisina nunc salvos nos facit. Quanquà vero referatur Pronomen illud ὧ à non- nullis ad nomen ὕδατος, cui scil. aquæ conforme, vel antitypon baptisma nos salvos facit: alii tamen, etiam B. Gerhardus noster malunt id referre ad to- tam sententiam, hoc sensu: quod isti conservationi tanquam typo spiritualis conservationis baptismus velut ἀντίτυπον respondeat, quomodo etiam Syrus accepit textum, sic reddens: Secundum quem typum vos quoque salvi facti estis. Vox ἀντίτυπος recte de veritate typo respondente explicatur, quia diluvium erat typo baptismi, & illa conservatio in diluvio fi- gura salutis, quam consequimur in baptismo. Male autem à Piscatore in h. l. & Chamiero IV. Panstrat. l. 2. c. 5. §. 9. conservatio illa in diluvio & arca, & ba- ptismus typi constituuntur. Sic enim non antity- pon typo successisset, sed typustypo: & Petro repu- gnante, baptismo non salus tribuetur; sed tantum significatio salutis. Sane Tossanus ipse reddit Ge- genbild. Pareus vero diserte in Ebr. IX 24. per an- titypon hic intelligit rem typo significatam, bapti- smum significatum aqua diluvii. Aretius in h. l. Diluvium, inquit, quatenus servavit Noachum cum suis, figura est baptismi. Trajectio illa ver- borum, quæ ita clariora fuissent, ᾧ ἀντίτυπον βά- πτισμα κὴ ἡμᾶς νῦν σώζει, non absimile exemplum habet 2. Petr. II. 19. ᾧ καλῶς ποιεῖτε προσέχοντες, pro ᾧ προσέχοντες ὡς λύχνῳ &c. καλῶς ποιεῖτε. Quanquã à baptismo non sequestrari debeat Ver- bum, est enim lavacrum aquæ in Verbo, Eph. V. 26. non tamen voce baptismi simul comprehenditur doctrina baptismi. Confertur autem Baptismo, qua nos salvat, diluvii aqua, quia in eadem im- mersi quidem infideles suffocati sunt, fideles au- tem natantes in aqua conservati, quia in arcaNoæ conclusi erant, in qua & peccata nostra, & Diabo- lus cum omni potestate sua suffocantur, & inter- eunt. Quod de Ecclesia nostra in precatione ba- ptismatos actui præmitti solita orat: Ut Deus, qui per diluvium mundum infidelem justo judicio con- demnavit, Noam vero cum suis secundum magnam misericordiam suam conservavit & Pharaonem indu- ratum cum omnibus suis in mari rubro suffocavit, aquas ad salutare peccatorum diluvium sanctifica- vit, & instituit, illos, qui baptizantur, vera fide in Spiritu sancto donare velit, ut per illud salutare di- luvium in ipsis suffocetur & intereat quicquid peccati ipsis ab Adamo congenitum, & ab ipsis pa- tratum est, utque separati à cætu infidelium in san- cta arca Ecclesiæ Christianæ securi conserventur. Quo pacto Gregorius M. libr.IX. epist. 39. Qui dicit peccata in baptismo non funditus dimitti, dicat in mari rubro Ægyptios non veraciter mortuos. Et Augustin. homil. XCI. de tempore: Quando in sa- lutari lavacro tertio Christiani merguntur, tunc Ægyptii, id est, originalia peccata, vel actualia pecca- ta quasi mari rubro sepeliuntur. Et Arator l. II. Histor. Apost.

--- Omnia Dæmonis arma. His merguntur aquis, quibus ille renascitur infans Qui captivus erat.

S. Cyprianus l. IV. epist. 7. ad Magnum: In ba- ptismo omnes nequitiæ vires Diabolus amittit. Basili- us M. in Psal. XXVII. τῇ λαμπέσῃ ψυχῇ ἀπὸ κα- τακλυσμῦ ἐνιδρυθεὶς ὁ Θεὸς οἱονεὶ θρόνον αὐτὴν ἑαυ- τῷ ἀπεργάζεται: Splendenti animæ statim post dilu- vium (baptismi) Deus insidens eam velut thronum sibi constituit. Sic aqua diluvii constituitur typus baptismi, arca typus Ecclesiæ. Beda in h. l. formam baptismi dicit assimilatam arcæ & aquis diluvii. Ambrosius de iis, qui initiantur mysteriis cap. III. Vides aquam? Vides lignum? Columbam aspicis & dubites de mysterio? Aqua est ergo, qua caro mer- gitur, ut omne abluatur peccatum, sepelitur illic omne vitium. Lignum est, in quo suffixus est Dominus Je- sus, cum pateretur pro nobis. Columba est, in cujus specie descendit Spiritus sanctus, tibi pacem animæ tranquillitatemque mentis inspirat. Comparationis tria potissima sunt membra: 1. Sicut aqua baptismi per se non salvavit Noam, sed mediante ligno: Sic aqua baptismi per se non salvat sed mediante ligno crucis vel passione Christi in eo exantlata. Omnis baptismi vis ex passione Christi ex ligno crucis de- scendit. Quo de Augustinus l. XII. 5. Faust. c. 14. Noæ cum suis per aquam & lignum liberatur; sicut familia Christi per baptismum crucis passione signa- tum 2. Aquæ diluvii suffocabant omne, in quo erat anima vivens. Sic Baptismus est peccatorum nostrorum, & veteris Adami suffocatio vel morti- ficatio. Glossa interlinearis in hoc loco: Per illos, qui submersi sunt in diluvio, significatur mortifi- catio carnis: Per illos, qui salvati sunt in arca, significatur vivificatio Spiritus. 3. Sicut aqua dilu- vii. conservavit pium Noam attollendo navem, ge- standoque per integrum annum, ut in tuto sit, aut in portu collocanda: Sit & baptismus nos attollit è mari mundi in altum, gestat, ac in portu collocat. Qui aquæ effectus, cum naves in ea servantur, mini- me accidentalis est respectu navium. Ita & ratio- ne navium Ecclesiæ in aqua baptismi vere conve- nit ex instituto Dei nostri coservatio & salus. Quod ad arcæ cum Ecclesia comparationem de ea Augu- stinus l. de unit. Eccles. c. 5. ita Ecclesiæ sententiam sistit: Nulli nostrum dubium est, per arcam Noë sal- va rerum gestarum fide, ut deletis peccatoribus do- mus justi à diluvio liberaretur, etiam Ecclesiam fuis- se figuratam, quæ forte humani ingenii conjectura videretur, nisi hæc Petrus Apostolus in sua epistola di- ceret. Et l. XV. de C. D. c. 22. Arca Noa procul dubio figura est peregrinantis in hoc seculo civitatis Dei, hoc est Ecclesia, quæ sit salva per lignum, in quo pependit Mediator Dei & hominum, Homo Jesus Christus. Extra arcam non erat salus: Ita salus non est extra Ecclesiam. Quod præter arcam, inquit Augustinus l. XII. contr. Faust. c. 17. omnis caro, quam terra sustentabat, diluvio consummata est, si- gnificat, quod præter Ecclesiæ societatem aqua bapti- smi, quamvis eadem sit, non solum non valet ad salu- tem, sed valet potius ad perniciem.

Οὐ σαρκὸς ἀπόθεσις ῥύπου] Non ei rei serviens, cui balnea sufficiunt. Τί γὰρ ὄφελος ἐκείνου τοῦ βαπτίσματος, ὃ τὴν σάρκα, καὶ μόνον τὸ σῶμα φαιδρύνει. ut ait Justinus colloquio cum Tryphone. Vide quæ dicta nobis ad Matth. III. 16.

Ἀλλὰ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς ἐπερώτημα εἰς Θεὸν] Ἐπερώ- τημα est vox juris, ut videre est apud Theophilum titulo Institut. de verborum obligationibus & sequentibus. Et apud Græcos Romani juris Interpretes alios. In Glos- sario ἐπερωτῶ stipulor, sed per Metonymiam, ut in jure sæpe, nomine stipulationis comprehenditur & responsio sive promissio. Nam & ἐπερωτῶμαι significat promitto, spondeo in eodem glossario. In baptismo Episcopus aut alius quis ejus nomine ita interrogabat, aut quod idem est stipulabatur, ἀποτάσσῃ τῷ Σατανᾷ; respondebat ba- ptizandus, ἀποτάσσομαι, rursum interrogatus συντάσσῃ τῷ χριστῷ; respondebat, συντάσσομαι. Hanc sponsionem salu- tis vocat Tertullianus de baptismo. Idem de resurre- ctione carnis: Anima enim non lavatione, sed respon- sione sancitur. Cyprianus interrogationem baptismi dixit ep. LXXX. & LXXVI. quare ἐπερώτημα συνειδήσεως ἀ- γαθῆς εἰς Θεὸν dicitur hic pro Θεῷ, nempe subaudito ποιηθέν. Sponsio Deo facta de pura conscientia. Vide quæ ad Matth. XXVIII. 19.

Non illam tantum responsionem reddebant ba- ptizandi: Sed imprimis etiam de fide: dum inter- rogati, an credant in Christum, bona conscientia, id est, serio, & ex animo respondebant, se credere, & abrenunciare, ut ex Beda Estius observat, eamque interrogationem apposite ἐπερώτημα dici, id est stipulationem ait, qua inter duos uno interrogante & altero respondente contractus fieri solet. Heinsius ἐρώ τημα & ἐπερώτημα interrogationem, & examen ex- plicat, quia conscientiæ examen, ac probatio ab adultis in baptismo æque ac in altero sacramento δοκιμασία sui ipsius requisita fuerit à Veteribus. Baptismum ergo esse bonæ secundum Deum conscien- tiæ probationem non in externarum sordium ablu- tione, sed in probatione sui, veraque in Deum fide consistere, eaque occasione conjectat, veteres suã in Baptismo ἐρώτησιν invexisse, cuj9 compendium fuit πιστεύειν εἰς αἰώνιον ζωὴν κὴ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν, ut habet Cyprianus epist. ad Jovin. Carthaginensi con- cilio præmissa: Idem ergo, inquit Heinsius, ἐπερώ- τημα, quod ἐπερώτησις, quæ ut ab alio institui: ita & ab adultis, qui baptizantur, & potest & debet. Ἐπερωτᾷ enim, qui ipse se examinat. Attulit si- milem interpretationem Cornelius à Lapide, sed a- lio sensu: Interrogatio i. e. probatio & exploratio, q. d. Baptismus nos salvos facit, quia facit, ut proba- tam coram Deo habeamus conscientiam, bonam scilicet, puram & mundam; Juxta illud Ebr. X. 22. aspersi corda a conscientia mala, & abluti corpus aqua munda, ut Metalepsis sit: Quomodo ab Estio, observante, ipsum baptismi effectum significari pu- tant, qui est aspersio sive mundatio cordium a consci- entia mala, ut loquitur Paulus Ebr. X. Nam ba- ptismus bonam facit conscientiam. Remittit enim peccata præterita, ut jam non debeat hominis consci- entia propter illa metuere ac trepidare: Quin auda- cter interroget Deum de gratia erga se. Quæ inter- rogatio vim habetEbræa phrasi vehementis asse- verationis, Gen. XIII. 2 Ezech. XXII. 2. Agnosci- musMetalepsin esse, & consequens poni proAnte- cedenti, quod in antithesi jam involvebatur hoc modo: Baptismus non est externa sordium corporis ablutio, sed interior ablutio sordium animi,unde o- ritur conscientiæ bonæ ἐπερώτημα, ut & interro- gari a Deo conscientiam nostram sustineamus, ut- pote mundatam ob gratiæ Divinæ certitudinem tranquillam, atque securam: & respondere Deo prompte possimus corda aspersi a mala conscientia, & abluti a peccatis aqua baptismi, Ebr. X. 22. atque mundati sanguine Christi ab operibus mortuis, Ebr.IX. 14. id est a peccatis, puram & pacatam habemo conscientiam. Ideo non verbum ipsum exponunt, sed sensum exprimunt GræcaScholia: Ἐπερώτημα τουτέστιν ἀῥῥαβὼν ἐνέχυρον ἀπόδειξιν arrhabo pignus & demonstratio bonæ conscientiæ, ac B. Lutherus cum fœdus interpretatur: quia baptismus confir- mat conscientiam nostram, quod simus in Dei gra- tia, & obsignat fœdus gratiæ, ut baptizati fiduciali- ter Deum possint compellare: Et baptismus fœdus vel stipulatio est, ac mutua obligatio, qua Deus ho- mini gratiam suam offerat, applicet & obsignet, ac vicissim conscientia de gratia Dei certior reddita testetur, se credere in Deum & ad voluntatem ejus observandam se obstringat. Quo pacto & Gagneius exposuit, aliique e Pontificiis stipulationem, pa- ctum, contractum,id est, interprete Cornelio a Lapi- pide, q. d. Baptismus nos salvos facit, quatenus est stipulatio & pactum inter Deum & baptizatum. Deus enim paciscitur in baptismo cum baptizato, eique ex pacto dat bonam conscientiam, puta remis- sionem peccatorum, gratiam, justitiam, & promissio- nem vitæ æternæ. Insuper promittit se ei fore Deum, Patrem, Provisorem & Protectorem: vice versa promittit baptizatus se Deo fore fidelem famulum & filium, & novam vitam initurum, bonam con- scientiam ab eo acceptam conservaturum, usque ad extremum vitæ spiritum, ejusque legi & mandatis in omnibus obediturum. Hac de causa olim in baptismo fidem Christianam professuri publice in cælum suspi- ciebant, ac manus dextras in altum erigebant, adhi- bito jurejurando coram testibus: ac jusjurandum manu baptizati subscriptum, ejusque annulo obsi- gnatum in tabulas referebatur: Utiex Patribus do- cet Josephus Vicecomes libr. II. de ritibus baptismi cap. 27. Paulo alienior est interpretatio Syri: Salvi facti estis per baptismum, non corpore abluti a sordi- bus, sed confitentes Deum in conscientia pura: Et Estii: Apostoli doctrina hoc loco est, fidem externam exteriori professione, dum quis baptizatur, expres- sam, id esse, quod in baptismate nos salvos facit. Non quo hunc effectum ab externa ablutionis ceremonia removeat, sed quo doceat, quid sit præcipuum. Sic enim loqui solet scriptura, cum aliud præ alio com- mendat, ut Oseæ VI. Misericordiam volui & non sacrificium. Nam Petrus 1. simpliciter negat, in ba- ptismo fieri ablutionem sordium corporis: qui ef- fectus est aquæ naturalis, nihil enim facit ad usum baptismi sacramentalem. Aqua enim hic spectan- da non est quoad usum physicum, sed quoad sacra- mentale officium. Ideo alienus hic est ille sensus comparativus. 2. E̓περώτημα non fides ipsa est in- terna, sed ex fide redundat. Nam cujus cor per fidem purificatum est, is demum testari potest de conscientia bona & fiducialiter Deum interrogare, Deoque respondere. 3. Exterior professio in bapti- smo sive adultorum propria, sive infantum per pa- trinos ex hac interrogatione vel stipulatione à Pe- tro designata in Ecclesia quidem originem traxit, non tamen illud ipsum ἐπερώτημα proprie est. 4. Quum fidem præcipuum faciat Estius in baptismo, fateri cogitur, baptismum non prodesse ex opere ope- rato. Interim nisi commoda interpretatione ad- mitti potest, quod addit: Nec fides à baptismo vim suam habet, sed baptismus à fide saltem ut dispositio- ne per se necessaria ad baptismi effectum. Nam fidem per baptismum ceu lavacrum regenerationis opera- tur Spiritus sanctus, Tit. III. 5. etsi baptismus à fide vim salvandi consequatur. Fides autem non est dispositio ad salutem, sed medium salutis: qua justi- ficamur & salvamur nō dispositive, sed ὀργανικω̃ς. Atque hoc sensu S. Augustinus tract. LXXX. super Joh. unde ista, inquit, tanta virtus aquæ, ut corpus tangat & cor abluat, nisi faciente Verbo: non quia dicitur, sed quia creditur.

E quibus patet falsō Cornelium à Lapide B. Lu- thero, & asseclis tribuere baptismum, salvos nos fa- cere non vi sua, quia merum signum sit, sed quia est testimonium bonæ, id est, fidelis conscientiæ ejusque fi- dem obsignat. Nam nos baptismo non tantum tri- buimus obsignationem fidei, sed etiam ejusdem operationem ac regenerationem, per quā fides in nobis oritur: nec baptismum cum Calvinianis fa- cimus signum mere σημαντικὸν, sed μεταδοτικὸν, quo nobis offertur & cōfertur regenerationis gra- tia, fides, remissio peccatorum, vel justificatio & sa- lus. Ideo vere baptismum nos salvare dicimus, non autem signum tantum merùm esse salutis: vere baptismum esse ablutionem non sordium corpo- ris, sed animæ: vere baptismum esse interrogatio- nem bonæ conscientiæ, quæ est depositio sordium animæ, vel confert remissionem peccatorum, ex qua oritur bona & tranquilla conscientia. Calvinia- norū vero sententiæ de baptismo interiori & exteri- ori hic ideo locum esse negamus, quod in baptismo nulla fiat exterior ablutio, sed tantum ablutio sor- dium animæ, teste S. Petro: Cui Papistæ à Calviniana distinctione, ut ex Estio constitit, non alieni, pa- lam contradicunt. B. Lutherus ad lotiones Leviti- cas alludi censet, in baptismo autem ablutionem corporis fieri negat, ita exponens: Damit wer- det ihr nicht behalten und seelig, daß ihr den Un- flat vom Fleisch abwaschet, daß der Leib rein sey, wie die Juden thâten. Solche Reinigkeit gilt nun nichts mehr, sondern der Bund des guten Gewis- sens mit GOtt, das ist, daß du in dir fühlest ein gut frölich Gewissen, das mit GOtt im Bund stehe, und sprechen könte, er hat mir das zugesagt, das wird er halten, denn er kan nicht lügen. Wann du also an seinem Wort hangest und hafftest, so múst du behalten werden. Baptismus igitur servat non ratione externæ illius lotionis aut operis operati, sed ratione hujus Divinæ promissionis, qua Deus tum verbo, tum etiam signo ei adjuncto sese nobis in Patrem propitium offert, nobisque credentibus Filii sui benefi- cia applicat & addicit. Et hoc est, quod Minister di- cit: Ego te baptizo in nomine Patris, & Filii, & Spi- ritus Sancti, id est ferio tecum fœdus, tibiǫ, certe gra- tiam addico, idque non mea aliqua autoritate, aut etiam temeritate, sed etiam mandato promissioneque Dei, ac nomine locoq́; ejus, idq́; ob Christi pro te passi meritum & intercessionem, ut hic Flacius habet.

Dn. D. Sebastianus Schmidius explicat ἐπερώ- τημα de petitione Ministri vel oratione in Colleg. Bibl. poster. cujus sententiam integram adscribere placet. Quid itaque, inquit, statuendum nobis? Resp. 1. nobis non valde placere mutuam stipulationem seu obligationem, nec ea adversarii abutantur, & ali- quam salutis conditionem saltem, sine qua non in no- stra stipulatione occultent, etsi nostrates in optimum sensum accipiamus & interpretemur, ut indicavi- mus tract. de circumsione p. 304. & seqq. Addimus 2. verbum ἐπερωτᾶν significare etiam quaerere. Hinc baptismum esse quaesitionem & acquisitionem bonae conscientiae erga Deum & apud Deum. Mentem ve- ro 3. ita amplius exponimus: Respicere videtur D. Petrus per nomen ἐπερωτήματος quaesitionis, petiti- onis, quam sequitur certa acquisitio, ad formulam ba- ptismi, qua baptizemus in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti. Haec formula etiam precatoria est, qua qui baptizat, a Deo aliquid quaerit & petit. In- vocatur enim, ut cum B. Gerhardo de Bapt. §. 80. loquamur super aquam baptismi nomen Patris, Filii, & Spiritus sancti, unius veri Dei, ut in actione bapti- smali a se mandata juxta promissionem suam adsit, & baptizatum gratiam recipiat. Nimirum vi man- dati (cum eodem loquimur) & institutionis Divinae, nomen Patris, Filii & Spiritus S. super baptizatum invocatur, & in baptismo aqua conjungitur. Hu- jus formulae mandato & institutione utuntur etiam preces Ecclesiasticae pro salute & bona conscientia ba- ptizati, quae in actu baptismi ab Ecclesia fieri solent. Ad hanc baptismi formulam 4. respici etiam vide- tur per hoc, quod totius sanctae Trinitatis mentio haud obscura fiat. Nam est petitio seu quaesitio bonae consci- entiae erga Deum Patrem per resurrectionem Jesu Christi in Spiritu S. dandae per purgationem consci- entiae Ebr. IX. 24. Vult itaque 5. Apostolus dicere, baptismum sacramentalem non in hoc consistere, quod Minister ejus abluat sordes carnis, easque depo- ni faciat, sed ut petat, quaerat & acquirat verbis for- mulae baptismi in nomine invocato Patris, Filii, & Spiritus sancti, bonam conscientiam, tanquam quae in baptismo per sanguinem Christi operatione Spiri- tus sancti applicatum purgetur. Et nescio 6. Num commodiori vocabulo ministerium baptizantis ex- primi potuerit, quam τῶ ἐπερωτήματος, quaesitionis, petitionis, rogationis bonae conscientiae: ad indican- dum quod minister baptismi precario agat & efficiat, quod agit & efficit omnem effectum suum vi verbo- rum institutionis a Deo, tanquam causa principali ex- orans. Haec Dn. D. Schmidius. Nos acquiesci- mus communi Patrum, & Theologorum nostro- rum explicationi, qui de baptizato, non baptizan- te intelligunt, uti nec nomen ἐπερώτημα aut ἐρώτη- μα facile pro quaesitione aut petitione, nedum pro acquisitione invenitur, sed quaestionem vel interro- gationem notat, quae verbi ἐρωτᾶν usitatissima est significatio; neque causa ministerialis baptismi se- per adhibet precationem in dispensatione sacra- menti, quod integrum est sine precationibus Ec- clesiasticis, si modo in nomine Patris & Filii & Spi- ritus sancti baptismus fiat: nec ministerium bapti- zantis proprie in invocatione, nedum in bonae co- scientiae petitione aut quaesitione, vel exoratione beneficiorum Divinorum situm sit, sed in aquae in nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus sancti aspersione; ac subordinatur in hoc sacro actu causa admini- strans principali, quod non apparet in petitione.

Δι ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ χριστῦ] Haec bonae conscientiae sponsio venit ex fide de resurrectione Christi, inde enim & nos spem resurrectionis concepimus.

Ab aliis refertur cum Syro non ad ἐπερώτημα, sed ad verbum σώζει. Salvat enim nos baptismus per resurrectionem Christi, quatenus Christus tra- ditus est propter peccata nostra, & resuscitatus est propter justitiam nostram, Rom. IV. v. ult. Referri tamen commode potest ad ἐπερώτημα. Nam ba- ptismus est ablutio peccati, & stipulatio bonæ con- scientiæ virtute meriti passionis & resurrectionis Christi. Sic cum B. Luthero Flacius: Istam porro stipulationem bonæ conscientiæ dicit fieri per resurre- Etionem Christi, sub qua etiam passio totumque ejus meritum aut efficacia intelligitur. Quatenus igitur baptismus efficaciam baptismi nobis applicat eatenus demum servat. Et B. Gerhardus: Concimnius re- fertur ad propinquius, & conjungitur cum proxime præcedente nomine ἐπερώτημα, subintellecto partici- pio γενόμενον, sensu eo, quod interrogatio illa bonæ conscientiæ apud Deum fiat per resurrectionem Chri- sti, quippe quæ est fidei promissionem de remissione peccatorum & Dei gratia in Christo oblata appre- bendentis fundamentum, 1. Cor. XV. 17. Si Chri- stus non resurrexit, vana est fides vestra, adhuc enim estis in peccatis vestris. Ergo à contrario sensu: Si Christus resurrexit, firma est fides nostra, & non su- mus amplius in peccatis nostris. Conscientia bona nititur resurrectione Christi, utpote quæ publi- cum est testimoniũ pro peccatis nostris plene esse satisfactum, nos Deo perfecte esse reconciliatos, mortem in victoriam esse absorptam, & omnia, quæ ad salutem nostrã promerendam spectabant, esse perfecte consummata. Recte Cornelius à Lapi- de: Per resurrectionem Jesu Christi: Primo q. d. Hanc vim, conscientiam scilicet bonam sanctamque efficiendi, babet baptismus ex merito passionis Christi, cujus terminus & complementum fuit resurrectio ejusdem juxta illud Rom. IV. 25. Secundo per resurre- Etionem, quia per eam Christus vicit & deglutivit mortem tum suam, tum consequenter & nostram, aditumque in cælum nobis aperuit, qui est secundus baptismi effectus, ut scilicet sicut dat nobis vitam gra- tiæ: Ita pariter post eam det vitam gloriæ, faciatque hæredes vitæ æternæ; ita Beda & Lyranus. Tertio quia Christi resurrectio est causa exemplaris & finalis nostræ sanctitatis, & novæ vitæ, quam baptismo accipimus & inimus. Ita Glossa, Hugo, & Thomas Anglicus. Denique solent Paulus & Apostoli tri- buere resurrectioni nostram justificationem & salu- tem, quia illa quasi clausula & sigillum omnia Christi dogmata & sacramenta obsignavit. Si enim Christus non resurrexit, inanis est fides & spes nostra, 1. Cor. XV. 15.

## 3:22
Vers. 22. Ὅς ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Θεοῦ]. The same expression Rom. VIII. 34. Similar Heb. I. 3. Here in certain Greek codices the Latin version shows there to have been somewhat more.

This is added not only so that it may be signified that the way into heaven is open to us through baptism, which is Bede's reason, but also so that the faith of the other may be established concerning the perfect satisfaction of Christ, who would not have been raised to the right hand of God unless he had made expiation for all sins and had consummated the salvation of the human race, Heb. I. 3. and concerning the most sufficient power of Christ our Mediator to preserve us for eternal salvation: and not only to comfort the pious, that he may be able to protect his own, but also to terrify the impenitent, that he may be able to powerfully strike them down. Finally, says Flacius, he celebrates Christ here, and that victory of his over sin, Satan, and death: so that he may both establish the firmness and efficacy of that covenant, which depends upon the victory and resurrection of Christ, and comfort the pious in the cross and struggle with Satan and their own infirmities, and the old man, while they hear that they have so powerful a Patron and Savior: and also terrify and condemn the impious, his despisers, while they hear that they have enmities with so powerful and glorious and now revived an adversary.

The words which are added here in the Vulgate, swallowing up death, so that we might be made heirs of eternal life, seem to have crept into the text by way of interpretation added by someone. Whence it is no wonder that Bede, and the ordinary gloss, and others expounded them, and Fulgentius, book on faith to Peter, ch. 8, repeated them. Estius recognizes that this passage is not held in the Greek and Syriac codices, nor does it seem that Rufinus acknowledged it in his exposition of the creed, and that it is added somewhat inconveniently after that, who is at the right hand of God, unless the present is taken in place of the past, but that what follows, having gone into heaven, is aptly connected with that part, who is at the right hand of God. Πορευθεὶς εἰς ὐρανὸν] See above 20. Rightly Estius: Observe, Peter now says having gone into heaven, whom a little before he had said had gone to the underworld. For he uses the same Greek word πορευθεὶς in both places, from which gather against Calvin, that the former place also must be expounded according to the assumed nature.

Ὑποταγέντων αὐτῷ Ἀγγέλων καὶ ἐξουσιῶν καὶ δυνάμεων] Angel is here a name of a species, not a genus, as also Rom. VIII. 38. For the discourse grows. Ἐξουσίας and you have Eph. I. 21. and Col. I. 16. II. 10. Δυνάμεων indeed Rom. VIII. 38. Eph. I. 21. to which places, see what we have said.

The Vulgate expounded it with the Angels subjected to him, but the Greek is properly, when the Angels were subjected to him, namely by the Father: Which was also observed by Estius. Compare 1 Cor. XV. 27. Heb. II. 8. Eph. I. 20. seqq. from which place it is also clear that these three orders of Angels are not to be understood exclusively, but inclusively. For the sitting at the right hand of God entails not only the subjection of some, but of all Angels, nay, of all creatures. Which therefore is not to be restricted, with Estius and Lorinus, only to the good Angels, even if they alone are named in this place, because He is established above every name not only that is named in this, but also in the future age, and nothing is excepted which is not subject to Him, Heb. II. 18, even if it does not yet appear that all things are subject: nor is it to be defined from the category of position with the Calvinists, but from the category of action, because it is the most present and most powerful governance of all things in heaven and on earth, and πλήρωσις τῶν ἑπάντων, Eph. IV. 10.
