At Barchocheba Judaeus fuit nunquam professus est Christianismum, ideoq; exi- re à veris Christianis non potuit. Etsi autem ne- mo magis adversetur Regi, quam qui Regium nomen sibi imponit: tamen is nocentius Regi se opponit, qui ejus abutens nomine autoritatem illius pessundat, conculcat edicto, opprimit sub- ditos. Non ergo debuit Anti-Christus esse aper- tus hostis Christi ad id, ut esset nocentissimus ad- versarius. Imo debuit tecte mysterium iniquitatis promovere, & in ipso templo sedere, ac assume- re sibi cornua Agni & pietatis prætextu omnia peragere.

Quid? quod deceptores illi Judæorum, de qui- bus Matth. XXIV. vers. 5. 24. non tam soliciti fuerint de Christi Evangelio evertendo, aut re- vocandis Christianis ab illius professione, quam de Romanorum jugo excutiendo, & Judæis ad- versus imperium concitandis. Neque enim contra Christianos arma sumebant, sed contra Romanos rebellabant, quemadmodum Judas Gaulonites non esse decorum dicebat, ut Regem alium homi- ni imponerent præter Deum, neque ut vocaretur Dominus, nisi Deus benedictus. Talia multa pro more hic nugatur Grotius, imprimis in Ap- pendice, ubi hæc sua commenta asserere cona- tus est, quæ sicco pede præterimus. Discussit illa sedulo Maresius l. c. e quo tantum hæc notamus: Per imperium Parthorum, inquit pag. 202. part. II. Anti-Christ. Revel. Evangelium disseminasse Pe- trum Apostolum, comite Johanne, forte, quo tem- pore Petrus Romæ Simonem Magum expugnabat, aut quando Romæ sub Babylonis nomine priorem suam scribebat epistolam, aut cum Johannes exula- bat jam a temporibus Claudii in Pathmo. Itinerum magnorum Petri Johannem Evangelistam fuisse comitem perpetuum. Neminem Apostolorum incir- cumcisis annuntiasse Evangelium, nisi ad id delega- tum vel substitutum a Paulo. Christianos illos, quos compellat Johannes, fuisse ex circumcisione, Judæo- rum conversioni potissimum Johannem institisse: metuisse eum, ne fideles sub Parthis degentes ad Ju- daismum transirent, & rebellanti Barchochebæ con- tra imperium Romanum se adjungerent. Decem tribuum reliquias, quæ ἐν τῇ διασπορᾷ trans Eu- phratem erant, valde solicitas fuisse de statu Judæ- orum in Palæstina, aut facile potuisse manu seditio- sis in Imperio Romano se conjungere, magna sunt Gro- tii postulata, partim cum illius placitis, partim cum veritate & ratione pugnantia, quæ facilius illi erit præsupponere, quam probare. Imitantur hæc prima scientiarum principia, quæ indemonstrabilia sunt. Ut fingebat Judæos exulantes Thessalonicæ, ad quos Paulus secundam scripserit, quæ illi prima est: Ita hic Parthos & Orientis, imo totius orbis Christia- nos, quibus Johannes scripsit, (est enim hæc epistola καθολικὴ καὶ ἐγκυκλικὴ, ut statuit saltem Lorinus Proleg. ad eam cap. 5. universitati fidelium, non di- stinctæ certæque provinciæ scripta: Nec enim as- sentitur Baronio, qui ad Parthos speciatim missam autumat) Judæos esse vult, quia vult, nullo teste, indice nullo. Verum quod omnibus illis ridicularum imaginationum phantasmatis discutiendis sufficiet, satis esto observasse hos revera, ad quos Johannes scribit, ubicunque terrarum fuerint ex gentilismo & idolorum cultu, maxima saltem sui parte, ad Christum fuisse conversos, quod evidenter patet ex ultimæ ejus epistolæ clausula: Filioli cavete vobis ab idolis, quibus verbis fideles dehortatur ab ea idolo- latria, ex qua fuerant liberati. Id dicat Viro Magno Lorinus Jesuita: Cum sit, inquit, verus Deus Chri- stus, opportune subjicitur hæc admonitio in fine, tum contra negantes Christum consubstantialem Patri, colentes tamen eum pro Deo, tum ne recens ab idolo- latria conversi relaberentur in eam. Hæc Maresius.

Quod autem negat Grotius, hic respici locum Pau- li, 2. Thessal. II. quod ibi ἀντικείμενος notetur, hic Ἀντίχριςος, vix meretur responsum. Annon enim Anti-Christus, vel qui se opponit Christo, & κατ᾽ ἐξοχὴν ita nominatur, vicissim ἀντικείμενος est. Nonne qui Christo se opponit, hostis est Dei summi?

Καὶ νῦν ἀντίχριςοι πολλοὶ γεγόνασι] Multi sane, de quibus egimus, Matth. XXIV. vers. 5. & in anteloquio ad hanc epi- stolam.

Ὅθεν γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἡ ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν] Nam cum primum multi tales existerent, qui sibi arriperent Messiæ partes, tum ut propinquum expectari debebat excidium templi & Reipu- blicæ ex prædicto Christi, Matth. XXIV, 8. ubi est illud: Πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων.

Antea de hisce ita scripserat:

Καὶ νῦν ἀντίχριςοι πολλοὶ γεγόνασιν, Et nunc Anti- Christi multi facti sunt] Etiã ante excidium urbis Hieroso lymarum venturos aliquos,qui sibiChristi nomen aut po- testatem arrogarent, Christus ipse dixerat, Matth. XXIV. 5. Tales autem fuere omnes isti Judæi, qui se libertatis vindices profitebantur. Nam ὁ μέλλων λυτρῶσθαι τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, qui redempturus est Israël, est περίφρασις cir- cumloquutio Messiæ. In his Theudas πλάνος, impo- stores, multi καὶ ἀπατεῶνες, ut Josephus loquitur, Fe- lice Judæam procurante. Ægyptius impostor eidem Jo- sepho & Actis Apostolicis nominatus Alous sub Festo σωτηρίαν ἐπαγγελόμενος καὶ παῦλαν κακῶν, promittens salutem & malorum finem. Simon Magus qui se dicebat δύναμιν Θεῦ vim Dei, Dositheus, qui se Christum vocari volebat, de quo vide Origenem lib.II. adversus Celsum & inMatth. tract.XXII.

Ὅθεν γινώσκομεν, ὅτι ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν, unde scimus, quia novissima hora est.] Hoc indicio certi sumus, nos vivere temporibus illis, quæ exitium Judaicæ gentis haud multum antecedunt. Nam de ubere illo Pseudo-Chri- storum proventu, & rebus connexis Christus loquutus ad- diderat: Ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων, hæc autem omnia initia sunt dolorum.

Quid vero illi Pseudo-Christi Matth. XXIV. 5. qui dicebant: Ego sum Christus, ad hos Anti- Christos, quos νῦν nunc suo tempore, cum hæc scribebat, factos dicit Johannes? Illi ante excidium Hjerosolymæ fuere: Hi post excidium. Illi se Christum professi sunt: De hisce Anti - Christis nimirum gentium, Prodromis Christi tale quid non legitur, quod directe se pro Messia vendita- rint. Communi ergo calculo hic intelliguntur Hæ- retici, qui Christo, sive Deitati, sive Humanæ Natu- ræ veritatem infestarunt, aut etiam officium Christi impugnarunt, quod uti à variis Hæreticis factum usque ad Anti-Christum illum Magnum: Ita in illo collavies quædam istorum confluxit. Anti Chri- stianismus enim Papalis quid aliud est, quam sen- tina variarum hæresium, Christi impugnatione in- signium? Porro licet præcesserat Pseudo-Christi excidium urbis, si Anti-Christi, de quibus Johan- nes, sunt illi, de quibus Matth. 24, 24. ut supra vo- lebat commentatio Grotiana, quomodo retro tra- hi possunt isti ad tempora ante excidium, ut illi censeantur, de quibus Matth. 24, 5. nisi diversos e- osdem fingamus? Adde quod Grotius Anti-Chri- stos dicat impostores Judæorum. Quomodo vero Ju- dæi impostores dici possunt Ægyptius ille, cujus mentio sit apud Josephum & in Actis, Simon Magus, & Dositheus: Et quomodo aut Theuda, aut Ægy- ptio illi conveniet, quod Anti-Christi dicuntur exiisse exChristianis, vel tales, ut Grotius explicat, qui Christo quidem nomen dederant, sed mox di- scesserant à Christiano cœtu. Alios insuper impo- stores vel hæreticos viam Barchochebæ stravisse, dici non potest, quia nec eum venturum prædixe- runt, nec eorum dicta vel facta ejus autoritati con- stabiliendæ inservierunt. Et cur illi potius prælusis- se alios impostores, qui præcesserant, credemus, quã ipsum aliis, qui sunt postea sequuti. Recti9 sine dubio hic habet Johannis Feri interpretatio: Ad

Pseudo-Prophetas revertamur. Nam & hos Johan- nes nominat Anti-Christos, hoc est, Christo contrarios vel adversarios. Duobus autem modis adversari Christo quis potest, doctrina videlicet & vita. De utroque etiam locus hic intelligi potest, quandoqui- dem viventibus etiam adhuc Apostolis inventi sunt, qui non tantum Christo contraria docerent, ut Ebion, Cerinthus, verum etiam qui contra doctrinam Chri- sti viverent, ut Simon Magus & Nicolaus ille unus è septem Diaconis, à quo Nicolaitæ nomen accepe- runt, denique & hi, quos Paulus deflebat ut inimi- cos crucis Christi, & qui ventrem suum pro Deo ha- bèrent. Johannes igitur non loquitur de Judæis & paganis, qui aperte se hostes Christi profitebantur, sed de iis, qui nomen Christi profitentur, contraria tamen Christo docent aut agunt. Estius hanc reddit para- phrasin: q. d. Unus quidem venturus est insignis ad- versarius Christi, cui proinde per Antonomasiam no- men Anti-Christi debeatur, sed ille multos jam incepit habere præcursores, eosdemque participatione nominis ejus Anti-Christos, quia quod ille facturus est in uni- versum, ut Christi nomen & gloriam extinguat, hoc isti partibus faciunt. Neque abnuunt Jesuitæ, cui societati valde addictus fuit Grotius: Et nunc An- ti-Christi multi facti sunt: Anti-Christi, inquit Cor- nelius, id est, contrarii Christo, & veri Anti-Chri- sti prodromi, quia æque ut ille Christi fidem, religio-’ nem, Ecclesiam, Sacramenta &c. imo ipsam Christi personam & naturam impugnant. Notat enim hæreti- cos sui ævi, quorum alii negabant, Christum esse De- um, alii esse verum hominem. Tales fuere Ebion, Ce- rinthus, Saturninus, Basilides, Menander, Simon hæ- reticorum primipilas, eorumque asseclæ, de quibus ait Paulus: Mysterium jam operatur iniquitatis, 2. Thess. 2. 7. Novissima jam mundi hora est, inquit Tirinus, id est novissimum tempus, quo tempore Anti-Christum venturum sæpius audivistis. Atqui plures jam Anti-Christi, id est seductores & imposto- res, antidici & hostes Christi, prodromi magni Anti- Christi Ebion, Cerinthus, Basilides, Menander & alii Simonis Magi asseclæ in lucem prodierunt, quod si- gnum est, mundum jam senuisse & ad finem vergere. Ætas enim mundi postrema scatebit seductoribus & impostoribus, donec tandem cum capite & Principe omnium seductorum, Anti-Christo proprie dicto, fi- nem accipiat. 2. Thess. II. 7. Hæc itaque mundi hora seu ætas etsi novissima sit, quam nulla alia ætas subse- quetur, tamen instar præcedentium ætatum magnam admittit latitudinem, de qua plura. Quod cum pri- mævi fideles, ut S. Cyprianus, Lactantius, Hie- ronymus, Gregorius & plures alii Patres non sat ad- verterent, putabant suo ævo instare finem mundi. Sed inter prodromos seu prænuntios & adventum Re- gis, quem prænunciant, sæpe magnum est intervallum, ut patuit in penultima & antepenultima mundi ætate inter Prophetas & Christum.

Schlichtingii criminationem, qui fidei Catho- licæ propugnatores prodromos Anti-Christi facit ob assertam Christi Deitatem, confutat ex profes- so confessio martyrum, de SS. Trinitate, quæ hic conferatur. Novissimam itaque horam Johannes intellexit non simpliciter, quatenus notat totum illum decursum ab adventu Christi usque ad finem mundi, sed quatenus is decursus temporis variis ærumnis & tentationibus juxta Christi prædictio- nes futurus erat obnoxius, quaque exordia in co- piosa illa hæreticorum segete jam tum ætate jo- hannis cernebantur.

## 2:19
Vers. 19.

Ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθον,] Simon Magus, who even claimed for himself things that belonged to Christ alone, had been in the Christian assembly: and many others, who followed this very man and other impostors. They went out from us, that is, from our assembly.

'Αλλ' ἐπέφανὲ ἐξ ἡμῶν] When some began these turbulent factions and others followed them, they were no longer ours; they had deserted our assemblies, because they knew that such seditious machinations could not consist with the discipline of the Church. 'Εξ ἡμῶν here means, truly ours. Εἰ γὰρ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν μεμενήκεισαν ἂν μεθ' ἡμῶν] If they had been Christians from the heart when they began these things, they would not have deserted our assemblies. He says this so that Christians might not be besmirched by the crime of such seditions. Those who began these things had already deserted the Christian profession. They had been among Christians, but they were no longer. They cease to be considered Christians among us, says Tertullian of such, and adds, that such people neither congregate nor participate with us. Not unlike that of Ignatius to the Trallians: For if they were branches of the Father, they would not be enemies of the cross of Christ.

He brought these things forward in this way in his previous commentary.

Verse 19.

'Εξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθον] They went out from us. Simon Magus and those who adhered to him, and many also of those who followed others, had indeed given their name to Christ, but soon had departed from the Christian assembly.

Α'λλ' ἐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν, but they were not of us] Lest anyone should impute these machinations of seditious men to the Gospel, he diligently notes that when they began these things, they had already sent a repudiation to the Christian flock, namely because they saw that the dogmas of the Gospel could not consist with these turbulent counsels, so that necessarily either the discipline of the Church had to be cast off, or one had to desist from such illicit attempts.

Εἰ γὰρ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν, for if they had been of us] If they had been truly Christians at that time. Tertullian in his Apologetic: But someone will say that even some of ours depart from the rule of discipline: yet they cease to be considered Christians among us. But those philosophers persist in the name and honor of wisdom among you with such deeds. The same author against the nations: They are not immediately what they are called, but because they are not, they are called so in vain and deceive those who attribute the thing to the name, when the status of the name should correspond to the thing. And yet such people neither congregate nor participate with us, having been made yours again through their offenses.

Μεμενήκεισαν ἂν μεθ' ἡμῶν] they would have remained with us. They would have stayed in our assemblies and would not have deserted them: see Heb. X. 25.

He is therefore forced to acknowledge that the discourse here is not properly about Pseudo-Christs, but about heretics. And yet these things cohere with the preceding ones and speak of the same. But what does that, but they were not of us, contribute to the fact that they only began their machinations when they had said farewell to the Church? That they were not of us is understood not only by the Calvinists, but also by the Jesuits Tirinus and Cornelius, as meaning that none of such were ever truly faithful. For they contend that these cannot fall away from the faith. But Estius acknowledges: That some who are truly faithful do fall away. It is probable, he says, that some were endowed with true faith. For thus the Apostle speaks of such, 1 Tim. IV, that in the last times some shall depart from the faith, and in the first chapter of the same epistle, that some having put away a good conscience have made shipwreck concerning the faith, and 2 Tim. II, that Hymenaeus and Philetus have fallen away from the truth. This therefore, they were not of us, he says, can be understood in two ways: First, that they are said not to have been of us, because although they lived among us and with us, participating in the Christian Sacraments with us, they were nevertheless not of the number of true Christ-faithful, but feigned faith: In which sense Augustine treats this place in his commentary, which Bede also follows. Otherwise and better, so that the sense may be: They were not of us, that is, of the number of the elect, or of the Church, in that part which contains the elect, who alone are members of the Church that will always remain. Which sense the same Augustine delivers elsewhere, and explains at greater length: as in the book on correction and grace, chapter 9, and on the gift of perseverance, chapter 8. Some take the pronoun ἡμῶν to refer to the Apostles, Catharinus and Melchior Cano, book 10, on Commonplaces, last chapter. But that sense is too narrow. Of us, he says, who are constant, or as Heb. X. 39. Paul speaks, but we are not children of subtraction unto perdition. But there is no reason for Estius to be anxious as to how John knew that those of whom he spoke were not elect, because he himself provides the reason from which it could be gathered: For if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. A manifest reason, says Estius; for those who do not remain in the Church, but depart from it never to return, by this very fact show that they do not belong to the number of the elect. There is here an emendation: They were at one time ours, they departed from us, nay rather they were never ours. For if they had been ours, they would have remained with us. Where what he says, ours, is taken differently not without grace of speech: first for those who are in the Church, then for the elect. It is an Antanaclasis.

̓Αλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῶσιν] Supply, this was permitted by God, or which is the same thing, they went out from us, which the Syrian adds here, provided you supply, by the providential permission of God. God permitted them to be tempted in such a way that they might lay bare the character they had hidden. What the character of Simon Magus was we see in Acts VIII. 19. But what that of the Simonians was, 2 Thess. II. 10, 12. The departure of such people benefits the Church; their crimes afterwards do not burden the Church. Nay, it is a great honor to the Church that it appears that these machinations cannot consist with the doctrine and discipline of the Church. See 1 Cor. XI. verse 19, 2 Tim. III. 9.

Ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶ πάντες ἐξ ἡμῶν] that is, for not all who are in our assemblies are Christians in spirit. Not all who are in these assemblies have faith, 2 Thess. III. verse 2, 3.

He had delivered the same things in the previous commentary.

̓Αλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῶσι, but that they might be manifest] There is an ἔλλειψις, a defect in the speech; namely, this was done by the providential permission of GOD, so that it might appear to all that those who undertook such things were alien to Christianity, and therefore the Church could by no right be defamed by their deeds. The departure of such men, therefore, is of the greatest benefit to the Church and makes the innocence of others more evident, 1 Cor. 11:19; 2 Tim. 3:9.

Ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶ πάντες ἐξ ἡμῶν, because not all are of us] Faith is not for everyone, says Paul, 2 Thess. 3:2. For many, as Paul shows in the same place, are ἄτοποι καὶ πονηροὶ, absurd and wicked men, who lie hidden in Christian flocks, namely when hostile storms are quiet. Such men, however, joined themselves to Christian assemblies because of the exceptional mercy of Christians toward their fellow members, which allowed no one to be oppressed by severe poverty; the same men, when some greater hope of advantages or honors had shone upon them from elsewhere, revealed who they were and where they were heading. So true is that saying even here: Things feigned quickly returned to their own nature. And what Lysias said, that one could feign his own character for a short time, no one hides his nature for long. What the nature of Simon Magus was, see Acts 8:19, and believe the same of others of that kind.

Concerning whom there is no reason for us to add anything, since it has already been warned that the temporary ones are not to be excluded here: except that the Simonians are rashly introduced here, 2 Thess. 2:10, 12. For those things pertain to the times of the Great Anti-Christ. Whose Simonian nature teaches more than enough that he is the offspring of Simon Magus, the Patriarch of all heretics. But 'that they might be manifest', in Greek: 'But that they might be made manifest', etc. The sense, however, is that God permits this, which he said concerning the Anti-Christs: 'They went out from us, that they might be made manifest, and might be avoided by the faithful': at the same time, that by their departure they might make it manifest to us that not all who are in the Church are the elect. That is indeed made manifest to us for this reason, that we who seem to stand may not think highly of ourselves, but that we may fear, and work out our salvation with fear. Therefore, God elicits a twofold good for his elect from that evil, namely the departure of certain ones from the Church, specifically that they may both avoid them more easily and that they themselves may be rendered more humble and more cautious, as Estius says here.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

Ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθον,] Simon Magus, qui & ipse sibi, quæ Christi solius erant, vindicavit, fuerat in cœtu Christiano: & multi alii, qui hunc ipsum & alios impostores sunt sequuti. Exierunt à nobis, id est, à nostro cœtu.

'Αλλ' ἐπέφανὲ ἐξ ἡμῶν] Cum istas factiones turbulentas a- lii inchoarent, alii sectarentur, non ultra jam erant nostri, deseruerant cœtus nostros, ideo quod tales molitiones sedi- tiosas scirent cum Ecclesiæ disciplina non posse consistere. 'Εξ ἡμῶν hic est, vere nostri. Εἰ γὰρ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν μεμενήκεισαν ἂν μεθ' ἡμῶν] Si illi tunc ex animo fuissent Christiani cum ista inciperent, non dese- ruissent cœtus nostros. Hoc ideo dicit, ne crimine talium seditionum Christiani aspergerentur. Qui ista cœptabant, jam deseruerant Christianam professionem. Fuerant inter Christianos, at non erant amplius. Desinunt haberi Christi- ani apud nos, ait de talibus Tertullianus, & adjicit, ejus- modi neque congregant, neque participant nobiscum. Non dissimile illud Ignatii ad Trallianos : Εἰ γὰρ ἦσαν τῦ πατρὸς κλάδοι, ὐκ ἂν ἦσαν ἐχθροὶ τῦ ςαυρῦ τῦ χριςῦ.

Hæc ita protulit in priori sua commentatione.

Vers. 19.

'Εξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθον] Ex nobis exierant. Simon Magus & qui ei adhæserant, multi etiam eorum, qui alios sunt secta- ti, Christo quidem nomen dederant, sed mox discesserant à Christiano cœtu.

Α'λλ' ἐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν, sed non erant ex nobis] Ne quis Evangelio imputaret istas hominum seditiosorum molitiones diligenter notat eos, cum ista cœptarent jam repudium mi- sisse Christiano gregi, nimirum quod viderent Evangelii dog- mata cum istis consiliis turbulentis non posse consistere, ita ut necessario aut exuenda esset disciplina Ecclesiæ, aut absti- stendum ab ejusmodi illicitis conatibus.

Εἰ γὰρ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν, nam si fuissent ex nobis] Si illi eo tempore fuissent vere Christiani. Tertullianus in Apologe- tico: Sed dicet aliquis etiam de nostris excedere quosdam à regula disciplinæ: desinunt tamẽ Christiani haberi penes nos. Philosophi vero illi cum talibus factis in nomine & honore sapientiæ perseverant apud vos. Idem adversus nationes: Non statim sunt, qui dicuntur, sed quia non sunt frustra di- cuntur & fallunt eos, qui rem nomini addicunt, cum de re status nominis competat. Et tamen ejusmodi neque con- gregant, neque participant nobiscum, facti per delicta de- nuo vestri.

Μεμενήκεισαν ἂν μεθ' ἡμῶν] permansissent utique nobis- cum. Mansissent in nostris cœtibus, neque eos deseruissent: vide Ebr. X. 25.

Agnoscere itaque cogitur non de Pseudo-Chri- stis proprie, sed de hæreticis hic sermonem esse. Atqui cohærent ista superioribus, ac de iisdem loquuntur. Quid vero illud, sed non erant ex nobis, facit ad id, quod suas molitiones tum demum cœ- perint, cum valedixissent Ecclesiæ. Illud non erant ex nobis non Calviniani tantum, sed & Jesuitæ Tirinus & Cornelius intelligunt, quod talium nulli vere fideles fuerint unquam. Hos enim fide exci- dere non posse contendunt. Sed agnoscit Estius: Nonnullos etiam vere fideles excidere. Probabile est, inquit, quosdam vera fide præditos fuisse. Sic enim de talibus loquitur Apostolus, 1. Tim. IV. quod in novissimis temporibus discedent quidam à fide, & ejusdem epistola cap. I. quod bonam conscientiam quidam repellentes circa fidem naufragaverunt, & 2. Timoth. II. quod Hymenæus & Philetus à veri- tate exciderunt. Hoc ergo non erant ex nobis, inquit, duobus modis intelligi potest: Primum, ut dicantur ex nobis non fuisse, quia quamvis inter nos ac no- biscum versarentur, Christiana nobiscum Sacra- menta participantes: non tamen erant de numero verorum Christi fidelium, sed fidem simulabant: Quo fere sensu tractat hunc locum Augustinus in commentario, quem & Beda sequitur. Aliter & melius ut sensus sit: Non erant ex nobis, id est, de numero electorum, sive de Ecclesia, qua parte conti- net electos, qui soli sunt Ecclesiæ membra semper mansura. Quem sensum idem Augustinus alibi tradit, ac pluribus explicat: ut libr. de corrupt. & gratia cap. 9. & de dono persever. cap. 8. Nonnulli pronomen ἡμῶν de Apostolis accipiunt Cathari- nus, & Melch. Canus l. 10. de Loc. c. ult. Sed ille sensus justo est angustior. Ex nobis, inquit, qui constantes sumus, vel ut Ebr. X. 39. Paulus loqui- tur, nos vero non sumus ὑποστολῆς subtractionis filii in perditionem. Non est autem quod solicitus sit Estius, unde Johannes sciverit eos, de quibus loquutus est, non esse electos, quia rationem, unde id colligi poterat, subjicit ipse: Nam si fuissent ex nobis, utique permansissent nobiscum. Ratio mani- festa, inquit Estius; Nam qui in Ecclesia non per- manent, sed ab ea recedunt nunquam redituri, per hoc ipsum ostendunt, ad electorum numerum se non pertinere. Est autem hic ἐπανόρθωσις: Fuerint ali- quando nostri illi, recesserunt a nobis, imo vero nunquam fuerunt nostri. Nam si nostri fuissent, per- mansissent nobiscum. Ubi quod dicit, nostri non sine gratia sermonis aliter & aliter accipitur: prius pro iis, qui sunt in Ecclesia, deinde pro electis. Est Antanaclasis.

̓Αλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῶσιν] Supple, permissum hoc est a Deo, aut quod idem est, egressi sunt ex nobis, quod Syrus hic ad- dit, modo suppleas, provido Dei permissu. Deus eos sic permisit tentari, ut quod occultaferant, ingenium nuda- rent. Quale fuerit Simonis Magi ingenium videmus Act. VIII. 19. Quale autem Simonianorum 2. Thess. II. 10. 12. Discessus talium prodest Ecclesiæ, facinora postea eorum Ecclesiam non onerant. Imo magnus honos est Ecclesiæ, quod istas molitiones apparet cum doctrina & disciplina Ecclesiæ non posse consistere. Vide 1. Cor. XI. vers. 19. 2. Tim. III. 9.

Ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶ πάντες ἐξ ἡμῶν] id est, non enim omnes animo sunt Christiani, qui in nostris sunt cœtibus. Non omnium, qui in istis sunt cœtibus, est fides, 2. Thessal. III. vers. 2. 3.

Eadem tradiderat in priori commentatione.

̓Αλλ' ἵνα φανερωθῶσι, sed ut manifesti sint] Est ἔλλει- ψις defectus in sermone, scilicet factum est hoc provi- do DEI permissu, ut appareret omnibus illos, qui talia cœptarent, a Christianismo alienos esse, ac propterea per illorum facta nullo jure Ecclesiam infamari posse. Talium ergo hominum discessio plurimum prodest Eccle- siæ & aliorum innocentiam facit testatiorem, 1. Cor. XI. 19. 2. Tim. III. 9.

Ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶ πάντες ἐξ ἡμῶν, quoniam non omnes sunt ex nobis] Non omnium est fides, ait Paulus. 2. Thess. III. vers. 2. Multi enim, ut ibidem ostendit Pau- lus, homines ἄτοποι καὶ πονηροὶ, opportuni & mali, la- tent in Christianis gregibus, nempe ubi quiescunt hostiles procellæ: addebant autem se tales homines Christianis cœtib9 ob eximiam Christianorum in congreges suos mi- sericordiam, quæ neminem gravi inopia premi patieba- tur, iidem homines, ubi aliunde spes aliqua major com- modorum honorumve affulserat, aperiebant se qui essent, quo tenderent. Adeo verum etiam hic est illud: Cito ad naturam ficta redierunt suam. Et quod Lysias dixerit, ὀλίγον χρόνον δύναιτ' ἄν τις πλάσα- σθαι τὸν τρόπον τὸν αὑτοῦ, nemo diu ingenium abscondat. Quale Simonis Magi fuerit ingenium, vide Act. VIII. 19. & idem de aliis ejus generis crede.

De quibus non est quod addamus quicquam, quum de προσκαίροις hic non excludendis ja mo- nitum fuerit: nisi quod temere hic Simoniani, 2. Thess. II. vers. 10. 12. ingerantur. Pertinent enim ista ad tempora Anti-Christi Magni. Quem tamen Simonis Magi Hæreticorum omnium Pa- triarchæ prolem esse ingenium ejus Simonianum plus satis edocet. Sed ut manifesti sint, Græce: Sed ut manifesti fierent &c. Sensus autem est, Deum idcirco permittere hoc, quod de Anti-Christis di- xit: Ex nobis exierunt, ut manifesti fiant, & a fi- delibus vitari possint: simul ut exitu suo nobis ma- nifestum faciant, non omnes, qui in Ecclesia sunt, esse electos. Id vero propterea nobis manifestatur, ne, qui stare nobis videmur, altum sapiamus, sed ut timeamus, & cum timore salutem nostram ope- remur. Itaque geminum bonum suorum electorum ex illo malo, scilicet egressu quorundam ex Ecclesia, Deus elicit, nempe ut & facilius illos vitent, & ut ipsi reddantur humiliores atque cautiores, ut hic Estius.

## 2:20
Verse 20.

Vers. 20. And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things.] As if he were saying, I warn those who are mindful. Kings and Priests were once consecrated with ointment. But the word anointing was also figuratively referred to other benefits of God, as in Psalm 23, v. 5. In the New Testament, where all are Kings and Priests, any grace of God is understood by ointment, as we said in Heb. 1:9 and Jas. 5:14. But especially that grace by which the Spirit suggests to us in individual circumstances both the precepts of Christ and the warnings that are suitable for each time, John 14:26. When, therefore, those Pseudo-Christs, who opposed themselves to empires with armed force, appeared, the Spirit of Christ showed to Christians that that kingdom of the Messiah foretold by the Prophets was not worldly, John 18, verse 36, nor coming with external pomp, Luke 17, v. 28. That things which are Caesar's are to be given to Caesar, Matt. 22, verse 21; that the right of the sword is not to be seized, Matt. 26, verse 52. but that souls are to be saved through patience, Luke 21, v. 19. I interpret 'Holy One' here as Christ, in the way that word is taken in Acts 3, v. 14 and Apoc. 3, v. 7. Thus 'Spirit of the Lord,' 2 Cor. 3, v. 17, 18; 'Spirit of Christ,' Eph. 3, v. 16; 'Spirit of Jesus Christ,' Phil. 1, v. 19. Thus below, verse 27, 'the anointing which you received from him.' What he says, 'you know all things,' understand as those things which are necessary for avoiding such impostors. For the universality of the words ought to be restricted by the subject matter. The Syriac understood 'man' under 'all things,' as if John were saying, you know how to discern good and evil Spirits. But I do not think that this matter, of which he will provide norms below in chapter 4, is properly being dealt with here.

rather that the matter being dealt with, the norms of which are provided in chapter IV, is clearly taught by a comparison with verses 21, 22, and 23 of the present chapter. And here are regarded the dogmas which John had commended to them concerning communion with the Father and the Son, concerning God as light, concerning the blood of Christ cleansing from sins, concerning the remission of sins, concerning the propitiation of Christ, concerning his παρακλήσει, etc., in which the Anti-Christ opposes himself to Christ, with his champions. 3. Knowledge is not to be restricted to solid cognition distinct from catechesis. For he addresses everyone, not only Fathers, but adolescents, but even little children under the name of παιδίων. However, not all are reached by this solid cognition. Nor indeed must it be said with Estius that these things pertain only to Churches and not to individual believers, as if to say, You have Bishops and Presbyters, by whose care and study your Church is sufficiently instructed, and is being instructed in those things which pertain to the truth of Christian doctrine. For they are not sent back to the Bishops and Presbyters, but that common grace is preached, that they have an anointing through which they know all things, just as he had also said of the little children, that they knew the Father. And Estius himself admits that every believer, insofar as he is truly a believer, holds by faith all things necessary for salvation; because otherwise he would not be a believer. But what he adds, 'at least implicitly,' extinguishes the faith which he had granted there, nor could he deny it without an ἀντικείμενον ἐν προσκειμέ- νῳ, such as is a believer without faith, and faith without those things without which faith cannot exist, namely without that cognition and knowledge. But implicit knowledge, by which someone believes about a certain object what the Church believes, even if he is ignorant of what he believes about that same Church, is in reality not cognition, but ignorance. And even if he is not ignorant of that, but the Church knows it, he who is called a believer, and is said to have faith, and to hold all things necessary for salvation, in reality is ignorant of it, however much he may profess to believe what the Church believes. The just shall live by his own faith, not by another's faith, not by the Church's faith, Hab. 2:4, Rom. 1:17, Gal. 3:11, Heb. 10:38. And that this knowledge pertains to them all, the following verse 21 sufficiently indicates: I have not written to you as if you were ignorant. He certainly did not write this only to Bishops and Presbyters. Anointing, says Tirinus here in his paraphrase, teaches you, O Christians, all things which pertain to faith and Christian morals; so St. Cyril, Gregory, Irenaeus, Turrianus, Saa, Bellarmine. Therefore, 'all things' does not designate here whatever can be known (for the anointing did not teach the Apostles all things in this way) but whatever it was necessary to know concerning faith and Christian morals.

Similar things are those which occur in the commentary published separately:

And you have an anointing.] But you have an anointing, 'καὶ' for 'but,' as both the Latin and the Syriac correctly interpret here; the permutation of words is frequent among the Hebrews. If any of you, he says, imitates such people, there is no reason why he should excuse himself by ignorance. Thus also Christ had said in Matt. 24:25, 'idè proeirēka hymin,' behold, I have foretold it to you. But 'chrisma' is ointment rather than anointing, the oil of gladness, Heb. 1:9. That Spirit, namely, which impresses holy dogmas more and more upon the mind, Rom. 5:5, c. 8:15, 16, 2 Cor. 1:22, c. 5:5, Eph. 1:13, 14, & c. 6:30.

From the Holy One.] From the Holy One, from Christ, John 1:16, c. 14:26, c. 16:13, 14, 15; he, however, is called by eminence 'ho hagios,' that Holy One, Acts 3:14, Apoc. 3:7. He opposes, however, the Spirit of Christ to the Anti-Christian Spirit, as those which fight against each other from opposite sides.

And you know all things,] not imbued with some light and perfunctory knowledge, but you are reached by a solid cognition of things; that is 'katagnōsis,' hearing 'shema'ta,' this is 'gnōsis,' knowledge, or 'epignōsis,' 'da'ath,' as the Hebrews distinguish. Luke in the prologue of the Gospel, Clement of Alexandria often. That 'panta,' all things, must be taken for the totality of those things of which it is treated here, as 1 Cor. 9:22, c. 15:27, and elsewhere. Understand, therefore, here all those things which are necessary for salvation and for avoiding such impostors: such as: the kingdom of Christ is not of this world, John 18:36; it does not come with any pride, Luke 17; souls are to be saved through patience, Luke 21:19; things which are Caesar's are to be given to Caesar, Matt. 22:21; the right of the sword is not to be seized, c. 26:52. These things cohere excellently with those which John just said, that one must walk as Christ walked, not love the world, and those things which pertain to the world.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

Vers. 20. Καὶ ὑμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου, καὶ οἴδατε πάντα.] Quasi dicat, memores moneo. Unguento olim sacrabantur Reges & Sacerdotes. Sed & ad alia Dei beneficia vox unctio- nis figurate referebatur, ut Psalm. 23. v. 5. in Novo Testamen- to, ubi omnes sunt Reges & Sacerdotes, per unguentum in- telligitur quævis Dei gratia, ut diximus Ebr. I, 9. & Jac. V, 14. Eximie vero illa, per quam Spiritus nobis in singulis cir- cumstantiis suggerit, & Christi præcepta & monita quæ cui- que tempori sunt idonea, Joh. 14, 26. Cum ergo illi Pseudo- Christi, qui vi armata se imperiis opponebant, apparerent, Spiritus Christi subjiciebat Christianis regnum illud Messiæ per Prophetas prænuntiatum non esse mundanum, Johan. 18. vers. 36. nec venire cum pompa externa, Luc. 17. v. 28. Dan- da Cæsari, quæ Cæsaris sunt, Matth. 22. vers. 21. non arripien- dum jus gladii, Matth. 26. vers. 52. sed per patientiam servan- das animas, Luc. 21. v. 19. Ἁγίου hic interpretor de Christo, quomodo ea vox sumitur, Act. 3. v. 14. & Apocal. 3. v. 7. Sic Πνεῦμα Κυρίου, 2. Cor. 3. v. 17. 18. Πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ, Eph. 3. v. 16. Πνεῦμα ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, Phil. I. v. 19. Sic infra 27. τὸ χρίσμα ὃ ἐλάβετε ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ. Quod ait, οἴδατε πάντα, intellige, quæ ad vitandos tales impostores sunt necessaria. Restringi enim debet vocum universalitas ex subjecta materia. Syrus ad pánta subintellexit ἅνθρωπον, quasi dicat Johannes, nostis discernere bonos & malos Spiritus. Sed de ea re cujus infra cap. 4. normas tradet, hic proprie agi non puto.

potius de ea re agi, cujus normæ cap. IV. traduntur, collatio cum cap. præsentis v. 21. 22. 23. luculenter docet. Et respiciuntur hic dogmata, quæ ipsis com- mendarat Johannes de communione cum Patre & Filio, de Deo luce, de sanguine Christi à peccatis pur- gante, de remissione peccatorum, de propitiatione Christi, de ejus παρακλήσει &c. in quibus AntiChri- stus sese opponit Christo, cum suis promachis. 3. Scientia non restringenda est ad solidam cogni- tionem à catechesi distinctam. Alloquitur enim omnes non Patres tantum, sed adolescentes, sed par- vulos etiam sub nomine παιδίων. Omnes autem ista solida cognitione pertińcti non sunt. Nec vero cum Estio dicendum, hæc ad Ecclesias tantum pertinere non ad fideles singulos, q. d. Habetis Episcopos & Presbyteros, quorum cura ac studio vestra Ecclesia sa- tis instructa sunt, & instruuntur in iis, quæ pertinent ad doctrinæ Christianæ veritatem. Non enim remit- tuntur ad Episcopos & Presbyteros, sed prædicatur illa communis gratia, quod unctionem habeant, per quam sciant omnia, quemadmodum etiam de parvulis dixerat, quod Patrem norint. Er fatetur Estius ipse, quod unusquisq́. fidelis, quatenus vere fide- lis est, fide teneat omnia ad salutem necessaria; quia alias fidelis non esset. Quod autem addit, saltem implicite, fidem extinguit, quam illic concessoerat, nec negare poterat citra ἀντικείμενον ἐν προσκειμέ- νῳ, quale est fidelis sine fide, & fides sine illis, sine quibus fides esse non potest, fine illa scilicet cogni- tione & notitia. Implicita autem notitia, qua quis de certo objecto credit, quod credit Ecclesia, etsi ne- scius sit, quid credat de eadem Ecclesia, revera non est cognitio, sed ignorantia. Etsi autem id non ignoret, sed sciat Ecclesia, is tamen qui fidelis dici- tur, & fidem habere, & omnia ad salutem necessaria tenere, id revera ignorat, utut profiteatur, sed id credere, quod Ecclesia credit. Justus sua fide vivet, non alterius fide, non Ecclesiæ fide, Hab. II, 4. Rom. I, 17. Gal. III, 11. Ebr. X, 38. Et ad eos omnes perti- nere hanc notitiam, v. seq. 21. satis indicat: Non scripsi vobis quasi ignorantibus. Non certe solis id Episcopis & Presbyteris scripsit. Unctio, inquit hic Tirinus in sua paraphrasi, docet vos, ó Christiani, omnia quæ ad fidem & mores Christianos pertinent, ita S. Cyrillus, Gregorius, Irenæus, Turrianus, Saa, Bellarminus. Omnia ergo non designat hic, quæcunq́. sciri possunt (nam ne quidem Apostolos docebat un- ctio sic omnia) sed quæcunque scire circa fidem & mores Christianos oportebat.

Similia sunt, quæ occurrunt in commentatione separatim edita:

Καὶ ὑμεῖς χρίσμα ἔχετε.] Sed vos unctionem habe- tis, καὶ pro sed, ut hic recte interpretantur & Latinus & Syrus, permutatio vocabularum Ebræis frequens. Si quis vestrum, inquit, tales imitetur, non est, quod se ignoran- tia excuset. Sic & Christus dixerat Matth. 24, 25. ἰδὲ προείρηκα ὑμῖν, ecce, prædixi vobis. Est autem χρίσμα unguentum potius, quam unctio, oleum lætitiæ Ebr. I, 9. Spiritus nimirum ille, qui sancta dogmata magis magis- que imprimit animo, Rom. 5, 5. c. 8, 15. 16. 2. Cor. I, 22. c. V, 5. Eph. I, 13. 14. & c. 6, 30.

Ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου.] A Sancto, à Christo Joh. I, 16. c. 14, 26. c.16, 13. 14. 15. is autem per eminentiam dicitur ὁ ἅγιος, Sanctus ille Act. 3, 14. Apoc. 3, 7. Opponit autem Spi- ritum Christi Spiritui Anti-Christiano, ut qui ex adver- so pugnent inter se.

Καὶ οἴδατε πάντα, & nostis omnia, ] non levi qua- dam & perfunctoria imbuti, sed solida cognitione re- rum pertinéti estis, illa est κατάγνωσις auditio שְׁמַעְתָּא, hac γνῶσις scientia, sive ἐπίγνωσις דַּעַת, ut distingu- unt Ebræi. Lucas in prologo Evangelii, Clemens Ale- xandrinus sæpe. Illud πάντα omnia sumendum pro uni- versitate earum rerum, de quibus hic agitur, ut 1. Cor. 9, 22. c. 15,27. & alibi. Intellige ergo hic omnia illa, quæ ad salutem & ad vitandos tales impostores sunt necessaria: qualia sunt: Regnum Christi non esse de hoc mundo, Joh. 18, 36. non venire cum fastu aliquo, Luc. 17. per pa- tientiam servandas animas, Luc. 21, 19. danda Cæsari, quæ Cæsaris sunt, Matth. 22, 21. Gladii jus non arripiendum, c. 26, 52. Optime hæc cohærent cum iis, quæ modo dixit Johannes, incedendum, qua Christus incessit, non dili- gendum mundum, & quæ ad mundum pertinent.

## 2:21
Vers. 21. Οὐκ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὀκ οἴδατε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι οἴδατε αὐτή.] I have not written to you, these things namely, as if you were ignorant of the Evangelical precepts, but as those who are well-informed; otherwise, I would have used a longer discourse with you. A word to the wise is sufficient; the Latin translator explained ὅτι as 'in that' [or 'as']. I interpret ἀλήθειαν as the doctrine of the Gospel, as in John 8:32, ch. 17:17, 2 Cor. 4:2, and elsewhere.

Concerning which these things are to be noted: 1. Heb. 1:9 and Psalm 45:7, that by the oil of gladness is understood not just any grace of God, but the Holy Spirit: and that by the word χρίσματος in this place, nothing else is designated than the Holy Spirit himself, in which interpreters easily agree, except that a few, with Jerome (Book II, on ch. III of Habakkuk), interpret it as baptism, in which the gift of the Holy Spirit was given. Concerning this ointment, see what is said at 1 Cor. 1:21. Personal predicates are attributed to this anointing in the present passage, that they have received τὸ χρίσμα, that it remains with them, that it teaches them (v. 27), which are attributed to the Holy Spirit in John 16, whence his hypostasis is asserted. For actions belong to supposita. 2. Although the Holy Spirit suggests necessary admonitions for the condition of any time and state: here, however, that those things are regarded which concern seditious men, attributing a temporal kingdom to the Messiah, and fighting for the same with secular arms, and opposing themselves to the ordinary Magistrate, is an ἄῤῥησις [assertion] of that which was in the beginning. Properly, however, here

Καὶ ὅτι πᾶν ψεῦδος ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ὀκ ἔστι.] These words ψεῦδος and ἀληθείας are to be taken here not formally, so to speak, but materially. You know that those dogmas of seditious men do not agree with the Gospel. He calls those dogmas, by the way, ψεῦδος: but the Gospel, as before, ἀλήθειαν, because the matter was truly so. Πᾶν with the following ὀκ denies universally among the Hebrews writing in Greek. That ἐγὼ is to be construed with οἴδατε, which preceded.

We now also subjoin how he had expressed these things before, although they are almost the same.

Οὐκ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, I have not written to you.] That was not my reason for writing, I have written, these things namely, as in 1 Peter 5:12.

Ὅτι ὀκ οἴδατε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, as if you were ignorant of the truth.] That the dogmas of the Gospel are unknown to you, especially those concerning patience and the contempt of worldly things. Thus ἀλήθεια, truth, is taken in John 3:21, ch. 8:31, 32, ch. 14:6, ch. 17:17, 2 Cor. 4:2, Gal. 2:5, and elsewhere. Thus the Latin translator well takes ὅτι as 'in that'.

…Καὶ ὅτι πᾶν ψεῦδος ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ὀκ ἔστι, and because every lie is not of the truth.] Since the precepts of the Gospel are well held by you, you easily see from this also that whatever dogmas are false in their very nature are such: since the straight is the index of itself and of its crooked. Those who bring forward anything dissenting from the Evangelical dogma cannot but be deceivers, and that cannot be hidden from you. Πᾶν ἐκ ἐστιν in Hebraism denies the whole, not particularly, as among the Greeks. The precepts of the Gospel are not looked at, but the Evangelical and mystical dogmas. Nor are precepts handed down in the Gospel, if you understand it properly, since the Gospel is a proclamation of grace, and ought not to be mixed with the law.

Latin:

Vers. 21. Οὐκ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, ὅτι ὀκ οἴδατε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι οἴδατε αὐτή.] Non scripsi vobis, hæc scilicet, quasi igno- rantibus Evangelica præcepta, sed quasi bene gnaris; alioqui scilicet longiori vobiscum usurus sermone. Sapienti dictum sat est, ὅτι per tanquam bene exposuit Latinus. Ἀλήθειαν ex- pono doctrinam Evangelii, ut Joh. 8, 32. cap. 17, 17. 2. Cor. 4, 2. & alibi.

Circa quæ hæc notanda: 1. Ebr. I, 9. & Psalm. XLV, 7. per oleum lætitiæ non quamvis Dei gratiam, sed Spiritum Sanctum intelligi: nec aliud voce χρίσματος hoc loco, quam ipsummet Spiritum Sanctum designari, in quo facile conveniunt Inter- pretes, nisi quod pauci cum Hieronym. l. II. in cap. III. Hab. de baptismo interpretentur, in quo daba- tur donum Spiritus Sancti. De quo unguento vid. quæ ad 1. Cor. I, 21. Tribuuntur unctioni huic in præ- senti loco prædicata personalia, quod acceperint τὸ χρίσμα, quod maneat apud ipsos, quod doceat eos v. 27. quæ Spiritui Sancto Joh. XVI. tributa sunt, un- de ejus hypostasis asseritur. Actiones enim sunt sup- positorum. 2. Quanquam suggerat Spiritus San- ctus monita necessaria pro cujusvis temporis, & status conditione: hic tamen ea spectari, quæ ad homines seditiosos, regnum temporale Messiæ tri- buentes, & armis sæcularibus pro eodem pugnan- tes, acMagistratui ordinario se opponentes, sermo- nem esse ἄῤῥησις est τῶ ἐν ἀρχῇ. Proprie autem hic

Καὶ ὅτι πᾶν ψεῦδος ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ὀκ ἔστι.] Voces istæ ψευδής & ἀληθείας hic sumendæ sunt non formaliter, ut ita loquar, sed materialiter. Scitis dogmata illa hominum seditio- sorum non congruere cum Evangelio. Vocat autem obiter illa quidem dogmata ψεῦδος: Evangelium autem, ut jam an- te ἀλήθειαν, quia revera ita se res habebat. Πᾶν postposito ὀκ apud Ebræos Græce scribentes universaliter negat. Illud ἐγὼ construendum cum οἴδατε, quod præcessit.

Subjicimus nunc etiam, quomodo hæc antea expresserat, licet fere eadem.

Οὐκ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, non scripsi vobis.] Non ea mihi scriben- di fuit causa, scripsi, hæc scilicet, ut 1. Petr. V, 12.

Ὅτι ὀκ οἴδατε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, quasi ignorantibus veritatem.] quod ignota vobis sint Evangelii dogmata, præsertim illa de patientia & mundanarum rerum despectu. Sic ἀλήθεια veritas sumitur Joh. 3, 21. c. 8, 31. 32. C. 14 6. c. 17, 17. 2. Cor. 4, 2. Gal. 2, 5. & alibi. Sic ὅτι loco bene sumit Latinus Interpres.

Καὶ ὅτι πᾶν ψεῦδος ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ὀκ ἔστι, & quoniam omne mendacium ex veritate non est.] Cum Evan- gelii præcepta bene teneatis, facile hinc etiam videtis, dogmata quæcunque re ipsa falsa sunt, esse talia: cum rectum & sui obliqui sit index. Non possunt non fallaces esse, qui aliquid afferunt ab Evangelico dogmate dissentaneum, idque vos latere non potest. Πᾶν ἐκ ἐστιν in Ebraismo negat universum, non particulariter, ut apud Græcos. Non respiciuntur Evangelii præcepta, sed Evangelica dogmata & mystica. Nec in Evangelio præcepta traduntur, si proprie id intelligas, quum Evangelium concio sit gratiæ, nec cum lege commisceri debeat.

## 2:22
Ver. 22. Who is the liar.] Who is it that should be called a liar and impostor with better right? For this comparison is to be taken, since there are also other kinds of impostors, but lesser ones. No deceivers are more pernicious than those who overturn that upon which the salvation of men depends. For if Jesus is not the Messiah, since he said that he was, nothing is to be believed of him.

Except he who denies that Jesus is not the Christ.] To deny with the negative particle added, which the Latins would omit, is nothing other than to deny firmly. A similar locution is in Luke 20:27 and ch. 22:34, and in Sophocles: And I do not deny that.

This is the Antichrist.] Not that that eminent first Antichrist is going to do this, but that he does it eminently and impudently above the others, and with greater effect. Previously he had interpreted those things thus: Who is the liar?] Who can be a greater impostor? For these comparisons are to be taken, since there are also other kinds of impostors.

Except he who denies that Jesus is not the Christ, unless he who denies that Jesus is the Christ.] In Latin we would say, unless he who denies that Jesus is the Christ. But in Greek and Hebrew a repeated negation denies more strongly, as also among the ancient Latins. Plautus: Swear that you will not harm any man in this matter. Ennius: Many are of a stony heart, whom no one pities. Certainly among impostors there is no class either more impudent or more destructive than those who deny that Jesus is the Messiah, since all of Jesus' miracles, and his death and resurrection, were given by God for this, and written down for this, that this very thing might be believed, that Jesus is the Messiah, John 20:31, indeed because the authority of both his precepts and his promises, which heals the human race, depends upon it.

This is the Antichrist.] That eminent one who is to come, the Antichrist, will do this more impudently than others, to whom those lesser ones act as a prelude, and therefore come into a partnership of the name.

We easily admit the explanation: provided that those Pseudo-Christs are not uniquely considered impostors who do not indeed deny so directly that Jesus is the Christ, but rather by consequence according to the mind. For if there be another Messiah, Jesus cannot be believed to be the true Messiah. But these deceivers, whom he generally calls Antichrists, deny that Jesus is that promised Messiah, i.e., the eternal Son of God, to be anointed by the Holy Spirit as the Savior of the world, or that as the unique Priest of the New Testament he offers himself for us, or that as King of Kings he rules and protects the universal Church with all power in heaven and on earth, and dominates in the midst of his enemies, or that as Prophet he announces the will of God and every counsel concerning salvation. These things are attacked by those who detract from the eternal Deity of the Son of God, or his true humanity, or his glory and Majesty, or his unique priesthood and sacrifice, or his Kingly or Prophetic office. Thus, by the name of Antichrists, says the blessed Hunnius, the Evangelists count all those who deny Christ either by reason of his person, or by reason of his office, or both. How this is done by the Papists and the great Antichrist is evident even from the Gerhardine disputations alone concerning the glory of God, etc., undermined by the Papists, not to mention countless other writings of Catholics opposed to the Pope and his followers. That the authority of the precepts and promises of Christ is the healer of the human race is more analogous to Socinian language than to the phraseology of Scripture. I add here Estius' commentary: Nor does the Apostle think that only those in the doctrine of religion are liars who deny that Jesus is the Christ (for there were at that time masters of other heresies, of whom Paul and Peter and Jude speak in their epistles), but that these are worse and more pestilential than the rest, that form of speaking signifies, just as we are accustomed to say: What is impiety, if this is not? In this sense, therefore, he says: Who is a liar, if not he who denies that Jesus is the Christ, by saying, Jesus is not the Christ? And indeed the Jews denied that Jesus is the Christ. But John is not dealing with them, but with those who, under the Christian name (which all heretics pretend), taught that Jesus the son of Mary is not the Christ. Such especially were Cerinthus and Ebion, already arisen in John's time. Such besides, whoever were dissolving Jesus, as the Apostle speaks below in chapter 4, that is, were detracting from him something pertaining to his nature, or were attributing something contrary, as other heretics did, moreover, in the time of the Apostles or those who followed afterwards.

He who denies the Father and the Son.] And here the Son is to be taken, as I said, materially, not formally. For they denied that Jesus is the Son of God, which John, speaking to Christians, posits as certain. To deny in this place is taken a little differently than above, and signifies to detract authority from someone, as Matthew 10:33, Luke 12:9, Acts 3:13, 14, ch. 7:35, 1 Timothy 5:8, 2 Timothy 2:12, ch. 3:5, Titus 1:16, he who detracts from Jesus' authority: because the Father acted in all ways to procure the greatest authority for Jesus, John 5:36, ch. 6:27, ch. 8:54.

Latin:

Vers. 22. Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ψεύστης.] Quis est, qui meliori jure mendax & impostor sit dicendus? Comparate enim hoc sumendum, cum sint & alia impostorum genera, sed minora. Nulli deceptores sunt perniciosiores, quam qui id evertunt, unde pendet hominum salus. Nam si Jesus non est Messias, cum se eum esse dixerit, nihil ei credendum est.

Εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀρνεύμενος, ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Χριστός.] Ἀρνεῖσθαι addita particula negativa, quam Latini omitterent, nihil aliud est, quam firme negare. Similis loquutio Luc. 20, 27. & c.22, 34. & Sophoclis: Καὶ οὐκ ἀπαρνοῦμαι τὸ μή.

Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Ἀντίχριστος.] Non quod eximius ille Antichristus primus id facturus sit, sed quod eximie & impudenter supra cæteros, ac majore cum effectu. Antehac ita illa interpretatus erat: Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ψεύστης, quis est mendax ?] Quis potest major esse impostor? Comparate enim hæc sumenda, cum sint & alia impostorum genera.

Εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀρνεύμενος, ὅτι ὁ Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Χριστὸς, nisi qui negat, quoniam Jesus est Christus.] Latine diceremus, nisi qui negat, Jesum esse Christum. Sed Græcis & Ebræis repetita negatio negat validius, ut & veteribus Latinis. Plautus: Jura te non nociturum esse homini hac de re nemini. Ennius: Lapideo sunt corde multi, quos non miseret neminis. Certe inter impostores nullum est genus aut impudentius, aut exitialius illis, qui negant, Jesum esse Messiam, cum omnia Jesu miracula, morsque & resurrectio in hoc à Deo sint data, in hoc perscripta, ut idipsum credatur, Jesum esse Messiam, Joh. XX, 31. nimirum quia & præceptorum & promissorum ejus autoritas humani generis sanatrix inde pendet.

Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Ἀντίχριστος, hic est Anti-Christus.] Faciet hoc supra alios impudenter eximius ille, qui venturus est, Anti-Christus, cui minores isti præludunt, ac propterea in nominis consortium veniunt.

Admittimus facile ἐξήγησιν: modo ne impostores Pseudo-Christi unice censeantur, qui vero non tam directe negant, Jesum esse Christum, quam κατὰ διάνοιαν per consequentiam. Nam si alius sit Messias, Jesus verus Messias credi non potest. Hi autem fallaces, quos generaliter Anti-Christos vocat, negant Jesum esse illum promissum Messiam, h. e. Filium Dei æternum, ungendum esse Spiritu Sancto in Servatorem mundi, vel ut tanquam Sacerdos unicus Novi Testamenti seipsum offerat pro nobis, tanquam Rex Regum cum omni potestate in cœlo & in terra regat & tueatur Ecclesiam universam, & dominetur in medio inimicorum suorum, tanquam Propheta annunciet voluntatem Dei & omne consilium de salute. Hæc impugnant qui vel Filii Dei æterna Deitati, aut veræ humanitati vel gloriæ ejusdem & Majestati, vel sacerdotio & sacrificio unico, vel Regio, aut Prophetico officio derogant. Sic Anti-Christorum nomine, inquit B. Hunnius, censent Evangelista omnes eos, qui Christum negant sive ratione personæ, sive ratione officii, sive utriusque. Quod quomodo à Pontificiis & Anti-Christo magno fiat, vel è solis dispp. Gerhardinis de gloria Dei &c. per Pontificios labefactata constat, ut innumera alia Catholicorum scripta Papæ, & asseclis ejus opposita taceam. Autoritatem præceptorum & promissorum Christi humani generis sanatricem esse, Socinianæ λέξει magis analoga est, quam scripturæ phrasi. Addo hic Estii com- mentarium: Neque sentit Apostolus solos eos in do- ctrina religionis esse mendaces, qui negant, Jesum esse Christum (erant enim illo tempore aliarum hæresium magistri, de quibus Paulus & Petrus & Judas in suis epistolis) sed hos esse cæteris pejores & pestilentiores, significat ista loquendi forma, quomodo solemus dice- re: Quæ est impietas, si hæc non est: Hoc igitur sensu dicit: Quis est mendax, si non ille, qui negat, Jesum esse Christum, dicendo, Jesus non est Christus? Et qui- dem Jesum esse Christum negarunt Judæi. Verum de his Johannes non agit, sed de iis, qui sub nomine Chri- stiano, (quod omnes hæretici prætendunt) docebant Jesum Mariæ filium non esse Christum. Quales im- primis fuerunt Cerinthus & Ebion, jam exorti Jo- hannis tempore. Quales præterea, quicunque Jesum solvebant, ut Apostolus loquitur infra cap. IV. id est, aliquid ad naturam ejus pertinens ei detrahebant, aut contrarium aliquid attribuebant, ut fecerunt alii insuper hæretici tempore Apostolorum aut postea subsequuti.

Ὁ ἀρνύμενος τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ τὸν Υἱόν.] Et hic τὸν Υἱὸν su- mendum, ut dixi, materialiter, non formaliter. Negabant enim illi Jesum esse Filium Dei, quod Johannes ut Christia- nis loquens pro certo ponit. Ἀρνεῖσθαι hoc loco paulo aliter sumitur, quam supra, & significat autoritatem alicui detrahe- re, ut Matth. 10, 33. Luc. 12, 9. Act. 3, 13. 14. c. 7, 35. 1. Tim. 5, 8. 2. Tim. 2, 12. c. 3, 5. Tit. 1, 16. qui Jesu autoritatem detrahit: quia Pater id omnibus modis egit, ut Jesu autoritatem maximam conciliaret, Joh. 5, 36. c. 6, 27. c. 8, 54.

## 2:23
V. 23. Everyone who denies the Son, does not have the Father.] He does not have the Father, that is, he does not hold what is the Father's ultimate and most perfect will, Matthew 11:27, John 1:18, ch. 14:6, 9, Hebrews 1:3, 2 Corinthians 4:4, Colossians 1:15, to which places, what we have said, there is no need to repeat here. Take 'to have' here as below in V. 12, he who has the Son, this Manuscript adds, which other Manuscripts also have, and the Latin and the Syrian, he who confesses the Son also has the Father, that is, he who acknowledges Jesus as truthful in words and deeds, he also shows that the Father's will is known to him.

And in the previous commentary: Ὁ ἀρνύμενος τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ τὸν Υἱὸν, who denies the Father & the Son.] John assumes as confessed that Jesus is the Son of God, speaking to Christians, who were Christians for the very reason that they believed this. Ἀρνεῖσθαι, however, here means to detract from the faith and authority, as in Matt. 10:33, Luke 12:9, Acts 3:13, 14, & ch. 7:35, & elsewhere; he who directly detracts from Jesus' authority, he by consequence detracts from the Father's. For the Father acted in every way to reconcile the authority of Jesus, John 5:36, ch. 6:27, ch. 8:24, 54.

Vers. 23. Πᾶς ὁ ἀρνύμενος τὸν Υἱὸν οὐδὲ τὸν Πατέρα ἔχει, everyone who denies the Son, does not have the Father either.] He who detracts from the authority of Jesus, he does not even hold to God, who is the Father of Jesus, that is, he does not know that will of God which is saving. In this sense Jesus himself said that there is no one who knows the Father except the Son, and he to whom the Son shall deign to reveal Him, Matt. 11:27, and that no one comes to the Father except through him, John 14:6. Add Heb. 1:3, 2 Cor. 4:4, Col. 1:15.

That indeed was certain, that Christ was the Son of God: But the χριστομάχοι of that time distinguished Jesus from Christ and the Son of God. Therefore the Evangelist could not assume this as an ὁμολογύμενον, which they rendered a κρινόμενον. And why should we take τὸν Υἱὸν only materially, not formally, where the relative opposition between Father and Son demands a formal meaning? That the Antichrist also, against whom St. John here moved his pen, suppose Cerinthus, with Ebion, formally denied the Son of God, that is, denied that Jesus was the Son of God begotten of the Father before the ages, and held him to be a mere man, as far as substance is concerned, has been shown before from the ancient Doctors. The words speak not of authority, but of the Deity of Jesus of Nazareth being detracted from, according to its proper meaning, which, just as those same θεοκτόνοι, or Deicides, as Ignatius calls them, denied, so in that regard not only Samosatenus, Arius, and Photinus followed them, but Even that great oriental Antichrist Mahomet with his followers, whose impious voices are known, [saying] that God does not have a Son, because he does not have a woman. If one prefers to interpret with Grotius that 'not having the Father' is not holding the will of the Father, which always is and has been the same: just as Jesus Christ is yesterday, today, and the same forever, Heb. XIII, 8, this will apply most especially not only to the oriental but also to the great occidental Antichrist, who perverts the will of God, both legal and evangelical, in many ways. This is not the place to expound upon this. But it deals directly with the denied nature of the Son, by the denial of which the nature of the Father is also removed, because Father and Son are relations, which posit and remove each other. Which also applies equally to the Holy Spirit, even if he is not mentioned here, because the Pneumatomachi had not yet arisen. For the Holy Spirit also has a relation to the Father and to the Son, from whom both he is breathed, as the Spirit of the Father and the Son, and these three are one, as St. John testifies, 1 Ep. V, 7. And those sayings, Heb. I, 3, 2 Cor. IV, 4, Col. I, 15, speak not of the will, but of the ὁμοεσία of the Father and the Son, as we have taught for each in its place. Therefore, he is not speaking of the Roman Antichrist, whom he had designated in v. 18 as about to come, and whom the Apostle called τὸν ἀντικείμενον, 2 Thess. II, 4, but he is already speaking of the forerunner of the Antichrist of his own age: who agree in this, that they oppose Christ, even if Christ is not infested by all in the same way, and those Antichrists in the time of St. John and the other Apostles were the great forerunners of that τῶ ἀντικειμέ- νω in that they especially undermined the office of Christ, asserting the observation of the law to be necessary for salvation, and thus evacuating the merit of Christ, Acts XV, Gal. II, v. ult. cap. V, 4. Estius explains this verse not of Mahomet, nor of the Antichrist foretold in 2 Thess. II, but equally of the heretics of that time, of whom he had already said, 'now many Antichrists have arisen.' For he says, in this part he points to them as if with a finger, saying: 'This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son,' as if he were saying: 'Whoever today denies the Father and the Son is an Antichrist, of the number of those whom I just called Antichrists.' This commentary, which Irenaeus hands down in lib. III, cap. 15, and others after him, agrees most with both the context and the Apostolic time. For these things are said especially against Cerinthus, the leader of the Judaizers, who, according to Epiphanius, invented the story that Christ came into Jesus in the form of a dove, and revealed to him a certain unknown Father. Concerning which Father the Carpocratians also invented many things. John therefore says that those who deny that Jesus is the Christ and the Son of God flatter themselves in vain regarding the Father. For the Jews did not acknowledge or expect any other Son of God than the Christ or Messiah promised to them. Whence their high priest said to Jesus: 'I adjure you by the living God, that you tell us if you are the Christ the Son of God,' Matth. XXVI. Wherefore, he who denied that Jesus was the Christ promised in the law, like the Cerinthians, consequently denied that he was the Son of God. Hence it is that John in this epistle, most especially in chapters IV and V, diligently inculcates this doctrine, that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, and finally, about to close the epistle, says: 'We know that the Son of God has come,' namely that very expected Messiah. What was brought forward for the previous opinions regarding the Greek article accomplishes nothing. For it is certain that the article is frequently used by Greek authors without emphasis, just as if it had not been added. But what Estius thinks, that those words of the Latin text, 'he who confesses the Son and the Father,' have fallen out of the Greek codices, is not to be admitted. For even if they are held in the Syriac text and in some Greek ones, as also in Cyril, l. IX, in Joh. c. 47, nevertheless these cannot prejudice the other codices, which are superior in number and authority, which Oecumenius supports by not reading them. Therefore others think that they were annotated by a reader of the people and crept into the text.

Latin:

V. 23. Πᾶς ὁ ἀρνύμενος τὸν Υἱὸν, οὐδὲ τὸν Πατέρα ἔχει.] Non habet Patrem, id est, non tenet, quæ sit Patris ultima & per- fectissima voluntas, Matth. 11, 27. Joh. I, 18. c. 14, 6. 9. Ebr. I, 3. 2. Cor. 4, 4. Col. I, 15. ad quæ loca, quæ diximus, nihil opus hic repeti. Habere hic sume ut infra V, 12. ὁ ἔχων τὸν Υἱὸν, ad- dit hic Manuscriptus, quod & alii Manuscripti habent & La- tinus & Syrus, ὁ ὁμολογῶν τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ τὸν Πατέρα ἔχει, id est, qui Jesum pro verace agnoscit verbis & factis, is & ostendit notam sibi esse Patris voluntatem.

Et in priori commentatione: Ὁ ἀρνύμενος τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ τὸν Υἱὸν, qui negat Patrem & Filium.] Filium Dei esse Jesum, pro confesso sumit Jo- hannes Christianis loquens, qui ideo, quod id crederent, erant Christiani. Ἀρνεῖσθαι autem hic est fidem autorita- temque detrahere, ut Matth. 10, 33. Luc. 12, 9. Act. 3, 13. 14. & c. 7, 35. & alibi, qui Jesu directe detrahit, autoritatem, is per consequentiam Patri eam detrahit. Pater enim omni modo id egit, ut Jesu autoritatem conciliaret, Joh. 5, 36. c. 6, 27. c. 8, 24. 54.

Vers. 23. Πᾶς ὁ ἀρνύμενος τὸν Υἱὸν οὐδὲ τὸν Πατέρα ἔχει, omnis, qui negat Filium, nec Patrem habet.] Qui Jesu detrahit autoritatem, is ne Deum quidem, qui Pater est Jesu, tenet, id est, non novit eam, quæ salutaris est, Dei voluntatem. Hoc sensu dixit ipse Jesus, neminem esse, qui Patrem noverit, præter Filium, & eum, cui Filius di- gnabitur revelare, Matth. 11, 27. & ad Patrem neminem venire, nisi per ipsum Joh. 14, 6. Adde Ebr. I, 3. 2. Cor. 4, 4. Col. I, 15.

Id quidem certum erat, Christum esse Filium Dei: Sed Jesum à Christo & Filio Dei discernebant istius temporis χριστομάχοι. Non ergo hoc tan- quam ὁμολογύμενον assumere poterat Evangelista, quod illi reddebant κρινόμενον. Et cur τὸν Υἱὸν sume- re deberemus tantum materialiter, non formaliter, ubi oppositio relativa inter Patrem & Filium po- tius formale significatum postulat? Anti-Christum etiam illum, contra quem stylum hic movit S. Jo- hannes, Cerinthum puta, cum Ebione, Filium Dei formaliter negasse, hoc est, inficiatum esse, Jesum esse Filium Dei à Patre ante secula genitum, eum- que pro puro homine, quantum ad substantiam, habuisse, antea è priscis Doctoribus ostensum. Non de autoritate, sed de Deitate Jesu Nazareno detra- cta verba secundum propriam significationem lo- quuntur, quam uti iidem illi θεοκτόνοι Deicidæ, quos vocat Ignatius, negarunt, ita sequutus in eo ipsos est non Samosatenus tantum, Arius & Photinus, sed etiam Anti-Christus ille Magnus orientalis Maho- metus cum asseclis, cujus impiæ voces notæ sunt, Deum non habere Filium, quia non habet mulie- rem. Si cum Grotio interpretari quis malit non ha- bere Patrem esse non tenere voluntatem Patris, quæ semper eadem est, & fuit: quemadmodum & Jesus Christus heri, hodie, idem & in secula, Ebr. XIII, 8. non orientali tantum, sed occidentali etiam Anti-Christo Magno id maxime conveniet, volun- tatem tam legalem, tum Evangelicam Dei multis modis pervertenti. Quod edisserere hujus non est loci. Sed agit directe de Filii natura abnegata, cu- jus abnegatione tollitur etiam natura Patris, quia relata sunt Pater & Filius, quæ se mutuo ponunt & tollunt. Quod etiam pariter de Spiritu sancto lo- cum habet, etsi hic commemoratus non sit, quia Pneumatomachi tum nondum orti erant. Nam & Spiritus sanctus relationem habet ad Patrem, & ad Filium, à quo utroque spiratur, ceu Spiritus Patris & Filii, & hi tres unum sunt, teste S. Johanne 1. ep. V, 7. Nec de voluntate, sed de ὁμοεσία Patris & Filii loquuntur illa dicta, Ebr. I, 3. 2. Cor. IV, 4. Col. I, 15. ut de singulis suo loco docui- mus. Non igitur de Anti-Christo Romano, quem v. 18. designarat ceu venturum, quemque τὸν ἀντι- κείμενον dixit Apostolus 2. Thess. II, 4. sed de prælu- sore Anti-Christi suæ ætatis jam loquitur: qui con- veniunt in eo, quod Christum oppugnent, etsi non eadem ratione Christus ab omnibus infestetur, & Anti-Christi illi tempore S. Johannis & aliorum Apostolorum prodromi magni illius τῶ ἀντικειμέ- νε in eo maxime fuerint, quod officium Christi labefactarint, legis observationem ad salutem ne- cessariam adserentes, & ita meritum Christi evacu- antes, Actor. XV. Gal. II. v. ult. cap. V, 4. Estius non de Mahometo, nec de Anti-Christo 2. Thess. II. præ- nunciato, sed de temporis istius hæreticis pariter hoc comma explicat, de quibus jam dixerat, nunc Anti-Christi multi facti sunt. Hæc enim, inquit, par- te jam eos quasi digito monstrat dicens: Hic est Anti- Christus, qui negat Patrem & Filium, ac si dicat: Quicunque hodie negat Patrem & Filium, Anti- Christus est, ex eorum numero, quos paulo dixi Anti- Christos. Hic commentarius, quem tradit Irenæus lib. III. cap. 15. & alii post eum, maxime convenit tam contextui, quam tempori Apostolico. Dicuntur enim hæc præcipue contra Cerinthum, Judaizantium Principem, qui referente Epiphanio, fabulabatur, Christum in specie columbæ venisse in Jesum, & re- velasse ei quemdam ignotum Patrem. De quo Patre etiam Carpocratiani plurima commenti sunt. Dicit ergo Johannes illos sibi frustra blandiri de Patre, qui Jesum negant esse Christum & Filium Dei. Non enim alium Dei Filium agnoscebant aut expectabant Ju- dæi, quam Christum seu Messiam sibi promissum. Un- de Pontifex eorum dicebat ad Jesum: Adjuro te per Deum vivum, ut dicas nobis, si tu es Christus Filius Dei, Matth. XXVI. Quare qui Jesum negabat Chri- stum in lege promissum, ut Cerinthiani, consequenter eum Filium Dei negabat. Hinc est, quod Johannes in hac epistola potissime cap. IV. & V. diligenter incul- cat hanc doctrinam, Jesum esse Christum Filium Dei, & denique clausurus epistolam dicit: Scimus quo- niam Filius Dei venit, scilicet ille ipse Messias expe- ctatus. Quod pro prioribus opinionibus afferebatur de articulo Græco, nihil efficit. Constat enim articu- lum frequenter à Græcis Autoribus usurpari sine em- phasi, perinde atque si additus non esset. Quod vero Estius putat, verba illa Latini textus, qui confitetur Filium & Patrem, excidisse è Græcis Codicibus, admittendum non est. Etsi enim in Syriaco textu habeantur & in Græcis nonnullis, ut & apud Cy- rillum l. IX. in Joh. c. 47. Non tamen hæc præjudi- care possunt codicibus cæteris, numero & autori- tate potioribus, quibus Oecumenius adstipulatur illa non legentibus. Ideo censent alii ea annotata à po- puli lectore in textum irrepsisse.

## 2:24
Vers. 24.

Ὑμεῖς ὃν ὃ ἠκούσατε ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, ἐν ὑμῖν μενέτω.] Let that which you have received from us Apostles be fixed in your hearts. I take 'from the beginning' regarding the time of the preached Gospel, and that from the subject matter, since otherwise that word is taken in various ways, as we said at the beginning of this epistle. Moreover, the construction is κατὰ σημαι- νόμενον, as also below in 27; for he begins the speech as if he were about to say: 'Retain what you heard from the beginning,' but for that 'retain' he put, which means the same thing, 'let it remain in you.' See a similar [construction] in Apocal. III, 12, and Eph. I, 13.

Ἐὰν ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ ὃ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ἠκούσατε, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν τῷ υἱῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ μενεῖτε;] That is, you will be most closely joined to the Father and the Son, you will enjoy their highest favor and friendship. He will now explain what is the consequence of this thing. See Joh. VI, 56.

Those things with which he had previously concluded the commentary on the present chapter are not dissimilar.

Ὑμεῖς ὧν ὃ ἠκούσατε ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ἐν ὑμῖν μενέτω, let what you heard from the beginning remain in you.] Thus he began the speech as if he were about to say: 'Therefore, guard what you learned from the beginning.' But for this 'guard,' he put, signifying the same thing, 'let it remain in you,' with no regard for the construction, while he looks to the meaning. A similar kind of speaking follows shortly in v. 27. 'From the beginning,' namely when the word of the Gospel was first announced to you: Thus 'from the beginning' is taken both elsewhere and above II, 7, and below III, 11. 'Let it remain in you,' that is, let it be deeply fixed in the mind, let each one be

Βαθεῖαν ἄλοκα διὰ φρενὸς καρπούμενος, Ἀφ᾽ ἧς τὰ κεδνὰ βλαστάνει βουλεύματα. Bearing deep furrows sunk through the heart, From which those beautiful counsels spring forth.

Ἐὰν ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ ὃ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ἠκούσατε καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ τῷ Πατρὶ μενεῖτε.] If what you heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son and in the Father. If you have preserved the evangelical dogma with careful custody of the mind, you will be most closely joined to both the Son and the Father, and all their benefits will pertain to you. Moreover, all those benefits are contained under the name of eternal life, as the following things explain.

But that not only the favor of the Father and the Son is indicated, but a most intimate communion, those things which we observed at chapter I, 3, teach. In the better Greek manuscripts it is not μενέτω (let it remain), but μένει (it remains) in you, by which they are made certain that the anointing will not depart, unless they cast it off by their own fault. Just as Oecumenius also reads it as an indicative.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

Ὑμεῖς ὃν ὃ ἠκούσατε ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, ἐν ὑμῖν μενέτω.] Fixum sit in cordibus vestris id, quod à nobis Apostolis accepistis. Ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς sumo, de tempore prædicati Evangelii, idque ex subje- cta materia, cum alioqui ea vox varie sumatur, ut diximus ad hujus epistolæ initium. Est autem constructio κατὰ σημαι- νόμενον, ut & infra 27. incipit enim orationem quasi dicturus: vos quod ab initio audistis, retinete : sed pro illo retinete po- suit, quod idem valet, maneat in vobis. Simile vide Apocal. III, 12. & Eph. I, 13.

Ἐὰν ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ ὃ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ἠκούσατε, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν τῷ υἱῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ μενεῖτε;] Id est, eritis conjunctissimi Patri & Filio, summo eorum favore & amicitia fruemini. Cui rei quid sit consequens, jam exponet. Vide Joh. VI, 56.

Non absimiliter habent ea, quibus commenta- tionem in præsens caput antea concluserat.

Ὑμεῖς ὧν ὃ ἠκούσατε ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ἐν ὑμῖν μενέτω, vos quod audistis ab initio in vobis permaneat.] Ita incœpit ora- tionem, quasi dicturus esset: vos ergo quod ab initio di- dicistis, id custodite. At pro hoc custodite, posuit idem significans, maneat in vobis, nulla habita constructionis ratione, dum τὸ σημαινόμενον respicit. Simile loquendi genus mox sequitur v. 27. Ab initio scilicet cum primum annuntiatus est vobis Evangelii sermo: Sic ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς tum alibi sumitur, tum supra II, 7. & infra III, 11. Maneat in vobis, id est, animo infixum penitus hæreat, sit quisque

Βαθεῖαν ἄλοκα διὰ φρενὸς καρπούμενος, Ἀφ᾽ ἧς τὰ κεδνὰ βλαστάνει βουλεύματα. Sulcos profundos corde demersos gerens ' Unde illa sese pulchra consilia exferunt.

Ἐὰν ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ ὃ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς ἠκούσατε καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ τῷ Πατρὶ μενεῖτε.] Si in vobis permanserit, quod audivistis ab initio, & vos in Filio & Patre manebitis. Si solicita animi custodia Evangelicum dogma conserva- veritis, eritis & Filio & Patri conjunctissimi, omnia- que eorum beneficia ad vos pertinebunt. Ea autem beneficia omnia vitæ æternæ nomine continentur, ut sequentia explicant.

Non autem favorem tantum indicari Patris & Filii, sed arctissumam communionem, ea, quæ ad cap. I, 3. observavimus, docent. In Græcis potioribus non est μενέτω maneat, sed μένει manet in vobis, quæ certi redduntur, non recessuram unctionem, nisi excutiant eam suapte culpa. Quemadmodum enunciativum etiam legit Oecumenius.

## 2:25
Verse 25. Καὶ ἅυτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐπαγγελία,] as if he were to say: ... For neither are light or trivial rewards sought.

He said 'promise' for the thing promised, as he now explains.

Ἣν αὐτὸς ἐπηγγείλατο ἡμῖν.] Αὐτὸς, namely the Son of God in the name of the Father. Thus also below in verse 27, ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ.

Τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον.] It is a construction similar to that: 'The city which I am building is yours': except that there the accusative is placed before the verb, here after the verb. But these things did not happen to our writers by art, but by chance.

Nothing here is to be imagined as casual or fortuitous, where all things are of art and divine inspiration: nor is there need for that comparison with the poet. For anyone sees that the construction is ordinary, provided a word derived from the noun is understood: an announcement, namely announcing eternal life.

Latin:

Vers. 25. Καὶ ἅυτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐπαγγελία,] quasi dicat: ... Nec enim levia aut ludicra petuntur Præmia.

Promissionem dixit pro re promissa, ut jam explicat.

Ἣν αὐτὸς ἐπηγγείλατο ἡμῖν.] Αὐτὸς nempe Filius DEI Pa- tris nomine. Sic & infra 27. ἀπ᾿ αὐτοῦ.

Τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον.] Est constructio similis illi: Urbem quam statuo vestra est: Nisi quod ibi Accusativus ante verbum ponitur, hic post ver- bum. Verum hæc nostris scriptoribus non ex arte, sed casu provenerunt.

Nihil hic casuale, aut fortuitum fingendum, ubi omnia artis & inspirationis divinæ sunt: neque col- latione illa cum Poëta opus est. Quilibet enim vi- det constructionem ordinariam esse, modo subin- telligatur verbum è nomine oriundum: annuntia- tio, vitam æternam scil. annuntians.

## 2:26
Verse 26. Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν περὶ τῶν πλανώντων ὑμᾶς.] Ὑμᾶς, that is, the Jews, from whose race you also are. On their account I began this discourse and extended it further. You have the verb πλανᾷν concerning that kind of men in Matthew 24, verses 4, 5, 11, 24.

It is evident here that those things which he wrote just before refer to the heretics of his own time.

Latin:

Vers. 26. Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν περὶ τῶν πλανώντων ὑμᾶς.] Ὑμᾶς, id est, Judæos, ex quorum gente & vos estis. Illorum occasione sermonem hunc orsus sum & produxi longius. Verbum πλανᾷν de illo hominum genere habes Matth. 24. v. 4. 5. 11. 24.

Patet hic ea, quæ proxime scripsit, respicere sui temporis hæreticos.

## 2:27
Verse 27. Καὶ ὑμεῖς τὸ χρίσμα, ὃ ἐλάβετε ἀπ᾽ ἀυτοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν μένει.] Καὶ here is for 'but'. For he opposes the believing Jews to the unbelieving. It is a construction equal to that which is above in verse 25. The matter, however, is the same as above in verse 20. He wishes to remove from himself the suspicion as if he hoped less well of them. Ἀπ᾿ ἀυτοῦ, from Christ; ἐν ὑμῖν μένει, is within you, the same as 'you have' above.

And you have no need that anyone should teach you.] Namely, concerning that which, as I have said, must be done in individual circumstances. You are taught of God, Jerem. 31, 34. Joh. 6, 45. For there are certain differences which times, places, and persons require. Therefore, there is often need of admonition to find the way of duties. See, if you wish, Seneca, epistle XCIV.

But as the same anointing teaches you concerning all things and is true, and is not a lie, and as it has taught you, you shall abide in it.] It is the language of one hoping well and wishing well. 'It is true and not a lie' is primarily a metonymy of the abstract for the concrete. For 'a lie' here signifies 'a liar,' just as 'truth' signifies 'true,' 2 Cor. IV, 14. Then the same thing is said twice, first by affirming, then by denying the opposite, just as above I, 5, and in this chapter III, 8. A similar expression is found in 1 Sam. I, 11. Ezech. 18, 21. c. 33, 15.

Latin:
