A greater unity is certainly required for the witnesses in heaven, because this testimony is the highest and the first; therefore it requires the firmest and highest unity, such as is not that which consists only in consent, but that which has ὁμοεσίαν as its foundation.

They are, however, εἰς τὸ ἓν not only by reason of the solemn ordinary promulgation through the sacred ministry of the dispensation, 1 Cor. IV. v. 1, of efficacy and power for the victory of the world, and of the object of men, which are destined for salvation, but also by reason of harmonic agreement, regarding the testimony concerning Jesus, which the Gospel exhibits to our hearts and senses, indeed with a sonorous voice to our ears, and baptism and the supper exhibit by a visible sacrament. Baptism testifies to the divine and human nature of Jesus: because we are baptized not in the name of the Son of God ἀσάρκγ but ἐνσάρκγ, conf. Matth. XXVIII. 19. Act. II. 38.

VIII. v. 16. & the supper, because it is the blood of man, but which is also the blood proper to God, meritorious for the remission of sins, Matth. XXVI. 26. & poured out for the redemption of the Church, Act. XX. 28. 1. Petr. I. 18. The water of baptism testifies concerning Jesus, that he is the Christ, in whose name we obtain regeneration, Joh. III. 5. & the remission of sins, Act. II. 38. The blood of Christ in the Eucharist testifies concerning our drinking into one mystical body of Christ, 1. Cor. XIII. 13. concerning the New Testament and the fruition of the covenant of grace, because the cup is the New Testament in the blood of Christ, Luc. XXII. 20. 1. Cor. XI. 14. concerning the immanence of Christ in us, & of us in Christ, Joh. VI. 56. concerning our vivification on account of Christ, v. 51. 53. 57. 58. concerning future resuscitation and the attainment of eternal life, v. 40. From this Johannine narrative it is evident how both the mystery of the most holy Trinity is asserted therefrom, since here we have the word Trinity, the plurality of Divine persons, their Trinity and order, as well as the ὁμοοσίαν or unity of essence, the personality of the Holy Spirit, as also the property of each Divine person, which the names exhibit when explained according to the sense of Scripture: and also the nature and character of the Word and the Sacraments: and indeed the divine origin and authority of the Word, which it has in itself and independently of the Church, the perspicuity and efficacy or power of the same, as it is held in the Church in the Scriptures through which God testifies: but the number of the Sacraments, that there are only two, not more in the New Testament, as also their common use, that the Laity are not to be excluded from the perception of the blood of Christ in the Holy supper, because by the blood they are to be confirmed in faith, and to overcome the world, and so that testimony of God they also ought to λαμβάνειν receive, as well as the salutary effect, that they are not bare signs but media ἐνεργητικὰ, as well as the definition of the marks of the Church, that indeed these, and no others, are the proper marks of the Church, the preaching of the Word, and the use of the sacraments of Baptism and the Eucharist, as being testimonies sufficient for our salvation concerning Jesus Christ, and so also sufficient for the Church, in which that salvation flourishes; In what place therefore ἐν τῇ γῇ I see these three testimonies flourishing without manifest external repugnance, in that place I perceive that the visible assembly of Christ is gathered, and so that it is the Church without doubt. For to them Jesus comes by water, not by water only, but by water and blood, and the Spirit himself is he who testifies among them, whose Word is the Gospel, they are born of God, and through the Word they overcome the world. Does not universally, says the Blessed Dorscheus l. c §. 32. we see it to be so arranged, that there is an assembly of some religion where the proper and primary testimonies of God, who is worshipped in that religion, appear without the repugnance and contradiction of that place. Thus there was gentilism, where oracles, responses, auspices, and the remaining primary documents of gentilism appear. Thus also there is Judaism, where the Talmudic perversion of the Old Testament, with circumcision and the vain observations of the Jews, is observed. There is Mahommedanism, where the Alcoran, as the dogmatic testimony of Mahommedanism, and other testimonies of it are urged. Thus therefore where the three testimonies of the Christian religion, the Word of the Gospel and the two Sacraments are observed, there is the Church of the Christian religion. See more concerning those three witnesses in heaven in the Blessed Gerhard, concerning these witnesses on earth in the disputations of the Blessed Dorscheus cited.

The testimony of God is greater] For the testimony of God outweighs many testimonies of men. For this is the testimony of God which he has testified concerning his Son] For here means now indeed. For he applies the general dictum to this special cause. That Spirit, that is, those works are the greatest testimony, by which God shows Jesus to be his Son, Joh. V. 36. X. 25, 38. XIV. 11. XV. 24. In the Manuscript, for he has testified.

As St. John deduced the cause of the world’s victory through faith and the origin of this victorious faith from that twin triplicity of witnesses ἐν οὐρανῷ and ἐν τῇ γῇ, so now he treats of receiving that testimony as truly divine. Since the μαρτυρία τoῦ θεoῦ is greater not only by reason of efficacy and ἐνεργείας than the μαρτυρία τῶν ἀνθρώπων: Conf. 1 Cor. I. 6, 7, 8. Grotius indeed rightly observes that the word ὅτι here signifies "now truly," but he does not rightly say that the general dictum of Deut. XVII. 6 is applied to this special case by this word. For no human testimonies had been adduced in the preceding verses, but rather those of God testifying both immediately, as Father, Word, and Holy Spirit, and mediately through the Word, the water, and the blood, which likewise testify. Nor is anything held in verse 9 concerning this Spirit or his works; much less are those works said to be the greatest testimony by which God shows that Jesus is His Son. Which is not even true. For the greatest testimony is that which those three witnesses in heaven bear: nor is that testimony of works, if miracles are understood, ordinary and perpetual in the Church, which nevertheless always needs witnesses, and can never be without witnesses; and the words which follow v. 11, expressly exhibit that testimony which God has testified concerning his Son, so that there is no need to have recourse elsewhere, or to understand testimony metonymically concerning the works through which God has testified,

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Ὅτι τρεῖς εἰσιν οἱ μαρτυροῦντες ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὁ πατὴρ, καὶ ὁ λόγος, καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, καὶ οἱ τρεῖς εἰς τὸ ἕν εἰσι. Καὶ τρεῖς εἰσιν οἱ μαρτυροῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸ αἷμα] Quæ plurima viri eruditi hoc de lo- co differeure, hic non repetam. Tantum dicam Manuscri- ptum illum antiquissimum, cujus autoritate plurimum u- tor, non aliud hic habere, quam, ὅτι τρεῖς εἰσιν οἱ μαρτυροῦν- τες τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸ αἷμα, non adjecto illo quod & Syrus & Arabs legere: καὶ οἱ τρεῖς ἕν εἶσι. Ego hanc quam ex Manuscripto posui lectionem, & quæ a mul- tis aliis confirmatur libris veteribus, veram puto. Neque vero Arianis ablatas voces quasdam, sed potius additas, un- de colligerent, Patrem & FILIUM & Spiritum Sanctum non esse unum nisi consensu, quomodo Spiritus, aqua & san- guis in unum testimonium consentiunt. Quod cum vide- rent Catholici, abstulisse quidem eos illud, quod de Patre, Filio & Spiritu Sancto insertum fuerat, sed reliquisse illud tres unum esse, quia id ita positum ipsis nocere non pote- rat. Alios vero relicto illo loco de Patre Filio & Spiritu Sancto ibi quidem posuisse, Unum sunt; de Spiritu vero, a- qua & sanguine, in unum sunt, ut alius modus unitatis significaretur. Johannes hic causam reddit, cur loquutus fuerit non de Spiritu tantum, cujus præcipua in hoc ne- gotio est autoritas, verum etiam de aqua & sanguine, quia in illis etiam non exigua est testimoniifides, & ter- narius numerus in testibus est perfectissimus. Μαρτυροῦν- τες Ebræo more pro μάρτυρες. Solet autem vox te- stis etiam de rebus inanimis dici, ut Genes. XXXI. v. 48. 51.

Textus hujus Canonicam autoritatem cum So- cinianis, & in eorum gratiam vellicat Grotius, quem olim Ariani mutilarunt, quos etiam de- levisse in Evangelio S. Johannis cap. VI. vers. 24. verba Πνεῦμα ὁ Θεὸς, testis est Ambrosius l. III. de Spiritu Sancto cap. 11. quemadmodum Socrates libr. VII. Hist. Eccles. cap. 32. & in Tripart. l. VII. cap. 4. perhibet, παλαιὺς ἑρμηνεῖς veteres Inter- pretes significasse, quod quidam epistolam illam pri- mam Johannis depravarint, ῥαδιουργήσαντες τὴν ἐπισολὴν, quo in Christo hominem à Deo separa- rent. Omnes enim parietes Ecclesiarum hæreticos (Arianos) possedisse docet Hieronymus in Psal. CXXXIII. unde questus Athanasius in epist. ad solit. vitam agent: Quæ nunc Ecclesia Christum libere adorat? Siquidem ea, si pia est, periculis sub- jacet. In illa orthodoxorum Episcoporum oppres- sione, Arianorum vero in sedes Episcopales e- vectione quid non tentavit hæretica audacia? Multo certe verisimilius est, comma hoc esse ab Arianis erasum è codicibus, quam additum â Ca- tholicis, quum de horum fraudibus nemo que- stus sit, habuerintque illi alia testimonia ὁμου- σίας, & Deitatis ejusdem Filii & Spiritus Sancti cum Patre; illorum vero fraudes, ut ostensum, notarint veteres, quemadmodum constat ἀλόγυς vel Alogianos totum Johannem expunxisse, casu vero facile excidere possit aliquis versiculus, in- seri non item. Et testatur Hieronymus in Pro- leg. epist. Canon. ad Eustach. de infidelibus translatoribus. Hæ epistolæ, inquit, si ut ab eis (Græcis Codicibus) digestæ sunt, ita quo- que ab Interpretibus verterentur fideliter in La- tinum eloquium, nec ambiguitatem legentibus facerent, nec sermonum sese varietas impugna- ret, illo PRÆCIPUE loco, ubi de unitate Trinitatis in prima Johannis positum legimus, in quo etiam ab INFIDELIBUS transla- toribus (Interpretibus Latinis, lue Ariana in- sectis) multum erratum esse à veritate comperi- mus, tria tantummodo vocabula, hoc est aqua, san- guinis, & Spiritus in ipsa sua editione ponentibus, & Patris, Verbique ac Spiritus testimonium omit- tentibus, in quo maxime fides Catholica robora- tur, & Patris & Filii & Spiritus Sancti una di- vinitatis essentia comprobatur. In quibus Hiero- nymi verbis B. Gerhardus tria potissimum obser- vanda esse monuit th. 9. 1. Tempore Hieronymi locum illum in Græcis Epistolarum Apostolicarum Codicibus extitisse, alias enim non posset Latinos Interpretes infidelitatis accusare, quod eum omise- rint. 2. In omnibus Græcis codicibus eo tempore il- lum fuisse, alias potuissent illi Interpretes Hierony- mo obvertere, quod non invenerint eum in omni- bus Codicibus. 3. Locum illum ex Hieronymi sen- tentia fidem Catholicam de Patris, Filii & Spiritus Sancti una divinitatis essentia maxime roborare. Atque si eo tempore fuisset locus dubius, suspectus & controversus, non potuisset illi tantum robur ac pondus tribui. Hæc recte se habent. Grotiana vero mere precariis hypothesibus & conjectu- ris vanissimis constant. Unde enim obsecro do- cebitur ab Arianis quasdam voces additas, eas- dem vicissim à Catholicis ablatas? Nonnullis ta- men relictis vel etiam immutatis.

Quo de multis veteribus libris Manuscripto Grotiano consentientibus dicitur, docendum e- rat, non nude asserendum. Plures certe co- dices comma illud asservarunt, etsi in nonnullis id desideretur, qui ad Latinam translationem efformati sunt. Recentiores enim illi sunt tem- poribus Hieronymi, cujus ævo adhuc in omni- bus Græcis codicibus textus ille inventus est. Qui- bus Hieronymi codicibus Britannicus vetustissimus addendus, qui tantæ autoritatis Erasmo fuit, ut ex eodem non dubitarit in posterioribus edi- tionibus accuratissima cura recognitis restitue- re. Addendi Codices illi, quos sequuti sunt e- ditionis Complutensis Anno 1517. autores, ad quam adhibita esse castigatissima, omni ex par- te, ac vetustissima exemplaria in præfatione monetur, nec non codices Laur. Valle, qui nullam his codicibus suis observavit discrepan- tiam, ut & codices Hervagii, qui Basileæ Græca Biblia Veteris & Novi Testamenti Anno 1545. edidit, & diversas lectiones ex optimorum ex- emplarium collatione adhibuit, in hoc autem loco nullam lectionis diversitatem invenit: I- tem codices Rob. Stephani, in quorum septem quidem desideratum fuit hoc tmema, inventum tamen in novem reliquis, quorum ceu potio- rum & antiquiorum fidem ipse sequutus est: De- nique ut alios taceam, codices Ariemontani, qui etiam Vaticana exemplaria se adhibuisse te- statur. Nec in Latinis omnibus desideratum fuisse hunc locum, Patrum, qui eundem ad- ducunt, testimonia confirmant: Quem in u- troque Constantiensi exemplari extitisse agnovit Erasmus: Adductus etiam fuit à Cypriano an- te exortos Arianos, qui circa ann. Christi 260. martyrio coronatus est l. de simplic. prælati seu de unit. Eccles. pag. 164. Dicit Dominus: E- go & Pater unum sumus: Et iterum de Patre & Filio & Spiritu Sancto scriptum est, & tres unum sunt. Adductus est ab Athanasio in disp. in Synodo Nicena habita cum Ario vel Ariano quopiam, & libr. I. ad Theophil. de unita Deitate Trinitatis, ut & libr. VII. necnon ab Ida- cio Claro circa ann. Christi 380. libr. III. adver- sus Varimondum Tom. IV. Bibl. Patr. itemque se- se- culo eodem à Phœbadio libr. IV. contra Arianos cap. 45. à Cyrillo Alexandrino, de recta in DEUM fide ad Reginas. Seculo quinto à Vi- ctore Uticensi in Africa Episcopo libr. II. de per- secut. Vandal. & Eugenio Carthaginensi, utpo- te quem ille in confessione fidei Catholicæ sic loquentem introducit: Ut adhuc luce clarius unius divinitatis esse cum Patre & Filio Spiritum Sanctum doceamus Johannis Evangelistæ testimo- nio comprobatur, ait enim, tres sunt qui testi- monium dant in cælo, Pater, Verbum, & Spiri- tus Sanctus, & hi tres unum sunt. Adductus etiam hic locus est Seculo sexto, à Fulgentio Ruspenfi Episcopo respons. ad objecta Arian. in in Hæreseol. Basil. Anno 1554. pag. 47. & in li- bro de Trinit. cum aliis Fulgentii opusculis Pa- risiis à Jac. Sirmundo edito, & à Johan. II. E- pist. Roman. Epist ad Valer. Episcop. Tom. II. Concil. Bin. pag. 403. Neque de eo sequen- tium Seculorum Scriptores dubitarunt, quin pro Canonico textu haberent, Ambrosius Ans- bert. Anno 760. in cap. I. Apoc. Radulphus Ar- dens ad epist. Dom. II. post Pasch. Ann. 1060. Ru- pertus Tutiensis de operibus Spiritus Sancti libr. III. de sapient. c. 2. Ann. 1119. Bernhardus Ann. 1130. duob. sermon. de tribus in cælo & in terra te- stibus in oct. Pasch. cap. 139. Hugo Victorin. lib. I. de anim. cap. 20. Alexander III. Epist. ad Sol- danum Iconii : Innocentius III. serm. II. in Festo Pentecost. de quibus vid. Coccius in Thesaur. Tom. I. lib. VI. pag. 726. Lateranense etiam con- cilium, cui Græci quoque Archi-Episcopi & Pa- triarchæ interfuerunt Can. II. Græcos ita legisse ostendit. Quid? quod in Ecclesia Occidentali Dom. Quasimodogeniti publice hæc verba sem- per prælecta fuerint. Quibus & illud Barthol. Petri judicio addi potest, ad demonstrandum vitiosos esse libros, qui omittunt vers. 7. illud in- quam, quod pauci illi sive libri sive Ecclesiastici scriptores, qui eum omittunt, non consentiunt inter se in lectione versus octavi, dum alii habent illud in terra, alii omittunt fortassis tanquam otiosum, postquam non est quicquam ad cujus distinctio- nem apponatur, sublata præcedente sententia vers. scil. 7. Omittebat Codex, quo usus est B. Augu- stinus loco supra citato. Item Codex quo utebatur S. Leo, ut itidem liquet ex loco prius citato. Omit- tunt B. Cyrillus & Oecumenius locis allegatis. In tex- tu Vener. Bedæ non omittitur.

Neque dubium est tum phrasi Johannea opti- me convenire, qui frequenter Filium Dei Λόγον vocat, Johan. I. 1. & Johan. I. 1. 2. & Apoc. XIX. 13. hoc nomen ejus esse testatus est ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ, necnon de Patre & Filio similiter loquitur, quod unum sint, cap. X. 30. tum scopo Johannis ac ma- teriæ præsenti congruere eum maxime. Nam & Deitatem æternam Jesu contra Cerinthum, & E- bionem adstruere voluit S. Joannes, unde ejus- dem essentiæ Λόγον cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto constituit, & hosce tres testes de Jesu testantes ceu cælestes, natura divinos, & omni exceptio- ne superiores introducit; tum denique textus συν- νεχείᾳ apprime quadrare. Siquidem uti antea S. Johannes Jesum qua venit in aqua & sanguine, per hæc ipsa confirmasse, ac Spiritum Sanctum testimonio suo ceu veritatem ipsam comprobas- se κρινόμενον illud, quod contra Anti-Christos af- ferendum erat, docuit, quæ testimonio erant in ipsis diebus carnis Jesu de eodem; ita nunc assur- gat ad testimonia, quæ perpetuo vigent in Eccle- sia, eaque ἀμέσως divina, quæ testes in cælo na- turæ divinæ Jesu Christo perhibent, Pater, Ver- bum, & Spiritus Sanctus, tum ἐμμέσως divina, testium in terris vel Ecclesiasticorum, quæ sunt Spiritus, id est Verbum Spiritus, sacramentum a- quæ & sacramentum cænæ per sanguinem Christi designatum, qui in eodem exhibetur. Ut enim solet Johannes iterato quæ dixit repetere, vel uberius illustrare aut confirmare, ita quum di- xiffet, Jesum per aquam, & sanguinem venisse, & Spiritum Sanctum insuper de isto testificari, nunc probanda illa duxit, quod particula ὅτι in- dicat, quia tres sunt, qui testificantur in cœlo naturæ cœlestis, & divinæ, adeoque supremis & ἀνυπεύθυνοι, & omni exceptione superiores te- stes, Pater, Verbum & Spiritus Sanctus, & hæ tres Divinitatis personæ non inmediate tantum testantur, sed etiam media illa instituerunt, per quæ perpetuo in Ecclesia testimonium de Jesu perhibent: Verbum, Baptismum & Eucharistiam.

Ad Patris testimonium provocat Christus ipse, ac, si ipse solum de semetipso, hoc est, sine Pa- tre testaretur, testimonium suum verum non fo- re profiteretur Johan. V. 31. 32. Ideo sibi Patrem te- stem conjungit, quum in ore duorum testium verum consistat. Ego, inquit, cap. VIII. 16. solus non sum, sed Ego & Pater, qui misit me: Et in lege vestra scriptum est: Duorum hominum testimo- nium verum esse (Deut. XVII. v. 6. cap. XIX. 15.) Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμαυτῦ, καὶ μαρτυρεῖ πε- ρὶ ἐμῦ ὁ πέμψας με Πατήρ. De quo Jesu testimo- nio S. Johannes Baptista Johan. III, v. 31. ὁ ἐκ τῦ ὀρα- νῦ ἐρχόμενος, ἐπάνω πάντων ἐσί· καὶ ὃ ἑώρακε καὶ ἤκυ- σε, τῦτο μαρτυρεῖ. Hic testis è cœlo venit, sed & in cœlo est, vers. 13. Filius Dei, cujus testimonium introducit S. Johannes. Tertium testem Spiritum Sanctum promittit Jesus de se itidem testificatu- rum, Johann. XV. v. 26. ideoque de se, & Spiri- tu Sancto loquitur in plurali, Johann. III. v. 11. Amen, amen dico tibi, quia quod novimus loqui- mur, & quod vidimus, testamur. Ita de Jesu te- status est Pater gemina vice de cœlo proclamans: Hic est Filius meus dilectus in quo complacui, Matth. III. v. 17. & Matth. XVII. v. 5. & de glo- rificatione nominis ejus, vox Patris è cœlo audi- ta, è Johan. XII. v. 28. ὁ λόγος testatus est de se, & officio suo fideique ἐνεργείᾳ concionibus va- riis, imprimis apud Johannem, utpote cap. III. 16. se esse Filium Unigenitum, in mundum vero missum, ut omnis qui credit habeat vitam æter- nam cap. IV. 26. se esse Messiam, cap. V. 51. Fi- lium Dei, panem vivum, qui de cœlo descen- dit &c. qui & testis fidelis dicitur Apocal. I. v. 5. cap. VI. cap. VIII. cap. X. cap. XII. &c. è cap. V. 36. cap. VIII. 12. Testatus & operibus suis Johan. V. 36. cap. X. 38. & testes ideo emisit Apostolos, Johan. XV. ult. & adhuc mittit Doctores, Ephes. IV. 11. Spiritus Sanctus uti testatus est per visibi- lem descensum super Christum Johan. I. 32. ita testari per Apostolorum & successorum præco- nium debuit Johan. XV. 26. 27. ideo Apostolis concessus Johan. XX. Actor. II. ut testificaretur de ipso, Actor. I. 8. cap. X. 42. Nec solum in No- vo Testamento per Apostolos, sed etiam in Ve- teri Testamento per Prophetas testificatus est, docente S. Petro, V. 43. 2. Petr. I. 21. Testes hi sunt in cælo: Pater de cœlo testatus est, Matth. X. 27. cap. XVII. Johan. XII. 18. Filius Dei est in sinu Patris, Johan. I. 18. & in cœlo cap. III. 13. è cælo venit, estque super omnia, Johan. III. 31. Spiritus Sanctus descendit è cælo Matth. III. 16. missus est è cœlo, Actor. II. Testes hi UNUM

SUNT, unius divinæ effentiæ. Pater enim est verus Deus. Porro Ego & Pater unum sumus, in- quit Filius Johan. X. 30. Hic est verus Deus & vi- ta æterna ait de Filio S. Johannes 1. epist. V. v. 20. Spiritus Sanctus est Deus Actor. V. 2. 5. Ideo in no- mine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti baptizamur, ceu unius veri Dei, per quem regeneramur, & ad cujus fidem & cultum hoc sacramento obstringi- mur, Matth. XXVIII. 19.

Nugæ sunt, quæ hic regeruntur à Schlichtin- gio: 1. Nullam esse cohærentiam cum superioribus, quam requirat particula ὅτι. Eam enim jam o- stendimus, quidni hæc cohæreant? Jesus venit per aquam & sanguinem, & Spiritus Sanctus est qui testificatur: quia ut in cœlo tres testes sunt, qui sunt unus ille effentia Deus: Pater, Verbum & Spiritus Sanctus: Ita testes constituti in terra sunt ipsis subordinati, Verbum Evangelii, quod est Spiritus secundum Johannem, & aqua baptismi, per quam regeneramur, & sanguis Christi, per quem potamur. 2. Patris testimonium inclu- ditur in Spiritus testimonio. Pater enim per Spi- ritum testimonium perhibuit Filio. Resp. Pater & Spiritus unum sunt τῇ ὐσίᾳ, distinguuntur tamen τῇ ὑποστάσει tanquam testis alius & alius. Et quam- vis à Patre procedat Spiritus Sanctus, tamen tan- quam distinctus testis introducitur, quia persona à Patre distinguitur, quod clare in θεοφανείᾳ ad Jordanem conspicitur, Matth. III. 16. uti Patres quondam Arianis dixere; Abi ad Jordanem & videbis. 3. Cum Pater dicatur respectu Filii jam pro concesso poneretur, Jesum Dei Filium esse. Resp. Non id probandum, quod Pater habeat Filium, sed quod Jesus Nazarenus sit ille Dei Filius. 4. Si personæ cælestes nominandæ sint, etiam Angelos non semel testatos esse de Jesu. Resp. Testes perpetuos in Ecclesia adducere voluit, eosque tum qui in cœlo sunt naturæ cælestis & divinæ, quia & unius ejusdemque effentiæ esse Filium cum Patre, & Spiritu Sancto, adeoque unum verum Deum, & tres tamen esse personas, quæ testificantur in cœ- lo, id est, in cælesti gloria, uti Pater noster in cœ- lo est, cujus est regnum & potentia & gloria in secula, Matth. VI. 7. 13. Testificantur autem in cœlo, quia sunt in cœlo, nec tantum homini- bus in terra, sed maxime cœlitibus testantur ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ. Trinitas, inquit Salmero, dat testimonium in cœlo, vel efficiendo visionem in beatis super eo, quod Christus sit Deus & homo, vel infundendo ho- minibus, qui adhuc viatores sunt, fidem, quæ Dei donum. Aqua autem, & sanguis testantur in terra, quia terrenæ conditionis & ad terram ad- stricti sunt, non pertinent ad beatos in cœlis, quomodo Christus τὰ ἐπίγεια & ἐπουράνια distin- guit, Johan. III. v. 12. Bartholomæus Petri explicat in cœlo testificari autoritate divina, ideoque o- mnium summa: In terra autoritate, quæ sit in- fra divinam, conferens Matth. XXI. 25. B. Gerhar- do simplicissima videtur illa expositio, quod tres bi testes in cælo dicantur, quia sunt cælestes ac di- vini testes, unde postea vers. 9. eorum testimo- nium vocatur Dei testimonium. Quæ etiam B. Dorschæo imprimis placuit l. c. §. 23. Simplicissima expositio est. Triada testium in cælis dici, quia non tantum est in terra, sed etiam in cælo, non tantum in regno gratiæ, sed etiam in regno potentiæ & gloriæ, quia cælum cælorum eam non capit, quia absoluta & divina Majestate testantur, uno verbo, quia divini sunt illi testes. Quid? quod Schlichtin- gius ipse citra inconvenientiam sibi videatur illa explanare: Si verba hæc, inquit, versiculi septi- mi recipienda sunt in contextum Apostolorum, Pa- ter Deus unus ille & Altissimus, qui in cælis habi- tat, testabatur de Jesu, cum cælestem illam vocem edidit, & ad Jordanem Christo baptizato & in monte illo sancto Christo transfigurato: Hic est ille Filius meus dilectus, in quo complacui. Λόγος qui ipse Christus est, & nunc in cælis residet, testaba- tur de se, cum Stephanus Protomartyr coram Sy- nedrio causam diceret, quo tempore vidit cælos aper- tos & Jesum stantem à dextris Dei, hoc enim haud dubie fuit ipsius Jesu opus. Testabatur item de se in Sauli conversione & aliis temporibus haud du- bie sæpius. Spiritus Sanctus, qui itidem in cælo est tanquam fons istius Spiritus, qui in terras ad ho- mines manat, testatur Jesum esse Dei Filium il- lum, testatur inquam per quendam effluxum suum, descendendo in Jesum, & in ejus discipulos specie visibili, & admirandos effectus in iis & per eos o- perando, Possumus etiam hoc trium istorum testi- monium intelligere de omnibus iis, quæ Pater & ὁ λόγος, & Spiritus Sanctus, (cujus fons in Deo & sic in cælis est) fecerunt apud homines in testi- monium de Jesu, & prædicationis ejus veritate. O- mnia enim in quibus divinitas aliqua circa prædi- cationem Evangelii apparuit, Patri & τῷ Λόγῳ & Spiritui Sancto tribuenda sunt. Quo sensu versi- culo sequenti vox Spiritus vitandæ tavtologiæ cau- sa de solis Spiritus Sancti donis & effectis admiran- dis accipienda foret. Hæc Schlichtingius. Cur er- go paratragœdiatur idem de commatis hujus in- convenientia? At contra inconveniens omnino fuisset, si, quum de testibus Jesu ex instituto hoc agatur, tres illi testes in cælis, qui summi sunt & bræcipui, omnino prætermitterentur, quorum testimonia alias tam diligenter annotavit S. Jo- hannes in Evangelica historia, & ad quos Jesus ipse provocavit. Nec conveniret illa particula de testibus IN TERRA, si non responderet illis testibus IN COELO. Quod quum intelligant Sociniani, laborant, ut & illa verba IN TER- RA eliminentur, imprimis Socinus ipse in Comm. in hunc loc. Sed extitere illa in Codicibus Græ- cis, tempore Hieronymi, & ante ipsum, nec ul- lum de iis fuit dubium, ut è Prolog. in epist. Ca- non. constat in Codice Britannico ab Erasmo in Annot. producto in Codicibus, quos ad Com- plutensem editionem Cardin. Ximenius ex variis & præcipuis Europæ Bibliothecis adsciverat, in Codicibus ab Ariasrnontano adhibitis ex Hispa- nia, Italia & Belgio conquisitis, in plerisque Rob. Stephani Codicibus, ut & Laur. Valle, & Fro- benii atque Hervagii in edit. Basileensi, necnon Froschoveri in Tigurina, Bezæ item &c. Legun- tur apud Veteres antea laudatos. Quæ demum scopum & verba ipsa Johannis requirere B. Dor- scheus dissert. de Spir. Aqua & Sangu. §. 8. docet, ubi de his tribus testibus in terra prolixe egit.

Sunt autem illi ἐν τῇ γῇ non tantum ratione ὑ- πάρξεως propter Spiritus Sancti institutionem & oikovoμiαν gratiosam, quum ἐν ὀυρανῷ testes sint non propter dispensationem superioris principii, sed ex summa perfectione & majestate: Sed etiam ratione μαρτυρίας, quam in Ecclesia per totum terrarum orbem expediunt, ubi victoria mundi, & fides victoriosa regnat, & ex Deo regeneran- tur homines, ut & ratione τρόπυ ὑπάρξεως, quia in terreno quodam habitu quasi & modo existen- di: quod ex testium illorum designatione con- stat.

Quinam vero illi sunt? Spiritus, aqua, & sanguis: Ubi per Spiritum nonnulli quidem cum Augustino, & glossa ordin. quam plerique Pon- tificii sequuntur, animam Christi intelligunt: sed quod Christus animam habeat, eamque in mor- te emiserit, testimonium quidem est veræ huma- nitatis, non autem vel divinitatis, vel officii Chri- sti, nec facit ad fidei, & salutis nostræ specialem certitudinem : alii Spiritum Sanctum designari volunt, qui testibus in terra etiam annumere- tur, quia non solum immediatè, ut unus ille cum Patre & Verbo Deus testetur, ceu testis cœle- stis naturæ divinæ, sed etiam in Ecclesia medi- ante Verbo ejusque præconio testimonium de Je- su perhibeat, quod novi Testamenti proprium est, quatenus huic individuo Jesu Nazareno con- venire testatur, quæ de Messia scripturæ sacræ tra- didere. De quo B. Gerhardus §. 17. ex B. Hunnio: Testibus in cælo conjungitur, quia non minus quam Pater & Filius persona Trinitatis, cujus æterno consilio & decreto Filius in mundo Messias nasci voluit, & quia in baptismo Christi corporali specie columbæ non minus quam Pater voce externa sese manifestavit, ac super Christum descendens imme- diatum de eo testimonium perhibuit. Testibus in terra conjungitur, quia est persona illa, quæ jux- ta promissum Salvatoris missa est ad instituendum in terris ministerium, ad quod donis suis instruxit & illuminavit Apostolos visibiliter super eos illa- psus, & postea per prædicationem illorum de Chri- sto testificatus est, atque etiamnum de eo per Verbi & Sacramentorum ministerium testificatur, idque in cordibus credentium obsignat, ut D. Hunnius in comm. h. l. admonet. In quam sententiam etiam Calvinum laudat : Valde igitur hic probamus ea, quæ fulgor veritatis Calvino hic expressit: Cum, Spiritus varie de Christo testetur, inquit, apte du- plex illi attribuitur testandi locus. Nam è cœlis Pa- ter cum æterna sua Sapientia & Spiritu tanquam pro imperio pronunciat, Jesum esse Christum. Er- go illic sola divinitatis Majestas nobis consideranda est. Quoniam vero Spiritus in cordibus nostris ha- bitans arrha, pignus & sigillum est, ad obsignan- dum illud decretum, hoc modo iterum in terra per gratiam suam loquitur. Præstat autem per Spiri- tum hoc loco intelligere Verbum Spiritus seu Ev- angelium per Metonymiam, quod 1. Spiritus di- citur phrasi Christo accepta Johan. VI. 63. verba quæ ego loquor, Spiritus & vita sunt: nec inusi- tata S. Johanni, Apoc. XIX. 10. quem locum Al- casar explicat, quod testimonium Jesu sit Evan- gelii prædicatio, ac Spiritus prophetiæ dicatur, ut denotetur Spiritum ac studium prædicandi Evan- gelium esse nobilissimum quemdam Prophetiæ Spiri- tum: quia doctrina Evangelica est magna illa Pro- phetia, quæ hominibus arcana Dei consilia & bono- rum ac malorum exitum detegit &c. Proinde qui prædicatoris Evangelici Spiritu insignitus est, illi Spiritum inesse prophetiæ. 2. Evangelium voca- tur testimonium, Es. VIII, v. 20. & Verbum Dei sacris literis comprehensum testificatur de Chri- sto, Johan. V. 39. de quo testimonio Evangelii vide 1. Cor. I. 6. cap. II. 1. 2. Tim. I. 8. & hoc 1. Joh. V. 9. 10. 11. Apoc. I. 2. 9. cap. VI. 9. cap. XII. 11. 17. cap. XIX. 10. 3. Evangelium est testis in Ecclesia peren- nis & perpetuus de Jesu, quod extra eum non sit salus, Actor. IV. 12. per totum orbem testificans de ipso, Rom. X. 8. 17. 18. Coloss. I. 23. 4. Distincta ratione ab aqua & sanguine testatur.

Per aquam autem, & sanguinem, ut ante, Baptismum & Eucharistiam synecdochice desi- gnari censemus; quia 1. nomine aquæ baptismus significatur, Ezech. XXXVI. v. 25. Ebr. X. vers. 23. quum administraretur in aqua Matth. III. v. 11. Marc. I. v. 9. Luc. III. v. 16. Johan. I. v. 26. Actor. I. v. 5. cap. VIII. v. 36. cap. X. v. 47. cap. XI. v. 15. Et nomine sanguinis optime designetur sacra cœ- na, in qua calix benedictus est communicatio sanguinis Christi, 1. Corinth. X. v. 16. quam vete- res sacramentum calicis dixere. Vid. Augustinus Tom. III. lib. 4. de doctr. Christi cap. 21. Paschas. Abb. Corbejens. de corp. & sangv. Dom. qui na- talem calicis vocat diem cœnæ Dominicæ. 2. Juxta cum Evangelio baptismus & sacra cœna eminentissimo & efficacissimo modo de Jesu te- stantur in Ecclesia, qui proinde testes præteriri non debebant. Dicuntur ideo visibilia rerum divinarum signacula Augustino de Catechiz. ru- dib. cap. 26. In baptismo namque est infallibilis assertio gratiosæ divinæ præsentiæ totius Sacrosan- ctæ Trinitatis suo nomine in sanguine Filii nos ad fœderationem sanctissimam recipientis, adeoque de efficacia reconciliationis per Christum partæ testifi- cantis, Matth. XXVIII. v. 16. unde cum Tit. III. v. 5. 6. de multiplici gratia per lavacrum regenera- tionis in nos à Spiritu Sancto propter Jesum Chri- stum effusa disseruisset Apostolus, additur vers. 8. πιστὸς ὁ λόγος. Adde 1. Petr. III. v. 21. Damasce- nus lib. IV. de orthodoxa fide cap. 5. baptismum vo- cat σφραγίδα καὶ φυλακτήριον & Φωτισμόν. Adde Dionysium de Hierarch. Eccles. cap. 2. In sacramen- to itidem cœnæ est infallibilis assertio de Jesu Chri- sto, corpus suum & sanguinem suum singularissimo secretissimoque modo ad remissionem peccatorum nobis communicante: ut B. Dorscheus l. cit. §. 15. 3. Quia testes hi proprii sunt Novi Testamenti, in quo de Jesu perhibendum est testimonium, sacramenta hæc sunt Novi Testamenti, organa sanctissima & divinissima, quibus quam maxime Novi Testamenti Ecclesia de divinæ gratiæ ope- ratione secura est. 4. Testantur baptismus & sacra cœna de JESU, in cujus nomine baptiza- mur, & cujus sanguine potamur: testantur con- tra Anti-Christos, quod vera illa & salutaris orbi vita apparuerit in orbe ἔνσαρκος, 1. Joh. I. vers. 2. cap. II. v. 18. 5. Testantur per omnia ad finem usque mundi secula, quum nunquam Ecclesia de- beat esse ἀμάρτυρος, & perpetuo salutem, quæ in Jesu est, oporteat esse certissimam. 6. Jesus per Evangelium, baptismum & Eucharistiam no- bilissimo & eminentissimo modo ad nos venit. Eminentissimum, inquit iterum B. Dorscheus th. 18. in accessu suo ad nos vestigium posuit Jesus è cœlo, sapientiam suam nobis communicans, successit al- terum è cœlo nobis fœdus cum Sacrosancta Trini- tate in baptismo concilians. Tertium supervenit, è substantia sua nos cibans potansque. 7. Evange- lium, Baptismus, sacra Cœna triplici, distincta- que ratione testantur, adeoque tres testes merito dicuntur, quum Evangelium voce & literis teste- tur, baptismus oculis hominum aquam sistat, sacra cœna panem & vinum: Evangelium generatim promittat, & exhibeat Jesum Christum θεάνθρω- πον, ejusque beneficia & in illis justitiam & salutem fide suscipiendam: Baptismus peculiarem quen- dam gradum præsentiæ gratiosæ exhibeat, quo sacrosancta Trinitas intuitu meriti Christi pecu- liariter mediante aqua adsit ad abluendum nos à peccatis, & suscipiendam in fœdus gratiæ; sacra cœna sanguinem Christi peculiariter ceu sangui- nem Novi Testamenti nobis propinet, ac singu- lari propriaque ratione ibi sub vino sistat. 8. Per aquam in baptismo, lavacro aquæ, & per sangui- nem Christi in sacra cœna nos non modo de Chri- sti θεανθρώπυ persona & beneficiis quam certif- simi reddimur: sed operatur Deus in nobis effi- caciter fidem, regenerat, & corroborat nos ad falutem per hæc media Ecclesiæ credita. Non sunt testimonia nuda vel σημαντικὰ, sed practica operativa, & μεταδοτικὰ κὴ ἐνεργητικὰ; in uno Spi- ritu nos omnes εἰς ἓν σῶμα ad unum corpus bapti- zamur (aqua) & omnes εἰς ἓν Πνεῦμα in unum Spi- ritum potamur in Eucharistia, Christi nempe san- guine, 1. Corinth. XII. v. 13. Ipsi dispensatores hu- jus triplicis in terra testimonii sunt per id efficaces ad regenerationem, illuminationem, conversio- nem, confirmationem & obsignationem fidei, Actor. XXVI. v. 18. Roman. XI. v. 14. 1. Corinth. III. vers. 5. 9. cap. IV. v. 15. 2. Corinth. IV. vers. 8. Gal. IV. v. 19. Ephes. III. vers. 8. ideoque multo magis ipsum hoc triplex testimonium efficaciam divi- nam & percellentem ad movendas mutandasque hominum mentes habebit. 9. Sic explicant Ve- teres non pauci. Tertullianus diserte lavacri aquæ & potionis sanguinis meminit. S. Cyprianus cæle- stia sacramenta nuncupat de unit. Eccles. Am- brosius lib. III. de S. S. cap. 11. Audi, inquit, quo- modo testis Spiritus Sanct. mentem renovat, aqua proficit ad lavacrum, sanguis spectat ad pretium. Spiritus enim per adoptionem nos filios Dei fecit, sacri fontis unda nos abluit, sanguis Domini nos redemit. Gregorius Nyssenus orat. contr. Jud. Cre- dimus nos tum per divinum baptisma, tum per san- cti sanguinis participationem & usum consecrari ac divinitatem inducere. Paulinus Nolanus in ep. ad Florent. aquam gratiæ & sanguinem sacramenti hic notavit. Cyrillus de recta fide ad Regin. San- ctificat, inquit, nos Spiritu, & purificat sanguine, & abluit iterum aqua munda. Leo M. epist. X. Spiritus utique, inquit, sanctificationis & sanguis redemptionis & aqua baptismatis: quæ tria unum sunt & individua manent. Beda de sacramentis Christi explicat, quibus semper refecti nutrimur ad salutem. Damascenus de aqua regenerationis & ablutionis peccati (in baptismo) & de sanguinis (Christi) potu (in sacra cœna) causa æternæ vitæ. Plures autores ad vers. 6. adducti sunt, qui facile consentiunt, etiam è Pontificiis & Reformatis.

Dicit autem de his tribus testibus in terra, non ut de illis in cœlo, καὶ ὗτοι οἱ τρεῖς ἕν εἰσι, sed κὴ οἱ τρεῖς εἰς τὸ ἕν εἰσι. Franciscus Lucas de hac parti- cula in not. Legitur, inquit, ut in Latinis aliis li- bris, ita & in reliquis, quæcunque vidimus, exem- plaribus Græcis, adhæc in Syriacis Testamentis, de- nique à Patribus, at differenter. Latini enim co- dices cum Augustino, Cyrillo, Leone, Beda, & hi tres unum sunt, habent. Græci vero cum Oecume- nio & Syriacis: Et hi tres ad vel in unum sunt. Ad Latinos provocat Socinus: Sed Græcus textus præferendus est, nec ab eo discedendum, impri- mis quia codices consentiunt, nec dissentit Syrus. Et quam facile excidere potuit præpositio ad vel in librariorum incuria. Major utique requiritur unitas ad testes in cœlo, quia testimonium hoc summum est & primum, ideo firmissimam & sum- mam unitatem requirit, qualis ea non est, quæ solo consensu constat, sed ea quæ ὁμοεσίαν pro fundamento habet.

Sunt autem εἰς τὸ ἓν non mo- do ratione solennis promulgationis ordinariæ per sacrum ministerium dispensationis 1. Cor. IV. v. 1. efficaciæ & virtutis ad victoriam mundi, & objecti hominum, quæ saluti destinata sunt, sed etiam ra- tione harmonicæ consensionis, quoad testificatio- nem de Jesu, quam cordibus & sensibus nostris & sonora quidem voce auribus Evangelium, visibili autem sacramento baptismus & cœna exhibet. De Jesu divina & humana natura testatur baptismus: quia in Filii Dei non ἀσάρκγ sed ἐνσάρκγ nomine baptizamur, conf. Matth. XXVIII. 19. Act. II. 38.

VIII. v. 16. & cœna quia sanguis est hominis, sed qui & Dei proprius sanguis, remissionis peccatorum meritorius Matth. XXVI. 26. & pro redemptione Ecclesiæ effusus, Act. XX. 28. 1. Petr. I. 18. Testatur aqua baptismi de Jesu, quod sit Christus, in cujus no- mine consequimur regenerationem Joh. III. 5. & re- missionem peccatorum, Act. II. 38. Testatur sanguis Christi in Eucharistia de potatione nostra ad unum corpus Christi mysticum, 1. Cor. XIII. 13. de N. Testa- mento & fœderis gratiæ fruitione, quia calix est No- vi Testamenti in sanguine Christi, Luc. XXII. 20. 1. Cor. XI. 14. de immanentia Christi in nobis, & no- stri in Christo, Joh. VI. 56. de vivificatione nostri pro- pter Christum, v. 51. 53. 57. 58. de resuscitatione futura & consequutione vitæ æternæ, v. 40. Ex hac Johannea διηγήσει patet, quomodo tum mysterium τῆς ὑπεραγίας Τριάδος inde asseratur, siquidem hic habemus Trinitatis vocem, personarum Divinarum pluralitatem, earum Trinitatem & or- dinem, nec non ὁμοοσίαν vel essentiæ unitatem, Spi- ritus Sancti personalitatem, ut & cujusque personæ Divinæ proprietatem, quam nomina exhibent se- cundum Scripturæ sensum exposita : tum Verbi atque Sacramentorum naturam & indolem: & Ver- bi quidem divinam originem & autoritatem, quam in se & independenter ab Ecclesia habet, ejusdem, prout in Scripturis, per quas Deus testatur, in Ec- clesia habetur, perspicuitatem & efficaciam vel vir- tutem: Sacramentorum vero numerum, quod duo tantum sint, non plura in Novo Testamento, ut & communem usum, quod Laici à sanguinis Christi in S. cœna perceptione excludendi non sint, quia per sanguinem de fide confirmari, & mundū vincere, adeoq; illud Dei testimonium etiam λαμβάνειν re- cipere debent, nec non effectum salutiferum, quod non nuda signa sint sed media ἐνεργητικὰ, tum no- tarum Ecclesiæ definitionem, quod nempe hæ, non aliæ sint notæ Ecclesiæ propriæ, Verbi prædica- tio, & sacramentorum Baptismi & Eucharistiæ usur- patio, utpote quæ testimonia sunt sufficientia ad sa- lutem nostram de Jesu Christo, adeoq; & sufficien- tia Ecclesiæ, in qua salus ista viget; In quo igitur loco ἐν τῇ γῇ testimonia ista tria sine manifesta ex- terna repugnantia vigere video, in eo loco cœ- tum visibilem Christi colligi, adeoque Ecclesiam esse indubie animadverto. Ad eos enim Jesus ve- nit per aquam non per aquam tantum, sed per aquam & sanguinem, & Spiritus ipse est, qui te- stificatur penes eos, cujus Verbum est Evange- lium, illi sunt ex Deo geniti, & per Verbum vin- cunt mundum. Nonne universaliter, inquit B. Dor- scheus l. c §. 32. ita comparatum esse videmus, ut ibi sit alicujus religionis cœtus, ubi testimonia propria & primaria Dei, qui in illa religione colitur sine repu- gnantia & contradictione illius loci apparent. Sic ibi erat gentilismus, ubi oracula, responsa, auspicia & re- liqua gentilismi primaria documenta comparent. Sic & ibi est Judaismus, ubi Thalmudica Veteris Te- stamenti perversio, cum circumcisione & vanis Judæ- orum observationibus observatur. Ibi est Mahumme- dismus, ubi Alcoranus, tanquam testimonium do- gmaticum Mahummedismi & alia testimonia ejus urgentur. Sic ergo ubi Christianæ religionis testimo- nia tria, Verbum Evangelii & duo Sacramenta ob- servantur, ibi Christianæ religionis Ecclesia est. Vid. de illis tribus in cælo testibus plura apud B. Gerhar- dum, de his in terra testibus apud B. Dorscheum dis- putationibus laudatis.

Ἡ μαρτυρία τoῦ Θεoῦ μείζων ἐστίν] Dei enim testimonium multis hominum testimoniis præponderat. ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν μαρτυρία τoῦ Θεoῦ ἣν μεμαρτύρηκε περὶ τoῦ υἱoῦ αὑ- τoῦ] ὅτι hic valet jam vero. Nam generale dictum huic speciali causæ applicat. Ille Spiritus, id est, illa opera sunt maximum testimonium, quo Deus ostendit Jesum esse Filium suum, Joh. V. 36. X. 25, 38. XIV. 11. XV. 24. In Manuscripto, ὅτι μεμαρτύρηκε.

Ut causam victoriæ mundi per fidem & originem victoriosæ hujus fidei è gemina illa testium triplicitate ἐν οὐρανῷ & ἐν τῇ γῇ deduxit S. Johannes: Ita nunc de recipienda illa testificatione ceu vere divina agit. Siquidem μαρτυρία τoῦ θεoῦ major sit non tantum ratione efficacitatis & ἐνεργείας, quam μαρτυρία τῶν ἀνθρώπων: Conf. 1. Cor. I. 6. 7. 8. Recte quidem Grotius vocem ὅτι observat hic valere jam vero, sed non recte ait generale dictum Deut. XVII. 6. huic speciali causæ hac voce applicari. Nam nulla hominum testimonia adducta erant in antecedentibus, sed Dei tum immediate testantis, utpote Patris, Verbi, & Spiritus Sancti, tum mediate per Verbum, aquam & sanguinem itidem testificantis. Nec de Spiritu hoc v. 9. aut de operibus ejus quicquam habetur; nedum opera illa maximum testimonium esse dicuntur, quo Deus ostendat, Jesum esse Filium suum. Quod ne verum quidem est. Nam maximum testimonium est, quod illi tres testes in cœlo perhibent: neque etiam illud testimonium operum, si miracula intelligantur, ordinarium est, ac perpetuum in Ecclesia, quæ tamen semper testibus indiget, nunquam esse potest ἀναμάρτυρος; & verba, quæ sequuntur v. 11, diserte μαρτυρίαν istam exhibent, quam Deus testificatus est de Filio suo, ut non opus sit aliorsum recurrere, vel μαρτυρίαν Metonymice de operibus, per quæ testatus est Deus, intelligere,

## 5:10
Verse 10.

Ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τòν υἱòν τoῦ Θεoῦ, ἔχει τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ] In the Manuscript: Τὴν μαρτυρίαν τoῦ Θεoῦ. He who places his trust in Jesus as the Son of God, he receives the testimony of God. He has it in himself, he said, instead of receives, because he who receives something, he has that thing in himself, that is, with himself. For ἐν is accustomed to be put for σὺν, as Matt. VI. 29: XVI. 27. XXVI. 31. 2. Tim. I. 13. Ὁ μὴ πιστεύων τῷ Θεῷ] The Latin reads τῷ υἱῷ, which is more correct. For John is accustomed to add to an affirmative sentence a negative one of the contrary matter. Ψεύστην πεποίηκεν αὐτóν] Namely God, about whom the discourse precedes. He makes him a liar, that is, he acts in such a way as if God were a liar. See above I. 10. Πεποίηκεν is a perfect for any time, in the Hebrew manner. So also πεπίστευκεν in the following words. ὅτι ἐ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν μεμαρτύρηκεν ὁ Θεòς περὶ τoῦ υἱoῦ αὑτοῦ] The Manuscript [reads] ὅτι οὐκ ἐπίστευσεν. Illud Θεòς est pro αὐτὸς, a noun for a pronoun in the Hebrew manner. The sense is: because he does not apply faith to that testimony by which He declared who His excellent Son was. Μαρτυρίαν μαρτυρεῖν, as to serve a servitude, to die a death, which is a frequent locution among the Hebrews, Greeks, and Latins. v. 11. Καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία, ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιoν ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεòς, καὶ αὕτη ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτoῦ ἐστιν] Ἐν for per and ἐστι for contingit. He means this: To that pronouncement, that Jesus is the Christ or the Son of God, this is connected, that God has opened to us through Jesus the way of coming to eternal life, and that through the same Jesus, because indeed it was said of the Messiah, in mystery, that he would be the Father of the future age, Is. IX. 6. John explains this I. 4. III. 15. 16. 36. V. 24. 26. 40. VI. 27. 33. 35. 40. 47. 48. 51. 53. 54. 63. 68. VIII. 12. X. 28. XI. 25. XII. 50. XIV. 6. XVII. 3. XX. 31. In Manuscripto est: Καὶ ἡ αὕτη ἐστιν ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ: that eternal life is that very thing which Jesus revealed. v. 12. Ὁ ἔχων τòν υἱòν ἔχει τὴν ζωὴν] He who retains the Son, that is, those words which the Father commanded the Son, in which sense we have ἔχειν and John V. 38, he also has life, that is, a certain right to eternal life, in the way you have ἔχειν ζωὴν αἰώνιoν in the cited chapter of the Gospel 24. VI. 47. 54. In a similar way Christ is said to dwell in us through faith Ephes. III 17.

Latin:

Vers 10.

Ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τòν υἱòν τoῦ Θεoῦ, ἔχει τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ] In Manuscripto: Τὴν μαρτυρίαν τoῦ Θεoῦ. Qui fiduciam suam in Jesum ut Dei Filium reponit, is recepit Dei testimonium. In se habet, dixit, pro recepit, quia qui recipit aliquid, is id in se, id est, secum habet. Ἐν enim pro συν poni solet, ut Matth. VI. 29: XVI. 27. XXVI. 31. 2. Tim. I. 13. Ὁ μὴ πιστεύων τῷ Θεῷ] Latinus legit τῷ υἱῷ, quod rectius. Solet enim Johannes affirmanti sententiæ addere negantem rei contrariæ. Ψεύστην πεποίηκεν αὐτóν] Nempe Deum, de quo sermo præcedit. Eum facit mendacem, id est, ita agit, quasi Deus mendax esset. Vide supra I. 10. Πεποίηκεν Præteritum pro quovis tempore, more Ebræo. Sic & πεπίστευκεν in verbis sequentibus. ὅτι ἐ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν μεμαρτύρηκεν ὁ Θεòς περὶ τoῦ υἱoῦ αὑτοῦ] Manuscriptus ὅτι οὐκ ἐπίστευσεν. Illud Θεòς est pro αὐτὸς nomen pro pronomine more Ebræo. Sensus est: quia fidem non adhibet ei testimonio, quo ille declaravit, quis esset eximius suus Filius. Μαρτυρίαν μαρτυρεῖν, ut servitutem servire, mortem mori, quæ loquutio frequens Ebræis, Græcis & Latinis. v. 11. Καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία, ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιoν ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεòς, καὶ αὕτη ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτoῦ ἐστιν] Ἐν pro per & ἐστι pro contingit. Hoc vult: Isti pronuntiato, Jesum esse Christum sive Dei Filium connexum est hoc, Deum nobis per Jesum aperuisse viam veniendi ad vitam æternam, idque per eundem Jesum, quia scilicet de Messia dictum est, in mysterio, eum fore Patrem futuri seculi, Es. IX. 6. Explicat hoc Johannes I. 4. III. 15. 16. 36. V. 24. 26. 40. VI. 27. 33. 35. 40. 47. 48. 51. 53. 54. 63. 68. VIII. 12. X. 28. XI. 25. XII. 50. XIV. 6. XVII. 3. XX. 31. In Manuscripto est: Καὶ ἡ αὕτη ἐστιν ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ: illa vita æterna ea ipsa est, quam Jesus revelavit. v. 12. Ὁ ἔχων τòν υἱòν ἔχει τὴν ζωὴν] Qui Filium retinet, id est, verba illa, quæ Pater Filio mandavit, quo sensu ἔχειν habemus & Johann. V. 38 is & vitam habet, id est jus certum ad vitam æternam, quomodo ἔχειν ζωὴν αἰώνιoν habes dicto capite Evangelii 24. VI. 47. 54. Pari modo Christus in nobis habitare dicitur per fidem Ephes. III 17.

## 5:12
He who does not have the Son of God, does not have life) Here again is an opposition, such as we have often had. It is to be understood concerning those to whom the Gospel has reached. The same sense in John III. 36. & VI. 53.

Just as St. John confirmed that the testimony concerning Jesus is to be received through faith by his divinity in verse 9, so now he commends it by the fruit and efficacy of faith, that he who receives it, and thus believes in the Son of GOD, by that very fact has and experiences the power and efficacy of that testimony within himself. B. Hunnius: We can safely give our name to Christ, because he who believes in him has the testimony in himself; namely, the testimony of the Holy Spirit, who confirms and seals this certainty and πληροφορίαν (full assurance) of faith in believers, so that now that testimony is not outside us, but inside us, inscribed as it were on our hearts by the Spirit of the living God. He adds to these an argument from the indignity of the contrary, that he who does not receive, or does not believe God testifying concerning Jesus, makes God a liar, in that he does not believe in the testimony which God has testified concerning his Son. Of this argument, B. Hunnius says: the meaning is this: It is an enormous impiety and blasphemy to charge God with a lie. But those who do not believe God testifying concerning the Son, in reality, as much as in them lies, make God a liar, and by casting the highest insult upon him, commit the crime of lèse-majesté against the divine Majesty. Therefore, faith must be had in his Word, which he has revealed concerning the Son, lest we seem to wish to make him a liar. Bartholomaeus Petri expresses these things thus: He who imagines Jesus to be less than the Father, or imagines that he was not a true man, but a phantom, inflicts this ignominy upon God, as much as is in him, so as to call him a liar, as one who has testified falsely concerning Jesus: he does, I say, just as if he were to say in express words that God the Father is a deceiver, while he is unwilling to believe his testimony.

Now therefore the Apostle adds what that testimony is, καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία, and this itself is that testimony, ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ αὕτη ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ ἐστι, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. To which testimony the following verse also still pertains, because he has testified not only concerning the divine δόσει (giving) or donation of eternal life in the donation of the Son, but also concerning our λήψει (taking) or reception, that indeed through faith we receive uniquely both the Son and in the Son eternal life, ὁ ἔχων τὸν υἱὸν, he who (through faith) has the Son, which he had said before ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν υἱὸν, ἔχει τὴν ζωὴν, he who believes in the Son, has life, namely eternal, and conversely, he who does not have the Son of GOD, does not have life. B. Hunnius here fashions a new argument, from the infinite utility, as he says, of this testimony apprehended by true faith, namely that it confers eternal life upon believers. Furthermore, God gives this, with whom alone the power of conferring it resides. He gives it, however, by means of that testimony by which he offers the benefits of his Son, and those are apprehended by faith as if by a certain hand. This life is placed in his Son and is applied to us, or becomes ours, if one believes in him who alone has produced eternal life for us: and therefore the Evangelist subsumes, he who has the Son, he has life, since the Son is life itself, and the attainment of eternal life depends on the knowledge and trust of him. And further: From the contrary: For just as he who has the Son, at the same time obtains the life included in the Son: So he who does not apprehend the Son through faith, he has no κοινωνίαν (communion) or fellowship with eternal life.

In the Grotian commentary we note these things: (1) that the Apostle does not say, he who believes in the Son of God, he receives GOD's testimony, but he has that testimony ἐν ἑαυτῷ (in himself), as it is held in the sacred text (Grotius incorrectly has ἐν ἀυτῷ, which however seems to be only a printer's error) namely as to the effect, or also as John III. 33. the Baptist says: Ὁ λαβὼν ἀυτῦ τὴν μαρτυρίαν, ἐσφράγισεν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἀληθής ἐσι (He who has received his testimony, has sealed that God is true). To be noted here is the confession of Cornelius against the Papistic doubt: This testimony can be taken concerning the believer's own regeneration, adoption, grace, and glory, i.e., He who believes in the Son of God, this one has in himself the testimony of God, by which indeed GOD attests to his soul and conscience that he, through this faith by which he believes in Christ and obeys him, is a faithful, just, son, and heir of GOD, and a co-heir of Christ. Whence explaining this very thing St. John soon adds, verse 11. And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, & this life is in his Son, so Beda and Oecumenius. (2) With no right does he prefer the Latin text to the Greek in verse 10, that τῷ Θεῷ is to be read, not ὑιῷ, and that the pronoun αὐτὸν refers to God, Grotius acknowledges and teaches. (3) Most poorly are the words of St. John v. 11 perverted, as if eternal life were given to us in the Son only by reason of manifestation, since indeed already in the Old Testament and by St. John the Proto-Baptist the way of eternal life had been manifested, but in the Son is said to be the life which God gives us through him, both by reason of acquisition and merit, because he gave his flesh for the life of the world, John VI. 51, and by reason of actual collation, because he who believes in the Son, through faith in his merit attains eternal life, John III, 16. How v. 13. in this place St. John interpreted himself: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life. (4) The phrase as to who the excellent Son of God might be smells of the lamp of Socinus, as we noted above. (5) To have the Son is not to retain those words which the Father commanded the Son, but to believe in the Son, to embrace with true trust and to receive the Son as the unique Savior. (6) Not only to those are they denied to have life, to whom the Gospel has reached, although it has penetrated into the whole world, Rom. X. 17. and has been announced to every creature which is under the Sun, Col. I. 23. even though many by their own fault have deprived themselves and their descendants of it, but simply all, who do not have the Son of GOD. Because there is no middle ground given between those who believe in the Son of GOD, and those who do not believe, of whom the former have life, the latter do not have it, just as no other way can be imagined either of escaping condemnation, or of obtaining salvation, than through the name of Jesus Acts IV. verse 12. received by faith Acts X. verse 43. And where are those to be placed in the other world, if to whom by chance the Gospel has not reached? Into heaven? Thus they would come into heaven without Christ, which is against Christ, Mark XVI. verse 16. John XIV. 6. and against Peter Acts IV. 12. and the definition of the council of Jerusalem, Acts XV. 10. Into hell? Grotius does not want that. A state must therefore be imagined in the other world outside of heaven and hell. Nor indeed can they betake themselves to the limbos of the Papists, since they belong neither to the limbos of the Fathers, nor of infants, nor finally to purgatory, if we admit the Papistic hypotheses. More sound is this Papist Bartholomæus Petri, who at verse 11. The Apostle explains that testimony of God the Father concerning Jesus, which must necessarily be believed, namely, that he is the true God and man, the only Redeemer and Savior of the human race. This Blessed John says here in other words. And with the testimonies compared John I. v. 4. chap. III. v. 16. 18. 36. chap. VI. v. 46. 47. Chapter XVII. 3. 1 John IV. 9. concludes: From all of which it is clear that this eternal life is so possessed by men through the Son of God, that without Him and faith in Him it cannot be possessed. This is what the Apostle also expresses in this place in clear words in the following verse. To which verse, with the Clementine edition corrected (the Pope's bull being held as of no account) from the Greek text and other good Latin and ancient concordances, namely with the word τῦ Θεῦ (of God) added, it has this: This is a repeated hortatory conclusion to faith in Jesus Christ, with an argument from spiritual utility, nay necessity, namely this, that without this faith true life can be obtained neither in this age nor in the future. Finally he adds: Great therefore is the testimony in this place concerning faith in the Mediator, that it always has been and is necessary for all for salvation. This is what the Apostle also inculcates in the following verse, so that with such great utility and therefore necessity proposed, he might confirm the faithful in retaining true faith in the Lord Jesus, against the sects of perdition rampant at that time. He speaks therefore as if in an epilogue (says Oecumenius), summarizing the aforementioned.

Latin:

Ὁ μὴ ἔχων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, τὴν ζωὴν οὐκ ἔχει) Hic rursus est oppositio, qualem saepe habuimus. Intelligendum de iis, ad quos Evangelium pervenit. Idem sensus Joh. III. 36. & VI. 53.

Uti testimonium de Jesu recipiendum esse per fidem confirmavit S. Johannes ab ejusdem divi- nitate vers. 9. Ita nunc a fidei fructu & efficacita- te id commendat, quod qui id recipit, adeoque in Filium DEI credit, eo ipso testimonii illius vim atque efficaciam in semetipso habeat & expe- riatur. B. Hunnius: Tuto possumus nomen dare Christo, quia qui credit in illum, testimonium ha- bet in seipso; testimonium scilicet Spiritus Sancti, qui hanc fidei certitudinem & πληροφορίαν con- firmat & obsignat in credentibus, ut jam testimo- nium illud non sit extra nos, sed intra nos, inscri- ptum quasi nostris cordibus per Spiritum Dei viven- tis. Addit his argumentum a contrarii indignitate, quod qui non recipit, vel Deo non credit testan- ti de Jesu, Deum mendacem faciat, eo quod non credat in testimonium, quod testatus est Deus de Filio suo. Hujus argumenti, inquit B. Hunnius: sententia haec est: Enormis est impietas & blasphe- mia, Deum mendacii arguere. Atqui non creden- tes testificanti Deo de Filio, reipsa, quantum quidem in se est, mendacem faciunt Deum, & summa jacta in illum contumelia crimen laesae divinae Majestatis committunt. Ergo fides habenda Verbo ejus, quod re- velavit de Filio, ne videlicet mendacem facere velle videamur. Bartholomaeus Petri haec ita effert: Qui Jesum fingit Patre minorem, aut fingit non verum hominem fuisse, sed phantasma, Deum hac ignomi- nia afficit, quantum quidem est in ipso, ut eum di- cat mendacem, tanquam qui falso sit testatus de Jesu: perinde, inquam, faciat, ac si disertis verbis diceret Deum Patrem esse fallacem, dum non vult credere ejus testimonio.

Jam ergo subjungit Apostolus, quodnam sit il- lud testimonium, καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία, & hoc ipsum est testimonium illud, ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔδω- κεν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ αὕτη ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ ἐστι, quod vitam internam dedit nobis Deus, & haec vita in Filio ejus est. Ad quod testimonium etiam se- quens comma adhuc pertinet, quia non tantum de δόσει divina vel donatione vitae aeternae in dona- tione Filii, sed etiam de λήψει nostra vel rece- ptione testatus est, quod nempe per fidem reci- piamus unice & Filium & in Filio vitam aeternam, ὁ ἔχων τὸν υἱὸν, qui (per fidem) habet Filium quod dixerat antea ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν υἱὸν, ἔχει τὴν ζωὴν, is habet vitam, aeternam scilicet, & ex ad- verso, qui non habet Filium DEI, vitam non ha- bet. B. Hunnius argumentum novum hic fingit, ab infinita utilitate, ut ait, testimonii hujus vera fide apprehensi, nempe quod credentibus confert vi- tam aeternam. Hanc porro dat Deus, penes quem solum facultas conferendae ejus residet. Dat autem mediante illo testimonio, quo beneficia Filii sui of- fert, eaque per fidem veluti manum quandam ap- prehenduntur. Haec vita posita est in Filio ejus & applicatur nobis, seu evadit nostra, si credatur in illum, qui solus vitam aeternam nobis peperit: ideo- que subsumit Evangelista, qui habet Filium, is vi- tam habet, quandoquidem Filius est vita ipsa, & consecutio vitae aeternae pendet a notitia fiduciaque ipsius. Et porro: A contrario: Sicut enim is, qui habet Filium, simul inclusam in Filio vitam obti- net: Sic qui Filium per fidem non apprehendit, is nec cum vita aeterna ullam habet κοινωνίαν sive con- sortium.

In Grotiano commento haec notamus (1) non dicere Apostolum, qui credit in Filium Dei, is re- cipit DEI testimonium, sed is habet illud testimo- nium ἐν ἑαυτῷ, uti in textu sacro habetur (perpe- ram Grotius habet ἐν ἀυτῷ, quod tamen typothe- tarum sphalma tantum videtur) scilicet quoad effectum, vel etiam prout Joh. III. 33. ait Baptista: Ὁ λαβὼν ἀυτῦ τὴν μαρτυρίαν, ἐσφράγισεν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἀληθής ἐσι. Notanda hic Cornelii confessio adversus dubitationem Papisticam: Hoc testimo- nium accipi potest de ipsa credentis regeneratione, adoptione, gratia & gloria, q. d. Qui credit in Fi- lium Dei, hic habet in se testimonium Dei, quo sci- licet DEUS attestatur ejus animæ & conscientiæ, ipsum per hanc fidem, qua in Christum credit, eique obedit, esse fidelem, justum, filium, & hæ- redem DEI, cohæredem autem Christi. Unde id- ipsum explicans S. Johannes mox subdit, vers. 11. Et hoc est testimonium, quoniam vitam æternam dedit nobis Deus, & hæc vita in Filio ejus est, ita Beda & Oecumenius. (2) Nullo jure præfert La- tinum textum Græco vers. 10. τῷ Θεῷ legendum esse non ὑιῷ pronomen αὐτὸν, quod Deum re- spicere agnoscit Grotius, docet. (3) Pessime verba S. Johannis v. 11. pervertuntur, quasi tantum data nobis vita æterna in Filio sit ratione manifesta- tionis, siquidem jam in Veteri Testamento & a S. Johanne Proto-Baptista via vitæ æternæ manife- stata fuerit, in Filio autem vita, quam Deus per ipsum nobis dat, esse dicitur tum ratione acqui- sitionis & meriti, quia carnem suam dedit pro mun- di vita, Joh. VI. 51. tum ratione actualis collatio- nis, quia qui in Filium credit, per fidem in meri- tum ejus vitam æternam consequitur, Joh. III, 16. Quomodo v. 13. hoc loco S. Johannes seipsum interpretatus est: Hæc scripsi vobis credentibus in nomen Filii Dei, ut sciatis, quod vitam æternam ha- beatis. (4) Phrasis quis esset eximius Dei Filius lucernam Socini olet, quemadmodum supra no- tavimus. (5) Filium habere non est retinere ver- ba illa, quæ Pater Filio mandavit, sed credere in Filium, vera fiducia amplecti & suscipere Filium ceu Salvatorem unicum. (6) Non illi tantum negantur vitam habere, ad quos Evangelium per- venit, quanquam id in totum orbem penetrarit, Rom. X. 17. omnique creaturæ, quæ sub Sole est, annuntiatum Col. I. 23. tametsi multi culpa sua semet & posteros eodem privarint, sed simplici- ter omnes, qui non habent Filium DEI. Quia nullum datur medium inter eos, qui in Filium DEI credunt, & qui non credunt, quorum illi vi- tam habent, hi non habent, uti nec alia ratio fin- gi potest sive effugiendi condemnationem, sive consequendi salutem, quam per nomen Jesu Act. IV. vers. 12. fide receptum Act. X. vers. 13. Et quor- sum collocandi illi in altero seculo, si ad quos forte Evangelium non pervenit? Num in cælum? Ita sine Christo in cælum venirent, quod est con- tra Christum, Marc. XVI. vers. 16. Johan. XIV. 6. & contra Petrum Act. IV. 12. ac definitionem con- cilii Hierosolymitani, Act. XV. 10. Num in infer- num? Id non vult Grotius. Fingendus ergo status in altero seculo alius extra cælum & infernum. Neq; sane ad Papistarum limbos se recipere pos- sunt, quum nec ad Patrum, nec ad infantum lim- bos, nec denique ad purgatorium pertineant, si Papisticas hypotheses admittamus. Magis sanus hic Bartholomæus Petri Pontificius, qui ad vers. 11. Explicat Apostolus illud Dei Patris de Jesu testimo- nium, cui necessario credendum sit, nimirum, esse illum verum Deum & hominem unicum Redempto- rem & Salvatorem humani generis. Hoc aliis ver- bis hic dicit B. Johannes. Et collatis testimoniis Joh. I. v. 4. cap. III. v. 16. 18. 36. cap. VI. v. 46. 47. cap. XVII. 3. 1. Joh. IV. 9. concludit: Ex quibus omnibus patet, quod vita ista aterna ab hominibus sic per Filium Dei habetur, ut sine eo ac fide in ipsum haberi non possit. Id quod etiam hoc loco Aposto- lus verbis disertis exprimit v. seq. Ad quem ver- sum emendata Clementina editione (susque deque habita Pontificis bulla) e textu Græco aliisque bonis Latinis & Veteribus concordantiis, addita nempe voce τῦ Θεῦ Filii DEI hæc habet: Est hic iterata conclusio adhortatoria ad fidem in Jesum Christum, cum argumento ex spirituali utilitate imo necessitate, hac videlicet, quod sine hac fide ve- ra vita neque in hoc seculo, neque in futuro obtineri possit. Addit denique: Magnum igitur hoc loco est testimonium de fide Mediatoris, quod omnibus ad salutem semper fuerit & sit necessaria. Id quod Apostolus sequente etiam versu inculcat, ut utilita- te tanta adeóq; necessitate proposita confirmet fide- les in retinenda vera de Domino Jesu fide, adversus grassantes eo tempore perditionis sectas. Ait ergo tanquam epilogo (inquit Oecumenius) summatim repetens prædicta.

## 5:13
Verse 13.

These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may believe in the name of the Son of God) Better in the Manuscript: These things I have written to you, that you may know that you have eternal life, you who believe in the name of the Son of God. Nor do the Syriac, Latin, or Arab read otherwise. Therefore I have written so many warnings and exhortations to you, that you might know that you have a certain right to eternal life, as long as you believe in God, through the author Jesus, He who is called by us and is the Son of GOD. What 'name' means in this place, see above III. 23.

He rashly corrects the Greek text from the versions, since it is perfectly fine as it is. Bartholomaus Petri is more equitable to the Greek truth: The Greek, he says, Codex has 'I have written' (ἔγραψα) instead of the present (I write), as many good Latin books also printed have, and the text of the Venerable Bede. But the sense is not changed. Furthermore, most Greek Codices attach that clause: 'You who believe in the name of the Son of God' to the beginning of this verse, thus: These things I have written to you who believe, etc., but that also is not of great moment. That which is of greater moment is that the same majority of Greek Codices add one clause to this verse, namely this, 'that you may also believe in the name of the Son of God.' Because of which addition even Erasmus himself fears that the Greek Codices in this place may be corrupted. Certainly Robert notes that he saw two ancient ones which, omitting that part, agreed with our Vulgate, and it seems sufficiently clear that our Interpreter did not have that clause in his Greek exemplar. Nor yet for that reason is it to be removed from the Greek books without greater authority, since, being retained, the whole verse can nevertheless have a convenient sense, which we receive from Oecumenius. It is written, however, to those believing in the name of Jesus, that they may know that they have eternal life, lest they lose that faith through apostasy or sins against conscience; that they who are in that very state in which they believe in the name of the Son of GOD know that they have life, and are certain by faith of the grace of GOD and the blessed state in which they are established in the kingdom of grace regarding justification and salvation in the present, is clear from the words themselves. It is written to them, therefore, that they may believe, that is, that they may constantly believe or continue to believe, or if you prefer to take it of the rest, that they also may believe. That this brings in confidence, the following words also teach.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν τοῖς πισεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τῦ ὑῦ τῦ Θεῦ, ἵνα εἰδῆτε, ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔχετε, καὶ ἵνα πισεύητε εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τῦ ὑῦ τῦ Θεῦ) Melius in Manuscripto: Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, ἵνα εἰδῆτε, ὅτι ζωὴν ἔχετε αἰώνιον, οἱ πισεύον- τες εἰς τὸ ὄνομα ὑῦ τῦ Θεῦ. Nec aliter legere Syrus, La- tinus, Arabs. Ideo tot monita & hortamenta vobis scripsi, ut sciretis certum vos jus habere ad vitam æternam, quam- diu creditis Deo, autore Jesu, illo, qui a nobis dicitur & est DEI Filius. Quid sit nomen hoc loco, de eo vide supra III. 23.

Temere corrigit Græcum textum e versioni- bus, quum optime ille se habeat. Æquior est Græ- cæ veritati Bartholomaus Petri: Græcus, inquit, Codex pro Præsente (scribo) habet scripsi ἔγραψα, ut habent multi boni Latini libri etiam impressi, & textus Venerabilis Bedæ. Verum sensus non muta- tur. Præterea illam clausulam: Qui creditis in no- mine Filii Dei pleriq; Codices Græci annectunt hu- jus versus principio, sic: Hæc scripsi vobis, qui cre- ditis &c. sed id quoque non magni momenti est. Illud majoris quod iidem plerique Codices Græci ad- dunt huic versui unam clausulam, istam nimirum, ut & credatis in nomine Filii Dei. Propter quam additionem ipse etiam Erasmus veretur, ne hoc loco Græci Codices sint depravati. Certe Robertus notat, sibi conspectos duos veteres, qui eam partem omit- tentes consentirent cum nostra Vulgata, & nostrum Interpretem in suo exemplari Græco clausulam istam non habuisse, satis apertum videtur. Nec tamen idcirco sine majori autoritate e Græcis libris est tollenda, quoniam ea retenta nihilominus totus ver- sus commodum sensum habere potest, quem accipi- mus ex Oecumenio. Scribitur autem credentibus in nomen Jesu, ut sciant, quod vitam æternam ha- beant, ne fidem illam deperdant per apostasiam, aut peccata contra conscientiam, quos vero eo ipso statu, quo credunt in nomen Filii DEI scire, quod vitam habeant, fideque certos esse de gra- tia DEI ac statu beato, in quo constituti sunt in regno gratiæ de justificatione & salute in præ- senti, ex ipsis verbis luculentum est. Illis ergo scribitur, ut credant, id est, constanter credant seu credere pergant, aut si de reliquis id malis acci- pere, ut & illi credant. Fiduciam ista inferre, qua credentes, etiam verba sequentia docent.

## 5:14
Verse 14.

And this is the confidence that we have toward Him) We who believe in God also have this confidence concerning Him, namely with the best of rights. Concerning the word παῥῥησίας, see above II. 21, III. 21.

That if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us) He explains more clearly here what he had said above III. 22. According to the will of GOD, one may absolutely ask for the increase of faith, Luke VII. 5, and the Holy Spirit, Luke XI. 13. Other things not except on this condition, if it be more glorious to God and more salutary for us that they be given to us than not given. Ἀκούει ἡμῶν, He hears us, present for any time; so also John IX. 31, XI. 41. In the Manuscript it is: We ask according to His name, that is, in Christ's name, as John XIV. 13, 14, XV. 16, XVI. 23, 24, 26.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

Καὶ αὕτη ἐσὶν ἡ παῥῥησία, ἧν ἔχομεν πρὸς αὐτὸν) Nos qui in Deum credimus, etiam hanc de eo fiduciam habe- mus, nempe jure optimo. De voce παῥῥησίας vide supra II. 21. III. 21.

Ὅτι ἐάν τι αἰτώμεθα κατὰ τὸ θέλημα αὐτῦ ἀκύει ἡμῶν) Clarius hic explicat, quod dixerat supra III. 22. secundum voluntatem DEI absolute peti possunt augmentum fidei Luc. VII. 5. & Spiritus Sanctus, Luc. XI. 13. Alia non nisi hac conditione, si ea nobis dari quam non dari sit Deo gloriosus nobisque salutarius. Ἀκούει ἡμῶν exaudit nos, praesens pro quovis tempore; Sic & Joh. IX. 31. XI. 41. in Manuscripto est : Αἰτώμεθα κατὰ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, id est in Christi nomine, ut Joh. XIV. 13. 14. XV. 16. XVI. 23. 24. 26.

## 5:15
Verse 15.

And if we know that He hears us in what we ask, we know that we have the requests which we have asked of Him) We have for we shall have, present for future. God hears immediately, but He does not give immediately.

What sense seems more suitable than that which Bartholomaeus Petri brings forward from Didymus: And we know that God hears us, whatever we have asked, if (that is, because, since, as often elsewhere) we know that we already have the petitions which we have heretofore requested from him: which he illustrates with the words of Eucherius of Lyon in Blessed Augustine, sermon CLXXVI de tempore: Let every faithful person, when he has already received so much, learn through those things which he recognizes have been granted to hope for those promised, and let him hold the past and present goodness of his God as a kind of security for future things.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

Καὶ ἐὰν οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀκούει ἡμῶν ὧν αἰτώμεθα, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἔχομεν τὰ αἰτήματα ἃ ᾐτήκαμεν παρ’ αὐτοῦ) Ἔχομεν pro ἕξομεν, praesens pro futuro. Deus statim exaudit, at non statim dat.

Qui sensus convenientior videtur, quam quem Bartholomaeus Petri e Didymo adducit: Et scimus quod audit nos Deus, quicquid petierimus, si (id est, quia, quandoquidem, ut saepe alias) scimus, quod jam habemus petitiones, quas antehac postu- lavimus ab eo: quem illustrat verbis Eucherii Lugdunensis apud B. Augustinum serm. CLXXVI. de tempore: Fidelis quisque, cum jam tanta perce- perit, per ea, quae cognoscit praestita, discat sperare promissa, & Dei sui praeteritam praesentemque bonita- tem quasi futurorum teneat cautionem.

## 5:16
Verse 16.

If anyone sees his brother sinning) It is a great thing that God hears us not only for ourselves, but also for others who have given their name to Christ. For thus the word ἀδελφὸς in this place must be taken from the subject matter, and all the more so because here αὑτοῦ is added, as in a similar case in Matthew XVIII. 15.

Which, however, as Blessed Hunnius warns, is not to be accepted as if the prayer of another obtains life for someone, whatever he may do, but if he does not violently repel the means of conversion from himself. But why should that not be extended to any neighbor whatsoever? Does not the Church also pray for the conversion and salvation of infidels? And why would it pray if it were certain that this was not done according to the will of GOD, or was not heard? Indeed, the Doctor of the Gentiles teaches that one must pray for the salvation of all men, 1 Tim. I. verse 1 seqq., because God wills the salvation of all men, and because Christ gave himself as a ransom for all, and he calls that good and acceptable in the sight of our Savior God. And one must pray here, according to the Evangelist, for him who does not have life, that is, who is not reborn, and therefore not a brother in the sense in which the reborn and faithful are our brothers: for we are commanded to pray for life for such a one, and the promise is, and he will give him life, therefore he was devoid of life.

Sin not unto death)

This question has long been much agitated, what is a sin unto death? Many of the ancients understood the sin unto death to be the sin of one who had been baptized, not however every sin which was committed with some deliberation or time given for deliberation, but one of those most grave ones, for instance, idolatry, homicide, adultery. For whoever had committed such things after baptism was in most places never received back to communion, just as in other crimes, if anyone had lapsed again. Such people were indeed not strictly excluded from the mercy of God, but because of the uncertainty of the outcome, the Church did not wish to be a sponsor. In the time of Tertullian, the Roman Bishop received those who had lapsed once into adultery to penance, and the Shepherd of Hermas shows that this opinion, although much agitated by Tertullian, was not entirely new at Rome. In the time of Cyprian, there was varied observation concerning those who had lapsed into idolatry or adultery, even in Africa. Therefore, he did not wish to determine anything concerning those who had lapsed into idolatry, except with the consent of other bishops outside Africa, and especially the Roman Bishop. And after long consideration, it was decided that even those who had lapsed in this way should be received, but after a long time. For they did not believe that a man was suddenly purified, but that the more grave the crime was, the more slowly and with more difficulty. And this was approved in the great Nicene Synod, which was long the rule of ecclesiastical government; and for those who had deliberately lapsed into idolatry, a time of penance of eleven years was prescribed, for others somewhat less according to the gravity of the crimes. That what I said about idolatry, homicide, and adultery is true appears from Tertullian's book De Pudicitia, especially chapter XIX, and from Socrates' history, book 10, where he calls this unpardonable, which the Novatians defended stubbornly. But that which I said concerning other crimes, if they were repeated after baptism, that reconciliation was not given by the fountains of the Church, we are taught by Tertullian in his work on repentance, when he says: He placed a second repentance in the vestibule, which may open to those who knock, but only once, because it is already the second time, but never again, because it is next to useless. For is not even this once enough? Where, when he says 'second repentance,' he understands it from baptism, which is the first repentance. There are similar things elsewhere in the same author. And indeed, as far as ancient customs are concerned, the matter stands thus. And Ambrose and others refer this passage to those customs. However, I do not think the sense of this passage points to that: but that they are said to sin unto death who, when they have sinned, continue to sin after being warned, or certainly do not wish to submit themselves to the discipline which has been established in the Church. For what hope of health is there for him who does not wish to listen to the physician given to him by God? Hermas, book 6. Whatever cattle you have seen very happy and exulting, these are they who have departed from God forever and have delivered themselves to the desires of this world. For them, therefore, there is no return to life through repentance, since indeed they have added to their other offenses and have attacked the name of the Lord with unspeakable words. Men of this kind are destined for death. These are the rotten branches in the same Hermas, III. 8. And Clement of Alexandria seems to intend nothing else, citing this passage in Stromata II, who also in Stromata VII calls them 'past feeling' (ἀπηλγηκότας), and says that a wise man justly invokes some temporal evils upon such people. Cyprian, Epistle LII. And therefore, dearest brother, we judge that those who do not perform repentance, nor testify to the sorrow of their offenses with their whole heart and a manifest profession of their lamentation, should be altogether prohibited from the hope of communion and peace, if they begin to entreat in infirmity and danger: because it is not the repentance of the offense, but the warning of impending death that compels them to ask, nor is he worthy to receive consolation in death who did not think that he was going to die. The same author denies that those who have been warned about sin and instructed can be forgiven, Epistle LXIII. Basil to Amphilochius, chapter LXXXIV. 'We write all these things so that the fruits of the mind may be squeezed out. For we do not judge such things entirely by time, but we pay attention to the manner of repentance.' 'But if they are difficult to detach from their own habits, and wish to serve the pleasures of the flesh rather than the Lord, and do not accept the life according to the Gospel, we have no common discourse with them.
