Vi- dit etiam septem sigilla aperiri, & unoquoque aperto visio quædam apparebat. Vidit item septem An- gelos, habentes septem tubas, & unoquoque illorum clangente fiebat signum, septimo vero clangente au- divit dicentes: Regnum mundi Domini factum est. Et arcam Testamenti vidit in cælo. Dein- de mulierem parturientem vidit & Draconem igni- tum, qui illam persequebatur. Mulier quidem servata est in solitudine, Draco vero abjectus in ignem. Post ista bestiam vidit habentem cornua de- cem & capita septem, & diadema ejus blasphemia plenum erat. Nomen vero ejus non patefecit, sed nu- merum nominis ejus, nempe sexcenti sexaginta sex. Et virgines audivit canentes & Agnum sequentes. Vidit etiam Angelum per medium cæli volantem, & post hunc alterum, post alterum, tertium quoque, deinde & nubem candidam vidit, & insidentem illi si- milem Filio hominis, in capite coronam auream ha- bentem & in manu sua falcem acutam. Denique se- ptem Angelos vidit habentes septem plagas novissimas & phialas aureas plenas iræ Dei. Post hæc ablatus est Spiritu in solitudinem & vidit mulierem sedentem super bestiam coccinam, habentem capita septem:

vidit bestiam ac Reges terræ, bellum facere volentes cum eo, qui sedebat super equum album. Et appre- hensa est bestia, & cum ipsa Pseudo-Propheta, qui est Anti-Christus, & vidit eos abjici in stagnum ignis. Post ista vidit Angelum descendentem de cælo, & ab- jicientem satanam cum his, qui characterem ipsius habebant, in abyssum, & claudentem super ipsum, ne posthac amplius seducat gentes, donec consumpti sint mille anni. Martyres deinde vidit cum gloria in Christo regnantes, & quod satanas post mille annos solvendus sit & abjiciendus in stagnum ignis cum Anti-Christo in secula seculorum. Post hæc vidit cæ- lum novum, terram novam, ac Jerusalem novam, & fluvium aquæ vivæ, ac servos Dei contemplantes fa- ciem ejus & habentes nomen ejus in frontibus suis. Cum hæc vidisset Johannes, procidit volens adorare Angelum, qui sibi hæc omnia ostenderat. At Angelus prohibuit illius conatum, dicens: Non me, sed Deum adora: Ego enim conservus tuus sum. Postquam au- tem ista vidit, audivit ab ipso Domino nostro JESU, quod existens sit, & idem ipse sit verbum Dei, quod posterioribus temporibus propter nos caro factum est: Homo inquam perfectus factus est, & Filius ho- minis vocatus est.

Partitionem exhibet ipse Apostolus cap. I. v. 19. Scribe, quæ vidisti, cum quæ sunt, tum quæ oportet fie- ri posthac. Agit ergo Johannes partim de iis, quæ sunt, vel de statu Ecclesiæ præsente, partim de iis, quæ deinceps futura erant, vel de statu Ecclesiæ futuro. Sed quia per modum Epistolæ ea Ecclesiis commen- dare voluitSpiritus sanctus ac titulum integro scri- pto præmisit, primum titulus occurrit, constans inscriptione libri v. 1. 2. & commendatione ejusdem v. 3. tum vero ipsum opus, in quo more epistolico observare est primo nomen Autoris, deinde Eccle- siarum illarum nomina quibus inscripta est Apoca- lypsis: Porro votum vel salutatio additur, denique lectoris excitatio commemoratione gloriosi ad- ventus Christi. Et hæc Exordii instar. Succedit postmodum narratio septem constans revelationi- bus, quarum prima est de statu Ecclesiæ præsenti, re- liquæ de statu futuro: Illa particularem Ecclesiam in Asia proprie concernit, hæc autem Ecclesiam universalem. Tandem subjungitur conclusio cap. 22. a v. 5. Nam eo usque se porrigit Apocalyptica narratio.

Visio prima est quasi præparatoria, quatenus S. Johannes ad hoc munus Propheticum vocatur & confirmatur & hac parte communis est cap. 1. Sed quatenus in ea visione proposita sunt, quæ de statu Ecclesiæ istius temporis perscribenda erant ad se- ptem Ecclesias Asiæ, quo pertinent secundum & tertium capp. Separata est hæc visio a sex reliquis, quæ specialius Prophetiæ nomine veniunt, quum illa prophetia ea ratione dicatur, non quod vatici- netur de futuris, sed quod præsentia, sed occulta re- velet: Quæ hic concernunt statum Ecclesiarum, Ephesinæ nempe, Smyrnensis, Pergamenfis, Thyati- rensis, cap. 2. ut & Sardensis, Philadelphensis & Lao- dicenæ cap. 3. Prophetia autem speciatim dicta est tum PRIMA tum SECUNDA: Siquidem cap. 10. vers. ult. indicatur Johanni: OPORTET te ITE- RUM prophetare: ubi eadem solenniter ad alteram prophetiam investitur.

Secunda visio cap. 4. 5. 6. 7. absolvitur, in quo primum παρασκευὴ occurrit cap. 4. repræsentatio- ne gloriæ SS. Trinitatis, & gloriosæ ejus celebrationis in cælis: & cap. 5. repræsentatione libri obsignati specialis providentiæ, vel fatorum Ecclesiæ, necnon Agni occisi, digni ad referendum librum, & ob id a toto choro Ecclesiæ in cælis & in terris celebrati.

Deinde relatio de spectaculis in sigillorum reseratio- ne visis, primi nempe, unde prodiit equus albus, secundi ex quo visus est prodire equus ruffus; ter- tii, unde conspectus est niger prodire: Quarti unde pallidus: Quinti quo aperto visæ sunt sub altari animæ occisorum vindictam Divinam provocan- tium, & sexti, unde terræ motus, solis obtenebratio, lunæ cruenta facies, stellarum casus, cæli convolutio, montium & insularum ac incolarum terræ gravissima commotio observata, de quibus cap. 6. sub quo et- iam adumbrata electorum in periculis obsignatio, & ad gaudia cælestia exaltatio: cap. 7.

Visio tertia est de septimo sigillo aperto, & Ange- lis tubicinibus cap. 8. 9. Et capite quidem septimo præparatio facta ad sigillum septimum aperien- dum, cujus gratia confortandi primo animi fide- lium erant ob quatuor Angelorum, ventum pro- hibentium damnum, idque per Angeli sigilliferi ob- signationem servorum Domini, ad avertendam eorum læsionem, factam; unde sequuta Dei & Agni glorificatio, ac Johannis de cœtu Candidatorum cæle- stium informatio. Hoc tamen caput 7. ita præ- paratio est ad sequentia, ut respiciat etiam antece- dentia, & consolationem in illis, quæ ibi prædictæ sunt, calamitatibus exhibeat, unde cum iisdem ad secundam visionem ceu generalem non immerito pertinere censetur. Sequenti autem cap. 8. refer- tur quomodo post silentium semihorulæ, in conspe- ctum producti septem Angeli tubicines, sed ante tubarum clangorem, per Angelum alium preces sanctorum Deo offerentem, de gratia Divina in futura calamitate sancti confirmati sint, atque ita IV. Angeli cecinerint tuba: Primo clangente, grando & ignis cum sulphure mixtus, secundo ma- re ardens, tertio stella de cœlo cadens damna fecit; quarto clangente sequuta obtenebratio solis, lunæ & stellarum est: Quorum clangorem Angeli per me- dium cæli væ, væ, væ, denuntiantis clamor auditus est. Sequitur porro cap. 9. quintæ tubæ væ primum concernens, ubi ex abysso fumus, & è fumo locu- stæ exitiosæ & terribiles prodiere sub Rege Abad- don, ut & sextæ tubæ, quæ secundum væ attinebat, & quatuor Angelorum ad Euphratem dimissio- nem ad occisionem tertiæ partis hominum. Et hucusque prima sese porrigit prophetia, adeoque terminanda hic tertia visio.

Succedit quarta ad septimum tubicinium per- tinens cap. 10. & 11. in qua primum cap. 10. alius Angelus fortis cum libro visus, jurans de temporis defitione, & librum devorandum Johanni tradens, ut iterum prophetaret, quæ præparatio fuit ad se- cundam prophetiam. Postmodum cap. 11. sum- matim tertium væ exhibetur sub dimensione tem- pli, ejectione chori, & conculcatione civitatis san- ctæ, necnon excitatione duorum testium, quorum potestas, occisio, vivificatio, & glorificatio sistitur cum voce magna cœlitum Deum celebrantium, & con- spectu arcæ fœderis in cœlo.

Porro visione quinta cap. 12. 13. & 14. compre- hensa partim sub imagine mulieris post partum in desertum fugientis, cujus gratia contra Draconem pugnat Michael, & occultanda mulier fuit, Ecclesiæ ejusque persecutio sub Antichristo adumbrata c. 12. partim bestia gemina ob ejus potentiam, & fraudulen- tiam describendam producta c. 13. eidemq; Agnus cum confessoribus in monte Sion oppositus, impri- mis vero cum Angelo æternum Evangelium prædi- cante, alio casum Babylonis intimante, ut & tertio æternam damnationem adoratoribus bestiæ de- nuntiante, & Filio hominis in nube Angeloque cum falce acuta vineam terræ vindemiante cap. 14.

Visio sexta septem plagas novissimas cum judicio super meretrice magna, & jubilo de eodem cœlesti, quinque seqq. cap. exhibet. Plagæ cap. 15. & 16. enumerantur: Illo Angeli eas habentes cum victo- ribus bestiæ ad mare vitreum canticum Mosis & Agni decantantibus visi, accipientes aureas phia- las ira divina plenas: Hoc vero septem phialæ effun- duntur in terram. Judicium meretricis cap. 17. & 18. propositum est. Illo meretrix ipsa Babylonica vivis coloribus depingitur: Hoc vero casus ejus- dem cum causa illius, & luctu amasiorum super ejusdem casu describitur. Jubilum vero cœlestis exercitus super eodem, ut & tripudium ob immi- nentes Agni nuptias, necnon apparitionem Regis Regum, & victoriam de bestia, & falso Propheta Cap. 19. exhibet.

Visione septima ligati ad mille annos, Draconis, ad breve tempus dimissi, & Gogum & Magogum in prælium congregantis, adversus castra sanctorum, illo (Gogo) igne de cœlo consumpto, in locum infernalem præcipitationem Cap. 20. necnon Ele- ctorum sub specie Hierosolymæ novæ & Sponsæ Agni beatitudinem adumbrat cap. 21. & 22. ad v. 5. Quibus subjicitur conclusio, & finis postremus ca- pite, ad v. 9.. Denique Epilogus totius libri vel epi- stolæ subjungitur v. 10. seq. quæ adhortatione & ob- testatione gravissima, ut & suspirio, ac voto finali ob- signatur.

B. Lutheri distributio cum explicatione succin- cta in præfatione ejus aurea legatur: Quam paucis alio sensu expositis B. Cluverus in diluculo Apoca- lyptico sic exhibet: Quod præmisso exordio, & nar- ratione cap. 1. revelatio qua priorem partem PRÆ- SENTIUM visionem cap. 2. & 3. qua posteriorem prophetiam capp. reliquis comprehensam conti- neat, & hanc tum primam cap. 4. ad 8. tum secun- dam capp. seqq. Prophetia autem prima & gene- ralis sit cap. 4. 5. 6. & 7. & specialis certis temporum rerumque circumstantiis definita cap. 8. & 9. Ge- neralis tribus segmentis constet: Primo præparatio continetur ad universam prophetiam 4. & 5. capp. quorum illo Dominus ipse cum cœlesti sua gloria, palatio, curia, totoque hoc gratioso regimine de- pingatur; hoc vero imperscrutabilis ejus providen- tia ac præscientia per secretorum libellum figure- tur una cum ejusdem patefactione, quæ per Chri- stum solum fieri & impetrari potest. Secundum operatorium facit, ipsam Dramaticam figuratio- nem complectens earum rerum, quæ hac peregri- natione nostra communiter & universim eveniunt, sex sigillis constans cap. 6. Tertium visionem ha- beat informatoriam, & consolatoriam, quid molian- tur Angeli tenebrarum, quomodo iisdem potenter à Deo resistatur & qualiter is electos suos tueatur, ac denique in æternas mansiones colligat Cap. 7. Specialis absolvitur sex tubis, quarum quatuor mi- nores cap. 8. pertractantur, duæ majores cap. 9. Ul- tima vero ceu maxima nova Prophetiæ materiam largiatur, & per undecim capita se extendat.

Prophetiam alteram quod attinet, tres ejus par- tes fecit B. Cluverus I. Exordium seu præparatio- nem per investituram Johannis novam Cap. 10. 2. Visionem ipsam væ tertium seu septimi Angeli tubicinium comprehendentem cap. 11. usque ad 22. v. 6. 3. Epilogum cap. 22, 6. 7. 8. 9. Visionem au- tem quadruplicem hic facit 1. generalem, quæ est ipsi Apocalypseos quarta, & pene omnium visio- num luculentissima, universam tertii væ periodum depingens cap. 11. 12. 13. 14. Summarium ejus- dem proponit c. 11. tractatio ipsa tribus partibus absolvitur tum parascene seu prologo à vers. 15. ad cap. 12. vers. 9. tum narratione tribus typis initium, progressum, vigoremque ipsum seu ἐπίτασιν tertià væ depingente de muliere exulante, Dracone pu- gnante & insidias horrendas struente cap. 12. & de duabus bestiis cap. 13. quarum prior regnum Anti- Christianum juxta potestatem secularem, altera Pseudo-Propheticum ejusdem statum exhibet: tum antithesi & antidoto partim de Christo Rege in monte Zion stante ejusque choro Anti-Christo opposito, partim de Præconibus Evangelii oppositis Pseudo- Prophetæ, partim de requie occisorum à bestia, partim de judicio Christi per falcem subinde hostes de- metente, Cap. 14. II. Specialis septem phiala- rum effusionem commemorans cap. 15. 16. 17. 18. 19. ad v. 11. in qua primum fit præparatio Cap. 15. tum habetur simplex prophetia cap. 16. postea ad- ditur Didactica vel informatoria visio tum de bestia meretricem portante, & scorto in ea equitante cap. 17. tum de Angelo Babyloni exitium denunciante cap. 18. tum de multitudine cœlesti Deo gratias agente, cap. 19. atque ista referuntur à B. Cluvero ad quin- tam visionem.

III. Bestiæ & Gogi exitium cap. 19. & 20. Quod sexta visione continetur duabus partibus absolu- ta; priori bellum Christi & Anti-Christi postre- mum cap. 19. reliquo: Posteriori ultimum diaboli conatum ejusque eventum præmissa parascenasti- ca narratione de Draconis diuturna captivitate ac statu mundi intermedio, qua pios pariter & impios describit. Cap. 20. v. 10. Septimam visionem consti- tuit B. Cluverus de mundi fine, utpote de Christi Judicis apparitione à v. 11. ad finem cap. 20. & de triumphante Ecclesia cap. 21. & 22. ad vers. 5. Deni- que epilogum posterioris prophetiæ constituit v. 6. 7. 8. Epilogum autem totius Apocalypseos ceu partem quartam libri verbis tum Christi tum Apostoli constantem à v. 9. ad finem assignat.

Alienæ omnino sunt interpretationes I. eorum qui vel generaliter pugnam carnis & Spiritus in ho- mine in Apocalypsi describi volunt, quod Aria- montano, vel dissidia inter probos & improbos, eo- rumque exitus, quod Tyconio, Primafio, Ansberto, Anshelmo, Ruperto, Haymoni, Richardo, Hugoni, Thomæ & Dionysio Carthusiano, ut & Titelmanno tribuunt, Cornelius & Cluverus, quæ ex varietate temporum & circumstantiarum nullo negotio re- fellitur.

Neque II. convenit Aureoli, Lyrani, Antonini, Ederi, Lizorazi interpretatio, quos Cornelius à Lapide cum Alcafare ait, primam visionem septem sigillorum ad Juliani tempora extendere, alteram septem tubarum ad Mauritium Imperatorem: Ter- tiam Draconis & duplicis bestiæ ad Caroli M. vi- ctorias: Quartam phialarum ad Henricum IV. Imperatorem & Hildebrandum seu Gregorium VII. Quintam Babylonis meretricis & bestiæ usque ad Anti-Christum: Sextam usque ad extremum ju- dicium; quam ceu hiulcam Alcaser, & Cornelius ceu falsam, ineptam & violentam Cluverus merito rejicit.

Neque III. calculum meretur sententia Abbatis Ubertini, & Seraphini de septem Ecclesiæ statibus primo fundationis in Apostolis, secundo persecutio- nis sub gentilibus Imperatoribus, tertio prosperita- tis sub Constantino, quarto divisionis sub hæreticis, quinto tranquillitatis & incrementi sub Carolo M. sexto ultimæ persecutionis sub Anti-Christo, septi- mo extremi judicii: Nam præterquam quod Anti- Christum falso reservet ultimo loco, explicatio hæc, ipsius Cornelii judicio, partim violenta est, partim invecta, atque tota ab ingenio humano conficta.

Novas alias & plures excogitarunt Jesuitæ interpretationes, in gratiam Pontificis, ne agnoscatur ille Anti-Christus à Johanne prædictus: Sed diversas & contrarias, mutuoque se intérementes. Ribera enim & Bellarminus ut & Blasius de Viegas pleraque vaticinia ad ultima tempora & triennalem suum Anti-Christum detorquent. Quæ proinde quarta est explicatio. Ludovicus vero ab Alcafar (quæ quinta est interpretatio) ad prima eandem refert tempora, & ad bellum Ecclesiæ cum Synagoga Judaica priora capita à c. 4. ad 11. posteriora vero usque ad 20. ad bellum cum gentilitate: Quem bonam partem sequutus est Grotius veluti conductius Pontificis Romani Advocatus. Sed ea ne quidem ipsis Jesuitis probare sese potuit. Cornelius certe eandem reprobat 1. quod nova sit, 2. mystica sit non literaria, 3. quod ex prophetia faciat historiam, 4. quod pleraque loca Apocalypseos ita clare ex communi Ecclesiæ Doctorum explicatione de temporibus novissimis loquantur, ut ad Ecclesiam Judæorum & gentilium victricem detorqueri non posse videantur. Quum autem opponatur Alcafari à Pareo, & aliis, prius bellum cum Synagoga jam ante revelatam prophetiam depugnatum fuisse, siquidem illa tum jam una cum templo in cineribus jacuerit: posterius bellum cum gentilitate etsi jam tunc flagraret, porro gravissime pressurum Christianos, longe tamen atrocius, cum Anti-Christo à S. Johanne prædictum esse, ὁμοθυμαδὸν omnes Interpretes, etiam ipsosmet Papistas consentire, ac judicium meretricis magnæ, Babylonisque ruinam non ut conversionis gratiam, sed ut scortationis pœnam, regno & sedi Anti-Christianæ novissimis temporibus infligendam exhiberi, adeoque de Romæ & gentilitatis ad fidem CHRISTI conversione sub Constantino & successoribus mox sub trecentesimum Christi annum facta, deque Romanæ Ecclesiæ atque Pontificis ad urbis & orbis imperium erectione id interpretari, esse, cum ratione insanire: Grotius novo commento interpolavit illam opinionem, sed toti antiquitati penitus adverso, nimirum ante desolationem Hierosolymæ visionem Johanneam factam esse: Babylonis vero combustionem ab Ostrogothis, & Totila factam designari contendit: quid vero per bestiæ interitum indigitetur, non invenit, nisi ad tempora, quæ ruinam urbis præcessere καθ' ὕστερον πρώτερον recurreret, ac felicitatem novi cæli & novæ terræ ad Ecclesiæ statum florentissimum, quem facit inde à temporibus Constantini ad tempora usq; Justiniani referret ac gloriam Hierosolymæ Cap. 21. descriptam de splendore Ecclesiæ Romanæ sub Principibus Christianis interpretaretur. Sed illa hysterologia minime admittenda, nec de felicitate Ecclesiæ militantis & persecutionibus maximis à Constantino ad Justinianum, quæ multa infelicitate ab Arianis & Eutychianis, quibus Justinianus ipse addictus fuisse creditur, aliisque hæreticis, & gravissimis incursionibus ab Attila, Genferico, Totila & similibus aliis terrarum flagellis illatis turbata: sed de beatitudine Ecclesiæ triumphantis in omnem æternitatem duratura S. Johannem extremis capitibus agere constans veterum & recentiorum Interpretum est sententia, textus sacri evidentiæ sole clariori innixa. De cætero Alcafaris ψευδερμηνείας confutatio, & quomodo fratres Cadmeos Alcafarem cum Ribera & Blasio de Viegas & Bellarmino, legi in diluc. B. Cluveri potest pag. 38. seqq. Pleniorem discussionem commentorum istorum & imprimis Grotii reservamus explicationi ipsius textus ejusdemque vindiciis.

Porro sexto nonnulli Apocalypsin non conti- nua serie periodorum, sed alia atque alia periodo- rum eorundem repræsentatione decurrere, atque eadem diversimode exhibere censent, qui iterum in divortia sententiarum abeunt. Plerique visio- nem de septem sigillis & septem tubiciniis, nec non visionem de muliere parturiente, Dracone & utraque bestia, denique de ligato, soluto, & judicato Dracone & nova Hierosolyma, universales faciunt, hoc est jux- ta ipsorum recensionem secundam, tertiam, quar- tam & septimam, quemadmodum particulares, illas de septem phialis & de judicio meretricis, ac ruinæ Babylonis constituunt, nimirum quintam & sex- tam, quæ Parei & Henrici à Diest, qui analysin apocalypseos exegeticam è Parei commentariis contexuit, aliorumque est sententia. Qui proin- de quatuor Ecclesiæ Christianæ periodos in universali- bus illis visionibus distinctis quatuor modis exhi- beri volunt : primam Ecclesiæ florentis & agoni- zantis sub tyrannis Romanis usque ad pacem Con- stantini M. Anno 315. secundam Ecclesiæ regnantis & luxuriantis sub Imperatoribus Christianis us- que ad exortum Anti-Christi sub Bonifacio III. an- no Christi 606. tertiam Ecclesiæ calcatæ atque op- pressæ ab Anti-Christo, imprimis occidentali usque ad dimensionem templi seu reformationem : Quar- tam Ecclesiæ à Papismo reformatæ & Papatus in- clinati usque ad finem mundi.

Verum enimvero nondum apertis sigillis jam exhibitas esse Ecclesiæ Christianæ periodos, deque iisdem libro adhuc clauso informationem acce- pisse S. Johannem, credendum non est. Et coacta sunt in ista explicatione non pauca, cum sigillis tu- bicinia, his reliquis duabus visionibus, quas uni- versales vocant, exhibita, ceu parallela applican- tur, denique ordo visionum turbatur, & particula- res universalibus commiscentur.

Minus adhuc congruunt (VII) eorum ἐξήγησις, qui phialas etiam sigillis, & tubis conferunt, quem- admodum Nicolaus Colladus voluit, quod sigillis ob- scurius præfiguratum, apertius tubis, apertissime ve- ro septem sigillis depingi : Quomodo septem phiala- rum visionem etiam universalem statui oportet, quam vero plagas novissimas solum concernere, nec nisi violenter ad periodos & visiones antece- dentes retrahi liquet, unde Pareus ipse hanc sen- tentiam profligavit ad cap. 16, 2. licet sit effectuum aliqua similitudo in sex tubis & sex phialis posterio- ribus, tamen septem phialæ septem sigillis & septem tubis non omnino respondent. Ratio aperta habetur ex vers. 2. tam hujus quam præcedentis capitis à tem- pore, quoniam phialæ incipiunt effundi in stigmaticos bestiæ cap. 16, 2. diu post exortum bestiæ, quando ea- dem jam vinci ab aliquibus cœperat cap. 15, 2. natales vero bestiæ ad sigillum sextum & tubam quintam demum pertinent.

Sed aberrant maxime, VIII. Qui easdem perio- dos in septem epistolis etiam quærunt : Quas tamen alii aliter distribuunt, & assignant Matthæus Hoff- mannus Macharopæus dictus primam epistolam, primum sigillum & primum tubicinium eandem periodum concernere vult, ut Angelus primus Ec- clesiæ nempe Ephesinæ primitivam Ecclesiam eamque totam sistat per 343. annos : eosdemque an- nos explicet primum sigillum, ut & primum tubici- nium. Angelus secundus Ecclesiæ Smyrnensis to- tam iterum Ecclesiam per sequentes 343. annos æræ Christianæ referat, quod pariter de sigillo se- cundo & secundo tubicinio contendit, atque ita porro de reliquis Angelis Ecclesiarum, & sigillis & tubiciniis: Quæ proinde summatim exhibeant septies 343. annos, ut tota periodus Ecclesiæ Novi

Testamenti sit 2400. annorum vel 24. seculorum, qui per 24. seniores etiam repræsentati sint. Quam sententiam ea confidentia ὁ Μακαρίτης proposuit, ut hoc decimo septimo seculo æræ Christianæ quæ- rendum esse Interpretem Apocalypseos Seniorem illum, qui Johannem monuerit ne fleret, Apoc. 5,6. seque hunc ipsum esse haud obscure innueret C. 7. p. 112. 113. Cap. 12. pag. 215. Falsum autem va- tem fuisse mors interveniens testatur, quæ non permisit, ut sigilla referaret, nec ultra sigillum quin- tum progrederetur chronotaxi sua Apocalyptica, quæ præterea perquam lubricis nititur principiis, verbi gratia, septem Angelos Ecclesiarum Asiæ se- ptem temporum universæ Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti esse periodos, septem etiam illos esse Angelos tu- bicinatores, & sic Ecclesias illas septem cum tubici- niis quoad synchronismos convenire ac quodlibet tubicinium Angelicum continere septem jubilæa vul- garia annos nempe 343. adeoque totam periodum Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti constare annis bis mille & quadringentis cum unitate, ac viginti quatuor seniores esse totidem generationes seu annorum centenarios; quæ recitasse est refutasse.

Rursus IX. alias parallelas lineas ducunt alios- que synchronismos fingunt quoad septem episto- las, septem sigilla, & septem tubas imo etiam quoad phialas septem Calviniani Bremenses, Ludovicus Crocius, Johannes Crocius & Balthasar Willius. Ille in præfatione syntagmatis sui Theologici, quod pro conditione, ut ait, Ecclesiæ Sardenfis adornavit anno 1636. primam Ecclesiæ Christianæ conditionem fecit Apostolicam, quæ significata fuerit Ecclesiæ Ephesinæ à Tiberio usque ad Trajanum Imperato- rem, quam auream vocat, & ad primi sigilli equum album, & ad primum tubicinium & phialam pri- mam Apoc. 2, 1. cap. 6, 2. cap. 8, 7. cap. 16, 2. trahit. Alteram μαρτυρευμένην comprobatam à Trajano us- que ad Constantinum M. Angelo Ecclesiæ Smyr- nensis significatam ab anno Christi 85. ad quem refert visionem Johannis in Patmo per decem dies, hoc est horis vel annis 240. ad annum usque 325. ad quam periodum refert equum rufum & phia- lam secundam, Apocal. 6, 4. C. 16, 3. nuncupatque ferream. Tertiam Polemicam sive Eristicam signi- ficatam Angelo Ecclesiæ Pergamenfis à Constanti- no M. usque ad Carolum M. sigilli tertii, equi nigri, tubæ tertiæ, casus stellæ magnæ, & phialæ tertiæ, Quartam religiosam atque devotam, significatam Angelo Thyatirensi sub Papatu Romano à tempore Caroli M. usque ad Carolum V. quam refert ad sigillum quartum, tubam quartam & phialam quar- tam, sed qua ratione, non explicat: forte quia ita placet. Quintam Politicam Angelo Sardenfi si- gnificatam inde ab imperio Caroli V. quam st anno confert, & ad sigillum quintum ac tubam & phialam quintam refert. Sextam fraternam Angelo Phila- delphensi significatam, quam argenteam appellat & ad sextum sigillum, sextamque tubam & phialam re- fert. Septimam tepidam Angelo Laodicensi signi- ficatam, quæ ad sigillum septimum, tubam item & phialam septimam pertineat, ipsi dicta plumbea, qua per dimidium horæ vel XXX. annos silentium futu- rum in cœlo, meræque paleæ in area Ecclesiæ ja- cebunt. Quum vero Apocalypsis partim scripta sit de iis, quæ sunt, partim de iis, quæ futura sunt post illæ, ac septem Epistolæ secundum tralatitiam plerorumque Interpretum opinionem contineant ea, quæ sunt historice, sigilla vero tubæ & phialæ ea quæ futura prophetice, Crocius contra septem epi- stolas non mere historicas, sed & vere propheticas esse contendit; duplicem, ut apparet, illis sensum assingens, & pro sensu Prophetico decem rationes, sed nullius pretii asserens, quas dilumbavit ejus- dem fidei socius Franc. Gomarus in digress. ad ex- plicationem epist. ad Galat. cap. I. Tom. I. Opp. p. 469. seqq. temerariam Crocii assertionem & fa- crarum literarum corruptelam, imo ineptias & inso- lens, vanumq; paradoxon, merito suo vocans, & va- nitatem rationum tum a nominibus Ecclesiarum, tum a re ipsa ostendens. Ecclesiae certe Ephesinae pe- riodus longe minori jure aurea censeri ex epistola ad Angelum ejus data poterit, quam Smyrnensis & Philadelphensis, si reprehensionem illius, horum vero elogia respiciamus: & motum fuisse Ephesi- na candelabrum, aut Ecclesiam illam, Johanne de- functo, sublatam esse, quod Crocius asserit, historiae repugnat: quam temerarius denique Crocius fue- rit in conditione Ecclesiae FRATERNA praedi- cenda, quasi illa jam tum imminuerit, experientia stultorum magistra docuit. Ecquis enim ignorat, ne quicquam tentatam Φιλαδελφίαν fuisse in collo- quio Cassellano, damnatumque Syncretismum il- lum cum Reformatis Ecclesiasticum unanimi sin- cere Augustanam Confessionem profitentium cal- culo; nullumque successum habuisse fraternitatem & concordiam cum Papistis, sive a Romano-Ca- tholicis in colloquio charitativo Thoruniensi Ann. 1645. sive a Calixtinis deinceps variis Irenicis pro- ductam. Sequutus tamen Crocium est Johannes Coccejus, nec in Apocalypticos epistolis tantum, sed etiam, quod mireris, in Veteris Testamenti libris easdem periodos monstrare conatus est, in Esaia, in Zacharia, in Cantico etiam Canticorum, & ubi non? Ad omnes certe Prophetas ista respicere innuit in praefat. ad Prophet. minores, ultimam, inquiens, omnium Apocalypsin digito intento nobis monstrare, quod de rebus Ecclesiae Christianae praedixerint O- MNES priores. Notavimus viri commentarios mirabiles in Prophetis passim in Bibliis illustra- tis Veteris Testamenti. Jam e Cantico Canticorum, quod etiam huc, sed obtorto pariter collo traxit, talia adducere juvat. Sic autem habent cogitatio- nes ejus de Cantico Canticorum in praefation. Syno- psin & medullam Cantici exhibente p. 4. Status Ecclesiae commemorantis gratiam suavitatis dilecti sui sive praedicantis Evangelium commode in septem periodos distinguitur: Prima periodus est praedica- tionis inter Judaeos & gentes ante ingravescentes per- secutiones, & destructum templum Cant. 1, 5. seqq. & cap. 2. Secunda probationis & consolationis Ec- clesiae in gravissimis diuturnis ac variis persecutio- nibus, usquedum destructis tyrannis per Princi- pes terrenos pax ei concederetur Cant. III, & IV. Tertia Ecclesiae pacatae a persecutionibus & tutae a gentibus, sed incipientis conflictari cum falsa Ec- clesia & cum hominum dominatione cap. 5. & 6. adv. 9. Quarta Ecclesiae verae in medio falsae Eccle- siae emicantis & se ostendentis usque ad divisionem a Cap. 6. v. 9. ad Cap. 7, 11. Quinta Ecclesiae post frustra petitam pacem & expectatam conversionem multitudinis adversariae sive reformationem, rece- dentis ab urbe magna, & in ea recessione exagitatae usque ad pacem ejus C. 7, 11. 12. 13. & C. 8. v. 1. 2. 3. Sexta Ecclesiae in nova angustia constitutae post pa- cem, quam a secessione consecuta erat, C. 8. v. 4. 5. Qui vero angustia illa in argentea aetate & periodo Philadelphensis Ecclesiae locum habitura? aegre sese expedient Novatores illi. Septima periodus Coc- cejo est Ecclesiae adspirantis post multa certamina ad regnum Christi, & praedicationem ejus in toto mundo, Cant. 8. a vers. 8. & 14. At quomodo id conciliabitur cum Crocianis cogitationibus de se- ptima periodo tepida, saturnalitia, & plumbea omniumque periculosissima? Cæterum cogitationes de hisce Coccejanis in Apocalypsin cum Crocianis for- tassis commodius conferemus in Epistol.trum & Prophetiarum dilucidatione.

Balthas. Willium jam audiamus. Hic in com- ment. in Zach. C. 11. p. 484. describit, inquit, pri- mario Apocalypsis historiam novæ Ecclesiæ sub septem Ecclesiis, quibus epistolæ totidem inscriptæ, septem si- gillis, septem tubis, & septem phialis. Atque inde ordinem desumendum esse censuit (mirabili in- terpretamento)quo ultimum Zachariæ vaticinium C. 12. 13. & 14. quod easdem septem novæ Ec- clesiæ Christi Periodos ORDINE describere, co- natur demonstrare. Nec vero tantum inter illa harmoniam fingit, sed eandem etiam in veteri Ec- clesia novo paradoxo quærit Willius : Nam & ve- tus Ecclesia, inquit p. 414. suam Ephesinam, Smyr- nensem, Thyatirensem, Pergamensem, Sardensem, Philadelphinensem & Laodicensem periodum habuit, & quidem obscuriorem in primis bis mille annis, il- lustriorem vero in bis mille sequentibus : Ephesina obscurior cœpit in Paradiso per promulgationem pri- mæ promissionis de semine mulieris caput serpentis contrituro Gen. 3, 15. & duravit ad parricidium Cai- ni usque fortasse per triginta vel plures etiam annos. Smyrnensis Abelis complectitur mactationem, & primam piorum persecutionem Genes. 4, 8. Perga- mensem præconium & concio de nomine Domini E- nochi sub nativitatem cœpta, & postea sub impiorum contradictionibus continuata repræsentat, Gen. 4, 26. Thyatirensem suppressio illa piorum per hominum profanitatem ac gigantum tyrannidem figurabit, de quibus Gen. 6, 1. 2. 3. 4. Sardensis habet Noachi refor- mationem & ipsum diluvium, Gen. 6, 7. Philadel- phiensis complectitur tempus post diluvium, usq; ad tempus turris Babylonicæ, Gen. 11. Laodicensis homi- num passivam profanitatem ad Abrahami usque vo- cationem. Postea primis bis mille annis fere exactis cœpere Ecclesiæ illustriores, Ephesina, quæ vocationem Abrahami, & iterationem promissionis eidem factæ, ejusdemque peregrinationem, ut & Isaaci & Jacobi complectitur : Smyrnensis, quæ angustias continet & servitutem in Ægypto : Pergamensis, quæ peregrina- tionem in deserto comprehendit, & introductionem in terram Canaan : Thyatyrensis, quæ Judicum tempo- re definitur : Sardensis, quæ Regum habet secula lim- pidissima eorumq; finitionem per captivitatem Baby- lonicam : Philadelphiensis, quæ post solutionem capti- vitatis ad tempom Aristobuli extenditur, qui primus Regium titulum resumpsit. Laodicensis, quæ ab illo tempore ad ultimum usque excidium continuatur. Hæc Willius, ineptias suas per Zachariæ posterio- ra capita deducens, sed prima rudimenta sententiæ suæ Ludovico Crocio accepta referens, easdemque ut δὶς καὶ τρὶς τὰ καλὰ dicantur, in præfatione re- petens, imo Esaiæ etiam Prophetæ (in comment. in Zach. XIV. p. 514.) affingens, quasi C. 59, 20. 21. post Sardensem, Philadelphiensem Ecclesiam descri- bere inceperit. Sed istis commentatoribus, Cocce- jum dico & Willium, facile fuit, quodlibet ex quoli- bet effingere, ubi ad suas illas periodos in Veteri Testamento demonstrandas vel Mosen, imprimis in verbis ultimis, vel Salomonem, vel Esaiam, Za- chariam, mirum cur non & Danielem, & Davidem, & Jobum interpretes & commentatores Apoca- lypseos Johanneæ etiam in Epistolis Filii Dei ad Ecclesias Asiæ constituendas animum induxerunt. Hi ergo autores Apocalypsin, quæ secundum Sal- meronem, si explicanda sit, instar quadraturæ circuli non immerito habetur, de qua dici solet, scibilis est, sed nondum scitu, Pannonia opus est immensae diffi- cultatis secundum alios, & imprimis Socin. absque singulari Dei revelatione prorsus incomprehensibilis est, glossis suis magis intricatam & perplexam reddiderunt. Sed προλεγομένων loco sufficiant de variis interpretamentis. Eorum enim senten- tias, qui olim jam Apocalypsin ad Veteris Testa- menti historias referre conati sunt, quum è libro Prophetico historicum sed ænigmaticum efformarint, nihil attinet commemorare.

SECTIO PRIOR GENERALIS, ET εἴσοδος AD PROPHET. AC VELUTI HI- STORICA. COMPLECTENS SIMUL VISIONEM PRIMAM.

## 1:1 Argument
CHAPTER I. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The title having been prefixed, St. John inscribes the book to the seven Churches in Asia, and after a prayer, he excites everyone with the intimation of the coming of the most recent Christ, and introduces Him as attesting to His eternal Deity and omnipotence. Then he describes the preliminary vision made on Patmos, which receives the declaration of the mystery of the seven stars seen in His hand, as also of the seven lampstands, after the voice and the august appearance of the Son of Man walking in the midst of the seven lampstands, at whose sight he was prostrated to the ground, raised by an imposed hand and a gentle address, and commanded to write what he saw, and what are, and what are to be hereafter.

There are three parts: I. The title of the book, and the commendation to v. 3. II. The epistolary inscription, and the greeting to v. 8. III. The description of the first vision, and the explanation to v. 20.

PART I. THE TITLE AND COMMENDATION OF THE BOOK.

Ver. 1.

Ἀποκάλυψις.] נגלה ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι is often found in Daniel, concerning those things the knowledge of which is had by a Divine gift. Hence ἀποκάλυψις, by which name that book of Enoch was called, of which we spoke at Jude. In Isaiah 25:7, בלע הלוט is a periphrasis of ἀποκάλυψις: the Greeks translated it, deliver all these things to the nations. Paul uses the word ἀποκάλυψις in this sense, as 1 Cor. 14:26, 2 Cor. 12:1, 7, Gal. 2:2.

The title first names the book, then the Author, furthermore the principal argument, next the Minister through whom the Apocalypse was delivered to the Writer, further the Writer himself designated by office and name in v. 1 and 2, and finally, the commendation of the book is subjoined to the title. The name of the book is ἀποκάλυψις, a revelation: which here is not common, such as is fitting for all the faithful, Matt. 11:25, ch. 16:17, 1 Cor. 2:10, Eph. 1:17, but singular and proper to Prophets: not that which consists in the interpretation of Scripture already revealed, Deut. 18:22, not that which happened in a dream, Dan. 3:4, but that which happened to one awake, such as Isa. 1:3, Dan. 7:14, and that which happened in an ecstasy, 2 Cor. 12:2, inasmuch as John was in the Spirit, Apoc. 1:10, and also caught up into heaven, he saw some things, ch. 4:1. But it is narrower than is just Cocceius' description of Prophecy: Prophecy is, as it were, a history of future things: For even the history of things not future but present, nay, even the revelation of past things but hidden ones, comes under the name of Prophecies. That description, however, tends to this, that it may be persuaded that John saw here only those things which were to be future what he had to write to the seven Churches concerns the Church of the world in distinct periods of future times.

Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.] That is, done through Jesus Christ. Ἣν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεός.] For just as the power: So also the knowledge of such things in Christ is from GOD the Father, John 7:16, ch. 14:10, below ch. 5:7. Thus Isaiah concerning his sons as heralds of future things אשר נתי לי יהוה ch. 8:18. Δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις ἀυτοῦ.] for εἰς τὸ δεῖξαι, that Christ himself might make these things manifest to his servants, that is, to the chief of the Christians, according to the promise which is in John 16:50. A similar way of speaking in Luke 1:72, John 6:52, and elsewhere.

The author of the Apocalypse or of this Prophecy is designated as Jesus Christ, because it is a Prophecy not of John, but of Christ himself, that great Prophet of Deut. 18, Luke 7. It was given, however, to Christ according to his human nature, according to which he was anointed with the Spirit of knowledge and wisdom, Isa. 11:1, ch. 61:1, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, Col. 2:3. Cornelius a Lapide says it was given and revealed to the soul of Christ at his incarnation: Others, with their Lombard, l. III. sentent. dist. 13, maintain the same thing, that the soul of Christ was subjectively filled with the knowledge of all things, so that he learned nothing afterwards which he did not know before: See Bellarm. l. IV. de Christi cap. I. But since Cornelius Jansenius admits in Conc. Evang. c. 12. that Christ, according to human wisdom, that is, that which belongs to him as a man, truly progressed, and that this infused knowledge of all things cannot be reconciled with progress in wisdom, or with the ignorance of the last day, which many ancient Fathers, Athanasius, Gregory Nazianzen, Theodoret, Cyril, and the author of the imperfect work on Matthew taught, as the Jesuit Maldonatus acknowledges in ch. 24 of Matthew; it must by no means be admitted that that knowledge of all things resided subjectively in the soul of Christ in the state of humiliation and from the first moment of conception; but that the infinite omniscience, which belongs to him by personal union in the state of κένωσις, is to be attributed to him not by reason of plenary use, but by reason of possession, is taught elsewhere.

Furthermore, this revelation or Prophecy is said to be given to Christ by God the Father, not that he might keep it to himself, but that he might make it manifest to his servants; δεῖξαι is to show. There is no doubt, therefore, that that prophecy, with Christ revealing it, can be understood by his servants in its twofold sense, not indeed through immediate revelation outside of Scripture, which fanatics dream of and expect; but mediate, which is obtained through prayer and diligent meditation on Scripture: For if it were not to be or could not be understood by anyone, God would not have given it to Christ to show it to his servants, but to hide it from them. Nor indeed does the gloss of Cornelius have any place, that this prophecy of Jesus Christ was indeed revealed by God the Father not enigmatically, but openly and clearly, but that he [Christ] was to make it manifest and reveal it not openly, but through enigmas and symbols to his servants, that is, to Christians: because that is repugnant both to the scope of the revelation and to the word δεῖξαι, cf. ch. 22:16, and to the command given to St. John in ch. 22:10, 'do not seal the words of this prophecy, for the time is near'; whence it is clear that God by no means wished the sense of this Prophecy to be hidden: and also to the promise, by which he promises blessedness to those who read, hear, and keep the words of this Prophecy, ch. 1:3, ch. 22:7, which would be in vain if no mortal at all could elicit its meaning; and to the exhortation

Divine ch. 13:18. Here is wisdom, let him who has a mind calculate the number of the beast ch. XVII:9. Here is the sense, let him who has wisdom: Cf. ch. 10, verse 11, ch. 13, v. 9.

Ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει] Other things more quickly: the latest, with one or two places excepted, which are added incidentally, within five hundred years. For this is little in relation to the time the world has stood: Thus Haggai 2:7, we said that 'a little while' is five hundred years, ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι מה די להוא Dan. 2:28.

The primary object of the ἀποκαλύψεως [revelation] are those things which must come to pass. For the principal part of the book is the Prophetic announcement of future things. That these alone are not comprised in the same, v. 19 teaches; because he is commanded to write not only ἃ μέλλει γίνεσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα [the things which shall be hereafter], but also ἅ ἐσι [the things which are]. In vain, therefore, do the Bremensians and others gather from the words ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι [the things which must come to pass] that the epistles described in chapters 2 and 3 also concern prophecies about future events. Cocceius is forced to acknowledge this: Some things, he says, in this prophecy are such as were already existing, some were impending, not to happen in an uninterrupted series until all were fulfilled. At the beginning he said, the things which must come to pass quickly: yet in those things which he saw, there are also contained those which were even then, as v. 19 says. Gomarus explains that δεῖ [must] as a necessity of hypothesis and of consequence in Oper. T. I. p. 748, citing Dionysius the Carthusian on this passage. Those future things do not need to come to pass by absolute necessity, since in themselves they are future contingencies not to be fulfilled without the great sin of the ungodly: But in that way in which it is necessary that offenses come, and it is necessary that heresies come, truly by a conditional necessity of the hypothesis of the consequence, not of the consequent. For since they have been foreseen by God, and preordained by the wisdom of God for the progress of the elect, they cannot but happen according to the respect. Nevertheless, the providence of God does not imprint necessity upon mutable things, nor does it take away the liberty of man. Yet the most fierce patron of absolute decrees deduces these from an immutable counsel and decree. But to refer to those things the sins which are comprised in this book, and the impiety, for example, of the Babylonian harlot, certainly does not lack impiety.

Ἐν τάχει [Shortly] refers to the beginning of future things, not just any future things. But that by that word five hundred years or thereabouts are signified is rashly believed. That 'little while' in Haggai 2:7 is indefinite, and does not definitely denote five hundred years, even if about that many have elapsed since that prophecy. Nor is it indicated in this place how much time those things which the Apocalypse predicts will take to happen, but when they are to begin. And therefore, even if five hundred years were most definitely indicated in Haggai, it would have nothing to do with the present place. But it is also false that the Apocalypse extends only to about 500 years: since it reaches to the very end of the world and the final judgment, to the casting of the enemies of the Church on the last day into the lake of hell, and to the glorious triumph in heaven of those who conquer through faith.

Καὶ ἐσήμανε [And he signified].] A copula for a relative pronoun: Which he signified: The Hebrews would say: והודיע.

Ἀποστείλας διὰ τοῦ Ἀγγέλου αὐτοῦ [Having sent by his Angel].] Now through this one, now through that Angel, whom he had sent. Moreover, the construction is not unlike Matthew 2:16 and ch. 14:10. Learn from this also, when God or Christ is said to have appeared, that it ought to be understood as through an Angel acting in the name of God or Christ, and representing his attributes. See what we have said in the Commentary on the Decalogue, and on Acts 18:9. See below v. 13.

Τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννῃ [To his servant John].] He does not say Apostle: because for those who are enlightened by Divine visions, submission of mind is most fitting. Thus also Isaiah calls himself the servant of God in ch. 49:5, and Daniel in ch. 9:17. Moreover, Prophets are accustomed to state and repeat their name several times, so that those who believe them to be good men may also give credence to their words.

The intermediate and ministerial persons are both the Angel, through whom God sent the Apocalypse, and John, to whom the Angel gave it, so that it might be given by him to the Churches. However, the things revealed through the Angel were not simply and entirely, as some think, but for the greatest part, as is evident even from the first vision, revealed immediately by Christ. But that now this Angel, now that one was sent, does not appear from the Apocalypse: For although many are mentioned in it, yet there is one to whom the δεῖξις and σημασία are attributed, who speaks with John, whom he wished to worship in Chapter 19, 10 and C. 22, 8, whom it is clear showed these things to him from the periphrasis of the same, defining that angelic individual: τοῦ δεικνύοντός μοι ταῦτα: Add v. 6 in the same place. How it is also permitted to conclude from this mission of the Son of God made through an Angel, when God or Christ is said to have appeared, that this ought to be understood as an Angel acting in the name of God or Christ, and representing his attributes, I do not see. The contrary is rather concluded from it: Namely, just as this Angel, through whom the Prophecy was sent as a Minister and legate of the Lord, is distinguished from Christ, by whom he was sent: So in the Old Testament, when an Angel sent by God appeared, he is not to be confused with God, which happens entirely when the names and attributes proper to the one sending or the Lord are attributed to the legate or Minister.

Pareus refers the word ἐσήμανεν to the Son of God, but the name of Christ is placed in the oblique case, whereas in the nominative is the name ὁ Θεὸς. Therefore, it must be referred to that. He explains the word ἐσήμανεν concerning the manifest revelation made to John, nor does he wish it to be restricted to revelation through signs and types. But it is not to be believed that besides that representation through signs the Angel added another revelation not comprised in this book: For if he had perceived it from the Angel, he would undoubtedly have consigned it to writing, just as he consigned the words which he heard, and which he received for the declaration of certain visions. Why then would he have kept silent about the rest, who was also ordered to write what was being revealed to him, with the exception only of the voices of the seven thunders, which when he wished to write, he was forbidden, C. X. vers. 4. Whence it is evident that he wrote, and ought to have written, the rest of what he saw and what he heard.

Latin:

CAPUT I. ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Præmisso titulo librum S. Johannes inscribit se- ptem Ecclesiis in Asia, & post votum excitat quosvis intimatione adventus Christi novis- simi, eamque æternam Deitatem & omnipo- tentiam suam attestantem introducit. Dein- de describit visionem in Pathmo factam præ- liminarem, quæ vocem, & apparitionis Filii hominis in medio septem candelabrorum ambulantis augustam speciem, cujus conspe- ctu in terram prostratus imposita manu, & blanda compellatione erectus, jussusque scribe- re, quæ vidit, & quæ sunt, & quæ futura sunt postea, accipit declarationem mysterii septem stellarum in manu sua visarum, ut & se- ptem candelabrorum.

Partes sunt tres: I. Libri titulus, & commendatio ad v. 3. II. Epistolica inscriptio, & salutatio ad v. 8. III. Visionis primæ descriptio, & explicatio ad v. 20.

PARS I. LIBRI TITULUS ET COMMENDA- TIO.

Vers. 1.

Ἀποκάλυψις.] נגלה ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι sæpe est apud Da- nielem, de iis rebus, quarum cognitio Divino habetur mune- re. Inde ἀποκάλυψις, quo nomine dicebatur liber ille Eno- chi, de quo diximus ad Judam. Apud Esaiam 25, 7. בלע הלוט est circumloquutio ἀποκαλύψεως: Græci verterunt παράδος ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. Utitur voce ἀποκαλύψεως hoc sen- su Paulus, ut 1. Cor. 14, 26. 2. Cor. 12, 1. 7. Gal. 2, 2.

Titulus primo librum nominat, tum Autorem, adhæc argumentum præcipuum, porro Ministrum, per quem ad Scriptorem delata Apocalypsis, ulte- rius ipsummet Scriptorem ab officio & nomine de- signatum v. 1. & 2. deniq; titulo subjuncta est libri commendatio. Nomen libri est ἀποκάλυψις revola- tio: Quæ hic non communis est, qualis omnibus fi- delibus convenit, Matth. 11, 25. c. 16, 17. 1. Cor. 2, 10. Eph. 1, 17. sed singularis Prophetis propria:non quæ versatur in Scripturæ pridem revelatæ interpreta- tione, sed in nova rerum abditarum patefactione, Deut. 18, 22. non quæ in somnio contigit, Dan. 3, 4. sed quæ vigilanti, qualis Esa. I, 3. Dan. 7, 14. & quæ in extasi 2. Cor. 12, 2. siquidem in Spiritu fuerit Jo- hannes Apoc. I, 10. & in cœlum quoq; raptus non- nulla viderit, C. 4, 1. Angustior autem justo est descriptio Prophetiae Cocceji: Prophetia est quasi rerum futurarum historia: Nam & historia rerum non futurarum sed praesentium, imo & praeteritarum rerum sed occultarum revelatio Prophetias nomine venit. Tendit autem eo illa descriptio, ut suadea- tur, Johannem ea, quae futura erant, tantum hic vi- disse, non quae praesentia, & quae Ecclesiis septem scribere debuit, concernere Ecclesiam orbis in di- stinctis temporum futurorum periodis.

Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.] Id est, facta per Jesum Christum. Ἣν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεός.] Sicut enim potestas: Ita & cogni- tio talium in Christo est a DEO Patre, Joh. 7, 16. c. 14, 10. in- fra c. 5, 7. Sic Esaias de filiis suis rerum futurarum praenuntiis אשר נתי לי יהוה cap. 8, 18. Δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις ἀυτοῦ.] pro εἰς τὸ δεῖξαι, ut ipse Christus servis suis, id est, Christianorum praecipuis ista patefaceret ex promisso, quod est Joh. 16, 50. Par loquendi genus Luc. I, 72. Joh. 6, 52. & alibi.

Autor Apocalypseos seu Prophetiae hujus desi- gnatur Jesus Christus, quod Prophetia sit non Jo- hannis, sed ipsius Christi magni illius Propheta Deut. 18. Luc. 7. Data autem est Christo secun- dum humanam naturam, secundum quam unctus est Spiritu scientiae & sapientiae Esa. 11, 1. C. 61, 1. in qua reconditi sunt omnes thesauri sapientiae & cogni- tionis, Col. 2, 3. Cornelius a Lapide datam ait & reve- latam animae Christi in ejus incarnatione: Idem, quod subjective anima Christi rerum omnium sci- entia repleta fuerit, statuunt cum Lombardo suo l. III. sentent. dist. 13. alii sic ut nihil postea didice- rit, quod antea nesciret: Vid. Bellarm. l. IV. de Chri- sti cap. I. At quum fateatur Cornelius Jansenius in Conc. Evang. c. 12. Christum secundum sapientiam humanam, hoc est, eam, quae ei ut homini competit, vere profecisse, neque infusa illa rerum omnium no- titia cum profectu in sapientia, aut ignorantia diei novissimae, quam multos veteres Patres, Athana- sium, Gregorium Nazianzenum, Theodoretum, Cy- rillum, Autorem operis imperfecti in Matthaeum do- cuisse, agnoscit Maldonatus Jesuita in c. 24. Matth. consistere possit; minime admittendum subjective inhaesisse animae Christi illam rerum omnium noti- tiam in statu exaninitionis & a primo conceptionis momento; infinitam vero omniscentiam, quae ipsi per unionem personalem competit in statu κενώ- σεως non ratione plenariae χρήσεως, sed ratione κτήσεως eidem tribuendam esse, alias docetur.

Porro data Christo dicitur haec revelatio vel Prophetia a Deo Patre, non ut sibi servaret, sed ut palam faceret eandem servis suis; δεῖξαι est ostende- re. Non ergo dubium est, quin prophetia illa, re- velante Christo, a servis ejus intelligi, sensu suo ge- mino, possit, non quidem per revelationem im- mediatam extra Scripturam, quam fanatici somni- ant, & expectant; sed mediatam, quae mediante ora- tione, ac sedula Scripturae meditatione obtine- tur: Si enim a nemine intelligi deberet aut posset, non dedisset eam Christo Deus, ut servis suis eam ostenderet, sed ut eam illis occultaret. Nec vero Cornelis glossa locum habet prophetiam hanc Jesu Christi quidem a Deo Patre non aenigmatice, sed palam & aperte revelatam, ast ista, ut eam palam fa- ceret & revelaret non aperte, sed per anigmata & symbola servis suis, id est, Christianis: quia id repu- gnat tum scopo revelationis, tum verbo δεῖξαι, conf. C. 22, 16. tum mandato S. Johanni dato C. 22, 10. ne obsignes sermones prophetiae hujus, tempus enim prope est; unde liquet, Deum minime voluisse sen- sum hujus Prophetiae occultari: tum promisso, quo beatitudinem pollicetur iis, qui legunt, audiunt, & conservant verba Prophetiae hujus, cap. 1, 3. cap. 22, 7. quod frustra esset, si nullus omnino morta- lium sensum ejus eruere posset; tum adhortationi

Divinæ cap. 13, 18. Hic est sapientia, qui mentem ha- bet, computet numerum bestiæ cap. XVII, 9. Hic est sensus, qui habet sapientiam: Conf. cap. 10. vers. 11. cap. 13. v. 9.

Ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει] Alia citius: serissima, uno aut altero loco exceptis, qui obiter adduntur cæteris intra annos supra quingentos. Parum enim hoc ad tempus, quo stetit mundus: Sic Aggæi 2, 7. adhuc modicum esse diximus annos quingentos, ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι מה די להוא Dan. 2, 28.

Objectum præcipuum ἀποκαλύψεως sunt ea, quæ fieri oportet. Nam præcipua pars libri est Prophe- tica futurorum prænuncia. Quod autem ea sola non sint comprehensa in eodem, v. 19. docet; quia scribere jubetur non tantum ἃ μέλλει γίνεσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα, sed etiam ἅ ἐσι quæ sunt. Nequicquam er- go è verbis ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι colligunt Bremenses & alii, epistolas cap. 2. & 3. descriptas etiam Prophetias de rebus futuris concernere. Agnoscere id cogi- tur Coccejus: Quædam, inquit, in hac prophetia sunt, quæ extabant, quædam imminebant, non inter- rupta serie ita eventura, donec omnia implerentur. Initio dixit, quæ oportet fieri cito: attamen in illis quæ vidit, continentur etiam, quæ jam tum erant, ut v. 19. dicit. Illud δεῖ oportet de necessitate ex hypothesi & consequentiæ quidem explicat Goma- rus in Oper. T. I. pag. 748. adducto Dionysio Car- thusiano ad h. l. Ista futura non oportet fieri necessi- tate absoluta, cum in se sint futura contingentia non sine magno impiorum peccato implenda: Sed eo modo, quo necesse est, ut veniant scandala, & oportet hæreses venire, verum necessitate conditionata ex hypothesi consequentia non consequentis. Cum enim à Deo præ- visa sint, & à Dei sapientia ad electorum profectum præordinata, non possunt non evenire secundum respe- ctum. Veruntamen providentia Dei mutabilibus ne- cessitatem non imprimit, nec libertatem hominis tollit. Ab immutabili tamen consilio, & decreto hæc de- ducit absolutorum decretorum Patronus acerri- mus. Sed ad ea referre peccata, quæ in hoc libro comprehenduntur, impietatemque, meretricis v. g. Babylonicæ, impietate certe non caret.

Ἐν τάχει cito initium respicit futurorum, non futura quævis. Illa autem voce annos quingen- tos præter propter significari, temere creditur. Modicum illud Agg. 2, 7. indefinitum est, non vero definite notat quingentos annos, etsi totidem cir- citer elapsi ab illo vaticinio sint. Neque hoc in loco, quanto tempore illa eventura sint, quæ prædi- cit Apocalypsis, sed quando inceptura sint, indica- tur. Ideoque etiamsi maxime quingenti anni apud Haggæum definite indicarentur, nihil id ad præsentem locum faceret. Sed & falsum est, quod tantum ad 500. annos circiter Apocalypsis se ex- tendat: quum ad finem usque mundi & extremum judicium ad projectionem novissimo die hostium Ecclesiæ futuram in lacum infernalem, & ad glo- riosum in cælis triumphum eorum, qui per fidem vincunt, sese porrigat.

Καὶ ἐσήμανε.] Copula pro pronomine relativo: Quæ si- gnificavit: Ebræi dicerent: והודיע.

Ἀποστείλας διὰ τοῦ Ἀγγέλου αὐτοῦ.] Modo per hunc modo per illum Angelum, quem miserat. Est autem constructio non dissimilis Matth. 2, 16. & c. 14, 10. Disce hinc etiam, cum Deus aut Christus dicitur apparuisse, id intelligi debere per Angelum Dei aut Christi nomine agentem, & ipsius at- tributa repræsentantem. Vide quæ diximus in Comment. ad Decalogum, & ad Act. 18, 9. Vide infra v. 13.

Τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννῃ.] Non dicit Apostolo: quia qui Divi- nis visis illustrantur, eos maxime decet animi submissio. Sic & Esaias servum Dei se vocat cap. 49, 5. & Daniel c. 9, 17. No- men autem suum & ponere & repetere aliquoties solent Pro- phetæ, ut qui ipsos viros bonos credunt, etiam dictis eorum adhibeant fidem.

Personae intermediae, & ministeriales sunt tum Angelus, per quem misit Apocalypsin Deus, tum Johannes, cui illam dedit Angelus, ut ab ipso dare- tur Ecclesiis. Revelata autem per Angelum non simpliciter, & omnino, ut quidam putant, sed maxi- ma ex parte, ut vel ex visione prima patet, a Christo immediate patefacta. Angelum autem modo hunc, modo illum missum esse, non apparet ex Apocaly- psi : Quanquam enim plures in illa commemoren- tur, unus tamen est, cui δεῖξις & σημασία tribuitur, qui cum Johanne colloquitur, quem adorare vo- lebat Cap. 19, 10. & C. 22, 8. quem ipsi haec mon- strasse ex περιφράσει ejusdem, Angelicum istud individuum definiente, liquet : τοῦ δεικνύοντός μοι ταῦτα : Adde v. 6. ibidem. Quomodo etiam col- ligere ex hac missione Filii Dei per Angelum facta liceat, cum Deus aut Christus apparuisse dicitur, id intelligi debere per Angelum Dei aut Christi nomine agentem, & ipsius attributa repraesentantem, non vi- deo. Contrarium potius inde concluditur : Ni- mirum, uti Angelus hic, per quem missa est Pro- phetia ceu Minister & legatus Domini distingui- tur a Christo, a quo missus est : Ita in Veteri Te- stamento, cum apparuit Angelus a Deo missus, eundem cum Deo confundendum non esse, quod omnino fit, cum nomina & attributa propria le- gantis vel Domini legato vel Ministro tribuun- tur.

Verbum ἐσήμανεν ad Filium Dei refert Pareus, sed Christi nomen in casu obliquo ponitur, in re- cto autem nomen ὁ Θεὸς. Ad illud ergo referendum est. Verbum ἐσήμανεν explicat de manifesta pate- factione Johanni facta, nec restringi vult ad revela- tionem per signa & typos. Sed praeter illam re- praesentationem per signa addidisse Angelum aliam patefactionem, non comprehensam hoc libro cre- dendum non est : Nam si eam ab Angelo perce- pisset, sine dubio literis eam consignasset, quemad- modum verba, quae audivit, quaeque ad declaratio- nem visorum quorundam accepit, consignavit. Cur ergo caetera tacuisset, qui etiam scribere jus- sus fuit, quae ipsi revelabantur, exceptis solum vocibus septem tonitruum, quae scribere cum vellet, prohibitus fuit, C. X. vers. 4. Unde pa- tet, quod caetera, quae vidit, & quae audivit, scri- pserit, & scribere debuerit.

## 1:2
Vers. 2.

Ὃς ἐμαρτύρησε τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ.] Because the name John (יוחנן) was common to many, he therefore designates himself more closely, and says that he is the one who announced the Word of GOD, that is, the precepts of the Gospel, to many peoples. Μαρτυρεῖν generally governs the Dative. But here the Accusative, because it is put for κηρύσσειν or ἀναγγέλλειν. See John 22, 24 and below chapter 22, 16, 20.

Καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.] The phrase ἐμαρτύρησε μαρτυρίαν is both Hebrew and Greek: Thus 2 Kings XVII, 13. Μαρτυρία αὐτῷ ὅσα διεμαρτύρατο. It is, however, a Metonymy in this place. For by μαρτυρίαν are understood the things themselves, concerning which testimony is borne, those things which Christ did, as the following things show.

Ὅσα εἶδε καὶ ἅτινά εἰσι, καὶ ἃ χρὴ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.] The best manuscripts have nothing more than ὅσα εἶδε. Nor does the Latin read otherwise. The rest crept in here from the clause below 19. He explains what he understands by the testimony of Jesus Christ, namely those things which he himself had seen, the miracles of Christ, his death, his life restored, his ascension into heaven. See the first epistle of St. John, chapter I, 1, 2, 3.

Some understand the hypostatic Word by τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ, which is the exposition of Ribera and Pareus. But to testify of the Word is indeed accustomed to be said of the Word of the Gospel, but it nowhere occurs to testify of the Son of God. Others think that the Gospel written by John is designated. Which we admit: but in an inclusive sense, not an exclusive one. For he testified to the Word of God not only in writing, but also by the proclamation of his living voice. There are those who wish all these writings of St. John the Apostle to be indicated here by distinct words; understanding by the testimony of the Word of God the epistles, by the testimony of Jesus Christ the Gospel, and by the things which he saw, the Apocalypse. Cornelius a Lapide refers all these things to the Apocalypse: which John here calls the Gospel, that is, the best news concerning the impending persecution for the sake of faith in Christ, and through it the martyrdom and happiness and eternal crown, which Christ here promises and shows to his own. It is simpler to take the Word of God generally, because the Apostles testified nothing outside of those things which Moses and the Prophets spoke, Acts 26:22. Then the testimony of the Gospel concerning Jesus, in whom we have the fulfillment of the Prophets, because St. John was chosen as a witness of Jesus, John 15:end, Acts 1:8. And those things which he saw, because he was an αὐτόπτης (eyewitness) witness, John 1:14, 1 John 1:1. Whence it is clear that St. John the Evangelist is designated by this periphrasis. We add, however, Gomarus's explanation: What if we bring forward a middle interpretation, so that the former part may be understood synonymously by a certain exposition in the manner of Scripture, that he excellently professed τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ, that is, the testimony concerning Jesus Christ, in writing and speech, just as a comparison of similar places seems to require, Chap. 1:9. I was in Patmos because of the WORD of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ, and Chap. 6:9. and Chap. 20:4, who were beheaded because of the testimony of Jesus and the word of God. Then, that the other part, and whatsoever he saw, may be referred primarily to the subject matter and visions of this prophecy, as Apoc. 1:11, 19, write what you see: and from there authority is gained for the work from the faithfulness of John, both in confessing Jesus Christ and in bravely bearing the cross and exile for his name: and then in describing this Apocalypse with equal faith: that is to say, that he testifies not to fictions, but to facts and things seen. And to this point seems to pertain the other reading, which Laurentius Valla cites: In our codices, he says, after whatsoever he saw, are missing καὶ ἅτινά εἰσι, κὶ ἃ χρὴ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα, which are and which must happen after these things. Thus in the Complutensian edition, which Plantin followed: And in the fifteenth Manuscript Codex of Robert Stephanus from the Royal Library it is read similarly. And Arethas says further, that in another copy these are added: κὶ ὅσα ἤκουσε κὶ ἅτινα δεῖ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα: which that Greek Author explains, and, as it seems, approves. Which, as a gloss, seems to have been written in the margin of the book from verse 19, which finally crept into the context of certain Codices: thus it does not poorly explain the scope of the passage.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

Ὃς ἐμαρτύρησε τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ.] Quia Johannis יוחנן nomen erat multis commune, ideo propius se designat, & se eum esse dicit, qui Verbum DEI, id est, Evangelii praecepta annuntiavit populis compluribus. Μαρτυρεῖν plerumque Dativum regit. At hic Accusativum, quia po- nitur pro κηρύσσειν sive ἀναγγέλλειν. Vide Joh. 22, 24. & infra cap. 22, 16. 20.

Καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.] Ἐμαρτύρησε μαρτυρίαν locutio & Ebraica & Graeca : Sic 2. Reg. XVII, 13. Μαρ- τυρία αὐτῷ ὅσα διεμαρτύρατο. Est autem hoc loco Μετω- νυμία. Nam per μαρτυρίαν intelliguntur res ipsae, de qui- bus fertur testimonium, ea quae fecit Christus, ut ostendunt sequentia.

Ὅσα εἶδε καὶ ἅτινά εἰσι, καὶ ἃ χρὴ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.] Manuscripti optimi nihil habent amplius, quam ὅσα εἶδε. Nec aliter legit Latinus. Caetera ex commate infra 19. huc irre- psere. Explicat quid intelligat per μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, nempe ea, quae ipse viderat Christi miracula, mortem, vitam redditam, evectionem in coelum. Vide epistolam S. Johan- nis I. cap. I, 1. 2. 3.

Nonnulli per τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ Verbum hypo- staticum intelligunt, quae Ribera & Parei est ex- positio. Sed testificari Verbum de verbo quidem Evangelii dici consuevit, nuspiam autem occurrit testificari Filium Dei. Alii Evangelium a Johanne scriptum designari censent. Quod admittimus: sed sensu inclusivo, non exclusivo. Testificatus e- nim est Verbum Dei non modo scripto, sed etiam vivæ vocis præconio. Sunt qui omnia ista scripta S. Johannis Apostoli verbis distinctis hic indigi- tari velint; Per testificationem Verbi Dei epistolas, per testimonium Jesu Christi Evangelium, per ea, quæ vidit, Apocalypsin intelligentes. Cornelius a Lapide hæc omnia ad Apocalypsin refert: quam hic Johannes vocet Evangelium, id est, optimam nun- cium de instante ob Christi fidem persecutione, & per eam martyrio & felicitate & corona æterna, quam suis hic Christus promittit & ostentat. Simplicius est Verbum Dei generaliter accipere, quia nihil te- stificati sunt Apostoli extra ea, quæ Moses & Prophe- tæ loquuti sunt, Actor. 26, 22. tum Evangelii testimo- nium de Jesu, in quo complementum habemus Prophetarum, quia electus erat S. Johannes testis Jesu, Johan. 15. ult. Actor. 1, 8. & ea, quæ vidit, quia αὐτόπτης testis fuit Joh. 1, 14. 1. Joh. 1, 1. Unde li- quet S. Johannem Evangelistam hac periphrasi de- signari. Addimus tamen Gomari explicationem: Quid si mediam interpretationem afferamus, ut prior pars συνωνύμως per expositionem quandam Scri- pturæ more intelligatur, quod τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ, hoc est, testimonium de Jesu Christo egregie professus sit scripto & sermone, quemadmodum locorum similium collatio videtur requirere Cap. 1, 9. Eram in Pathmo propter λόγον DEI & testimonium Jesu Christi, & Cap. 6, 9. & Cap. 20, 4. qui securi percussi propter te- stimonium Jesu & sermonem Dei. Deinde ut altera pars & quæcunq; vidit ad hujus prophetiæ materiam ac visiones imprimis referatur, ut Apoc. 1, 11. 19. scri- be quod vides: atque inde concilietur operi autoritas ex fidelitate Johannis cum in Jesu Christo confitendo, & ejus nomine crucem atq; exilium fortiter ferendo: tum in Apocalypsi hac pari fide describenda: quod videlicet non ficta, sed facta & visa testificetur. Atq; huc videtur pertinere altera lectio, quam citat Lau- rentius Valla: In nostris, inquit, codicibus desunt post quæcunq; vidit, καὶ ἅτινά εἰσι, κὶ ἃ χρὴ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα, quæ sunt & quæ oportet fieri post hæc. Sic in Complutensi editione, quam sequutus est Plantinus: Et in decimo quinto Roberti Stephani Manuscripto Codice ex Regia Bibliotheca similiter legitur. Et Are- tas amplius ait, in altero exemplari hæc addi κὶ ὅσα ἤκουσε κὶ ἅτινα δεῖ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα: quæ Autor ille Græcus exponit, &, ut videtur, probat. Quod ut glossema videtur ex vers. 19. ad oram libri adscriptum, quod tandem in quorundam Codicum contextum ir- repsit: ita loci scopum non male explicat.

## 1:3
Vers. 3.

Μακάριος ὁ ἀναγινώσκων (Blessed is he who reads).] Thus Dan. 12:12, Μακάριος ὁ ὑπομένων (Blessed is he who endures). To Christians vexed everywhere, the foreshadowed punishments of God against the Jews and Romans could bring great comfort. See below chapter 13:10.

Καὶ οἱ ἀκούοντες τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας (And those who hear the words of the prophecy).] That is, of this prophecy, as the Latin took it. See what we said at Rom. 11:29. He adds this because this book was not going to reach everyone immediately, but those who had obtained it were to recite to others in good faith the things which they had read.

Καὶ τηροῦντες τὰ ἐν ἀυτῇ γεγραμμένα (And keeping the things written in it).] Retaining these writings with a mindful spirit, so that indeed they may be compared with the events, whence Christians are strengthened more and more in the faith. Τηρεῖν here is as συντηρεῖν, Luke 2:19, διατηρεῖν in the same place 51.

Ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς ἐγγύς (For the time is near).] Of some, as concerning the civil wars of the Romans and the destruction of Jerusalem. Frequent among the Prophets is יום קרוב (a near day), as Deut. 32:35, Isa. 13:6, Jer. 48:16, Joel 1:15, Obad. v. 15, Zeph. 1:7, 15. John does not wish to have objected against him what had been objected to Ezekiel, chap. 12:27. Concerning the word καιρὸς, see Acts 1:7.

This recommendation of the book is both from the blessedness of the readers, who read and hear the words of this prophecy, but in such a way that they keep those things which are written in it, not only by guarding them with a faithful memory, but also by expressing them in practice itself, such as by fleeing the Babylonian harlot, by admitting the word of the witnesses of Christ, etc. Solid comfort cannot be had from vengeance against enemies, whom Grotius rashly calls Jews and Romans τῇ ὑποθέσει δυ- λεύων; but from the proclamation of the eternal Gospel, received by faith, and the faithful promises made in this book: then from the imminent fulfillment of the predictions, on account of which the Divine consolatory promises had to be guarded regarding the sad fates of the Church, and regarding the joyful promises, especially indeed concerning heavenly blessedness, as in the conclusions of the epistles, in the midst of the visions, and at the end of the book, exhortations were to be observed here throughout, so that the readers and hearers of the prophecy might be rendered participants in the promises; who are not distinguished by the reason that the book was not immediately to reach them so that it could be read, and that those who were content with hearing it would be the ones to perceive it; but because the word of God was propagated both by the reading of Scripture and by preaching. For the Holy Spirit does not refer to an uncertain report, nor is there a reason why a book destined for the whole Church should not have been communicated. That which Grotius brings forward at C. 17, 1, rests on no foundation, and concerns only chapter 17 and those following. The things that are brought forward concerning the fulfillment of certain things, which he says were imminent at the time of the Johannine vision, but concerning the civil wars of the Romans and the destruction of Jerusalem, are repugnant to historical truth. Those things were not imminent when the ἀποκάλυψις was given to St. John, but had already happened. For it was given to John when he was on Patmos, to which he was relegated only under the reign of Domitian, whereas the destruction happened while Vespasian was reigning. But persecutions and heresies were imminent shortly, which this revelation predicted, as also other public evils, manifested when the former seals were opened.

PART II. The inscription and greeting of the epistle.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

Μακάριος ὁ ἀναγινώσκων.] Sic Dan. 12, 12. Μακάριος ὁ ὁ ὑπομένων. Christianis ubique vexatis magnum solatium af- ferre poterant præsignificatæ Dei ultiones in Judæos & Ro- manos. Vide infra cap. 13, 10.

Καὶ οἱ ἀκούοντες τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας.] Id est, ταύτης προφητείας, quomodo accepit Latinus. Vide quæ diximus Rom. XI, 29. Addit hoc, quia liber hic non statim ad omnes erat perventurus, sed qui eum nacti erant, aliis ea, quæ lege- rant, bona fide erant recitaturi.

Καὶ τηροῦντες τὰ ἐν ἀυτῇ γεγραμμένα.] Memori ani- mo retinentes hæc scripta, ut nempe cum eventibus comparentur, unde magis & magis in fide roborantur Christiani. Τηρεῖν hic quod συντηρεῖν, Luc. II, 19. διατηρεῖν ibidem 51.

Ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς ἐγγύς.] Quorundam ut de bellis civilibus Romanorum de Hierosolymorum excidio. Frequens apud Prophetas יום קרוב ut Deuter. 32, 35. Esa. 13, 6. Jer. 48, 16. Joel. I. vers. 15. Abd. v. 15. Soh. I, 7. 15. Non vult sibi obji- ci Johannes, quod Ezechieli objectum fuerat cap. 12, 27. De voce καιρὸς vide Act. 1, 7.

Commendatio hæc libri est tum à lectorum beati- tudine, qui legunt & audiunt Prophetiæ hujus ver- ba, sed ita, ut servent ea, quæ in ea scripta sunt, non tantum fideli memoria illa custodiendo, sed etiam praxi ipsa illa exprimendo, utpote fugiendo mere- tricem Babylonicam, testium Christi verbum admit- tendo &c. Ex ultione adversus hostes, quos Judæos & Romanos temere vocat Grotius τῇ ὑποθέσει δυ- λεύων, solidum haberi nequit solatium; sed ex æter- ni Evangelii præconio, fide suscepto, & promissis fi- delibus in hoc libro factis: tum ab imminente præ- dictionum complemento, ob quod quoad tristia fata Ecclesiæ custodiendæ erant promissiones Divinæ consolatoriæ, & quoad læta promissa, imprimis ve- ro de cœlesti beatitudine, utpote in clausulis epi- stolarum, in medio visionum & in fine libri, adhor- tationes observandæ erant passim hic traditæ, ut promissorum participes reddantur lectores, & au- ditores prophetiæ; qui non ea ratione distinguun- tur, quod liber ad eos non statim perventurus, ut legi possit, qui auditione ejus contenta percepturi sint; sed quia verbum Dei tum Scripturæ lectione, tum prædicatione propagatum fuit. Non enim ad incertam relationem remittit Spiritus sanctus, neque causa est, cur liber Ecclesiæ toti destinatus com- municandus non fuerit. Quam ad C. 17, 1. affert Grotius, ea nec fundamento nititur, & caput 17. so- lum ac sequentia concernit. Quæ de complemen- to quorundam, quod tempore visionis Johanneæ, ait, imminuisse adferuntur, at de bellis civilibus Romanorum, & de Hierosolymæ excidio, histori- cæ veritati repugnant. Non imminebant illa, cum ἀποκάλυψις daretur S. Johanni, sed facta jam erant. Data enim illa est Johanni cum in Pathmo esset, quo relegatus fuit demum sub Domitiani imperio, quum excidium factum sit imperante Vespasiano. Brevi autem imminebant persecutiones & hære- ses, quas prædixit hæc revelatio, ut & alia mala pu- blica, sigillis prioribus apertis manifestata.

PARS II. Epistolæ inscriptio & salutatio.

## 1:4
Verse 4.

John to the seven churches which are in Asia.] To the principal churches in Asia properly so called, where the kingdom of Gog had been. He writes to them specifically because, while he was able, he had ruled them in person. But under their name he tacitly includes other churches as well, because their states and qualities can be reduced to seven kinds, as it were, of which those Asian ones provide an example.

Now follows the dedication of the book: which was made to the seven churches in Asia, both because epistles were to be written to each of them by Christ's command, and because they had been committed particularly to the governance of John: whence he thought the whole revelation should be inscribed to them by name. Although it is certain that this Apocalypse, like the whole of Scripture, pertains entirely to other churches, it is not done for the reason that the states and qualities of the churches can be reduced to seven kinds, as it were, of which these seven churches provide an example (how that could be done, Grotius did not teach), but because the Holy Scriptures are destined for all churches, even if some were sent and inscribed to particular churches, provinces, or persons. Gomarus subscribes to this opinion: Many maintain that the universality of the churches is understood under the seven churches, but not sufficiently appropriately. For although perfection is sometimes denoted by the number seven: that, however, does not have a place when the names and circumstances of the things numbered are expressed, as happens in this place. For John does not say generally to seven churches, but adds of Asia, namely the lesser, and which ones they are is openly expressed in the following v. 11. Wherefore he inscribed the Apocalypse only to certain specific churches, yet in such a way that by their ministry (from the common scope of Scripture) the communication and use pertains to all. Those who understand all the churches are mainly these: Forbes, Coccejus, Brightmann, Hofmann, Crocius.

Grace to you and peace.] In the same way Paul is accustomed to greet the churches, as 1 Cor. 1:3, 2 Cor. 1:2, Gal. 1:3, Eph. 1:2, and elsewhere.

From Him who is, who was, and who is to come.] He did not wish to decline these articles and participles, so that he might the more show the immutability of God, as Proclus says τῷ ἀεὶ on Timaeus, as we said on Mark 7, 40. But because εἰμὶ does not have a past participle, for that reason, for the signification of the past, he was compelled to use the voice of the Indicative mood. So also below in chapter 4, 8. c. 11, 17. Ἐρχόμενος, however, signifies the same as the Latin futurus, as also below in chapter 4, 9. and John 16, 13. Acts 18, 21. and elsewhere. The Hebrews thus use הבא. So also 1 Thess. 1, 10. ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς ἐρχομένης is the same as ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς, Matt. 3, 7. Luke 3, 7. see also Heb. 10, 37.

And from the seven Spirits, which are before His throne.] In the Manuscript πνευμάτων τῶν ἐνώπιον: Many have thought that the seven Spirits, both here and below in chapter 5, 6. and chapter 8, 2., are Angels, because it is accepted among the Hebrews that there are seven greatest Angels who stand before God, namely, just as seven Princes stood before the King of the Persians, which court, because it was most magnificent, for that reason the Hebrews form the court of God after its likeness. See Tobit chapter 12, 15. Matt. 18, 10. and what we have said in both places. Add Hermas II, 9. Clement, Strom. VI. But he who will weigh everything rightly, and will compare the passage which is below in chapter 5, 6., where likewise the Spirits are called the eyes of GOD, by which eyes we said in Zechariah chapter 4, 10. that the multiform providence of GOD is signified, will be carried rather to this, that he should think that those seven, as it were, members of Divine providence are denoted, which are named below in chapter 5, 12. and chapter 7, 11. And thus it will be ἓν διὰ δυοῖν. For peace is wished from GOD and the seven Spirits, that is, from GOD working through these seven modes. This interpretation is strengthened by the fact that below in chapter 5 the Spirits and Angels are distinguished.

Blasius de Viegas in h. l. Pazmann. l. 13. Hodegi c. 4. Cudssemius in desperat.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

Ἰωάννης ταῖς ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαις ταῖς ἐν Ἀσίᾳ.] Præcipuis Ec- clesiis in Asia proprie sic dicta, ubi fuerat regnum Gog. Ad eas specialiter scribit, quia, dum poterat, eas præsens re- xerat. Sed sub earum nomine tacite comprehendit & alias Ecclesias, quia earum status & qualitates ad septem quasi genera possunt revocari, quorum exemplum præbent illæ A- siaticæ.

Sequitur jam libri dedicatio: Quæ facta est se- ptem Ecclesiis in Asia, tum quod ad singulas earum exarandæ essent è Christi mandato epistolæ, tum quod illæ peculiariter regimini Johannis commis- sæ fuerint: Unde iis universam revelationem no- minatim inscribendam duxit. Quanquam vero ad alias Ecclesias hanc Apocalypsin ut totam Scriptu- ram omnino pertinere certum sit, non tamen id ideo fit, quod Ecclesiarum status & qualitates ad se- ptem quasi genera revocari possint, quarum exem- plum hæ septem Ecclesiæ præbeant (quod quo- modo fieri possit, non docuit Grotius) sed quod Scripturæ Sacræ destinatæ sint omnibus Ecclesiis, etiamsi missæ nonnullæ sint, & inscriptæ peculiari- bus Ecclesiis, provinciis, aut personis. Subscribit huic sententiæ Gomarus: Sub septem Ecclesiis uni- versitatem Ecclesiarum intelligi multi statuunt, sed non satis accommodate. Quamvis enim septenario numero interdum perfectio denotetur: illud tamen non habet locum, cum rerum numeratarum nomina & circumstantiæ exprimuntur, ut hoc in loco accidit. Johannes enim non ait generatim septem Ecclesiis, sed adjungit Asiæ, scilicet minoris, & quænam illæ sint a- perte v. 11. sequenti exprimitur. Quare certis qui- busdam Ecclesiis Apocalypsin solummodo inscripsit, ita tamen, ut earum ministerio (ex communi scopo Scripturae) communicatio & usus pertineat ad omnes. Qui universas Ecclesias intelligunt, hi praecipue sunt: Forbes. Coccejus, Brightmann. Hofmann. Cro- cius.

Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη.] Eodem modo Paulus Ecclesias sa- lutare solet, ut 1. Corinth. 1, 3. 2. Cor. 1, 2. Gal. 1, 3. Eph. 1, 2. & alibi.
