Τάδε λέγει ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος) Is qui cum summæ esset dignitatis, summam ignominiam pertulit: Supra I. 8. Hoc eo pertinet, ne Smyrnæ Episcopus ignominiam defu- giat. In Manuscripto: Ὁ πρωτότοκος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος.

Ὃς ἐγένετο νεκρὸς καὶ ἔζησεν) Hoc eo pertinet, ne idem Episcopus mortis metu ab officio abduceretur, sed certus essset, sicut Christus revixit, sic & se revicturum. Vid. indi- catum jam locum sup. I. 8.

Ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος non sunt nomina status, quasi cum summa dignitas, tum summa ignominia notetur, sed æternitatis, ut ad æternam beatitudi- nem se ab eo, qui primus est, & novissimus, servan- dum cogitaret.

## 2:9
Verse 9.

I know your works) Diligence in performing duty.

Also other works of holiness, for which Polycarp is greatly celebrated, and which he uttered, and from his epistle to the Philippians p. 21: Let us therefore be made imitators of his tolerance, and if we have suffered for his name, let us glorify him: for this is the evidence he set for us concerning himself, and we have believed this. I ask you therefore all to persist in the word of justice and patience, which you have also seen with your own eyes, not only in those most blessed Ignatius and Zosimus and Rufus: but also in others who are of you, and in Paul himself and the other Apostles: trusting that all these did not run in vain, but in faith and justice, and went to the place due to them from the Lord, with whom they also suffered: because they did not love this age, but him who died for them and for us, and was raised by God.

And the tribulation) Perpetual fears. In the Manuscript it is only: I know your tribulation, as in the Latin.

Θλίψις denotes not fear, but affliction: And the afflictions of Christians, both from the Jews and from the Gentiles, are sufficiently evident from 1 Thess. II. 14, 15, Heb. X, and the history of the Acts of the Apostles.

Καὶ τὴν πτωχείαν) That Bishop was in difficulty as to how he might live, because those who were Christians at Smyrna were poor. See a similar case in 1 Cor. I. 20. We have spoken about the word πτωχῶν at Matt. V. 3. Our authors express extreme poverty in this way. Thus ἐπτώχευσε is used of Christ in 2 Cor. VIII. 9. Thus πτωχεία in 2 Cor. VIII. 2, 9.

Ἀλλὰ πλούσιος εἶ) This is to be read as a parenthesis, as if he were saying, although you are rich. Rich, namely, in piety and contentment, 1 Tim. VI. 6, 18, Matt. VI. 20, Jas. II. 5. A similar antithesis is in 2 Cor. VI. 10, VIII. 2, 9. Rupertus paraphrases it thus: What I said about your poverty, I said according to the false estimation of men: for according to the truth of the matter, you are rich: Concerning these spiritual riches, see Luke XII. 21, 1 Cor. I. 5, Eph. I. 5, 2 Cor. VIII. 9, Heb. X. 34, Rev. III. 18. Jerome to Heliodorus: He is abundantly rich who is poor with Christ. Καὶ τὴν βλασφημίαν τῶν λεγόντων Ἰουδαίους εἶναι ἑαυτὲς) Βλασφημίαν means most grievous slanders. Thus βλασφημεῖν in Matt. XXVII. 39, Mark XV. 29, Acts XIII. 45, XVII. 6, and elsewhere. He calls them Jews in name, not in reality, alluding to the origin of the word, just as Paul does in Romans II. 28. How can they be true Jews who do not acknowledge God revealed in Christ? Ἀλλὰ συναγωγὴ τῆ Σατανᾶ) They call themselves the congregation of the Lord, ועד יהוה, Num. XXXI. 16. But in reality they are the synagogue of Satan, because they imitate him, both by slandering the good and by plotting against their lives. For the same reason, Christ said they were of their father the Devil, John VIII. 44.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα) Diligentiam in obeundo munere.

Etiam opera alia sanctitatis, a qua valde celebra- tur Polycarpus, quæque effatus, & ex epistola ejus ad Philippenses p. 21. Imitatores ergo efficiamur to- lerantiæ ejus, & si passi fuerimus pro nomine ejus, glorificemus eum: hoc enim indicium posuit nobis de seipso, & nos hoc credidimus. Rogo igitur vos omnes insistere verbo justitiæ & patientiæ, quam & oculata fide vidistis, non solum in beatissimis illis Ignatio & Zosimo & Rufo: sed & in aliis, qui ex vobis sunt, & in ipso Paulo & cæteris Apostolis: confidentes, quia hi omnes non in vacuo cucurrerunt, sed in fide & justitia, & ad debitum sibi locum a Domino, cui & compassi sunt, abierunt: quia non hoc seculum dilexerunt, sed eum qui pro ipsis & pro nobis mor- tuus est, & a Deo resuscitatus.

Καὶ τὴν θλίψιν) Metus perpetuos. In Manuscripto tan- tum est: Οἶδά σου τὴν θλίψιν, ut in Latino.

Θλίψις non metum, sed afflictionem notat: Et afflictiones Christianorum tum a Judæis, tum a gentilibus, e 1. Thessal. II. 14. 15. Ebr. X. & Actuum Apostolicorum historia satis constant.

Καὶ τὴν πτωχείαν) Ægre habebat ille Episcopus, unde vi- veret, ideo quod Smyrnæ qui effent Christiani, essent pau- peres. Vide simile 1 Cor. I. 20. De voce πτωχῶν diximus ad Matth. V. 3. Autores nostri summam inopiam sic expri- munt. Sic ἐπτώχευσε de Christo 2. Cor. VIII. 9. Sic πτωχεία 2. Cor. VIII. 2. 9.

Ἀλλὰ πλούσιος εἶ) Hoc per παρένθεσιν legendum, quasi dicat, cum tamen dives sis. Dives nempe pietate & ἀυταρ- κείᾳ, 1. Tim. VI. 6. 18. Matth. VI. 20. Jac. II. 5. Simile ἀντί- θετον 2. Cor. VI. 10. VIII. 2. 9. Rupertus ita παραφράζει: Quod dixi pauperta- tem tuam, dixi secundum falsam æstimationem ho- minum: nam secundum rei veritatem dives es: De his divitiis spiritualibus, vid. Luc. XII. 21. 1. Corinth. I. 5. Eph. I. 5. 2. Cor. IIX. 9. Ebr. X. 34. Apoc. III. 18. Hie- ronymus ad Heliod. Affatim dives est, qui cum Chri- sto pauper est. Καὶ τὴν βλασφημίαν τῶν λεγόντων Ἰουδαίους εἶναι ἑαυτὲς) Βλασφημίαν maledicta gravissima. Sic βλασφημεῖν Matth. XXVII. 39. Marc. XV. 29. Act. XIII. 45. XVII. 6. & alibi. Judæos illos dicit nomine, non re, alludens ad originem vocis plane ut Paulus Roman. II. 28. Quomodo vere Judæi sint, qui Deum in Christo patefactum non agnoscunt? Ἀλλὰ συναγωγὴ τῆ Σατανᾶ) Vocant se συναγωγὴν τῆ Κυρίε ועד יהוה Num. XXXI. 16. Sed re ipsa sunt Satanæ synagoga, quia eum imitantur, tum calumniando bonos, tum eorum vitæ insidiando. Pari de causa eos ex Diabolo Patre esse dixit Christus Joh. VIII. 44.

## 2:10
Vers. 10.

Μηδὲν φοβῦ ἃ μέλλεις πάσχειν) Do not fear, even if greater things should threaten. For I am he whom I said I was above, 8. Ἰδὲ · μέλλει βαλεῖν ὁ Διάβολος ἐξ ὑμῶν εἰς φυλακὴν) Foreseen arrows wound less. Therefore you will see that almost all the more serious persecutions were predicted long ago to the Churches. He says, however, that the Devil will do what the pagan magistrates were about to do, with the Devil instigating them, Eph. II. 2. Do not refer this to the times of M. Aurelius, Verus, and Antoninus. For closer times are being looked at, but their history, like many others, has not reached us. Ἐξ ὑμῶν supply τινας, concerning which locution we have spoken at Matt. 23, 34. Ἵνα πειρασθῆτε) That a trial of your constancy may be made more than before. See Jas. I. 2. Καὶ ἕξετε θλίψιν ἡμερῶν δέκα) Not just any θλίψιν, but that one, namely, the imprisonment of many. A manuscript explains this more clearly, where it is καὶ ἔχητε θλίψιν, that is, that you may have distress. And understand ten days literally. Est enim consolatio ex brevitate temporis. For there is consolation in the brevity of time. Days also among the Prophets are days, not years, as some dream. What I say is clear from Daniel, who, when he had predicted that the matter would last two thousand three hundred years, VIII. 14, says that this vision is true, VIII. 26, that is, it is to be understood simply, not figuratively, as the comparison of the passage Dan. 11. 45 teaches. Those who think otherwise bring forward nothing that is to the point. For the word ἑβδομάς is general, and can be taken as much of years as of days and other things: but how it should be taken, the subject matter of each passage ought to teach us. As for the numbers in Num. XIV. 33, the name of days is not given to years, but the delay in the desert places is drawn out for as many years as those spies had wrongly spent days in exploring the land. Apud Ezechielem VI. the Prophet is commanded to lie on his side for forty days, so that he might understand the patience of God, who had endured the very bad customs of the people for forty years. But these Christians of Smyrna were freed from prison after ten days, the magistrates having been taught better things about their life, or other letters having been received from Rome. Ten days is a short time, Num. XI. 19. Yet enough to make a test, Dan. I. 12.

Nonnulli censent sub Domitiano, others think these things happened under Trajan: B. Cluverus inclines to the former opinion: Some explain ten days indefinitely, and indeed some explain it as many days from the comparison of Gen. XXXI. 17, 41, 2 Sam. XIX. 43, Job XIX. 3. Cornelius a Lapide: Ten, that is, all the days of life: for there is no place for joy where the whole life of man is a temptation. Thus Primasius, Beda, and Rupertus. For the denarius in the Decalogue and elsewhere signifies universality, and is taken for all things. Others take it as a few, from Gen. XXIV. 55, Am. V. 3, VI. 9. Most, however, think a definite, certain, and indeed long time is expressed, Beda, Haymo, Lyranus, and Joachim, namely, the ten persecutions from Nero to Diocletian: Ludov. Capellus [thinks it refers] to Licinius, who was removed by Constantine, [meaning] a year, namely 240, from the time of the banishment of John. Ludovicus Crocius, however, resolving ten days into 240 hours, and forming years from the hours: so that ten days make 240 years, which from the year of Christ, in which he thinks this epistle was written, 85, to He counts the year of Christ 325, in which Licinius was removed by Constantine. But this is a mere ἰδία ἐπίλυσις (private interpretation). Others explain the ten days as the ten years (as in Dan. IX. 20) of the reign of Trajan, during which a great persecution arose, and they count them from the year of the martyrdom of Ignatius, from the 109th year of Christ to the beginning of the reign of Hadrian, the year of Christ 119. Coccejus fluctuates: They can, he says, (as is evident from the event) be understood as the persecutions of the same ten Emperors, or the final one of Diocletian, which lasted for ten years. Thus, Christians could raise themselves to the hope of liberation, both through the number of persecutions and persecutors (who perhaps are also signified by the ten horns of the Dragon, ch. XII. v. 3), and especially by the duration of the tenth persecution. But because in these letters a literal style seems more to be approved; it is altogether better with the blessed Cluverus to understand a decade; during which, under Domitian, those cast into prison for denying Christ; but afterwards, when they persisted unmoved, were dismissed. D. Hoë, Ribera, and Corn. a Lap. wish a long time, or several years, to be denoted indefinitely. Truly, consolation is rather insinuated here by the brevity of the time. It is therefore more correctly said that the number of days is put for a short time, as in Am. V. 3, by the authority of B. Gerhard. Which explanation was also that of Andreas, of Vinar, of Kromayer, and from the Reformed, of Pareus and Sibelius. And what prevents us from acquiescing in the literal meaning? In the passage of Amos, a comparison is instituted between a thousand and a hundred, and a hundred and ten men: such as does not appear here. B. Cluverus [takes it] literally as ten days, Lyra, Junius, Piscator, and Hogel as the same number of years from Trajan to Hadrian, from the flight of Mahomet in the year 621. of Christ to his death in 631. Hofmann accepts.

Γίνε πιστὸς ἄχρι θανάτε) Persist until the very end of life. The same warning as in Matt. X. 22, XXIV. 13, Mark XIII. 13.

Indeed, that you may also be prepared to undergo death for the sake of Christ, Heb. XII. 4, Matt. X. 39, ch. XVI. 25, Mark VIII. 35 ff., Luke IX. 24, 25, 26, ch. XVIII. 33.

Καὶ δώσω σοι τὸν σέφανον τῆς ζωῆς) I will give you Royal honor in that eternal life. The same expression in Jas. I. 12, where see the remarks, and Isa. LXII. 3, and Ps. XXI. 4.

The crown of life promised here to the Bishop is to be attributed to all the faithful, Jas. I. 12. It is called the crown of glory, 1 Pet. V. 4, the crown of righteousness, 2 Tim. IV. 4, which can be explained in a formal sense as a vital crown, a glorious crown, a righteous crown, or righteousness shining: because the diadems and crowns which are expected will consist in mere life, mere glory, mere righteousness, and will shine with the same: which will not consist of roses, not of gems, but of the most illustrious gifts and splendors of heavenly glory, life, and eternal righteousness: Or if different meanings of the Genitive please, the crown of life, which will be obtained in the other life, the crown of glory, which will be very illustrious and glorious; or glory of the crown by hypallage, that is, the glory of the heavenly kingdom, or glory crowning, surrounding, adorning, and blessing the elect on all sides: The crown of righteousness, which depends upon the righteousness of the just Judge tempered by mercy, or founded in his own righteousness, not in ours. The crown of the other life is called heavenly blessedness, because it will make us crowned sons and heirs of the heavenly kingdom, and thus Kings, Rev. V. 10. We do not dwell on the commentaries of the Scholastics, who, besides the essential crown and glory common to all the blessed, also assign an accidental one, and that a triple one, which they call an aureola: the first of martyrs: the second of virgins: the third of Doctors, as if written in the stars; but we leave them to their most trivial disputes, which can be read in Thomas at this place and at IV. dist. 49. Cornelius a Lapide acknowledges the crown promised to the Bishop to be called eternal happiness: first because it is given to those struggling and conquering: second because a round crown signifies the perfection and complex of all goods: lacking beginning and end like a circle and a crown: third because it is most precious like a crown adorned with gems. Cf. Ps. XXI. 4. It is called, however, the crown of LIFE, so that it may be signified to the saints, who have laid down their life for Christ, that it is not a lost life, but one changed into a better one, constant, always flourishing with delights, glory, and all goods and joys which life includes. Let us always contemplate this vital, immense, and eternal crown, so that we may fight the good fight, and patiently and constantly persevere in the faith and profession of the name of Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

Μηδὲν φοβῦ ἃ μέλλεις πάσχειν) Non metue, etsi majora ingruant. Sum enim is, quem me esse dixi supra 8. Ἰδὲ · μέλλει βαλεῖν ὁ Διάβολος ἐξ ὑμῶν εἰς φυλακὴν) Prævisa tela minus feriunt. Ideo persecutiones gravio- res videbis ferme omnes olim prædictas Ecclesiis. Di- cit autem Diabolum facturum, quod facturi erant pagani Magistratus, Diabolo instigante, Eph. II. 2. Noli hoc refer- re ad tempora M. Aurelii, Veri, & Antonini. Propiora enim tempora respiciuntur, sed quorum historia, ut multæ aliæ, ad nos non pervenit. Ἐξ ὑμῶν supple τινας, de qua locutio- ne diximus ad Matth. 23, 34. Ἵνα πειρασθῆτε) Ut magis quam antehac periculum fiat constantiæ vestræ. Vide Jac. I. 2. Καὶ ἕξετε θλίψιν ἡμερῶν δέκα) Non quamlibet θλίψιν, sed istam, nempe captivitatis plurimorum. Clarius id explicat Manuscriptus, ubi est, καὶ ἔχητε θλίψιν, id est, ut habeatis angustias. Et decem dies intellige proprie. Est enim consolatio ex brevitate temporis. Dies etiam apud Prophetas dies sunt, non anni, ut quidam somniant. Apertum est, quod dico ex Daniele, qui cum prædixisset rem duraturam annos bis mille trecentos VIII. 14. ait visionem hanc esse veram VIII. 26. id est, simpliciter, non figurate intelligendam, ut docet collatio loci Dan. 11. 45. Nihil afferunt, quod ad rem sit, qui contra sen- tiunt. Nam vox ἑβδομάς generalis est, & tam de annis, quam de diebus rebusque aliis accipi potest: quomodo autem accipienda sit, docere nos debet loci cujusque materia. Numerorum vero XIV. 33. Non annis datur dierum nomen, sed per totidem annos per- trahitur mora in locis desertis, quos dies exploratores isti in exploranda terra male insumpserant. Apud Eze- chielem VI. jubetur Propheta per quadraginta dies incum- bere lateri suo, ut intelligat Dei patientiam, qui per annos tum quadraginta pessimos mores populi pertulisset. Chri- stiani autem isti Smyrnæi post decem dies liberati sunt a carcere, magistratibus meliora de ipsorum vita edoctis, aut aliis acceptis a Roma literis. Decem dies tempus exiguum Num. XI. 19. Satis tamen ad experimentum capiendum Dan. I. 12.

Nonnulli censent sub Domitiano, alii sub Tra- jano hæc accidisse: ad priorem sententiam incli- nat B. Cluverus: Decem dies nonnulli indefinite ex- plicant, & quidem aliqui de diebus pluribus e col- latione Gen. XXXI. 17. 41. 2. Sam. XIX. 43. Job. XIX. 3. Cornelius a Lapide: Decem, id est, omni- bus diebus vitæ: neque enim gaudii locus est, ubi vita qui? hominis tota est tentatio. Ita Primasius, Beda & Ru- pertus. Denarius enim in Decalogo & alibi significat universitatem, capiturque pro omibus. Alii de pau- cis e Gen. XXIV. 55. Am. V. 3. VI. 9. Plerique tamen definite certum tempus exprimi putant & proli- xum quidem, Beda, Haymo, Lyranus, & Joachimus, decem nempe persecutionum a Nerone ad Diocle- tianum: ad Licinium a Constantino sublatum Lu- dov. Capellus annuum nempe 240. inde a relegatione Johannis. Ludovicus Crocius vero decem dies in horas 240. resolvens, & ex horis annos formans: ut decem dies efficiant 240. annos, quos ab anno Christi, quo hanc epistolam exaratam putat 85. ad annum Christi 325. numerat, quo Licinius a Con- stantino sublatus est. Sed haec mere ἰδία ἐπίλυσις est. Dies decem alii de annis decem, (ut Dan. IX. 20.) imperii Trajani, quibus magna extitit persecutio, explicant, eosq; numerant ab anno martyrii Igna- tii, a Christi 109. ad initium imperii Adriani, annum Christi 119. Coccejus fluctuat: Possunt, inquit, (ut ex eventu constat) intelligi persecutiones totidem de- cem Imperatorum, vel postrema Diocletiani, quae du- ravit per decem annos. Ita Christiani potuerunt se erigere ad spem liberationis, tum per numerum per- secutionum, & persecutorum, (qui fortasse & per de- cem cornua Draconis cap. XII. v. 3. significatur) im- primis decimae persecutionis diuturnitate. Sed quia in hisce epistolis magis videtur probandus stylus proprius; omnino praestat cum B. Cluvero decen- nium intelligere; quo sub Domitiano ad abnegan- dum Christum in carcerem conjecti; post autem cum immoti persisterent, dimissi sunt. Tempus longum, vel annos plures indefinite denotari vo- lunt D. Hoë, Ribera, Corn. a Lap. Verum consola- tio potius hic insinuatur a temporis brevitate. Re- ctius ergo dicitur numerum dierum poni pro exi- guo tempore, ut Am. V. 3. B. Gerhardo autore. Quae etiam explicatio fuit Andreae, Vinariens. Kromaje- ri, & e Reformatis Parei, & Sibelii. Et quid obstat, quo minus propriae significationi acquiescamus? In loco Amos comparatio instituta est mille cum centum, & centum cum decem hominibus: qualis hic non comparet. Proprie decem dies B. Cluverus, totidem annos a Trajano ad Hadrianum, Lyra, Junius, Piscator Hogel. a fuga Mahummedis ann. 621. Christi ad mortem ejus 631. Hofmann. acci- piunt.

Γίνε πιστὸς ἄχρι θανάτε) Persta ad finem usque vitae. Idem monitum, quod Matth. X. 22. XXIV. 13. Marc. XIII. 13.

Imo ut paratus etiam sis mortem subire propter Christum Ebr. XII. 4. Matth. X. 39. cap. XVI. 25. Marc. IIX. 35. seqq. Luc. IX. 24. 25. 26. cap. XVIII. 33.

Καὶ δώσω σοι τὸν σέφανον τῆς ζωῆς) Dabo tibi honorem Regium in vita illa aeterna. Eadem locutio Jac. I. 12. ubi dicta vide, & Esa. LXII. 3. & Ps. XXI. 4.

Corona vitae Episcopo hic promissa omnibus fidelibus tribuenda est, Jac. I. 12. Vocatur corona gloriae, 1. Petr. V. 4. corona justitiae, 2. Tim. IV. 4. quae exponi potest sensu formali corona vitalis, corona gloriosa, corona justa, seu justitia coruscans : quia diademata & coronae, quae expectantur, in mera vita, mera gloria, mera justitia consistent, eademq; coruscabunt: quae non ex rosis, non ex gemmis, sed gloriae coelestis, vitae ac justitiae aeternae dotibus & splendoribus illustrissimis constabunt: Vel si di- versae Genitivi placeant significationes, corona vi- tae, quae in altera vita obtinget, corona gloriae, quae valde illustris & gloriosa futura; vel gloria coronae per hypallagen, id est, gloria regni coelestis, aut gloria undique coronans, ambiens, ornans & beans electos: Corona justitiae, quae a justitia justi Judicis tempe- rata misericordia, vel fundata in ejusdem propria non in nostra justitia dependet. Corona alterius vitae dicitur beatitudo coelestis, quia faciet nos co- ronatos filios & haeredes regni coelestis, adeoque Reges, Apoc. V. 10. Scholasticorum commenta, qui praeter coronam & gloriam essentialem com- munem omnibus beatis assignant quoque acci- dentalem, eamque triplicem, quam aureolam vo- cant: primam martyrum: secundam virginum: ter- tiam Doctorum, ceu ἄτεργραφῆς producta non moramur; sed illorum nugacissimis disputatio- bus relinquimus, quae apud Thomam h. l. & ad IV. distinct. 49. legi poterunt. Cornelius a Lapide coro- nam dici aeternam felicitatem agnoscit Episcopo promisam: primo quod detur certantibus & vin- centibus: secundo quia corona rotunda significat perfectionem & complexum omnium bonorum: principio & fine carentem instar circuli & coronæ: tertio quia pretiosissima est instar coronæ gemmis exornatæ. Conf.Ps.XXI.4. Vocatur autem corona VITÆ, ut significetur sanctis, qui pro Christo vi- tam posuerunt, non amissam vitam, sed in melio- rem commutatam, deliciis,gloria,omnibusque bo- nis & gaudiis,quæ includit vita,semper vigentibus, constantem. Quam coronam vitalem,immensam, & æternam semper intueamur, ut bonum certa- men certemus, ac patienter & constanter perseve- remus in fide ac professione nominis Christi.

## 2:11
Vers. 11. He that hath an ear, let him hear) See above 7. What the Spirit saith) See in the same place. To the Churches) Namely to Smyrna and others of the same episcopate. He that overcometh) Who will not suffer himself to be overcome by poverty, nor by prison, nor by the fear of more grievous things. See above 7. He shall not be hurt by the second death) Because those who suffer injury are harmed; therefore the Chaldean נזק in Ezra IV. 13, Dan. VI. 3, and the Greek ἀδικῶ, is taken for to harm by metonymy. You have mention of the second death below XX. 6, 14, in the Chaldean Paraphrast, Deut. 33, 6, Is. 22, 14, where Kimchi explains it as בעולם הבוא מיתת דנפש.

As the first death is that by which the body dies in this life, of which v. 10, Be thou faithful unto death: So the second death, by which soul and body die forever in hell, Apoc. XX. 14, chap. XXI. 8, Matt. X. 28, as Andreas, Bede, and Lyranus rightly explain. That by the second death is understood the apostasy that will spread throughout the whole world is a new invention of Cocceius.

PART III. THE THIRD EPISTLE TO THE ANGEL OF PERGAMUM.

Latin:

Vers. 11. Ὁ ἔχων ὖς, ἀκουσάτω) Vide supra 7. Τί τὸ Πνεῦμα λέγει) Vide ibidem. Ταῖς Ἐκκλησίαις) Nempe Smyrnæ & aliis ejusdem ἐπι- σκοπῆς. Ὁ νικῶν) Qui nec paupertate, nec carcere, nec graviorum metu se vinci patietur. Vide supra 7. Οὐ μὴ ἀδικηθῇ ἐκ τῦ θανάτε τῦ δευτέρυ) Quia qui inju- riam patiuntur, iis nocetur; ideo Chaldaicum נזק Esdræ IV. 13. Dan. VI. 3. & Græcum ἀδικῶ, sumitur pro nocere per μετάληψιν. Mortis secundæ mentionem habes infra XX. 6. 14. apud Chaldæum Paraphrasten, Deut. 33, 6. Es.22, 14. ubi Kimchi exponit בעולם הבוא מיתת דנפש.

Ut mors prima est, qua corpus in hac vita mori- tur, de qua v. 10. Esto fidelis usque ad mortem: Ita mors secunda, qua anima & corpus semper mori- untur in inferno, Apoc.XX.14.cap.XXI.8.Matth.X. 28.ut recte Andreas, Beda,& Lyranus explicant. Per mortem secundam intelligi ἀποσασίαν grassatu- ram in toto mundo, novum ἔυρημα Coccejanů est.

PARS IIL EPISTOLA TERTIA AD ANGELUM PERGAMENSEM.

## 2:12
Vers. 12. And to the Angel of the Church in Pergamum write) This is Pergamum, the Royal City of the Attalids,

Pergamum, a most famous city of Asia, the fatherland of Galen, in which, as Varro testifies, parchments were discovered, thence called pergamenæ: whose Bishop S. Carpus, Aureolus and Lyranus make him to be, while others ingenuously confess with Pererius and Alcazar that they do not know who he was.

These things saith he that hath the sharp two-edged sword) Who makes the most exact dissection of all things, even the most intimate in man, and searches all things. See above 1. 6, and what is said there.

Others say that Christ is described by the sword, so that by that symbol it may be indicated that one must fear not Caesar, but Christ, who can dissect and destroy soul and body with his sword, Matt. X. 28, Luke XII. 46, or so that the Bishop may be warned to use the sword of the word courageously against heretics, by the example of Christ the King: which pleases Joachim the Abbot more, and is approved by us. For the vision in Apoc. I. 16 is to be understood of the sword of the word. It was necessary to resist the followers of Balaam with it: just as the Son of God himself stood with drawn sword against Balaam, Num. XXII. 23. This is the paraphrase of Cocceius: I am he whose word is living and efficacious, dividing the dictate of conscience from the reasonings of concupiscence; opening all things that are in man, and which has swift effects in those who do not obey it. These things are opposed to the word which men speak, learned in human wisdom. Which is like a leaden dagger, nay rather like chaff, Jer. XXIII. 28, 29.

I know thy works) Many good works: In the Manuscript it is: I know where thou dwellest, just as the Latin also reads. And where thou dwellest where the throne of Satan is) Thou dwellest in that city where Satan reigns in the idol of Aesculapius. See Papinius in Coma Earini, and Aristides concerning the well of Aesculapius. Wherefore Aretas rightly says here: He calls Pergamum the throne of Satan, as being more idolatrous than all of Asia. Satan ruled there not only through paganism and idolaters; but also through the heresy of the Nicolaitans: and therefore so that neither the persecutions of the Gentiles let him fear, and let the Bishop of Pergamum, being stirred up, strongly oppose the Nicolaitans. Satan dwelt and reigned there, promulgating his decrees concerning the worship of demons there through Gentile governors, and shedding the blood of those who were opposed to them, and polluting the sacred assembly with the contagion of most foul heresies. Although indeed the proper dwelling-place of Satan is the abyss or hell, Apoc. XX. 1. 2. Petr. II. 4. Jud. v. 5. Yet, before he is thrust down completely into the infernal prison, by Divine permission he seeks and prepares for himself a seat here and there on earth, therefore he is called the Prince of the world, Joh. XII. 16.

And you hold fast my name) That is, although you dwell in the chief seat of pagan superstition, yet you have retained the Christian profession. It is a great thing to show oneself good among the wicked, 2. Petr. II. 7. Phil. II. 25. The name of Christ is the profession of the doctrine handed down by Christ, as Act. XXI. 13. and elsewhere. But to hold fast is to retain, not to let slip, as below II. 25. III. 11.

And you have not denied my faith in the days in which Antipas, my faithful witness, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells) In the Manuscript it is in the days of Antipas my witness, my faithful one, who &c. nor does the Latin read otherwise. There is, however, an elliptical construction together with a transposition, such as, the city which I am establishing is yours, for the city, which city I am establishing, is yours. Thus here the sense is: in the days of Antipas, who Antipas my witness, my faithful one was killed. That which is said here from the late Greek menologies, that Antipas suffered under Domitian, deserves no more credit than that which is said, that he was thrown into a brazen ox, which kind of punishment is unknown to Roman laws, which were also in force at Pergamum. Wherefore it ought to be held as true that this Antipas was killed by the populace stirred up by the priests of Aesculapius: such as the dangers of death Paul often encountered. It was a great thing not to have been terrified by so savage a death. To deny the faith is either by words or deeds to deny that one is a Christian: which is to deny the name below III. 8. Why Satan is said to dwell at Pergamum rather than elsewhere, we have already said.

There is no need for another reading nor for a transposition of words: an ellipsis at least is to be supplied from the preceding: And you hold my name, and you have not denied my faith even in those days, in which Antipas my faithful witness, to wit, did not deny my faith: Who was killed among you, where Satan dwells. For thus he extols the constancy of the Bishop, that not even when that truculent slaughter of Antipas was seen, and the danger of a like punishment was known, did he deny the faith. But why Grotius departs from the opinion of Arethas and other ancients concerning the martyrdom of Antipas, the cause is by no means sufficient; that that punishment was ordinarily unknown: for it is most well known that extraordinary punishments were devised in many ways, to which the martyrs were exposed. The gloss of Cocceius here is again enigmatic and changeable: Arethas or Andreas says that a certain Antipas was killed among the Pergamenes; but it is much to be feared that he made history out of a prophetic enigma. It is certain that the Nicene Synod was held by Constantine in Bithynia, where the consubstantiality with the Father and with the Son was asserted. Antipas is truncated from Antipalatros. This signifies as it were equal to the Father. Nor could a name be made more apt for signifying the assertors of the consubstantiality, whose way it is to call the Son equal to the Father, Joh. V. 18. But that martyr, or all the assertors of this doctrine, were then both slaughtered by sentence, and some vexed and killed by the Arians, whose supporters were Constantius and other Emperors of the East.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Καὶ τῷ Ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Περγάμῳ Ἐκκλησίας γρά- ψον) Hæc est Pergamus, Regia Attalidarum,

Pergamum, urbs clarissima Asiæ, Galeni patria, in qua, Varrone teste, membranæ repertæ,pergame- næ inde dictæ: cujus Episcopum S. Carpum Aureo- lus & Lyranus faciunt, alii se ignorare, quis fuerit, ingenue cum Pererio & Alcazare fatentur.

Τάδε λέγει ὁ ἔχων τὴν ῥομφαίαν τὴν δίσομον τὴν ὀξεῖαν) Qui omnium etiam intimorum in homine exactissimam facit dissectionem & omnia rimatur. Vide supra l. 6. & ibi dicta.

Alii a rhomphæa describi Christum ajunt, ut eo symbolo indicetur, timendum esse non Cæsarem, sed Christum,qui animam & corpus rhomphæa sua dissecare potest & perdere Matth.X.28. Luc. XII. 46. vel ut moneatur Episcopus, ut animose rhom- phæam verbi contra hæreticos adhibeat, Chri- sti Regis exemplo: quod Joachimo Abbati magis placet, nobisque probatur. Nam de verbi rhom- phæa visio Apoc.I.16. intelligenda. Balaami secta- toribus ea resistendum erat: quemadmodum ipse Filius Dei evaginato gladio contra Balaamum ste- tit, Num.XXII.23. Cocceji hæc est paraphrasis: Ego sum is, cujus verbum est vivum & efficax, dividens conscientiæ dictatum a concupiscentiæ ratiociniis; omnia aperiens, quæ in homine sunt, & quod celeres effectus habet in iis, qui ei non obediunt. Opposita hæc verbo, quod homines loquuntur docti humana sapi- entià. Quod est ut plumbeus pugio, imo ut palea, Jer. XXIII.28.29.

Οἶδα τὰ ἔργα συ) Bona opera plurima: In Manuscripto est: Οἶδα πῦ κατοικεῖς, quomodo legit & Latinus. Καὶ πῦ κατοικεῖς ὅπε ὁ θρόνω τῦ Σατανᾶ) Habitas in ea urbe, ubi Satanas regnat in idolo Æsculapii. Vide Papi- nium in Coma Earini, & Aristidem de puteo Æsculapii. Quare recte hic Aretas: Θρόνον δὲ τῦ Σατανᾶ Πέργαμον κα- λεῖ, ὡς κατείδωλον ὖσαν ὑπὲρ τὴν Ἀσίαν πᾶσαν. Dominabatur ibi Satan non solum per Ethnici- sinum & idololatras; sed etiam per Nicolaitarum hæresin: ideoque ut nec gentilium persecutiones metuat, & fortiter Nicolaitis sese opponat, excita- tur Pergami Episcopus. Habitabat ibi & regna- bat Satanas sua de adorandis Daemonibus ibidem per gentiles Praesides promulgans decreta, & illo- rum, qui adversi erant iisdem, sanguinem fundens, ac coetum sacrum teterrimarum haeresium conta- gione polluens. Quanquam vero proprium Sata- nae habitaculum abyssus sit vel infernus, Apoc. XX. 1. 2. Petr. II. 4. Jud. v. 5. Sedem tamen sibi, an- tequam detrudatur penitus in carcerem inferna- lem, permissu Divino passim in terris quaerit ac pa- rat, ideo Princeps mundi dicitur, Joh. XII. 16.

Καὶ κρατεῖς τὸ ὄνομά µε) Id est, quanquam in praeci- pua paganicae superstitionis sede habitas, tamen retinuisti professionem Christianam. Magnum est inter malos bo- num se praestare, 2. Petr. II. 7. Phil. II. 25. Ὄνοµα Christi est professio doctrinae a Christo traditae, ut Act. XXI. 13. & alibi. Κρατεῖν vero retinere, non sinere elabi, ut infra II. 25. III 11.

Καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσω τὴν πίστιν µε ἐν ταῖς ἡµέραις, ἐν αἷς Ἀντί- πας, ὁ µάρτυς µε ὁ πιστὸς, ὃς ἀπεκτάνθη παρ᾽ ὑµῖν, ὅπε ὁ Σα- τανᾶς κατοικεῖ) In Manuscripto est ἐν ταῖς ἡµέραις Ἀντί- πας ὁ µάρτυς µε ὁ πιστός µε, ὃς &c. nec aliter legit Lati- nus. Est autem ἐλλειπτικὴ constructio simul cum trajectio- ne, qualis, urbem quam statuo vestra est, pro urbs, quam urbem statuo, vestra est. Ita hic sensus est : ἐν ταῖς ἡµέραις Ἀντίπα, ὃς Ἀντίπας ὁ µάρτυς µε, ὁ πιστός µε ἀπεκτάνθη. Quod ex seris Graecorum menologiis dicitur hic Antipas passus sub Domitiano, non magis fidem meretur, quam quod dicitur in bovem conjectus aeneum, quale supplicium ignotum est Romanis legibus, quae & Pergami valebant. Quare pro vero haberi debet, Antipam hunc fuisse interfe- ctum a plebe commota per Sacerdotes Aesculapii : qualis mortis pericula saepe adiit Paulus. Multum erat tam saeva morte non fuisse territum. Ἀρνεῖσθαι πίστιν est aut verbis aut factis negare se esse Christianum: quod ἀρνεῖσθαι τὸ ὄνοµα infra III. 8. Cur Satanas potius Pergami, quam alibi ha- bitare dicatur, jam diximus.

Non opus est alia lectione nec verborum traje- ctione: Ellipsis saltim e praecedentibus supplenda: Et tenes nomen meum, & non negasti fidem meam etiam in diebus illis, in quibus Antipas testis fidelis meus scil. non negavit fidem meam: Qui occisus est apud vos, ubi habitat Satanas. Nam ita extollit con- stantiam Episcopi, quod ne quidem visa illa Antipae truculenta caede, cognitoque parilis supplicii peri- culo fidem abneget. Cur autem ab Areta, aliorumq; Veterum de martyrio Antipae sententia Grotius discedat, causa minime sufficiens est; quod suppli- cium illud ordinarie ignotum fuerit: nam excogi- tata esse extraordinaria supplicia multivaria, qui- bus expositi martyres, notissimum est. Glossa Coc- ceji hic iterum aenigmatica est & mutabilis: Are- thas sive Andreas dicit, apud Pergamenos Antipam quendam occisum esse; sed valde verendum, ne is ex aenigmate prophetico fecerit historiam. Certum est, a Constantino habitam Synodum Nicenam in Bi- thynia, ubi assertum fuit τὸ ὁµοούσιον τῷ Πατρὸς καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ. Antipas est truncatum ex Ἀντίπαλτρος. Hoc significat quasi ἰσόπαλτρον vel ἴσον τῷ Πατρὶ, aequalem Patri. Neque potuit nomen aptius fieri ad signifi- candos τῷ ὁµοουσίᾳ assertores, quorum est Filium di- cere ἴσον τῷ Πατρὶ, Joh. V. 18. Is autem martyr, sive omnes hujus doctrinae assertores tum sententia jugu- lati sunt, tum quidam vexati & interfecti ab Aria- nis, quorum fautores Constantius fuerunt & alii Im- peratores Orientis.

## 2:14
Vers. 14. But I have a few things against you) See above 5.

Because you have there those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak) The King of the Midianites Num. XXII. and following. But that which is narrated Num. XXV. to have been done by the counsel of Balaam, has always been established by tradition among the Hebrews, as we have said both at that passage of Moses, and Micah VI. 5. and at 2. Petr. II. 15. and Jude 11. And the same thing can be gathered from another passage Num. XXXI. 14.

To cast a stumbling block before the sons of Israel) That is, to contrive ruin for the Israelites, by making God angry at them. Thus stumbling block is taken in Joshua XXIII. 13. 2. Sam. XVIII. 21.

Ps. LXIX. 27. CVI. 34. Before with the Genitive here is worth only as much as the Dative. Thus before is often among the Hebrews. In the Manuscript it is: who taught Balak the king a stumbling block, that is, he taught the Midianites for the use and at the prayers of Balak the King. To eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit fornication) Not only did those Israelites eat of the things sacrificed, but they had also shown worship to the gods of the Midianites. But Christ had enough here to say that which those Israelites had in common with the Nicolaitans. Vers. 15. So you also have those who hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans) You ought to have used the sword of Christ against them. Just as that Angel having a sword had resisted Balaam, Num. XXII. 22. 23. Why should we take stumbling block in any other than the usual sense and interpret it concerning ruin? But it is evident from this that the worst heresy of the Nicolaitans, by which against the synodical decree Act. XV. 25. they held as indifferent things whoredoms and the commerce of idols, Irenaeus teaching in book I. chapter 27, that it is compared to the impious doctrine of Balaam. But how far and wide it had been disseminated, the prior epistle to the Ephesian, and the subsequent one to the Thyatirene, with this epistle to the Pergamene Angel, testify. The tolerance of impious doctrine is therefore disapproved, even if for the rest the Bishop is tenacious of the true faith, and faithfully performs his duty, and it is so disapproved that the Son of God threatens that the Bishop must even be removed, and another substituted in his place, who will not tolerate such things. But why did he say a few things? Not that this oversight is trivial, but whether because it could easily be corrected, or because the Lord looks upon the infirmities of the saints with a kinder eye, in view of other illustrious deeds, which the histories of the Patriarchs and other Heroes attest: yet so that that warning may not be held in contempt, as if of no great moment, a threat by no means to be neglected has been added. Vers. 16. Ὁμοίως μετανόησον ) That ὁμοίως pertains in the Manuscript to the preceding clause, so that there is a pleonasm in ἕτως and ὁμοίως. Thus ὁμοίως καὶ ὡς, Luke XVII. 28. And because that pleonasm offended some, it came about that in certain codices here ὁμοίως was changed into ὃ μισῶ. That μετανόησον, however, in this place signifies, do not be so remiss hereafter. Use sharp remedies, as in a grave danger. In the Manuscript there is more, μετανόησον οὖν. Rashly, in favor of the Vulgate, which has similarly 'do penance', he marks the authentic text, in which the codices agree sufficiently, ὃ μισῶ: by which the Son of God declares his displeasure and hatred against that tolerance, and therefore exhorts the Bishop to repentance, that he may acknowledge the ἀμάρτημα, and amend it. Εἰ δὲ μὴ ) If you do not do that. Ἔρχομάι σοι ταχὺ ) The same expression, which is above 5. Καὶ πολεμήσω μετ᾽ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ῥομφάιᾳ τῦ στόματός με ) I will raise up prophets in the Church, who may do that which the Bishop neglects, and may strongly oppose the Nicolaitans, and draw the people away from them. Christ is said to do what he does through the Prophets, just as God is said to have fought for the fighting Israelites, Exod. 14, 14. 25. Deut. 1, 30. c. 3, 22. Joshua c. 10, 42. cap. 23, 3. 2 Chron. 20, 15. There is an allusion to ancient history; For both Balaam and the Israelites who followed his counsel perished by the sword. Num. 25, 5. cap. 31, 8. I will fight, namely through another Bishop, not through Prophets, who were not ordinarily raised up then; nor through someone to be excited from the people, while the Bishop is in power, as Lyra and Alcafar thought: Therefore he easily threatens his removal, unless he repents. I will come to YOU quickly, says the Lord. Some refer this to the extreme judgment as if it were imminent: But it is a particular judgment against this Bishop, joined with the fight against the Nicolaitans. He fights, indeed, not only by verbal refutation; but also by capital sentences, as in c. XIX, which the Bishops announce, but do not execute: To which pertains the comparison with the history of Balaam, Num. XXII. Of which Rupertus says: That sword in the hand of the Angel, that vengeance upon the Midianites signifies that judgment of which the Apostle says: God will judge fornicators and adulterers, Heb. XIII.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Ἀλλ᾽ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ ὀλίγα) Vide supra 5.

Ὅτι ἔχεις ἐκεῖ τὺς κρατοῦντας τὴν διδαχὴν βαλαὰµ ὃς ἐδί- δαξε τὸν Βαλὰκ) Regem Madianitarum Num. XXII. & sequentibus. Id vero quod narratur Num. XXV. factum esse ex Balaami consilio, ex traditione semper apud Ebraeos constitit, ut diximus tum ad illum Mosis locum, & Michaeae VI. 5. tum ad 2. Petr. II. 15. & Judae 11. Et colligi idipsum potest ex alio loco Num. XXXI. 14.

Βαλεῖν σκάνδαλον ἐνώπιον τῶν ὑιῶν ἰσραὴλ) Id est perni- ciem struere Israëlitis, Deum ipsis faciendo iratum. Sic σκάνδαλον sumitur Josuae XXIII. 13. 2. Sam. XVIII. 21.

Pf. LXIX. 27. CVI. 34. Ἐνώπιον cum Genitivo hic tan- tum valet, quantum Dativus. Sic לפני sæpe apud Ebræos. In Manuscripto est : ὃς ἐδίδαξε τῷ Βάλακ βασιλεῖ σκάνδαλον, id est,docuit Madianitas in usum & ad preces Balaci Regis. Φαγεῖν εἰδωλόθυτα καὶ πορνεῦσαι ) Non tantum Israëlitæ illi ederant de immolatis, sed & Diis Madianitarum cultum exhibuerant. Verum satis hic habuit Christus id dicere, quod illi Israëlitæ cum Nicolaitis habebant commune. Vers. 15. Οὕτως ἔχεις καὶ σὺ κρατοῦντας τὴν διδαχὴν τῶν Νικολαϊτῶν ) Debueras adversus eos uti gladio Christi. Sicut Angelus ille gladium habens Balaamo restiterat, Num. XXII. 22. 23. Cur σκάνδαλον alio quam usitato sensu accipia- mus & de pernitie interpretemur ? Patet autem hinc pessima Nicolaitarum hæresis, qua contra de- cretum Synodicum Act. XV. 25. pro adiaphoris ha- buere scortationes & idolorum com̃ercia, Irenæo l. I. cap. 27. docente, quod impiæ Balaami doctrinæ comparetur. Quam vero longe lateque dissemi- natam fuisse, cum hac ad Pergamensem Angelum epistola prior ad Ephesinum, & subsequens ad Thyatirensem testantur. Impro batur ergo toleran- tia impiæ doctrinæ, etiamsi de cætero fidei veræ te- nax sit Episcopus,& fideliter suo fungatur munere, atq; ita impro batur, ut etiam submovendum Epi- scopum,aliumque in ejus locum surrogandum ef- se, qui non toleraturus sit talia, minitetur Filius Dei. Sed cur ὀλίγα pauca dixit ? Non quod exigu- um hoc sit παρόραμα, sed sive quia facile corrigi poterat, sive quod infirmitates sanctorum benigni- ori oculo adspiciat Dominus, intuitu aliorum præ- clarorum factorum, quod Patriarchales aliorumq; Heroum historiæ testantur: ne tamen insuper ha- beatur illa commonitio, ceu non magni momenti, comminatio minime posthabenda adjecta est. Vers. 16. Ὁμοίως μετανόησον ) Illud ὁμοίως pertinet in Manuscripto ad præcedens κόμμα, ut sit πλεονασμὸς in ἕτως & ὁμοίως. Sic ὁμοίως καὶ ὡς, Luc. XVII. 28. Et quia πλεονασμὸς iste quosdam offendebat, eo factum est, ut in quibusdam hic codicibus ὁμοίως mutaretur in ὃ μισῶ. Illud autem μετανόησον hoc loco significat, noli posthac tam re- missus esse. Utere acribus remediis, ut in gravi periculo. In Manuscripto amplius est μετανόησον οὖν. Temere in gratiam Vulgatæ, quæ habet simili- ter pœnitentiam age, notat textum authenticum, in quo satis consentienter habent codices, ὃ μισῶ: quo displicentiam & odium adversus illam tole- rantiam declarat Filius Dei, ideoque hortatur Epi- scopum ad pœnitentiam, ut agnoscat ἀμάρτημα, idque emendet. Εἰ δὲ μὴ ) Ni id facis. Ἔρχομάι σοι ταχὺ ) Eadem locutio, quæ supra 5. Καὶ πολεμήσω μετ᾽ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ῥομφάιᾳ τῦ στόματός με ) Prophetas suscitabo in Ecclesia, qui id faciant, quod Epi- scopus negligit, & fortiter se opponant Nicolaitis, & ple- bem ab eis abstrahant. Dicitur Christus facere, quod per Prophetas facit, sicut Deus dicitur pugnasse pugnantibus Israëlitis, Exod. 24, 14. 25. Deut. 1, 36. c. 3, 22. Josuæ c. 10, 42. cap.23, 3. 2. Paral. 20, 15. Allusio est ad historiam veterem; Nam & Balaam & ejus consilium secuti Israëlitæ gladio pe- riere. Num. 25, 5. cap. 31, 8. Pugnabo, scilicet per alium Episcopum, non per Prophetas, qui ordinarie tum non suscitabantur; neque per aliquem e plebe excitandum, dominan- te Episcopo, ut Lyra & Alcafar censuit: Illius ergo amotionem, nisi resipuerit, facile minatur. Veniam TIBI cito, inquit Dominus. Ad judicium extre- mum quasi imminens id nonnulli referunt: Sed est particulare judicium adversus hunc Episcopum, conjunctum cum pugna adversus Nicolaitas. Pu- gnat vero non tantum verbali consutathione; sed et- iam sententiis capitalibus, ut c. XIX. quam indicunt, non exequuntur Episcopi: Quo pertinet collatio cum historia Balaami Num. XXII. Qua de Ruper- tus: Ille gladius in manu Angeli, illa ultio in Ma- dianitas judicium illud significat, de quo Apostolus: Fornicatores & adulteros judicabit Deus, Ebr. XIII.

## 2:17
Vers. 17. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches) What this vision wishes to be said to the Church of Pergamum and its daughters. See above 7. 11.

To him that overcometh) To him who strenuously opposes the Nicolaitans.

I will give him to eat) For victors were accustomed to be received with a banquet, Gen. XIV. 8. In the manuscript it is not 'to eat', but 'I will give him the manna', as the Latin reads.

Of the hidden manna) That is, the intelligible. See what we have said concerning similar locutions at Matt. XXVI. 29, Luke XXII. 16. Thus 'he that is in secret' Rom. II. 29, 'the hidden man', 1 Pet. III. 4. Moreover, the intelligible manna is a more exact knowledge not only of the precepts of God, but also of his dispensations. See what is said at John VI. 33. That thing has in itself a great sweetness, which is shadowed forth by the sweetness of manna.

And I will give him a white stone) To those who had won in the sacred contests of the Greeks, 'eiselastika' were given, that is, certain grain allowances or revenues. Vitruvius in the preface to book IX, Pliny in his epistle to Trajan 119 and the following, and Justin to Zenas teach us this. Concerning that matter, when they departed from the contest, they received a token with an inscription of the quantity of that which they were about to receive. And this is what Arethas wishes to say here. And the Holy Spirit is here compared to the token, and he who has it is certain of perpetual abundance.

He renders the clearly splendid promise too thin, by fetching in profane rites. The knowledge of the precepts of God and his dispensations is not promised; for sufficient knowledge of those can be had from the law: but the knowledge of these neither contributes to the present state of grace, and is very insufficient for exhausting the blessedness of the vision of God. Something more is designated by the eating of the hidden manna. The 'intelligible' was expressed by Christ himself, John VI, who taught that he is the true manna. He wishes, therefore, to feed and refresh us with the enjoyment of himself: just as he testified in John XVII. 3 that eternal life is situated in that knowledge. We do indeed enjoy Christ even here in the kingdom of grace, John VI. 52, in the word and sacraments, as Ticonius, Bede, Rupert, and Aretas explain concerning the manna of the Eucharist in the present passage: and Cornelius a Lapide concerning the spiritual consolations of the Word: But nevertheless we shall enjoy the same primarily in the kingdom of glory; here by faith, there by sight, 2 Cor. V. 7. Haymo in this place: The manna which is here promised to the faithful is indeed received now by faith, but at some time they will receive it in truth by sight, and what now remains hidden will then be manifest to them. Therefore, he who shall have overcome his own desires and the temptations of demons, I will give him the hidden manna, that is, after the labors of this life are finished, the blessed contemplation and vision of myself, so that now he can truly say with the Psalmist: I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear. Manna is accustomed to be established as a type 1. Of the Gospel, which is hidden before the wise of the world, Matt. XI. 25; by it souls are fed in the desert of this world. 2. Of Christ himself, John VI. 32. 3. Of the joy and comfort with which the elect will be satisfied in eternal life. I will make him a partaker of the heavenly goods which are stored up for the saints in heaven, just as a gomer of manna was stored up in the tabernacle, Exod. XVI. 32, Heb. IX. 4, as it is in Gerhard. But here joy and comfort, or rather the cause of the same, the enjoyment of the heavenly and blessed Christ, is designated. With which beatific vision of Christ we shall be eternally satisfied in the other life, 1 John III. 2. If, however, any allusion is made by the 'white stone', we are not to be referred to the tokens for grain allowances, but to judicial absolution; since judges, when acquitting the accused, were accustomed to cast a white pebble into the urn in testimony of innocence. And therefore the eternal enjoyment of blessedness, and absolution from the condemnation of the law and the punishment of eternal death, is promised to those who through faith overcome the seductions of vices and impious dogmas, and the temptations of persecutors and heretics, and persevere in the faith unto the end. Such faithful confessors Christ will confess again on the day of judgment, and will adorn them with a good testimony, which the version of the blessed Luther has expressed here. The interpretations of the white stone concerning Christ as a carbuncle (Haymo), and of Jerome in epistle 143 to Pammachius concerning the body made white in baptism, of the glory of the resurrection (Sulfuro), of the most perfect degree (Bede, Rupert, and Hugo), of the highest imitation of Christ (Alcazar), and of charity (Ansbert) are foreign.

And in the stone a new name written) The name of the Son of God, in the Evangelical sense. The new appellation of the name is taken from Isaiah LXII. 2, LXV. 15, as it is in the Greek,

Ὃ οὐδεὶς ἔγνω, εἰ μὴ ὁ λαμβάνων) No one knows the value of this name, except he who experiences it, Gal. IV. 6. Joh. I. 12. See how much this token differs from those εἰσελαστικοῖς. In those, anyone can read what they are worth. How much this one is worth, only he who has it knows.

That name is said to be inscribed on a white stone, because by Divine judgment he who receives it is designated a Son of God and heir of the heavenly kingdom. It is called a new name in opposition to oldness; because the latter is from carnal generation, the former from spiritual regeneration. We are born children of wrath Eph. II. 3. But we are reborn children of God, Joh. III. 5. 1. Petr. I. 3. Nor is it a wonder that one does not understand the power and dignity of this name, unless he who receives it; because not even those who receive it understand it fully, 1. Joh. III. 12. Some wish to refer to the custom where the names of those to be elected to a magistracy were inscribed on a white pebble and thrown into an urn, and hidden in it until they were manifested in the election. But it is not so much the election that is said to be unknown, as the power of the new name. The new name, says the Caesarean, is entirely unknown to this present life. For neither has the eye seen, nor the mind comprehended those future goods, just as neither that new name, which the saints will possess by inheritance. According to Pererius, three most desirable goods are denoted here: by the Manna, the sweetness of ineffable happiness: by the stone, the hope and price of the same: by the name, the brightness of fame and glory.

PART IV. FOURTH EPISTLE TO THE ANGEL OF THYATIRA.

Latin:

Vers. 17. Ὁ ἔχων ὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ Πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς Ἐκ- κλησίαις) Quid visum hoc dici velit Pergamenæ Ecclesiæ & ejus filiabus. Vide supra 7. 11.

Τῷ νικῶντι) Strenue se opponenti Nicolaitis.

Δώσω αὐτῷ φαγεῖν) Nam solebant victores epulo excipi, Gen. XIV. 8. In Manuscripto non est φαγεῖν, sed δώσω αὐτῷ τὸ μάννα, quomodo legit Latinus.

Ἀπὸ τῶ μάννα τῶ κεκρυμμένε) Id est, τῶ νοητῶ. Vide quæ de similibus locutionibus diximus ad Matth. XXV!. 29. Luc. XXII. 16. Sic ὁ ἐν κρυπτῷ Rom. II. 29. ὁ κρυπτὸς ἄν- θρωπΘ, 1. Petr. III. 4. Est autem μάννα τὸ νοητὸν cogni- tio exactior non tantum præceptorum DEI, sed & dispensa- tionum ejus. Vide quæ dicta ad Joh. VI. 33. Ea res magnam in se habet dulcedinem, quæ per mannæ dulcedinem adum- brata est.

Καὶ δώσω αὐτῷ ψῆφον λευκὴν) Iis qui in sacris Græcorum certaminibus vicerant, dabantur εἰσελαστικὰ, id est frumen- tationes aut reditus quidam. Docent id nos Vitruvius præ- fatione libri IX. Plinius epistola ad Trajanum 119. & se- quente, Justinus ad Zenam. De ea re cum a certamine abi- bant, accipiebant tesseram cum inscriptione quantitatis ejus, quod accepturi erant. Et hoc est, quod dicere hic vult Arethas. Et tesseræ hic comparatur Spiritus sanctus, quem qui habet, certus est perpetuæ opimitatis.

Nimis tenue reddit promissum luculenter splen- didum, accersitis prophanis ritibus. Non præce- ptorum Dei & dispensationum ejus cognitio pro- mittitur; nam illorum notitia ex lege haberi potest sufficiens: harum vero cognitio neque ad præsen- tem gratiæ statum facit, & ad exhauriendam visio- nis Dei beatitudinem valde insufficiens est. Am- plius quid designatur per esum absconditi Mannæ. Τὸ νοητὸν expressum est ab ipso Christo, Joh. VI. qui se esse verum manna docuit. Sui ergo fruitione nos pascere ac reficere vult: Quemadmodum te- status est Joh. XVII. 3. in ea cognitione æternam vi- tam sitam esse. Fruimur Christo quidem etiam hic in regno gratiæ, Joh. VI. 52. in verbo & sacramentis, uti de Eucharistiæ Manna in præsenti loco expli- cant Ticonius, Beda, Rupertus, Aretas: & de con- solationibus spiritualibus Verbi Cornelius a Lapi- de: Sed imprimis tamen eadem fruemur in regno gloriæ; hic per fidem, illic per speciem, 2. Cor. V. 7. Haymo in h. l. Manna quod hic promittitur fideli- bus, nunc quidem accipitur per fidem, aliquando au- tem in veritate per speciem accipient, & quod nunc manet absconditum, tunc erit illis manifestum. Qui itaque vicerit proprias cupiditates & Dæmonum tentamenta, dabo illi Manna absconditum, id est, post finitos hujus vitæ labores beatam mei ipsius contem- plationem atque visionem, ut nunc vere cum Psalmi- sta dicere possit: Satiabor cum apparuerit gloria tua. Manna solet constitui typus 1. Evangelii, quod est ab- sconditum coram sapientibus mundi, Matth. XI. 25. per illud in deserto hujus mundi animæ cibantur. 2. Ipsius Christi Joh. VI. 32. 3. Gaudii & solatii, quo ele- cti in vita æterna satiabuntur. Consortem eum fa- ciam cælestium bonorum, quæ sanctis in cælo asservan- tur, sicut gomor ex manna in tabernaculo asservaba- tur, Exod. XVI. 32. Ebr. IX. 4. ut est apud Gerhar- dum. Sed hic gaudium & solatium, vel potius causaej usdem, fruitio Christi cœlestis & beata de- signatur. Qua beatifica Christi visione æternum satiabimur in altera vita, 1. Joh. III. 2. Si qua vero allusio fiat per ψῆφον λευκὴν, non ad frumentatio- num tesseras remittendi sumus, sed ad absolutio- nem judiciariam; siquidem judices accusatum ab- solventes candidum lapillum urnæ injicere con- sueverint in testimonium innocentiæ. Et beati- tudinis ergo æterna fruitio, & a condemnatione le- gis & mortis æternæ pœna absolutio promissa est illis, qui per fidem vincunt seductiones vitiorum & dogmatum impiorum, ac tentationes persecuto- rum & hæreticorum, & in fide perseverant usque ad finem. Tales confessores fideles confitebitur iterum Christus in die judicii, ornabitque bono testimonio, quod hic expressit B. Lutheri versio. Alieni ores sunt interpretationes albi calculi de Christo carbunculo Haymon. & Hieronymi ep. 143. ad Pam. de corpore in baptismo candidato, gloria resurrectionis sulfuro, Beda, Ruperti & Hugonis de gradu perfectissimo, altissima Christi imitatione Alcazaris, de charitate Ansberti.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ψῆφον ὄνομα καινὸν γεγραμμένον) Nomen Filii Dei, in sensu Evangelico. Nominis nova appellatio desum- pta est ex Esaia LXII. 2. LXV. 15. ut est in Græco,

Ὃ οὐδεὶς ἔγνω, εἰ μὴ ὁ λαμβάνων) Id nomen quanti sit nemo scit, nisi qui id experitur, Gal. IV. 6. Joh. I. 12. Vide quan- tum differat hæc tessera ab illis εἰσελαστικοῖς. In illis quivis legit quid valeant. Hæc quantum valeat, novit is demum, qui eam habet.

Nomen illud inscriptum albo calculo dicitur, quod judicio Divino Filius Dei & hæres regni cœ- lestis, qui illum accipit, designatur. Dicitur autem novum nomen in oppositione ad vetustatem; quia hæc e generatione carnali est, illud e regeneratione spirituali. Nascimur filii iræ Eph. II. 3. Renascimur autem filii Dei, Joh. III. 5. 1. Petr. I. 3. Non mirum autem non intelligere vim & dignitatem istius no- minis, nisi qui id accipit; quia ne quidem illi, qui accipiunt, plene eam intelligunt, 1. Joh. III. 12. Non- nulli respici volunt morem, qui eligendorum in Magistratum nomina candido lapillo inscripta ur- næ injecta, inque ea abscondita fuerint, donec in electione manifestarentur. Sed non tam electio incognita dicitur, quam vis novi nominis. Novum nomen, inquit Cæsariensis, præsenti huic vitæ pror- sus incognitum. Neque enim oculus vidit, aut mens comprehendit bona ista ventura, ut nec nomen illud novum, quod sancti hæreditate possidebunt. Secun- dum Pererium tria hic denotantur optatissima bo- na: Per Manna ineffabilis felicitatis dulcedo: per calculum ejusdem spes & pretium: per nomen famæ & gloriæ claritas.

PARS IV. EPISTOLA QUARTA AD ANGE- LUM THYATIRENSEM.

## 2:18
Vers. 18. Καὶ τῷ Ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Θυατείροις Ἐκκλησίας γράψον) It was not Carpus here, but someone older than him. But as to what those who contradicted the Apocalypse brought forward as an argument, that there was no Church of Thyatira when John wrote these things, I answer to that, that there was a Church, but from the Jews, not from the Gentiles, as at Thessalonica before Paul's arrival. Moreover, Thyatira is a city attributed sometimes to Mysia, sometimes to Lydia.

A citizen of this city was Lydia the seller of purple, Act. XVI. 14. who was without doubt a Gentile, and later led others of her own people to the faith. And why should we restrict this Church to the Jews? What had the Jews to do with things sacrificed to idols at that time? It is certain that he was not a bishop. Irenaeus lived much later than John; whether it was Carpus, which seemed so to some, even to Cornelius a Lapide, is not clear. But it is not likely that someone older than him is designated. For Chronology does not support that.

Τάδε λέγει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ἔχων τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ ὡς φλόγα πυρὸς) That is, who is most clear-sighted. Above I. 14. Αὐτοῦ is missing in the Manuscript, as in the Latin.

Καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὅμοιοι χαλκολιβάνῳ) Whose actions are all both pure and splendid.

The eyes like a flame of fire denote omniscience searching even the hearts and reins from verse 23; but the feet like chalcolibanus designate judgment following visitation. Where he is and walks, there he burns up everything contrary. Conf. c. I. 15. cap. X. 1. Dan. X. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 18. Καὶ τῷ Ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Θυατείροις Ἐκκλησίας γράψον) Non fuit hic Carpus, sed aliquis eo vetustior. Quod autem ii qui Apocalypsi contradicebant, in argumen- tum afferebant, non fuisse, cum Johannes hæc scriberet, Ec- clesiam Thyatiræ, ad id respondeo, fuisse Ecclesiam, sed ex Judæis, non ex gentibus, ut Thessalonicæ ante Pauli adven- tum. Est autem Thyatira urbs modo Mysiæ, modo Lydiæ attributa.

Urbis hujus civis fuit purpuraria Lydia, Act. XVI. 14. quæ sine dubio gentilis, aliosque suæ gen- tis ad fidem deinde perduxit. Et cur ad Judæos hanc restringamus Ecclesiam? Quid Judæis cum idolothytis illo tempore? Episcopum illum cer- tum est non fuisse. Irenæus multo posterior Jo- hanne vixit, an Carpus fuerit, quod nonnullis vi- sum, etiam Cornelio a Lapide, non liquet. An- tiquiorem autem quempiam illo designari non est verisimile. Non enim id fert Chronologia.

Τάδε λέγει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ἔχων τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ ὡς φλόγα πυρὸς) Id est, qui est perspicacissimus. Supra I. 14. Αὐτοῦ deest in Manuscripto, ut in Latino.

Καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὅμοιοι χαλκολιβάνῳ) Cujus actiones omnes sunt & puræ & splendidæ.

Oculi instar flammæ ignis omniscientiam corda & renes etiam scrutantem denotant e vers. 23. pedes vero instar chalcolibani judicium visitationem con- sequens designant. Ubi est & ambulat, ibi exurit omne contrarium. Conf. c. I. 15. cap. X. 1. Dan. X. 6.

## 2:19
Vers. 19. Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα) Praiseworthy deeds.

And love, and faith) An excellent pair, Gal. 5, 6. Eph. 6, 23. 1. Thess. 3, 6. 1. Tim. 1, 14. c 6, 11. 2. Tim. 1, 13. cap. 2, 22.

And service) Benefits toward the poor. Thus that word is taken 2. Cor. IX. 11, 12, 13.

And your patience) Constancy in bearing adversities.

And your last works, more than the first) Great

the praise of the Bishop, not only not to grow weary under long labor and evils, but to progress daily for the better.

The Vulgate omitted faith. But Grotius rightly adheres to the source. He designates charity, which reveals itself more, and extends equally to God and neighbor, in the first place: then διακονίαν (ministry), through which is noted not the care of the poor, as that pertains to charity, but the function of the Holy Ministry, of which charity ought to be the moderator, which Christ hints at in John XXI. 15. See Acts I. 17, 25, ch. X. 24, ch. XXI. 19, Rom. XI. v. 13, 2 Cor. III. 6. After faith, which is the mother of charity, Gal. V. 6. Others understand faith in the ministry from Luke XII. But that is included under διακονία (ministry). For this praised faith was at the same time praised in 1 Cor. IV. 2. Finally, τὴν ὑπομονὴν (patience), constancy in faith or patience.

To these commended things he adds, for the greater praise of the Bishop, progress in all these, namely the increase of charity, diligence in the Ministry, faith, and patience; whereas, on the contrary, he had reproved the Ephesian because he had abandoned his first charity.

Latin:

Vers. 19. Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα) Facta laudabilia.

Καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην, καὶ τὴν πίστιν) Egregiam bigam, Gal. 5, 6. Eph. 6, 23. 1. Thess. 3, 6. 1. Tim. 1, 14. c 6, 11. 2. Tim. 1, 13. cap. 2, 22.

Καὶ τὴν διακονίαν) Benefacta in pauperes. Ita vox ista su- mitur 2. Cor. IX. 11, 12, 13.

Καὶ τὴν ὑπομονήν σου) In adversis ferendis constantiam.

Καὶ τὰ ἔργα σου τὰ ἔσχατα, πλείονα τῶν πρώτων) Magna

laus Episcopi, non modo non fatiscere sub longo labore ac malis, sed indies proficere in melius.

Vulgata omisit fidem. Sed recte fonti adhæret Grotius. Charitatem, quæ se magis prodit, & ad Deum pariter & proximum extendit, primo loco designat: tum διακονίαν, per quam non cura pau- perum, utpote quæ ad charitatem pertinet, sed fun- ctio S. Ministerii notatur, cujus moderatrix chari- tas esse debet, quod innuit Christus Joh. XXI. 15. Vi- de Act. I. 17. 25. cap. X. 24. t. XXI. 19. Rom. XI. v. 13. 2. Cor. III. 6. Post fidem, quæ charitatis mater est, Gal. V. 6. Fidem in ministerio alii intelligunt e Luc. XII. Sed ea comprehensa sub διακονίᾳ. Hac enim laudata fides simul laudata fuit 1. Cor. IV. 2. Deniq; τὴν ὑπομονὴν constantiam in fide vel patientiam.

Quibus commendatis adjicit ad majorem Episco- pi laudem profectum in istis omnibus, nempe in- crementum charitatis, diligentiæ in Ministerio, fi- dei ac patientiæ; quum contra Ephesinum repre- henderit, quod primam charitatem deseruerit.

## 2:20
Verse 20. Ἀλλ’ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ (But I have against you) as above IV. 14.

Ὅτι ἀφεῖς τὴν γυναῖκά σου τὴν Ἰεζαβὲλ (That you allow your wife Jezebel) Thus also the Manuscript, and so read all the ancients, who think this woman was the Bishop's wife, called Jezebel, for the reason that she was a teacher of evil things, and the wife of the first man in the Church; just as that first Jezebel was the wife of King Ahab 1 Kings XVI. 31. But it is written here through carelessness ἀφεῖς for ἀφῇς, and ὅτι is causal, as Matt. XXVI. 54, 1 Cor. XI. 17, 23, 2 Cor. I. 14, and elsewhere. For the sense is, I want you to dismiss that wife. For that is what ἀφιέναι (to dismiss) means, as can be seen in 1 Cor. VII. 11, 12, 13. But truly ἀφεῖς in the Indicative is not said in Greek.

Ἡ λέγουσα ἑαυτὴν προφῆτιν (Who calls herself a prophetess) Just as in those times there were certain women truly instructed with the gift of prophecy, Acts XXI. 9, so there were those who falsely arrogated that to themselves, such as later in those places Priscilla, Maximilla, Quintilla. In the Manuscript, ἡ λέγουσα ἑαυτὴν, so that it is nominative instead of oblique. Which is very familiar to John.

Καὶ διδάσκει καὶ πλανᾷ τὸς ἐμὸς δέλες (And teaches and leads astray my servants) That is, ἡ διδάσκουσα πλανᾷ (she who teaches leads astray). She teaches, indeed, as if by a prophetic Spirit: for otherwise women were not permitted to teach. See what was said in 1 Cor. XIV. 35.

Πορνεῦσαι καὶ φαγεῖν εἰδωλόθυτα (To commit fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols) Both are against the Apostolic decree, Acts XV. 29, where see what is said.

That she was called Jezebel by analogy to the ancient one is certain: and therefore not an entire assembly or Jewish synagogue, as Alcazar wishes, whom this very Cornelius reproves, as snatching everything toward his own goal, which he has preconceived: but a certain woman or the wife of the Bishop himself, which view is also held by Bede, Rupert, Primasius, Haymo, and Anselm, Albert and Thomas, or some other woman boasting of prophetic visions, who because she was very powerful and wealthy, providing hospitality to the Nicolaitans, gained many followers, on account of revelations especially sold and miracles perhaps added by magic. Although indeed Ambrose, Pererius, Viegas, and Alcazar understand spiritual fornication, that is to say heresy or idolatry, nevertheless Cornelius acknowledges that Ribera and others more simply take it as fornication properly so called. Whoredom is distinguished from the eating of things sacrificed to idols, which brings about communion with idols, and thus spiritual whoredom. However, there is no need for an emendation of the Greek codices; since the more approved ones, which R. Stephanus and Curcellaeus followed, read ὅτι ἐᾷς.

Latin:

Vers. 20. Ἀλλ’ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ) ut supra IV. 14.

Ὅτι ἀφεῖς τὴν γυναῖκά σου τὴν Ἰεζαβὲλ) Sic & Manuscri- ptus, & ita legerunt veteres omnes, qui hanc fœminam fuisse putant Episcopi uxorem, dictam Jezabel, ideo quod rerum malarum esset magistra, & in Ecclesia primi viri uxor; sicut prima illa Jezabel Regis uxor fuit Achabi 1. Reg. XVI. 31. Scriptum autem hic per incuriam ἀφεῖς pro ἀφῇς, & ὅτι est σιδικὸν, ut Matth. XXVI. 54. 1. Cor. XI. 17. 23. 2. Cor. I. 14. & alibi. Sensus enim est, volo ut dimittas illam uxorem. Id enim ἀφιέναι ut videre est 1. Cor. VII. 11. 12. 13. At vero ἀφεῖς in Indicativo Græce non dicitur.

Ἡ λέγου ἑαυτὴν προφῆτιν) Sicut illis temporibus erant quædam fœminæ vere instructæ prophetiæ dono, Act. XXI. 9. ita erant quæ falso id sibi arrogarent, quales postea illis in locis Priscilla, Maximilla, Quintilla. In Manuscripto, ἡ λέγουσα ἑαυτὴν, ut rectus sit pro obliquo. Quod Johanni perquam familiare.

Καὶ διδάσκει καὶ πλανᾷ τὸς ἐμὸς δέλες) Id est ἡ διδάσκου- σα πλανᾷ. Docet nimirum quasi prophetico Spiritu: Nam alioqui fœminis docere non permittebatur. Vide quæ dicta 1. Cor. XIV. 35.

Πορνεῦσαι καὶ φαγεῖν εἰδωλόθυτα) Utrumque contra de- cretum Apostolicum, Act. XV. 29. ubi dicta vide.

Jezabelem κατ’ ἀναλογίαν veteris dictam cer- tum: ideoque non cœtus integer vel synagoga Ju- daica, ut vult Alcazar, quem reprobat hic ipse Cornelius, ceu omnia ad scopum suum, quem præ- concepit, rapientem: sed mulier quædam sive uxor ipsius Episcopi, quod visum etiam cum Beda, Ru- perto, Primasio, Haymone, & Anshelmo, Alberto & Thoma, seu alia quæpiam propheticas visiones ja- ctitantes, quæ quia præpotens & opulenta Nicolai- tis præbens hospitia multos adepta sectatores, ob venditatas imprimis revelationes & adjecta forte per magiam miracula. Quanquam vero Ambrosius, Pererius, Viegas & Alcazar fornicationem spiri- tualem intelligant, hæresin puta vel idololatriam, agnoscit tamen Cornelius, simplicius Riberam, & alios proprie fornicationem accipere. Distingui- tur scortatio ab esu idolothytorum, qui communio- nem cum idolis, adeoque scortationem spiritua- lem infert. Non autem opus est emendatione codicum Græcorum; quum probatiores, quos R. Stephani & Curcellæus sequuti, legant ὅτι ἐᾷς.

## 2:21
Vers. 21. Καὶ ἔδωκα αὐτῇ χρόνον, ἵνα μετανοήσῃ) I did not immediately snatch her from this life, as she deserved, even according to the law of Moses, since she added her own unchastity to her evil doctrines, the Bishop perhaps suspecting it, but not fully knowing it. Dio of Prusa says that it is easy to come from fornication to adultery. These things do not stand where they begin.

Καὶ ὀ θέλει μετανοῆσαι ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς) Πορνεία is often taken so generally that it includes μοιχεία, as also in Matt. V. 32, XIX. 9. And it is to be taken so here, as the matter shows, and as the following words in the Manuscript show: Καὶ ἐκ ἠθέλησεν.

Latin:

Vers. 21. Καὶ ἔδωκα αὐτῇ χρόνον, ἵνα μετανοήσῃ) Non sta- tim illam ex hac vita eripui, sicut merebatur, etiam secun- dum Mosis legem, cum ad malas doctrinas etiam suam im- pudicitiam adjungeret, suspicante forte, sed non plene id sciente Episcopo. Facile a scortatione ad adulteria veniri ait Dion Prusæensis. Non stant ista ubi incipiunt.

Καὶ ὀ θέλει μετανοῆσαι ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς) Πορνεία sæ- pe ita generaliter sumitur, ut μοιχείαν comprehendat, ut & Matth. V. 32. XIX. 9. Et ita hic sumendum, tum res ostendit, tum verba sequentia in Manuscripto: Καὶ ἐκ ἠθέ- λησεν.

## 2:22
Vers. 22. ἰδὲ βάλω αὐτὴν εἰς κλίνην) Not into a bed of love, but into a bed in which the sick lie, concerning which see

2. Sam. XIII. 56. 2. Reg. I. 4. 1. Macc. VI. 8. In the Manuscript εἰς φυλακὴν, which crept in by error, from the fact that it is above in 10.

Rupert, Bede, and Richard understand this as a sending into hell; Alcazar as the storms of wars; Ansbert and Primasius as security and impunity in sinning: But it is more simply taken as a bed. That is to say, I will bring it about that she, who now rests in the bed of her pleasures and sins, shall lie down in a bed of sickness. Compare Sir. XXXII. 14, 15. Ps. CVII. 17. Job V. 14. Heb. XIII. 4.

Καὶ τῆς μοιχεύοντας μετ' αὐτῆς εἰς θλίψιν μεγάλην) And I understand this simply. She was committing adultery with many men of her own opinions: to whom God threatens heavy evils. Compare Ezek. XIII. 18 and following, and what we have said there.

Ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσωσιν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῆς) Unless they abstain from adulteries with her.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ἰδὲ βάλω αὐτὴν εἰς κλίνην) Non in lectum amoris, sed in lectum, in quo cubant ægroti, de quo vide

2. Sam. XIII. 56. 2. Reg. I. 4. 1. Macc. VI. 8. In Manuscripto εἰς φυλακὴν, quod irrepsit per errorem, ex eo quod supra est 10.

De missione in infernum Rupertus, Beda, Richardus intelligunt, de bellorum tempestatibus Alcazar, de securitate & impunitate peccandi Ansbertus & Primasius: Sed simplicius accipitur de lecto. q. d. efficiam, ut, quæ modo in voluptatum & peccatorum suorum lecto quiescit, decumbat in lecto ægritudinis. Conf. Sir. XXXII. 14. 15. Psal. CVII. 17. Job. V. 14. Ebr. XIII. 4.

Καὶ τῆς μοιχεύοντας μετ' αὐτῆς εἰς θλίψιν μεγάλην) Et hoc simpliciter intelligo. Mœchabatur illa cum multis suarum sententiarum hominibus: quibus Deus mala gravia minatur. Confer Ezech. XIII. 18. & sequentia, & ibi a nobis dicta.

Ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσωσιν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῆς) Nisi abstineant ab adulteriis cum ea.

## 2:23
Vers. 23. Καὶ τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς ἀποκτενῶ ἐν θανάτῳ) I will kill her adulterous offspring with pestilence, so that it may not reach an inheritance not owed to it. For that is called θάνατος by way of eminence, as in Matt. XXIV. 7.

Καὶ γνώσονται πᾶσαι αἱ Ἐκκλησίαι) Which are in Lydia, Mysia, and neighboring places.

Ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἐρευνῶν νεφροὺς καὶ καρδίας) The same expression in VII. 10. Jer. XI. 20. XVII. 10. XX. 12. By the kidneys are understood desires, as also in Ps. CXXXIX. 13. Jer. XII. 2. Prov. XXIII. 6. By the heart, thoughts, 1 Sam. XVI. 7. 1 Kings VIII. 39. 1 Chron. XXVIII. 9. 2 Chron. VI. 30. 1 John III. 20. Christ means this: How could adulteries, however much hidden, escape me; I who look into both the first desires and the deliberations tending toward them?

And I will give to you each according to your works) This discourse pertains to the Thyatireans, who allowed themselves to be deceived by the false Prophetess. The Bishop is commanded to say these things to them: but to the good, those things which follow.

Children are understood not by generation, but by instruction. For although the offspring of fornicators does not grow up, Wis. III. 16, 17, ch. IV. 3, seqq., which is evident from the example of the children of Jezebel cut off by Jehu, 2 Kings 10: yet here punishment is indicated for those who can perform penance: and therefore those seduced by that Pseudo-Prophetess are regarded, just as the prophets adhering to Jezebel were slaughtered in great number by Divine instinct, 1 Kings XVIII.

Latin:

Vers. 23. Καὶ τὰ τέκνα αὐτῆς ἀποκτενῶ ἐν θανάτῳ) Adulterinam ejus sobolem, ne ad hæreditatem sibi non debitam perveniat, interficiam peste. Nam ea κατ' ἐξοχὴν dicitur θάνατος, ut Matth. XXIV. 7.

Καὶ γνώσονται πᾶσαι αἱ Ἐκκλησίαι) Quæ sunt in Lydia, Mysia, & locis vicinis.

Ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἐρευνῶν νεφροὺς καὶ καρδίας) Eadem locutio VII. 10. Jerem. XI. 20. XVII. 10. XX. 12. Per renes intelliguntur desideria, ut & Psal. CXXXIX. 13. Jerem. XII. 2. Prov. XXIII. 6. Per cor cogitata, 1. Sam. XVI. 7. 1. Reg. VIII. 39. 1. Paral. XXVIII. 9. 2. Paral. VI. 30. 1. Joh. III. 20. Hoc vult Christus: Quomodo adulteria quamvis maxime tecta me laterent; qui & primas cupiditates & deliberationes eo tendentes introspicio?

Καὶ δώσω ὑμῖν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ ἔργα ὑμῶν) Hic sermo pertinet ad Thyatirenses, qui se a falsa Prophetide decipi siverunt. Jubetur Episcopus hæc illis dicere: Bonis vero ea, quæ sequuntur.

Filii intelliguntur non generatione, sed institutione. Quamvis enim & scortatorum genus non adolescat, Sap. III. 16. 17. cap. IV. 3. seqq. quod exemplo liberorum Jesabelis a Jehu excisorum 2. Reg. 10. patet: tamen hic pœna illis indicitur, qui pœnitentiam agere possunt: ideoque respiciuntur seducti ab illa Pseudo-Prophetide, quemadmodum Jesabeli adhærentes Prophetæ magno numero instinctu Divino trucidati 1. Reg. XVIII.

## 2:24
Vers. 24. But to you the rest who are in Thyatira) So also the Manuscript: not and to the rest. And rightly. For Christ designates two kinds of Thyatireans.

As many as do not have this teaching) Of that Pseudo-Prophetess. Here he said to have, which above was to hold, to adhere to the doctrine. This is a verb of the third person, for a verb of the second person, which is frequent among the Hebrews after a relative pronoun.

Who have not known the depths of Satan as they say) That as they say is to be referred to the depths. They themselves called them the depths of knowledge עמקות חכמה, thinking that they perceived what others did not perceive, that it was a matter of indifference to fornicate and to eat things sacrificed to idols. But Christ says they are the depths of Satan, the cunning counsels of Satan, to which are opposed the depths of God, 1 Cor. II. 10, Rom. XI. 33. A similar manner of speaking, where in the speech of another are placed words not congruent to that person but to the thing, you have in Is. XXXI. 10 and XLIV. 19.

Rupertus and Haymo, with Bede and Primasius, understand the height of Satan as pride, from which he wishes sacrifices to be offered to him by the Thyatireans. But depth signifies profundity, which Gagnejus explains as the depth of sins. Cornelius a Lapide explains it as the boasted depth of dogmas. But more correctly the depths of Satan are understood as frauds, with Andreas Caesariensis: namely, those things which underlie heresies and which they have in reserve, as if they were deeper things that the simpler ones do not penetrate. Heretics peddled mere deep mysteries; but the Son of God calls them the depths of Satan. To this pertains that of Irenaeus, book III, ch. 15: Persuasive and plausible is the error that seeks out disguises, but truth is without disguise. Cf. Rom. XVI. 18, 2 Cor. XI. 13, 1 Tim. VI. 20. Andreas rightly has beside the souls, after having so resisted such evil and sagacious impostors through simplicity of character you cannot, inasmuch as you are not taught the depths of Satan, as you say; I do not ask of you a contest of words with them, but the custody of the doctrine which you have received, until I shall have taken you from here.

I will cast upon you no other burden) They boast of their knowledge of many things; I do not demand that from you. To cast a burden upon some, the same as to impose a burden, to demand something as necessary for salvation, Acts 15:28.

Others, including the blessed Gerhard, more correctly: I will not send upon you such tribulations as I have threatened against the Nicolaitans: If only you will observe what I command. Or as the blessed Cluverus has it: That warfare against Jezebel and her Satanic depths, which you have hitherto stoutly sustained, suffices for you, nor have you submitted your neck to her idols, allurements, or forces, having preferred my easy yoke, Matt. 11:29. Therefore I will not impose upon you any other burden of tribulation, temptation, or command. For it is a great burden to contend with scandals and heresies. However, Osiander, the blessed Winckelmann, the blessed Gerhard, and the blessed Gravius explain this concerning the plagues and punishments of Jezebel; Thomas Szeged, Piscator, Napier, Pareus, Sibelius, Ribera, Cornel. a Lap., and others, including our own blessed Chytreus, etc., explain it concerning the yoke of the law, but less appropriately.

Latin:

Vers. 24. Ὑμῖν δὲ λέγω τοῖς λοιποῖς τοῖς ἐν Θυατείροις) Sic & Manuscriptus: non καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς. Et bene. Duo enim Thyatirensium designat genera Christus.

Ὅσοι ἐκ ἔχεσι τὴν διδαχὴν ταύτην) Istius Pseudo-Prophetidos. Hic dixit ἔχειν, quod supra κρατεῖν, adhærere doctrinæ. Est hic verbum tertiæ personæ, pro verbo secundæ personæ, quod frequens apud Hebræos post pronomen relativum.

Οἵτινες ἐκ ἔγνωσαν τὰ βαθέα τῶ Σατανᾶ ὡς λέγουσιν) Illud ὡς λέγουσιν referendum ad τὰ βαθέα. Ipsi vocabant τὰ βαθέα τῆς γνώσεως עמקות חכמה, putantes se perspicere, quod non perspicerent alii, adiaphora esse scortari & vesci immolatitiis. At Christus dicit esse τὰ βαθέα τῶ Σατανᾶ, solertia Satanæ consilia, quibus opponuntur τὰ βάθη Θεῦ 1. Cor. II. 10. Rom. XI. 33. Simile loquendi genus, ubi in sermone alieno ponuntur verba rei non personæ isti congruentia, habes Es. XXXI. 10. & XLIV. 19.

Altitudinem Satanæ de superbia intelligit Rupertus & Haymo cum Beda & Primafio, ex qua sibi velit offerri a Thyatirensibus sacrificia. Sed βάθος profunditatem significat, quam de profunditate peccatorum Gagnejus explicat. Cornelius a Lapide de jactata profunditate dogmatum. At rectius profunda Satanæ fraudes cum Andr. Cæsar. intelliguntur: ea scilicet, quæ subsunt hæresibus quæque illæ in recessu habent, ceu profundiora non penetrant simpliciores.
