For it is now openly established that there is a communion of the Jesuits with the Zwinglians, whose Nestorianism Blessed Luther, Blessed Chemnitius, Blessed Schröder, and Blessed D. Joh. Dietericus have clearly shown: Which has also been demonstrated by us in the Examination of the doctrine of the reformers. And to whom is the agreement made in the previous century between the Witteberg Crypto-Calvinists and the Jesuits obscure, when the latter caused the theses of the former to be reprinted with the recommendation of the Rector, in the XXXIV of which these things are read: Divine idioms can be ascribed to the Human nature neither by word nor in reality. Busaeus: Catholics, he says, disp. on the person of Christ, An. 1583, th. 14, teach that natures, and their properties, were neither in reality nor by word communicated in the person of Christ, nor could they be communicated. Likewise th. 29. That the divine nature could not be really communicated to the humanity of Christ, nor was all the Majesty of the Son of God, which is contained in the complex of divine properties, really communicated to the same Humanity by the benefit of the hypostatic union. If the divine nature of the Son of God is not communicated to the human, it is not united either. For union and communication behave in the same way. If communication is denied, union is denied, if it is a true and real union. If the ἑνώσει κοινωνικῇ (communal union) is denied, there is no place for communion, and vice versa; if the latter is denied, the former is also denied. If the communication of the divine nature is denied, the communication of the divine hypostasis of the Son of God is also denied, which in divine matters are really the same. Concerning which, see expressly in Metaphys. divin. If you please, see the twin passages to those of Busaeus in Gregor. de Valent. in defens. disp. contr. fundam. ubiqu. p. 54. Bellarmin. l. III. de Christo c. 9. Gretser in destruct. Labyr. Hunn. p. 56. Laur. Forer. in Bello Ubiquit. p. 295. Thom. Clagius in the disquisitions of the Ubiquitists published under the name of Didymus Hermonovillanus. Therefore, the blessed Doctor Philippus Nicolai interprets the locusts as the Calvinists in his de regno Christi l. II. c. 5. T. II. opp. p. 180, and following him, the blessed Doctor Henricus Baumannus in the tail of the scorpion of the Calvinist locusts, demonstrated here at my suggestion to Elias Gribenitius in the year 1663; the blessed Doctor Gravius interprets the locusts as the Arians. Furthermore, the Papists agree remarkably well with the locusts in other respects: 1. by reason of their origin; because these are born from smoke, those from the perverse doctrine of heretics, receiving from the Jews holidays, the choice of foods, anointings, consecrations, and fasts; from the Gentiles, idols, pilgrimages to statues, the shaving of the head, sects of monks, Vestal Nuns, and the celibacy of the clergy; from the Tatianists, the prohibition of marriage; and from the Pelagians, the freedom of the will; 2. by reason of their process of disputing, because like locusts, which neither fly straight nor walk on the ground, but rather hop, they are accustomed to hop rather than fly in their most empty speculations, etc.; 3. by reason of the strident noise which they make with their wings, as if they were other birds, to which I refer their voices and books, by which they produce no small clamor; 4. by reason of- of the obscuring of the sun; since they greatly obscure the sun of righteousness, Christ, and his merit. 5. by reason of their wandering about, since they traverse immense tracts, penetrating into India itself. 6. by reason of the scorching of the crop of Scripture and the Gospel, etc.

They are indeed not unlike scorpions, because they are flattering in appearance, but they sting with secretly poisonous bites, so that the blow is not felt immediately, until the poison spreads itself, which God uses to exert his wrath, Sir. XL. reserving however always for himself some seed, 1 Kings XIX. verse 18. Is. I. verse 9. Is. XVI. verse 14.

Latin:

Vers. 3. Καὶ ἐκ τῦ καπνῦ ἐξῆλθον ἀκρίδες εἰς τὴν γῆν )

Kαὶ hic valet nam. Causam reddit, cur luctuosum fue- rit illud dogma, quia inde enata pessima factio Zelota- rum, qui & Hierosolymis & per omnem Judæam alios pacis amantes spoliavit, & plurimis modis vexavit, de quo- rum sceleribus late Josephus. Locustis comparantur ra- ptores, quia omnia post se vacua relinquunt. Utitur hac si- militudine Joseph. belli Judaici IV. 7. Aristoph. Acharnens. Ὅσοι τὸ χἐπμα παριόντων προσέρχεται: Ubi Scholiastes : βόλελαι πολὺ πλῆθος σημαίνουσι, οἷδε δὲ ἀκρίδων οἱ πύργο- πες, recte quod & multitudinem per locustas significari ait. Sic & Judic. VII. 12. Sic & Achmes CCC. Apud Joelem exercitus Phulis, Thiglathphilafaris, Salmanasaris, Sen- nacheribi vocantur erucæ, locustæ, bruchi, attelabi, uti ibi diximus. Hic quoque respicitur ad plagam Ægypti, quan- quam sensu Allegorico, ut supra in grandine. Vide Exod. X. 4. Εἰς τὴν γῆν in Judæam, ut sæpe jam vidimus.

Καὶ ἐδόθη ἀυταῖς ἐξυσία, ὡς ἔχυσιν ἐξυσίαν οἱ σκορπίοι τῆς γῆς)

Ut lento malo civitatem exhaurirent, ut solent scorpii. Plin. II. 25. Prov. XXIII. 31. Vide infra 5, 10. Scorpio damnum & morbum significat. Achmes CCLXXXV. Ἐξυσία hic & infra ad permissum Dei referendum.

Per locustas e fumo falsarum doctrinarum ab abyssi Principe Diabolo enatas intelliguntur A- rianorum pulli, Nestoriani, Semi-Ariani, Aëtia- ni, Eunomiani, Photiniani, Macedoniani, item ac Acaciani. In Africa & Syria majores nascun- tur locustæ, alis firmioribus præditæ, quæ herbis, frugibus & arboribus valde infestæ sunt, easque morsu erodunt, contactu polluunt, quales per ven- tum orientalem in Ægyptum adductæ sunt. Ex. X. Nam sicut locustæ (teste Plinio l. II. c. 29.) autumni tempore ova densa pariunt, quæ hyeme durant sub terra: Subsequenti anno exitu Veris, emittunt partus nigrantes, & sine cruribus pennisq́; reptan- tes. Ita Origenes, Samosatenus & alii, tanquam ova pepererunt malignarum opinionum, mediocri Ecclesiæ tranquillitate, quæ persecutionum tempore perdurantes, cum Vere Ecclesiastico, ut primum pa- cis serenitas effulsit, Arium, Euzojum, Eusebium Nicomediensem, Eudoxium, Aëtium & similes pro- crearunt Theologastros, ingenti numero, parvos quidem initio & velut humi reptantes, sed mox be- nignitate tali confirmatos: Mori matres locusta- rum, cum pepererint, certum esse confirmat Plinius, vermiculo statim circa fauces innascente, qui eas strangulet. Atq́; alias gregatim sublatas vento in maria aut stagna decidere. Sic Ario, Eunomio, Photino, Nestorio & aliis tum corporaliter tum spi- ritualiter lethalis erat hæreseos partus, divina eos consequente vindicta. Et reliquis omnibus hære- ticarum opinionum magistris exitio est sempiterno partus suus, ni resipiscant: sæpissime etiam tota eo- rum agmina synodali aut Cæsarea autoritate Eccle- siis expulsa, penitusq́; extincta sunt. Conf. histo- riam Exod. X. 19. Non nascuntur, nisi in planis & rimosis locis. Nec hæretici oriuntur, nisi facilibus & obviis ad irrependum animis. Lege historiam Presbyteri illius Ariani, qui Constantiæ Licinii vi- duæ persuasit, Arium inique esse damnatum, quique postea ex sororis commendatione Constantino cha- rus æstimatusque & testamenti ejus custos factus Constantium sibi devinxit, atq́; hoc pacto Arium ab exilio revocari, & hæresin ejus plenis velis in Eccle- siam introduci effecit apud Ruffin. l. 1. Hist. cap. 11. So- zomenum lib. 2. cap. 26. Locustæ turmatim vo- lant, agros & hortos infestant, & contaminant: Ita & Ariani turmatim magno agmine in Eccle- siam irrepserunt, hortum & agrum Ecclesiæ infe- starunt, spoliarunt, & perverso doctrinæ suæ ve- neno conspurcarunt. Adde quod Ariani neque in altum volent cum S. Johanne Aquila cœlesti ad divinæ naturæ Christi contemplationem; nec in- ferne gradiantur secundum Verbi Dei Canonem, sed per superbiam elati rursum in terram deci- dant, jam sublimia quædam de Christo dicant; mox iterum humiliter de ipso sentiant. Locustæ immensos permeant tractus, diraque messibus contegunt nube, omnia morsu erodentes, unde ab acuta erosione ἀκρίδες videntur dictæ. Et hæ- retici illi præsertim Ariani totius Orientis, & Occidentis Ecclesias ceu fertilissimos agros va- starunt, quas consumere, inque suam sententiam trahere nequibant, contactu tamen adurentes. Locustæ, (inquit Haymo) rectos gressus non habent, nec volant ut aves. Sic hæretici fidem rectam non habent ad volandum in cælum, nec rectos gressus ad bene operandum. Idem porro ita ait: Locustæ dant saltus & virentia corrodunt: Sic hæretici per ja- ctantiam elevantur, & animas fide virentes occi- dunt, quando possunt. B. Gerhardus intelligit varios ordines monasteriales, qui post introductam doctri- nam de purgatorio & alios errores Anti-Christia- nos, in Ecclesia invaluerunt. Illi enim abduxerunt homines ad merita operum, ad opera supererogationis, ad proprias satisfactiones, ad Papales indulgentias &c. Item Quæstores indulgentiarii, qui literas indulgentiarum per orbem universum circumtulerunt ac vendiderunt. Item Sophistæ, qui Papales errores & doctrinam Anti-Christianam scriptis propugnarunt, illi comparantur locustis, quia magna copia sese longe lateque propagarunt, & omnia ad se rapuerunt ac absumpserunt. Quos comprehendere hoc locustarum exercitu omnino, judicio nostro, licet, quia jam Nestorianismo accedunt Papistæ, Jesuitæ, & alii, negantes idiomatum communicationem, ob quam negatam Nestorius ab Ephesino concilio damnatus est. Constat enim jam palam communio Jesuitarum cum Zwinglianis, quorum Nestorianismum B. Lutherus, B. Chemnitius, B. Schröderus, B. D. Joh. Dietericus luculenter ostenderunt: Qui a nobis etiam in Examine doctrinæ reformatorum demonstratus est. Et cuinam obscura est Crypto-Calvinianorum Wittebergensium ac Jesuitarum superiori seculo facta contesseratio, quando illorum theses hi recudi fecerunt cum Rectoris commendatione, in quarum XXXIV. hæc leguntur: Idiomata divina neq; voce neq; reipsa Humanæ naturæ adscribi possunt. Busæus: Catholici, inquit disp. de pers. Christi An. 1583. th. 14. docent, nec re, nec voce in persona Christi aut communicatas esse, aut communicari potuisse naturas, earumq́; proprietates, Item th. 29. Naturam divinam humanitati Christi realiter communicari non potuisse, nec Majestatem omnem Filii Dei, quæ proprietatum divinarum complexu continetur, beneficio unionis hypostaticæ eidem Humanitati realiter communicatam esse. Si non communicata est natura divina Filii Dei humanæ, nec unita est. Pariter enim se habent unio & communicatio. Negata communicatione negatur unio, si vera & realis unio sit. Negata ἑνώσει κοινωνικῇ, locum non habet κοινωνία, & vice versa, negata hac negatur & illa. Negata communicatione divinæ naturæ, negatur & communicatio divinæ hypostaseos Filii Dei, quæ in divinis realiter idem sunt. De quo in Metaphys. divin. ex professo. Busæanis gemina, si placet, vide sis apud Gregor. de Valent. in defens. disp. contr. fundam. ubiqu. p. 54. Bellarmin. l. III. de Christo c. 9. Gretser in destruct. Labyr. Hunn. p. 56. Laur. Forer. in Bello Ubiquit. p. 295. Thom. Clagium in disquisitionibus Ubiquitist. sub nomine Didymi Hermonovillani editis. Locustas ergo de Calvinianis nobiscum interpretatur B. D. Philippus Nicolai in de regno Christi l. II. c. 5. T. II. opp. p. 180. & ex eo B. D. Henricus Baumannus in cauda scorpionis locustarum Calvinianarum Eliæ Gribenizio hic meo monitu demonstrata Anno 1663. de Arianis locustas interpretatur B. D. Gravius. Cæterum conveniunt & in aliis Papicolæ egregie cum locustis 1. ratione ortus; quia hæ ex fumo, illi ex perversa hæreticorum doctrina nascuntur, a Judæis ferias, & delectum ciborum, unctiones, consecrationes, jejunia, a gentilibus idola, peregrinationes ad statuas, capitis rasuras, monachorum sectas, Vestales Nonnas, cælibatum Clericorum, a Tatianis conjugii prohibitionem, a Pelagianis libertatem arbitrii accipientes; 2. ratione disputandi processus, quia locustarum instar, quæ nec recte volitant, nec inferne gradiuntur, sed saltitant potius, inanissimas speculationes saltitare potius quam volitare solent &c. 3. ratione stridoris, quem pennis efficiunt, ac si aliæ essent alites, quo refero voces & libros ipsorum, quibus clamorem non exiguum edunt. 4. ratione- obumbrationis solis; siquidem solem justitiae Chri- stum ejusque meritum valde obfuscent. 5. ratione circumvagatiouis, siquidem immensos tractus permeent, in ipsam Indiam penetrantes. 6. ra- tione adustionis segetis Scripturae & Evangelii &c.

Scorpionibus vero non absimiles sunt, quia blan- di in speciem, sed occulte venenatis morsibus pungunt, ut ictus non sentiatur statim, donec se diffundat venenum, quibus Deus ad exerendam suam iram utitur, Sir. XL. reservans tamen sibi semper aliquod semen, 1. Reg. XIX. vers. 18. Es. I. vers. 9. Es. XVI. vers. 14.

## 9:4
Ver. 4. And it was said to them) God or his Angels are said to say this, whose causes they arrange.

That they should not harm the grass of the earth, nor any green thing, nor any tree) God did not permit them to burn either the crops, or the city and the temple, which the Romans did afterwards, with God coming by certain steps to the final things. The Hebrews also call crops grass, as is clear in Matt. XIII. 26. See also what was said by us in Matt. VI. 30. Concerning the word tree, it was spoken of above VII. 1. 3. It is the nature of locusts to devastate both crops and trees. Exod. X. 5. This is alluded to here.

Except only those men who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads) Here except is not an exceptive, but an adversative particle, in the way that if not is taken in Gal. II. 16. So also below XXI. 27. He gives the reason why such great power was given to those worst men over the inhabitants of Jerusalem: namely because those who remained in the city, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, had not professed the faith of Christ, which is signified here allegorically by the mark on the forehead. Only and of them is absent in the Manuscript.

Latin:

Vers. 4. Καὶ ἐῤῥέθη ἀυταῖς) Dicitur Deus aut Angeli ejus id dicere, quorum causas disponunt.

Ἵνα μὴ ἀδικήσωσι τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς, ὀδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν, ὀδὲ πᾶν δένδρον) Non permisit illis Deus, ut aut sata, aut urbem templumque incenderent, quod postea fecerunt Romani, Deo per gradus quosdam ad ultima veniente. Ebraei etiam fruges χόρτον vocant, ut apertum est Matth. XIII. 26. Vide & quae dicta a nobis Matth. VI. 30. De vo- ce δένδρον dictum supra VII. 1. 3. Locustarum est vastare & sata & arbores. Exod. X. 5. Eo hic alluditur.

Εἰ μὴ τὲς ἀνθρώπες μόνες, ὅσοι ἐκ ἔχεσι τὴν σφραγῖδα τῦ Θεῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων ἀυτῶν) Hic εἰ μὴ non est exce- ptiva, sed adversativa particula, quomodo ἐὰν μὴ sumitur Gal. II. 16. Sic & infra XXI. 27. Causam reddit cur pessi- mis illis hominibus tanta potestas data sit in Hierosolymi- tas: nimirum quia illi, qui in urbe restabant, Hierosolymitae, fidem Christi non erant professi, quod hic per signum in fronte ἀλληγορικῶς significatur. μόνες & ἀυτῶν abest in Manuscripto.

## 9:5
Ver. 5. And it was given to them, that they should not kill them) That they should not kill the people by a single slaughter, which would have been easy for them, after they had summoned the Idumeans, had not God reserved this for the Romans.

But that they should torment them five months) Up until the arrival of Titus. See Josephus, Jewish War V. 11. In the Manuscript they shall be tormented, namely they themselves.

Josephus says nothing there about five months. By the grass of the earth and the trees, according to the analogy of other similitudes, and by way of opposition, are to be understood true Christians flourishing in the midst of persecutions by a constant confession of the Catholic faith, and distinguished by the Nicene symbol. But men not having the seal of God are those who were not distinguished by the profession of the symbol of faith concerning Christ, and were therefore strangers to the sincerity of Christian doctrine, and what is its companion, true piety, Gal. V. v. 6. Jas. II. 18. To others, the grass of the earth are the rude and simple in faith, who seem easily able to be deceived, just as grass is easily burned. But the green things are trees somewhat verdant in Evangelical doctrine, who have now become robust in faith and fruitful works, Is. LXI. called trees of righteousness for the glory of the Lord. Men who do not have the sign of God, unbelieving and faithless, living according to the desires of the flesh, 2. Tim. II. 19. For these do not have the testimony and sealing of the Spirit, that they are truly children of God through faith.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Καὶ ἐδόθη ἀυταῖς, ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν ἀυτὸς) Ne una strage edita populum occiderent, quod facile illis fuisset, postquam Idumaeos acciverant, nisi Deus hoc Roma- nis reservasset.

Ἀλλ’ ἵνα βασανίσωσι μῆνας πέντε) Ad usque Titi adven- tum. Vide Josephum belli Judaici V. 11. In Manuscripto βασανισθήσονται nempe ἀυτοὶ.

Nihil ibi Josephus de quinque mensibus. Per gramen terrae & arbores ad analogiam alia- rum similitudinum, & vi oppositionis intelli- gendi veri Christiani florentes in mediis per- secutionibus constanti fidei Catholicae confessio- ne, & symbolo Niceno insigniti. Homines vero sigillum Dei non habentes sunt, qui professione symboli fidei de Christo insigniti non erant, adeo- que alieni erant a doctrinae Christianae sinceritate, & quae ejus comes est, vera pietate, Gal. V. v. 6. Jac. II. 18. Aliis faenum terrae sunt rudes & simpli- ces in fide, qui videntur facile decipi posse, sicuti facile exuritur foenum. Viride vero sunt aliquan- tulum virentes in doctrina Evangelica arbores, qui jam robusti in fide & operibus fructuosis effe- cti sunt, Es. LXI. arbores justitiae dicti in Domi- ni gloriam. Homines, qui non habent signum Dei, increduli & infideles juxta carnis cupiditates viventes, 2. Tim. II. 19. Hi enim non habent testi- monium, & obsignationem Spiritus, quod vere sint filii Dei per fidem.

## 9:6
Ver. 6. And their torment as the torment of a scorpion, when it strikes a man) they were snatching away not only other good things, but also necessary food from the miserable citizens.

And in those days men shall seek death (the better manuscripts have ζητήσεσιν, they shall desire death) because of a most grievous famine. Cyprian: It was not permitted to those wishing to die to be killed. Pliny: Death so often invoked.

Καὶ ἐ μὴ ἐυρήσεσιν ἀυτὸν) No one will wish to kill them. Thus Job III. 21. למות ואיננו המחכים In Greek: οἱ ἱμείρονται τῦ θανάτε, καὶ ἐ τυγχάνεσι.

(And he shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them) Twice the same in the Hebrew manner, to signify the vehemence of the desire. In the Manuscript it is φεύγει, as in a present matter.

Lyra, the Interlinear Gloss, Thomas, Luther, Osiander, and Gravius apply these things to the pious; Nicolaus, Gerhard, Riccardus, Coccejus, Kromejer, and Cluverus apply them to the impious. Cluverus understands them of spiritual death, Doling of eternal death.

Latin:

Vers. 6. Καὶ ὁ βασανισμὸς ἀυτῶν ὡς βασανισμὸς σκορπίου, ὅταν παίξῃ ἄνθρωπον) non bona tantum caetera, sed & ne- cessaria alimenta eripiebant miseris civibus.

Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ζητῦσιν ἄνθρωποι τὸν θάνα- τον) ζητήσεσιν habent codices meliores, optabunt mortem pra fame gravissima. Cyprianus: Volentibus mori non per- mittebatur occidi. Plinius: Toties invocata mors.

Καὶ ἐ μὴ ἐυρήσεσιν ἀυτὸν) Nemo eos volet interficere. Sic Jobi III. 21. למות ואיננו המחכים Graece: οἱ ἱμείρονται τῦ θανάτε, καὶ ἐ τυγχάνεσι.

Καὶ ἐπιθυμήσεσιν ἀποθανεῖν καὶ φεύξεται ἀπ’ ἀυτῶν ὁ θά- νατος) Bis idem more Ebraeo, ad significandam desiderij vehementiam. In Manuscripto φεύγει velut in re praesente.

Piis haec applicant Lyra, Glossa interlin. Tho- mas, Lutherus, Osiander, Gravius: Impiis Nicolai, Gerhardus, Riccardus, Coccejus, Kromejer, Cluverus, Doling. De morte spirituali Cluverus, de aeterna Doling intelligunt.

## 9:7
Vers. 7. Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων, ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοιμασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον) The word ὁμοίωμα here refers to what is seen by the eyes, so that they will be fierce in appearance, like war-horses. Taken from Joel II. 4.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφὰλας αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι χρυσοῖ) He does not say golden crowns, but as golden crowns. Those crowns will be deceitful. They will boast as if they held the victory over the Romans in their own power.

Καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων) They assumed the appearance of honest men. See Dan. VII. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 7. Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων, ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοι- μασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον) ὁμοίωμα hic ad oculos refertur, ita ic truces erunt adspectu, quasi equi bellatores. Sumptum ex Joële II. 4.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι χρυσοῖ) Non dicit στέφανοι χρυσοῖ, sed ὡς στέφανοι χρυσοῖ. Coronæ istæ mendaces erunt. Jactabunt se quasi in potestate sua haberent victoriam contra Romanos.

Καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων) Speciem sumebant honesti. Vide Dan. VII. 4.

## 9:8
Verse 8.

Καὶ εἶχον τρίχας, ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν) In truth they will be unwarlike no less than women, who are known especially by their hair. Of such men Aristophanes says: Ὄντες οἴκοι μὲν λέοντες ἐν μάχῃ δ' ἀλώπεκες, to be feared only by their hosts, as Tacitus says in Histories III. A predator among his allies and himself the prey of his enemies, as Sallust says, helmeted hares. This is rightly expressed by the sex, which Papinius called the effeminate iron. Such is that of Homer: Ἀχαΐδες, οὐκέτ' Ἀχαιοί. And of Virgil: O vere Phrygiæ, neque enim Phryges.

Καὶ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν) Most voracious men, from Joel 1:6. Hence the proverbial expression, the teeth of a lion, Sirach 21:7.

The Arian heresy at first glance had a great appearance of being pleasing, because it was consistent with reason. This cannot be said of Popery, as far as its principal head is concerned. However, the pleasant face of the locusts with women's hair seems to indicate this: unless perhaps these refer to those august women through whom we have said Arianism was propagated. B. Cluverus, comparing Cant. IV. 1 and VI. 4, says, that womanly hair was in the heretics, both because of the soothing and alluring zeal for insinuating themselves, by which they bound men to themselves everywhere, and also because of the female patronage by which they notably succeeded. For first, through Constantia, the widow of Licinius, that friend of Arius won favor for himself with Constantine, and brought it about that he was recalled from exile; then he obtained that the Emperor's will be entrusted to him, and by delivering it promptly to Constantius, he bound him to himself. Third, the wife of Valens, previously orthodox, having been deceived by the Arians, seduced her husband just as Eve did Adam, as Theodoret testifies in book IV, ch. 11. Fourth, the Empress Justina, mother of Valentinian II, favored them to such an extent that she nearly destroyed the most celebrated Bishop Ambrose for their sake. Fifth, Eudoxia, wife of Arcadius, aided the enemies of Chrysostom. Sixth, the eunuch Chrysaphius, a man of feminine character, protected Dioscorus and Nestorius before the Emperor Theodosius. And just as women win love for themselves with the pigments and adornments of their hair, so they contracted authority and friendship for themselves with the fabrications of specious narratives. Their faces, however, were like those of horses, and they had leonine teeth on account of the calumnies with which they bit and lacerated the reputation of true Christians, and they desired, as much as lay in them, to tear them to pieces and drove them into exile, which was established primarily by the example of Athanasius. Whence many Christians, exhausted by the most savage persecutions of the Arians, desired rather to die peacefully and piously than to live in anxiety, but they did not find such a death. For the tyranny was as great as was scarcely seen under the persecutions of the heathens: by means of violence the faithful were driven to the Arian heresy, by many things, prisons, tortures, exiles, all of which were intolerable.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

Καὶ εἶχον τρίχας, ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν) Revera erunt imbelles non minus quam fœminæ, quæ ex coma maxime noscuntur. De talibus Aristophanes: Ὄντες οἴκοι μὲν λέοντες ἐν μάχῃ δ' ἀλώπεκες, Hospitibus tantum metuendi, ut ait Tacitus Histor. III. Prædator e sociis & ipse præda hostium, ut Sallustius, galeati lepores. Hoc recte exprimitur per sexum, quem insicium ferri dixit Papinius. Tale illud Homeri: Ἀχαΐδες, οὐκέτ' Ἀχαιοί. Et Virgilii: O vere Phrygiæ, neque enim Phryges.

Καὶ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν) Homines voracissimi ex Joële I. 6. Hinc factum proverbiale, dentes leonis, Sirach. XXI. vers. 7.

Arianæ hæresis primo aspectu grata magnam habebat speciem, quia rationi consentanea. Quod de Papismo dici nequit, quantum ad præcipuum ejus caput. Indicare autem id videtur facies locustarum amœna cum capillis muliebribus: nisi hi forte respiciant mulieres illas augustas, per quas propagatum diximus Arianismum. B. Cluverus conferens Cant. IV. 1. cap. VI. 4. capillus, inquit, iste muliebris in hæreticis fuit, cum delenificum & illecebrosum sese insinuandi studium, quo passim sibi homines devinxere, tum etiam muliebre patrocinium, quo insigniter profecere. Nam primo per Constantiam Licinii viduam apud Constantinum gratiam sibi conciliavit ille Arii amicus, effecitque ut ab exilio revocaretur; Deinde testamentum sibi Imperatoris committi obtinuit, eoque ad Constantium mature delato eum sibi devinxit. Tertio Valentis antea orthodoxi conjux ab Arianis decepta herum suum sicut Eva Adamum seduxit, teste Theodoreto libr. IV. c. 11. Quarto Justina Imperatrix Valentiniani II. mater adeo ipsis favit, ut celeberrimum Episcopum Ambrosium pene in ipsorum gratiam perderet. Quinto Eudoxia Arcadii Conjux Chrysostomi hostes adjuvit. Sexto Chrysaphius Eunuchus muliebris, Dioscorum & Nestorium apud Imp. Theodosium protexit. Ac sicut mulieres capillitii pigmentis & ornatu amorem sibi conciliant: Sic illi speciosarum narrationum figmentis autoritatem sibi & amicitiam contraxerunt. Facies autem erant equorum instar, & dentes habebant leoninos ob calumnias, quibus mordebant, & lacerabant famam Christianorum verorum, eosque, quantum in ipsis erat, dilacerare cupiebant, & in exilium agebant, quod exemplo Athanasii imprimis constitit. Unde multi Christianorum truculentissimis Arianorum persecutionibus defatigati placide pieque mori potius, quam in anxietate vivere desiderabant, sed talem mortem non inveniebant. Tanta enim erat tyrannis, quanta vix sub Ethnicis persecutionibus: Mediis violentiis adigebantur fideles ad hæresin Arianam, multis, carceribus, tormentis, exiliis, quæ omnia erant intolerabilia.

## 9:9
Vers. 9. Καὶ εἶχον θώρακας, ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς)

You might think them to be such as Horace describes: 'He had oak and triple bronze around his breast.' For by the breastplate, the breast is understood; by the iron, hardness.

Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν) He says this because he gave them the appearance of locusts.

Ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον) They do everything with a great noise. An expression from Joel 2:5.

The Arian locusts had iron breastplates, that is, weapons and external political power; because they defended their heresy with an armed hand and by the secular arm. Many horses running to war and the sound of wings (for they are compared to locusts) like the sound of chariots denotes a very great number of soldiers and the utmost speed, just as it is established that the Vandals, Goths, and Huns, addicted to the Arian heresy, having poured into the East and Africa in great hosts, afflicted the Christian world most grievously like locusts. Many horses denote diverse heresies, unanimously attacking the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Καὶ εἶχον θώρακας, ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς)

Putes esse tales, quales describit Horatius: Illi robur & æs triplex Circum pectus erat. Nam per loricam pectus, per ferrum durities intelligitur.

Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν) Hoc dicit, quia locustarum eis speciem dedit.

Ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον) Magno omnia cum strepitu agunt. Locutio ex Joële II. 5.

Habebant locustæ Arianicæ loricas ferreas, id est, arma, & externam potentiam politicam; quia hæresin suam propugnabant armata manu & per brachium seculare. Equi multi ad bellum currentes & vox alarum (locustis enim compa- rantur) sicut vox curruum notat maximum mili- tum numerum summamque celeritatem, quemad- modum constat Vandalos, Gothos, & Hunnos Arianæ hæresi addictos magnis agminibus in Ori- entem & Africam insusos, locustarum instar gra- vissime orbem Christianum afflixisse. Multi equi diversas hæreses, unanimiter in Ecclesiam impu- gnantes notant.

## 9:10
Vers. 10. Καὶ ἔχουσιν ὀυρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα) that is, κέντρα ὀυρῶν ὁμοίας σκορπίοις. Nicander said: Κέντρα κεκορυθμένοι ἀλγηόεντι Σκορπίον. Cicero: The hostile scorpion carrying forward a mournful sting. Avienus: - the scorpion, which with the venomous train of its tail, is raised up in great numbers. Tertullian on Scorpions: A single gesture of all in violence, harmful from the tail. The power of other serpents is in the head: scorpions wound from where it is least expected. Thus the Zealots used to harm where they were least thought to be about to harm. They entered as defenders, they left as plunderers. Apuleius teaches us that barbaric men and those of sick morals are accustomed to be called scorpions. But also Ezech. 11. vers. 6.

They had tails of scorpions stinging consciences, because they took away the foundations of life-giving consolation. There is no greater punishment, says Bernard on the evil conscience, than a bad conscience. For it is itself the witness, itself the judge, itself the torturer, itself the prison of all our offenses. It accuses, it judges, it punishes, it condemns.

They had crowns on their heads, either because they triumphed with victories, or because Emperors and Kings placed and found their protection with a crowned head. For Constantine, as the blessed Cluverus has summarized these things, persuaded by his sister, protected Arius and those Tyrian and Jerusalemite Fathers with his royal power, unaware of their frauds, and punished certain innocent men with exile. Constantius clearly went over to their opinion. Julian treated the heterodox and the orthodox indifferently. Valens so adhered to the heretics that he was harsh and bitter toward the Catholics. Valentinian was troublesome to no one regarding religion. Gratian permitted each to practice his own worship. Theodosius proved burdensome to no one. Justina, addicted to the Arians, attacked the orthodox. Arcadius also and Honorius granted each to practice his own religion. Theodosius the Younger was as if made for gentleness, and was an enemy to persecutors and men of a more fervent spirit. Nestorius and Eutyches earned his patronage for some time. In sum, there were always, whether among the Emperors or others bearing iron and arms, those who showed themselves patrons of heretics or of contentiously arguing theologians. The iron audacity and impudence of those men is evident everywhere. There was no crime they did not dare to undertake, provided they hoped to promote their cause. Those whom they could not crush with calumnies, they trampled with manifest force. They despised swearing and perjuring with an iron heart. To profess or deny the faith, to utter blasphemies at times, to anathematize, and to devote themselves to curses, was a game, nay, a praise.

Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ὀυραῖς ἀυτῶν ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσι τοῦ ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε) He repeats this again, because a time so defined provides a notable testimony of divine providence. In the Manuscript: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ὀυραῖς ἀυτῶν ἡ ἐξουσία ἀυτῶν. But the Latin reads, as certain Codices have: Καὶ κέντρα ἐν ταῖς ὀυραῖς ἀυτῶν, καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία ἀυτῶν &c.

Locusts live for five months. For they come forth in April, and last until September. Balth. Richter counts here 1050 years. 95. Döling. Most others 150, such as Joachim the Abbot, Junius, Nicolai, Napier, Mede, Cotterius, Hoffmann, Hogelius, likewise Osiander, Gravius, Dürfeld, Cluverus. The Arian heresy indeed lasted much longer; yet it could not exercise its power, tyranny, and persecutions beyond 150 years, indicated by five months, or 150 days. He does not say there would be no locusts after five months, but he defines the time of their torment in that way; Arianism made its decline at the rise of John I after the Council of Chalcedon.

Latin:

Vers. 10. Καὶ ἔχουσιν ὀυρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα) id est κέντρα ὀυρῶν ὁμοίας σκορπίοις. Nicander dixit: Κέντρα κεκορυθμένοι ἀλγηόεντι Σκορπίον. Cicero: Scorpius infestus præportans flebile acumen. Avienus: - venenato qui Scorpius agmine caudæ Plurimus erigitur. Tertullianus de Scorpiis: Unus omnium violentia gestus, nocens de cauda. Aliorum serpentum vis in capite: Scor- piones inde vulnerant, unde id minus expectatur. Sic Ze- lotæ lædebant, ubi minime læsuri putabantur. Intrabant ut defensores, exibant raptores. Homines barbari & ægris moribus solere scorpios dici, docet nos Apulejus. Sed & Ezech. 11. vers. 6.

Caudas habebant scorpionum pungentes con- scientias, quia fundamenta vivificæ consolationis tollebant. Nulla pœna major est, inquit Bernhar- dus de conscient. mala conscientia. Omnium si- quidem delictorum nostrorum ipsa est testis, ipsa judex, ipsa tortor, ipsa carcer. Ipsa accusat, ipsa ju- dicat, ipsa punit, ipsa damnat.

Coronas habebant in capitibus, sive quia victoriis triumphabant, sive quod Imperatores & Reges capite coronato præ- sidium suum posuerint, & invenerint. Constanti- nus enim, ut summatim hæc complexus est B. Clu- verus, a sorore persuasus Arium & Tyrios illos ac Hierosolymitanos Patres, inscius fraudum potentia sua Regali protexit, & innocentes quosdam exilio multavit. Constantius plane in eorum sententiam ivit. Julianus heterodoxos & orthodoxos indifferen- ter habuit. Valens hæreticis ita adhæsit, ut immitis & acerbus esset Catholicis. Valentinianus nulli de religione erat molestus. Gratianus singulis suum cul- tum exercere permisit. Theodosius nulli gravis ex- titit. Justina Arianis addicta orthodoxos oppugna- vit. Arcadius quoque & Honorius singulis suam re- ligionem colere concesserunt. Theodosius Junior ad mansuetudinem quasi factus persecutoribus & fer- vidioris animi viris inimicus fuit. Nestorius & Eu- tyches illius aliquandiu patrocinium meruere. Sum- ma, fuerunt semper sive ex Imperatoribus, sive ex aliis ferrum & arma gestantibus alii, qui hæretico- rum aut contentiose Theologantium patronos se præ- stitere. Audacia & impudentia illorum ferrea pas- sim patet. Nullum crimen aggredi non sunt ausi, dummodo suam promovere causam sperarent. Quos calumniis opprimere nequibant, manifesta vi pro- triverunt. Jurare, pejerare, ferreo pectore contem- pserunt. Fidem profiteri aut negare, blasphemias interdum proferre, anathematizare, seque ipsos diris devovere, ludo fuit, imo laude.

Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ὀυραῖς ἀυτῶν ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσι τοῦ ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε) Hoc iterum repetit, quia tempus adeo definitum insigne præbet divinæ providentiæ testimonium. In Manuscripto: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ὀυραῖς ἀυτῶν ἡ ἐξουσία ἀυτῶν. At Latinus legit, ut quidam Codices habent: Καὶ κέντρα ἐν ταῖς ὀυραῖς ἀυτῶν, καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία ἀυτῶν &c.

Locustæ per quinque menses vivunt. In Aprili enim prodeunt, & durant usque in Septembrem. Numerat hic annos 1050. Balth. Richter. 95. Dö- ling. Plerique alii 150. utpote Joachimus Abbas, Junius, Nicolai, Napeirus, Medus, Cotterius, Hoff- mannus, Hogelius, Osiander item, Gravius, Dür- feld, Cluverus. Duravit quidem longe diutius hæ- resis Ariana; potentiam tamen, tyrannidem, & persecutiones ultra 150. annos, quinque mensibus, seu 150. diebus indicatos exercere non potuit. Non dicit nullas fôre post quinque menses lo- custas, sed tempus cruciatus illarum ita definit; Decrementa fecit Johannis I. ortu Arianismus post concilium Chalcedonense.

## 9:11
Vers. 11. Ἔχουσαι) He uses the feminine gender because of the figure of the locusts (ἀκρίδων). But in the Manuscript ἔχουσι. Βασιλέα ἐφ᾽ αὑτῶν) They said they wished to have no King but God, but the matter stood otherwise. Τὸν Ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου) Satan, whom God shuts in prison, where He wills. Below XVIII. 1. 2. In the Manuscript: Τὸν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἀβύσσου τὸν Ἄγγελον. Ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἀβαδδών) אבדון properly destruction, ἀπώλεια, as Job XXVIII. 22. But among those nations, abstract and concrete words are accustomed to be interchanged. Thus it happened that אבדון signifies the same as אשמורי, about which we spoke at 1. Cor. X. 10. You have the name אבדון given to a Demon in the Aruch. That name is given in Rome in the Jerusalem Targum. This name is the opposite of the name of Jesus יהושוע. God uses the work of evil Angels and men to afflict the good. He uses both good and evil, as much men as Angels, to afflict the wicked. But truly destructive was the Spirit that agitated those Zealots, from which destruction was born both to the city and to the temple,

In the Greek language it has the name Ἀπολλύων) he could have said ὀλοθρευτής or ἐξολοθρεύων: but he preferred to allude to the name of Apollo, which was as it were the proper deity for the Caesars. Ovid: And with Caesarean Phoebus, domestic Vesta. Namely from the Actian victory, where, as Virgil wished to be believed, Actian Apollo, seeing these things, was bending his bow from above. See Suetonius, Octavius 29. But just as the Jews were accustomed to change the names of false gods with a slight inflection into a term of reproach, so also is it done here in the Greek name. For Ἀπόλλων and Ἀπολλύων are similar. Someone might perhaps think that the etymology was also considered. For some of the Greeks think that Apollo is called ἑκατηϐολότην and λοίμιον, because he sends diseases, and they confirm this from the first book of the Iliad. Regarding that passage of Aeschylus in the Agamemnon: 'Apollo, Apollo, guardian of the ways, my destroyer.' The scholiast says it becomes Ἀπολλύων, by reason of the homonymy. But the sense is excellent. Those Zealots say that they are enemies to the Caesars, as being idolaters, when nevertheless they themselves serve the same Spirit whom the Caesars worship in the name of Apollo, and they promote the Roman greatness and the destruction of their own nation as much as possible.

These names, one in the Hebrew language and the other in the Greek, denote a destroyer, אבדון and ἀπολλύων, who by antonomasia is Satan. For they were ruled by him, both in doctrine as the Father of lies, John 8:44, and in life, as a murderer from the very beginning of his defection, the Arians: just as the remnants of them, the Nestorianizing Papists, fight under the same Leader, unless one prefers to point to the Pope himself with these names, along with Luther, Flacius, Chytraeus, Osiander, Philipp Nicolai, Mede, Crugot, Winckelmann, Cramer, Cluver, Gerhard, Gravius, Dürfeld. Likewise Piscator, Forbes, and finally Andrew of Lyra, the Interlinear Gloss, Thomas, the Scholastics, Bellarmine, Ribera, who rightly deserves the same title, the common destroyer of the world, whom he destroys in body, and by wars stirred up on account of the profession of the Evangelical faith, but especially by the destruction of souls on account of a dogma noxious and lethal, hidden like the poison of a scorpion. Thus concerning the Antichrist, who is called the son of perdition, 2 Thess. 2:3, by a name common with Judas the traitor, John 17:12, and Ἀπολλύων in an active sense, because he himself destroys others not only in their souls through corrupt doctrine, but also in their bodies through horrendous cruelty, or corporally and spiritually, as Hugo holds. See Alabaster's new Prophet's new opinion concerning Abaddon in Helvicus in the appendix of his disputations against the Jews. Some, as cited by the blessed Gerhard, understand Saladin, the Emperor of the Saracens, who devastated the Jerusalemite kingdom recently founded by Godfrey of Bouillon and almost all of Asia around the year 1195.

Latin:

Vers. 11. Ἔχουσαι) Fœmininum genus usurpat ob figuram ἀκρίδων. At in Manuscripto ἔχουσι. Βασιλέα ἐφ᾽ αὑτῶν) Dicebant se nullum Regem habere velle, nisi Deum, sed aliter se res habebat. Τὸν Ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου) Satanam, quem Deus carceri in- cludit, ubi vult. Infra XVIII. 1. 2. In Manuscripto : Τὸν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἀβύσσου τὸν Ἄγγελον. Ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἀβαδδών) אבדון proprie perni- cies ἀπώλεια, ut Job. XXVIII. 22. Sed solent apud illas gentes voces abstractæ & concretæ inter se permutari. Sic fa- ctum ut אבדון idem significet, quod אשמורי, de quo diximus 1. Cor. X. 10. Habes nomen אבדון datum Dæ- moni in Aruch. Datur Romæ id nomen in Targume Hiero- solymitano. Oppositum hoc nomen nomini Jesu יהושוע. Deus ad affligendos bonos utitur opera Angelorum & ho- minum malorum. Ad affligendos malos utitur & bonis & malis tam hominibus quam Angelis. Vere autem exi- tialis fuit Spiritus, qui Zelotas illos agitabat, unde exitium natum est & urbi & templo,

Ἐν δὲ Ἑλληνικῇ ὄνομα ἔχει ὁ Ἀπολλύων) poterat dixisse ὀλοθρευτής vel ἐξολοθρεύων: sed maluit alludere ad nomen Apollinis, quod velut proprium numen Cæsaribus. Ovidius: Et cum Cæsarea tu Phœbe domestice Vesta. nempe ex victoria Actiaca, ubi, ut Virgilius credi voluit, Actius hæc cernens arcum intendebat Apollo Desuper. Vide Suetonium Octavio 29. Sicut autem Judæi solebant falsorum Deorum nomina levi flexu in contumeliam mu- tare, ita & hic fit in Græco nomine. Vicina enim sunt Ἀπόλ- λων & Ἀπολλύων. Putet forte aliquis & etymologiam spe- ctatam. Nam Græcorum nonnulli Ἀπόλλωνα ut ἑκατηϐολό- την & λοίμιον dictum putant, quod morbos immittat, idque confirmant ex Iliados primo. Ad illud Æschyli in Agamem. Ἄπολλον, Ἄπολλον ἁγυιεῦ τ᾽ ἀπόλλων ἐμοί. Schol. ἀπολλύων fit, παρὰ τὴν ὁμωνυμίαν. Sensus autem est egregius. Dicunt illi Zelotæ inimicos se Cæsaribus, utpote idololatris, cum tamen ipsi eidem Spiritui serviant, quem in Apollinis no- mine Cæsares colunt, & magnitudinem Romanam suæque gentis exitium quam maxime promoveant.

Nomina hæc alterum inEbræa alterum inGræca lingua perditorem notant אבדון & ἀπολλύων, qui κατ᾿ ἀντονομασίαν est Satanas. Ab hoc enim regebantur cum in doctrina ceu Patre mendacii Joh. IIX. 44. tum in vita, ceu ἀνθρωποκτόνῳ ab ipso defectionis suæ initio Ariani: quemadmo- dum sub eodem Duce militant reliquiæ eorum, Nestorianizantes Papicolæ, nisi Papam ipsum in- digitari nominibus istis quis malit cum Luthero, Flacio, Chytrao, Osiandro, Philippo Nicolai, Medo, Crugotio, Winckelmanno, Cramero, Cluvero, Ger- hardo, Gravio, Dürfeld. Piscatore item, Forbesio, Andrea deniq; Lyrano Glossa interlin. Thoma, Scho- lasticis, Bellarm. Ribera, qui insigne jure eadem meretur, communis perditor orbis, quem corpo- re perdit, ac bellis ob fidei Evangelicæ professio- nem excitatis, maxime autem animæ exitio ob dogma Scorpiaci veneni instar latenter noxium, & lethiferum. Sic de Anti- Christo, qui filius perdi- tionis 2. Thess. II. 3. communi cum Juda proditore nomine vocatur, Joh. XVII. 12. & ἀπολλύων sensu activo, quod ipse alios perdat non solum in animis per pravam doctrinam, sed etiam in corpori- bus per horrendam sævitiam seu corporaliter & spiritualiter, ut habet Hugo. Alabastri novi Pro- phetæ novam de Abaddon sententiam vide apud Helvic. in appendic. disput. contra Judæos. Non- nulli, citante B. Gerhardo, intelligunt Saladinum Saracenorum Imperat. qui regnum Hierosolymi- tanum a Godofredo Bulionæo nuper conditum ac totam fere Asiam vastavit circa annum 1195.

## 9:12
Vers. 12. The one woe has passed) That rapacity of the Zealots finally ceased after five months upon the arrival of Titus, as we said above. Behold, there come yet two, and after these) of the siege and destruction.

He indicates, however, not by reason of the signification, but by reason of the vision, that he is now about to manifest a double or second Woe. As to the signification, Mohammedanism began while Arianism still lasted; indeed, Arianism passed into Mohammedanism, just as the Arian monk, Sergius, was employed in forging the Alcoran. Arianism therefore acquired a new form, as far as the old one at least passed away.

PART II. CONCERNING THE OPENING OF THE SIXTH SEAL, AND THE SLAUGHTER OF THE THIRD PART OF THE WORLD.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Ἡ ἐὼ μία ἀπῆλθεν) Cessavit tandem illa Zelota- rum rapacitas post menses quinque adventante Tito, ut su- pra diximus. Ἰδὲ ἔρχεται ἔτι δύο καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα) obsidionis & excidii.

Non tamen ratione significationis, quam ratione visionis indicat, se jam geminum vel alterum Væ manifestaturum. Quod ad significationem, cœpit Mahometismus durante adhuc Arianismo; imo Arianismus transiit in Mahometismum, sicut in cudendo Alcorano Monachus Arianus, Sergius, adhibitus fuit. Novam ergo speciem Arianismus adeptus, quoad veterem saltim transiit.

PARS II. DE SEXTI SIGILLI APERTIONE, ET TERTIÆ PARTIS ORBIS OCCISIONE.

## 9:13
Vers. 13. And the sixth Angel sounded) A sign given for new evils.

And I heard one voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is before God, saying to the sixth Angel) God, having heard the prayers of those exiles who at some time were longing to return to their ancestral seats, ordered the siege, which had been delayed for a long time by fate, to be hastened, so that when those things which God wished to be accomplished were finished, the armies might depart, and a safe return might be granted to the villas and fields, and if any of the towns remained. For the elect the days shall be shortened, Matth. XXIV. 22. The golden altar is the altar of incense, by which prayers are signified. There were four horns on that altar, Exod. XXX. 2. By them understand here all the places in which the Jews who worshipped Christ were living in exile: for they were not all at Pella.

Latin:

Vers. 13. Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος Ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισε) Datum signum ad nova mala.

Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων κεράτων τοῦ θυ- σιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ τοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, λέγουσαν τῷ ἕκτῳ Ἀγγέλῳ) Deus auditis precibus illorum exulantium, qui aliquando in sedes avitas redire gestiebant, properari jus- sit obsidium fatis diu dilatum, ut rebus iis confectis, quas Deus confieri volebat, abirent exercitus, & tutus daretur in villas & agros, & si qua oppidorum restabant, reditus. Διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς κολοβωθήσονται αἱ ἡμέραι, Matth. XXIV. 22. Altare aureum est altare suffituum, per quos significantur preces. Quatuor cornua erant in eo altari, Exod. XXX. 2. Per ea hic intellige omnia loca, in quibus exulabant Judæi Christum colentes: neque enim omnes erant Pellæ.

## 9:14
Vers. 14. Saying to the sixth Angel: loose the four Angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates) These four Angels are the leaders and guardians of Vespasian, Titus, Mucianus, and Tiberius Alexander, whose huge armies were reaching as far as the Euphrates: and although it had long been their plan to besiege Jerusalem, the matter was nevertheless delayed by divine counsel until the time destined for it. Vespasian was taking a pretext for delay, because he wanted Jerusalem to be broken first by internal discords: in reality, he wanted to wait to see how the Roman affairs would turn out: Josephus, Jewish War IV. 21. During that time the Angels, who were about to incite them, are said to have been bound, that is, restrained by God. To the Euphrates is added the title of a great river, because there were also other smaller ones by the name of פרת, as we have said elsewhere. The Syrian legions were reaching the Euphrates. Josephus V. 6. Thus also Philo in his embassy said the camps which were by the Euphrates.

How foreign these inventions are has already appeared from the Chronology. They are commonly explained concerning Mohammedanism: and they fit it skillfully: although Bullinger, and after him Marloratus with Cocceius, understand it concerning the fury of the Roman Pontiff, and Andreas Caesar, etc., concerning the fury of the barbarian peoples. We add our vote to those who explain the second Woe concerning the Turks of the Ottoman family, such as Piscator, Pareus, Forbes, Riccardus, Cartesius, as also Luther, Osiander, Winckelmann, Flacius, Wolterus, Cramer, Nicolai, Gerhard, Dölingius, Dürfeld. It does not sufficiently fit the Anti-Christ, as Pareus warns, because of what is held here concerning the Euphrates, which is mentioned in the history of creation and here and there in the Scriptures, which, descending from the mountains of Armenia, flowed through the middle of Chaldea and Babylonia. This river had been until now the boundary of the Roman Empire, separating the Christian world from the barbarians. Beyond, towards the north and the east, the Scythians, Tartars, and Turks had their seats. Below, towards the south, the Arabs and Saracens had their seats and until now, by divine command, were keeping themselves tranquil. Now these four Angels, that is, the peoples, Arabs, Saracens, Tartars, Turks, are divinely loosed, or the reins are loosened for them, so that they may go forth armed against the Christians. The Angels, therefore, according to this opinion, are called these peoples not by nature, but by ministry; because they were divinely excited and sent to punish the Christians. And they are different from those four Angels in chapter VII, who were the secular and spiritual ministers of the Western Anti-Christ, opposing themselves to the doctrine of the Gospel, so that it might not be preached in the Christian world. These, however, are only the secular ministers of the Eastern Anti-Christ, not prohibiting the Gospel from being preached, but bringing about a sad desolation by raging against the Christians with arms and slaughter. But because Angels in the Apocalypse nowhere denote peoples, they were indeed properly seen as Angels, and evil ones at that, as in Apoc. VII. But by that vision were signified the leaders of the peoples, just as bishops in the sacred order are spiritual leaders, and come under the name of Angels, not the Church itself over which they preside: unless the demons themselves bound at the Euphrates are understood, because they had long since plotted that there, for the execution of which they are now permitted, having been hitherto restrained by God, without doubt, out of a singular long-suffering, inviting the Christian world to repentance in vain, Rom. II. 4. More correctly, says the blessed Gerhard, it is said that malignant spirits are noted, who from all parts of the world incited kings and peoples around the Euphrates against the Christians, so that they might attack them in war. They were, however, bound until now, that is, Christ by his divine power repressed them, so that they could not incite the shedding of blood at their pleasure. That voice from the horns of the altar is the voice of Christ, whose office is around the golden altar, not of any created Angel. For every priest had to be taken from among men, Heb. V. 1. The four horns of the altar are explained with respect to the four Evangelists, so that that voice from the four horns denotes the concordant preaching of all the Evangelicals founded in the four Gospels: which Evangelists are the four horns of the golden altar, that is, of Christ offered for us, and for whom the blood of the pious afflicted by the Anti-Christ is offered: Just as in the Old Testament the blood of the offered animal was placed on the four horns of the altar, according to the interpretation of Marloratus. Cf. Exod. XXVII. 2, ch. XXXVIII. 2, Heb. XIII. 10, 1 Pet. II. 5, Apoc. VI. 9. Which voice of the four Evangelists sounded in the whole world. But after the saving doctrine concerning the golden altar, the person of Christ, His office, and His benefits was obscured both in the East and in the West by various heresies, and the kingdom of the Anti-Christ began its origin in the East, by the just judgment and permission of God these four evil Angels, who were bound about the Euphrates, were again loosed, and there arose in the East disturbers and devastators of the Roman Empire and the Church, the Arabs, Saracens, and Turks, to whom, on account of the sins of men, it was permitted that they should stir up bloody wars and shed blood copiously, and thus, according to the Woe, bring it upon the Church. The name of the river Euphrates, at which those Angels are said to have been bound and afterwards loosed, leads us to this exposition. For it rises in Armenia, flows past Syria and Mesopotamia, and empties itself into the Persian Sea, which regions the Saracens occupied. Also situated by the Persian Sea is the city of Mecca, where the tomb of Muhammad is, to which daily pilgrimages are instituted by the Turks with a great concourse of people. Now Muhammad was born in the city of Jethrib, as Schindler observes in his Lexicon, and boasted of revelations, as Flacius, Szegedin, Gerhard, and the Vinarienses testify. By the Euphrates, indeed the most famous river of Asia, was situated Babylon, the seat of the Oriental Monarchy, and the most powerful peoples of the East, the Assyrians, Babylonians, Medes, and Persians, who had been masters of affairs before the Macedonian and Roman Monarchy, seemed as it were submerged, buried, and hidden, and thus bound in that river. For the Western Macedonians, and soon the Romans, had become masters of affairs. The most powerful nations, which we have just named, were subject to them. But when the golden altar was defiled in the way we have described, both in the East and

When countless peoples in the West fell away from the true Christian faith, God again stirred up the eastern destroyers of the world, once somehow lulled to sleep. For the Prophets testify that those nations were scourges of the world: therefore, God again brought forth the same scourges by His just judgment, as Bullinger says. Thus, the four Angels of the peoples of the East were noted: the Arabs, Saracens, Turks, and Tartars. The four Angels used these armies to kill a third part of men. By this, says B. Gravius, are understood the leaders of the peoples living by the Euphrates, namely: (1) the Huns, under the leader Attila, (2) the Persians, (3) the Arabs and Saracens, (4) the Turks and Tartars, who are properly called GOGITAE, in the northern region, not far from the sources of the Euphrates. Among the Angels who are said to be released by the sounding of the sixth trumpet, the chief was Mahomet the False Prophet, born in Arabia, who, at the instigation of the Devil, devised a new and blasphemous doctrine concocted from Judaism, Gentilism, and Christianity, and in the progress of time bound the said four peoples together with it, and with an armed hand, having stirred up sedition against the Roman Empire, strove to oppress the Church. This happened around the times of the Emperor Heraclius, who had won a notable victory over Cosroes, King of the Persians, with the help of the Saracens. But when he denied pay to the Saracens, they themselves, under the leader Omar, defected to Mahomet, having drawn the other Arabs into an alliance of war. Joined to these were the Turks and Tartars, who, having assumed the Mahometan religion, conspired into one empire, which, though weakened among the Saracens, resumed its strength in the Ottoman race in the year of Christ 1292.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Λέγουσαν τῷ ἕκτῳ Ἀγγέλῳ· λῦσον τοὺς τέσσαρας Ἀγγέλους τοὺς δεδεμένους ἐπὶ ποταμῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ Εὐφράτῃ) Hi quatuor Angeli sunt Duces & custodes Vespasiani, Titi Muciani & Tiberii Alexandri, quorum ingentes exercitus ad Euphratem usque pertingebant: & cum diu consilium iis fuisset Hierosolyma obsidere, res tamen divino con- silio dilata fuit in tempus ipsi destinatum. Vespasianus præ- textum moræ sumebat, quod vellet Hierosolyma internis primum discordiis infringi: revera volebat expectare, quor- sum se daturæ essent res Romanæ: Josephus belli Judaici IV. 21. Per id tempus Angeli, qui eos incitaturi erant, vin- cti fuisse dicuntur, id est, a Deo inhibiti. Euphrati additur titulus magni fluminis, quia & alia minora erant nomi- ne פרת, ut alibi diximus. Syriacæ legiones attingebant Euphratem. Josephus V. 6. Sic & Philo in legatione dixit στρατόπεδα τὰ πρὸς Εὐφράτῃ.

Quam aliena sint hæc commenta, è Chrono- logia jam patuit. Communiter ea de Mahome- tismo explicantur: eique affabre conveniunt: etsi Bullingerus, & ex eo Marloratus cum Coccejo de furore Romani Pontificis, Andreas Cæsar. &c. de furore barbarorum populorum intelligant. Nos calculum adjicimus iis, qui de Turcis Otto- mannicæ familiæ secundum Væ exponunt, quales sunt Piscator, Pareus, Forbesius, Riccardus, Carte- sius, ut & Lutherus, Osiander, Winckelmannus, Flacius, Wolterus, Cramerus, Nicolai, Gerhardus, Dölingius, Dürfeld. Anti-Christo non satis congruit, monente Pareo, quod de Euphrate hic habetur, cu- jus in historia creationis & passim in Scripturis fit mentio, qui ex Armeniæ montibus descendens Chal- dæam & Babyloniam mediam interluebat. Fuerat is fluvius hucusque, imperii Romani limes, Christia- norum orbem a barbaris separans. Ultra cum septen- trionem & ortum versus Scythæ, Tartari, & Turcæ. Infra cum meridiem versus Arabes & Saraceni se- des habebant & hactenus divino jussu tranquilli se continebant. Nunc quatuor isti Angeli, hoc est, po- puli, Arabes, Saraceni, Tartari, Turcæ divinitus solvuntur, seu habenæ eis laxantur, ut armati in Christianos prodeant. Angeli ergo juxta hanc sen- tentiam hi populi vocantur non natura, sed mini- sterio; quia divinitus excitati & missi ad punien- dum Christianos. Et diversi ab illis quatuor An- gelis c. VII. qui administri erant Anti-Christi Oc- cidentalis seculares & spirituales, opponentes se do- ctrina Evangelii, ne prædicaretur in orbe Christia- no. Isti vero sunt administri tantum seculares Anti- Christi Orientalis, non prohibentes prædicari Ev- angelium, sed armis & cædibus in Christianos gras- sando tristem vastitatem inducentes. Sed quia An- geli in Apocalypsi nuspiam populos denotant, proprie quidem Angeli visi sunt, iique mali, ut Ap. VII. Sed per visionem illam significati Duces po- pulorum, quemadmodum Episcopi in ordine sa- cro Duces spirituales sunt, & Angelorum nomine veniunt, non ipsa Ecclesia, cui præsunt: nisi ipsi- met Dæmones ligati ad Euphratem intelligantur, quod pridem id moliti sint ibidem, ad quod exe- quendum nunc permittuntur, hactenus a Deo in- hibiti, fine dubio, ex μακροθυμίᾳ singulari, ad pœ- nitentiam orbem Christianum nequicquam invi- tante, Rom. II. 4. Rectius, inquit B. Gerhardus, di- citur, notari Spiritus malignos, qui ex omnibus mun- di plagis circa Euphratem Reges & populos contra Christianos concitarunt, ut bello eos aggrederentur. Fuerunt autem hactenus ligati, id est, Christus di- vina sua potentia eos repressit, ut non potuerint pro lubitu sanguinis effusiones excitare. Vox illa e cor- nibus altaris Christi vox est, cujus munus est cir- ca aureum altare, non Angeli creati ullius. Omnis enim Sacerdos ex hominibus assumendus erat, Ebr. V. 1. Quatuor altaris cornua explicantur cum respectu ad quatuor Evangelistas, ut vox illa e qua- tuor cornibus notet concordem prædicationem omni- um Evangelicorum in quatuor Evangeliis funda- tam: qui Evangelistæ sunt quatuor cornua altaris aurci, id est, Christi pro nobis oblati, & pro quo of- fertur sanguis piorum afflictorum ab Anti-Christo: Sicut in V. Test. sanguis animalis oblati ponebatur in quatuor cornibus altaris, interprete Marlorato. Conf. Exod. XXVII. 2. c. XXXIIX. 2. Ebr. XIII. 10. 1. Petr. II. 5. Apoc. VI. 9. Quæ vox IV. Evangeli- starum in toto orbe sonuit. Postquam vero sa- lutaris doctrina de altari aureo, de Christi perso- na, officio, & beneficiis tum in Oriente tum in Occidente per varias hæreses fuit obscurata, & regnum Anti-Christi in Oriente originem cœpit, justo Dei judicio, & permissione hi quatuor An- geli mali, qui erant circa Euphratem ligati, sunt iterum soluti, ac in Oriente exorti sunt turbato- res ac devastatores Imperii Romani & Ecclesiæ, Arabes, Saraceni, & Turci, quibus ob peccata ho- minum permissum fuit, ut excitarent cruenta bel- la, & sanguinem copiose effunderent, sicq; secun- dum Væ super Ecclesiam inducerent. Ad hanc ex- positionem nos deducit nomen fluvii Euphratis, ad quem Angeli illi dicuntur ligati & postea solu- ti. Is namque oritur in Armenia, præterlabitur Syriam & Mesopotamiam, ac exonerat se in mare Persicum, quas regiones Saraceni occuparunt. Ad mare Persicum etiam sita est urbs Mecha, ubi est sepulchrum Muhammedis, ad quod a Turcis quotidianæ peregrinationes magno hominum concursu instituuntur. Fuit autem Mahometh in urbe Jethrib natus, Schindlero in Lexic. observan- te, gloriatus de revelationibus, teste Flacio, Szege- dino, Gerhardo, Vinariensibus. Ad Euphratem qui- dem famosissimum Asiæ flumen sita fuit Babylon, se- des Monarchiæ Orientalis, ac populi quidem Ori- entis Potentissimi Assyrii, Babylonii, Medi & Persæ, qui rerum Domini fuerant ante Monarchiam Ma- cedonicam & Romanam veluti submersi, sepulti & abditi, adeoque alligati videbantur in illo flumine. Nam rerum Domini facti fuerant Occidentales Mace- dones, mox Romani. Serviebant his potentissimæ gen- tes, quas modo nominavimus. Ubi vero altare aure- um ita, ut diximus, conspurcaretur, & in Oriente &

Occidente defecerent a vera fide Christiana innu- meri populi, excitavit iterum Deus vastatores orbis orientales, olim utcunque sopitos. Nam Prophetæ te- stantur, gentes illas flagella fuisse orbis: eadem ergo flagella iterum justo suo judicio protulit Deus, di- cente Bullingero. Notati ergo Angeli quatuor populorum Orientis, Arabum, Saracenorum, Tur- carum, Tartarorum. Hisce exercitibus uteban- tur quatuor Angeli ad interficiendum partem ter- tiam hominum. Intelliguntur hic, inquit B. Gra- vius, Ductores populorum ad Euphraten habitan- tium, videl. (1) Hunnorum, duce Attila, (2) Per- sarum, (3) Arabum & Saracenorum, (4) Turca- rum & Tartarorum, qui proprie GOGITÆ dicun- tur, in septentrionali plaga, non procul ab Euphra- tis fontibus. Inter Angelos qui soluti dicuntur clan- gore sextæ tubæ, præcipuus fuit Mahumetes Pseudo- Propheta in Arabia natus, qui novam atque blasphe- mam doctrinam ex Judaismo, Gentilismo & Chri- stianismo, conflatam, instigante Diabolo excogitavit, eaque dictos quatuor populos temporis progressu con- glutinavit, & armata manu excitata contra Impe- rium Romanum seditione Ecclesiam opprimere stu- duit. Factum hoc est circa tempora Heraclii Impe- rat. qui auxilio Saracenorum insignem de Cosroe Persarum Rege reportaverat victoriam. Sed cum Saracenis stipendia denegaret, illi ipsi Duce Homare defecerunt ad Mahumetem, attractis in belli socie- tatem Arabibus cæteris. His conjuncti sunt Turcæ & Tartari, qui assumpta religione Mahumetica in unum conspirarunt imperium, quod quidem in Sa- racenis labefactatum in gente Ottomannica vires resumpsit anno Christi 1292.

## 9:15
V. 15. And the four Angels were released, who had been prepared for the hour, and day, and month, and year) Those three, at the urging of the Angels, handed over their forces to the fourth, that is, Titus, to besiege Jerusalem, and that at the time pre-signified by the Prophets of that time.

Prepared for all hours, every hour, every moment, is taken most simply in this way, and in this manner the interlinear Glosses, Flacius, Pareus, Winckelmann, Hœus, Gerhard, Gravius, and Dölingius understand an indefinite time; others desire a definite time, and collect the time of duration, so that one day may be 1000 years (Ps. 91), each day of the month may be each year, and thus a month may make 30 years; a year may denote a solar year, an hour 25 years, from which 1055 years emerge, the beginning of which they assign to the year of Christ 597, so the end will be 1653. Brightman counts from the year of Christ 1300 and establishes a span of 396 years, namely one year of 365 days and so many years, a month of 30, to which he adds a day or a year, so that that number of years may emerge which will end in the year of Christ 1696. But all those things are assumed precariously and without analogy; and therefore they are deservedly rejected by Pareus (and other Reformed). Both of whom, with Bullinger and Marloratus, agree with us concerning the burning zeal for doing harm, that they are always and at any hour prompt and prepared for it.

That they should kill the third part of men) Namely, of the Jerusalemites by battles and famine before the city was captured.

The vision does not sound of a third part of the City, but simply of the men, that is, of the whole world. Which, however, is to be understood not mathematically, but morally. For it is not precisely a third part of men that has been lost to Mahometanism, but about a fifth according to the Englishman Edward Brerewood in his 'Enquiries touching the diversity of religions', ch. 14. A great multitude of men was signified, which might seem to be a third part of the world. Or the third part of men is to be understood as the word 'men' was accepted before in v. 4, specifically, of the sealed, namely the faithful: Or also, as Pareus, the third part of the armies which the Christian leaders opposed to the Turks, the greater part of whom subsequently perished in slaughter. Then the third part of the citizens, of whom many thousands were subsequently slaughtered in the Turkish wars or led away into miserable slavery. In that one war which they call holy, it is gathered from William of Tyre that two hundred million were slaughtered by the Turks in not many years. Hardly eleven hundred million Turks are read to have perished in the same war. Thirdly, a third part of the Christian Churches was at least devastated and overturned by the same. For where once most ample Churches flourished in Palestine, Syria, Egypt, Asia, Armenia, Thrace, Pontus, Mysia, Bosnia, etc., there today Mahometan blasphemies dominate. Scarcely ruins of Christianity remain. Finally, a third part of the provinces of the Christian world was slaughtered, snatched away, and subjugated by the Turks within three hundred years. Mahomet I alone took away two empires and four kingdoms from the Christians. Throughout the entire maritime Africa, Egypt, Arabia, Babylon, Mesopotamia, both Armenias, Palestine, Syria, Asia, Thrace, and Greece, these enemies now dominate far and wide. Although Christians sometimes won victories over the Saracens and Turks, yet they were light if we consider the multitude of the enemies. Much more grievously did the Saracens and Turks afflict the Christians, and took away from them the greatest part of Asia and Africa. In the year of Christ 1453, Mahomet, Emperor of the Turks, having conquered Constantinople, the imperial seat of the Greeks, took away two empires and four kingdoms from the Christians, whence his successors poured into Hungary and occupied it, except for small remnants, made Mysia, Servia, and other regions subject to their law, and now have extended the borders of their empire toward all regions of the world, and dominate with impunity throughout the entire maritime Africa, greater and lesser Asia, Arabia, Egypt, Babylon, Mesopotamia, Armenia, Palestine, Syria, Greece, Thrace, etc., says B. Gravius.

Latin:

V. 15. Καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες Ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμέ- νοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν, καὶ μῆνα, καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν) Tres illi, Angelis im- pellentibus, quarto, id est Tito, copias suas tradidere ad obsidenda Hierosolyma, idque tempore præsignificato per ejus temporis Prophetas.

Parati in omnes horas, alle Stunde, alle Augen- blick, ita simplicissime accipitur, & hoc modo tem- pus indefinitum intelligunt Glossæ interlin. Flacius, Pareus, Winckelmannus, Hœus, Gerhardus, Gra- vius, Dölingius; Alii tempus definitum volunt, & tempus durationis colligunt, ut dies unus sit 1000. annorum Psal. XCI. singuli mensis dies anni singuli sint, adeoque mensis faciat 30. annos; annus sola- rem annum notet, hora 25. annos, unde prodeunt anni 1055. quorum initium assignant annum Chri- sti 597. terminus ergo erit 1653. Brigtmannus nu- merat ab anno Christi 1300. & spatium constituit 396. annorum, nimirum annum unum 365. die- rum id & tot annorum, mensem 30. quibus diem addit vel annum, ut numerus ille annorum prodeat, qui finientur An. Christi 1696. Sed illa omnia pre- cario, & citra analogiam assumuntur; ideoque me- rito a Pareo (& aliis Reformatis) rejiciuntur. Qui uterque cum Bullingero, & Marlorato nobis annuit, de ardente nocendi studio, quod semper & quavis hora ad id prompti sint & parati.

Ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσι τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων) Hierosolymita- rum nempe pugnis & fame ante captam urbem.

Non de parte tertia Urbis, sed simpliciter τῶν ἀνθρώπων, hominum, hoc est, totius orbis sonat visio. Quæ tamen non Mathematice, sed mora- liter intelligenda. Non enim præcise tertia ho- minum pars Mahometismo perdita est, sed quinta circiter secundum Eduardum Brerevvrodum Angl. in sua investigata religion. c. 14. Significata fuit magna hominum multitudo, quæ pars tertia orbis videri queat. Aut intelligenda pars tertia homi- num, prout vox hominum antea v. 4. accepta est specialiter, signatorum, fidelium nempe : Vel etiam, ut Pareus, tertia pars exercituum, quos Duces Chri- stiani Turcis opposuerunt, quorum subinde major pars cæsa interiit. Deinde tertia pars civium, quo- rum subinde in bellis Turcicis multa millia cæsa vel in miseram servitutem abducta fuere. Bello unico illo, quod sacrum vocant, ex Wilhelmo Tyrio colli- guntur a Turcis cæsa non multis annis bis millies centena millia. Turcarum vix undecies centena millia eodem bello interiisse leguntur. Tertio tertia pars minimum Ecclesiarum Christianorum ab iis- dem vastata atque eversa. Ubi enim olim florebant amplissima Ecclesiæ in Palæstina, Syria, Ægypto, Asia, Armenia, Thracia, Ponto, Mysia, Bosnia &c. ibi hodie Mahumetana blasphemiæ dominantur. Chri- stianismi vix rudera supersunt. Deniǵ tertia pars provinciarum orbis Christiani intra trecentos an- nos a Turcis cæsa, erepta, subjugata. Solus Mahometh primus duo imperia & quatuor regna Christianis ade- mit. Per universam Africam maritimam, Ægyptum, Arabiam, Babylonem, Mesopotamiam, Armeniam utramque Palæstinam, Syriam, Asiam, Thraciam, Græciam longe lateq́ dominantur nunc isti hostes. Quamvis Christiani aliquoties victorias de Sarace- nis & Turcis reportarunt, tamen leves eæ fuerunt, si hostium consideremus multitudinem. Multo gra- vius Saraceni & Turcæ afflixerunt Christianos, iisq́ maximam Asiæ & Africæ partem ademerunt. A. C. 1453. Mahometh Turcarum Imperator expugna- ta Constantinopoli imperiali Græcorum sede, duo im- peria & quatuor regna Christianis ademit, unde ejus successores in Hungariam effusi, eam exceptis exi- guis reliquiis occuparunt, Mysiam, Serviam, ali- asque regiones sui juris fecerunt, & nunc versus omnes mundi plagas imperii sui fines extenderunt, ac per universam Africam maritimam, Asiam ma- jorem & minorem, Arabiam, Ægyptum, Babylonem, Mesopotamiam, Armen. Palæstin. Syriam, Græciam, Thraciam &c. impune dominantur, ait B. Gravius.

## 9:16
V. 16. And the number of the armies of the horse were myriads of myriads) He says this, that besides those legions there was a huge cavalry, not only of legionaries, who according to Roman custom were present with the legions, and of the auxiliary troops by which the battle line was protected, but also from the allies, that is, from the cities of Syria, from Antiochus King of Commagene, from Sohemus of the Ituraeans, from the Arabs and others, and from Agrippa the Younger, who held Galilee with certain neighboring regions, and from other nations, which by sending aid in rivalry, were preparing favor for themselves with the new Prince and his son. See Josephus, Jewish War V. 6. and Tacitus, Histories V. There is here a hypallage of 'the horse' for 'the horses'. Otherwise, when the Greeks wish to speak of cavalry, they say 'the horse'. Myriads of myriads (רבו רבין) is accepted to signify a huge number, as above in V. 11.

I heard the number of them) I heard the number recited, as if from a military roll.

Latin:

V. 16. Καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν ςρατευμάτων τοῦ ἵππου μυριά- δες μυριάδων) Hoc dicit, præter illas legiones ingentem fuisse equitatum, non tantum legionariorum, qui Romano more legionibus aderant, & alarium quibus acies protege- batur, verum etiam a sociis, id est, a Syriæ civitatibus, ab Antiocho Comagenorum Rege, a Sohemo Iturzorum, ab Arabibus aliis & ab Agrippa Juniore, qui Galilæam cum vi- cinis quibusdam regionibus tenebat, & ab aliis gentibus, quæ certatim missis auxiliis, gratiam sibi apud novum Prin- cipem ejusque filium parabant. Vide Josephum Belli Judaici V. 6. & Tacitum Historiarum V. Est hic ὑπαλλαγὴ τοῦ ἵππου pro τῶν ἵππων. Alioqui equitatum cum volunt dicere, Græci dicunt τὸν ἵππον. Μυριάδες μυριάδων רבו רבין receptum ad significandum numerum ingentem, ut supra V. 11.

Ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν ἀυτῶν) Audivi recitari numerum, velut ex matricula militari.

## 9:17
V. 17. And thus I saw the horses in the vision) I myself also in the vision beheld the equestrian troop, corresponding to such a number.

Twenty thousand thousands, that is, two millions, a finite number for an infinite one, Dan. VII, 10. Thus indefinitely Blessed Luther: Many thousand times thousand. For we admit that an innumerable multitude is denoted. Some explain it as referring to the Goths, Vandals, and Huns, whose King Attila was called the scourge of the world, who led with him a numerous army, through which they devastated everything. For Cotterius, the horses with the riders make one subject. Ticonius, Primasius, Lyra, the Glossa Ordinaria, Thomas, Ribera, and Cluverus define the riders as evil spirits; Andreas defines the horses as evil men; Nicolai, Hoë, and Döling define them as barbarian nations. We understand these specifically as referring to the Turks and Saracens.

And those sitting upon them having breastplates fiery and hyacinthine and brimstone-colored) They had breastplates, according to the variety of the nations, of various color, flame-colored, violet, pale. Linen for many nations is made of flax. Livy is a witness in books IX and XXXI. Festus in the word 'Legio', and Suetonius in 'Galba'. Alexander also used such, according to Plutarch. I interpret the sulfurous breastplates as pale, just as Martial called sulfurous things pale.

And the heads of the horses as the heads of lions) the jaws of the horses are bloodstained, such as a lion’s after devouring cattle.

And out of their mouths proceedeth fire and smoke and brimstone) The word ὡς is understood. The situation was such as if fire, smoking and sulphurous, were proceeding from the mouths of the horses. Thus he poetically describes the fire-darts, which the horsemen, full of sulphur, resin, bitumen, tow, and the oil which is called incendiary, were hurling to set fire to the towers of Jerusalem. Valerius Flaccus, describing Titus engaged in this very matter, that is, in the siege of Jerusalem, depicts him thus: Solymo nigrantem pulvere fratrem Spargentemque faces, & in omni turre furentem.

By the fiery and sulphurous breastplates it is signified that those armies are about to set on fire and devastate everything with flames, fire, and sulphur. Sulphur can also be referred to their lusts, on account of which they approve of polygamy. What? That the Alcoran, which proceeded from the mouth of Mahomet, breathes nothing else than wars and effusions of blood, blasphemies against Christ, corruptions of heavenly doctrine prefigured by smoke, and lusts prefigured by sulphur. By smoke, Thomas, Flacius, Nicolai, Winckelmannus, Gerhardus, Cluverus, Döling, Napeirus, Pareus, and Szegedinus understand false doctrine and darkness. Concerning the stench of errors, Lyra and the Glossa Ordinaria; concerning foul and fetid impurity, Thomas, Nicolai, Cluverus, Osiander, Flacius, Szegedinus, Winckelmannus, Gerhardus, Döling, and the Vinarienses.

Latin:

V. 17. Καὶ ὕτως εἶδον τὲς ἵππες ἐν ὁράσει) Ipse etiam in viso conspexi agmen equestre, tanto numero congruens.

Vicies millena millia, hoc est, duo milliones, nu- merus finitus pro infinito, Dan. VII, 10. Ita inde- finite B. Lutherus: Viel tausendmal tausend. No- tari enim innumeram multitudinem admittimus. Nonnulli de Gothis, Vandalis ac Hunnis, quorum Rex Attila mundi flagellum dictus, qui numero- sum secum duxerunt exercitum, per quem omnia devastarunt, explicant. Cotterio equi cum equiti- bus unum faciunt suppositum. Equites Spiritus malos Ticonius, Primasius, Lyra, Glossa Ordin. Thomas, Ribera, Cluverus, Equos homines malos Andreas; barbaras gentes Nicolai, Hoë, Döling. definiunt. Nos in specie de Turcis, & Saracenis hæc intelligimus.

Καὶ τὲς καθημένως ἐπ᾽ ἀυτῶν ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνες καὶ ὑακινθίνες καὶ θειώδεις) Loricas habebent, pro gentium varietate, coloris varii, flammeas, violaceas, pallidas. Linea multis gentibus e lino. Testis Livius libr. IX. & XXXI. Fe- stus in verbo, Legio, & Suetonius Galba. Usus tali & Ale- xander teste Plutarcho. Sulphureas loricas interpretor pal- lidas, sicut pallentia sulphurata dixit Martialis.

Καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων) rictus equorum fanguinolenti, qualis leoni post devoratas pe- cudes.

Καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον) Subauditur ὡς. Ita res se habebat quasi ab ore equorum ignis fumigans & sulphureus procederent. Ita Poëtice describit falaricas, quas plenas sulphure, resina, bi- tumine, stuppis, & oleo, quod incendiarium dicitur, jacie- bant equites, ad incendendas Hierosolymorum turres. Va- lerius Flaccus, in hac ipsa re, id est, in Hierosolymorum oppugnatione versantem Titum sic describit: Solymo nigrantem pulvere fratrem Spargentemque faces, & in omni turre furentem.

Per loricas igneas & sulphureas significatur, quod exercitus isti flammis, igne ac sulphure omnia sint incensuri ac devastaturi. Sulphur etiam re- ferri potest ad libidines eorum, ob quas polyga- miam probant. Quid? quod Alcoranus, qui ex ore Mahamedis prodiit, nihil aliud spiret, quam bella, & effusiones sanguinis, blasphemias contra Christum, corruptelas doctrinæ cœlestis per fu- mum, & libidines per sulphur præfiguratas. Fu- mum de doctrina falsa tenebris Thomas, Flacius, Nicolai, Winckelmannus, Gerhardus, Cluverus, Döling, Napeirus, Pareus, Szegedinus intelligunt. De fœtore errorum Lyra, Glossa Ordin. Thomas, Nicolai, Cluverus de impuritate fœda & fœtida Osiander, Flacius, Szegedinus, Winckelm. Gerhard. Döling. Vinarienses.

## 9:18
Verse 18.

By these three plagues was the third part of men killed, by the fire and by the smoke and by the brimstone (Ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἐκ τῦ πυρὸς καὶ τῦ καπνῦ καὶ τῦ θείυ). There is a synthesis in τρίτον and ἀπεκτάνθησαν, such as: they cut the part into pieces. He says that very many of these defenders perished by those fire-darts and other ignited missiles.

Τῦ ἐκπορευομένῦ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν) which seemed to proceed from the mouths of the horses, because those missiles were flying before the mouths of the horses, just as if they were proceeding from their mouths.

We have already stated how those plagues proceeded from the impure mouth of Mahomet; the sulphur of lusts, the smoke of false doctrines, and the fire of wars. Some, in Gravius, interpret them as referring to engines of war and horrendous cannons, from which fire, smoke, and sulphur are ejected, by which the Turks storm the most secure cities and fortifications, and often reduce them to ashes.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

Ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἐκ τῦ πυρὸς καὶ τῦ καπνῦ καὶ τῦ θείυ) Est synthesis in τρίτον & ἀπεκτάνθησαν, qualis: Pars in frusta se- cant. Hos dicit defensores plurimos illis falaricis aliisque missilibus ignitis interiisse.
