Non datus est Johanni funiculus, quia non erat restituendum templum, sed metiendum alia de causa. καὶ ἑἱστήκει ὁ ἄγγελος λέγων· ἔγειραι καὶ μέτρησον τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ) Omnia hæc sunt μετωνυμικὰ. Templum voca- tur arca illa, in qua steterant adytum & basilica היכל & דביר. {Similis locutio: Omnis homo fumat Neptunia Troja, καὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον] Locum altaris victimarii, quod ho- locaustorum dici solet, καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας ἐν αὐτῷ) Id est, locum in quo po- pulus Deum adorare folebat, Atrium Israelitarum. Metiri autem jubetur Johannes hoc spatium, quia Deus id ob me- moriam veteris sanctimoniæ intactum erat servaturus à Gen- tibus. Inter excidium & Adriani tempora, nihil Hieroso- lymis memoratu dignum acciderat. Paucæ turres in mo- numentum victoriæ aliquæ factæ erant à Tito, apud quas pri- mum poni tentoria, deinde & domus aliquæ strui cœ- perunt.

## 11:2
Verf. 2. And the court which is outside the temple cast out, and do not measure it] This latter is an exposition of the former. And so he said 'cast out', which Latin surveyors call 'exclude'. See Frontinus. But he calls 'the court which is outside' here every space outside the footprints of the temple. For 'hatzer', which the Greeks translate as 'court', is to the Hebrews everything that is covered by no roof. The Latins would well call it an area.

Prophecy follows the preparation, which does not deal with the former things, but as something NEW, predicts other things. Therefore, the Grotius gloss is not appropriate, that it is still a question of the destruction of the temple; concerning which there was neither talk in the preceding parts, nor is there in this place. For that measurement of the temple does not concern the material Jerusalem temple, as far as its meaning is concerned, but the spiritual temple of God, the Church, 1 Tim. III. 15. That had already been destroyed, and it was not to be trampled underfoot from this time only for 42 months, that is 1260 days, but until the consummation of the age, because the destruction was not determined until the end of the world after so many years for the Anti-Christ, namely at the coming of Christ, 2 Thess. II. And Luke XXI. 24 connects the trampling of Jerusalem by the Gentiles with the fulfillment of the time of the Gentiles, and the consummation of the age. For the Anti-Christ was to dwell in the temple, and was to profane it, 2. Thess. II. 4. nay, was to trample it underfoot. Therefore, it is a question of the Anti-Christian persecution, which was to afflict the holy city, the Church, by the authors who are accomplices of the Anti-Christ, who are not unjustly compared to the Gentiles on account of their ignorance of God, idolatry, and ferocity. But the inner place of the temple, namely the sanctuary, was to be measured entirely, so that it might be understood that little of it remained which pertains to the worship of God: namely, that a small space would remain for the faithful, namely the temple (called ἐξοχικῶς, the holy of holies) and the altar and the place of worship. This is a symbol of the paucity of the faithful, as spiritual priests, says Blessed Gerhard. Doubtless, it is free from doubt that the Jerusalem temple was a type of the Church, the house of the living God, of which the standard for measuring with a reed or cord is compared to Scripture, Gal. 6, 16. Ps. 19, 5. Rom. 10, 18. To others also, the blessed Winckelmann, the measuring of the temple, the altar, and those who worship in it signifies the sanctioning of decrees, canons, and laws by which the Church is bound and constrained, so that conformity of ceremonies is required everywhere. Therefore, the reed given to John is the very laws by which the Church is, as it were, measured and constrained: Those who read τὴν ἔξωθεν instead of ὴν ἔσωθεν understand by the inner court the faithful, because they are to be cast out under the Anti-Christ. But the Latin copies have the court which is outside (without) the temple, cast out, which Grotius chooses. However, the former reading, which is also that of the blessed Luther, is to be preferred: whether the sense of Grotius prevails concerning the passing over in the measurement, or the common one concerning the ejection of the faithful, as being those whom the Roman Anti-Christ holds unworthy of measurement and excludes with his anathemas, as much as in him lies, not only from the Church, but from heaven itself. The blessed Cluverus says: Some copies, he says, read ἔσωθεν. Whichever you approve, it makes no difference. For the temple is most properly called the holy of holies with the holy place. And thus the court is not inside but outside the temple, whether you take it as the court of the Priests or of the people, 2 Kings 21, 5. 2 Chron. 4, 9. For he declares that the Church is most truly said to be built to the exact standard of the Divine Word. But the court, in which the crowd of the people is always seen, is occupied by such as are inept and unworthy to be measured by that standard. And therefore he does not wish that to be counted even as a part of the true temple any longer, but to be cast out as unclean. The blessed John is commanded, says Pareus, to institute the measurement, that is, by this type to announce beforehand that it would come to pass that after the Anti-Christ has occupied, devastated, and oppressed the temple of God, Christ, with the measuring reed given to his witnesses, will measure it again for the purpose of repairing and restoring it whole. This command, therefore, concerning the measuring of the devastated temple is a prophetic promise concerning the reforming of the Church devastated and oppressed by the Western Anti-Christ. And afterwards: He is commanded also to measure the altar, namely the golden one, from whose four horns he had heard the voice, chap. 9, 13; that was a type of Christ. What, you ask? Is he commanded to measure Christ? Indeed. Christ had been driven from his possession under his own name by the Anti-Christ, the faith of Christ oppressed, and liberty turned into miserable servitude. The altar of Christ will therefore be measured when the faith of Christ is vindicated from the perfidy of the Anti-Christ, and Christian liberty from his tyranny. The altar can indeed be understood synecdochically as the whole of worship. But why it should be taken as the golden altar of incense rather than the bronze altar of burnt offerings will be understood presently. Thus also my Anonymous: And the altar, that is, Christ. Which Anonymous is John Purvey. Others explain the election of the court-dwellers, who do not worship Christ but perform sacred rites for the Anti-Christ. Concerning the Anti-Christ, who is understood by the court which is outside being cast out, or by being insinuated as cast out from the fellowship of the faithful, the Anonymous interprets; Pareus and most others interpret it as the court of the Priests, who have the lower choir, being cast out, or preaching that it is to be cast out. What is added, for it is given to the nations, contains the cause; therefore that priestly court, that is, the Priests, ought to be cast out, because the clergy will become gentile, or will degenerate into Paganism; not indeed by open profession, but by masked idolomania and a gentile life. Anonymous: Because it is given to the nations, that is, because they themselves have been made conformable to the unbelieving nations.

which Eusebius says was colonized from the race of the Gentiles, that is, filled with men who were not Jews, namely for the most part. For the same Eusebius teaches us in his Chronicle that it was also granted to Jews to dwell there before the end of the war with Barchocheba.

καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν πατήσουσι μῆνας τεσσαράκοντα δύο.] Jerusalem was accustomed to be called the holy city, as we saw in Matt. IV. verse 5. The same name is now given to Aelia, because it was situated in the same places, and retained the old name among the Jews. It is called holy, however, because it had once been consecrated to God, in a manner of speaking such as we have in Matt. XXI. 31. Understand πατήσουσι as they will profane, namely by the temple built to Jupiter Capitolinus, not on Moriah, where the temple had been, but on Zion. For thus the Hebrews more accurately than Dion. The Hebrew רמס, which is translated as to tread, signifies to trample contemptuously, as in Isa. XXVIII. 3. Forty-two months, or one thousand two hundred and sixty days, make almost three years and a half: which number we shall often have in this apocalypse. For it was famous from Daniel; because the most grievous evils under Antiochus lasted for that much time, the city being also profaned at that time. God, however, willed that similar evils be included in an equal space of time, so that he might show that he now has the same care for the pious that he had of old. This time, however, ought to be thought of as from the time the temple of Jupiter Capitolinus began to be built, until the Jewish movement under the leader Barchocheba. Dion also teaches us that some time intervened between these. It seems, however, that God chose the time of three years and a half not only in the affairs of Antiochus, but also in the drought which was in the time of Elijah, James V. 17, because that makes the other half of the week of years, which is a perfect time. And thus God brings salvation to his own in the midst of the years, as Habakkuk speaks, chapter III. verse 2. Thus also Christ is believed to have been freed from his labors after three years and a half.

Aelia, in which the temple of Jupiter was, never had the name of a holy city; nor did the Jews inhabit the same to such an extent; who indeed even then had claimed the name of a holy people. Grotius acknowledges that it was for the most part occupied by the Gentiles. Nor was it trodden by the Gentiles; but rather, by the judgment of GOD, it was so shaken by an earthquake that not a stone was found upon a stone; workmen also, under Julian the Judaizer, intending to rebuild the city, were burned by fire either sent down from heaven, or, as Nazianzen and Sozomen report, bursting forth from the foundations of the temple, and being terrified by a sign shining in the sky through crosses that had fallen from heaven, impressed in a dark color upon the garments of the Jews, which could in no way be washed off, they were forced to desist from the work.

Moreover, the 42 months, according to the calculation approved in the ἀποκαλύψει, do not make three years and a half, but 1260 years. Neither did Grotius find those three years and a half, nor does he mention any interval of time indefinitely from Dio.

B. Cluverus conveniently expressed the sense of the prophecy: It is given to the Gentiles: The guilty are the unclean and uncircumcised, whoever they may be, to whom it was otherwise not permitted to tread the holy court of God. For it is a singular blessedness to dwell in the courts of the Lord (Psalm 65:5), and Nehemiah cast out the goods of Tobiah the Ammonite from the courts, chapter 13, verse 7. But here the court is given to the Gentiles, that is, it is permitted to the unclean and those who have the likeness of Gentiles to tread those places which ought to have been open only to pure and true Israelites. This is, power is given to the Anti-Christ and his followers to sit and move about in the courts of the house of the Lord and to perform those duties which the pious and holy Ministers of GOD ought to perform. And hence Paul says that the Anti-Christ will sit in the temple of GOD, and will exalt himself in its place and stead, 2 Thess. 2, verse 4. Thus Andreas, Aretas, the Gloss, Anselm, and others explain this very thing, from whom not a few have collected, or have followed those who collected it.

The court (says the gloss), that is, the false Christians, who pretend to be the Church and deny it by their deeds, cast out, that is, show by excommunicating that they are on the outside. Because it has been given to the nations, that is, they have been made conformable to the nations. And they will trample the holy city, that is, they will persecute the Church gathered to live by the law. For forty-two months, namely, the whole time of the preaching of the Anti-Christ. Those nations, therefore, are those who either did not know God at all, or even if they knew Him, are nevertheless assimilated by their deeds and superstitions to those who are ignorant. Hence Christ commands that a brother disobedient to the Church be held as a Gentile, Matt. XVIII. And Peter judges those to be worse who, if they have acknowledged GOD, and having acknowledged Him, deny Him again, 2 Pet. II. To this belong those things which the Roman Catholics have in common with the nations, such as that they converted the ancient Pantheon into a temple of all the Saints; that instead of God they adore their Saints and Divines, often no better than those whom the Gentiles adored; that they worship their supreme Pontiff similarly to them; that they purify men with holy water similarly to them; that they believe in purgatorial fires similarly to them; that they impose celibacy on certain orders of priests and vestal virgins similarly to them; that they consecrate wines, meats, and other foodstuffs similarly to them; similarly to them they celebrate various ἀποθεώσεις (apotheoses) of deceased men; similarly to them they doubt about salvation; finally, similarly to them they live impiously. Conf. here Polyd. Vergil. de invent. rer. B. Nicolaus Hunnius de Apostas. Rom. Eccl. B. Gerh. in Conf. Cathol. The Pope, says B. Cluverus again, took for himself the keys of the kingdom of heaven with his Scribes and Pharisees and shut it, as much as he could; he himself neither entered, nor permitted those who were about to enter to go in, Matt. XXIII. 13. And just as Manasseh once erected idols to the hosts of heaven in the courts of the house of God, so the Pope drew temples and basilicas for the Saints dwelling in heaven, and so filled the visible Christian world with their worship that men often could scarcely find the true worship of God. Beautifully Augustine or Ticonius on this passage: They are the court who seem to be in the Church and are on the outside, whether they are heretics or ill-living Catholics. Those who are excluded, and those to whom it will be given, both will trample it. Conf. Is. I. verse 12. Rev. XI. verse 8. chapter XVII. concerning the holy city, which has become a harlot. Regarding the trampling of the city, Pareus has it thus: It is to be observed that the Angel speaking these things, that is, Christ, is alluding to His own words: Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled: by which the siege, conquest, and destruction of the city and temple by the Romans was predicted. To be trampled, therefore, is to be occupied, plundered, and devastated in a hostile manner: which had happened to Jerusalem not long before then by the soldier of Titus. Now, just as Jerusalem was a type of the Christian Church, so the trampling of Jerusalem by the Roman nations was a type of the trampling of the Church by the similarly Roman nations. For Rome, just as it had been Jerusalem, so also the Church will be κακὸν κακῆς πῆμα (an evil bane of an evil thing). What is clearer than that the Church is to be occupied, trampled, and devastated by the Roman Anti-Christ and his retinue? But that does not apply here, except by way of allusion.

As for the time of the 42 months, it coincides with the period of the reign of the beast, chap. XIII. 5, of the witnesses of the Lord according to the 1260 days, Rev. XI. 3, of the nourishment of the Church in the desert, Rev. XII. 6, and verse 14, where it is computed by a time (a year of 360 days), times (two prophetic years of 720 common years), and half a year (mystical, that is, in the common way of speaking, 180), which joined together make 1260 lunar years, each of which contains 12 months of 30 days or 360 days, such as occur in Gen. VII. 11, 24, ch. VIII. 3, 4. Hugo, however, undoubtedly wished to gratify the Papists with that short term, they imagining that the Anti-Christ would reign for three years and a half. Although indeed some of the ancients also inclined toward that, before the event, the best interpreter of prophecies, taught them more correctly: yet even under the Papacy there were not lacking those who began to acknowledge the truth here, as the Waldenses are a testimony and example, who around the year of Christ 1160 acknowledged that the Roman Church had begun to fail from the time of Sylvester, and had become the Babylonian harlot, and that the Roman Pontiff was the Anti-Christ (concerning which see Rainerus in his Summa, Jacobus Rebirius, Jodocus, Coccius T. I. thes. 7. art. 6.), in which same century, around the times of Hildebrand, the Bishop of Florence taught publicly that the Anti-Christ had already come and was publicly ruling in the Church, which Aventinus J. U. Ann. page 552 is the author that most people then preached about Hildebrand; indeed, before him in the year 1010, Aretas (others refer him to the eighth or ninth century) in his Commentary on the Apocalypse wrote that after the fall of Constantine the Great, the Anti-Christ had emerged. Guilh. Aurifex, the prophet of the Albigensians, in Coccius T. I. th. I. 7. art. 17, around the year of Christ 1250, called the Pope the Anti-Christ and Rome Babylon. Around A. C. 1306, Petrus Johannes the Minorite testified that the Pope was the mystical one, as Bellarm. reports in his Chron. Around the year of Christ 1320, Nilus, Archbishop of Thessalonica, wrote against the Primacy of the Pope and taught that the Anti-Christ had already been born long ago in the Church of GOD, and that he was the Pope of ancient Rome. Around the year of Christ 1340, Johannes de Rupescissa taught that the Roman Church was the harlot, the Pope the minister of the Anti-Christ, and the Cardinals pseudo-prophets, and he was attempting to prove all his sayings through the Apocalypse and the ancient books of the holy Prophets. Around the year of Christ 1352. John Wycliffe taught that the Pope is not only not the vicar of Christ, but is even the Antichrist, which cause of his condemnation Coccius brings forward in T. I. th. I. 7. art. 17. and l. IV. Dial. cap. 32. He testified that it seems to many that among all the sufferings which Christ endures from the injuries of wayfarers, this one is among the greatest, that He permits the Antichrist to reign for so long, and to seduce so many people. Around the year of Christ 1380, Matthias of Paris wrote a lengthy book about the Antichrist, and taught that he is the Roman Pontiff. That commentator on the Apocalypse whom we praised earlier, John Purvey, who around the year of Christ 1390 flourished: Whether, he says, these years are only usual ones, or much longer, God knows, since this is hidden from every Doctor explaining this text: But that the whole time of the persecution of the Church by the Antichrist will be much longer, experience itself teaches, and for that reason Daniel designates the time of the Antichrist indefinitely by a time and times and half a time, by this conveying that how long in total the Antichrist ought to reign cannot and should not be defined by any Doctor, with spiritual revelation withdrawn. The same man also testified that he holds the Pope to be the Antichrist, John Huss, Martyr, burned at Constance in the year 1415, in Anatom. Anti-Chr. c. 42. This principle, he says, is to be embraced catholically, that no wayfarer is more suited than the Roman Pontiff, to be the principal vicar of Satan and the preeminent Anti-Christ. The Jesuit Joseph Acosta, in his work on the last times, book II, chapter 8, acknowledges that no man knows for certain the precise duration of the Anti-Christ's reign, and therefore those three years and a half signify nothing but the extremity, the summit, or the pinnacle of his kingdom. We have taught, regarding Daniel VII. 8, that the passage of Daniel concerning the time, times, and half a time, to which Grotius appeals, is not to be taken grammatically but mystically concerning 1260 years, and that it does not treat of Antiochus, but of the Anti-Christ. Nor does the opinion of the Papists hold together, as Pareus shows, since what they imagine their Anti-Christ must accomplish, he cannot accomplish in the space of three years and a half any more than a snail can crawl over the entire globe in the space of three days. He must be acknowledged as the Messiah by the Jewish people dispersed throughout the entire world: He must sit in the Jerusalem temple, which has lain in ashes for so many centuries: He must slaughter three Kings of Egypt, Libya, and Ethiopia, and subjugate seven other Kings: he must restore Rome, burned by those ten Kings, and sit there as Monarch after the Pope has been cast out: he must persecute and destroy the Christian religion throughout the whole world, and finally make the Church and the empire of the whole world subject to his power, etc. Who, I ask, would dream that these things will happen in less than four years? What Mercuries, therefore, will the Anti-Christ send to suddenly announce and persuade the Jews, dispersed throughout the whole world, of the arrival of their Messiah? He will, forsooth, rebuild in three days the temple which Solomon, with all materials prepared, could barely complete in seven years, and which Zerubbabel could barely repair in forty-six years; the Anti-Christ himself, at four years old, will surely expel the Turk from Syria, the Persian from the East, the Khan from the North, Prester John from the South, and the whole universe in a moment. What is more trifling? The Papists themselves admit that if the 3 1/2 years are to be understood precisely, the time of the last day would be certain, which they acknowledge is repugnant to the words of Christ; Didacus Stella on Luke XXI, p. 263; Viguerius, Theological Institutions, chapter 21; Barradius, Vol. III, book 9, chapter 6. And since the Anti-Christ is only to be abolished by the coming of Christ to judgment, how will those witnesses lie unburied for three days and a half, and revive on the fourth, that is, after the last day itself? Hentenius, preface to the Commentary of Arethas on the Apocalypse. It would not be possible for him (the Anti-Christ) to obtain so many kingdoms and provinces in so short a time. Thus, 42 months are attributed to the beast of Apocalypse XIII. 5, by which some among the Papists understand the Roman empire; Bellarmine, book III, On the Roman Pontiff, chapter 15, section 'respondeo'. But neither the old nor the new Roman empire lasted only for 42 months or 3 1/2 years. Indeed, Johannes Ferus on Matthew chapter XXIV, and Gagnejus on 2 Thessalonians II, hold that the kingdom of the Anti-Christ began immediately in the times of the Apostles. There are certainly not lacking those who, even if they acknowledge that designation of times to be mystical, nevertheless explain it otherwise. Alcafar himself rejects the common opinion of the Papists concerning three ordinary years and a half. Justin Martyr, in his Dialogue with Trypho, observes that the Jews understood 'a time' as one hundred years, 'times' as two hundred, and 'half a time' as 50 years, so that 350 years would emerge. Raphaël Eglinus, in his Epilysis p. 327, posits that the beast arose under Julian in the year of Christ 376; he extends the first 'time' until the establishment of the Eastern and Western Anti-Christ; he produces the 'times' to the year 1456, with Greece and the entire Constantinopolitan empire occupied, and the power of the East increased; he terminates the 'half' in the year 1656, and thus divines that the second power of the beast will be destitute. Which opinion has already been convicted of falsehood by experience. B. Philippus Nicolai, book II, On the Kingdom of Christ, chapter 6, refers the beginning to the year of Christ 360, when Pope Damasus contended with Ursatius for the Pontifical seat with drawn swords; but he places the end in the year 1625, to which B. Gravius also assents, distinguishing the two witnesses from that, and the three years and a half assigned to them, of which later. Almost all of our people, with B. Luther and the Magdeburg Centuriators, understand 1260 years, which B. Cluverus calculates from Leo the Great, that is, from the year of Christ 440, because in the Council of Chalcedon, Leo's legates, according to Evagrius book II, chapter 14, extolled Leo thus: 'Therefore the most holy and most blessed Archbishop of great and ancient Rome, Leo, through us and the present council, together with the most blessed and all-praiseworthy Apostle Peter, who is the rock and base of the Catholic Church and the foundation of the orthodox faith, has stripped him of all Episcopal dignity and has utterly deposed him from all Priestly ministry.' Thus the 1260 years would end with the year of Christ 1700. He sets 'a time' at the year of our Lord 800, when the Anti-Christ had already attained so much power that he dared to create a new Emperor of the West, Charles, having plainly scorned the majesty of the Greek Emperor; and he terminates 'a time' in the year 1529, when B. Luther first began to attack the recognized Anti-Christ. Finally, they observe that those three Popes, under whom these conversions of affairs happened, bore the same name by some fate. For Leo I founded the Papacy. Leo III, by crowning Charles, increased the Papacy; Leo X undermined the Papacy (by his indulgences and the excommunicatory wars of B. Luther): 'Perhaps also,' he says, 'some fourth one will destroy the Papacy.' Most, however, hold that the 1260 years are to be counted from the beginning of the Papacy, from the death of Gregory the Great, when Phocas the Caesaricide confirmed the title of Oecumenical Bishop with Boniface III, to which B. Luther in Vol. VIII of the Jena edition, page 218, assents, so that the end is the year of our Lord 1866. Yet the days, which will be shortened for the sake of the elect, are uncertain. Nor is the year of the beginning of the Anti-Christ so certain that the year of the final end of the world can be defined with it with certainty.

PART II. Concerning the killing of the two witnesses of Christ.

Latin:

Verf. 2. κὴ τὴν αὐτὴν τὴν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ναοῦ ἔκβαλε ἔξωθεν, κὴ μὴ αὐτὴν μετρήσῃς] Posterius hoc prioris est expositio. Itaque ἐκβάλλειν ἔξω dixit, quod Latini menfores, extracludere. Vide Frontinum. Αὐλὴν vero τὴν ἔξωθεν hic vocat omne spatium extra templi vestigia. Nam חצר quod αὐλὴν ver- tunt Græci, Ebræis id omne, quod tecto nullo tegitur. A- ream dicerent bene Latini.

Præparationem sequitur Prophetia, quæ non de prioribus agit, sed tanquam NOVA, alia prædicit. Non ergo convenit Grotiana glossa, quod adhuc de templi excidio agatur; de quo ne- que in præcedentibus sermo fuit, neque hoc lo- co est. Nam illa dimensio templi, non concer- nit templum materiale Hierosolymitanum, quan- tum ad significationem, sed spirituale Dei tem- plum Ecclesiam, 1. Tim. III. 15. Illud jam de- structum erat, neque ex hoc tempore tantum per 42. menses, hoc est 1260. dies conculcandum erat, sed ad consummationem usque seculi, quia non nisi cum fine mundi post tot annos Anti- Christo definitum fuit excidium, sub adyentum nempe Christi, 2. Thess. II. Et connectitur Luc. XXI. 24. conculcatio Hierosolyma è gentibus futura cum adimpletione temporis gentium, & consumma- tione seculi. Anti-Christus enim in templo habita- turus erat, illudque profanaturus, 2. Thess. II. 4. imo conculcaturus. De persecutione ergo Anti- Christiana, Ecclesiam sanctam civitatem afflictura, autoribus Anti-Christi complicibus, qui Ethnicis ob ignorantiam Dei, idololatriam & ferociam non injuria comparantur, agitur. Interior vero templi locus, sanctuarium nempe, omnino dimetiendus erat, ut intelligeretur, parum de eo superare, quod ad cultum Dei pertineat: Exiguum nempe spatium reliquum fore pro fidelibus, templo nempe(ἐξοχικῶς dicto, sancto fanctorum) & altari & loco adorandi. Symbolum hoc est paucitatis fidelium, tanquam spi- ritualium Sacerdotum, ait B. Gerhard. Nimirum templum Hierosolymitanum typum fuisse Eccle- siæ, domus Dei viventis, dubitatione vacat, cujus mensurandæ norma calamo vel funiculo compa- rata est Scriptura S. Gal. 6, 16. Psal. 19, 5. Rom. 10, 18. Aliis etiam B. Winckelmanno, mensuratio templi, altaris, & adorantium in eo significat decretorum, canonum & legum sanctionem, quibus Ecclesia alli- gatur & adstringitur, ita ut passim requiratur ce- remoniarum conformitas. Proinde calamus Johan- ni datus sunt ipsæ leges, quibus Ecclesia quasi mensu- ratur & constringitur: Qui pro voce τὴν ἔξωθεν le- gunt ὴν ἔσωθεν, per atrium interius intelligunt fi- deles, quod ejiciendi sint foras sub Anti-Christo. Sed Latina exemplaria habent atrium, quod est fo- ris (extra) templum ejice foras, quod eligit Grotius. Præferenda autem prior lectio, quæ etiam B. Lu- theri est: sive sensus Grotii obtineat de præteritio- ne in dimensione, sive communis de ejectione fide- lium, utpote quos indignos habet dimensione, & excludit anathematismis suis, quantum in ipso est, non Ecclesia tantum, sed cœlo ipso Romanus An- ti-Christus. B. Cluverus: Nonnulla exemplaria, inquit, legunt ἔσωθεν. Utrumvis probes, nihil refert. Nam templum propriissime dicitur sanctum sancto- rum cum sancto. Et sic atrium non est intra sed extra templum sive de Sacerdotum, sive de populi atrio ac- cipias, 2. Reg. 21. 5. 2. Chron. 4, 9. Nam Ecclcsiam ve- rissime dictum ad exactam Verbi Divini amussim es- se extructam declarat. Atrium autem, in quo fre- quentia semper populi conspicitur, à talibus occupari, qui norma ista mensurari inepti indigniq́; sunt. Ideo- que illud ne computari quidem pro veri templi par- te vult amplius, sed foras velut immundum ejici. Ju- betur B. Johannes, inquit Pareus, dimensionem in- stituere, hoc est, typo hoc prænunciare, futurum, ut postquam Anti-Christus templum Dei occupaverit, vastaverit, oppresserit, Christus calamo mensorio te- stibus suis dato illud rursus dimetiatur ad reparan- dum & integrum restituendum. Est igitur manda- tum hoc de mensurando templo vastato prophetica pro- missio de reformanda Ecclesia per AntiChristum Oc- cidentalem vastata & oppressa. Et postea: Jubetur & dimetiri altare, nempe aureum, ex cujus quatuor cornibus audiverat vocem, cap. 9, 13. id erat typus Christi. Quid, inquis? Num jubetur mensurare Christum? Sane. Erat Christus sub nomine suo pulsus possessione sua ab AntiChristo, fide Christi oppressa, li- bertate in servitutem miserabilem conversa. Mensura- bitur igitur altare Christi, quando fides Christi à perfidia AntiChristi: libertas Christiana à tyrannide ejusdem vindicabitur. Potest quidem altare de toto cultu Synecdochice intelligi. Cur vero de aureo thy- miamatum potius, quam de æneo holocaustorum alta- ri accipiendum sit, mox intelligetur. Sic etiam Ano- nymus meus: Et altare, id est, Christum. Qui Ano- nymus est Joh. Purveus. De electione atriensium, qui non adorant Christum, sed sacra AntiChristo fa- ciunt, alii explicant. De AntiChristo, qui atrium quod foras est, intelligatur ejiciendo, vel è con- sortio fidelium ejecto insinuando Anonym9, de a- trio Sacerdotum, qui chorum inferiorem habent, Romanensium ejiciendo vel prædicando, quod ejiciendum sit, interpretatur Pare9, & alii plerique. Quod additur, nam datum est gentibus, causam con- tinet; ideo atrium illud sacerdotale, hoc est, Sacer- dotes ejici debere, quia clerus fiet gentilis, seu de- generabit ad Paganismum; non utiq́; aperta professio- ne, sed fucata idolomania & vita gentili. Anonymus: Quia datum est gentibus, hoc est, quia ipsi confor- mes facti sunt gentibus incredulis.

quam ex ἀλλοφύλων γένους ἀποικηθεῖσαν ait Eusebius, id est im- pletam hominibus non Judæis, nempe ex maxima parte. Nam & Judæis ibi habitare concessum ante finem belli cum Barchocheba idem Eusebius Chronico nos docet.

καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν πατήσουσι μῆνας τεσσαράκοντα δύο.] πόλις ἁγία dici solebat Hierosolyma, ut vidimus Matth. IV. vers. 5. Idem nomen datur nunc Æliæ, quia in iisdem lo- cis erat reposita, & apud Judæos vetus nomen retinebat. Di- citur autem sancta, quia Deo sacrata olim fuerat, locutione qualem habemus Matth. XXI. 31. πατήσουσι intellige profa- nabunt, nempe templo structo Jovi Capitolino, non in Moria, ubi templum fuerat, sed in Sione. Ita enim Ebræi accuratius quam Dion. רמס Ebræum, quod πατεῖν verti- tur, significat contemptim conculcare, ut Esa. XXVIII. 3. Menses quadraginta duo, sive dies mille ducentæ & sexa- ginta, faciunt ferme tres annos cum dimidio: quem nu- merum sæpe habebimus in hac apocalypsi. Celebris enim erat ex Daniele; quia per tantum temporis durarunt gravis- sima sub Antiocho mala, urbe etiam tunc profanata. Vo- luit autem Deus mala similia pari temporis spatio includi, ut eandem sibi nunc esse piorum curam ostendat, quæ olim fue- rat. Tempus autem hoc putari debet, ex quo strui cœpit templum Jovis Capitolini, ad motum usque Judaicum, du- ce Barchocheba. Aliquod tempus inter hæc intervenisse e- tiam Dion nos docet. Videtur autem non in rebus Antio- chi tantum, sed & ἐν τῇ ἀνομβρίᾳ, quæ fuit Eliæ tempore, Jac. V. 17. Deus elegisse tempus trium annorum & dimi- dii, quia id facit partem alteram hebdomadis annorum, quod est tempus perfectum. Atque ita Deus salutem suis af- fert in medio annorum, ut loquitur Abac. III. vers. 2. Sic & Christus a laboribus suis liberatus creditur post tres annos & dimidium.

Ælia, in qua templum Jovis fuit, nunquam no- men habuit civitatis sanctæ; neque inhabitarunt eandem adeo Judæi; qui vero tum etiam sancti po- puli nomen duxerant. Maximam partem eam a gentibus occupatam fuisse, agnoscit Grotius. Nec calcata ea a gentibus; sed potius, judicio DEI, terræ motu ita concussa, ut nec lapis super lapi- dem inveniretur; operarii etiam sub Juliano Ju- daizante, urbem reædificaturi, igne sive cœlitus de- misso, seu ut Nazianzenus & Sozomenus referunt, ex templi fundamentis emicante adusti, fignoque in cœlo fulgente per cruces cœlitus delapsas, vesti- bus Judæorum atro colore impressas, quæ nulla- tenus ablui potuerint, absterriti ab opere, desiste- re coacti sunt.

Menses autem XLII. juxta computum in ἀποκαλύψει probatum non tres annos cum di- midio, sed 1260. annos efficiunt. Neque tres illos annos cum dimidio invenit Grotius, neque e Dione aliquod temporis intervallum indefinite commemorat.

Sensum Prophetiæ commode expressit B. Clu- verus: Datum est gentibus: Sontes sunt immundi & incircumcisi quicunque, quibus alias atrium Dei sanctum calcare non licebat. Nam singularis bea- titudinis est, habitare in atriis Domini (Psal. 65, 5.) & Nehemias extra artium projecit Tobiæ Ammo- nitæ munera, cap. 13. vers. 7. At hic atrium genti- bus datur, scilicet immundis & gentilium instar habentibus permittitur, ut calcent ea loca, quæ puris tantummodo & veris Israelitis patere debe- bant. Hoc est, Anti-Christo & ejus sectatoribus datur potestas sedendi & versandi in atriis do- mus Domini eaque obeundi munia, quæ pios sanctosque DEI Ministros obire oportebat. At- que hinc Paulus ait, Anti-Christum sessurum in templo DEI, & vice locoque ejus se exaltatu- rum, 2. Thessal. 2. vers. 4. Ita explicant hoc i- psum Andreas, Aretas, Glossa, Anshelmus & re- liqui, ex quibus collecta est, vel collectam sunt sequuti non pauci.

Atrium (inquit glossa) id est falsos Christianos, qui se Ecclesiam simulant & factis abnegant, ejice, id est, excommunicando esse foris ostende. Quoniam da- tum est gentibus, id est, conformes facti sunt gentibus. Et civitatem sanctam conculcabunt, hoc est, Ecclesi- am ad jure vivendum congregatam persequentur. Mensibus quadraginta duobus scilicet toto tempore praedicationis Anti-Christi. Gentes ergo illi sunt, qui vel plane Deum non noverant, vel etiamsi eum noverunt, factis tamen & superstitionibus illis igno- rantibus assimilantur. Proinde Christus fratrem Ecclesiae inobedientem pro Ethnico jubet habere Matth. XVIII. Et Petrus deteriores judicat, qui si agnoverint DEUM, agnitumque rursus abnegent 2. Petr. II. Quo faciunt ea, quae Romano-Catho- lici, cum gentibus communia habent, ut quod Pan- theon antiquum converterunt in templum omnium Sanctorum; quod loco Dei adorant Sanctos & Di- vos suos, saepe nihilo meliores illis, quos adorabant Ethnici, quod similiter illis suum colunt summum Pontificem: quod similiter illis expiant aqua lu- strali homines: quod similiter illis credunt ignes purgatorios: quod similiter illis certis Sacerdotum ordinibus virginibusque vestalibus imponunt caeli- batum: Quod similiter illis consecrant vina, car- nes, aliaque cibaria: Similiter illis varias celebrant hominum defunctorum ἀποθεώσεις; similiter illis dubitant de salute; Similiter denique illis impie vi- vunt. Conf. hic Polyd. Vergil. de invent. rer. B. Nicolaus Hunnius de Apostas. Rom. Eccl. B. Gerh. in Conf. Cathol. Sumsit sibi, inquit iterum B. Cluverus, claves regni caelorum Papa cum Scri- bis & Pharisaeis suis & occlusit illud, quantum potu- it, ipse nec ingressus est, nec ingressuros introire per- misit, Matth. XXIII. 13. Et quemadmodum olim Manasses idola erexit exercitibus caelorum in atriis domus Dei: sic Papa Sanctis in caelo habitantibus templa & basilicas extraxit, eorumque cultu sic implevit visibilem orbem Christianum, ut verum Dei cultum saepe vix homines invenirent. Pulchre Augustinus vel Ticonius in h. l. Ipsi atrium sunt, qui in Ecclesia videntur esse, & foris sunt sive haere- tici sive male viventes Catholici. Qui excludun- tur, & quibus dabitur, utrique calcabunt eam. Conf. Es. I. vers. 12. Ap. XI. vers. 8. cap. XVII. de civitate sancta, quae meretrix facta. De concul- catione urbis ita habet Pareus: Observandum, Angelum ista loquentem, hoc est Christum allude- re ad sua ipsius verba: Jerusalem calcabitur à gen- tibus, usquequo impleantur tempora gentium: quibus praedicta fuit obsidio, expugnatio ac ever- sio urbis & templi per Romanos. Calcari igitur est hostiliter occupari, diripi, vastari: quod non multo ante tunc Hierosolymae à Titi milite contige- rat. Jam sicut Hierosolyma typus fuit Ecclesiae Chri- stianae, sic calcatio Hierosolymae per gentes Roma- nas facta, typus fuit calcationis Ecclesiae per gentes similiter Romanas futurae. Roma enim sicut fu- erat Hierosolyma, sic etiam Ecclesia erit κακὸν κακῆς πῆμα. Quid apertius, quam Ecclesiam occupan- dam, calcandam, vastandamque à Romano Anti- Christo, ejusque satellitio. Sed id huc non facit, nisi allusive.

Quod ad tempus XLII. mensium, coincidit id cum periodo regni bestiae, cap. XIII. 5. testium Domini secundum dies 1260. Apoc. XI. 3. nutri- tionis Ecclesiae in deserto Apoc. XII. 6. & vers. 14. ubi computatur per tempus (annum 360. dies) tempora (duos annos propheticos 720. annos vulgares) & dimidium annum (mysticum, ho- est, vulgari loquendi modo, 180.) qui conjun- cti efficiunt 1260. annos lunares, quorum quis- que 12. menses, 30. dierum vel 360. dies continet, quales Gen. VII. 11. 24. c. IIX. 3. 4. occurrunt. Gratificari autem curto illo termino Pontificiis, sine dubio, voluit Hugo, comminiscentibus per tres annos cum dimidio regnaturum Anti-Chri- stum. Quanquam vero eo etiam veteres non- nulli inclinarent, antequam eventus, optimus Interpres vaticiniorum, eos rectius edocuerit: tamen etiam sub Papatu non defuerunt, qui ve- ritatem hic agnoscere cœperint, ut testimonio & exemplo sunt Waldenses, qui circa ann. Chri- sti 1160. Rom. Ecclesiam inde á Sylvestro cœpis- se deficere, ac fieri meretricem Babylonicam, & Pontificem Romanum Anti-Christum agno- verunt (quo de vid. Rainerus in summa, Jaco- bus Rebirius, Jodocus, Coccius T. I. thes. 7. art. 6.) quo eodem seculo circa Hildebrandi tempo- ra Episcopus Florentinus publice docuit, Anti- Christum jam venisse, & in Ecclesia publice do- minari, quod plerosque de Hildebrando tum prædicasse, Aventinus J. U. Ann. pag. 552. Au- tor est, imo ante eum Anno 1010. Aretas (alii ad octavum, vel nonum seculum eum referunt) in Comment. super Apoc. scripsit, post occasum Constantini M. Anti-Christum emersisse. Guilh. Aurifex, Albigensium Propheta, apud Coccium T. I. th. I. 7. art. 17. circa annum Christi 1250. Pa- pam dixit Anti-Christum, Romam Babylonem. Circa A. C. 1306. Petrus Johannes Minorita Papam esse mysticum, Bellarm. in Chron. refe- rente testatus est. Circa ann. Christi 1320. Ni- lus Archi-Episcopus Thessal. scripsit contra Pa- pæ Primatum, & Anti-Christum jam olim in Ec- clesia DEI natum esse docuit, eumque Papam esse antiquæ Romæ. Circ. ann. Christi 1340. Jo- hannes de Rupescissa docuit, Rom. Ecclesiam esse meretricem, Papam Ministrum Anti-Christi, Cardinales Pseudo Prophetas, probaturumque se, agebat, omnia sua dicta per Apocalypsin, & veteres libros S. Prophetarum. Circa annum Christi 1352. Johannes Wiclefus docuit, Papam non solum non esse vicarium Christi, sed etiam Anti-Christum, quam causam condemnationis ejus affert Coccius T. I. th. I. 7. art. 17. & l. IV. Dial. cap. 32. testatus est, multis videri, quod inter omnes patientias, quas Christus habet de injuriis viatorum, hæc una de maximis sit, quod permittat Anti-Christum tamdiu regnare, & tan- tum populum seducere. Circa Ann. Christi 1380. Matthias Parisiensis prolixum librum de Anti- Christo scripsit, eumque Pontificem Romanum esse docuit. Ille in Apocalypsin commentator, quem antea laudavimus Johann. Purveus, qui cir- ca ann. Christi 1390. floruit: Utrum, inquit, an- ni isti sint solummodo usuales, sive multo longiores, Deus novit, quoniam hoc absconditum est ab omni Doctore, exponente textum istum : Sed quod to- tum tempus persecutionis Ecclesiæ ab Anti-Christo multo longius erit, docet ipsa experientia, & pro- pterea designat Daniel tempus Anti-Christi in- definite per tempus & tempora, & dimidium temporis, per hoc tradens, quod quantum in toto debeat regnare Anti-Christus, non debeat, nec possit subducta spirituali revelatione ab aliquo Doctore de- finiri. Testatus etiam idem est, se Papam habe- re pro Anti-Christo, Joh. Huss. Martyr. An. 1415. Constantiæ exustus in Anatom. Anti-Chr. c. 42. Istud principium est, inquit, Catholice amplecten- dum, quod nullus viator est aptior Romano Ponti- fice, ut sit vicarius principalis Satanæ & præcipuus Anti-Christus. Joseph. Acosta Jesuita de temp. novissim. l. II. c. 8. cognoscit, neminem homi- num certo scire præcisam regnaturi Anti-Christi durationem, ac proinde tres illos annos cum di- midio nihil nisi regni ejus extremitatem, summi- tatem, aut fastigium significare. Locum Danie- lis de tempore, temporibus & dimidio tempo- ris, ad quem provocat Grotius non Grammati- ce sed mystice accipiendum esse de 1260. annis, nec de Antiocho agere, sed de Anti-Christo ad Dan. VII. 8. docuimus. Neque secum consi- stit Papistarum sententia, ut ostendit Pareus, quo- niam quæ fingunt Anti-Christum suum efficere de- bere, spatio trium annorum cum dimidio eum con- ficere non magis est possibile, quam cochleam tridui spatio totum terrarum orbem perreptare. Debet à gente Judaica per universum orbem dispersa pro Messia agnosci: Debet sedere in templo Hierosoly- mitano, quod tot secula jacet in cineribus: Debet tres Reges Ægypti, Libyæ, Æthiopiæ trucidare, septem alios Reges subjugare: debet Romam à de- cem illis Regibus exustam instaurare, ibique Pontifi- ce excusso tanquam Monarcha sedere: Christia- nam religionem toto orbe persequi & delere, Eccle- siam denique & totius orbis imperium suæ potesta- tis facere, &c. Quis quæso hæc per febrim somniet quadriennio non integro futura? Quos igitur An- ti-Christus mittet Mercurios, qui Judæis toto orbe dispersis adventum sui Messiæ repente nuncient, per- suadeant? Templum scilicet triduo ræædificabit, quod Salomon ex omni materia præparata Septennio ab- solvere, Zerubabel quadraginta sex annis repa- rare vix potuit, Turcam Syria, Persam Oriente, Chamum Septentrione, Preto Johannem, Austro universo Anti-Christus ipse quadrimulus momento nimirum expellet. Quid nugacius? Fatentur ipsi- met Papistæ, si præcise anni 3 1/2. intelligendi cer- tum fore tempus diei novissimæ, quod Christi verbis repugnare agnoscunt Didacus Stella ad Luc. XXI. p. 263. Viguerius Instit. Theol. cap. 21. Barradius T. III. l. 9. c. 6. Et quum Anti-Chri- stus per adventum Christi ad judicium demum abolendus sit, quomodo tres dies, cum dimidio, jacebunt testes illi inhumati, & quarto reviviscent, hoc est, post ipsum diem novissimum. Hentenius præfat. in Comment. Aretæ in Apoc. Non esset possibile, ipsum (Anti-Christum) tam parvo tem- pore tam multa regna & provincias obtinere. Ita bestiæ Apoc. XIII. 5. per quam nonnulli è Ponti- ficiis intelligunt Romanum imperium, Bellarm. l. III. de Rom. Pontifice c. 15. §. respondeo, tri- buuntur 42. menses. At neque vetus, neque no- vum Rom. imperium tantum per 42. menses vel 3 1/2. annos duravit. Imo concidit Joh. Ferus ad c. XXIV. Matthæi, & Gagnejus in 2. Thess. II. re- gnum Anti-Christi statim Apostolorum tempo- ribus cœpisse. Non desunt sane, qui designa- tionem illam temporum, etsi mysticam agnoscant, aliter tamen explicent. Alcafar ipse communem Papistarum opinionem de tribus annis vulgaribus cum dimidio reprobat. Justinus Martyr. Dial. cum Tryphone Judæos tempus de centum annis, tempora de ducentis, dimidium de 50. annis intel- lexisse ut prodirent 350. anni observat. Raphaël E- glinus in Epilysi p. 327. exortam ponit bestiam sub Juliano Anno Christi 376. tempus primum exten- dit usque ad stabilitum Anti-Christum Orienta- lem, & Occidentalem; tempora producit ad annum 1456. occupata Græcia, & Constantinopolitano imperio universo, auctam potentiam Orientalis, dimidium terminat anno 1656. eoque secundam destituram potestatem bestiæ divinat. Quæ senten- tia per experientiam jam falsitatis convicta est. B. Philippus Nicolai l. II. de regn. Christ. c. 6. initium refert ad an. Christi 360. quo Damasus Papa cum Ursatio decertavit de sede Pontificia strictis gla- diis; finem vero collocat in annum 1625. cui et- iam annuit B. Gravius duorum testium ab illo di- stinguens, & tres illos annos cum dimidio ipsis assignatos, de quo postea. Nostrates pene omnes cum B. Luthero, Centuriatoribus Magdeburg. an- nos intelligunt 1260. quos B. Cluverus computat à Leone M. hoc est, anno Christi CCCCXL. quia in Concilio Chalcedonensi Leonis Legati apud Evagrium l. II. c. 14. ita Leonem extulerunt: Idcirco sanctissimus & beatissimus Archi-Episcopus magno & antiquæ Romæ Leo per nos & præsens con- cilium cum beatissimo & omni laude celebrando A- postolo Petro, qui est petra & basis Catholicæ Ecclesiæ, & fidei orthodoxæ fundamentum spoliavit omni di- gnitate Episcopali, & omni Sacerdotali ministerio prorsus abdicavit. Finirentur ita anni 1260. cum anno Christi 1700. Καιρὸν sinit anno Domini 800. quo tantum jam potestatis consecutus erat An- ti-Christus, ut novum Imperatorem Occidentis creare auderet Carolum, spreto plane Impera- toris Græci fastigio; Καιρὸς vero terminat Anno 1529. quo B. Lutherus primum cœpit Anti-Chri- stum agnitum impugnare. Denique observant tres illos Pontifices, sub quibus istæ rerum conversi- ones accidere, idem fato quodam nomen ges- sisse. Leo enim I. fundavit Papatum. Leo III. coronato Carolo auxit Papatum, Leo X. labefacta- vit, (indulgentiis suis & bellis excommunicatori- is B. Lutheri) Papatum: Forte etiam, inquit, quartus aliquis perdet Papatum. Plerique autem 1260. annos ab initio Papatus inde à morte Gre- gorii M. cum Bonifacio III. Phocas Cæsaricida ti- tulum Episcopi Oecumenici confirmavit, B. Luthe- ro T. IIX. Jen. pag. 218. annuente, numerandos esse, ut finis sit annus Domin. 1866. Dies tamen, qui abbreviabuntur propter electos, incerti sunt. Neque adeo certus annus initii Anti-Christi, ut certo definiri possit cum ejus termino annus mun- di finalis.

PARS II. De duorum testium Christi occisione.

## 11:3
Verse 3.

And I will give to my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and sixty days] The Hebrew idiom δώσω καὶ προφητεύσουσι for δώσω προφητεύειν: I will give that they may do those things which are of the Prophets. A similar locution in Jerem. IX. 1, Psal. LV. v. 6, CXIX. 34. When it began to be founded with Elias, from the multitude having been led to that point, two kinds of Christians arose, sprung from the Jews and from the foreigners: who, since they spoke a different language, the Jews Hebrew, the foreigners Greek, as the most common, which Paul also used when writing to the Romans, necessarily formed two assemblies or Churches. But because all universities form a certain mystical person, therefore they are often wont to be described under the names of one person, as the Roman people in Florus, the Jewish people under the name of a woman in the Prophets: sometimes also under the name of a son, as Ose. XI, Jerem. XXXI. 20. Here those assemblies are called two witnesses, because they bore an illustrious testimony to God. And because the Christians made from the Jews opposed themselves to the vices of other Jews, just as Moses had done of old, therefore they are compared to Moses: And because those called from the Gentiles opposed idolatry; therefore they are compared to Elias, who had also destroyed idolatry of old. Moreover, those two witnesses are said to prophesy, because after the manner of the Prophets they explained the commands of God to all, with the gift of prophecy also being present. The time, however, expressed here terminates, as we have said, at the beginning of the Jewish movement, which was under Hadrian.

Witnesses, who oppose themselves for Christ to the Anti-Christian nations, to the Roman Pontiff, and to their partners, are given and stirred up by God, Jer. III. 15. Joh. XV. 27. Eph. IV. 11, et seqq. Two are mentioned, not because there will precisely be only two, as the Papists trifle after Moses and Elijah, whom Grotius has gratified in this matter, D. Hoe, D. Gerhard, D. Danhauer, Nic. Hunnius, Cluverus, and also Rivetus think: to Zach. IV. v. 14 is manifest. That, however, which Grotius chatters about Elijah and two peoples is entirely ἀπόῤῥητον (ineffable); because the discourse was not about Gentiles by nature, but by the similarity of the last verse of the preceding chapter. But the witnesses of the truth are all those who truly resisted the Anti-Christ, who was a Gentile regarding his doctrine and pagan life, among whom two stood out in almost every age, namely, in the seventh century, Gregory the Great. the Roman Pontiff himself, but not yet marked with the character of the beast, inasmuch as he rather held the title of universal Bishop to be Anti-Christian, l. V. ep. 34. l. VI. ep. 30. and from that title being usurped by John, Bishop of Constantinople, he concluded that the times of the Anti-Christ were near, with Eulogius, Bishop of Antioch, not denying it, to whom he wrote for that reason, l. IV. epist. XXXVI. In the eighth century, Charlemagne condemned the decrees concerning the worship of images and asserted the Catholic faith at the Council of Frankfurt. In the ninth, John Damascene opposed himself to the Anti-Christ, along with a few others in Asia and Thrace oppressed by the tyranny of the patrons of the Anti-Christ. Add Gunther and Tetgaud, the Bishops of Cologne and Trier, in their letters to Pope Nicholas I, in Aventinus, l. IV. annal. p. 255. In the tenth, Ansbertus taught correctly concerning justification through faith and free will against the Papacy, along with Smaragdus and Theophylact. See Catalogus Testium Veritatis, l. XI. Claudius, Bishop of Turin, a strenuous opponent of images, as was Huldericus, Bishop of Augsburg, an opponent of the celibacy of priests, and Arnulphus, Bishop of Orleans, who around the year 991 designated the Anti-Christ. In the eleventh, Gaubertus, Archbishop of Reims (afterwards raised to the Papal height by magic arts, called Sylvester II, in the synod of Reims), complained that Rome had poured forth monstrous darkness; and especially concerning the malefactor (Boniface), a horrendous monster in the Papacy surpassing all mortals in wickedness, he said that the Anti-Christ was sitting in the temple of God. To whom add in that century Peter, Bishop of the Church of Pavia, and Rodulphus Glaber of this century, and Arethas in the Apocalypse, a writer on the rise of the Anti-Christ. In the twelfth, the Waldenses, or the poor of Lyons, called the Pope the Anti-Christ and the Roman Church the purple-clad harlot, according to Coccius, T. I. Thesaur. l. 7. art. 6. By which also Honorius of Autun understood the apocalyptic prophecies concerning the beast and Babylon, concerning the Pope and the Roman Church. See Catalogus testium veritatis, cent. XII. c. 7. p. 39. 5. In the thirteenth, Joachim the Abbot, in his commentary on Isaiah, Ap. XVII, says: the woman gilded with gold fornicates indiscriminately with the princes of the earth. That is the Roman Church, which, having been transformed into Babylon by the confusion of life, commits adultery. William of Saint-Amour, a Parisian theologian, celebrated by Bellarmine as a learned and pious man, openly taught that the Pope is the Anti-Christ and Rome is Babylon, in his book on the collation of benefits, etc., which Lawrence the Englishman, Master, did not hesitate to defend by publishing a defense. William the Goldsmith, in Coccius T. I. l. 7. art. 17, called the Pope the Anti-Christ and Rome Babylon. Eberhard, Bishop of Salzburg, in the Council of Regensburg, before the Emperor and the ecclesiastical and political princes, made a profession in a public speech, which is in Aventinus, l. VII. annal. pag. 420: Hildebrand, one hundred and seventy years ago, was the first to lay the foundations of the Anti-Christian empire under the guise of religion. In the fourteenth, Peter John of the diocese of Biren in Aquitaine, a Minorite, in Bernhard Lutzelburg's Catalogus Hæreticorum, Guido of Perpignan on heresies, and Coccius, said that the Pope is the mystical Anti-Christ, and that Babylon, that great harlot, is the Roman Church. John Wycliffe, who wrote more than 100 volumes, and his disciple Walter Brute, taught that the Pope is not only not the vicar of Christ, but is even the Anti-Christ. In the fifteenth, John Huss, martyr, in Anatomia Anti-Christi, as testified by John Cochlaeus, l. III. Hist. Hussit. and Coccius, said that the Pope is the vicar of the Anti-Christ, that beast of which it is written in the Apocalypse; indeed, in Anatomia Anti-Christi c. 42, he professed that he is the principal Anti-Christ. Jerome Savonarola of Florence, burned by the order of Alexander VI, said that the Pope retains neither the life nor the doctrine of Christ, because he attributes more to his indulgences and little traditions than to the merits of Christ, and therefore that he is the Anti-Christ. In the sixteenth, the two Martins, B. Luther and B. Chemnitz. In the seventeenth, B. Aegidius Hunnius and B. John Gerhard contributed their primary efforts to destroying the Papacy, and therefore they deserved the name of those two witnesses above others.

But the Grotian witnesses are neither approved by the Papists themselves, nor do they agree in any way. For Hadrian did not found Aelia before the Jewish war was finished and Bar Kokhba was killed, so that he never saw it, let alone entered it and ruled there, which will be taught by no historian. Baronius indeed says that many Christians were killed by him, but that this happened in Jerusalem, no historian will prove. Nor could Aelia be called the holy city, which was trampled by the Gentiles. For it was full of profane Gentiles. Nor was it then deformed by Sodomitic lust and the oppression of the saints, so that it should have been marked by their name. Certainly, nothing is read about Aelia in the times of Hadrian. Furthermore, the holy city was trampled by the Gentiles for three years and a half; that does not fit Aelia, in whatever way the years are taken. The ethnic Gentiles were converted up to Constantine the Great. And how could the temple then be measured, which did not exist in the time of Hadrian? How could the outer court of the temple be trodden under foot, when it had been cut off by Hadrian's new city, Aelia? Whence also will it be taught that Aelia had two bishops? Who, by the Papists and therefore not even by Hamann, who sides here with Grotius, are not admitted in one city: nor are they found in the catalogue of either Eusebius or others, who recount the bishops of Jerusalem, where bishops up to Hadrian occur from the Jews and speaking only the Hebrew language. Nor did the proclamation in Aelia last for only 3 1/2 years: It lasted until Constantine. Nor can those years be shown in Hadrian. For in the eleventh year of Hadrian the war of Bar-Cochba began, and in the 20th it was finished. To say nothing of the fact that no such miracles were performed in Ælia in the days of Hadrian, nor did the city begin to flourish in turn after 3 1/2 years, or even after Barchochebam was crushed and the Jews were defeated. For the dominion of the Romans was continued, the idol of Jupiter Olympius was worshipped, and besides, the images of Venus and Adonis were religiously honored in the same place.

Although indeed Isidorus Clarius on ch. 4 of Zachariah, Catharinus on Gen. ch. 2, Gagnejus on this place and ch. 17 of Matthew, Jansenius in Conc. Ev. ch. 67, and others assent concerning Moses and Aelia, and Ludovicus ab Alcafar also brings forward Arboreus and Joachim the Abbot, as also Hilary on Matthew XVII, Ambrose on Luke IX, while Maldonado indeed quite boldly, according to Jesuit custom, pronounces on ch. XVII of Matthew, that John in the Apocalypse

c. XI. 3. 6. to write so openly that Moses and Elijah were to come, that no one could deny it not only without rashness, but not even without impudence: yet Lorinus in 2 Pet. 1.16 did not hesitate to contend about impudence with his associates in the same Jesuitical order. Maldonatus, he says, in c. XVII of Matthew. Truly, he considers the opinion opposed to Moses, which is far more common and truer, to be rash and impudent, and there are indeed not a few who prefer to interpret these two witnesses as Enoch and Elijah; to which opinion Alcafar brings Arethas, Ambrose, Haymo, Richard, Ansbert, Strabo, Hugh of St. Cher, Dionysius, Clarius, Vatablus, Ribera, Viegas, Suarez, part III, T. 2, disp. 55, sect. 2, Pamelius on Tertullian, Mendoza on that, Pererius in Pancil., Malvenda l. IX de Anti-Christo. Not to mention that others, according to Alcafar, explain it as two men indeed; but not of the time of the Anti-Christ: Of whom then? Either of the time of the primitive Church, who suspect it to be Christ and John, as Ubertinus de Casatis and Cittingerus: of those two priests of JESUS, and Ananus, (whom the Idumeans killed) as Caponsachius: of Pope Sylvester and Patriarch Mena fighting against the Eutychians, as Aureolus, Antoninus, Lyranus, Ederus, Lizarazus: Or of Francis and Dominic, as some do according to Cornelius à Lapide. Others accept it of the time of the Anti-Christ indeed, but not of two men, as Ticonius, Primasius, Beda, Hortulinus, Pannonicus. Others understand it neither of two men, nor of the time of the Anti-Christ: But either of all the ages of the Christian faith with Pannonicus, (as Thomas Aquinas in this place) who says that all preachers who are now and will be are designated by the two witnesses, who are therefore placed under a binary because they take what they preach from the two testaments: Or as Lyranus has it; because the Lord sent disciples in pairs to preach, to which Arias Montanus looks, who wants the two witnesses to be the law and prophecy: or finally (which is the opinion of Alcafar, to whom Grotius otherwise does not entirely disagree here) of two witnesses in the time of the primitive Church, whom he says truly represent the great wisdom and great holiness of the Ministers of the Gospel, assuming from chapter IV up to XI the discourse is about the way in which GOD conducted Himself with the Jews and peoples during the times of the primitive Church, and from chapter XII up to XX about the action of GOD with the Gentile people. Alcafar, however, refutes the opinion about Enoch and Elijah with Jerome ep. 148: about Enoch and Elijah, whom the Apocalypse reports will come, and are to die, is not a dispute of this time, since that whole book must either be understood spiritually, or one must acquiesce to fables; and he destroys its foundations. Finally, he prefers what Victorinus thought, that Jeremiah would come in the times of the Anti-Christ, and Blasius de Viegas and Sixtus Senensis l. I under the title of Irenaeus observe that this was the opinion of many, which Hilary Conc. XX in Matthew reports. Barradius, however, [argues] with many arguments and testimonies (Theophylact, Arethas, Hippolytus, Metaphrastes, Damascenus, Trapezuntius, Catharinus) that it ought to be probable, T. IV Concord. Evangel. l. IX. c. 4. that with Enoch and Elijah, John the Evangelist also would return from the earthly Paradise to these lands in the time of the Anti-Christ, and thus that two witnesses are not precisely understood here, which Lorinus, however, pronounces false regarding Jeremiah and John. Ticonius: Every suspicion of some, he says, who think these two witnesses are two men, is excluded. For how could the inhabitants of the earth rejoice over the death of two, when they were dying in one city, and send gifts to one another, if it is three days. Because before they rejoice over the death, they will be saddened by the resurrection. And how, I ask, does it fit for two bodies to be cast in the street of one city, and to be seen by all nations, peoples, and tongues? How can those who have already been admitted to the blessed vision of God, and no longer have mortal bodies 1 Cor. XV. 50, but glorified ones Luke IX. 31, and were translated so that they would not see death, be killed? Those who are witnesses here are soon called virgins. Two witnesses, 144,000 virgins. Witnesses by office, virgins by quality or adjunct: namely, incorrupt in purity and chastity, both of doctrine and of life, from the loves of the Babylonian whore. A great number teaches that there will not be few, a binary [teaches] few, but comparatively, with respect to the abundance of the Anti-Christians. Let Bellarmine go now and still judge it heresy or next to heresy to deny that Enoch and Elijah will not return in person for the conversion of the Jews, to be killed by the Anti-Christ.

And they shall prophesy 1260 days) Some understand the 1260 days vulgarly, others mystically. Grotius sides with them and with most Papists, and one of ours, but in another sense and with another intention, B. Gravius. Understanding by the beast the whole Romano-Papal kingdom, and the victory not spiritual but corporal, and the killing a persecution similar to that of the Evangelicals: whom it is helpful to hear speaking in his own words: In the year 1625, the Papists, most closely allied, handled bloody counsels, which in the following years, with the arms of the Evangelical Princes oppressed, obtained their effect. For the most noble provinces, cities, towns, and fortifications of the Evangelicals were occupied, partly stormed, partly destroyed and laid waste. An Anti-Christian reformation was undertaken throughout almost all of Germany, the public exercise of the Gospel or divine word was abrogated everywhere, with the Ministers and orthodox Doctors of the Church, and all Evangelicals who refused to adore the Anti-Christian idol, being driven into exile. This persecution of the Evangelical Church and the two witnesses lasted THREE YEARS and a HALF, that is, from the end of the year 1625 until about the year 30, to the greatest triumph and jubilation of the Papists, just as it is said in v. 10: And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them (namely, spiritually in their consciences through the refutation of Papal dogmas) that dwell on the earth, that is, earthly men and those who are wise in earthly things in the Pontifical kingdom. The events of the preceding years testify exactly that these things truly happened in this way. I add what it contains, for a full exposition of the sentence: And after three days and a half the Spirit of life entered into them. These things were fulfilled or began to be fulfilled in the year of Christ 1630, at which time, with the arrival of the northern lion, the power of the Leaguers was gradually weakened and diminished from day to day, and in the progress of time the public exercise of the Gospel or divine word was restored, with the mass-priests, Monks, and Jesuits, and their idol-mania and superstition, being expelled from the recovered Evangelical provinces and cities. Thus these two witnesses divinely recovered their former life and authority in the ecclesiastical heaven, and, God willing, they will declare that glory of theirs, recovered more and more hereafter, in the Church to the greatest sorrow and terror of the enemies of the Church. For from the end of the year 1629 that great earthquake begins, that is, the shaking and commotion of peoples and kingdoms through the din and tumult of arms, which at the same hour and at the same moment was stirred up with the beginning of the exaltation of the two witnesses, at which THE TENTH PART OF THE CITY (namely the Babylonian, or of the Anti-Christian kingdom) fell, verse 13. For by the arms of the King of the North and of the Evangelical Princes, the forces of the Leaguers were worn down in a short space of time, and the most noble and powerful regions and provinces of the Papists were occupied. Indeed, after the death of Leo, the Spanish power was also most strongly diminished and shaken, even amidst the various dissensions and war-movements of the Evangelical Princes, by the admirable counsel of God, so that it can truly be said that more than a tenth part of the Anti-Christian kingdom and power was reduced almost to nothing. But how long this commotion of the peoples is to last is not added in the text. Mr. Phil. Nicolai, on the Kingdom of Christ, book 2, from the words of verse 13, 'and in that hour there was an earthquake,' attempts to define a certain time, namely 20 years, to be finished about the year of Christ 1670, but that this hour is to be understood without mystery is declared above in table 12, from Apoc. IX, verse 15. For the Holy Spirit wishes to intimate that at the same time and point of the exaltation of the two witnesses this spiritual earthquake is to arise, which experience testifies has been fulfilled and is still being fulfilled. So he, in the year 1647. At which time indeed the earthquake was still lasting, but shortly after, quiet followed and universal peace. Furthermore, just as the rest is to be understood mystically, so here it is not fitting to adhere to the letter. The days are not natural but mystical: the victory is spiritual, not bodily: because it is of the witnesses of the truth, who conquer with the mouth, not with the sword, with the heavenly fire of the Spirit, not with the fire of the cannons of gunpowder. But these things proceed from the hypothesis of the blessed Phil. Nicolai, book II, on the Kingdom of Christ, that the period of the witnesses ought to begin from the contentions of Damasus and Ursatius concerning the Pontifical seat in Ammianus Marcellinus, book 27, to be finished in the year 1625, which is deduced from chapter XIV, 20, that sixteen hundred stadia are as many years, during which the hour of the harvest, 1/24th part of a day, which consists of a thousand years according to Moses, Psalm XC, and Peter, 2nd epistle III, which makes 41 2/3 years. All of which are assumed without proof. But those things which we brought forward before are more agreeable to the truth. Brightman takes it precisely as 3 1/2 years, and accommodates it to the Council of Trent, in which the Fathers similarly rejoiced for three years and a half over the trampled scriptures of the Old and New Testament (for these he makes the two witnesses). Which indeed had great probability. But whether the Spirit looked to this, I do not define, says Pareus. It is safer, the same continues, that we approach the opinion of those who understand three days and a half indefinitely as a short time, during which the reproach of the martyrs and the triumph of the enemies will last. It will scarcely be half a week. It is a matter of three or three and a half years, then the priests' dance will have an end. This circumstance of time is therefore introduced for the sake of consolation, which scripture everywhere suggests to the pious oppressed by the cross, from the brevity of calamities and the impending liberation, John XVI, verse 16, 2 Cor. IV, 7. Some of our own also observe, such as the blessed Cluverus, the histories of the Anti-Christian persecution of 3 1/2 years, namely lasting through the Council of Constance, in which Huss and Jerome of Prague were condemned, and from the year 1547, in which our faith was struck with anathema in the Council of Trent and its primary assertors, the Elector and the Landgrave, were captured, and matters were utterly desperate, up to the year 1550.

Παραβεβλημένοι σάκκους] in the habit of mourners, namely because they saw in the city consecrated to God an idol and most of the Jews becoming no better in such great evils.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

Καὶ δώσω τοῖς δυσὶ μάρτυσί με, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν ἡμέρας χι- λίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα] Ebræa locutio δώσω καὶ προφητεύ- σουσι pro δώσω προφητεύειν: Dabo ut faciant ea, quæ sunt Prophetarum. Par loquutio Jerem. IX. 1 Psal. LV. v. 6. CXIX. 34. Cum Ælia condi cœpit ex multitudine eo dedu- cta duo Christianorum genera extiterunt ex Judæis orta & ex alienigenis: qui cum diversa lingua loquerentur, Judæi Ebraica, alienigenæ Græca, ut maxime communi, qua e- tiam Paulus ad Romanos scribens usus est, necessario & du- os fecere conventus sive Ecclesias. Quia autem universita- tes omnes mysticam quandam personam faciunt, ideo sæpe solent sub personæ unius nominibus describi, ut populus Romanus apud Florum, populus Judæus sub fœminæ voca- bulo apud Prophetas: interdum & sub filii nomine, ut Ose. XI. Jerem. XXXI. 20. Hic deo illi conventus vocantur te- stes duo, quia illustre Deo testimonium præbebant. Et quia facti ex Judæis Christiani opponebant se aliorum Judæ- orum vitiis, sicut olim Moses fecerat, ideo Mosi comparan- tur: Et quia vocati ex gentibus idololatriam oppugnabant; ideo Eliæ comparantur, qui idololatriam & olim destruxerat. Dicuntur autem duo illi testes προφητεύσειν, quia Propheta- rum more Dei mandata explicabant omnibus accedente & prophetiæ dono. Tempus autem hic expressum termina- tur, ut diximus, in principio motus Judaici, qui fuit A- driano.

Testes, qui opponunt sese pro Christo gentibus Anti-Christianis, Pontifici Romano, & eorum consortibus, à Deo dantur, & excitantur, Jer. III. 15. Joh. XV. 27. Eph. IV. 11, seqq. Duo dicuntur, non quod præcise tantum duo futuri, ut post Pontificios de Mose & Elia nugantes, quibus hic gratificatus est Grotius D. Hoe, D. Gerhard. D. Danhauer. Nic. Hunnius, Cluverus item & Rivetus existimant: Sed quod paucis admodum in comparatione Para- statarum Anti-Christi Allusio ad Zach. IV. v. 14. manifesta est. Illud vero, quod garrit Grotius de Ælia duobus populis, ἀπόῤῥητον prorsus; quia non de gentilibus natura, sed similitudine vers. ult. cap. præcedentis sermo erat. Testes autem ve- ritatis universi, qui Anti-Christo vere gentili quo ad doctrinam, & vitam paganam, restiterunt, in- ter quos duo quovis fere ævo eminuere, nimirum secuto septimo Gregorius M. ipse Pontifex Roma- nus, sed nondum charactere bestiæ insignis, ut- pote qui potius titulum universalis Episcopi pro Anti-Christiano habuit l. V. ep. 34. l. VI. ep. 30. at- que ex eo à Johanne Constantinopolitano Episcopo usurpato propinqua esse tempora Anti-Christi collegit non abnuente Eulogio Episcopo Antio- cheno, ad quos eas de causa l. IV. epist. XXXVI. scripsit. Seculo octavo Carolus M. decreta de ima- ginum cultu damnavit, fidemque Catholicam in Francof. Concilio adseruit. Nono Joh. Damus An- tiChristo se opposuit, cum paucis quibusdam in Asia & Thracia oppressis tyrannide patronorum AntiChristi. Adde Guntherum & Tetgaudum Co- loniensem ac Trevirensem Episcopos in literis ad Nicol. 1. Pontif. Rom. apud Aventin. l. IV. an- nal. p. 255. Decimo Ansbertus de justitia per fi- dem & libero arbitrio contra Papatum cum Sma- ragdo & Theophylacto recte docuit, Vid. Cat. Test. Verit. l. XI. Claudius Taurinensis Episcopus strenu- us imaginum, ut & Huldericus Episcopus Augusta- nus cœlibatus Sacerdotum impugnator, & Arnul- phus Aurelianensis Episcopus, qui circa ann. 991. AntiChristum designavit. Undecimo Gaubertus ArchiEpiscopusRhevensis (postea adPapale fasti- gium Magicis artibus evectus, Sylvester II. appel- latus in synodo Rhemensi) Romam monstrosas tenebras effudisse questus est; & imprimis de Ma- lefacico (Bonifacio) horrendo in Pontificatu monstro cunctos mortales nequitia superante, AntiChri- stum in templo Dei sedentem dixit. Cui adde isto secuto Petrum, Papiensis Ecclesiæ Antistitem & Glabrum Rodulphum hujus seculi, & Aretam in Apoc. de ortu AntiChristi scriptorem. Duodecimo Waldenses, vel pauperes de Lugduno, Papam Anti- Christum, Romanam Ecclesiam apud Coccium T. I. Thesaur. l. 7. art. 6. purpuratam meretricem vo- carunt. Quo etiam Honorius Augustodunensis pro- phetias Apocalypticas de bestia, & Babylone, de Papa, & Ecclesia Romana intellexit. Vid. Catal. te- stium verit. cent. XII. c. 7. p. 39. 5. Decimo tertio Joach. Abbas comment. in Esaiam Ap. XVII. in- quit, mulier auro inaurata indifferenter cum terræ principibus fornicatur. Romana Ecclesia est ista, quæ in Babylonem vitæ confusione transfusa mœcha- tur. Guilhelmus de sancto amore, Parisiensis Theo- logus à Bellar. ceu Vir doctus & pius celebratus Pa- pam Anti-Christum & Romam Babylonem esse pa- lam docuit, libr. de collat. benef. &c. quem Lau- rentius Anglicus Magister edita defensione tueri non dubitavit. Guilhelmus Aurifex apud Coccium T. I. l. 7. art. 17. Papam Anti-Christum, Romam Babylonem dixit. Eberhardus Episcopus Salisburi- ensis in Concilio Reginoburgensi coram Impera- tore ac Principibus Ecclesiasticis & politicis pro- fessus publica oratione est apud Aventinum l. VII. annal. pag. 420. Hildebrandus ante annos centum atque septuaginta primus specie religionis Anti- Christi imperii fundamenta jecit. Decimo quarto Petrus Johannes Diœcesis Bircnensis Aquitanus Mi- norita apud Bernhardum Lutzelburgium in Catal. Hæret. Guidonem Perpinian. de hæresib. & Coccium Papam dixit mysticum esse Anti-Christum, Babylonem meretricem illam magnam esse Romanam Ecclesiam. Johannes Wiclefus, qui plus quam 100. volumina scripsit: ejusque discipulus Gualtherus Brutus Papam docuit non solum non esse vicarium Christi, sed etiam Anti-Christum. Decimo quinto Johannes Huss. Martyr in Anatom. Anti-Christ. teste Johanne Cochlæo l. III. Hist. Hussit. & Coccio, dixit, Papam vicarium esse Anti-Christi, bestiam il- lam de qua in Apocalypsi; imo in Anatom. Anti- Christi c. 42. professus est, eum esse præcipuum An- ti-Christum. Hieronymus Savanarola Florentiæ jussu Alexandri VI. combustus Papam dixit nec vitam nec doctrinam Christi retinere, quia plus suis indulgen- tiis & traditiunculis quam Christi meritis tribuat, adeoque eum esse Anti-Christum. Decimo sexto duo Martini B. Lutherus & B. Chemnitius. Decimo septimo B. Ægid. Hunnius & B. Joh. Gerhardus Papatui destruendo præcipuas contulerunt ope- ras ideoque duorum illorum testium nomen præ aliis meriti sunt.

Grotiani vero testes nec ab ipsis Papistis appro- bantur, nec ullatenus conveniunt. Nam Æliam non condidit Adrianus ante bellum judaicum fini- tum, & Barchochebam necatum, adeo, ut hic eam nunquam viderit, nedum ingressus sit ibique do- minatus fuerit, quod è nullo Historico docebitur. Multos quidem Christianos ab eo necatos dicit Baronius, sed id Hierosolymis factum, nec ullus Historicus probabit. Neq; Ælia civitas sancta dici potuit, quæ à gentibus conculcata. Plena enim fuit gentibus profanis. Nec tamen tum deformata fuit libidine Sodomitica & sanctorum oppressione in- famis, ut inde illarum nomine insigniri debuerit. Nihil certe de Ælia temporibus Adriani legitur. Porro civitas sancta conculcata est à gentibus tri- bus annis & dimidio, id Eliæ non convenit, qua- cunque ratione anni accipiantur. Gentes Ethnicæ conversæ sunt usque ad Constantinum M. Et quo- modo tum mensurari templum poterat, quod Adri- ani tempore non extabat? quomodo atrium templi exterius conculcari, quum illud à nova Adriani urbe Ælia seclusum fuerit? Unde etiam duos ha- buisse Æliam Episcopos docebitur? qui à Papistis adeoque nec ab Hamano hic cum Grotio facien- te, in una civitate non admittuntur: nec in catalogo sive Eusebii sive aliorum, Episcopos Hieroso- lymitanos recensentium, inveniuntur, ubi Episco- pi usque ad Adrianum è Judæis & Ebræa solum lingua loquentes occurrunt. Neque per 3 1/2 tantum annos duravit præconium in Ælia: Duravit usque ad Constantinum. Nec monstrari illi anni in Adri- ano possunt. Undecimo enim Adriani anno Bar- chochebæ bellum cœpit, & 20. finitum est. Ut ta- ceam, quod nulla diebus Adriani talia edita mira- cula sint in Ælia, nec florere vicissim civitas cœpe- rit post 3 1/2 annos, aut etiam post Barchochebam oppressum, & devictos Judæos. Dominium enim Romanorum continuatum, idolum Jovis Olym- pici cultum, & simulacra præterea Veneris & A- donidis religiose honorata ibidem sunt.

Quanquam vero de Mose & Ælia annuant Isi- dorus Clarius in c. 4. Zach. Catharin. in Gen. c. 2. Gagnejus h. l. & c. 17. Mat. Jansenius in Conc. Ev. c. 67. aliique Ludovicus ab Alcafar etiam adducat Arboreum & Joach. Abbatem, ut & Hilarium in Matth. XVII. Ambrosium in Luc. IX. Maldona- tus vero satis audacter pro more Jesuitico in c. XVII. Matth. pronunciet, Johannem in Apocal.

c. XI. 3. 6. tam aperte scribere, Mosen & Eliam esse venturos, ut nemo non solum sine temeritate, sed nec sine impudentia negare possit: non dubitavit ta- men in eodem Lojolitico ordine cum sociis de impudentia certare Lorinus in 2. Petr. I. 16. Mal- donatus inquit, in c. XVII. Matth. Minus profe- cto recte oppositam de Mose opinionem, quæ lon- ge communior & verior est, censet temerariam & impudentem, & reperiuntur profecto non pauci, qui malunt hosce duos testes de Enocho & Elia interpretari ; in quam sententiam addu- cit Alcafar Aretam, Ambrosium, Haymonem, Ri- chardum, Ansbertum, Strabum, Hugonem Cardin. Dionysium, Clarium, Vatablum, Riberam, Vie- gam, Suarezium, part. III. T. 2. disp. 55. sect. 2. Pamelium ad Tertull. Mendozam in quod I. Pe- rerium in Pancil. Malvendam l. IX. de Anti- Christo. Ut taceam quod de duobus viris qui- dem alii apud Alcafarem explicent; sed non de tempore Anti-Christi: De quonam ergo? Vel de tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ, qui suspicantur esse Christum & Johannem, ut Ubertinus de Casatis, & Cittingerus: de duobus illis Sacerdotibus de JESU, & Anano, (quos occiderunt Idumæi) ut Caponsachius: de Sylvestro Papa, & Mena Patri- archa pugnantibus contraEutychianos, ut Au- reolus, Antoninus, Lyranus, Ederus, Lizarazus: Vel de Francisco & Dominico, ut nonnulli apud Cornelium à Lapide. Alii de tempore quidem Anti- Christi accipiunt, sed non de duobus viris, ut Ticonius, Primasius, Beda, Hortulinus, Panno- nius.
