Alii nec de duobus viris, nec de Anti-Chri- sti tempore intelligunt: Sed vel de cunctis fidei Christianæ seculis cum Pannonio, (quomodo Tho- mas de Aquino in h. l.) per duos testes desiguari ait omnes prædicatores, qui sunt modo & erunt, qui ideo sub binario ponantur, quia de duobus testamentis accipiunt, quod prædicant: Vel ut Ly- ranus habet; quia Dominus binos misit discipulos ad prædicandum, quo spectat Ariasmontanus, qui testes duos esse vult legem & prophetiam: vel de- nique (quæ Alcafaris, cui cæteroquin hic non omnino abnuit Grotius, est sententia) de duo- bus testibus tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quos ve- ro dicit magnam sapientiam & magnam sanctita- tem Ministrorum Evangelii supponens à cap. IV. usque ad XI. sermonem esse de modo, quo DE- US se gesserit cum Judæis & populis sub Ecclesiæ primitivæ tempora, cap. XII. usque ad XX. de actione DEI cum populo gentili. Refellit autem Alcafar sententiam de Enoch & Elia cum Hiero- nymo ep. CXLIIX. de Enoch & Elia, quos Apo- calypsis refert venturos, & esse morituros, non est istius temporis disputatio, cum omnis ille li- ber, aut spiritualiter intelligendus sit, aut fabulis acquiescendum; & fundamenta ejusdem dejicit. Denique præfert, quod Jeremiam temporibus Anti-Christi venturum Victorinum sensisse, eam- que multorum fuisse sententiam Hilarium Conc. XX. in Matth. referre observat Blasius de Viegas & Sixtus Senensis l. I. sub tit. Irenæi. Barradius vero multis argumentis & testimoniis, (Theo- phylacti, Aretæ, Hippolyti, Metaphrasti, Dama- sceni, Trapezuntii, Catharini) probabile esse do- bet T. IV. Concord. Evangel. l. IX. c. 4. cum Eno- cho & Elia etiam Johannem Evangelistam è Pa- radiso terrestri Anti-Christi tempore in has terras rediturum, adeoque non præcise duos testes hic intelligi, quæ tamen de Jeremia & Johanne falsa pronunciat Lorinus. Ticonius: Excluditur, in- quit, omnis suspicio quorundam, qui putant, hos duos testes viros duos esse. Quomodo enim po- test tuerunt habitantes terram de duorum nece gau- dere, quum in una civitate morerentur, & mune- ra invicem mittere, si tres dies sunt. Quia ante- quam gaudeant de nece, contristabuntur de resur- rectione. Et quomodo obsecro convenit duo corpora in unius civitatis platea jactis, & ab omni- bus gentibus, populis, linguisque conspici? Quo- modo illi, qui ad beatam visionem Dei jam ad- missi, corpora non amplius mortalia habent 1. Cor. XV. 50. sed glorificata Luc. IX. 31. & translati funt, ne viderent mortem, occidi poterunt? Qui hic testes, mox virgines dicuntur. Testes duo, vir- gines 144000. testes ab officio, virgines a qualitate vel adjuncto: nimirum incorrupta ab amoribus scorti Babylonici puritate ac castitate tum doctri- næ tum vitæ. Numerus magnus non paucos fore docet, binarius paucos, sed comparate, respectu copiæ Anti-Christianorum. Eat nunc Bellarmi- nus & adhuc hæresin aut hæresi proximum judi- cet, negare Henochum & Eliam in persona non rediturum ad Judæorum conversionem, occiden- dos ab Anti-Christo.

Καὶ προφητεύσωσιν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἐ- ξήκοντα) Dies 1260. alii intelligunt vulgariter, alii mystice. Cum illis facit cum Papistis plerisque Grotius, & è nostris, sed alio sensu aliaque inten- tione B. Gravius. Per bestiam intelligens totum regnum Romano-Papisticum, victoriam vero non spiritualem sed corporalem, & occisionem si- milem Evangelicorum persecutionem: quem au- dire juvat αὐτοφώνως ita loquentem: Anno 1625. Papistæ arctissime confœderati sanguinolenta tra- ctarunt consilia, quæ sequentibus annis, oppressis Ev- angelicorum Principum armis, effectum suum sunt sortita. Occupatæ enim nobilissimæ sunt Evangelico- rum provinciæ, urbes, oppida, & munitiones par- tim expugnatæ, partim extisæ & desolatæ fuerunt. Suscepta fuit per totam ferme Germaniam Anti- Christiana reformatio, abrogatum passim publicum Evangelii seu verbi divini exercitium, pulsis in exi- lium Ecclesiæ Ministris & Doctoribus orthodoxis, omnibusque Evangelicis, idolum Anti-Christianum adorare recusantibus. Duravit hæc Ecclesiæ Evange- licæ & duorum testium persecutio TRES AN- NOS cum DIMIDIO, hoc est à fine anni 1625. usq; ad annum circiter 30. maximo Papistarum trium- pho atq; jubilo, quemadmodum dicitur v. 10. Et in- habitantes terram super illis gaudebunt & lætabun- tur, & munera mittent invicem, quoniam hi duo Prophetæ cruciarunt eos, (spiritualiter sc. in consci- entiis per refutationem dogmatum Papalium) qui habitant super terram, h. e. homines terrenos & ter- rena sapientes in regno Pontificio. Hæc vere ita eve- nisse superiorum annorum res gestæ ad amussim te- stantur. Addo, quæ habet, ob plenam sententiæ ἔκθεσιν: Et post tres dies & dimidium Spiritus vi- tæ intravit in eos. Hæc impleta sunt seu impleri cœ- perunt Ann. Chr. 1630. quo tempore adventante leo- ne septentrionali paulatim de die in diem labefacta- ta & imminuta potentia Ligistarum, progressu tem- poris restitutum fuit publicum Evangelii seu verbi di- vini exercitium, expulsis ex recuperatis Evangelico- rum provinciis & civitatibq sacrificulis, Monachis & Jesuitis, eorumque idolomania & superstitione. Ita vitam & autoritatem pristinam divinitus in cœlo Ec- clesiastico hi duo testes recuperarunt, & volente Deo magis magisque imposterum recuperatam illam glo- riam suam in Ecclesia declarabunt maximo hostium Ecclesiæ mœrore ac terrore. Nam à fine Anni 1629. inchoatur magnus ille terræ motus, h. e. concussio & commotio populorum & regnorum per armorum strepitum atq; tumultum, qui eadem hora eodemque momento excitatus fuit cum duorum testium exaltationis initio, quo DECIMA PARS CIVITATIS (Babylonica scil. seu regni Anti- Christiani) cecidit vers. 13. Armis enim Regis se- ptentrionalis & Evangelicorum Principum brevi temporis spatio attrita sunt vires Ligistarum, oc- cupatæ nobilissimæ ac potentissimæ Pontificiorum regio- nes & provinciæ. Imo post mortem Leonis fortissi- mi etiam inter varia Evangelicorum Principum dissi- dia & bellorum motus admirando Dei consilio sum- mopere diminuta est atque labefactata potentia Hi- spanica, ut vere dici possit, ultra decimam regni & potentiæ Anti-Christianæ partem in nihilum quasi re- dactam esse. Quamdiu vero hæc populorum commo- tio duratura sit, in textu non additur. Dn. Phil. Nicolai de regn. Christ. l. 2. ex verbis v. 13. & in illa hora factus est terræ motus, certum tempus, nempe 20. annos circa an. Christ. 1670. finiendos definire conatur, sed absque mysterio horam hanc intelligen- dam esse sup. tab. 12. ex Apoc. IX. v. 15. declaratur. Innuere enim vult Spiritus S. quod eodem tempo- re & puncto exaltationis duorum testium spiritua- lis hic terræ motus sit oriturus, quod & impletum esse, & adhuc impleri testatur experientia. Hæc ille Anno 1647. Quo quidem adhuc durabat terræ motus, sed paulo post quies sequuta & pax universalis. Cæterum uti reliqua mystice intelligenda; ita hic literæ inhærere non con- venit. Dies non naturales sed mystici: Victo- ria spiritualis, non corporalis: quia testium ve- ritatis, qui vincunt ore, non gladio, igne cœ- lesti Spiritus, non igne bombardarum pulveris tormentarii. Prodeunt autem illa ex hypothesi B. Phil. Nicolai l. II. de regn. Christ. quod perio- dus testium inchoari debeat à contentionibus Da- masi & Ursatii de sede Pontificia apud Ammian. Marcell. l. 27. finiri An. 1625. quæ deducitur è c. XIV. 20. mille & sexcenta stadia esse totidem an- nos, quibus hora messis ÷ 24. pars diei, qui an- nos millenario secundum Mosen Psal. XC. & Pe- trum 2. ep. III. constat, quæ efficit annos 41 2/3. Quæ omnia gratis sumuntur. Veritati autem magis consentana sunt, quæ antea adduximus. Brigt- mannus præcise de 3 1/2. annis accipit, & concilio Tridentino accommodat, in quo Patres similiter tres annos & dimidium de concultatis scripturis Veteris & Novi Testamenti (hos enim facit duos te- stes) gaudebant. Quæ quidem magnam habebant probabilitatem. Utrum vero Spiritus huc respe- xerit, non definio, inquit Pareus. Tutius, pergit idem, accedemus eorum sententiæ, qui indefinite tres dies & dimidium intelligunt de brevi tempore, quo durabit martyrum contumelia & hostium tri- umphus. Vix dimidia erit hebdomada. Es ist umb drey oder vierdthalb Jahr zu thun, so hat der Pfaffen-Tantz ein Ende. Inferitur ergo hæc tem- poris circumstantia consolationis ergo, quam scriptura passim ingerit piis cruce oppressis à brevitate cala- mitatum & instante liberatione, Joh. XVI. v. 16. 2. Cor. IV. 7. Observant & è nostris nonnulli, ut- pote B. Cluverus, historias Anti-Christianæ perse- cutionis 3 1/2. annorum, nimirum durantis concilii Constantiensis, quo Hussus & Hieronymus Pra- gensis damnatus, & ab anno 1547. quo in conci- lio Tidentino fides nostra anathemate percussa & primarii assertores ejusdem Elector & Landgraf. capti, ac res penitus desperatæ fuerunt usque ad ann. 1550.

Παραβεβλημένοι σάκκους] habitu lugentium, nempe quod viderent in urbe Deo sacrata idolum & Judæorum plerosque in tantis malis nihilo fieri meliores.

## 11:4
Verse 4.

Ἧτοί εἰσιν αἱ δύο ἐλαῖαι] By which name formerly in Zacha-

riah IV. 3, 11, Joshua the Priest and the Prince Zerubbabel were designated. Thus also these, through Christ, were Kings and Priests to GOD the Father, see above I. 6, verse 10, as full of the Holy Spirit as the olive is of oil, 2 Cor. I. 21, 1 John II. 20, 27.

Καὶ αἱ δύο λυχνίαι] that is, the two Churches, as we have already said. The author of this our interpretation is Christ himself, above I. 20.

Αἱ ἐvώπιοv τoῦ Κυρίου τῆς γῆς ἑστῶσαι] Taken from Zechariah IV. 14. The sense is that those two Churches serve GOD perpetually. For that is what it means among the Hebrews to stand before someone. See above VIII. 2.

By the two olives or sons of oil, the blessed Gravius understands the Old and New Testament, because in them the grace of God, peace, and tranquility of conscience are exhibited to us, Rom. V. 1, and he explains the two candlesticks as the Word of God, 2 Peter I, verse 29, Psalm CXIX, 14; but since the killing of the witnesses follows, and the Word of God cannot perish, Ticonius more correctly interprets them as Christians preaching the two testaments and clothed in sacred garments; Primasius interprets them as the Church preaching and prophesying through the two testaments. In which manner it is alluded not only to Zerubbabel, but also to other ancient histories concerning Abraham and Lot in Palestine and Sodom, Moses and Aaron in Egypt, Joshua and Caleb in the desert, Elijah and Elisha in Israel, Haggai and Zechariah in Judea, Paul and Barnabas, Peter and John in Jerusalem, and preaching and testifying among the nations. Sackcloth is a vile, dark, and mournful garment, denoting those who are mourning or their sins, when they were doing penance, 1. Kings 21, verse 27, Joel 1, verse 13, Jonah 3, verse 5, Nehemiah 9, verse 1, or other evils, whether private, Psalm 30, 12, or public, such as impiety, Psalm 69, verse 12, or misfortunes, Psalm 35, verse 14, Jeremiah 6, verse 26, Lamentations 2, verse 10, Ez. 27, verse 31, Joel 1, verse 8, 13, Amos 8, verse 10. But the witnesses are like olive trees 1. because of the spiritual fatness which they draw from Christ, the good olive tree, into which they are grafted, Rom. 11, verse 17, 24, John 1. 17, with whose Spirit they are filled as with the oil of gladness: for from him they have the anointing and the Spirit, Psalm 45, verse 7, 1 John 2; Eph. 2. 2. because of the symbolic signification of peace. For the olive among the Romans is a symbol of peace, just as the olive was also a sign of a placated God, Rom. 8, which is why the witnesses of the Gospel announce peace and reconciliation, Isaiah 52, verse 7, 2 Cor. 5, verse 17. 3. Because of the foreshadowing of victory. The Romans crowned the troops of the victors with olive: Thus also are Doctors to be adorned who conquer by faith, 1 John 5:4, Eph. 6:4. Because of the usefulness of the olive, it provides fuel for lights, fruit for food and medicines, Ps. 104:15. Thus Doctors provide fuel and food for others who are enlightened, when they inflame them toward piety, and feed and refresh themselves and others through the Word of God, Matt. 4, Ps. 119. They are compared to λυχνίαις, candlesticks, or rather lamps, because they shine before the world, Matt. 5:14, John 5:35, and to the house of the Lord 1 Tim. 3:15, and perhaps two, not as in ch. 1:20, seven in Asia, designate meager illumination or in few places under the Papacy. They are said to stand before the Lord both because of service and readiness for it; and because of the signification of the confidence of intercession 2 Chron. 18:18, Gen. 18:22, Jer. 18:20. Before the Lord of the earth, because all the earth was marveling at his dominion in the beast, which indeed also remained, even under the pretended dominion of the beast it was the Lord of heaven's Ps. 20:1.

Vers. 4.

Ἧτοί εἰσιν αἱ δύο ἐλαῖαι] Quo nomine olim apud Za- |

char. IV. 3. 11. designati Josue Sacerdos & Princeps Zorobabel. Sic & hi per Christum DEO Patri erant Reges & Sacerdotes supra I. 6. v. 10. tam pleni Spiritu Sancto, quam olea est olei 2. Cor. I. 21. 1. Joh. II. 20. 27.

Καὶ αἱ δύο λυχνίαι] id est, duæ Ecclesiæ, ut jam diximus. Interpretationis hujus nostræ Autor ipse Christus supra I. 20.

Αἱ ἐvώπιοv τoῦ Κυρίου τῆς γῆς ἑστῶσαι] Sumptum de Zacharia IV. 14. Sensus est, illas duas Ecclesias DEO perpetuo inservire. Id enim apud Ebræos stare coram aliquo. Vide supra VIII. 2.

Per duas olivas vel filios olei vetus & novum Test. intelligit B. Gravius, quia in illis nobis exhibetur Dei gratia, pax & tranquillitas conscientiæ, Rom. V. 1. & duo candelabra explicat de Verbo Dei 2. Petr. I. v. 29. Psal. CXIX. 14. sed quum de occisione testium sequatur, Verbum autem Dei interire non possit; rectius Ticonius de Christianis duo testamenta prædicantibus & sacris indutis; Primasius de Ecclesia duobus testamentis prædicante & prophetante interpretantur. Quo pacto non tantum ad Zorobabelem, sed etiam ad alias veteres historias alluditur de Abraham & Lotho in Palæstina & Sodoma, Mose & Aarone, in Ægypto, Josua & Caleb in deserto, Elia & Eliseo in Israële, Aggeo & Zacharia in Judæa, Paulo & Barnaba, Petro & Johanne Hierosolymis, & inter gentes prædicantibus ac testantibus. Saccus indumentum vile, atrum & lugubre, notans lugentium vel peccata, cum pœnitentiam agebant, 1. Reg. 21, v. 27. Joel. 1, vers. 13. Jon. 3, vers. 5. Nehem. 9, v. 1. vel mala alia seu privata Psal. 30, 12. seu publica, utpote impietatem Psal. 69, vers. 12. vel infortunia, Psal. 35, vers. 14. Jerem. 6, vers. 26. Thren. 2, vers. 10. Ez. 27, vers. 31. Joel. 1, vers. 8. 13. Amos 8, vers. 10. Similes autem sunt testes oleæ 1. ob pinguedinem spiritualem, quam attrahunt à Christo καλλιέλαιῳ, cui inseruntur, Rom. 11, v. 17. 24. Joh. 1. 17. cujus Spiritu ceu oleo lætitiæ implentur: ab ipso enim unctionem & Spiritum habent, Psal. 45, v. 7. 1. Joh. 2.; Eph. 2. 2. ob symbolicam pacis significationem. Olea enim apud Romanos symbolum pacis est, ut olea placati Dei signum etiam fuit Rom. 8. quod nisi pacem & reconciliationem annuncient testes Evangelii, Esa. 52, vers. 7. 2. Cor. 5, vers. 17. 3. Ob victoriæ adumbrationem. Olea Romani turmas victorum coronarunt: Ita etiam ornandi sunt Doctores fide vincentes, 1. Johan. 5, 4. Eph. 6, 4. Ob oleæ utilitatem, Præbet luminibus pabulum, cibis & medicamentis fructum, Psal. 104. vers. 15. Sic Doctores aliis illuminatis pabulum & cibum sufficiunt, cum ad pietatem inflammant, seque & alios per Verbum Dei pascunt & reficiunt, Matth. 4. Psal. 119. Conferuntur λυχνίαις candelabris, vel potius lucernis, quia mundo prælucent, Matth. 5, vers. 14. Joh. 5, vers. 35. & domui Domini 1. Tim, 3. vers. 15. & duo fortassis non ut c. I. 20. in Asia septem exiguam illuminationem aut in paucis locis sub Papatu designant. Coram Domino autem stare dicuntur tum ob servitium ejusque promptitudinem; tum ob fiduciæ intercessionis significationem 2. Par. 18, vers. 18. Gen. 18, 22. Jerem. 18, 20. Coram Domino terræ, quia dominium illius omnis terra in bestia admirabatur, quod vero & manebat, etiam sub prætensa dominatione bestiæ erat Domini cœli Psal. 20, 1.

## 11:5
Vers. 5.

And if anyone wishes to harm them] If anyone, whether Jew or foreigner, oppresses them.

Fire goes out of their mouth) and devours their enemies, that is, their prayers excite the wrath of God to the destruction of the enemies. See above VIII. v. 4, 5, and Rom. XII. v.20. Moreover, the history is referred to and applied mystically, which is 1 Kings 1:10, 12.

And if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed) That word οὕτω is missing in the manuscript. The sense, however, is the same as below in chapter 13, verse 10. And there is an allusion to the burnt offerings, as above in chapter 8, verse 5.

Concerning the efficacy of the Word, these things are commonly explained, to which those who resist succumb, Heb. 4:12, ch. 5:1. If not corporally, certainly spiritually: just as it was necessary for the Baalites and the soldiers of the King resisting Elijah to perish by fire, 1 Kings 19, 2 Kings 1:10, 12, Psalm 2:12. The matter is carried out by the mouth by the witnesses; it is the prerogative of Kings to punish with the sword, not of those who prophesy. Jer. 5:14, ch. 20:9, ch. 23:19, Psalm 29:7, Sir. 48:1, 2. See also Blessed Luther, Vol. VII, Jena, German, page 239, concerning the Papacy founded by the Devil.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

Καὶ εἴ τις αὐτοὺς θέλῃ ἀδικῆσαι] Si quis aut Judæus aut alienigena eos opprimat.

Πῦρ ἐκπορεύεται ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτῶν) καὶ κατεσθίει τοὺς ἐχθροὺς αὐτῶν, id est, preces illorum Dei iram excitant in perniciem hostium. Vide supra VIII. v. 4. 5. & Rom. XII. v.20. Refpicitur autem & applicatur μυσικῶς historia, quæ est 1. Reg. I. 10. 12.

Καὶ εἴτις θέλῃ αὐτὸς ἀδικῆσαι, ὕτω δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀποκτανθῆναι) Illud ὅτω deeft in Manuscripto. Est autem sensus idem, qui infra XIII. vers. 10.. Et allusio est ad holocausta, ut supra VIII. vers. 5.

De efficacia Verbi commúniter hæc explican- tur, cui qui resistunt, occumbunt, Ebr. IV. 12. c. V. 1. Si non corporaliter, certe spiritualiter: quem- admodum Baalitas, & milites Regis Eliæ resisten- tes igne perire oportebat, 1. Reg. XIX. 2. Reg. I. 10. 12. Psal. II. 12. Ore res agitur à testibus, gladio punire Regum est proprium, non prophetantium. Jer. V. 14. cap. XX. 9. cap. XXIII. 19. Psalm. XXIX. 7. Sir. XLIIX. 1. 2. Vid. & B. Lutherus Tom. VII. Jen. Germ. pag. 239. de Papatu à Diabolo fun- dato.

## 11:6
Verse 6.

These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy) The sense is: There is nothing so great and stupendous that they do not obtain from God, if there is need. That, however, is explained by the likeness of those things which God had once done, for the sake of both Elijah and Moses. And this indeed concerning the rain is taken manifestly from the history of Elijah, 1 Kings 17, 18. James also uses that example to show that there is nothing that cannot be obtained by the prayers of Christians. Τὰς ἡμέρας, that is, κατὰ τὰς ἡμέρας.

Here again, the rain is to be understood spiritually, which is the Gospel, Deut. 34:1, Is. 5:6, ch. 44:3, 55:10, Ez. 34:26, Psalm 68:14, Zech. 14:17, 18, Heb. 6:7, by which being withheld, spiritual irrigation and fertilization fail, and consequently the fruit of the word, Is. 5:6, Am. 8:12, Zech. 14:17, just as famine and the high price of grain followed the lack of rain in the time of Elijah, 1 Kings 18:3. Which the Papacy experienced with the removal of the rain, by its own fault and by the just judgment of God, 2 Thess. 2:9, 10, Zech. 14:17, it came to pass that the vineyard brought forth not grapes but wild grapes, Is. 5:6; for the zeal of sincere piety, a show and some froth of religion; for faith in Christ, the veneration of the cross; for the imitation of the Saints, the adoration of bones and various relics; for the observance of the commandments of GOD, the superstition of rules; for works of mutual love, eremitic and monastic vanities. Cf. Psalm 68:7, Honorius of Autun around the year 1220. In his Dialogue on Predestination and the Antichrist, he has it thus: I behold the Princes of Babylon, and behold, the seat of the beast is placed in them. At all times they are intent on evil, always occupied inexhaustibly with the business of iniquity; they not only commit crimes, but also instruct others to do so; they sell holy things, they buy wickedness, they labor with all their might so that they may not go to hell alone. Turn yourself to the clergy, and you will see in them the tent of the beast; they neglect the service of God, they serve earthly gains, they pollute the priesthood through uncleanness, they seduce the people through hypocrisy, they neglect God through evil works, they reject all scriptures pertaining to salvation, they lay snares for the ruin of the people in every way, whom they, being blind themselves, lead to destruction.

And they have power over the waters to turn them to blood) This is taken from the history of Moses, Exod. 7:17.

And to smite the earth with all plagues as often as they will) And this looks to the history of Moses. By the name of plagues, understand all those things which, besides the waters turned into blood, Moses obtained from God in Egypt.

Nowhere is it read that Elijah or Enoch did such a thing. How then does this fit the interpretation of the Papists? For one must not be satisfied with a bare category of miracles or with hyperbole, as Grotius is, when a special reason for analogy can be held. Which conversion of waters—not of rain, but of the seas, from which the beast ascends, that is, of many peoples, Apoc. 17:1—is the conversion of the Gospel into blood, when the world was filled with the blood of the people, by various wars and the slaughters of persecutions, both regarding the blood of the martyrs and that of the persecutors themselves, with the judgment of God: Pope against Anti-Popes, Popes likewise against Emperors, and finally against those who opposed themselves to the Anti-Christ, the Waldensians, Albigensians, Bohemians. Germans, Belgians, French, English contending, who thirsted for blood, they had to shed copious blood, who struck others with various plagues, and were in turn afflicted with other plagues, Ap. 16:5, 6, 17:6, which are indeed attributed to the witnesses and their sighs and groans, Ap. 6:10, in the manner of Scripture, but have proceeded from God as the principal cause, Jer. 1:10, ch. 25:15, Ezech. 5:1, whence Blessed D. Hoëus, I know not by what author, reports that within 30 years, from the year of the Christian era 1550 to 1580, in Belgium, Italy, France, and England, nine hundred thousand were killed on account of religion, and among them 39 Princes, 148 Counts, 235 Barons, 14,751 nobles, 700,060 commoners. Can the seas not be said to have been turned into blood in this way?

Latin:

Vers. 6.

Οὗτοι ἔχυσιν ἐξυσίαν κλεῖσαι τὸν ἐρανὸν, ἵνα μὴ ὑετὸς βρέχῃ τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς προφητείας αὐτῶν) Sensus est: Ni- hil tam magnum ac stupendum est, quod non à Deo impe- trent, si opus sit. Id autem explicatur per similitudinem e orum, quæ Deus olim fecerat, tum Eliæ, tum Mosis cau- sa. Et hoc quidem de imbre manifesto sumptum est de E- liæ historia 1. Reg. XVII. XVIII. Utitur eo exemplo & Ja- cobus, ut ostendat nihil non impetrabile esse Christiano- rum precibus. Τὰς ἡμέρας, id est, κατὰ τὰς ἡμέ- ρας.

Spiritualis hic iterum intelligenda pluvia, quæ Evangelii est, Deut. XXXIV. 1. Es. V. 6. c. XLIV. 3. LV. 10. Ez. XXXIV. 26. Psal. LXIIX. 14. Zach. XIV. 17. 18. Ebr. VI. 7. qua retenta deficit irri- gatio & fœcundatio spiritualis, adeoque fructus verbi, Es. V. v. 6. Am. IIX. 12. Zach. XIV. 17. ut fames & annonæ caritas pluviæ defectum tem- pore Eliæ sequuta, 1. Reg. XIIX. 3. Quod exper- tus est Papatus cum ablatione pluviæ culpa pro- pria justo Dei judicio, 2. Thess. II. 9. 10. Zach. XIV. 17. factum, ut vinea non uvas sed labruscas, Es. V. 6. pro sinceræ pietatis studio speciem & spumam aliquam religionis, pro fide in Christum venerationem crucis, pro Sanctorum imitatio- ne adorationem ossium & reliquias varias, pro observatione mandatorum DEI regularum su- perstitionem, pro operibus mutuæ dilectionis eremiticas & monasticas vanitates proferret. Conf. Psal. LXIIX. 7. Honorius Augustod. circa ann. 1220. An Christum Dial. de prædest. & L. A. ita habens: Intueor Principes Babylonis, & ec- ce posita est in eis sedes bestiæ. Omni tempore ad malum sunt intenti, semper negotiis iniquitatis in- explebiliter occupati, flagitia non solum faciunt; sed & alios facere instruunt, sancta vendunt, scele- ra emunt, totis viribus laborant, ne soli ad tartara veniant. Verte te ad clerum, & videbis in eis be- stiæ tentorium, Dei servitium negligunt, terrenis lucris inserviunt, sacerdotium per immunditiem polluunt, populum per simultationem seducunt, De- um per mala opera negligunt, omnes scripturas ad sa- lutem pertinentes abdicant, omnibus modis laqueos ad ruinam populi substernunt, quem cæcum ipsi cæci ad interitum præcedunt.

## 11:7
Verse 7.

And when they shall have finished their testimony) τελέσωσιν here as τελεσθῇ. Below chapter XX. It is to be taken not in a complete sense but in an incomplete one, as if he were saying, when the time was now near, at which God wished to put an end to their labors.

the beast that ascendeth out of the abyss] In the Manuscript: the fourth beast. But I think it was written the monstrous one: unless perhaps the first beast is the dragon, the second from the sea, the third risen from the earth, but this one the fourth. Barchochebas is indicated here, whom Satan, released from his prison, stirred up. Concerning this meaning of the word abyss, see above chapter IX. v. 1. 2. Moreover, Barchochebas is well called by the name of a beast, a murderous and thievish man, as Eusebius speaks in History IV. 6, adding also this: Destroying myriads of men, children, and women all at once.

he will make war with them, and will overcome them and will kill them] The matter is here pre-signified, which the same Eusebius narrates in his Chronicle: Chochebas, leader of the Jewish faction, not wishing the Christians to bring him aid against the Roman soldiery, kills them with all manner of tortures. Justin in his second Apology: For indeed in the Jewish war that has now occurred, Barchochebas, the leader of the Jewish revolt, ordered only the Christians to be led away to terrible punishments, unless they would deny Jesus the Christ and blaspheme. Orosius concerning Hadrian: He took vengeance on the Christians, whom they (the Jews) were torturing because they did not show themselves against the Romans. Moreover, you may learn from Dio that the faction of Barchochebas also prevailed for some time in Jerusalem or Aelia. For he says: all Judea was stirred up. And it is credible that the beginning of the fighting was made there, where the temple of Jupiter Capitolinus was, the greatest pretext. Understand that 'he will make war with them' not as meaning that those Christians used force against force, but that they were treated in a purely hostile manner. Thus the same expression is used also below in chapter XII. 17, chapter XIII. 7. 'He will overcome,' that is, he will effect what he wishes, God permitting it for a time. That 'and will kill them' is to be taken synecdochically, that is, he will kill many from both assemblies.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Καὶ ὅταν τελέσωσι τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὑτῶν) τελέσωσιν hic ut τελεσθῇ. Infra cap. XX. Non in sensu completo sed in in- completo sumendum est, quasi diceret, cum jam prope es- set tempus, quo Deus ipsorum laboribus finem volebat im- ponere.

τὸ θηρίον τὸ ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου] In Manuscripto: τὸ θηρίον τὸ τέταρτον. Sed puto scriptum fuisse τὸ τεράστιον: nisi forte prima fera est draco, altera ex mari, tertia ex ter- ra orta, hæc vero quarta. Indicatur hic Barchochebas, quem Satan è carcere suo emissus suscitavit. De hoc signifi- catu vocis ἀβύσσου vide supra cap. IX. v. 1. 2. Bene autem fe- ræ nomine appellatur Barchochebas, Φονικὸς καὶ λῃστρικὸς ἀνὴρ ut loquitur Eusebius historiæ IV. 6. addens & hoc: Μυ- ριάδας ἀθρόως ἀνδρῶν ὁμοῦ καὶ παίδων καὶ γυναικῶν διαφθεί- ραν.

ποιήσει μετ' αὐτῶν πόλεμον, καὶ νικήσει αὐτοὺς καὶ ἀπο- κτενεῖ αὐτούς] Res hic præsignificatur, quam Eusebius idem in Chronico narrat: Chochebas Dux Judaicæ factionis no- lentes sibi Christianos adversum Romanum militem ferre subsi- dium, omnimodis cruciatibus necat. Justinus in Apologe- tico altero: Καὶ γὰρ ἐν τῷ νῦν γεγενημένῳ Ἰουδαϊκῷ πολέμῳ Βαρχοχέβας ὁ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀποστάσεως ἀρχηγέτης χριστιανοὺς μόνους εἰς τιμωρίας δεινάς, εἰ μὴ ἀρνοῖντο Ἰησοῦ τὸν χριστὸν καὶ βλα- σφημοῖεν, ἐκέλευεν ἀπάγεσθαι. Orosius de Adriano Ultus, que est Christianos, quos illi (Judæi) quod sibi adversus Ro- manos non ostentarentur, excruciabant. Factionem au- tem Barchochebæ aliquo tempore etiam Hierosolymis sive Æliæ invaluisse, ex Dione cognoscas. Ait enim: ἥτε Ἰυ- δαία πᾶσα κεκίνητο. Et credibile est, ibi factum initium, u- bi erat templum Jovis Capitolini, bellandi maxima πρόφα- σις. Illud ποιήσει μετ' αὐτῶν πόλεμον intellige, non quod illi Christiani vi contra vim usi sint, sed quod tractati sint plane hostiliter. Sic eadem loquutio & infra usurpatur cap. XII. 17. cap. XIII. 7. νικήσει, id est, efficiet, quod volet, Deo ad tempus id permittente. Illud καὶ ἀποκτενεῖ αὐτοὺς sumendum συνεκδοχικῶς, id est, multos de utroque conven- tu interficiet.

## 11:8
Vers. 8.

And their dead bodies upon the street of the great city) It is a change of number for upon the streets, in the streets, as the Latin here has it. Moreover, 'shall be' is understood.

which is called spiritually) That is, according to the mystery, by a certain likeness. Thus 'a spiritual house' 1 Pet. II. 5, and you have 'spiritual sacrifices' in the same place.

Sodom] The Prophets often compare Judea to Sodom in sins and in punishment, Deut. XXXII. v. 32, Isa. I. v. 10, III. 9, Jer. XXIII. 14, Lam. IV. 6. Add 2 Pet. II. 6, Jude 7, and what is said there.

And Egypt] Namely because just as Egypt had oppressed the people of Jacob by force, so Jerusalem oppressed the people of Christ. Christ himself had predicted this in Matt. XXIII. 34. Above, the same likeness was tacitly indicated when allusion was made to the plagues of Egypt. And Ezekiel XXIII. 19 also complains that the Hebrews retained much of Egyptian customs.

where also their Lord was crucified) 'Their,' namely of the witnesses. Christ is said to have been crucified at Jerusalem, because places in the vicinity are reckoned as belonging to the cities. See Luke XIII. 37. Thus in the Hebrew, Josh. V. 13, Joshua is said to have been in Jericho, when he was in places very near to that city. It is no wonder that what had happened to the Master should happen to the disciples, John XV. 20.

Vers. 8.

Καὶ τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τῆς πλατείας τῆς πόλεως μεγά- λης) Est ἐναλλαγὴ numeri pro ἐπὶ ταῖς πλατείαις, in plateis, ut hic Latinus. Subauditur autem ἔσονται.

ἥτις καλεῖται πνευματικῶς) Id est κατὰ τὸ μυστήριον, per si- militudinem quandam. Sic οἶκος πνευματικὸς 1. Petr. II. 5. & θυσίαι πνευματικαὶ habes ibidem.

Σόδομα] Sæpe Prophetæ Judæam Sodomis comparant in peccatis & in pœna, Deut. XXXII. v. 32. Esa. I. v. 10. III. 9. Jerem. XXIII. 14. Lam. IV. 6. Adde 2. Petr. II. 6. Judæ 7. & ibi dicta.

Καὶ Αἴγυπτος] Nempe quia sicut Ægyptus Jacobi popu- lum vi oppresserat, ita Hierosolyma Christi populum. Præ- dixerat id Christus ipse Matth. XXIII. 34. Supra eadem si- militudo tacite indicata, cum ad plagas Ægypti allusum fu- it. Et de moribus Ægyptiis multum retinuisse Ebræos que- ritur etiam Ezechiel XXIII. 19.

ὅπου καὶ ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν ἐσταυρώθη) αὐτῶν, nempe τῶν μαρ- τύρων. Christus Hierosolymis crucifixus dicitur, quia con- tinentia loca urbibus accensentur. Vide Luc. XIII. 37. Sic in Ebræo Jos. V. 13. Josua Jerichunte fuisse dicitur, cum es- fet in locis ei urbi proximis. Nil mirum discipulis evenite, quod Magistro evenerat, Joh. XV. 20.

## 11:9
Vers. 9. And they of the peoples and kindreds and nations see

καὶ γλωσσῶν] 'some' is understood, as in Matt. 23:34, Luke 11:49, 21:16, John 16:17. There were many of Aelia from all languages and nations when that faction of Bar Kokhba prevailed for no long time. Ἐκ παντὸς ἔθνες καὶ φυλῶν καὶ λαῶν you have also above at 7:9.

Τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν ἡμέρας τρεῖς ἥμισυ] namely, as long as the faction of Bar Kokhba prevailed in Aelia. Moreover, there is an allusion, not obscure, to the passage in Hos. 6:3.

Καὶ τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν ἐκ ἀφήσουσι τεθῆναι εἰς μνῆμα]. Those who are cruel are accustomed to keep even the bodies of those they hate from burial, as Agamemnon in the Ajax and Creon the Theban in the Antigone of Sophocles: which Seneca said was a mark of Scythian savagery. Let him who has leisure see what I have brought forward on this matter in Book II of De jure belli ac pacis, 19.1.3. Add Psalm 79:3, Ezekiel 28:25, where streets are similarly named.

Concerning the slain witnesses of the truth, it is thus certain. Concerning the unburied bodies, there can be no doubt, since those beastly tyrants consider it a crime to bury the bodies of martyrs, which have not been reduced to ashes, just as they do those of heretics. But what is that great city? By the great consensus of interpreters, it is Rome, which is called that 'spiritually' in which our Lord was crucified. For where is the blood of the Lord held in greater profanity, and the Lord crucified, than at Rome? Where are his mystical members more crucified—that is, the Lord in his members—than in that same place or in the entire Papacy? For Rome is to be taken for the Roman Papacy, and that city in which the Lord is crucified extends itself through the whole world or the entire Roman Papacy: over which the Pope with his clergy dominates everywhere. Therefore, in verses 9 and 10, the city is explained as being of tribes, peoples, and languages, indeed of all who dwell upon the earth; it is not expressed by one name, so that it might be clear from the diverse names of one city that it is not to be understood as one city according to the letter. Nor could its character be sufficiently expressed by one name; it is therefore called Jerusalem, where Christ was crucified, because of the manifold crucifixion of Christ; Sodom, because of both bodily and spiritual fornication; Egypt, because of idolatry and tyranny over the people of the Lord. Most Papists, however, prefer to understand Jerusalem, which they make the seat of the Antichrist. Tirinus, in particular, wishes to prove from this verse that the Antichrist, as the Messiah promised to the Jews, so that he may be held as the heir of the throne of David and Solomon, will raise up Jerusalem again from the ruins together with the Solomonic temple, the royal seat having likely been transferred there, having previously been fixed at Babylon, referring to Bellarmine, Book III, De Romano Pontifice; and by that reasoning he thinks our Achilles regarding the Roman Pontiff as Antichrist falls. But how will it be taught from this oracle that Jerusalem will be the seat of the Antichrist? How is Jerusalem to be understood properly, that it is Sodom itself according to the letter, if Sodom and Egypt are to be taken improperly? And how is the whole kingdom of Egypt Jerusalem? Since, therefore, these things undoubtedly have a mystical sense, and the Holy Spirit himself wished to indicate it by the word πνευματικῶς, these things are explained entirely concerning that city which can mystically be called both Sodom and Egypt, and the place where Christ was crucified. How, likewise, can the temple of Solomon be said to be raised up again, when the temple of Zerubbabel is called the 'latter' in Haggai 2? Who does not see that all these Papistical inventions are unworthy of refutation? No city, therefore, will be more conveniently named in this way than Rome itself. Whence the English Rhemists, at Apoc. 17:18, do not withhold their calculation from us here: 'If these things are understood of any one city, it is most likely that ancient Rome is denoted, as some of the Greeks explain.' For by the authority of the ancient Roman empire, Christ was first delivered to death, and subsequently the two Princes of the Apostles, and their successors, and an infinite multitude of Christians. And the place at Rome on the Appian Way is celebrated under the name 'Domine, quo vadis?' because Christ is said to have answered Peter, who was fleeing and asking this: 'To Rome, to be crucified again.' See Bellarmine, Book I, De Romano Pontifice, ch. 23. To this contribute those words of St. Bernard, praised by Hugo de S. Charo, Cardinal, in his Postilla on 2 John: 'It seems, good Jesus, that the universality of Christians has conspired against you, and those are the first in your persecution who seem to hold the primacy and exercise leadership in your Church.' The Waldensians certainly professed openly around the year of Christ 1160 that the Roman Church is not the bride of Jesus Christ, but the Church of the malignant, drunk with the blood of the Saints. Bellarmine, Book IV, De Ecclesia, ch. 18, § 'tempore', has it thus: 'In the time of Innocent III, in Gaul, one hundred thousand Albigensian heretics were slain by eight thousand Catholics in one battle, as Aemilius writes in Book VI of the History of the Franks.' Rome corresponds to Jerusalem regarding splendor, fame, and boasting—especially concerning the temple of the Lord (Jer. 6)—and pride regarding security, extreme impiety, hatred, and tyranny against Christ and his saints (Matt. 23).

Moreover, Christ is crucified in that city, first in his members and witnesses (Ezek. 37:24, Dan. 8:25, Acts 9:4). Secondly, he is crucified daily and killed and sacrificed in the Mass sacrifice. Thirdly, in the blasphemies of his cross and death (Heb. 10:29). Fourthly, in impiety, because they hold the cross and death of Christ for a game and a fable (Heb. 6), which the sale of merit, the ridiculous representation of the crucifixion and death of Christ, and profane mockery in words and deeds testify. Fifthly, Christ was truly crucified by Rome, inasmuch as he was delivered to the Roman Governor so that he might be affixed to the cross by Roman citizens, since the Jews confessed that it was not lawful for them to kill anyone (John 18:3).

Egypt is also deservedly called Rome on account of the affliction of the Lord's people, the seduction, the idolatry, Ezek. 16:26, Amos 4:10, the upbringing of the people by Moses in the bosom of the Egyptians, and the wonderful sustenance of those instructed in their wisdom, which also happened to the Church educated and informed by blessed Luther in the Papacy: the opulence and fertility of Egypt, Ezek. 31:18, Num. 11:5, just as the Roman Church is also very opulent and most fertile in all treasures: the Egyptian and Anti-Christian darkness and the light in the land of Goshen, the truly Catholic Church: the divine preservation and propagation of the Church among the miracles of Egypt and Rome to be admired on account of the obstinacy of Jannes and Jambres and the Roman False Prophet's twin but fictitious miracles, Apoc. 13:11: finally the punishment of Egypt and Rome: the destruction of the former in water, of the latter in the abyss of hell, Apoc. 19:20. Finally, it is not undeservedly compared to Sodom on account of the unspeakable lust which the Roman Pontiff fosters by granting brothels (the counsel of the chosen Cardinals offered to Paul III, Vol. 3 of the Councils, p. 823; Corn. Agrippa, Vanity of the Sciences, ch. 64) and by recommending (Tanner, part 3, Anatomy of Demonstrations, § 270) fornications to priests in place of marriage according to the prophecies of Dan. 11:37, 1 Tim. 4:7, by tolerating, nay approving, Sodomy and its public praises (witness the book of Giovanni della Casa in Sleidan, book 21, and Bale in his catalogue) and catamite pamphlets (such as that of Hieronymus Mutius, fortified by the bull of Julius III), by dispensing for incestuous marriages, and even by committing and perpetrating incest, which the tomb of Lucretia erected by Giovanni Gioviano Pontano teaches concerning the Roman Pontiff Alexander VI, who was most addicted to women:

Lucretia lies in this tomb by name, but in reality a Thais, daughter of Alexander, married, a daughter-in-law. Furthermore, by indulging in polygamy, a grave one. Stat. Imp. Can. 75. 91. Espens. in Tit. I. page 67. Caus. 32. q. 7. c. 28. what you proposed etc. Innocent III gave King Charles of the Gauls the power of divorce from his betrothed wife Margaret, daughter of Maximilian, and approved the abduction of the same, by which he violently seized the bride of the same Maximilian, Anna of Brittany, according to Micraelius, and on account of the punishment of fire, sent down from heaven, and hellish. Wilhelm. Paris. de collat. benefic. says the sins of Prelates and Priests are not simply sins, but most terrible monsters of sins, that they are not the Church, but Babylon, Egypt and Sodom; Arnulphus, Archbishop of Lyon, witness Trithemius in Chronic. Hirsaug. He said to the Papal Clergy: It is no wonder if you are about to hand over to death me, a sinner, announcing the truth to you, since even if St. Peter were to rise again today and rebuke your vices, which have multiplied too much, you would by no means spare him. Bale in the preface to the Acts of the Roman Pontiffs. King Henry VIII, when he had caused the monasteries of the cowled ones and the colleges of the sacrificers to be visited by venerable Doctors of laws, Thomas Legh, Richard Layton, and others in his kingdom before their final dissolution, which took place in the year 1538 from the birth of Christ, there were found in them such a number of fornicators, catamites, gluttons, boy-lovers, pederasts, sodomites, Ganymedes, yet all Votaries and Celibates, that you would have believed a new Gomorrah was present in each one of them. Their book is called The Breviary of the Corrupt in Monasteries etc., in which very many names of sodomites are read expressed. Aelia was not held in such high regard that it could be compared to Jerusalem and come under the name of a great city: nor is it situated in the same place: and the war of Barchocheba, neither by reason of time, nor by reason of the slain, who were not finished by war on account of the name of Christ, but because they would not receive Barchocheba as the Messiah, and because they themselves would not bear aid against the Roman soldier; nor is it certain about the bodies then unburied in the street: nor did those things concern the nations, tribes and tongues throughout the whole earth: wherefore they are wrongly and without sufficient cause restricted to Judea for the sake of ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως. He calls the inhabitants of the earth out of contempt, as in chapter VI, 10, men given to the earth, sworn to the beast, sons of the earth, immersed in earthly pursuits. This is the Catholic Anti-Christ Church on earth. What will they do? They will rejoice at the death and insult of the Martyrs: They will send gifts to one another as a sign of joy, as is accustomed to be done in Panegyric triumphs and public rejoicings. And yet it is too inhuman, not to say diabolical wickedness, to rejoice at the evils of others, to insult the afflicted. The sin, says Rupertus, is the most terrible of all, for the impious to rejoice when they have done evil and to exult in the worst things. For what will they laugh at? Certainly their own wickedness: at which they will rejoice, but they will laugh a Sardonic laugh. In the Council of Constance, regarding the burned Martyrs, there was public applause, public banquets were held, games were celebrated, as if over defeated enemies. Even today, as often as the faithful are burned, the locusts hold feasts and banquets: they sing the Te Deum Laudamus together, they congratulate one another with gospels and gifts sent. Therefore, this ἐπιχαιρεκακία of the beast's allies is not a reason why we should be offended today, but rather why we should be strengthened in the faith. For by such daring acts they prove the Anti-Christ to us, as here Paraeus.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Καὶ βλέπουσιν ἐκ τῶν λαῶν καὶ φυλῶν καὶ ἐθνῶν

καὶ γλωσσῶν] subauditur τινες, ut Matth. 23, 34. Luc. XI. 49. XXI. 16. Joh. XVI. 17. Multi erant Æliæ ex omnibus lin- guis & gentibus cum illa factio Barchochebæ ad tempus non longum prævaluit. Ἐκ παντὸς ἔθνες καὶ φυλῶν καὶ λαῶν ha- bes & supra VII. 9.

Τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν ἡμέρας τρεῖς ἥμισυ] nempe quamdiu factio Barchochebæ in Ælia prævaluit. Allusio autem non obscura ad locum Of. VI. 3.

Καὶ τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν ἐκ ἀφήσουσι τεθῆναι εἰς μνῆμα]. So- lent qui crudeles sunt etiam sepultura arcere eorum quæ ode- runt corpora, ut Agamemnon in Ajace & Geon Thebanus in Antigone apud Sophoclem: quod esse immanitatis Scy- thicæ dixit Seneca: Videat si cui vacat, quæ de ea re attu- limus libro II. de jure belli ac pacis XIX. 1. 3. Adde Psalm. LXXIX. 3. Ezech. XXVIII. 25. ubi similiter plateæ nominan- tur.

De interfectis testibus veritatis ita constat. De corporibus inhumatis dubium esse nequit, quum martyrum corpora, quæ non in cineres redacta, ceu hæreticorum sepelire nefas habeant bestiales illi tyranni. Quænam autem illa civitas magna? Magno consensu Interpretum Roma est, quæ πνευ- ματικῶς dicta illa, in qua Dominus noster cruci- fixus est. Ubi enim magis sanguis Domini pro- phanus habetur, & Dominus crucifigitur, quam Romæ? Ubi magis crucifiguntur membra ejus mystica, hoc est Dominus in membris suis, quam ibidem vel in Papatu universo? Nam Roma pro Papatu accipienda Romano, & civitas illa, in qua crucifigitur Dominus, extendit sese per univer- sum orbem vel totum Papatum Romanum: Cui ubique Papa cum Clero suo dominatur: Ideo ex- plicatur v. 9. 10. civitas de tribubus, populis & linguis, imo omnibus habitantibus super terram, uno nomine non expressa est, ut e diversis nomini- bus unius civitatis constaret, non esse intelligen- dum secundum literam unam civitatem. Nec satis exprimi indoles ejus potuit uno nomine; vocatur itaque Hierosolyma, ubi Christus crucifixus est, ob crucifixionem Christi multiplicem, Sodoma ob scortationem tum corporalem tum spiritualem; Ægyptus ob idololatriam & tyrannidem in po- pulum Domini. Hierosolymam tamen plerique Pontificii, quam Anti-Christi sedem faciunt, intel- ligere malunt. Tirinus imprimis ex hoc comma- te probare vult, Anti-Christum ceu Messiam Ju- dæis promissum, ut hæres solii Davidis & Salo- monis haberi possit, è ruderibus iterum excitatu- rum Hierosolymam una cum templo Salomonico, translata eo verisimiliter sede Regia, Babylone prius fi- xa, ad Bellarminum l. III. de R. P. remittens, eaque ratione putat corruere Achillem nostrum de Roma- no Pontifice Anti-Christo. Sed quomodo ex hoc oraculo docebitur, Hierosolymam fore sedem An- ti-Christi? Quomodo Hierosolyma proprie intel- ligenda, quod sit ipsa Sodoma secundum literam, si Sodoma & Ægyptus improprie accipienda? & quomodo totum Ægypti regnum est Hierosoly- ma? Quum ergo indubie mysticum hæc sensum habeant, eumque ipse Spiritus Sanctus voce πνευματικῶς indicatu voluerit, de ea civitate hæc omnino explicantur, quæ mystice & Sodoma & Ægyptus, & locus, ubi Christus crucifixus est, nun- cupari queat. Quomodo item templum Salomo- nis denuo excitandum dici potest, quum templum Zorobabelis novissimum dicatur, Hagg. II? Quis non videt omnia hæc commenta Papistica indigna confutatione? Nulla ergo civitas convenientius ita nominabitur, quam Roma ipsa. Unde An- glo Rhemenses ad Apoc. XVII. 18. calculum suum hic nobis non subtrahunt: Si hæc intelli- gantur de una aliqua civitate, verisimillimum est, Romam veterem denotari, ut ex Græcis nonnulli exponunt. Autoritate enim veteris Romani im- perii Christus primum neci traditus est, & dein- ceps de duo Principes Apostoli, eorumque successo- res, & infinita Christianorum multitudo. Et cele- bratur locus Romæ in via Appia sub nomine, Do- mine, quo vadis? quod Christus Petro profugo ita interroganti responderit: Romam iterum cru- cifigi. Vid. Bellarm. l. I. de R. P. c. 23. Quo faci- unt ilia S. Bernhardi ab Hugone de S.Charo Cardin. in Postilla ad 2. Joh. laudata: Videtur, bone Jesu, versus te conspirasse universitas Christianorum, & isti in tua persecutione primi sunt, qui in Ecclesia tua videntur primatum tenere, & gerere principa- tum. Waldenses certe palam circa Ann. Chri- sti 1160. professi sunt, quod Ecclesia Romana non sit Jesu Christi sponsa, sed Ecclesia malignantium, ebria sanguine Sanctorum. Bellarm. libr. IV. de Ec- cles. cap. 18. §. tempore sic habet: Tempore Inno- centii III. in Gallia ab octo millibus Catholicorum cæsa sunt uno prælio centum millia Albigensium hære- ticorum, ut scribit Æmilius l. VI. Histor. Franc. Respondet Roma Hierosolyma quoad splendorem, famam, jactantiam; de templo imprimis Domini Jer. VI. & superbiam quoad securitatem, extremam impietatem, odium & tyrannidem adversus Christum & sanctos ejus, Matth. XXIII.

Crucifixus autem Christus in illa civitate pri- mo in membris & testibus suis, Ezech. XXXVII. 24. Dan. VIII. 25. Act. IX. 4. Deinde crucifigitur quo- tidie & interficitur atque immolatur in Missati- co sacrificio: tertio in blasphemiis crucis & mortis suæ, Ebr. X. 29. quarto in impietate, quia pro lu- do & fabula habent crucem & mortem Christi, Ebr. VI. quod venditio meriti, crucifixionis & mor- tis Christi ridicula repræsentatio, & in dictis actisque profana irrisio testantur: quinto à Roma revera crucifixus est Christus, siquidem Romano Præsidi traditus, ut sic à Romanis civibus cruci affigere- tur, quum Judæi fassi sint, sibi ipsis non licere quen- quam interficere, Joh. XVIII. 3.

Ægyptus etiam merito dicitur Roma ob popu- li Domini afflictionem, seductionem, idololatriam, Ezech. XVI. 26. Am. IV. 26. populi per Mosen in Ægyptiorum sinu educationem, ipsorumque sa- pientia instructum, mirabilem sustentationem, quæ Ecclesiæ etiam per B. Lutherum in Papatu educatum & informatum accidit: Ægypti opulen- tiam & fœcunditatem, Ezech. XXXI. 18. Num. XI. 5. quemadmodum & Romana Ecclesia opulenta admodum est, omnibusq; thesauris fœcundissima: Ægyptiacas & Anti-Christianas tenebras & lucem in terra Gosen, Ecclesia vere Catholica: Ægypti & Romæ inter miracula admiranda divina conservatio- nis & propagationis Ecclesiæ propter Jannis & Jambres & Pseudo-Prophetæ Romani gemina sed fictitia miracula obstinationem. Apoc. XIII. 11. Ægy- pti denique & Romæ punitionem: illius in aqua, hu- jus in abysso inferni interitum Apoc. XIX. 20. Tan- dem & Sodoma non immerito confertur propter nefandam libidinem, quam Pontifex Romanus fo- vet, lupanaria concedendo (consil. delect. Cardin. Paulo III. oblatum T. III. Concil. p. 823. Corn. Agr. Vanit. Scient. c. 64) & commendando (Tanner. part. III. Anat. demonstr. §. 270.) Sacerdotibus loco con- jugii scortationes juxta vaticinia Dan. XI. 37. 1. Tim. IV. 7. permittendo, Sodomiam & laudes ejus publicas (testis est liber Joh. Casa apud Sleidanum l. XXI. & Balæum in catal.) & Cinædicos libellos (qualis est Hi- eronymi Zehed Mutii bulla Julii III. munitus) tole- rando, imo approbando, de incestuosis conjugiis dis- pensando, incestus etiam committendo, & perpe- trando, quod de Pontifice Rom. Alexandro VI. mulieribus maxime addicto tumul9 Lucretiæ à Jo- hanne Jovian. Pontano erectus docet:

Hoc jacet in tumulo Lucretia nomine, sed re Thais, Alexandri filia, nupta, nurus. Polygamiam insuper indulgendo, gravam. Stat. Imp. Can. 75. 91. Espens. in Tit. I. pag. 67. Caus. 32. q. 7. c. 28. quod proposuisti &c. Innocentius III. Carolo Regi Galliarum potestatem divortii cum uxore desponsata Margaretha, filia Maximiliani dedit, & ejusdem raptum, quo sponsam ejusdem Maximiliani Annam Britannicam vi rapuit, pro- bavit, apud Micrælium & propter pœnam ignis, de cœlo demissi, & infernalis. Wilhelm. Paris. de collat. benefic. peccata Prælatorum ac Sacerdo- tum dicit non simpliciter peccata esse, sed peccato- rum monstra terribilissima, eos non Ecclesiam, sed Babylonem, Ægyptum & Sodomam esse; Arnul- phus, Archi-Episcopus Lugdun. teste Trithemio in Chronic. Hirsaug. Clero Papali dixit: Non mi- rum, si hominem me peccatorem vobis veritatem annunciantem morti tradituri estis, cum etiamsi S. Petrus hodie resurgeret & vitia vestra, quæ nimis multiplicata sunt, reprehenderet, ei minime par- ceretis. Balæus in præfat. super Acta Pontif. Rom. Rex Henricus IIX. cum cuculligerorum cœ- nobia & sacrificorum collegia per venerabiles le- gum Doctores, Thomam Leum, Ricardum Lay- tonum, & alios in suo regno visitari fecisset ante ex- tremam eorum dissolutionem, quæ fiebat anno à Christi nativitate 1538. reperti sunt in illis tanto numero scortatores, Cinædi, Ganeones, Prædicones, Puerarii, Pæderastæ, Sodomitæ, Ganymedes, Vo- tarii tamen ac Cælibes omnes, ut in unoquoque eo- rum novam credideris adesse Gomorrham. Li- ber eorum vocatur Breviarium corruptorum in monasteriis &c. in quo nomina Sodomitarum ex- pressa leguntur bene multa. Ælia tanti non fuit habita, ut Hierosolymæ conferri & civitatis magnæ nomine venire queat: nec in eodem pla- ne loco sita: & Barchochebæ bellum neque ra- tione temporis, neque ratione interfectorum, qui non propter nomen Christi, sed quod Bar- chochebam pro Messia recipere nollent, bello confecti sunt, & quod ipsi nollent adversus Ro- manum militem ferre subsidium; nec de inhu- matis tum in platea corporibus constat: neque ea concernebant gentes, tribus & linguas per uni- versam terram: quare perperam & citra cau- sam sufficientem ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως gratia ad Judæ- am restringuntur. Incolas terræ per despectum, ut cap. VI, 10. vocat homines terræ deditos, bestiæ ju- ratos, terræ filios, terrenis studiis immersos. Hæc est Catholica Anti-Christi Ecclesia in terris. Quid facient? Gaudebunt nece & contumelia Marty- rum: Xenia invicem mittent in signum lætitiæ, ut solet fieri in Panegyricis triumphis lætitiis pu- blicis. Atqui nimis inhumanum, ne dicam ne- quitia diabolica est malis alienis lætari, afflictis insultare. Peccatum, inquit Rupertus, omnium dsterrimum est impios lætari, cum malefecerint & exultare in rebus pessimis. Quid enim ridebunt? Utique scelus suum: de quo gaudebunt, sed risum Sardonium ridebunt. In Concilio Constantiensi de Martyribus exustis publicus erat plausus, pu- blica convivia agitata, ludi celebrati, quasi de hostibus victis. Etiam hodie, quoties exuruntur fideles, locustæ festa & convivia agitant: Te De- um Laudamus concinunt, evangeliis & muneri- bus missis invicem gratulantur. Hæc igitur be- stiæ sociorum ἐπιχαιρεκακία non est cur hodie of- fendamur, sed potius cur in fide firmemur. Ta- libus enim ausis Anti-Christum nobis probant, ut hic Paræus.

## 11:10
Verse 10. Those who dwell on the earth.) In Judea, both Jews and foreigners, who had not been converted to Christ. They will rejoice over them, and will be glad.) Present for future. But other books have they will rejoice, to rejoice is referred to the mind, to be glad to the signs of the mind, such as feasts. And they will send gifts to one another.) As was the custom to be done in public joy. Esther IX, 19. 22. Because the two prophets.) Two lampstands, two Churches, which were of Elijah. They tormented those who dwell on the earth.) They had been troublesome both to the Jews, to whom they reproached evil customs, about which it was said above IX, 20. 21. Luke XV, 23. XVI, 19. and to the foreigners, to whom they reproached besides evil customs also idolatry, both by teaching and by living otherwise. Verse 11. And after three days and a half.) That faction having been ejected from the city by the Roman soldiers running together from all sides. The spirit of life from God went out upon them and they stood upon their feet.) Here again and they stood is placed in the Hebrew manner for so that they stood, upon them namely the witnesses, those two groups, which with the Roman state recovering immediately revived from those evils, and recovered their former state, and deservedly, because they had been enemies to the new things. Just as the Hebrews call good things life: so spirit is the cause of good things, Lam. IV, 20. To stand upon the feet is to be freed from fear, Ezekiel II, 1. 2.

Grotian matters can be judged from the things said before. The spirit of life is said to have entered into the slain, either because the Heralds of truth seemed completely extinguished, and buried with the very preaching of the Gospel; it will happen, however, by the wonderful goodness of Christ, that shortly, with the tyrants removed from the midst, they will revive, that is, that the preachers will be recalled from exile, freed from chains, absolved from slanders and sycophancies, and restored to their function after being dismissed, as here B. Hoë: Or, because Flacius, Chytreus, Cramerus, Winckelmannus, Heilbrunnerus, Wolterus, Gerhardus, Cluverus, Danhawerus, Junius, Pareus, add, because when GOD was continually raising up other witnesses, that was the same as if GOD were raising up the slain, just as Elijah could be believed to be raised up, when John was raised up acting in the spirit and power of Elijah; or because those witnesses are predicted here to be recalled to life again, as is explained later, on the last day, and to be exalted; which they testified with great boldness in the midst of death and the torments of martyrdom by the example of the Maccabean brothers, so that the tyrants themselves might be convinced of it in their conscience, as if they were already seeing it with their own eyes. When, says Pareus, the Anti-Christ shall think that he has oppressed all the witnesses of Christ, others having come to life again will renew the struggle. Just as therefore Elijah is said to have lived again in John the Baptist, not by Pythagorean metempsychosis, but by the condition of his office, because John came in the power and spirit of Elijah, preparing the way for Christ. So the two witnesses, suppose Huss and the Bohemian, having been taken away by the beast, after three days and a half lived again in Luther, Melanchthon, and others, etc. Nor does it obscurely contribute to this, that Huss, when he was being led to martyrdom, said to his enemies: After a hundred years have revolved (which before GOD are scarcely three days) you will answer to GOD and to me. He also said, that now indeed they were burning a goose (for Huss sounds like goose to the Bohemians) but from his ashes a swan would be born, which they would not be able to roast, presaging what would happen, which did come to pass. For so many years after Huss was burned, Luther began to attack Papal indulgences: which was the beginning of the purified doctrine and the decline of the Papacy. Which is to be observed against other Calvinists: But blessed Hoë rightly observes here: what it is for the satellites of the Anti-Christ to torture: Namely, if the heralds of truth deliver the Prophetic and Apostolic doctrine uncorrupted: if they send thirsting souls to the only fountain of righteousness and salvation, Jesus Christ, and not to the muddy marshes or empty cisterns of their own merits: If they [preach] that one God and not the saints is rightly invoked: if they fearlessly assert that there is no purgatory in which souls are tormented: that Papal indulgences are worth nothing: that the Roman Pope errs, nay, is the great Anti-Christ himself. These things sting, these things vex the adversaries of the truth most grievously. Hence those tears, and hence they complain of torment, especially if threats are added, that unless they repent, unless they abandon the Papacy, temporal and eternal punishments will be sent upon them. Such sermons are mere torments in the souls of the impious, mere tortures.

Latin:

Vers. 10. Οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.) In Judæa, tum Judæi, tum alienigenæ, qui ad Christum non erant conversi. Χαίρουσιν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ εὐφρανθήσονται.) Præsens pro futuro. Sed alii libri habent χαροῦσιν, χαίρειν ad animum refertur, εὐφραίνεσθαι ad signa animi, qualia sunt epulæ. Καὶ δῶρα πέμψουσιν ἀλλήλοις.) Ut in publica lætitia fieri mos erat. Esther IX, 19. 22. Ὅτι οἱ δύο προφῆται.) Duo candelabra duæ Ecclesiæ, quæ erant Eliæ. Ἐβασάνισαν τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.) Molesti fuerant & Judæis, quibus malos mores, de quibus dictum supra IX, 20. 21. Luc. XV, 23. XVI, 19. & alienigenis, quibus præter malos mores etiam idololatriam, tum docendo, tum aliter vivendo exprobrabant. Vers. 11. Καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ ἥμισυ.) Factione illa per milites Romanos undique concurrentes ex urbe ejecta. Πνεῦμα ζωῆς ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς καὶ ἔστησαν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας αὑτῶν.) Hic rursus καὶ ἔστησαν more Ebræo ponitur pro ὥστε τὸ στῆναι, ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς nempe τοὺς μάρτυρας, illos duos cœtus, qui Romana re revalescente statim ex illis malis revixerunt, & priorem statum recuperarunt, & merito, quia inimici fuerant rebus novis. Sicut vitam vocant Ebræi res bonas: ita spiritum causam rerum bonarum, Lam. IV, 20. Stare super pedes est à metu liberari Ezech. II, 1. 2.

Grotiana ex antea dictis dijudicari poterunt. Spiritus vitæ intrasse in occisos dicitur, vel quod videbantur Præcones veritatis penitus extincti, & cum ipsa prædicatione Evangelii sepulti; fiet tamen miranda bonitate Christi, ut brevi, sublatis è medio tyrannis, reviviscant, hoc est, ut prædicatores ab exilio revocentur, è vinculis liberentur, à calumniis & sycophantiis absolvantur, & exautorati functioni suæ restituantur, ut hic B. Hoë: Vel, quod Flacius, Chytreus, Cramerus, Winckelmannus, Heilbrunnerus, Wolterus, Gerhardus, Cluverus, Danhawerus, Junius, Pareus, addunt, quia cum alios subinde testes DEUS excitaret, idem id erat, ac si DEUS occisos excitaret, quemadmodum Elias excitatus credi poterat, cum excitaretur Johannes in spiritu & virtute Eliæ agens; vel quia testes illi denuo, ut postea explicatur, in vitam revocandi in novissimo die, & exaltandi hic prædicuntur; quod magna cum παῤῥησίᾳ media in morte ac tormentis martyriorum exemplo fratrum Maccabaicorum testati sunt, ut in conscientia de eo ipsomet Tyranni convincerentur, quasi id jam oculis suis viderent. Quando, inquit Pareus, Anti-Christus putabit, se omnes Christi testes oppressisse, redivivi alii certamen renovabunt. Sicut ergo Elias dicitur revixisse in Johanne Baptista, non μετεμψυχώσει Pythagorica, sed officii conditione, quia Johannes venit in virtute & spiritu Eliæ, Christo viam præparans. Ita duo testes puta Hussus & Pragensis à bestia sublati post tres dies & dimidium revixerunt in Luthero, Melanchtone aliis &c. Nec obscurè huc facit, quod Hussus, cum ad martyrium duceretur, hostibus dixit: Centum revolutis annis (qui coram DEO vix triduum sunt) DEO & mihi respondebitis. Dixit quoque, nunc quidem anserem eos exurere (Huss enim Bohemis anserem sonat) ex cineribus vero suis nasciturum olorem, quem torrere non poterunt, præsagiens futurum, quod evenit. Tot annis enim Lutherus post Hussum exustum indulgentias Papales oppugnare cœpit: quod initium fuit repurgatæ doctrinæ & inclinati Papatus. Quod contra alios Calvinianos observandum: Recte autem hic observat B. Hoë: quid sit Anti-Christi satellitibus cruciare: Nimirum si præcones veritatis doctrinam Propheticam & Apostolicam incorrupte tradunt: si animas sitientes ad unicum fontem justitiæ & salutis Jesum Christum, & non ad paludes turbidas vel cisternas vacuas propriorum meritorum mittunt: Si unum Deum & non san- ctos recte invocari: si nullum purgatorium, in quo torquentur animæ: si nihil valere Papales indulgen- tias: si Papam Romanum errare, imo ipsum esse An- ti-Christum magnum intrepide afferunt. Hæc urunt, hæc pessime habent veritatis Adversarios. Hinc illæ lacrymæ, & hinc de cruciatu quiritantur, præsertim si accedant minæ, nisi resipuerint, nisi Papatum dese- ruerint, fore ut temporales & æternæ pœnæ ipsis im- mittantur. Tales conciones mera sunt in animis im- piorum tormenta, meri cruciatus.

## 11:11
And great fear fell upon those who were watching them.] Who saw them restored in such a short time from the aforementioned state, and that by idolaters. The words are taken from Dan. X, 7.

They feared lest they should be tormented again by the witnesses; or because they were beginning to shudder at their future glory and blessedness, Wisd. V, 20. seqq. B. Hoë says: History and experience, even of our own times, most clearly testify that the event corresponds exactly to the words. For after the Papists took the most pious confessors of the truth, Jerome of Prague, Huss, Savonarola, and others, out of the way, they thought they had already won the victory against the witnesses and the testimony of Christ and were secure: But when they perceived Huss and Savonarola reviving in Luther, his colleagues and successors, and as it were reassuming their spirits, good God, what trepidation arose among them everywhere! For they saw that by banishing, burning, and killing they were accomplishing nothing at all, and could not inhibit or hold back the course of the Gospel by those violent means: but rather that the blood of the martyrs is the seed of the Church, so that the more witnesses of the Truth are burned and killed, the more are born and arise daily. Such, clearly, is the power of God, that it can drive even the boldest of the bold to a trembling of despair, as it were, and to extreme terror: a fact which is manifest from the history of the passion alone.

Latin:

Καὶ φόβος μέγας ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τοὺς θεωροῦντας αὐτούς.] Qui eos ex prædicto videbant tam brevi restitutos, idque per ido- lolatras. Verba sumpta ex Dan. X, 7.

Metuebant, ne iterum à testibus cruciarentur; sive quod ob gloriam & beatitudinem illorum futuram jam horrere inciperent Sap. V, 20. seqq. B. Hoë: Eventum, inquit, exacte respondere ver- bis vel nostrorum temporum historia & experientia luculentissime testatur. Postquam enim Pontificii piissimos veritatis confessores Hieronymum Pragen- sem, Hussum, Savanarolam, & alios è medio sustule- runt, jamjam se victoriam adversus testes & testimo- nium Christi reportasse putarunt & securi fuerunt: Cum vero Hussum & Savanarolam in Luthero, colle- gis & successoribus reviviscere, & quasi Spiritus suos reassumere deprehenderunt, Deum immortalem, quanta ubique trepidatio apud ipsos oborta fuit! Vi- derunt enim se relegando, comburendo, occidendo ni- bil prorsus efficere, & cursum Evangelii violentis illis mediis inhibere ac retrahere non posse: quin potius sanguinem Martyrum semen Ecclesiæ esse, ut quo plu- res Veritatis testes comburuntur & occiduntur, eo plures indies nascantur & oriantur. Tanta videli- cet est Dei potentia, ut audaculos etiam audacissimos ad tremorem desperationis quasi & extremum pavo- rem adigere possit: id, quod vel ex sola passionis histo- ria manifeste patet.

## 11:12
Vers. 12. And I heard a great voice from heaven, saying to them.] To those witnesses, that is, to the two Churches.

Come up here.] Just as it had been said to John above III, 1. But that pertains to this, that they might understand the new mysteries of God, as if admitted into the cabinet.

And they ascended into heaven in the cloud.] The cloud here also signifies the efficacy of God, as above I, 1.

Those two witnesses are said to have heard these things about the ascension into heaven, because they are to raise themselves up in these persecutions, with the Holy Spirit dwelling in them confirming them, Romans VIII. v. 17. whom God also overshadowed with the cloud of His omnipotence and grace, Psalm XCI. And although their bodies are inglorious and unburied, their souls shall nevertheless be gloriously assumed, Apoc. XIV.

And their enemies beheld them.] Sight among the Hebrews signifies every sense, whether internal or external. But here it seems to be taken for to wonder, as in the Greek of Psalm XLVI, 18. LXVIII, 25. LXXIII, 2. Before, they had not believed the predictions of the Christians. Now, seeing them fulfilled, with the faction of Bar Kokhba ejected from the city of Aelia, they marveled at all things they were saying as if divinely revealed.

From their constancy, patience, and happy death, the faithful could gather that they had been servants of God, and therefore were received into heavenly glory.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, λεγούσης αὐτοῖς.] Testibus illis, id est, Ecclesiis duabus.

Ἀνάβατε ὧδε.] Sicut Johanni dictum fuerat supra III, 1. Id autem eo pertinet, ut nova Dei arcana intelligant, velut in secretarium admissi.

Καὶ ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ.] Nubes hic quo- que efficaciam Dei significat, ut supra I, 1.

Audivisse duo illi testes hæc dicuntur de ascen- sione in cælum, quod ea se erecturi sint in istis per- secutionibus, confirmante ipsos Spiritu Sancto habitante in illis, Roman. IIX. v. 17. quos etiam omnipotentiæ & gratiæ suæ nube obumbravit Deus, Psalm. XCI. Et quamvis eorum corpora ingloria sint, & inhumata, animæ tamen gloriose assumentur, Apoc. XIV.

Καὶ ἐθεώρησαν αὐτοὺς οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτῶν.] Visus apud Ebræos omnem sensum, sive internum, sive externum significat. Hic vero sumi videtur pro mirari, ut in Græco Psalm. XLVI, 18. LXVIII, 25. LXXIII, 2. Ante non crediderant Christiano- rum prædictis. Nunc ea impleta videntes, ejecta ex urbe Æ- lia factione Barchochebæ, omnia quæ dicebant, tanquam di- vinitus revelata admirabantur.

Ex ipsorum constantia, patientia, εὐθανασίᾳ colligere poterant fideles, illos Dei servos fuisse, ac proinde in cœlestem gloriam recipi.

## 11:13
Vers. 13. And in that day there was a great earthquake.] An earthquake signifies a change of affairs. 'Was' here is pluperfect. For it shows how the Churches recovered their state, namely, when the Romans were prevailing.

By this earthquake is signified the grave shaking of the Anti-Christian kingdom, which was brought about not only by various foreign and barbaric peoples, Huns, Goths, Vandals, of whom one, Attila, is said to have been called the scourge of GOD, and to have killed eleven thousand of the female sex alone and of the breath of life near Cologne. The Lombards, with King Alboin entering Italy around the year of Christ 568, presuming to destroy all Christians with the sword, and attempting it in reality by tearing down temples, hanging monks, killing priests, and slaughtering the Milanese; Vergerius reports that in the space of barely 30 years 150,000 Christians were finished off by various kinds of death by the Papal inquisition: But it was also suffered by Christian Kings and Emperors themselves: Whom, however, it stirred up against its own neck. Probus, Bishop of Toul, in a speech delivered to his colleagues in the year 1280, professed: How long, dearest colleagues, will those Romulean vultures abuse our patience, not to say our stupidity? How long shall we tolerate their outrages, avarice, pride, and luxury? This WORST kind of Archisynagogue will not cease until it has reduced everyone to poverty and HARDEST SLAVERY. Our discord has caused this evil to grow; our discord those SCOUNDRELS have used. Nor, as long as they remain safe, will it ever be permitted for Christians to maintain a firm peace, to refrain from arms, or to cultivate piety among themselves. Recently they set the Saxons and Swabians against one another: then they deprived the divine Frederick II, most useful to the Christian Republic, and Conrad IV, the Swabians, and the best Princes, of their Empire and their lives at the same time. In Germany, the agents of Satan and the ANTICHRIST have sown the evils of discord. Afterwards, they intercepted Conrad, a most innocent, most undeserving youth of excellent character, the offspring of divine men, who was seeking the inheritance of his ancestors by the law of nations, through fraud and deceit, and killed him most cruelly. They set the Swabians and the Austrian Franks against one another in arms, as if composing a spectacle and a match for themselves. Then they incited the Spaniards against them. Now they strive to incite us against the nobles of Gaul and Spain, our kinsmen who once set out from Germany. Keep in mind what that truly egregious tenth [Pope] did with the tithes twelve years ago: the fourth [Pope] will do the same with the fourths. In order for the most vigilant Gregory to milk those from us, he armed the Scythians, Arabs, and Turks against us. I would be lying if I said they do not want the enemy (namely, the greatest tax) to be MORE SAFE THAN US, etc.

And the tenth of the city fell.] No less than a tenth part of Aelia perished, both from the faction of Bar Kokhba and from those who had imprudently followed that faction.

Latin:

Vers. 13. Καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγένετο σεισμὸς μέγας.] Ter- ræ motus rerum mutationem significat. Ἐγένετο hic est plus- quamperfectum. Ostendit enim, quomodo Ecclesiæ statum suum receperint, nempe Romanis præpollentibus.

Per hunc terræ motum significatur gravis re- gni Anti-Christiani concussio, quam non tan- tum à variis exteris & barbaricis populis Hun- nis, Gothis, Vandalis, è quibus unus Attila flagel- lum DEI dictus fertur virginei solum sexus, & flatus apud Coloniam Agrippinam undecies mil- lia peremisse. Longobardi Rege Albiano circa Ann. Christi 568. Italiam ingresso præsumente omnes Christianos gladio delere, atque id reapse tentante, templa diruendo, Monachos suspendendo, Sacerdotes interficiendo, Mediolanenses caedendo; Vergerius refert vix 30. annorum spatio 150000. Christianorum variis mortis generibus inquisitione Papali confectorum: Sed ab ipsis etiam Christianis Regibus & Imperatoribus id passum est: Quos ipsos tamen in cervicem suam excitavit. Probus Episcopus Tullensis apud Aventinum oratione anno 1280. ad collegas habita professus est: Quousque collegae charissimi Romulei illi vultures patientia nostra, ne dicam stultitia abutentur? Quousque eorum flagitia, avaritiam, superbiam, luxum tolerabimus? Non cessabit hoc genus Archisynagogam PESSIMUM, nisi omnes ad egestatem & SERVITUTEM DURISSIMAM redegerit. Discordia nostra hocce malum crevit, discordia nostra ILLI NEBULONES usi sunt. Nec unquam quamdiu illi salvi fuerint, Christianis fistam pacem servare, ab armis feriari, pietatem inter se colere licebit. Nuper Saxones atque Suevos inter se commiserunt: deinde Divum Fridericum II. Reipublicae Christianae utilissimum, Conradum IV. Suevos atque optimos Principes Imperio simul atque vita privarunt. In Germania discordiae mala Satanae & ANTICHRISTI satrapae seminarunt. Conradum postea insontissimum, immeritissimum, & optimae indolis adolescentem, prolem Divorum, jure gentium haereditatem majorum repetentem, fraude, dolo interceperunt, ac crudelissime necarunt. Suevos atque Francos Vestriacos inter se armis, veluti spectaculum sibi ac paria componentes commiserunt. Deinde adversus hos Hispanos concitarunt. Nunc nos adversus Galliae & Hispaniae proceres cognatos nostros ex Germania quondam profectos concitare nituntur. In memoria habete, quid ante duodecim annos ille sane egregius decimus cum decimis egerit: idem quartus cum quartis aget. Ut illas Gregorius vigilantissimus a nobis emungeret, Scythas, Arabes, Turcas in nos armavit. Mentiar nisi hoste (nempe maximum vectigal) MAGIS SALVOS, QUAM NOS, esse velint, &c.

Καὶ τὸ δέκατον τη̃ς πόλεως ἔπεσε.] Non minus parte decima interiit Aeliae, tum ex factione Barchochebae, tum ex iis, qui eam factionem improvide erant secuti.

## 11:14
Verse 14. And in the earthquake were killed seven thousand names of men.] This is significant in the new colony, 'names of men,' that is, of every sex, provided they are called human beings. See above III, 4.

The tenth part of the city, according to the interpretation of B. Hoë, falls: 1. corporally: For they will be struck by deserved plagues from GOD, because they thirsted for blood, they will die in blood. 2. spiritually: for its authority will be diminished, its power will fall, its opulence will fall, its dread among many peoples and nations will fall: obedience will fall: all observance toward the Roman see will fall: so that those who were previously entirely addicted to the Papal Kingdom will most strongly oppose it. See how gravely GOD wishes and is able to avenge the injuries inflicted upon his servants. If all these things are compared with histories, they will become clearer and more illustrious: Did not a great commotion of the peoples follow immediately when Jerome of Prague and John Huss were burned at Constance? The Bohemians certainly harassed the Romans with a most grave war and afflicted them in a horrible manner: Just as Aeneas Sylvius, the Pontiff himself, Roman, described the whole history of that Bohemian commotion, and by no means denied that many thousands of men were killed in that movement: that very many also defected from the Papacy and gave glory to God: but also when, within our memory, a savage persecution was stirred up against Christians at the instigation of the Anti-Christian see, Rome was captured (in the year 1527) beyond all expectation and was so afflicted and plundered that that calamity can be compared with the ancient and greatest ruins and calamities of Rome. Let the last seven books of Sleidan’s histories be read; they will interpret this period concerning the fates of the Anti-Christians most beautifully: but because the Apostle says that precisely the tenth part of the city will fall, and seven thousand men will be killed, we learn from that not to strike at God with blind fury and like Andabatae, but that those whom He wishes to be struck with His scourges are designated as if by name. Let everyone, therefore, open their eyes in time, and see diligently that they are not deceived by the harlot-like enticements of the Anti-Christian, and thus be dragged by GOD along with other Anti-Christians to just punishments. How miserably even the Popes themselves perished by the just judgment of God, the blessed Gerhard teaches in Conf. Cath. lib. II. p. 1278. In the appendix to chapter 19 of the second distinction, concerning Anastasius II. (who sat around the year 496) it is read thus: Because he gave these rescripts illicitly and not canonically, but against the decrees of his predecessors and successors, as Felix and Gelasius prove, who excommunicated Acacius before Anastasius, and Hormisdas, who, being the third after Anastasius himself, later condemned the same Acacius, therefore he is repudiated by the Roman Church, and is read to have been struck by God. Johannes de Turrecremata in his book on the power of the Church: It is well read that Anastasius perished, struck by a divine nod. Sylvester II (who sat around the year 898), when he had celebrated mass in the Basilica of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem at Rome, was extinguished by the Devil according to a pact. Christopher I (who sat around the year 902) ended his life miserably in prison. John X (who sat around the year 913) was suffocated in prison with a pillow thrust into his mouth. John XIII (who sat around the year 965) perished having confessed to adultery. Boniface VII. (who sat around the year 974) perished by a sudden death, tormented by the conscience of his crimes. Hadrian IV (who sat around the year 1154), while he himself, cursed by God, was denoting excommunication against the Emperor, as he wished to draw water from a spring, a fly flying into his mouth stuck to his throat, by which he was miserably suffocated. Nicholas III (who sat around the year 1277) died suddenly. Paul II (who sat around the year 1464) died in the middle of the night, with no one present, although he had been cheerful in the Consistory on that same day, and had consumed two melons the day before his death. Alexander VI (who sat around the year 1492) perished by poison, incautiously served, which he had ordered to be prepared for another. But why many words? It is known to be celebrated by a proverb that poison is the death of Popes. Let Platina, Johannes Stella, Bale, Nauclerus, Sabellicus, and others who have written about the lives of the Popes be seen.
