John of Salisbury in Policraticus, book 6, chapter 24, writes that he thinks the Popes live so briefly and die so suddenly, lest they corrupt the whole Church. Where more is read about other clerics. The blessed Cluverus explains the names of men thus: How are the names of men killed, unless when they are removed, depressed, and cast down as if into dust? Thus the reputations and authorities of Apostolic nuncios, Cardinals, Proctors, Legates a latere, Abbots, Priors, and I know not whom else having the name and value of the beast are diminished, expunged, and mystically killed, when the dignity of the Roman Church falls through an earthquake. Living practice shows the fulfillment. If you wish for the names of men to stand for the men themselves, as above in chapter III, 4, the fulfillment is likewise clear. For in the violent and sudden mutations of empires and republics, a sufficiently large multitude of Romanists also perished, as is conspicuous in the histories of the German, Gallic, Scottish, English, Belgian, and Bohemian wars. Moreover, the number seven is sacred and perfect in the whole Apocalypse, and so it is also in this place, so that it is not necessary to aspire to a determined number, or to undertake anxious thought about it.

And the rest became afraid.] Namely, those who were Elijah’s, they no longer dared to oppose the Romans.

The blessed Hoëas applies all these things excellently to the blessed Luther, whose words it is pleasing to use here: No one except an enemy and an envious person detracts from the praises of the olive tree and the candlestick from the blessed Luther: how great his power was, the matter even now speaks: Did not the fire of the divine word go out from his mouth? Did not that fire devour many of his enemies? And did he not kill spiritually, indeed more than forty heretics, as the blessed Luther writes that he slaughtered with this single ignited sword of the word? Did he not predict all kinds of plagues and punishments for the Anti-Christian flock, and successfully obtain the vengeance of the divine name by his prayers: so that the enemies of truth had to lack rain and heavenly dew, and had to see water turned into blood and the earth struck with every plague. Indeed, the blessed Luther also finished his testimony, and persevered in zeal and hatred against the Pope until the very last breath of his life. On the contrary, throughout the whole course of his ministry he felt the persecutions of the Anti-Christ: for the Roman beast, which ascended from the abyss, fought most bitterly against him: and although it could not openly kill this wonder-worker by force, yet by its frequent proscriptions, calumnies, machinations, and other means of this kind, it prematurely deprived the holy Man of God of his life, and when the death of Luther became known, it is unspeakable how that beast exulted at this name: how those inhabiting the earth rejoiced for joy, how they sent congratulatory gifts to one another: because that Prophet had died, who had so greatly tormented the seat of the Anti-Christ. And although they thought they had completely emerged as victors over Luther, and dreamed that the memory and doctrine of Luther would be completely buried: yet they were wonderfully disappointed in their hope: for the spirit of life from God entered into him, and he stood upon his feet in his faithful disciples and successors: so that when the Papists saw the doctrine of Luther propagated by succeeding theologians with such a Spirit, they were overwhelmed with very great fear: And although they consigned Luther to the Evil Spirit with their brute thunderbolts: yet they saw and recognized by the fates that he had ascended into heaven with his faithful colleagues, because the impious Romanists will also one day see Luther resting in the bosom of God with great gnashing of teeth. Concerning the earthquake, the fall of the city, and the defection from the Papacy, it is not necessary to say anything more. Our walls bear witness that all these things happened within the memory of our ancestors concerning the doctrine of St. Luther, and are happening today, nor does it help to weave in historical accounts now, since they have been sufficiently described in Sleidan and the sixteenth century of Osiander. B. Cluverus explains these things thus: He does not mean this, that all the citizens of Babylon who were not killed were truly converted to Christ (for that is openly denied in chapter XVI and following), but that out of fear, when they saw that so many names of men had perished, they did not dare to attempt anything further against the witnesses, but were compelled to give honor to God. Thus, the forced confession of the glory of God is understood in Josh. 7:19, John 9:24. He does not, however, reject the former sense; and thus when he denies that the λοιποὺς ἀνθρώπους, who were killed, repented, he does not mean all the rest (for otherwise he would leave no pious people on earth) but simply others. Thus Matt. 27:49, Luke 8:10, and 18:11. λοιποὶ means others, and the word has a similar value throughout.

Καὶ ἔδωκαν δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.] Many, having seen these things, were converted to Christ.

Such, for example, are those who in France, England, Belgium, Bohemia, Hungary, Poland, Livonia, Courland, Lithuania, Prussia, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Lapland, etc., having recognized the Papal idolomania, gave glory to God and began to worship Him alone, being very numerous as assertors and defenders of the true faith against the Roman Anti-Christ, and most strong in the power of the Spirit, 2 Cor. 10:4. He complains about this

Bellarminus, book on the Anti-Christ, ch. 21, § & ab hoc: From that time, when by your account the Pope began to be the Anti-Christ, his empire has not only not grown, but has always decreased more and more. In the time of Leo the Great, that is, one hundred and fifty years before the Anti-Christ was born according to your opinion, the Roman Pope presided over more nations than the borders of the Roman Empire extended themselves. For thus the same Leo writes in sermon I on the birthday of the Apostles: (Rome), having been made the head of the world through the holy seat of St. Peter, presides more widely through divine religion than through earthly domination. For although, increased by many victories, you have extended the right of your empire by land and sea, yet that which warlike labor has subdued for you is less than that which the Christian peace has subjected. And Prosper in the book on the ungrateful: The Roman seat of Peter, which has been made the head of pastoral honor for the world, holds whatever it does not possess by arms, by religion. But afterwards, with the Anti-Christ (as you wish) reigning, the Roman seat gradually lost almost all of Africa, the greatest part of Asia, and the whole of Greece. In our own times, however, in which you shout that the Anti-Christ is raging most, all things have succeeded so prosperously for him that he has lost a great part of Germany, Sweden, Gothia, Norway, the whole of Denmark, and a good part of England, France, Switzerland, Poland, Bohemia, and Pannonia. Therefore, if to act prosperously is a mark of the Anti-Christ, not the Pope, who has been stripped of so many provinces, but Luther, who by the preaching of carnal liberty seduced so many peoples and acted so prosperously that from a private monk he emerged as the prophet of all Germany and a kind of Pope, can deservedly be called the Anti-Christ. This is the singular B. Gravius: It is added in the same v. 13 that seven thousand names of men were killed, that is, a huge multitude of famous men, both ecclesiastical and political, leaders of war, nobles, and the wealthy perished, who partly fell in battles, partly were driven out when cities and regions were devastated, and perished in exile. If therefore so many famous men fell, without doubt an infinite number of commoners perished during this war. The rest, however, are said to have been terrified and to have given glory to God, v. 13. For without doubt the remaining Papists and their supporters, seeing that it is impossible to kick against the pricks, will desire peace or will be converted. B. Micraelius also reports examples concerning the Italians, Hist. Eccles. book III, p. 402. From Italy itself Luther in the year XLII received letters from Modena and Bologna, as also two years later from Venice and Vicenza, from those who applauded him. And already in the time of Clement VII, when the Pope was being harassed by the Imperialists, very many were preaching the Gospel in private houses of cities and especially in the territory of the Pontiff at Faenza, as witnessed by Petr. Suav. Polanus in the history of the Council of Trent, book I. We have already said above that Varaglinus, the author of the Capuchin Order, a Piedmontese, acknowledged the truth of the faith and completed his martyrdom. Sleidanus testifies to the same in book XXI, where he describes the conversion of the Vergerii and their Evangelical sermons. Petrus Martyr, a Florentine, of whom we have already spoken above, having held various dignities in Italy, led not a few, and among them the Spaniard Johannes Valdesius, a jurist, out of darkness with him, and courageously taught the Gospel at Lucca and Pisa, and having been driven from Italy, he taught theology at Strasbourg, in England, and in Switzerland. In the court of Renata, daughter of Louis XII, King of France, who was married to Hercules, Duke of Ferrara, illuminated by the light of the Gospel, flourished M. Antonius Flaminius, Marcellus Palingenius, Daniel Tossanus, and others. Galeacius Caracciolus, Marquis of Vico, nephew of Paul V by his sister, having put aside the dignity of the Marquisate, of which he was the heir, and having left his most beautiful wife with six children, betook himself to Geneva for the sake of religion, and remained unmoved in the acknowledgment of the truth, content with a private but sufficiently blessed life, and in the year LXXXVI, having taken a wife after the former one, who had made a divorce, he died piously. Johannes Bernhardinus Bonifacius, Marquis of Oria, preferred Christ to all the goods of this life in perpetual exile. For the Italians had begun to perceive what Nic. Machiavelli the Florentine says in his time, book I, Discourses on the Republic, ch. 12: That nowhere is there less piety or religion than in those men who live nearer to Rome: and if anyone compares that cult of religion which is in use in this age with the first institution of the Christian religion and its true foundations, he cannot but fear either its destruction or dread divine vengeance: that the Swiss themselves, who alone seem to preserve the ancient cult of religion and military discipline, would be corrupted by the gravity of the Roman curia if it were brought to them. Concerning the holy war or the crusade, a certain monk Hottinger. sect. XI, p. 484, reports thus: In the conquest of Jerusalem alone so much human blood was shed that, if faith is to be placed in Robert the Monk, the bodies of the slain swam and floated in the wave of blood: so much so that such a horrible shedding of blood struck horror even into the victors themselves; Paris p. 46. Concerning Pope John who was deposed, see the same p. 196. And concerning the wars p. 408. Around the same stretch of time all the Bishops, Princes, leaders, and standard-bearers of the civil war, by which the Republic was worn down for seventeen years, were extinguished in one year. He reports from Walram that Burchard of Halberstadt stood in battle against the Emperor thirteen times, Calv. A.C. 1087. From Baronius p. 17. Thus indeed all things at Rome, both sacred and profane, were mixed with factions, so that the promotion to the Apostolic Roman seat was in the power of that party. of the Pontiff, which appeared more powerful, so that now the Roman nobles, now the Prince of Etruria, might intrude by secular power whom he wished, and cast down whom he could, a Roman Pontiff promoted by the opposing faction. These things were transacted during almost this whole century, until the Emperors of Germany, the OTHONES (cf. Naucl. Gen. 33. p. 143. Platin. in Bened. VI. where he calls Otho a very good man, and a most keen defender of the Roman Church), intervened as mediators between both opposing parties, although they themselves also arrogated to themselves equally the election and deposition of Popes. Victor III. p. 547. is crowned, but it was not permitted for him to be secure for long. For Clement III., coming to Rome, drives Victor into the citadel of St. Angelo, and celebrates mass in the temple of Maria Rotunda. Urban, substituted for Victor, writes to the Bishop of Constance, that a synod being convened, he should excommunicate Pope Clement. In England, Anselm acknowledges Urban as the legitimate Pontiff. But the King [acknowledges] Clement III., who in the year of Christ 1098, at Rome in the Church of Maria Rotunda, through a legate, proclaimed a Council for the 7th of August, in which, with safe conduct, he summoned all who were of the parties of Hildebrand or Urban, that they might render an account why for sixteen years they had disturbed the Church with schism. But when they did not appear, their decrees were burned. Aventinus, Annal. lib. V. p. 531, speaks of three Popes sitting at Rome at one time, besides very many others. The Saracens, p. 650, invading Etruria and Latium, plundered Rome. In the year 846, Illyria and Dalmatia having been vexed, crossing the Adriatic sea, they plundered and burned Ancona, a city of Picenum. Drechsler, lib. Hist. Arab. A. 860, occupied the lands of the Romans lived Omar, son of Abidus, Actaus, and from them he carried off 70,000 men. Elm. p. 151. year 864. Emperor Constantine on the 17th of August, year 766, proposes an edict concerning monks, that they be expelled from monasteries, and take wives, and lead a civil life. In Miscell. The following year Constantine summoned all monks from all of Asia to Ephesus, and commanded them the same thing that he had in the previous year in Europe, that they should either, having been induced to wear common clothes, take wives, or, having had their eyes gouged out, be deported to Cyprus. Cedren. The same edict was repeated by the same Emperor in the year of Christ 770. See also Zonaras on Constantine Copronymus, p. 551. The Eastern Pontiffs resisted him, especially the Patriarchs of Constantinople, saying that they were at times equal or superior to the Roman Pontiff, Geneb. year of Christ 885. The struggles between Photius and the Pope are well known. See Catal. Test. Verit. book 9, p. 12 and 21. Then also he had a huge struggle with the Roman Pontiff concerning that matter, because he, out of ambition, claimed for himself dominion over the Churches, and contended that all controversies should be defined by his own sole judgment and opinion, and he wrote a book against Pope Nicholas, which he took care to have subscribed to by many Bishops: as is evident from the Pontifical book in the life of Hadrian. How many hostile incursions (for something must also be said about these) the Roman Empire sustained in this century from the Saracens and Persians alone, can hardly be told. See Elmacinus in the Saracen history, Zonaras in the annals. Let us bring forward a few things from the history of the Arabs by Wolffgang Drechsler. 638. Jerusalem was devastated by the Saracens after a two-year siege. 639. All of Syria was afflicted by a disaster from the Saracens. 640. The Saracens defected from the Roman Emperor. 641. Antioch was overturned by the Saracens, Damascus captured, Phoenicia attacked, Egypt subjugated. 648. The Saracens subjugated the greatest part of Africa to their empire. 655. Rhodes, a most noble island, was attacked by the Saracens, and capturing it, they carried off a great deal of gold from it: and they are said to have loaded nine hundred camels with the bronze of the Colossus of the Sun, a noble statue 110 feet high, which was sold to the Jews. 656. They infested the Aegean Sea with piracy, and brought many damages to the Cyclades islands. 663. The Saracens routed Olympius, the Exarch of Italy, in Sicily with his whole army. 672. The Saracens broke into Sicily, and having captured Syracuse and devastated every land, they returned to Alexandria. 686. The Saracens, with King Amirath, invaded Africa and Libya, enriched with many spoils. 687. When Constantine died, Justinian entered into peace with the Saracens on such conditions that, with Africa and Libya restored to the empire, they would pay for ten years one thousand gold pieces every day, and a horse with a noble boy in place of tribute. 688. This treaty having been broken, Justinian, entering into battle with the Saracens, suffered much damage from them. 692. The Romans having been routed by the Saracens, the Saracen name grew, the dignity of the Romans was greatly diminished. We have seen this slaughter inflicted upon the Roman Empire by the Saracens in a very short time. Nor were the Persians much more merciful in this century under Phocas, with Zonaras as witness; they subjugated Syria, Palestine, and Phoenicia. They made plundering incursions into Armenia, Cappadocia, Paphlagonia, and Dalmatia, having progressed as far as Chalcedon. Thus it is reported in the history of Heraclius, that the Persians, raiding the Eastern provinces, subjugated some and plundered others, and the Roman legions were defeated and slaughtered by them, with few escaping by flight. And when, as Chosroes writes, he was plundering and devastating everything, and Palestine having been occupied, he had also stormed Jerusalem. it is said that an infinite multitude of Christians was destroyed: but neither did the Jews cease to fish in troubled waters, and indeed to insult the Christians along with other enemies. For a sedition having been stirred up at Antioch under Phocas against the Christians, they killed many, and they even burned Anastasius the Patriarch himself and his corpse in the forum, as Zonaras has it in Phocas. Rodericus Tol. hist. Arab. c. 12. He performed many things prosperously in Romania and in the parts of the East, not personally, but through Dukes sent by land and sea, and he did nothing remarkable in the parts of the West. Moreover, the provinces subject to his dominion, and defiled by the sect of Mahomet, must be expressed by their proper names, namely Iconia, whose metropolis is Iconium; Lystria, whose metropolis is Lystris; Alapia, whose metropolis is of the same name; Chaldea, whose metropolis is the destroyed Babylon; Assyria, whose metropolis is Nineveh; Hircanias, whose metropolis is Antiolos; Persis, whose metropolis is Susa; Mesopotamia, whose metropolis is Aram or Sarra; Upper Syria, whose metropolis is Damascus; Celesyria or Phoenicia, whose metropolis is Tyre; Lower Syria, whose metropolis is Alexandria; Greater Arabia, whose metropolis is Baldac; Ethiopia, whose metropolis is Nadavor; Africa, whose metropolis is Carthage; Spain, whose metropolis is Toledo. The sect and sword of Mahomet subjugated all these provinces. Sometimes he also subjugated to his power Sicily, whose metropolis is Panormus, and Calabria, whose ancient metropolis is Rhegium, and part of Apulia, and Gothic Gaul, whose metropolis is Narbonne, and the Vasconias, whose metropolis is Auxis, and Bordeaux, p. 498. The Hungarians (p. 589) invaded Rome and other goods of the Church for a long time, just as the Goths once did, and thus the tribulation is continued, fasc. temp. p. 67. b. and Abbas Urspeng. year of the Lord 899. Emperor Arnulf died, and soon in that year the Hungarians, having heard of his death, having collected a very large army, invaded the nation of the Maravini, whom Emperor Arnulf had subjugated to himself with their help, and claimed them for themselves. They also occupy the borders of the Bavarians, tear down castles, consume churches with fire, slaughter the peoples, and so that they may be feared more and more, they drink the blood of the slain. Plat. in Joh. X. " he says, that they invaded Italy first, then Germany, with almost no one resisting. Concerning the wars of the Roman Pontiffs Nicholas, Gregory, Julius II, and Leo, see Hottinger, part II, p. 45 sqq. & 700. Concerning Bajazet King of the Turks, Amurath, and Mahomet II in the occupation of Constantinople, see B. Pappus p. 509. In which storming, the cruelty of the wicked Turkish race proceeded to such a pitch of fury and impiety that there was no number to the slaughters, rapes, and other outrages. Constantine perished in this persecution, trampled underfoot at the gate of the city; his head was placed on a pole and carried around to the ignominy of the Christians: 40,000 Christians were miserably slaughtered, 150,000 captives were led away and sold into slavery, Naucl. Hist. Gener. 49. This Mahomet II wickedly and by arms withdrew 14 kingdoms and 20 cities from the empire of the Christians, according to Aventinus. See also Urspeng. Chron. under the year 1443. Concerning Selim: In the year of Christ 1512, Selim, the third Emperor of the Turks, utterly extirpated the Saracens, and on April 13, 1517, he killed their Sultan after having tortured him most cruelly. He captured the city of Allkeyer and subjected the whole of Egypt to himself by war. You see, therefore, not without grief and tears, that the Turks have snatched from us the three kingdoms of Trebizond, Constantinople, and Egypt, and have subjugated them to themselves through force and bloody arms. Passing over others, in the year of Christ 1566, Solyman, in the siege of Szigetvár, which at that time was the strongest of the Christians' bulwark against the Turks, and was being defended bitterly and bravely by Nicholas Zrinski, a most valiant Count and most strenuous warrior, afflicted the Christians miserably. The Turks, concealing the Emperor's death in the camp for two days, stormed Szigetvár on September 7th; they killed Zrinski at the gate with 3 cannonballs, cut him to pieces, and after his head had been raised on a pole for some days and displayed, they finally wrapped it in silk and sent it via the Pasha of Buda to Count Salm at the camp of Maximilian. The Turks led away 2000 captives, counting wives and children, toward Constantinople; but more than 25,000 of their own, and among these many of the primary ones, were killed, Chytraeus in Chron. Sax. A.D. 1570. Selim II, the fifth Turkish Emperor, hostilely invaded the island of Cyprus, and finally subjected it to himself. In this expedition he led away many Christian captives, and butchered and slaughtered such a multitude of them that it seemed to exceed almost all belief. Nat. Com. l. 21. hist. f. 457. The Christians received a particularly great slaughter in the storming of the city of Nicosia. For they report that 25,000 men were killed inside and outside the walls: of whom many preferred to lay violent hands upon themselves and their own children than to subject themselves to such great servitude. The same f. 460. Which huge slaughters of Christians are without doubt to be attributed, among other things, to the just judgment of God on account of the tyranny of the Anti-Christ. In the year of Christ 1518 and following, 150,000 Christians were slaughtered in 30 different places by Papist inquisition through various kinds of torments and punishments, as Paulus Vergerius reports in his Epistle. of Justinopolis, whom the Roman Pontiff sent several times into Germany to refute the Lutheran doctrine, Echar. in Papa Pharif. p. 394. Barth. de las Casas, in B. Gerh. Conf. Cath. l. 2. p. 1206, teaches how he raged in the conversion of the Indies: that fifteen million human beings were extinguished by the Spaniards in India and the new Islands in the space of forty years, [and] that several thousand were thrown to be torn apart by dogs. That the Peruvian and neighboring regions were so devastated that twenty million human beings were destroyed in the space of a few years, [and] that a tract of land five times larger than Spain was devastated by countless engines of torture, etc. Of the three million Indians who existed in Hispaniola alone at the arrival of the Christians, scarcely twenty remained as survivors, and in the Lucayan Islands five million human beings were mercilessly slaughtered.

The second woe has passed.] We said, he says, above about the slaughter which took place when Jerusalem was stormed. Above X, 2. 3. 4. where Josephus, Jewish War VI, 45, says that eleven hundred thousand perished, [and] ninety thousand were made captives by right of war.

The third woe, behold, it comes quickly.] Another slaughter, no less, after the faction of Bar Kokhba, having been justly ejected from Aelia, had retreated to Bethar and into more than nine hundred fortresses and villages. Dio says that five hundred and eighty thousand were killed there. Rabbi Johannes in Echa Rabathi says that eight hundred thousand human beings perished in the whole war. But the Salmantican [says] double that number, which had gone out from Egypt: which cannot be less than twelve hundred thousand human beings. He counts, of course, a great multitude of those who perished by famine, disease, and fire.

Only discourse and report are arranged by these, not indeed the meaning of the visions, as we warned before. For the Eastern Anti-Christ did not cease, with the Western one encroaching, and the last act is regarded primarily, and the outcome of the seventh trumpet, which is sown with the last day and the trumpet of the Archangel: in which sense our blessed Gerhard rightly [says]: By the first two woes, bodily punishments of every kind are denounced to the impious; but by the third (as regards the catastrophe), infernal and eternal punishment, Ap. VIII, 13. ch. IX, 12. Lipsius (in B. Gerh. C. C. l. 2. p. 1207.) l. 2. de Const. int. 6. 22. p. 200. A few Iberians, brought eighty years ago into those vast and new lands, what deaths (good God!) they produced, what slaughters! Nor do I argue about the causes or the right of war, only about the events. I behold that huge space of lands (which it is a great thing to have seen, I will not say to have conquered) being overrun by twenty or thirty soldiers and those unarmed flocks being mown down everywhere like grain by a sickle. Where are you, greatest of islands, Cuba? You, Haiti? You, Jamaica? Which were once packed with five or six hundred thousand human beings, [but] elsewhere you have scarcely retained fifteen of them as seed. Show yourself also a little, you Peruvian [coast], you Mexican coast. Alas, the miserable, miserable face! That immense tract and truly another world appears vast and worn away, not otherwise than if it had been burned up by some celestial fire. p. 1288. Secretary of Paul IV. Act. 2. on whether the decrees of the Council of Trent are to be commanded by arms p. 72. Eugenius IV, about to fight against the Bohemians as schismatics, proclaimed a crusade, but unsuccessfully and unhappily. For in that war almost all who were signed with the cross perished, but the schismatics emerged as victors. To the earthquake then, says Pareus, pertain the seditions, wars, tumults, disturbances, changes of minds, [and] contentions about religion that arose throughout the whole Papacy after the Gospel was restored. Soon after the Council of Constance, an earthquake shook the Papacy gravely. For the Bohemians, avengers of the hated death of the two Martyrs, raged hostilely with arms against the Papal clergy, [and] repressed the armies of the Empire by which they were attacked with huge slaughters, [and] reported very many victories that were clearly miraculous over their enemies. And the earthquake did indeed quiet down a little after the Council of Basel through the COMPACTATA (as they called them) granted to the Bohemians: but not long after, by the preaching of Luther in Saxony, Zwingli in Switzerland, Viret in France, [and] others in other parts, a more serious shaking followed: and that which follows was done. Ribera prudently passed over this: because he did not wish to explain what he understood to have evidently happened to the Papacy by the preaching of the Gospel. For the great city is the kingdom of the Roman Anti-Christ, whose head is Rome, Babylon, Sodom, which by the preaching of Luther and his associates was not indeed entirely overturned, but was cast down by a tenth part, with the jurisdiction, tyranny, religion, taxes, annates, and sacred revenues of the Roman Pontiff diminished throughout Germany. For Germany, which embraced the Gospel and returned from the Anti-Christ to Christ, is deservedly reckoned as a tenth part of the great city. But, you say, not all of Germany defected from the Pope. For there remain very many Archbishops, Bishops, and Principalities sworn to the Pope. What then? Other kingdoms have made up for the deficiency of the tenth part, which subsequently, one by one, with the Papacy repelled, have come to the faith of the Gospel, either entirely, as Great Britain, Denmark, Sweden, or in part, as France, Poland, Pannonia. These things are so clear that they cannot be denied. Just as in the history of Elijah, God had reserved for Himself seven thousand who had not bowed their knees to Baal for many: These indeed are the heads of men, the Anti-Christian enemies, whom the ruin of the tenth part of the city crushed. But how? Some understand it of the bloody wars and commotions which the Anti-Christ stirred up against the Gospel to his own detriment. For many myriads of men addicted to him were consumed in those wars: whence the great city suffered no light loss, but perhaps no less, nay more, blood of the pious was shed by the Anti-Christians in the civil wars of France, in Spain, England, Belgium, and elsewhere. Others therefore prefer to interpret it of the spiritual destruction of enemies by the preaching of the Gospel. For through this, very many Papists, more blinded and hardened, perished eternally with gnashing of teeth. Brichtmannus interprets it of the ecclesiastics of the Papacy, who, despoiled by the rise of the Gospel of the revenues of monasteries and the incomes of colleges, in which they previously lived in luxury, now lie starving or dead. But the former is worse on account of what follows.

PART III. A summary representation of the seventh trumpet-blast. Ver. 15.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Καὶ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν τω̃ σεισμω̃ ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων χιλιάδες ἐπτά. ] Multum hoc in nova colonia, ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων, id est, omnis sexus, qui modo homines nominantur. Vide supra III, 4.

Decima pars civitatis, Interprete B. Hoëo cadit 1. corporaliter: Plagis enim meritis a DEO percutientur, quia sanguinem sitierunt, in sanguine morientur. 2. spiritualiter: imminuetur enim ejus autoritas, cadet potentia, cadet opulentia, cadet formido apud multos populos & nationes: cadet obedientia: cadet omnis erga sedem Romanam observantia: ita, ut qui prius toti Regno Papistico addicti fuerunt, eidem fortissime se opposituri sint. Vide quam graviter DEUS injurias servis suis illatas ulcsci velit & valeat. Omnia haec si cum historiis conferantur, clariora & illustriora fient: Annon cum Hieronymus Pragensis & Johannes Hussus Constantiae concremarentur, statim secuta est magna populorum commotio? Bohemi certe gravissimo bello Romanos infestarent, & horrendum in modum afflixerunt: Sicut ipse Aeneas Sylvius Pontif. Roman. totam commotionis illius Bohemiae historiam descripsit, & minime negavit, occisa esse in illo motu multa hominum millia: plurimos quoque a Papata defecisse & Deo gloriam dedisse: sed & cum nostra memoria instinctu sedis Anti-Christianae saeva in Christianos moveretur persecutio, praeter omnium omnem expectationem Roma capta est (Anno 1527.) & ita afflicta & direpta, ut ea calamitas cum veteri- bus & maximis illis Romæ ruinis & calamitatibus conferri potest. Legantur libri historiarum postre- mi septem Sleidani, illi pulcherrime periodum hanc de fatis Anti-Christianorum interpretabuntur: quod autem præcise partem casuram urbis deci- mam, & occisum iri septem hominum millia dicit Apostolus, inde non cæco furore & instar Andabata- rum ferire Deum homines discimus, sed quasi nomi- natim designari, quos flagellis suis velit cædi. Quisq; ergo oculos mature aperiat, & ne lenociniis mere- tricis Anti-Christianæ decipiatur, adeoque cum aliis Anti-Christicolis a DEO ad pœnas justas trahatur, diligenter videat. Quam misere etiam Pontifices ipsi justo Dei judicio perierint, docet B. Gerhard. conf. Cath. l. II. p. 1278. In appendice c. Secundum. dist. 19. de Anastasio II. (qui sedit circa ann. 496.) sic legitur: Quia illicite & non canonice sed contra de- creta Prædecessorum & Successorum suorum hæc re- scripta dedit, ut probat Felix & Gelasius, qui Acati- um ante Anastasium excommunicaverunt, & Or- misda, qui ab ipso Anastasio tertius eundem Acati- um postea damnavit, ideo ab Ecclesia Romana repu- diatur, & a Deo percussus legitur. Johannes de Tur- recremata lib. de pot. Eccl. Bene legitur Anastasium divino nutu percussum interiisse. Sylvester II. (qui sedit circa ann. 898.) cum in Basilica S. Crucis Ro- mæ in Hierusalem missificasset, a Diabolo ex pacto extinctus est. Christophorus I. (qui sedit circa ann. 902.) in carcere misere vitam finiit. Johannes X. (qui sedit circa ann. 913.) cervicali in os injecto in carcere suffocatus est. Johannes XIII. (qui sedit cir- ca ann. 965.) in adulterio confessus periit. Bonifaci- us VII. (qui sedit circa ann. 974.) suorum scelerum conscientia excruciatus subitanea morte periit. Ha- drianus IV. (qui sedit circa ann. 1154.) excommuni- cationem Imperatori denotat ipse a Deo maledictus, cum aquam e fonte haurire vellet, musca in os ejus involans gutturi adhæsit, qua misere suffocatus est. Nicolaus III. (qui sedit circa ann. 1277.) subito mor- tuus est. Paulus II. (qui sedit circa ann. 1464. mo- ritur media nocte, nemine præsente, cum lætus eodem die fuisset in Consistorio, & duos pepones ante mortem pridie absumpsisset. Alexander VI. (qui sedit circa ann. 1492.) veneno periit incautius propinato, quod alteri parari jusserat. Sed quid multis? Proverbio celebrari notum, quod venenum sit mors Pontificum. Videantur Platina, Johannes Stella, Balæus, Nau- clerus, Sabellicus & alii, qui de vitis Pontificum scri- pserunt. Johannes Sarisberiensis in Policratico l. 6. c. 24. scribit, se putare, Pontifices tam brevi vivere, & tam repente mori, ne totam Ecclesiam corrumpe- rent. Ubi de aliis clericis plura leguntur. Nomi- na hominum ita exponit B. Cluverus: Nomina ho- minum quomodo occiduntur, nisi quum tolluntur, deprimuntur, & tanquam in pulverem dejiciun- tur? Sic nunciorum Apostolicorum, Cardinalium, Procuratorum, Legatorum a latere, Abbatum, Prio- rum & nescio quorum nomen & valorem bestiæ ha- bentium existimationes & autoritates diminuun- tur, expunguntur, & mystice occiduntur, quum per terræ motum ruit Ecclesiæ Romanæ dignitas. Im- pletionem viva praxis ostendit. Si vis nomina homi- num pro ipsis hominibus sicut supra c. III, 4. itidem perspicua est impletio. Nam in violentis & subitaneis imperiorum & Rerump. mutationibus Romanensium quoq; satis magna periit multitudo, prout in Germa- nicis, Gallicis, Scoticis, Anglicis, Belgicis, Bohemicis bellorum historiis conspicuum est. Numerus autem se- ptenarius totæ Apocalypsi sacer & perfectus est, & sic etiam hoc loco, ut necesse non sit ad determinatum nu- merum adspirare, aut sollicitam de eo cogitationem su- scipere.

Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἔμφοβοι ἐγένοντο.] Nempe qui erant Eliæ, non ultra ausi sunt se Romanis opponere.

Applicat hæc omnia eximie B. Luthero B. Hoëas, cujus verbis hic uti placet: B. Luthero elogia olivæ & candelabri nemo nisi hostis & invidus detrahit: potestas ejus quanta fuerit, res etiamnum loquitur: Annon ignis verbi divini ex ore ejus exiit? Annon ignis iste multos hostium devoravit? & spiritualiter occidit, utique plures quam quadraginta hæreticos unico hoc verbi ignito gladio se jugulasse scribit B. Lutherus? Annon omnis generis plagas & pœnas Anti-Christiano gregi prædixit, & vindictam nominis divini feliciter precibus suis impetravit: ita, ut pluvia & rore cælesti hostes veritatis carere, ut aquam in sanguinem conversam & terram omni plaga percussam videre debuerint. Finiit vero etiam testimonium suum B. Lutherus, & ad ultimum usq; vitæ halitum in zelo & odio adversus Papam perseveravit. E contra toto ministerii sui curriculo persecutiones Anti-Christi sensit: Bestia enim Romana, quæ ascendit ex abysso, adversus ipsum acerrime bellavit: & quamvis aperte vi Thaumasiandrum istum occidere non potuit, crebris tamen suis proscriptionibus, calumniis, molitionibus & aliis bujusmodi mediis Virum Dei sanctum præmature vita sua privavit, cumq; mors Lutheri innotescenet, infandum, quam bestia illa hoc nomine exultaverit: quam inhabitantes terram præ gaudio letati, quomodo munera congratulatoria invicem miserint: quod Propheta ille diem obiit, qui tantopere sedem Anti-Christi cruciavit. Etsi vero se penitus victores Lutheri evasisse existimarunt, & Lutheri memoriam ac doctrinam plane sepultam fore somniarunt: tamen mirifice spe sua exciderunt: Spiritus enim vitæ à Deo intravit in ipsum, stetitque in discipulis & successoribus fidis super pedes suos: ita, ut cum viderent Pontificii per succedentes Theologos tanto Spiritu doctrinam Lutheri propagari, timore admodum magno obruti fuerint: Et quanquam ipsi Lutherum Cacodaemoni brutis suis fulminibus manciparunt: videre tamen & fatis cognovere, quod cum fidis collegis in cælum ascenderit, quia & olim Lutherum in sinu Dei recumbentem magno stridore dentium impii Romanenses videbunt. De terræ motu, de casu civitatis, de defectione à Papatu nihil attinet amplius dicere. Parietes nostri testantur, hæc omnia majorum nostrorum memoria super S. Lutheri doctrina contigisse, hodieque contingere, neque juvat, historica nunc attexere, cum in Sleidano & decima sexta Osiandri centuria sufficienter descripta sint. B. Cluverus hæc ita explicat: Non hoc vult, omnes Babylonis cives, qui non sint interfecti, conversos esse revera ad Christum (illud enim c. XVI. & seqq. aperte negatur) sed præ pavore, cum tot nomina hominum interiisse viderent, non ausos fuisse quicquam tentare adversus testes amplius, sed coactos Deo honorem tribuere. Sic de coacta gloria Dei confessione accipitur Jos. VII, 19. Joh. IX, 24. Priorem tamen sensum non reprobat; atq; ita quando λοιποὺς ἀνθρώπους, qui occisi sunt, resipuisse negat, non reliquos omnes intelligit: (alioquin enim nullos pios relinqueret in terra) sed simpliciter alios. Sic Matth. XXVII, 49. Luc. IIX, 10. & XIIX, 11. λοιποὶ sunt alii & similiter valet ea vox passim.

Καὶ ἔδωκαν δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.] Multi his rebus conspectis ad Christum conversi.

Tales e. g. sunt, qui in Gallia, Anglia, Belgio, Bohemia, Hungaria, Polonia, Livonia, Curlandia, Lithuania, Prussia, Suecia, Dania, Norwegia, Finonia, Laplandia &c. agnita idolomania Papali Deo gloriam dedere, eumque unum colere cœperunt, veræ fidei contra Anti-Christum Romanum assertores & defensores numero plurimi, robore Spiritus fortissimi, 2. Cor. X, 4. Queritur de hoc

Bellarminus l. de Anti-Christo c. 21. §. & ab hoc: Ab eo tempore, quo per vos Papa Anti-Christus esse cœpit, non modo non crevit ejus imperium, sed sem- per magis ac magis decrevit. Leonis Magni tempore, id est, annis centum quinquaginta, antequam Anti- Christus vestra sententia nasceretur, Papa Roma- nus pluribus gentibus præsidebat, quam sese Romani Imperii fines extenderent. Sic enim scribit idem Leo serm. I. de natali Apostolorum: Per sacram D. Petri sedem caput orbis effecta (Roma) latius Præsides re- ligione divina, quam dominatione terrena. Quam- vis enim multis aucta victoriis jus imperii tui terra marique protuleris, minus tamen est, quod tibi bellicus labor subdidit, quam quod pax Christiana subjecit. Et Prosper in libro de ingratis: Sedes Roma Petri, quæ pastoralis honoris Facta caput mundo, quicquid non possidet armis, Religione tenet. " At postea, Anti-Christo (ut vos vultis) regnante, " paulatim amisit Romana sedes Africam pene to- tam, Asiæ maximam partem, Græciam universam. " Nostris vero temporibus, quibus vos Anti-Chri- stum maxime furere vociferamini, tam prospere " illi omnia successerunt, ut magnam Germaniæ par- " tem amiserit, Sueciam, Gothiam, Norwegiam, Daniam universam, bonam Angliæ, Galliæ, Hel- " vetiæ, Poloniæ, Bohemiæ ac Pannoniæ partem. Itaque si prospere agere nota est Anti-Christi, " non Papa, qui tot provinciis exutus est, sed Luthe- " rus, qui prædicatione carnalis libertatis tot popu- los seduxit, & tam prospere egit, ut ex privato " Monacho totius Germaniæ Propheta & quasi Papa quidam evaserit, Anti-Christus merito dici " potest. Singularis hic est B. Gravius: Additur eodem v. 13. quod occisa sint septem millia nomi- " na hominum, hoc est, ingentem multitudinem " hominum celebrium tam Ecclesiasticorum quam Politicorum, belli Ducum, Nobilium & Divi- " tum interiisse, qui partim in præliis ceciderunt, " partim devastatis urbibus & regionibus pulsi & fugati in exilio perierunt. Si igitur tot homines " celebres ceciderunt, procul dubio infinitus ple- bejorum numerus, durante hoc bello periit. Cæ- " teri vero dicuntur territi, & dedisse gloriam Deo, " v. 13. Procul dubio enim reliqui Papistæ eorum- que fautores cernentes impossibile esse contra " stimulum calcitrare, pacem exoptabunt vel con- vertentur. De Italis etiam exempla refert B. Mi- " crælius l. III. Hist. Eccles. p. 402. Ex ipsa Italia Lu- " therus anno XLII. e Mutina & Bononia, ut & post biennium ex Venetiis & Vincentia literas ab ipsis " accepit, qui illi applaudebant. Et jam tempore Clementis VII. cum a Cæsareanis vexabatur Pa- " pa permulti in privatis civitatum ædibus & ma- xime Faënzæ Pontificis territorio Evangelium " prædicabant, teste Petr. Suav. Polano in hist. Con- " cil. Trid. lib. I. Jam supra diximus Varaglinum, Capucini Ordinis Autorem, Pedemontanum veri- " tatem fidei agnovisse & martyrium consummasse. Idem testatur Sleidanus l. XXI. ubi Vergeriorum " conversionem & conciones Evangelicas descri- " bit. Petrus Martyr, Florentinus, de quo jam su- pra diximus, variis dignitatibus in Italia functus, " non paucos, & inter eos Johannem Valdesium Hispanum JCtum secum ex tenebris eduxit, & " Lucæ atque Pisis animose Evangelium docuit, " atque ex Italia pulsus Argentinæ in Anglia in Hel- vetia Theologiam professus est. In Renatæ Lu- " dovici XII. Regis Galliarum filiæ Herculi Duci Ferariæ nuptæ aula luce Evangelii illustrata flo- " ruerunt M. Antonius Flaminius, Marcellus Palin- " genius, Daniel Tossanus & alii. Galeacius Caraç- ciolus Marchio Vici, Pauli V. ex sorore Nepos, " posthabita Marchionatus dignitate, cujus hæres erat, relicta pulcherrima uxore cum sex liberis " Genevam religionis causa se contulit, & immotus " in agnitione veritatis perstitit, vita privata, sed sa- tis beata contentus, & anno LXXXVI. uxore su- " perinducta priori, quæ divortium fecerat, pie de- functus. Johannes Bernhardinus Bonifacius, " Marchio Oriæ, perpetuo exilio Christum omni- bus vitæ hujus bonis prætulit. Subolfacere enim " Itali cœperant, quod suo tempore Nic. Machia- " vellus Florentinus lib. I. disp. de rep. cap. 12. dicit: Nusquam minus pietatis vel religionis esse, quam " in iis hominibus, qui Romæ viciniores habitant: & si quis conferat eum religionis cultum, qui hac " ætate in usu est cum prima Christianæ religionis " institutione ac veris fundamentis, eum non posse vel illius interitum non metuere, vel divinam ul- " tionem non formidare: ipsos Helvetios, qui soli " veterem religionis cultum & disciplinam milita- rem conservare videantur, corruptos iri curiæ " Romanæ gravitate, si ad illos deferretur. De bello sacro vel expeditione cruciata Monachi cujusdam " Hottinger. sect. XI. p. 484. ita refert: In sola Hiero- solymitana expugnatione tantum humani sangui- " nis fuit fusum, ut si fides adhibenda sit Roberto " Monacho, corpora cæsorum unda sanguinis im- pellente natarint ac fluitarint: adeo, ut ipsis victo- " ribus tam horrenda sanguinis effusio horrorem incusserit; Paris p. 46. De Johanne Pontifice abro- " gato vid. idem p. 196. Et de bellis p. 408. Circa eun- " dem temporis tractum universi Episcopi, Princi- pes, faces, & antesignani civilis belli, quo septen- " decim annos Respublica attrita fuit, uno anno ex- tincti sunt. De Burchardo Halberstadiensi, ter de- " cies Episcopum in acie contra Imperatorem ste- " tisse refert ex Walramo Calv. A. C. 1087. E Baro- nio p. 17. Ita quidem omnia Romæ tam sacra quam " profana factionibus miscebantur, ut penes illam partem esset promotio ad Apostol. sedem Rom. " Pontificis, quæ potentior appareret, ut modo Ro- " manorum proceres, modo Hetruriæ Princeps in- truderet seculari potentia, quem vellet, & dejice- " ret, quem posset Rom. Pontificem à contraria fa- ctione promotum. Quæ toto hoc ferme seculo " sunt actitata, quousque Germaniæ Imperatores " OTHONES (conf. Naucl. Gen. 33. p. 143. Platin. in Bened. VI. ubi Othonem vocat Virum optimum, " & Ecclesiæ Rom. defensorem acerrimum) medii intercessere utriq; parti contrarii arrogantes licet " & ipsi sibi pariter Papæ electionem atque dejectio- " nem. Victor III. p. 547. coronatur, sed ipsi non diu licuit esse securo. Clemens enim III. Romam veni- " ens Victorem in arcem S. Angeli pellit, & missam in templo Mariæ Rotundæ celebrat. Urbanus Vi- " ctori surrogatus Constantiensi scribit Episcopo, " ut coacta synodo Papam Clementem excommuni- cet. In Anglia Anshelmus Urbanum pro legitimo " agnoscit Pontifice. Rex vero Clementem III. qui A. C. 1098. Romæ in Eccl. Mariæ rotundæ per le- " gatum Concil. d. 7. Aug. indixit, in quo salvo con- " ductu omnes evocat, qui partium Hildebrandi aut Urbani essent, ut rationem redderent, cur annis se- " decim Ecclesiam schismate turbassent. Cum vero non comparerent, eorum decreta combusta sunt. " De tribus una vice sedentibus Romæ Papis loqui- " tur præter plurimos alios Avent. annal. l. V. p. 531. Saraceni, p. 650. invadentes Hetruriam & Latium " Romam deprædati sunt. An. 846. Illyria & Dal- matia vexata Adriaticum mare transeuntes, Anco- " nam, Piceni urbem direptam incenderunt. Drechs " l. Hist. Arab. A. 860. Romanorum terras occupa- " vit Omar, fil. Abidi, Actaus, atque ex iis avexit 70. hominum millia Elm. p. 151. an. 864. Constantinus Imperator d. 17. Aug. an. 766. proponit edictum de Monachis, ut monasteriis expellantur, & uxo- res ducant, vitamque civilem agant. In Miscell. Se- quenti anno Constantinus omnes Monachos ex tota Asia Ephesum convocavit, idemque iis im- peravit, quod superiori anno in Europa, ut vel in- ducti plebejis vestimentis uxores ducerent, vel e- rutis oculis in Cyprum deportarentur. Cedren. Idem ab eodem Imperatore edictum repetitum est A. C. 770. Videatur etiam Zonaras in Constant. Copron. p. 551. Reluctabantur ei 1. Pontifices Ori- entales, Patriarchæ cumprimis Constantinopoli- tani, Romano se Pontifici æquales interdum su- periores dicentes, Geneb. an. Chr. 885. Nota sunt certamina inter Photium & Papam. Vide Catal. Test. Verit. l. 9. p. 12. & 21. Deinde etiam cum Ponti- fice Rom. ipsi ea de re certamen fuit ingens, quod is ex ambitione dominatum sibi super Ecclesias vendicaret, ac omnes controversias ad suum so- lius arbitrium & sententiam definiri contenderet, ac scripsit librum contra Nicolaum Pontificem, quem à pluribus Episcopis subscribi curavit: ut patet ex libro Pontificali in vita Adriani. Quot ho- stiles incursiones, (nam & de iis aliquid dicendum) seculo hoc Imperium Rom. sustinuerit à solis Sa- racenis & Persis, dici vix potest. Videatur Elmaci- nus in historia Saracenica, Zonaras in annal. Infe- remus pauca ex Wolffg. Drechsleri historia Ara- bum 638. Hierosolyma post biennalem obsidionem à Saracenis devastata. 639. Tota Syria à Saracenis clade affecta est. 640. Saraceni ab Imperat. Rom. defecerunt 641. Antiochia à Saracenis eversa, Da- mascus capta, Phœnicia oppugnata, subacta Ægy- ptus. 648. Maximam partem Africæ Saraceni suo imperio subjugarunt. 655. Rhodus nobilissima In- sula à Saracenis oppugnata est, quam capientes plurimum ex ea auri avexerunt: & Colossum solis nobilem, altum 110. ped. ex cujus ære Judæis ven- dito noningentos camelos onerasse dicuntur. 656. Ægeum mare piratica infestarunt, & Cycladibus insulis multa damna intulerunt. 663. Saraceni O- lympium Italiæ Exarchum in Sicilia cum toto ex- ercitu fuderunt. 672. Irrupere Saraceni in Siciliam, & Syracusis captis omniq; terra devastata in Alex- andriam rediere. 686. Saraceni Rege Amiratho Africam & Lybiam invaserunt, multis spoliis dita- ti. 687. Mortuo Constantino Justinianus ejusmo- di conditionibus cum Saracenis pacem iniit, ut Africa & Lybia imperio restituta per decem an- nos singulis diebus mille aureos, & equum cum nobili puero loco tributi penderent. 688. Hoc fœdere rupto Justinianus pugnam cum Saracenis iniens plurimum damni ab iis retulit. 692. Fusis per Saracenos Romanis nomen Saracenum crevit, di- gnitas Romanorum valde iminuta est. Hanc Rom. Imperio brevissimo tempore vidimus stragem à Saracenis tantum illatam. Nec multo clementiores fuerunt hoc seculo Persæ sub Phoca, Zonara teste, Syriam, Palæstinam & Phœniciam subegerunt. In Armeniam, Cappadociam, Paphlagoniam & Dal- matiam incursiones fecerunt populabundi Chal- cedonem usque progressi. Ita in historia Heraclii refert, quod Persiæ Orientales provincias incur- santes alias subegerint, alias spoliaverint, Roma- næq; legiones ab eis sint victæ cæsæque, paucis fuga elapsis. Quumque ut scribit Chosroës omnia præ- daretur & vastaret, & Palæstina occupata Hieroso- lymam quoq; expugnasset. λέγεται ἀπειρόν τι πλῆ- θος ἀναιρεθῆναι τῶν χρισιανῶν, dicitur infinita Chri- stianorum multitudo sublata: sed nec Judæi in tur- bido piscari, atq; adeo Christianis cum aliis hosti- " bus insultare desierunt. Mota enim Antiochiæ sub " Phoca contra Christianos seditione multos occi- " derunt, ipsumq; etiam Anastasium Patriarcham e- " jusq; cadaver in foro combusserunt, ut Zonar. ha- " bet in Phoca. Rodericus Tol. hist. Arab. c. 12. Hi- " stam, in Romania & in partibus Orientis prospere " multa gessit non præsentialiter, sed per Duces ter- " ra & pelago destinatos, & in Occidentis partibus " nihil egit præclarum. Provinciæ autem dominio " ejus subditæ, & secta Mahometi inquinatæ, neces- " se est, ut propriis nominibus exprimantur, videli- " cet Iconia, cujus metropolis Iconium, Lystria, cu- " jus metropolis Lystris; Alapia, cujus metropolis " ejusdem nominis, Chaldæa, cujus metropolis Ba- " bylon destructa, Assyria, cujus metropolis Nini- " ve, Hircanias, cujus metropolis Antiolos, Persis, " cujus metropolis Susa, Mesopotamia, cujus me- " tropolis Aram sive Sarra: Syria superior, cujus " metropolis Damascus, Celesyria sive Phœnicia, " cujus metropolis Tyrus, Syria inferior, cujus me- " tropolis Alexandria, Arabia major, cujus metro- " polis Baldac, Æthiopia, cujus metropolis Nada- " vor, Africa, cujus metropolis Carthago, Hispania, " cujus metropolis Toletum. Has omnes provin- " cias subjugavit secta & gladius Mahometi. Ali- " quando etiam Siciliam, cujus metropolis Panor- " mum, & Calabriam, cujus antiqua metropolis " Rhegium, & partem Apuliæ, & Galliam Gothi- " cam, cujus metropolis Narbona, & Vascanias, cu- " jus metropolis Auxis & Burdigaliam suæ potentiæ " subjugavit, p. 498. Hungari (p. 589) Romam & " alia bona Ecclesiæ per longum tempus invaserunt, " sicut olim Gothi, & sic continuatur tribulatio " fasc. temp. p. 67. b. & Abbas Urspeng. ann. D. 899. " Arnolfus Imperator obiit, moxque eo anno Hun- " gari morte ejus audita, collecto permagno exerci- " tu, Maravinorum gentem, quam illorum auxilio " Arnolfus Imperator sibi subdiderat, invadunt, sibi- " que vendicant. Bajoariorum quoque fines occu- " pant, castella diruunt, Ecclesias igni consumunt, " populos jugulant, & ut magis magisque timeantur, " interfectorum se sanguine potant. Plat. in Joh. X. " ait, eos Italiam primo, deinde Germaniam inva- " sisse, nemine prope resistente. De Nicolao, Grego- " rio, Julio II. Leone, Pontificum Rom. bellis vid. Hot- " ting. p. II. p. 45. seqq. & 700. De Bajaceti Regis Tur- " carum, Amurathis, Mahometi II. in occupatione " Constantinopoleos B. Pappus p. 509. In qua expu- " gnatione eo furoris & impietatis scelerata gentis " Turcicæ immanitas est progressa, ut internecio- " num, stuprorum, aliorumque flagitiorum non fue- " rit numerus. Constantinus in hac persecutione " sub porto urbis pedibus conculcatus interiit, ca- " put ejus perticæ impositum in ignominiam Chri- " stianorum circumferebatur: Christianorum 40000. " misere trucidabantur, 150000. captivi abduceban- " tur & in mancipia vendebantur, Naucl. Hist. Ge- " ner. 49. Hic Mahometus M. 14. regna & 20. urbes " Christianorum imperio per nefas & arma subtra- " xit, teste Aventino. Vide quoque Urspeng. Chron. " sub An. 1443. De Selymo: An. Chr. M.D. XII. Se- " lymus Imperator Turcarum III. Saracenos penitus " extirpavit, eorumq; Sultanum pessime cruciatum " an. Chr. M.D. XVII. 13. Apr. interemit. Cœpit ur- " bem Allkeyer, totamque Ægyptum sibi bello subje- " cit. Vides ergo non sine dolore & lacrymis Tur- " cas tria regna Trapizuntiacum, Constantinopoli- " tanum & Ægyptiacum nostris eripuisse, perq; vim " & arma cruenta sibi subjugasse. Missis aliis an. Chr. " M. D. LXVI. Solymannus in obsidione Zygethi, " quod tum temporis fortissimum Christianorum " contra Turcas erat propugnaculum, & à Nicolao Serinio Comite fortissimo & bellatore strenuissi- mo acriter & fortiter defendebatur, Christianos misere afflixit. Turcæ Imperatoris mortem in castris per duos dies celantes Zygethum 7. Sept. expugnabant, Serinium in porta 3. globis tormen- tariis interfectum obtruncabant, caputque per di- es aliquot pertica sublatum & spectatum propo- situm tandem serico involutum per Bassam Bu- densem ad Eccium Comitem Salmensem in Ma- ximiliani castra mittebant. Abduxerunt Turcæ 2000. uxoribus & liberis annumeratis captivos Constantinopolin versus: ipsorum vero plus- quam 25000. & inter hos multi ex primariis sunt occisi, Chýtræus in Chron. Sax. A. C. M. D. LXX. Selymus II. Turcicus Imperator quintus insulam Cyprum hostiliter invadebat, tandemque sibi sub- jiciebat. In hac expeditione multos Christianos captivos abduxit, tantamq; multitudinem eorum excarnificavit atque trucidavit, ut omnem fidem fere superare videretur. Nat. Com. l. 21. hist. f. 457. Cladem cumprimis permagnam Christiani acce- perunt in expugnatione urbis Nicosiæ. Namq; fe- runt intra & extra mœnia 25000. hominum occi- sos fuisse: ex quibus multi sibi suisq; liberis malu- erunt violenter manus inferre, quam tantæ servi- tuti se subjicere. Idem f. 460. Quæ Christianorum ingentes clades procul ambiguo justo Dei judicio in- ter alia ob Anti-Christi tyrannidem tribuenda. An. Chr. M. D. XIIX. & seqq. 30. diversis in locis ex in- quisitione Papistica 150000. Christiani variis tor- mentorum generibus ac suppliciis trucidati sunt, ut refert Paulus Vergerius Ep. Justinopolitanus, quem aliquoties Pontifex Rom. misit in Germa- niam, ut Lutheranam doctrinam refutaret Echar. in Papa Pharif. p. 394. Quomodo in Indiarum con- versione sævierit, Barth. de la Casas apud B. Gerh. Conf. Cath. l. 2. p. 1206. docet: Centies quinquagies centena millia hominum quadraginta annorum spatio extincta esse ab Hispanis in India & novis Insulis, aliquot millia canibus dilaceranda esse ob- jecta. Peruanam & vicinas regiones adeo vastatas esse, ut hominum bis mille myriades paucorum annorum spatio sint deletæ, innumeris tormento- rum molitionibus tractum terræ quinquies Hispa- nia majorem vastatum &c. Ex tribus millionibus Indorum, qui in sola Hispaniola sub adventum Christianorum extiterunt, vix viginti superstites manserunt, & in Insulis Luccaios quinque millio- nes hominum immisericorditer trucidatos fuisse.

Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ δευτέρα ἀπῆλθεν.] Diximus, inquit, supra de stra- ge, quæ facta est, expugnatis Hierosolymis. Supra X, 2. 3. 4. ubi undecies centena millia periisse, nonaginta millia captiva belli jure facta, ait Josephus Belli Judaici VI, 45.

Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ τρίτη ἰδὺ ἔρχεται ταχύ.] Strages alia non minor, postquam factio Barchochebæ ab Ælia juste ejecta se Betho- ram & in arces vicosque supra nongentos receperat. Dio interfecta ait ibi millia quingenta & octoginta. Rabbinus Johannes in Echa Rabathi periisse in toto bello ait homi- num millia octingenta. At Salmanticensis duplum ejus numeri, qui Ægypto exierat: quod non minus esse potest, quam duodecies centena hominum millia. Annumerat ni- mirum magnam multitudinem eorum, qui fame, morbis & incendio periere.

Ordinatur hisce tantum sermo, & relatio, non vero visionum significatio, ut ante monuimus. Nam non desiit Anti-Christus Orientalis, ingruente Occidentali & respicitur imprimis actus ultimus, & exitus septimæ tubæ, quæ seminatur cum die novissimo & tuba Archangeli: quo sensu recte B. Gerh. noster: Per duo væ priora denunciantur im- piis omnis generis pœnæ corporales; per tertium vero, (quoad catastrophen) pœna infernalis & æ- terna, Ap. IIX, 13. c. IX, 12. Lipsius (apud B. Gerh. C. C. l. 2. p. 1207.) l. 2. de Const. int. 6. 22. p. 200. Pau- culi Iberi ante annos octoginta in vastas illas & novas terras delati, quæ funera (Deus bone!) ediderunt, quas strages! Nec de causis aut jure belli differo, tantum de eventis. Cerno ingens illud terrarum spatium (quod vi- disse magnum sit, non dicam vicisse) à vicenis tricenisq́ militibus pervadi & passim inermes illos greges sterni, ut segetem à falce. Ubi tu es, insularum maxima, Cu- ba? Tu Hayta? Tu Jucaia? quæ olim quingentis aut sexcestis hominum millibus succinctæ alibi vix quinde- cim ex iis retinuistis in semen. Ostende etiam te paulu- lum tu Peruana, tu Mexicana ora. Heu miseram mi- seramque faciem! Immensus ille tractus & vere alter orbis vastus attritusq́; apparet, non aliter, quam sicæ- lesti quodam igne deflagrasset. pag. 1288. Secretarius Pauli IV. Act. 2. an decreta Concilii Trid. armis im- peranda p. 72. Eugenius IV. contra Bohemos utpote schismaticos pugnaturus cruciatam indixit, sed infau- ste atq́; infeliciter. Nam in illo bello periere fere omnes cruce signati, schismatici vero victores evaserunt. Ad terræ motum tunc, inquit Pareus, pertinent seditio- nes, bella, tumultus, disputationes, animorum muta- tiones, concertationes de religione per totum Papatum exortæ post Evangelium reparatum. Mox à Concilio Constantiensi terræ motus Papatum graviter concus- sit. Bohemi enim vindices invisæ necis duorum Marty- rum in clerum Papalem hostiliter armis sævierunt, ex- ercitus Imperii quibus petebantur, cladibus ingentibus represserunt, victorias plurimas plane miraculosas de hostibus reportaverunt. Et conquievit quidem paulu- lum terræ motus post Concil. Basiliense per COMPA- CTATA, (quæ vocabant) Bohemis concessa: sed non multo post prædicatione Lutheri in Saxonia, Zwinglii in Helvetia, Vireti in Gallia, aliorum in aliis partibus concussio gravior est consequuta: factumq́; id, quod se- quitur. Hoc Ribera prudens præteriit: quia explica- re noluit, quod Papatui prædicatione Evangelii evi- denter contigisse intellexit. Urbs enim magna regnum est Anti-Christi Romani, cujus caput Roma, Babylon, Sodoma, quod prædicatione Lutheri & Parastata- rum, non quidem totum eversum, decima vero parte dejectum est, Pontificis Romani jurisdictione, tyranni- de, religione, censibus, annatis, commandis vectigali- bus sacris per Germaniam diminutis. Germania enim, quæ Evangelium amplexa, ab Antichristo ad Christum rediit decima pars urbis magnæ merito censetur. At, inquis, non tota Germania defecit à Papa. Manent enim Papæ jurati plurimi Archi-Episcopi, Episcopi, Principatus. Quid tum? Suppleverunt defectum de- cimæ partis alia regna, quæ deinceps paulatim, Papatu repulso ad Evangelii fidem accesserunt vel integra, ut magna Britannia, Dania, Suecia, vel ex parte, ut Gal- lia, Polonia, Pannonia. Hæc tam sunt aperta, ut negari non possint. Sicut in historia Eliæ Deus sibi servaverat septies mille, qui non flexerant genua Baa- li pro plurimos: Hæc vero capita hominum sunt ho- stium Anti-Christianorum, quos ruina decimæ partis urbis oppressit. Quomodo autem? Quidam de cru- entis bellis & motibus intelligunt, quod Anti-Christus adversus Evangelium suo malo concitavit. Num mul- tæ myriades hominum ipsi addictorum bellis illis ab- sumptæ sunt: unde non levem jacturam fecit urbs ma- gna, sed forte non minus, imo plus sanguinis piorum effusum est ab Anti-Christianis in bellis civilibus Gal- liæ, in Hispania, Anglia, Belgio alibi. Alii igitur ma- lunt interpretari de interitu hostium spirituali ex præ- dicatione Evangelii. Per hanc enim Papistæ plurimi magis excæcati & indurati cum fremitu æternum pe- rierunt. Brichtmannus de Ecclesiasticis Papatus in- terpretatur, qui exortu Evangelii spoliati reditibus monasteriorum & collegiorum proventibus, quibus delitiabantur prius, famelici vel morti nunc jacent. Sed prius malo propter sequentia.

PARS III. Septimi tubicinii Summaria repræsentatio. Vers. 15.

## 11:15
And the seventh angel sounded.] Giving a sign to the Romans to fulfill that third woe. The Apostle is accustomed to pass over grave evils with brief but effective words, and to speak of good things liberally. Indeed: Light cares speak, great ones are struck dumb. Thus, the painter, in the sacrifice of Iphigenia, had made Menelaus and the other nobles weeping; but the grief of Agamemnon, as one that could not be expressed, he had covered with a cloak.

And there were great voices in heaven.] The voices of angels praising God, because liberty had been given to Christians to live and to worship God and Christ in Jerusalem, all Jews who were not Christians having been ejected and forbidden ever to approach it, except on one day each year, for the sake of testifying to their grief. Justin is a witness in his second Apology: Eusebius, History IV, 6, and in his Chronicle. Hilary on Ps. 58. Jerome on Zephaniah 2 and on Isaiah 6. Procopius of Gaza on Isaiah 1:7. This is what Tertullian says in his Apology: Dispersed, wandering, and exiles from their own sky and soil, they roam through the world without a name, without a God-King: to whom it is not granted, even by the right of strangers, to salute their fatherland with so much as a footprint. What Orosius says: The city was permitted only to Christians. Understand this among those who were Jews by birth. And because after that time no Jews were permitted to dwell there who, at the time of that edict, had not professed themselves Christians, therefore bishops were chosen, not as before from the circumcision, but from the Gentiles, the first of whom was Marcus, as we are taught both by Eusebius and by Sulpicius Severus, who teaches that this was to some extent necessary for the Church, so that the Jewish rites might gradually die out.

Saying: The kingdom of the world has become our Lord's and his Christ's.] That is, in Judea, which is often תבל to the Jews, ἡ γῆ in the Apocalypse thus far, and οἰκουμένη above in III, 10. Κύριος in this place, as among the LXX, is יהוה. Thus also above XI, 4. God reigns through Christ, and Christ in the name of God, always—but they are said to reign pre-eminently there where the Gospel is freely preached. It is an imitation of Psalm 93.

And he shall reign for ever and ever.] The Christian religion will always be in Judea, which was true first under Pagan Emperors, much more under Christian ones, but also under the Saracens and Turks to this day. I would not, however, affirm that John understood that it would last for ages, but that it would last while the world stood.

The blast of the seventh trumpet, as to its contents, which it intimates, is exhibited epitomically through a representation of the heavenly glorification and blessedness of the Elect, which is the beginning, as to hope and foretaste, and the completion, as to the thing itself and the plenary perception of those things which are predicted here. Therefore, it is instituted under the auspices of the doxology of God and Christ by the heavenly psalmody of the angels and the spirits of perfect just men, and other heavenly beings, which St. John heard and which we perceive with him; unless perhaps these things should rather be taken concerning the militant Church, as far as the signification of the vision is concerned: or understood conjunctively concerning both the assembly of the militant and the triumphant Church. For it is properly one and the same Church of those who have been saved by hope, and who enjoy salvation in reality, even if the former walk by faith, the latter by sight, 2 Cor. 5, which pertains only to the mode and the economy. The blessed Osiander thus hands down the coherence with the preceding: Although the Muhammadans, by their persecutions and blasphemies, and Satan, through the Pope, by human traditions, superstitions, errors, and idolatrous worship, may attempt to destroy the kingdom of Christ, to overwhelm and utterly oppress the Church of Christ, and to obscure the glory of Christ our Savior: yet they shall effect nothing, but our Lord Jesus Christ shall reign on the throne of His Majesty for all eternity, and shall direct all things to the glory of His name and to the eternal happiness of His Church. For to Him all power has been given in heaven and on earth, Matt. 28. They celebrate God, therefore, not because of the liberty given to celebrate God and Christ in Jerusalem, but throughout the whole world; ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ κόσμου. Certainly, Judea nowhere comes under the name of τοῦ κόσμου.

Christ does not only reign in the name of God as man, but He also reigns by the same title and right with the Father, as true and one God with the Father and the Holy Spirit, 1 John 5:7, Apoc. 4:6.

The kingdom of the world has therefore become the Lord's and His Christ's, because His Lord and Christ is recognized throughout the world as the one Lord, Zech. 14:9, Is. 45:23, to whom the kingdoms of the world now obey and are subject, Ps. 72:1, 10, and 2:8, 96:5, 98:4, 6, 99:1, seqq., 102:16, 93:1, 89:28, Is. 60:3, 10, Dan. 2:44, ch. 7:14. Nor does His kingdom extend only until the end of the world, but for ages of ages, as the express letter has it, here, and Ap. 22:5. Of His kingdom there shall be no end, Luke 1:33, Is. 9:7. That the Christian religion has always remained in Judea will hardly be taught, and that it will always remain is nowhere promised. Therefore, that is rashly assumed. Alcasar, in Cluverus, recounts various opinions here: Others are pleased that this should be referred to the time of the victory won over the Anti-Christ. Thus Seraphinus, having perhaps followed Joachim, who explains it concerning the time of a certain great liberty, which pertains, as he says, to the Holy Spirit. Others refer it to the time of the liberty of the Church under the Emperor Justinian. Thus Aureolus, Antoninus, Lyranus, Ederus, and Lizarazus. Others to the day of the universal judgment itself, such as Andreas, Aretas, Beda, Primasius, Albertus, Ribera, and Viegas: to whom most of our own agree. Alcasar wishes it to be about the conversion of the Gentiles here.

Latin:

Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισε.] Signum dans Roma- nis ad explendum væ illud tertium. Solet Apostolus mala gra- via brevibus verbis, sed efficacibus prætervehi, bona eloqui liberaliter. Nimirum: Curæ leves loquuntur, ingentes stupent. Sic pictor in mactatione Iphigeniæ plorantes fecerat Mene- laum & proceres alios: Agamemnonis luctum, ut qui expri- mi non posset, obvolverat pallio.

Καὶ ἐγένοντο φωναὶ μεγάλαι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ.] Voces Angelo- rum Deum laudantium, quod Christianis libertas data esset vivendi & Deum ac Christum colendi Hierosolymis, ejectis Judæis omnibus, qui Christiani non essent, & vetitis unquam eo accedere, nisi uno die quotannis, luctus sui testandi causa. Testis Justinus in Apologetico secundo: Eusebius Historiæ IV, 6. & in Chron. Hilarius ad Ps. LVIII. Hieronymus ad So- phoniam II. & ad Esaiam VI. Procopius Gazensis ad Esaiam I, 7. Hoc est, quod ait Tertullianus Apologetico: Dispersi, palabundi, & cæli, & soli sui extorres vagantur per orbem si- ne nomine, sine Deo Rege: quibus nec advenarum jure patriam saltem vestigio salutare conceditur. Quod Orosius ait: Chri- stianis tantum civitate permissa. Intellige inter eos, qui ortu erant Judæi. Et quia post id tempus nulli ibi habitare permis- si Judæi, qui tempore istius edicti Christianis unum professi non essent, ideo Episcopi lecti, non ut ante ex circumcisione, sed ex gentibus, quorum primus fuit Marcus, ut docemur & ab Eusebio, & à Severo Sulpitio, qui docet, hoc Ecclesiæ ali- quatenus fuisse necessarium, ut paulatim ritus Judaici exo- lescerent.

Λέγουσαι· ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ κόσμου τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ.] Id est, in Judæa, quæ תבל Judæis sæpe ἡ γῆ in Apocalypsi hactenus, & οἰκουμένη supra III, 10. Κύριος hoc loco, ut apud LXX. est יהוה. Sic & supra XI, 4. Deus per Christum, & Christus Dei nomine regnant semper, -sed ibi eximie regnare dicuntur, ubi libere prædicatur Evangelium. Est imitatio Psalmi XCIII.

Καὶ βασιλεύσει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.] Semper erit in Judæa Christiana religio, quod verum fuit primum sub Paga- nis Imperatoribus, multo magis sub Christianis, sed & sub Sa- racenis & Turcis in hunc diem. Non tamen affirmem intel- lectum Johanni, quod seculis id esse duraturum, sed duratu- rum, dum mundus staret.

Septimæ tubæ clangor, quod ad contenta, quæ in- timat ἐπιτομικῶς exhibetur per repræsentationem cœlestis glorificationis & beatitudinis Electo- rum, quæ initium est, quod ad spem & prægustum, & complementum, quoad rem ac plenariam per- ceptionem eorum, quæ hic prædicuntur. Ideo sub auspicium δοξολογία Dei & Christi instituitur cœ- lesti Psalmodia Angelorum & Spirituum perfe- ctorum justorum, aliorumque cœlitum, quam S. Johannes exaudiit & nos cum percipimus ; nisi hæc fortassis de militante Ecclesia, quantum ad vi- sionis significationem, potius accipienda sint: vel conjunctim de utroque & militantis & triumphan- tis Ecclesiæ cœtu intelligenda. Est enim proprie u- na & eadem Ecclesia eorum, qui spe salvi facti sunt, & qui reipsa salute fruuntur, etsi illi ambulent per fidem, hi per speciem, 2. Cor. V. quod ad modum tantum & οἰκονομίαν pertinet. Cohærentiam cum præcedentibus ita tradit B. Osiander: Tametsi Mu- hametistæ & persecutionibus & blasphemiis suis re- gnum Christi delere, & satanas per Pontificem huma- nis traditionibus, superstitionibus, erroribus, & idolo- latricis cultibus Ecclesiam Christi obruere, prorsus opprimere, & gloriam Christi Salvatoris nostri obscu- rare conentur: tamen nihil efficient, sed regnabit Do- minus noster Jesus Christus in solio Majestatis suæ in omnem æternitatem, & omnia ad nominis sui gloriam & ad æternam Ecclesiæ suæ felicitatem diriget. Ipsi enim data est omnis potestas in cælo & in terra, Matth. 28. Celebrant ergo Deum non ob liberta- tem Deum & Christum Hierosolymis celebrandi datam, sed per totum orbem; ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ κόσμου. Nuspiam certe Judæa nomine τοῦ κόσμου venit.

Christus non tantum Dei nomine regnat ut homo, sed regnat etiam eodem titulo ac jure cum Patre, ut verus & unus cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto Deus, 1. Joh. V, 7. Apoc. IV, 6.

Factum itaque regnum mundi Domini & Chri- sti ejus, quia Dominus & Christus ejus per orbem agnoscitur unus Dominus, Zach. XIV, 9. Es. XLV, 23. cui regna mundi jam parent ac subdita sunt, Psal. LXXII, 1. 10. & II, 8. XCVI, 5. XCIIX, 4. 6. XCIX, 1. seqq. CII, 16. XCIII, 1. XXCIX, 28. Esa. LX, 3. 10. Dan. II, 44. c. VII, 14. Nec vero regnum ejus se tantum extendit usque ad finem mundi, sed in secula seculorum, ut habet expressa litera, hic, & Ap. XXII, 5. Regni ejus non erit finis, Luc. I, 33. Esa. IX, 7. In Judæa semper religionem Christia- nam mansisse, vix docebitur, semper mansuram, nuspiam promittitur. Temere ergo id assumitur. Varias hic recenset sententias Alcasar apud Cluve- rum: Aliis placet, hoc esse referendum ad tempus vi- ctoriæ ex Anti-Christo partæ. Ita Seraphinus sequu- tus fortasse Joachimum, qui exponit de tempore ma- gnæ cujusdam libertatis, quæ pertinet, ut ille ait, ad Spiritum Sanctum. Alii referunt ad tempus liberta- tis Ecclesiæ sub Justiniano Imperatore. Sic Aureolus, Antoninus, Lyranus, Ederus & Lizarazus. Alii ad ipsium universalis judicii diem, ut Andreas, Aretas, Beda, Primasius, Albertus, Ribera & Viegas: qui- bus plerique nostri annuunt. Alcasar de gentium conversione hic agi vult.

## 11:16
Ver. 16. And the twenty-four elders.] The elders who were governing that Church which existed in the times of Claudius: concerning whom it was treated above in IV, 4, 10, V, 8, 14.

The fable about the 24 priests in the Church of Jerusalem is refuted with the same ease with which it is introduced: Grotius is allowed whatever he pleases; but he pleases what he thinks serves his own stage and hypothesis.

Οἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καθήμενοι ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους αὑτῶν.] Those who judged in the place of God in the Church of Jerusalem, see above IV, v. 4. See also II, 26. III, 21.

Sitting before God upon thrones is nowhere explained in this way regarding the government of the Church, but it occurs regarding heavenly happiness and also regarding judicial power, communicated to the Elders as assessors of the Divine judgment on the last day, Matt. XIX, 28. Luke XXII, 30. 1 Cor. VI, 2.

Ἔπεσον ἐπὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὑτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ Θεῷ.] As above IV, 10. V, 8. 14. VII, 11. The sense is that those Elders would do this as soon as they were made more certain of this revelation pertaining to the Jews. A great consolation to foresee in evils the happy outcome of their plans.

Latin:

Vers. 16. Καὶ οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι.] Seniores, qui illam, quæ Claudii temporibus erat, Ecclesiam regebant: De quibus actum supra IV, 4. 10. V, 8. 14.

Fabula de Sacerdotibus 24. in Ecclesia Hieroso- lymitana ea facilitate reprobatur, qua adducitur: Grotio licet, quod lubet: lubet autem, quod suæ scenæ & hypothesi inservire censet.

Οἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καθήμενοι ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους αὑτῶν.] Qui vi- ce Dei in Ecclesia Hierosolymitana judicabant supra IV. v. 4. Vide & II, 26. III, 21.

Sessio coram Deo super thronos nuspiam ita expo- nitur de regimine Ecclesiæ, sed de felicitate cœle- sti occurrit necnon de judiciaria potestate, Senio- ribus ceu assessoribus judicii Divini in novissima die communicata, Matth. XIX, 28. Luc. XXII, 30. 1. Cor. VI, 2.

Ἔπεσον ἐπὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὑτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ Θεῷ.] Ut supra IV, 10. V, 8. 14. VII, 11. Sensus est, hoc facturos illos Seniores simul atque hujus revelationis ad Judæos pertinentis certiores essent redditi. Magnum solatium in malis prospice- re consiliorum suorum felicem exitum.

## 11:17
Vers. 17. Λέγοντες εὐχαριστοῦμέν σοι Κύριε.] יהוה as above. Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ.] אלהי הצבאות Hos. XII, 6. and elsewhere. See above I, 8. IV, 8.

Ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος.] Above I, 4. 8. IV, 8.

Ὅτι εἴληφας τὴν δύναμίν σου τὴν μεγάλην.] Because you used the Romans as your attendants. See above X, 2. and what is said there.

Καὶ ἐβασίλευσας.] You have executed your decrees through them.

He is said to have received power because he called it into use and exerted and demonstrated it: Because things are then accustomed to be said to be done when they are manifested as done. That power was demonstrated in the occupation and propagation of the kingdom of Christ, while the Anti-Christ, both Eastern and Western, raged in vain against it, and in the preservation of the same until the consummation of the age, Matt. XXIX, v. last. To reign over some is something far more than to execute one's decrees through them. And God often executes his decrees through the enemies of his kingdom, as is evident from the example of the Babylonians, Romans, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 17. Λέγοντες εὐχαριστοῦμέν σοι Κύριε.] יהוה ut supra. Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ.] אלהי הצבאות Ose. XII, 6. & alibi. Vide supra I, 8. IV, 8.

Ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος.] Supra I, 4. 8. IV, 8.

Ὅτι εἴληφας τὴν δύναμίν σου τὴν μεγάλην.] Quod usus es Ro- manis tanquam satellitibus tuis. Vide supra X, 2. & ibi dicta.

Καὶ ἐβασίλευσας.] Decreta tua per eos exequutus es.

Accepisse dicitur potestatem, quod eum in usum vocarit atque exeruerit ac demonstrarit: Quia res tum fieri dici solent, cum factæ manifestantur. Ea potestas demonstrata in occupatione ac propaga- tione regni Christi nequicquam fremente contra Anti-Christo cum Orientali tum Occidentali & conservatione ejusdem usque ad consummationem seculi, Matth. XXIX. v. ult. Regnare super aliquos longe amplius quid, quam decreta sua per eos ex- sequi. Et exsequitur Deus decreta sua sæpe per hostes regni sui, ut exemplo Babyloniorum, Ro- manorum &c. constat.

## 11:18
Καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ὠργίσθησαν.] Those not worthy to be called Jews, since they live in a heathen manner. Thus above the same are the synagogue of Satan II, 9. III, 9. worshippers of demons IX, 20. He added to Psalm II and XCIX, 1.

Roman Catholics, Anti-Christians, are not worthy to be called Christians. By their manifold idolatry, and their religious worship of images, Saints, Angels, Mary, and others, they are akin to the idol-mania of the Heathens. Καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῶν νεκρῶν κριθῆναι.] Supply ἦλθε. The time has come when the dead are to be vindicated for the name of Christ. Κρίνειν often means to vindicate. And so שׁפט, which is κρίνειν or δικάζειν, is translated by ἐκδικεῖν, Ezek. 7, 3. 27. ch. 15, 37. ch. 23, 24. 45. Obad. 21. See also Isa. 59, 9. 11. The sense is that the time has now come when that which had been deferred above, VI, 11, has been abundantly fulfilled, namely, after so many others had been added to those first martyrs, especially in the times of Bar Kokhba, as we have shown. Καὶ δῦναι τὸν μισθὸν τοῖς δούλοις σου τοῖς προφήταις.] To the prophets of the New Testament, of whom above X, 7. The reward of the patience which is being discussed is religious liberty. Καὶ τοῖς ἁγίοις.] To the perfect Christians. Καὶ τοῖς φοβουμένοις τὸ ὄνομά σου τοῖς μικροῖς καὶ μεγάλοις.] Even to those who have the first beginnings of Christianity, who are called little ones, Matt. 10, 42. ch. 18, 10. 14. Mark 9, 42. Luke 17, 2. 1 Cor. 3, 1. Heb. 4, 12. 13. 1 John 2, 12. 14. Καὶ διαφθεῖραι τοὺς προφθείροντας τὴν γῆν.] Those Jews, the worst of men, similar to the men before the flood, and deserving no better treatment, is here a πλοκὴ, for the verb διαφθείρειν is placed twice, but in a different sense. Those are said διαφθείρειν τὴν γῆν who corrupt others by evil example. How: Evil communications corrupt good manners, 1 Cor. XV, 33. This is a prayer, that they may wish that that time be present as soon as possible. For this is the desire of the Elect in heaven as well as of the faithful on earth, Apoc. XXII, last. However, these things refer primarily to the time of the final judgment, which is called so absolutely and in its entirety, in which a reward is given to all the servants of the Lord, but one that is gratuitous and unmerited at the same time: to which also pertains the clear vision of the ark of the covenant. For here it is not permitted to behold it. Therefore, these things are not to be explained concerning the reward of patience as religious liberty. But the reward is given to the small and the great, that is, not small in regard to knowledge and faith: but in regard to stature and age, Apoc. XX, 12. We do not, however, disagree so much if anyone, with Osiander, prefers to understand the obscure and the clear. Those destroying the earth here are not so much the Jews as the Anti-Christians. For these, by idolatry, whoredom, and various other sins, seduce and destroy those who seek earthly things, Coloss. III, so that not only bodies, but even souls themselves perish with them, 2 Pet. II, 1. 2. 3. Apoc. XX, 10. 13. ch. XIV, 8. 10.
