The day comes, says the blessed Gerhard, in which those are to be cast into eternal destruction who, partly through idolatry and false doctrine, partly through an impious and scandalous life, and partly through the shedding of blood and fires, have corrupted and devastated the inhabitants of the earth, and have persisted in these worst works without repentance. However, the blessed Cluverus does not wish to take this as referring to the final judgment, lest the proper operation of the seventh trumpet or the third woe be constituted as the final judgment itself. But the positing of one is not the exclusion of the other. Even if we admit with him that certain excellent first-fruits of future glory and the portents of that great universal judgment are recounted here: we do not, however, think that the very power of that glory and judgment should be excluded in this place. For the judgment and the kingdom, of which we speak here, extends itself for ages of ages.

Latin:

Καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ὠργίσθησαν.] Illi non digni, qui appellentur Ju- dæi, cum vivant ἐθνικῶς. Sic supra iidem συναγωγὴ τοῦ Σατα- νᾶ II, 9. III, 9. προσκυνῆτες τὰ δαιμόνια IX, 20. Addidit ad Psalm. II. & XCIX, 1.

Non digni Romano-Catholici, Anti-Christia- ni, qui Christiani vocentur. Idololatria multiplice, religioso imaginum, Sanctorum, Angelorum, Mariæ & aliorum cultu Ethnicorum idolomaniæ affines. Καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῶν νεκρῶν κριθῆναι.] Supple ἦλθε. Venit tempus quo vindicentur mortui ob Christi nomen. Κρίνειν sæpe est vindicare. Itaque שׁפט, quod est κρίνειν vel δικάζειν per ἐκδικεῖν vertitur, Ezech. 7, 3. 27. c. 15, 37. c. 23, 24. 45. Abd. 21. Vide & Esa. 59, 9. 11. Sensus est, venisse jam tempus, quo impletum abunde quod supra dilatum fuerat, VI, 11. nem- pe postquam ad primos ilios martyres tot alii accesserant, Barchochebæ maxime temporibus, ut ostendimus. Καὶ δῦναι τὸν μισθὸν τοῖς δούλοις σου τοῖς προφήταις.] Prophe- tis Novi Testamenti, de quibus supra X, 7. Merces patien- tiæ, de qua agitur, est religionis libertas. Καὶ τοῖς ἁγίοις.] Perfecte Christianis. Καὶ τοῖς φοβουμένοις τὸ ὄνομά σου τοῖς μικροῖς καὶ μεγάλοις.] Etiam illis, qui prima initia habent Christianismi, qui parvuli dicuntur Matth.10,42. c.18,10.14. Marc.9,42. Luc.17,2. 1.Cor. 3,1. Ebr.4,12.13. 1.Joh.2,12.14. Καὶ διαφθεῖραι τοὺς προφθείροντας τὴν γῆν.] Judæos illos hominum pessimos, similes hominibus ante diluvium, nec melius meritos tractari, est hic πλοκὴ, nam verbum διαφθείρειν bis ponitur, sed sensu diverso. Διαφθείρειν τὴν γῆν dicuntur, qui alios pravo exemplo corrumpunt. Quomodo: Φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρῆσθ᾽ ὁμιλίαι κακαὶ. 1. Cor. XV, 33. Votum hoc est, quod optent, quamprimum tempus illud adsit. Hoc enim desiderium est tam Electorum in cælis, quam fidelium in terris, Apocal. XXII. ult. Respiciunt autem hæc imprimis tem- pus extremi judicii, quod ἐξολικῶς & absolute ita dicitur, in quo omnibus servis Domini merces sed gratuita & indebita simul datur: Quo etiam pertinet clara visio arcæ fœderis. Hic enim eam intueri non licet. Non ergo de mercede patien- tiæ libertate religionis hæc explicanda. Parvis autem & magnis datur merces, hoc est non parvis, quoad cognitionem & fidem: sed quantum ad sta- turam & ætatem, Ap. XX, 12. Non refragamur ta- men adeo, si quis cum Osiandro malit obscuros & claros intelligere. Perdentes terram hic non tam Judæi quam Anti-Christiani sunt. Hi enim ido- lolatria, scortatione, variisque peccatis aliis sedu- cunt & perdunt terrena sectantes, Coloss. III. ut non corpora tantum, sed & animæ ipsæ cum ipsis pereant, 2. Petr. II, 1. 2. 3. Apoc. XX, 10. 13. cap. XIV, 8. 10. Venit dies, inquit B. Gerhardus, in qua in æter- num exitium præcipitandi, qui partim per idolola- triam & falsam doctrinam, partim per vitam im- piam & scandalosam, partim per sanguinis effusio- nem & incendia inhabitatores terræ corruperunt, devastarunt, ac sine pœnitentia in his operibus pes- simis perseverarunt. De judicio tamen novissimo accipere non vult B. Cluverus, ne propria septimi tubicinii operatio seu væ tertium constituatur ipsum extremum judicium. Sed unius positio non est alterius exclusio. Etsi ergo cum eodem primitias hic quasdam excellentes futuræ gloriæ ac magni istius universalis judicii præjudicia enar- rari admittamus: non tamen ideo ipsam gloriæ & judicii istius vim hoc loco excludendam cense- mus. Judicium enim & regnum, de quo hic, por- rigit sese in sæcula sæculorum.

## 11:19
Vers. 19.

Καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ὤφθη ἡ κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης τοῦ Κυρίου ἐν τῷ ναῷ ἀυτοῦ.] It is an objection. Those who were Christians in the time of Elijah could have said: it is indeed a great thing that we have. But that temple of Solomon has not been restored, nor that ark of the covenant. Therefore, both the temple and the ark are shown to John, but in heaven. By this, Christians who were in Judea are commanded to always lift their minds to the highest heaven, where GOD dwells with supreme Majesty, where the ark of the covenant is, that is, where the goods of the new covenant are stored and kept. See what is above IV, V. 1. 2. 3. 4. The Latins also call the sky a temple, and Varro says that it is a temple by nature, and that others are so by similarity, and he asserts that line from Hecuba: O great temples of the gods mixed with shining stars! Add that line of Ennius: The great temple of Jove the High-Thunderer trembled. So also Lucretius: — and the high temples of the sky shining far from the earth.

It is manifest that this does not concern the Mosaic ark of the covenant, which was indeed lost; but its antitype: this, however, is Christ, Rom. III, 25. Heb. IV, 16. Coloss. II, 3. 4. not the Word of God, or the Church, in which the goods of the new covenant are kept. For it is shown in heaven, where Christ is, Col. III, 1. And therefore, the blessed vision of Christ, and the enjoyment of the grace which is dispensed at this ark of the covenant, is exhibited as a consolation to the Saints afflicted by the Anti-Christ, because this mystical ark wishes to go before and protect them, just as the Levitical ark went before and protected the Israelites in battles who adhered to and served God at the ark of the covenant, Num. X, 35. John III, 11. ch. VI, 9. 1 Sam. IV, 5. The ark, says the blessed Osiander, of the testament or covenant seen in heaven signifies that God (amidst the fury of enemies) remembers the covenant of grace, which He made with His Church (through the intervention of the blood of Christ): and therefore it was not permitted that the persecutors should destroy the true Church, even though it itself labors under many and great infirmities. But the lightnings, thunders, and hail teach that the Lord shows examples of His just wrath and vengeance even in this age, in punishing and destroying the tyrants who afflict His Church. The blessed Gravius wishes the opening of heaven to signify the opening of the Church, and that this is hinted: that after the glorification of the two witnesses, the true Evangelical Church is not to be closed but opened, so that many who are wandering from the truth may be able to enter it, and become true and living members of the same, according to the prophecy, Isa. II, 3. All nations shall flow to the mountain of God, and shall say, come let us ascend to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us his ways, etc. Conf. Mich. IV, 1. The orthodox Evangelical Church was previously closed by the tyranny of the Anti-Christ, with the witnesses of the truth having been killed: But now it is opened, and all Christians have free access to it without any prohibition or impediment, and the public exercise of the Evangelical religion flourishes, and will flourish more and more hereafter. And further: By the ark of the Testament is understood here Christ himself with all his merit and benefits, foreshadowed by the ark and the mercy seat of the Old Testament. But just as the ark of the covenant, once placed in the Holy of Holies and covered by a veil, could not be seen by the whole Israelite people: So Christ, the spiritual ark of the covenant, under the Papistic Anti-Christian priesthood, as if clouded by a veil of human traditions, could not be seen by the eyes of faith, hidden from the eyes of many. But after the exaltation of the two witnesses, the veil of Papal superstitions was removed, so that now Christ with his Gospel, grace, and merit can be seen by all Christians without any impediment, according to that, John VI, 40. This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees (with the eyes of faith) the Son, and believes in him, may have eternal life. By the opening of the temple of God in heaven is signified the most clear manifestation of the glory and happiness which the blessed obtain in heaven, Coloss. III, 4. 1. John III, 2. that the Elect are about to enter into heavenly glory, that they may serve GOD, Apocal. VII, 15. That Apocal. XXI, 22. that it is denied that there is a temple in the heavenly Jerusalem, that is to be understood of a material and earthly temple. By the ark 1. some wish to be signified the secret mysteries of future things, which are prefigured in the ark on account of its concealment, so that the sense may be:

God has revealed to the Church his mysteries, which had hitherto been hidden from it. 2. Primasius, Bede, and Rupertus understand this of the human nature of Christ, which shows itself to the elect to be seen and enjoyed. Both interpretations can be combined. Jesus Christ, prefigured by the ark of the covenant in the Old Testament, will then be seen by all the elect in ineffable joy, and he will most clearly manifest all mysteries to them, as the blessed Gerhard says here. By the ark, Cornelius understands the same thing, the humanity of Christ; he says that the most beautiful and glorious humanity of Christ is signified, which exhibits itself in heaven to the saints to be seen and enjoyed, and this was shown by a vision here to St. John, who, just as he was wonderfully delighted by the humanity of Christ in this life, and was refreshed by it, so he is much more wonderfully delighted by it in that other heavenly life, and is refreshed by it. Thus Richard, Victor, Bede, and Rupertus. He adds, however, that it should consequently be understood of St. Mary, because she enclosed Christ within herself like Manna, just as she did the law of God, citing St. Bernard in his sermon on St. Mary, and the prayers of the Church in the Litany. But the human nature of Christ is now more clearly indicated in the heavenly Psalmody: The kingdom of this world has become our Lord's and his Christ's, etc.

And there were lightnings and voices and thunders and a great hail.] This is the beginning, not only of chapter XII, but also of a new prophecy pertaining to the Romans. And it appears from Arethas that the division was once established in this way. Just as the hail poured out upon the earth above in VIII, 7 signified the hardening of the Jews: so here the hardness of heart in the Romans is signified. The lightnings and the sound of thunder signify the threats of God, as above in IV, 5. Among the punishments, however, which God threatens, the hardening of hearts stands out. We have had the full victory of Christ over the Jews explained through its stages up to the triumph. We shall now have the victory over the Romans with the most complete destruction of the idolatry which had raged so much. That 'and' deceived the copyists, which in Greek connects the preceding to the following: but in Hebrew it often begins a book, as in Num. I, 1, Josh. I, 1, 1 Sam. I, 1, and elsewhere.

The punishments of the Anti-Christians are intimated, not those of the pagan Romans. For that Rome is designated where Christ was crucified; which was not done in pagan Rome as it is done in Anti-Christian Rome, in the Church itself, in which the Anti-Christ sits: And the following prophecies and their exegesis will teach that they pertain to Anti-Christian Rome, not pagan. On the day of the final judgment, lightnings and thunders will be sent forth against the Anti-Christ and his followers, that is, a condemnatory sentence will be passed, by which they will be cast down into hell as if by a lightning bolt, Apoc. XXI, 14. Nevertheless, other judgments which are designated subsequently in this book are not to be excluded. Wherefore, as the blessed Cluverus warns, Joachim Abbas, Lyranus, Brightman, Alcafar, and others have rightly observed that the conversion and illumination of the kingdoms of the world are predicted here, although they apply it to different times. For Alcafar understands the first conversion of the nations accomplished through the Apostles; Lyranus, the defeat of the Goths under Justin and Justinian; Joachim, a singular illumination of the Church and the nations that will happen in the final times; Brightman, the liberation of certain kingdoms of Europe, such as Britain, Denmark, Sweden, and the like, from the Papacy. But we have warned before that the prophecy about the Papacy begins here, which is its ordinary treatment here, which was indeed preceded in the preceding sections by the shaking of the kingdoms of the world, as it was from this that the Bishop of the city of Rome took the occasion for his tyranny. But concerning the time of the dead, which has come, that they may be judged, the blessed one asks: Which dead? The nations raging against GOD. If they are raging, how are they dead? I answer: The nations are understood to have been raging, but now the wrath of the Lord is coming upon them, and the time of the dead, that those raging and cruel nations may be judged. The ark of the covenant is explained from Primasius: namely, that the mystery of the Incarnation of Christ is designated, who carries within himself the tablets of the testament like that ark, since he did not come to destroy the law, but to fulfill it, and all the promises of GOD are 'Amen' in him, 2 Cor. I, 20. Who also has the golden urn with Manna, because he carries spiritual food within a body adorned with the splendor of wisdom to be dispensed to others through the intellect, John VI, v. 51. Also the rod of Aaron, because, having been born in a singularly new birth from an undefiled Virgin, he has all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden within himself under the covering of the flesh, like an almond, Coloss. II, 3. This exposition, drawn from the most ancient sources, fits this passage most beautifully. For just as formerly over the ark and the mercy seat: so now in the body of Christ we have GOD undoubtedly present. Just as he had promised there that he would be propitious: so now in the blood of Christ, Rom. III, 25. Just as in that one the tablets of the testament were restored, to which the people were bound to show obedience: so in Christ is the fulfillment of our law, Romans VIII, 3. Just as the ark was in the Holy of Holies: so is Christ in heaven itself. Finally, just as the veil of the Holy of Holies was torn, and the ark of the Testament appeared when Christ was dying: so the mystery of the incarnation and of his entire office was revealed under the New Testament, and especially became conspicuous in the eyes of all nations, when, with the veil of ignorance, hatred, and pagan superstitions removed, the secrets of the Christian Religion became known to all. For before, the nations had thought very differently about Christ than they felt after the times of Constantine, when the secrets of the coming of Christ were revealed. Furthermore: The lightnings, says Primasius, are the mighty works by which Christ the Lord made his disciples shine, the voices and thunders are the preachings by which the Apostles thundered to the peoples like clouds. Earthquakes, noise, the agitation of peoples, which frequently brought on the persecutions of the growing Church, when it always harms itself more by breaking against the waves, and by devastating itself, it shatters. Thus also the savage multitude of nations, which persecuted the faith of Christ, by later following it, became in number either small or nothing. He had said these things were done, and in the description of the seven Angels from the very advent of the Lord, and generally from the beginning to the end: Then by parts how they were done; so also now as the temple of God opened in heaven. We do not disapprove of this sense approved by the blessed Cluverius: provided that our exposition concerning the judgment of God is joined with it. For both can be designated by this similitude not inconveniently, whatever grace from God and Christ under the Anti-Christ and whatever wrath was to befall the enemies of Christ, and especially the Anti-Christ. For we have said that a summary complex of all things is exhibited here.

THE FIFTH VISION CONCERNING THE PERSECUTION OF THE GREAT ANTI-CHRIST, AND THE GENERAL FIGURATION OF HIS JUDGMENT.

I. THE PERSECUTION OF THE ANTI-CHRIST.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

Καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ὤφθη ἡ κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης τοῦ Κυρίου ἐν τῷ ναῷ ἀυτοῦ.] Est Anthypophora. Poterant dicere illi, qui Eliæ erant Christiani: magnum quidem est, quod habemus. At non restitutum est tem- plum illud Salomonis, & arca illa fœderis. Ideo ostendi- tur Johanni & templum & arca, sed in cælo. Per hoc juben- tur Christiani, qui in Judæa erant, animos semper ad sum- mum cælum attollere, ubi DEUS habitat cum summa Maje- state, ubi arca fœderis, id est, ubi bona fœderis novi reposita servantur. Vide quæ supra IV, V. 1. 2.3. 4. Etiam Latini cœ- lum templum vocant, & id natura templum esse, ait Varro, cætera similitudine, assęrtque ex Hecuba illud : O magna templa cælitum commixta stellis splendidis! Adde illud Ennii : Contremuit templum magnum Jovis Altitonantis. Sic & Lucretius : - - altaque cæli Densabant procul à terris fulgentia templa.

Manifestum est, non de arca fœderis Mosaica, quæ quidem deperdita erat; sed ejus antitypo agi: hoc vero Christus est, Roman. III, 25. Ebr. IV, 16. Coloss. II, 3. 4. non Verbum Dei, vel Ecclesia, in qua bona fœderis novi asservantur. Nam in cœlo monstratur, ubi Christus est, Col. III, 1. Ideoq́, beata Christi visio, & gratiæ, quæ ad arcam hanc fœderis dispensatur fruitio Sanctorum ab Anti-Christo af- flictorum solatio exhibetur, quod præire & tueri velit eos hæc mystica arca, quemadmodum arca Levitica præcedebat & tuebatur in præliis Israeli- tas Deo adhærentes & servientes ad arcam fœderis Num. X, 35. Joh. III, 11. c. VI, 9. 1. Sam. IV, 5. Arca, inquit B. Osiander, testamenti seu fœderis visa in cælo significat, Deum (inter medios hostium furores) me- minisse fœderis gratiæ, quod cum Ecclesia sua (inter- ventu sanguinis Christi) pepigit : ideoq́, non commis- sum, ut persecutores Ecclesiam veram deleant, tamétsį ipsa multis & magnis infirmitatibus laborat. Fulgura vero, tonitrua, & grando docent, Dominum exempla justæ suæ iræ ac vindictæ etiam in hoc seculo ostendere, in puniendis & perdendis tyrannis, qui ipsius Ecclesiam affligunt. B. Gravius apertionem cœli significare vult apertionem Ecclesiæ, idque innui : Post glori- ficationem duorum testium veram Ecclesiam Evange- licam non claudendam sed aperiendam esse, ut multi à veritate aberrantes eam intrare possint, & fierive- ra ac viva ejusdem membra, juxta vaticinium, Esa. II, 3. Confluent ad montem Dei omnes gentes, & dicent, venite ascendamus ad montem Domini, & ad domum Dei Jacob, & docebit nos vias suas, &c. Conf. Mich. IV, 1. Clausa erat antea per tyrannidem Anti-Christi orthodoxa Ecclesia Evangelica, inter- fectis veritatis testibus : Sed nunc aperitur, & adi- tum habent ad eam liberum omnes Christiani abs- que ulla prohibitione seu impedimento vigetque pu- publicum Evangelicæ religionis exercitium, & magis magisque deinceps vigebit. Et porro : Per ar- cam Testamenti hic intelligitur ipse Christus cum omni suo merito & beneficiis per arcam & propitia- torium V. Test. adumbratis. Quemadmodum au- tem arca fœderis olim in Sancto Sanctorum posita velo tecta conspici ab universo populo Israëlitico non poterat : Ita Christus spiritualis arca fœderis sub sa- cerdotio Papistico Anti-Christiano, velo traditio- num humanarum quasi obnubilata, à multorum oculis abscondita oculis fidei conspici non potuit. Sed post duorum testium exaltationem velum supersti- tionum Papalium remotum fuit, ita ut nunc Christus libere cum suo Evangelio gratia & merito ab omni- bus Christianis absque ullo impedimento possit con- spici juxta illud, Joh. VI, 40. Hæc est voluntas ejus, qui misit me, ut omnis, qui videt (oculis fidei) Fi- lium, & credit in eum, habeat vitam æternam. Per apertionem templi Dei in cælo significatur cla- rissima patefactio gloriæ & felicitatis, quam beati in cælo obtinent, Coloss. III, 4. 1. Johan. III, 2. quod ingressuri sint Electi in gloriam cælestem, ut DEO serviant, Apocal. VII, 15. Quod Apocal. XXI, 22. quod negatur in cælesti Hierosolyma esse templum, id de templo materiali & terreno accipiendum. Per arcam 1. quidam volunt significari arcana my- steria rerum futurarum, quæ in arca pro- pter absconsionem præfigurentur, ut sit sensus:

Deus mysteria sua, quæ Ecclesiæ hactenus fuerunt abscondita, ipsi patefecit. 2. Primasius, Beda, Ru- pertus accipiunt de humana Christi natura, quæ se videndam & fruendam electis demonstrat. Potest utraque expositio conjungi. Christus Jesus per ar- cam fœderis in V. T. præfiguratus tunc ab omnibus electis in lætitia inenarrabili conspicietur, ac omnia mysteria ipsis clarissime manifestabit, ut hic B. Ger- hardus. Per arcam Cornelius intelligit idem Humanitatem Christi; Significatur, inquit, Chri- sti Humanitas pulcherrima & gloriosissima, quæ in cœlo sanctis se videndam & fruendam exhibet, idque per visionem ostensum est hic S. Johanni, qui sicut in hac vita Christi humanitate mire delectatus est, cum eaque diffuaviatus; ita multo magis in alte- ra illa cœlesti mire ea delectatur, cum eaque diffua- viatur. Ita Richardus, Victor, Beda & Ruper- tus. Addit autem de S. Maria consequenter eam intelligendam esse, quia hæc Christum quasi Manna, æque ac legem Dei in se conclusit, S. Bernhardum serm. de S. Maria adducens, & Ec- clesiæ preces in Litan. Sed Humana Christi natura jam clarius indicata in Psalmodia cœlesti: Factum est regnum hujus mundi Domini & Christi ejus, &c.

Καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταὶ καὶ χάλαζα με- γάλη.] Hoc est initium, non tantum capitis XII. sed & novæ prophetiæ pertinentis ad Romanos. Et sic olim institutam fuisse divisionem ex Aretha apparet. Sicut supra grando in terram effusa IIX, 7. obdurationem significavit Judæorum: Ita hic significatur durities animi in Romanis. Fulmina & tonitruum soni minas Dei significant, ut supra IV, 5. Inter pœnas autem quas Deus comminatur, eminet animorum ob- duratio. Habuimus plenam Christi victoriam de Judæis per suos gradus explicatam ad triumphum usque. Habebimus nunc victoriam de Romanis cum plenissima idololatriæ, quæ adeo sævierat, destructione. Decepit exscriptores illud καὶ, quod apud Græcos priora posterioribus connectit: at apud Ebræos sæpe librum inchoat, ut Num. I, 1. Jos. I, 1. 1.Sam. I, 1. & alibi.

Non Ethnicorum Romanorum; sed Anti-Chri- stianorum pœnæ intimantur. Illa enim Roma desi- gnatur, ubi Christus crucifixus est; quod non ita in Roma Ethnica factum est, ut fit in Anti-Christia- na, in ipsa Ecclesia, in qua sedet Anti-Christus : Et ad Anti-Christianam Romam, non paganam, per- tinere, sequentia vaticinia & ἐξήγησις eorum do- cebit. In die judicii novissimi adversus Antichri- stum & asseclas emittentur fulgura & tonitrua, hoc est, feretur sententia condemnatoria, qua velut fulmine prosternentur in infernum, Apoc. XXI, 14. Non excludenda tamen alia judicia, quæ deinceps in hoc libro designata. Quamobrem recte, monen- te B. Cluvero, Joachimus Abbas, Lyranus, Bricht- mannus, Alcafar & alii regnorum mundi conversio- nem & illuminationem hic prædici observarunt, quanquam ad diversa illam tempora applicant. Al- cafar enim primam gentium conversionem per Apo- stolos factam, Lyranus Gothorum debellationem sub Justino & Justiniano, Joachimus singularem Ecclesiæ & gentium illustrationem extremis temporibus futu- ram, Brichtmannus regnorum quorundam Europæ ut Britanniæ, Daniæ, Sueciæ & similium à Papatu liberationem intelligit. Sed monuimus antea, in- cipere hic prophetiam de Papatu, quæ ordinaria hic ejus tractatio est, quam vero præcessit jam in superioribus regnorum mundi concussio, utpote à qua occasionem suæ tyrannidis sumpsit Roma- næ urbis Episcopus. De tempore vero mor- tuorum, quod venit, ut judicentur ὁ Μακαρίτης: Quinam mortui? Gentes DEO irascentes. Si irascentur, quomodo sunt mortui? Respondeo: Gentes intelliguntur iratæ fuisse, sed jam venire iram Domini super illas, & tempus mortuorum, ut gentes illæ iracundæ & crudeles judicentur. Arca fœderis explicatur è Primasio: Mysterium scilicet designari Incarnationis Christi, qui more illius arcæ tabulas testamenti intra se gerat, quan- doquidem non venerit legem solvere, sed adim- plere, & omnes promissiones DEI in ipso sint Amen. 2. Cor. I, 20. Qui urnam quoque habeat auream cum Manna, quia spirituale pabulum in- tra corpus sapientiæ fulgore decorum gerat per intellectum aliis prærogandum. Johan. VI. v. 51. Virgam etiam Aaron, eo quod intemerata Vir- gine singulariter novo ortu progenitus inter te- ctorium carnis instar amygdalæ omnes thesauros sapientiæ & scientiæ penes se habeat abscondi- tos, Coloss. II, 3. Quæ expositio à vetustissimis hau- sta belliffime huic loco convenit. Nam sicut olim super arca & propitiatorio: Ita nunc in corpore Christi indubitanter præsentem habemus DEUM. Sicut ibi propitium se fore promiserat: Ita nunc in sanguine Christi, Rom. III, 25. Sicut in illa ta- bulæ erant testamenti reparatæ, quibus obedientiam populus præstare debebat: Sic in Christo est nostræ legis impletio, Roman. IIX, 3. Sicut in ipso San- cto sanctorum erat arca: Sic Christus in ipso cælo. Denique sicut velum sancti sanctorum rumpeba- tur, & arca Testamenti apparebat moriente Chri- sto: Sic mysterium incarnationis totiusque officii ejus patescebat sub Novo Testamento, ac præsertim conspicuum evadebat in oculis omnium gentium, quum dempto ignorantiæ, odii & superstitionum Ethnicanum velo, secreta Religionis Christianæ omnibus innotescerent. Nam antea longe aliter de Christo senserant gentes, quam post Constantini tem- pora, revelatis adventus Christi arcanis sentiebant. Porro: Fulgura, inquit Primasius, sunt virtu- tes, quibus suos Christus Dominus fecit fulgere discipulos, voces & tonitrua prædicationes, quibus tanquam nubes Apostoli populis intonabant. Ter- ræ motus, strepitus, concitatus populorum, qui per- secutiones crescentis Ecclesiæ sæpius ingerebant, quando semper se plus frangendo fluctibus illisa, nocet, seque vastando comminuit. Sic etiam sæva gentium multitudo, quæ fidem Christi persequeba- tur, ipsum postea sectando, facta est numero vel parva vel nulla. Hæc dixerat facta, & in descri- ptione septem Angelorum ab ipso adventu Domini, & generaliter ab origine in finem: Deinde per par- tes quemadmodum facta sint; ita & nunc ut tem- plum Dei in cælo apertum. Quem sensum à B. Cluvero approbatum non improbamus: modo cum eodem conjungatur nostra de judicio Dei ex- positio. Nam utrumque ista similitudine designa- ri potest non incommode, quicquid gratiæ à Deo & Christo sub Anti-Christo & quicquid iræ hosti- bus Christi, & imprimis Anti-Christo obventu- rum erat. Summariam enim omnium complexio- nem hìc exhiberi diximus.

VISIO QUINTA DE ANTI-CHRISTI MAGNI PER- SECUTIONE, EJUSQUE JUDICII GE- NERALI FIGURATIONE.

I. PERSECUTIO ANTI-CHRISTI.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

A pregnant woman seen with a red Dragon about to devour her son, but the son was withdrawn, and the woman fleeing into the desert was preserved for 1260 days. With Michael fighting against the Dragon, and him being cast out, and because of that a victory song being celebrated, the Dragon pursues the woman, fleeing into the desert, he follows her by pouring a river from his mouth, but the earth absorbs it, but the Dragon goes away to fight with the rest of the woman's seed.

There are three parts: I. The Satanic pursuit of the pregnant woman, and the divine withdrawal to verse 6. II. The battle of Michael with the Dragon, and the defeat of the latter to verse 12. III. The new persecution of the woman fleeing into the desert to verse 17.

PART I. The Satanic pursuit of the pregnant woman & the divine withdrawal of the same.

Vers. 1.

Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ.] These must be connected, as I said, with the last things which had preceded. Σημεῖον here is a portent not in reality, but ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ as presently 3. & XV, 1. ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ, that is, in the air, a middle place between heaven and earth. It signifies that in the thing signified, celestial and terrestrial causes run together. Thus also below XV, 1.

Now a little more distinctly and clearly chapter XII prophesies concerning the operation of the seventh trumpet, and first indeed under the images of the woman bringing forth, and the Dragon following, then of Michael fighting, and overcoming the Dragon, finally of the river poured from the mouth of the Dragon against the woman, and absorbed by the earth, helping her: but afterwards chapter XIII, under the form of the Anti-Christ and the Anti-Christian kingdom, depicting the Roman caesaropapism and papocaesarism, exhibiting through a double beast: To which is opposed chapter XIV. of Christ, and those who follow him, on Mount Zion, a new song, and also the prophecy of the Angels or heralds of the Word concerning the kingdom of Christ the Gospel, and concerning the fall and ruin of Babylon and the Anti-Christ, as also concerning the punishment and penalty of his followers, and concerning the blessedness and rest of those adhering to the Lord by true faith, a heavenly consolation, finally a Prophetic scheme concerning the judgment and harvest and the treading of the branches in the winepress of Divine wrath, and the punitive fire that will afflict the Anti-Christ and his assistants. Which judgment is afterwards revealed more distinctly by the introduction of the Angels with seven vials: but that constitutes a new vision, of which hereafter. However, no connection with the preceding is hinted at here; but a new and indeed a fifth vision, which the words sufficiently indicate: And a great sign was seen in heaven. For Saint John is accustomed to prefix some indication when a new vision follows: nor is it unusual for him to append a more special explanation to a general adumbration by a peculiar vision, which the following sixth vision will also confirm.

But why ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ ought to be explained as in the air, which also pleased Cornelius, rather than in the ether, as was done in other visions, I see no reason. For the things which John saw in the Spirit in the Majestatic heaven, we have already seen above their significations fulfilled in the Ecclesiastical heaven. Cornelius says that this battle was not fought in reality in heaven, but on earth, as is evident from verse 6, where it is said that the woman fled from this battle, from the place of the battle, into the wilderness.

Γυνὴ.] The Church, by the name of the Catholic Church, both universal and particular, is described now in the masculine form on account of fortitude and the imitation of Christ, Ephesians IV, verse 13, in which way we shall presently have υἱὸν ἄῤῥενα, and we have already had two Prophets; now in the form of a woman, because Christ as a husband loves, rules, makes fruitful, and protects them, 2 Corinthians XI, 2. Eph. V, 32.

Nothing is added concerning the condition, and we see that those things are often called by names which they are not, which they are said to be: just as those who were not Jews called themselves Jews, Ap. II, 9. and all heretics, as Augustine testifies in lib. IV. c. fundam. Epist. Manich., wish to be called Catholics and Christians. Most interpreters admit that the woman is the Church. I say with Ambrose, says Cornelius, Ticonius, Primasius, Andrew of Caesarea, Haymo, Richard, Bede, and Methodius, whom Arethas cites, that by this woman is understood the Church, especially that which will be at the end of the world. Which, however, we do not prove concerning the end of the world. The sustenance of the woman does indeed reach that far, but it lasts for 1260 years. Alcafar understands the primitive Church by the woman, and the same by the son, because a rod of iron is given to him. But less conveniently.

Περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον.] Understand ὡς, that is, as if suffused on all sides by the light of Christ, like the sun. Christ is compared to the sun, Mal. IV, 2. Eph. V, 14. And deservedly, because in Him is the fullness of divine light, John I, 4. 5. 8. 9.

This garment is added here, because it is proper to the faithful: For as many as have been baptized into Christ, have put on Christ, Galat. III, 27. and it is opposed to the garment of the Anti-Christ. For they prefer to appear before the tribunal of God with their own works, and they trust that they can stand better if they are clothed in a garment of their own righteousness and charity, than, as Cornelius wishes, in a garment of the righteousness of Christ and faith, since he calls faith unformed, which is not formed except by charity, and receives its form from it, by their own judgment. But B. Cluverus rightly says: The Church is clothed with Christ in two ways, 1. as a gift, because His righteousness shines, so that it may be radiant in the sight and judgment of God, Isa. LXI, 10. 2. as an example, because it holds Him forth as the purest light, in doctrine and in all its deeds, Ephes. V. v. 2. 14. But the false Church does not shine with CHRIST as with a most decent garment, but with fine linen, purple, gold, and silver, as will appear below in Chapter XVII. v. 4. and therefore it is called a harlot, not a holy mother.

Καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς.] The moon is indeed a mutable star: and therefore fleeting and mutable things are rightly seen to be able to be indicated by the moon. But since in the Holy Scriptures the moon added to the sun and the stars designates some light, as Gen. XXXVII, 8. Job XXV, 5. Ecclesiastes XII, 5. Isa. XIII. v. 10. chap. XXX, 26. chap. LX, 19. 20. Ezek. XXXVII. verse 7. Joel III, 15. Psalm CXXXVI, 9. CXXXIX, 38. it will be more correct here to understand by the moon the light of the Law and the Prophets, much lesser than the light of Christ, upon which, however, the Catholic Church to some extent relies, as upon a footstool. For in that sense that 'under the feet' is sometimes used, as Psalm XVIII. v. 10. Exod. XXIV. v. 10. The writings of Moses and the Prophets bear witness to Christ, Luke XXIV. v. 46. John V. verse 39. chap. VI. v. 45.

To be under the feet by force of opposition is to be subjected in this place, not to be unsupported in a way: for the Law and the Prophets were not destitute of light necessary and sufficient for salvation, 2. Pet. I, 18. More correctly, therefore, the Doctors are understood, who borrow their light from Christ, the Sun of righteousness, like the moon, and are mutable after its manner. The moon is the lowest of the stars. Gregory the Great, Andrew of Caesarea, Methodius, Arethas, and others understand the moon as overcome, trodden upon, despised, and through it all sublunary and temporal things. To Cornelius, the Divinity of CHRIST is as it were the greater light, which presides over the day of blessedness in heaven; but humanity is the lesser light, which presides over the night of this age, as Saint Augustine says in Ps. 73, verse 16. But by reason of light, the splendor of Christ's humanity does not differ, except that the latter has the same κατ' ἄλλο by the grace of union, and the divine nature κατ' ἑαυτὴν and by itself. Again, just as the moon, says the Jesuit Lapideus, is the humanity of Christ: so the moon is also the Virgin Mother of God. For she is as it were the Lucina of the Church in labor, so that that Virgilian line may be said of her: Chaste Lucina, favor us, your Apollo now reigns. But we leave these delights to the Papists.

And upon her head a crown of twelve stars.] Namely, a crown having stars for gems. For stars are like gems, as was said above in I, 16. These stars κατὰ τὸ μυσικὸν are the twelve Apostles. For by that number that college was instituted at the beginning, and that number was restored to it by the election of Matthias. And so they are often called οἱ δώδεκα even when someone was absent from that number, as in John 20, verse 24. Paul therefore and Barnabas and whoever were like them are ὑπεράριθμοι, just as sometimes in the empire of Kings certain men are added to a college beyond the legitimate number. We have seen teachers called by the number of stars above in I, 20. But the Apostles excel in that genus, as stars of the first magnitude. These communicate the light received from the Sun, Christ, to the Church, even after their death, through doctrine preserved partly by writings, partly by tradition.

Above the head of the Church are twelve stars, or twelve Apostles, shining both by their preaching and by their writings throughout the whole world, to whom all other Teachers are deservedly subjected. Cornelius è Viega recounts various things concerning the number twelve, to which allusion might be made here: the 12 Patriarchs and tribes of Israel, the fountains of Elim in Exod. 15, the titles erected by Moses in Ex. 24, the gems of the breastplate in chapter 28, the stones from the Jordan in Jos. 4, the bronze oxen in 1 Kings 7, the lion cubs in chapter 10, the loaves of the presence in Levit. 24, the spies in Num. 13, the stars of the Zodiac, as also the twelve stars of the superstitious rosary. Others understand the twelve stars as the twelve prerogatives of the Church of Christ over the synagogues. B. Cluverus understands the moon as the Auditors: that the phrase 'under her feet' simply designates a place without any mark of contempt or rejection has been well observed by Alcafar, Psalm 18, v. 10, Exod. 34, 10, Num. 16, 32. For just as the moon is inferior to the stars: so are auditors to Teachers. But just as the moon sheds a clearer splendor from itself: so the whole assembly of the learning Church illuminates the night of this world more clearly than if you were to consider or see the Teachers alone. Then, just as the moon with the stars borrows light from the Sun; so the Church, both in its Teachers and its Auditors, owes the light of doctrine and life to Christ. Finally, just as the moon is variable, while the Sun is most constant: so the learning Church is variable, but the light of Christ the Lord is immutable. By the woman some understand Mary, and by the child whom she had conceived, the Son of God. Piscator and Tossanus wish to refer to the time when Christ was to be born. But Methodius, cited by Andreas of Caesarea, as well as Victorinus, Primasius, and others, rightly denies that the Blessed Virgin is prefigured here, since the birth of Christ had already taken place; whereas John is dealing with future things. Nor did the Blessed Mary feel the pains of childbirth, but the Church did feel them when it was about to bring forth the confession of faith in the persecutions which it sustained on her account under the Heathen Emperors. Therefore, it is incongruous and without foundation that Bernard here assigned 12 prerogatives to the Virgin Theotokos above other Saints.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Mulier prægnans cum rufo Dracone filium ejus devoraturo visa, sed subductus filius, fu- giensque mulier in deserto conservata 1260. diebus. Pugnante Michaele cum Dracone, eoque ejecto, & ob id epinicio celebrato, Draco persequitur mulierem, in desertum fugientem, effuso tamen ex ore flumine in- sectatur, sed terra id absorbet, Draco au- tem cum reliquo mulieris semine pugna- tum abit.

Partes sunt tres: I. Satanica Mulieris gravida insectatio, & divina subductio ad vers. 6. II. Mi- chaëlis cum Dracone pugna, hujusque devictio ad vers. 12. III. Mulieris in desertum fugitiva nova persecutio ad vers. 17.

PARS I. Satanica mulieris gravida insectatio & divi- na ejusdem subductio.

Vers. 1.

Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ.] Connectenda hæc, ut dixi, cum postremis, quæ præcesserant. Σημεῖον hic est ostentum non in re, sed ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ ut mox 3. & XV, 1. ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ, id est, in aëre, medio loco inter cœlum & terram. Id significat in re significata inter se concurrere causas cœle- stes & terrestres. Sic & infra XV, 1.

Nunc paulo distinctius & luculentius c. XII. va- ticinatur de operatione septimæ tubæ, & primum quidem sub imaginibus mulieris parturientis, & Draconis insequentis, deinde Michaëlis pugnan- tis, & Draconem superantis, denique flumi- nis ex ore Draconis in mulierem effusi, & à ter- ra, ipsam adjuvante, absorpti: postea vero cap. XIII. sub forma Anti-Christum & Anti-Chri- stianum regnum, depingente καισαροπαπίαν Ro- manam & παποκαισαρίαν, per geminam bestiam exhibente: Cui opponitur cap. XIV. Christi, & qui eum sectantur, in monte Zion, canticum novum nec non Angelorum vel præconum Verbi de re- gno Christi Evangelium, & de casu ac ruina Ba- bylonis & Anti-Christi ut & de supplicio, ac pœna assectarum vaticinium, deque beatitudine ac re- quie Domino vera fide adhærentium, cœleste sola- tium, denique de judicio & messe ac calcatione pal- mitum in torculari iræ Divinæ, atque igne punito- rio Anti-Christum ejusque parastatas afflicturo sche- ma Propheticum. Quod judicium postmodum distinctius revelatur introductione Angelorum cum septem phialis: sed ea novam visionem con- stituit, de qua deinceps. Non autem hic conne- xio cum præcedentibus innuitur; sed nova & qui- dem quintæ visio, quam satis indicant verba: Et visum est signum magnum in cælo. Solet enim S. Johannes aliquod indicium præmittere, cum vi- sio nova sequitur: neque insolens ipsi est genera- li adumbrationi subjungere specialiorem explicatio- nem visione peculiari, quod & sequens sexta vi- sio confirmabit.

Cur vero ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ explicari potius debeat in aëre, quod Cornelio etiam placuit, quam in æthere, ut in aliis visionibus factum, causam nul- lam video. Nam quæ in Spiritu in cœlo Majestati- co vidit Johannes, eorum significata adimpleta in cœlo Ecclesiastico jam supra vidimus. Re ipsa hoc prælium non fuisse gestum in cælo, sed in terra, patere ex v. 6. ait Cornelius, ubi dicitur mulier ex hoc præ- lio ex prælii loco fugisse in solitudinem.

Γυνὴ.] Ecclesia nomine Catholica Ecclesiæ tum univer- sales tum particulares modo virili specie describuntur ob fortitudinem & imitationem Christi Ephes. IV. v. 13, quo- modo mox habebimus υἱὸν ἄῤῥενα, & jam ante habuimus duos Prophetas; modo fœminæ, quia Christus velut ma- ritus eas amat, regit, fœcundat, protegit, 2. Corinth. XI, 2. Eph. V, 32.

De conditione nihil additur, & cognominari videmus fæpe, quæ non sunt, quod esse dicuntur: quomodo Judæos se dicebant, qui non erant, Ap. II, 9. & omnes hæretici, teste Augustino lib. IV. c. fundam. Epist. Manich. Catholicos se & Christia- nos dici volunt. Ecclesiam esse mulierem, admit- tunt plerique interpretes. Dico cum Ambrosio, inquit Cornelius, Ticonio, Primasio, Andrea, Cæsa- riensi, Haymone, Richardo, Beda, & Methodio, quem citat Aretas, per mulierem hanc intelligi Ec- clesiam, maxime quæ erit sub finem mundi. Quod tamen de fine mundi non probamus. Pertingit quidem sustentatio mulieris eo usque, sed annis durat 1260. Per mulierem Ecclesiam primi- tivam, eandemque per filium intelligit Alcafar, quia illi datur virga ferrea. Sed minus com- mode.

Περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον.] Subaudi ὡς, id est, luce Christi velut solis, undique perfusa. Christus soli comparatur, Mal. IV, 2. Eph. V, 14. Et merito, quia in ipso est divinæ lu- cis plenitudo, Joh. I, 4. 5. 8. 9.

Additur hic amictus, quia fidelium est pro- prius: Quotquot enim in Christum baptizati sunt, Christum induerunt, Galat. III, 27. & Anti-Chri- sti amictui oppositus. Illi enim malunt cum ope- ribus suis coram tribunali Dei comparere, se- que potius consistere posse confidunt, si amicti fuerint veste propriæ justitiæ, & charitatis, quam ut Cornelius vult, veste justitiæ Christi & fidei, quum fidem informem dicat, quæ non nisi chari- tate formetur, & ab ea formam consequatur, ipso- rum judicio. Sed recte B. Cluverus: Induta est Christo dupliciter Ecclesia, 1. tanquam dono, quia justitia ipsius coruscat, ut sit fulgida in conspectu & judicio Dei, Esa. LXI, 10. 2. tanquam exemplo, quia ipsum tanquam lumen purissimum præfert, in doctrina omnibusque factis suis, Ephes. V. v. 2. 14. At falsa Ecclesia non CHRISTO tanquam vestitu decentissimo, sed bysso, purpura, auro & ar- gento fulget, ut apparebit infra Cap. XVII. v. 4. ac proinde meretrix non sancta mater appella- tur.

Καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς.] Est quidem luna mutabile sidus: ideoque res caducæ & mutabiles recte videntur per lunam posse indicari. Sed cum in sacris lite- ris luna addita soli ac sideribus lucem aliquam designat, ut Genes. XXXVII, 8. Job. XXV, 5. Ecclesiastæ XII, 5. Ef. XIII. v. 10. cap. XXX, 26. cap. LX, 19. 20. Ezech. XXXVII. vers. 7. Joel. III, 15. Psalm. CXXXVI, 9. CXXXIX, 38. rectius hic erit per lunam intelligere lucem legis ac Prophetarum, luce Christi multo minorem, cui tamen Ecclesia Catholica ali- quatenus innititur, velut suppedaneo. Nam eo sensu i- lud sub pedibus interdum usurpatur, ut Psalm. XVIII. v. 10. Exod. XXIV. v. 10. Scripta Mosis & Prophetarum Christo præbent testimonium, Luc. XXIV. v. 46. Johan. V. vers. 39. cap. VI. v. 45.

Sub pedibus esse vi oppositionis subjici hoc lo- co est, non sustinere quodammodo: nec enim lu- ce necessaria, ac sufficiente ad salutem lex ac Pro- phetæ destituti fuere, 2. Petr. I, 18. Rectius itaque Doctores intelliguntur, qui lumen suum à Chri- sto, sole justitiæ, instar lunæ mutuantur ejusque more mutabiles sunt. Luna stellarum infima est. Lunam devictam, calcatam, contemptam & per eam res omnes sublunares & tempora- les intelligunt Gregorius Magnus, Andr. Cæsar. Methodius, Aretas & alii. Cornelio CHRI- STI Divinitas est quasi luminare majus, quod præest diei beatitudinis in cælo; humanitas vero est luminare minus, quod præest nocti hujus sæculi, ut ait Sanctus Augustinus in Psam. LXXIII, vers. 16. Sed ratione luminis non differt huma- nitatis Christi splendor, nisi quod illa eandem habeat κατ' ἄλλο per unionis gratiam, & divina natura κατ' ἑαυτὴν & per se. Rursus sicut luna, inquit Jesuita Lapideus, est humanitas Christi: ita luna est & Virgo Deipara. Hæc est enim quasi Lucina Ecclesiæ parturientis, ut de ea dici possit illud Virgilianum: Casta fave Lucina, tuus jam regnat Apollo. Sed istas delitias Papistis relinquimus.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς στέφανος ἀστέρων δώδεκα.] Nimi- rum corona pro gemmis habens stellas. Sunt enim gem- mis similes stellæ, ut dictum supra I, 16. Stellæ hæ κατὰ τὸ μυσικὸν sunt Apostoli duodecim. Eo enim numero id collegium initio institutum fuit, & is numerus ei redditus electione Matthiæ. Itaque sæpe vocantur οἱ δώδεκα etiam cum aliquis abesset ab eo numero, ut Joh. XX. vers. 24. Pau- lus ergo & Barnabas & si qui fuere eis similes, sunt ὑπερά- ριθμοι, sicut interdum Regum imperio quidam collegio ad- duntur supra numerum legitimum. Doctores stellarum nu- mero appellari vidimus supra I, 20. Apostoli autem in eo ge- nere eminent, ut primæ magnitudinis stellæ. Hi lucem a So- le Christo acceptam Ecclesiæ communicant, etiam post mor- tem suam, per doctrinam partim scriptis, partim traditione conservatam.

Super caput Ecclesiæ duodecim stellæ, seu duo- decim Apostoli sunt, fulgentes tum præconio tum scriptis per orbem universum, quibus sub- jiciuntur merito omnes alii Doctores. Cornelius è Viega recenset de numero duodenario varia, ad quæ hic allusio fiat, XII. Patriarchas & tribus Israel, fontes Elim Exod. XV. titulos à Mose ere- ctos, Ex. XXIV. gemmas pectoralis cap. XXVIII. lapides è Jordane, Jos. IV. boves Æneos, 1. Reg. VII. leunculos cap. X. panes expositionis Levit. XXIV. exploratores Num. XIII. stellas Zodiaci, uti etiam superstitiosi rosarii duodecim stellas. Alii intelligunt duodecim stellas de duodecim prærogativis Ecclesiæ Christi præ synagogis. B. Cluverus per lunam intelligit Auditores: Phrasin sub pedibus simpliciter locum designare absque ulla despicientiæ aut abjectionis notæ bene observatum est ab Alcafare, Psalm. XVIII. v. 10. Exod. XXXIV, 10. Num. XVI, 32. Sicut enim luna inferior est stellis: Ita auditores Doctoribus. Sic- ut autem clariorem de se fundit luna splendorem: Sic totus discentis Ecclesiæ cœtus clarius noctem hujus mundi illustrat, quam si Doctores solos con- sideres aut videas. Tum sicut luna cum stellis lu- men à Sole mutuatur; Sic Ecclesia tam in Docto- ribus quam Auditoribus doctrinæ vitæque lumen Christo debet. Denique sicut varium est luna, constantissimum Solis: Sic varium est discentis Ecclesiæ, immutabile autem Christi Domini lu- men. Per mulierem nonnulli Mariam intelli- gunt, & per puerum, quem conceperat, Filium DEI. Piscator & Tossanus tempus, quo Chri- stus nasci debuit, respici volunt. Sed recte ne- gat Methodius, citante Andrea Cæsariensi, ut & Victorinus, Primasius, aliiqve, B. Virginem hic præfigurari, cum nativitas Christi jam dum fa- cta fuerit; Johannes autem agat de rebus futu- ris. Neque dolores partus sensit Beata Maria, sensit autem Ecclesia fidei confessionem editura in persecutionibus, quas ejus causa sub Impe- ratoribus Ethnicis sustinuit. Incongrue ergo & citra fundamentum etiam Virgini Θεοτόκῳ Bernhardus hic XII. prærogativas præ aliis Sanctis assignavit.

## 12:2
And being with child, she cried out, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered.] She was bringing forth the Roman people to Christ. The same expression is in Galat. 4:19, 'my little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you.' But that could not be done without great labor and trouble. 'So great a task was it to found the Roman race?' To Christ, that is. In a similar way, the synagogue, or the university of the Jews, is called a mother, and individual Jews her children, Hos. 2:2, 3, Isa. 54:1, so Kimchi, who also adds chapter 16 of Ezekiel. Homer is praised because he expressed the pains of a woman in labor to the life. There are also words here very effective for that matter: 'she cried out' and 'pained.' You have similar descriptions of the same thing in John 16:21, Galat. 4:27. And for that reason, 'travail' and 'pains' are said of any pain, as in Matt. 24:8, Mark 13:8, Isa. 66:7, Jerem. 30:6, 7. Concerning the phrase 'being with child,' see Matt. 22.

Latin:

Καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἔκραζεν ὠδίνουσα καὶ βασανιζομένη τε- κεῖν.] Parturiebat populum Romanum Christo. Eadem lo- quutio Galat. IV, 19. τεκνία με ὧς πάλιν ὠδίνω, ἄχρις ὗ μο- φωθῇ χρισός ἐν ὑμῖν. Id vero sine magno labore ac molestia fieri non poterat. Tanta molis erat Romanam condere gentem? CHRISTO scilicet. Pari modo synagoga, sive univer- sitas Judæorum mater dicitur, singuli Judæi ejus filii, Os. II. vers. 2. 3, Esa. LIV. vers. 1. ita Kimchi, qui addit etiam cap. XVI. Ezechielis. Laudatur Homerus, quod parturien- tis dolores ad vivum expresserit. Sunt & hic verba ad eam rem valde efficacia ἔκραζεν & βασανιζομένη. Similes ejusdem rei ὑποτυπώσεις habes Joh. XVI. v. 21. Galat. IV. vers. 27. Et propterea ὠδῖνει & ὠδῖνες de quovis dolore di- cuntur, ut Matth. XXIV. v. 8. Marc. XIII. v. 8. Esa. LXVI. v. 7. Jerem. XXX. v. 6. 7. De locutione ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα, vi- de Matth. XXII.

## 12:3
Verse 3.

And there appeared another sign in heaven.] Another portent in the same air.

And behold a dragon.] Servius says that a dragon is properly so called in temples, and Lucan calls dragons deities. Others say that the dragon is nothing other than the old serpent: which sense seems to be taken here, because the same one who is called a dragon here and below in 12:4, 7, 9, 16, 17, 13:2, 4, 11, 13, 16:13, 20:20 is called a serpent in 12:4, 15, and indeed the 'ancient serpent' below here in 9 and 20:2, which in Hebrew is נחש הקדמוני. And the Rabbis interpret 'dragon' by 'serpent.' But by this name among the Hebrews, as also here, an evil spirit or demon is usually understood. Here, however, not just any demon, but the one who presided over the city of Rome. And he was called Mars by the Romans themselves, whence 'Martial Rome'.

Great.] Great and powerful. Rome is named from strength.

Πυῤῥός.] אדום a blood-red deity. See above chapter VI, 4. The Hebrews call the Roman Empire אדום.

Ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἐπτά.] Presiding over the seven-hilled city: Which surrounded seven citadels for itself with one wall.

Καὶ κέρατα δέκα. ] To which city ten kings easily serve, whom Tacitus calls instruments of servitude: Lucan calls the purple serving Latium. Strabo XVII, concerning Roman rule: Of this and the whole region, one part is ruled by kings, and the other part they hold themselves. That some codices here have ἑπτὰ instead of δέκα is an error arising from the numeral signs.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς ἀυτῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα.] Seven Caesars, of whom it will be treated in this Apocalypse. They begin with Claudius, because he first began to be troublesome to the Christians: and by his order John had been deported. Thus also Ezekiel always reckons times from his own deportation. I said that the diadems are the Caesars, because in such figures subjects and attributes, abstracts and concretes, are accustomed to be taken for the same thing.

That point about Claudius, by whose order John was deported, contradicts all historians, if you except the oversight of Epiphanius alone. But the diadems are not so much Caesars as they are forms of government used up to the Anti-Christ. There were, however, 1. Kings, 2. Consuls, 3. Decemvirs, 4. Military Tribunes, 5. Dictators, 6. Caesars, 7. Goths and Vandals, or rather Odoacer, who ruled Rome in a manner entirely different from the others, or even the Roman Pontiffs. Furthermore, that special application to the Dragon, such as it exhibits itself at Rome in its member and its principal organ, can well consist with the general explanation.

By the great and red dragon, the prince of demons, Lucifer, whose symbol he calls the red color, Viegas and Alcasar understand, on account of continuous slaughters, πυῤῥὸν, that is, fiery, such as were the serpents in the desert in Numbers XXI. For Tirinus, the seven symbolic heads of Lucifer are the capital vices: the pride of the Lion, The avarice of the tiger, the luxury of the bear, the gluttony of the wolf, the envy of the serpent, the wrath of the viper, the sloth of the ass: ten horns, the manifold weapons, force, and power of demons, Gregory, Morals, book 31, ch. 31; Cassian, Conferences 1, ch. 2. But what will be accomplished by that reasoning if the three horns are killed? Will the Anti-Christ kill the capital vices? Absurd. Others among the ancients wish for the seven heads to be designated as the seven evils in the heart of the enemy, and the seven powers against which the seven virtues of the Holy Spirit contend.

As regards the childbirth of the Church, B. Cluverus notes concerning it that we find a twofold one in the scriptures; one by which she herself bears children to Christ: another by which she bears Christ himself in her children. In the former childbirth, the Church, as the wife of the Lord and mother of all the pious, spiritually pregnant with the seed of the divine word, is said to beget children for Christ through her preaching and sacraments, Isa. 54:1. In the latter mystical childbirth, the Church begets Christ in the hearts of others, so that they may rightly acknowledge him by faith, cherish him with love, and express him in their life, Gal. 4; Matt. 12. In this respect, the Church is said to be pregnant with Christ, whom she thus wishes to bring to light, so that the Lord and Ruler of the world may be known as true and genuine in the hearts of all nations. In this labor of hers, she cries out with prayers to God, Isa. 26:16, to promote the birth, and also with exhortations to men, so that each may bring help according to his place and vocation.

Latin:

Verf. 3.

Καὶ ὤφθη ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ ἐρανῷ.) Aliud ostentum in eodem aëre.

Καὶ ἰδὲ δράκων. ] Draconem in templis proprie dici ait Servius, & Lucanus Dracones numina vocat. Alii Dra- conem nihil aliud esse ajunt, quam serpentem veterem: qui sensus hic sumendus videtur, quia idem qui hic & in- fra XII. v. 4. 7. 9. 16. 17. XIII. v. 2. 4. 11. 13. XVI. v. 13. XX. v. 20. Δράκων vocatur ὄφις XII. v. 4. 15. & quidem ὄφις ἀρ- χαῖος infra hic 9. & XX. vers. 2. quod Ebraice est נחש הקדמוני. Et Rabini דרקון interpretantur per נחש. In- telligi autem hoc nomine apud Ebræos solet, ut & hic Spiri- tus malus, sive Dæmon. Hic vero non quilibet Dæmon, sed is, qui Romanæ urbi præsidebat. Is autem Mars ab ipsis Ro- manis dicebatur, unde Roma Martia.

Μέγας.] Magnus & validus. Ῥώμη à robore di- cta.

Πυῤῥός.] אדום sanguinolentum numen. Vide su- pra cap. VI, 4. Ebræi imperium Romanum אדום vo- cant.

Ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἐπτά.] Præsidens urbi septicoli: Quæ septem una sibi muro circumdedit arces.

Καὶ κέρατα δέκα. ] Cui urbi Reges facile decem serviunt, quos instrumenta servitutis Tacitus vocat: servientem La- tio purpuram Lucanus. Strabo XVII. de Romana ditione: Ταύτης κρὶ τῆς συμπάσης χώρας ἡ μὲν βασιλεύεται, ἧς δ' ἔ- χεσιν αὐτοί. Quod hic quidam Codices pro δέκα habent ἑπτὰ error est ex notis numeralibus.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς ἀυτῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα.] Septem Cæsares, de quibus in hac Apocalypsi agetur. Ii incipiunt Claudio, quia is primus Christianis molestus esse cœpit: & ejus jussu Johannes fuerat deportatus. Sic & Ezechiel tempora semper putat à sua deportatione. Diademata dixi esse Cæsares, quia in talibus figuris solent pro eo- dem sumi subjecta & attributa, abstracta & concre- ta.

Illud de Claudio, cujus jussu fuerit Johan- nes deportatus, repugnat omnibus Historicis, si unius Epiphanii παρόραμα excipias. Diadema- ta vero non tam Cæsares, quam formæ regiminis sunt usque ad Anti-Christum usitatæ. Fuerunt autem 1. Reges, 2. Consules, 3. Decem-Vi- ri, 4. Tribuni militum, 5. Dictatores, 6. Cæ- sares, 7. Gothi & Vandali, vel potius Odoacer, qui Romam alio plane more, quam cæteri, re- xit, vel etiam Pontifices Romani. Cæterum ap- plicatio ista specialis ad Draconem, qualem se- se Romæ exhibet in membro, & organo suo præcipuo, cum generali explicatione probe con- sistere potest.

Per Draconem autem magnum & rusum princi- pem Dæmonum Luciferum, cujus symbolum colorem rusum dicit, Viegas, & Alcasar propter continuas cædes πυῤῥὸν, id est, ignitum, quales erant serpentes in deserto Numeror. XXI. intelli- gunt. Tirino septem Luciferi capita symbo- lica sunt vitia capitalia, Leonis superbia, Tigridis avaritia, ursi luxuria, lupi gula, serpentis invidia, viperæ ira, asini desidia: decem cornua multiplicia dæmonum arma, vis, & potentia Gre- gorio l. XXXI. Moral. c. 31. Cassiano collat. I. c. 2. Sed quid ea ratione fiet tribus cornibus occisis? Num Anti-Christus occidet vitia capitalia? Ἄτοπον. Alii veterum septem capita de septem malitiis in corde inimici, & septem potestatibus, quibus septem Spi- ritus Sancti virtutibus adversatur, designari vo- lunt.

Partum Ecclesiæ quod attinet, de eo notat B. Cluverus, quod duplicem in scripturis reperia- mus; unum quo ipsa Christo filios parit: alterum quo ipsum Christum in filiis parit. Priore partu Ec- clesia velut uxor Domini & mater omnium piorum semine verbi divini spiritualiter gravida per ejus prædicationem & sacramenta filios Christo gignere dicitur, Esa. LIV, 1. Posteriore partu mystico gignit Ecclesia Christum in cordibus aliorum, ut recte ipsum fide agnoscant, dilectione foveant, vitaque ex- primant, Gal. IV. Matth. XII. Hoc respectu gravida dicitur Christo Ecclesia, quem sic vult edere in lucem, ut in cordibus omnium gentium Dominus ac Rector terrarum orbis verus & genuinus cognoscatur. Hæc in labore suo clamat cum precibus ad Deum, Esa. XXVI, 16. ut partum promoveat, tum hortatibus ad homines, ut quilibet pro suo loco & vocatione au- xilium afferat.

## 12:4
Verse 4. And his tail draws the third part of the stars of heaven. The power of serpents is usually in the head, as we said in Gen. 3:15. Therefore, because this serpent is said to do harm with its tail, it is to be understood as acting in deed, as above in 9:5. The Dragon had drawn to himself a third part, not only of the common people but also of the Doctors, through his instrument Simon Magus, as we said in 2 Thess. 2:11-12, partly by magical prodigies, partly by a doctrine flattering to many, that the worship of gods is not an illicit matter, and that the mind is not defiled by the works of the flesh. See Irenaeus and others. Therefore, by Cyril, Simon is called from the name of his master the first dragon of wickedness. And note how much Christians excel the Jews: of the Christians, a third part perishes; of the Jews, a third part is saved, Zech. 13:8.

What would Simon have to do here, where visions are not instituted concerning past things, but future ones? And how could the clergy of Rome at that time have been seduced by Simon in such great numbers, when there was no clergy there; nor is it read anywhere that the Roman clergy was seduced by Simon or his disciples. And although some understand a violent dragging—because, as Pliny testifies, the tail of the Dragon is of such strength that it suffocates elephants—we nevertheless admit the meaning, which is that of most, concerning the fraudulent dragging peculiar to the Anti-Christ. See Origen, tract 30 on Matthew. But such things must be introduced so that the revelation concerning the Roman Anti-Christ and the Doctors in his kingdom may be obscured. The Anti-Christ is not understood quite conveniently by the tail of the Dragon by Gregory, Morals, book 31, ch. 14, Ribera, and Cornelius à Lapide, who, in the judgment of Tirinus, would more correctly be called the head of the Dragon. But the third part of the stars is rightly explained by Jerome, Theodoret, and others as the Doctors. What the Scholastics dispute here, whether a third part of the angels fell, arises from a false interpretation of the third part of the stars, by which not angels but Doctors of the Church are understood. See Cornelius.

And he cast them to the earth. He caused them, being cast down, to care for earthly things instead of heavenly ones.

Most bishops of the Papacy treat of nothing less than heavenly things: they treat of nothing more than earthly things, devoted to the belly, to lust, to Mars, and to other secular matters, as history and experience testify.

And the Dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she had given birth, he might devour her child. Simon Magus having been brought to Rome, he acted to destroy the Roman people, who were already beginning to be born to Christ, with an evil dogma. Thus we had 'to devour' above in 11:5, and we shall have it below in 20:9, except that in those places it concerns the destruction of the body, whereas here it concerns the destruction of the soul. This is a mystical explanation of the histories concerning Pharaoh, Exod. 1:16, and concerning Herod the Great, Matt. 2:16. And note that the comparison proceeds well. For Pliny, 8:14, teaches that there are also serpents by which infants are devoured.

Latin:

Vers. 4. Καὶ ἡ οὐρὰ ἀυτῶ σύρει τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ ὀυρα- νῶ.] Vis serpentum in capite esse solet, ut diximus Gen. III, 15. Quod ergo serpens hic cauda nocere dicitur, eo intelli- gendus est actu agere, ut supra IX, 5. Tertiam partem non de plebe tantum, sed & Doctoribus ad se traxerat Draco per instrumentum suum Simonem Magum, ut diximus 2.Thess. II; 11. 12. partim scilicet magicis prodigiis, partim doctrina multis abblandiente, cultum Deorum rem esse non illicitam, & operibus carnis animum non pollui. Vide Irenæum & alios. Ideo Cyrillo Simon ex Magistri sui nomine dicitur ὁ πρῶτος τῆς κακίας δράκων. Et nota, quanto Judæis præstent Christiani: De Christianis perit pars tertia: De Judæis pars tertia servatur Zachar. XIII, 8.

Quid huc faceret Simon, ubi non de præteri- tis instituuntur visiones, sed de futuris. Et quomodo tum temporis clerus Romæ à Simone tanto numero seduci potuisset, quum nullus ibi clerus fuerit; nec uspiam clerus Romanus à Si- mone aut discipulis ejusdem seductus legatur. Etsi autem nonnulli violentam tractionem, quia, Plinio teste, caudæ Draconis tanti roboris est, ut Elephantes suffocat, intelligant, admittimus ta- men sensum, qui plerorumque est de tractione fraudulenta Anti-Christo propria. Vid. Origen. tr. 30. in Matth. Sed ingerenda talia sunt, ut ob- fuscetur ἀποκάλυψις de Anti-Christo Romano, & Doctoribus in regno ejus. Per caudam Draco- nis non satis commode Anti-Christus intelligitur à Gregorio l. XXXI. moral. c. 14. Ribera, Cornelio à Lapide, qui rectius caput Draconis, Tirini qui- dem judicio diceretur. Tertia autem pars stella- rum de Doctoribus recte ab Hieronymo, Theodo- reto & aliis explicatur. Quæ Scholastici hic disputant, an tertia pars Angelorum ceciderit, è falsa interpretatione tertiæ partis stellarum, per quas non Angeli sed Doctores Ecclesiæ intelligun- tur, oriuntur. Vid. Cornelius.

Καὶ ἔβαλεν ἀυτὸς εἰς τὴν γῆν.] Fecit, ut illi dejecti pro cœ- lestibus terrestria curarent.

Nihil minus quam cœlestia tractant plerique Episcopi Papatus: nihil magis quam terrestria ven- tri, veneri, marti & aliis rebus secularibus dediti, teste Historia, & experientia.

Καὶ ὁ Δράκων ἔστηκεν ἐνώπιον τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς μελλούσης τίκτειν, ἵνα ὅταν τέκῃ τὸ τέκνον ἀυτῆς καταφάγῃ.] Simo- ne Mago Romam perducto, id egit, ut populum Roma- num jam Christo nasci incipientem malo dogmate perde- ret. Sic κατεσθίειν habuimus supra XI, 5. & habebimus infra XX, 9. nisi quod istis locis de pernicie corporis, hic de animi pernicie agitur. Est hic explicatio mystica histo- riarum de Pharaone, Exod. I. vers. 16. & de Herode Magno Matth. II. vers. 16. Et nota bene procedere comparationem. Nam & serpentes esse, à quibus infantes devorentur, docet Plinius IIX, 14.

## 12:5
Verse 5.

And she brought forth a male child. Those dispersed from Judea, among whom were Aquila, Acts 18:2, and Apollos, instruments of the Catholic Church, begat many of the Roman people for Christ. These are called here the male offspring because of the constancy which appeared great in the Roman Church of those times. Thus Philo said of Cain that he brought forth a virtuous offspring to God. In that 'male' there is an allusion to the passage in Isa. 66:17.

Who is to rule all nations with a rod of iron. The iron rod is the sword. The sword is the Word of God, as we said above in 2:27. To feed is to rule. The Roman Church has this above other Churches, that no other subdued more peoples by the Word of God, so that its victories through the weapons of Christ were greater than those of ancient Rome through the weapons of Mars. Furthermore, the governance of other Churches after the death of the Apostles pertained to that Church.

And her child was caught up to God, and to his throne.] Simon seduced so many in Rome that the Christian people no longer appeared there. Those things which do not appear to men are said to be with God. See John 1, verse 1. But when 'and his throne' is added, it is understood that God reigned in the souls of those who, although they were hidden for a time. There is an allusion to the history of Joash snatched from Athaliah, 2 Kings 11:2.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

Καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱὸν ἄῤῥενα.] Dispersi ex Judæa, in quibus Aqui- la, Act. XIIX. v. 2. & Apollos, instrumenta Ecclesiæ Ca- tholicæ, multos de populo Romano Christo genuere. Hi dicuntur hic partus masculinus ob constantiam, quæ magna apparuit in Ecclesia Romana illorum temporum. Sic virtu- tem partum Deo edere dixit Philo de Caino. In illo ἄῤῥενα allusio est ad locum Esa. LXVI, 17.

Ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ.] Vir- ga ferrea, gladius. Gladius Verbum DEI, ut diximus su- pra II, 27. Pascere est regere. Ecclesia Romana hoc habet supra alias Ecclesias, quod nulla plures populos subegit Verbo DEI, ita, ut minores fuerint ejus victoriæ per Chri- sti arma, quam veteris Romæ per arma Martis. Deinde & aliarum Ecclesiarum regimen post Apostolorum mortem ad illam Ecclesiam pertinuit.

Καὶ ἡρπάγη τὸ τέκνον ἀυτῆς πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον ἀυτῦ.] Tam multos Romæ Simon seduxit, ut Christiana plebs ibi non amplius appareret. Quæ ho- minibus non apparent, ea apud Deum esse dicuntur. Vide Johan. I. vers. 1. Cum autem additur & solium ejus, intelligitur Deus in illorum quanquam ad tempus latentium animis regnasse. Alluditur ad historiam de Joaso erepto A- thaliæ, 2. Reg. XI, 2.

## 12:6
Vers. 6.

And the woman fled into the wilderness.] Compare this statement. For if smaller towns and provinces are compared with Rome, they are as it were a desert. In the same way, the word 'desert' is used in Isaiah 35:1, 41:19. The Christian Church betook itself to those places. There is an allusion, moreover, to the ancient history of the Israelite people, who betook themselves from Egypt into the desert, and to the history of David, who after his wings mentions the desert, Psalm 55:7, 8.

Where she has there a place prepared by God.] 'Where there' is a Hebrew idiom, for which 'where' would suffice for the Greeks. GOD had prepared for them less frequented places, where they might live safely.

That they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and sixty days.] Another Hebraism of the active plural with the person not expressed for the passive singular. The sense is: That that woman, that is, the Catholic Church, might be nourished there. See below 14, where a second flight is signified. Reference is made to the history of Elijah, 1 Kings 17:4. The time here is again three years and a half.

But how could they then rule all nations converted to the faith of Christ, if indeed in the second year of Claudius very few and of very little authority had been converted, as Church History testifies? Moreover, the rule of the Roman Church over all others was so far from being established then, that many, as was observed before, in the midst of the Papacy have held its affectation to be a mark of the Anti-Christ. Nor at that time was the Roman Church conspicuous as a woman clothed with the Sun, and crowned with twelve stars, which then had scarcely begun to wail in its cradle, which neither Peter nor Paul had even seen at that time. Nor is a flight of the Jews on account of Simon read of, who rather favored the Jews to the prejudice of the Christians; not to mention that their expulsion from Rome, as Baronius himself demonstrates, did not happen before the ninth year of Claudius. But that painful birth of the woman is most rightly understood by many concerning the profession of the Nicene faith, and the sons born to God from the Church amidst the persecutions of the Gentiles, professing that faith. Which birth was brought to light in the days of Constantine the Great, after she had been pregnant

The Church for 270 Angelic days or as many years, namely from the age of the Apostles, because the Church did not remain a Virgin for long, as Eusebius testifies, up to the Council of Nicaea. The male child is not the Christian people, but rather Christ in the souls of Christians. Thus B. Cluverus explains it concerning Christ, so that the emphasis of the words from Psalm 2 and their immediate sense may be retained: The Church labors in this, that she might form Him in the souls of Caesars and Magistrates, and having formed Him, bring Him forth, and through them rule over the nations of the whole world. And the birth finally succeeded happily, and she brought forth a male child, powerful and robust, who would be the ruler of all nations both here and forever, and would break all those resisting him with a rod of iron like earthen vessels. But whence such audacity in the Devil, you say, that he dares to hope to devour Christ himself? What, I say, when he has dared to tempt, dared to crucify? But you insist: Having made him immortal, who dared to attack him again? I answer, in his honor and name. For if he is said to ἀνασταυροῦν and παραδειγματίζειν Christ, who knowingly and willingly opposes his glory, Heb. 6:6, to whom will that be assigned more rightly than to Satan, by whose instinct men blaspheme him? And if Nebuchadnezzar as a Dragon κατέπιε Jerusalem, when he conquered it, Jer. 51:34, surely the Devil, desiring to conquer the honor of Christ, is rightly asserted to wish to devour him. However, the formation in the soul through faith was followed by the bringing forth into the light, such as when the fetus is brought forth into the light through the profession of the Nicene faith. Caught up to the throne can be understood either of the declaration of that axiom then made publicly, or of the security and Divine protection which happened to the professors of the faith; because by the singular power of the right hand of God they were withdrawn from the venomous maw of the Dragon and his calumnious teeth. By the wilderness, however, is not understood a place entirely desolate, but land comparatively desert or more uncultivated, as Arabia was, Isa. 42:11, such as the Christian assembly is, if you institute a σύγκρισιν with the multitude of the Anti-Christian assembly, especially because it is intermixed with nations either ignorant of or despising the true worship of God, Ps. 120:5, Apoc. 11:2.

We dismiss Tirinus, who thinks there is an allusion to the first battle of Lucifer which he calls the one with Michael: But he wrongly draws Gen. 1:1 into it and makes the revelation of the hypostatic union the cause of the battle. Most others, however, do not wrongly restrict this to the first three hundred years with Origen, Ambrose, Augustine, Hilary, Basil, Victorinus, Ticonius, and Tirinus. For although this battle is perpetual, those times are nevertheless looked to primarily, indeed uniquely, during which the bloody persecution of the Dragon lasted. For the subsequent times will be dealt with later. Furthermore, Satan is compared to a Dragon because of cruelty, Jer. 51:34, 1 Pet. 5; cunning, which the name נחש indicates; appearance, Gen. 3, Apoc. 12:8; horrible magnitude, Ezech. 29:3, Luke 11:23, and h.l.; and venomous devastation, Deut. 32:33, Num. 21:9, John 3:34; but he is called red because of slaughter, Apoc. 6:4.

PART II. THE BATTLE OF MICHAEL WITH THE DRAGON, AND HIS EJECTION.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

Καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.] Dictum hoc compara- te. Nam si cum Roma comparentur oppida minora & provinciæ, sunt quasi desertum. Pari modo deserti vox ponitur apud Esaiam XXXV, 1. c. XLI, 19. In ea loca se recepit Ecclesia Christiana. Alluditur autem ad veterem historiam populi Israelitici, qui ex Ægypto in desertum se re- cepit, & ad historiam Davidis, qui post alas meminit deserti Psalm. LV, 7. 8.

Ὅπου ἔχει ἐκεῖ τόπον ἡτοιμασμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεῦ.] Ὅπου ἐκεῖ Ebræa loquutio, pro qua Græcis sufficeret ὅπου. DEUS paraverat illis loca minus frequentia, ubi tuto vi- verent.

Ἵνα ἐκεῖ ἐκτρέφωσιν ἀυτὴν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξή- κοντα.] Alius Ebraismus activi pluralis persona non ex- pressa pro singulari passivo. Sensus est: Ut ibi aleretur illa mulier, id est, Catholica Ecclesia. Vide infra 14. ubi altera fuga significatur. Respicitur Historia Eliæ 1. Reg. XVII, 4. Tempus hic rursum annorum trium & dimidii.

At quomodo omnes gentes tum regere po- terant ad fidem Christi conversi, siquidem Clau- dii secundo pauci admodum & perexiguæ autori- tatis conversi fuerint, teste Historia Ecclesiasti- ca. Regimen autem Romanæ Ecclesiæ super omnes alias adeo tum non fundatum fuit, ut plu- rimi, quod ante observatum, in medio Papa- tu ejus affectationem pro Anti-Christi characte- re habuerint. Neque isto tempore Romana Ec- clesia ut mulier Sole vestita, & duodecim stellis coronata conspicua fuit, quæ tum vix cœperat in cunis vagire, quam neque Petrus, neque Paulus isto quidem tempore viderat. Neque fuga Ju- dæorum ob Simonem facta legitur, qui Judæis potius in Christianorum præjudicium favebat; ut taceam, quod eorum à Roma ejectio, Ba- ronio ipso demonstrante, non contigerit ante no- num Claudii. Partus autem ille mulieris doloro- sus de professione fidei Nicenæ, & filiis Deo interme- dias Ethnicorum persecutiones ab Ecclesia genitis fidem illam profitentibus rectissime à plerisque intelligitur. Qui partus luci expositus est Con- stantini M. diebus, postquam gravida fuit

Ecclesia per 270. dies Angelicos vel totidem annos, inde scilicet ab Apostolorum aetate, quia non diu Virgo mansit Ecclesia, teste Eusebio, usque ad Con- cilium Nicenum. Filius masculus non est popu- lus Christianus, sed Christus potius in animis Chri- stianorum. Sic de Christo, ut emphasis verborum e Psal. 2. sensusque immediatus retineatur, expli- cat B. Cluverus: In eo laborat Ecclesia, ut ipsum in animis Caesarum & Magistratuum formaret, forma- tumq; ederet, ac per eos totius mundi gentibus impe- raret. Et cessit tandem feliciter partus, peperitq; fi- lium masculum potentem & robustum, qui & hic & in aeternum omnium esset gentium rector, omnesq; sibi reluctantes baculo ferreo tanquam vasa testacea con- fringeret. At unde tanta Diabolo audacia, ais, ut Christum ipsum devorandum ausit sperare? Quid inquam, cum sit ausus tentare, ausus crucifigere? Sed instas: Immortalem factum, qui denuo ausus im- petere? Respondeo in honore & nomine ejus. Nam si Christum dicitur ἀνασταυροῦν & παραδειγματί- ζειν, qui sciens volens gloriae ejus adversatur Ebr. 6, 6. Cui id rectius, quam Satanae, cujus instinctu homines illum blasphemant, assignabitur? Ac si Nabuchodo- nosor tanquam Draco κατέπιε Hierosolymam, quan- do eam expugnavit, Jerem. 51, 34. sane Diabolus ex- pugnare honorem Christi cupiens ipsum devorare velle recte asseritur. Formationem tamen in animo per fidem sequuta est in lucem expositio, qualis est, quum foetus in lucem expositus per Nicenae fidei professionem. Raptus in thronum vel de declaratio- ne axiomatos istius tum publice facta, vel de se- curitate intelligi potest & protectione Divina, quae professoribus fidei contigit; quia singulari dextrae Dei virtute venenato Draconis rictui & calumnio- sis ejus dentibus subtracti sunt. Per solitudinem autem non locus plane desolatus, sed terra compa- rate deserta vel incultior intelligitur, ut Arabia erat, Esa. 42, 11. qualis est coetus Christianus, si σύγκρισιν instituas, cum multitudine coetus Anti- Christiani, imprimis quia ille gentibus verum Dei cultum vel ignorantibus vel contemnentibus im- mixtus est, Psal. 120, 5. Apoc. 11, 2.

Tirinum alludi censentem ad primum quod vocat cum Michaele Luciferi praelium mittimus: Perperam autem eo trahit Gen. 1, 1. & unionis hypo- staticae revelationem causam praelii constituit. Ad primos autem trecentos annos haec non male re- stringunt cum Origene, Ambrosio, Augustino, Hila- rio, Basilio, Victorino, Ticonio, Tirino, plerique alii. Etsi enim haec pugna sit perpetua; respiciuntur tamen illa imprimis tempora, imo unice, quibus duravit cruenta Draconis persecutio. Nam de subsequentibus temporibus deinde agetur. Cae- terum Draconi comparatur Satanas ob crudelita- tem Jerem. 51, 34. 1. Petr. 5. calliditatem, quam no- men נחש indicat, apparitionem, Gen. 3. Apoc. 12, 8. magnitudinem horribilem Ezech. 29, 3. Luc. 11, 23. & h. l. venenatam vastitatem, Deut. 32, 33. Num. 21, 9. Johan. 3, 34. ruffus autem dicitur ob caedem, Apoc. 6, 4.

PARS II. MICHAELIS CUM DRACONE PU- GNA, HUJUSQUE EJECTIO.

## 12:7
Vers. 7.

And there was war in heaven) In the air. Why it is said so, see above v. 1. Πόλεμος often signifies battle in our writers. מלחמה.

Michael and his angels) An expression clearly similar to that: And there was a great contest of Corydon with Thyrsis.
