For he calls them warriors, as Papinius, the huge war of one womb, using the abstract for the concrete. Michael was once the president of the Jewish people, but now of the Christian under King Christ. He, with the angels of his cohort, was a helper to Peter at Rome.

To fight with the dragon) This was being done, that they might oppose themselves to the Dragon acting through Simon. And here πολεμῆσαι is לָהֶם to fight. And this, like other things, is taken from the traditions of the Jews. For the battle of the Dragon with the good angels is mentioned in the Gemara. John indeed shows that something of truth lies hidden in those traditions, which the Rabbis did not see. So also concerning the thousand years, concerning Gog and Magog.

And the dragon fought and his angels) Simon and the Simonians produced many prodigies, so that Simon obtained Divine honors from the Romans, as Justin, Irenaeus, and others testify.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Καὶ ἐγένετο πόλεμος ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ) In aëre. Cur id ita di- catur, vide supra v. 1. Πόλεμος saepe nostris Scriptoribus pugnam significat. מלחמה.

Ὁ Μιχαὴλ καὶ Ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ) Locutio plane similis illi: Et certamen erat Corydon cum Thyrside magnum.

Bellatores enim vocat, ut Papinius, unius ingens bellum uteri, abstractum usurpans pro concreto. Michaël olim præses Judaici populi, nunc vero Christiani sub Rege Chri- sto. Is cum Angelis suæ cohortis Petro adjutor fuit Romæ.

Τῷ πολεμῆσαι μετὰ τῦ δράκοντος) Id agebatur, ut illi se opponerent Dragoni agenti per Simonem. Et hic πο- λεμῆσαι est לָהֶם pugnare. Et hoc, ut alia desumptum ex Judæorum traditionibus. Nam Draconis pugna cum bonis Angelis memoratur in Gemara. Ostendit vero Jo- hannes in illis traditionibus latere aliquid veri, quod Rab- bini non videbant. Sic & de mille annis, de Gog & Magog.

Καὶ ὁ δράκων ἐπολέμησε καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι ἀυτῦ) Simon & Simoniani multa edidere ostenta, ita ut Simon a Romanis Divinos honores consequeretur, teste Justino, Irenæo & aliis.

## 12:8
Vers. 8.

Καὶ ἐκ ἴσχυσe) Simon could do nothing against the most efficacious prayers of Peter. Witnesses are Clement, Arnobius, Eusebius, Philastrius, Augustine, Palladius, and others. ἰσχύειν here means to prevail. מִכֹּל Job 36:9, Joel 3:10. There is, moreover, a litotes in 'not to prevail' for 'they were conquered.' Similar modes of speaking are found in Prov. 10:2, ch. 12:3, ch. 17:23.

He returns to his trifles about Simon, but they are more ludicrous, and in the judgment of most learned men more fabulous, than to deserve to be brought forward for such visions. That Michael, however, is not some created Angel—which Grotius maintains along with the Papist angel-worshippers, Bellarmine, Veiga, Ribera, Colladone, Cornelius a Lapide, Philipp Melanchthon, likewise Jacob Martini, Cluver, and Dürfeld—but the Son of God, who is also called so in Daniel ch. 11:3, ch. 12:1, is clear even from the fact that it would have been inappropriate for the chief of the angelic army to be passed over in silence, when the leader of the satanic army had been so prolixly described; and since he is celebrated in the song of victory, why should he not also be designated in the battle? Historians dispute whether Peter ever saw Rome, and the case is still sub judice. At that time, certainly, he had not yet come to Rome, namely in the second year of Claudius. What witness for this matter will either Grotius or Hammond bring forward? Nor did he have need of an Angel as a helper, who always had Christ as a helper in his office, Matt. 28, last verse. The flight of Simon has long since been exposed as fictitious, along with the casting down of Peter, and if it were true, it would have happened before John was relegated to Patmos. Therefore, it could not be shown as a future event by this vision, which occurred long after the death of Peter and Simon Magus. Nor does the time of the exile fit. For after the death of Simon in the 12th year of Nero, the civil wars of Otho, Galba, and Vitellius occurred, but peace flourished among the Christians, as Grotius does not deny; therefore, the Church was not put to flight at that time. But the persecution which occurred in the 10th year of Nero did not last for 3½ years, but for only one year. But it is so far from the case that after the destruction of Simon his accomplices and followers were cast out of heaven, or that peace was restored to the Church, that the Gnostics arising from his school vexed the Church far more: and the Apostles Peter and Paul were killed by Nero in revenge for Simon, and the Church was dissipated by a huge persecution. That peace was restored to the Church of Christ from the persecutions of the heathens in the time of Constantine the Great is known to everyone: to which the Tablet of Constantine in Eusebius, book III of the life of the same, contributes. Compare Theodoret, book I, ch. 15. Cocceius understands the battle as occurring after the ascension of Christ, Mede as the primitive Church against the Romans before Constantine the Great, B. Cluver, Grave, Kromajer, and Pareus as under Constantine the Great, and Woltzærus, Hoë, and Danhauer as the battle with the Anti-Christ.

Οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη ἀυτῷ ἔτι ἐν τῷ ὀρανῷ) When Simon was flying in the air, he was cast down through the prayers of Peter. This expression is found in Psalm 37:10, Dan. 2:31.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

Καὶ ἐκ ἴσχυσe) Nihil potuit Simon contra efficacissimas Petri preces. Testes Clemens, Arnobius, Eusebius, Phi- lastrius, Augustinus, Palladius & alii. ἰσχύειν hic est præ- valere. מִכֹּל Job. 36, 9. Joel 3, 10. Est præterea λιτότης non prævalere pro victi sunt. Similia loquendi genera Prov. 10, 2. c. 12, 3. c. 17, 23.

Redit ad nugas suas de Simone, sed magis ludi- cra illa, & plurimorum eruditorum judicio fabulo- sa, quam ut ad tantas visiones afferri mereantur. Michaëlem autem non esse Angelum aliquem crea- tum, quod cum Papistis Angelolatris, Bellarmino, Veiga, Ribera, Colladone, Cornelio a Lapide, Philipp. Melanchthone, item, Jacobo Martini, Cluvero, & Dürfeld vult Grotius, sed Filium Dei, qui sic etiam Danieli c. 11, 3. c. 12, 1. dictus, vel ex eo liquet, quod inconveniens fuerit, subticeri præcipuum exerci- tus Angelici Ducem, ubi tam prolixe descriptus erat Dux exercitus Satanici; & quum in Epinicio is celebretur, quidni in pugna etiam designaretur? Petrum autem unquam Romam vidisse historici certant, & adhuc sub judice lis est. Tum certe Ro- mam nondum venerat, anno nempe Claudii secun- do. Quem ejus rei testem adducet sive Grotius, si- ve Hamondus? Nec adjutore Angelo opus habe- bat, qui Christum adjutorem semper in munere suo habebat, Matth. 28. v. ult. Volatus Simonis jam pridem detectus est fictitius cum Petrina dejectio- ne, & contigisset, si verus esset, antequam in Path- mum relegaretur Johannes. Non ergo hac visio- ne, quæ diu post Petri & Simonis Magi mortem accidit, ut futurus ostendi poterat. Neque con- gruit tempus exilii. Nam post Simonis mortem Neronis XII. anno bella contigerunt civilia Otto- nis, Galbæ, & Vitellii, pax autem florebat penes Christianos, non diffitente Grotio; fugata ergo tum non fuit Ecclesia. Quæ autem X. Neronis ac- cidit persequutio, non per 3½. annos, sed unum tan- tum annum duravit. Tantum autem abest, ut post Simonis interitum e cœlo sint ejecti ejus compli- ces, & sectatores, aut pax reddita Ecclesiæ fuerit; ut longe plus vexarint Ecclesiam Gnostici e schola ejus oriundi: Et Apostoli Petrus, & Paulus in vin- dictam Simonis a Nerone occisi sint, & Ecclesia ingenti persecutione dissipata. Ecclesiæ vero Chri- sti a persecutionibus Ethnicorum tempore Con- stantini M. pacem redditam esse nemini non no- tum est: Quo facit Tabula Constantini apud Eu- seb. l. III. de vita ejusdem. Conf. Theodor. l. 1. c. 15. Pugnam post ascensionem Christi Coccejus, primitivæ Ecclesiæ contra Romanos ante Constantinum M. Medus sub Constantino M. B. Cluverus, Grave, Kromajer, Pareus, pugnam cum Anti-Christo Wol- tzærus, Hoë, Danhauer intelligunt.

Οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη ἀυτῷ ἔτι ἐν τῷ ὀρανῷ) Cum in aëre volaret Simon, per Petri preces dejectus fuit. Locutio hæc reperitur Psal. 37, 10. Dan. 2, 31.

## 12:9
Verse 9.

And the great dragon was cast out) Acting in Simon. The old serpent) That veteran. See above v. 3. the serpent that acted wickedly from the beginning. Justin against Trypho.

He who is called the Devil and Satan) He places two names, Greek and Hebrew, writing for the use of Hebrews and Gentiles. Such are yea and Amen. Abba Father, Abaddon and Apollyon, Devil from slandering, Satan from opposing. No adversary is harsher than one who slanders. Wherefore also the word שטן is accustomed to be translated by ἐνδιαβάλλειν (to slander) Num. 22, 22. Ps. 38, 21. Ps. 71, 13. Ps. 109, 4. 20. 29. And the Greek interpreters retain the Hebrew name שטן elsewhere, elsewhere they translate it by Devil, as 1 Chron. 21, 1. Zech. 3, 1. 2. and in many places in Job. You see here the names of the sign and the thing signified mixed together, as Gen. 3, 14. 15. Wisd. 2, 24. Rom. 16, 20.

He who deceives the whole world) By the worship of idols, which other vices are accustomed to accompany, Rom. 1, 21. 22. 23. 24. 25. 26. etc.

Was cast out) a reference, for the word which had preceded is repeated: this is frequent where a parenthesis has intervened, such as the long description of the Dragon here. For that which had preceded is recalled to the reader's memory.

Unto the earth) as those are accustomed to be who are thrown down in a struggle. An allegorical locution and a literal meaning coincide here in the same words: which often happens in prophecies concerning Christ.

And his angels with him were cast out) Namely, among the Simonians, who, having been defeated, did not dare to lift their heads.

Concerning the inept distortion of this locution by Joseph Antonius Gonzag, see Christianus Schottanus in Tohu, page 155. The place of the Dragon was no longer found regarding that public and universal idolatry, which was ceasing as the shrines of the demons were either closed or destroyed, nor regarding the persecution in the city of the Romans, the chief seat of the Church: in which way Satan is also said to be bound for a thousand years, Rev. 20, until he was loosed when the Turkish power emerged, with the Tartars in addition, and beastly Pseudo-Catholics cruelly attacking the Church everywhere. But he was cast into the earth, hell, and the more abject places of the earth, to which that passage in Gen. 3, 15 seems to be referred: upon thy belly shalt thou go. By that ejection of the Devil, Coccejus understands the deletion of the Jewish Republic, Alcafar the conversion of the Gentiles through the Apostles, Wolterus, Hoë, Danhauer, Döling, and Richterus the reformation of B. Luther. Osiander, Cluverus, Gravius, Dürfeld, Kromayer, Medus, etc., determine this to be the ejection under Constantine the Great. Thus also B. Gerhard, although he understands the efficacy of the glorious and victorious resurrection and ascension of Christ, and wishes to imply the victory obtained through death and resurrection against the Devil (which we do not deny on the basis of the foundation), nevertheless acknowledges that these concern the times of Constantine, and wishes to refer especially to our own times the Anti-Christ cast out through the preaching of the Gospel (which we judge to be less consistent with the Apocalyptic series); therefore Lyranus understands Michael as the Emperor Heraclius, who waged war against Chosroes for the Christians, while most others understand him as Constantine, who carried off the victory over Maxentius, Maximinus, and Licinius; whom, however, B. Gerhard rightly explains as Christ, along with Ambrose, Ansbert, and the Reformed: Bullinger, Szegedinus, Aretius, Piscator, Riccardus, Junius, Forbesius, Crugotius, and Cotterius. Nor does Lud. deny this. Alcafar, although with Grotius he falsely thinks, and contrary to the series of the Apocalypse, that Nero, Simon Magus, and others, through whom the infernal Dragon wished to attack the Church, are designated by the Dragon and his angels. That Drusius (ad Jos. p. 4) urges the word νικητὰς (victors) from v. 12 so that Michael may not be understood as Christ, is futile, because according to the heavenly voice, those angels fighting and conquering with Michael also pertain to the brothers of the blessed Christians militant on earth, 2 Cor. 10, 5, who conquer through the blood of the Lamb. For these bring about the application. Concerning the fulfillment, Sozomenus, book 1, ch. 8: 'But Constantine, when he had now gained possession of the whole empire alone, commanded his subjects living toward the east by public edict that they should worship the Christian religion, and studiously venerate the Divine power, and consider that alone to be the Divine power: which in truth it is, and which at all times has sufficient strength and power in itself.' For those who devoted their effort to worshipping Him diligently, all good things were accustomed to abound for them, and whatever they undertook with good hope, succeeded according to their desire; but those who failed in worshipping God the best and greatest, all things public and private in war and peace turned out unhappily. Furthermore, he affirmed that he was speaking not that he might boast insolently, but that he might give thanks to God, because God, judging him to be a suitable administrator of His will, had led him from the British sea even to the regions situated in the East, so that the Christian religion might then be increased. And further: For almost all Christians began to hold the magistracies of the Roman empire and forbade everyone from henceforth undertaking either to sacrifice to idols, or to use divinations or wicked mysteries, or to erect statues, or to celebrate pagan festivals. Many other ancient institutions of the cities were besides changed. Finally, among the Egyptians, that cubit by which the inundation of the Nile is accustomed to be noted was no longer, as was the custom, brought to the temples of the pagans, but from that time to the churches of the Christians.

.Vers. 10.. Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ ὀυρανῷ) The acclamation of the heavenly Angels, such as above c. 5, 11. c. 11. v. 15.

Latin:

Verf. 9.

Καὶ ἐβλήθη Δράκων ὁ μέγας) Agens in Simone. Ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος) Veteranvs ille. Vide fupra v. 3. ὁ πονη- ρευσάμενος τὴν ἀρχὴν ὄφις. Justinus contra Triphonem.

Ὁ καλέμενος Διάβολος καὶ Σατανᾶς) Duo nomina ponit Græcum & Ebræum scribens in usum Ebræorum & gen- tium. Talia ναὶ καὶ Ἀμὴν. Ἀββᾶ ὁ πατὴρ, Ἀβαδδὼν καὶ ὁ Ἀ- πολύων, Διάβολος a calumniando, Σατανᾶς ab adversando. Nemo durior adversarius, quam qui calumniatur. Quare & verbum שטן solet per ἐνδιαβάλλειν verti Num. 22, 22. Psal. 38, 21. Ps. 71, 13. Ps. 109, 4. 20. 29. Et nomen Ebræum שטן ali- bi retinent Græci Interpretes, alibi vertunt per Διάβολος, ut 1. Paral. 21, 1. Zach. 3, 1. 2. & in Jobo multis locis. Vides hic misceri inter se nomina signi & rei significatæ, ut Gen. 3, 14. 15. Sap. 2, 24. Rom. 16, 20.

Ὁ πλανῶν τὴν ὀικυμένην ὅλην) Idolorum cultu, quem alia vitia comitari solent, Rom. 1, 21. 22. 23. 24. 25. 26. &c.

Ἐβλήθη) ἀναφορὰ, repetitur enim vox, quæ præcesserat: id frequens est, ubi παρενθήκη intercessit, qualis hic longa Draconis descriptio. Revocatur enim lectori in memoriam id, quod præcesserat.

Εἰς τὴν γῆν) ut solent, qui in lucta dejiciuntur. Concur- runt hic loquutio ἀλληγορικὴ & κυριολεξία in easdem voces: Quod sæpe evenit in vaticiniis de Christo.

Καὶ οἱ Ἄγγελοι ἀυτῶ μετ᾿ ἀυτῦ ἐβλήθησαν) Nempe in Si- monianis, qui victi caput attollere ausi non sunt.

De loquutionis hujus inepta detorsione Josephi Antonii Gonzag. videatur Christianus Schottanus in Tohu pag. 155. Non est inventus amplius locus Draconis quoad publicam illam & universalem tum idololatriam, quæ cessabat delubris Dæmo- num vel clausis vel dirutis, tum persequutionem in urbe Romanorum sede Ecclesiæ præcipua: quo- modo & per mille annos ligatus dicitur Satanas, Apoc. 20. donec Turcica potentia emergente Tar- taris insuper, & bestialibus Pseudo - Catholicis passim Ecclesiam crudeliter oppugnantibus solve- retur. Projectus autem est in terram, infernum, & abjectiora terræ loca, quo respici videtur istud Gen. 3, 15. super ventrem gradieris. Per ejectionem istam Diaboli deletionem Reip. Judaicæ Coccejus, conversionem gentium per Apostolos Alcafar, refor- mationem B. Lutheri Wolterus, Hoë, Danhauer, Döling, Richterus intelligunt. Ad ejectionem sub Constantino M. determinant Osiander, Cluverus, Gravius, Dürfeld, Kromayer, Medus, &c. Sic etiam B. Gerhardus etsi efficaciam gloriosæ & vi- &oriosæ resurrectionis & ascensionis Christi intelli- gat, & victoriam per mortem & resurrectionem adversus Diabolum obtentam innui velit (quod ratione fundamenti non abnuimus) tempora Con- stantini tamen hæc concernere agnoscit, ac præci- pue nostra tempora respici vult ejecti per præco- nium Evangelii Anti-Christi (quod seriei Apocaly- pticæ minus congruere arbitramur) ideo de Hera- clio Imperatore, qui adversus Cosroem pro Christia- nis bellum gessit, Lyranus, de Constantino, qui de Maxentio, Maximino & Licinio victoriam repor- tavit, plerique alii Michaelem intelligunt; quem vero merito B. Gerhardus cum Ambrosio, Ansber- to, & Reformatis, Bullingero, Szegedino, Aretio, Pi- scatore, Riccardo, Junio, Forbesio, Crugotio, Cotterio de Christo explicat. Nec abnuit Lud. Alcafar, et- si cum Grotio per Draconem & Angelos ejus Ne- ronem, Simonem Magum & alios, per quos Draco infernalis Ecclesiam adoriri voluit, designari falso, & contra seriem Apocalypseos existimet. Quod e v. 12. νικητὰς urget Drusius ad Jos. p. 4. ne Michael intelligatur Christus, futile est, quia ad illos Ange- los cum Michaele pugnantes & vincentes perti- nent secundum vocem cælestem & fratres beato- rum Christiani in terris militantes, 2. Cor. 10, 5. qui per sanguinem Agni vincunt. Hæc enim applica- tionem inferunt. De complemento Sozomenus l. 1. c. 8. Constantinus autem cum jam solus universo im- perio potitus esset, subditis suis versus orientem habi- tantibus edicto publico mandavit, ut religionem Chri- stianam colerent, & Divinum numen studiose vene- rarentur, illudque solum Numen Divinum censerent: quod revera sit, quodque omni tempore satis in se vi- rium & potentiæ habeat. Nam qui in eo diligenter co- lendo studium suum ponerent, his omnia bona affluen- ter suppetere solere, & quæcunque cum spe bona moli- rentur, ex sententia succedere; at qui in Deo opt. max. adorando delinquerent, res omnes publicè & privatim in bello & pace infeliciter evenire. Porro autem non quo insolenter gloriaretur, sed quo Deo gratias ageret, se dicere affirmavit, Deum cum ipsum idoneum suæ voluntatis administrum esse judicaret, a mari Bri- tannico ad regiones usque in Oriente sitas deduxisse, quo tum Christiana augeretur religio. Et porro: Nam Christiani omnes fere Romani imperii magi- stratus gerere cœperunt interdixeruntque omnibus, ne de cætero vel simulachris immolare, vel divinationi- bus nefandisve mysteriis uti vel statuas erigere, vel fe- sta gentilitia celebrare aggrederentur. Multa præ- terea vetera civitatum instituta fuere mutata. Postre- mo apud Ægyptios cubitus ille, quo inundatio Nili notari solet, non amplius, ut moris erat, ad fana gen- tilium, sed ex illo tempore ad Christianorum Ecclesias delatus est.

.Vers. 10.. Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ ὀυρανῷ) Acclamationem Angelorum cœlestium, qualis supra c. 5, 11. c. 11. v. 15.

## 12:10
Λέγουσαν, ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία) That is, praise on account of the preserved Christian religion. By metonymy above c. 7, 10.

Καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν) above c. 11, 17. Καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀυτοῦ) The same sense as above v. 12. Ἐξουσία שליטן empire.

Ὅτι κατεβλήθη ὁ κατήγορος τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν) He spoke significantly. For καταβάλλειν is a word proper to wrestling: Whence καταβλητικώτερος in the saying of the Laconian. Διάβολος and κατήγορος are the same, as often as this is taken in a bad sense. And so the Devil is called קטגור in Musar. Note that Christians are called brothers by the Angels, because they are under a common head, Christ.

Ὁ κατηγορῶν ἀυτῶν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς) Taken from the history of Job c. 1, 9. 10. 11. 12. 14. The Demon had said to God: the faith of Christians is not to be magnified: they overcome light temptations, they will succumb under the fear of death.

Latin:

Λέγουσαν, ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία) Id est, laus ob conser- vatam religionem Christianam. Per μετατονομία supra c. 7, 10.

Καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν) supra c. 11, 17. Καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀυτοῦ) Sensus idem, qui supra v. 12. Ἐξουσία שליטן imperium.

Ὅτι κατεβλήθη ὁ κατήγορος τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν) Signate lo- quutus est. Nam καταβάλλειν vox propria luctæ: Unde κατα- βλητικώτερος in dicto Laconis. Idem est Διάβολος & κατή- γορος, quoties in malam partem hoc sumitur. Itaque Dia- bolus dicitur קטגור in Musar. Nota Christianos fratres ab Angelis dici, quia sub communi capite sunt Christo.

Ὁ κατηγορῶν ἀυτῶν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς) Sumptum ex Jobi historia c. 1, 9. 10. 11. 12. 14. Dixerat Dæ- mon Deo: non magnificienda est fides Christianorum: le- via tentamenta superant, sub mortis metu succumbent.

## 12:11
Vers. 11. Καὶ ἀυτοὶ ἐνίκησαν ἀυτὸν) they refuted his calumny.

Διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀρνίου) Because of the example of Christ, who had not refused death for the sake of sanctioning his doctrine.

Καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας ἀυτῶν) And because of the Evangelical word embracing both the precepts and the heavenly promises, to which word they themselves bore witness by their words and deeds. See above 1. 2. 9. c. 6, 9. c. 11, 7.

Καὶ ὀυκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν ἀυτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου) their soul, that is, themselves. They did not love, that is, they esteemed little for Christ's sake, even unto death, that is, even with the danger of death impending, Acts 20, 24. But understand the danger of death here not from the edicts of the Caesars, about which it will begin to be treated later, but from the sedition which often beset those Christians exiling from Rome, as Aquila and his companions at Corinth Acts 15, 6. 9. 16.

Latin:

Vers. 11. Καὶ ἀυτοὶ ἐνίκησαν ἀυτὸν) refutarunt ipsius ca- lumniam.

Διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀρνίου) Propter exemplum Christi, qui mor- tem doctrinæ suæ sanciendæ causa non recusarat.

Καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας ἀυτῶν) Et propter sermo- nem Evangelicum complectentem & præcepta & promissa cœlestia, cui sermoni ipsi verbis & factis suis testimonium reddebant. Vid. sup. 1. 2. 9. c. 6, 9. c. 11, 7.

Καὶ ὀυκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν ἀυτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου) animam suam, id est, semetipsos. Non dilexerunt, id est, parvi duxe- runt pro Christo, usque ad mortem, id est, etiam instante mor- tis periculo, Act. 20, 24. Periculum autem mortis hic in- tellige non ex Cæsarum edictis, de quibus postea agi inci- piet, sed ex seditione, quæ illos Christianos a Roma exulan- tes sæpe incessebat, ut Aquilam & comites ejus Corinthi Act. 15, 6. 9. 16.

## 12:12
Vers. 12. Διὰ τοῦτο ἐυφραίνεσθε οἱ ὀυρανοὶ) personification such as Psalm 148, 1.

And those dwelling in them) Angels, for they excite one another.

Woe to the earth and to the sea) that is, to the Roman empire and to the Roman state. For just as in the former part, which was about the Jews, the earth was Judea, the sea the state or the people of Jerusalem, so here the earth is all things that were under Roman dominion, but the sea is the multitude that was at Rome. The Angels prophesy evil to these, because, as the following vision will now explain, the evil intended against the Christians God turned against the Roman citizens and the Roman provinces, first by the wars of Vindex and Galba, then of Otho, Vitellius, and Vespasian, which wars brought immense slaughters both at Rome and elsewhere.

Because the Devil has come down to us) he has come down for he will come down.

In the prophetic manner. When he can no longer harm the Christians, he will pour out his wrath upon you, having stirred up civil wars, with God so directing matters.

Ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν) he has conceived great wrath, which he is absolutely going to vomit forth at some point.

Εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει) Foreseeing the future, that he will not always sway the Roman Empire at his nod. For there had also been an omen of this matter in the prostrated gods of Egypt, Exod. 12, 12. Num. 33, 4.

A great voice in heaven, both of the Angels and of other blessed Spirits, namely the perfect just ones, as they are called in Heb. 12. There is no reason, therefore, to believe that the brethren are called Angels, since they can be understood as the elect from the peoples and nations triumphing in the heavens, and singing in harmony with the militant and victorious Church. That Διὰ can also signify 'through' is proven by B. Cluverus from chapter IV. 11 and XIII. 14, and from that Greek usage δι᾽ ἄγνοιαν ἀνομεῖν, to sin through ignorance. But the more common meaning of the pronoun constructed with the accusative case can be conveniently retained here, as the Vulgate rendered it, 'through the blood of the Lamb,' because this is the meritorious cause of the victory. And we have here not only the meritorious cause, but on the part of God, the organic cause through the word of testimony on our part, and on their part the constancy of faith, because they are said not to have loved their life, even unto death, which is included in this description of victory. Wrongly, therefore, as Cornelius warns, do some Theologians gather from this passage that the Angels received grace and victory, and consequently glory and a crown, from the blood and merits of Christ. For John is speaking about men, not about Angels.

But the gloss of the Socinianizing Grotius, because of the example of Christ, is to be entirely rejected: because even if we are commanded to imitate the example of Christ, there is nevertheless no one who is able to imitate it in such a way that he can overcome any temptations of the Devil: nor indeed was the death of Christ merely a martyrdom of doctrine, but a λύτρον or price of redemption paid in our stead, Matth. 20, 20. Marc. 10, 45. 1. Tim. 2, 6.

PART III. THE NEW PERSECUTION OF THE WOMAN WHO HAD FLED INTO THE DESERT.

Latin:

Vers. 12. Διὰ τοῦτο ἐυφραίνεσθε οἱ ὀυρανοὶ) προσωποποιΐα qualis Psal. 148, 1.

Καὶ οἱ ἐν ἀυτοῖς σκηνοῦντες) Angeli, excitant n. se mutuo.

Οὐαὶ τῇ γῇ καὶ τῇ θαλάσσῃ) id est imperio Romano & ci- vitati Romanæ. Nam sicut in parte priore, quæ de Judæis erat, terra erat Judæa, mare civitas sive populus Hierosoly- morum, ita hic terra, omnia quæ sub ditione erant Romana, mare vero multitudo, quæ erat Romæ. His Angeli malum vaticinantur, quia ut jam ὀπτασία sequens explicabit, ma- lum in Christianos cogitatum Deus vertit in Romanos ci- ves & in provincias Romanas, bellis primum Vindicis & Galbæ, deinde Othonis, Vitellii, Vespasiani, quæ bella im- mensas strages & Romæ & alibi attulere.

Ὅτι κατέβη ὁ Διάβολος πρὸς ἡμᾶς) κατέβη pro καταβήσεται

Prophetico more. Cum Christianis amplius nocere non poterit, in vos iram suam effundet, suscitatis bellis civilibus Deo ita res dirigente.

Ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν) iram magnam concepit, quam omni- no aliquo evomiturus est.

Εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει) Prævidens futurum, ut non semper imperium Romanum pro nutu verset. Nam & au- gurium ejus rei fuerat in prostratis Ægypti diis, Exod. 12, 12. Num. 33, 4.

Vox magna in cœlo tum Angelorum tum alio- rum beatorum Spirituum, justorum nempe perfe- ctorum, ut vocantur Ebr. 12. Non ergo est, quod fratres Angelos dici credamus, quum intelligi pos- sint electi e populis & gentibus in cœlis triumphantes, & militanti Ecclesiæ ac vincenti accinentes. Διὰ significare etiam per e cap. IV. 11. & XIII. 14. & illo Græcanico δι᾽ ἄγνοιαν ἀνομεῖν per ignorantiam pec- care B. Cluverus probat. Sed retineri hic commode potest usitatior pronominis cum quarto casu con- structi significatio, ut Vulgatus reddidit, per sangui- nem Agni, quia hic est causa victoriæ meritoria. Et habemus hic non modo causam meritoriam, sed ex parte Dei tum organicam Verbo testimonii ex parte nostri, tum ex parte ipsorum constantiam fidei, quia dicuntur non amasse vitam, usq; ad mor- tem, hac descriptione victoriæ comprehensum. Per- peram ergo, monente Cornelio, aliqui Theologi ex hoc loco colligunt, Angelos ex Christi sanguine & me- ritis accepisse gratiam & victoriam, ac consequenter gloriam & coronam. Johannes enim loquitur de ho- minibus, non de Angelis.

Glossa vero Grotii Socinianizantis propter ex- emplum Christi reprobanda omnino est: quia etsi jubeamur Christi exemplum imitari, non est ta- men quisquam, qui ita id imitari valeat, ut Diaboli tentationes quasvis superare possit: neque vero Christi mors martyrium tantum doctrinæ fuit, sed λύτρον vel solutionis pretium nostri loco præsti- tum, Matth. 20, 20. Marc. 10, 45. 1. Tim. 2, 6.

PARS III. MULIERIS IN DESERTUM FUGA- TÆ NOVA PERSEQUUTIO.

## 12:13
Ver. 13.

Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ Δράκων) After the voices of the Angels are finished, John now pursues the remainder of the vision.

Ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς γῆν) that the fallacies of Simon did not succeed.

Ἐδίωξε τὴν γυναῖκα, ἥτις ἔτεκε τὸν ἄῤῥενα) thinking: This did not succeed, I must enter by another way. And so, after the fox-like, he takes on the lion-like. He stirs up Nero, so that he might destroy by force the Church, which had begun to appear in Rome after Simon was prostrated. But he names the woman here rather than the infant, because Christians were flocking to Rome from all places.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ Δράκων) Post absolutas voces Angelorum Johannes jam reliqua τῆς ὀπτασίας persequitur.

Ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς γῆν) non successisse fallacias Simonis.

Ἐδίωξε τὴν γυναῖκα, ἥτις ἔτεκε τὸν ἄῤῥενα) cogitans: Hac non successit, alia ingrediendum est via. Itaque post vulpinam sumit leoninam. Suscitat Nero- nem, ut Ecclesiam, quæ Romæ post Simonem prostratum ap- parere cœperat, per vim disjiceret. Potius autem mulierem hic nominat, quam infantem, quia ex omnibus locis Chri- stiani Romam concurrebant.

## 12:14
Ver. 14. And there were given to the woman two wings of the great eagle) Wings denote flight, Ps. 55:5. Its swiftness is eagle-like, Prov. 23:5, Isa. 40:31, Exod. 19:4, Lam. 4:5. But larger eagles are even swifter, Ezek. 17:3, 7.

That she might fly into the wilderness) into less frequented places, as above, 5.

Into her place) that is, into the places which God had prepared for her, so that she might be safe there, as above, 6.

That she might be nourished there for a time, and times, and half a time) From Dan. 7:25 and ch. 12:7, where the matter itself speaks that times are years, and the passages of Daniel 4:20, 21, just as the Scholiasts note that Homer also speaks. Here too is again the same space of time which we have had several times above. We have brought forward the reason above. Justin, disputing with Trypho, refutes certain of the Jews who wished for a hundred years to be understood by a time.

From the face of the serpent) These are to be construed with she might fly, so that the rest may be taken by way of parenthesis: A similar locution, Ps. 3:1, Ps. 57:1, Ps. 68:1, and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Καὶ ἐδόθησαν τῇ γυναικὶ δύο πτέρυγες τῶ ἀετῶ τῶ μεγάλυ) Alæ fugam notant Psal. 55, 5. ejus celeritatem aquilinæ Prov. 23, 5. Esa. 40, 31. Exod. 19, 4. Lam. 4, 5. Gran- diores autem aquilæ etiam celeriores, Ezech. 17, 3. 7.

Ἵνα πέτηται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον) in loca minus frequentia, ut su- pra 5.

Εἰς τὸν τόπον ἀυτῆς) id est, in loca, quæ ei Deus parave- rat, ut ibi tuta esset, quomodo supra 6.

Ὅπως τρέφηται ἐκεῖ καιρὸν καὶ καιρὸς καὶ ἥμισυ καιρῶ) Ex Dan. 7, 25. & c. 12, 7. ubi tempora esse annos & res ipsa lo- quitur & loca Danielis 4, 20. 21. quomodo & Homerum lo- qui notant Scholiastæ. Est & hic iterum idem temporis spatium, quod supra habuimus aliquoties. Causam supra attulimus. Refutat Justinus cum Tryphone disputans Ju- dæorum quosdam, qui per χρόνον centum annos intelligi vo- lebant.

Ἀπὸ προσώπυ τῶ ὄφεως) Construenda hæc cum πέτη- ται, ut cætera παρενθέσεως modo accipiantur: Similis lo- quutio Psal. 3, 1. Ps. 57, 1. Ps. 68, 1. & alibi.

## 12:15
Ver. 15. And the serpent cast out of his mouth after the woman water as a river) A river signifies adverse things, as we said at Matt. 7:27. Add Ps. 124:4, but especially those which suddenly rush in, Isa. 8:7, ch. 59:19, ch. 25:4, Jer. 46:8, Ps. 93:3, because the flooding of rivers happens suddenly. The Devil wished to infest the Church of Christ everywhere, even outside of Rome; how he did this through Domitian and Trajan, we shall see in the following chapter. The Dragon poured out hatred against Christians from Rome: this is shown in this chapter, but from Rome into all the provinces, which is the subject of the following chapter.

That he might make her carried away by the river) that he might submerge her, snatched away by the force of the river. Thus the Greeks say anemophorēta, those things which are carried away by the wind.

Blessed Gravius has this to say concerning these and the following: The herald wishes to intimate here that it is better that they endure the fury of the two-horned beast for a time, and nevertheless keep the commandments and the faith of Jesus, than that, having received the mark of the beast, they sustain so many punishments, tortures, and torments with it forever. By the saints he understands not those whom the Pope has canonized, but those who, sanctified through faith, keep the commandments of God and are afflicted by the Anti-Christians. Furthermore: The particle aparti denotes the time of the doctrine purified through the three Angel heralds, so that the sense is: From this time they are blessed, not indeed for the first time (since many others also were saved before the proclamation of these Angels), but because, with the Platonic purgatory and the fiction of satisfactions and indulgences now exploded, it becomes known to all Christians that for those who die in Christ, after this life, the torments of fire are no longer to be feared, but their souls are in the hand of God and have rest in the heavenly dwelling: Then it is added that their works follow them, not as merit, but as the fruits of faith, and carry with them a gratuitous retribution, Rom. 5:23. The persecutions of Domitian and Trajan have nothing to do with this. For the order is thus disturbed. For that pouring out of the river from the mouth follows the persecution of the Dragon which took place up to the times of Constantine the Great, and it is the offspring already brought to light, by which double criterion, both of the swelling and of the offspring already brought forth, this new persecution is denoted, which was made by the Arian cohort. For they persecuted the profession of the Nicene faith and the homoousion with mouth and pen, with doctrine and writings. Nor do the three years and a half agree: For the persecution of Domitian alone, which began in his ninth year, when he cast John into a vessel filled with boiling oil at Rome, and in the twelfth year took away Antipas at Pergamum, Ignatius at Antioch, and Cletus at Rome, did not cease until his death in his sixteenth year. Blessed Cluverius prefers that it be explained concerning the expeditions of the Huns, Persians, Scythians, and similar disturbances, about which he discourses learnedly and at length. But we acquiesce in the interpretation brought forward, with which, however, we allow that one to be joined, Blessed Hoe not dissenting: And the serpent cast out of his mouth after the woman water as a river, that he might make her potamophorēton, to be snatched away by the river (that he might, as it were, wash away or drown the Church), by which ejection of water or river nothing else is intimated than that the Dragon poured out a sea of evils, heresies, schisms, disturbances, contentions, and persecutions into the Church and flooded almost the whole world with rivers of heretics and persecutors, with the purpose that he might be able to extirpate, destroy, and sink into the deep every piety and all Christians root and branch, Ps. 124:3, 4. There is no reason why we should interpret the eagle scrupulously.

By the eagle wings of the Christian Roman Emperors, the protective wings are more correctly designated, just as the Mede, the great Eagle, he says, is the Roman empire, B. Cluver explains the wings of the Christian empire, Forbes the great eagle Constantine M; he does it more correctly: which two angelic warnings to the Magi and Mary Matt. 2, 12. 13. which is Aretius's exposition, two testaments, which are those of Primasius, Ticonius, Rupert, the interlinear Gloss or Napier; or the hope and faith of Cotterius, or even the zeal for prayers and good works of Aretius, or also two great regions Spain and Gaul, in which the beginning was given of the nourishment of the Church in the Diocletian persecution by Constantine the Great, according to Coccejus.

Furthermore, concerning the time, times, and half a time, it must be spoken of again here, which John Foxe in his English Martyrology most correctly accepts in the same sense as 3 1/2 years, 42 months, and 1260 days; however, others—Junius, and those who follow him, Polanus, Diodati, Napier, the English Annotators, and others—distinguish those, whether here or in Daniel: assuming them to be astronomical in Daniel and prophetic in the Apocalypse, and there not a half, but a small part of a year reduced to ten days from the Maccabean books; which is done by the recent English Annotators: whom Junius designates in Dan. 12:1 as the 3 1/2 years from the beginning of the Jewish war to the ruin of the city, and explains in chapter 7:25 as concerning Antiochus. But he rashly begins the prophetic calculation from the passion of Christ, since prophecy is made not of past things but of future ones, and it ends in the year 1294, at which time the fury against the enemies had not yet cooled. Napier begins from the empire of Constantine and the donation of Sylvester, and ends at the shaking off of the Scottish-English Papal yoke in the year 1560; but it should have been ended in the year 1573, in which no significant defection from the Pope occurred. Bullinger, Bibliander, Albertus, Pareus, and Basilius are with us; however, in this they depart from us: Thomas, Brightman, Joseph, Mede, Thomas, Harcker, and Ephraim Huit, who set the term at the year of Christ 1650, marked by the empire of the City of Rome and the Antichrist, the final conversion of the Jews, and the fifth monarchy of the saints, concerning which Scripture has nothing, and who have already been refuted by experience itself. John Foxe, without precedent in this book, assumes sabbatical months, as if taught by Divine inspiration, which no man has, and begins them from the slaughter of John, and terminates them at the beginning of Constantine; afterwards, he resumes the same a second time from the persecutions of the Turks in the year 1300, and ends them, as Basilius recounts, in the year 1596, when, if that unusual doubling is to be admitted, it ought to be finished in 1594. How Papists explain these years concerning the Antichrist has been said before. They spread not long ago, as Maresius reports in Anti-Tirinus on page 228, that the Antichrist was born in Babylon, whose description and very admirable miracles they were accurately reporting, so that nothing would be missing from the history. But whoever compares these things, which were even described in print and solicitously dispersed throughout all of Belgium, with those which Simon Goulart had already reported before in his 'Admirables' (vol. 1, p. 52) under the title of apparitions in the air, as if from letters written by the prefect of the Knights of Malta in the year 1532, and also those which Baptista Le Crain, Councilor and Master of Royal Petitions, commemorates in the first Decade of the History of Louis XIII, book 5, p. 182, for the year 1615, where he says that letters were also spread from the Maltese Prefect concerning the arrival of the Antichrist, will discover that the same lie, slightly interpolated, is frequently recalled to the stage by Papists, with no other end than that in the question concerning the Antichrist, one should look to someone other than the Pope. Concerning Dan. 7:8, interpreters vary.

and swallowed the water which it cast. The comparison proceeds well. For it is established that certain rivers are absorbed by the earth.

Vers. 15. Καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ὄφις ἐκ τῶ σόματος ἀυτῶ ὀπίσω $\tilde{\tau}$ γυναικὸς ὕδωρ ὡς ποταμόν) Flumen res adversas signifi- cat, ut diximus ad Matth. 7, 27. Adde Ps. 124, 4. præ- cipue vero eas, quæ subito ingruunt. Esa. 8. 7. c. 59, 19. c. 25, 4. Jerem. 46, 8. Psal. 93, 3. quia eluviones amnium subito eveniunt. Diabolus Ecclesiam Christi ubique etiam extra Romam voluit infestare, quod quomodo fecerit per Domitianum & Trajanum, videbimus capite sequenti. Draco Romæ effudit odium in Christianos: id hoc capite ostenditur, Romæ vero in omnes provincias, quod argumen- tum est capitis sequentis.

Ἱνα αὐτὴν ποταμοφόρητον ποιήσῃ) ut eam vi fluminis ab- reptam submergeret. Sic ἀνεμοφόρητὰ dicunt Græci, quæ vento auferuntur.

B. Gravius de his & sqq. ita habet: Innuere vult hic præco, melius esse, ut furorem bestiæ bicornis ad tempus perferant, ac nihilominus mandata & fidem Jesu custodiant; quam ut accepto charactere bestiæ tot pœnas cruciatus & tormenta cum ea in perpetuum sustineant. Per sanctos intelligit non eos, quos Papa ca- nonizavit, sed qui per fidem sanctificati mandata Dei servant, & ab Anti-Christianis affliguntur. Porro: Particula ἀπάρτι denotat tempus repurgatæ doctri- næ per tres Angelos præcones, ut sit sensus: Ab hoc tempore beatos non quidem primum esse (cum & multi alii ante horum Angelorum præconium fuerint salvati) sed quod exploso jam Platonico purgatorio, satisfactionum & indulgentiarum commento, omni- bus Christianis innotescat, mortuis in Christo post hanc vitam non amplius metuenda esse tormenta ignis, sed illorum animas esse in manu Dei, & requiem habere in cœlesti habitaculo: Deinde additur, quod opera se- quantur ipsos, non ut meritum, sed tanquam fructus fidei, & trahere secum retributionem gratuitam, Ro- man. 5, 23. Persecutiones Domitiani & Trajani huc nihil faciunt. Turbatur enim sic ordo. Nam sequi- tur illa fluminis ex ore effusio persequutionem Draconis ad Constantini M. tempora factam, estq; fœtus jam in lucem editi, quo gemino tumoris, tum fœtus jam editi κριτηρίῳ denotatur nova hæc persecutio, a cohorte Ariana facta. Nam illi insecta- bantur professionem fidei Nicenæ, & τὸ ὁμοόσιον ore & calamo, doctrina & scriptis. Neq; congruunt tres anni cum dimidio: Nam unius Domitiani per- secutio, quæ nono ejus anno cœpit, cum Johan- nem in vas ferventi oleo repletum Romæ immisit duodecimo Antipam Pergami, Ignatium Antio- chiæ, Cletum Romæ sustulit, non nisi cum morte anno ejus 16. desiit. B. Cluverus mavult de expe- ditionibus Hunnorum, Persarum, Scytharum, & si- milium turbarum explicari, de quibus erudite ac prolixe differit. Sed acquiescimus in adducta in- terpretatione, cum qua tamen illam conjungi per- mittimus, non abnuente B. Hoë̈o: Et ejecit serpens ex ore suo post mulierem aquam tanquam flumen, ut faceret eam ποταμοφόρητον rapi a flumine (daß er die Kirche gleichsam hinweg schwemmen oder er- säuffen möchte) qua aquæ seu fluminis ejectione ni- hil aliud innuitur, quam quod Draco mare malo- rum, hæreseon, schismatum, turbarum, contentionum & persecutionum in Ecclesiam effuderit & totum quasi orbem fluminibus hæreticorum & persecuto- rum inundaverit, eo proposito, ut omnem pietatem, & Christianos universos radicitus extirpare, delere & in profundum mergere possit, Psal. 124. vers. 3. 4. Aquilam non est, quod scrupulose interpretemur.

Per alas aquilinas Romanorum Imperatorum Christianorum alæ protectoriæ rectius designantur, quomodo Medus, Aquila magna, inquit, est impe- rium Romanum, B. Cluver. alas imperii Christiani explicat, Forbesius aquilam magnam Constanti- num M; rectius facit: quam duo monita Angeli- ca ad Magos & Mariam Matth. 2, 12. 13. quæ Are- tæ ἔκθεσις est, duo testamenta, quæ Primafii, Ticonii, Ruperti, Glossæ interlin. vel Napeiri; vel spes & fi- des Cotterii, vel etiam Aretii precum & bonorum operum studium, aut etiam duæ regiones magnæ Hispania & Gallia, in quibus initium datum nutri- tionis Ecclesiæ in Diocletiani persecutione a Con- stantino M. juxta Coccejum.

Porro de tempore, temporibus & dimidio tempo- ris hic iterum dicendum, quæ cum 3 1/2. annis & men- sibus 42. & diebus 1260. pariis sensu accipit Joh. Foxus in Martyrol. Anglic. rectissime, distinguunt autem illa sive hic, sive in Daniele alii Junius, & qui eum sequuntur Polanus, Deodatus, Napeirus, An- notatores Anglici, alii: In Daniele Astronomicos, in Apocalypsi Propheticos assumentes, & ibi non dimidium sed particulam anni ex Maccabaicis ad decem dies reductam; quod ab Annot. Angl. po- stremis fit: quos Dan. 12, 1. de 3 1/2. annis ab initio bel- li Judaici ad urbis ruinam designat Junius, & cap. 7, 25. de Antiocho explicat. Temere autem inchoat calculum Propheticum a passione Christi, quum prophetia non de præteritis sed futuris fiant, & fi- niat ann. 1294. quo nondum furor in hostes de- ferbuit. Napeirus inchoat ab imperio Constantini & donatione Sylvestri, & sinit in excussione jugi Pontificii Scotico-Anglicani anno 1560. sed ita si- niendus esset anno 1573. quo nulla facta est a Pon- tifice insignis defectio. Bullingerus, Bibliander, Albertus, Pareus, Basilius nobiscum facit: in eo au- tem abeunt a nobis Thomas, Brightmannus, Josephus, Medus, Thomas, Harckerus, Ephraim Huitus, qui terminum constituunt anno Christi 1650. Romam imperio Urbis, & Anti-Christi utriusque finali Ju- dæorum conversione, & quinta sanctorum Monar- chia, de quibus Scriptura nihil habet, insigni, qui ab ipsa experientia consutati jam sunt. Johannes Foxus sine exemplo in hoc libro menses sabbaticos, quasi edoctus Divina inspiratione, quæ homini nulla est, assumit, & a cæde Johannis eos inchoat, in Constantini principio terminat, postea iterata vice a persecutionibus Turcarum anno 1300. eosdem resumit, sinitque recensente Basilio anno 1596. quum 1594. si insolens illa geminatio admittenda, finiri debeat. Quomodo de Anti-Christo hos annos explicent Papistæ, antea dictum. Sparserunt non ita pridem, referente in Anti-Tirinio Maresio pag. 228. Anti-Christum Babylone esse natum, cujus etiam descriptionem & miracula valde admiranda, ne quid deesfet ad Historiam, accurate referebant. Sed qui hæc typis etiam descripta & solicite per totum Belgi- um dispersa contulerit cum iis, quæ jam antea in suis admirandis retulerat Simon Goulartius t. 1. pag. 52. sub titulo apparitionum in aëre, tanquam ex literis a Melitensium equitum præfecto scriptis an. 1532. nec- non iis, quæ commemorat Baptista Le Crain, Consilia- rius & libellorum supplicum Magister Regius in prima Decade Historiæ Ludovici XIII. libr. 5. p. 182. ad ann. 1615. quo dicit literas quoq; sparsas fuisse Me- litensis Præfecti de adventu Anti-Christi, deprehendet idem mendacium parumper interpolatum sæpius a Papicolis in scenam revocari, non alio fine, quam ut in quæstione de Anti-Christo alio quam ad Papam re- spiciatur. De Dan. 7, 8. variant Interpretes.

καὶ κατέπιε τὸ ὕδωρ ὃ ἔβαλεν. Bene procedit comparatio. Nam flumina quædam a terra absorberi constat.

Vers. 16.

Καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον ἢ θαλάσσης) On the shore of Patmos: For there the ὀπτασία concerning the beast, which now follows, happened to John. And for that reason, the things that follow should not have been separated from these; and in Arethas they cohere. Visions formerly happened to the Prophets on riverbanks, Ezek. 1, 1. Dan. 8, 2. ch. 10, 4. To John on the shore. There is a greater catch in the sea than in rivers.

Καὶ ἐβοήθησεν ἡ γῆ γυναικὶ) The Roman empire succeeded into the place of the Christians. For all that savagery of the Devil was diverted onto it. Similar is that in Is. 43, 3. Ἐποίησα ἄλλαγμά σε ἄἴγυπτον καὶ Αἰθιοπίαν, that is, when the Assyrian wanted to rush into Judea, the Ethiopian, supported by the help of Egypt, was set against him in place of the Jews, as we said at that passage.

We proved, when we treated that passage, that the statement in Gen. 3, 15 cannot be taken μυσικῶς concerning a collective seed, but must necessarily be explained μοναδικῶς & individually concerning Christ.

Καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ ςόμα ἀυτῆς, καὶ κατέπιε τὸν πόλα- μὸν, ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ ςόματος ἀυτοῦ) The parts of the Roman empire felt those evils which Rome was threatening against Christians everywhere among the nations. The Romans, fighting among themselves, had no time to think about the Christians. In the Manuscript

Et propterea quæ sequuntur ab his divellenda non fuerant; Et apud Aretham cohærent. Olim Prophetis visa in ripis obtigerunt, Ezech. 1, 1. Dan. 8, 2. c. 10, 4. Johanni in littore. Major captura est in mari, quam in flu- minibus.

Ἐποίησα ἄλλαγμά σε ἄἴγυπτον καὶ Αἰθιοπίαν, id est, cum Assyrius vellet in Judæam irruere, pro Judæis ei objici Æthiopem, suffultum ope Ægypti, ut ad eum locum diximus.

Dictum Gen. 3, 15. non posse μυσικῶς accipi de semine collectivo, sed μοναδικῶς & individualiter ne- cessario explicandum esse de Christo, cum illum locum tractavimus, evicimus.

Καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ ςόμα ἀυτῆς, καὶ κατέπιε τὸν πόλα- μὸν, ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ ςόματος ἀυτοῦ) Imperii Romani partes ea mala sensere, quæ Roma Christianis ubi- que gentium minabatur. Non vacavit Romanis inter se pugnantibus cogitare de Christianis. In Manuscripto

## 12:17
Verse 17.

And the Dragon was angry with the woman) Here a new section should have begun. For one now comes to the times of Domitian first, then Trajan, which brought two persecutions upon the Christians after the Neronian one, the first and more general ones after the Neronian, which had remained within Rome. But from those persecutions of Domitian and Trajan, similar ones ought to be understood, just as from the seven other churches, others are understood. The sense is: the Roman civil wars having been finished, the Devil returned to his former designs against the Christians.

The Greek word does not imply succession into the place of another, but help. By the earth helping the woman, Lyra and the soldiers of Heraclius, defeating the Persian Chosroes, Ribera and Cornelius a Lapide understand the earth properly; Woltberus, Winckelmann, and Danhavv understand pious magistrates, the death and burial of enemies, such as Julian, etc.; B. Gerhard and B. Grav. wish wars, famine, and pestilence to be noted; Cramer and Foxe do so. But they say that this assistance was made through the abolition of the enemies: Cluverus, Grav., Döling, Dürfeld, and mutual slaughter in Cluv. Epit. Hist. p. 363, Centur. Magdeburg. Cent. VI. f. 845. Through the conversion of enemies: Winckelmann, Cluverus, Brightman, Dürfeld. See Evagr. H. E. l. IV. c. 28, Centur. Magdeb. VI. f. 40. But the earth is said here to have helped the woman, because even earthly men repelled the Dragon's wrath against the Church: which has happened more often, with God so directing it, lest the whole Church be swallowed up, just as we see it happening today under the Antichrist. For does not France, which is otherwise joined to the Antichrist, do not other provinces twin to it, often resist him, when he himself intends our extermination, and desires us to be extinguished by a river, as it were, of persecutions? There the earth helps the woman, and can be said to bring her aid, even if it intends everything else. Which likewise happens when the Eastern Antichrist represses and restrains the Western one, the Turk the Roman Pope.

And went away to make war with the rest of her seed) to make war is nothing else here than to treat hostiley, although they were to oppose no force. See above c. 11:7. You see here the seed of the woman, which is Gen. 3:15, mystically explained concerning the members of the Christian Church, in which sense Paul uses the words of the same place in Rom. 16:20. The second Adam is Christ: the second Eve, that is, the mother of the living, is the whole Church: her seed, the individuals who belong to the Church.

Of those keeping the commandments of God) Namely those which are in the Gospel, and note that 'keeping' is construed with that 'seed,' which word here is singular in sound, and signifies a multitude, like people, flock, army. To keep the commandments in this sense, the same John said here in his 1st Epistle c. 2:14, c. 3:22, c. 5:3.

Καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ) Of those retaining the profession concerning Jesus the Savior. The same expression is above in ch. 6, 9.

Vers. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

Καὶ ὠργίσθη ὁ Δράκων ἐπὶ τῇ γυναικὶ) Hic incipere de- buit nova sectio. Venitur enim jam ad tempora Domitia- ni primum, deinde Trajani, quæ duas persecutiones attule- re in Christianos post Neronianam, primas ac generaliores Neroniana, quæ intra Romam constiterat. Ex istis autem Domitiani & Trajani persecutionibus & similes debent in- telligi, quomodo ex septem aliis Ecclesiis aliæ. Sensus est, peractis bellis Romanorum civilibus, rediit Diabolus ad pristinas cogitationes contra Christianos.

Vox Græca non successionem in locum alterius, sed auxilium infert. Per terram mulierem adju- vantem Lyra Græcos & milites Heraclii, Bansam Cosroën vincentes, Ribera & Cornelius a Lapide proprie terram; Woltberus, Winckelmannus, Danhavv. pios Magistratus, mortem & sepul- chrum hostium, utpote Juliani &c. B. Gerhard. & B. Grav. bella, famem, pestem notari volunt, Cra- merus & Foxus. Opitulationem autem illam factam esse ajunt per hostium abolitionem, Cluve- rus, Grav. Döling, Dürfeld, mutuam internecio- nem apud Cluv. Epit. Hist. p. 363. Centur. Magde- burg. Cent. VI. f. 845. Per hostium conversio- nem Winckelmann, Cluverus, Brigtmannus, Dür- feld. Vid. Evagr. H. E. l. IV. c. 28. Centur. Mag- deb. VI. f. 40. Verum terræ hic opitulata dicitur mulierem, quia etiam terreni homines Draconis iram adversus Ecclesiam propulsarunt: Quod sæ- pius factum, Deo ita dirigente, ne absorberetur to- ta Ecclesia, quemadmodum & hodie id sub Anti- Christo fieri videmus. Annon enim Gallia, quæ Anti-Christo alias addita est, annon aliæ provinciæ illi geminæ, eidem sæpe resistunt, cum ipse exter- minium nostri intendit, & flumine veluti quodam persecutionum nos extinctos cupit? Ibi terra ad- juvat mulierem, eique auxilium ferre dici potest, etsi alia omnia intendat. Quod pariter sit, cum An- ti-Christus Orientalis reprimit & compescit Occi- dentalem, Turca Papam Romanum.

Καὶ ἀπῆλθε ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σπέρμα- τος αὐτῆς) ποιῆσαι πόλεμον nihil aliud est hic quam tra- ctare hostiliter, quamvis nullam vim opposituros. Vide supra c. 11, 7. Vides hic semen mulieris quod est Genes. 3, 15. μυσικῶς explicari de membris Ecclesiæ Christianæ, quo sensu verba ejusdem loci usurpat Paulus Rom. 16, 20. A- dam secundus est Christus: Eva secunda, id est, mater vi- ventium, Ecclesia tota: semen ejus, singuli qui ad Ecclesiam pertinent.

Τῶν τηρέντων τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ Θεοῦ) Nempe eas quæ sunt in Evangelio, & nota τηρέντων construi cum illo σπέρματος, quæ vox hic sono est singularis, & multitudi- nem significat, ut populus, grex, exercitus. Ἐντολὰς τηρεῖν hoc sensu dixit idem hic Johannes epistola 1. c. 2, 14. c. 3, 22. c. 5, 3.

Καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ) Retinentium professionem de Jesu Servatore. Eadem loquutio supra c. 6, 9.

Vers. 18.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

Two beasts are seen, one from the sea, distinguished by 7 heads and crowns with blasphemous names, 10 horns, like a leopard, a bear, a lion, with one head wounded but healed to the admiration of the whole earth, holy, conquering under the Dragon, and worshipped by the world, but likewise to be struck by the sword; the other ascending from the earth with two horns, as if of a lamb, and the tongue of the Dragon, procuring veneration for the former animated image through miracles and the taking of its mark.

It is therefore divided into two parts, I. concerning the beast from the sea, to verse 10. II. concerning the beast from the earth to verse 18.

PART I. CONCERNING THE BEAST FROM THE SEA.

Ver. 1.

Καὶ εἶδον) A new vision, not now, as I said, extending to the Romans alone, but to all the lands of the Roman Empire. Εἶδον מַרְאֶה Ezech. 1, 1. Dan. 8, 14. c. 10, 4.

Ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης) From the Roman people. For waters are a people: the sea is a vast people. Thus also Dan. 5, verse 3. Ezech. 26, 3.

Θηρίον) a wild beast. Lactantius called it a monster. No one can describe the savagery of this monster according to its merits, which, lying in one place, rages through the whole world with iron teeth, and not only dissipates the limbs of men, but also crushes the very bones and rages into ashes. Among the Daniels, Jacchiades says that idolatrous kingdoms are designated by the name of wild beasts, because, forsooth, they do not have the understanding of those things which are most necessary to be known. Here, however, idolatry itself, or false religion, is rather signified, just as concrete and abstract things are wont to be mixed together in Prophetic figures.

Not here only, but also in the preceding, it was not about Rome alone, but about the Roman people. It is evident from Daniel that kingdoms are designated by the name of wild beasts in general without regard to idolatry; much less do they signify idolatry in the abstract. The metaphor is taken from strength, cruelty, and other qualities of both empires and wild beasts, not from religion, which relates to them indifferently and must be determined abundantly. Conf. here Dan. 5, 27. c. 7, 7. Grotius had treated this chapter before for the sake of the Roman Pontiff, so that he would no longer be believed to be the beast seen here. Therefore, it is pleasing to repeat those things, lest by chance they be missed by anyone, and lest they remain untouched and undiscussed, if they exhibit anything different from these, included here in more contracted lines:

Ver. 1. Καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον, and I saw a beast ascending from the sea) That εἶδον, I saw, is a word frequent in the Prophets in Hebrew מַרְאֶה, Ezech 1, 1. Dan. 8, 2. c. 10, 4. and elsewhere. Θηρίον, beast, in this place is idolatry raging in a beastly manner. Ἀναβαῖνον, ascending, signifies acquiring power, Dan. 4, 8. and cap. 8. 8. From the sea, that is, not from popular sedition, but from the force and power of the empire. For just as waters signify peoples below c. 17, 15. So the sea is that force or power gathered from the obedience of peoples.

If waters are peoples, the sea will not be force and power gathered from the obedience of peoples: But a gathering of waters, that is, of peoples. This is what that definition of the sea imports. But Grotius perverts everything.

Ἀναβαῖνον) having an origin. To ascend, to arise for the Hebrews, Is 55, 17. Mark 4, 7. Thus Daniel 7, 3. concerning the wild beasts סָלְקָן ἀνέβαινον. Idolatry had always been in Rome, but it had arisen as if new with the addition of deceased Caesars to the Gods. Claudian: And if Rome received any or gave any Gods herself.

Having ten horns) Having very many Kings, following that example. And what is the wonder, when even Jewish Kings, for the sake of the Caesars, fell away from the customs of their fathers, as Josephus speaks, by instituting in Judea itself athletic contests, theaters, amphitheaters, games, gymnastic, musical, and thymelic performances, and outside of Jewish soil even temples built in honor of the Caesars. To these now add the Kings of the Arabs, Iturea, the Comageni, Pontus Polemoniacus, Armenia, Thrace, Galatia, Adiabene, the Suevi, and the Alps. The matter is not the same in all respects, which is noted here and below in chapter 17. Here ten Kings are signified who follow Roman rites: those ten Kings arose much later, whom God would use to tear apart the Roman empire.

And seven heads) that is, seven mountains, so that we may understand that idolatry is designated here, not Phrygian, not Egyptian, not Chaldean, but properly Roman, received by Roman laws. Furthermore, the seven heads, as we learn below, also signify something else, namely seven Princes, whose names we have already had, but whose deeds were pre-signified in the preceding. They are Claudius, Nero, Galba, Otho, Vitellius, Vespasian, and Titus. It had to begin from Claudius, because he was the first to decree exiles against the Teachers of Christianity, which Tiberius had not done.

And upon his horns ten diadems) Diadems signify full right over subjects, such as those Kings had, although they were in the faith and reverence of the Roman empire. And so Augustus said to Herod the Great that he could appoint concerning his son, both as father and as King: And Antony, that it was unjust for Herod to be called to render accounts for those things which he had done as King. For thus he would not even be a King. A diadem is a royal insignia, 1 Macc. 1:10, ch. 11:13, ch. 13:32. Diadema צניף Isa. 62:3.

And upon his heads) Upon the mountains, that is, upon the city itself, which is unambiguously designated by the seven mountains. See Festus under the word Septimontium. Horace: The gods to whom the seven hills were pleasing. Propertius on Rome: The city high on seven ridges, etc. See also above ch. 12:3 and ch. 17:7, 9.

Names of blasphemy) many books have name of blasphemy, that indeed is, the eternal city. Thus Jerome explains in the eleventh question to Algasia. Prosper: Who does not understand what the Apocalypse calls the one bearing the cup full of the abominations of the uncleanness and fornication of the earth? When it is called eternal, which is temporal, it is a name of blasphemy. Caesar used to say that the Roman people had ten legions which could even tear down the sky.

A completely new idolatry has arisen, which the other of the beasts brought about, by which the Anti-Christ is to be understood, or his empire of caesaropapism, the Imperial Papacy, just as by the former is designated papocaesarism, the Papal Empire, that is, the Roman empire indeed, but as it is subject to the Pope. The reason for both is clear from the description: And indeed that the Roman empire, because the beasts denote empires in Prophetic passages, is designated by that figure of the beast: because it had seven heads and crowns, ten horns, and was seen under the appearance of different animals, which concur uniquely in the Roman empire: because of the mixture it has analogies with the others, from the first Babylonian empire namely the lion's mouth, which is of fortitude, avarice, pride, and blasphemy, which reveal themselves by the mouth, and by Papal edicts: from the second Persian, of ursine cunning, which is for breaking into kingdoms at the feet, for scraping together wealth; See Lactantius. See ch. 11 concerning the third, the Greek, namely of speed and variety, Jer. 5:6, Hab. 1:8, which appeared in Alexander the Great: And the Dragon gave to this one, not as it is an empire, but as it is subject to the Pope, the power of beastly cruelty, etc. For imperial power otherwise and as such is from God, Dan. 2:11, Rom. 13:1, Prov. 8:16. Cruelty, blasphemy, persecution of the saints, and the admission of religious worship from the Dragon, Matt. 4:9, John 8:44, Apoc. 12:9. By the seven heads they designate the mountains of Rome, which is called seven-hilled according to the common explanation of Interpreters drawn from ch. 17:9:

The city high on seven ridges which presides over the whole world. says Propertius book III, Elegy, concerning Rome, such as are the Palatine, Capitoline, Aventine, Esquiline, Caelian, Viminal, Quirinal. Galatinus thinks that the seven persecutions of the Church are designated, which he himself enumerates.

Lessius, who is unique here, understands the Devil reigning over the world through the beast. There are seven impious kings of the seven ages of the world. But the figure of the beast teaches that the Roman empire is described, and the Dragon is openly distinguished from the beast. Others, according to Gerhard, wish for the seven principal cities of the Roman empire to be designated by the seven heads: 1. Rome in Italy, 2. Constantinople in Thrace, 3. Antioch in Asia, 4. Alexandria in Egypt, 5. Jerusalem in Syria, 6. Carthage in Africa, 7. Toledo in Spain, all of which passed from the true faith to the impious dogmas of the Anti-Christ, both Muhammedan and Papist. But these are more correctly referred to the seven crowns or Kings, Apoc. 17, 9. For they were as it were the crowned queens of the other cities. The seven forms of government with King James of Great Britain. Maresius understands the horns crowned with diadems to be ten principal kingdoms: Syria and Assyria, Egypt, Asia Minor, Greece, Italy, Gaul, Spain, Africa, Germany, England with Scotland, Ireland and the neighboring northern kingdoms, or islands added to the continent and with minor provinces omitted, Hungary, Bulgaria, etc. Blessed Gerhard, along with most others, presumes the ancient Roman Empire, under the heathen Emperors, to be the beast from the persecutions and idolatry. But we prefer to understand it as the Papal empire because of the series of visions, which ought not to be disturbed.

Osiander and Joh. Christ. Artopoeus [understand] the wounded head as Julius Caesar, so named from that; Bullinger, Piscator, Junius, Szegedinus, the Vinarienses, and Alcazar [understand it] as Nero, in whom the family of Julius Caesar perished, but the healing was done to the Roman Empire by Flavius Vespasian; Coccejus [understands it] as Greece wounded by Julian; Mede [as] the heathen empire wounded in battle with Michael; Flacius [as] the Constantinopolitan empire now changed into the Turkish; Beda, Primasius, Anselm, Richard, Ansbert, Haymo, the Gloss, Thomas, and Bellarmine think the Anti-Christ is denoted, to whom Cornelius, Tirinus, and others agree. Pareus explains it as the Popes from the year 1378 to the year 1414. Ribera and Suarez [explain it] as the principal King of those adhering to the Anti-Christ; Blessed Phil. Nicolai [as] Spain wounded for 700 years from the year of Christ 720, healed by the victories against the Saracens by Ferdinand V. Alphonsus Mantuanus, according to Pareus, Danhauer, and Döling [explain it] as the Roman. Empire as if wounded by Luther, restored again in Gaul, England, Hungary, and Poland by the Papists, and especially by the Jesuits. But others more correctly understand by the first and principal head of the beast, Rome or Italy, wounded by the incursions of the barbarians, such as Foxe, Brightman, Colladon, Hoë, and Dürfeld, to whom others, with Napier, Forbes, Hopfner, Cluver, and Richter, add the seventh head, or the Christian Roman Empire, wounded from the year of Christ 400 until death by Attila, Totila, Gaiseric, Huneric, Odoacer, and Adolphus, as also in the East by the Saracens, Persians, Mahomet, and the Turks; Rome itself was devastated six times, Italy occupied by the Lombards for 77 years and by the Goths for 206 years, whence for 324 years no Emperor held power in the West, until Romulus or Augustulus, and Charlemagne, by whom the Roman Empire was healed, who was helped by the work of Leo III, as can be read in the Centuries. Magdeburg Centuries, Century VIII, fol. 752, 340. The empire came to the Germans after he [the Pope], having been accused of wishing to subject Rome to himself, and having been captured and having escaped from captivity, had betaken himself to Charles and was sent back to Rome with his army: but Charles, arriving there, was received with honor, and having purged himself by oath of the crimes alleged, and having given the Roman people counsel about electing Charles as Roman Emperor: who also in the Basilica of St. Peter in the year 800 of the Christian era, on the very feast of the birth of Christ, proclaimed, anointed, and crowned the same as Roman Emperor. This translation of the empire made by the Pope, Cardinal Bellarmine wished to support in a special writing, nor does Blessed Luther deny it in his preface to the Apocalypse and in chapter 12, as well as in the marginal gloss. Dan. 2, 41. He did not, however, concede it, nor should it be conceded, in any other sense than that it was done by the persuasion and counsel of the Pope, who did not have it in his own hand, Rome having been held for 200 years under the power of the Lombards with the Bishop, and the Roman empire and its name in the East remaining with the Emperors even after Charlemagne; but that he anointed and crowned Charles, he did that by the concession of the people, not as Pope, but as the Roman Bishop, just as today Roman Emperors are anointed and crowned by the Archbishop of Mainz, the King of Denmark by the Archbishop of Copenhagen, and the King of Sweden by the Archbishop of Uppsala, without any axiom of Papal dignity or Oecumenical Episcopacy. Nor did Charles obtain any lands in Italy from the Roman Pope, who was Patrician of Rome and Lord in Italy and at Rome before he was declared King or Emperor of the Romans. to which dignity he was properly raised by the nobles of the empire and the Roman people, not by the Bishop, much less by the Roman Pope as such. Concerning which, let Blessed Luther's tract, 'Dass das Pabstthum zu Rom vom Teuffel gestifftet sey' (That the Papacy at Rome was founded by the Devil), adorned in the year 1545, part III, be read. Charles enters Rome, says Cluver in his Epitome of History, p. 682, at the end of the year 94 (according to those who began the new year at the feast of the Nativity), corrupted by bribery and promises, so that he would not exact punishment for crimes from the most filthy Pope. He is inaugurated there with the Sicilian kingdom, and having exhausted the resources of the Neapolitan kingdom, he imposes garrisons upon it. Whether the eternal city is the name of blasphemy that occurs here, let the philologists see. Concerning which also Prosper in 'De dimidio temporis', book 7: 'When that which is temporal is called eternal, it is a name of blasphemy.' They also called it a Goddess, as can be seen in Martial, 'Goddess of the lands and moon of the nations'. They erected a temple to him, which was made by the Smyrnaeans, as Tacitus testifies in Annals IV. The Caesars did not refuse to be called Gods, Divine, and August, although they were mortals, says Prosper again in the same place, even though Kings are spoken of in that way, and suppliants say to him, 'To your Divinity, to your altars, to your perpetuity,' etc., which vanity, not truth, has handed down, and those things are execrable. For these things are owed to the eternal God. But what is this to the idolatry which Grotius wishes to be understood as not the city itself, because Rome is called the eternal city? But although ancient Rome expressed that form most expressly in all respects, it is nevertheless sufficient that by these signs Rome itself and the Papal Roman Empire are sufficiently betrayed. The overthrow of the Roman Empire certainly happened in the time of Augustulus, and thus, as Tertullian speaks, its departure into ten Kings, or dissipation into several kingdoms; yet the modern German empire imitates its form in a certain way, whence it is called its image. There is still enough blasphemy in the city, which is notorious not only to the old, but also to the new. God is blasphemed, the Divine power, Christ, whom the little priests are able to create daily, the kingdom and people of Christ, the Divine law, which is believed to be imperfect and corrupted in the Pharisaic manner at Rome, and what not? They call Mary Lady in the Marian Psalter of Bonaventure, even in those places where the name יהוה is used, as in Psalm 30, 'In you, O Lady, have I hoped,' Psalm 50, 'Have mercy on me, O Lady': Which Psalter was confirmed by Sixtus IV and Innocent VIII; they say that the τρισάγιον was acclaimed to her by the Angels, Antoninus part IV, Title 15, chapter 44, to the throne of God

Osorius, Vol. III, p. 139, applies to him what was said concerning the eternal generation of the hypostatic wisdom; the same Osorius and Blasius Viegas, in Apoc. 12. I know, they say, in the Antidotarium animae, that you can do all things that you wish, you who are mercy itself; the most strong tower, says Bernardin de Busto in his Mariale to Alexander VI, is the name of the Lady, to her the sinner will flee, and he will be saved: and in Marial. Book II, part 1, ch. 24. If Mary is for us, who is against us? If she justifies, who shall condemn? Salvation is sometimes swifter by the mentioned name of Mary than by the invoked name of Jesus, as is held in the book on the excellence of the Virgin by Anselm and in the Thesaurus praecon. Deipar. in the year 1539. Blasius de Viegas in Apoc. p. 543, did not hesitate to praise that of Gerson: That God had given half of his kingdom to the Virgin Mary, and that God, while retaining his power, had in a certain way yielded the mercy of God to the mother and queenly spouse: And therefore, that the Virgin has a divided empire with God. Vincentius Pimpinella, Archbishop of Toulouse, Apostolic Nuncio to Ferdinand, King of Hungary and Bohemia: You Key-bearer (Peter), open the hard and marble hearts of Princes and of all men whatsoever. You Sword-bearer, vessel of Election (Paul), cut, separate, and shake off from the breasts of mortals their unheard-of hardness: come in the clouds of heaven, scatter the nations that desire wars against the Christians; convert both the Simon Maguses, the Attilas and the Totilas, as many as there are, and recall them to the original faith of Christ. What? That the idolatry and blasphemy of the Papists becomes evident in breviaries, Rosaries, books of hours, Antidotaries, Antiphons, Collects, Mariales, Processionals, Missals, Rituals, and similar public writings sanctioned by Papal authority, Apostolic Briefs, and Papal Bulls; the denomination of which the Roman Catholics could not bear at all in the Colloquy of Thorn, when I called them into use for the principles of clarifying Roman Catholic doctrine, because they could be evidently convicted from that by the very daily practice of the Roman Catholic Church concerning superstitions, idolatries, and public blasphemies, so that they even seized upon that as an occasion for breaking off the colloquy, lest their venerable things be openly detected, namely, how they do not fear to seek from Mary and the Saints the remission of sins, reconciliation with God, the bestowing of grace and of gifts through grace even spiritual, the illumination of minds, understanding of Scripture, defense from enemies, liberation from the power of Satan, and help in the hour of death. In the Missal of the Church of Toul these things are read: O happy mother, cleanse our sins, by the right of a Mother command the Redeemer, etc.

How and how often cruelty has been a companion to the Roman Papal empire, and the nature of lions and bears, from which those who presided even had their names, is not easily unknown to anyone. For they even raged against their own bowels. Sergius III bound his predecessor Christopher in stricter custody, and disapproved of the deeds of Formosus, to such an extent that he ordered his exhumed corpse to be subjected to capital punishment and thrown again into the Tiber: Which they say was later found by fishermen and brought into the Basilica of the Apostles, and, if it is lawful to believe, was received by the images of the Saints with a reverent bowing of their heads. This Sergius begot Pope John XI from the prostitute Marozia, according to the testimony of Liutprand. With the leaders of the Christian law thus raging against one another, the Hungarians were sent by God as avengers. For they, having been led to Ticinum by plundering, killed Berengar, then King of Italy, who was supported by immense forces, at the river Breme with a huge slaughter: Part of them devastated Italy, part Germany most extensively. Let the epitome of Cluverius in Epit. Histor. p. 465 be read. Thus Romanus I, according to Platina, disapproved of the acts of his predecessor Stephen; Theodorus, the successor of Romanus, by defending the acts of Formosus, stirred up such a sedition that it was very little short of a just battle; having gone to Ravenna, he rescinded the sanctions of Stephen in a council; such things historians suggest in countless numbers. Nor do they bear less testimony concerning the impiety and frauds of the Pontiffs, that Hildebrand ascended the Papacy by simoniacal arts, but that having taken the body of the Lord he brought upon himself a sudden death, if he arrived at the Papacy in that way, and finally that the ex-Pope confessed his crimes before death, as B. Cluverius noted from Sigebert and Brenno the Cardinal. Concerning Paschal: Nothing, he says, milder toward Henry than his predecessors, he takes care to be persuaded by his son Henry the Younger, that he should prefer the obedience sworn to the Church, as they called it, to the subjection sworn to his Father, little mindful of how no sanction of Divine law constitutes a son the avenger of a father's guilt. The Pontifical Legate insisted to the disarmed and most brave Prince that he should confess that Hildebrand and the Pontifical Majesty had been unjustly violated by him. Concerning Alexander VI, to reduce Jerome Savonarola of Florence to ashes with his associates at the instigation of the Pontiff, whose horrible crimes and tyranny he was criticizing. To the man, famous for the holiness of his life and his predictions, was imputed the crime of stirring up dissension in the Republic, a charge accustomed to be leveled against the other Apostles, the witnesses of Christ. Nor indeed was Alexander VI any better than Caiaphas, as the Pontifical historiographers testify (Guic. book 1, Volater. book 23, Anthr. Onuphrio) First, the Cardinals, from whom he had bought the Pontificate, were variously condemned by him, and paid, as Onuphrius says, the due penalties of their wicked zeal and venal suffrage. Then, having pursued the Orsinis with war for one summer, when he brought back nothing from it except disgrace, he received them back into favor. Then he strove uniquely to flaunt his bastards openly, following the example of Innocent, and to heap honors and riches upon them with all discipline cast aside. Lucretia, his daughter, having been taken away from the Spaniard to whom she had been married, he bestowed upon three Princes, first to John Sforza of Pesaro, then to Louis of Aragon, thirdly to Alfonso d'Este, Duke of Ferrara, against right and law, while at the same time he himself held her in loves and delights, the sons being rivals of the father: Whence Pontanus and Sannazaro joked in verses about these crimes. Pontanus:

Lucretia lies in this tomb, by name, but in reality a Thais, the daughter, wife, and daughter-in-law of Alexander.

Actius Sannazaro:

The Roman priest, having promised heaven and the stars, opens a path to the Styx through crimes and slaughters.

And the same on Lucretia:

Therefore Sextus will always desire you, Lucretia! O fate of a dire Divinity, this is the Father.

From his illegitimate children, he made the youngest Prince of the kingdom of Sicily; the middle one, Caesar Borgia, a Cardinal; the eldest, Duke of Gandia in Spain. But the Cardinal ordered him to be killed by ambush while wandering at night and thrown into the Tiber. After his death, spurning the priesthood and desirous of ruling, he betook himself to Gaul with a great force of gold and furnishings. It cannot be told in a few words how much deceit and slaughter the Pontiff and his son perpetrated in order to fulfill their execrable desires. Volaterranus, Guicciardini, Jovius, and Onuphrius following them, let these be suitable witnesses.
