Philo rem eandem explicans dicit: Τῶν εἰς δελείαν τῶν χει- ροκμήτων ἑαυτὲς κατεσιζόντων σιδήρῳ πεπυρωμένῳ. Partes maxime frequentes corporis, quibus aut literæ, aut signa, aut numeri imprimebantur, erant frons & illa junctura inter manum & brachium. Frontis notandæ mos ex Oriente, ubi servi in fronte gerebant Dominorum nomina, ut nosci possent. Ostendimus id supra VII. 3. Vide & IX. 4. & Plutarchum Nicia in fine: ubi est σίζοντες ἵπποι εἰς τὸ μέ- τωπον. Dii autem sunt Domini sibi servientium, unde no- men בעלים, de parte altera testimonium est apud Luci- anum, de Dea Syria, ubi Assyrios dicit σίζεσθαι εἰς καρπὸς. Is mos ductus à militibus. Nam σίγματα ἐσι τῶν ςρατευομένων ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν, ait Julianus: punctis signorum scriptos mili- tes Vegetius l. 8. Idem σφραγῖδα τῆ ςρατιώτε vocat Chryso- stomus ad Romanos IV. 11. Ad imitationem militum notati fabricenses. Stigmata hoc est nota publica fabricensium bra- chiis ad imitationem tironum infligantur, ajunt Imperatores L. Stigmata C. de Fabricensibus. Notati & aquarii & aqua- rum custodes, quos hydrophylacas nominant, qui omnium a- quaductuum hujus Regiæ urbis custodes deputati sunt, singulis manibus eorum felici nomine pietatis nostræ impresso signari de- cernimus. L. Decernimus C. de Aquæductu. Idem autem est brachia signari aut manus: quia signum imprimebatur parti ei, quæ est inter manum & brachium, τῷ καρπῷ ut jam dixi- mus. Uterque modus signandi mansit in Africa & Oriente. Vide Leonem Afrum lib. IV. ubi de Broscha.

Et tractatu priori: Vers. 16.

Καὶ ποιεῖ πάντας τὲς μικρὸς, καὶ τὲς μεγάλες, καὶ τὲς πλυσίες, καὶ τὲς πτωχὸς, καὶ τὲς ἐλευθέρες, καὶ τὲς δύλες, ἵνα δῶσιν ἀυτοῖς χαράγματα, & faciet omnes pusillos, & magnos & divites & pauperes & liberos & servos habere characterem] Hoc quoque magia exemplo suo obtinuit, ut essent sodalitates nobilium, equitum, plebejorum, li- bertinorum, servorum Romæ, in provinciis, in coloniis & municipiis, quæ sodalitates suam quandam habebant pe- culiarem notam. Exemplo sint Dendrophori Carthagine ex tali nota sive professione gentilitia, ut loquitur lex XX. C. Theod. de Paganis, sacrificiis & templis. Fuere tales & Romæ, Comi, Veronæ, & alibi, ut ostendunt inscripti- ones, inter eas quas Gruterus edidit p. 14. 175. 261. 350 438. 494. Vetuit quidam Trajanus edicto hetærias, ut videre est apud Plinium l. X. epist. 97. sed excipiebantur ab eodem edicto collegia, quæ religionis, paganicæ scilicet, causa coibant l. 1. §. sed religionis D. de collegiis. Tali- um collegiorum, & quidem circa hæc maxime tempora plurima mentio in Gruterianis inscriptionibus: vide in- dicis cap. 4. legendum hic ἀυτοῖς, id est sibimetipsis, aut ἀυ- τοῖς eo sensu sumendum. Veteres libri adspirationes adscri- ptas non habebant. Et sic hunc locum explicat Arethas. Ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς ἀυτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς, in dextra manu sua] imitatione militum: Στίγματά ἐσι τῶν ςρατευομένων ἐν ταῖς χερσί, puncturæ militum sunt in manibus, ait Ælianus. Hoc ipsum σφραγῖδα τῆ ςρατιώτε signum militis vocat Chrysostomus ad Romanos IV. vers. 11. Punctis scriptos milites dixit Vegetius. Sic & stigmata, hoc est, notæ publicæ, fabricensium brachiis ad imitationem tironum inflicta, L. stigmata C. de fabricensibus. Sic & Zeno Im- perator aquarum custodes nomine suo manibus eorum impresso signari voluit, ut eo signo militiæ quodammodo sociarentur L. decernimus. C. de Aquæductu. Η ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων ἀυτῶ, aut in frontibus suis] id ma- xime in Oriente factum puto, ubi mos, servos in fron- te signari, non pœnæ causa, ut apud Romanos, sed ut noscerentur eorum Domini. Vide de Babyloniis He- sychium voce ἱεράνια & Σαμίων δῆμῷ. Ad eum mo- rem alludit Ezech. IX. 4. In eum modum corporati isti aliquem Deorum sibi tanquam Dominum mancipia in- scribebant. Meminit Philo I. de Monarchia τῶν εἰς δελείαν τῶν χειροκμήτων ἑαυτὲς κατασιζόντων σιδήρῳ πεπυρωμένῳ

corum, qui ferro ignito notabant auctorabantque operibus humanarum manuum.

Annon vero etiam ante Apollonium ortumque magiæ ipsius Romæ sodalitates tales quoque, ut à Philone notatæ fuere? Thomas characterem bestiæ intelligi posse ait professionem illiciti cultus q. 63. art. 3. quæ in Papatu notoria, etiam cum notis quibusdam expressis, signo crucis, chrisma- te confirmationis, quæ fronti imprimitur, unctio sa- crificulorum in manu dextra, vel character indele- bilis cum tonsura, sine quibus nullum cum bestia haberi potest commercium, sive officiorum sacro- rum, sive beneficiorum. Et hoc modo quoque ex- plicant characterem in manu Augustinus l. 20. de C. D. c. 9. Primasius, Ticonius, Lyra, Thomas, B. Nicolai, B. Winckelmannus, B. Cluverus, Pa- reus, Ribera, ut sit operatio; characterem vero in fronte, ut sit professio, ille sit Pater nostrum orbi- culare in catena, hic chrisma sacerdotale vel con- firmationis. Sodalitates vero & hetærias quis de- siderabit, ubi omnia plena claustris & monasteri- is ac confraternitatibus? Non autem proscripti fu- ere olim Christiani, quotquot alicui sodalitati sa- cræ nomen suum non dedissent; nec præscriptio exprimitur uspiam per negatam emendi vel venden- di facultatem. Notum autem est, in Papatu ex- communicari per Bullam Cænæ Dom. omnes, qui commercium ullum,etiam in rebus ad bellum perti- nentibus habent cum hæreticis: nec tutum esse in Hispania & Italia negotiari, propter inquisitionis sævitiam, nec Mechtildis Angliæ Regina permisit id Pontifici Rom. haud addictis, teste Bertholdo. Cui etiam (commercio) cum Oriente Clemens V. & VIII. & Johann. XXII. interdixit, ac Martinus V. peculiari constitutione prohibuit domicilia te- nere, contractus inire, negotiationes quaslibet exerce- re, aut humanitatis solatia cum Christi fidelibus habere: quamvis de jure Babylonis plane peculiari sermonem esse stigma ipsi proprium convincat, c. 18, 3. 11. 13. 15, quale est, quod beneficia & præben- dæ emantur & vendantur vicissim aliis, Canonicatus, pallia Episcopalia, indulgentiæ, taxæ pœnitentiariæ, reditus lupanarium, & dispensationes: nam dulcis odor lucri ex re qualibet, etsi spurca, Pontifici, ut alia sicco pede præteream. Et ad hanc imagi- nem bestiæ & characterem ejus facit, quod Ar- chi-Episcopi, Episcopi, Cardinales, Abbates, Do- ctores & Professores characterem in manu recipere, hoc est, juramento se obligare cogantur, etiam il- li, qui seducuntur ad Romanam Ecclesiam, qui- bus jurandum est, quod tot vel tot annorum spa- tio hæreticæ, impiæ & damnatæ doctrinæ Lutheri adhæserint, idque confitendum B. Virgini Mariæ, omnibusque Sanctis &c.

## 13:16
v. 16. And he causes the small, and the great, and the rich and the poor and the free, and the slaves] He well distributed those who were in the Roman empire into free and slaves, the free into rich and poor, the rich into those honored and those lacking honor.

The prior commentary on these matters holds as follows:

Latin:

v. 16. Καὶ ποιεῖ τὺς μικρὺς, καὶ τὺς μεγάλυς, καὶ τὺς πλυσί- υς κὶ τὺς πτωχὺς καὶ ἐλευθέρες, καὶ τὺς δύλες] Bene distri- buit eos, qui in imperio Romano erant in liberos ac servos, li- beros in divites & pauperes, divites in honoratos & honore carectes.

Prior commentatio de hisce ita habet:

## 13:17
vers. 17. And that no man might be able to buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name] He who was not enrolled in any college consecrated to the Gods, was by that very fact suspected of Christianity. But Christians were kept from the baths and the market: this is apparent from the edict of Diocletian in Eusebius. That part of the edict was traditional, that is, transcribed from the edict of Trajan. Orosius calls the Christians proscribed: Eusebius elsewhere: To be deprived of freedom. Thucydides also mentions such a punishment, V. And such injustice, that they might neither hold office, nor be masters in buying or selling. Three, as we have said, and here we see openly, were the ways of marking those enrolled in the colleges of the Gods: The first by a mark, that is, the badge of some God. The Etymologist Writer: Gallus the Philopator Ptolemy; because of the ivy leaves branded on him like the Galli. Therefore an ivy leaf was imprinted on the sodales of Father Liber. Such also were the Dendrophori, a gentile profession, as the Emperors speak in law Sacerdotales in the Theodosian Code concerning pagans. Such were in Carthage, Rome, Como, Verona and elsewhere, as can be seen in the Gruterian inscriptions on pages 14, 175, 261, 550, 438, 494. The second custom was of inscribing the very names of the Gods, such as Zeus, Ares, Dionysus, or in Syriac Sarna, Aziz, Baalat, Baal. The third custom was of placing a number, by which the name of GOD might be covered, having mystical letters, which collected would make such a number. Mention of such mystical names, that is, known only to the initiates, is in many places in Servius. The mystical name of the Sun reached the number of eight hundred and six, as Martianus Capella teaches us. It was noted thus XN. The name of the beast is the name of some God, to whom idolatry was serving.

Latin:

vers. 17. Καὶ ἵνα μή τις δύνηται ἀγοράσαι ἢ πωλῆσαι, εἰ μὴ ὁ ἔχων τὸ χάραγμα, ἢ τὸ ὄνομα τoῦ θηρίου, ἢ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τoῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ] Qui nulli collegio Diis sacrato erat adscriptus,is eo ipso suspectus eratChristianismi. Christiani autem τῶν βαλανείων καὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς εἴργοντο: apparet id ex Diocletiani edicto a- pud Eusebium. Ea pars edicti erat tralatitia id est transferi- pta ex edicto Trajani. ProscriptosChristianos dicit Orosius: Eusebius alibi: Ἐλευθερίαν ὑσερῆνθαι. Meminit talis pœnæ & Thucydides V. Ἀδικίαν δὲ τοιάσδε, ὥστε μήτε ἄρχειν, μή- τε πριαμένους ἢ πωλε͂ντας κυρίους εἶναι. Tres, ut diximus, & hic aperto videmus, modi erant fignandi adscriptos Deorum collegiis: Primus per χάραγμα, id est, insigne Dei alicujus. Etymologi Scriptor : Γάλλος ὁ Φιλοπάτωρ Πτολεμαῖος· διὰ τὰ φύλλα κισσοῦ κατεστίχθαι ὡς οἱ Γάλλοι. Hederæ ergo folium imprimebatur sodalibus Liberi Patris. Tales & Dendrophori, professio gentilitia, ut loquuntur Imperatores l. Sacerdotales C. Theodosiano de paganis. Erant tales Carthagine, Romæ, Comi, Veronæ & alibi, ut videre est in Gruterianis inscri- ptionibus paginis 14. 175. 261. 550. 438. 494. Alter mos erat inscribendi ipsa Deorum nomina, ut Ζεὺς, Ἄρης, Διόνυσος, aut Syriace סרנא, עזיז, בעלת, בעל. Tertius mos erat ponendi numerum, quo obtegeretur nomen DEI mysticum literas habens, quæ collectæ uumerum talem facerent. Nominum talium mysticorum, id est, non nisi mystis cognitorum mentio multis locis apud Servium. Nomen Solis mysticum ad numerum perveniebat octo & sexcentorum, ut nos docet Martianus Capella. Id sic notabatur XN. Ὄνομα θηρίου est nomen Dei alicujus, cui idololatria serviebat.

## 13:17
v. 17. And that no one might be able to buy or sell] That is the effect, that those who did not profess themselves to be worshippers of idols were interdicted from water and fire. Such was also the edict of Diocletian in later times: by which the Christians, as Eusebius speaks, were prohibited from the baths and the market. Elsewhere he says they were deprived of liberty, Orosius says they were proscribed. Unless he who has the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name,] By synecdoche through inclusion, that is, who would not in some way show that he belonged to some one of the Gods. And understand here by the beast the first, the first beast, that is, Roman idolatry. There were, however, three ways to be noted, for either some Hieroglyphic mark, such as a thunderbolt, trident, helmet, or caduceus was imprinted on them, signifying Jupiter, Neptune, Mars, or Mercury: or the names of the Gods themselves: or in place of the names that number, which the Greek letters of the name collected into a sum made up, which the Christians followed in their documents. The secret name of the Sun, known only to the initiates, made the number of eight hundred and six, as Martianus Capella teaches us. We learn from Servius that such mystical names also existed for other Gods. They were hidden by their numbers. v. 18. Here is wisdom] So below 17, v. 9. here is the mind that has wisdom, and here is the sense that has wisdom. That is said, where a thing, person, or some time is circumscribed by those marks, which are not vague, but certain and defined in testimony of divine providence. He who has understanding let him calculate) in the Greek manner, in which language this book was written. The number of the beast) Of the time, namely, in which idolatry, having been greatly wounded, resumed its strength, both by open force and by interdicting commerce and all dignities to Christians. For it is the number of a man) The name is that of a man, a prince, from whom, after liberty was stripped from the republic, times were mostly known. And his number is six hundred sixty six,]

O - 70 U - 400 L - 30 P - 80 I - 10

The name of Trajan was indeed Ulpius, as all histories teach us. And he is called so by the Greeks for the most part, even in the Greek inscription, which is in the Gruterian edition on page 60. But just as we today write the number six in this way, with a stigma at the end, namely, so the Ancients very often wrote C, which is a stigma, for the same six, as can be seen in the inscription made in honor of Daton, son of Philo, in the same Gruterian edition, page 327. or also in this manner S, in which way that mark is read in the Paschal Canon of Hippolytus, which was written in the times of Alexander Mammea; and likewise in many Manuscripts, among others of Ptolemy, in the royal library. Under Domitian, as everyone knows, the vexation of the Christians had been most bitter. Nerva by one edict abolished all the edicts of Domitian, among which were also those against the Christians, many of whom returned from exiles, as Eusebius notes in his Chronicle and history. Trajan revived cruelty with a new edict, in the tenth year of his principate, as the same Eusebius notes in Hist. III. 27. Augustine de Civ. Dei l. 18. c. 52, Sulpitius Severus lib. hist. 2, and Orosius l. hist. 7. c. 12 count this as the third persecution of the Christians. To these may be added the well-known letter of Pliny concerning the punishments of the Christians, and Tertullian in his Apology. From that edict, Simon son of Cleophas, Bishop of Jerusalem, was crucified: Ignatius, Bishop of the Church of Antioch, was thrown to the beasts at Rome, as noted by Eusebius in both cases. It is also noted in the monuments of the Church that Onesimus, Bishop of Ephesus, and Anacletus, Bishop of Rome, met death for Christ by the same edict. Both Irenaeus and Arethas hold it as beyond controversy that it is the Roman Emperor who is indicated by this number. The same thing happened to many of the ancient Christians as to the Jews. The Jews refer what was said in Daniel concerning Antiochus, and long since fulfilled, as noted by Josephus, to much later times; some of them even now expect their outcome, as can be known from their writings and discourses. Not a few Christians always expected as future things that had been predicted by Paul and by John, which had an end not so long after their own times, or later; and when they did not see the things they had pictured in their minds, they wished for the same to be expected by their successors, with the time always postponed. Tertullian already believed in the times of Severus that time was in a collection, that is, that little remained until the end of the world. The same Tertullian believed and wrote in his Apology that such force would come upon the world as soon as the Roman Empire had ceased to be. The same concerning the resurrection of the flesh: the departure of the Roman Empire, he says, dispersed into ten Kings, will bring on the Anti-Christ. Then he believed would follow the prerogative of the first resurrection and a thousand years of earthly happiness, which the universal resurrection is to follow. In his book on flight in persecution, he adds that the Anti-Christ is already imminent. He did not believe that the world would last until the times in which Lactantius lived. Lactantius, so much later, in book VII of his Divine Institutes, c. XXV, says that the fall and ruin of things will be shortly, except that with the City intact, nothing of that kind seemed to be feared. Doubtless, he too, no less than the ancients, was expecting the destruction of the Roman city as if it were near, and from that the Anti-Christ, and immediately the end of things, the first resurrection, and after a thousand years new evils, and then the second or universal resurrection. He adds more boldly that all expectation seems to be of no more than two hundred years, and he says that the world will fall with the destruction of that light, that is, of Rome. And indeed, his conjecture of time did not deceive him much concerning the burning of Rome. The event shows how much he and Jerome, to Gerontia, and others erred concerning the end of the world. No more explored are the things they say about the Anti-Christ, collected from different places in Scripture that are about other matters, by conjecture, with the Jews as guides, whom they often follow in their prophecies of future things. For even by the Jews, the Anti-Christ, who is called by them ארמילוס Armilus, is believed to be about to conquer shortly before the ruin of the world. In a similar way, and with the same Jews as authors, Christians thought that Elijah would return around the same times, and many still think so now, nor do they see that what Malachi had said about the coming of Elijah, the sole foundation of that opinion, is explained by Christ himself in a figurative sense concerning John the Baptist. Therefore, just as they expected that what had long since been fulfilled concerning Elijah would happen, so also they applied to that Anti-Christ whom they were expecting what John had said in his epistle περὶ τῆ Ἀντιχρίστε, what Paul had said about him who was to seat himself in the temple of God, and about him who was to deceive many with signs and wonders, and what were found in the Apocalypse concerning the man having a name with the numbers ͵IϚCLXVI. ἰσόψηφον, they reported on the basis of mere conjecture. In which matter it is no more surprising that they were deceived than in that other divination concerning the return of Elias, and in many others, which one may see in Irenaeus, who, mixing the sayings of Daniel, already long since fulfilled, with the obscure passages of the Apocalypse, imagines wondrous things, τερατεύεται.

It is to be observed here 1. that that name does not properly pertain to the first but to the second beast; B. Nicolai & Napier assign it to the first beast; Osiander & Wolterus to the second: Although the matter comes to almost the same thing. 2. This name of the beast with the mark on the forehead and hand are the same for Alcafar, Colladon, Piscator, Diestius, Gerhard, but different for Cotterius. 3. That the healing of the wound falls not in the times of Trajan but of Vespasian. 4. Nor that idolatry, previously broken, resumed its strength under Trajan, but that the blood of the martyrs provided a seedbed for the Church. 5. That the last letter in the word οὔλπιος, which is sigma, is rashly confused with ϛ, the sign of the number six, in arithmetical calculation, since ο equals 70, υ 400, λ 30, π 80, ι 10, ο 70, ς 200, according to the Greeks' custom of numbering, from which the name of the beast χξ̅ IɔC L X V I does not emerge, but IɔCCCLX. just as in the word of Irenaeus ἔυαντας, and the name Νεῖλος, which makes up the number of the days of the year 365, it is established that the signs 200, as also in the name of Basilides ἄβραξας, are valid. Sigma, whether in the middle or at the end and however it may be written, is not taken otherwise among the ancients, but always in the same way. 6. The name Ulpios was common to many: Why therefore should it be used over another which was proper to Trajan, when a certain person was to be designated 7. The name λατεῖνος, which Irenaeus in book V and Aretas in this place assume, exactly makes up the number 666, and thus expresses the name of the beast, which is deservedly so called, inasmuch as, sitting in Latium, using the Latin language in sacred rites, even if it is not understood by the common people, in the mass, prayers, litany, the citation of the Biblical codex, and every cult which the Roman Pontiff ordained and employs, and they do not allow anyone to die unless in Latin; everywhere preferring the Latin Vulgate to the authentic Hebrew and Greek text, and decreeing it to be preferred; and the time of its rise, which is to be referred to about the year of Christ 666, around which Boniface III obtained the title of universal Bishop with Phocas granting it. This word also has the most recent kingdom. For they are Latins who now reign. It also has the same name Τείταν, but this number of the name (he says) he shows, so that we may beware of him who is coming, knowing who he is. But he kept silent about the name, because it is not worthy to be proclaimed by the Holy Spirit. And since he will go into perdition as if he were not, so neither is his name proclaimed. For the name of that which is not is not proclaimed. It is possible to find many according to the blessed Hippolytus and others, names containing this number, both appellative and proper. Proper, such as lampetes, teitan from teino according to Hippolytus, teinos similarly through a diphthong, Benedictus by imitation perhaps truly blessed by Christ, but appellative, evil guide, ancient sorcerer, true harmful, unjust lamb, etc., says Andreas Caesar: To which similar ones occur in Aretas: Thus Primasius wishes the name to be in the number, and likewise he also produces the mark arnamai Greek and anemos, because they were Greeks to whom the Apostle wrote. Irenaeus adds that the number 666 is included here because it is a recapitulation of his entire apostasy, which was done in the space of 6000 years. For in as many days, he says, as this world was made, in so many thousands of years it is completed. On the name of the beast, says Schwarez in book V on the Anti-Christ. ALL teach that it will be such that it consists of letters which, reduced to the ratio of numbers according to the custom of the Greek language, contain the number 666. Nor does King James of England fix the number of years otherwise than in Benedict II, who introduced and obtained what he had exceeded of the Emperor's power over the Pontiffs, so that the election of these no longer needed Imperial confirmation, in which he established the liberty of the Roman Church, Baronius at the year 648, no. 1. Through the number of the name of the beast, the Gloss. ordin. and Thomas [understand] the remuneration of the Anti-Christ, the highest degree of knowledge of Canon law, Fr. Junius, the simulation of Papistic religion of Nicolai, the impiety of Medus, the human nature of the beast of the Gloss. interlin. Thomas, Gerhard, the Vinarienses, Döling, the time of the destruction or ruin of Rome A.D. 1666. A certain anonymous person found in London, who understands the name of the Pontiff or the beast, that is, the Anti-Christ, either proper or appellative, from the order or value of the letters of the Alphabet entering the name. But most interpreters side with Irenaeus, and besides those brought forward, Bellarmine, Barradius, Ribera, Cornelius à Lapide, Pareus, Nigrinus, Osiander, Flacius, Gerhard, Hoë, Heilbrunner, Höpfner, Gravius, Kromejer, Danhawer, Döling, Dürfeld can be added, and they bring forward these names especially, Θεός εἰμι ἐπὶ γαίης, ἡ κίσπα ἡ παπική. See Colladon. But that number is also found in the numeral signs of the Latins or Romans received in the age of John, joined together DCLXVI, besides which they have none, for the sign CIɔ is composed of two, and it is found in others pertaining to this, e.g., CoDeX LatInVs EX CarDInaLatV. DeCLaratVs PontIfeX. AnnVLI pIsCatorII DIVInator. In CatheDra PetrI ApostoLI hæres SpIrI- tVs orbIs pestIs. FILIVs per DItIonIs In BabeLe noVa. FILII DeI VICarIVs. HæresIarCha fraVDVLentVs. PoterloCLeptes eXhorrenDVs. TransVbstantIator CVLpanDVs. Add here certain proper names of Pontiffs, and the jest about the Jesuits, the chief pillars of the Papacy. Pareus adds the name ב ע ל ל א ר מ י נ ו ס ו ע ס א י ט א (666. 1. 9. 10. 1. 60. 70. 10. 60. 6. 50. 10. 40. 200. 1. 30. 30. 70. 2. Lindanus Martin Lauter, but he ineptly drags it here. For this name contains 1056, and if D is added or DoCtor 1556, or 1656. But what do these have to do with the Johannine number? GeLasIus seCVnDVs. Alexander VI. D. Calixtus. Paul V. Vice God. Ignatius Loyola, basis of the Devil & the Papacy. The fraud and deceit of the Spaniard Ignatius Loyola. The Jesuits are the iniquitous cohort of the Devil. The Jesuits are certainly the Devils themselves. You will find more such wordplay in the Leipzig Disputation of M. Praetorius, such as from the Hebrew language ר כוענוש & פפע רומיית : רוכוענוש and other Greek ones, Τεῖταν Sol, παράδοσις tradition, Εκκλησία λατίνα, ἰταλικὰ ἐκκλησία, & Belgica, De Paawest; in most of which, however, except for the fact that St. John wrote in Greek, not Hebrew or Latin, some things are deservedly to be desired, because they are written less elegantly or mix the Greek and Latin languages, with the exception perhaps of the last ones. These things teach, however, how truly the Jesuit Thyraeus wrote in his dissertation on the Anti- Christ c. III. p. 26. It is a wonder that there have been wicked and insulting men against the Roman Pontiff, not only ours, but also heretics of all times: and yet until now none has been found who has discovered the number of the beast either in the proper name of one Pontiff, or in some common one: But he who, contradicting himself, does not wish to deny that the word τείταν can fall upon the Roman… see: is without doubt led by the authority of Innocent III, who in decret. Gregor. l. 1. tit. 33. de major. & obed. C. solitæ ad Const. Imper. did not hesitate to write thus: You ought to have known that God made two great lights in the firmament of heaven: 1. the greater light, that it might rule the day, and the lesser light, that it might rule the night; both great, but one greater. Therefore, for the firmament of heaven, that is, the universal Church, God made two great lights; that is, he instituted two dignities, which are the Pontifical authority and the Royal power. But that which rules over the days, that is, spiritual things, is greater. Carierus l. II. de potest. R. Pontif. cap. 12. Such is the proportion between the supreme Pontiff and the Emperor, as is between the sun and the moon. But the sun is far more excellent and eminent than the moon; and the latter borrows splendor and light from the former. Therefore the Pope is more eminent than the Emperor, and the authority of the emperor depends on the supreme Pontiff. Bellarm. de potest. summi Pontif. adversus Barclai cap. XIII. Innocent III rightly compared the Pontifical power to the sun and the Royal power to the moon.

8. That the name is the same as the character, that is, of the beast, not of a monadic person, whose image the mutilation of idols is, but Grotius himself acknowledges that χάραγμα is not Trajan's. Neither captivity nor the sword could be denounced to Trajan, who is known to have died a dry death. Beat. Gravius is singular here in the explanation of the two: By these two horns is understood the Spanish empire, in the two most powerful provinces, Spain and Italy, which indeed above v. 1 are also called heads, but here are called horns on account of their power. This very thing is confirmed in Ap. XVII. 9. Where it is said that of the seven heads (of the Anti-Christian Kingdom) five have fallen, that is, illuminated by the light of the Gospel, having shaken off the Anti-Christian yoke, they have admitted the free exercise of the Evangelical religion, namely Germany, Gaul, Britain, Hungary, Poland. There remain therefore of the seven heads or provinces only two, namely Spain and Italy (with respect to Sicily, Apulia, and Lombardy) which alone under the Spanish empire still champion the Anti-Christ, and defend him with all their might, admitting no exercise of the Evangelical religion. But what is said, that these two horns are like the Lamb, denotes that the Spanish kingdom, under the title of Catholic, bears a great show of holiness, and under the guise of the Christian religion, afflicts Christ in his members. It has a voice and speech like the Dragon, of whom it is said above v. 2, that he gave to the Papal beast his virtue, and his seat, and great power. The speech of the same Dragon is attributed to this two-horned beast, so that it may be signified that the Spanish empire holds the doctrine of Demons 2. Thess. II. 1. Tim. IV. and propagates it with all zeal through its LOJOLItas by means of feigned miracles, as will be clear from the following. And it exercises all the power of the first beast in his sight. For seeing the power and authority of the Pontiff and the Roman Church, that it has been greatly worn down and shaken by the voice of the Gospel through the ministry of B. Luther, it directs all its strength so that the Papacy may be restored, and its leaven and idolomania may be preserved. But it exercises this power in the sight of the first beast, that is, with the Roman Pontiff and his Prelates looking on and approving with applause, in whose favor the Emperor Charles V undertook the most disastrous persecutions against the Evangelicals, which his successors the Kings of Spain Philip II, Philip III, and Philip IV have continued to this very day, and have fought tyrannically for Papistic idolomania as if for altars and hearths, not without the destruction of many men; concerning which matter Sleidan, Thuanus, Metteranus, and other historians can be read. And it makes the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed, that is, in all lands and provinces, not only those subject to itself but also foreign ones, it attempts to propagate the Anti-Christian virus by violent means, and to force it upon Christians. The histories of previous years clearly testify that an infinite multitude of men has been forced to the veneration of the Anti-Christian beast through Spanish tyranny. It is well known that the Jesuits, emissaries of the Spanish Empire, boast of miracles. But as for what they do in making fire descend from heaven; it is not to be understood properly, but metaphorically, Luke XII. 29. I have come, says Christ, to send fire upon the earth: which he understands concerning the propagation of the Christian faith, of which the King of Spain is most studious, sending out Jesuits through the East, West, and South, who in America, India, and other most remote islands and regions preach the Gospel, not in the way and manner in which they are accustomed to propagate it in Europe, but according to the Apostolic practice, beginning from the fall of the Protoplasts, concerning the misery of man and the remedies for misery to be sought in Christ the Savior. Through this preaching of the Gospel (though done by an impure ministry, and contaminated by Papal traditions) the Holy Spirit is effective, and converts many. By this zeal the King of Spain gains for himself great authority in the whole world. He performs this through the Jesuits, the preachers of his miracles, who seduce many men fascinated by feigned miracles from the true faith, yet not without forced means or ample promises. He orders an image of the beast to be made v. 14. With every effort, the Spanish Empire strives for this: to restore the pristine form of the Anti-Christian beast, and that all should venerate the Roman Church with its Pontiff, as if it still held complete dominion over the lost heads. And it wishes that all should firmly imagine this for themselves. It animates the image of the beast and makes it speak, v. 15, that is, by its power it restores authority to the Roman see, and that the image of the beast may speak, that is, that the Pontiff may issue new decrees and thunderbolts of excommunication, and that everywhere in the world, through the work of the monks, Papistic doctrine may have great increases. It orders the killing of Christians who refuse to adore, that is, to venerate the Anti-Christian beast. A general INQUISITION was introduced in Spain against Jews and Saracens; but in the progress of time, it was also usurped against Evangelical Christians, many thousands of whom, having been caught by the inquisitors, were killed on account of their confession of faith. Especially the character and name of the beast. For it compels men of every kind to confess by voice and hand that they are Roman Catholics, and that no one can travel or safely conduct trade in Spain who is unwilling to confess this. And to this very day, no one is permitted in Spain to confess that they are an Evangelical Christian, but it is necessary that they simulate being a Catholic if they wish to reside there safely.

Nomen vero Trajani erat Ulpius, ut omnes historiae nos docent. Et sic appellatur a Graecis plerumque, etiam in inscriptione Graeca, quae est in editione Gruteriana pag. 60. Sicut autem nos hodie senarium numerum sic scribimus, ut stigma in fine, scilicet, ita Veteres C, quod est stigma, saepissime scribebant pro eodem senario, ut videre est in inscriptione, facta in honorem Datonis Phi- lonis filii, in eadem Gruteriana editione, pag. 327. aut etiam hunc in modum S, quomodo ea nota legitur in Ca- none Paschali Hippolyti, qui scriptus fuit Alexandri Mam- meae temporibus; itemque in Manuscriptis multis, inter alios Ptolomaei, in bibliotheca regia. Sub Domitiano, ut omnes sciunt, acerbissima fuerat Christianorum vexa- tio. Nerva uno edicto omnia Domitiani edicta sustulit, inter quae & illa contra Christianos, quorum plurimi ab exiliis reversi, ut Eusebius in Chronico & historia notat. Resuscitavit saevitiam novo edicto Trajanus, anno prin- cipatus sui decimo, ut idem Eusebius notat histor. III. 27. Hanc Christianorum tertiam persecutionem numerant Augustinus de Civ. Dei l. 18. c. 52. Sulpitius Severus lib. hist. 2. Orosius l. hist. 7. c. 12. Quibus addi potest notissi- ma Plinii epistola de poenis Christianorum, & Tertullianus Apologetico. Ex eo edicto crucifixus Simon filius Cleo- pae Hierosolymorum Episcopus: Ignatius Antiochenae Ec- clesiae Episc. Romae feris objectus, notante utrumque Eu- sebio. Etiam Onesimum Ephesi Episc. & Romae Episc. A- nacletum, ex eodem edicto mortem pro Christo oppetiis- se, Ecclesiae monumentis notatur. Imperatorem autem Romanum esse, qui hoc numero notetur, & Irenaeus & Arethas pro minime controverso habent. Idem evenit multis veterum Christianorum quod Judaeis. Judaei, quae apud Danielem de Antiocho dicta sunt, & impleta pridem, ut Josepho notatum, alii ad multo seriora tem- pora referunt, quidam eorum eventum exspectant eti- amnunc, ut ex eorum scriptis sermonibusque datur co- gnoscere. Christiani non pauci, quae a Paulo, quaeque a Johanne praedicta, finem non ita longe ab ipsorum tem- poribus, alia posterius habuere, exspectarunt semper ut futura, & cum qualia sibi animo figuraverant, non vide- rent, exspectari eadem prolatato semper tempore a poste- ris suis voluere. Tempus in collecto esse, id est parum ad mundi finem restare, jam Severi temporibus credidit Tertullianus. Eam vim superventuram orbi, ut primum Romanum imperium esse desiisset credidit scripsitque in Apologetico idem Tertullianus. Idem de resurrectione carnis: Romani, inquit, imperii absessio in decem Reges di- sfersa Anti-Christum superducet. Tunc secuturam credidit primae resurrectionis praerogativam & mille annos terre- stris felicitatis, quam secutura sit universalis resurrectio. Libro de fuga in persecutione Anti-Christum jam instare adjicit. Duraturum mundum ad tempora, quibus vixit La- ctantius, ille non credidit. Lactantius tanto jam posterior lib. VII. Institutionum c. XXV. lapsum ruinamque rerum brevi ait fore, nisi quod incolumi Urbe nihil istiusmodi videretur esse metuendum. Nimirum & ille non minus quam veteres Romanae urbis excidium tanquam de pro- ximo exspectabat, inde Anti-Christum, statimque finem rerum, resurrectionem primam & post mille annos no- va mala, ac deinde resurrectionem secundam sive uni- versalem. Adjicit audacius omnem expectationem non amplius quam ducentorum videri annorum, luminisque illius, id est, Romae interitu mundum ait lapsurum. Et de Romae quidem incendio non multum eum fefellit tem- poris conjectura. De orbis terrarum fine quam ille & ad Gerontiam Hieronymus aliique erraverint, res ostendit. Nihilo magis explorata quae de Antichristo dicunt, colle- cta ex diversis & aliud agentibus scripturae locis conjecta- tione, Judaeis ducibus, quos saepe illi in rerum futurarum praesagiis sequuntur. Nam & a Judaeis Anti-Christus, qui ipsis ארמילוס Armilus dicitur, paulo ante rui- nam orbis terrarum victurus creditur. Simili modo iis- demque Judaeis autoribus Christiani circa eadem tempora Eliam rediturum putarunt, putantque nunc etiam multi, neque vident quae de Elia venturo dixerat Malachias, solus ejus sententiae fundus, ea ab ipso Chri- sto sensu figurato de Johanne Baptista explicari. Sicut igitur quod pridem impletum erat de Elia, futurum expe- ctabant, sic etiam quae Johannes in epistola περὶ τῆ Ἀν- τιχρίστε, quae Paulus de eo, qui in templum Dei se collo- caturus esset, deque illo, qui signis & prodigiis dece- pturus esset multos, dixerat, quaeque in Apocalypsi de homine nomen habente numeris ͵IϚCLXVI. ἰσόψηφον reperiebantur, ad illum quem expectabant AntiChristum, sola conjectura autore retulerunt. Qua in re non ma- gis mirum est si decepti sunt, quam in altera illa de Elia redituro ariolatione, inque multis aliis, quas apud Ire- næum videre licet, qui dicta Danielis jam olim impleta cum obscuris Apocalypseos permiscens mira, τερατεύεται, imaginatur.

Habet idem & nomen Τείταν, hunc autem numerum nominis (inquit) ostendit, ut caveamus illum ve- nientem, scientes quis sit. Nomen autem tacuit, quia dignum non est præconiari à Spiritu Sancto. Et quoniam in perditionem vadet quasi non sit, sic nec nomen ejus præconiatum est. Ejus enim quod non est, nomen non præconiatur. Πολλά ἐσιν εὑ- ρεῖν κατὰ τὸν μακάριον Ἱππόλυτον καὶ ἑτέρες, ὀνό- ματα τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῦτον περιέχοντα προσηγορικά τε, κ᾿ κυρία. Κυρία μὲν, οἷον λαμπέτης, τείταν ἐκ τῶ τεί- νω καθ' Ἱππόλυτον τεῖνος ὁμοίας διὰ διφθόγγε, Βενέδικτος κατὰ μίμησιν τυχὸν ἀληθῶς εὐλογημέ- νε τῶ χριστ̃, προσηγορικὰ δὲ κακὸς ὁδηγὸς, παλαι- βάσκανος, ἀληθὴς βλαβερός ἀμνὸς ἄδικος &c. in- quit Andreas Cæsar : Quibus gemina occurrunt apud Aretam: Ita Primasius in numero vult nomen esse, & pariter notam etiam producit ἀρνᾶμαι Græ- cum & ἄνεμος, quia Græci fuerint, ad quos scripse- rit Apostolus. Irenæus addit, ideo 666. numerum hic comprehendi, quia sit recapitulatio universæ apostasiæ ejus, quæ facta sit in 6000. annorum spatio. Quot enim diebus, inquit, factus est hic mundus, tot & millenis annis consummatur. De nomine bestiæ, inquit Schwarez l. V. de Anti-Chri- sto. OMNES docent, tale futurum esse, ut ex lite- ris constet, quæ ad rationem numerorum juxta Græ- cæ linguæ morem redactæ numerum 666. conti- neant. Nec aliter Jacobus Rex Angliæ nume- rum annorum figit in Benedicto II. qui quod fu- perat potentiæ Imperator. in Pontifices induxit & obtinuit, ne amplius horum electio confirma- tione opus haberet Imperatoria, in quo liberta- tem Romanæ Ecclesiæ constituit Baronius ad ann. 648. n. 1. Prætorii, utpote ex Ebræa lingua ר כוענוש & פפע רומיית : רוכוענוש Græcisque aliis Τεῖταν Sol παράδοσις traditio, Εκκλησία λατίνα, ἰταλικὰ ἐκκλησία, & Belgica, De Paawest; in quibus tamen plerisque omnibus, præterquam quod Græce scri- pserit S. Johannes, non Ebraice vel Latine, nonnul- la merito desideranda, quod minus concinne scri- pta vel linguas Græcam, & Latinam commisceant, exceptis forte ultimis. Docent autem hæc, quam vere scripserit Thyraus Jesuita dissert. de Anti- „ Christo c. III. p. 26. Mirum est in Romanum Pon- tificem fuisse improbos & contumeliosos , non „ nostros solum, verum etiam omnium temporum hæreticos : & tamen adhuc nullum esse inventum, „ qui numerum bestiæ aut in unius Pontificis no- mine proprio, aut in communi aliquo deprehen- „ derit: Qui vero, sibi ipsi contradicens, negare non vult, vocem τείταν in Rom. sedem cadere posse: sine dubio inductus autoritate Innocentii III. qui decret. Gregor. l. 1. tit. 33. de major. & obed. C. solitæ ad Con- stant. Imper. sic scribere non dubitavit: Nosse de- „ bueras, quod Deus fecit duo magna luminaria in „ firmamento cœli: 1. luminare maj9, ut præesset diei, „ & luminare minus, ut præesset nocti; utrumq; ma- „ gnum, sed alterum majus. Ad firmamentum igitur „ cœli, id est universalis Eccles. fecit De9 duo magna „ luminaria; id est duas instituit dignitates, quæ sunt Pontificialis antoritas, & Regalis potestas. Sed „ illa quæ præest diebus, id est, spiritualibus, ma- jor est. Carierus l. II. de potest. R. Pontif. cap. „ 12. Ea est proportio inter summum Pontificem & Imperatorem, quæ est inter solem & lurtam. Sed „ sol est valde præstantior ac eminentior luna; & hæc ab illo mutuatur splendorem, & lucem. Igi- „ tur Papa est eminentior Imperatore, & imperato- ris autoritas pendet a summo Pontifice. Bellarm. de „ potest. summi Pontif. adversus Barclai cap. XIII. Recte comparavit Innocentig III. potestatem Pon- „ tificiam soli & potestatem Regiam lunæ.

8. Ejusdem esse nomen, cujus est character, hoc est bestiæ, non monadicæ personæ, cujus imaginem mutilationem simulachrorum esse, χάραγμα ve- ro non esse Trajani, Grotius ipse agnoscit. Tra- jano nec captivitas nec gladius denunciari potuit, quem sicca morte cbiisse constat. Singularis hic in explicatione duorum est Beat. Gravius: Per duo hæc cornua intelligitur imperium Hispa- nicum, in duabus potentissimis provinciis Hispa- nia & Italia, quæ quidem supra v. 1. etiam capita, „ hic vero propter potentiam cornua nominantur. Confirmatur hoc ipsum Ap. XVII. 9. Ubi dicitur „ quod ex septem capitibus (Anti-Christiani Regni) quinque ceciderint, hoc est, luce Evangelii illu- „ strata, excusso AntiChristiano jugo liberum Ev- angelicæ religionis admiserint exercitium, videli- „ cet Germania, Gallia, Britannia, Hungaria, Po- lonia. Remanent igitur ex septem capitibus seu „ provinciis tantum duo, Hispania videlicet & Ita- lia (respectu Siciliæ, Apuliæ, & Longobardiæ) „ quæ sub imperio Hispanico solæ adhuc AntiChri- stum propugnant, & totis viribus defendunt, nul- „ lum Evangelicæ religionis admittentes exerciti- um. Quod autem dicitur, duo hæc cornua esse „ similia Agno, notatur regnum Hispanicum, sub titulo Catholici magnam præ se ferre sanctitatem, „ & sub specie religionis Christianæ, Christum in suis membris affligere. Vocem & loquelam ha- „ bet sicut Draco, de quo sup. v. 2. dicitur, quod be- stiæ Papali dederit virtutem suam, & sedem suam, „ & potestatem magnam. Ejusdem Draconis lo- quela tribuitur huic bestiæ bicorni, ut significetur „ Hispanicum imperium tenere doctrinam Dæmo- niorum 2. Thess. II. 1. Tim. IV. eamque fictis mi- „ raculis per suos LOJOLItas omni studio propa- gare, quemadmodum patebit ex sequentibus. „ Et potestatem prioris bestiæ omnem facit in con- spectu ejus. Videns enim potentiam & autorita- „ tem Pontificis & Ecclesiæ Romanæ, per vocem Evangelii ministerio B. Lutheri sumoopere attri- „ tam & labefactatam esse, omne robur eo dirigit, ut Papatus instauretur, & illius fermentum & idio- lomania conservetur. Facit autem hanc potesta- tem in conspectu prioris bestiæ, hoc est intuente & cum plausu approbante Pontifice Romano ejusque Prælatis, in quorum gratiam Carolus V. Imperator funestissimas contra Evangelicos susce- pit persecutiones, quas ipsius successores Reges Hispaniarum Philippus II. Philippus III. & Philip- pus IV. in hodiernum usque diem continuarunt, atque pro idolomania Papistica tanquam pro aris & focis non sine multorum hominum interitu ty- rannice pugnarunt; qua de re legi possunt Sleida- nus, Thuanus, Metteranus, aliique historici. Et facit terram & habitantes in ea adorare besti- am primam, cujus curata est plaga mortis, hoc est, in omnibus terris ac provinciis, non tantum sibi subjectis sed etiam alienis, violentis mediis virus Anti- Christianum propagare, & Christia- nis obtrudere conatur. Infinitam hominum mul- titudinem ad venerationem bestiæ AntiChristia- næ coactam esse per tyrannidem Hispanicam superiorum annorum historiæ luculenter testan- tur. De miraculis gloriari Imperii Hispanici emis- sarios Jesuitas, notissimum est. Quod autem igne faciunt de cælo descendere; non proprie, sed Me- taphorice intelligendum est, Luc. XII. 29. Ignem, inquit Christus, veni missurus in terram: quod intelligit de propagatione Christianæ fidei, cujus Rex Hispaniarum est studiosissimus, emittens Je- suitas per Orientem, Occidentem & Meridiem, qui in America, India, & aliis remotissimis insu- lis & regionibus prædicant Evangelium, non eo modo & ratione, ut in Europa idipsum propa- gere solent, sed secundum praxin Apostolicam, in- cipientes de lapsu Protoplastorum, de hominis miseria & miseriæ remediis in Christo Servatore quærendis. Per hanc prædicationem Evangelii (ab impuro quamvis ministerio factam, & tradi- tionibus Papalibus contaminatam) Spiritus S. est efficax, & multos convertit. Quo studio Rex Hispaniarum magnam sibi in toto orbe conciliat autoritatem. Præstat hoc per Jesuitas, miraculo- rum suorum prædicatores, qui multos homines fictis miraculis fascinatos à vera fide seducunt, non tamen sine coactis mediis vel amplis promissis. Imaginem jubet fieri bestiæ v. 14. Omni conatu hoc agit imperium Hispanicum, ut pristinam for- mam bestiæ AntiChristianæ restituat, & ut omnes venerentur Ecclesiam Romanam cum suo Ponti- fice, ac si integrum super amissa capita adhuc do- minium habeat. Et vult ut omnes hoc firmiter sibi imaginentur. Imaginem bestiæ animat & loqui facit v. 15. h. e. potentia sua reddit autoritatem sedi Romanæ, & ut imago bestiæ loquatur, h. e. ut Pon- tifex edat nova decreta & excommunicationis fulmina & ubique terrarum opera Monachorum doctrina Papistica habeat magna incrementa. Oc- cidi jubet Christianos detrectantes adorare, hoc est, venerari bestiam Anti-Christianam. Intro- ducta fuit in Hispania generalis INQVISITIO, contra Judæos & Saracenos; Sed progressu tem- poris usurpata etiam fuit contra Evangelicos Chri- stianos, quorum multa millia ab inquisitoribus de- prehensi ob confessionem fidei occisi fuerunt. Im- primis characterem & nomen bestiæ. Cogit e- nim omnis generis homines, ut voce & manu con- fiteantur, se esse Romano-Catholicos, & ut nemo in Hispania peregrinari vel mercaturam tuto ex- ercere possit, qui hoc confiteri nolit. Et in hunc usque diem nemini permittitur in Hispania con- fiteri se esse Christianum Evangelicum, sed neces- sum est, ut simulet se Catholicum, si tuto ibi subsite- re velit.

## 13:18
Verse 18.

Here is wisdom] In this you will see the wisdom of God, that just as that Prince, who is about to command these things, hid the names of the Gods with numbers, so Christ has now already designated his name through numbers. Take ὧδε as above XIII. 10. He who has understanding let him calculate the number of the beast] He who is wise, let him note the time of idolatry resuming its spirits and strengths. When that has happened, the foreknowledge of Christ will appear. For it is the number of a man] that is, that time is designated by the name of the Prince, just as now among the Romans times are accustomed to be denominated, which were once denoted by the Consuls. And his number is six hundred sixty six] ΟΥΛΠΙΟΣ is the most well-known name of Trajan. And it is written thus in the Greek inscription, which Gruter has on p. LX. That name makes the number IϘC LXVI. if at the end you write not Σ, which is worth two hundred, but ϲ, as we now always write at the end, or C. as not rarely in inscriptions. C. is placed for the number six in an inscription made in honor of Daton, son of Philo, in the Gruterian edition on page CCCXXVIII. and in many other inscriptions, which the excellent and most learned youth Isaac Vossius, son of the great man Gerard Vossius, pointed out to me. But Ϛ is always placed for the same number six in the Paschal Canon of Hippolytus and in the Manuscript of Ptolemy. Bede from the ancients: The first is Ϛ. which is called episemon, and is the mark of the number VI. In the Old Alphabet after the Catalecta of Virgil you have E Ϛ Z. Wherever the six is lacking for a number, it could not be marked otherwise than by C. or Ϛ. And rightly the same mark is placed at the end of numbers, which we are accustomed to place at the end of names. Moreover, the same number has something remarkable in units, tens, and hundreds. Thus the vow of Fabius Maximus for three hundred thirty-three sesterces. A denarius of the same amount according to Plutarch. But then the number six signifies the things of this world: as the number seven signifies the things of a better age.

The prior commentary of this was of this tenor.

Latin:

Vers 18.

Ὧδε ἡ σοφία ἐστὶν] In hoc videbis Dei sapientiam, quod sicut is Princeps, qui hæc imperaturus est, Deorum nomina numeris occultavit, ita Christus jam nunc per numeros nomen ejus designavit. ὧδε sume ut supra XIII. 10. Ὁ ἔχων νῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου] Qui sapit, notet tempus idololatriæ animos & vires resumentis. Ubi id evenerit, apparebit Christi præscientia. Ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστὶ] id est, tempus illud designatur per nomen Principis, sicut nunc apud Romanos tempora denominari solent, quæ olim à Consulibus denotabantur. Καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ] ΟΥΛΠΙΟΣ est nomen Trajani notissimum. Et sic scribitur in inscriptione Græca, quam habet Gruterus p. LX. Id nomen facit numerum IϘC LXVI. si in fine scribas non Σ, quod valet ducentos, sed ϲ, ut nos nunc semper in fine scribimus, aut C. ut non raro in inscriptionibus. C. n. pro senario ponitur in inscriptione facta in honorem Datonis Philonis filii in editione Gruteriana pag. CCCXXVIII. & in inscriptionibus aliis multis, quas mihi indicavit optimus & eruditissimus Juvenis Isaacus Vossius Viri summi Gerardi Vossii filius. Ϛ autem pro eodem numero senario semper ponitur in Canone Paschali Hippolyti & in Manuscripto Ptolomæi. Beda ex antiquis: Prima est Ϛ. quæ dicitur episemon, & est nota numeri VI. In Alphabeto Veteri post Catalecta Virgilii habes E Ϛ Z. Ubicunque senarius ad numerum deficit, is aliter signari non poterat, quam per C. sive Ϛ. Et recte in fine numerorum eadem ponitur nota, quam ponere solemus in fine nominum. Habet autem aliquid insigne numerus idem in singulis, denis & centenis. Sic Fabii Maximi votum de sestertium trecentis triginta tribus. Denarius totidem apud Plutarchum. Tum vero senarius numerus res hujus mundi significat: ut septenarius res seculi melioris.

Prior commentarius hujus erat tenor is.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The Lamb is seen on Mount Sion with the 144,000 having the name of the Father, and a huge voice is heard of virgins playing the lyre and singing a new song, which no one could learn except those virgins; moreover, those virgins are seen everywhere following the Lamb, blameless. Angels are also seen, one with the eternal Gospel, another announcing the fall of Babylon, a third intimating to those worshipping the beast and its image, and those receiving its mark, the drinking from the wine of the wrath of God; a heavenly voice is also heard concerning those dying blessed in the Lord, and the Son of Man is seen on a cloud with a sickle, with an angel, the harvest being instituted, and again by another, the clusters being demanded to be trodden in the winepress of the wrath. There are two parts. I. The vision of the Lamb with the virgins following him to v. 5. II. Of the diverse angels and the Son of Man to v. 20.

PART I. THE VISION OF THE LAMB WITH THE VIRGINS FOLLOWING HIM.

Ver. 1.

Καὶ εἶδον.] A new vision pertaining to the times of Trajan. Καὶ ἰδὺ ἀρνίον ἑςηκὸς ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σιών. ] On the mystical Mount Sion, that is, the heavenly palace. For Sion was the palace of David. See above XI, 19. Here also the article is missing, as above XIII, 11. Καὶ μετ' αὐτᾶ.] With him: in spirit, namely, as above IV, 4. Ἑκατὸν τεσσαράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες. ] That is, those converted from the Jews. For this number is the same which we had above VII, 4. It is gathered from the twelve numbers which are explained there. Ἔχυσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτᾶ κὶ τὸ ὄνομα τᾶ πατρὸς αὐτᾶ γεγραμ- μένον ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὑτῶν.] He opposes this to those idolatrous marks, concerning which it was treated above. And this figure signifies those who in the midst of evils professed the worship of God and Christ. For what we openly profess, that we are said to carry on our forehead. Thus there is 'verissima fronte' in Cicero. 'Frons animi janua' is in the same author. Aaron carried on his forehead קדש ליהוה, Exod. 39, 30. All Christians are in this equal to Aaron.

But why must this vision be restricted to the times of Trajan? Did not all the elect pertain to those things, whom the comparison of chapter 7 teaches to be designated, and the opposition of those whose names are not written in the book of life? To the vision of the beasts is opposed the vision of the Lamb, of the Babylonian harlot, and of the late one imitating the Lamb, the vision of the Virgins following the Lamb, and for the voice speaking great blasphemies is heard a chorus of those playing the lyre, celebrating: For the mark of the Anti-Christ are exhibited foreheads signed with the name of the Father, and consecrated to Christ, and the preaching of the eternal Gospel, the fall of Babylon, and the damnation of those receiving its mark, and the blessedness of those dying in the Lord is announced, with the imminent judgment of the Son of Man carrying the sickle of the harvest, and treading the clusters in the winepress of wrath, just as on the contrary, for those not bearing the mark of the beast, slaughter and proscription had been previously intimated. That Lamb is Christ, not slain in mystical Jerusalem, or seen at Rome, but on Mount Sion, that is, the Church, Heb. XII, and that a militant one, in which the new song concerning the slaughter and redemption of the Lamb, and our consecration as first-fruits to God and the Lamb, and a blameless life resounds. Of the holy virgins, namely, that is, of the faithful, who retain an uncorrupted faith and an immaculate life, or the virginity and chastity of faith and life, both following Christ, Matth. XVI, 28. 2. Petr. II, 21. 2. Cor. XI, 2. Eph. V, 26. Ose. II, 20. Apoc. XIX, 7. 8. Virgins are to be understood not only as chaste in body, but especially the whole Church, which holds a pure faith, as is held in 2. Cor. XI, 2. according to the Ordinary Gloss, Tuitiensis, and Wicelius in Demegor. fol. 57. such as were also the innocent children, in whose feast the Roman Church reads this text, because they are called the first-fruits of the Lamb: Blasius de Viegas and Tirinus understand this place as Apoc. VII, which they explain concerning the Virgins collected from the Jews; Jacobus Schopperus concerning all believers, they are not defiled with women, that is, they do not indulge in sins and carnal concupiscences, but crucify the flesh and the vices of this. The same number and the same signature of the faithful occurred also in Apoc. VII, nor yet are only those converted from the Jews designated here, just as neither there, but from the nations, tribes, tongues, and peoples, since the Jews were only one people, yet representing in the Old Testament the universal Church of the New Testament, indeed constituting one body with the same. That song no one could learn, that is, receive; for words of knowledge include affection, except the faithful, because no one can say Jesus is Lord without the Holy Spirit, who does not dwell except in the faithful, Joh. XIV, 17. 21. 1. Cor. III, 5. 16, 17. c. VI, 17. 19. c. XII, 3. 2. Cor. VI, 15. 16. Who are called blameless comparatively with respect to those who bear the mark of the Anti-Christ, and in a certain respect, as far as imputed righteousness is concerned, but not indeed inherent, which is only begun; nor free from stains, if it is considered legally, Job XIV, 4. Prov. XX, 9. Psal. CXLIII, 2. Phil. III, 7. Es. LXIV, 16. even if evangelically, insofar as it is covered by the garment of the righteousness of Christ, those Virgins are sincere and without stain, Esa. LXI, 10. Eph. V, 27. Apoc. III, 18. c. XIX, 8. nor is guile found in their mouth, v. 2. because they follow the Lamb, Es. LIII, 9. both by faith and by holiness, Matth. XI, 29. 1. 1 Pet. 1:16, 22, 23, namely in a reduplicative sense. For to follow the Lamb is to imitate him not only in the cross, but in doctrine, life, death, and readiness to die, and after life in the leading to the fountain of living waters, Rev. 7:17. Ps. 31:6. Luke 23:46. Acts 7:59. Luke 2:29. Phil. 1:23. Rev. 14:13. But beware of inferring from this, as the Papists do, the omnipresence of the saints, because Christ is omnipresent; for they only follow where they are led by him, not as if they themselves are present everywhere, because he alone, having been taken up into the communion of the divine nature and the hypostasis of the Son of God himself, constitutes one ὑφισάμενον with him.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Agnus in monte Sion cum 144000. nomen Pa- tris habentibus videtur, auditurque vox in- gens virginum cytharizantium, & novum canticum cantantium, quod nemo extra vir- gines illas discere poterat, videntur autem ubique virgines illæ agnum sequentes, incul- patæ. Videntur & Angeli, unus cum æterno Evangelio, alter casum Babylonis nuncians, tertius adorantibus bestiam & imaginem ejus, ac suscipientes characterem ejus inti- mans baustum ex vino iræ Dei; auditur quo- que vox cælestis de beatis in Domino morien- tibus, & conspicitur filius hominis, in nube cum falce angelo, messem institui, & rursus alio, botras in stagno iræ calcari postulante. Partes sunt duæ. I. Visio agni cum virginibus se- quentibus ipsum ad v. 5. II. Angelorum diversorum & filii hominis ad v. 20.

PARS I. VISIO AGNI CUM VIRGINIBUS ILLUM SEQUENTIBUS.

Vers. 1.

Καὶ εἶδον.] Nova visio ad tempora Trajani pertinens. Καὶ ἰδὺ ἀρνίον ἑςηκὸς ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σιών. ] In monte Sionis mystico, id est, cælesti regia. Nam Sion regia fuit Davidis. Vide supra XI, 19. Etiam hic articulus deest, ut supra XIII, 11. Καὶ μετ' αὐτᾶ.] Apud ipsum: animo nempe, ut supra IV, 4. Ἑκατὸν τεσσαράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες. ] Id est, conversi ex Judæis. Hic enim numerus idem, quem supra habuimus VII, 4. Colligitur ex duodecim numeris, qui ibi explicantur. Ἔχυσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτᾶ κὶ τὸ ὄνομα τᾶ πατρὸς αὐτᾶ γεγραμ- μένον ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὑτῶν.] Opponit hoc notis illis idolo- latricis, de quibus actum supra. Et significat hæc figura illos in mediis malis professos cultum Dei & Christi. Nam quod aperte profitemur, id dicimur in fronte præferre. Sic verissi- ma fronte est apud Ciceronem. Frons animi janua, est apud eundem. Aaron in fronte gerebat קדש ליהוה, Exod. 39, 30. Christiani omnes in hoc pares Aaroni.

Cur vero hæc visio ad Trajani restringenda tem- pora? Num electi omnes ad ea pertinuerunt, quos designari collatio c. 7. docet, & oppositio eorum, quorum nomina scripta non sunt in libro vitæ. Vi- sioni bestiarum visio Agni, meretricis Babylonicæ, se- raque Agnum imitantis, Virginum opponitur visio Agnum sequentium, & pro voce magnablaspheman- te auditur chorus cytharizantium, celebrantium: Pro charactere Anti-Christi exhibentur frontes si- gnatæ nomine Patris, & Christo sacratæ, ac prædica- tio æterni Evangelii, lapsus Babylonis, & damnatio characterem ejus suscipientium, ac beatitudo in Domino decedentium annunciatur, cum imminen- ti judicio Filii hominis falcem messis gerentis, ac botras in torculari iræ calcantis, quemadmodum ex adverso bestiæ characterem non gerentibus oc- cisio, ac proscriptio antea intimata erat. Agnus ille est Christus non in Hierosolyma mystica occisus, vel Romæ visus, sed in monte Sion, hoc est Ecclesia, Ebr. XII. eaque militante, in qua Canticum novum de occifione, ac redemptione Agni, nostrique in primi- tias Deo, & Agno consecratione, atque inculpatæ vitæ resonat. Virginum nempe sanctarum, hoc est, fide- lium, quæ incorruptam fidem & vitam immacula- tam, seu virginitatem ac castitatem fidei & vitæ, utra- que Christum sequentes Matth. XVI, 28. 2. Petr. II, 21. retinent. 2. Cor. XI, 2. Eph. V, 26. Ose. II, 20. Apoc. XIX, 7. 8. Virgines intelligendæ non solum corpore ca- stæ, sed maxime omnis Ecclesia, quæ fidem puram te- net, sicut habetur 2. Cor. XI, 2. secundum Gloss. am- ordinar. Tuitiens. & Wicelium in Demegor. fol. 57. quales & fuere pueri innocentes, in quorum festo Ecclesia Rom. hunc textum legit, quod primitiæ agni dicantur: Blasius de Viegas, & Tirinus intel- ligunt hunc locum, ut Apoc. VII. quem de Virgi- nibus ex Judæis collectis explicant; Jacobus Schopper- rus de omnibus credentibus, non sunt cum mulieri- bus coinquinati, hoc est, non indulgent peccatis & concupiscentiis carnalibus, sed carnem & vitia hu- jus crucifigunt. Numerus idem, & signatura eadem fidelium occurrebat & Apoc. VII. nec tamen tan- tum conversi ex Judæis hic designati, quemadmo- dum nec illic, sed e gentibus, tribubus, linguis & po- pulis, quum Judæi unus tantum populus fuerit, re- præsentans tamen in Veteri Testamento Ecclesiam universam Novi Testam. imo cum eodem unum corpus constituens. Canticum illud nemo discere, id est, suscipere; verba notitiæ enim includunt affe- ctum, poterat, extra fideles, quia nemo Jesum dicere potest Dominum sine Spiritu Sancto, qui non habi- tat nisi in fidelibus Joh. XIV, 17. 21. 1. Cor. III 5. 16 17. c. VI, 17. 19. c. XII, 3. 2. Cor. VI, 15. 16. Qui inculpati di- cuntur συγκριτικῶς respectu eorum, qui characte- rem Anti-Christi gestant, & κατά τι secundum quid, quantum ad justitiam imputatam, non vero inhæ- rentem, quæ tantum inchoata est; nec maculæ ex- pers, si legaliter consideretur, Job. XIV, 4. Prov. XX, 9. Psal. CXLIII, 2. Phil. III, 7. Es. LXIV, 16. etsi Evan- gelice quatenus tegitur veste justitiæ Christi, Virgi- nes illæ sinceræ sint & sine macula, Esa. LXI, 10. Eph. V, 27. Apoc. III, 18. c. XIX, 8. nec inveniatur dolus in ore ipsorum, v. 2. quia Agnum sectantur, Es. LIII, 9. tum fide, tum sanctitate, Matth. XI, 29. 1. Petr. I, 16. 22. 23, sensu nempe reduplicativo. Agnum enim sequi est eum non tantum in cruce, sed in doctrina, vita, mor- te, & moriendi promptitudine, ac post vitam in de- ductione ad fontem aquarum vivarum sectari, Apoc. VII, 17. Psal. XXXI, 6. Luc. XXIII, 46. Act. VII, 59. Luc. II, 29. Phil. I, 23. Apoc. XIV, 13. Cave autem infe- ras inde cum Papisequis omnipræsentiam Sancto- rum, quia Christus omnipræsens est, sequuntur enim tantum, quo ab ipso ducuntur, non ut ipse ubique adsunt, quia ipse solus in divinæ naturæ communionem & hypostasin ipsius Filii Dei susce- ptus unum cum ipso constituit ὑφισάμενον.

## 14:2
Verse 2. And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters.) Here are indicated the innumerable converts from the Gentiles, as was said above in 7:9. How great the number of Christians was in the times of Trajan can be known from the letters of Pliny. These also are heard by John as being placed in heaven, because their citizenship is there. You have a similar passage in Ezek. 43:2.

And the voice which I heard as of harpers harping with their harps.) That sound was indeed great, but modulated, and harmonious. כנר is translated as harping, Isa. 23:16. Harps are instruments of praise above in 5:8. You have a song in heaven also below in 19:2, and in the Chaldean and Greek versions at the aforementioned place in Ezek. 43:2.

Latin:

Vers. 2. Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολ- λῶν.) Hic indicantur conversi ex gentibus innumerabiles, ut dictum supra VII, 9. Quantus fuerit Christianorum numerus Trajani temporibus ex Plinii epistolis cognoscere est. Hi quo- que ut in cœlo collocati audiuntur ab Johanne, quia ibi est ipsorum πολίτευμα. Simile habes Ezech. XLIII, 2.

Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς κιθαρῳδῶν κιθαριζόντων ταῖς κιθά- ραις αὐτῶν.) Erat quidem magnus ille sonus, sed modulatus, καὶ ἐναρμόνιος. כנר vertitur κιθαρίζειν, Esa. XXIII, 16. Ci- tharæ instrumenta laudis supra V, 8. Cantum in cœlo habes & infra XIX, 2, & apud Chaldæum & Græcos dicto loco Ezech. XLIII, 2.

## 14:3
Verse 3. And they sing a new song.) A sign of joy, Isa. 42:9. Ps. 40:3. Those Christians who were Jews by nation rejoiced in exiles and persecutions, because they could suffer for the name of Christ, as the Apostles did of old, Acts 5:41.

Before the throne.) That is, in the presence of God. A metonymy.

And before the four living creatures.) In the presence of the spirits of those Apostles or Apostolic men, of whom above in 4:6; for they had all died in the times of which we are treating here.

And of the elders.] In the presence of those who presided over each church gathered from the Gentiles.

And no one was able to learn the song.) No man could understand the cause of such great joy.

Except the hundred and forty-four thousand.) Converts from the Jews, of whom above, endowed with the same Spirit as those converted from the Gentiles.

Those redeemed from the earth.) Redeemed, that is, freed from vices (as above in 5:9) from all parts of the Roman empire, which is denoted by the name of earth in this part of the Apocalypse. Here ἀπὸ is in that sense, as ἐκ in the stated passage V, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 3. Καὶ ᾄδουσιν ᾠδὴν καινήν.) Signum gaudii, Es. XLII, 9. Psalm. XL, 3. Christiani illi gente Judæi in exiliis & persecu- tionibus gaudebant, quod pati possent ob nomen Christi, ut olim Apostoli, Act. V, 41.

Ενώπιον τοῦ θρόνου.) Id est, coram Deo. Μετωνυμία.

Καὶ ἐνώπιον τῶν τεσσάρων ζώων.) Coram Spiritibus illorum Apostolorum aut Apostolicorum virorum, de quibus supra IV, 6. ii enim omnes obierant temporibus, de quibus hic agi- tur.

Καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων.] Coram illis, qui Ecclesiæ cuique collectæ ex gentibus præerant.

Καὶ ἐδεὶς ἐδύνατο μαθεῖν τὴν ᾠδήν.) Nemo hominum intel- ligere potuit tanti gaudii causam.

Εἰ μὴ αἱ ἑκατὸν τεσσαράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες.) Conversi ex Judæis, de quibus supra, pari donati Spiritu, quo illi ex gentibus conversi.

Οἱ ἠγορασμένοι ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.) Redempti, id est, à vitiis li- berati (ut supra V, 9.) ex omnibus partibus Romani im- perii, quod γῆς nomine in hac parte Apocalypseos denotatur. Est hic ἀπὸ eo sensu, quod ἐκ dicto loco V, 9.

## 14:4
Vers. 4. These are they who were not defiled with women.] Men, when the subject is idolatry, are compared to women: and therefore those things which belong to women are attributed to them; but μετὰ here signifies imitation. They were not defiled like the idolatrous nations. Μολύνεσθαι here is to be defiled, as in Zach. XIV, 2. in the Greek. To be defiled, however, here signifies to subject oneself to idols, as in Jer. III, 6. Ezech. XVI. and often elsewhere. That ὗτοι is to be taken as much of the Jews as of others converted to Christ.

For they are virgins.] The noun παρθένος is also feminine among the Greeks. But here it is applied to men for the reason I have stated. See also 2 Cor. XI, 2. Philo, in his book on the special laws, says that the mind is compared to a virgin when it keeps itself: holy and uncorrupted from pleasures and desires and fears, and evil things that beset it. He also called widows virgins in his book on Humanity.

These are they who follow the Lamb whithersoever he goes.] It is incorrectly written in some Codices ὅπε γὰρ ἂν ὑπάγῃ.] The sense is: They follow Christ, whithersoever he leads them, even to the cross. To go for to lead is a metonymy.

For these were bought by Jesus.] They are freed from vices, as above in 7.

From among men.] That is, from among men, they are exempted from the life of the rest of men.

The firstfruits to God and to the Lamb.] They are called firstfruits with respect to the Christians who are to be after them. See Rom. 16, 5. 1 Cor. 16, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 4. Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἳ μετὰ γυναικῶν ἐκ ἐμολύνθησαν.] Viri, ubi de idololatria agitur, comparantur fœminis: & propterea tribuuntur eis, quæ sunt fœminarum, μετὰ vero hic imitatio- nem significat. Non polluti sunt illi sicut gentes idololatri- cæ. Μολύνεσθαι hic est constuprari, ut Zach. XIV, 2. in Græco. Constuprari autem hic significat, idolis se subjicere, ut Jer. III, 6. Ezech. XVI. & alibi sæpe. Illud ὗτοι sumendum tam de Ju- dæis, quam de aliis ad Christum conversis.

Παρθένοι γάρ εἰσιν.] Etiam nomen παρθένος fœmininum est apud Græcos. Sed hic viris aptatur ea, quam dixi, de cau- sa. Vide & 2. Cor. XI, 2. Philo libro de legibus specialibus, διάνοιαν ait virgini comparari, ubi se custodit: ἁγίαν κὴ ἀδιά- φθορον ἀπὸ τε ἡδονῶν καὶ ἐπιθυμιῶν καὶ φόβων, ἐπιβέλων κακῶν. Idem παρθένες χήρας dixit libro de Humanitate.

Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀκολουθῶντες τῷ ἀρνίῳ ὅπε ὑπάγῃ.] Male in quibusdam Codicibus ὅπε γὰρ ἂν ὑπάγῃ.] Sensus est: Sequun- tur Christum, quocunque eos ducit, vel in crucem. Ire pro ducere est Μετωνυμία.

Οὗτοι γὰρ ὑπὸ ἰησο͂ ἠγοράσθησαν.] A vitiis liberati sunt, ut supra 7.

Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.] Id est, ἐκ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, exempti sunt cæterorum hominum vitæ.

Ἀπαρχὴ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ.] Ἀπαρχαὶ illi dicuntur re- spectu Christianorum, qui post ipsos sunt futuri. Vide Rom. 16, 5. 1. Cor. 16, 15.

## 14:5
Vers. 5. And in their mouth was found no lie.] They did not call those gods who are not gods. A lie always adheres to idolatry, below 21, 8. Rom. I, 25. Isa. 28, 15. Jerem. 16, 19. Amos 2, 4. in the Hebrew Soph. 3, 13. there is no deceit in his spirit, Psalm 32, 2.

For they are without blemish.] They correspond to those cattle from which מום, i.e., μῶμος, was absent, Eph. I, 4. V, 27. Col. I, 22. Jude v. 24.

Not only those converted from the nations, but also faithful Jews. For by the force of the continuity of the chapters, there is an adequate opposition of the faithful and the unfaithful, of those following the beast and receiving his mark, and of the followers of Christ and those signed with his mark, and finally of those blaspheming and those celebrating. The sound of the harp is pleasant and grateful, the voice of the beast is horrible, as it is itself not at all grateful. Moreover, the assembly of the Church militant and triumphant can be properly joined, because in truth there is only one Church, Heb. XII, 22, 23, 24, even if this assembly was properly seen by St. John in the heavens, but signified in this place as that which is the Church in Zion, Ps. II, 5. Isa. II, 2. Mich. IV, 1, 2. Freed from the earth or earthly desires and vices, from the evil world, Gal. I, 4, 1. John V, 19. it is not understood as those from all parts of the Roman empire, for this is not the whole earth, nor should one rashly depart from the letter, from sin, I say, and vain conversation, 1 Pet. I, 18. from all lawlessness, and impiety, and worldly desires, Tit. II, 12, 14. This liberation, however, is Catholic both with respect to men and with respect to sins and transgressions, Isa. 53, 4 seqq. John I, 29. 2 Cor. V, 19 seqq. 1 John 1, 7. c. 2, 2. Heb. 2, 9, 15. c. 9, 26. c. 10, 10. Rom. 3, 23, 24. c. 4, 7, 25. c. 5, 1, 12, 15, 17, 18. 1 Tim. 2, 6. Consecrated to God and the Lamb, or to Christ the God-man, by whom they were therefore redeemed, Tit. 2, 12, 14, in the manner of the firstfruits of the Old Testament, which were to be offered to God to consecrate the whole harvest, Exod. 23, 19. c. 34, 26. 1 Cor. 16, 15. Jas. 1, 18. Lev. 22, 10. Num. 18, 13, 14, 17. Deut. 14, 23. c. 18, 4. c. 26, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Καὶ ἐν τῷ ςόματι ἀυτῶν ἐχ εὑρέθη ψεῦδος.] Non vocarunt eos Deos, qui Dii non sunt. Mendacium semper adhæret idololatriæ infra 21, 8. Rom. I, 25. Esa. 28, 15. Jerem. 16, 19. Amos. 2, 4. in Ebræo Soph. 3, 13. אין ברוחו רמיה Psalm. 32, 2.

Ἄμωμοι γάρ εἰσι.] Respondent pecudibus illis, à quibus aberat מום, i. e. μῶμος, Eph. I, 4. V, 27. Col. I, 22. Judæ v. 24.

Non tantum conversi ex gentibus, sed etiam Ju- dæi fideles. Est enim vi συνεχείας capitum, adæquata oppositio fidelium & infidelium, sectantium bestiam ejusque characterem suscipientium & sectatorum Christi, ejusque charactere signatorum blaspheman- tium, deniq; & celebrantium. Citharæ sonus jucun- dus est & gratus, bestiæ vox horrenda, ut ipsa mini- meque grata. Conjungi autem probe potest cœtus Ecclesiæ militantis & triumphantis, quia revera una tantum est Ecclesia, Ebr. XII, 22. 23. 24. etsi in cœlis proprie hic cœtus à S. Johanne visus, significatus autem hoc in loco illo, qui est in Zione Ecclesia, Ps. II, 5. Es. II, 2. Mich. IV, 1. 2. Liberati à terra vel terre- nis cupiditatibus & vitiis, à mundo maligno, Gal. I, 4. 1. Joh. V, 19. non intelliguntur, qui ex omnibus parti- bus Romani imperii, hoc enim non est universa ter- ra, nec temere discedendum est à litera, à peccato, inquam, & conversatione vana, 1. Petr. I, 18. ἀπὸ πά- σης ἀνομίας, κὴ ἀσεβείας, κὴ ταῖς κοσμικαῖς ἐπιθυμί- αις, Tit. II, 12. 14. Liberatio autem hæc est Catholica cum ratione hominum, tum ratione peccatorum & transgressionum, Es. 53. 4. seqq. Joh. I, 29. 2. Cor. V, 19. seqq. 1. Joh. 1, 7. c. 2, 2. Ebr. 2, 9. 15. c. 9, 26. c. 10, 10. Rom. 3, 23. 24. c. 4, 7. 25. c. 5, 1. 12. 15. 17. 18. 1. Tim. 2, 6. Consecra- ti Deo & Agno, vel Christo Θεανθρώπῳ, à quo ideo redempti sunt, Tit. 2, 12. 14. more primitiarum Vet. Testamenti, quæ Deo erant offerendæ ad conse- crandam totam messem, Exod. 23, 19. c. 34, 26. 1. Cor. 16, 15. Jac. 1, 18. Lev. 22, 10. Num. 18, 13. 14. 17. Deut. 14, 23. c. 18, 4. c. 26, 2.

## 14:6
Vers. 6. And I saw another Angel.] Another from those we had before.

Πετώμενον ἐν μεσερανήματι.] In the middle air between earth and heaven, so that it may signify a matter decreed in heaven, to be performed on earth. See above VIII, 13 and XII, 1. The Angel flies, because Cherubim and Seraphim are shown winged.

Ἔχοντα ἐυαγγέλιον αἰώνιον.] The good news long since defined by God. Thus you have χρόνοις αἰωνίοις in Rom. 16, 25. So also Ps. 76, 4 in the Greek: Prov. 22, 8. c. 23, 10.

Εὐαγγελίσαι τῆς καθημένοις ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.] Εὐαγγελίζεσθαι in an active sense here governs the accusative of the person, as in Luke III, 10 and elsewhere. But in the Manuscript it is ἐυαγγελίσαι ἐπὶ τὼς καθημένως &c., in agreement with what follows. But understand those sitting on the earth here as men of humble condition, such as the Christians were for the most part at that time. It is that expression in Isa. XLVII, 1 and Lam. II. v. 10. Such people have need of good news, by which they may be refreshed. Εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, that is, εἰς τὸ ἐυαγγελίζεσθαι.

Καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶν ἔθνος καὶ φυλὴν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ λαόν.) That first καὶ here is explanatory. For it divides those of whom it had spoken into nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, as above V, 9. VII, 9. X, 11, XI, 9. XIII, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 6. Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον Ἄγγελον.] Alium ab illis, quos an- te habuimus.

Πετώμενον ἐν μεσερανήματι.] In aëre medio inter terram & cœlum, ut significetur res in cœlo decreta, in terris pera- genda. Vide supra IIX, 13. & XII, 1. Volat Angelus, quia alati ostenduntur Cherubini & Seraphini.

Ἔχοντα ἐυαγγέλιον αἰώνιον.] Bonum nuntium jam pridem à Deo definitum. Sic χρόνοις αἰωνίοις habes Rom. 16, 25. Sic & Ps. 76, 4. in Græco: Prov. 22, 8. c. 23, 10.

Εὐαγγελίσαι τῆς καθημένοις ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.] Εὐαγγελίζεσθαι sensu activo hic accusativum personæ regit, ut Luc. III, 10. & alibi. At in Manuscripto est ἐυαγγελίσαι ἐπὶ τὼς καθημένως &c. congruenter sequentibus. Sedentes in terra hic intelli- ge humilis conditionis homines, quales ferme tunc erant Christiani. Est ea loquutio Esa. XLVII, 1. & Lam. II. v. 10. Talibus opus bono nuntio, quo recreentur. Εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, id est, εἰς τὸ ἐυαγγελίζεσθαι.

Καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶν ἔθνος καὶ φυλὴν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ λαόν.) Illud καὶ primum hic est ἐξηγητικόν. Partitur enim illos, de quibus dixerat, in gentes, tribus, populos, linguas, ut supra V, 9. VII, 9. X, 11, XI, 9. XIII, 7.

## 14:7
Vers. 7. Λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ.) So also the Manuscript. And λέγων is construed with εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, because it has the same value as if it had said εὐαγγελίσαται λέγων.

Φοβήθητε τὸν Θεὸν.) You Christians, persist in the true religion, which is the fear of God to the Hebrews.

Καὶ δότε αὐτῷ δόξαν.) Emphasis on the word αὐτῷ, to Him himself, not to false gods.

Ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῆς κρίσεως αὐτῦ.) The judgment, namely, upon the Romans, which judgment we shall soon see poured out by seven Angels, just as the judgment of God had been poured out by seven Angels upon the contumacious Jews above VIII. IX. X. XI. The near vengeance of God upon oppressors is a great comfort to the oppressed.

Καὶ προσκυνήσατε τῷ ποιήσαντι τὸν ὐρανὸν, καὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων.) That καὶ here means therefore. Since you are certain that vengeance is imminent, continue to worship the true God, who is best distinguished from false gods by this mark, that He is the maker of this world. Above 10, 6. Acts 4, 24. Isa. 42, 5. 44, 24. 45, 18. Zech. 12, 1. Psalm 46, 6.

Most Angels were of a spiritual nature: He indeed saw such an Angel, different in number from the others: but he was signified through him, as in c. I, II. III. A singular Doctor of the Church; yet not the only one, except in respect of profession and doctrine, even if he is the one preeminent among many and therefore figured by the flight of one, whose flight denotes a swift course, the doctrine, the Gospel, which he has in his hand, as if entrusted to him, and to be promulgated by him: Whom we call the great man B. Luther, as the sequence of the revelations demands. He sustains the name of Angel by reason of his office, because he was sent to teach the Gospel, both when he was called to the Holy ministry, and when he was promoted to be a Doctor, or as Doctors of Theology were called then, Master of Theology, and is a Professor of Sacred Theology, so that he might teach it sincerely by word of mouth and by writings in the Academy and the Church according to the Canon of Scripture or the Old & N. Testam. which the Hebrew Bible there, and the Greek text here, constitute, not only in this Witteberg Church and School, but throughout the Christian world: because public authority to inform the whole Church by writings, and to propagate heavenly truth, is granted to Doctors of Theology, which is not denied to others, but is formally granted to these by the right of the Doctorate and belongs to them ordinarily. An Angel of God sent by the Lord, executing the mandate of the Lord according to His will, and instituting his doctrine from nothing but the word of God comprised in the Scriptures as an undoubted Canon, passing over human traditions, and recalling any heterodoxy whatsoever to that Lydian stone, reproving and condemning it. Whence in thesis alike and antithesis he followed the Rule of Scripture solely: he distinguished Canonical and Apocryphal Scriptures, as accurately as was then permitted, he separated dogmatic and ceremonial matters, assigning the former as necessary and the latter as free, nor did he burden the Church with various rites without cause; he wished pious rites, and those not contrary to the word of God, to be retained, but he disapproved of and abrogated superstitious and impious ones by all means.

He was the Angel of God not only by reason of doctrine, but also by reason of the holiness of life, by which he shone before others, and to the whole Church like an Angel. By devout psalmodies, which he also composed for the use of the Church, and by virtues of every kind, he provided an illustrious example, as a light shining most brightly in the house of the Lord, and as a faithful servant of the Lord in all His house, like Moses the servant of the Lord, Heb. III.
