As for what the Papists, those architects of absurdities, lies, and calumnies, are accustomed to yelp in great numbers against the doctrine and life, and no less against the calling and ordination of this Angel of the Lord—Cochlaeus, Wetter, Staphylus, Ungersdorff, Albertus Hunger, Bellarmine, Gretser, Sartorius, and that most impudent apostate L. Frommius—abundantly Our people have refuted [these], especially the blessed Joh. Gerhard, the blessed Nic. Hunnius, Mr. Kesler, the blessed D. Müller, and Mr. D. Tenzelius, who may be consulted. It is not our business to do what has already been done.

Moreover, the proper confessions of the Papists can be opposed to the Papists: Paulus Langius, certainly a monk, in his Chronicon Citicense in the year 1570, did not hesitate to call Luther a most profound theologian, easily the wisest of all the theologians of our time, a prince, a consummate and incomparable theologian, who attempted to recall sacred theology to its foundational dignity and primeval purity, as well as to its evangelical sincerity and its own simple innocence, having completely exploded all secular philosophy. Erasmus was accustomed to say that there was no interpreter more dexterous than Luther among all those whose writings are extant since the Apostles. Joh. Fischer, Bishop of Rochester, said he was skilled in the scriptures even to the point of a miracle. Joh. Cellarius says that he handles scripture with such faith that he far carries off the palm from all Italian, Greek, and Hebrew adversaries. Matth. Schirnerus, Bishop and Cardinal of Sion: O Luther, Luther, he said, you are truly according to your name a 'Luter' [purifier], and clear. Furthermore, Ulrich von Hutten, a knight, asserted that Martin Luther was a man so approved in life and morals that he could not be disapproved of even by an enemy, a preacher of truth and a most faithful dispenser of evangelical doctrine. Similarly, Erasmus to Thomas, Cardinal of York, book 11, Epistle 1: The life of the man (he points to Luther) is approved by the great consensus of all; now that is no light prejudice, that there is such integrity of morals that even his enemies find nothing to slander. Emperor Charles V himself was accustomed to say: If our clergy and priests had cultivated piety of their own accord, we would not have needed the help of Luther. See Vol. V of Luther, fol. 281. What of the fact that in the very Diet of Augsburg the Papists confessed that the Augsburg Confession could not be refuted from the scriptures? Eck also testified that the doctrine of the Protestants could indeed be refuted by the writings of the Fathers, but by no means from the scriptures. Albert, Archbishop of Mainz, having found a biblical codex by chance and having perused certain leaves in it, said: Indeed, I do not know what kind of book this is; I see this, that all things contained in it are adverse to us. Another bishop said: Do you know what I would do with the epistles of Paul if I had them alone? Let it be said under the rose, I would throw them into the fire. And then the whole arsenal of the Lutherans would be destroyed. See Wolffius, Century 16, p. 623.

This Angel flew, as if equipped with wings, because his doctrine was propagated with remarkable speed, and his writings flew everywhere throughout the world, eagerly received; he flew through the midst of the ecclesiastical heaven, or through the Church, because with the Roman Anti-Christ sitting in the Church of God and presiding over it, the course of the Gospel preached by him in the Church could in no way be hindered by him, concerning which Cardinal Bellarmine complained gravely in an oration prefixed to Vol. IV of his Works. Flying chariots indicate the wonderful speed with which this new sect (of the Lutherans) poured itself out like a pestilential contagion through various regions: for not content with the western and northern kingdoms, it dared to sail also to the East and to the South, to the Greeks, to the Indians, and to the New World itself. And in the preface to Vol. I of his Controversies. Who is ignorant that the Lutheran plague, having arisen a little before in Saxony, soon occupied Germany, having penetrated it, and from there having gone to the North and East, consumed Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Gothia, Pannonia, and Hungary: then, carried with equal speed to the West and South, it ravaged France, England, and Scotland, once most flourishing kingdoms, in a short time, and finally crossed the Alps and penetrated even into Italy. Among the Ruthenians also, at the streams of the Prosqui, the Augsburg Confession found a safe and honored seat. The blessed Phil. Nicolai, in book 1 of his work on the Kingdom of Christ, ch. 1, taught this from Odervoca. The secretary of Paul IV, in the acts of the Council of Trent, on the propagation of arms, § 69, to the Pope himself: I think you know, he said, that in all your cities there are some who are infected with the Lutheran poison; and these not only from the lowest dregs of the people, but also from men of the middle and highest ranks. That it penetrated even Albania and Iberia and the Caspian Sea, the blessed Phil. Nicolai likewise taught in the same place; and that it finally reached even the Spains and the monasteries of the Spaniards, Jac. Aug. Thuanus, book 23, and Petrus Suavis Polanus, book V of the History of the Council of Trent, p. 486, have reported.

And lest the adversaries say that Luther is not of such importance that God would have wanted predictions to be made about him; I reply: the evangelical doctrine was certainly of such importance (whatever may be the case regarding the person of Luther) that its restoration deserved that prediction, for which it is established that an instrument was designated even through other prophecies for the sake of the doctrine itself; for his name, LUTHERUS, was found on a certain statue in the year 1152. Alighieri Dante in the year 1321 predicted that one who is five hundred and ten and five (the year noted 1515, in which he was made a Doctor) was sent by God. John Huss the martyr prophesied in the year 1414: Today you are roasting a goose (which the name Hus denotes in the Bohemian language), but after a hundred years a swan will be born from my ashes, which you will not be able to roast. Jerome of Prague, however, likewise noble in his martyrdom, said: After a hundred years you will answer to God and to me: which was fulfilled when Luther, after 100 years, began to sing as a swan (this new song) and the Papists had to answer to Jerome (in Luther as if he were alive again), but they were unable to, just as it is established that Jerome Savonarola, in the year 1498, because he contradicted the Pope, was burned, and he himself had predicted that a Doctor would soon arise to whom no one could resist: Likewise: That someone like Cyrus would cross the Alps and would devastate the whole (Papistic) Church, which was fulfilled in the blessed Luther a little later: To which it is said that John Heltenius predicted similar things: Another will come in the year of our Lord 1516 (in which the blessed Luther proposed his first theses against the Papists, Vol. I of Latin Works, Jena, fol.) who will destroy you, and you will not be able to resist. Such things as could be brought forward in greater number.

The Gospel, which blessed Luther always held in his hand and, by divine aid, did not allow to be shaken from him, flying throughout the world—even though Papists slanderously call it a new and fifth Gospel—is nevertheless called a new song here by the Spirit himself, without detriment to the truth and the title of the eternal Gospel. It is a new song because, after the ancient one concerning the law of the Lord inscribed upon the minds of men and prescribed in Paradise concerning the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which was violated, this counsel concerning the salvation of men, brought forth as if new from the eternal bosom of God the Father, and subsequently repeated as if new in comparison with the old covenant (which was handed down more frequently and more clearly than it in the books of the Old Testament and illustrated with examples), just as conversely in the books of the New Testament the doctrine of the Gospel is handed down much more clearly and frequently, and must be cherished and repeated perpetually as if new in a renewed and new heart. Which is also called new for this reason, that it is very excellent (which 'new' is accustomed to signify) and now, even after the reformation of the Gospel, must be sung as if renewed, where it has been vindicated from the old depravation of the heavenly song and the divine word by a divine hero and a heavenly angel. These are truly the newest of all things that are under heaven, because it concerns that one thing under the sun which is new, which alone is new, as Damascenus speaks from Jeremiah 31, namely that confessedly great mystery

the sign of the truth, that God was manifest in the flesh, etc. 1 Tim. 3:16. How greatly this was corrupted in the Papacy is manifest even from the Smalcald Articles, principal article, part II, illustrated by the writings of Megalander. The eternal Gospel, therefore, which Megalander restored, is concerning Christ, that Lamb slain for the sins of the whole world, John 1:29, 1 John 2:2, and the gratuitous remission of sins on account of his δικαίωμα and satisfaction promised to us in the Old Testament, Exod. 34, Jer. 31, exhibited in the New Testament, Acts 10:43, and concerning the gracious imputation of his righteousness, Isa. 45:24, Jer. 23:6, ch. 33:16, Rom. 5:18, 19, ch. 4:5, 6, Phil. 3:9, 2 Cor. 5:21, which is apprehended by us and appropriated to us only through faith, Rom. 3:23 ff., ch. 4:11, 25, Phil. 3:9, Gal. 2:20. Which is eternal from the part before, as they call it, because the Lamb was slain from the foundation of the world, Rev. 13:8, Heb. 13:8, and from the part after, because that word remains forever, 1 Pet. 1:23, 25.

With what Spirit, with what contention the blessed Luther preached this to the peoples and to the whole world, which was ἡ φωνὴ ἡ μεγάλη, Rev. 14:7, can be testified by the Smalcald Articles; concerning this article, he says, part II, art. 1, no one of the pious can yield, or grant or permit anything against it, even if heaven and earth and all things should collapse, his profession made in Tom. V. Jen. Germ. with truly heroic boldness in these very words: Because I see that the devil must always blaspheme this chief article through his pillar-teachers, and cannot rest nor cease; so I, D. M. Luther, unworthy evangelist of our Lord Jesus Christ, say that this article (faith alone, without any works, makes one righteous before God) shall be left to stand and remain, the Roman Emperor, the Turkish, Tartar Emperor, the Persian Emperor, the Pope, all Cardinals, Bishops, Prelates, Priests, Monks, Nuns, Kings, Princes, Lords, all the world, together with all the devils, and they shall have the hellish fire for it upon their head, and no thanks for it. That is my, D. Luther's, inspiration from the Holy Spirit, and the true Holy Gospel. For there stands the article which the children pray: I believe in Jesus Christ, crucified, dead, etc. For no one has died for our sins but Jesus Christ alone, God's Son; once again I say, Jesus God's Son alone has redeemed us from sins, that is certainly true, and the whole Scripture, and should all devils and the world tear themselves apart and burst, so it is true.

The necessity, truth, and sweetness of which eternal Gospel those who are raised up by it in their agony recognized and tasted even in the midst of the Papacy, and recognize and taste today as well, of whom is the heavenly voice: Blessed from now on are those who die in the Lord, i.e., who depart in that faith in Christ Jesus. Let the Mainz Agenda be a testimony: Do you believe that you arrive at glory by the merits of our Redeemer's passion, and not by your own? I believe. Likewise the more recent Mainz agenda of the year 1551 and 1599: Now, however, not only your own, but also the merits of all men are far too small and too slight for a man to be able to comfort himself for salvation by his own works. But since our works and own merits are lacking, we must hold to the merits of Christ, our common Savior, whom God, out of divine love toward us, gave into the world so that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. Upon him God previously laid your sin and the sin of all men, and let him be wounded and painfully beaten for your sin. And the punishment which you should justly suffer for your sin according to the strict justice of God, that God has previously exacted upon his only and beloved Son, and let him suffer painfully for your sin, so that he might spare you. Upon this gracious and merciful God you should set your trust, take a joyful, confident heart, and fear nothing, but have a firm hope and undoubted confidence. Also the Roman Sacerdotal, according to Cardinal Hosius in his confession of faith at Petricau, ch. 73: Do you believe that you arrive at glory not by your own merits, but by the virtue and merit of the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ? The infirm person answers: I believe. Again the Priest: Do you believe that our Lord Jesus Christ died for our salvation, and that no one can be saved by their own merits or in any other way, unless in the merit of his passion? The infirm person answers: I believe. Add the Monastic ritual of the just, for those instructing the dying, taken from all the best sources and especially the Roman and more ancient one, edited at Sammielli in the year 1627: In which the Priest asks: Do you believe that you arrive at glory not by your own merits, but by the virtue and merit of the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ? The infirm person answers: I believe. The Priest further asks: Do you believe that our Lord Jesus Christ died for our salvation, and that BY HIS OWN MERITS, OR IN ANY OTHER WAY, NO ONE CAN BE SAVED, UNLESS BY THE MERIT OF HIS PASSION? The infirm person answers: I believe. The Order of Baptizing with the manner of visiting the sick, reprinted at Venice in the year 1575, formerly had these things, which have now been expunged by the Expurgatory Index of the Roman Beast: Do you believe that you arrive at glory not by your own merits, but by the virtue and merit of the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ? Likewise: Do you believe that our Lord Jesus Christ died for our salvation, and that by your own merits or IN ANY OTHER WAY NO ONE can be saved, unless by the merit of his passion? Caspar Ulenberg, on the causes of apostasy, Cologne, year 1589: I found a certain book in the parochial sacristy of our Church written in the year of salvation 1475, which we have always used since that time in visiting those preparing for death. In which these things are read: Do you believe that you cannot be saved EXCEPT through the death of Christ, etc. The infirm person answers: Yes. Then it is said to him: Act therefore while there is still soul in you, place your trust in this death alone, have trust in no other thing, cover yourself entirely with this alone, immerse yourself entirely in this death, wrap yourself entirely in this death: And if the Lord God wishes to judge you, say: Lord, I interpose the death of our Lord Jesus Christ between me and your judgment. If He says to you that you have deserved damnation, say: Lord, I hold forth the death of our Lord Jesus Christ between me and my evil merits, and I offer His merit for the merit which I ought to have had, and do not have. In the Summula of Raimundus, Cologne edition, year 1498, the priest asks: Whether he believes he will arrive at the kingdom of God not by his own merits, but through the merits of Jesus Christ and His most bitter passion. In the Hortulus Animae, and in Anselm of Canterbury. Bishop. Here this dialogue is held: Do you believe that the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, died for you? Yes. Do you believe that you cannot be saved except through His death? Yes. Many such things could be brought forward, and illustrated by the examples of those who died piously under the Papacy, to confirm the eternal Gospel, which is uniquely salvific and the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes, Rom. 1:16. To this Angel Evangelist, a certain Franciscan bore witness, as reported by Johannes Gastius, Memorabilia, Book I, year 1539: The Gospel, he says, is preached as clearly and solidly in our age as in the times of the Apostles. He truly predicted the same

Sebastian, Doctor of Theology, Canon of Erfurt, and Canon in the high church of the Blessed Virgin in the year 1500. The time will come when one will also read the Gospel from the book. This is without doubt the Gospel which was seen in the hand of the Angel by St. John. And Richard of Armagh, in his Epistle on the New Testament, says that when this book is found, the truth will be manifested to the whole world. John Cellarius of Leipzig wrote thus of Luther in the year 1520: Martin loves EVANGELICAL truth more than all his adversaries.

To the proclamation of the eternal Gospel, which that Angel had in his hand, and to the twofold new song which the elect faithful virgins of the Lord sing in the Evangelical Church, follows that voice: Fear the Lord, since to the mystery of piety must be joined the fear of the Lord and the adoration of the Triune God, in the name of the Mediator Christ, the God-man, which under the Papacy was either silent, with the honor of the Redeemer buried for the most part, and replaced or at least coordinated with it (which can no more exist together than the God of Israel and the idol of the Philistines, Dagon, 1 Sam. 5:2) a religious veneration of Saints and Angels, which the first table demands for the one God alone; or it was obscured by Mariolatry, Angelolatry, Hagiolatry, etc., a truly manifold superstitious and impious practice: but it was vindicated by the voice and writings of the Angel-Evangelist throughout the Christian world, as history and experience testify. This is the first and principal article, says the blessed Luther in the Smalcald Articles, that Jesus Christ, our God and Lord, died for our sins and rose again for our justification, Rom. 4. And that he alone is the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world, John 1. And that God has laid the iniquities of us all upon him, Isa. 53. All have sinned and are justified freely without works or personal merits by his grace through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus, in his blood, Rom. 3. Since it is necessary to believe this, and it cannot be acquired or apprehended by any work, law, or merit, it is certain and manifest that this faith alone justifies us, as Paul says in Rom. 3: We conclude that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law. Likewise: That he himself might be just and the justifier of him who is of the faith of Jesus Christ. And concerning the invocation of Saints: The invocation of Saints is also a part of the abuses and errors of the Anti-Christ, fighting against the first principal article and destroying the acknowledgment of Christ. It is not commanded, nor does it rest on counsel, example, or the testimony of Scripture. All things are proposed to us better and more certainly in Christ, so that we do not need the invocation of Saints, even if it were a precious thing, whereas it is a most pernicious one. Even if the Angels in heaven pray for us (as Christ himself also does) and the saints on earth and perhaps even in heaven, it does not follow from that that Angels and Saints are to be invoked by us, adored, or honored with fasts, holidays, masses, offerings of temples, foundations of altars, and other ways, as Patrons and intercessors, and that certain aids are to be attributed to each of them, as the Papists teach and do. For this is idolatrous, and this honor is to be attributed to God alone. Concerning the mass: That the mass in the Papacy is the greatest and most horrible abomination, simply and hostilely fighting diametrically against the first article, which nevertheless was the highest and most specious of all other Pontifical idolatries. For they established that this sacrifice, or the work of the mass, even when performed by an impious and lost scoundrel, frees a man from sins, both in this life and in purgatory, when yet the Lamb of God alone frees us. In this article concerning the mass, the council will labor most and will be consumed. For even if it were possible that they would concede all the remaining articles to us, yet they will not be able to concede this one, just as Campeggio said at Augsburg, that he would sooner suffer all tortures, the tearing apart of his limbs, and death, than let the Mass be dismissed. And I also, by the help of God, will suffer my body to be reduced to ashes and burned, rather than endure that a Mass-belly, whether good or bad, be equated to Christ Jesus, my Lord and Savior, or be considered superior to him. Thus, indeed, we are eternally separated and are contrary to one another. They feel very well: if the mass falls, the Papacy falls. Before they suffer this, they will slaughter us all, if they can. And further: That tail of the Dragon (I mean the Mass) has brought forth manifold abominations and idolatries, which are listed there in order: 1. purgatory, 2. apparitions of souls, 3. pilgrimages, 4. brotherhoods, 5. relics of Saints, filled with various lies, ineptitudes, and follies, 6. Indulgences granted to the living and the dead for money. To these let there be added the cathedral colleges of Canons and monasteries, such as they were in the Papacy with the infinite and divine power of the Pope: which Papal idolomania, when understood with the commandment exclusively according to scripture and the proclamation of the Angel, 'fear God,' many nations, tribes, languages, and peoples now acknowledge and detest, having been convicted in the writings of the Great Man as truly manifold and abominable, as is in the open.

Furthermore, the voice of the Gospel is not to be taken in a general sense of good news, as if it were for the faithful converted from the Gentiles concerning the punishment of the oppressed Romans and the divine vengeance shortly to follow against them, from which little comfort could come to them; but specifically of that good news which in these books is so called by antonomasia and is to be taken in a more famous meaning, namely, of that divine grace exhibited to the whole human race in Christ JESUS, that Lamb slain for us, which the faithful enjoy with the blessing of the divine name. Which the blessed Luther brought back into the light and asserted with a loud, powerful, and effective proclamation, and is celebrated by the elect who adhere to the same doctrine. For we have said that the new song and the eternal Gospel are materially the same here. It is called the eternal Gospel because it contains some part of the eternal counsel and the book of life concerning the slain Lamb from the foundation of the world, Rev. 13:8, ch. 17:8. and extends itself into eternity by its efficacy, Rom. 1:16. For that Gospel is the power of God unto (eternal) salvation to every one that believeth: Which the blessed Luther taught most especially in his golden commentaries on the Galatians. For that reason, that eternal Gospel cannot be called a message about the punishing of the Romans.

But concerning the judgment indicated by the seven vials, which is not at all relevant here (if the Grotius gloss about the punishing of the pagan, idolatrous Romans is retained here), since the vials concern the Roman Papacy, later.

Adoration can properly be coupled with fear, so that there is no need for an illative sense, since the proper use of the conjunction can be retained, and the exegetical one dismissed. Nor must that ἐξηγητικῶς in v. 6 be necessarily accepted, since the more common copulative sense has a place, indeed not, as Grotius seems to intend by the exegetical sense, about only converted Gentiles, but that the discourse is about any peoples and tribes, Jewish and Ethnic, brought to the faith of Christ, acting in the Church, and the angelic proclamation is directed to all peoples, that honor is to be deferred only to God the creator of heaven, earth, the sea, and the rivers, both so that the true σέβασμα may be distinguished from false ones, whether they be in heaven or on earth, angels and saints, which are worshipped in the Papacy, and so that this duty of veneration may be taught to be incumbent upon all their inhabitants.

But the hour of judgment is said to be imminent, not a particular one for the Romans, but a universal one for all men. Because this is called judgment κατ' ἐξοχὴν [by way of excellence] and absolutely: and this proclamation is made to all nations and peoples throughout the world, and the religious veneration of that God is enjoined upon all. Therefore, the reason which is brought forward, from the obligation both toward the one Creator and toward the future judge, to whom all knees shall be bound to bow, Isa. 45, 23. Rom. 14, 11. 12., ought to be common and universal: such as a certain particular judgment is not; The sound of this preaching, says the blessed Gravius, penetrated Spain itself, the Gauls, Italy, Sicily, and Greece itself and the Orient: To this effective preaching and the swift flight of the herald Angel pertains the return of the woman from the desert, which is first particular, and then toward the end of the 1260 days, universal. But the end of the days is the limit of the dwelling in the desert and the end of the world. Therefore no return is to be hoped for, much less a universal one.

II. THE ANGEL ANNOUNCING ANOTHER FALL OF BABYLON. Ver. 8.

And another second Angel followed saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen.] It is the past tense for the future in the Prophetic manner. And briefly it is predicted here, what is more fully [predicted] below 18, 2. Pagan Rome, or certainly Rome not purged of paganism, is called Babylon, as Tertullian rightly explains against the Jews and III against Marcion, Jerome in the prologue to Didymus at the end of the second against Jovinian, on Isa. 24 and 47, in the epistle to Algasia and the other to Marcella, and others; because, namely, it was equally a great kingdom, proud, and a vanquisher of the saints, as Tertullian says, add also other things which you have in Orosius II, 2. The words are taken from Isa. 21, 9. Jer. 51, 8. In the Manuscript: And another second Angel. She has made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.] The Manuscript [reads] the wine etc. Just as the Latin also reads. But θυμὸς [thumos] here signifies poison, as Deut. 32, 24. Job 6, 4. c. 20, 16. Psalm 58, 5. Therefore οἶν@- θυμῶ [wine of wrath] is poisoned wine, a deadly potion. Πορνεία [fornication] here is idolatry, which Rome had offered to the nations subjected and allied to it. It is compared to wine, whatever alienates the mind, below XVII, 14. Men are easily corrupted by examples, see 1 Macc. 1, 45. That other Angel is not undeservedly established by the blessed Gravius as the blessed Chemnitius, the other Martin, who denounced, nay demonstrated, the fall of Babylon through the Examination of the Council of Trent, by which it attempted to erect that Babylon, and uncovered to the world its spiritual whoredom, idolatry, and foul and manifold superstition: which a most grave penal fall is certainly going to follow. The blessed Nic. Hunnius also manifested the apostasy of Rome: That great Babylon, which has hitherto committed whoredom with most in the world, and has offered the wine of whoredom to all nations, that great city, the great whore, demonstrated by the Angels of God, has fallen in the minds of many, in whom it once had a seat and dominion. The Antichrist has been finished by the voice of the Lord, and is also near to a fall, joined with temporal bodily, as well as eternal with infernal destruction. That Rome is called Babylon, not only pagan but also Antichristian, will be taught at the XIII chapter. But that which is said concerning θυμῶ [thumos], we do not with difficulty admit that poison is signified by it. From the wine of poison, says the blessed Glassius in Gramm. S., i.e., from poisoned wine. For θυμὸς in this place is poison from the usage of the Hellenistic language, in which θυμὸς corresponds to the Hebrew word חמה [chemah], which signifies both fury and poison (Ps. 58, 5. Ps. 140, 4. Job 6, 4. Deut. 32, 33). But the customary meaning of the word θυμῶ can be retained. For God permits such seductions by just judgment, so that the contempt of the Gospel may be punished, 2 Thess. 2, 10. Luther seems not to have read the word θυμῶ. Therefore the second Angel proclaims concerning the fall and ruin of Babylon 1. spiritual: partly because it fell from the throne of infallibility, which it boasted of in the doctrine of faith, but was cast down from there by its own testimony C. Si Papa. dist. 40. It is also certain, with Adrian VI admitting in l. IV. sentent. de sacr. confirm. art. 3., that the Pontiff can err by asserting heresy through his determination or decretal, and that some Pontiffs were heretics, such as are considered Zephyrinus, Montanizing according to the blessed Rhenanus l. Tertull. c. prax., Liberius Arianizing, compil. Chron., Honorius I Monothelite, Adrian in the year 772 an idolater, Gregory VII a disciple of Berengarius, John XXIII. denying eternal life after this life, declared a heretic by Eugenius IV in the council of Basel, sess. 4. A. 1439, etc., partly because it defected from Christian truth to pagan superstitions and rites and ceremonies, which the blessed Nic. Hunnius demonstrated in Apost. Rom. Eccl.: Is this not a notable fall? 2. Bodily from the throne of Majesty, because the ten horns or Kings were conquered by the Lamb, namely, of England, Scotland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Hungary, Bohemia, Germany, Poland, Russia or Muscovy, in which empire the Roman Pontiff is excommunicated annually on Dominica Quadragesima. Whose empire's ten horns therefore fall, that [empire] must have suffered a notable ruin worthy of such a clamor. Add that, by the testimony of the Pontifical writers themselves, the donation of Constantine has also fallen, and thus the Roman Pontiff has also fallen out of Italy. What greater ruin could happen to him? Since the Roman Pontiff, as the Pseudo-Prophet, is shortly to be cast into the lake of eternal fire, Apoc. XX, 10, which ruin is not so much indicated here as it is intimated in Apoc. XIX, 20.

III. THE THIRD ANGEL, DENOUNCING PUNISHMENT TO THOSE WORSHIPPING THE BEAST.

Latin:

Vers. 7. Λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ.) Sic & Manuscriptus. Et construitur λέγων cum εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, quia idem valet, ac si dixisset εὐαγγελίσαται λέγων.

Φοβήθητε τὸν Θεὸν.) Vos Christiani perstate in vera religione, quæ timor Dei Ebræis.

Καὶ δότε αὐτῷ δόξαν.) Ἔμφασις in voce αὐτῷ ipsi, non Diis falsis.

Ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῆς κρίσεως αὐτῦ.) Judicii nempe in Romanos, quod judicium per septem Angelos mox videbimus effundi, sicut per septem Angelos effusum fuerat judicium Dei in contumaces Judæos supra IIX. IX. X. XI. Multum solatur oppressos propinqua Dei ultio in opprimentes.

Καὶ προσκυνήσατε τῷ ποιήσαντι τὸν ὐρανὸν, καὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων.) Illud καὶ hic valet ergo. Cum certifitis ultionem imminere, pergite colere verum Deum, qui hac nota à Diis falsis optime discernitur, quod mundi hujus sit opifex. Supra 10, 6. Act. 4, 24. Esa. 42, 5. 44, 24. 45, 18. Zachar. 12, 1. Psalm. 46, 6.

Plerique Angeli fuere natura spiritualis: Hic vidit quidem talem Angelum numero ab aliis diversum: significatus autem fuit per illum, ut c. I, II. III. Doctor singularis Ecclesiæ; nec tamen unicus, nisi professione & doctrinæ respectu, etsi è pluribus præcipue unus atque ideo unius volatu figuratus, cujus volatus celerem notat cursum, doctrinam, Evangelium, quod in manu habet, ceu ipsi creditum, & ab ipso promulgandum: Quem Megalandrum B. Lutherum, poscente id ἀκολουθείᾳ revelationum, dicimus. Is Angeli nomen ratione officii sustinet, quod missus sit ad docendum Evangelium, cum ubi vocatus est ad S. ministerium, tum ubi Doctor, vel uti tum Doctores Theologiæ vocabantur, Magister Theologiæ promotus, & Professor SS. Theologiæ est, ut viva voce ac scriptis in Academia & Ecclesia id sincere juxta Canonem Scripturæ seu Vet. & N. Testam. quem ibi Ebræa Biblia, hic Græcus textus constituunt, doceret, non in hac tantum Wittebergensi Ecclesia & Schola, sed per orbem Christianum: quia publica potestas universam Ecclesiam scriptis informandi, & veritatem cœlestem propagandi conceditur Doctoribus Theologiæ, quæ nec aliis denegata est, his autem solenniter concessa jure Doctoratus ordinarie convenit. Angelus Dei missus à Domino Domini mandatum, juxta voluntatem ejus exequens, nec nisi è verbo Dei Scripturis ceu indubitati Canonis comprehenso doctrinam suam, prætermissis humanis traditionibus instituens, & heterodoxiam quamvis ad istum lapidem Lydium revocans, reprobans & condemnans. Unde in thesi pariter & antithesi Scripturæ Regulam sequutus est unice: Scripturas Canonicas & Apocryphas distinxit, quantum tum licuit, accurate dogmatica & ceremonialia separavit, illis necessariis, hisce liberis adfertis, nec ritibus variis, præter causam, Ecclesiam oneravit, pios, nec verbo Dei contrarios retineri voluit, superstitiosos autem, & impios omnibus modis improbavit atque abrogavit.

Angelus Dei fuit non ratione doctrinæ tantum, sed etiam ratione sanctitatis vitæ, qua præluxit aliis, totique Ecclesiæ instar Angeli. Psalmodiis devotis, quas in Ecclesiæ usum etiam concinnavit, omnisq; generis virtutibus illustre exemplum, ceu lux in domo Domini splendens fulgidissima præbens, fidusq; Domini in tota domo fidelis instar Mosis servi Domini, Ebr. III. Quæ contra de doctrina & vita, nec minus de vocatione & ordinatione hujus Angeli Domini Papistæ ineptiarum, mendaciorum & calumniarum architecti, magno numero solent oggannire, Cochleus, Wetterus, Staphylus, Ungersdorff, Albertus Hungerus, Bellarminus, Gretserus, Sartorius & Apostata impudentissimus L. Frommius abunde Nostri diluerunt, imprimis B. Joh. Gerhardus, B. Nic. Hunnius, Dn. Keslerus, B. D. Müllerus, & Dn. D. Tenzelius, qui conferantur. Nostrum non est actum agere.

Opponi autem Papistis posfunt Papistarum pro- priæ confessiones: Paulus Langius certe Monachus in Chron. Citicensi anno 1570. non dubitavit, Lu- therum profundissimum Theologum, Theologorum nostræ tempestatis omnium facile sapientissimum, Principem, Theologum consumatum, incompara- bilem, vocare, qui S. Theologiam ad fontalem di- gnitatem, primævamque puritatem, necnon Evan- gelicam sinceritatem simplicemque suam illam in- nocentiam, omnia prorsus seculari Philosophia ex- plosa, revocare conatus sit. Erasmus dicere solitus est, neminem esse Interpretem dexteriorem omnium, quorum extant scripta, post Apostolos Luthero. Joh. Fischer. Episc. Roff. dixit, eum scripturarum usque ad miraculum peritum. Joh. Cellarius, ea fide eum scripturam tractare ait, qua palmam omnibus adver- sariis Italis, Græcis & Ebræis longe præripiat. Matth. Schirnerus Epist. & Cardin. Sedunensis: O Luthere, Luthere, inquit, tu sane secundum nomen tuum Lu- therus es, & limpidus. Porro Uldaricus ab Hutten Eques Martinum Lutherum hominem vitæ & mo- ribus sic probatum asseruit, ut ne ab inimico quidem improbetur, prædicatorem veritatis & Evangelicæ doctrinæ dispensatorem fidelissimum. Similiter Era- smus ad Thom. Card. Eborac. l. 11. Epist. I. Hominis (Lutherum indigitat) vita, magno omnium consen- su, probatur; jam id non leve præjudicium est, tan- tam esse morum integritatem, ut nec hostes reperiant, quod calumnientur. Carolus V. Imperat. ipse solitus fuit dicere: Si nostri Clerici & Sacrificuli sua sponte pietatem coluissent, non eguissemus opem Lutheri. Vid. T. V. Luth. f. 281. Quid? quod in ipsis Co- mitiis August. Pontificii confessi sint, Augustanam Confessionem non posse ex scripturis refutari. Eccius etiam testatus, Patrum quidem scriptis doctrinam Protestantium refutari posse, minime vero ex scriptu- ris. Albert. vero Mogunt. Archi-Episc. invento forte codice Biblico, ac foliis quibusdam in eo perlustra- tis dixit: Equidem nescio, quid hoc libri sit, Illud video, omnia, quæ eo continentur, nobis adversa esse. Episcopus alius dixit: Scitisne quid ego cum Pauli epistolis agerem, si eas solas haberem? Sub rosa di- ctum sit, in ignem eas conjicerem. Et tunc dirutum omne Lutheranorum armamentarium foret. Vid. Wolffius Cent. 16. p. 623.

Volitavit hic Angelus, ceu alis instructus, quia doctrina ejus celeritate insigni propagata, scripta per orbem undiquaque volarunt avide suscepta, volitavit per medium cœli Ecclesiastici, vel per Ec- clesiam, quia Romano Anti-Christo in Ecclesia Dei se- dente illiq; licet præsidente nequicquam impediri cursus Evangelii ab ipso prædicati in Ecclesia po- tuit, de quo graviter questus est Cardin. Bellarmi- nus in orat. T. IV. Oper. præfix. Volantes currus mi- ram indicant velocitatem, qua nova ista Secta (Lu- theranorum) instar pestiferæ tabis sese per varias re- giones effudit: nam non contenta occiduis & aquilo- naribus regnis ad Orientem quoque & meridiem, ad Græcos, ad Indos, ad ipsum novum orbem navigare ausa est. Et in præfat. T. I. Controv. Quis ignorat pestem Lutheranam in Saxonia paulo ante exortam Germaniam penetratam mox occupasse, inde ad A- quilonem & Orientem profectam, Daniam, Norwe- giam, Sueciam, Gothiam, Pannoniam, Hungariam absumpsisse: tum ad Occidentem & Meridiem pari celeritate delatam, & Galliam, Angliam, Scotiam, florentissima quondam regna brevi tempore popula- tam ad extremum Alpes transscendisse, & in Italiam usque penetrasse. Apud Ruthenos quoque ad Prosqui fluenta invenisse Augustanam Confessionem tutam & honoratam sedem. B. Phil. Nicolai l. I. de regn. Christ. c. 1. ex Odervoca docuit. Secretarius Pauli IV. in action.an Conc. Trid. armis propag.§.69.ad Pontificem ipsum: Puto te scire, inquit, in omnibus tuis urbibus nonnullos esse, qui Lutherano veneno in- fecti sunt; neque hos ex infima tantum populi face, sed ex mediis etiam & summis viris. Albaniam imo & Iberiam & Caspium mare penetrasse Aug. Conf. l. c. itidem docuit B. Phil. Nicolai, in ipsas denique Hi- spanias & cœnobia Hispaniorum pervenisse Jac. Aug. Thuanus l. 23. Petrus Suavis Polan. l. V. Hist. Conc. Trid. p. 486. tradidere.

Neve adversarii dicant, Lutherum tanti non esse, ut Deus de illo prædictiones fieri voluerit; Resp. tanti certe fuit (quicquid de persona Lutheri sit) doctri- na Evangelica,ut ejus restitutio meruerit illam præ- dictionem, cujus organum etiam per alia vaticinia doctrinæ ipsius causa designatum fuisse constat; In- ventum enim nomen ejus, LUTHERUS, in statua quadam anno 1152. Aligerius Dantes anno 1321. præ- dixit, quo unus quinquies centum & decem, & quin- que (annus notatus 1515. quo Doctor renunciatus est) missus à Deo est. Joh. Huss martyr vaticinatus est anno 1414. Hodie anserem (quem notat nomen Hus lingua Bohemica) uritis, sed post centum annos ex meis cineribus nascetur cygnus, quem non poteritis assare. Hieronymus Pragensis vero itidem martyrio nobilis: Post centum annos respondebitis Deo & mi- hi,inquit: quod impletum cum Lutherus post 100. annos cygnus canere cœpit (novum hocce canti- cum) & respondere debuerunt Hieronymo (in Luthe- ro quasi redivivo) Papistæ, sed non valuere, quem- admodum de Hier. Savanarol. Anno 1498. quod Papæ contradiceret,exusto constat, ipsum prædixis- se, brevi oriturum Doctorem talem, cui nemo possit resistere: Item: Quendam instar Cyri Alpes transi- turum, & totam Ecclesiam (Papisticam) vastaturum, quod in B. Luthero paulo post impletum fuit:Qui- bus gemina prædixisse Joh. Heltenius dicitur: Alius quidam veniet Anno Domini 1516. (quo primas suas propositiones contra Pontificios proposuit B. Lu- therus T. I. Oper. Lat. Jen. f.) qui destruet vos, nec poteritis resistere. Qualia adduci possent plura.

Evangelium, quod in manu semper tenuit, ac ope divina excuti sibi passus non est B.Luther9 per orbem volitans etsi novum & quintum Evangelium calumniosse vocitent Papistæ, novum tamen canti- cum hic ab ipsoSpiritu S. citra veritatis & elogiiEv- angelii æterni detrimentum vocatur. Novum est Canticum, quia post antiquum de lege Domini mentibus hominum insculpta,& in Paradiso de ar- bore cognitionis boni &mali præscripta violatum, hoc ceu novum de salute hominum consilium ex æ- terno Dei Patris sinu productum, ac subinde, ceu novum, comparatione cum veteri pacto,quod fre- quentius & magis luculenter præ illo in libris Vet. Test. traditum, & exemplis illustratum est, repeti- tum, uti vice versa in N. T. libris oppido luculen- tius & frequentius doctrinaEvangelii tradita est,& perpetuo ceu novum in corde renovato ac novo fo- veri, repeti debet. Quod etiam novum eo nomine dicitur, quod valde eximium(quod novum signifi- care solet) jam etiam post Evangelii reformationẽ ceu renovatũ decantari debet, ubi à veteri depra- vatione cœlestis cantici, & verbi divini, per Heroa divinum, Angelumq; cœlestem id vindicatum est. Quæ vere novorum omnium, quæ sub cælo, novissi- ma sunt, quia unum illud sub sole novum,quod so- lum novum est, concernit, ut è Jer. XXXI. loquitur Damascenus, illud nempe ὁμολογεμένως μέγα μυ-

σήμιον τῆς ἀληθείας, quod Deus manifestatus est in carne &c. 1. Tim. 3, 16. Quod quantopere in Papatu corruptum fuerit, vel ex Articulis Smalcaldicis art. principali p. II. per scripta Megalandri illustratis manifestum est. Evangelium itaque æternum,quod Megalanders restituit, est de Christo, Agno illo pro pec- catis totius mundi occiso, Joh. I, 29. 1. Joh. II, 2. & gra- tuita remissione peccatorum propter δικαίωμα & satisfactionem ejus nobis in Veteri Testam. promif- sam, Exod. 34. Jerem. 31. in Novo Testamento ex- hibitam, Act. X, 43. deque gratiosa imputatione ju- stitiæ ejus, Esa. XLV, 24. Jer. XXIII, 6. c. XXXIII, 16. Rom.V, 18, 19. c. IV, 5. 6. Phil. III, 9. 2. Cor. V, 21. quæ non nisi per fidem apprehenditur, nobisq́; ap- propriatur, Rom. III, 23. seqq. c. IV, 11. 25. Phil. III, 9. Gal. II, 20. Quod æternum est à parte ante, uti vo- cant, quia Agnus occisus est ab origine mundi, Ap. XIII, 8. Ebr. XIII, 8. & à parte post, quia verbum illud manet in æternum, 1. Petr. I, 23. 25.

Id quanto Spiritu, qua contentione prædicarit populis & orbi universo B. Lutherus, quæ erat ἡ φωνὴ ἡ μεγάλη, Apoc. XIV, 7. testari potest cum articulis Smalcaldicis ; de hoc articulo, inquiens, part. II. art. 1. cedere, aut aliquid contra illum lar- giri aut permittere nemo piorum potest, etiamsi cœ- lum & terra & omnia corruant, professio ejus Tom. V. Jen. Germ. μετὰ παῤῥησίας vere Heroicæ facta his omnino verbis: Weil ich sehe/ daß diesen Haupt-Artickel der Teuffel immer muß lästern/ durch seine Säul-Lehrer, und nicht ruhen noch auf- hören kan; so sage ich D. M. Luther, unsers HErrn JEsu Christi unwürdiger Evangelist, daß diesen Artickel, (der Glaube allein, ohne alle Wercke,macht gerecht vor GOtt) soll lassen stehen und bleiben der Röm. Käyser, der Türckische, Tartarische Käyser, der Persen Käyser, der Papst, alle Cardinäle, Bi- schöfe, Prälaten, Pfaffen, Mönche, Nonnen, Kö- nige, Fürsten, Herren, alle Welt, sammt allen Teu- feln, und sollen das höllische Feuer darzu haben auf ihren Kopff, und keinen Danck darzu. Das sey meine D. Luthers Einsprechung vom H. Geiste, und das rechte H. Evangelium. Denn da stehet der Artickel, den die Kinder beten: Ich glaube an JE- sum Christum, gecreutziget, gestorben, 2c. Es ist ja niemand für unsere Sünde gestorben, denn allein JEsus Christus, GOttes Sohn; noch einmal sage ich, allein JEsus GOttes Sohn, hat uns von Sün- den erlöset, das ist gewißlich wahr, und die ganze Schrifft, und sollten alle Teufel und Welt sich zer- reissen und bersten, so ists wahr.

Cujus æterni Evangelii necessitatem, veritatem & suavitatem agnoverunt & degustarunt etiam sub medio Papatu, atque hodie quoque agnoscunt & degustant, qui ex eodem in agone eriguntur, de quibus vox cœlestis: Beati a modo, qui in Domino moriuntur,h. e. in fide illa in Christum Jesum dece- dunt. Testimonio sint Agenda Moguntina: Credis te meritis passionis Redemptoris nostri, & non pro- priis ad gloriam pervenire? Credo. Item recentiora agenda Moguntina de anno 1551. & 1599. Nun sind aber nicht allein deine, sondern auch aller Men- schen Verdienste viel zu klein und zu geringe darzu, daß ein Mensch sich der Seligkeit auf seine Wercke getrösten möchte. Da es aber an unsern Wercken und eigenen Verdiensten mangelt, da haben wir uns an die Verdienste Christi, unsers gemeinen Heylandes, zu halten, den GOtt aus Göttlicher Liebe gegen uns darum in die Welt gegeben hat, daß, wer an ihn gläubet, nicht verderben, sondern das ewige Leben haben soll. Auff den hat GOtt zuvor deine und aller Menschen Sünde geleget, und ihn um deine Sünde lassen verwundet und schmerz- lich geschlagen werden. Und die Straffe, die du für deine Sünde nach strenger Gerechtigkeit GOttes billig gedulden solltest, die hat GOtt zuvor an sei- nem einigen und geliebten Sohne erholen, und ihn schmertzlich leiden lassen für deine Sünde, auff daß er dein verschonen möchte. Auff diesen gnädi- gen und erbarmenden GOtt sollt du dein Vertrau- en steuren, ein frölich getrost Herke fassen, und dich für nichts fürchten, sondern eine steiffe Hoffnung und ungezweiffelte Zuversicht haben. Necnon Sa- cerdotale Roman. apud Cardin. Hosium in confessione fidei Petric. cap. 73. Credis non propriis meritis, sed passionis Domini nostri Jesu Christi virtute & merito ad gloriam perveniri? Respondet infirmus: Credo. Iterum Sacerdos : Credis, quod Dominus noster Jesus Christus pro nostra salute mortuus sit, & quod pro- priis meritis vel alio modo nullus possit salvari, nisi in merito passionis ejus? respondet infirmus:Credo.Ad- de rituale Monasticum justorum, informantibus moribundos, ex optimis quibusque ac Romano bræcipue & antiquiore depromptum Anno 1627. Sammielli editum: In quo Sacerdos quærit : Credis, non propriis meritis, sed passionis Domini nostri Jesu Christi virtute & merito ad gloriam perveniri? Respondet infirmus: Credo. Quærit porro Sacerdos : Credis, Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum pro nostra salute mortuum, & propriis meritis, vel ALIO MODO NULLUM POSSE SALVA- RI, NISI MERITO PASSIONIS EJUS? Re- spondet infirmus: Credo. Ordo baptizandi cum modo visitandi ægrotos Venetiis recusús Anno 1575. hæc habuit quondam, quæ jam expuncta sunt per indic.Expurgat.Bestiæ Roman. Credis, non pro- priis meritis, sed passionis Domini nostri Jesu Christi virtute & merito ad gloriam perveniri? Item: Cre- dis, quod Dominus noster Jesus Christus pro nostra salute mortuus sit, & quod ex propriis meritis vel ALIO MODO NULLUS possit salvari, nisi meri- to passionis ejus? Caspar Ulenbergius de caus. apo- stas. Colon. Anno 1589. Inveni librum quemdam in sacrario parochiali Ecclesiæ nostræ scriptum Anno salutis 1475. quo semper ab eo tempore in visitandis ad mortem præparandis usi sumus. In quo hæc le- guntur: Credis, te non posse salvari NISI per mortem Christi, &c. Respondet infirmus: Etiam. Tumilli di- citur: Age ergo dum superest in te anima, in hac sola morte fiduciam tuam constitue, in nulla alia re fidu- ciam habe, hac sola te totum contege, totum immisce te in hac morte, in hac morte totum te involve : Et si Dominus Deus voluerit te judicare, dic: Domine, mortem Domini nostri Jesu Christi objicio inter me & tuum judicium. Si dixerit tibi, quod meruisti damnationem, dic: Domine, mortem Domini no- stri Jesu Christi obtendo inter me & mala merita mea, ipsiusque meritum offero pro merito, quod ego debuissem habere, nec habeo. In summula Rai- mundi Colonienf. ann. 1498. edit. quærit Sacerdos: An credat pervenire ad regnum Dei non meritis suis, sed per merita Jesu Christi, & amarissimam ejus pas- sionem. In hortulo animæ, & apud Anshelm. Can- tuar. Episc. hic Dialogismus habetur: Credis, quod propter te est mortuus Dominus Jesus Christus Filius Dei? Etiam. Credis, non posse salvari, nisi per mortem ejus? Etiam. Talia plura adduci possent, & exem- plis pie defunctorum sub Papatu illustrari ad con- firmandum æternum Evangelium, quod unice sal- vificum est, & potentia Dei ad salutem omni cre- denti, Rom. I, 16. Huic Angelo Evangelistæ testimo- nium perhibuit referente Joh. Gastio Memorab.l.I. anno 1539. quidam Franciscanus: Evangelium, in- quit, tam clare & solide prædicatur nostro seculo atq́; temporibus Apostolorum. Prædixit vero Eundem

Sebastianus Doctor Theologiæ, Canonicus Erfurdi- ensis, & Canonicator in summo templo B. Virginis ann. 1500. Es wird die Zeit kommen, daß man auch das Evangelium wird aus dem Buche lesen. Hoc sine dubio Evangelium est, quod in manu Angeli visum est à S. Johanne. Et Richardus Armach. Epist. de N. T. cum hic liber inventus fuerit, inquiens, veritas toti mundo manifestabitur. Joh. Cellarius Li- psiæ ann. 1520. de Luthero sic scripsit: Martinus EVANGELICAM veritatem magis amat ac omnes adversarii.

Ad Evangelii æterni, quod in manu sua habuit Angelus ille, præconium, eiq; geminum Canticum novum, quod virgines electæ fideles Domini de- cantant in Ecclesia Evangelica, sequitur vox illa: Timete Dominum, siquidem pietatis mysterio hæc jun- genda sint timor Domini, & adoratio Tri-Unius Dei, in nomine Mediatoris Christi Θεανθρώπη, quæ sub Papatu vel siluit, sepulto magnam partem honore Redemptoris, & substituta vel certe coordinata illi (quæ tam simul consistere nequeunt, quam Deus Israëlis & idolum Philistinorum Dagon 1. Sam. V, 2.) Sanctorum & Angelorum veneratione religiosa, quam quoad unum Deum postulat prima tabula; vel obscurata fuit, per Mariolatriam, Angelola- triam, Hagiolatriam &c.multivariam vere supersti- tiosam & impiam: Vindicata autem voce ac scriptis Angeli Evangelistæ per orbem Christianum, teste historia & experientia. Hic primus & principalis articulus est, inquit B. Lutherus in articulis Smal- caldicis, quod Jesus Christus Deus & Dominus noster sit propter peccata nostra mortuus, & propter justi- tiam nostram resurrexerit Rom. IV. Et quod ipse solus sit Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi Joh. I. Et quod Deus omnium nostrum iniquitates in ipsum posuerit Esa. LIII. Omnes peccaverunt & justificantur gratis absque operibus seu meritis propriis ex ipsius gratia per redemptionem, quæ est in Christo Jesu, in sanguine ejus Rom. III. Hoc cum credere necesse sit, & nullo ope- re, lege aut merito acquiri & apprehendi possit, cer- tum est, & manifestum, solam hanc fidem nos justifi- care, sicut Paulus Rom. 3. inquit: Statuimus homi- nem justificari per fidem absque operibus legis. Item: Ut sit ipse justus & justificans eum, qui est ex fide Jesu Christi. Et de invocatione Sanctorum: Invocatio Sanctorum est etiam pars abusuum & errorum An- ti-Christi, pugnans cum primo principali articulo, & delens agnitionem Christi. Non etiam est mandata nec consilio nec exemplo, nec testimonio Scripturæ ni- titur. Omnia in Christo melius & certius nobis sunt proposita, ut non egeamus invocatione Sanctorum, etiamsi res pretiosa esset, cum tamen sit res maxime perniciosa. Etsi Angeli in cælo pro nobis orent (sicut ipse quoque Christus facit) & sancti in terris & for- tassis etiam in cælis, tamen inde non sequitur, Angelos & Sanctos à nobis esse invocandos, adorandos, jeju- niis, feriis, missis, oblationibus templorum, altarium cultuum fundationibus & aliis modis honorandos, ut Patronos & intercessores, & unicuique eorum cer- ta auxilia esse tribuenda, ut Papistæ docent & faci- unt. Hoc enim idololatricum est, & hic honos soli Deo tribuendus est. De missa: Quod missa in Papatu sit maxima & horrenda abominatio simpliciter & ho- stiliter è diametro pugnans contra articulum primum, quæ tamen præ omnibus aliis Pontificiis idololatriis summa & speciosissima fuit. Statuerunt enim, quod sacrificium istud, seu opus missæ etiam ab impio ac perdito nebulone præstitum liberet hominem à pec- catis, cum in hac vita, tum in purgatorio, cum tamen solus Agnus Dei nos liberet. In hoc articulo de missa concilium potissimum sudabit & consummabitur. Et- si enim possibile esset, ut omnes reliquos articulos nobis l concederent, tamen hunc concedere non poterunt, quemadmodum Campegius Augustæ dixit, se prius omnia tormenta, membrorum dilaniationem & mor- tem passurum, quam Missam missam facturum esse. Et ego etiam per Dei opem in cineres corpus meum re- digi & concremari patiar prius, quam ut Missarium ventrem, vel bonum vel malum, equiparari Christo Jesu, Domino & Servatori meo, aut eo superiorem esse feram. Sic scilicet in æternum disjungimur, & con- trarii invicem sumus. Sentiunt quidem optime: Ca- dente missa,cadere Papatum. Hoc priusquam patian- tur, omnes nos trucidabunt, si poterunt. Et porro: Draconis cauda ista (Missam intelligo) peperit multi- plices abominationes & idololatrias, quæ ordine ibi recensentur: 1. purgatorium, 2. apparitiones anima- rum, 3. peregrinationes, 4. fraternitates, 5. reliquiæ Sanctorum, refertæ variis mendaciis, ineptiis & fa- tuitatibus, 6. Indulgentiæ vivis & defunctis pro pecu- niæ attributæ. Addantur his collegia Canonicorum cathedralia, & monasteria, qualia in Papatu fuerunt cum Papæ potestate infinita & divina: Quam ido- lomaniam Papalem cum præcepto exclusive intel- ligendo secundum scripturam & Angeli præconi- um, timete Deum, multiplicem sane atque abomi- nandam in scriptis Megalandri convictam agno- scunt, & detestantur nunc post Angeli præconium multæ gentes,tribus,linguæ & populi, ut in aprico est.

Cæterum vox Evangelii non in genere de bono nuntio, utpote fidelibus è gentibus conversis de Ro- manorum oppressorum pœna, & ultione divina ad- versus eosdem brevi sequutura,ex quo illis quidem parum solatii accedere poterat; sed in specie de bo- no illo nuntio, quod in his libris ita κατ' ἀντονο- μασίαν vocatur, & significatu famosiori accipien- dum est, de gratia nempe divina in Christo JESU Agno illo pro nobis occiso toti generi humano exhi- bita, qua fruuntur fideles cum Eulogia nominis di- vini. Quod in lucem vicissim protulit, & magna voce, potenti, & efficaci præconio asseruit B. Lu- therus, ab electis celebratur, ejusdem doctrinæ ad- hærentibus. Canticum enim novum & Evangelium æternum hic idem esse materialiter diximus. Quod æternum dicitur Evangelium, quia consilii æterni & libri vitæ de agno occiso ab origine mundi partem ali- quam continet, Apoc.XIII, 8. c. XVII, 8. & in æter- num sese efficacia sua porrigit, Rom.I, 16. Est enim Evangelium illud potentia Dei ad salutem (æternam) omni credenti: Quod in aureis suis ad Galatas com- mentariis maxime B. Lutherus docuit. Ea ratione æternum Evangelium illud nuntium de puniendis Romanis dici non potest.

De judicio autem per septem phialas indicato, quod huc minime facit (si retineatur hic glossa Grotiana de puniendis Romanis gentilibus, idolola- tris,) quum Romanum Papatum concernant phia- læ, postea.

Adoratio copulari probe potest cum timore, ut non opus sit sensu illativo, quum proprius retineri copulæ usus queat, & exegeticus dimitti. Neque illud ἐξηγητικῶς v.6.necessario accipiendum,quum sensus usitatior copulativus locũ habeat, imo non, quod intendere Grotius per exegeticum sensum videtur,de gentibus tantum conversis,sed quibus- vis populis &tribubus Judaicis & Ethnicis ad fidem Christi perductis, in Ecclesia agentibus, sermo sit, & ad omnes populos præconium Angelicum diri- gatur, soli Deo conditori cœli, terræ, maris, & flu- minum honor deferendus prædicatur, tum ut ve- rum σέβασμα à falsis sive in cœlo, sive in terra sint, Angelis, & Sanctis, quæ in Papatu coluntur, discer- natur, tum ut omnibus illorum incolis officium istud venerationis incumbere doceatur.

Hora autem judicii non particularis in Romanos, sed universalis in omnes homines imminere dicitur. Quia hoc κατ' ἐξοχὴν, & absolute dicitur judici- um: & hoc præconium fit omnibus gentibus & populis per orbem, omnibusq; injungitur Dei illius venera- tio religiosa. Ideo etiam causam, quæ affertur, ab obligatione tum erga unum creatorem, tum erga futurum judicem, cui omnium genua flectere se te- nebuntur, Esa. 45, 23. Rom. 14, 11. 12. communis esse debet atque universalis: qualis non est particulare quoddam judicium; Sonus prædicationis hujus, in- quit B. Gravius, ipsam Hispaniam, Gallias, Italiam, Siciliam ipsamque Græciam & Orientem penetravit: Ad hanc efficacem prædicationem & celerem Angeli præconis volatum pertinet mulieris ex deserto redi- tus isque primo particularis, & deinde sub finem 1260. dierum universalis. Sed finis dierum est terminus mansionis in deserto & finis mundi. Nullus ergo sperandus reditus, nedum universalis.

II. ANGELUS ALIUM CASUM BABY- LONIS INTIMANS. Vers. 8.

Καὶ ἄλλ@ Ἄγγελο- δεύτερ@- ἠκολούθησε λέγων, ἔπεσεν ἔπε- σε Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη.] Est Præteritum pro futuro more Pro- phetico. Et breviter hic prædicitur, quod infra plenius 18, 2. Roma pagana, aut sane à paganismo non repurgata vocatur Babylon, ut recte explicant Tertullianus adversus Judæos & III. contra Marcionem, Hieronymus prologo ad Didymum fine secundi adversus Jovianum, ad Esa. 24. & 47. epistola ad Algasiam & altera ad Marcellam, & alii; quia scilicet perin- de erat magna regno superba, & sanctorum debellatrix, ut ait Tertullianus, adde & alia, quæ habes apud Orosium II, 2. Sumpta verba ex Esa. 21, 9. Jer. 51, 8. In Manuscripto: Καὶ ἄλλ@- Ἄγγελο- δεύτερ@-. Ἐκ τῶ οἴνε τῶ θυμῶ τῆς πορνείας ἀυτῆς πεπότικε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.] Manuscriptus ἡ ἐκ τῶ οἴνε &c. Quomodo & Latinus legit. Θυμὸς autem hic venenum significat, ut Deut. 32, 24. Job. 6,4. c. 20, 16. Psalm. 58, 5. Est ergo οἶν@- θυμῶ vinum venena- tum potio lethifera. Πορνεία hic est idolatria, quam Roma gentibus subditis sociisque propinaverat. Vino comparatur, quicquid mentem externat, infra XVII, 14. Exemplis facile corrumpuntur homines, vid. 1. Macc. I, 45. Angelus ille alter non immerito constituitur à B. Gravio B. Chemnitius, alter Martinus, qui Baby- lonis casum per Examen Concilii Tridentini, quo erigereBabylonem illud conatum est, denunciavit, imo demonstravit, ejusque scortationem spiritua- lem, idololatriam & superstitionem fædam ac multi- plicem orbi detexit: quam casus gravissimus pœna- lis certo sequuturus est. Apostasiam Romæ etiam manifestavit B. Nic. Hunnius: Ea per Angelos Dei demonstrata cecidit Babylon magna, quæ scortata est hactenus cum plerisque in orbe, & vinum scor- tationis propinavit omnibus gentibus, magna illa ci- vitas magna scortatrix, cecidit in mentibus plurimo- rum, in quibus sedem & dominium quondam ha- buit. Confectus est Antichristus voce Domini, pro- ximus etiam casui cum temporali corporali, tum æ- terno cum infernali exitio conjuncto. Romam Ba- bylonem vocari non paganam tantum, sed etiam An- tichristianam ad XIII. caput docebitur. Quod vero de θυμῶ dicitur, eo venenum significari non diffi- culter admittimus. Ex vino veneni, inquit B. Glassius in Gramm. S. h. e. ex vino venenato. Θυμὸς enim hoc loco venenum est ex usu linguæ Hellenisticæ, qua θυ- μὸς voci Ebrææ חמה respondet, quæ & excandescen- tiam & venenum (Pf. LIIX, 5. Pf. CXL, 4. Job. VI, 4. Deut. XXXII, 33.) significat. Sed potest usitata signi- ficatio vocis θυμῶ retineri. Permittit enim Deus justo judicio tales seductiones, ut contemtus Evan- gelii puniatur, 2. Thess. II, 10. Lutherus vocem θυμῶ videtur non legisse. Proclamat ergo Angelus alter de casu & ruina Babylonis 1. spirituali: partim quia cecidit de throno infallibilitatis, quam in doctrina fidei jactitavit, sed dejecta inde est proprio suo te- stimonio C. Si Papa. dist. 40. Certum etiam est fa- tente Adriano VI. l. IV. sentent. de sacr. confirm. art. 3. quod Pontifex errare possit hæresin per suam deter- minationem aut decretalem asserendo, & Pontifices nonnullos hæreticos fuisse, quales censentur Zephe- rinus Montanizans à B. Rhenano l. Tertull. c. prax. Liberius Arianizans, compil. Chron. Honorius I. Monotheleta, Adrianus anno 772. idololatra, Gre- gorius VII. Berengarii discipulus, Johannes XXIII. vitam æternam post hanc vitam esse negans Eugenii IV. in concil. Basil. sess. 4. A. 1439. hæreticus declara- tus &c. partim quia defecit à Christiana veritate ad superstitiones & ritus ac ceremonias paganas, quod in Apost. Rom. Eccl. demonstravit B. Nic. Hunnius: Nonne hic insignis est casus? 2. Corporali à throno Majestatis, quia decem cornua vel Reges devicti sunt ab Agno, utpote, Angliæ, Scotiæ, Daniæ, Nor- wegiæ, Sueciæ, Hungariæ, Bohemiæ, Germaniæ, Po- loniæ, Russiæ vel Moscoviæ, in quo imperio Domi- nica Quadragesima quotannis Pontifex Rom. ex- communicatur. Cujus ergo imperii decem cornua ruunt, illud insignem ruinam tanto clamore digna perpessum esse oportet. Adde quod, testibus ipsis- met Pontificiis scriptoribus, ceciderit quoque do- natio Constantini, atque ita etiam Italia exciderit Pontifex Rom. Quæ major ipsi accidere ruina po- terat? 3. Æternali: quandoquidem Pontifex Ro- manus ceu Pseudo-Propheta brevi in stagnum ignis æterni conjiciendus sit Apoc. XX, 10. quæ ruina non tam hic indicata est, quam Apoc. XIX, 20. intimata.

III. TERTIUS ANGELUS, POENAM ADO- RANTIBUS BESTIAM DENUNTIANS.

## 14:9
Ver. 9. And another third Angel followed them.] As many things to be announced, so many messengers. In the Manuscript instead of αὐτοῖς [them] is αὐτῷ [him].

Saying with a loud voice. As heralds about to publish edicts.

If anyone worships the beast. If anyone as an idolater enslaves himself. Above XIII, 4. 12. Προσκυνεῖν sometimes governs the Dative, sometimes the Accusative.

And his image. Here 'Καὶ' is put for 'or': or if anyone bows down before an idolatrous image.

And receives a mark on his forehead, or on his hand. Again 'καὶ' for a disjunctive. And by 'χάραγμα' he understands equally those things which are equivalent, namely the name or the number, as above XIII, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 9. Καὶ ἄλλος Ἄγγελος τρίτος ἠκολούθησεν αὐτοῖς.] Quot res nunciandæ, totidem nuntii. In Manuscripto pro αὐτοῖς est αὐτῷ.

Λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ.] Ut præcones edicta publicaturi.

Εἴ τις προσκυνεῖ τὸ θηρίον.] Si quis idololatrix se manci- pat. Supra XIII, 4. 12. Προσκυνεῖν modo Dativum regit, mo- do Accusativum.

Καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ.] Καὶ hic pro vel ponitur: aut si quis procumbat ante simulachrum idololatricum.

Καὶ λαμβάνει χάραγμα ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου αὐτοῦ, ἢ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖ- ρα αὐτοῦ.] Rursum καὶ pro disjunctiva. Et per χάραγμα simul intelligit ea, quæ sunt paria, nomen scilicet aut numerum, ut supra XIII, 16.

## 14:10
Vers. 10. And he shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation. God will give them also a deadly potion. A cup or goblet is called a portion, attributed to each by God of good or evil, in which sense 'two urns on the floor of Zeus' [are found], in Homer. The cup of wrath is sad things. See Psalm 75:8, Isaiah 51:17, 22, Habakkuk 2:16, Jeremiah 25:15, ch. 49:12, ch. 51:7, below 18:6. Thence is taken the expression which is in Isaiah 19:14. 'κεράννυσθαι' properly is to mix, as Plutarch explains: by catachresis it is also taken for to pour in. But here it can be taken properly, so that it is understood as unmixed wine mixed with poisonous herbs. It does not lack efficacy, what he said, 'unmixed' [merum]. For diluted wine attracts the poisonous force less. In the Manuscript it is: 'Ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου'.

And he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy Angels and in the presence of the Lamb. These words are indeed sufficiently apt to signify the punishments after the resurrection, as can be seen in Matthew 5:22, 13:41, 50, 18:8, 9, 25:41. But since below, where the words are similar to these in 19:20, it is not a matter of that time, as the following shows, it seems that here too that interpretation should be taken which pertains to this cup, so that it is understood as the conscience burning within, with Christ and the Angels aware: which is a certain kind of lodging of Gehenna. Thus poets say that breasts are burned by the torches of the Furies.

Latin:

Vers. 10. Καὶ αὐτὸς πίεται ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, τοῦ κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ.] Deus illis quoque potionem letiferam dabit. Calix aut poculum dici- tur portio, cuique à Deo attributa boni aut mali, quo sensu δύω πίθοι ἐν Διὸς οὔδει, apud Homerum. Poculum iræ sunt res tristes. Vide Psalm. 75, 8. Esa. 51, 17. 22. Abac. 2, 16. Jer. 25, 15. c. 49, 12. c. 51, 7. infra 18, 6. Inde sumpta loquutio, quæ est Esa. 19, 14. κεράννυσθαι proprie est miscere, ut exponit Plutarchus: per κατάχρησιν sumitur etiam pro infundere. At hic potest proprie sumi, ut intelligatur merum mixtum herbis venenife- ris. Non caret efficacia, quod dixit merum. Nam vinum di- lutum minus attrahit vim venenatam. In Manuscripto est: Ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου.

Καὶ βασανισθήσεται ἐν πυρὶ κὶ θείῳ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἁγίων Ἀγγέ- λων καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου.] Sunt quidem hæc verba satis apta ad significanda supplicia post resurrectionem, ut videre est Matth. V, 22. XIII, 41. 50. XVIII, 8. 9. XXV, 41. Sed cum infra ubi verba sunt his similia XIX, 20. non agatur de illo tempo- re, ut sequentia ostendunt, videtur & hic ea sumenda inter- pretatio, quæ ad hoc poculum pertineat, ut intelligatur con- scientia intus adurens, conscio Christo & Angelis: quod est quoddam velut hospitium gehennæ. Sic furiarum facibus adu- ri pectora dicunt & Poëtæ.

## 14:11
Vers. 11. And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever. The memory of the tortures which they endured will remain forever. For words testifying to the lacerations of the soul often break forth from the impious, as in Tiberius in the letter which is in Tacitus and Suetonius. Smoke is a sign of a conflagration, Isaiah 34:10, where see the remarks, and below 19:3.

And they have no rest day and night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name. They are compelled

To carry one's own witness by night and by day. Formerly, in the times of ignorance, concerning which Acts 14:15, 17:30-31, those things were done without any sense of conscience. This could not happen now, since the Gospel had such great testimonies of its truth, the miracles of Christ and his disciples, a most holy life, and constancy in enduring death. These could not but prick the minds, however hardened. See above 11:10, where it is ἐβασάνισαν τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. There is no peace for the wicked, Isa. 48:22, 57:21.

Punishment follows guilt. Spiritual fornication is the judgment of God against the lovers of the harlot, the worshippers of the beast. Therefore, it treats of the fall, which is like guilt, and of the destruction, which is like punishment. The judgment that awaits the worshippers of the beast is now denounced, which will soon be intimated to the worshippers of God by a heavenly voice. Finally, it will be taught by another Angel that judgment regarding both, and in general, all the faithful and unfaithful, is imminent on the day of universal judgment: which will bring a blessed harvest to the former, but to the latter a most unhappy one, joined with trampling in the winepress of Divine wrath. Therefore, the Song of the faithful and the proclamation of the Gospel are joined with the blessedness of those who accept it and cease to worship Babylon; but the temporal and eternal punishment of the unfaithful and those adhering to the beast for their apostasy from the Gospel is intimated in this chapter and denounced by different Angels. Those who take the place of this third Angel are those who, opposing with great spirit those who attempt to support the falling Babylon, and who teach that the βδελύγματα of the Roman and Antichristian Papacy are to be tolerated without anathemas—we call them Calixtines—have openly demonstrated that those who commit fornication with that great harlot, and receive her mark, or lead by the hand or excuse those who receive it, will drink of the wine of Divine wrath and be tormented eternally; such as were those in the previous century who, not without great danger, manfully opposed themselves to the Augustan Sphinx in the Metaxic book, both orthodox Theologians and Confessing Princes alike, as well as those who, when Calixtus with his associates and Helmstadt brood—namely, the Son, Horneius, Musaeus, (I point to Petrus), Henichius, Latermannus, Mich. Behmius, Drejerus, etc.—devoted effort to recalling and propagating Interimistic errors. They met the Rinteln and Königsberg men with the usual writings, fearing nothing from the threats and dangers of great Princes: such as the blessed Wellerus, the blessed Hülsemannus, the blessed Myslenta, and others, among whom I, the most unworthy of all, have professed my name not without danger, yet fearlessly, and still do, as the necessity of the matter demands.

But how alien Calixtus and his associates are from the judgment of this Angel, with their judgment and the Julian piety, as they call it, is clearer than the sun. For they fight tooth and nail that Papal and Anti-Christian dogmas and the Pontificians asserting them—which is manifest from all those making a profession of the Tridentine faith according to the command of the Anti-Christ—can and ought to be borne without anathema: but this Angel denounces against them a most grave anathema, with the Apostle of the Gentiles leading the way, Gal. 1:7, 9: If I or an Angel from heaven should preach another Gospel, let him be anathema: Concerning which, in the commentary on that place, when things said by him and from our blessed Luther are seen, with a loud voice, so that it may be heard by all (by the Calixtines at any rate), if anyone has worshipped the beast, etc., and he (with the beast itself) will be tormented with fire before the Lamb, to whom the beast opposed itself, and the bloody smoke of him will ascend for ever and ever. Whether a more brilliant condemnatory sentence could have been brought against the Calixtine, I for my part do not doubt without cause, and all the orthodox doubt with me, abominating the beast, as is fitting, according to the prayer of the blessed Luther: may God fill us with hatred of the Pope. We add the ὁμοψηφίαν of the blessed Gravius: Some understand by the third Angel Chemnitius, who quite openly exposed the marks of the beast in his examination of the Council of Trent. But he is rather to be referred to the class of the second Angel, as one who clearly exposed the fall of Babylon to the whole world. In my own judgment (yet without prejudice to others), I posit that there is noted here some distinguished and spirited Doctor of the Church, who in this turbulent century is to rebuke with a heroic Spirit, along with his assistants, the hypocrisy and inconstancy of many Evangelicals, because they have partly returned to the flesh-pots of Egypt out of fear, partly, by worshipping the two-horned beast, have with it attacked the orthodox Church, and partly because, struck by excessive terror, they have been neither cold nor hot spectators of such tyranny? And therefore this Angel will warn them in time, so that they may repent, lest they taste the wine of the wrath of God, offered to the Babylonian harlot, and be made partakers with her of both temporal and eternal punishments. What else is a conscience burning within for ever and ever than the eternal infernal punishment, which will be the perpetual gnawing worm and the unquenchable fire, Isa. 66, last verse, Mark 9:48.

A HEAVENLY VOICE CONCERNING THE BLESSEDNESS OF THOSE DYING IN THE LORD.

Latin:

Vers. 11. Καὶ ὁ καπνὸς τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῶν εἰς αἰῶνας αἰώ- νων ἀναβαίνει.] Manebit semper memoria cruciatuum quos pertulere. Errumpunt enim impiis sæpe verba laniationes ani- mi testantia, ut Tiberio in epistola, quæ est apud Tacitum & Suetonium. Fumus nota incendii, Esa. 34, 10. ubi dicta vide, & infra 19, 3.

Καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσι ἀνάπαυσιν ἡμέρας κὶ νυκτὸς οἱ προσκυνοῦντες τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἴ τις λαμβάνει τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ ὀ- νόματος αὐτοῦ.] Coguntur

Nocte dieque suum gestare in pectore testem. Olim ignorantiæ temporibus, de quibus Act. XIV, 15. XVII, 30. 31. fiebant ista sine sensu ullo conscientiæ. Id nunc fieri non poterat, cum Evangelium tanta haberet veritatis suæ te- stimonia, miracula Christi & discipulorum ejus, vitam sanctis- simam, constantiam in perferenda morte. Hæc animos, quam- vis durissimos, non poterant non vellicare. Vide supra XI, 10. ubi est ἐβασάνισαν τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. Non est pax impiis, Esa. XLVIII, 22. LVII, 21.

Culpam sequitur pœna. Fornicationem spiri- tualem judicium Dei contra amasios meretricis cultores bestiæ. De casu ergo, qui culpæ, & de exi- tio, quod pœnæ instar est, agitur. Judicium, quod manet cultores bestiæ, jam denunciatur, quod cul- tores Dei, mox à cœlesti voce intimabitur. Tan- dem ab Angelo alio judicium quoad utrosque, & in genere, fideles & infideles universos in die panto- critico imminere docebitur: quod illis beatam mes- sem, his vero infelicissimam & cum conculcatione in torculari iræ Divinæ conjunctam afferet. Fide- lium ergo Canticum & Evangelii præconium cum suscipientium & Babylonem colere desinentium beatitudine conjunctum: infidelium autem & be- stiæ adhærentium apostasiæ ab Evangelio supplici- um temporale & æternum hoc capite intimatur, & ab Angelis diversis denunciatur. Tertij hujus An- geli vicem sunt, qui ruenti Babyloni dextram sup- ponere conatis, βδελύγματα Romani & Antichri- stiani Papatus citra anathemata toleranda, docen- tibus Calixtinos dicimus, sese magno animo oppo- nentes, palam demonstrarunt, cum meretrice illa magna scortantes, & characterem ejus suscipientes, vel eos, qui suscipiunt manu ducentes, aut excusan- tes, bibituros ex vino iræ Divinæ æternum crucian- dos, quales seculo superiori fuerunt, qui sese Sphyn- gi Augustanæ libro Metaxico, non absque magnó discrimine opposuerunt masculè, orthodoxi Theo- logi pariter & Principes Confessores, necnon qui In- terimisticis erroribus revocandis & propugnandis quum operam navaret Calixtus cum sociis & pullis Helmstadiensibus Filio nempe, Hornejo, Museo, (Petrum indigito) Henichio, Latermanno, Mich. Behmio, Drejero, &c. Rintelensibus & Regiomonta- nis solitis scriptis iisdem obviam iverunt, nihil ex- timescentes minas & pericula magnorum Princi- pum: utpote B. Wellerus, B. Hülsemannus, B. Mys- lenta, & alii, inter quos Ego, indignissimus omnium, nomen meum non absque periculo, in- trepide tamen, professus sum, & adhuc, exigente rei necessitate, profiteor.

Quam autem alieni sint ab hujus Angeli judicio Calixtus, & socii cum suo judicio & pietate Julia, quam vocant, sole clarius est. Illi enim sine ana- themate ferri posse ac debere, & dogmata Papalia Anti-Christiana & Pontificios illa profitentes ad- serentes, quod ab omnibus fieri professionem fidei Tridentinæ juxta præceptum Anti-Christi facien- tibus in propatulo est, πὺξ καὶ λὰξ dimicant: Hic vero denunciat illis gravissimum anathema, præ- eunte gentium Apostolo, Gal. I, 7. 9. Si ego vel An- gelus de cœlo aliud Evangelium prædicaverit, ana- thema esto: Quo de in comment. ad istum locum cum, & ex B. Luthero nostro dicta videantur, voce magna, ut ab omnibus exaudiatur (à Calixtinis utique exaudita) si quis bestiam adoraverit, &c. & ille, (cum ipsa bestia) cruciabitur igne coram Agno, cui se opposuit bestia, & fumus cruentus ejus ascendet in secula seculorum. Quæ sententia condemnatoria num luculentior adversus Calixti- num ferri potuisset, equidem non immerito dubi- to, dubitantque mecum omnes orthodoxi, besti- am, prout par est, juxta B. Lutheri votum, impleat nos Deus odio Papæ, abominantes. Addimus ὁμο- ψηφίαν B. Gravii: Per tertium Angelum intelligunt nonnulli Chemnitium, qui characteres bestiæ in exami- ne concilii Tridentini satis aperte detexit. Sed is potius ad classem secundi Angeli referendus, utpote qui la- psum Babylonis toti mundo luculenter exposuit. Meo quidem judicio (sine tamen aliorum prejudicio) sta- tuo notari hic insignem aliquem & animosum Eccle- siæ Doctorem, qui hoc turbulento seculo heroico Spi- ritu cum suis Parastatis reprehensurus sit multorum Evangelicorum hypocrisin & inconstantiam, quod partim metu reversi sint ad ollas Ægyptiacas, partim bestiam bicornem venerantes, cum eadem orthodoxam Ecclesiam oppugnarint, partim quod nimio terrore perculsi neque frigidi, neque calidi spectatores tantæ tyrannidis fuerint? Ideoque mature, ut resipiscant, monebit Angelus hic, ne gustent vinum iræ Dei, me- retrici Babylonicæ propinatum, & tam temporalium quam æternarum pœnarum cum ea participes red- dantur. Conscientia intus adurens in secula secu- lorum quid aliud est, quam pœna infernalis æter- na, quæ erit vermis rodens perpetuus, & ignis in- extinguibilis, Es. 66. vers. ult. Marc. 9, 48.

VOX CŒLESTIS DE BEATITUDINE MORIENTIUM IN DOMINO.

## 14:12
Verse 12.

Here is the patience of the saints, here are those who keep the commandments of God and the faith.] In the Manuscript: here is the patience of the saints, those who keep, so that it is keeping instead of of those keeping, a locution which we have had more than once, namely nominatives instead of obliques, as we said is found in Homer at Mark 6:40. Nor does the Latin read and accept it otherwise here. In this matter is the patience of the saints, who keep the faith and precepts of God: that is, from this matter arises, through this matter is sustained, the fact that they know idolaters are not absolved by their own judgment. Thus we had ὧδε above 13:10, 18. The sense is from Daniel 12:12.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

Ὧδε ὑπομονὴ τῶν ἁγίων ἐστὶν, ὧδε οἱ τηρῶντες τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ Θεῦ καὶ τὴν πίσιν.] In Manuscripto: ὧδε ἡ ὑπομονὴ τῶν ἁγίων ἐστὶν, οἱ τηρῶντες, ut sit τηρῶντες pro τηρούντων, qualem loquutio- ne.n non semel habuimus, rectos nimirum pro obliquis, ut apud Homerum reperiri diximus ad Marc. VI, 40. Neque ali- ter hic legit & accepit Latinus. In hac re est patientia sancto- rum, qui Dei fidem ac præcepta servant: id est, ex hac re ori- tur, per hanc rem sustentatur, quod sciunt idololatras suopte judicio non absolvi. Sic ὧδε habuimus supra 13, 10. 18. Sen- sus ex Daniele 12, 12.

## 14:13
Verse 13. And I heard a voice from heaven, saying to me.] He hears a Divine voice, so that the matter might be more certain. See Matt. 3:17, ch. 17:7, John 12:28.

Write. Write a noble sentence.

Blessed are the dead.] Just as מות is called a grievous vexation by the Hebrews, so מתים are νεκροὶ, those who are grievously vexed, to whom life is not vital, Coloss. III, 3.

Those who die in the Lord.] That is, those who undergo the dangers of death for the sake of Christ. Thus ἀποθνήσκειν is taken in 1 Cor. 15, 31. Ἐν Κυρίῳ means for the sake of the Lord, after the manner of the Hebrews, who use ב in this way. See Rom. 16, 1, 8, 12. Gen. 18, 28, and following, c. 29, 18, 20. Hosea 12, 13. So also Eph. 4, 1.

From now on, says the Spirit, yes, that they may rest from their labors.] Even now I promise for certain, says the Spirit of God, that it shall be that they will rest from their labors. Ἄρτι means now, Matth. 11, 12, c. 26, 53, Joh. 2, 10; ἀπ᾿ ἄρτι, from this time, even now, Joh. 13, 18, מעתה. Ναὶ is of one promising, as μάλιστα in law, 2 Cor. I, 17, 18, 19, 20, above I, 7. And thus ἵνα follows correctly after ναί. They will not only be blessed in the other life hereafter, but also at this very time. They labor indeed, but in their labor they have rest, that is, peace of conscience opposed to the torments of the wicked, of whom it was treated above. See Psalm 116, 6.

And their works follow with them.] In the manuscript it is better: Τὰ γὰρ, just as the Latin also reads. That peace arises from the memory of things rightly done. Deeds by metonymy for the memory of things rightly done. Ἀκολουθεῖν often governs the accusative without a preposition; sometimes a preposition is attached, as ὀπίσω, 1 Kings 19, 20, Isa. 45, 14, Ezek. 29, 16, Matth. 10, 38. Here μετὰ.
