Thus Isocrates in the Plataicus: They were compelled to follow with their bodies after them. There is a similar sentiment among the Hebrews: Thy righteousness shall go before thy face. It is read twice in the book concerning the life and death of Moses.

So that they may be stirred up to constancy and patience, holding the faith of Jesus and keeping the Divine commandments, and not fail from the faith, by the blessedness of those dying in the Lord, by the rest from the labors of even afflictions, and by the works of celebration and confession of the Divine which will follow them, if they persevere to the end, in the midst of afflictions also, not about to desert the same, they are admonished. I interpret the works that will follow them as those to which they devoted effort here, namely the works of confession and celebration of the divine name of holiness and justice. For they will be given over to them forever, and consequently they will also perceive their fruit and gracious reward forever, namely, heavenly blessedness consisting in rest from every evil and in an abundance of all-encompassing happiness: which is promised to the constant faithful and holy. This passage makes entirely against of the final judgment, as Bellarmine, l. I. de purgat. c. 8, and Costerus in Enchirid. c. 6, wish; but from the death of each individual, as Richard of St. Victor and Haymo explain it, and Bellarmine and James Tirinus do not entirely deny this in this place; from now, that is, from this moment, not waiting for the day of the final judgment. The Lord wished to signify, says Gregory of Valencia, l. de purgat. c. 8, p. 285, at this very time, in which the Church now militates on earth, that there is also in the heavenly kingdom some triumphant Church, where the blessed may rest. Blasius Viegas calls this the common explanation. See Ribera on this passage. Aretas arranges the words so that the Spirit may console those who will then live and militate, and that they may always be blessed who die in the Lord. Therefore, from now signifies from the time of death, as Augustine, Haymo, and Bede explain from Psalm CXXVI; the Anglo-Rheims translators on this passage indeed wish nothing else to be implied than that they rest from the labors of this life: to which Salmeron adds in 1 Cor. XV, disp. 26. See also Tirinus on this passage. But Viega compares Heb. IV, where the Apostle calls heavenly glory a Sabbatism, because it is an entry into the rest of the Lord, of which Psalm XIV and CXIV speak. Ribera, however, explicitly says on this passage: To be blessed is to perceive perfect blessedness. Suidas also renders it as clearly, entirely, and completely, ἀπηρτισμένως, to which nothing can be added. But such perfect blessedness of man will follow in the world to come. Moreover, neither does that which souls perceive immediately upon their departure consist with the flames and punishments of purgatory, which the Papists commonly believe differs from the fire of hell only in duration; and Grotius here plays the midwife to them. Nor indeed is there any reason why we should think, with certain Papists who are accustomed to object this, especially Alcazar, as well as Ambrose, that St. John is speaking only of living perfect and holy martyrs. Viega acknowledges as more true the common opinion, which refers this passage not only to martyrs, but to all the saints. For, he says, Bede, Andreas Caesariensis, Primasius Pannonius, Joachim Abbas, Ansbertus, Haymo, and Richard of St. Victor teach this. Bernard understood it thus in Epistle XCVIII. Which Church he also proposes in the office of the dead for all the just, and therefore Lorinus on Acts VII, on the words 'he fell asleep in the Lord,' professes that it must be retained. And Grotius acknowledges thus far the truth of our explanation, when he renders this meaning: Not only will they be blessed in the other life, but also at this very time. However, he does not explain quite conveniently that 'their deeds will follow them': That peace will arise from the memory of deeds rightly done. For although the causal sense of the particle ᾑ can be admitted, which does not conflict with our explanation, yet what solid joy can there be from the memory of deeds rightly done, when no one lives always without sin, 1 Kings VIII, Prov. XX, and we all stumble in many things, James III, 2. St. Augustine also explains it concerning a spiritual wound.

THE ANGEL INDICATING THE HARVEST AND THE VINTAGE.

Latin:

Vers. 13. Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ ὀρανοῦ, λεγούσης μοι.] Vo- cem audit Divinam, quo res esset certior. Vide Matth. 3, 17. c. 17, 7. Joh. 12, 28.

Γράψον.] Scribe nobilem sententiam.

Μακάριοι οἱ νεκροὶ.] Sicut מות Ebræis dicitur gravis ve- xatio, ita מתים νεκροὶ, qui graviter vexantur, quibus vita vitalis non est Coloss. III, 3.

Οἱ ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀποθνήσκοντες.] Id est, qui Christi causa mortis pericula adeunt. Ita ἀποθνήσκειν sumitur 1. Cor. 15, 31. Ἐν Κυρίῳ propter Dominum, Ebræorum more, qui ב fic usurpant. Vi- de Rom. 16, 1. 8. 12. Gen. 18, 28. & deinceps c. 29, 18. 20. Oseæ 12, 13. Sic & Eph. 4, 1.

Ἀπάρτι λέγει ναὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα, ἵνα ἀναπαύσωνται ἐκ τῶν κόπων αὐτῶν.] Jam nunc pro certo polliceor, ait Dei Spiritus, fore, ut a laboribus suis quiescant. Ἄρτι nunc Matth. 11, 12. c. 26, 53. Joh. 2, 10. ἀπ᾿ ἄρτι, ab hoc tempore, jam nunc, Joh. 13, 18. מעתה. Ναὶ est promittentis, ut μάλισα in jure, 2. Cor. I, 17. 18. 19. 20. supra I, 7. Et ita ἵνα recte sequetur post ναί. Non tantum olim beati erunt in altera vita, sed & hoc ipso tempo- re. Laborant quidem, sed in labore habent quietem, id est, pacem conscientiæ oppositam tormentis impiorum, de qui- bus actum est supra. Vide Psalm. 116, 6.

Τὰ δὲ ἔργα αὐτῶν ἀκολουθεῖ μετ᾿ αὐτῶν.] In Manuscripto melius: Τὰ γὰρ, quomodo & Latinus legit. Pax illa oritur ex memoria recte factorum. Facta per μετωνυμίαν pro memo- ria recte factorum. Ἀκολουθεῖν sæpe Accusativum regit sine bræpositione, interdum Præpositio subnectitur, ut ὀπίσω, 1. Reg. 19, 20. Esa. 45, 14. Ezech. 29, 16. Matth. 10, 38. Hic με- τὰ. Sic Isocrates in Plataico: Τοῖς μὲν σώμασι μετ᾿ ἐκείνων ἀ- κολουθεῖν ἠναγκάζοντο. Est sententia similis apud Ebræos: Justitia tua ante faciem tuam ibit. Bis legitur in libro de vita & morte Mosis.

Ut ad constantiam & patientiam fidem Jesu te- nentes & mandata Divina custodientes, nec defi- ciant à fide, beatitudine decedentium in Domi- no, quiete à laboribus etiam afflictionum, & ope- ribus celebrationis & confessionis Divinæ sequutu- ris ipsos excitentur, si ad finem perseverarint, in mediis quoque afflictionibus, eandem haud deser- turi, commonefiunt. Opera sequutura illos interpre- tor, quibus hic operam navarunt, utpote opera con- fessionis, & celebrationis nominis divini sanctitatis & justitia. Illis enim in æternum dediti erunt, & pro- inde æternum etiam eorum fructum, ac præmium gratiosum sentient beatitudinem nempe cœlestem in quiete ab omni malo, & affluentia felicitatis omnigenæ consistentem: quæ constantibus fideli- bus & sanctis promissa est. Facit hic locus omnino contra purgatorium Papisticum. Vox enim ἀπάρτι non est inde ab extremo judicio, ut Bellarm. l. I. de purgat. c. 8. Costerus in Enchirid. c. 6. volunt; sed à morte uniuscujusq́;, ut Richardo de S. Victore, Hay- moni, sic explicanti non plane abnuunt Bellarmi- nus, & Jacobus Tirinus in h. l. à modo id est, ex nunc, jam non expectando diem extremi judicii. Voluit Dominus significare, inquit Gregorius de Valentia, l. de purgat. c. 8. p. 285. hoc ipso tempore, quo Eccle- sia nunc in terris militat, habere etiam in regno cœle- sti suum locum Ecclesiam aliquam triumphantem, ubi beati requiescant. Blasius Viegas communem hanc dicit explicationem. V. Ribera in h. l. Aretas ita verba ordinat, ut Spiritus Eos, qui tunc vivent & militabunt, consoletur, ac semper beati sint, qui in Domino moriuntur. A modo igitur significat à tem- pore mortis, ut exponunt Augustinus, Haymo, Be- da ex Psalm. CXXVI, Anglo Remenses in h. l. qui- dem nihil aliud innui volunt, quam quod requie- scant à laboribus hujus vitæ: quibus accedit Salme- ro in 1. Cor. XV. disp. 26. Vid. & Tirinus ad h. l. Sed Viega confert Ebr. IV. ubi Apostolus gloriam cœlestem Sabbatismum appellat, quia est ingressus in requiem Domini, de quo Psal. XIV. & CXIV. Ri- bera vero diserte in h. l. Beatum esse est perfectam beatitudinem percipere. Suidas reddit etiam, plane, omnino, & explete, ἀπηρτισμένως cui nihil accidere possit. Sed talis perfecta hominis beatitudo in se- culo venturo sequetur, Cæterum nec illa, quam ani- mæstatim ab excessu percipiunt, consistit cum flam- mis & pœnis ignis purgatorii, quem sola duratione ab igne infernali differre credunt communiter Papi- stæ; & illis hic obstetricatur Grotius. Nec vero est, quod solum de vivis perfectis ac sanctis Martyri- bus S. Johannem loqui cum Pontificiis quibusdam, qui id obvertere solent, imprimis Alcafare, ut & Ambrosio, censeamus. Veriorem agnoscit Viega communem sententiam, quæ hunc locum non ad Martyres tantum refert, sed ad sanctos universos. Eam enim, inquit, tradunt Beda, Andr. Cæsar. Pri- mas. Pannonius, Joach. Abbas, Ansbertus, Haymo & Richardus de S. Victore. Sic eam intellexit Bernhardus Epist. XCVIII. Quam Ecclesiam etiam proponere in officio defunctorum de omnibus ju- stis, & ideo retinendam esse profitetur Lorinus ad Act. VII. ad verba obdormivit in Domino. Et agno- scit hactenus Grotius veritatem explicationis no- stræ, cum hunc reddit sensum: Non tantum olim erunt beati in altera vita, sed & hoc ipso tempore. Illa autem non satis commode exponit, facta eo- rum sequentur ipsos: Pax illa orietur ex memoria recte factorum. Quanquam enim admitti possit sen- sus causalis particulæ ᾑ, qui nec nostræ explicatio- ni repugnat, ecquod tamen solidum gaudium ex re- cte factorum memoria, quum nemo sic semper sine crimine vivat, 1. Reg. IIX. Prov. XX. in mul- tisque labamur omnes, Jac. III, 2. De plaga spiri- tuali explicat etiam S. Augustinus.

ANGELUS MESSEM ET VINDEMIAM INDICANS.

## 14:14
Verse 14. And I saw, and behold.) As above 1. A white cloud.) By this white cloud, just as above VI, 2, by the white horse, the Gospel is signified. The cloud signifies speed no less than the horse. The whiteness signifies the purity of the doctrine itself.

And upon the cloud one sitting like the Son of man, that is

to the Son of man by the omission of the article, examples of which we have already had above. That Angel was like Christ, representing the person of Christ, just as in the Old Testament the Angel of God represented the person of God. We have had such forms from the beginning of the Apocalypse.

Having on his head a golden crown.) A sign of the victory which Christ had obtained by converting many daily from the Roman Empire even in the midst of persecutions. The blood of the martyrs was the seed of the Church. See above IV, 4, where his part in this victory of Christ is attributed to the Elders.

And in his hand a sharp sickle.) This is indeed from Zech. III, 13, but in another sense: as are many things from the Prophets in this Apocalypse. The sickle in this place is the preaching of the Gospel, which reaps men from the earth, so that they may be brought into the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδὲ.) Ut supra 1. Νεφέλη λευκὴ.) Per hanc nubem candidam sicut supra VI, 2. Per equum candidum significatur Evangelium. Nu- bes non minus, quam equus celeritatem significat. Candor doctrinæ ipsius puritatem.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν νεφέλην καθήμενον ὅμοιον ὕῷ ἀνθρώπυ, id est

τῷ ὑίῷ ἀνθρώπου per reticentiam articuli, cujus exempla jam supra habuimus. Is similis Christo fuit Angelus personam Christi referens, sicut in Veteri fœdere Angelus Dei personam referebat. Tales formas habuimus ab initio Apocalypseos.

Ἔχων ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὑτῶ στέφανον χρυσοῦν.) Signum victo- riæ, quam Christus erat consecutus, convertendo quotidie plurimos de imperio Romano etiam in mediis persecutio- nibus. Semen erat Ecclesiæ martyrum sanguis. Vide supra IV, 4. ubi Presbyteris tribuitur pars sua in hac Christi victoria.

Καὶ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ ἁυτῦ δρέπανον ὀξύ.) Est quidem hoc ex Za- char. III, 13. sed sensu alio: quomodo multa ex Prophetis in hac Apocalypsi. Falx hoc loco est prædicatio Evangelii, quæ homines à terra demetit, ut Ecclesiæ inferantur.

## 14:15
Verse 15.

Καὶ ἄλλος Ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῦ ναῦ.) From the heavenly temple, that is, from God. See above XI, 19.

Κράζων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῆς νεφαλῆς.) Not bringing commands to him himself, but approving his deed, and urging him on as he was already hastening.

Πέμψον τὸ δρέπανόν συ κὶ θέρισον.) To reap is taken here as in Matt. IX, 37 and the following. Luke X, 2. John IV, 35.

Ὅτι ἧλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῦ θερίσαι.) The harvest is coming, John in the cited place. It is time to press on with the work.

Ὅτι ἐξηράνθη ὁ θερισμὸς τῆς γῆς.) Fields white for harvest in the same place in John, where see the things said. בשל קציר Joel IV, 13. The harvest has ripened, that is, the crop to be reaped: just as here also the harvest, with the name taken from that which was about to happen immediately, just as sheep are spoken of, John X, 16. The people of Christ, Acts 18, 20. Ξηραίνεσθαι elsewhere is to wither, as here to become solid, no longer to be fluid.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

Καὶ ἄλλος Ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῦ ναῦ.) E templo cœlesti, id est, à Deo. Vide supra XI, 19.

Κράζων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῆς νεφαλῆς.) Non ipsi mandata afferens, sed factum ejus approbans, & σπεύδον- τα καὶ αὐτὸν ὀτρύνων.

Πέμψον τὸ δρέπανόν συ κὶ θέρισον.) Metere hic sumitur, ut Matth. IX, 37. & sequentibus. Luc. X, 2. Joh. IV, 35.

Ὅτι ἧλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῦ θερίσαι.) ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται Joh. di- cto loco. Tempus est instare operi.

Ὅτι ἐξηράνθη ὁ θερισμὸς τῆς γῆς.) Χῶραι λευκαὶ πρὸς θερι- σμὸν eodem Johannis loco, ubi dicta vide. בשל קציר Jo- el. IV, 13. maturuit messis, id est, seges metenda: quomodo & hic θερισμὸς ex eo, quod proxime futurum erat, sumpto nomine, quomodo dicuntur oves, Joh. X, 16. Populus Christi Act. 18, 20. Ξηραίνεσθαι alibi est exarescere, ut hic solidescere, non amplius fluitare.

## 14:16
Vers. 16.

Καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν νεφέλην τὸ δρέπανον ἁυτῦ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.) Naturally through the disciples of Paul, John, and other Apostles.

Καὶ ἐθερίσθη ἡ γῆ.) Very many from the Roman Empire added themselves to the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν νεφέλην τὸ δρέπανον ἁυτῦ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.) Nimirum per discipulos Pauli, Johannis, alio- rumque Apostolorum.

Καὶ ἐθερίσθη ἡ γῆ.) Plurimi ex imperio Romano Ecclesiæ se addidere.

## 14:17
Vers. 17.

Καὶ ἄλλος Ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῦ ναῦ τῦ ἐν τῷ ὁρανῷ ἔχων καὶ αὐτὸς δρέπανον ὀξύ.) He likewise comes from God, but for a very different matter. Understand here a pruning sickle, or, as Varro speaks, a vine-sickle.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

Καὶ ἄλλος Ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῦ ναῦ τῦ ἐν τῷ ὁρανῷ ἔχων καὶ αὐτὸς δρέπανον ὀξύ.) Itidem à Deo venit, sed in rem longe aliam. Falcem hic intellige putatoriam, sive, ut Varro loqui- tur, vineaticam.

## 14:18
Vers. 18.

Καὶ ἄλλος Ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῦ θυσιασηρίυ.) From the altar of burnt offerings: to which burnt offerings the impious are compared, as we said above 8, 5, and at Mark 9, 49. In the manuscript, ἐξῆλθεν is missing.

Having authority over the fire.) Having the ministry of Divine wrath, see above 8, 5. 7. c. 9, 17. c. 11, 5.

And he cried with a loud voice to him who had the sharp sickle.) To the vintager. In the manuscript it is ἐφώνησε φωνῇ, without the preceding κραυγῇ. And these cohere well with the preceding, because in that book, as we have said, ἐξῆλθε is absent.

Saying, send your sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth.) That is, gather the huge multitude of the Jews into a few places. The Jews were once called the vine of God, Is. 5. Jer. 12, 10. which retains the name from antiquity, even after it brought forth wild grapes, Is. 5, 4. Matt. 21, 33. and the following verses of Mark 12, 1. Luke 20, 9. What is said here, although pertaining mostly to the Jews, is referred here to the prophecies concerning the nations, which executed this judgment of God, and from thence ought to have taken an example for themselves, by that argument which Paul uses in Rom. 11, 21.

the clusters of the earth, the Jews, who are everywhere in the Roman empire.

For her grapes are ripe.) The grapes have matured, that is, the contumacy and cruelty of the Jews have reached their peak.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

Καὶ ἄλλος Ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῦ θυσιασηρίυ.) Ab altari holocaustorum: quibus holocaustis impii comparantur, ut diximus supra 8, 5. & ad Marc. 9, 49. In Manusc. deest ἐξῆλθεν.

Ἔχων ἐξυσίαν ἐπὶ τῦ πυρὸς.) Habens ministerium iræ Divi- næ, supra 8, 5. 7. c. 9, 17. c. 11, 5.

Καὶ ἐκραὐγασε φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ ἔχοντι τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξύ.) Vindemiatori. In Manuscripto ἐφώνησε φωνῇ, non præmisso κραυγῇ. Et bene cohærent hæc cum superioribus, quia abest in eo libro, ut diximus, ἐξῆλθε.

Λέγων πέμψον συ τὸ δρέπανον ὀξὺ, κὶ τρίγησον τὺς βότρυας τῆς ἀμπέλυ τῆς γῆς.) Id est, contrahe in pauca loca ingentem Judæorum multitudinem. Judæi olim dicti Dei vinea, Es. 5. Jerem. 12, 10. quæ nomen ex antiquo retinet, etiam postquam labruscas peperit, Es. 5, 4. Matth. 21, 33. & sequentibus Marci 12, 1. Luc. 20, 9. Quod hic dicitur, quanquam ad Judæos plu- rimum pertinens, refertur huc in vaticinia de gentibus, quæ hoc Dei judicium exsequtæ sunt, & inde sibi exemplum ca- pere debebant, eo argumento, quo Paulus utitur Rom. 11, 21.

τὺς βότρυας τῆς γῆς, Judæos, qui ubique sunt in imperio Ro- mano.

Ὅτι ἤκμασαν αἱ σταφυλαὶ αὐτῆς.) Maturuerunt uvæ, id est, contumacia & sævitia Judæorum ad summum pervenit.

## 14:19
And the Angel cast his sickle into the earth.) Into Judea, as above in the first part.

And he gathered the vine of the earth.) He gathered the Jews into one.

A white cloud can be properly understood, since the Son of man is said to be coming in a cloud in judgment, Matt. XXIV, 30. c. XXVI, 64. Acts I, 11. Matt. XXIV, 30. c. XX, 27. Acts I, 7. which is a symbol of holiness and purity, of justice and equity, of royal Majesty and perfect happiness. But by the one like the Son of man, the Angel sustaining his person is not signified, but the Son of man himself. He appeared like him in this vision, yet the Son of man himself was signified, as in Acts VIII, 5. Dan. VII, 13. Rev. I, 13. The Judge of the living and the dead, Acts XVII, 13. to whom the Father has given all judgment, because he is the Son of man, John V, 23. The Judge of all the earth, Gen. XVIII, 25. Like the likeness of truth, as the Hebrew Caph implies. The golden crown designates the dominion of the Son of Man, Matt. 18:19, inasmuch as He is the Prince of the kings of the earth, Rev. 1:5, King of Kings and Lord of Lords, ch. 17:14, ch. 19:16, crowned by the Father, Psalm 8:6, Heb. 11:7. For it is the duty of kings to wear crowns. It also designates the victory of Christ, which He achieves over the enemies of the Church on the day of judgment, both particular and especially universal. Cf. Rev. 17:14. The victory over the enemies of the Church is not in the conversion of some from the Roman Empire, nor any particular judgment, as the blessed Cluverus wishes; but in the trampling down of all enemies, even the last one, who is understood to be death, which will happen at the end of the world, 1 Cor. 15:25. For the sharp sickle pertains to that, namely to the harvest of the last day. For then comes the hour of the harvest, that is, the hour of judgment, v. 7. Therefore, the harvest is not to be instituted by the disciples of Paul or John, but by the Angels. Moreover, the sharp sickle signifies Divine power and virtue, according to which He will punish the impious in judgment, and will strike them down with as easy a task as a reaper cuts down ripe crops with his sickle and lays them on the ground, when they are ripe for punishment and have filled the measure of their sins. But the Angel cries out, v. 15, not because he wishes to command the judgment; but so that he may set forth the desire of the Angels and the blessed, by which they await the coming of the time of judgment against the impious, so that the impious may be overthrown and the faithful finally liberated, ch. 6:10, ch. 12:17. Nor is there any reason why we should understand the three persons of the Godhead by the three Angels. We remain in the customary meaning of the word. For the Father cannot be called an Angel, inasmuch as He is sent by no one. Arethas accepts the Angels from the ministering powers, Matt. 13:39. One of them, the blessed Cluverus, from a comparison with ch. 8:5. makes Christ. But he, v. 18, is openly distinguished from Christ the Son of Man. Christ, the blessed Cluverus himself says, commands with a loud voice that the Angel execute his judgment, just as above, ch. 9:13, a voice resounding from the altar enjoins the Angel to release those four evil ones, intended for the slaughter of men. For they willingly carry out his commands. If anyone, says the same blessed Author, with Andreas Caesariensis and other Ancients, wishes to establish that this Angel is set over the element of fire and that other one, ch. 16:6, over the waters, and others over other creatures, let him enjoy his own opinion for all we care. Sometimes Christ is distinguished from the Angel, sometimes the same things that are said to the Angel are attributed to Christ. The blessed Gravius understands the Angel having power over the fire as the Ministers of the Word, who have power over the fire, not infernal but the spiritual fire of the Word of God, so that in that ruin of Babylon some may be converted to the true faith of Christ. Who cry out to Christ through indefatigable prayers, that He may take due punishment from the Anti-Christian beast. That vine-sickle also looks to the same thing as the other. But it is not necessary to invent different meanings. The same thing is expressed by different visions, as in the dream of Pharaoh explained by Joseph, Gen. 41:25, and that for the sake of certainty. By the one having power over fire, remaining within the more famous meaning, one can understand the Angel having power over infernal fire, or who is to cast the reprobate into the same. Others understand the fire of the sacrifices, like the blessed Osiander; the care of the sacrifices was committed to this Angel over the fire which was kept on the altar. And this signified the pious Angel-Ministers and other sincere Christians, who in the New Testament offer spiritual sacrifices to God, Heb. 13, ch. But this is not about the gathering of the multitude of the Jews into a few places, but about all the reprobate being cast into the pit of the winepress of Divine wrath. Nor is it necessary that the earth be restricted to Judea, since the whole earth can, and indeed should, be understood. For since Scripture does not restrict, it is not for us to restrict. Therefore, a particular judgment is not to be understood with the blessed Cluverus, which does not strike the whole earth. Who, he says, men are born from the earth, grow, flourish, and wither in their pursuits, just like crops, some in virtues, but most in vices, to whom there is a special regard here. Then indeed they are mowed down by the sickle of the Lord through death, so that the pious are gathered into the bundle of the living and the barns of the Father, but the impious are heaped into piles and stored for the furnace of fire. Such a harvest is made by the sending of pestilential diseases, wars, and similar calamities, by which men are wont to be snatched away in crowds. But the pious ripen when they have completed the course of their faith and piety, and have been sufficiently tested in the struggles of the fire of afflictions, so that they may be released and depart from their station. The evil ripen when they have filled the measure of their iniquity, so that they may finally pay the deserved penalties, just as something of the sort is said about the Amorites, Gen. 18:21, and the Jews, Joel 3:18, Matt. 23:32. And the Roman Babylonians, ch. 18:5. For God is wont to await the repentance of men up to the harvest, that is, the maturity and consummation of sin, 2 Pet. 3:9, Rom. 2:4, Luke 13:8, 9, Matt. 3:10. Therefore, one must flee maturely from the impending wrath. For sometimes He anticipates that maturity, as we have seen in Isa. 18:5, 6.

Vers. 19.

And he cast into the great winepress of the wrath of God.] Winepress here signifies the press together with the vat, as in Matt. 21:33. But by the pressing of grapes, where the wrath of God is either named, as here, or understood from the circumstances, a huge shedding of blood is usually denoted, which blood is compared to wine, as wine to blood, Isa. 63:2, 3, Lam. 1:15, Joel 3:13.

Latin:

Καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ Ἄγγελος τὸ δρέπανον ἁυτῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν.) In Ju- dæam, ut supra in parte prima.

Καὶ ἐτρύγησε τὴν ἄμπελον τῆς γῆς.) Judæos in unum col- legit.

Nubes candida proprie intelligi potest, quum Fi- lius hominis in judicio in nube venturus dicatur, Matth. XXIV, 30. c. XXVI, 64. Actor. I, 11. Matth. XXIV, 30. c. XX, 27. Act. I, 7. quæ symbolum est san- ctitatis & puritatis, justitiæ & æquitatis, regiæ Ma- jestatis & perfectæ felicitatis. Non autem per simi- lem Filio hominis Angelus personam ejus sustinens, sed ipse Filius hominis significatur. Similis visus est in hac ὀπτασίᾳ, atqui significatus est ipse Filius hominis, uti Act. IIX, 5. Dan. VII, 13. Ap. I, 13. Ju- dex vivorum & mortuorum Act. XVII, 13. cui Pater dedit omne judicium, quia est Filius hominis, Joh. V, 23. Judex universæ terræ, Genes. XIIX, 25. Ὄμοιος similitudinem veritatis, ut Caph Ebræum importat. Corona aurea designat filii hominis dominium Matth. XVIII, 19. utpote qui Princeps est Regum terræ, Apoc. I, 5. Rex Regum & Dominus Dominan- tium, c. XVII, 14. cap. XIX, 16. coronatus à Patre, Psalm. IIX, 6. Ebr. XI, 7. Regum enim est gesta- re coronas. Designat & victoriam Christi, quam in die judicii tum particularis tum maxime univer- salis reportat ab hostibus Ecclesiæ. Conf. Apoc. XVII. vers. 14. Victoria ab hostibus Ecclesiæ non est in conversione nonnullorum de Romano Im- perio, nec judicium aliquod particulare, ut B. Clu- verus vult; sed in conculcatione hostium omnium, etiam novissimi, qui mors in fine mundi futura, 1. Cor. XV, 25. intelligitur. Eo enim pertinet falx acu- ta, ad messem diei nempe novissimæ. Tum enim venit hora messis, hoc est, hora judicii, v. 7. Non igi- tur per discipulos Pauli vel Johannis, sed per Ange- los messis instituenda. Significat autem falx acuta Divinam potentiam & virtutem, juxta quam impios in judicio puniet, ac tam facili negotio ipsos deprimet, quam messor fruges maturas falce sua demetit, & in terram deponit, quando ad pœnam sunt maturi, & mensuram suorum peccatorum impleverunt. Clamat autem Angelus v. 15. non quod judici velit imperare; sed ut Angelorum & beatorum desiderium, quo ex- pectant advenire tempus judicii adversus impios, exponat ut impii evertantur, & fideles tandem li- bèrentur c. VI, 10. c. XII, 17. Neque est, quod per Angelos tres intelligamus tres personas Deitatis. Manemus in usitata vocis significatione. Nec enim Pater Angelus dici potest, utpote à nemine missus. De Angelis ἐκ τῶν λειτυργικῶν δυνάμεων accipit A- rethas Matth. XIII, 39. Unum ex illis B. Cluverus è collatione c. IIX, 5. Christum facit. Sed ille v. 18. apertè à Christo Filio hominis distinguitur. Christus, inquit ipse B. Cluverus, magna voce imperat, ut exe- quatur Angelus judicium suum, sicut & supra c. IX, 13. vox ex altari resonans injungit Angelo, ut solvat malos illos quatuor, ad hominum intentos occisionem. Hujus enim jussa libenter illi expediunt. Si quis, in- quit idem B. Autor, cum Andrea Cæsar. & Veteri- bus aliis statuere velit, hunc Angelum ignis elemento esse præpositum & alterum illum cap. XVI, 6. aquis, alios aliis creaturis, is suo per nos fruatur sensu. Mo- do autem distinguitur Christus ab Angelo, modo eadem, quæ Angelo dicta, dicta Christo traduntur. Angelum potestatem in ignem habentem B. Gravius de Ministris Verbi intelligit, qui habeant potesta- tem super ignem non infernalem sed spiritualem Verbi Dei, ut in ruina illa Babylonis nonnulli ad fidem Christi veram convertantur. Qui per inde- fessas preces ad Christum clamant, ut debitum sup- plicium de bestia Anti-Christiana sumat. Falx etiam illa vineatica eadem quæ altera respicit. At non est necessum diversa significata fingere. Idem diversis exprimitur visionibus, ut in somnio Pharaonis à Jo- sepho explicato, Genes. XLI, 25. idque certitudinis causa. Per habentem potestatem ignis, manendo intra significatum famosius, intelligi potest Ange- lus habens potestatem infernalis ignis, vel intrusurus in eundem reprobos. Alii ignem sacrificiorum in- telligunt, ut B. Osiander; Supra ignem, qui foveba- tur in altari, huic Angelo commissa erat cura sacrifi- ciorum. Et hic Angelos pios Ministros & alios since- ros Christianos significabat, qui in Novo Testamento hostias spirituales Deo offerunt, Ebr. XIII. cap. Non autem hic de contrahenda in pauca loca Judæo- rum multitudine, sed de reprobis universis in la- cum torcularis iræ Divinæ projiciendis agitur. Nec est ut terra ad Judæam restringatur, quum universa terra intelligi possit, imo debeat. Scriptura enim non restringente nostrum non est restringere. Ne- que ergo judicium particulare intelligendum cum B. Cluvero, quod non ferit totam terram. Qui, na- scuntur, inquit, homines e terra, crescunt, florent, & arescunt in studiis suis, perinde ut segetes, quidam in virtutibus, plurimi autem in vitiis, ad quos præsertim hic est respectus. Tum vero falce Domini per mortem demetuntur, ut pii in fasciculum viventium & horrea Patris, impii vero in acervos congesti ad caminum ignis reponantur. Ejusmodi messis fit immissione pesti- lentialium morborum, bellorum, & similium cladium, quibus homines confertim solent abripi. Mature- scunt autem pii, cum cursum fidei & pietatis suæ ab- solverunt, & satis in certaminibus igne afflictionum sunt probati, ut solvantur & abeant statione sua. Ma- turescunt mali, quum impleverunt mensuram iniqui- tatis suæ, ut pœnas tandem meritas luant, sicut tale quid dicitur de Amorrhæis, Gen. XIIX, 21. & Judæis Joël. III, 18. Matth. XXIII, 32. Et Babyloniis Roma- nis, cap. XIIX, 5. Expectare enim solet Deus pœniten- tiam hominum usq; ad messem, hoc est, maturitatem & consummationem peccati, 2. Petr. III, 9. Rom. II, 4. Luc. XIII, 8. 9. Matth. III, 10. Fugiendum igitur mature ab ira impendente. Interdum enim eam ma- turitatem præoccupat, sicut vidimus Es. XIIX, 5. 6.

## 14:20
Vers. 20.

And the winepress was trodden.] Metonymy, for he calls that which was in the winepress, that is, the grapes, the winepress. Thus the cup is put for the wine. To tread the grapes, a custom for those nations, below 19:1, Isa. 16:9.

Outside the city.] Not Jerusalem, which is always understood by the name of the city, where the matter concerns the Jews. This did not happen in the city, because there were no Jews left there.

And blood came out of the winepress even unto the bridles of the horses.] A hyperbolic expression, which signifies a huge quantity of blood. You have a similar one in Isa. 8:7. But here is an apodosis mixed with a comparison. For instead of wine he said blood, because the wine signified blood. Similar to Matt. 24, where see the things said. You have similar ones in Amos 9:11, 12, Hab. 1:17.

Ἀπὸ σταδίων χιλίων ἑξακοσίων.] That is, outside the borders of Judea. For the length of Judea, according to the testimony of Jerome, who lived in those places and explored everything accurately, extended to 160 miles. A mile, however, contains ten stadia: whence scholars conclude that Judea extended in length to 1600 stadia. The Jerusalem Talmud and Menahem on Genesis give Judea 4000 stadia in square. The matter predicted here is true. For this huge effusion of the blood of Jews and Gentiles took place while Trajan was emperor, not in Judea, but in places neighboring Judea, that is, Syria, Egypt, Cyrenaica, and Cyprus. Dion says in book 68 that 460,000 perished. Infinite thousands of Jews were slaughtered, says Eusebius. Orosius 7.12 treats this matter at length. This history is correctly relegated to this place, because it both happened outside Judea and also cost much blood of other nations.

Jerusalem is not always understood by the name of the city; but sometimes Rome as well, as we have seen in this very chapter XIV. Once the sense is assumed that in the vision the blood was seen outside the borders of Judea: something else can be understood in the signification. It is a question not so much of the destruction of the Jews as of the Anti-Christian people, whose punishment was to be intimated. They wish to indicate, therefore, that it will be horrible and abominable, Isa. LXVI. v. 24, just as it would be if one were to see a rider through 1600 stadia, that is, through 50 German miles, in blood reaching up to the horse's bridle. Albertus, on this passage, from an old gloss, has these words: The vengeance of blood or of sin upon the very rulers of the wicked.

demons, or reach the Prelates, who as they shall be similar in sins, so also they may be similar in punishments and be more severely punished. B. Cluverus says that the expression appears similar to that which the Lord uses in Isaiah chapter XXX, 27, 28. Where He threatens a flood of such indignation that it reaches up to the middle of the neck, and by which the nations are shaken as if by a sieve, falling to the ground like chaff, (conf. Amos IX, 9, 10) and are turned around by a bridle like horses, not knowing where they are turning. And Hab. III, 13. You struck the head from the house of the wicked, you laid bare the foundations up to the neck. B. Gerhardus: It signifies, he says, 1. a great multitude of the damned. 2. The most just and eternal punishment of the wicked. 3. The horrible torments of hell. Cornelius a Lapide and Ribera understand such a capacity of hell, taking those stadia literally, as much, namely, as the interval is between Rome and Bologna, Brussels and Paris. But we leave these speculations to the Jesuits. Cæsariensis thinks the perfection of malice is indicated: because the numbers one thousand, one hundred, and six are perfect numbers. If you listen to John Purvæus, they are punishments inflicted for every difference of sins committed in the stadium of this world. Victorinus Martyr, the treading, he says, of the winepress is the retribution for sins, and vengeance will go out as far as the Princes of the peoples for 1600 stadia, that is, the four parts of the world. For four times four hundred is sixteen hundred. Others understand years by stadia, but without scripture. But Tirinus opposes Lessius: Who proves: Even if it were only one league, it could nevertheless contain eight hundred million million bodies, with six square feet of space assigned to each body. It is nevertheless likely to him that there will be many more millions of the damned, especially if (as he himself opines with Cornelius a Lapide and others) all the demons also are surrounded by these ignited bodies. But we also dismiss the vain and idle speculations of the Monks. If those years are computed and the treading begins from the year 1600, we shall experience it collapsing in this century; which we have altogether experienced from the year 1618, B. Cluverus, as also B. Gravius, think: Although that computation may be rejected by some, for the reason that stadia are attributed to gross things and not to time, B. Gravius nevertheless judges it not absurd nor alien to Scripture to understand time through gross and bodily things. For Gen. XL, 13 and 19, three days are denoted by three branches and as many baskets; chapter XLI, 25, seven years are understood by three cows and as many ears of corn. Thus it will not be absurd, in his judgment, to expound these 1600 stadia mystically as so many years of the Church of the New Testament, especially since the Jubilees of the New Testament compared with the age of Christ correspond exactly. Although the circumstances of the text imply that this passage, Rev. XIV, 19, 20, is to be understood not of the destruction of the Jewish polity, but of the ruin of the Anti-Christians, this genuine exposition of the years is nevertheless not repugnant to this computation. And the sense can be that such a slaughter of Anti-Christians was wrought by the Ligistic wars as had not been made in all that time during which the Church stood after the Jewish destruction. So he. Philippus Nicolai refers them to the 1600 years destined for the duration of the Church of the New Testament, with the beginning made from the times of the Gentiles, which fall into the desolation of the city of Jerusalem and terminate in the year of Christ 1670. Which calculation, however, has already been convicted of falsehood by the event. Joh. Cocceji had these thoughts concerning these stadia: If it is true that the Roman dominion has 1600 stadia, as Medus reports in the Clavis Apocalyptica, we can say that 'from the stadia' signifies the final tract of flowing blood, i.e., the blood will flow from the winepresses for so long until it fills that territory which has so many stadia. It is also permitted to compare this number with other numbers already demonstrated, e.g., the months of the locusts, and to consider whether these stadia, taken for years, fall into the same term of time, e.g., if we begin from the Jewish war, as the first 'beginning of sorrows', Matt. XXIV, 8, and proceed to the end of the months which are assigned to the locusts: or to the end of the days which Daniel counts in Chapter XII. If there is furthermore another meaning of this number, time will reveal it. Lessius in Fromondus book XIII, chapter 14, on the perfection of God, refers that space of 1600 stadia to the place which all the reprobate will occupy in the valley of Jehoshaphat and around it at the time of the universal judgment. For that place, he says, calculation having been made, suffices to receive thirty thousand million men standing on the surface of the earth. Which Fromondus rejects, but for a reason of no moment, namely that St. John is not speaking of all the reprobate. For why should this not be taken concerning all the reprobate? But in our judgment, the perfection or magnitude of the punishment is noted: because the discourse is about judgment, Is. LXIII, Rev. XIX. Which can be understood in this place, even if the dimension of hell is not established literally according to the Jesuit calculation. tam and reap the clusters: The crimes of the Roman Pontiffs and his followers are truly ripe for Divine vengeance, which they have provoked for several centuries of years; For they have corrupted the doctrine of the Gospel, they have oppressed the Church of Christ with human traditions, they have instituted manifold idolatry: they have horribly raged against contradicting pious Ministers and Hearers with prisons, sword, and fire, they have scraped together the wealth of the world by their impostures and lies, and they have contaminated their bodies and souls and those of others with wicked lusts. Such a quantity of blood signifies that GOD will take horrible punishments from the Papal persecutors (who rage against the members of the Church of Christ for the sake of the Roman Pontiffs), so that they who thirsted for blood, and of which they were always insatiable, may swim and be suffocated in blood, says Osiander. And these things concerning chapter XIV, in which were described both the singular Worshippers of Christ, and the three excellent Reformers of the world admiring the Anti-Christ: then the sweetest consolations of those who die in the Lord at this time: then the most grave threats of the judgments of GOD against the Anti-Christ and his accomplices and other reprobate.

THE SIXTH VISION OF THE SEVEN VIALS.

Vers. 20.

Καὶ ἐπατήθη ἡ ληνὸς.] Μετωνυμία, ληνὸν enim vocat id, quod erat ἐν τῇ ληνῷ, id est, uvas. Sic calix pro vino ponitur. Cal- care uvas, mos illis gentibus infra 19, 1. Esa. 16, 9.

Ἔξωθεν τῆς πόλεως.] Non Hierosolymis, quæ semper πό- λεως nomine intelligi solet, ubi de Judæis res est. Non acci- dit hoc in urbe, quia nulli ibi amplius erant Judæi.

Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αἷμα ἐκ τῦ ληνῦ ἄχρι τῶν χαλινῶν τῶν ἵππων.] Hyperbolica loqutio, quæ significat ingentem sanguinis co- piam. Simile habes Esa. 8, 7. Est autem hic ἀπόδοσις permixta comparationi. Nam pro vino dixit sanguinem, quia vinum significabat sanguinem. Simile Matth. 24. ubi dicta vide. Si- milia habes Amos 9, 11. 12. Abac. I, 17.

Ἀπὸ σταδίων χιλίων ἑξακοσίων.] Id est, extra Judææ termi- nos. Judææ enim longitudo teste Hieronymo, qui in illis lo- cis vixit, & omnia accurate exploravit, porrigebatur in mil- liaria CLX. Milliare autem continet stadia decem: un- de colligunt eruditi, Judæam exiisse in longitudinem stadio- rum cIɔ Iɔc. Thalmud Hierosolymitanum & Menahem ad Genesin dant Judææ quater mille stadia in quadro. Vera res est, quæ hic prædicitur. Nam ingens hæc effusio sanguinis Judæorum & gentium facta est Trajano imperante non in Ju- dæa, sed in locis Judææ vicinis, id est, Syria, Ægypto, Cyrenai- ca & Cypro. Quadringenta sexaginta millia periisse ait Dion libro LXIIX. Infinita millia Judæorum cæsa, ait Eusebius. Late eam rem exequitur Orosius VII, 12. Hæc historia recte huc rejecta est, quia & extra Judæam evenit, & multo etiam aliarum gentium stetit sanguine.

Non semper Hierosolyma πόλεως nomine intel- ligitur; sed quandoque etiam Roma, ut habuimus hoc ipso capite XIV. Assumpto in visione sensu extra Judææ terminos conspectum fuisse sangui- nem: in significatione aliud quid intelligi potest. De interitu non tam Judæorum, quam Anti-Chri- stiani populi agitur, cujus supplicium intimandum erat. Id ergo horrendum & abominabile fore indicare volunt, Esa. LXVI. v. 24. quemadmo- dum foret, si quis videret equitantem per 1600. stadia, hoc est per 50. milliaria Germani- ca in sanguine, usque ad equi frenum pertinente. Albertus ad h. l. ex veteri glossa hæc habet: Vindi- ctam sanguinis seu peccati ad ipsos rectores iniquorum

Dæmones, vel Prælatos pertingere, qui sicut similes fuerint in culpis, sic etiam similes in pœnis ac gravi- us puniantur. B. Cluverus similem dicit apparere loquutionem illi, qua utitur Dominus apud Esaiam cap. XXX, 27. 28. Ubi tantum indignationis diluvi- um comminatur, quod usque ad medium collum pertingat, & quo quasi cribro agitentur gentes, tan- quam palea in terram decidentes, (conf. Amos IX, 9. 10.) ac freno circumagantur equorum instar, quo se vertant, ignorantes. Et Hab. III, 13. Percussisti ca- put de Domino impii, denudasti fundamenta usque ad collum. B. Gerhardus: Significatur, inquit, 1. magna damnatorum multitudo. 2. Justissima & æterna impiorum pœna. 3. Horrenda inferni suppli- cia. Cornelius a Lapide ac Ribera tantam capaci- tatem inferni intelligunt, stadia illa proprie accipi- entes, quantum scil. sit intervallum inter Romam & Bononiam, Bruxellas & Parisios. Sed has specu- lationes Jesuitis relinquimus. Cæsariensis perfe- ctionem malitiæ indicari censet: quia millenarius centenarius & senarius numeri perfecti sunt. Si audias Johannem Purvæum, sunt pœnæ pro qua- cunque differentia peccatorum in stadio hujus mundi commissorum inflictæ. Victorinus Mar- tyr, calcatio, inquit, torcularis retributio est pec- catorum, & exibit ultio usque ad Principes popu- lorum per stadia 1600. id est, quatuor mundi par- tes. Quatuor enim quadringenti mille fexcenti. Alii per stadia annos sed ἀτεχ γραφῆς intelligunt. Sed opponit Lessium Tirinus: Qui probat: Etsi una tantum esset leuca, capere tamen posse octingenta millia millionum corporum, consignato singulis cor- poribus spatio sex pedum quadratorum. Verisimile tamen ipsi est, multo plures fore damnatorum millio- nes, maxime si, (quod cum Cornelio a Lapide & ali- is ipse opinatur) Dæmones quoque omnes corpori- bus istis ignitis circumdentur. Sed mittimus quoque vanas & otiosas Monachorum specula- tiones. Anni illi si computentur & ab anno 1600. calcatio incipiat, hoc seculo corruere eam experi- emur; quam omnino nos expertos esse ab anno 1618. B. Cluverus, ut & B. Gravius censent: Etsi autem computatio illa a quibusdam rejiciatur, eo quod stadia rebus crassis non vero tempori tribu- antur, non absurdum tamen nec alienum judicat a Scriptura B. Gravius per res crassas & corporales tempus intelligere. Nam Gen. XL, 13. & 19. per tres palmites & totidem corbes notantur tres dies cap. XLI, 25. per tres vaccas & totidem aristas septem intelliguntur anni. Ita nec absurdum erit, ipso ju- dice, stadia hæc M. DC. mystice de totidem annis Ecclesiæ N. T. exponere, præsertim cum Jubilæi N. T. cum Christi ætate collati exacte respondeant. Quam- vis vero textus circumstantiæ innuant, locum hunc Apoc. XIV, 19. 20. non de excidio politiæ Judaicæ, sed de interitu Anti- Christianorum intelligendum esse, genuina tamen hæc expositio annorum huic computationi non repugnat. Et sensus esse potest, tantam stragem Anti- Christianorum bellis Ligisticis editam esse, qualis facta fuerit non toto illo, quo post Judaicum excidium Ecclesia steterit, tempore. Hæc ille. Philippus Nicolai refert ea ad 1600. annos durationi Ecclesiæ N. T. destinatos initio facto a temporibus gentilium, quæ in desolationem urbis Hierosolymitanæ incidunt & terminantur Ann. C. 1670. Qui vero calculus jam ab eventu falsitatis convictus est. Joh. Cocceji de hisce stadiis hæ fue- re cogitationes: Si verum est, ditionem Romanam habere stadia 1600. ut tradit Medus in clavi Apo- calyptica, possumus dicere ἀπὸ σταδιων significare ul- timum tractum manantis sanguinis, q. d. tamdiu ma- nabit sanguis ex torcularibus, donec impleat territo- rium illud, quod habet tot stadia. Licet etiam hunc nu- merum conferre cum aliis numeris jam demonstratis, v. g. mensibus locustarum, & considerare, annon in eundem terminum temporis incidant haec stadia pro annis accepta, v. g. si incipiamus a bello Judaico, ut prima ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων, Matth. XXIV, 8. & proceda- mus ad finem mensium, qui assignantur locustis: aut ad finem dierum, quos numerat Daniel in Cap. XII. Si praeterea est alia hujus numeri significatio, eam tempus aperiet. Lessius apud Fromondum l. XIII. cap. 14. de perfect. Div. spatium illud 1600. stadio- rum refert ad locum, quem omnes reprobi in valle Jo- saphat & circa occupabunt tempore judicii univer- salis. Nam locus ille, ait, facta supputatione sufficit ad tricies mille milliones hominum in terrae superficie consistentium excipiendos. Quod rejicit Fromon- dus, sed ex causa nullius momenti, quod scilicet non loquatur S. Johannes de omnibus reprobis. Cur enim non de omnibus reprobis haec accipienda? Sed nostro judicio perfectio vel magnitudo su- plicii notatur: quia de judicio sermo est, Es. LXIII. Apoc. XIX. Quae intelligi hoc loco potest, etsi di- mensio inferni propria juxta computum Jesuiti- cum haud instituatur. Mitte falcem tuam acu- tam & vindemia botros: Vere sunt matura scelera Romanorum Pontificum & asseclarum ejus ad vin- dictam Divinam, quam per aliquot annorum cen- turias provocarunt; Nam doctrinam Evangelii corruperunt, Ecclesiam Christi humanis traditioni- bus oppresserunt, multiplicem idololatriam institue- runt: in contradicentes pios Ministros & Audito- res carceribus, ferro, ignique horribiliter sunt grassa- ti, imposturis suis & mendaciis opes mundi corrase- runt, & nefandis libidinibus corpora & animas suas & aliorum contaminarunt. Tanta sanguinis co- pia significat, DEUM de Pontificiis persecutoribus (qui in gratiam Pontificum Romanorum in Ecclesia Christi membra saeviunt) horribiles poenas sumptu- rum, ut in sanguine natent & suffocentur, qui san- guinem sitiverunt, & cujus semper inexplebiles fue- runt, inquit Osiander. Atque haec de capite XIV. quo descripti tum singulares Christi Veneratores, tum tres eximii mundi Anti-Christum admirantis Reformatores: tum suavissimae eorum, qui in Do- mino isto tempore decedunt, consolationes: tum gravissimae judiciorum DEI adversus Anti-Chri- stum & complices aliosque reprobos commina- tiones.

VISIO SEXTA SEPTEM PHIALARUM.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.

The seven last plagues are designated first generally by the introduction of the seven vials: then explained specifically. Moreover, the song of Moses & the Lamb is heard first, as if in the place of a Prologue, at the sea of glass mingled with fire: by which the true & just ways of the Lord are celebrated: and then, the temple being opened, the seven angels are seen filling it with the seven plagues from golden vials by the grace of God, so that no one could enter it.

There are two parts: I. The song of Moses and the Lamb is heard. II. Seven angels with seven vials are seen.

PART I. THE HEARING OF THE SONG OF MOSES.

Ver. 1.

And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous.] These things which follow seem to have occurred to John at Ephesus, in the time of the Emperor Vespasian. And they have a more extensive explanation of those things which were briefly said about the Empire, as often happens to the Prophets, especially to Daniel.

Seven angels.] Against the Roman Empire, as against the Jews above VII, 1. They love the Heptad, a sign most significant of God, among the Hebrews.

Having seven last plagues.] New punishments after those wars of Galba, Otho, Vitellius, and Vespasian, after the fall of the Capitol: after those movements of the Jews in Syria and Egypt.

For in them is filled up the wrath of God.] Deservedly, he says, did I call them the last, because they end in the final effect of divine wrath against the Roman idolaters. Thus general things are set before special things, even in chapter VIII.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Septem plagae ultimae designantur primum gene- ratim introductis septem phialis: Deinde spe- cialiter explicatis. Auditur autem prius can- ticum Mosis & Agni, velut Prologi loco ad mare vitreum igni mixtum: quo vera & ju- sta celebrantur viae Domini: & tum aperto templo conspiciuntur angeli septem plagas phialis aureis implente illud gratia Dei, ut nemo id ingredi potuerit.

Partes duae sunt: I. Canticum Mosis & agni auditur. II. Septem Angeli cum septem phialis vi- dentur.

PARS I. ἌΚΟΥΣΜΑ CANTICI MOSIS.

Vers. 1.

Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ ὀυρανῷ μέγα καὶ θαυμαστόν.] Hæc quæ sequuntur visa Johanni obtigisse videntur Ephesi, Ve- spasiano Principe. Et habent eorum, quæ de Imperio brevi- ter dicta sunt, explicationem fusiorem, ut sæpe Prophetis eve- nit, maxime Danieli.

Ἀγγέλους ἑπτά.] Contra Romanum Imperium, ut contra Judæos supra VII, 1. Res Dei maxime insigni Heptada amant apud Hebræos.

Ἔχοντας πληγὰς ἑπτὰ τὰς ἐσχάτας.] Novas pœnas post bella illa Galbæ, Othonis, Vitellii, Vespasiani, post la- psum Capitolium: post motus illos Judæorum in Syria & Ægypto.

Ὅτι ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐτελέσθη ὁ θυμὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ.] Merito, inquit, di- xi ultimas, quia desinunt in ultimum iræ divinæ effectum contra idololatras Romanos. Sic generalia præmittuntur spe- cialibus etiam capite VIII.

## 15:2
Ver. 2.

And I saw as it were a sea of glass.] Above IV, 6, the glassy sea was the Christian people from the Jews: here it is gathered from the Gentiles, whose thoughts God looks into, and finds them pure, like the purest glass, that is, crystal.

Mingled with fire.] Kindled with great love for God. Love is compared to fire. Cant. VIII, 7.

When Caesar and Areta the Papists prefer to understand it concerning the multitude of men who will follow the Anti-Christ, as Ribera explains, which are called a sea because they always seethe and swell with various desires and certain waves; glassy, because the thoughts of the impious are most manifest to God: to Tirinus the glassy, crystalline, transparent sea is the empyrean heaven, mixed with fire, that is, sparkling with the splendor of the Divine presence, and seething with the ardor of the charity of the Saints. Blasius de Viegas thinks that in the sea one should understand Baptism, in the glass faith, which is received in baptism, in the fire either the Holy Spirit or tribulation; and that the glassy sea mixed with fire adumbrates the faith of Baptism proven by persecutions, upon which sea the victors of the Anti-Christ stand securely, having harps, and singing the Song of Moses, since they retained the faith received in baptism superior to the terrors of the Anti-Christ. Interlinear Gloss. ad h. l. A glassy sea, because in it the Holy Spirit is given to the baptized. Which sense the blessed Gerhard approves, comparing the passage of Matthew III, 11. The blessed Cluverus also assents, bringing forward Primasius to that opinion, that the water of baptism is designated by the fire of the Holy Spirit.

And them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over the number of his name.] Confessors, who could be induced neither by flatteries nor by threats to either invoke the Roman gods, or bow themselves before an image, or receive even some sign of idolatry. You may rightly translate 'ex' here as 'from' [ab], as 'Victor from the Aurora' [is from] the peoples.

Standing by the sea of glass.] Just as mountains stand around an immobile sea.

Having the harps of God.] That is, rendering praise to God. See above V, 8. XIV, 2. They are called harps of God because they are consecrated to GOD.

There appears no reason why these should be referred to the times of Vespasian. The order indicates rather the contrary. For the pouring out of the vials looks to the last age of the world, and is connected with the final judgment. But the thread of the Apocalypse must not be neglected. Otherwise we shall have nothing certain in it. The vision of another new and wonderful sign indicates a new Prophetic vision. That was great and wonderful in vision, and such it was in signification. But these things happened at the sea of glass. By which is meant not the Christian people from the Jews, but baptism, as indicated above in ch. IV, which is in the Church, so that it may be hinted that that which is signified here is to happen in it. The mixture of fire teaches that the wrath of grace is to be mingled. Baptism is a means of grace: this fire is a symbol of wrath, Deut. IV, 24. Heb. XII, 29. Namely, that grace will not be denied to the penitent even in the midst of the flames of Divine wrath against the reprobate is designated, so that some perhaps may be recalled to repentance.

But why at Ephesus, and not in Patmos, like those other things seen by John? And how under Prince Vespasian, who had already yielded to fate? If they have a briefly more diffuse explanation of the sayings, what do they have to do with Vespasian? For those things were predicted as still to come, but the times of Vespasian had already passed. But it is not the final effect of Divine wrath against the pagans that is noted, but against the Antichristians who were in Rome. Therefore, the confessors are hinted at, whom the Roman beast, the Great Antichrist, could not overcome, and their εὐλογία. Furthermore, that the angels report the state of the world to God is gathered from Zech. I, 11. Matt. XVIII, 10, 31. Tob. XII, 13. For although He Himself beholds all things, yet He delights in their ministry. Therefore, this angel, having explored the condition of men, reports to the Lord what he has learned. And now with great zeal, having gone forth from the temple of heaven, where those Powers serve God, he calls out that Christ is now prepared to judge the earth, so that He may do what He has decreed to do. For thus the earth is prepared, that it awaits His reaping sickle, as the blessed Cluverus has it here. But concerning the fact that the singers stood by the glassy sea, he has this: For where would they stand more conveniently than by the limpid fountain of Israel, from which the light and wisdom of the Spirit shines forth? Where more willingly than by that open vein which was given to the house of GOD against sin and uncleanness, Zech. XIII, 1. Primasius likewise understands the water of baptism consecrated by the fire of the Holy Spirit, and those standing upon it as stable in the faith. But the Caesarean interprets the glassy sea as the multitude of those who are saved, and the purity of the future rest, and the splendor of the saints, as does Aretas. And the fire of probation, that of which Paul 1. Cor. III, 13, which illuminates the good and burns the wicked. He adds, however, that it is probable that by fire is signified Divine knowledge and the grace of the life-giving Spirit, since God appeared to Moses in fire, and through it the Holy Spirit visited the Apostles. And from there he seeks a description of the Church, that it is an assembly of those who attend decently to the pure Word and the sacraments of Christ, and obtain the palm over the power and fraud of the Roman Pontiff, and praise God from the testament of Moses and Christ, and fear and glorify Him. But here are designated in particular the victors of the beast now inclining toward its end and to be overwhelmed by the latest plagues, though others are not excluded. Aretas understands the law by the song of Moses, from the reason annexed, because it is evident that the only holy One, the only God, is to be feared, Deut. XXXII, v. 4. The δικαιώματα of the Lord, Psalm XIX, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

Καὶ εἶδον ὡς θαλάσσην ὑαλίνην.] Supra IV, 6. mare vitreum fuit plebs Christiana è Judæis: hic collecta ex Gentibus, cu- jus cogitationes Deus introspicit, & ut vitrum purissimum, id est, Crystallum, puras invenit.

Πυρὶ μεμιγμένην.] Incensam magno Dei amore. Amor igni comparatur. Cant. VIII, 7.

Cum Cæsar. & Areta Pontificii contra de mul- titudine hominum, qui Anti-Christum sequentur, in- telligere malunt, quomodo explicat Ribera, quæ mare vocantur, quia semper fervent & tumescunt variis cupiditatibus & fluctibus quibusdam; vitre- am, quia cogitationes impiorum Deo manifestissimæ sunt: Tirino mare vitreum, crystallinum, pelluci- dum est cœlum empyreum, mistum igne, id est, coru- scum splendore Divinæ præsentiæ, & fervens ardore charitatis Sanctorum. Blasius de Viegas in mari Baptismum, in vitro fidem, quæ in baptisino suscipi- tur, in igne vel Spiritum S. vel tribulationem intelli- gendam esse putat ac mare vitreum mistum igne fidem Baptismi persecutionibus probatam adumbrare, supra quod mare victores Anti-Christi securi stant, habentes cytharas, & cantantes Canticum Mosis, quoniam fidem in baptismo susceptam Anti-Christi terroribus superiorem retinuerunt. Glossa Interlin. ad h. l. Mare vitreum, quia in eo baptizatis datur Spiritus Sanctus. Quem sensum probat B. Gerhar- dus conferens locum Matthæi III, 11. Annuit & B. Cluverus, adducens in eam sententiam Prima- sium, quod aqua baptismi S. S. igne conservata designetur.

Καὶ τοὺς νικῶντας ἐκ τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τῆς εἰκόνος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.] Confessores, qui neque blan- ditiis, neque minis adduci poterant, ut aut Deos Romanos invocarent, aut coram imagine se flecterent, aut signum sal- tem aliquod idololatriæ susciperent. Ἐκ hic recte vertas ab, ut Victor ab Aurora populis.

Ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὴν θαλάσσην τὴν ὑαλίνην.] Sicut montes stant circa mare immobile.

Ἔχοντας κιθάρας τοῦ Θεοῦ.] Id est, laudem Deo reddentes. Vide supra V, 8. XIV, 2. Dei citharæ dicuntur, quia DEO sunt sacratæ.

Non apparet ratio, cur hæc ad Vespasiani tem- pora referenda. Contrarium potius ordo indicat. Nam phialarum effusio ad ultimam spectat mundi ætatem, & connexa est cum extremo judicio. Non autem negligendum filum Apocalypseos. Alias nihil certi in ea habebimus. Visio alterius novi, & admirandi signi novam indicat visionem Prophe- ticam. Magnum id erat & admirandum visione, ta- le erat & significatione. Facta autem hæc sunt ad mare vitreum. Quo non plebs Christiana è Judæis, sed baptismus, ut supra c. IV. indicatum, qui est in Ecclesia, ut scilicet innuatur id, quod hic significa- tur in ea eventurum. Mixtio ignis iram gratiæ ad- miscendam docet. Baptismus medium est gratiæ: ignis hic symbolum iræ, Deut. IV, 24. Ebr. XII, 29. Gratiam nempe non denegatum iri pœnitentibus etiam in iræ Divinæ mediis flammis adversus re- probos designatur, ut nonnulli forte ad pœniten- tiam revocari possint.

Cur autem Ephesi, & non in Pathmo, ut cætera illa Johanni visa? Et quomodo sub Vespasiano Prin- cipe, qui jam fatis cesserat? Si explicationem dicto- rum breviter fusiorem habent, quid ad Vespafia- num faciunt? Illa enim demum adhuc futura præ- dicta sunt, Vespasiani autem tempora jam transie- rant. Non autem ultimus effectus iræ Divinæ con- tra paganos, sed Antichristianos, qui Romæ erant, notatur. Confessores ergo innuuntur, quos bestia Romana Antichristus Magnus vincere non potuit, eorumque εὐλογία. Cæterum Angelos referre Deo statum mundi, colligitur è Zach. I, 11. Matth. XIIX, 10. 31. Tob. XII, 13. Quanquam enim ipse omnia in- tuetur, tamen gaudet ministerio ipsorum. Angelus igitur hic explorata hominum conditione refert ad Dominum, quid cognoverit. Et nunc magno zelo è templo cæli, ubi Deo serviunt Potestates ille egres- sus inclamat Christum jam ad judicandam terram paratam, ut faciat, quod decrevit facere. Sic enim comparatam esse terram, ut falcem ipsius messoriam exspectet, ut hic B. Cluverus habet. De eo autem quod ad vitreum mare steterint Cantores, ita ha- bet: Ubi enim commodius consisterent, quam ad limpidum Israëlis fontem, ex quo lumen & sapientia Spiritus promicat? Ubi lubentius, quàm ad paten- tem illam venam, quæ data est domui DEI adversus peccatum & immunditiam Zach. XIII, 1. Prima- sius itidem aquam baptismi igne Spiritus sancti conse- cratam intelligit, superstitantes vero stabiles in fide. Cæsariensis vero multitudinem eorum, qui servantur, futuræq́; quietis puritatem, ac sanctorum splendorem interpretatur mare vitreum sicut & Aretas. Ignem vero probationis illum, de quo Paulus 1. Cor. III, 13. qui bonos illuminet, pravos adurat. Addit autem probabile esse, quod per ignem Divina scientia & vi- vifici Spiritus gratia significetur, quandoquidem Deus Mosi in igne apparuerit, perque illum Spiritus S. Apostolos visitaverit. Atque inde petit descriptio- nem Ecclesiæ, quod sit cœtus eorum, qui ad purum Verbum & sacramenta Christi decenter attendunt, & de Pontificis Romani potestate & fraude palmam consequuntur, Deum vero è Mosis & Christi testa- mento laudant, ipsumque timent & glorificant. Sunt autem hic peculiariter designati victores bestiæ jam ad exitum inclinantis, & novissimis plagis ob- ruendæ, cæteris tamen non exclusis. Aretas per canticum Mosis legem intelligit, è ratione annexa, quia solus sanctus solum Deum timendum esse pa- tet Deuter. XXXII. v. 4. Τὰ δικαιώματα Domini Psalm. XIX, 9.

## 15:3
Vers. 3.

And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God.] Namely, that song which Moses sang at the Red Sea, where, the Egyptians having been destroyed, he who was then the people of GOD was saved, Exod. XV. This is because they had been taught that the Romans were to experience things equal to those which the Egyptians had experienced. Moses is called δῦλος Θεοῦ by a certain preeminence, Josh. XIV, 7. ch. XXII, 4. Psalm CV, 26.

And the song of the Lamb.] That is, the song of Moses applied to Christ and the things of Christ.

Saying, great and wonderful are thy works, O Lord, God the Almighty.] The sense is from verse 6 of Exodus in the cited place. Παντοκράτωρ is צבאות, as we said above I, 9. IV, 8. XI, 17.

The song of the Lamb is also called the song of Moses, either because the Lamb, the Son of God, was celebrated on account of the victory over Pharaoh, as that Lord who had led the Israelites in a pillar of cloud and fire, and had cast the King of the Egyptians into the Red Sea, which was a certain image of baptism, in which Satan is submerged with his power, Col. II. Cf. Exod. III. c. XIV. c. XXIII. Isa. LXIII. 1 Cor. X, 9. or because the song of Moses can rightly be adapted to Christ and his affairs; or because the same Divine benefits are celebrated by Moses and the Lamb in the heavens. For the Son does not cease to defer glory to the Father, being subject to him for all eternity, by which the human nature's dependence on the Father, even if it is of the same Majesty as he, by which the infinite glory communicated to him by the Father, which is not double, nor can it be, as the Calvinists and Jesuits trifle, but only unique.

Just and true are thy ways, O King of the nations.] You do injury to no one, and you stand by your promises. The sense is from verse 13 of the said place in Exodus. The words are almost the very ones from Deut. XXXII, 4. and Hosea XIV, 10. You show yourself to be the Lord not only of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles. The manuscript has 'nations' here, not 'saints' or 'ages', as others do. This title of God is taken from Jer. X, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

Καὶ ᾄδεσι τὴν ᾠδὴν τῶ Μωϋσέως τῶ δέλε τῶ Θεῶ.] Nempe eum cantum, quem Moses cecinit ad mare rubrum, ubi Æ- gyptiis perditis, servatus erat is, qui tunc erat DEI populus, Exod. XV. Hoc ideo, quia paria iis, quæ Ægyptii sense- rant, sensuros Romanos edocti erant. Moses δῦλος Θε per emmentiam quandam dicitur Jos. XIV, 7. cap. XXII, 4. Psalm. CV, 26.

Καὶ τὴν ᾠδὴν τῶ ἀρνίε.] Id est, Mosis canticum applicatum Christo & rebus Christi.

Λέγοντες, μεγάλα καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργά σε, Κύριε, ὁ Θεὸς ὁ Παντοκράτωρ.] Sensus ex commate 6. Exodi dicto loco. Παντοκράτωρ צבאות, ut diximus supra I, 9. IV, 8. XI, 17.

Canticum Agni dicitur etiam Mofis canticum sive quod Agnus Dei Filius ob victoriam de Pharaone et- iam celebratus fuerit, utpote Dominus ille, qui Ifmë- litas in columna nubis & ignis deduxerat, & Regem Ægyptiorum in mare rubrum præcipitarat, quod erat imago quædam baptismi, in quo satanas sub- mergitur cum potestate sua, Col. II. Conf. Exod. III. c. XIV. c. XXIII. Efa. LXIII. 1. Cor. X, 9. sive quod Mofis canticum recte accommodari queat Christo, & rebus ejus; sive quod eadem à Mose & Agno in cœlis celebrentur Divina beneficia. Non cessat enim Patri gloriam deferre Filius, subjectus ei in omnem æternitatem, qua Humanæ naturæ dependen- tiam à Patre, etsi ejusdem cum ipso sit Majestatis, qua gloriam infinitam sibi à Patre communicatam, quæ gemina non est, nec esse potest, uti Calviniani nu- gantur & Jesuitæ, sed unica tantum.

Δίκαιαι καὶ ἀληθιναὶ αἱ ὁδοί σου, ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν ἐθνῶν.] Ne- mini injuriam facis, & stas promissis. Sensus ex commate 13. dicto Exodi loco. Verba prope ipsa ex Deut. XXXII, 4. & Ofeæ XIV, 10. Ostendis te Dominum non Judæorum tan- tum, sed & gentium. Ἐθνῶν hic habet Manuscriptus, non ἁ- γίων, aut αἰώνων, ut alii. Sumptus hic Dei titulus ex Jer. X, 7.

## 15:4
Ver. 4.

Who shall not fear thee, O Lord?) From verse 15 of the said place in Exodus. In the manuscript: Who shall not fear before thee, O Lord, because the nations, with those things in the middle omitted.

And glorify thy name.) From the verse in Exodus.

For thou only art holy.) From verse 11 in the same place.

For all the nations shall come and worship before thee.) From verse 16 of the said place. It was fulfilled then, when idolatry was extinguished throughout the whole Roman empire. They shall come and worship, that is, they shall come, that they may worship.

For thy righteous acts have been made manifest.) From verse 7 of the said place. Moreover, this is a past tense for the future, prophetically. δικαιώματά σου = משפטיך.

The ways of the Lord are celebrated on account of justice, but that admirable justice of God in the supreme work of Redemption, exceeding by far the grasp of the very Angels themselves, tempered with the IMMENSE mercy of God in an incomprehensible and ineffable manner. Whence the Apostle, out of great admiration, exclaims: O the depth of the riches (of mercy) and wisdom! How ineffable are the judgments of God! See here what is said there in Rom. XI, 32. 33. Which admirable judgments of God are also conspicuous from time to time in the economy of the Divine government in the Church, and are sung throughout this book of the Apocalypse. Who these singers were is not expressed, perhaps because they had already been designated in the preceding chapter. For the same ones seem to be introduced here as well. And the subject matter of the song is almost the same on both sides, namely, concerning the redemption of Christ, in whom the admirable justice and mercy of God shine forth most greatly. But it is not to be fulfilled here at last, as in the Grotius sense, that idolatry was extinguished throughout the whole Roman empire, which indeed, according to the opinion of the Holy Spirit, is not to have an end until the end of the world: namely, the idolatry of the Roman Anti-Christ, who is to be finished by the final coming of the Son of GOD, which concerns his final destruction.

PART II. THE SUM OF THE ANGELIC SEPTENARY WITH THE GOLDEN VIALS.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

Τίς ὐ μὴ φοβηθῇ σε, Κύριε.) Ex commate 15. dicti loci in Exodo. In Manuscripto: Τίς ὐ μὴ φοβηθῇ ἐνώπιόν σε Κύριε, ὅτι τὰ ἔθνη, omissis quæ in medio.

Καὶ δοξάσῃ τὸ ὄνομά σου.) Ex commate in Exodo.

Ὅτι μόνος ἅγιος εἶ.) Ex commate 11. ibidem.

Ὅτι πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἥξουσι καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιόν σου.) Ex commate 16. dicti loci. Impletum tunc, cum idololatria ex- tincta est per omne imperium Romanum. Venient & adora- bunt, id est, venient, ut adorent.

Ὅτι τὰ δικαιώματά σου ἐφανερώθησαν.) Ex commate 7. di- cti loci. Est autem hic Præteritum pro futuro προφητικῶς. .משפטיך Δικαιώματά σου

Viæ Domini ob justitiam celebrantur, sed illam admirandam Dei justitiam in opere Redemptionis summo, ipsorummet Angelorum captum longiffi- me excedente cum IMMENSA Dei misericordia, incomprehensibili & ineffabili ratione tempera- tam. Unde Apostolus præ admiratione ingenti exclamat: O profunditatem divitiarum (misericor- diæ) & sapientiæ! Quam ineffabilia sunt judicia Dei! Vid. hic quæ ibi dicta Rom. XI, 32. 33. Quæ admiranda Dei judicia etiam in οἰκονομίᾳ regiminis Divini in Ecclesia subinde conspicua, in hoc Apo- calypseos libro passim decantata. Qui Cantores hic fuerint, non exprimitur, forte quia jam cap. præ- cedenti designati erant. Iidem enim hic quoque in- troduci videntur. Et materia cantici fere eadem est utrobique de redemptione nempe Christi, in quo maxime effulget admiranda Dei cum justitia tum misericordia. Non autem hîc implenda demum idololatria per omne imperium Romanum sensu Grotiano extincta, quæ vero secundum sententiam Spiritus S. non nisi cum fine mundi habitura est fi- nem: Anti-Christi nempe Romani idololatria, qui conficiendus est per adventum Filii DEI novissi- mum, quod ad finalem ejus interitum.

PARS II. OMMA SEPTENARII ANGELICI CUM PHIALIS AUREIS.

## 15:5
Ver. 5.

And after these things I saw and the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony was opened in heaven.) The heavenly sanctuary. He refers, however, not to the times of Solomon but of Moses: And this ναὸς here has the same value as דביר, for which the Latin Psalmist (Ps. 28:2) used the word temple, because, clearly, it provided the use of a temple. By this are signified the oracles of GOD now about to be brought forth. For GOD used to return answers from that sanctuary. Σκηνὴ μαρτυρίε is אהל מועד (Exodus 27:21). And elsewhere: So called, because God would exhibit there the testimony of His Majesty. Others translate it 'tent of meeting,' because the word יעד has a double meaning.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον καὶ ἀνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τῆς σκηνῆς τᾶ μαρ- τυρίε ἐν τῷ ὐρανῷ.) Adytum cœleste. Respicit autem non Salomonis sed Mosis tempora: Et ναὸς hic idem valet, quod דביר, pro quo templi vocem posuit Latinus Psalm. XXVIII. v. 2. quia scilicet templi præbebat usum. Per hoc significantur DEI oracula jam proditura. Nam respon- sa reddebat DEUS ex illo adyto. Σκηνὴ μαρτυρίε est אהל מועד Exodi XXVII. v. 21. Et alibi: Ita dicta, quod Deus ibi Majestatis suæ testimonium exhiberet. Alii vertunt tentorium conventus, quia verbum יעד duplicem habet fi- gnificatum.

## 15:6
And the seven Angels went out who had the seven plagues from heaven.) That ἐκ τῦ ὀρανῦ is to be construed with the verb ἐξῆλ- θον, and by heaven is understood that heavenly sanctuary which John had seen. The prophets figure heaven after the manner of their own temple: There are the νοητὰ (intelligible things), which are the ἐιθητά (visible things) in the temple (Exodus 25:40).

Who were clothed in linen, pure and bright.) Fine linen: Below 19:8. See also above 1:13, Ezekiel 9:2, Daniel 10:5. This garment shows that the judgments which those Angels are about to bring will be both pure and splendid. For λίνον, some books have λίθον, and thus the Latin reads through an error of the scribes, as I think.

And girded about the breasts with golden girdles.) They are signified to be girded for Royal affairs. For the golden belt is of Kings, as we showed above 1:13.

Latin:

Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ ἑπτὰ Ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες ἑπτὰ πληγὰς ἐκ τῦ ὀρανῦ.) Illud ἐκ τῦ ὀρανῦ conftruendum cum Verbo ἐξῆλ- θον, & per cœlum intelligitur adytum illud cœleste, quod Jo- hannes viderat. Prophetæ cœlum figurant ad modum sui templi: Ibi sunt νοητὰ, quæ in templo ἐιθητά Exod. 25, 40.

Οἱ ἦσαν ἐνδεδυμένοι λίνον κὰι καθαρὸν καὶ λαμπρόν. ) Bys- sum: Infra XIX, 8. Vide & supra I, 13. Ez. IX, 2. Dan: X, 5. Hic amictus ostendit judicia, quæ illi Angeli alla- turi sunt, fore & pura & splendida. Pro λίνον libri quidam habent λίθον, & sic legit Latinus per errorem scribarum, ut puto.

Καὶ περιεζωσμένοι περὶ τὰ σήθη ζώνας χρυσᾶς.) Significan- tur accingi ad res Regales. Nam aureus baltheus Regum, ut ostendimus supra I, 13.

## 15:7
Verse 7.

And one of the four living creatures.) The Spirit of Peter, who briefly predicted these things in 2 Peter 1:11, 12. Prophets are said to do what they predict (Jeremiah 1:10). Such is that: 'Then he surrounds the Phaethontiades with the moss of bitter bark.'

He gave to the Angels seven golden Vials.) Understand vials here not as incense-vessels, but as full of fire. They are golden, because these judgments are immutable.

Full of the wrath of the living GOD for ever and ever.) That is, with fire, which signified the wrath of God. For here also are mixed an ἀπόδοσις (rendering) and a comparison, as above 14:20. Thus you have vessels of wrath in Jeremiah 50:25. The title which is here given to God is repeated from the preceding 4:9, 16; 5:14; 10:6.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Καὶ ἓν ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζώων. ) Spiritus Petri, qui hæc breviter prædixit 2. epist. I, 11. 12. Dicuntur Prophetæ fa- cere, quod prædicunt, Jerem. I, 10. Tale illud: Tum Phaëtontiadas musco circumdat amaræ Corticis.

Ἔδωκε τοῖς Ἀγγέλοις ἑπτὰ Φίαλας χρυσᾶς.) Phialas hîc in- tellige non suffitorias, sed plenas ignis. Aureæ sunt, quia im- mutabilia hæc judicia.

Γεμύσας τῦ θυμῦ τῦ Θεῦ τῦ ζῶντος εἰς τὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώ- νων.) Id est, igne, qui iram Dei significabat. Miscentur enim & hic ἀπόδοσις & comparatio, ut supra XIV, 20. Sic vasa iræ habes apud Jerem. L, 25. Titulus, qui hic Deo datur, repeti- tus est ex superioribus IV, 9. 16. V, 14. X, 6.

## 15:8
Verse 8.

And the temple was filled with smoke.) Smoke accompanies fire, as above 14:11, Isaiah 6:4. And it is accustomed to be placed where the wrath of God is treated, Psalm 18:9, 74:1, 80:5.

From the glory of GOD, and from His power.) A hendiadys. For the sense is: on account of the glorious power of God, which is clearly about to appear in those judgments.

And no one was able to enter into the temple.) God did not wish to give any other oracles besides these. The words are taken from Exodus 40:35. Add 1 Kings 8:10, 2 Chronicles 5:14. To enter into the sanctuary is to learn the secrets of God, Psalm 73:16.

Until the seven plagues of the Angels are finished.) For concerning the times after those plagues, new oracles will begin in chapter XX below.

Aretas understands the temple of the tabernacle being opened as referring to the mysteries opened through the coming of Christ: But here it is a matter of the manifestation of the latest plagues, even if the opening made in heaven is a sign of the revelation of the secrets of God, which, having been placed again by Luther on the sun's disk, had been obscured before a great part. The garments of clean linen, according to Andreas, denote angelic nature, purity, and the splendor of virtues; gold denotes wisdom; others, including B. Cluverus, refer it to the priesthood. But that does not suit the Angels. One living creature, thinking it is said for the first, they understand as the lion, the assembly of the Evangelicals in Germany and especially their leader B. Luther. God is called living in contrast to the gods of the nations, as Aretas notes again. The smoke seems to indicate the blindness of the inhabitants of the earth. Compare Isaiah VI. The denial of entry, according to Primasius, is because the secrets of the judgments of GOD cannot be penetrated by all; and the minds of mortals grow dark and tremble at the consideration of the inflicted plagues.

The ark of the covenant, at which the oracles of God were perceived in the Church, is Christ, always present to it. At which and because of which the oracles of God are perceived, when assemblies are celebrated in his name, Matt. 18:20, ch. 28:20. Grotius says, not without self-contradiction, that God did not wish to issue any other oracles besides that one. For he is about to say in chapter 20 that new oracles begin concerning the times after those plagues: although in truth they are not new oracles, for the final judgment was also included in those plagues generally, which, as soon observed by Grotius himself, is described more expressly. Moreover, that phrase 'no one could enter into the temple' indicates the inaccessible Divine glory and the unknown revelation; until, that is, it should subsequently be explained by God himself.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

Καὶ ἐγεμίσθη ὁ ναὸς καπνῦ.) Fumus ignem comitatur, ut supra XIV, 11. Es. VI, 4. Et solet poni, ubi de ira Dei agitur, Psalm. XIIX. 9. LXXIV, 1. LXXX, 5.

Ἐκ τῆς δόξης τῦ Θεῦ, καὶ τῆς δυνάμεως ἀυτῦ.) ἔν διὰ δυοῖν. Sensus enim est ob potentiam Dei gloriosam, apparituram scilicet in illis judiciis.

Καὶ ἐδὺς ἠδύνατο εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν ναόν.) Nulla Deus alia edere voluit oracula præter ista. Verba sumpta ex Exod. XI, 33. Adde 1. Reg. IIX, 10. 2. Paral. V, 14. Intrare in adytum est Dei arcana discere, Psalm. LXXIII, 16.

Ἄχρι τελεσθῶσιν αἱ ἑπτά πληγαὶ τῶν Ἀγγέλων.) Nam de temporibus post illas plagas nova oracula incipient cap. XX. infra.

Templum tabernaculi apertum de apertis per Christi adventum mysteriis Aretas intelligit : Sed hic de manifestatione plagarum novissimarum agi- tur, etsi apertio in cælo facta signum sit revelationis secretorum Dei, quæ per Lutherum in solis disco iterum posita, ante magnam partem obfuscata fue- re. Vestes lini mundi secundum Andream Ange- lica natura puritatem, virtutumque splendorem, au- rum sapientiam notant; alii, etiam B. Cluverus ad sacerdotium referunt. Sed Angelis id non conve- nit. Animal unum, pro primo dictum putantes, intelligunt leonem cœtum Evangelicorum in Ger- mania eorumque imprimis Antesignanum B. Lu- therum. Deus vivens dicitur in ἀντιθέσει ad Deos gentium notante iterum Aretas. Fumus cæcitatem habitatorum terræ indicare videtur. Cons. Es. VI. Negatio ingressus secundum Primasium est, quod non ab omnibus judiciorum DEI arcana penetrari queant; mentesque mortalium inflictarum confide- ratione plagarum caligent palpitantes.

Arca fœderis, ad quam oracula Dei percipie- bantur in Ecclesia, est Christus, illi semper præsens. Ad quam & propter quam oracula Dei percipiun- tur, cum in nomine ejus conventus celebrantur, Matth. 18, 20. cap. 28, 20. Nulla Deum alia edere voluisse oracula, præter istud, non sine ἑαυτομα- χίᾳ dicit Grotius. Nam de temporibus post illas plagas nova oracula incipere cap. 20. jam jam di- cturus est: Licet revera non sint nova oracula, Nam & judicium novissimum illis plagis comprehensum fuit γενικῶς, quod mox à Grotio ipso observatum, expressius describitur.
