Vinar, Dannhauer, and others wish for Christian Kings to be designated: in which sense the ancients and others also say that Kings from the rising of the sun are named because they are devoted to Christ; such as Primasius, Ticonius, the Ordinary Gloss, Thomas, Flacius, Picard, Pareus, Estius, Richter, Cluver, Döling, Kromajer. Fox opposed them, but without cause. They say that Kings illuminated by the knowledge of the Gospel are called so, or because light signifies good and happy things: for they teach that a good and happy thing is signified from a comparison of a similar phrase in 2 Sam. 23, 4; Ps. 2, 1. 2; Es. 41, 26; Dan. 11, 44; Act. 7, 2.

But those three frogs, coming out of the mouth of the Dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and of the false Prophet, are without doubt three orders of the enemies of Christ, for their names testify that they are those enemies, since frogs croaking with their unpleasant clamor offend the ears. Such enemies are therefore noted who are going to attack the doctrine, person, and office of Christ the most: inasmuch as they are called three unclean spirits, just as heretics are described, whose doctrine and life is an unclean sense, an unclean conscience (Tit. I. 15.). They are also said to come out of the mouth of the Dragon (Apoc. 12, 15. 16.), just as one can read concerning the false Prophets in the time of Ahab (1 Reg. 20, 15.) that a heavenly army appeared before God, inasmuch as devils mix themselves with heavenly armies, transforming themselves into Angels of light (1 Cor. 11, 14.), and that some notable seducer from the order of evil angels received that he would go out and be a false Spirit in the mouth of the false Prophets of Ahab, so that he might enter into war against the Syrians (v. 21.), which in Luc. 11, 24 is called τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα.

By the beast some understand the Roman Anti-Christ himself, or the second beast, namely the marine one, Apoc. 13, 1. sqq. But since by that former beast the Roman empire itself is designated, insofar as it serves the Roman Pontiff and protects him with its Anti-Christian machinations, while here he is openly indicated by the name of False Prophet, Apoc. 16, 13. Conf. c. 17, 7. c. 14, 10, 11. more correctly with Blessed Gerhard, here the Roman Anti-Christ himself is understood. Moreover, three spirits are mentioned, according to others indeed, in Pietro Soave, History of the Council of Trent, book 2, page 97, the Apostolic nuncio in the Council of Trent, namely John Maria Montanus, Marcellus Cervinus, and Reginald Pole, who all were afterwards in their order raised to the papal throne; according to others, and especially Cocceius, they are called three spirits because they go forth from the mouth of the three, the Dragon, the beast, and the False Prophet: But since the False Prophet and the beast are subordinate to the Dragon, they are not conveniently separated from one another; others therefore more correctly wish a triple reason for the spirits to be indicated, namely the spirit of homicide, of the desire for temporal things, and the spirit of lying and of false doctrine, to be encrusted with every artifice: To others, however, it pleases that one should look not so much to a determined and specific plurality as to the sufficiency of the spirits: but it is better, because most things in the Apocalypse imply a definite number, to establish that three orders are designated: namely those subordinate to the Dragon, with the Jesuits, the ultimate excrement of the Dragon, by Ignatius of Loyola (if I may be forgiven the expression) in the year 1537, whose order was confirmed at the beginning of the year 1540 by Pope Paul III, later by Julius II, then by Paul IV, as well as by Pius of the same number, and finally by the Council of Trent: in which in the year 1543, by virtue of a diploma of the Roman Pontiff, 64 of them were admitted, although today their number has grown beyond 600, nay, beyond 6000. To these are added in the second place similar broods of vipers, the Capuchins, sanctioned in the year 1530 by Clement VII. Of the third order are the Calvinists, who partly, like the Zwinglians, elide the force of the sayings of Scripture concerning the birth, passion, and death of the Son of God: partly by the Piscatorian Synecdoche restrict the same to the human nature alone; partly make identical propositions out of them, so that finally nothing of κοινωνίας remains: in addition to this, they communicate the majesty to the flesh of Christ, and so the power of giving life, and the ἐνέργειαν, as far as the flesh is concerned, given for the life of the world, John VI. 51, they overturn, and for that reason they oppose both the mutual communion of natures, and the communication of idioms, and the cooperation of ἐνεργημάτων in the acts of office, and in the ἐνεργείαις θεανδρικαῖς, nay, they even remove the personal union in the Nestorian manner; not to mention that the Calvinists contend that the emptying and exaltation of Christ took place according to both natures, and that the Jesuits are very closely related to Stancarianism; and that I shall now involve in silence the particularity of the merit and satisfaction of Christ, restricted by the Calvinists to the absolutely elect alone, and the negation of the fulfillment of the law made by Christ for us, chosen by Piscator and most other Calvinists, which two latter φορτικὰ ἀκούσματα concern the Mediatorial and Priestly office of Christ. But who would doubt that Christ, the Sun of justice, is thus darkened, both as to his person and suppositum, and as to his office, and his Pontifical and Royal dignity? And that this is done with biting and chewing against the truth asserted by us, the public writings of those who are on the opposite side testify: it is done also with blasphemy against the orthodox, the properly and truly Catholic, and also against Christ Jesus himself, the God-man, for whom it is set forth in public, and as they say, in the very disk of the sun, that they perform no penance for these things. Now those impure spirits are said to go forth unto the kings of the whole earth, because the Jesuits and monks, and Papists, and other little priests, especially the Apostolic Nuncios, Cardinals, and Confessors, possess the greatest power in the courts of Emperors and Catholic Kings, as they call them, as well as in great Republics by their authority: at whose nod and counsel those are in great part directed: which things indeed are directed primarily, if not solely, to the destruction of the kingdom of Christ, the propagation of the Anti-Christian, and the dissemination of the Roman Catholic Religion throughout the whole world, even with the shaking of the entire globe. Of which, rich experience of events testifies from elsewhere, with the groaning, and tears, and detestation of all the pious.

Now therefore, as to the sixth, concerning that Angel, by whom preparation is made for the crossing through the Euphrates, by the pouring out of the sixth vial, so that it may become fordable for the Kings, and the way may be opened for those who come from the rising of the sun, which phrase seems to imply a place and a term from which, and to confirm a literal sense. Which explanation we deservedly leave to the judgment of the readers, and of the pious and learned searchers of the Holy Scriptures. For before the completion, a prophecy is rarely wont to be clear. But since these things which we have said have now been proven by the event, there is no doubt that the congregation of that assembly of Roman Catholic Kings of the earth, and the crossing through that great river Euphrates, is to be expected on that day which God Almighty has defined in the secrets of his judgments: Therefore, we are stirred by Christ himself, as was done in Rev. II, III, XIV, XXII, to vigilance and to a stricter custody of the garments by which the shame of our nakedness may be covered, namely, of such priests, and of nuptial garments: and this by a voice sounding from heaven, so that it may be heard by all. Which office and benefit of his most gracious mercy and long-suffering is to be accepted with a grateful mind by all means, Rom. II. 4.

But concerning the signs and miracles by which the Anti-Christ, and his companions and satellites, and emissaries show themselves off, it has been spoken at Matthew XXIV. 23, 2. Thess. II. 9. Which, it is evident even from 2. Thess. II. 3, are wont to happen to and be joined with the croaking of these mystical frogs.

But the place of the congregation, why it is called Harmageddon, is not so obvious, and therefore interpreters inquire into it laboriously. I will not, however, say that Aretas has ἑρμαγεδὼν, for this is a slip of the eye. The explanation of the blessed Luther pleases me more: Damned soldiers, cursed armies, unhappy warriors, which was also approved by the blessed D. Gravius in his tables of the Apocalypse. For he reads Chorma-Gedon, which is an ill-omened and execrable League, or confederation, which Gravius not badly refers to the Spanish League, constructed and bound together to cut off the heretics, as they call them, and confederated for the last (would that it had truly been the last) Ligistic war: and he wishes there to be a reference to the city of Hormah of the tribe of Simeon, at which the Israelites first cursed the Canaanites. Num. XXI. 3. Concerning which see at ch. XIX. 11. seq. the blessed one, Tab. XLVII. p. 73, designated: The Papists, bearing most grievously the occasion of the desolation of Babylon, and the destruction or weakening of the Anti-Christian Kingdom in various places, especially the Jesuitical Frog, will attempt extreme measures, will implore the aid of Kings and Magnates, and will gather them into the war of that great day of God Almighty, Rev. XVI. 14. For Rome will not be desolated and burned, or the whole Kingdom of Anti-Christ destroyed in one assault, and reduced to nothing, (for this is against the express text, 2. Thess. II. 8. whom the Lord will consume with the Spirit of his mouth, and will destroy with the brightness of his coming) but no small remnants will remain in the regions of the Papists, and the Pope himself will place his seat either in Spain or Sicily, Sardinia, the Balearic Islands, or other lands still addicted to the Anti-Christian superstition, and will oppose Christ, as much as in him lies, until at length in the last war stirred up by the Jesuits, he shall have been overcome by Christ, the supreme leader of the Church, and his army, and his entire Monarchy shall clearly collapse, in Harmageddon. By the two-horned beast, he understands in a singular explanation the Spaniard, with his confederates, i.e., the Kings of the earth, Princes and Papal Dynasts, belonging to the Spanish League, or some similar one newly to be entered into: but more correctly that conspiracy is extended more generally to all who conspire for the destruction of the kingdom of Christ. He interprets the False Prophet concerning the order of the Lojolitae [Jesuits]: but more truly are included at the same time other orders of Monks, and the rest of the Papists, the slaves, satellites, creatures, and champions of the Roman Anti-Christ, whom we have already mentioned. For all these conspire for the ruin of the Catholic Church. Nor is this trio to be taken in any other sense in chapter XIX. 20. He also refers to this the term of the bound Dragon: which, as regards the beginning of the binding, he does not refer with others to the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel throughout the whole world, namely the year of Christ 70 (for this beginning he himself assigned), nor to the victories of Constantine the Great, which is the opinion of many, nor to the year of Christ 300, in which Gog and Magog, i.e., the Turkish Empire in the Ottoman family, nor with the Blessed D. Nicolai to the year of Christ 521, in which the Emperor Justinian, admonished by Hormisdas, Bishop of Rome, undertook the extermination of the Arians, Nestorians, Eutychians, Monothelites, etc., the Blessed D. G. refers, which last beginning not to the distinction it makes, and therefore it is deservedly neglected; but for the propagation of the kingdom of Christ: the end indeed in the year of Christ 1521, in which the Mahometanizing sects began to be freed from the bonds of the Angel the key-bearer, that is, the Roman Pope. But in truth, since the Roman Pontiff is nowhere in the Scriptures called the key-bearer, even though he constitutes himself the key-bearer by way of excellence, and the infernal abyss is constituted not by him—who is himself one day to be finally cast into the same—but by the infernal Dragon and that ancient serpent in chapter IX. 1: Now the beginning of the binding of Satan was made by D. G. in the year 401, in which Attila, King of the Huns, after he had tyrannically and cruelly harassed the Empire, both Eastern and Western, with a huge army, in the Catalaunian fields in Gaul alone, with one hundred and ninety thousand Huns lost in the battle, led the remaining armies into Pannonia, having gathered his strength in the year 453. having entered Italy, he threatened Rome with dire things: but appeased by the intercession of Leo, the Roman Pontiff, he departed: whence some establish the limit of this millennium as the year 1453, to which B. D. G. adds, in which Gog or the Turk, having recovered his strength, conquered Constantinople and took the Empire of the whole East away from the Christians, and thus opened a way for himself anew to infest the mountains of Israel, until he himself also is one day finished off in the mountains of Israel. He himself explains the place of the slaughter, Harmageddon, as some place by the Baltic Sea, and conjecturally assigns it between Lübeck and Hamburg. The same opinion regarding the etymology of the Hebrew word sat with Drusius, namely that it is composed of חרמ, destruction, and גדוהן, their army: which others prefer to establish as composed of two Hebrew words, הר מגדו, the mount of Megiddo, which place is famous for the mournful slaughter of King Josiah 2. Kings XXIII. 29, which two latter opinions are approved by us above others, although the blessed Gerhard prefers the last. Who understands by the beast the Anti-Christian kingdom, that is, not as we do the Roman Empire, insofar as it supports the Roman Anti-Christ, but the Roman Anti-Christ himself, the head, namely, of the Anti-Christian kingdom, together with the Cardinals, Bishops, and Prelates. He wishes the spirits to be called like frogs because they will clamor against the true Doctors of the Church and be troublesome with their croaking, nay, even inflame the Papal nobles with calumnies against the confessors of the Gospel.

Finally, the seventh Angel is said to be about to pour out his vial into the air, not because the Roman Anti-Christ is about to enter into a pact through magical arts with the Devil, the Prince of the air, Eph. VI. 12, as the late, that distinguished theologian, the blessed Gerhard, believed: much less is it to be believed, as it seemed to the blessed Gravius, that the completion of that vision is to be sought in the most glorious victories of GUSTAVUS ADOLPHUS, King of the Swedes, of most glorious memory, against the Leaguers: but as the same blessed Gerhard more correctly interprets, in the final destruction and ruin of the Anti-Christian kingdom, which is to come, when God is about to destroy it under the end of the world through thunders, lightnings, and bolts from heaven, so that that great city may fall, c. XIV. 8. 9. c. XVII. 18, together with all its inhabitants, men of the highest, middle, and lowest condition. Which distinction others refer to the dissensions preceding that total destruction, in the Ecclesiastical, Political, and Economic state: the blessed Gravius observes that it is referred by others to three kinds of Religions, namely Anti-Christian, Christian, and Neutral, while others reduce it to those three primary sects, the Lutheran, the Papal, and the Calvinist; he himself, however, in the explanation of his own opinion, warns that Babylon is said to be divided into three parts, yet so that Babylon remained: but that the Lutherans and Calvinists are no longer in Babylon, but have gone out, and are not its parts, but its most intense adversaries and enemies, and therefore he prefers to understand the dissensions that have arisen between the Kings and Princes themselves in the Papal kingdom. But since Babylon is here predicted to be cut off, and that totally and finally, there will certainly be no place for those distributions. And therefore it is better with others to refer these to the Kings and those deserting Babylon, Rome, and the Roman Anti-Christ, who become its enemies and conquerors. Which excision of it is here prefigured not only as temporal, but also as eternal, as is especially to be understood from c. XIX. and XX. Whence Bertho in his Allegories handed down this opinion on Apoc. XIIX: When the Angel (Christ) has cast a millstone upon the sinners (a hard sentence, and the weight of eternal damnation, which will crush them in hell), then Babylon (the congregation of the impious) will be cast impetuously and quickly into hell, where there will be no voice of the harp (any melodious joy), nor voice of the mill (delicate bread, and the delight of any flavor), nor voice of the bridegroom (the conjunction of any love), Jer. LI. 64, nor light of a lamp (the brightness of any splendor). The phrase taken from the voice of the harp seems to be from Is. XXIV. 8, Jer. VII. 34, XXV. 10. Ezech. XXVI. 13, of the voice of the bride from Jer. VII. 34, XVI. 9, XXV. 10, XXXIII. 11. Mention of the cup of divine wrath is made in Is. LI. 22, 28, Jer. XXV. 15. By hail is noted the weight of divine wrath, with respect to Exod. IX. 22 and Jos. X. 11. By the golden cup some understand the Mass-cup from Apoc. XVII. 14.

Now most judge correctly that the corporal burning of Babylon, or Rome, is designated, since both the context and the paraphrases of the text, and the sequence of the connection in c. XVIII, favor this sense: but the spiritual burning should be attributed to the Ecclesiastical ministry, not to earthly Kings. Furthermore, by the Angel seen in Ap. XIIX. 1, some wish Christ himself to be designated, yet most others understand some distinguished Doctor, whom Gerhard and Gravius interpret particularly as the blessed Luther: as one who illuminated almost the whole world with the clarity of Evangelical doctrine, 2 Cor. IV. 6, whom also the blessed Gerhard in c. XXI. 1 thought was predicted here as the key-bearing Angel, the future binder of the Dragon, with the Weimar Paraphrasts agreeing, although the blessed Osiander seems to favor a ministering Angel. But these things are concerning c. XVI.

Latin:

Καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν Θεὸν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς τῆς χαλάζης, ὅτι μεγάλη ἐστὶν ἡ πληγὴ αὐτὴ σφόδρα) Tanta erat animorum obduratio, ut reliquiæ idololatrarum in Romano imperio magis magisque Christianis maledicerent, tanquam ipsorum religio omnium horum malorum causa esset. Hic fuit ultimus singultus moribundæ idololatriæ. In- telligendi autem hic præcipue Senatores Romani, qui per Italiam sparsi, alii hic, alii illic a Gothis sunt interfecti.

Non inrecte se habet interpretatio, modo Ro- mam Christianam vel potius Anti-Christianam in locum Paganæ vel Ethnicæ, Romanum Pontificem in Imperatoris Romani gentilis & Cardinales Ro- manos in Senatorum locum surroget, & ultimum quasi singultum & conatum idololatriæ Papalis jam- jam cum adventu Christi exterminandæ & igne in- fernali puniendæ intelligat.

Juvat autem nunc per ἀνακεφαλαίωσιν repete- re, & in summum redigere ea, quæ de septem phialis Apocalypticis dicta sunt, utpote quæ non uni In- terpp. crucem fixerunt. Hæc autem omnibus ex- pensis, nostra est de illis sententia: Quod nempe per primum Angelum, per ulcera, penes illos pro- tuberantia, qui characterem bestiæ habent, indice- tur ulcus conscientiæ, quæ saucienda inde erit, quod certi non esse permittantur de gratia DEI. Hæc enim propinqua est ad desperationem via Marc. IX. 46. Es. XLVI. 24. idcirco dicuntur habere κε- καυτηριασμένην τὴν ἰδίαν συνείδησιν 1. Tim. IV. 2. cauteriatam conscientiam: συνείδησιν πονηρὰν, ma- lam conscientiam Ebr. X. 22.

Alter Angelus effundet temporib9 novissimis pro- ximis phialam in mare, ex qua redundabit sanguis ut mortui, qui nuper mortuus erat: nam e corpore mortuo naturaliter rubicund9 sanguis raro prodire solet, unde animantia in mari oportebit interire v. 3.

Tertius in fluvios & fontes aquarum tertiam phia- lam effundet, unde orietur sanguis. Quo facto de- prædicabitur divina justitia, ab Angelo, alio dicen- te, Justus es, Domine, qui es, & qui eras, & sanctus, quod ista judicaris. Quia sanguinem sanctorum & Prophetarum effuderunt, & sanguinem ipsorum de- disti ipsis bibere: digni enim sunt. Et audita est alia vox ex altari, auro obducto, dicens: Vere Domine Deus omnipotens, veracia & justa sunt judicia tua. Per mare intelligitur collectio aquarum, multitudo insignis populorum. Denotantur ergo integri po- puli, regiones & regna, interprete ipsomet Spiritu Sancto. Apoc. XVII. 15. Aquæ, quas vidisti, qui- bus insidet meretrix, sunt populi, & exercitus, & gentes, & linguæ. Fluvii vero & fontes ceu minores, sunt civitates, & oppida, vel pagi; vel si malis, ma- gnates & Magistratus, nec non inferioris ordinis, & plebejos, ut & subditos, intelligere poteris, hosce omnes justo Dei judicio inficiet meretrix scortati- onibus suis, unde illis conscientiæ vermis mordens in animabus ipsorum exorietur, in æternum eos- dem consumens.

Quartus Angelus occupatur in effusione quartæ phialæ, quæ effunditur in solem; cui datur igne urere homines, & urentur flamma ingenti, & blasphema- ri sunt nomen Dei in plagas istas potestatem habentis : nec tamen per pœnitentiam daturi Deo sunt glo- riam. Sol mystice est Christus, qui sol justitiæ dici- tur Mal. IV. 1. Jehovah justitia nostra, Jer. XXIII. 6. factusque nobis a Deo est justitia, ut in ipso solo, so- laque ipsius justitia, gloriemur Jer. IX. 24. 1. Cor. I. 30. 31. ideo Ecclesia dicitur περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον, quod induat Christi justitiam Gal. III. 27. ac vestem justitiæ hujus sacerdotis sui, eaque ornetur ceu pul- cherrimo habitu sponsi sui, stola sacerdotali justi- tiæ Es. LXI. 10. ac gaudet in hoc Domino suo tam insigni amictu, ceu regia sponsa in decore suo pul- cerrimo Psal. XLV. 8. vestibus acupictis ornata v. 15. vestibus feriarum solennium ornata Zach. III. 5. de quibus etiam legere est Matth. XVII. 12. Apoc. III. 18. c. XIV. 15. c. XIX. 8. 9. Quibus qui destitui- tur, eum æternum exulare, atque excludi oportet e nuptiis agni Apoc. XIX. 7. Matth. XXII. 12. Terra ibi (in βασιλείᾳ ἐσκοτωμένῃ) tenebrosa & obscura, quia & fumo & nebulis fœtoris obscuratur. Terra oblivionis, quia, sicut ipsi obliti sunt Dei, ita eorum obliviscitur Deus misereri, ut habet Anshelmus, l. 4. de imag. mundi c. II. Tunc coacte in tenebras exte- riores mittentur, qui nunc interioribus voluntarie delectantur, dicente Gregorio M. l. XXV. moral. c. cent. Ignis lucebit miseris non ad consolationis obje- ctum, sed ad miseriæ augmentum, ut cernant, unde doleant divina virtute, secundum Basilium M. in Psal. 28. Parabitur ignis ab ejus adustiva virtute: claritas cedet in gaudium sanctorum, ustiva pars in tormentum damnatorum. Flamma ignis iram Dei & ignem infernalem designant, urentem in infernum usque, Deut. 32, 22. Psal. 97, 10. 2. Thess. 5, 8. 9. 2. Pet. III. 11. nunquam defiturum, Es. 66, 24. Marc. 9, 44. Apoc. 14, 10. 11. c. 18, 7. c. 17, 4. c. 20, 10. Unde Deus ob iram infinitam & æternam ignis consumens dici- tur πῦρ καταναλίσκον Ebr. 12, 29. Deut. 4, 24.

Quinto effundenda erit phiala in ipsum thronum bestiæ, & inde regnum ejus obtenebrabitur valde, & linguas suas manducabunt præ dolore. Quo ad- umbrantur cruciatus infernales exquisitissimi, ab igneo fluvio accendendi, præ quorum summa ma- gnitudine manducabunt reprobi dentes suos, Es. 30, 33. c. 22, 13. de quibus etiam vide Apoc. 17, 16. Luc. 16, 23. 24. 25. ob quos dolores infernales gravissimos damnati in tenebris illis exterioribus, uti vocantur Matth. 8, 22. c. 22, 13. 1. Petr. 2, 4. 6. 7. 8. vehemen- tius blasphemabunt nomen Domini sanctissimum, juxta cum Diabolo, & angelis ejus damnatis; unde magis magisque augebuntur cruciatus ipsorum, nullumque unquam finem habituri sunt, nullam ipsis requiem, nullum intervallum relinquent, nun- quam desinent cruciari, quia nunquam desinent nomen Domini blasphemare, ac criminari. Ut ul- cus ad vermem conscientiæ non moriturum, sic ca- lor & flamma ad ignem inextinguibilem pertinent, quo utroque cruciatus infernales, tum interni, tum externi designantur. Nullus autem est in inferno pœnitentiæ, nullus remissioni aut requiei pœna- rum locus, nullus finis, aut terminus. Damnati enim quærent quidem mortem, & non invenient, Apoc. 9, 6. In carne cruciabuntur sine intermissioneper ignem, in animam per conscientiæ vermem: Sic morientur, ut semper vivant, sic vivent, ut semper moriantur, dicente in Medit. Bernhardo. Quamdiu vivet De- us, vivent electi : quamdiu vivent electi, morientur reprobi, h. e. in secula seculorum. Non erunt ibi homines ante mortem, & post mortem, sed semper in morte ait August. XIII. de C. D. c. 11. ac per hoc nunquam viventes, nunquam mortui, sed sine fine morientes. Nunquam enim erit homini pejus in morte, quam ubi erit mors ipsa sine morte, ut insignis quidam Theologus loquitur. Sic ignis urit, ait Bern- hard. med. mort. c. 3. ut semper reservet, sic tormen- ta aguntur, ut semper reonerentur: & ut Paulinus de obitu Celsi flebiliter canit ex humana compassione: Vita erit his sine fine mori, & mors vivere pœnis Et durante sua pascere carne cruces. Ipse suos proprie peccator corpore gignit Carnifices, & erit vermibus esca suis. Mentem enim, ut Isidorus in med. habet uret tristi- tia, corpus flamma. Erit fletus ex dolore, uti Bern- hardus ait serm. VIII. in Psalmo: Qui habitat: Stri- dor dentium ex furore. Si enim, ut hoc ex Augusti- no l. VI. de C. D. c. 6. repetam, anima in pœnis vivit æternis, mors illa potius æterna dicenda est, quam vi- ta: nulla quippe major & pejor est mors, quam ubi non moritur mors. Neque ratio tanti judicii deest, Nam (quod Gregor. in moral. suggerit) ad distri- cti judicii sententiam pertinet, ut nunquam careant supplicio, quorum mens in hac vita nunquam carere voluit peccato.

Sexto Angelus describitur cum phiala, quam ef- fundet ipse in Euphratem fluvium Assyriam trans- euntem, Gen. II. 14. ut siccetur, & Regibus ab oriente solis via paretur, cum conjuncta visione trium ra- narum. Sicut Euphratis, inquit B. Gerhard. p. 121. Ba- bylon beneficio eam alluentis, tantas collegit divitias: sic Romanus Anti-Christus habuit retia sua pecunia- ria, proventus scil. maximos, ex indulgentiis, palliis, annatis, bullis, &c. Hosce acquirendi modos taxasse Angelum sextum censet. Sed pœna hic recensentur Babylonis, effusione phialarum designatæ, non cul- pæ, supplicia, non delicta. Rectius autem idem por- ro Euphrates, ait, est Symbolum opum, quibus muni- tur Babylon mystica, h. e. Roma: sicut olim Babylon orientalis Euphrate fuit munita. Cyrus Babylonem oppugnans Euphratem ac flumina urbi vicina alio derivavit, ut viam in urbem sibi pararet Jer. LI. 31. sic hoc loco prædicitur, quod Deus Regibus ab ortu so- lis venturis viam præparaturus sit, ut regnum Anti- Christi, quod est Babylon mystica, destruere possint. De Cyro hæc Historici tradunt, ab Usserio in Chro- nologia p. 144. laudati: Cyrus circa urbis murum ab eo ductæ fossæ ostia aperiens, aqua fluminis eo derivata pristinum ejus alveum (duorum stadio- rum latitudine per urbem tendentem) hominibus pervium reddidit (Herodot. l. 1. c. 190. 191. Xenoph. Instit. l. III. cum Jeremia c. L. 38. & LI. 32. 36.). Per fluvium vero jam vadosum Cyrus cum exercitu transiens, observatis omnibus, quæ ad flumen fere- bant, portulis, conscensisque septis, urbem (Baby- lonem) invasit, cum die festo agitarentur convivia, Jer. LI. 39. 57. Tantaque urbis erat magnitudo, ut (quemadmodum narrabant incolæ) quum capti jam essent, qui extremas urbis partes incolebant, ii qui mediam habitabant partem id non animad- verterant (Herodot. l. 1. c. 19.) Quo spectant & illa Prophetæ Jer. LI. 31. Cursori obviam cursori curret, & nuncius obviam nuncio, ad indicandum Regi Babylo- niæ, captam esse civitatem ejus ad extremitatem. Conf. Dan. V. 2. 3. 10. 30. Xenoph. Instit. l. 7. Es. 13. 14. 21. 43. 46. 47. Hab. 2. Jer. 25. 50. 51. Dan. 5, 21. c. 5, 8. 12. 15. Alii de exsiccatione magnorum redituum, cum Sze- gedino, Dölino. Dürf. Franz. Kromeicro, hæc accipi- unt, quæ facta per Evangelii præconium in Svecia, Dania, Pomerania, &c. Quanquam vero hæc ne- que fidei, neque vaticinii analogiæ contraria sint, ordo tamen Prophetiæ alium sensum poscit, ideo cum Turcæ non opus habeant Euphratis transitu, quippe qui jam pridem in Ungaria, & Trans-Syl- vania sedem fixere, non reprobanda interpretatio metaphorica, a comparatione transitus Regis Persi- ci, B. Gerhardi explicatio, facilius admitti etiam judicio potest: quia quæ de Regibus ab ortu solis adventantibus cum aliis nonnullis circa hunc lo- cum ex nostro textu observantur Reges nempe hostiles intelligi, quales olim fuere Rex Medorum Darius & Rex Persarum Cyrus: prae quibus rectius in genere intelligit pios Reges & Principes, qui, re- pudiatis erroribus Anti-Christianis, lucem Evan- gelii recipiunt, siquidem ortus solis symbolum sit rei bonae ac faustae, Apoc. VII. 2. & doctrina Evangelii doctrina sit de Christo, qui est oriens ex alto Luc. I. 78. De devastatione ergo, ac poena finali Babylonis haec accipiunt Richterus, Gerhardus, Cluverus, Erasm. Schmidius, & Pareus. Christianos autem Reges designari volunt Vinar. Dannhauer. & alii: quo sensu etiam Reges ab ortu solis nominari vete- res aliique ajunt, quia Christo dediti sunt; utpote Primasius, Ticonius, Glossa ordinar. Thomas, Fla- cius, Picardus, Pareus, Estius, Richterus, Cluverus, Döling. Kromajer. Quibus sese opposuit, sed citra causam Foxus. Reges autem notitia Evangelii illu- minatos vocari dicunt, vel quia lux significat bona & laeta: rem enim bonam & laetam significari, do- cent e collatione phraseos consimilis 2. Sam. 23, 4. Ps. 2, 1. 2. Es. 41, 26. Dan. 11, 44. Act. 7, 2.

Tres vero illae ranae, exeuntes ex ore Draconis, & ex ore bestiae, & falsi Prophetae, sine dubio, sunt tres ordines hostium Christi, nam hostes illos esse testan- tur nomina eorum, quum ranae coaxantes clamore suo ingrato aures offendant. Tales ergo notantur hostes, qui Christi doctrinam, personam, & officium maxime impugnaturi sunt: utpote qui dicuntur tres Spiritus immundi, quemadmodum describun- tur haeretici, quorum doctrina & vita impura est immundus sensus, immunda conscientia, Tit. I. 15. Exi- re etiam dicuntur ex ore Draconis Apoc. 12, 15. 16. quemadmodum de falsis Prophetis, tempore Achabi 1. Reg. 20, 15. legere est, quod comparuerit coram Deo exercitus coelestis, siquidem coelestibus exer- citibus immiscseant sese Diaboli, transformantes sese in Angelos lucis, 1. Cor. 11, 14. quodque rece- perit ex ordine malorum angelorum insignis ali- quis seductor, sese egressurum, & futurum in ore falsorum Prophetarum Achabi falsum Spiritum, ut bellum adversus Syros ineat v. 21. qui Luc. 11, 24. τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα dicitur.

Per bestiam nonnulli intelligunt ipsummet Anti- Christum Romanum, vel secundam bestiam, marinam nempe Ap. 13, 1. sq. Sed quum per bestiam illam prio- rem designatum sit ipsum Romanum imperium, quatenus inservit Pontifici Romano, eundemque cum Anti-Christianis suis molitionibus tuetur, hic vero aperte nomine Pseudo-Prophetae indigitetur Apoc. 12, 10. Conf. c. 27, 7. c. 14, 10, 11. rectius cum B. Gerhardo, hic intelligitur ipse Anti-Christus Roma- nus. Dicuntur autem tres Spiritus, juxta alios qui- dem, apud Petr. Suavem Hist. C. T. l. 2. pag. 97. nuncius Apostolicus in Conc. Trid. utpote Joh. Maria Montanus, Marcellus Cervinus, & Reginaldus Polus, qui omnes postea ordine suo ad thronum papalem evecti sunt, juxta alios, & imprimis Coc- ceium, tres spiritus dicuntur, quia ex trium ore, Draconis, bestiae, & Pseudo-Prophetae exeunt: Sed quum subordinati Draconi sunt Pseudo-Prophe- tae cum bestia, non commode ab invicem secer- nuntur; triplicem ergo rationem Spirituum alii re- ctius indigitari volunt, spiritus nempe homicidii, cu- piditatis rerum temporalium, & Spiritus mendacii, & falsae doctrinae, cum omni artificio incrustandae: Aliis tamen placet non tam ad determinatam & specificam pluralitatem, quam ad sufficientiam Spi- rituum respici: sed praestat, quia pleraque in Apo- calypsi numerum definitum inferunt, tres ordines designari, statuere: utpote Draconi subordinatos, cum Jesuïtas, extremum Draconis excrementum, ab Ignatio Lojola (sit venia verbis) An. 1537. excretum, quorum ordo initio An. 1540. a Papa Paulo III. postea a Julio II. tum a Paulo IV. necnon a Pio ejus- dem numeri, & deniq; a Concilio Tridentino confir- matus est: in quo An. 1543. vi diplomatis R. Pontif. illorum 64. admittuntur, cum hodie numerus eo- rum ultra 600. excreverit, imo ultra 6000. Quibus secundo adduntur similia viperarum genimina, Ca- puccini, ann. 1530. a Clemente VII. sanciti. Tertii or- dinis sunt Calviniani, qui partim Zwingliani allæosi elidunt vim dictorum Scripturæ de nativitate, pas- sione, ac morte Filii Dei: partim Piscatoriana Synec- doche eadem ad solam humanam naturam restrin- gunt; partim identicas propositiones ex iisdem faci- unt, ut tandem nihil κοινωνίας relinquatur: ad hæc majestatem carni Christi communicatam, adeoq; vim vivificandi, & ἐνέργειαν, quoad carnem, pro mundi vita datam Job. VI. 51. evertunt, eaque ratione tum communionem mutuam naturarum, tum idiomatum communicationem, tum ἐνεργημάτων in actibus of- ficii, & ἐνεργείαις θεανδρικαῖς cooperationem op- pugnant, quin & unionem personalem more Ne- storiano, tollunt; ne de eo quod Calvinianum exina- nitionem & exaltationem Christi secūdum utram- que naturam factam contendant, quoque Stancari- smo Jesuitæ valde affines sint; utque Calviniani me- riti & satisfactionis Christi particularitatem, ad solos absolute electos restrictam, & impletionis legis a Chri- sto pro nobis factæ negationem a Piscatore, ac ple- risque aliis Calvinianis electam, quæ duo posteriora φορτικὰ ἀκούσματα officium Christi Mediatorium, & Sacerdotale concernunt, silentio jam involvam. Ita vero obtenebrari Christum, solem justitiæ, tum qua personam, & suppositum, tum qua officium, & Ponti- ficium, & Regium, ecquis dubitaret? Idq; cum morsu & manducatione adversus veritatem a nobis ad- sertam fieri, scripta τῶν ἐξ ἐναντίας publica testan- tur: fieri etiam cum blasphemia adversus orthodo- xos, proprie & vere Catholicos, nec non adversus ipsummet Christum Jesum θεάνθρωπον, quos nul- lam de his agere pœnitentiam in propatulo, & quod ajunt, in ipso solis disco positum est. Dicun- tur autem illi impuri Spiritus procedere in Reges to- tius terræ, quia Jesuitæ & Monachi, ac Papistæ, & Sa- crificuli alii, Nuncii imprimis Apostolici, Cardinales, & Confessionarii maxime summa pollent in aulis Imperatorum & Regum Catholicorum, quos vo- cant, necnon in magnis Rebuspubl. autoritate: ad quorum nutum & consilio magnam partem illæ di- riguntur: quæ vero imprimis directa sunt, si non unice, ad regni Christi destructionem, Anti-Christiani propagationem, & Religionis Romano-Catholicæ, etsi cum concussione totius terrarum orbis, per univer- sum mundum disseminationem. De quo locuples rerum experientia aliunde testatur, cum omnium piorum gemitu, & lachrymis ac detestatione.

Jam ergo sexto quod ad illum Angelum, a quo præparatio fit ad transitum per Euphratem, per effu- sionem sextæ phialæ, ut Regibus vadosus ille eva- dat, & via pateat illis, qui ab ortu solis veniunt, quæ phrasis videtur inferre locum & terminum a quo, & literalem sensum confirmare. Quam explicationem arbitrio lectorum, & scrutatorum S. literarum pio- rum, atque eruditorum merito relinquimus. Ante complementum enim vaticinium raro solet esse a- pertum. Quum autem hæc jam ab eventu compro- bata sint, quæ diximus dubitandum non est, in pro- pinquo esse congregationem istam Regum terræ Ro- mano-Catholicorum, & transitum per magnum il- lum fluvium Euphratem, in die illo expectandum, quem Deus omnipotens in arcanis judiciorum suorum definivit: Idcirco ad vigilantiam, & vestium, quibus tegantur pudenda nuditatis nostræ, Sacerdo- tum talium, nempe, ac nuptialium, arctiorem custodiam ab ipsomet Christo, uti Apoc. II. III. XIV. XXII. fa- ctum, excitamur: idque voce de cœlo sonante, ut ab omnibus exaudiatur. Quod misericordiæ & longa- nimitatis ejus gratiosissimæ officium, ac beneficium mente grata omnino acceptandum, Rom. II. 4.

De signis vero & miraculis, quibus Anti-Christus, ejusq; sodales & satellites, atq; emissarii sese osten- tant, dictum est ad Matth. XXIV. 23. 2. Thess. II. 9. Quæ coaxationi ranarum harum mysticarum acci- dere, ac conjuncta esse solere, vel e 2. Thess. II. 3. patet.

Locus autem congregationis, cur Harmageddon dictus sit, non adeo est obvium, ideoq; operose dis- quirunt de eo interpretes. Non autem dicam, quod Aretas habeat ἑρμαγεδὼν, hoc enim παρόραμα est. Magis placet B. Lutheri explicatio: Damnati mili- tes, maledicti exercitus, infelices bellatores, quæ etiam B. D. Gravio probata in tabulis Apocal. fuit. Legit enim Chorma-Gedon, quod est infausta & execran- da Liga, seu confœderatio, quam ad Ligam Hispani- cam non male refert Gravius, ad exscindendos he- reticos, quos vocant, constructam & colligatam, & ad ultimum (utinam vero ultimum id fuisset) bellum Ligisticum confœderatam: & respectum haberi vult ad Horma civitatem tribus Simeonis, ad quam Israë- litæ Cananæos primum execrati sunt. Num. XXI. 3. Quo de ad c. XIX. 11. seq. ὁ μακαρίτης Tab. XLVII. p. 73. designavit: Occasionem desolationis Babylo- nis, & destructionis seu labefactationis Regni Anti- Christiani variis in locis quam ægerrime ferentes Pon- tificii, cumprimis Rana Jesuitica, extrema tentabunt, auxilium Regum & Magnatum implorabunt, eos- que congregabunt in bellum diei illius magni Dei omnipotentis Apoc. XVI. 14. Non enim desolata & exusta Roma, aut totum Anti-Christi Regnum uno impetu destruetur, & in nihilum redigetur, (est enim hoc contra expressum textum, 2. Thess. II. 8. quem Dominus conficiet Spiritu oris sui, & abolebit claritate adventus sui) sed permanebunt reliquiæ non exiguæ in Pontificiorum Regionibus, & ipse Pontifex vel in Hispania vel Sicilia, Sardinia, Ba- learibus, vel aliis terris, superstitioni Anti-Christia- næ adhuc addictis sedem collocabit, & Christum, quantum in ipso erit, oppugnabit, donec tandem in ultimo bello a Jesuitis concitato, a Christo supre- mo Ecclesiæ duce, ejusque exercitu superatus fue- rit, & plane corruat universa ipsius Monarchia, in Harmageddon. Per bestiam bicornem idem singulari explicatione Hispanum, cum suis confœderatis, h. e Regibus terræ, Principibus & Dynastis Pontificiis, ad Ligam Hispanicam, vel similem aliquam noviter ineundam pertinentibus intelligit: sed rectius illa conspiratio generalius extenditur ad omnes in de- structionem regni Christi conspirantes. Pseudo-Pro- phetam interpretatur de ordine Lojolitarum: verius autem comprehenduntur simul alii ordines Mona- chorum, cæterique Papistæ, Anti-Christi Romani mancipia, Satellites, Creaturæ, & propugnatores, quos jam diximus. Conspirant n. hi omnes in per- niciem Ecclesiæ Catholicæ. Nec alio sensu hæc triga est accipienda c. XIX. 20. Refert etiam huc termi- num alligati Draconis: quem uti quoad initium alli- gationis non cum aliis ad initium prædicationis Evangelii per totum orbem, annum scil. Christi LXX. (hoc enim initium ipse assignavit) nec ad vi- ctorias Constantini M. quæ sententia plurium est, nec ad ann. C. 300. quo Gog & Magog, h. e. Imperium Turcicum in familia Ottomannica, nec cum B. D. Nicolai ad ann. Christi 521. quo Justin. Imperat. ad- monitus ab Hormisda P. R. exterminationem Arianizantium, Nestorianorum, Eutychianorum, Monotheletarum &c. susceperit, refert B. D. G. quod postremum initium non ad distinctionem facit, ideoque merito negligitur; verum ad propa- gationem regni Christi: finem vero in ann. Chr. 1521. quo Mahometurientes sectæ liberari a vinculis An- geli clavigeri, h. e. Papæ Romani cœperunt. Verum enim vero quum Pontifex Romanus nuspiam in Scripturis claviger dicatur, etsi semetipsum clavige- rum κατ' ἐξοχὴν constituat, abysso vero infernali non ipse, olim in eundem finaliter præcipitandus, sed Draco infernalis, & serpens ille antiquus cap. IX. 1. constituatur: Initium autem alligationis Sa- tanæ fecerit D. G. annum 401. quo Attila Hunno- rum Rex, postquam ingenti exercitu imperium, tam Orientale, quam Occidentale tyrannice, ac cru- deliter vexasset, in Galliis solis in campis Catalau- nicis, insigni clade desideratis ex prælio centum & nonaginta millibus Hunnorum, reliquos exercitus in Pannoniam induxit, recollectis viribus Ann. 453. Italiam ingressus Romæ dira minatus est: sed Leo- nis P. R. intercessione placatus discessit: unde ter- minum hujus millenarii nonnulli an. 1453. quibus accedit B. D. G. constituunt, quo Gog seu Turca re- cuperatis viribus Constantinopolin expugnavit, & totius Orientis Imperium Christianis ademit, adeoque ita de novo viam sibi patefecit, montes Israëlis infestandi, donec ipse etiam aliquando in montibus Israëlis conficiatur. Locum stragis Har- mageddon ipse explicat de loco aliquo ad mare Bal- thicum, & στοχαστικῶς assignat inter Lubecam & Hamburgum. Eadem de Etymo vocis Ebrææ Dru- sio sedit sententia, quod scilicet composita sit ex חרמ excidio, & גדוהן exercitus eorum: quam alii malunt compositam statuere ex duabus Hebraicis הר מגדו mons Megiddonis, qui locus a lugubri Jo- siæ Regis clade celebris est 2. Reg. XXIII. 29. quæ duæ posteriores sententiæ nobis præ aliis proban- tur, etsi ultimam præfert B. Gerhardus. Qui per be- stiam regnum Anti-Christianum, id est, non uti nos imperium Romanum, prout adminiculatur Romano Anti-Christo, sed ipsummet Romanum Anti-Chri- stum, caput scil. regni Anti-Christiani, una cum Car- dinalibus, Episcopis, & Præsulibus intelligit. Spiritus autem similes ranis dici vult, quod obstrepent veris Ecclesiæ Doctoribus, ac coaxatione sua molesti sint, imo calumniis etiam adversus confessores Ev- angelii Proceres Pontificios inflamment.

Septimus denique Angelus phialam εἰς τὸν ἀέρα in aërem effusurus dicitur, non quod per artes Ma- gicas, cum Diabolo aëris Principe Eph. VI. 12. pa- ctum initurus sit Anti-Christus Romanus, uti ὁ μα- καρίτης, insignis ille Theologus, B. Gerhardus cre- didit: multo minus vero credendum, quod hic B. Gravio visum, quod complementum illius visionis in GUSTAVI ADOLPHI, Suecorum Regis Glo- riosissimæ recordationis, victoriis adversus Ligistas gloriosissimis quærendum sit: sed uti idem B. Ger- hardus rectius interpretatur, in finali destructione, ac interitu regni Anti-Christiani, quæ ventura est, cum Deus per tonitrua, fulgura & fulmina ὀρανόθεν sub finem mundi destructurus est, ut corruat urbs illa magna c. XIV. 8. 9. c. XVII. 18. una cum omnibus incolis, supremæ, mediæ, & infimæ conditionis ho- minibus. Quam distinctionem alii ad dissensiones πανωλεθρίᾳ isti præcedaneas, in statu Ecclesiastico, Politico, & Oeconomico referunt: B. Gravius ab aliis ad tria genera Religionum, Anti-Christianos nem- pe Christianos, & Neutrales referri, alii vero ad tres illas sectas primarias, Lutheranam, Pontificiam, & Calvinianam reducere observat, ipse vero, in pro- priæ sententiæ explicatione, monet, divisam dici Babylonem in tres partes, ita tamen, ut manferit Babylon: Lutheranos autem & Calvinistas non am- plius esse in Babylone, sed exiisse, nec ejus partes, sed infensissimos adversarios & hostes esse, ideoq; mavult intelligere dissensiones inter ipsos Reges & Principes in regno Pontificio ortas. Sed quum Baby- lon exscindenda prædicatur hic, & totaliter & fina- liter, illis utique distributionibus non erit locus. Ideoque præstat cum aliis hæc referre ad Reges & Babylonem, Romam & Anti-Christum Romanum deserentes, qui evadunt hostes ejusdem, & expu- gnatores. Quæ ejus excisio non tantum temporalis, sed æterna etiam hic præfiguratur, ut e c. XIX. & XX. imprimis intelligere est. Unde Apoc. XIIX. Bertho in Alleg. hanc tradidit sententiam : Quando Ange- lus (Christus) projecerit in peccatores lapidem mola- rem (duram sententiam, & pondus æternæ damna- tionis, quæ ipsos in inferno conteret) tunc Babylon (congregatio impiorum) impetuosè ac cito mittetur in infernum, ubi non erit vox cytharæ (lætitiæ alicujus canoræ) nec vox molæ (panis delicatus, ac delecta- mentum alicujus saporis) nec vox sponsi, (conjunctio alicujus amoris) Jer. LI. 64. nec lux lucernæ (limpi- tudo alicujus splendoris) Phrasis de Cytharæ voce deprompta videtur ex Es. XXIV. 8. Jer. VII. 34. XXV. 10. Ezech. XXVI. 13. de voce sponsæ e Jer. VII. 34. XVI. 9. XXV. 10. XXXIII. 11. Poculi ira divina men- tio fit Es. LII. 22. 28. Jer. XXV. 15. Per grandinem no- tatur pondus iræ divinæ, cum respectu ad Exod. IX. 22. & Jos. X. 11. Per poculum aureum nonnulli pocu- lum missaticum intelligunt ex Apoc. XVII. 14.

Exustionem autem Babylonis, vel Romæ corporalem plerique designari recte judicant, cum & συνέχεια & peraphrases textus, & εἱρμῷ τῆς ἀκολουθείας c. XVIII. huic sensui faveant : Spiritualis vero exu- stio ministerio Ecclesiastico tribuenda sit, non ter- renis Regibus. Cæterum per Angelum Ap. XIIX. 1. conspectum nonnulli ipsummet Christum designa- tum volunt, plerique tamen alii insignem aliquem Doctorem intelligunt, quem peculiariter de B. Lu- thero Gerhardus & Gravius interpretantur : utpote qui claritate doctrinæ Evangelicæ totum fere orbem colillustravit 2. Cor. IV. 6. quem etiam B. Gerhardus c. XXI. 1. clavigerum Angelum, Draconis colligato- rem futurum hic prædictum censuit, annuentibus Paraphrastis Vinariensibus, etsi B. Osiander videa- tur Angelo ministro favere. Sed hæc de cap. XVI.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII. ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The judgment of the whoredom of the woman sitting upon the beast is shown, highly adorned, holding a harlot's cup in her hand, of great Babylon, drunk with the blood of the martyrs, and her mystery is explained to the wondering John, what it was, and is no more, and what the seven heads denote, and the five which have fallen, the one which remains, and that which is to come, and what it will do, the battle with the Lamb, and what the waters are, and the victory of this one, and the burning of the conquered Babylon.

There are two parts: I. The explanation of the mystery of the harlot woman to verse 13. II. The excision of Babylon conquered by the Lamb to verse 18.

PART I. EXPLANATION OF THE MYSTERY OF THE HARLOT WOMAN.

Vers. 1. Καὶ ἦλθεν) At another time. In the Manuscript: Ἐξῆλθεν.

But why at another time? The Angel had once said that John saw this ἀποκάλυψιν on the Lord's Day, nor did he designate any other time anywhere. Therefore, one must adhere to the same time. What scripture joins, it is not for us to separate. But that this chapter with the following ones ... was in the hands of a few, whence will Grotius prove it? They were without doubt joined, not separated: because, as we have said, they were exhibited together, and seen on the same day: nor could they be separated conveniently enough, because they mutually illustrate each other in several respects.

Εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ Ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας) The seventh is about to explain more clearly and fully those things which he had briefly said concerning the ruin of Rome. Therefore I think this chapter and the following ones were in the hands of few: and hence it happened that the Apocalypse was less known to the common people.

Who that one Angel is, is not certain. Franc. Ribera conjectures that he was the first among the seven, Thomas Brightman the fifth, Emser the sixth; but the former opinion agrees with the Hebrew custom of speaking, by which one is said for first, concerning the first Angel, who namely had poured out the first vial; or certainly the seventh, who was named most recently, is to be understood, whose plague and judgment is now more fully explained.

Καὶ ἐλάλησε μετ’ ἐμῦ) As a friend with a friend.

Λέγων Δεῦρο) δεῦρο is the same as ὕπαγε above X. 8. Come hither.

Δείξω σοι τὸ κρίμα τῆς πόρνης τῆς μεγάλης τῆς καθημένης ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων τῶν πολλῶν) I will show you both that beast of the sea from whence it is ruled, and what that Babylon is of which I spoke, and in what ways God is about to exercise his judgments upon it. Πόρνη is the same as Babylon before, as appears below 31, 45. Roman dominion, just as Babylonian dominion is described in the likeness of a woman in Isa. XLVII. 1. Πόρνη, however, because of manifold idolatry. See Isa. I. 21. Mic. I. 7. Nah. III. 4. and what is above XIV. 4. She sits upon many waters, because she rules both the sea and the rivers, that is, the people, who are at Rome, and who are in other cities. See below 15. above XVI. 3. 4. But the words are taken from Jer. LI. 13. where in the Greek it is κατασκη- νῶσας ἐφ’ ὕδασι πολλοῖς.

From whence the beast is ruled is not contained in these words δείξω σοι, as if it were handed down in the explanation. Therefore it was not to be investigated by a paraphrase of these words. The word δείξω, from the usage of Xenophon, Demosthenes, Thucydides, and the Holy Spirit himself in John V. 32, 2 Cor. XII. 31, implies to bring into the theater, to show ocularly, to make manifest, to the contemplation of which St. John is invited. But the harlot is shown not to be a common prostitute, but a truly great one, with whom spiritual fornication, that is, idolatry, has been practiced, concerning which Jud. II. 17, ch. IIX. 27, 1 Par. V. 25, 2 Par. XXI. 13, Ps. LXXII. 27, Ps. CV. 39, Jer. III. 1, 5, Ezek. VI. 9, Hos. IV. 10, etc. Under the name of the Babylonian harlot comes the Pope, because he is presented like a woman and a city. Which name suits him both because of bodily fornication, by which not a few of them have become notorious. Sergius III., whom Marozia, a most noble harlot, had as the Prince of her lovers: at which time the Pontiffs securely observed their pleasures, as Platina expressly noted on John XIII; John XIII, who was struck down in adultery, by the testimony of the same Platina; Benedict IX; Gregory VII, who used Mechtilde familiarly; Clement VII, who is called a public fornicator by Urspergensis; John XXII, condemned at the Council of Constance because he had committed incest with his brother's wife and with nuns, rape with virgins, adultery with married women, and other crimes of incontinence. See the Appendix to the Council of Constance. Sixtus IV was entirely infamous on account of pimping and most nefarious lusts. Concerning Innocent VIII, these verses are circulated:

Octavius begat eight boys, and as many girls; Rome may deservedly call this man Father. Filth, gluttony, avarice, and sloth, Octavius, lie buried in this tomb in which you are covered.

Nor were the beastly lusts of Leo X unknown, what do I say? they were most known to the whole world. Yet Paul II is read to have surpassed all the Pontiffs in his filthiness, inasmuch as, having been raised to the Cardinal dignity by Alexander VI after selling his sister, he committed various rapes, adulteries, and incests, took away the husband of his daughter by poison so that he might possess her alone, and was caught in the bed of his niece Laria and received a severe wound, etc. In Rome alone at the time of the Council of Trent there were found over 24,080 harlots. How many shall we believe were found then throughout all of Italy, how many lay hidden there? But if only those come into the census, the Roman Pontiff is nevertheless held to render an account for them, who tolerated the same.

Furthermore, she is also described by πορνείᾳ because of spiritual fornication, which we judge is properly looked to here, lest we have need to attribute a double meaning to the same word, proper and improper, which in our judgment is ἄτοπον. Nor yet do we doubt that the present metaphorical appellation was used by the Holy Spirit because He foresaw with how many acts of whoredom and foul impurities this seat would be infamous, even those properly so called, from which therefore it pleased Him to derive the cause of that similarity when He named the Babylonian harlot.

Under the name of the harlot comes he who in 2 Thess. II, 3 is called the son of perdition, namely that great Anti-Christ, because he entices innumerable peoples to spiritual whoredom by his harlot-like pimping, and offers them the cup of fornication, and has been especially famous for vices proper to this sex: virulence, fury, anger, machinations, deceit, splendor, luxury, and lasciviousness: not to mention that the Holy Spirit foresaw that Joanna VIII would occupy the Papal throne, which, when Papists deny today, they deny most impudently, and act just as if they would deny that the sun shines at midday. Don Piero de Maxia described the history in the Iberian language and dedicated it to Charles V, and both chroniclers and historians have testified to the truth of the matter: Anastasius, almost a contemporary of Joanna, Radulphus Flaviacensis, Marianus Scotus, a Benedictine monk, circa the year of Christ 1086, in book III, age 6, to the year 854. and who was prior to them in reporting this history, as also to most who follow these. Sigebert, Abbot of Gembloux (c. year 1111) in Chron. 854. Radulphus Havieci A. 1157. Geoffrey Arthur, Bishop of St. Asaph A. 1160. Otto of Freising, book VII of Chron. (c. year 1161). Godfrey of Viterbo (c. year 1282). Penitentiary of the Roman Pontiff Nicholas III, Archbishop of Cosenza. Robertus Gallus c. year 1290. John of Paris A. 1290. William of Ockham c. 124, work 90 days (year 1320). Bernard Gui, Bishop of Lodève, year 1331. Martin the Minorite in Chron. A. 1330, where it is reported that Joanna, adjuring a certain demoniac as to when he would depart, replied: Pope, Father of fathers, reveal the birth of the Popess, And then I will tell you when I shall depart from the body. Ranulph in Polychron. book V, ch. 32, year 1360. Ranulph Higden of Chester, year 1363. Fr. Petrarch, Italian Chron., year 1374. Joh. Baracius de Clar. mulier. ch. 99, A. 1378. John Huss de Eccl. ch. 7, A. 1400. Chron. Constant. A. 1400. John of Marcoville, a Frenchman, de bon. & mal. sex. fœmin. year 1410. Theodoric of Niem, secretary to the Roman Pontiff, year 1446. Matteo Palmieri of Florence, Chron. year 1449. Antoninus, Archbishop of Florence, vol. 16, part 2, ch. 1, year 1457. Platina de vit. Pontif. year 1460. Chronological compilation, year 1470. Guilb. Brevius de sept. Princip. Eccles. 1617. German Chron. of Augsburg, reprinted year 1487. Rodrigo Sánchez, Bishop of Palencia, year 1464. Battista Fregoso, year 1483. Old Chronicle of Ulm, printed year 1486. William Jacobi, monk of Eemstein, de vit. Pontif. year 1440. Aeneas Sylvius, VI M. æt. A. 1493 (afterwards Roman Pontiff, called Pius II). Werner Rolfinck in fascic. tempor. year 1494. Abbot Trithemius in Chron. Hirschaug. year 1495. Marcus Antonius Coccius Sabellicus, Ennead 9, book 1, A. 1495. Joh. Marius the Belgian, book de schism. A. 1498. Albert Krantz, Chron. 1500. Nuremberg Chronicle of Hartmann Schedel. Johannes Baptista Mantuanus A. 1500, book II, Topoth. Tartar. Hermann Ædituus, book II, part 2, A. 1500. Stephanus Blanck of Passau to Alexander VI. On the miracles of Rome, A.D. 1500. Joh. Nauclerus, Chronicle, A.D. 1500. Jac. Philipp. Bergomensis, Supplement to the Chronicle, A.D. 1503. Joh. Stella in the lives, 230. R. P. Franc. Picus Mirandulanus on faith and the order of belief. Raphael Volaterranus, A.D. 1500, in the Commentaries. The Burden of the Church, year 1517. Joh. Trithemius, A.D. 1517. Joh. Lasiardus, A.D. 1517. Joh. Nevizanus of Asti, Bishop, at the same time, Joh. Bishop of Chemens, likewise a contemporary, Nicolaus Ægidius at the same time, Author of the Burden of the Church, ch. XIX, A.D. 1517. Annals of Aquitaine. Johann. Ravisius Textor. Johan. Heraldus the Gaul on the state of the Church, A.D. 1518. Corn. Agrippa on the nobility of the female sex, A.D. 1520. History of famous women, A.D. 1520. Roman Book of Indulgences, A.D. 1525. Richardus Wasseburg of Verdun in the Chronicle of Austria, A.D. 1527. The Childbirth of the Pope, A.D. 1530. Bernhardus Girardus, Historiographer of the Kingdom of France, A.D. 1530. Dominic. Jacobatius, Cardinal, book IX, on councils, art. 9, n. 6, 7, A.D. 1530. Valerius Anshelmus in the Chronicle, 1530. Paulus Constantinus Phrygio in the Chronicle, 1534. F. Amandus Ziriczœus, Chronicle, A.D. 1534. Achilles Gassarvs, Chronicle, A.D. 1538. Christian. Massæus, Chronicle, 1540. Ludov. Cælius Rhodiginus, Italian, Vol. 4, art. sect., A.D. 1540. M. Guazzius in the Italian Chronicle, A.D. 1546. Valent. Münzerus, A.D. 1549. Leander Albertus, Dominican, A.D. 1550. Petrus Mexias, contemporary. Jacobus Curio in Chronology, A.D. 1558. Johan. Lucidus in the Venetian Chronicle, year 1575. Petrus Flandrus, A.D. 1593. Petrus Gregor. Tholosanus in the Synopsis of Law, book XV, ch. 3, n. 22. Alphonsus a Castro, book II, on the punishment of heretics. Dominicus a Soto, year 1560. Anton. Sabellicus in the Enneads IX. Malleolus of Zurich, contemporary of the Council of Basel, etc. Barthol. Caranza, Archbishop of Toledo, A.D. 1575. Johan. Turcius, notes on the Chronicle. Suffriedus Petri of Leeuwarden, A.D. 1580. Bernhardus Girardus Hullanus in the history of France, A.D. 1590. Petrus Pellojus, medical abuse, A.D. 1586. Hermann. Magistr. Rom. Joh. Nicolaus Selian, compendium of History. Claudius Falcet, Antiquities, book IX, ch. 96, A.D. 1610. Steph. Paschasius, contemporary, book III, disquisitions on the Franks, ch. 4. Joh. Pannonius, Bishop of Pécs, year 1500, Epigrams. Marullus, contemporary, in Innocent VIII. Added to these are the Saxon Chronicle cited by the Magdeburg Centuriators, by John Jewel, Sarifortus, the Chronicle of Chronicles, and Valerius Anshelmus, Ried, the Rhythmic book of Thomas Merton and Wilhelmus Menachus, and Joh. Baptista Ignatius, book VII, ch. 3, and from the Greeks, Laonicus Chalcocondylas, A.D. 1460, book VI, on Turkish affairs, and also Balaam Calaber, Bishop of Hieracium, A.D. 1303, book on the primacy of the Pope. Add also the manuscript German Chronicle of Jacobus de Regis curia, the Swiss Chronicle, the Chronicle of Kempten, the Annals of Augsburg, MS. Likewise public paintings and statues in the temple of Siena, Italian Itinerary, according to Antoninus, Steph. Blanck. Old fragment on the Roman Schools, Greek. Also Isengreen, Chronicle, A.D. 1564, edited by Döling, as also Petr. Paul. Vergerius, Bishop of Koper, in a separate book, and an anonymous writing, A.D. 1597, under this title: That the Jesuits falsely and in vain deny that Pope Joan VIII was a woman, in which most of these testimonies are read. One may also see here Joh. Wolffius in the Memorable Readings, Vol. I, cent. 9, p. 224. Assertion of the historical truth concerning Pope Joan VIII, C. Bellarmine and Baronius. Conradus Deckerus, Catalogue of the witnesses of the truth, book X, p. 1103. And these are almost all the historians, chronologists, theologians, jurists, bishops, archbishops, cardinals, who acknowledged Pope Joan the Englishwoman, who, born in the lands of Mainz, feigned a male sex and succeeded in the place of Leo IV, most of them Italian writers and sufficiently ancient, bordering on that region, if not contemporaries; to whom those born yesterday or the day before are opposed in vain: Onuphrius Panvinius, A.D. 1568, Michaël Bachingerus, A.D. 1534, Joh. Thurmar, A.D. 1550, Thomas Hardingus, Nic. Sanderus and Alcangcopus, as also Gilbertus Genebrardus, Papirius Massonus, Arnoldus, Pontanus, Florimundus, Raimundus, or Ludov. Rocheonius, Possevinus, Suertius, which are to be opposed to Cardinal Baronius, Cardinal Bellarmine, etc., and most recently to David Blondellus, Professor of History at the Amsterdam School, who was not indeed occupied with this subject to the honor of the Dutch. Whence Samuel Maresius rightly opposed to him the destitute Pope Joan, whose examination of the question concerning the female Pope deserves to be read entirely.

Nor are we indeed the first who say that Rome is that Babylonian harlot; it was done by many, and indeed in the middle of the Papacy. Some in England proclaimed her such as early as A.D. 969, as Matthew Paris observes, book IV, History. Honorius of Autun, in a dialogue at the end of Vol. II of the Supplement to the Library of the Fathers, Paris edition, A.D. 610, did not hesitate to apply the prophecies of the Apocalypse concerning the beast and Babylon to the Roman Pontiff and the Roman Court. Around the year 1130, Bernard, a monk of Cluny, in a certain satire, called the Roman Pontiff the King of Babylon. In the year 1160, the Waldenses, otherwise called the Poor of Lyon, declared that the Roman Pontiff was the Babylonian harlot, as Coccius admits, book 7, thesis, art. 9. Around the year 1240, many not only in Germany, France, and England, but even in Italy itself, taught that Rome is Babylon and that great harlot: Gerhardus Sagarelli of Parma and Dulcinus of Navarre also named her so about 250 years ago. According to Coccius, Vol. I, thesaurus, book 7, art. 6, p. 826, around the year of Christ 1252, and around the year 1288, Petrus Joh. Bittaccensis, a Minorite of Aquitaine, according to Bernh. Lützelburg in the Catalogue of Heretics, and Guidon. Perpinianus on heresies, and the Code of Coccius, Vol. I, book 7, art. 17. Ubertinus de Casali, a Minorite, A.D. 1308, often cited by the author of the Burden of the Church in his book on the seven states of the Church. Michaël Cesenas, General of the Minorites, A.D. 1523, on the tyranny and pride of the Roman Pontiff. Johannes de Rupescissa, a Franciscan, A.D. 1349. Havabalus, a Minorite monk, according to the testimony of Henr. de Erphordia, around the year of Christ 1345. Gregorius Heimburg on the Primacy of the Pope, A.D. 1434. Nicolaus Cusanus, Cardinal, 1494. Add to these the golden mirror of the year 1404. Add especially the confession of Francisco Ribera, who understands Rome not as it once was under the pagan Emperors, but as it is to be at the end of the world, with which Viega agrees in chapter 17 of the Apocalypse. For 1. That old and pagan Rome was not the Queen of the kings of the American earth; certainly it could not administer justice, nor could it command other lands which it had not yet subjugated. 2. It was not apostate from Christ: for it had never given its name to Him. 3. It did not win lovers for itself by a love potion, but made subjects by the sword. 4. Its persecution was not a mystery, but a matter all too open. 5. Therefore that Babylon is marked by John which has the name mystery inscribed on its forehead. But the city, as it was defiled by wicked morals and contaminated by pagan idolatry, did not have the name of mystery inscribed. These were not mysteries, but public and notorious βδελύγματα. 6. Nor is it without mystery that this name MYSTERY was once inscribed in diamond letters on the Papal tiara: concerning which see Scaliger, in his notes to the New Testament. Vignorius, for the sake of confirming this matter, in part 2 of the Theater of the Anti-Christ, chapter 1, number 7, cites Jacobus Brocardus of Venice on the 17th of the Apocalypse and Franciscus Lemoine, a Celestinian monk, who publicly testified that he had seen it on the tiara of Clement VIII. Which was noted by the Belgian interpreters on 2 Thessalonians 4, namely that very many bear witness to it. 7. Nor was it destroyed by Kings, but as it began under Augustus, so it ended under Augustus. Therefore Cornelius acknowledges that these things are to be understood not of Rome as it once was, but as it is to be in the future at the end of the world when it will have fallen into heresy.

8. Whether the name of the beast is Τείταν or λατεῖνος, it does not fit Pagan Rome as it does the Papal and Anti-Christian one. For the Anti-Christian Beast did not claim for itself the name of the sun and dominion over the entire empire as Pagan Rome did, nor did it boast that it illuminated the whole world with the light of its doctrine, nor did it arrogate to itself the Papacy and universal episcopacy, nor did it order sacred rites to be performed in the Latin language, nor did it raise the Latin version of the Bibles to the pinnacle of Canonical authority, and for that reason reject the Hebrew text in the Old Testament and the Greek in the New from Canonical dignity: so much so that greater dignity has never been attributed to the LATIN language. Nor did Pagan Rome undertake to fight openly against the supreme Deity: but it is characteristic of the Papal one to wage war with Christ, whom it acknowledges as the highest God, and to cast Him down from His divine throne.

9. That Rome is understood which made all nations drunk with its cup. But this cannot be said of Pagan Rome: for this one rather imbibed idol-mania from others, and worshipped the gods and goddesses of all, even establishing by decree of the Senate that the wise man must worship all gods: concerning which Leo the Great, sermon 1 on Peter and Paul: 'But this city, ignorant of the Author of its perfection, while it ruled over almost all nations, served the errors of all nations, and seemed to itself to have assumed a great religion, because it rejected no falsehood.' Whose gross and overly manifest insanity against the V and VI commandments is rebuked in Rom. 1. 10. Nor indeed does Pagan Rome sit upon the ten-horned one, Apoc. XIII, that is, the Anti-Christ, which is the same as the scarlet beast full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns: as Alcazar and Suarez admit, 3rd part, Tom. II, disp. LIX, a. 6, sect. 2, and others. 11. Furthermore, that Pagan Rome at that time, when it persecuted the pious, felt that dignity which the Apocalypse attributes to Babylon, because the ten horns, which in the form of provinces had hitherto been subject to the Roman empire, and thus had not yet received a kingdom or proper Royal jurisdiction, and were designating future Kings, received in one hour all that power which the Kings had had with the beast, cannot be proven. Moreover 12. Pagan Rome did not follow, but preceded the Arian heresy and the impiety of Mahomet, and it pertains to the seals, not to the trumpets; much less to the seventh trumpet and the triple woe, which is to be feared by the Church from Rome. 3. The text speaks of one and the same Rome, which sinned, and which ought to sustain punishments. And who will admit that the holy city, which for 1300 years held up the torch of doctrine to the world, is to be overturned because of the crimes of those citizens who were already cast down to the infernal regions 1600 years ago. 14. Rome must be overturned from the foundations and reduced to eternal desolation. But no one would say that this happened to Pagan Rome. 15. That the seven vials designate the latest plagues of the world is beyond doubt. For the final judgment is connected with them. Unless it is contained in the pouring out of the seventh, insofar as it is to be exercised against the Romans. But the destruction of Rome, not the Pagan but the Papal one, pertains to the last vial, and is joined with the final judgment. 16. What, I ask, and where were signs and miracles of such a kind performed under ancient Rome, such as are predicted to be performed under the beast and the Babylonian harlot c. XIII. 12 17. What did St. John have to admire in the idol-mania and cruelty of ancient Rome, which he himself had experienced sufficiently in so many martyrs and in himself. 18. The seventh King had not yet come in John's time, much less the eighth, who is the same as the beast, and the Apocalyptic harlot v. 10. Concerning the Roman Pontiff. The blessed Phil. Nicolai, blessed Heilbrunner, blessed Cluver, Dürfeldt, Richter, Forbes, Cotter, along with Pareus, interpret the eighth king with us. Others, however, prefer to understand Urban VIII, just as Dölingius explains it as Mahomet, who was indeed the last King of the Turks by name, by which name one cannot understand Urban VIII, the Roman Pontiff: for he also had successors until now, and will have them in the future, without doubt, someone still exists. Therefore it is better to acquiesce to the more common interpretation of our people, the blessed D. Hoën, blessed D. Cluver, blessed D. Gerhard, blessed D. Gravius and others. 19. Gentile Rome has already ceased for 1300 years, and yet the Anti-Christ or the Babylonian harlot has not come. 20. That destruction which arises from the most grievous indignation of God is not to be taken as spiritual illumination except rashly and perversely. 21. The communion of which city is to be fled is set forth here; that its conversion is proposed in the same place cannot be established in any way.

The harlot therefore sitting upon many waters, that is, ruling over peoples, Ps. CX. 1. 1 Cor. XV. 25. is the beast itself, the Pontiff, or the Anti-Christ, ruling over various nations throughout the world, nay, the whole earth, and presuming to dominate.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII. ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Ostenditur judicium scortationis mulieris super bestiam sedentis, valde ornatæ, poculum me- retricium in manu habentis, Babylonis ma- gnæ, ebriæ sanguine martyrum, ejusque my- sterium admiranti Johanni exponitur, quod fuerit, nec sit amplius, & quid septem capi- ta notent, & quinque quæ deciderunt, unum quod superat, & quod venturum est, & quid acturum, pugna cum Agno, & quid aquæ, hujusque victoria, & devictæ Babylonis combustio.

Partes duæ sunt I. Mysterii mulieris scortatricis explicatio ad v. 13. II. Babylonis ab Agno devictæ excisio ad v. 18.

PARS I. MYSTERII MULIERIS SCORTATRICIS EXPLICATIO.

Vers. 1. Καὶ ἦλθεν) Alio tempore. In Manuscripto : Ἐξῆλθεν.

Cur vero alio tempore? In die Dominica Johan- nem vidisse hanc ἀποκάλυψιν semel dixerat Ange- lus, nec aliud tempus uspiam designavit. Eidem er- go tempori inhærendum. Quæ conjungit scriptura, nostrum non est separare. Hoc autem caput cum sequentibus ... paucorum manibus fuisse, unde do- cebit Grotius? Conjuncta sine dubio fuere, non separata: quia, ut diximus, conjunctim exhibita, & eadem die visa: nec commode satis separari pote- rant, quia mutuo se in plusculis illustrat.

Εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ Ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας) Septimus ea quæ de Romæ ruina breviter dixerat clarius fusiusque explicaturus. Ideo hoc caput & sequentia puto in paucorum fuisse manibus: & inde factum, ut Apoca- lypsis minus nota esset vulgo.

Quis Angelus ille unus sit, non constat. Primum inter septem fuisse, Franc. Ribera, quintum Thomas Brigthmannus, sextum Emserus conjectat; Ebrai- cæ a. loquendi consuetudini, qua unus pro primo dicitur sententia prior convenit, de Angelo primo, qui scilicet primam phialam effuderat; vel certe proxime nominatus septimus intelligendus, cujus plaga & judicium plenius jam explicatur.

Καὶ ἐλάλησε μετ’ ἐμῦ) Ut amicus cum amico.

Λέγων Δεῦρο) δεῦρο idem quod ὕπαγε supra X. 8. Adesdum.

Δείξω σοι τὸ κρίμα τῆς πόρνης τῆς μεγάλης τῆς καθημένης ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων τῶν πολλῶν) Ostendam tibi & bestia illa ma- ris unde regatur, & quæ sit illa Babylon de qua dixi, & quibus modis Deus sua in eam judicia sit exerciturus. Πόρνη est eadem quæ ante Babylon, ut apparet infra 31, 45. Ro- mana dominatio, sicut Babylonica dominatio mulieris spe- cie describitur apud Esa. XLVII. 1. Πόρνη autem ob multi- plicem idololatriam. Vide Esa. I. 21. Mich. I. 7. Nah. III. 4. & quæ supra XIV. 4. Sedet ea super aquas multas, quia im- perat & mari & fluminibus, id est, populo, qui Romæ est, & qui in aliis urbibus. Vide infra 15. supra XVI. 3. 4. Sunt autem verba sumpta de Jer. LI. 13. ubi in Græco est κατασκη- νῶσας ἐφ’ ὕδασι πολλοῖς.

Unde regatur bestia hisce verbis δείξω σοι non continetur, ut in explicatione id traditum sit. Non ergo id indagandum erat horum verborum para- phrasi. Verbum δείξω ex usu Xenophontis, Demo- sthenis Thucydidis & ipsius Spiritus Sancti Joh. V. 32. 2. Cor. XII. 31. infert in theatrum producere, ocula- riter monstrare, palam facere, ad cujus contempla- tionem invitatur S. Johannes. Meretrix autem ostenditur non obolaria, sed quadrantaria, vere magna, cum qua fornicatio spiritualis idololatria exercita, de qua Jud. II. 17. c. IIX. 27. 1. Par. V. 25. 2. Par. XXI. 13. Ps. LXXII. 27. Ps. CV. 39. Jer. III. 1. 5. Ezech. VI. 9. Os. IV. 10. &c. Meretricis Babylonicæ nomine venit Papa, quia instar fæminæ, & civitatis sistitur. Quod nomen ei convenit tum ob fornica- tionem corporalem, qua non pauci ex ipsis inclarue- runt. Sergius III. quam Marozia scortum nobilissi- mum, Amasiorum suorum Principem habuit: quo tempore Pontifices secure voluptates suas expresse observavit in Joh. XIII. Platina, Johannes XIII. qui in adulterio confossus fuit, eodem Platina teste, Be- nedictus IX. Gregorius VII. Mechtilde familiariter usus, Clemens VII. qui Urspergensi publicus fornica- tor dicitur, Johannes XXII. in Concilio Constan- tiensi condemnatus, quod cum uxore fratris sui, & cum monialibus incestum, cum virginibus stu- prum, cum conjugatis adulterium, & alia inconti- nentiæ crimina commisisset. Vide Append. Concil. Constant. Sixtus IV. propter lenocinium & libidi- nes nefandissimas totus erat infamis. De Innocen- tio IIX. hi circumferuntur versus:

Octo Nocens pueros genuit, totidemque puellas Hunc merito poterit dicere Roma Patrem. Spurcities, gula, avaritia atque ignavia defes, Hoc Octave jacent, quo tegeris tumulo.

Nec ignotæ, quid? notissimæ toti orbi fuere Leonis X. libidines belluinæ. Paulus tamen II. Pontifices omnes spurcitie sua superasse legitur, utpote qui divendita Alexandro VI. sorore sua ad Cardinali- tiam dignitatem evectus, varia stupra, adulteria, & incestus commisit, filiæ maritum veneno sustulit, ut ea solus potiretur, in cubili neptis Lariæ depre- hensus vulnus grave accepit. &c. In Roma sola tem- pore Concilii Tridentini inventa sunt ultra 24080. scorta. Quot credemus per totam Italiam inventa tum fuisse, quot latenter illic extitere? Sed si illa tantum in censum veniant, de iis tamen rationem reddere tenetur P. R. qui eadem toleravit.

Porro etiam a πορνείᾳ describitur ob spiritua- lem fornicationem, quam proprie hic respici cen- semus, ne eidem voci geminam significationem tri- buere opus habeamus, propriam & impropriam, quod nostro judicio ἄτοπον est. Neque tamen du- bitamus Metaphoricam appellationem præsentem ideo adhibitam a Spiritu S. fuisse, quod præviderit, quam multis scortationibus, & fœdis impuritatib9 infamis futura sit hæc sedes, etiam proprie dictis, a quibus proinde similitudinis istius causam derivare placuit, cum Babylonicam meretricem nuncupavit.

Meretricis nomine venit qui 2.Thess. II, 3. filius per- ditionis dictus est, Anti-Christus nempe ille Ma- gnus, quia meretriciis suis lenociniis innumeros populos ad scortationem spiritualem allicit, iisque poculum fornicationis propinat, vitiisq; huic sexui propriis imprimis claruit, virulentia, furore, ira, ma- chinationibus, fuco, splendore, luxu & lascivia: ne di- cam quod Spiritus S. præviderit Johannam IIX. thronum Papalem occupaturam, quod cum negant hodie Papistæ, impudentissime negant, & perinde faciunt ac si solem in meridie lucere inficientur. Neque vero nos primi sumus, qui Romam esse Babylonicam illam meretricem dicimus, factum id a pluribus, & sub medio quidem Papatu. Proclama- runt eam talem quidam in Anglia, jam A. 969. ob- servante Matthæo Parisiens. l. IV. Hist. Honorius Augustodunensis dial. ad calc. T. II. Auctar. Bibl. Patr. edit. Paris. A. 610. vaticinia Apocalypseos de bestia & Babylone P. R. & C. R. applicare non du- bitavit. Circa An. 1130. Bernhardus Monachus Clu- niacens. in Satyr. quadam P. R. vocavit Regem Ba- bylonis. Ann. 1160. Waldenses, alias Pauperes de Lugduno dicti Pontificem R. esse meretricem Ba- bylonicam dictitarunt fatente Coccino l. 7. thes. art. 9. Circa ann. 1240. multi non in Germania tantum Francia, & Anglia, sed in ipsa etiam Italia docue- runt Romam esse Babylonem & meretricem illam magnam: Nominavit ita eam etiam ante 250. circi- ter annos Gerhardus Sagarelli Parmensis, & Dulci- nus Navarensis. Gener. A. 1523. C. Tyran. & fastum. R. P. Johannes de Rupescissa Francisc. An. 1349. Havabalus Monachus Minorita teste Henr. de Erphord. circa ann. Christi 1345. Gregorius Heim- burg. de Prim. Pap. A. 1434. Nicolaus Cusanus Card. 1494. Adde his speculum aureum de A. 1404. Adde imprimis confessionem Franc. Riberæ, qui de Roma intelligit non qualis sub Ethnicis Imperatoribus olim fuit, sed qualis in fine mundi futura est, cui consonat Viega in c. XVII. Apoc. Nam 1. Roma ve- tus illa ac Ethnica non fuit Regina Regum terræ A- mericæ, utiq; jus dicere non potuit, nec aliis terris, quas nondum subjugarat imperare potuit. 2. Non fuit apostatica a Christo: huic enim nomen nun- quam dederat. 3. Non philtro amasios sibi concilia- vit, sed ferro subditos fecit. 4. Persecutio illius non fuit mysterium, sed res nimis quam aperta. 5. Illa itaq; Babylon notata est a Johanne, quæ in fronte inscriptum habet nomen mysterium. At non urbs prout scelestis inquinata moribus & idololatria contaminata Ethnica fuit, nomen mysterii inscri- ptum habuit. Hæc non erant mysteria, sed publica & notoria βδελύγματα. 6. Neque caret mysterio, quod hoc nomen MYSTERIUM literis Adaman- tinis tiaræ Pontificiæ olim inscriptum: quo de vid. Scaliger, notis ad N. T. Vignorius ejus rei confir- mandæ gratia part. II. Theatr. Anti-Christi c. 1. n. 7. adducit Jacob. Brocard. Venet. in XVII. Apocal. & Franciscum Lemoine Cælestini Monach. qui id se vidisse in tiara Clementis IIX. publice testatus est. Quod a Belgis Interpp. ad 2. Thess. IV. annotatum, nimirum plurimos de eo testimonium perhibere. 7. Nec a Regibus illa destructa fuit, sed ut in Augusto cœpit, ita in Augusto desiit. Ideo Corne- lius agnoscit, non de Roma, qualis olim fuit, sed qua- lis in fine mundi futura est in hærefin lapsura hæc in- telligenda esse.

8. Nomen bestiæ sive Τείταν sit, sive λατεῖνος non in Romam Ethnicam ita quadrat, ut in Papa- lem & Anti-Christianam. Bestia enim Anti-Chri- stiana non Roma Ethnica nomen solis & dominium in universum imperium sibi vindicavit, luce do- ctrinæ totum mundum sese illustrare per suos ja- ctavit, & Papatum atque ἐπισκοπὴν universalem sibi arrogavit, sacra fieri Latina lingua jussit, & La- tinam Bibliorum versionem in fastigium authentias Canonicæ evexit, ejusque causa Ebræum textum in Vet. & Græcum in N.Test. a dignitate Canonica rejecit: adeo ut LATINÆ linguæ major dignitas nunquam tributa sit. Neque Roma Ethnica insti- tuit cum supremo Numine aperto Marte pugnare: Papali autem id proprium est cum Christo, quem summum Deum agnoscit, præliari, eumque solio divino deturbare.

9. Illa intelligitur Roma, quæ poculo suo ine- briavit omnes gentes. Id vero de Roma Ethnica di- ci nequit: Hæc enim potius ab aliis imbibit idolo- maniam, ac omnium Deos Divosǫ; coluit, Senatus- consulto etiam statuens, Sapienti omnes Deos co- lendos: de qua Leo M. serm. I. de Petro & Paulo: Hæc autem civitas ignorans suæ perfectionis Auto- rem, cum pene omnibus dominaretur gentibus, omni- um gentium serviebat erroribus, & magnam videba- tur sibi assumpsisse religionem, quia nullam respuebat falsitatem. Cujus crassæ nimisque aperta insania contra V. & VI. præceptum reprehenditur Rom. I. 10. Neque vero Roma Ethnica insidet decicorni, Apoc. XIII. h.e. Anti-Christo, quæ eadem cum be- stia coccinea plena sermonibus blasphemiæ, habente septem capita & decem cornua: fatente Alcafare & Suarez 3. part. Tom. II. disp. LIX. a. 6. sect. 2. aliis. 11.
