Porro Ethnicam Romam illo tempore, quo per secuta est pios eam Dignitatem, quam Apocalypsis Babyloni tribuit, sensisse, quod decem cornua, quæ provinciarum forma hactenus Romano imperio subjecta, adeoque regnum seu propriam jurisdi- ctionem Regiam nondum acceperant, Regesque futuros designabant, acceperint una hora potesta- tem illam omnem, quam habuerant Reges cum be- stia, probari non potest. Adhæc 12. Ethnica Roma non sequuta est, sed antecessit hæresin Arianam & Mahometis impietatem, & ad sigilla pertinet, non ad tubas; nedum ad tubam septimam & trinum væ, quod Ecclesiæ a Roma metuendum. 3. Textus de una eademque Roma loquitur, quæ peccavit, & quæ pœnas sustinere debeat. Et quis admittet civi- tatem sanctam, quæ 1300. annis orbi terrarum fa- cem doctrinæ præluxit, propter eorum civium sce- lera everti, qui jam ante 1600. annos ad inferos de- trusi. 14. Roma funditus everti, & ad æternam vasti- tatem redigi debet. Id vero in Roma Ethnica fa- ctum nemo dixerit. 15. Septem phialis novissimas mundi plagas designari, dubio vacat. Cum illis enim connectitur extremum judicium. Si non se- ptimæ potius effusione id quatenus adversus Ro- manos exerendum est, comprehendatur. At Romæ non Ethnicæ sed Papalis excidium ad phialam ulti- mam pertinet, & cum extremo judicio conjuncta est. 16. Quænam obsecro, & ubinam signa & mira- cula ejusmodi sub Roma veteri edita, qualia sub bestia & meretrice Babylonica edenda prædicun- tur c. XIII. 12 17. Quid admirari habebat S. Johan- nes Romæ veteris idolomaniam & crudelitatem, quam ipse in tot martyribus & in semetipso satis expertus erat. 18. Nondum venerat septimus Rex Johannis tempore, nedum octavus, qui idem be- stia est, & meretrix Apocalyptica v. 10. De Pontif. Rom. Regem octavum nobiscum interpretan- tur B. Phil. Nicolai, B. Heilbrunnerus, B. Clu- verus, Dürfeldius, Richterus, Forbesius, Cotterius, cum Pareo. Alii tamen intelligere malunt Urba- num Octavum, utpote Dölingius explicat de Ma- homete, qui vero nomine ultimus Turcarum Rex fuit, quo nomine nec Urbanum intelligere licet IIX. Romanum Pontificem : nam & is Suc- cessores adhuc habuit, & porro habiturus, fine du- bio, aliquis adhuc est. Ideo præstat acquiescere communiori nostratium interpretationi B. D. Hoën, B. D. Cluveri, B. D. Gerhardi, B. D. Gravii & aliorum. 19. Desiit jam 1300. annis gentilis Ro- ma, nec tamen venit Anti-Christus vel meretrix Ba- bylonica. 20. Quod exitium ab indignatione Dei gravissima oritur, id de spirituali illuminatione non nisi temere ac perverse accipitur. 21. Cujus civita- tis communio fugienda hic sistitur; illius conversio- nem eodem loco proponi, nullo modo statui potest.

Meretrix itaque multis aquis, id est, populis insi- dens, vel imperans Psal. CX. 1. 1. Cor. XV. 25. est ipsa bestia, Pontifex, vel Anti-Christus Rom. variis gen- tibus per orbem, imo terræ universæ imperans, ac dominari præsumens.

## 17:2
With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication) They followed her authority and example, as above XII. 3. XIII. 14. Nay, they even worshipped her. Which very thing can also be understood by these words, as can be seen in Jer. 3, 9. Ezech. 16, 17. 23, 37.

And the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication) See above XIV. 8. and what is said there. There 'the nations', which here 'the earth', the whole complex as great as the Roman empire was. See also below XVIII. 3. Taken from Jeremiah LI. 7. where it treats of Babylon.

Roman Babylon poured into the cup of fornication another Savior to be offered daily, another righteousness founded on one's own works or the merits of the Saints, and satisfactions, other Mediators before God, other Mediatrices, other sacraments, vending other means and remedies of our salvation, the mass sacrifice as a panacea, in trades, pilgrimages, vows, contracts, marriages, grain, vintage, clear weather for the health of an Ass, and by that name it is said to serve the cup of spiritual fornication, etc. Now, how much money is collected through the intoxication of that golden cup for whoredom, and the baiting of minds hitherto practiced by this Papal Circe, can hardly be believed. The annates alone from the 32 Bishoprics of Germany mentioned in the Grievances of the German nation procure 119,533 florins for the Pontiff every year. In Spain, nine tons of gold and 61,600 florins are collected annually from the bishoprics. The palls of the bishops, of which 3,000 are counted at 600 tons of gold, are believed to enrich the chamber of the Roman Pontiff. What and how much will be collected from appeals to the Roman curia and from the toleration of concubines and brothels, from reserved cases, from indults, from the relaxation of penalties, from the confirmations of Emperors, Kings, and kingdoms, from solemn processions, from Jubilee years, from priesthoods which the Pope himself confers, from private masses, from the tax on the new Islands, from the revenues of the Teutonic order, from other indulgences, titles, and names, which, devised without number daily in the Papacy, by which purses are incredibly drained, so much so that the Roman Pontiff is judged to have acquired at the very least 366,084 millions of gold by his commerce up to the year of Christ 1609. From the mass alone, the annual proceeds are counted at one hundred tons of gold. Rightly, therefore, may Cardinal Benno exclaim here: Alas, how much the fable of the wheaten Christ has profited, which he impiously [said] of the true Christ. How they attempt to intoxicate the kings of the earth with this golden cup; it is to be read in Vincent of Beauvais, book 32 of the Speculum Historiale, chapter 19, who reports concerning John of Plano Carpini, legate of Innocent III, to Wafil, Duke of Russia, that he sought to have all the Bishops convened, and obtained the reading of the Pope's letters, so that they might submit themselves to the Roman Church, and he teaches how craftily they intoxicated the Russians. But it is recorded in chapter 20 that he attempted this in vain; since the Tartars answered the Papal Legate Asellinus manfully: With what face do you Christians dare to say that the Pope is greater in dignity than every man? For who has ever heard that your Pope has acquired for himself as many and as great kingdoms as the Son of God Cham, God granting this to him, has acquired? Finally, the Prince of the Tartars also handed over letters of this kind to be carried to the Pope: If you wish to sit upon our land, water, and patrimony, it is necessary that you, the Pope yourself, come in your own person, and approach him who holds the face of the whole earth. How they attempted to intoxicate the Emperor of the Turks with the same cup, and that by letters sent by Julius II after Constantinople was conquered, let the words of the Pope himself teach: He warned him to receive Baptism, adding what follows: If you do this, there will not be a Prince in the world who surpasses you in glory, or is able to equal you in power. We will call you Emperor of the Greeks and of the East, and what you now occupy by force, and hold with injury, you will possess by right. And just as our predecessors, Stephen, Adrian, Leo, summoned Pepin and Charlemagne against Aistulf and Desiderius, Kings of the Lombard nation, and, freed from the tyrannical hand, transferred the empire from the Greeks to the liberators themselves: so also we would use your patronage in the necessities of the Church, and would return the favor of the benefit received.

Latin:

Μεθ’ ἧς ἐπόρνευσαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς) Sequuti ejus auto- ritatem & exemplum, ut supra XII. 3. XIII. 14. Imo & ipsam adorarunt. Quod ipsum etiam his verbis intelligi potest, ut videre est Jer. 3, 9. Ezech. 16, 17. 23, 37.

Καὶ ἐμεθύσθησαν οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν γῆν ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς πορ- νείας αὐτῆς) Vide supra XIV. 8. & ibi dicta. Ibi τὰ ἔθνη, quod hic τὴν γῆν totum complexum quantus quantus erat imperii Romani. Vide & infra XVIII. 3. Sumptum de Jere- mia LI. 7. ubi de Babylone agitur.

Infudit Babylon Romana in poculum τῆς πορνεί- ας alium Salvatorem quotidie offerendum, aliam justitiam in propriis operibus vel Sanctorum meritis, & satisfactionibus fundatam, alios apud Deum Me- diatores, alias Mediatrices, alia sacramenta, alia sa- lutis nostræ media & remedia venditans, sacrificium missaticum pro panacæa, in mercaturis, peregrina- tionibus, votis, contractibus, matrimoniis, annona, vindemia, clemente aëre pro salute Asini, eoque no- mine poculum fornicationis spiritualis propinare dicitur &c. Jam quantum pecuniæ confletur per intoxicationem aurei istius poculi ad scortationem, mentiumque inescationem a Circe ista Papali hacte- nus exercitam, credi vix potest. Solæ annatæ ex 32. Germaniæ Episcopatibus in Gravaminib. nation. German. commemoratis quotannis Pontifici con- ciliant 119533. flor. In Hispania ex Episcopatibus quotannis colliguntur novem tonnæ auri & floreni 61600. pallia Episcoporum, quorum 3000. nume- rantur 600. tonnis auri, creduntur cameram Rom. Pontificis locupletare. Quid & quantum colligetur ex appellationibus ad Romanam curiam & toleran- tiis concubinarum & lupanarium e casibus reserva- tis, ex indultis, e pœnarum relaxationibus, e Casa- rum, Regum & regnorum confirmationibus, e pro- cessionibus solennibus, ex annis Jubilæis, e Sacerdo- tiis, quæ Papa ipsa confert, e missis privatis, e vecti- gali, enovis Insulis, e censibus ordinis Teutonici, ex indulgentiis aliis, titulis & nominibus, quæ sine nu- mero excogitata quotidie in Papatu, quibus incre- dibiliter loculi emunguntur, adeo, ut Pontifex R. sua mercatura usque ad ann. Christi 1609. ad mini- mum acquivisisse censeatur milliones auri 366084. E sola missa proventus annui numerantur centum tonnæ auri. Merito ergo hic exclamet Card. Benno : Hem quantum profuit fabula de Christo triticeo, quod impie ille de vero Christo. Quomodo po- culo hocce aureo inebriare conentur Reges terræ; a Vincentii Bellovisii l. 32. Spec. Histor. c. 19. lege- re est, qui de Legato Innocentii III. Johanne de Plano Carpi ad Wafilium Russiæ Ducem refert, quod convocari petierit omnes Episcopos, ac lite- ras Pontificis R. prælegi obtinuerit, ut sese Ecclesiæ Rom. subjicerent, docetque, quam vafre Russos in- ebriarint. Frustra autem id tentasse c. 20. comme- moratur; siquidem Legato Pontificio Asellino Tar- tari masculè responderint: Quâ fronte vos Christia- ni audetis dicere, quod Papa sit omni homine major dignitate. Quis enim unquam audivit, quod Papa vester tot & tanta regna sibi acquisiverit, quot & quanta Filius Dei Cham, Deo sibi hoc largiente, acqui- sivit? Tandem etiam Tartarorum Princeps ejus- modi literas ad Papam perferendas tradidit: Si vul- tis super terram nostram, aquam & patrimonium si- dere, oportet, ut Tu Papa ipse in personâ propriâ ve- nias, & ad eum, qui faciem totius terræ continet, ac- cedas. Quomodo tentarint eodem poculo Turca- rum Imperatorem inebriare, idque literis a Julio II. expugnatâ Constantinopoli missis, verba Papæ ipsius edoceant: Monuit, ut Baptismum susciperet, ad- dens, quæ sequuntur: Hoc si feceris, non erit in orbe Princeps, qui te gloriâ superet, aut æquare potentiâ valeat. Nos te Græcorum & Orientis Imperatorem appellabimus, & quod modo vi occupas, & cum in- juriâ tenes, possidebis jure. Et sicut nostri Antecesso- res, Stephanus, Adrianus, Leo, adversus Haistul- phum, & Desiderium gentis Longobardæ Reges Ro- pinum & Carolum M. accersiverunt, & liberati de manu Tyrannicâ imperium a Græcis ad ipsos libera- tores transtulerunt: ita & nos in Ecclesiæ necessitati- bus Tuo Patrocinio uteremur, & vicem redderemus accepti beneficii.

## 17:3
Vers. 3. And he carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness) Concerning the word in the spirit see above book 11. He saw the wilderness, so that he might understand that such would be the end of that populous city. See concerning Babylon Jer. ch. 13. 51. 63.

And I saw a woman sitting upon a scarlet beast) A scarlet beast, that is, dyed in scarlet, covered in scarlet: namely because the cloaks of the Roman Emperors were accustomed to be dyed with that color Plin. XXII. 2. Thus the shields of the Labisci are said to be painted. It signifies more clearly, therefore, concerning idolatry that he had dealt with others than the Roman above. A woman sat upon it, who is the Roman dominion, ruling idolatry and driving it where she wished. For there was an old decree that no one should be a God unless approved by the Senate. Tertullian is a witness in his Apologeticus.

The scarlet color corresponds to the blood-red, originating from the gore of the martyrs drunk by the beast. Purple was a fish of the shellfish kind, having in its throat a liquid of congealed blood, and imbued with the color of a blackish rose, concerning which Julius Pollux writes. But the kermes is a dyeing grain, rendering a color similar to purple, but with purple nevertheless excelling it. In the desert the Babylonian harlot was seen, scarlet, drunk with the blood of the martyrs, where the Church was sustained: For she sits in the Church in the temple of God, 2 Thess. II. 4. Primasius wishes the absence of Paradise to be designated, the Caesarean wishes the future devastation of the woman: Which are not opposed, even if the Church itself is by no means deserted by God in the desert. Apoc. XII. 6. 14. Harlots, says the blessed Gravius, for the most part seek solitary places, where they may practice the filthiness of their bodies. Thus this Babylonian harlot, alien from the fellowship of the true Church, practices spiritual whoredom, that is, idolomania, superstitions, and horrendous sins. Some understand by the Wilderness the Gentilism to which the Roman Papacy is conformable. But the Holy Spirit seems to hint that this whorish woman (who had previously driven the Church of Christ into the desert) is finally to be deserted by her worshippers. She is called a woman because of her lovers Isa. LXII. 4. 5. The heads of the beast, upon which she sits, reign over nations, tongues, and crowds, but the harlot reigns over the beast: because the Roman Pontiff rules over the Roman Papal empire, as such, that is, as sworn to him, or addicted and subject. The Anti-Christian kingdom, consisting mostly of the clergy, sits through its head, the Pontiff, upon the waters, or dominates the peoples: it commands even the heads themselves, Kings and Emperors, as they are subject to the Pontiff or Pope. And it is not denied except rashly by Ribera that this beast is the beast described in chapter XIII: For they agree entirely in origin, heads, horns, veneration, names, blasphemy, battle with the Saints, and other things, except that here she has the woman sitting upon her, because it is now explained more distinctly what kind of beast is understood, and that she is seen as scarlet here: since in the last centuries whoredom and drunkenness ought to appear more, which was done especially when it was brought into the open by Luther. For then it was intoxicated with bloody impiety and corruptions as if with blood, according to the interpretation of Primasius: just as the Dragon himself, by whom she is ruled, was seen red ch. XII. 3. So that I may pass over in silence the purple hats and scarlet cloaks, which he attributes to Cardinals and Bishops, to which the Holy Scriptures have without doubt looked in this metaphor. The right of creating Bishops, Archbishops, and Cardinals also rests with him, whom Bellarmine does not hesitate to equate to Kings, to whom he therefore attributes the symbol of royal honor, the scarlet and purple garment, even if these are distinguished in v. 4 and chapter XVIII. 16, since royal and cardinal dignities are entirely distinct. For they are similar honors, not the same. Kermes is a dyeing grain procuring a color almost similar to purple. For with the splendor of the true empire extinguished, the true purple is believed to have ceased. See Plin. book XXII. ch. 2. 1 Macc. X. 20. Cant. VII. 5. That Emperors are ordered to be in the place of a beast of burden is clear from the fact that the Roman Pontiff decrees that the Emperor hold the stirrup for him as he mounts: But if the Pope wishes to be carried in a chair, the Emperor should carry him on his shoulders book I. Cerem. Rom. sect. II. title order of procession: and also from the history of the Emperor Frederick Barbarossa. whom the Roman Pontiff ordered to seek pardon prostrate on the ground, and having fallen to his knees, he trampled his neck with his foot, with this proud acclamation: You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you shall trample the Lion and the Dragon.

Full of names of blasphemy) Full of Gods, who were so called to the injury of the true God. Names of blasphemy here are those who are called gods 1 Cor. VIII. 5. Concerning the word blasphemy see above XIII. 5.

By the cup of the harlot is understood the system of Papal doctrine, which like gold, on account of the pomp of ceremonies, shines in the eyes of the ignorant, but contains mere superstitions, Matt. XXIII. 25. 27. Which is especially evident concerning the mass-cup. Furthermore, that Rome is full of gods, as they were so called, is unknown to no one; holy angels are worshipped as gods, who sometimes were the worst of mortals, etc. Do not these things tend to the injury of the one true God? Therefore it is said to be full of names of blasphemy, which it vomits from its impious mouth, and sanctions with its decrees and bulls, such as have been designated heretofore. Clothed in purple and scarlet, as a Queen and adorned with gold, precious stone, and pearls with an entirely Royal adornment, which he who does not know the adornment of the Pontiff, when he wishes to present himself to be seen in his dignity, knows in the proper sense, and in the mystical: since indeed it carries before it the adornment of the bride described in Psalm XLV. and in the Solomonic canticle with pomp of words and boasting μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας, and for that reason allows itself to be described and honored, nay, rejoices.

Ἔχου κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ) Which have a double meaning both of Emperors, whom John had known from coins, and their faces were on these seven heads: and of the seven mountains or hills, on which no one was ignorant that Rome was situated.

And ten horns.) These ten horns in this vision signify ten Kings, who in the time of John were not yet in the faith and reverence of the Roman Empire. Let that be manifest below in 12 and the following.

These things will then be explained by the Angel in Verse 12, for which we reserve the same.

Latin:

Vers. 3. Καὶ ἀπήνεγκέ με εἰς ἔρημον ἐν πνεύματι) De voce ἐν πνεύματι vide supra l. 11. Vidit solitudinem, ut intellige- ret talem fore populosæ illius urbis exitum. Vide de Baby- lone Jer. L. 13. LI. 63.

Καὶ εἶδον γυναῖκα καθημένην ἐπὶ θηρίον κόκκινον) Cocci- neam feram, id est, coccinatam, coccino instratam: nimi- rum quia eo colore tingi solebant Imperatorum Romano- rum paludamenta Plin. XXII. 2. Sic dicuntur picti scuta Labisci. Clarius ergo significat de idololatriâ se alia quam Romana supra egisse. Ei insidebat mulier, quæ est Romana dominatio, idololatriam regens & qua vellet agitans. Erat enim decretum vetus, ne quis Deus esset, nisi a Senatu pro- batus. Testis in Apologetico Tertullianus.

Coccineus color respondet sanguineo, e cruore martyrum hausto a fera oriundo. Purpura erat pi- scis ex concharum genere, in faucibus liquorem ha- bens concreti sanguinis, & nigricantis rosæ colore im- butum, de quo Julius Pollux. Coccus vero granum tinctorium est, assimilem purpure colorem reddens, sed antecellente tamen ei purpura. In deserto visa meretrix Babylonica coccinea, cruore martyrum ebria, ubi Ecclesia sustentata: Nam in Ecclesia se- det in templo Domini, 2. Thess. II. 4. Primasius Para- disi absentiam, Cæsariensis vastationem mulieris futuram designari volunt: Quæ non opposita sunt, etsi in deserto Ecclesia ipsa minime a Deo deserta. Apoc. XII. 6. 14. Meretrices, inquit B. Gravius, loca ut plurimum quærunt solitaria, ubi fœditatem corpo- rum exerceant. Ita hæc meretrix Babylonica aliena a consortio veræ Ecclesiæ scortationem exercet spiritua- lem, hoc est idolomaniam, superstitiones & horrenda peccata. Quidam per Eremum intelligunt Gentilis- simum, cui conformis est Papatus Romanus. Sed vi- detur innuere Spiritus s. mulierem hanc fornicariam (quæ prius Ecclesiam Christi in desertum fugave- rat) a suis cultoribus tandem deserendam esse. Mu- lier vocatur ob amasios Esa. LXII. 4. 5. Bestiæ capita, quibus insidet, regnant gentibus, linguis & turbis, meretrix autem bestiæ: quia Pontifex Romanus imperio Romano Papali imperat, qua tali, hoc est, qua sibi jurato, vel addicto & obnoxio. Regnum Anti-Christianum ex clero maxime constans per caput Pontificem infidet aquis, vel dominatur po- pulis: imperat ipsis etiam capitibus, Regibus, & Im- peratoribus, qua Pontifici vel Papæ obnoxii sunt. Nec nisi temere negatur a Ribera, bestiam hanc esse feram cap. XIII. descriptam: Conveniunt enim ex asse ortus, capita, cornua, veneratio, nomina, blasphemia, prælium cum Sanctis & alia, nisi quod hic mulierem sibi habeat insidentem, quia distin- ctius jam explicatur, qualis fera intelligatur, quod- que coccinea hic conspiciatur: quum postremis se- culis scortatio, & ebrietas magis apparere debeat, quod imprimis factum ea per Lutherum in apri- cum producta. Tum enim impietate cruenta, & corruptionibus tanquam sanguinibus inebriata est, interprete Primasio: quemadmodum & Draco ipse, a quo illa regitur, ruffus est visus c. XII. 3. Ut purpureos galeros & paludamenta coccinea, quæ Cardinalibus, & Episcopis tribuit, ad quæ S. S. hac metaphora procul ambiguo respexit, silentio in- volvam. Penes ipsum quoque jus creandi est Epi- scopos, Archi-Episcopos, Cardinales, quos æquiparare Bellarminus Regibus non dubitat, qui- bus proinde tribuit Regii honoris symbolum, ve- stimentum coccineum purpureum geminum, etsi hæc v. 4. & cap. XIIX. 16. distinguantur, siquidem omnino distinctæ dignitates sint Regia, & Cardina- litia. Similes enim honores sunt, non iidem. Coc- cus granum tinctorium est fere similem colorem purpuræ concilians. Extincto enim veri imperii splendore purpura vera desiisse creditur. Vid. Plin. l. XXII. c. 2. 1. Macc. X. 20. Cant. VII. 5. Quod Impe- ratores jumenti loco esse jubeantur, ex eo liquet, quod Pontifex Romanus decernat, ut sibi ascen- denti equum Imperator scupham teneat: Si autem sella vehi velit Papa, humeris suis Imperator illum portet l. I. Cerem. Rom. sect. II. tit. ordo processio- nis: nec non ex historia Friderici Barbarossæ Im- perat. quem Pontifex Rom. jussit, humi prostratus veniam peteret, & ad genua devoluti collum pede conculcavit, cum hac superba acclamatione: Super aspidem & basiliscum ambulabis, & conculcabis Leonem & Draconem.

Γέμων ὀνομάτων βλασφημίας) Plena Diis, qui ita diceban- tur in veri Dei injuriam. Ὀνόματα βλασφημίας hic sunt οἱ λεγόμενοι l. Cor. VIII. 5. De voce βλασφημίας vide supra XIII. 5.

Per poculum meretricis intelligitur systema do- ctrinæ Papalis, quæ auri instar, ob ceremoniarum pompam in oculis imperitorum splendet, sed me- ras superstitiones continet, Matth. XXIII. 25. 27. Quod de poculo missatico præcipue constat. Cæ- terum quam plena Diis, qui ita dicebantur, Roma sit, nemini ignotum est; coluntur ut Dii Angeli sancti, qui quandoq; pessimi mortalium fuere &c. Annon hæc in unius veri Dei injuriam vergunt? Plena itaque dicitur nominibus blasphemiæ, quæ evo- mit ex ore impio, decretisque ac bullis suis sancit, qualia antehac designata sunt. Amicta purpura & coccino, ceu Regina & ornata auro, lapide pretioso, & margaritis ornatu prorsus Regio, quæ & sensu proprio vera novit, qui ornatum Pontificis, quum in dignitate sua se conspiciendum eodem præbere vult, non nescit, & mystico: Siquidem ornatum sponsæ Psal. XLV. & in cantico Salomoneo descri- ptum verborum pompa & jactantia præ se ferat μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας, eoque se describi & ho- norari patiatur, imo gaudeat.

Ἔχου κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ) Quæ duplicem habent significa- tionem & Imperatorum, quos ex nummis Johannes nove- rat, eorum autem facies erant in his septem capitibus: & septem montium sive collium, in quibus sitam Romam ne- mo ignorabat.

Καὶ κέρατα δέκα.) Haec cornua decem in hac visione signi- ficant decem Reges, qui tempore Johannis nondum erant in fide & reverentia Romani Imperii. Manifestum id sit infra 12. & sequentibus.

Haec deinde explicabuntur ab Angelo Vers. 12. quo eadem reservamus.

## 17:4
Verse 4.

And the woman arrayed in purple and scarlet.) Scarlet is the Roman military garment, purple is of peace, both in the whole toga of the Emperors and in the broad stripe of the Senators. Jerome in his prologue to Didymus: When I was staying in Babylon, and was a colonist of the purple-clad harlot. While to Algasia: Whence in the Apocalypse of John the name of blasphemy is written on the forehead of the purple-clad harlot, that is, eternal Rome. And to Eph. XXIV. Babylon, which sits on seven mountains, purple-clad. And to Marcella: Read the Apocalypse of John and behold what is sung concerning the purple-clad woman, and the blasphemy written on her forehead, the seven mountains, the many waters, and the exit of Babylon; In the Manuscript it is πορφυρᾶ̃, namely, a garment. And note that the harlot has taken for herself the ornament of the divine tabernacle. For in Exodus XXV, verse 4, there is ארגמן ויולעת שני in Greek purple, scarlet double.

Gilded with gold and precious stone and pearls.] It signifies both wealth and luxury. Nor do I doubt that images of the City of Rome in temples were with such ornament. The adornment of women in gold, silver, and gems and garments is reckoned by Tertullian. Like the ornament of the King of Tyre, Ezech. XXVIII. Gilded מדהבה of Babylon Esa. XIV, 4. But here is a syllepsis. For gilded is properly said of gold, improperly of stones and gems. Precious stone or costly אבן יקרה 2 Sam. XII, 30. 1 Reg. V, 17. c. VII, 9. 10. 2 Reg. X, 2. 10. 11. 1 Par. XX, 2. XXIX, 2. 2 Paral. III, 6. cap. IX, 1. Proverb. III, 5. Daniel. XI, 38.

Purple is not enough; gold, gems, and pearls are accustomed to be added to royal ornament, and to be seen in Roman habit. Oracles, temples, palaces, and shrines glitter, as does the tiara of the Pontiff, Cardinals, and Bishops, so that there is no need for commentary. Tirinus explains concerning necklaces, bracelets, and golden robes, but in a double way: For he says, goldsmiths in magnificent work are accustomed to cover and gild common gold with other more excellent and shining gold. But those things do not appear from the text. With gold, gems, and pearls, the temples, altars, statues, and priestly vestments of the Pontificals glitter even to the point of astonishment.

Having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations.) He calls the cup golden because of riches, as also Jerem. LI, 7. But abominations in the vision are to be understood as a foul humor, but in reality as false Gods, which the Greeks call abominations, where in the Hebrew is אליל as Esa. XX, 8. 20. אלהים with the addition of the word of the nations, as 1 Reg. XI, 5. 33. גלולים, 1 Reg. XXI, 26. Ezech. XXX, 13. חמנים, Esa. XVII, 8. but in very many places שקצים and תועבות. These are they whom Rome received Or gave herself Gods.

It was fitting, of course, for the harlot to invite lovers with a cup, so that by the sweetness of its appearance she might commend the wine of her whoredom. Because the cup is golden, hinting at the splendor and riches of this Thais, and having drained it, she begins to offer her communion to the inhabitants of the earth. For those who seek the company of harlots are accustomed first to drink with them and to be gorged from their cups. This cup, therefore, of the Roman state, by which she entices Kings and Princes, what will it be other than the most splendid eulogy of the Apostolic see and the universal vicariate of Christ, by which all the filth of her abominations is contained? This captures the eyes of all, nor do they think that anything other than the most excellent wine of delights can be offered by it. For who would suspect that poison is contained in a golden cup? And from the Apostolic see, from the chair of Peter, from the vicar of Christ, who would fear false doctrine for himself? As B. Cluverus has it. The golden cup in her hand, which she offers to the Kings of the earth, is full of abominations, of idolatrous dogmas against the first and second table of the law, by which it is wonderful how much the zeal for piety is undermined, as the Great Gerhard demonstrated in his disputation on separated things. Full of impurity and whoredoms, because she offers this also to the heads of the earth, so that they may be drunk, and love to commit whoredom with her, with their own sense; for that see was not destitute of harlots and fornicators, witness Pope Joan and others addicted to this vice, then figuratively, regarding spiritual whoredom, manifold idolatry. But not only idols, as Grotius wishes, but also any impious dogmas, along with vices or foul actions, whether sprouting from thence, or otherwise customary at Rome, of which brothels, sodomy, and simony at Rome bear rich testimony, are understood. For all these are truly in the words of the abominations. Is not the dogma of Bellarmine abominable, that Scripture is to be postponed to the custom of the Church? l. de sacr. c. 26. Is not the opinion abominable and detestable, that sacred scripture is a nose of wax, which was the reproach of the Cologne censure Dial. IV. and Cardinal Hosius, who compared it to the fables of Aesop? Is not a horrendous abomination and abominable idolatry that small images in the form of a Lamb fashioned from white wax by the Roman Pontiff, and anointed with oil and hung from the neck, purge the sins of men just as much as the very blood of the Son of God? Cerem. Pontif. l. 1. s. 7. Is it not abominable that the image of Christ is to be adored with the same adoration with which Christ himself is adored? Thom. part. 3. q. 25. art. 3. 4. It is an abomination indeed that the wood of the cross is called our hope, and that the worship of latria is exhibited to it, which with Thom. II. St. Albert, Book III of the Sentences, dist. 9, art. 4, wishes that the saints be invoked more ardently than God himself, which Bodin in Methodus Historica, ch. 5, testifies is done in Italy and Narbonensian Gaul. It is abominable that bells be baptized in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. It is abominable that a man, by preaching naked, by this act and his work merits eternal life, in the Book of Conformities of Francis, fol. 119. It is abominable that Francis gives perpetual seats in the kingdom of heaven, according to the well-known rhymes: Francis, typical Jesus, Leader and rule of the Friars, give us a perpetual seat in the kingdom of heaven. It is abominable that the Council of Trent, sess. VI, ch. 15, defines the faithful as fornicators, adulterers, effeminate, abusers of themselves with mankind, thieves, covetous, drunkards, revilers, extortioners, and all who commit mortal sins. What shall I say of the Popish Mass, which B. D. Hoë not undeservedly asserted to be filled with as many foul abominations as the sea with drops, the empyrean heaven with angels, the firmament with stars, the sun with atoms, the earth with grains of sand, which finally, however golden it may appear in external appearance, is nevertheless nothing other than a sink of all abominations, so that the entire globe of the earth cannot comprehend the immensity, sublimity, and depth of its idolatry and blasphemies.

And the unclean things of her fornication.) The Manuscript also has it thus. But if we follow that explanatory καὶ, to explain what the cup of abominations is; namely, the impurities of whoredom, that is, of idolatry itself, which the harlot offers to others to drink. But other Codices have ἀκαθαρτότητος πορνείας ἀυτῆς, in which way the Latin translator seems to have read it. Arethas, however, has καὶ τῶν ἀκαθάρτων τῆς πορνείας τῆς γῆς.

Concerning the impure fornications, whether they are understood spiritually or in the common sense, it has already been said.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

Καὶ ἡ γυνὴ περιβεβλημένη πορφύραν καὶ κόκκινον.) Cocci- neum belli gestamen Romanum, purpura pacis, tum in tota toga Imperatorum, tum in lato clavo Senatorum. Hierony- mus prologo ad Didymum: Cum in Babylone versarer, & pur- puratae meretricis essem colonus. Dum ad Algasiam: Unde Apocalypsin Johannis in fronte purpuratae meretricis scriptum est nomen blasphemiae, id est, Roma aeterna. Et ad Ef. XXIV. Babylon, quae sedet in septem montibus purpurata. Et ad Mar- cellam: Lege Apocalypsin Johannis & quid de muliere purpura- ta, & scripta in ejus fronte blasphemia, septem montibus, aquis multis & Babylonis cantetur exitu, contuere; In Manuscripto est πορφυρᾶ̃, nempe ἱμάτιον. Et nota meretricem sumpsisse sibi ornatum tabernaculi divini. Nam Exodi XXV. vers. 4. est ארגמן ויולעת שני in Graeco πορφύραν, κόκκινον διπλῶν.

Κεχρυσωμένη χρυσῷ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίταις.] Opes simul & luxum significat. Neque dubito, quin imagines Urbis Romae in templis cum tali ornatu fuerint. Mulierum cultus in auro, argento & gemmis & vestibus deputatur apud Tertullianum. Par ornatus Regis Tyri, Ezech. XXVIII. Κε- χρυσωμένη מדהבה de Babylone Esa. XIV, 4. Sed est hic σύλληψις. Nam κεχρυσωμένη de auro proprie dicitur de lapi- dibus & gemmis improprie. Λίθῳ τιμίῳ aut πολυτελῆς אבן יקרה 2. Sam. XII, 30. 1. Reg. V, 17. c. VII, 9. 10. 2. Reg. X, 2. 10. 11. 1. Par. XX, 2. XXIX, 2. 2. Paral. III, 6. cap. IX, 1. Proverb. III, 5. Daniel. XI, 38.

Non sufficit purpura; aurum, gemmae & unio- nes ad Regium ornatum accedere solent, & in Romano habitu conspici. Coruscant oraculum, templa, palatia, & sacraria, tiara item Pontificis, Cardinalium & Episcoporum, ut opus non sit commentatione. Tirinus de torquibus, armil- lis & syrmate aureo, sed duplici explicat: Solent enim, inquit, aurifices in opere magnifico aurum vulgare cooperire & inaurare alio praestantiore & fulgentiore auro. Sed ista è textu non appa- rent. Auro, gemmis & margaritis Pontificio- rum templa, altaria, statuae, vestimenta Sacerdo- talia ad stuporem usque fulgent.

Ἔχουσα χρυσοῦν ποτήριον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτῆς γέμον βδελυγμά- των.) Aureum dicit poculum ob divitias, ut & Jerem. LI, 7. Βδελύγματα autem in viso quidem intelligendo humor foe- tens, in re vero Dii falsi, quos Graeci vocant βδελύγματα, ubi in Ebraeo אליל ut Esa. XX, 8. 20. אלהים addito gentium vocabulo, ut 1. Reg. XI, 5. 33. גלולים, 1. Reg. XXI, 26. Ezech. XXX, 13. חמנים, Esa. XVII, 8. plurimis vero in locis שקצים & תועבות. Hi sunt quos Roma recepit Aut dedit ipsa Deos.

Decebat scilicet meretricem poculo quondam invitare amasios, ut suavitate aspectus commen- daret vinum scortationis suae. Quod poculum aureum est, splendorem & divitias hujus Thaidis innuens, eoque hausto communionem illa sui prae- bere incipit habitatoribus terrae. Combibere enim meretricibus, & de poculis earum ingurgitari so- lent primum, qui consuetudinem earum appe- tunt. Hoc igitur poculum Romanae civitatis, qua allicit Reges & Principes, quodnam erit aliud, quam splendidissimum elogium sedis A- postolicae & vicariatus Christi universalis, quo omnis foeditas abominationum ejus continetur? Hoc omnium oculos in se rapit, nec posse eo quic- quam aliud, quam praestantissimum deliciarum vinum propinari autumant. Poculo enim aureo quis venenum inesse suspicetur? Et à sede Aposto- lica, à cathedra Petri, à vicario Christi quis sibi falsam doctrinam metuat? Ut habet B. Clu- verus. Poculum aureum in manu ejus, quod propinat Regibus terrae, plenum est abomina- tionum, dogmatum idololatricorum adversus primam & secundam legis tabulam, quibus mi- rum quantum pietatis studium labefactatur, ut Magnus Gerhardus disput. separatis demonstra- vit. Plenum impuritate & scortationibus, quia & hanc propinat terræ capitibus, ut inebrien- tur, amentque secum scortari, cum proprio sen- su; non enim sedes illa destituta fuit scortis, & fornicatoribus, teste Johanne Papissa aliisque huic vitio deditis, tum tralatitio, quoad scorta- tionem spiritualem, idololatriam multiplicem. Non autem tantum idola, ut Grotius vult, sed & impia quævis dogmata, cum vitiis sive fœdis actionibus, seu inde propullulantibus, seu alias Romæ solennibus, de quibus lupanaria, sodo- mia, ac simonia Romæ locuples perhibent testi- monium, intelliguntur. Hæc enim omnia vere in verbis De βδελύγματα sunt. Annon abomi- nabile dogma est Bellarmin. quod Scriptura con- suetudini Ecclesiæ sit postponenda? l. de sacr. c. 26. Annon abominabilis & detestanda est senten- tia, scripturam sacram esse nasum cereum, quod con- vitium erat Coloniensis censuræ Dial. IV. & Cardin. Hosti, qui eam fabulis Æsopi comparavit? Annon horrendum βδέλυγμα & abominabilis idolola- tria est, quod imagunculæ in forma Agni à Rom. Pontifice ex cera alba efficti, & oleo delibuti de collo suspensæ hominum peccata æque purgent, ac ipse sanguis Filii Dei? Cerem. Pontif. l. 1. s. 7. Annon abominabile, imaginem Christi eadem adoratione adorandam esse, qua ipsum Christum? Thom. part. 3. q. 25. art. 3. 4. Abominatio uti- que est, lignum crucis dici spem nostram, eique la- triæ cultum exhiberi, quod cum Thom. II. S. Al- bertus l. III. sent. dist. 9. art. 4. vult; sanctos ar- dentius invocari quam Deum ipsum, quod in Italia, & Gallia Narbonensi fieri Bodinus in Meth. Hist. c. 5. testatur. Abominabile est cam- panas in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti ba- ptizari. Abominabile, hominem nudum con- cionantem, hoc facto, & opere suo mereri vitam æternam in libr. conform. Franc. f. 119. Abomina- bile Franciscum sedes perpetuas dare regni cælo- rum, juxta rhytmos notissimos: Francisce, Jesu typice, Dux, normaq; Minorum Sedes nobis perpetuo da regni cælorum. Abominabile, quod Conc. Trid. sess. VI. c. 15. fide- les desiniantur fornicarii, adulteri, molles, mascu- lorum concubitores, fures, avari, ebrii, maledici, ra- paces, & omnes, qui lethalia committunt peccata. Quid de Missa Papistica dicam, quam non imme- rito B. D. Hoë tot abominationum fœditatibus re- pletam asseruit, quot mare guttis, cælum empyre- um Angelis, firmamentum stellis, sol atomis, terra arenulis, quæ denique utut externa specie videa- tur aurea, tamen nihil aliud sit, quam omnium abominationum sentina, ut universus terrarum or- bis idololatria & blasphemiarum immensitatem, sublimitatem & profunditatem comprehendere ne- queat.

Καὶ τὰ ἀκάθαρτα τῆς πορνείας ἀυτῆς.) Ita habet & Manu- scriptus. Quod si sequimur illud καὶ ἐξηγητικὸν, ad expli- candum quid sit poculum abominationum; nempe impuri- tates scortationis, id est, idololatriæ ipsius, quas meretrix aliis propinat. At alii Codices habent ἀκαθαρτότητος πορνείας ἀυ- τῆς, quomodo videtur legisse Latinus. Arethas vero, καὶ τῶν ἀκαθάρτων τῆς πορνείας τῆς γῆς.

De impuris fornicationibus, sive spiritualiter, sive vulgari sensu intelligantur, jam dictum.

## 17:5
Verse 5.

And upon her forehead a name written) She herself also had to appear with a name on her forehead, because she was the cause for others to inscribe their foreheads with names.

Mystery.) [Hebrew text], that is, a name which is not as it is commonly called, but enigmatic. It is called a mystery, and that by which something is latently signified, and that which is signified, as above I, 20, and below 7. But that acceptance is metonymical, which we have here, is more proper.

On her forehead is written the name Mystery, which according to the numbers makes 1178.. 82 are missing, which perhaps flowed from the birth of Christ until the time of the Johannine vision. For John is said to have been transported to Patmos under Domitian, whose reign began in the 18th year of Christ: since all things are to be taken mystically, as we said that the name teaches, it does not seem incorrectly that that name also is explained mystically.

Babylon the great.) So also XVI, 19, where we have brought forward the reasons for this appellation.

The mother of harlots.) Aretas has 'of fornications', and the Latin reads it thus. She is the mother of whoredoms, because she propagated her idolatry most widely.

And of the abominations of the earth.) Because she had both given new Gods, and was herself among the Gods.

She is called Babylon the great, both by reason of her empire, and by reason of her notable whoredoms and abominations, of which she is the mother, cause, and origin, and by her doctrine and edicts, because as she is presented here as a Queen, she is to be marked below by the name of the Pseudo-Prophet. Moreover, Rome is compared, which most Papists acknowledge to be called Babylon in 1 Peter V, so that they may maintain that Peter was at Rome; some deny this regarding this passage in 1 Peter V with Babylon 1, because of the confusion. Bede says: He calls Rome Babylon typically, namely because of the confusion of manifold idolatry. 2. Because of pride. Tertullian, against the Jews, against Marcion, book III, ch. 13: Babylon in John bears Rome, and great, and proud in kingdom, and the conqueror of the saints. How Rome claims for herself the fasces of empire through pride has been said before: with a triple crown she boasts herself the mistress of heaven and earth and the underworld. 3. Because of cruelty; how she raged against the saints, as Babylon once did against the Jews, the people of God, has likewise been demonstrated already. See regarding the comparison of Rome and Babylon, Augustine on 1 Peter V, 13, and Orosius, book II, History, ch. 4.

But that Grotius, Alcafar, Cornelius a Lapide, and others among the Papists wish Rome to be understood in this passage, such as it was in the time of John and under the Heathen Emperors, is vain and frivolous. That it is understood as it will be in the final times, Arnold Wion acknowledged in the Chronicles of the Order of St. Benedict, book II, ch. 48: In the final persecution of the Holy Roman Church, Peter the Roman Pontiff will sit, who will feed the sheep in many tribulations: when these are passed, the seven-hilled city of Rome will be destroyed, and the terrible Judge will judge his people a little later. Which testimony Tirinus praised, after he taught in this place by many votes that Rome was designated here: That by the great harlot, to whom the mystical name is Babylon, no other can be understood here than Rome, is clear from verse 9, where she is said to sit upon seven mountains: which belongs to no other city having empire over the Kings of the earth. And St. Peter calls her by the same name, and St. Paul says her ruin will be a sign of the present Antichrist. And thus Lactantius, Tertullian, Jerome, Ambrose, Augustine, and Augustine's disciple Paul Orosius, Oecumenius, Andreas of Caesarea expressly teach: Aretas, Victorinus, Sixtus Senensis, Lindanus, Bellarmine, Bozius, Suarez, Salmeron, Pererius, Pradus, a Lapide, Alcafar, and even our heretics: the Anglo-Rhenish, in this place. It can happen not inconveniently, they say, that that great Anti-Christ has his seat at Rome, others warn that it is to be taken of both Romes. Blasius de Viega in this place: The name of Babylon is to be transferred to that Rome which, before it received the faith of Christ, had served idols, and to that which will be in the time of the Anti-Christ, which John in this chapter XVII and the following commemorates as having defected from the Supreme Pontiff, and thus from the faith. Ribera on Ap. XIV, n. 39. John speaks in the Apocalypse of Rome, such as it was under the Heathen Emperors, and such as, after it has defected from the Roman Pontiff, it will be at the end of the age. John does not prophesy of Rome which defected in the Pontiff, but which adheres to that beast. But we have shown in the Apostolic Roman Theology that the beast has defected from the pristine Roman Apostolic faith. Blessed Nic. Hunnius has demonstrated that the same Heathen idolomania and multivarious superstition has been brought back into the Christian Church.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον ἀυτῆς ὄνομα γεγραμμένον) Debebat & ipsa apparere cum nomine in fronte, quia aliis causa erat, ut frontem nominibus inscriberent.

Μυστήριον.) [Hebrew text], id est, quod nomen non est quale vul- go vocatur, sed αἰνιγματικὸν. Vocatur μυστήριον & id, quo latenter significatur aliquid, & id, quod significatur, ut supra I, 20. & infra 7. Sed ea acceptio est μετωνυμικὴ, quam his ha- bemus, magis propria.

In fronte ejus scriptum nomen μυστήριον, quod secundum numeros facit 1178.. desunt 82. quod forte a nativitate Christi fluxere usque ad tem- pus visionis Johanneæ. Nam sub Domitiano in Pathmum transportatus dicitur Johannes, cu- jus imperium anno Christi 18. cœpit: quum omnia mystice accipienda sint, ut id nominis docere di- ximus, non inrecte nomen etiam illud mystice ex- plicari videtur.

Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη.) Sic & XVI, 19. ubi causas attulimus hujus appellationis.

Ἡ μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν.) Τῶν πορνειῶν habet Aretas, & ita le- git Latinus. Mater scortationum est, quia latissime propaga- vit idololatriam suam.

Καὶ τῶν βδελυγμάτων τῆς γῆς.) Quia & novos Deos dede- rat, & ipsa inter Deos erat.

Babylon magna dicitur, cum ratione imperii, tum ratione insignium scortationum & abomi- nationum, quarum mater, causa & origo est, & doctrina, & edictis suis, quia ut Regina hic sisti- tur, infra Pseudo-Prophetæ nomine insignienda. Confertur autem Roma, quam Babylonem ple- rique Pontificii I. Petr. V. dici agnoscunt, ut Romæ Petrum fuisse obtineant, de hoc loco nonnulli negant in 1. Petr. V. cum Babylone 1. propter confusionem. Beda: Babylonem, inquit, typice Romam dicit, videlicet propter confusionem multiplicis idololatriæ. 2. Propter superbiam. Tertullianus adv. Jud. contr. Marcion. lib. III. c. 13. Babylon apud Johannem Roma portat, & ma- gna, & regno superbæ, & sanctorum debellatricis. Quomodo per fastum Roma sibi imperii fasces vindicet, antea dictum: trifida corona jactat se cœli & terræ & inferorum Dominam. 3. Pro- pter sævitiam; quomodo sævierit in sanctos, ut Babyloni quondam in Judæos, Dei populum, iti- dem jam demonstratum. Vide de comparatio- ne Romæ & Babylonis Augustinum ad 1. Petr. V, 13. & Oros. lib. II. Hist. c. 4.

Quod autem Grotius, Alcafar, Cornelius a La- pide, & alii e Pontificiis Romam intellectam hoc loco velint, qualis erat tempore Johannis, & sub Imperatoribus Ethnicis, vanum est, & frivolum. Intelligi eam, qualis extremis futura est tempo- ribus, agnovit Arnoldus Wione in Chronicis Ordin. S. Bened. lib. II. c. 48. In persecutione extrema S. R. E. sedebit Pontifex Petrus Romanus, qui pascet oves in multis tribulationibus: quibus transactis civitas Roma septicollis diruetur, & Judex tremendus judicabit post paulo populum su- um. Quod testimonium laudavit Tirinus, post- quam h. l. suffragiis plurimis Romam hic desi- gnatam esse docuit: Per meretricem magnam, cui mysticum nomen Babylon, non aliam hic intelligi posse quam Romam, patet e v. 9. ubi dicitur sedere super septem montes: quod nulli alteri urbi com- petit habenti imperium super Reges terræ. Et eo- dem nomine vocat eam S. Petrus, & hujus rui- nam ait S. Paulus signum fore præsentis Antichri- sti. Et ita expresse docent Lactantius, Tertullia- nus, Hieronymus, Ambrosius, Augustinus, & Au- gustini discipulus Paulus Orosius, Oecumenius, Andreas Cæsar: Aretas, Victorinus, Sixtus Senen- sis, Lindanus, Bellarminus, Bozius, Suarez, Sal- meron, Pererius, Pradus, a Lapide, Alcafar, & etiam hæretici nostri: Anglo-Rhenienses, in h. l. Fieri haud incommode potest, inquiunt, ut Romæ magnus ille Anti-Christus sedem suam habeat, de de utraque Roma accipi, alii monent. Blasius de Viega in h. l. Nomen Babylonis ad eam Romam transferen- dum, quæ antequam reciperet fidem Christi, idolis servierat & ad eam, quæ erit tempore Anti-Chri- sti, quam à summo Pontifice, atque adeò à fide de- fecturam Johannes hoc capite XVII. & sequenti commemorat. Ribera in Ap. XIV. n. 39. Loquitur Johannes in Apocalypsi de Roma, qualis sub Ethni- cis Imperatoribus fuit, & qualis, postquam à Ro- mano Pontifice defecerit, in seculi fine futura est. Non de Roma, quæ in Pontifice defecit, sed quæ bestiæ illi adhæret, vaticinatur Johannes. Bestiam autem à fide pristina Romana Apostolica defecis- se in Theol. Apostol. Rom. ostendimus. Eandem Ethnicam idolomaniam & superstitionem multiva- riam in Christianam Ecclesiam reduxisse demon- stravit B. Nic. Hunnius.

## 17:6
Vers. 6.

And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus.) He saw her with a rabid, foaming mouth, and vomiting blood, as drunkards are wont to do. Here he calls any Christians saints: martyrs, the Doctors, who in an exceptional way above others bore witness to Christ.

And I wondered when I saw her with great wonder.] I wondered that a woman so beautiful, so adorned, should act so drunkenly and be bloodied. He had not beheld this woman in that vision of the head in chapter XIII.

He implies that this harlot is 1. thirsty for blood. For unless she were thirsty for blood, she would never get drunk on it. For how the Roman curia thirsts for blood has been proven by various butcheries of men perpetrated against both the faith and civil honesty. Then, to shed blood with delight, and finally to gorge herself on it to such an extent that she appears furious and drunk. Boasting, indeed, of evil deeds, and exulting in her own turpitude, having forgotten honesty and modesty, Sir. XXVI, 11. Therefore Bellarmine places temporal happiness among the marks of the Church, such as he recounts here: In the time, he says, of Innocent III, in Gaul, one hundred thousand Albigensian heretics were slain by eight thousand Catholics in one battle, as Aemilius writes in book 6 of the history of the Franks. In our times, in the year 1531, the Catholic Swiss fought five battles for the faith against the heretical Swiss, and the Catholics always won, although they were much inferior in number and arms. Charles won a victory over the Lutherans in the year 1547 by a divine miracle. In Gaul also and in Belgium, the Catholics have won many victories over the heretics not without a miracle; the heretics have hardly ever been superior when a fair battle was fought. This woman is drunk with the blood which she sheds either by herself or through others. Guilliadinus, book II, says: The office of the Popes was judged to be greater in increasing the empire of the Pontifical see by arms and the blood of Christians than in devoting effort to their salvation, for the sake of which they boast that they were appointed by Christ as his vicars on earth, by the example of their lives and by correcting and vindicating depraved morals. It is reported of John X that he was more a soldier than a Bishop, as are also things related about Lucius II, Leo XI, Paschal II, Innocent II, Boniface, and others, that they visited camps more willingly than temples, and were accustomed to inspect their weapons more often than to read the Bibles. Julius II took part in public battles, and once, having thrown the keys into the Tiber, said: If the keys of Peter do not help, let the sword of Paul help. In his time, it is written that more than a million men perished, all of whom the Roman Pontiff destroyed by his condemned lust for warring. When the kingdom of Sicily and Naples, as also the Duchy of Swabia, had no successor, soon Clement IV ordered the younger heir Conradin's head to be cut off with a sword, so that he might bring the kingdom of Sicily under his own power. He struck Henry IV with the thunderbolt of excommunication, and did not admit the Emperor, who was waiting for three days at the gate of the palace, as one constrained by constant fornications, nor did he cease until he commanded the Son to kill his father Henry IV, who was enclosed in a squalid prison, with grief and stench. Alexander III persecuted Frederick Barbarossa, having entered into a treaty with the Turk, and having sent his effigy, he sought that he might capture the Caesar in battle. He killed Henry IV with a host poisoned with venom, which was also done to the Emperor Louis. And although we do not make all these martyrs, they nevertheless testify to the tyranny and the spirit of the Roman Pontiffs, which knows not how to be satisfied with blood. But since from the year 1550 to the year 1580, nine hundred thousand men were killed by the Roman Pontiff, and since in the Parisian weddings alone in the year 1572 over 30,000 were wickedly deprived of life, what else do they teach, than that that harlot could not be satisfied with the blood of the martyrs. For she drank herself with the blood of countless others, as history testifies.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

Καὶ εἶδον τὴν γυναῖκα μεθύουσαν ἐκ τῶ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων καὶ ἐκ τῶ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησῦ.) Vidit eam ore rabido, despumante, & evomente sanguinem, ut ebrii solent. Sanctos hic vocat Christianos quosvis: μάρτυρας Doctores, qui exi- mie supra alios testimonium Christi præbebant.

Καὶ ἐθαύμασα ἰδὼν αὐτὴν θαῦμα μέγα.] Miratus sum fœminam tam speciosam, tam ornatam, ita temulentam age- re & cruentari. Hanc mulierem in illo viso capite cap. XIII. non conspexerat.

Innuit meretricem hanc 1. sanguinis esse sitien- tem. Nisi enim sanguinem sitiret, nunquam se eo inebriaret. Quam enim curia Romana sangui- nem sitiat, variis hominum lanienis contra fidem quoque & honestatem civilem patratis probatum est. Deinde sanguinem fundere cum delectatione, ac denique adeo se eo ingurgitare, ut furiosa & ebria videatur. Glorians nempe de malefactis, & in turpitudine sua exultans honestatis & pudoris oblitæ, Sir. XXVI, 11. Ideo Bellarminus inter notas Ecclesiæ collocat felicitatem tempora- lem, qualem hanc recenset: Tempore, inquit, Innocentii III. in Gallia ab octo millibus Catholico- rum cæsa sunt uno prælio centum millia Albigen- sium hæreticorum, ut scribit Æmilius lib. 6. hi- storiæ Francorum. Nostris temporibus anno 1531. quinque prælia commiserunt pro fide Catholici Helvetii cum hæreticis Helvetiis, & semper Ca- tholici vicerunt, cum tamen essent numero & ar- mis multo inferiores. Carolus miraculo Divino victoriam retulit de Lutheranis Anno 1547. In Gallia quoque & Belgio multas victorias Catholi- ci de hæreticis non sine miraculo reportarunt, vix unquam fuerunt hæretici superiores, quando justo prælio dimicatum est. Ebria hæc mulier est san- guine, quem vel per se, vel per alios profundit. Guilliadinus lib. II. Pontificum, inquit, munus ma- jus judicatum fuit armis & Christianorum san- guine Pontificiæ sedis imperium augere, quam ad illorum salutem, cujus gratia ipsi se à Christo in terris vicarios constitutos jactitant vitæ exemplo & depravatis moribus corrigendis atque vindi- candis operam dare. De Johanne X. refertur, eum magis militem, quam Episcopum fuisse, qualia et- iam de Lucio II. De Leone XI. De Paschali II. Innocentio II. Bonifacio, aliisque traduntur, quod libentius castra, quam templa visitarint, & sæpius arma sua inspicere, quam Biblia legere consueverint. Julius II. publicis pugnis inter- fuit, & aliquando clavibus in Tiberim projectis dixit: Si claves Petri non juvant, juvet gladius Pauli. Illius tempore ultra millies millena millia homines occubuisse scribuntur, quos omnes Romanus Pontifex, damnata sua bellandi li- bidine perdidit. Cum regnum Siciliæ & Neapo- lis, ut & Ducatus Sueviae nullum successorem habuit, haeredem juniorem Conradinum, mox Clemens IV. caput fulcone amputari jussit, ut re- gnum Siciliae in suam potestatem redigeret. Hen- ricum IV. excommunicationis fulmine feriebat, Imperatorem ad portam palatii per triduum ex- pectantem, utpote fornicationibus districtus assiduis, non intromisit, nec prius desiit, quam Filio mandaret, ut Patrem Henricum IV. carce- re squalido inclusum maerore & foetore occide- ret. Alexander III. Fridericum Barbarossam persecutus est, inito cum Turca foedere, missa- que ejusdem effigie petiit, ut in pugna Caesarem caperet. Henricum IV. hostia veneno tincta ne- cabat, quod etiam Ludovico Imperatori factum. Et licet istos omnes Martyres non faciamus, te- stantur tamen illa tyrannidem, & animum san- guine expleri nescium Pontificum Romanorum. Sed quum ab anno 1550. ad annum 1580, a Roma- no Pontifice interfecti novies centeni mille homi- nes, quum in nuptiis solis Parisiensibus An. 1572. ultra 30000. vita scelerate privati, quid aliud do- cent, quam meretricem illam exsatiari sanguine martyrum minime potuisse. Nam innume- rorum aliorum sanguine se potavit, teste Hi- storia.

## 17:7
Vers. 7.

And the Angel said to me, why did you marvel?) where you understand the matter, you will not marvel at this vision. I will tell you the mystery of the woman.) What lies hidden under this figure. Thus above I, 20. And of the beast that carries her.) The beast upon which she is carried. He says to the beast because mention was made of it above in 13. Of him who has the seven heads and the seven horns.) above 3. XIII, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Καὶ εἶπέ μοι ὁ Ἄγγελος, διὰ τί ἐθαύμασας;) ubi rem intel- liges, non miraberis hoc visum. Ἐγώ σοι ἐρῶ τὸ μυστήριον τῆς γυναικός.) Quid sub hac figura lateat. Sic supra I, 20. Καὶ τοῦ θηρίου τοῦ βαστάζοντος αὐτήν.) Ferae cui illa invecta- tur. Dicit τῷ θηρίῳ quia supra 13. ejus facta mentio. Τοῦ ἔχοντος τὰς ἑπτὰ κεφαλὰς καὶ τὰ ἑπτὰ κέρατα.) supra 3. XIII, 1.

## 17:8
Vers. 8.

The beast which you saw, was.) Here he calls it a beast by synecdoche, him who was the most powerful part, that is, the mouth of the beast above XIII, 2. He had been Domitian while his father was absent, that is, he had received the name and seat of Caesar, as Tacitus says. Martial about him: Alone when he already held the reins, he handed over the Jews, and was the third in his world. Vespasian wrote to him: I give thanks to you alone, because you did not take the empire from me: as Dio testifies. He boasted that he had given the empire to both his father and his brother, as Suetonius says. In sum, he was exceeding the limits of his age and other things granted to a son, which are the very words of Tacitus. Josephus has similar things at the end of the fourth book of the Jewish War.

And is not.) This time, that is, when John was living in Ephesus under the Prince Vespasian, Domitian was not with the Empire, but reduced to the manner of a private citizen, he feigned modesty, and especially a study of poetry, as Suetonius says. But as Tacitus says, he was also omitting the moderate and previously usurped duties of the empire, hidden in the height of the image of simplicity and modesty, and feigning a study of literature and a love of poems.

And is about to ascend from the abyss.) He will lift himself from his hiding places, he will emerge powerful from obscurity.

And to go into destruction.) עדי אבד, Num. XXV. v. 24. destruction here, as also in John 17, 12. 2 Thess. 2. verse 3. does not signify just any death, but the worst end, such as befell Domitian, killed by the hands of his own household: about whom Suetonius and Philostratus can be seen. It is to be noted, however, that just as the name of a beast is given to Domitian, as the principal member of the beast, so in his affairs are shadowed the things of idolatry itself, which sometimes had exercised its cruelty, as under Claudius, Nero, and others, sometimes rested, as under Vespasian, resumed cruelty, as under Domitian, Trajan and others, and finally perished utterly, as we shall see below XIX, 20. 21.

And those dwelling on the earth will marvel.) They will marvel that the end corresponds to many omens, about which Suetonius and Dion can be seen.

Whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world.) We have said what is signified by this locution above XII, 8. The sense is that Christians versed in the scriptures will not marvel that what happened to Domitian in Rome, happened once to Belshazzar in Babylon Dan. V, 30. who likewise could not avoid the predicted end.

Seeing the beast which was, and is not, although it is.) ὅτι here is a pronoun, not a conjunction. In the Manuscript it is Βλεπόντων. Not badly: For the Greeks are accustomed to put the participle even alone in the Genitive, where the Latins would put a noun or pronoun and at the same time a participle, both placed absolutely, as the Grammarians say.

This vision is not to be restricted, with Brocard, Graser, and Brightman, to the sixteenth century, since the words of the text in v. 12 clearly testify that the earlier centuries are included, because the kings had not yet received the kingdom. Moreover, the angel who revealed this mystery is rashly identified as Peter or Paul, whom the Romanists falsely assert to have founded the Roman Church. For their faith was already announced in the whole world, Rom. 1:8, when Paul had not yet come to Rome. Add v. 1, where Paul claims for himself the work of confirmation, not of foundation: 'I long to see you, that I may impart some spiritual grace to strengthen you.' But what Alcafar saw in these chapters 17 and 18, when he rashly dreamed that the happy state of Rome was being predicted, I cannot see, nor, I think, will anyone else see. The beast is said to have been, such as it was indeed seen, in that splendor and power, the mistress and empress of so many crowned heads: and not to be, because it is predicted that some of those same heads will fail. It emerged from the abyss, and is being driven into perdition, partly on account of the heads failing from it, which will bring no small destruction upon it, and partly as a whole, partly in corporal and external desolation, and partly in spiritual and eternal destruction, Rev. 20. Thus, therefore, it will be forced to descend in turn into the abyss from whence it had ascended. And those who dwell on the earth, who worshipped it like some divinity, will marvel both in this age and in the future: whose names are not written in the book of life. In hell itself they will both marvel at it and detest it, as being that by which they were seduced into eternal perdition, when they see that it was once in such honor, is now no more, but is in eternal ignominy: and yet it is and remains forever. For it will never die. Blessed Cluverus writes somewhat differently about these things: If you represent to your mind the ancient state of that empire, it was and is no more. If you look at the Roman city, with the kingdoms and nations once subject to it, it is still the mistress of those kingdoms and nations, but under a completely different head, and by a far different power. It is the Roman Empire, whose head is the King and Lord of the Roman state. That King and Lord is the Pope, whose authority and power the Caesar and the kings clothed in gilded purple adore. And indeed the kings of those nations which once were subject to the Roman Caesars. Whence it is clear how acutely it was said by the Angel that the inhabitants of the earth would marvel that this empire was, and is not, although it is. The Angel speaks in the present, in the past, and in the future, and requires that wisdom be applied to this discourse. For the Roman empire was in John's time, and had been before that time, and another was to be in the following time.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

Τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδες, ἦν.) Hic θηρίον vocat κατὰ συνεκδοχὴν, il- lum qui pars potissima, id est, os erat τοῦ θηρίου supra XIII, 2. Is Domitianus patre absente fuerat, id est, nomen sedemque Caesaris acceperat, ut ait Tacitus. Martialis de eo: Solus Judaeos cum jam retineret habenas Tradidit, inque suo tertius orbe fuit. Scripsit ei Vespasianus: Gratias tibi soli habeo, quod mihi imperium non abstulisti: teste Dione. Jactavit se & patri & fratri imperium dedisse, ut ait Suetonius. In summa terminos aetatis & alia concessa filio egrediebatur, quae & ipsa Taciti sunt verba. Paria habet Josephus fine libri quarti de bello Judaico.

Καὶ οὐκ ἔστι.) Hoc tempus, id est, cum Vespasiano Principe Ephesi ageret Johannes, non erat cum Imperio Domitianus, sed in privati modum redactus modestiam, imprimisque stu- dium Poeticae simulabat, ut ait Suetonius. Ut vero Tacitus, modica quoque & usurpata antea imperii munia omittebat, simplicitatis ac modestiae imagine in altitudinem conditus, studiumque literarum & amorem carminum simulans.

Καὶ μέλλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου.) Attollet se ex suis la- tebris, ex obscuro potens evadet.

Καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγειν.) עדי אבד, Num. XXV. v. 24. ἀπώλεια hic, ut & Joh. 17, 12. 2. Thess. 2. vers. 3. non mortem quamlibet, sed pessimum exitum significat, qualis Domitiano obtigit, interfecto domesticorum suorum manibus: de quo videri potest Suetonius & Philostratus. Notandum autem sicut Domitiano ferae nomen datur, ut praecipuo ferae mem- bro, ita in ejus rebus adumbratas res ipsius idololatriae, quae interdum saevitiam suam exercuerat, ut sub Claudio, Nerone, & aliis interdum conquievit, ut sub Vespasiano, resumpsit sae- vitiam, ut sub Domitiano, Trajano & aliis, ac postremum funditus interiit, ut videbimus infra XIX, 20. 21.

Καὶ θαυμάσονται οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.) Mirabuntur exitum respondere multis ostentis, de quibus videri potest Suetonius & Dion.

Ὧν οὐ γέγραπται τὰ ὀνόματα, ἐπὶ τὸ βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς, κόσμου.) Hac loquutione quid significetur dixi- mus supra XII, 8. Sensus est Christianos in scripturis versa- tos non miraturos evenire Domitiano Romae, quod olim Balthasari Babylone Dan. V, 30. qui itidem praedictum exitum vitare non potuit.

Βλέποντες τὸ θηρίον ὃ, τι ἦν, καὶ ὐκ ἔστι, καίπερ ἐστιν.) ὅ- τι hic est pronomen, non conjunctio. In Manuscripto est Βλεπόντων. Non male: Solent enim Græci participium et- iam solum in Genitivo ponere, ubi Latini ponerent nomen aut pronomen & simul participium, utraque absolute posita, ut loquuntur Grammatici.

Visio hæc non restringenda cum Brocardo, Grasero, Brigtmanno ad seculum decimum sex- tum, siquidem priora secula includi verba tex- tus v. 12. luculenta, quod Reges βασιλείαν non- dum acceperint, testantur. Angelus autem, qui hoc mysterium revelavit, temere Petrus vel Paulus constituitur, quos Ecclesiam Romanam fundasse falso asserunt Romanenses. Fides enim eorum jam annunciata erat in universo mundo, Rom. I, 8. cum Paulus Romam nondum venisset. Adde v. 1. ubi confirmationis operam non fun- dationis sibi vendicat Paulus: Desidero videre vos, ut aliquid impertiar gratiæ spiritualis ad con- firmandos vos. Quid vero Alcafar in hisce capp. XVII. XIIX. viderit, cum statum felicem Romæ temere prædici somniavit, videre non possum, nec, puto, quisquam visurus est. Fera dicitur fuisse, qualis nempe visa est, in eo splendore & im- perio, tot capitum coronatorum Domina, & Imperatrix: & non esse, quia prædicitur, defectu- ra eadem capita nonnulla. Emersit ex abysso, & in perditionem agitur, tum ex parte per de- ficientia ab eadem capita, quæ non exiguam ipsi ἀπώλειαν afferent, tum ὁλικῶς partim in corpora- li & externa desolatione, partim in spirituali & æterna ἀπωλείᾳ & perditione Apocal. XX. Ita ergo vicissim in abyssum descendere cogetur, un- de ascenderat. Et admirabuntur tum in hoc, tum in futuro seculo habitantes terram, qui instar Numinis cujusdam ipsam coluere: Quorum no- mina non sunt scripta in libro vitæ. In ipso in- ferno & admirabuntur & detestabuntur eam, ut- pote à qua in æternam seducti sunt perditionem, cum videbunt, quod fuerit quondam in tanto honore, jam non sit, sed in ignominia sempi- terna: & tamen sit ac maneat in æternum. Nunquam enim morietur. Paulo aliter de his- ce B. Cluverus: Si priscum istius Imperii statum animo repræsentes, fuit & non est amplius. Si Ro- manam urbem, cum regnis & nationibus ei olim subditis inspicias, est adhuc illa eorum re- gnorum & nationum Domina, sed sub alio pla- ne capite, & perlonge diversa potestate. Est Romanum Imperium, cujus caput est Rex & Dominus Romanæ civitatis. Ille Rex & Domi- nus Papa est, cujus authoritatem & potentiam adorant Cæsar, & aurato vestiti murice Reges. Et Reges quidem earum nationum, quæ olim Cæ- saribus Romanis suberant. Unde patet, quam acute dictum sit ab Angelo, admiraturos esse ha- bitatores terræ, quod fuerit hoc imperium, & non sit, quanquam sit. Loquitur Angelus in præsenti, in præterito & futuro, & huic sermoni sapientiam adhibendam requirit. Erat enim Romanum imperium Johannis tempore, & fuerat ante illud tempus, & futurum erat aliud tempore sequenti.

## 17:9
Vers. 9.

Ὧδε ὁ νοῦς.) This is a clearer explanation of the figures, which now follows.

Ὁ ἔχων σοφίαν.) Which explanation shows the wonderful wisdom of God, setting before our eyes things past, present, and future at the same time. See above 13:18. Often in prophetic discourses, past things are exhibited together with future things because of their connection or similarity, as in Ezek. 17, 19, 23, 31; Zech. 5, 6, 11.

The seven heads are seven mountains, where the woman sits upon them.) The Greeks would say ἐφ' ὧν ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται. But John, more than others, loves Hebrew idioms. The Roman dominion sits upon seven mountains, because the seat of the empire was there, as Tacitus speaks.

And they are seven kings.) At the same time, by those heads are noted also seven Emperors, whose faces appeared on those heads, just as on coins.

That Victorinus establishes Nero as the seventh King, who is to return and be received by the Jews for Christ, and thus is to be the Anti-Christ, is too fabulous. For just as the Christ of the Jews will never come; so too that Anti-Christ of Victorinus will never appear, which I would like to note for those who rave with him that the Anti-Christ is to be received by the Jews as the Messiah. For the same people likewise admire the rest of the ravings of Victorinus, Hippolytus, and the others concerning the Anti-Christ, that Nero is to come from the underworld, or I know not where; but what can be more vain than this figment? as the blessed Cluverus holds here.

We subjoin, however, what Grotius had handed down in a special treatise on this chapter, intending to do the same for the individual verses of the chapter following:

Vers. 9.

And seven heads, seven heads.) One thing signifies two.

Seven mountains are, seven mountains are.) The mountains are sufficiently known from the poets and historians. Nor could any more illustrious mark be brought forward to describe Rome.

Where the woman sits upon them, upon whom the woman sits.) A Hebrew phrase for ἐφ' ὧν ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται. The woman is Rome, according to the interpretation of Jerome in Epistle XVII and in the book against Jovinian. But it is to be noted that with the city, the empire of the city is noted at the same time, which is expressed in Hebrew by the feminine מלכות, as in Latin 'dominatio'. Thus the Babylonian empire, a type of the Roman (Babylon in John is a figure of the Roman city, says Tertullian in two places), is described in the form of a woman in Isaiah XLVII, 7, 8. But 'sits' is said in effect, as 'The city high on seven ridges, which presides over the whole world,' in Propertius.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

Ὧδε ὁ νοῦς.) Hæc est apertior figurarum explicatio, quæ jam sequitur.

Ὁ ἔχων σοφίαν.) Quæ explicatio ostendit mirabilem Dei sapientiam, res præteritas & præsentes & futuras simul ob oculos ponentis. Vide supra XIII, 18. Sæpe in propheticis sermonibus cum futuris simul exhibentur præterita ob connexum aut similitudinem, ut Ezech. XVII. XIX. XXIII. XXXI. Zach. V. VI. XI.

Αἱ ἑπτά κεφαλαὶ ἑπτά ὄρη εἰσὶν, ὅπου ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται ἐπὶ αὐτῶν.) Græci dicerent ἐφ' ὧν ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται. Sed Johan- nes præter cæteros amat locutiones Ebraicas. Dominatio Romana septem montibus insidet, quia ibi erat sedes imperii, ut Tacitus loquitur.

Καὶ βασιλεῖς ἑπτά εἰσι.) Simul per illa capita notantur & Imperatores septem, quorum facies in illis capitibus appare- bant, ita ut in nummis.

Quod Neronem septimum Regem statuit Victo- rinus, qui rediturus, atque à Judæis pro Christo recipiendus, adeoque Anti-Christus futurus sit, ni- mis fabulosum est. Sicut enim Judæorum Chri- stus nunquam veniet; sic & Victorini ille An- ti-Christus nunquam comparebit, quod annotare velim istos, qui Anti-Christum à Judæis pro Mes- sia recipiendum delirant cum ipso. Iidem enim pariter reliqua Victorini, Hippolyti & reliquo- rum de Anti-Christo deliria suspiciant, quod Nero ab inferis, vel nescio unde venturus; sed pro figmento quid potest esse vanius? ut hic habet B. Cluverus.

Subjungimus autem, quæ in peculiari tractatu in hoc caput tradiderat Grotius, idem facturi ad singula capitis commata sequentia:

Vers. 9.

Καὶ ἑπτὰ κεφαλαὶ, septem capita.) Una res duas signi- ficat.

Ἑπτὰ ὄρη εἰσὶ, septem montes sunt.) Noti satis montes ex Poëtis & Historicis. Nec ulla poterat ad describendam Ro- mam afferri nota illustrior.

Ὅπου ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται ἐπ' αὐτῶν, super quos mulier sedet.) Phrasis Ebraica pro ἐφ' ὧν ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται. Mulier est Roma interprete Hieronymo Epistola XVII. & adversus Jovinia- num libro. Sed notandum cum urbe simul notari imperi- um urbis, quod Ebræis fœminino exprimitur מלכות, ut Latine dominatio. Sic imperium Babylonicum Romani ty- pus (Babylon apud Johannem Romanæ urbis figura est, ait duobus locis Tertullianus) mulieris forma describitur Esa. XLVII, 7. 8. sedet autem effectu dictum, ut Septem urbs alta jugis, toti quæ præsidet orbi. Apud Propertium.

## 17:10
And seven kings are, and seven kings are.) Not seen at one time, which are comprised in this book. They did not obey John any more than they did the prophets whose books contain them. But John began to be in Patmos and to be enlightened by the visions of God in the times of Claudius, which is the opinion of the most ancient Christians, not of Domitian, as others have wished. See Epiphanius on the heresy of the Alogi. Claudius had driven the Jews, under whose name the Christians were also reckoned at that time, as has been observed by many learned men, from Rome, Acts XVIII, 2, which example there is no doubt that many governors of Roman provinces imitated, thus John was expelled from Ephesus. The seven Emperors are Claudius, Nero, Galba, Otho, Vitellius, Vespasian, Titus. These things were written while Vespasian was reigning. But speaking Greek, he rightly calls the Emperors βασιλέας, although the Romans abstained from the word 'Kings'. For the thing was the same. Appian in the preface: And this empire is until now under one ruler, whom they do not call kings, as I think, respecting the ancient oath, but they name them emperors, which was also the name of those who were in charge of armies for a time, in reality they are all kings. And all this empire is until now under one Prince: They do not call these Princes Kings out of reverence, as I think, for the ancient oath, but Emperors, which was also the appellation of those who were in charge of armies for a time: In reality, however, they are Kings. For the Roman Emperor was, to use the words of the historian Dio: Truly self-sufficient and absolute, both of himself and of the laws, and he does all things that he wishes, and does nothing of those things that he would not wish, with supreme right and entirely powerful over both himself and the laws, so that he does all things that he wishes, and does nothing of those things that he does not wish.

Chronology forbids understanding these things of Domitian, since the series of the Johannine revelation is to be observed. History also forbids it otherwise. In the time of Claudius, Rome had not yet tasted Christian blood: of Nero, however, it had not yet been thoroughly inebriated by it. If St. John counts the years from his deportation, he ought to have begun from Domitian. But this was not done. Grotius says these things were seen and written under Vespasian. But he could not prove it. The authority of Epiphanius alone cannot prejudice the other Fathers and Doctors, such as Irenaeus, Arethas, Victorinus, Eusebius, Jerome, and others. It is rashly asserted that no harm was brought to the Christian religion under Tiberius. For Grotius himself says that Stephen was stoned under him, and thus Christians were harassed throughout all Syria, so that they were not safe even in Macedonia. Nor are Augustus and Tiberius innocent here, or to be excused from the persecutions of the Jews, whom Claudius indeed harassed, but not those converted to Christ. The first persecution is ascribed by all not to Claudius but to Nero. Galba, Otho, and Vitellius are read to have decreed nothing harsher against the Christians. Vespasian, however, restored the Capitol and adorned it with the spoils of the temple, and by that he greatly opposed the Christian religion, indeed he was even intensely devoted to Apollonius.

If, however, those seven Kings are seven Caesars, why is Claudius established as the first, with Tiberius and Augustus omitted? Seven heads and seven mountains, according to Andreas, are seven monarchies or kingdoms: the first of the Assyrians in Nineveh, the second of the Medes in Ecbatana under Prince Arbaces, the third of the Chaldeans in Babylon, the fourth of Cyrus in Susa, the fifth of Alexander in Macedonia, the sixth of Augustus and the Emperors in ancient Rome, the seventh of Constantine in the new and Christian Rome. Consequently, the seven Kings are the first Ninus, the second Arbaces, the third Nebuchadnezzar, the fourth Cyrus, the fifth Alexander, the sixth Augustus, the seventh Constantine. But he confuses these mountains with the Kings, which must be distinguished. Furthermore, he places Constantine, a faithful nursing father to the Church, among the heads of the beast. Cornelius à Lapide: A collection of tyrants who reigned in the world, or in the kingdom of impiety and the Devil, during seven ages or centuries, and who persecuted the faithful and the Church. Thus Richard, Ambrose, Bede, and others: as is evident from the following. For John says that five have passed, the sixth still survives, the seventh is expected, and will reign for a short time. The first King, therefore, is Cain with the giants and others like them, who persecuted the faithful and the pious in the first age of the world from Adam down to Noah and the flood. The second is Nimrod with the builders of the tower of Babel in the second age of the world from Noah down to Abraham. The third are the Kings of Sodom and the Pharaohs of Egypt before Moses in the third age of the world, which was from Abraham to Moses. The fourth are the impious Kings of Israel and Judah with others like them, who lived from the time of Moses down to the Babylonian captivity, which was the fourth age of the world. The fifth are the Kings of the Chaldeans, such as Nebuchadnezzar, and of Asia and Syria, such as Antiochus Epiphanes, and others from the Babylonian captivity down to Christ, which was the fifth age of the world. The sixth are the pagan Roman Emperors; likewise the Saracens, Turks, and others who have been, are, and will be from Christ down to the Antichrist. Whence it is said of him here: One is still here. The seventh is the Antichrist, who is to come, and will reign for a short time, namely three years and a half. Thus Gagneius, Ribera, and Viegas, who asserts that this is the common exposition. Richard and his followers also agree, except that he assigns the fourth age from Moses to David, when there were Balaam, Balak, the Moabites, Edomites, Philistines, and similar enemies of the people of God, namely the Israelites, but he designates the fifth from David down to Christ. In which likewise are missing while, because Constantine the Great, Charles the Great, and other Christian Kings and Emperors are numbered among the heads of the beast, and because so many heads are drawn to preceding times.
