Yet there is this truth in it, that the Pope is one of the seven heads and yet is called the eighth, with Prosper as author in Sim. temp. c. 8. and Haymo, who says of the Roman Pontiff, he will rule and persecute the Church seven times more than all the other superior tyrants, the monarch of all preceding ones: which was fulfilled completely in the Roman Anti-Christ. It is therefore more correctly said that seven forms of government are understood, of which five had already passed, the sixth of the Caesars or Emperors was then prevailing, the seventh, destined to last for a very short time under Odoacer, was to follow in its own time. And how can it be said that someone was and is not absolutely, because he abstained for a time from the authority of the empire, previously exercised precariously, and afterwards to be resumed with the fullest right? Therefore Maresius in his dissertation, page 173: This beast is not idolatry, not magic, not Trajan, as Piscator seems to suspect, not Domitian, but the Roman empire. It is said in a certain sense to John to have been, and to be no longer, and yet still to be; because, namely, here Rome is considered under the empire of the Anti-Christ himself and the Roman Pontiff, under whom it is no longer the same as it once was, a merely political empire; but yet it is the same, as regards imitation and likeness, insofar as the second beast fashioned an image of the former, and finally proposed it to the peoples to be adored. Therefore this beast is said to be the eighth of the Kings, and consequently as it were the eighth head of the former, because the Roman Pontiff, whose triple crown is called in Italian the II. Regno, himself brought into Rome from some in Italy a kingly eighth form of government, entirely unlike the former seven. Therefore here he is called ὄγδοος, the eighth, ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ, from the seven, not because Domitian was one of those seven, namely the son of Vespasian, but because the Papal government is no less in the former beast as regards authority than one of the seven former ones, and because the dignity of the Pontiffs has grown to this degree by the favor and benefits of the Emperors now converted to the Christian faith. Compare B. Cluverus on the seven forms of empire, and you will find how he answers Cornelius here and satisfies one who understands Eclinus through the sixth head, Julian the Apostate, and through the eighth, that face of the empire which began after Constantine the Great. He adds these conclusions: No Lord of the Roman City was found after the empire was healed, except the Pope, therefore he is the eighth King himself. But the eighth King is the very head of the beast described by John, which beast is the Anti-Christ. Therefore the Pope is the Anti-Christ. Another: The Anti-Christ is not a singular person. For such as those seven former Kings were, such also is the eighth, since the judgment is the same concerning similar things. But they were not singular persons or individuals, but royal statuses, therefore such also is the Anti-Christ. Moreover, he is the eighth and yet is of the seven. For the Pope is not an Emperor properly, nor the legitimate head of the Roman empire: And yet he is a head, and superior to the Emperor. B. Gravius agrees with our opinion; By the beast is understood the kingdom of the Anti-Christ itself, which arose in the VII provinces of the western empire after the desolation of the City of Rome by the barbarian nations, which indeed WAS in the highest vigor, but by the benefit of the reformation, brought about by the ministry of B. Luther, CEASED TO BE, that is, after the defection of the 5 heads, it represents only the naked IMAGE OF THE BEAST. This interpreting Angel therefore looks to the last times of the reformation, in which the Papal beast lost its former power and flower. For he says expressly in verse 10 that five heads have fallen, which should not be doubted to be understood of the reformation. And another has not yet come, verse 10, that is Spain, which for over seven hundred years was for the most part subject to the Saracens and Moors. And when he shall have come (that is, when he shall fully subject himself to the Church) he must remain a short time, that is, he will not remain long under Papal dominion. Concerning the eighth he truly says: He rules not only over the most flourishing regions, which they call the PATRIMONY OF PETER or STATIO DI CHIESA: But also over the whole of Calabria or the kingdom of Naples, which the Kings of Spain possess by the name of a fief from the Papal see.

Verse 10.

Οἱ πέντε ἔπεσον.] They perished by violence. For that is נָבַיל to the Hebrews, Exodus 32:28, Leviticus 16:8, Ezekiel 32:20, Hosea 7:7, 15, Psalm 91:6, and elsewhere. These five are Claudius, Nero, Galba, Otho, Vitellius. He begins from Claudius, because there is no notice of Christians under Tiberius and Gaius. And just as Ezekiel always reckons times from his deportation: so also John counts the Princes from his. Ὁ εἷς ἐστι.] Vespasian: concerning whom nothing evil is predicted, because he did not harm the Christians, as Tertullian testifies. Ὁ ἄλλος ὄπω ἦλθε.] Titus, whose face was likewise seen in the last head. Καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ.] Namely to the Principate, for that is ἕρ- χεσθαι here. He who begins some office is said ἕρχεσθαι, Matthew 17:18, and elsewhere. Ὀλίγον αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι.] He is to live for a short time after having attained the principate, namely two years and two months, as Suetonius notes. Δεῖ here is a note of the future, as in Matthew 17:18, and elsewhere.

Concerning these in the former commentary thus: Verse 10.

Οἱ πέντε ἔπεσον, five have fallen.] By violent death, of which it is properly said to fall. Claudius, Nero, Galba, Otho, Vitellius. Ὁ εἷς ἐστι, one is.) Vespasian was ruling when these things were written. Ὁ ἄλλος ὄπω ἦλθεν, and another has not yet come.) Titus Vespasianus. For ἔρχεσθαι signifies to begin one's office, as in Matthew 3:11, 17, and often elsewhere. Καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὀλίγον δεῖ αὐτὸν μεῖναι, and when he shall have come, he must remain a short time.) Δεῖ, it must, for the future, Matthew 17, v. 18, and often elsewhere. But Titus ruled only two years and two months, as Suetonius notes.

Five (Kings) have fallen, i.e., five kingdoms shall fail: Germany, Gaul, Britain, Poland, & Hungary. One, that is, one still remains, Italy, which entirely fosters the Papacy, and another has not yet come, Spain, to wit, overwhelmed by Saracen storms and subjected to the Mahometans, is not yet joined to the Pontifical kingdom, and when it shall have come, it must remain a short time, that is, it will not long adhere to the Papacy, either because it is to return to the Mahometan yoke by the just judgment of God, on account of the cruelty of the Spanish Inquisition; or because it too is to admit the doctrine of the Gospel purged of Papal corruptions. And the beast, that is, that Pontifical Monarchy in the Regions of the West, which was once the Roman empire, and is not, that is, it has lost the flower &c. Majesty of the first empire, and has been transformed into a new Hierarchy, ascends from the abyss. And he himself is the eighth and is of the seven heads, so he is an eighth thing, that he nevertheless subsists in those seven heads as if the one soul of them all, diffused through Italy, Spain, Gaul, Britain, Germany, Poland & Hungary, and goes into destruction, that is, is finally resolved by the voice of the Gospel into its beginnings, which is an elegant explanation of the blessed Phil. Nicolai, book 1, on the kingdom of Christ, chapter VIII, in the judgment of the blessed Gerhard to be preferred to the others. That hierarchical empire is truly an image both of the ancient empire and also of the modern one itself. For the kings represent the Cardinals, Princes, Bishops, Counts, Abbots, Barons, Priors, & Provosts, the equestrian order of Prelates: the Roman Pontiff as the supreme head, the Emperor, whose creatures they are. Kings have not yet received the kingdom, says St. John, who in his time was still ruled by the governors of the provinces, those ten powerful provinces: Germany, Bohemia, Hungary, Poland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Scotland, England, France. But they fought with the Lamb, because they opposed themselves to the Hierarchy, the Papal kingdom, & the doctrine of the Anti-Christ. And therefore, by the beast having seven heads and ten horns, it is not right to understand simply the Roman empire, but as it puts on the Papal Hierarchy. Nor is the destruction of the beast the destruction of the empire itself. For this, as the fourth and last Monarchy, lasts until the consummation of the age, Daniel II, 44. chap. VII, 9.

Latin:

Καὶ βασιλεῖς ἑπτά εἰσιν, & Reges septem sunt.) Non uno tempore visa, quæ in hoc libro comprehenduntur. Johanni paruere non magis quam Prophetis ea, quæ eorum libris continentur. Cœpit autem Johannes in Pathmo esse, & Dei visis illustrari Claudii temporibus, quæ vetustissimorumChri- stianorum est sententia, non Domitiani, ut voluere alii. Vi- de Epiphanium hæresi Alogorum. Claudius Judæos, sub quo- rum nomine tunc & Christiani censebantur, ut multis viris doctis observatum est, Roma pepulerat, Act. XVIII, 2. quod exemplum non dubium est, quin imitati sint multi Præsides Romanarum provinciarum, ita Epheso expulsus Johannes. Imperatores septem sunt Claudius, Nero, Galba, Ottho, Vi- tellius, Vespasianus, Titus. Scripta hæc Vespasiano impe- rante. Bene autem Imperatores Græce loquens βασιλέας vocat, quanquam Romani Regum vocabulo abstinebant.Res enim erat eadem. Appianus in præfatione: Καὶ ἔστιν ἥδε ἡ ἀρχὴ μέχρι νῦν ὑφ' ἑνὶ ἄρχοντι, ὃς βασιλέας μὲν ἐ λέγουσιν ὡς ἐ- γὼ νομίζω, τὸν ὅρκον αἰδόμενοι τὸν πάλαι, αὐτοκράτορας δὲ ὀνο- μάζουσιν, ὃ καὶ τῶν προσκαίρων στρατηγῶν ὄνομα ἦν, εἰσὶν ἔργα πάντα βασιλεῖς. Et est omne hoc imperium usque nunc sub uno Principe: Eos Principes Reges non appellant ob reverentiam, ut puto, jurisjurandi veteris, sed Imperatores, quæ & eorum, qui ad tempus exercitibus præerant, fuit appellatio: Revera autem Reges sunt. Erat enim Romanus Imperator, ut Dio- nis historicis verbis utar: Αὐτοτελὴς ὄντως καὶ αὐτοκράτωρ, καὶ ἑαυτῦ καὶ τῶν νόμων, πάντα τε ὅσα βύληται ποιῇ, καὶ πάνθ' ὅσα ἂν βύλοιτο μὴ πράττῃ, summo cum jure omninoque & sui & legum potens, ita, ut quæ velit, faciat omnia, & eorum, quæ non vult, faciat nihil.

De Domitiano hæc intelligere vetat Chrono- logia, quum series revelationis Johanneæ sit ob- servanda. Vetat & cæteroquin Historia. Clau- dii tempore Roma nondum Christianum san- guinem gustarat: Neronis vero nondum eo- dem penitus inebriata fuerat. Si à sua deportatio- ne numerat annos S. Johannes, à Domitiano de- buit ordiri. At hoc factum non est. Sub Ve- spasiano hæc visa & scripta esse ait Grotius. At pro- bare non potuit. Unius Epiphanii autoritas cæ- teris Patribus & Doctoribus præjudicare non po- test, Irenæo puta, Areta, Victorino, Eusebio, Hie- ronymo, aliis. Sub Tiberio nihil nocumenti al- latum fuisse Christianæ religioni temere afferi- tur. Sub ipso enim Stephanum lapidatum ait ipse Grotius, itaque vexatos tota Syria Christia- nos, ut nec in Macedonia tuti essent. Nec in- sontes hic Augustus & Tiberius, aut excusandi à persecutionibus Judæorum, quos infestavit qui- dem Claudius, sed non conversos ad Christum. Prima persecutio non Claudio sed Neroni ab omnibus adscribitur. Galba, Ottho, Vitellius, nihil durius statuisse in Christianos leguntur. Ve- spasianus autem restituit Capitolium, & spoliis templi ornavit, eoque multum obstitit religio- ni Christianæ, quin impense etiam addictus fuit Apollonio.

Si autem septem illi Reges septem Cæsares sunt, cur primus constituitur Claudius, omisso Tibe- rio, & Augusto? Septem capita & septem mon- tes Andrea sunt septem monarchiæ regna: Primum Assyriorum in Ninive, secundum Medorum in Ec- batanis sub Principe Arbace, tertium Chaldæorum in Babylone, quartum Cyri in Susis, quintum Alexandri in Macedonia, sextum Augusti & Impe- ratorum in Roma antiqua, septimum Constantini in nova & Christiana Roma. Consequenter septem Reges sunt primus Ninus, secundus Arbaces, ter- tius Nabuchodonosor, quartus Cyrus, quintus Alexander, sextus Augustus, septimus Constan- tinus. Verum hic montes cum Regibus confun- dit, qui distinguendi sunt. Ad hæc Constanti- num fidelem Ecclesiæ quasi nutritium ponit in- ter capita bestiæ. Cornelio à Lapide: Collectio tyrannorum, qui septem ætatibus sive seculis regnarunt in mundo, sive in regno impieta- tis & Diaboli, atque fideles & Ecclesiam per- secuti sunt. Ita Richardus, Ambrosius, Be- da & alii: ut patet ex sequentibus. Ait e- nim Johannes, quinque transiisse, sextum adhuc superesse, septimum expectari, & regnaturum per breve tempus. Primus ergo Rex est Cain cum gigantibus, aliisque similibus, qui fideles & pios persecuti sunt prima mundi ætate ab A- dam usque ad Noe & diluvium. Secundus est Nimrod cum fabris turris Babel in secun- da mundi ætate à Noe usque ad Abraham. Tertius sunt Reges Sodomæ & Pharaones Ægypti ante Mosen in tertia mundi ætate, quæ fuit ab Abraham ad Mosen. Quartus sunt impii Reges Israël & Juda cum aliis simi- libus, qui vixerunt à tempore Mosis usque ad captivitatem Babylonicam, quæ fuit quarta mundi ætas. Quintus sunt Chaldæorum Reges, ut Nabuchodonosor, ac Asiæ & Syriæ, ut Antiochus Epiphanes, aliique à captivitate Babylonica, us- que ad Christum, quæ fuit quinta mundi ætas. Sex- tus sunt Imperatores Ethnici Romani; Item Sara- ceni, Turcæ, aliique, qui à Christo usque ad Anti- christum fuerunt, sunt, & erunt. Unde de eo dici- tur hic: Unus adhuc est. Septimus est Anti-Chri- stus, qui venturus est, & per breve tempus, puta tres annos cum medio regnabit. Ita Gagnejus, Ribera & Viegas, qui asserit hanc esse communem expositionem. Accedit & Richardus cum suis, nisi quod ipse quartam ætatem consignet à Mose ad Davidem, quando fuerunt Balaam, Balac, Moa- bitæ, Idumæi, Philistæi & similes hostes populi Dei, puta Israëlitis, quintam vero designat a Davide usque ad Christum. In quibus itidem desideran- dum, quod Constantinus M. Carolus M. alii- que Christiani Reges & Imperatores capitibus bestiæ annumerentur, quodque tot capita ad præ- cedentia tempora trahantur. Id tamen veri sub- est, quod Papa unus è septem capitibus & tamen octavus dicatur, Prospero Autore in Sim. temp. c. 8. & Haymone, qui septies, inquit de Rom. Pontifice, amplius dominabitur, ac persequetur Ecclesiam, quam reliqui omnes superiores tyranni, Monarcha omnium præcedentium: quod ex asse in Rom. An- ti-Christo impletum. Rectius itaque dicitur septem regiminis for- mas intelligi, quarum jam præterierant quinque, sexta Cæsarum sive Imperatorum tum obtinebat, septima brevi admodum duratura sub Odoacro, suo tempore erat sequutura. Et quì dicatur ali- quis fuisse nec esse absolute, eo quod imperii au- toritate antea precario exercita, & postea cum plenissimo jure resumenda ad tempus abstinue- rit? Ideo Maresius in dissert. pag. 173. Bestia hæc non idololatria, non Magia, non Trajanus, uti vi- detur Piscator suspicari, non Domitianus, sed Ro- manum imperium. Ea quodam sensu dicitur Jo- hanni fuisse, nec amplius esse, & tamen adhuc esse; quia scilicet hic Roma consideratur sub ipsius An- ti-Christi & Romani Pontificis imperio, sub quo non est amplìus idem, quod olim, imperium mere politicum; sed tamen idem est, quoad imitationem & similitudinem, quatenus secunda bestia imagi- nem fabricata est prioris, & tandem adorandam populis proposuit. Ideo hæc bestia dicitur esse Re- gum octavus, & per consequens quasi octavum ca- put prioris, quia Pontifex Romanus, cujus triplex corona, II. Regno, Italis dicitur, ipse à nonnullis Italiæ Rex octavam regiminis formam prioribus septem plane dissimilem Romæ intulit. Ideo hic ὄγδοος dicitur, octavus ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ex septem, non quia Domitianus unus ex septem illis, Vespasiani scilicet, filius erat, sed quod regimen Papale non mi- nus sit in bestia priore quoad autoritatem, quam unum ex septem prioribus, & quod favore & bene- ficiis Imperatorum jam ad fidem Christianam con- versorum ad hunc gradum excreverit dignitas Pontificum. Confer. de septem formis imperii B. Cluverus, & quomodo Cornelio hic respon- deat & Eclino per sextum caput Julianum Apo- statam, per octavum faciem imperii illam, quæ cœpit post Constantinum M. intelligenti satis- faciat, invenies. Addit has conclusiones: Nul- lus Dominus Urbis Romanæ post imperium sana- tum fuit, nisi Papa, Octavus ergo Rex ipse. Octa- vus autem Rex caput ipsissimum bestiæ est, à Jo- hanne descriptæ, quæ bestia Anti-Christus. Ergo Papa Anti-Christus. Altera: Anti-Christus non est persona singularis. Quales enim Reges fuerunt septem illi priores, talis etiam octavus, cum de si- milibus idem judicium sit. At illi non fuerunt sin- gulares personæ aut individua, sed status Regii, talis ergo & Anti-Christus. Est autem octavus & tamen est de septem. Papa enim non est Imperator proprie, nec caput imperii Romani legitimum: Et tamen caput est, & Imperatore superior. Nostræ sententiæ accedit B. Gravius; Per bestiam intel- ligitur ipsum Anti-Christi regnum in VII. pro- vinciis occidentalis imperii post desolationem Ur- bis Romæ per barbaras gentes ortum, quod qui- dem in summo FUIT vigore, sed reformationis be- neficio, ministerio B. Lutheri facta, ESSE DESIIT, hoc est post desectionem 5. capitum, nudam tantum IMAGINEM BESTIÆ repræsentat. Re- spicit ergo hic Angelus Interpres ad ultima refor- mationis tempora, quibus bestia Papalis pristinam suam potentiam & florem amisit. Dicit enim ex- presse vers. 10. quinque capita cecidisse, id quod de reformatione intelligendum esse dubitari non de- bet. Et alius nondum venit vers. 10. hoc est Hispa- nia, quæ ultra septingentos annos maximam par- tem subjecta fuit Saracenis & Mauris. Et cum venerit (hoc est, quando plenarie sese Ecclesiæ subji- ciet) oportet illum breve tempus manere, hoc est, sub dominio Papali non diu manebit. De octavo vere inquit: Imperat non tantum florentissimis re- gionibus, quas PATRIMONIUM PETRI seu STATIO DI CHIESA vocant: Sed etiam toti Ca- labriæ seu regno Neapolitano, quod feudi nomine Re- ges Hispaniarum à sede Papali possident.

Vers. 10.

Οἱ πέντε ἔπεσον.] Vi periere. Id enim נָבַיל Ebræis, Ex- odi 32, 28. Lev. XVI, 8. Ezech. 32, 20. Oseæ 7,7.15. Psalm. 91,6. & alibi. Hi quinque sunt Claudius, Nero, Galba, Ottho, Vitellius. Incipit à Claudio, quia Tiberio & Cajo nulla notitia Christianorum. Et sicut Ezechiel semper tempora putat à sua deportatione: ita & Johannes à sua numerat Principes. Ὁ εἷς ἐστι.] Vespasianus: de quo nihil mali prædicitur, quia Christianis non nocuit, teste Tertulliano. Ὁ ἄλλος ὄπω ἦλθε.] Titus, cujus facies itidem in capite ul- timo conspiciebatur. Καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ.] Nempe ad Principatum, id enim hic ἕρ- χεσθαι. Qui munus aliquod auspicatur, dicitur ἕρχεσθαι Matth. 17, 18. & alibi. Ὀλίγον αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι.] Exiguo tempore victurus est post adeptum principatum, biennio scilicet & mensibus duobus, ut notat Suetonius. Δεῖ hic nota futuri, ut Matth. 17,18. & alibi.

De his in priori commentatione ita: Vers. 10.

Οἱ πέντε ἔπεσον, quinque ceciderunt.] Morte violenta, de qua proprie dicitur cadere. Claudius, Nero, Galba, Ottho, Vitellius. Ὁ εἷς ἐστι, unus est.) Vespasianus imperabat, cum hæc scri- berentur. Ὁ ἄλλος ὄπω ἦλθεν, & alius nondum venit.) Titus Vespa- sianus. Nam ἔρχεσθαι significat munus suum auspicari, ut Matth. III, 11. 17. & alibi sæpe. Καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὀλίγον δεῖ αὐτὸν μεῖναι, & cum venerit, opor- tet illum breve tempus manere.) Δεῖ oportet pro futuro, Matth. 17. v. 18. & alibi sæpe. Imperavit autem Titus biennium tan- tum, & menses duos, ut notat Suetonius.

Quinque (Reges) ceciderunt, h. e. quinque regna deficient: Germania, Gallia, Britannia, Po- lonia, & Hungaria. Unus, id est, una adhuc super- est Italia, quæ tota Papatum fovet, & alius non- dum venit, Hispania, sc. Saracenicis procellis ob- ruta, & Mahumetaris subjecta, regno Pontifi- cio nondum est agglutinata, & cum venerit, oportet illum breve tempus manere, id est, non diu adherebit Papatui, sive quod reditura sit ad ju- gum Mahumeticum ex justo Dei judicio, ob cru- delitatem inquisitionis Hispanicæ; sive quod ipsa quoque doctrinam Evangelii à Papalibus cor- ruptelis repurgatam sit religionem admissura. Et bestia, id est, Monarchia illa Pontificia in Regio- nibus Occidentis, quæ erat Romanum quondam imperium, & non est, id est, amisit primi imperii florem &c. Majestatem, & in novam Hierarchi- am est transformata de abysso ascendit. Et ipse est octavus & de septem est capitibus, ita octavum quid est, ut tamen in septenis illis capitibus tan- quam una omnium anima subsistat, diffusa per Italiam, Hispaniam, Galliam, Britanniam, Ger- maniam, Poloniam & Hungariam, & in interi- tum vadit, id est, Evangelii voce in sua primor- dia tandem resolvitur, quæ elegans explicatio est B. Phil. Nicolai l. 1. de regn. Christi cap. VIII. judicio B. Gerhardi cæteris præferenda. Hie- rarchicum illud imperium vere imago tan- tum est imperii veteris, tum etiam ipsius moderni. Reges enim referunt Cardina- les, Principes, Episcopi, Comites, Abbates, Barones, Priores, & Præpositi, equestrem ordinem Præla- ti: Summum caput Imperatorem Pontifex Roma- nus, cujus illi creaturæ sunt. Reges nondum ac- cepisse regnum, dicit S. Johannes, qui ejus tempo- re per Præsides provinciarum decem illæ potentes provinciæ adhuc regebantur Germania, Bohemia, Hungaria, Polonia, Suecia, Dania, Norwegia, Scotia, Anglia, Francia. Pugnarunt autem cum Agno, quia pro Hierarchia, Papali regno, & do- ctrinæ Anti-Christi se opposuerunt. Ideoque per bestiam septem capita & cornua decem haben- tem non fas est simpliciter intelligere Romanum imperium, sed qua Hierarchiam Papalem indu- it. Neque bestiæ interitus est imperii ipsius in- teritus. Hæc enim ceu quarta & ultima Monar- chia durat usque ad consummationem seculi, Da- nielis II, 44. cap. VII, 9.

## 17:11
Vers. 11.

Καὶ τὸ θηρίον.) The mouth of the beast. A synecdoche, as we have said. That mouth had leonine teeth. Seneca and the Apostle Paul called Nero a Lion. Domitian was called a Bald Nero: a portion of Nero regarding cruelty in the Apologeticus of Tertullian.

Ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστι καὶ αὐτὸς ὄγδοός ἐστι.) The final καὶ is redundant here, in the Hebrew manner. He whom I said was the mouth of the beast is the eighth in the order of Princes who had dealings with the Christians.

Καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστι.) He was born from one of those seven whom I mentioned, namely from Vespasian. Ἐκ or ἐξ is accustomed to be used in signifying the origin of someone, as Matt. 1, 3. 5. 6. Luke 1, 27. John 1, 3. Acts 17, 26. Rom. 1, 3. chap. 9, 10. 2 Tim. 8, 2. Heb. 7, 8. above 7, 4. and following. Furthermore, ἐκ τῶν is said briefly for ἐκ τινῶν τῶν, concerning which manner of speaking we have dealt with at Matt. 23, 34. Luke 22, 16.

Καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει.) He will perish by an evil death. The present for the future in the prophetic manner.

We add what it has in the prior treatment: Vers. 11.

Καὶ τὸ θηρίον, & the beast.) Θηρίον in this place is the Emperor with a beastly nature, namely Domitian. Thus Nero is called a Lion in 2 Tim. 4, 7, of whom Seneca had said that it would not be the case for that savage lion, once the blood of a man had been tasted, that his innate savagery would not return, as the Scholiast narrates on Juvenal's fifth Satire. Octavia in the tragedy of her name: I shall overcome the savage lions and fierce tigers before the beast, which is the heart of a cruel tyrant. Indeed, the Hebrews also understand Nebuchadnezzar by the name of a lion at Amos V. Domitian, however, is so similar to Nero that he was called a Bald Nero at Rome: a portion of Nero regarding cruelty in Tertullian's Apologeticus. Zeno in the Lion Iconoclast: Τὸ γὰρ θηρίον βασιλέα δηλοῖ, the beast signifies the Emperor. Eminently, however, θηρίον and fera in Latin is a Lion. Elsewhere θηρίον in this book is the idolatry of the Roman empire raging in the manner of a beast: but it is not surprising in figurative and especially prophetic locutions that the same words are not taken in the same meaning.

Ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστι, which was, and is not.) Repeated from the eighth verse. Domitian, with his father absent through Syria and Egypt, had exercised all the force of domination at Rome, to speak with Suetonius. Tacitus about that time: Domitian had received the name and seat of Caesar. Afterwards: Vespasian receives adverse rumor about Domitian, as if he were exceeding the limits of his age and what was granted to a son. Dio adds: Ὥστε τὸν Οὐεσπασιανὸν ἐπιστεῖλαί ποτε τῷ υἱῷ Δομιτιανῷ, ὅτι χάριν ἔχω σοι τέκνον, ὅτι με ἐᾷς ἄρχειν, καὶ οὐδέπω με καταλέλυκας : So that Vespasian wrote at one time to his son Domitian: I give thanks to you, son, that you allow me to be Prince, and have not yet deposed me. Suetonius: Having attained the principate, he did not hesitate to boast in the senate that he had given the empire to his father and brother, and they had returned it to him. To this pertains that flattery of Martial applied to the character of the master: When he alone already held the Julian reins, he handed them over, and was third in his own world. See also Josephus at the end of the fourth book of the Jewish War. Therefore ἦν, Domitian had been master of affairs, with his father absent. Καὶ οὐκ ἔστι, and is not, while John writes these things, for having been reduced to the manner of a private citizen by his father, he feigned modesty and especially a study of poetry, as we learn from Suetonius. Tacitus hist.

IV. Domitianus: Seeing his youth despised by the elders, he omitted even the moderate and previously usurped duties of the empire, hidden in the height by an image of simplicity and modesty: and feigning a study of letters and a love of poems, by which he might veil his mind, and be withdrawn from the emulation of his brother.

And he himself is the eighth, and he is the eighth.) By Claudius, when those things which John writes began to be seen.

And he is of the seven.) It is a curtailed expression for 'he is of some of the seven.' Thus John 16:17. 'I said, then, of the disciples,' supply 'some.' Matt. 23:34. 'And of them you will kill and crucify, and of them you will scourge,' where 'some' is twice missing. Luke 21:15. 'They will put to death some of you.' Domitian was one of those seven, namely the son of Vespasian. Moreover, the word in that sense is frequent, as Matt. 1:3, 5, 6. Luke 1:27. John 1:13. Acts 17:26. Rom. 1:3, ch. 9:10, ch. 2:8. Heb. 7:8. Rev. 7:4, and following.

Brightman has it thus concerning these: The Roman Empire was first most powerful and most flourishing; but afterwards it was devastated and dissipated by the Goths, Vandals, Lombards, Alemanni, Franks, Burgundians, English, and Huns, and thus ceased to be, if you look at its former Majesty. At length, healed again by the zeal of Leo the Great, it grew into a Papal empire, which is the eighth form of government, which itself must at length go into destruction. Others, whom Grotius followed in part, understand by those seven Kings and the eighth who is to come, the Emperors who held power in the time of John. Nero, however, cast such a stain upon the kingdom by his cruelty that you would have said that, as far as he was concerned, it had perished. Five Caesars followed him in the time of John, namely Galba, Otho, Vitellius, Vespasian, Titus, who all fell in the age of John, and ONE IS, namely Domitian, under whom John, having been relegated to Patmos, received the Apocalypse. AND ANOTHER HAS NOT YET COME, this is Nerva, who reigns for only one year, and adopted Trajan, through whom the empire was transferred to foreigners, who, together with the remaining seven predecessor Emperors, persecuted the Christians and at length went into destruction. But the same judgment can be passed on this exposition as we previously passed on the Grotian one, and will still pass in the following.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

Καὶ τὸ θηρίον.) Os feræ. Συνεκδοχὴ ut diximus. Os illud dentes habebat leoninos. Seneca & Paulus Apostolus Neronem Leonem dixere. Domitianus dictus Calvus Nero: Portio Neronis de crudelitate in Apologetico Tertul- liani.

Ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστι καὶ αὐτὸς ὄγδοός ἐστι.) Καὶ postremum hic abundat, more Ebræo. Is quem feræ os esse dixi, est octavus in ordine Principum, quibus res fuit cum Christianis.

Καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστι.) Natus est ex uno illorum septem, quos dixi, nempe ex Vespasiano. Ἐκ vel ἐξ poni solet in signifi- canda alicujus origine, ut Matth. 1, 3. 5. 6. Luc. 1, 27. Johan. 1, 3. Act. 17, 26. Rom. 1, 3. cap. 9, 10. 2. Tim. 8, 2. Ebr. 7, 8. supra 7, 4. & sequentibus. Deinde ἐκ τῶν breviter dictum pro ἐκ τι- νῶν τῶν, de quo loquendi genere egimus ad Matth. 23, 34. Luc. 22, 16.

Καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει.) Mala morte peribit. Præsens pro futuro more prophetico.

Addimus, quæ in priori tractatione habet: Vers. 11.

Καὶ τὸ θηρίον, & bestia.) Θηρίον hoc loco est Imperator ferino ingenio, Domitianus scilicet. Sic Nero Leo dicitur 2. Tim. 4, 7. de quo Seneca dixerat, non fore sævo illi leoni, quin gustato semel hominis cruore ingenita rediret sævitia, ut nar- rat ad Juvenalis Satyram quintam Scholiastes. Octavia in tragœdia sui nominis: Vincam sævos Ante leones tigresque truces Fera, quam sævi corda tyranni. Nempe & Ebræi leonis nomine apud Amos. V. Nabucho- donosorem intelligunt. Domitianus autem ita Neroni si- milis, ut Calvus Nero Romæ dictus sit: portio Neronis de crudelitate Tertulliano in Apologetico. Zeno in Leone Iconomacho: Τὸ γὰρ θηρίον βασιλέα δηλοῖ, bestia Imperato- rem significat. Eminenter autem θηρίον & fera Latine est Leo. Alibi θηρίον in hoc libro est idololatria Romani impe- rii feræ more sæviens: sed non mirum in figuratis ac prophe- ticis maxime locutionibus voces easdem non eodem sumi si- gnificatu.

Ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστι, quæ erat, & non est.) Repetita ex versu octavo. Domitianus Patre per Syriam & Ægyptum absente omnem vim dominationis exercuerat Romæ, ut cum Sueto- nio loquar. Tacitus de eo tempore: Nomen sedemque Cæsa- ris Domitianus acceperat. Postea: Vespasianus adversam de Domitiano famam accipit, tanquam terminos ætatis & conces- sa filio egrederetur. Addit Dion: Ὥστε τὸν Οὐεσπασιανὸν ἐπιστεῖλαί ποτε τῷ υἱῷ Δομιτιανῷ, ὅτι χάριν ἔχω σοι τέκνον, ὅτι με ἐᾷς ἄρχειν, καὶ οὐδέπω με καταλέλυκας : Ita, ut Vespasianus filio Domitiano scripserit aliquando: Gratias tibi, fili, habeo, quod me sinis esse Principem, nec mihi imperium abstulisti. Sue- tonius: Principatum vero adeptus neque in senatu jactare dubitavit, & Patri se & fratri imperium dedisse, illos sibi red- didisse. Huc illa pertinet Martialis ad ingenium Domini ap- posita adulatio: Solus Julæas cum jam retineret habenas Tradidit, inque suo tertius orbe fuit. Vide & Josephum fine libri quarti de bello Judaico. Er- go ἦν fuerat Domitianus rerum compos, absente Patre. Καὶ οὐκ ἔστι & non est, dum hæc scribit Johannes, nam in privati modum redactus à patre modestiam imprimisque Poëticæ studium simulabat, ut ex Suetonio discimus. Tacitus hist.

IV. Domitianus: Sperni à Senioribus juventam suam cernens modica quoque & usurpata antea munia imperii omittebat, simplicitatis ac modestiæ imagine in altitudinem conditus: stu- diumque literarum & amorem carminum simulans, quo ve- laret animum, & fratris æmulationi subduceretur.

Καὶ ἀυτὸς ὄγδοός ἐστι, & ipse octavus est.) A Claudio, cum videri cœpta, quæ Johannes scribit.

Καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστιν, & de septem est.) Est loquutio cur- tata pro ἐκ τινῶν τῶν ἑπτά ἐστι. Sic Johannes XVI, 17. Εἶπον ἦν ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν supple τινες Matth. XXIII, 34. Ἐξ ἀυτῶν ἀ- ποκτενεῖτε καὶ ςαυρώσετε, καὶ ἐξ ἀυτῶν μασιγώσετε, ubi bis de- est τινας. Luc. XXI, 15. θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν. Erat Domitia- nus unius septem illorum Vespasiani nimirum filius. Vox autem in illo sensu est frequens, ut Matth. 1, 3. 5. 6. Luc. 1, 27. Joh. 1, 13. Act. 17, 26. Rom. 1, 3. c. 9, 10. c. 2, 8. Ebr. 7, 8. Apoc. 7, 4. & seqq.

Brightmannus de his ita habet: Imperium Ro- manum erat primum potentissimum & florentissi- mum; postea vero à Gothis, Vandalis, Longobardis, Alemannis, Francis, Burgundis, Anglis, & Hun- nis vastatum ac dissipatum fuit, sicque esse desiit, si pristinam ejus Majestatem spectes. Tandem iterum sanatum studio Leonis M. evasit in impe- rium Papale, quæ est octava regiminis forma, quam ipsam tandem in interitum abire necesse est. Alii, quos ex parte sequutus est Grotius, per se- ptem illos Reges, & Octavum venturum intelli- gunt Imperatores, qui tempore Johannis rerum potiti sunt. Nero autem maximam crudelitate sua regno maculam adspersit, ut quantum ad ipsum illud intercidisse dixisses. Hunc sequuti sunt quinque Cæsares tempore Johannis, videli- cet Galba, Ottho, Vitellius, Vespasianus, Titus, qui omnes Johannis ætate ceciderunt, & UNUS EST, nempe Domitianus, sub quo Johannes in Pathmum relegatus Apocalypsin accepit. ET ALIUS NONDUM VENIT, hic est Nerva, qui uno duntaxat anno regnat, & adoptavit Traja- num, per quem ad extraneos imperium est trans- latum, qui una cum reliquis septem Imperato- ribus Antecessoribus Christianos persecutus in interitum tandem abiit. Verum idem ferri ju- dicium de hac expositione potest, quod de Gro- tiana antea tulimus, & in sequentibus adhuc fe- remus.

## 17:12
Ver. 12.

And the ten horns, which you saw.) Namely, in this last vision. For other kings had been signified in the vision of chapter 13. But as they had shown reverence to the Roman empire, so also will these show it, in their own time.

Ten kings they are.) He calls successions of kings 'kings,' as in Dan. 7:17 in the Hebrew and 8:20, as Jerome noted there. So also Jer. 25:11.

Who have not yet received a kingdom.) Namely, in the parts of the Roman empire.

But they receive authority as kings for one hour with the beast.) At the same time they will receive kingdoms within the limits of the Roman empire, and will embrace Roman rites. But for a short time. For that is what 'one hour' means. This is repeated in this sense in the Greek of Dan. 4:6, where in the Chaldean it is 'in one hour.' For the same thing Paul said 'for an hour' in Philemon 15, 'for a season of an hour,' 1 Thess. 2:17. And thus Andreas and Arethas explain this passage. So also below 18:17.

These things thus before:

Ver. 12.

And the horns which you saw are ten kings.) Horns are the weapons of rams, bulls, and other animals. Thus those kings were instruments of Roman power. It was the accepted custom of the Roman people, says Tacitus in the life of his father-in-law, to have even kings as instruments of servitude.

Οἵτινες βασιλείαν ὔπω ἔλαβον, who have not yet received the kingdom.) Namely in the parts of the Roman empire.

Ἀλλ' ἐξουσίαν ὡς βασιλεῖς μίαν ὥραν λαμβάνουσι μετὰ τῶ θη- ρίου, but they will receive power as Kings for one hour with the beast.] Within the borders of the Roman empire, they will reign with the Romans themselves conceding. Μίαν ὥραν one hour, that is, πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας for a time of an hour, as 1 Thess. II, 17 πρὸς ὥραν for an hour, Philem. 15. For to speak with Lucan: Let there not be discordant concord of narrow time.

As the ten horns of the former beast denoted the ten primary provinces of the Roman Empire, a certain number for an uncertain: So those ten Kings denote those who, in those provinces, the empire having already been overthrown, were to obtain Royal authority with the Roman Pontiff, and were to enter into a most strict alliance with him: not for a short time, as that man wishes, but for one hour, as the Vulgate Interpreter well says: as if John were saying, at nearly the same time that the Roman Pontiff will begin, after the empire is overturned, to establish his own authority, in that same empire, out of its former provinces, various kingdoms will come to be, which will defer all obedience to the Roman see, will communicate their counsels with it, and will hang upon its nod, and will destine all their forces to defending, strengthening, and promoting it out of a preposterous zeal for religion. One must be entirely a stranger to history who does not yet know the effects and fulfillment of this prophecy, as Maresius has it here, to which we append his own refutation in the dissertation, so that it may be permitted to proceed to examine the Appendix, opposed to the dissertation in the discordant concord, or discussed in the Revealed Anti-Christ: Here again, says the Commentator, he fashions dreams for himself, he posits that the ten Kings were Goths, and the peoples allied with them, who at that time indeed had not yet received a kingdom in parts of the Roman empire, but afterwards within the borders of the empire, with the Romans conceding, were to reign, but for a short time, because that concord by which they were allied to the Romans was not long-lasting. But first, if this beast, with which those ten Kings were to receive their dominion, is Domitian, as the Commentator was already interpreting, the Goths and their allies cannot be those Kings, since the alliance of the first Goths with the Romans was made only in the time of Maximian, as he himself notes from Jornandes. Furthermore, these peoples or Kings cannot be said to have ever been horns or arms of Roman power, as our author interprets, since they were not received into the society of the empire except after various disasters inflicted upon the empire, so much so that, reigning within the borders of the Empire, they did not reign with the Caesars, as Tatius once did with Romulus, but in a certain way over them, and finally overturned all their authority. These were strange horns of Roman power, by which it was not promoted, but removed and destroyed: So far is it from the case that they gave their power and virtue to the empire to fight for it with unanimous consent, that on the contrary they never deployed their forces except against the empire itself and for its ruin. I add that what he had noted concerning the devastation of the empire at Matt. XXIV, 19 does not agree with these. For the names there are different and they are called foreign nations, and conquered by Christ, or converted to Christ. The things which are disputed in the Appendix of Grotius and the discordant concord of Maresius do not contribute much to the sense of the Apocalypse, and can be read there, refuted primarily by Maresius, therefore we omit them. Horns are fixed and glued to heads, but they do not rule the beast itself, or immediately encompass its life, but insofar as they are on the head, they defend, protect, adorn, and fight for the whole body, each in its own place, says B. Cluverus. How aptly these things fit the mystical horns no one fails to see. Concerning the Preposition μετὰ, B. Cluverus has it thus: In the source it is μετὰ τῶ θηρίω, not μετὰ τὸ θηρίον. And therefore the Vulgate Interpreter translates wrongly, after the beast, since μετὰ does not signify after when joined to the second case. Οὗτοι μίαν γνώμην ἔχουσι καὶ τὴν δύναμιν, καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἑυτω̃ν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασι.] With the custom of the Roman people received, that it might have instruments of servitude and Kings, as Tacitus speaks in the life of his father-in-law. Lucan: And wherever the purple serves the sword in all Latium. They will confer, he says, their forces and the right of empire to this end, that they may serve both the Romans and their religion. The Goths were the first of all to become allies of the Romans. Procopius teaches us this in Gothic War IV, before the times of Maximin, as we learn from Jornandes. But those ten barbarian Kings, who were in reverence of the Roman Empire for a short time, are the Ostrogoths: Visigoths: Vandals: Gepidae: Lombards: Heruli: Burgundians: Huns: Franks: English or Saxons. All these held kingdoms within the ancient borders of the Roman empire, as you may learn from Procopius, Jornandes, Orosius, Paul the Deacon. The Visigoths were present for the Romans against Attila: the Ostrogoths against the Heruli: the Vandals against the Suebi, the Gepidae against those Heruli I mentioned, and against the Ostrogoths: the Lombards against the Gepidae, then against the Ostrogoths and Franks: the Heruli against the Pesi, then against the Vandals: the Burgundians against the Franks and against the Ostrogoths: the Franks against the Ostrogoths and Visigoths and Suebi, the Anglo-Saxons against the Picts and Britons.

These things thus before: Vers. 23.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

Καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα, ἃ εἶδες.) Nempe in hoc viso postremo. Alii enim Reges significati erant in viso cap. 13. Sed ut illi reverentiam exhibuerant Romano imperio, ita & hi exhibe- bunt, suo tempore.

Δέκα βασιλεῖς εἰσι.) Successiones Regum Reges vocat, ut Dan. 7, 17 in Ebræo & 8, 20. ut ibi annotavit Hieronymus. Sic & Jerem. 25, 11.

Οἵτινες βασιλείαν ὔπω ἔλαβον.) Nempe in partibus Roma- ni imperii.

Ἀλλὰ ἐξουσίαν ὡς βασιλεῖς μίαν ὥραν λαμβάνουσι μετὰ τῶ θη- ρίου.) Simul & regna accipient intra Romani imperii limites, & Romana sacra amplectentur. Sed ad modicum tempus. Id enim vult μίαν ὥραν. Repetitur hoc sensu in Græco Dan. 4, 6. ubi in Chaldaico בשעה חדא. Pro eodem dixit Paulus πρὸς ὥραν Philem. 15. πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας, 1. Thessal. 2. vers. 17. Et ita hunc locum explicant Andreas & Arethas. Sic & in- fra 18, 17.

Hæc ita prius :

Vers. 12.

Καὶ τὰ κέρατα ἃ εἶδες δέκα βασιλεῖς εἰσιν, & decem cornua, quæ vidisti, decem Reges sunt.) Cornua sunt arma arietum, taurorum, aliorumque animantium. Sic isti Reges instrumen- ta erant potentiæ Romanæ. Recepta populi Romani consue- tudine, ait in soceri vita Tacitus, ut haberet instrumenta ser- vitutis & Reges.

Οἵτινες βασιλείαν ὔπω ἔλαβον, qui regnum nondum accepe- runt.) Nempe in partibus imperii Romani.

Ἀλλ' ἐξουσίαν ὡς βασιλεῖς μίαν ὥραν λαμβάνουσι μετὰ τῶ θη- ρίου, sed potestatem tanquam Reges accipient una hora cum bestia.] Intra fines imperii Romani, Romanis ipsis con- cedentibus regnabunt. Μίαν ὥραν una hora, id est, πρὸς και- ρὸν ὥρας ad tempus horæ, ut 1.Thess. II, 17. πρὸς ὥραν ad ho- ram, Philem. 15. Nam ut cum Lucano loquar: Temporis angusti non sit concordia discors.

Ut decem cornua prioris bestiæ decem primarias Romani Imperii provincias denotabant, numero certo pro incerto: Sic decem isti Reges eos deno- tant, qui in illis provinciis subruto jam imperio Regiam autoritatem erant adepturi cum Pontifi- ce Romano, atque cum illo fœdus arctissimum ini- turi: non ad breve tempus, ut iste vult, sed una ho- ra, ut bene Vulgatus Interpres: ac si diceret Johan- nes, ferme eodem tempore, quo Pontifex Romanus incipiet post eversum imperium suam autorita- tem stabilire, in eodem imperio, ex illius antea pro- vinciis, fient varia regna, quæ sedi Romanæ omne deferent obsequium, cum illa consilia sua commu- nicabunt, & ex illius nutu pendebunt, omnesque vires suas ei defendendæ, firmandæ, promovendæ ex zelo religionis præpostero destinabunt. Omnino peregrinum esse oportet in historia, qui hujus va- ticinii effecta & complementum adhuc nesciat, ut hic habet Maresius, quibus subjicimus ejusdem elenchum in dissert. ut ad Appendicem dispi- ciendam progredi liceat, dissertationi oppositam in concordia discorde, vel Anti-Christo Revelato discussam: Hic iterum, inquit, Commentator sibi somnia fingit, decem Reges statuit Gothos fuisse, & illis fœderatos populos, qui tunc quidem in parti- bus imperii Romani regnum nondum acceperant, sed postea intra fines imperii, concedentibus Roma- nis erant regnaturi, sed brevi tempore, quod non fuerit diuturna concordia illa, qua Romanis fue- runt fœderati. Sed primo si bestia hæc, cum qua decem illi Reges erant suam dominationem acce- pturi, Domitianus est, ut jam Commentator inter- pretabatur, non possunt Gothi eorumque fœdera- ti isti Reges esse, cum primorum Gothorum fœdus cum Romanis factum fuerit demum Maximiani tempore, ut ipse annotat ex Jornande. Præterea non possunt dici hi populi vel Reges unquam fuis- se cornua sive arma Romanæ potentiæ, ut interpre- tatur noster, cum in societatem imperii recepti non fuerint, nisi post varias clades illatas imperio, adeo, ut intra fines Imperii regnantes non regnaverint cum Cæsaribus, ut quondam Tatius cum Romulo, sed quodammodo in illos, & eorum tandem autori- tatem omnem everterint. Mira hæc erant cornua potentiæ Romanæ, quibus non promota, sed remota & destructa fuit: Tantum abest, ut suam poten- tiam & virtutem dederint imperio unanimi con- sensu pro illo pugnaturi, ut è contra nunquam vi- res suas expedierint, nisi adversus ipsummet impe- rium & in illius ruinam. Addo quod quæ de va- statione imperii annotarat ad Matth. XXIV, 19. hisce non conveniant. Nam & nomina ibi di- versa & gentes exteræ dicuntur, & devictæ à Chri- sto, vel ad Christum conversæ. Quæ in Append. Grotii & concord. disc. Maresii disputantur, non multum ad Apocalypseos sensum faciunt, ibi- que legi possunt, refutata imprimis à Maresio, ideo illa mittimus. Cornua capitibus infixa & agglutinata sunt, non autem ipsam feram regunt, aut vitam ejus immediate complectuntur, sed quatenus sunt in capite, defendunt, tuentur, or- nant & propugnant corpus universum, quodlibet suo loco, inquit B. Cluverus. Quæ quam apte cornibus mysticis conveniant nemo non videt. De Præpositione μετὰ ita habet B. Cluverus: In fonte est μετὰ τῶ θηρίω non μετὰ τὸ θηρίον. Ac proinde perperam vertit Vulgatus Interpres, post bœ- bestiam, cum μετὰ non significet post, secundo casui junctum. Οὗτοι μίαν γνώμην ἔχουσι καὶ τὴν δύναμιν, καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἑυτω̃ν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασι.] Recepta populi Romani consuetu- dine, ut haberet instrumenta servitutis & Reges, ut Tacitus loquitur in Soceri vita. Lucanus: Atque omni Latio qua servit purpura ferro. Vires, inquit, suas & jus imperii eo conferent, ut & Ro- manis & eorum religioni inserviant. Primi omnium Gothi facti sunt fœderati Romanorum. Docet id nos Procopius Gothicorum IV. ante tempora Maximini, ut ex Jornande discimus. Decem autem illi Reges barbari, qui in reverentia fuere Romani Imperii ob breve tempus sunt Ostrogothi: Wi- sigothi: Vandali: Gepidæ: Longobardi: Heruli: Burgun- diones: Hunni: Franci: Angli sive Saxones. Hi omnes re- gna habuere intra fines veteres Romani imperii, ut ex Proco- pio, Jornande, Orosio, Paulo Diacono discas. Wisigothi contra Attilam Romanis adfuere: contra Herulos Ostrogo- thi: contra Suevos Wandali, contra eos, quos dixi Herulos, Gepidæ, & contra Ostrogothos: Longobardi contra Gepi- das, deinde contra Ostrogothos & Francos: Heruli contra Pesas, deinde contra Wandalos: Burgundiones contra Fran- cos & contra Ostrogothos: Franci contra Ostrogothos & Wisigothos & Suevos, Anglosaxones contra Pictos & Brit- tones.

Hæc ita prius: Vers. 23.

## 17:13
Οὗτοι γνώμην μίαν ἔχουσι καὶ τὴν δύναμιν καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἀνα τῶν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασι, these have one counsel, and will hand over their virtue and power to the beast.) The Goths were the first to become allies of the Roman Empire. Thence both the name and the thing passed to other peoples. Procopius teaches us this in Gothic War IV. Among the same Procopius you will find these allied peoples: the Ostrogoths, Visigoths, Vandals, Gepidae, Lombards, Heruli, Burgundians, Huns, Franks, Anglo-Saxons.

By what reason the Northern peoples, the Goths, Vandals, Gepidae, Lombards, Heruli, Burgundians, Huns, Franks, Anglo-Saxons, were of one mind, I do not see. For even if by chance they are called allies by Procopius, certainly these alliances must have been entered into only after the ruin of the empire, or toward it, but not so that they ever conspired together or separately to preserve its dignity. Nor will his number ten hold here, since the Ostrogoths and Visigoths did not constitute two peoples at the beginning, and more could be added, such as the Rugi, Turcilingi, Alani, Thuringi, and many other barbarian nations, some of which are named by Paul the Deacon in History of the Lombards. Book I. Chapter I. They yield their power and the sinews of their kingdoms for the most part to the Roman Pontiff, by choosing Cardinals, Bishops, and Abbots to have crowns placed upon them by the Pope or his legates, by allowing oaths of fidelity to be enjoined, and the dignity of the Emperor to be consecrated: they have subjected their kingdoms almost like fiefs, E. C. Inas King of Britain in the year 740. Andrew the Neapolitan kingdom &c. The formula of the oath of fidelity exists in dist. LXIII. chapter Tibi Domino. To you, Lord Pope John, I, King Otto, do promise and swear by the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and by this wood of the life-giving cross and by these relics of the saints, that if by the Lord's permission I come to Rome, I will exalt the holy Roman Church and you, its ruler, according to my power, and you shall never lose life or limbs, and that honor itself which you have, by my will or my counsel or my consent or my exhortation: And in the Roman city I will make no plea or ordinance concerning all things that pertain to you or to the Romans without your counsel: and whatever of the land of St. Peter shall come into our power, I will restore to you: and whomever I shall entrust with the Italian kingdom, I will make him swear that he shall be your helper to defend the land of St. Peter according to his power. So help me God, and these holy Gospels. Concerning the concession of the Roman state and Principate, the same distinction is held thus: I, Louis, Emperor Augustus, decree and grant by this pact of our confirmation to you, blessed Peter, Prince of the Apostles, and through you to your vicar, Lord Paschal, Supreme Pontiff and universal Pope, and to his successors forever: Just as from our predecessors until now you have held and disposed in your power the Roman city with its Duchy, and all its suburbs and small villages, and its mountainous territories, and maritime shores and ports, or all cities, castles, towns, and villas in the parts of Tuscany.

Latin:

Οὗτοι γνώμην μίαν ἔχουσι καὶ τὴν δύναμιν καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἀνα τῶν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασι, hi unum consilium habent, & virtutem & potestatem suam bestiæ tradent.) Primi Gothi facti sunt fœ- derati Imperii Romani. Inde & nomen & res ad alios transiit populos. Docet nos id Procopius Gothicorum IV. Apud eun- dem Procopium fœderatos populos hos reperies Ostrogothos, Wisigothos, Vandalos, Gepidas, Longobardos, Herulos, Bur- gundiones, Hunnos, Francos, Anglosaxones.

Qua ratione unius sententiæ fuerint populi Septentrionales, Gothi, Vandali, Gepidæ, Longo- bardi, Heruli, Burgundiones, Hunni, Franci, An- glo-Saxones, non video. Etsi enim forte Procopio dicantur fœderati, certe hæc fœdera inita opor- tet demum post ruinam imperii, aut ad illam, non vero ut unquam simul vel seorsim ad illius dignitatem conservandam conspirarint. Nec denarium suum hic habebit numerum, cum O- strogothi, & Wisigothi duos initio non consti- tuerint populos, & plures poterant adjici, ut Rugi, Turcilingi, Alani, Thuringi, multæque aliæ barbaræ nationes, quarum nonnullæ no- minantur Paulo Diacono Hist. Longob. Libr. I. cap. I. Potestatem suam & regnorum ner- vos magnam partem Romano Pontifici cef- ferunt, legendo Cardinales, Episcopos, Abba- tes à Papa aut legatis ejus coronas sibi imponi, juramenta fidelitatis injungi, dignitatem Impe- rat, consecrari permittentes: Regna pene feu- dorum instar subjecere, E. C. Inas Britanniæ Rex Ann. 740. Andreas Neapolitanum regnum &c. Formula Juramenti fidelitatis extat dist. LXIII. cap. Tibi Domino. Tibi Domino Jo- hanni Papæ ego Rex Ottho promittere & jurare facio per Patrem & Filium & Spiritum San- ctum, & per lignum hoc vivificæ crucis & per has reliquias sanctorum, quod si permittente Domino Romam venero, sanctam Romanam Ecclesiam, & te Rectorem ejus exaltabo secundum posse me- um, & nunquam vitam aut membra, & ipsum honorem, quem habes mea voluntate & meo consilio aut meo consensu aut mea exhortatione perdes: Et in Romana urbe nullum placitum aut ordinationem faciam, de omnibus quæ ad te aut ad Romanos pertinent sine tuo consilio: & quicquid de terra S. Petri ad nostram potestatem pervenerit, tibi reddam: & cuicunque Italicum re- gnum commisero, jurare faciam illum, ut adjutor tui sit ad defendendum terram Sancti Petri secun- dum suum posse. Sic me Deus adjuvet, & hæc sancta Evangelia? De concessione civitatis Ro- manæ & Principatus eadem distinctio ita habe- tur: Ego Ludovicus Imperator Augustus statuo & concedo per hoc pactum confirmationis nostræ tibi beato Petro Principi Apostolorum, & per te vicario tuo Domino Paschali summo Pontifici, & universali Papa & successoribus ejus in perpetuum: Sicut à prædecessoribus nostris usque nunc in vestra potestate tenuistis & disposuistis Romanam civitatem cum Du- catu suo, & suburbanis atque viculis omnibus, & territoriis ejus montanis, & maritimis littoribus & portubus seu cunctis civitatibus, castellis, oppidis ac villis in Thusciæ partibus.

## 17:14
Vers. 14.

Οὗτοι μετὰ τῦ ἀρνίυ πολεμήσουσι.] That is, they will rage against the Christians after the example of the Romans. In that sense we had ποιεῖν πόλεμον above XII, 7. XI, 17. XIII, 7. The same locution is found in Jeremiah I, 19.

Καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτούς.] Christ will bring it about that all those peoples and their Kings will at length become Christians. Jerome, where he enumerates the Christian peoples of his time, adds also the Goths. Regarding the others, the matter is also clear.

Ὅτι Κύριος Κυρίων ἐστὶ καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων.] God had already promised long ago that it would come to pass that very many Kings and Dynasts would obey Christ, Psalm II. Dan. VII, 27. See above 15. Κύριος Κυρίων, or Κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων, as in 1 Timoth. VI. v. 15. אדון אדונים.

Καὶ οἱ μετ' αὐτῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πισοὶ.] They too will conquer the Kings by their patience and the example of a good life and sound sermons. Thus also above XII, 11. Note the three degrees: to be called, then to be chosen, Matth. XX, 16. XXII, 14. Lastly to persevere, 2 Petr. I, 1.

In the prior commentary he has these things: Vers. 14.

Οὗτοι μετὰ τῦ ἀρνίυ πολεμήσουσιν, these will fight with the Lamb.] For thus in the times of Maximin the Goths had come into alliance with the Romans, as Jordanes notes, at which time, just as other Roman soldiers were executing Roman edicts against the Christians, so also were these and other federates.

Καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτὸς, and the Lamb will conquer them.] For all those peoples arrived at length at the Christian religion.

Ὅτι Κύριος Κυρίων ἐστὶ καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων, because he is Lord of Lords, and King of Kings.] To whom the Father gave all power, and promised that kingdoms would obey him.

Καὶ οἱ μετ' αὐτῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πισοὶ, and they who are with him are called, elect, and faithful.) By their patience, of course, which is the only kind of conquering that befits Christ and Christians, as such. The first is to be called, then to be chosen Matth. 20, 16. c. 22, 14. lastly to persevere, 2 Petr. 1, 1.

Not that the peoples whom the Commentator enumerates served the Ethnic Emperors in executing edicts against the Christians. For most of them did not come into a treaty with the Romans until after the Emperors had already become Christians, and peace was restored to the Churches, which is known to everyone. but because these kingdoms, emerging from the ruins of the Empire along with the Pontifical dignity, were to serve the authority of the Pontiff, to such an extent that their Kings, hanging upon the nod of the Pope, were to harass pious and faithful Christians with various persecutions, just as the Waldensians, Albigensians, Lollards, Picards, and Reformed are read to have been harassed everywhere by the authority of Princes for the sake of the Roman see, until those Kings, conquered by the Lamb and overcome by the patience of the innocent, desisted from persecution, with some even openly sending word to the Pontiff, which we now see has happened in England, Scotland, Sweden, Denmark, the United Netherlands, and many other places in Europe.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

Οὗτοι μετὰ τῦ ἀρνίυ πολεμήσουσι.] Id est, in Christianos sævient Romanorum exemplo. Eo sensu ποιεῖν πόλεμον ha- buimus supra XII, 7. XI, 17. XIII, 7. Eadem loquutio apud Jeremiam I, 19.

Καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτούς.] Christus efficiet, ut omnes illi populi eorumque Reges tandem fiant Christiani. Hierony- mus ubi Christianos populos sui temporis enumerat, addit & Gothos. De cæteris quoque res in aperto.

Ὅτι Κύριος Κυρίων ἐστὶ καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων.] Deus jam olim promiserat, fore, ut Christo plurimi Reges ac Dynastæ obedirent, Psalm. II. Dan. VII, 27. Vide supra 15. Κύριος Κυρίων, sive Κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων, ut 1. Timoth. VI. v. 15. אדון אדונים.

Καὶ οἱ μετ' αὐτῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πισοὶ.] Etiam illi sua patientia & bonæ vitæ exemplo & sanis sermonibus Re- ges vincent. Sic & supra XII, 11. Nota tres gradus, voca- ri, deinde eligi, Matth. XX, 16. XXII, 14. Postremum perse- verare, 2. Petr. I, 1.

In priori commentatione hæc habet: Vers. 14.

Οὗτοι μετὰ τῦ ἀρνίυ πολεμήσουσιν, hi cum Agno pugnabunt.] Ita enim Maxomini temporibus Gothi in societatem Romano- rum venerant, ut Jordanes notat, quo tempore sicut alii Ro- manorum milites edicta Romana contra Christianos exerce- bant, ita & hi aliique fœderati.

Καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτὸς, & Agnus vincet illos.] Per- venere enim omnes illi populi tandem ad Christianam reli- gionem.

Ὅτι Κύριος Κυρίων ἐστὶ καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων, quoniam Dominus Dominorum est, & Rex Regum.] Cui omnem po- testatem Pater dedit, & regna ei paritura promisit.

Καὶ οἱ μετ' αὐτῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πισοὶ, & qui cum illo sunt vocati electi & fideles.) Patientia nimirum sua, quod so- lum genus vincendi Christum & Christianos, qua tales sunt, decet. Primum est vocari, deinde eligi Matth. 20, 16. c. 22, 14. postremum perseverare, 2. Petr. I, 1.

Non quod inservierint populi, quos enumerat Commentator Imperatoribus Ethnicis in Edictis contra Christianos exercendis. Nam plerique ex illis non venerunt in fœdus cum Romanis, ni- si postquam Imperatores jam facti erant Chri- stiani, & pax reddita Ecclesiis, quod cuivis notum: sed quod hæc regna una ex Imperii ruinis cum Pontificia dignitate emersura inservitura erant Pontificis autoritati, adeo, ut eorum Reges è Pa- pæ nutu pendentes pios & fideles Christianos es- sent variis persecutionibus insectaturi, prout Wal- denses, Albigenses, Lollardi, Picardi, Reformati ubi- que Principum autoritate in gratiam sedis Roma- næ exagitati leguntur, donec illi Reges ab Agno victi & innocentum patientia superati, à persecu- tione destiterunt, nonnullis etiam nuncium pa- lam remittentibus Pontifici, quod jam in Anglia, Scotia, Suecia, Dania, Fœderato Belgio & multis aliis Europæ locis factum videmus.

## 17:15
Vers. 15.

Καὶ λέγει μοι, τὰ ὕδατα, ἃ εἶδες, ὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶ καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι.] We have had this distribution several times already, as above V, 5. VII, 8. XI, 9. XIII, 7. XIV, 6. That there were men of many languages under the Roman empire is known from Virgil and Martial. Concerning these peoples, see Appian at the beginning. You have it among the ancients that by waters are understood nations.

Achmetem CLXXVIII. Water succeeds water, and the same sea or river remains: Thus men succeed men, and the same people remains. Philosophers use this simile, whom we mentioned in Lib. II. de jure belli ac pacis IX, 3. In Nahum II, 8, Nineveh is a pool of waters, that is, a populous city, according to the Chaldean interpreter. These things thus previously:

Vers. 15.

Καὶ λέγει μοι, τὰ ὕδατα, ἃ εἶδες, ὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶ καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι, and he said to me, the waters which you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples and nations and languages.) Πόρνη, harlot, that woman is called because of the multitude of Gods, whose worship is πορνεία to the Prophets: We have received into your Roman sacred rites Isis, and the demigod dogs and the sistrums demanding mourning, And the man whom you, weeping, testify is Osiris. Water signifies something immense, whence the sea is ἄβυσσος to the Greeks who Hebraize, and Greek and Latin poets, when they wish to express that which lacks number, call it the waters of the sea. But it is best adapted to so many nations and peoples subject to the Roman empire: concerning whom see Appian at the beginning. Λαοὶ seem to be nations that had lived under Kings. Ὄχλοι are free nations, ἔθνη are great bodies in which there are many nations: just as Tacitus in his work on the customs of the Germans and elsewhere distinguishes a gens from a natio, as the whole from the part. Languages, however, are sometimes common to many nations, as once Greek, now Slavonic. Concerning their diversity, Martial to Domitian: A diverse voice sounds, yet the voice of the peoples is one when you are called the true Father of the fatherland. Virgil, Aeneid VIII: The conquered nations march in a long line, as varied in languages as in the style of their clothing and arms.

These Kings are evidently distinct from the preceding ones. Those were heads, these are much smaller and are called only horns. But the beast can live with its horns amputated, but by no means with its heads cut off. Thus, while those ten Kings held the harlot in hatred, the beast could still live and carry the harlot, as if it would collapse as if dead only when the last head was clearly amputated. Then the seven Royal heads succeed one another, nor do they stand erect at the same time; for as one falls, another is born beneath it, just as the Angel clearly indicates. Five have fallen, one is, another has not yet come, and when that one is as it were killed, the eighth will come. But the Kings designated by the ten horns are in the beast at the same time, nor does one succeed another: Thirdly, just as those seven Kings constitute the beast itself and pertain to its essence, as the nature of heads requires: So these ten, similar to horns, are not so intimate to the beastly substance, but are born only after it, nor do they cultivate perpetual friendship with the ruling city, but in the end they drive it headlong and kill it. All of which things most clearly apply to the Kings who, after the destruction of the Western Empire, took crowns in the provinces and nations of the Romans. For they did not give the beast its first life, but strengthened it once born. They did not erect the Papacy, but defended it once erected: Likewise, they bore scepters and crowns, and very often most gravely violated Rome itself and the empire: as here again the learned B. Cluverus.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

Καὶ λέγει μοι, τὰ ὕδατα, ἃ εἶδες, ὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶ καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι.] Hanc distributionem ha- buimus jam aliquoties, ut supra V, 5. VII, 8. XI, 9. XIII, 7. XIV, 6. Multarum linguarum homines sub imperio Ro- mano fuisse notum ex Virgilio & Martiale. De his populis vide Appianum initio. Per aquas intelligi gentes habes apud

Achmetem CLXXVIII. Aqua aquæ succedit, & manet idem mare aut amnis : Sic homines hominibus, & manet idem populus. Utuntur hac similitudine Philosophi, quorum meminimus Lib. II. de jure belli ac pacis IX, 3. Apud Nahu- mum II, 8. Ninive piscina aquarum, id est, urbs populosa interprete Chaldæo. Hæc ita prius:

Vers. 15.

Καὶ λέγει μοι, τὰ ὕδατα, ἃ εἶδες, ὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶ καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι, & dixit mihi, aquæ quas vi- disti, ubi meretrix sedet, populi sunt & gentes & linguæ.) Πόρ- νη meretrix, dicitur illa mulier ob multitudinem Deorum, quorum cultus πορνεία Prophetis : Nos in sacra tuam Romana recepimus Isim, Semideosque canes & sistra jubentia luctum, Et quem tu plangens hominem testaris Osirim. Aqua immensum aliquod significat, unde mare ἄβυσσος Græcis Ebraizantibus, & Poëtæ Græci Latinique, ubi id, quod numero caret, volunt simili exprimere, aquas maris dicunt. Optime autem id adaptatur tot gentibus ac populis Romano imperio subditis : de quibus vide Appianum initio. Λαοὶ vi- dentur esse nationes, quæ sub Regibus vixerant. Ὄχλοι na- tiones liberæ, ἔθνη magna corpora, in quibus plures nationes: quomodo Tacitus de moribus Germanicis & alibi distinguit gentem à natione, ut totum à parte. Linguæ vero interdum & multis gentibus communes, ut olim Græca, nunc Sclavoni- ca. De earum diversitate Martialis ad Domitianum : Vox diversa sonat, populorum est vox tamen una Cum verus patriæ diceris esse Pater. Virgilius IIX. Æneidos. Incedunt victæ longo ordine gentes, Quam variæ linguis habitu tam vestis & armis.

Hi Reges à præcedentibus evidenter sunt distincti. Illi capita erant, hi multo minores cornua dunta- xat appellantur. Cornibus vero amputatis vivere potest bestia, capitibus recisis nequaquam. Sic Re- gibus illis decem odio habentibus meretricem, vivere tamen posset bestia, & meretricem bajulare, ut ca- pite ultimo plane amputato quasi mortua concideret. Deinde Regia septem capita succedunt sibi invicem, nec pariter stant erecta; Ruente enim uno subnasci- tur alterum, prout Angelus clare indicat. Quin- que cecidisse, unum esse, alterum nondum venisse, & illo quasi occiso venturum octavum. At decem cornibus designati Reges simul insunt bestiæ, nec unus succedit alteri : Tertio sicut Reges illi septem constituunt ipsam bestiam & ad essentiam ejus per- tinent, quemadmodum capitum requirit natura : Ita decem hi cornibus assimiles non sunt adeo intimi substantiæ bestiali, sed post eam demum enascuntur, nec perpetuam cum rectrice civitate amicitiam co- lunt, verum ipsam tandem præcipitem agunt & oc- cidunt. Quæ omnia Regibus, qui post exitium Imperii Occidentalis coronas in provinciis & natio- nibus Romanorum sumpsere, clarissime competunt. Ihi enim vitam bestiæ primam non dedere, sed na- tam firmavere. Non erexerunt Papatum, sed erectum defenderunt : Pariter sceptra & coronas ges- serunt, & sæpenumero ipsam Romam & impe- rium gravissime violarunt: ut hic iterum erudite B. Cluverus.

## 17:16
Vers. 16.

Καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες καὶ τὸ θηρίον.] Ἐπὶ τὸ θηρίον, Arethas and many books have, nor does the Latin read otherwise. Οὗτοι μισήσουσι τὴν πόρνην.] In their own time they will rise up hostilely against the Roman domination. This was most seen in the times of Honorius, as can be seen in Procopius and other historians. This is the falling away of the Roman state into ten Kings according to Tertullian: The defection of the Roman Kingdom according to Ambrose: The departure of the nations from the Roman empire according to Jerome. εἰς δέκα βασιλέας διηρῆσθαι τὴν οἰκουμένην, says Arethas. Καὶ ἠρημωμένην ποιήσουσιν αὐτήν.] They will afflict it more with disasters: They killed all the men, as many as there were, in all places alike, both old men and young, sparing neither women nor children. Καὶ γυμνὴν ποιήσουσιν αὐτήν.] They will strip away the gold, stones, and pearls. This was done by Alaric the Goth, and by Gaiseric the Vandal. Of him Procopius: 'In Rome, they left behind nothing of public or private property.' Of the other, indeed: 'Having loaded a great quantity of gold and silver and other royal possessions onto the ships, he sailed to Carthage; he also plundered the temple of Jupiter Capitolinus.'

And they shall eat her flesh.] They will turn the provinces to their own uses, having spurned the friendship of the Romans. Thus, this or that people invaded Dacia, Pannonia, Thrace, Illyricum: furthermore, both Goths, Burgundians, and Franks invaded Gaul; Vandals first, then Visigoths invaded Spain; Vandals invaded Africa; Anglo-Saxons invaded Britain; Ostrogoths, then Longobards, invaded Italy itself along with the Dalmatians, the Alps, and Noricum. The expression is taken from Isaiah 10:18 and 44:16.

And they shall burn her with fire.) They will burn Babylon herself, the harlot herself, namely the third part, which must be understood from the preceding 16:19. Such a synecdoche is also frequent among historians. Thus, 1 Maccabees 1:33, Jerusalem was burned by the men of Antiochus, which Josephus interprets as referring to certain most beautiful buildings, and the consequence in both Maccabean books shows the history. Such an expression is most frequent among the prophets, as Ezekiel 29:12 and often elsewhere. There was an ancient tradition among the Jews that Rome would be burned. You have indications of it in Bachai and in Jonathan, 1 Samuel 2:5, Ezekiel 39:16. John approves of it here, as he does not a few other things of that kind. This was fulfilled by the Ostrogoths under Totila. Procopius, Gothic War IX: 'For Totila happened to have burned many of the buildings of the city.' Nor is there any reason for anyone to object that Rome was Christian at that time. For on the contrary, it is true that even after the Emperors had become Christian, idolatry remained in Rome, both in the Senate and among the plebs. And not only were there pagans in the Senate, but they also obtained the consulship, such as Symmachus, whose oration for pagan rites still exists. Jerome, on Isaiah 57, dealing with his own times: 'And Rome herself, the mistress of the world, venerating the image of a guardian with candles and lamps in individual islands and houses—which they call by that name for the protection of the buildings—so that those entering and leaving their house are always reminded of their unaccustomed error.' And this is the reason why the same Jerome, when he lived in Rome, says he was a colonist of the purple harlot in his Prologue to Didymus. When Totila invaded the city, most of the citizens had already fled, many had perished from famine, many had been slaughtered, so that there were scarcely five hundred left of the plebs. In addition to this, when the burning of many buildings in Rome followed, the gates were destroyed, and a third part of the walls was demolished, the Roman Senators and others who had left, tainted by paganism, refused to return. These words here are taken from the passage in Daniel 7:11. In a like cause, a like result. See how great was the patience of God in seeking the conversion of idolaters.

Grotius had handed down these things in this way in his previous commentary.

Verse 16.

And the ten horns which you saw and the beast.) Other books more correctly have 'against the beast' (κατὰ τὸ θηρίον). For the preposition is accustomed to be used with the accusative where something precedes that is inherent in the thing or is around the thing. 'These will hate the harlot.' Those who had been federated peoples and kings will become enemies. Which began to happen in the times of Honorius. See Procopius, Vandal War I, and add the others who wrote Roman history or the chronicles of those times in Greek and Latin. Irenaeus: 'To the ten kings, into which the empire that now reigns will be divided.' Tertullian calls what is predicted here the departure of the Roman state, dispersed into ten kings. Ambrose truly said that the defection of the Roman Empire was to be expected. Jerome calls the secession of the nations from the Roman Empire the very same thing. Arethas, from the ancients: 'The world is divided into ten kingdoms.' And they shall make her desolate.) They will wear down and exhaust the Roman Empire with great disasters, so that there will be desolation in many places. Procopius, Vandal War I: 'They were killing all the men whom they found, likewise the old, likewise the young, sparing neither women nor children.' And they shall make her naked.) They will despoil her of riches and ornaments, as Alaric the Goth and Gaiseric the Vandal did. Of the former, Procopius: 'In Rome, they left behind nothing of public or private property.' Of the latter, indeed, in this manner: 'Having loaded a great quantity of gold and silver and other royal possessions onto the ships, they sailed to Carthage.' He also plundered the temple of Jupiter Capitolinus. When he had loaded a huge amount of gold, silver, and other things belonging to the Emperor onto the ships, he sailed to Carthage: He even despoiled the temple of Jupiter Capitolinus.

And they shall eat her flesh.) They will make her provinces their own, as most of those peoples we mentioned did with Dacia, Pannonia, Thrace, and Illyricum; furthermore, the Franks, Burgundians, and both Goths with Gaul; the Vandals first, then the Visigoths with Spain; the Vandals with Africa; the Anglo-Saxons with Britain; the Ostrogoths, then the Longobards, with Italy itself along with the Dalmatians and the Alps.

And they shall burn her with fire.) This was done by Totila, not indeed to the whole city (nor is it necessary for this prophecy to be fulfilled), but to a part of it, at the time when he first captured Rome, and he spared burning the whole thing due to the warnings of Belisarius. But the gates were burned, and not a few buildings. Procopius, Gothic War III, where he narrates the second entry into Rome: 'He ordered everything that he himself had happened to pull down and burn when he first captured Rome to be rebuilt as quickly as possible.' The same author, Gothic War IV: 'Totila had burned many of the buildings of the city.' Regarding the third part of the walls being demolished, see what the same Procopius has in the same book in the earlier entry of Totila. See likewise what follows shortly concerning the miserable sight of the city, and the gates restored by Belisarius. From which you may best understand those things which are predicted here briefly, but more broadly in the following chapter.

The Commentator seems to have read καὶ τὸ θηρίον, for which he thinks κατὰ τὸ θηρίον should be substituted, although most of the most corrected Codices, specifically those of the Stephanuses, have ἐπὶ. He says the hatred of the harlot and her ruin happened then, when those federated peoples and Kings began to become enemies of the empire. Incorrectly, because the Kings were not made, nor did they establish kingdoms, until after the empire was overturned, which was that secession of the Roman empire mentioned by Tertullian into ten Kings, which would bring about the Anti-Christ; for they seized the kingdom together with this later beast. And it is strange that the Commentator, who seemed to have rejected that opinion of Tertullian at chapter XIII. near the end on p. 46, should twist it hither: Nor does that secession, which he supposes, begin first through the Goths under Honorius, as he wishes; for much earlier, namely in the year of Christ 254, they had begun to break into the Empire, against whom Decius, fighting, fell, betrayed by Trebonianus Gallus. And when, with Honorius reigning, action had been taken everywhere against Ethnic idolatry, with all its temples overturned, as Baronius notes at the year 399, no. 9, by what reason could Rome at that time, or the Roman empire, almost everywhere Christian, retain the name of harlot and fornicatress? Wherefore that [rising] of the ten Kings together with the beast against her, who is without doubt the purple-clad harlot, must be long after this secession, and pertain to the ruin of the Roman Pontiff to be carried out gradually by the same Kings, who themselves had previously seemed to have favored him so greatly: which has begun in part, and will further happen, God granting, so that Rome may finally remain destitute of all authority, fully stripped of its riches, and deprived of those provinces and kingdoms which had previously been subject to it as fiefs of the Church and patrimony of Peter, as England once was. Nor does this prophecy concerning the city to be burned pertain to the fire of Totila, which was not total. The Papists themselves threaten Rome with a far graver evil than this, as Ribera [does] in the supreme destruction of the Anti-Christ, which is described more expressly in the following chapter. This is Maresius. Franciscus Suarez, 3. p. tomo 2. disp. 59. art. 6. sect. 2., considers it uncertain whether the Roman Empire, and much more whether the city of Rome, is to be overthrown before the Antichrist, or by the Antichrist himself. Ribera and Viegas here consider that it is to be overthrown before the Antichrist, and they think they demonstrate this from the fact that Rome is said here to be overthrown by ten Kings, therefore before the Antichrist. For the Antichrist, upon coming, will immediately defeat three Kings and kill them, so that only seven remain, who will voluntarily submit themselves to him. Since, therefore, there are to be only seven Kings under the Antichrist, it follows that Rome is not to be overthrown then, but before, when, of course, there will be ten Kings in the world. This opinion, says Cornelius, is probable, and I have followed it on 2. Thess. II, 9., and St. Jerome on Dan. VII seems to favor it. The contrary, departing from himself 2. Thess. II. he now embraces: namely, that Rome and the Roman Empire are to be overturned not before the Anti-Christ, but by the Anti-Christ through ten Kings already subject to him. This is proved first because Daniel c. 7, in recounting the series of Monarchies, teaches that just as the monarchy of the Chaldeans was overturned by the Persians, that of the Persians by the Greeks, and that of the Greeks by the Romans, so the Roman empire will be overturned by the Anti-Christ himself. Secondly, because it is the common opinion of the Doctors that the Roman empire is the last and will endure until the end of the world, and this is the opinion not only of recent Doctors but also of the Fathers in general, as witnessed by St. Jerome in Dan. c. IX; this is the tradition, and it is, as it seems, Apostolic. Therefore, it will not be overturned by ten Kings but by the Anti-Christ at the end of the world. It is confirmed because Dan. II. v. 8. & 24. he saw a little horn, which designates the Anti-Christ, rising among the ten horns, that is, the ten Kings, from the beast, which designates the Roman empire. Therefore, the Anti-Christ will arise from the Roman Empire. It will therefore stand until his arrival, and will be overturned by him. Furthermore, since in this passage the woman, that is, Rome, is said to sit upon the same beast, having these ten horns, it follows that Rome will dominate the Roman Empire and the ten Kings, until it is overturned and burned by the little horn, that is, the Anti-Christ arising from it, through the ten Kings rebelling against it, as is said here in v. 16. Thirdly, because the sequence of the Apocalypse demands this: for it is divided into two parts: the former, up to the eleventh chapter, contains and narrates the seven seals of the sealed book: the latter, from the eleventh chapter to the end, contains the contents of the book itself. Now the seals contain those things which must precede the time of the Anti-Christ, but the book contains those things which will happen in the time of the Anti-Christ. Therefore, since these two chapters XVII. § XVIII. are contained in the sealed book itself, it follows that they pertain to the Antichrist himself and his time. Ribera replies that this is a hysterology or a disturbed order. For he claims that these two chapters, or rather this destruction of Babylon, that is, of Rome, ought to be placed in the correct order earlier, namely at chapter IX, 13, in the trumpet of the sixth Angel. But this hysterology is too harsh and preposterous; for it disturbs the entire order of the Apocalypse. Add that in this way the seals of the book themselves would be far greater and more copious than the book itself: remove these two chapters, and others which pertain to the same, and you will leave a meager subject matter for the book. Thus, so that in the sequence of the Apocalypse we may avoid this hysterology and these not insignificant inconveniences, it must be said that these, just as those preceding from the eleventh chapter and onwards, pertain to the sealed book itself and consequently to the times of the Antichrist. For thus the whole series of the Apocalypse turns out to be plain. It is confirmed, because one of the Angels from those who were seen by John in the preceding chapter to have the vials and the last plagues, revealed these things concerning the destruction of Babylon to John; therefore this very thing pertains to the last plagues of the world.
