For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.] The Prophetic Spirit, which has been given to you, is a testimony by which Jesus shows that you are his legate. The message concerning the remission of sins and eternal life given to believers through Christ is no less than that concerning the conversion of Emperors. All Christians are Kings through Christ. Among them, however, the Apostles excel.

The confirmation of the sayings is added: These words are true: The Word of God is truth itself, John XVII, 17. And the reverence of St. John, who wished to pursue the Angel with religious veneration because of those gospels, perhaps unaware whether he was created or uncreated, until he professed himself to be a fellow-servant of his and a brother of his having, holding, or as long as they have the testimony of Jesus, concerning which the Prophets and Apostles have testified, and all the faithful are openly prepared to testify, Rom. X, 9, 10, but he was forbidden: See, do not do it, namely. For religious veneration, as the worship of the first table, is proper to God alone. These things must be opposed to the angel-worship, saint-worship, and Mary-worship of the Papacy, which, since the Jesuits understand that it cannot consist with the adoration of God alone, they strenuously deny that the Saints are invoked by them, Lessius, book II, on Justice and Law, ch. 38, and others. But is this not a horrendous idolatry, when they attribute divine attributes and divine honors to the Saints, e.g., when they call Mary omnipotent with Gregory of Nicomedia; when they blaspheme that all power in heaven and on earth has been given to her with Peter Damian; when with Bernardo de Bustis in Mariale, book 1, ch. 2, they assign to her a mercy more than divine, saying, sinners flee more confidently to the mother of mercy, and often those whom the justice of the Son condemns, the mercy of the Mother delivers. When they attribute omnipresence and omniscience to the Saints, that they see all things everywhere (Bellarmine, book 1, on the Beatitude of the Saints, ch. 20).

The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy. It is explained what testimony he understands. That which is from the Spirit of Prophecy, if a metonymy is to be admitted, or that which is like the soul of prophecy, if a metaphor. Although the soul is properly called spirit, without the testimony concerning Jesus there are no Prophets, Acts X, 43, strictly so called; the testimony of Jesus written is the Holy Scripture itself, in which Jesus is the A. and Ω., the beginning and the end; the testimony concerning Jesus makes every page in it.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

Καὶ ἔπεσον ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῦ.] Nempe summo honore afficiens rei tantæ nuntium, sic & infra XXII, 8. Ad pedes accedere honor erat, qui Regibus virisque summis ex- hibebatur in Orientis partibus. Γονυπετεῖς ἕδρας προσπι- πτῶσι ἄναξ, τὸν οἴκοθεν νόμον σέβων, ajunt Phœnissæ Regis filio apud Euripidem. Legatos Carthaginensium Livius di- cens more adorantium procubuisse addit, accepto credo ri- tu ex ea regione unde oriundi erant, id est, ex Phœnice. Scri- ptor vitæ Cononis: Venerari Regem, quod προσκυνεῖν ipsi vocant. Plura de hoc ritu attulimus in majore nostra ad Decalogum commentatione. Solebant sancti veterum tem- porum pari modo adorare Angelos de rebus magnis missos, tanquam Satrapas regni cœlestis. Exempla habes Genes. XVII, 17. Jud. XIII, 20.

Καὶ λέγει μοι, ὅρα μή.] Sic & infra XXII, 8. Cave fece- ris; ὁρᾶν cavere, 1. Thess. V, 15. & alibi.

Σύνδουλός σε εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σε, τῶν ἐχόντων τὴν μαρ- τυρίαν τῦ Ἰησῦ.] Honor ille exhiberi solet multo majo- ribus. Nos inter nos pares sumus ejusdem Regis Legati. Per fratres habentes sive servantes testimonium hic intellige A- postolos & alios donis Apostolicis præditos. Manifestum id ex loco simili infra XXII, 8. Philo Abrahamum vocat An- gelorum σύνδουλον libro de Abrahamo.

Τῷ Θεῷ προσκύνησον.) Non dicit προσκύνησιν soli Deo licite exhiberi, repugnat enim tota vetus historia, & ea, quæ diximus ad Matth. VIII, 2. Sed benigne agit, ut si quis col- lega collegæ dicat : Serva hunc honorem Regi.

Ἡ γὰρ μαρτυρία τῦ Ἰησῦ ἐστὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς προφητείας.] Spiritus Propheticus, qui tibi datus est, testimonium est, quo Jesus ostendit, te suum esse legatum. Non minor est nun- tius de remissione peccatorum & de vita æterna per Chri- stum data credentibus: quam de Imperatorum conversione. Omnes Christiani per Christum sunt Reges. Inter eos vero excellunt Apostoli.

Additur dictorum βεβαίωσις : Hi sermones veri sunt: Verbum Dei est ipsa veritas Joh. XVII, 17. Et reverentia S. Johannis, qui religiosa veneratio- ne prosequi volebat Angelum ob illa ἐυαγγέλια, nescius fortè, creatusne an increatus sit, donec profiteretur se σύνδυλον conservum ipsius & fra- trem ejus habentium, retinentium, vel quousque ha- bent testimonium Jesu, quo de testati sunt Prophetæ & Apostoli, & testari palam parati sunt omnes fideles Rom. X, 9. 10. sed prohibebatur : Vide, ne feceris scil. Religiosa enim veneratio, ut cultus primæ tabulæ, Deo uni propria est. Opponenda hæc sunt τῇ Ἀγγελολατρείᾳ, Ἁγιολατρείᾳ & Μαριολατρείᾳ Papatus, quam cum solius Dei adoratione consi- stere non posse quum intelligant Jesuitæ, strenue negant, Sanctos abs se invocari, Lessius l. II. de Ju- stit. & jure c. 38. & alii. Sed annon horrenda hæc est idololatria, cum divina attributa & honores divinos Sanctis tribuunt, e. g. cum Mariam cum Gregor. Nicomed. omnipotentem vocant, cum Pe- tro Damiani ei datam esse omnem potestatem in cælo & in terra blasphemant; cum Bernhardo de Busto in Marial. l. 1. c. 2. misericordiam plus quam divi- nam eidem assignant, peccatores, inquiens, fidu- cialius ad matrem misericordiæ confugiunt, & sæpe quos justitia Filii damnat, Matris misericordia libe- rat. Cum Sanctis omnipræsentiam & omniscienti- am, quod ubique omnia videant, (Bellarm. l. 1. de sanct. Beatit. c. 20.) tribuunt.

Testimonium Jesu est Spiritus prophetiæ. Expo- nitur, quodnam testimonium intelligat. Quod à Spiritu Prophetiæ est, si Metonymia admittenda, vel quod instar animæ est prophetiæ, si Metaphora. Quamvis proprie anima dicatur πνεῦμα sine testi- monio de Jesu non sunt Prophetæ, Actor. X, 43. κυρίως ita dicti, Testimonium Jesu scriptum est ipsa Scriptura sacra, in qua Jesus A. & Ω. principium est & finis; testimonium de Jesu utramque in eâ facit paginam.

## 19:11
Ver. 11.

And I saw heaven opened.) The anticipation of a great vision. Above IV, 1. XI, 19. See Matt. III, 16, and what is said there.

And behold a white horse.) The Gospel as above, VI, 2.

And he who sat upon it.) Christ as in the aforementioned place VI, 2.

Called faithful and true) Above III, 14. Christ is indeed always such, but he is called so especially when he fulfills his promises. That word 'called' is absent in the Manuscript.

And in righteousness he judges.] He exercises most just judgments upon Maxentius and other idolaters and persecutors of Christians.

And he makes war.] He wages wars from heaven, by which he casts down his enemies, above I, 6. New husbands are accustomed to compete in games in honor of the wedding. What is playful there, is serious here.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

Καὶ εἶδον τὸν ὐρανὸν ἀνεωγμένον.) Magni visi antecessio. Supra IV, 1. XI, 19. Vid. Matth. III, 16. & ibi dicta.

Καὶ ἰδὺ ἵππος λευκὸς.) Evangelium ut supra, VI, 2.

Καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπ’ αὐτὸν.) Christus ut dicto loco VI, 2.

Καλύμενος πιστὸς καὶ ἀληθινὸς) Supra III, 14. Sem- per quidem talis est Christus, sed eximie sic vocatur, cum promissa sua implet. Illud καλύμενος abest in Manu- scripto.

Καὶ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ κρίνει.] Justissima exercet judicia in Maxentium & alios idololatras & Christianorum persecu- tores.

Καὶ πολεμεῖ.] Bella ex cœlo gerit, quibus hostes suos dejicit, supra I, 6. Solent novi mariti in nuptiarum hono- rem ludis certare. Quod ibi ludicrum, id hic serium est.

## 19:12
Ver. 12.

And his eyes were as a flame of fire.] Above I, 2. He inspects the innermost recesses of souls: He knows whom he ought to break and whom to bend.

And on his head were many crowns.] Excellently. For kings were accustomed, for as many other kings as they had defeated, to place as many crowns upon themselves, 1 Sam. XII, 30. 1 Macc. XI, 13.

Having names written.) Many names, such as Son of David, the Dayspring, Savior of the world, Light of the Gentiles.

And a name written, that no man knows but he himself.) Just as the gods of the nations have a secret name, so also he has one, known to no man. That name signifies the Author of the good things which no one understands, namely, of the other life. See 1 Cor. II, 9. 1 John III, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

Οἱ δὲ Ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῦ φλὸξ πυρός.] Supra I, 2. Intimos animorum recessus inspicit : Scit quos frangere quos flecte- re debeat.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτῦ διαδήματα πολλά.] Egregrie. Solebant enim Reges, quot alios Reges devicerant, toti- dem sibi imponere diademata, 1. Sam. XII, 30. 1. Maccab. XI, 13.

Ἔχων ὀνόματα γεγραμμένα.) Multa nomina, ut ὑὸς Δα- βὶδ, ἀνατολὴ, σωτὴρ κόσμυ, φῶς ἐθνῶν.

Καὶ ὄνομα γεγραμμένον, ὃ ὐδεὶς οἶδεν εἰ μὴ αὐτός.) Sicut Dii gentium habent nomen arcanum, sic & ille habet, nulli cognitum homini. Id nomen significat Autorem bonorum, quæ nemo intelligit, vitæ scilicet alterius. Vide 1. Cor. II, 9. 1. Joh. III, 2.

## 19:13
And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood.) Dipped not in the blood of the pious, as Rome, but of the impious. A figure of this matter is in Isa. LXIII, 2, from which passage we shall also have the words taken very soon. This color could not but please the new bride.

And his name is called The Word of God.) By the Word God created the world: by the Word he also reformed the world for the better. Concerning this name Word of God, see this Apostle in the Gospel I, 1, and what is said there.

Latin:

Καὶ περιβεβλημένος ἱμάτιον βεβαμμένον αἵματι.) Tinctum non piorum sanguine, ut Roma, sed impiorum. Ejus rei figura Esa. LXIII, 2. ex quo loco deprompta verba etiam jam mox habebimus. Color hic non poterat non placere novæ nuptæ.

Καὶ καλεῖται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῦ ὁ λόγος τῦ Θεῦ.) Verbo Deus mundum creavit: Verbo etiam mundum reformavit in melius. De hoc nomine Λόγος Θεῦ vide hunc Apostolum in Evangelio I, 1. & ibi dicta.

## 19:14
Ver. 14.

And the armies which were in heaven followed him.) The heavenly militia here are the Angels, as in Luke II, 2. Matt. XXII, 7, where see what is said.

Upon white horses.) They themselves also serving the Gospel.

Clothed in fine linen, white and clean.) So great are the virtues of Christians before God, that they are equaled to the virtues of the Angels. See above 8.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

Καὶ τὰ ςρατεύματα τὰ ἐν ὐρανῷ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.) Militia cœlestis hic sunt Angeli, ut Luc. II, 2. Matth. XXII, 7. ubi dicta vide.

Ἐπὶ ἵπποις λευκοῖς.) Servientes & ipsi Evangelio.

Ἐνδεδυμένοι βύσσινον λευκὸν καθαρὸν.) Tanti sunt virtutes Christianorum apud Deum, ut Angelorum virtutibus æquentur. Vide supra 8.

## 19:15
Ver. 15.

And out of his mouth goeth a sharp two-edged sword.] A sharp and two-edged sword signifies sometimes the whole Gospel, sometimes a part of it, that is, threats against the impious, and those certainly to come to pass. See Heb. IV, 12. above I, 16. II, 12. below here 21.

That with it he should smite the nations.] By the nations understand the contumacious idolaters. What God had done in Maxentius, he was about to do in Licinius and Maximinus.

And he shall rule them with a rod of iron.] It is a metalepsis. For by the iron rod the sword is understood, and by the sword the decrees of God. And by to rule is understood to govern, but for to govern, to punish. See above II, 7. XII, 5.

And he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness of the wrath of God the Almighty.) Shadowed forth from Isaiah LXIII, 3. But there blood flows from the press, here the wine of fierceness, that is, as we have already said several times, poisoned wine. By that is understood death with torments. In the Glossary, a treader, a presser. Theocritus said treading the winepress. See above XIV, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

Καὶ ἐκ τῦ ςόματος αὐτῦ ἐκπορεύεται ῥομφαῖα δίςομος ὀξεῖα.] Gladius acutus & anceps modo Evangelium totum significat, modo partem ejus, id est, minas adversus impios, easque certo eventuras. Vide Ebr. IV, 12. supra I, 16. II, 12. infra hic 21.

Ἵνα ἐν αὐτῇ πατάσσῃ τὰ ἔθνη.] Τὰ ἔθνη intellige idololatras contumaces. Quod in Maxentio fecerat Deus, idem facturus erat in Licinio & Maximino.

Καὶ αὐτὸς ποιμανεῖ αὐτὺς ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ.] Est Μετάληψις. Nam per virgam ferream gladius, per gladium Dei decreta intelliguntur. Et per ποιμαίνειν intelligitur regere, pro regere vero punire. Vide supra II, 7. XII, 5.

Καὶ αὐτὸς πατεῖ τὴν ληνὸν τῦ οἴνε τῦ θυμῦ τῆς ὀργῆς τῦ Θεῦ τῦ παντοκράτορος.) Adumbratum ex Esaiæ LXIII, 3. Sed ibi sanguis fluit è torculari, hic οἶνος Θυμῦ, id est, ut jam aliquoties diximus, vinum venenatum. Per id intelligitur mors cum cruciatibus. In Glossario ληνοβάτης calcator, torculator. Ληνὸν ἐπιβήσκων dixit Theocritus. Vide supra XIV, 20.

## 19:16
Vers. 16.

And he hath on his vesture.) Upon his imperial cloak.

And on his thigh.) That is, on the hilt of the sword, which hung at his thigh.

A name written: King of Kings, and Lord of Lords.) This is that new name, which we said was hinted at above in III, 12. Truly new, if you look not at the right, but at the outcome of the right. Nebuchadnezzar gives this name to God, after he heard of the destruction of kingdoms, Dan. II, 47.

In the description of the bridegroom, the opening of Heaven is set forth, which according to some is a symbolic signification of a new vision, as according to the blessed Gerhard and others. But it is instituted 1. from the form; like a rider on a white horse to designate the purity, holiness, chastity of soul and body of both himself and his ministers. Ribera and Alcafar, as also Sebast. Majerus and Mart. Borrheus, rightly hold this white horse as a sign of victory; and with the blessed Winckelmann, the ministers of the word are understood, not with Origen the body or soul of Christ; or with the Anonymous the most pure flesh of Christ, or with the blessed Chytraeus a bright cloud, or with Pareus the Majesty of Christ, or with Alfonso Conrad the Gospel concerning Christ. For Christ is the Rider himself sitting on the white horse, not the horse, as all acknowledge. 2. From the name which is common, faithful and true, for we all ought to be such, Apoc. III. such we were in the state of integrity, Gen. I, 26. Ephes. IV, 23. such we shall be in the state of eternal happiness 1. John III. It is added he judges in righteousness, because it is a matter of judgment, especially against the Antichrist, against whom he fights. 3. From the face or upper part of the body. For his eyes also are seen radiating because of the brightness, light, and splendor of knowledge, which penetrate all things, and nothing is hidden from them Heb. IV, 12. Sirach XXIII, 11. Job II. ch. XXI.

like a flame of fire above c. l. Knowledge, however, joined with the affection of avenging and of wrath: and his head crowned with a manifold crown of victory, of justice, of glory, of the kingdom, of the Priesthood. There follows 4. a proper name that can be held, ὁ λόγος τῶ θεῷ. For this is the same as the Son of God, expressing his eternal generation: which is his characteristic property, see John I, 1. it is said to be written, namely on his garment, that is, on his forehead, as the name of Aaron the high priest Exod. XXVIII. and that no one knew it, except himself Prov. XXX, 4. Matth. XI, 27. 5. Garment. His garment sprinkled with blood on account of the bloody passion, whether that which he sustained in his own, or that which he sustained in his mystical body, Acts IX. Zachar. II. Is. LXIII, 2. Gen. XLIX, 11. in the compression of the Redeemer and Treader, garments are wont to be sprinkled, Is. LXIII, 3. 6. The hosts of fellow-soldiers in heaven, viz. the Church, of whose garment a little before. 7. Arms; a two-edged sword, Heb. IV, 12. and its use against the nations; that is, all those resisting him, Psalm II. 8. The Sceptre, which he would rather rule kindly, those whom he is forced to strike and shake, Psalm CX. He is said to be about to rule the nations with a rod of iron, not those killed, viz. by spiritual death; for those have no need of ruling, but those constituted under the dominion of Antichrist, by spiritually crushing and converting them, which pleased Origen, Hilary, Augustine, Gregory the Great, Cassiodorus, Bruno, Remigius, Richard, Pampolitanus, Bede, and others, or by severely punishing them, which is approved by Cyprian, Jerome, Cornel. Jansenius, Genebrardus, Fulcapius, Mich. Higrianus, Clarius, Vatablus, Melch. Lindanus, Eman. à Saa, Eugubinus, Gagneius, Trevet. and is more approved by Johannes Campensis, or regarding the total overthrow of their kingdom; to which opinion we add our vote; because that destruction is immediately declared by the striking of the sharp sword, and the treading of the winepress of the wrath of God. Therefore the Romanists feed themselves with one hope of the victory of the Anti-Christ, against the Christian army and the Church of Christ, when on the contrary the Holy Spirit threatens him with the most severe and final punishment. 9. The outcome of the battle, the treading of the enemies in the winepress of divine wrath. Cf. Is. LXVIII. Finally, so that the description may be fuller, another name is still attributed to him likewise written on his garment; King of Kings, and Lord of Lords, by which his eternal divinity and supreme power 1. Timoth. VI, 15. Matth. XXVII, 19. Apoc. I, 6. of the triple kingdom, which the diadems designate, of power, of grace, of glory; nay, and independence, and immutability, because the name κυρίε corresponds to the name יהוה is designated Ephes. III, 14. Malach. III. Apocal. XVII. In the triumphal entry, heralds will proclaim the glorious titles of the Victor, which also happens in the coupling of spouses. This seems to fit better here, on account of the explicit mention of the bride.

By the thigh some understand power, others generative force, or with Alcazar, sons and grandsons. Aretas best: The garment, he says, enigmatically represents the flesh, the thigh the nature of the flesh as properly human, and not according to phantasy. For the thigh is accepted by Scripture for the demonstration of him.

PART III. OF CHAPTER XIX. INVITATION OF THE BIRDS TO DEVOUR THE FLESH OF THE ANTICHRISTIAN HOST.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

Καὶ ἔχει ἐπὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον.) Super paludamentum suum imperatorium.

Καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν μηρὸν αὐτῦ.) Id est in capulo ensis, qui pendebat ad femur.

Ὄνομα γεγραμμένον· Βασιλεὺς Βασιλέων, καὶ Κύριος Κυρίων.) Hoc est nomen illud novum, quod innui diximus supra III, 12. Vere novum, si non jus spectes, sed juris eventum. Nabuchodonosor hoc nomen Deo dat, postquam audivit destructionem regnorum, Dan. II, 47.

In sponsi descriptione præmittitur Cæli apertio, quæ juxta nonnullos est Symbolica novæ visionis significatio, utpote secundum B. Gerhardum & alios. Instituitur autem illa 1. à formâ; instar equitis in equo candido ad designandam tum ipsius tum Ministrorum ejus puritatem, sanctitatem, castitatem animæ, & corporis visus est. Equum hunc album Ribera & Alcafar, ut & Sebast. Majerus & Mart. Borrheus recte pro signo victoriæ habent; & cum B. Winckelmanno Ministri verbi intelliguntur, non cum Origene corpus aut anima Christi; vel cum Anonymo caro Christi purissima, aut cum B. Chytreo nubes lucida, aut cum Pareo Majestas Christi, aut cum Alfonso Conrado Evangelium de Christo. Nam Christus est Eques ipse sedens in equo albo, non equus, ut omnes agnoscunt. 2. A nomine quod cum commune est, πιστὸς & ἀληθινὸς, omnes enim tales esse debemus, Apoc. III. tales in statu integritatis fuimus, Genes. I, 26. Ephes. IV, 23. tales in statu æternæ felicitatis erimus 1. Johann. III. Additur in justitia judicat, quia de judicio agitur, imprimis adversus Antichristum, contra quem pugnat. 3. A facie vel parte superiori corporis. Nam & oculi ejus conspiciuntur radiantes ob claritatem, lucem, splendorem scientiæ, quam cuncta penetrent, nihil iis absconditum sit Ebr. IV, 12. Sirac. XXIII, 11. Job. II. c. XXI.

instar flammæ ignis supra c. l. Scientia autem cum affectu vindicandi & iræ conjuncta: &, caput ejus coronâ multiplici victoriæ, justitiæ, gloriæ, regni, Sacerdotii redimitum. Sequitur 4. nomen proprium haberi potest ὁ λόγος τῶ θεῷ. Hoc enim idem est, quod Filius Dei, æternam generationem exprimens: quæ ejus proprietas characteristica, vide Joh. I, 1. dicitur scriptum, scilicet in vestitu ejus, putà in fronte, ut Aaronis summi pontificis nomen Exod. XXVIII. idque nemo novisse, nisi ipse Proverb. XXX, 4. Matth. XI, 27. 5. Amictus. Vestimentum ejus aspersum sanguine ob passionem cruentam, sive quam sustinuit in proprio, sive quam in mystico corpore, Act. IX. Zachar. II. Es. LXIII, 2. Genes. XLIX, 11. in Redemptoris & Conculcatoris compressione vestimenta conspergi solent, Esa. LXIII, 3. 6. Agmina commilitonum in cœlo, scil. Ecclesiæ, de quorum vestitu paulo ante. 7. Arma; gladius bisacutus, Ebr. IV, 12. ejusque usus adversus gentes; id est, omnes ipsi repugnantes, Psalm. II. 8. Sceptrum, quæ eosdem, quos ferire cogitur, & concutere, comiter mallet regere Psalm. CX. Recturus gentes virgâ ferreâ dicitur non occisas, morte scil. spirituali; illæ enim opus regimine non habent, sed sub Antichristi dominio constitutas, spiritualiter easdem conterendo & convertendo, quod Origeni, Hilario, Augustino, Gregorio M. Cassiodoro, Brunoni, Remigio, Richardo, Pampolitano, Bedæ, aliis placuit, vel graviter puniendo, quod Cypriano, Hieronymo, Cornel. Jansenio, Genebrardo, Fulcapio, Mich. Higriano, Clario, Vatablo, Melch. Lindano, Eman. à Saa, Eugubino, Gagneio, Trevet. & Johanni Campensi magis probatur, vel quoad totalem regni earundem eversionem; cui sententiæ calculum adjicimus; quia statim illa contritio percussione gladii acuti, & calcatione torcularis vini furoris Dei declaratur. Una ergo sese spe lactant Romanenses victoriæ Anti-Christi, adversus exercitum Christianum & Ecclesiam Christi, quum contra Spiritus Sanctus illi minetur gravissimum & novissimum supplicium. 9. Pugnæ eventus, conculcatio hostium in torculari iræ divinæ. Conf. Es. LXVIII. Tandem ut plenior sit descriptio, aliud adhuc nomen ei tribuitur itidem in vestimento scriptum; Rex Regum, & Dominus dominantium, quo æterna ejus divinitas & summa potestas 1. Timoth. VI, 15. Matth. XXVII, 19. Apoc. I, 6. regni triplicis, quod diademata designant, potentiæ, gratiæ, gloriæ; imo & independentia, & immutabilitas, quia nomen κυρίε respondet nomini יהוה designatur Ephes. III, 14. Malach. III. Apocal. XVII. In ingressu triumphali præcones gloriosos Victoris titulos proclamabunt, quod etiam fit in sponsorum copulatione. Id magis hic convenire videtur, ob disertam sponsæ mentionem.

Per femur nonnulli potentiam, alii vim generativam, vel cum Alcasare filios & nepotes intelligunt. Optime Aretas: Vestis, ait, carnem ænigmatice repræsentat, femur naturam carnis tanquam proprie humanæ, & non secundum phantasiam. Nam in demonstrationem ejus femur à Scriptura accipitur.

PARS III. CAPITIS XIX. VOLUCRIUM AD DEVORANDAS ANTICHRISTIANI AGMINIS CARNES INVITATIO.

## 19:17
Vers. 17.

Καὶ εἶδον ἕνα Ἄγγελον, ἑστῶτα ἐν τῷ ἡλίῳ.] It is signified that that which this Angel announces will be very conspicuous.

Καὶ ἔκραξε φωνῇ μεγάλῃ לέγων πᾶσι τοῖς ὀρνέοις τοῖς πε- τωμένοις ἐν τῷ μεσουρανήματι.) In the air, as above VIII, 13. XIV, 6. This poetical address to the birds is taken from Ezekiel XXXIX, 17. and following. You have similar things in Jeremiah XII, 9. Add 1. Sam. XVII, 49. and Is. XVIII, 6. Jeremiah VII, 33.

Δεῦτε, συνάχθητε.) In Ezekiel συνάχθητε καὶ ἔρχεσθε. A similar address in Jeremiah XII, 9.

Εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τὸ μέγα τοῦ Θεοῦ.) God in Ezekiel: Ἐπὶ τὴν θυσίαν, ἣν τέθυκα ὑμῖν θυσίαν μεγάλην. After the sacrifice, feasts were wont to follow: therefore it follows in Ezekiel: ἐπλήσθητε τῆς τραπέζης μου. Thus here it is called a great slaughter. Add Isaiah XXV, 6. XXXIV, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

Καὶ εἶδον ἕνα Ἄγγελον, ἑστῶτα ἐν τῷ ἡλίῳ.] Significatur valde conspicuum fore id quod hic Angelus nuntiat.

Καὶ ἔκραξε φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων πᾶσι τοῖς ὀρνέοις τοῖς πε- τωμένοις ἐν τῷ μεσουρανήματι.) In aëre, ut supra VIII, 13. XIV, 6. Sumpta haec ad volucres poëtica allocutio ex Ezechiel. XXXIX, 17. & sequentibus. Paria habes Jerem. XII, 9. Adde 1. Sam. XVII, 49. & Esa. XVIII, 6. Jerem. VII, 33.

Δεῦτε, συνάχθητε.) In Ezechiele συνάχθητε καὶ ἔρχεσθε. Similis allocutio Jerem. XII, 9.

Εἰς τὸ δεῖπνον τὸ μέγα τοῦ Θεοῦ.) Deus apud Ezechielem: Ἐπὶ τὴν θυσίαν, ἣν τέθυκα ὑμῖν θυσίαν μεγάλην. Post sacrifi- cium sequi solebant epulae: ideo sequitur apud Ezechielem: ἐπλήσθητε τῆς τραπέζης μου. Ita hic vocatur strages magna. Adde Esaiae XXV, 6. XXXIV, 6.

## 19:18
Vers. 18.

That you may eat the flesh of kings.) In Ezekiel: you shall eat the flesh of giants. This is to be understood here of Julian, Anatolius, and others, whom the Persians killed; Julian's fingers were cut off and fell to the ground as food for the birds. See Zosimus and Ammianus himself. By our writers, kings are also called Prefects.

And the flesh of captains of thousands and the flesh of the mighty.) In Ezekiel: and you shall drink the blood of the princes of the earth. Soldiers are called גבורים, that is, mighty, Jerem. XLVI, 5.

And the flesh of horses and of those who sit upon them.) In Ezekiel: horse and rider.

And the flesh of all, both free and bond, both small and great.) A similar division above XIII, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

Ἵνα φάγητε σάρκας βασιλέων.) In Ezechiele: κρέα γιγάν- των φάγεσθε. Intelligendum id hic de Juliano, Anatolio, & aliis, quos Persae occiderunt, Juliano digiti abscissi in ter- ram cecidere esca volucribus. Vide Zosimum & Ammia- num ipsum. Βασιλεῖς nostris Scriptoribus vocantur etiam Praefecti.

Καὶ σάρκας χιλιάρχων καὶ σάρκας ἰσχυρῶν.) In Ezechiele: καὶ αἷμα ἀρχόντων τῆς γῆς πίεσθε. Milites vocantur גבורים, id est ἰσχυροὶ Jerem. XLVI, 5.

Καὶ σάρκας ἵππων καὶ τῶν καθημένων ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν.) In Eze- chiele: ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην.

Καὶ σάρκα πάντων ἐλευθέρων τε καὶ δούλων μικρῶν τε καὶ με- γάλων.) Similis partitio supra XIII, 16.

## 19:19
Vers. 19.

And I saw the beast.) Idolatry.

And the kings of the earth.) Julian with his nobles.

And their armies gathered together.) For Julian also used armies against the Christians. See what was brought forward in book II of the law of war and peace, chapter XXVI, 3.

To make war with him who sat upon the horse.) Here 'to make' is in the sense of the pluperfect. I saw that they had waged war against Christ. Thus I understood the cause of that slaughter. The Hebrews use one past tense for all. Whence often past tenses or aorists ought to be translated by the pluperfect. We noted this at Matt. XIV, 3 and at several places of the Old Testament.

And with his army.) Against the Church above XII, 6. 'With' here signifies hostility, as above II, 16. XI, 7. XII, 17. XIII, 4. 7. XVII, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

Καὶ εἶδον τὸ θηρίον.) Idololatriam.

Καὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς.) Julianum cum suis Proce- ribus.

Καὶ τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτῶν συνηγμένα.) Nam & exerciti- bus in Christianos usus Julianus. Vide quae adducta libro II. de jure belli ac pacis cap. XXVI, 3.

Ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ ἵππου.) Hic ποιῆσαι est in sensu plusquam perfecto. Videbam eos intu- lisse bellum Christo. Sic intelligebam causam illius cladis. Ebraei uno praeterito pro omnibus utuntur. Unde saepe praeterita vel ἀόριστοι verti debent per plusquam perfectum. Notavimus hoc ad Matth. XIV, 3. & ad complura loca Ve- teris Testamenti.

Καὶ μετὰ τοῦ στρατεύματος αὐτοῦ.) In Ecclesiam supra XII, 6. μετὰ hic hostilitatem significat, ut supra II, 16. XI, 7. XII, 17. XIII, 4. 7. XVII, 14.

## 19:20
And the beast was taken.] The public idolatry of the empire. Ἐπιάσθη תפש. In battle some are killed, some are captured, concerning whom judgment is made afterwards.

And with him the false prophet.] There is here again the singular for the plural, because the totality of false teachers is designated, just as 'two witnesses' and 'two prophets' above XI, 3. 10. In the manuscript it is also clearer what we are saying. For it is written: 'and those with him, the false prophet' by synthesis. Among those false teachers, however, the chief was Iamblichus, famous for magic arts, who killed himself with poison. Socrates, Sozomen, Zonaras, and Paul the Deacon recount this in their history.

Ὁ ποιήσας τὰ σημεῖα ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.] That is, in honor of idolatry, as above XIII, 12. Eunapius narrates that Iamblichus was snatched into the air: he made two boys, whom he called Ἔρωτα καὶ Ἀντέρωτα, suddenly appear in a bath, and many other things of that kind.

Ἐν οἷς ἐπλάνησε τοὺς λαβόντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου, καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ.] He either led Julian and others to idolatry, or confirmed them in idolatry. See the second oration of Nazianzen against Julian. Again, εἰκόνα is singular for plural, as above XIII, 14. 15. XIV, 9. 11. XV, 2. XVI, 2. We have said what χάραγμα is XIII, 16. 17. XIV, 9. 11. XV, 2. XVI, 2.

Ζῶντες ἐβλήθησαν δύο εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς τὴν καιομένην ἐν θείῳ.] This same thing is repeated below XX, 10, where the Devil is also added. He understands idolatry and idolatrous doctrine to be publicly extinguished in such a way that nothing more of it would appear than of a burned thing, I think of Sodom and the neighboring cities. Thus Daniel II, 35 says the four kingdoms were reduced as if to ash. See below XX, 4, where there is a similar expression concerning death and hell, and a not dissimilar comparison, Isa. XXX, 14. Sulphurous fire is more vehement than others, Psalm XI, 6. Isa. XXXIV, 9. See above IX, 17. Theodosius the Great abolished the public sacrifices of the Pagans. Against magicians there are the laws of Valentinian and Valens, likewise of Theodosius the Great and Arcadius.

Latin:

Καὶ ἐπιάσθη τὸ θηρίον.] Idololatria publica imperii. Ἐπι- άσθη תפש. In praelio quidam occiduntur, quidam capiun- tur, de quibus postea judicium fit.

Καὶ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης.] Est hic iterum singu- laris pro plurali, quia designatur universitas falsorum Do- ctorum, quomodo & δύο μάρτυρες & δύο προφῆται supra XI, 3. 10. In Manuscripto etiam clarius patet, quod dici- mus. Scribitur enim: καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης per σύνθεσιν. Inter illos autem falsos Doctores praecipuus fuit Jamblichius, magicis artibus clarus, qui semet veneno interemit. Narrant id in historia Socrates, Sozomenus, Zo- naras, Paulus Diaconus.

Ὁ ποιήσας τὰ σημεῖα ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.] Id est, in hono- rem idololatriae, ut supra XIII, 12. Jamblichium in aërem raptum narrat Eunapius: in balneo subito apparere duos pueros, quos vocabat Ἔρωτα καὶ Ἀντέρωτα, fecit, multaque alia ejusmodi.

Ἐν οἷς ἐπλάνησε τοὺς λαβόντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου, καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ.] Julianum & alios aut ad idololatriam traduxit, aut in idololatria confirmavit. Vide Nazianzeni orationem alteram in Julianum. Iterum εἰκόνα singulare pro plurali, ut supra XIII, 14. 15. XIV, 9. 11. XV, 2. XVI, 2. Quid sit χάραγμα diximus XIII, 16. 17. XIV, 9. 11. XV, 2. XVI, 2.

Ζῶντες ἐβλήθησαν δύο εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς τὴν καιομένην ἐν θείῳ.] Repetitur idem hoc infra XX, 10. ubi & Diabo- lus additur. Intelligit idololatriam & doctrinam idolo- latricam publice sic extinctam, ut ejus non magis quic- quam appareret, quam rei combustae, puto Sodomorum & vicinarum urbium. Sic regna quatuor quasi in favil- lam redacta ait Daniel II, 35. Vide infra XX, 4. ubi par locutio de morte & inferno, & comparationem non dissi- milem, Esa. XXX, 14. Ignis sulphuratus vehementior aliis Psalm. XI, 6. Esa. XXXIV, 9. Vide supra IX, 17. Theodo- sius Magnus sustulit sacrificia publica Paganorum. Con- tra magos leges sunt Valentiniani & Valentis, item Theodo- sii Magni & Arcadii.

## 19:21
Verf. 21.

Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ.) Clandestine idolaters, who were many until the times of Justinian. See Procopius, Secret History.

᾿Απεκτάνθησαν ἐν τῇ ῥομφαίᾳ τῦ καθημένε ἐπὶ τῶ ἵππε τῇ ἐξελθέσῃ ἐκ τῦ ςόματῷ αὐτῶ.) By the decree of Christ, who used Justinian for this purpose, that he might punish the idolaters with death. That law is written in the Greek language; it held the last place under the title of the Code concerning Pagans. Procopius mentions it from the said book.

Καὶ πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα ἐχορτάσθησαν ἐκ τῶν σαρκῶν ἀυτῶν.) Thus, you will feed the crows on the cross, said Horace. Add Gen. 40:19, 2 Sam. 21:11.

The Angel invites, because it is a notable banquet, to which such great ministers do not disdain to invite on account of the just vengeance against the enemies of Christ, and he is standing in the sun, by which he is bathed in the greatest light, by which his admirable brightness is designated. By that Angel in the sun are indicated the heralds of the Word, who with a hardened brow opposed themselves to the Roman Anti-Christ. For these could not lie hidden, but came forth into the open light of the sun, and set forth the Evangelical doctrine in the disk of the sun, as it is called. Cocceius's citation of the birds notes the bringing in of barbarian nations, so that they might pour themselves into the middle of the Roman world, although he also understands the birds flying in the midst of heaven in a rational sense. That Angel acclaims the birds with a loud voice, testifying to a fierce desire that they be gathered and fly to the spot in great number; therefore the cry resounds through the midst of heaven, so that it may be heard on every side, testifying also that the religion and devotion against Divine justice is not common. He calls it the great supper of God, which was prepared by God the Best and Greatest. It is great because of its author, great because of the equipment, which was provided by the Lord of Lords and great Kings, the destroyers of the Great Anti-Christ: not only of Kings, but also of any others who were ministers of the Anti-Christ; great because of the enemies, from whose flesh it was adorned, a huge army, great because of the number of enemies, an immense multitude of birds, who are both invited and gathered to the same. Cf. Jer. 7:34, ch. 12:9, Isa. 39:17. The desire for the vengeance of the enemies is hinted at, which the voice of the Angel does not so much approve as intimate. Primasius understands the spiritual birds as the Elect, as does Thomas Brightman. That whole nation, he says, formerly Papist, will henceforth obey the Reformed Church: which seems to be signified by the birds sated with the flesh of this slain army. Others say that evil spirits are designated, as the same Primasius holds: In a bad sense, the birds can also be understood as the transgressing Angels, who, when they have led their followers to destruction, are said to be sated with the flesh of the lost, having thus fulfilled their evil desire, catching satiety from their damnation, to whom they showed themselves as authors of error. Arctius agrees with this opinion in this place. Andreas of Caesarea explains it as good Angels, whose food is to fulfill the will of the Father, John 4:3, 4, but the interpretation of others is simpler, that he wished to make a display of the abundance of food with which all the birds could be sated, and thus in that way to depict the slaughter of a very great army.

Latin:

Verf. 21.

Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ.) Clandestini idololatræ, qui multi fuere ad tempora Justiniani. Vide Procopium arcana historia.

᾿Απεκτάνθησαν ἐν τῇ ῥομφαίᾳ τῦ καθημένε ἐπὶ τῶ ἵππε τῇ ἐξελθέσῃ ἐκ τῦ ςόματῷ αὐτῶ.) Decreto Christi, qui ad id Justiniano usus est, ut morte puniret idololatras. Lex ea est Græco sermone scripta, ultimum habuitilocum ti- tulo Codicis de Paganis. Meminit ejus ex dicto libro Pro- copius.

Καὶ πάντα τὰ ὄρνεα ἐχορτάσθησαν ἐκ τῶν σαρκῶν ἀυτῶν.) Sic, pasces in cruce corvos, dixit Horatius. Adde Gen. XL, 19. 2. Sam. XXI, 11.

Angelus invitat, quia insigne est convivium, ad quod non dedignantur tanti Ministri invitare ob justam adversus hostes Christi vindictam, is- que in sole stans, à quo luce maxima perfundi- tur, quo designatur admiranda ejus claritas. In- dicantur autem per illum Angelum in sole Verbi præcones, qui commasculata fronte sese Anti- Christo Romano opposuerunt. Hi enim lati- tare non potuerunt, sed in apricum solis prodie- runt, & doctrinam Evangelicam in disco solis, quod dicitur, exposuerunt. Coccejo citatio vo- lucrium notat adductionem barbararum gentium, ut sese effunderent in meditullio orbis Romani, quanquam & alites volantes in media cæli ratio- ne intelligat. Acclamat Angelus ille volucres ma- gnâvoce, testatus ferium desiderium, ut congre- gentur, & advolent, magno numero, idcirco clamor resonat per medium cæli, ut undiquaque exaudiatur, testatus & religionem & devotio- nem adversus Divinam justitiam non proletari- am. Cænam magnam Dei dicit, quæ à Deo Opti- mo Maximo parata. Magna est, ob autorem, magna ob apparatum, qui à Domino Dominan- tium & Regibus magnis instructus erat, debella- toribus Anti-Christi Magni: Non Regum tan- tum, sed & aliorum quorumvis Anti - Christi parastarum; magna ob hostium, è quorum car- nibus adornata, ingentem exercitum, magna ob hostium numerum, immensam volucrum multi- tudinem, qui & invitantur & congregantur ad eandem. Conf. Jerem. VII, 34. cap. XII, 9. Esa. XXXIX, 17. Innuitur a. cupiditas vindictæ hosti- um, quam non tam approbat vox Angeli, quam intimat. Aves spirituales intelligit Ele- ctos Primasius, ut & Thomas Brigtmannus. Tota, inquit, illa natio pridem Pontificia parebit deinceps Reformatæ Ecclesiæ: quod videtur significari per aves saturatas carnibus occisi hujus exercitus. Alii Spi- ritus malos designari ajunt, ut idem Primasius ha- bet: Possunt & in malo aves intelligi Angeli trans- gressores, qui cum suos ad interitum perduxerint se- ctatores, sic malo desiderio expleto dicuntur satiari carnibus perditorum, de eorum captantes damna- tione satietatem, quibus se autores præbuerunt ad errorem. Cui sententiæ Arctius in h. l. accedit. Andr. Cæsariensis de Angelis bonis explicat, quo- rum cibus est implere voluntatem Patris Job. IV, 3. 4. sed simplicior est aliorum interpretatio, quod voluerit πρὸς ὄμμα ποιεῖν copiam ciborum, quibus saturari omnes volucres possint, adeoque stragem ma- ximi exercitus ea ratione depingere.

## 20:1 Argument
CHAPTER XX.

ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The Angel of the abyss, having opened it, binds the Dragon for a thousand years, thrones are seen for judgment, the dead rise again, Gog and Magog are led out to battle, the Devil and the False Prophet are cast into the lake of fire, the earth flees from the sight of the judge, the dead are seen returned from the sea, death and hell, death and hell are cast into the lake of fire, and those who are not found written in the book of life.

There are two parts: I. The extreme efforts of the Devil, bound but loosed again, the battle through Gog and Magog, to v. 9. II. The casting of the same and his worshippers into the lake of fire to v. 15. Or, if you prefer, 1. The antecedents of the last judgment, situated in the binding and loosing of the Dragon. 2. Its concomitants, the end and consummation of the 1000 years. 3. The consequences: the condemnation of the Beast, to which is bound the glorification of the elect, described in the following chapter.

PART I.

THE BATTLE OF THE DEVIL BOUND, BUT RELEASED AGAIN.

Ver. 1.

Καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τῶ ὐρανῶ.) Another vision is presented signifying the tranquility which was first given to the Churches through Constantine, increased by his successors, and which would indeed be long, yet not until the end of the world. The descent of the Angel from heaven signifies a great benefit of God, as above III, 12, below XXI, 2, 10. Elsewhere, judgment, as X, 1.

Ἔχοντα κλεῖδα τῆς ἀβύσσου.) That is, of the deep prison. Above IX, 1, 2. Luke VIII, 31. And this very interpretation of this word is set forth below in 7.

Καὶ ἄλυσιν μεγάλην ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα ἀυτῶ.) For the guilty are accustomed to be bound, so that they may be led into prison, lest they be able to go elsewhere.

Others, especially Ribera, Cornelius à Lapide, etc., make him a created angel. But we, with Pareus, maintain that the uncreated Son of God is to be understood, 1. because He descends from heaven to bind Satan, as in John III, 8.

2. He has the key of the abyss, Apocal. II, 18, chap. IX, 1.

3. He has the power to seize the Dragon, whom Michael is said to have cast down to the earth when he seized him, Apocal. XII. It was shown in that same place that this is indeed Christ.

4. Through the Lord's passion, the powers of Satan were bound, according to Andreas. By His coming, Christ delivered the nations from seduction in a certain way, concerning which see August. book XX, de C. D. chap.

7. To this end the Devil was bound and shut up in the abyss, that he might no longer seduce the nations, from which the Church is composed. For it was not said that he should not seduce anyone, but that he should no longer seduce the nations, in which he undoubtedly did not wish the Church to be understood. Since no one can overcome with efficacy, cast into the abyss, shut the abyss, and prohibit free roaming, except that stronger One coming upon the Devil, the Son of God, Luke XI, 22, John XII, 31, chap. XVI, 11, 2 Pet. II, 4. Compare Psalm LXVIII, 19, Coloss. II, 15. Primasius, Rupertus, and Richardus explain the present passage concerning Christ, from whom we do not easily allow ourselves to be torn away without reasons.

Latin:

CAPUT XX.

ARGUMENTUM ET PAR- TITIO.

Angelus abyssi ea aperta ligat Draconem ad mille annos, conspiciuntur throni ad judi- cium, resurgunt mortui, Gog & Magog in prælium educitur, Diabolus & Pseudo - Pro- pheta in stagnum ignis projicitur, à conspectu judicis fugit terra, videntur mortui redditi à ma- ri, morte & inferno, mors & infernus in lacum ignis projiciuntur, & qui non inveniuntur scri- pti in libro vitæ.

Partes sunt duæ: I. Diaboli ligati, sed iterum soluti extremi conatus, per Gog & Magog præliatio, ad v. 9. II. Ejusdem & cultorum ipsius in lacum ignis projectio ad v. 15. vel, si mavis, 1. Novissimi ju- dicii antecedentia, in Draconis ligatione & solutio- ne sita. 2. Ejusdem concomitantia, finis & consum- matio 1000. annorum 3. Consequentia: Bestiæ condemnatio, cui devincta est electorum glorifi- catio, cap. seq. descripta.

PARS I.

DIABOLI LIGATI, SED ITERUM DIMISSI PRÆLIATIO.

Vers. 1.

Καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τῶ ὐρανῶ.) Aliud est visum significans tranquillitatem, quæ Ecclesiis per Con- stantinum erat primum data, aucta per successores, fo- re quidem longam, non tamen usque ad mundi interi- tum. Descensus Angeli de cœlo magnum Dei beneficium significat, ut supra III, 12. infra XXI, 2. 10. Alibi judici- um ut X, 1.

Ἔχοντα κλεῖδα τῆς ἀβύσσου.) Id est profundi carceris. Su- pra IX, 1. 2. Luc. VIII, 31. Et hæc ipsa interpretatio hujus vocis ponitur infra 7.

Καὶ ἄλυσιν μεγάλην ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα ἀυτῶ.) Solent enim son- tes vinciri, ut in carcerem ducantur, ne alibi possint.

Angelum creatum faciunt & alii, imprimis Ri- bera, Cornelius à Lapide &c. Sed increatum Dei Filium intelligi cum Pareo statuimus, 1. quia is de cœlo descendit, ut Satanam ligaret in Joh. III, 8.

2. Is clavem abyssi habet Apocal. II, 18. cap. IX, 1.

3. Apprehendere Draconem potenter valet, quem apprehendens in terram projecisse dicitur Mi- chaël Apocal. XII. Hunc vero Christum esse ibi- dem ostensum fuit.

4. Per Dominicam passio- nem Satanæ vires ligatæ sunt, interprete Andrea. Christus adventu suo gentes à seductione certo modo liberavit, quo de August. l. XX. de C. D. c.

7. Ad hoc ligatus est Diabolus & inclusus in a- bysso, ut jam non seducat gentes, ex quibus constat Ecclesia. Nec enim dictum est, ut non seduceret aliquem, sed ut non seduceret jam gentes in quibus procul dubio Ecclesiam noluit intelligi. Cùm efficacia vincere, in abyssum detrudere, abyssum claudere, liberam grassa- tionem prohibere, nemo potest, nisi fortior il- le Diabolo superveniens Filius Dei Luc. XI, 22. Joh. XII, 31. cap. XVI, 11. 2. Petr. II, 4. Conf, Psalm. LXVIII, 19. Coloss. II, 15. de Christo lo- cum præsentem explicant Primasius, Rupertus, Richardus, à quibus citra rationes ægre nos di- velli patimur.

## 20:2
Ver. 2.

And he seized.) Namely that chain.

The dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the Devil and Satan.) Repeated from the passage which is above at XII, 3. 9., where see what is said. In the manuscript, it is again the nominative instead of the oblique case, frequent in John, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος.

Who deceives the whole world.) Repeated from the same passage. And here πλανῶν is placed for πλανήσας after the manner of the Hebrews, who, since they do not have past participles, use present ones for every tense.

The diabolical [interpretation] of the death of Christ having been made with Augustine, Primasius, Gregory the Great, Bede, Andreas, Ribera, & Blasio de Viega, not to mention the binding made from the exit of the Word with Prosper, least of all the binding of Satan for eternity by Pope Calixtus with Aureolus, because he took away from the Emperor the right of investing Bishops and Abbots, nor is the happiness of the time after the Anti-Christ was killed to be understood with Joachim the Abbot, Ubertinus de Casalis, Teraphinus of Fermo, Pannonicus, & Bullinger, nor indeed with Rutulanus concerning spiritual happiness, nor even is this to be explained concerning blessed eternity with Alfonso à Castro, nor is it to be accepted with Alcafare and Turriconus concerning that binding which followed the Church's victory over Ethnic Rome. For it is said rashly that after this victory a thousand years of ecclesiastical happiness and tranquility are to be expected, nor can it consist with the calamities of the latest times. Nor is Cocceius sufficiently convenient here: From the times of Constantine up to the times of Louis the Bavarian this mode of time is found: who last resisted the Popes and was the κατέχων and hindering them 2 Thess. II, 7. Rightly, however, the time of Constantine the Great is praised. But how he was bound then (if that was the mind of Cocceius, as it appears). Then, he says, he devoted effort to Satan, so that Kings might hand over their power to the beast, and acknowledge the image of the beast as head. Then Satan incited the Pseudo-Prophet to say and do those things through which the ὁ ἄνομος, bringing in law beyond the law, might be exposed, and so that with maximum force all might be impelled to defection. That was the occasion for the faithful to contradict, and thus at last the eternal Gospel began to be preached. The matter proceeded to such a point that through the Council of Trent the authority of the Pope and of traditions was established, and interpretation was bound to the chair, and lies were foisted upon us as articles of faith, and the truth, especially Evangelical justice, was condemned. Thus the faithful were cast out from the midst of the great city, and the nations ceased to nourish the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

Καὶ ἐκράτησε.) Nempe ista catena.

Τὸν δράκοντα τὸν ὄφιν τὸν ἀρχαῖον, ὅς ἐσι Διάβολος, καὶ Σα- τανᾶς.) Repetitum ex loco, qui supra XII, 3. 9. ubi dicta vide. In Manuscripto rursus est rectus pro obliquo frequens Johanni, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος.

῾Ο πλανῶν τὴν ὀικεμένην ὅλην.) Repetitum ex eodem lo- co. Et est hic πλανῶν positum pro πλανήσας more Ebræo- rum, qui cum participia præterita non habeant, præsentibus pro omni tempore utuntur.

Diabolice morte Christi facta cum Augustino, Pri- masio, Gregorio M. Beda, Andrea, Ribera, & Blasio de Viega, nedum alligatio facta ab exitu Verbi cum Prospero, minime omnium, Calixti P. R. ligatio Sa- tana in æternum duratura cum Aureolo, quod su- stulerit Imperatori jus investiendi Episcopos & Abba- tes, nec felicitas temporis post Anti-Christum oc- cisum, cum Joachimo Abbate, Ubertino de Casalis, Teraphino de Fermo, Pannonio, & Bullingero intel- ligenda, nec quidem cum Rutulano de spirituali felicitate, neque etiam de beata æternitate cum Alfonso à Castro hæc explicanda, nec cum Alcafare ac Turricono de ea alligatione accipienda, quæ consequuta est Ecclesiæ victoriam de Roma Ethnica. Nam post hanc victoriam mille annos felicitatis & tranquillitatis Ecclesiasticæ expectandos esse, temere dicitur, nec cum calamitatibus novissimo- rum temporum consistere potest. Nec satis com- modè Coccejus hic: A temporibus Constantini us- que ad Ludovici Bavari tempora hic modus temporis invenitur: qui ultimus Papis restitit & fuit κατέ- χων ac impediens ipsos 2. Thess. II, 7. Recte tamen laudatur Constantini M. tempus. Ligatus vero quomodo tum fuerit (si ea mens Coccejo ut ap- paret, fuit.) Tum Satanæ, inquit, operam nava- vit, ut Reges traderent potestatem suam bestiæ, & imaginem bestiæ agnoscerent pro capite. Tum inci- tavit Pseudo-Prophetam Satanas ad ea dicendum & faciendum, per quæ denudaretur ὁ ἄνομος legem ferens præter legem, & ut maxima vi omnes ad de- fectionem impellerentur. Ea occasio fuit fidelibus contradicendi, & ita tandem æternum Evangeli- um prædicare cœptum est. Res eo processit, ut per Concilium Tridentinum stabiliretur autori- tas Papæ & traditionum, & interpretatio alliga- retur cathedræ, & mendacia pro articulis fidei obtruderentur, & veritas, imprimis justitia Ev- angelica damnaretur. Ita ejecti sunt fideles ex medio civitatis magnæ, & Ecclesiam desierunt gentes alere.

## 20:3
Vers. 3.

Καὶ ἔδησεν ἀυτὸν χίλια ἔτη, καὶ ἔβαλεν ἀυτὸν εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον καὶ ἔκλεισε.] A transposition and at the same time a Hebrew idiom, for which it is permitted to say: Καὶ δήσοντα ἀυτὸν, καὶ βληθέντα εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον ἔκλεισεν εἰς χίλια ἔτη. Thus the Demon is bound back and shut up, so that he may not harm Tob. VIII, 3. In Valerius Maximus VII, 6. there is a dream about Dionysius bound with iron chains to the throne of Jupiter, then released from the bonds with the destruction of many cities. But liberty here is to be understood as that ἐξουσία, concerning which it was treated above XIII, 3. Of exercising his cruelty against Christians through Roman idolatry, or through idolatrous Princes: and therefore the beginning of those thousand years ought to be led from the edict of Constantine, which is in Eusebius, in which there is mention of the bound Dragon. But the Roman Emperors followed the example of the Kings, some sooner, some later, just as before they had imitated the cruelty of the Emperors against the Christians. To the thousand happy years the Jews refer the passages of Daniel VII, 25. VIII, 14. where see Jachiades, Isa. XI, 6. and following. LX, 18. 22. LXV, 19. 20. See Justin in the dialogue with Trypho. The thousand happy years through the second Adam correspond to the nearly thousand years through which the misery of the first Adam lasted.

Καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ἐπάνω ἀυτῶ.] He sealed the prison, so that no one might open it. See Daniel VI, 17. In the Manuscript: Καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ὀμμάτως ἀυτὸν.

Ἵνα μὴ πλανᾷ ἔτι τὰ ἔθνη.] The nations, namely, which were of the Roman Empire. So that he might not deceive them, namely, to be inflamed to the slaughter of the pious. See below 7.

Ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη.] For then he will be about to stir up other evils, concerning which below 7.

Concerning those thousand years there are most serious contentions, which the chiliasts or millenarians understand definitely as just so many, most others indefinitely: taking a certain and finite number for an uncertain and indefinite one. Of those, a double class is given.

To the first pertain the ancients from almost the very beginning of the Apocalypse, namely Papias, whom Irenaeus and Jerome make a hearer of St. John the Apostle, but against his own will: who, near the beginning of his commentary, testifies that he never heard the holy Apostles, but received that tradition about the thousand years from the Presbyters, disciples of the Apostles. Eusebius judges him to have been too credulous and little judicious, having snatched up many fables for truth. Justin, however, followed that tradition in his Dialogue with Trypho, as did Irenaeus in book V. Nepos, Bishop of Egypt, refuted by Dionysius of Alexandria in Eusebius, book VII, ch. 10. Likewise Tertullian, book III against Marcion; Lactantius, book VII of the Institutes, ch. 23; Victorinus of Pettau on the Apocalypse; and formerly also Augustine, in the aforementioned book. But he who later changed his opinion, because the Papists Viegas, Ribera, Pererius, Cornelius a Lapide, and Tirinus observe that Augustine, in book XX of The City of God, ch. 7, along with Ambrose and Gregory the Great in book IV of the Moralia, ch. 12, understands the thousand years as the entire time of the reign of Christ up to the Anti-Christ, which the cited Papists also approve. But these thousand years pertain rather to the times that followed from the reign of Constantine the Great, which the Gogitic war will later succeed. Jerome calls that Jewish tradition δευτέρωσιν. Papias is also said to have been followed by Apollinarius and Suevus Coracion, nor did Jerome dare to condemn that tradition in book IV on Jeremiah, ch. XIX, because many of our ecclesiastics and martyrs approved it. Yet he himself rejected the same in ch. XXXVI of Ezekiel and ch. VII of Daniel. Furthermore, Cerinthus asserted the opinion about a thousand-year earthly reign of Christ after the resurrection, and one full of carnal delights, as witnessed by Eusebius in book III of the Ecclesiastical History, ch. 25, and Dionysius of Alexandria; the pious ancients held otherwise: dismissing that dream of bodily delights, which in part renewed the burden of the Church with the Anabaptists of Münster and some fanatics. The more recent ones, however, seem to want to have nothing to do with that dream, such as Johann Piscator and Alstedius.

Furthermore, others explain the designated years indefinitely as the whole course of times from the ascension of Christ up to the last day, following the lead of Augustine in book XX of The City of God, ch. 7. With whom, however, as we warned before, Bede, Anselm, and others do not fix the limit at the last day, but at the coming of the Anti-Christ. Some, according to Lyra, regarding Pope Calixtus binding the Emperor Henry V by excommunication, declared it to be through 1000 years, that is, up to the Anti-Christ: which sense he rejects, explaining it as Innocent confirming the Franciscan and Dominican orders to repress the power of demons. But this explanation is equally inept. How excellently the brothers of the Order of Minors and Preachers repress the Dragon, their own mutual contentions may teach. John of Viterbo, in this place, promises Sixtus the victory predicted here over the Saracen race in the year 1481. But experience refuted him. Ubertinus de Casalis says that Satan was bound under Constantine and loosed, as John XXII writes, in the year 1315, whom he calls the mystical Anti-Christ. There are those who understand the infinite time through the 1000 years as eternity itself. That the wicked, who are not to rise again and are not to reign with Christ, will not reign as long as the saints will reign with Christ, i.e., forever. Thus Alphonsus a Castro, in book III against heresies, under the word 'Beatitude', heresy 2, wishes to denote by these years the eternity of the blessed in heavenly joy and glory.

St. John teaches that after a thousand years Gog and Magog will be gathered for battle.

Blessed Philipp Nicolai brings forward another interpretation in book II of the kingdom of CHRIST, chapter 5. That the martyrs, having rejected the Papacy, lived with Christ a spiritual life in the true knowledge of God during the 1000 years of the Papal reign, and that the rest would live again afterwards, when the son of perdition was manifested. But these explanations, once a truer one is proposed, will easily be wiped away, to which we are therefore now hastening.

Moreover, Blessed Phil. Nicolai interprets in the cited place, p. 225, of the R. E. [Roman Empire] Hormisdas binding the Emperor Justin with an exhortation to the extermination of the Mahomet-followers, namely the Arians and Nestorians. But since the Pope himself today bears or approves of Nestorianizing Jesuits? Does he not in that part act as a midwife to the Dragon? Most people, understanding the thousand years definitely and exactly, place their beginning in the year of Christ 73, in which the Apostles had finished their course in these lands; others assign the time of the reign of Constantine the Great, assigning their end to the Papacy of Gregory VII, Hildebrand, very famous for his tyranny; at which time the Saracens also devastated many churches in the East, in the year 1300, around which time the Turkish empire under the Ottomans acquired its greatest strength, having occupied a most flourishing part of the world, and finally having captured Constantinople, the seat of the Eastern Empire, which the Ottoman Porte still holds. See Joh. Bapt. Nizar, in Wolff's Lect. memor. Cent. XVI, p. 884. Since the Mahometans snatched from the hands of the Christians Bithynia, Cappadocia, Lycia, Greater and Lesser Armenia, Caria, Lydia, Paphlagonia, Phrygia, Pontus, Pamphylia, Galatia, and in sum the whole of Asia Minor (called Turkey) and with Babylonia, Ethiopia. Furthermore, that perfidious Tyrant, having crossed the sea, entered Europe, and thus took possession of Achaia, Attica, all of Thrace with the Constantinopolitan Empire, Boeotia, Aeolia, the Peloponnese, Morea, Epirus, Macedonia, Albania, and having overcome the kingdoms of Bulgaria, Bosnia, Serbia, Russia, Rhodes, Negroponte, Belgrade, and almost all of Dalmatia, Croatia, Slavonia, Poland, Hungary, and Syria; and not yet satisfied with his empire, he desired to invade Germany, Italy, France, and Spain, so that he makes himself be called Emperor of Emperors, King of Kings, Lord of Lords, and Lord of the earthly Paradise and of Jerusalem, Prince of Princes, and Subjugator of Tartary, Persia, the Indies, and great Cairo: so that the wrath of the Lord against us miserable Christians was indeed remarkable, who permitted the Turk to extort so many bishoprics and so many churches from the hands of the Christians, and, which is of greater moment, the holy land itself, where Christ shed his most holy blood. Nor is it absurd to say that by the release of Satan from his chains after a thousand years, performed by the Angel, the arrival of the Mahometan Ottomans can be understood. Whence John XX. in the Apocalypse says that the Angel bound Satan for a thousand years, so that he would not disturb the faithful, and this was done under Constantine (as many skilled and learned men opine) around the three hundred and twentieth year, which brought the greater part of the seditious peoples and perverse nations into a sufficiently tolerable state, whence, the millennium having been completed, behold, Satan was bound again by the Angel, that is, by the Divine will, for some space of time, and this happened around 1300 with the eruption of the Ottoman family, namely from the Tartar Ottoman: which indeed will last for a very short time, and afterwards Satan will be cast out again. Whence those are to be called blessed who have patiently borne this Mahometan and Ottoman persecution until now, since the holy scripture says: Blessed are those who suffer persecution. Regarding this Ottoman persecution of the faithful and its almost prefixed term, Daniel prophesied in chapter XII, saying (according to the genuine Hebrew exposition): Blessed is he who waits and arrives at the days of one thousand three hundred and thirty-five. But that this number of days ought to be understood regarding the time of the arrival of the Ottomans, the resolution (in my judgment) will be made in this manner. Since Daniel is speaking in this place of the blessedness of those who will arrive at the 1335 days, while it stands that Christians will be afflicted then, three things come to be considered regarding this statement: first, the number of days; second, their quality; third, their beginning. To the first proposition I say that ancient Interpreters were accustomed to take a day for a year, and also for many years: so it is necessary to understand 1335 as the same number of years. To the second, speaking of the quality of such days or years understood through these days, whether solar or lunar years are to be understood, I say (since the Prophet in this place deals with the blessedness of those who are to arrive at the time of those days) that solar ones are to be understood, since the years prefixed for good events were solar, but lunar ones for unfortunate ones. Thus he. Ferdinandus Castrus agrees in book 9 of the Histor. Turc. p. II, c. 1. To whose opinion also, above others, Blessed Gerhard subscribes in disp. III, de nov. fanat. §. 15. There is also another new joining of the Chiliastic kingdom delineated in the writing of P. E. Hosl. (perhaps P. Egard's Posaune): who took the Angel binding Satan, from Joh. Arnd, casting the old man into the abyss of the scripture of perdition and grace, as the thousand years of three years and nine months, and made their beginning from the year 1625, in which those who would live again in the Spirit, Joh. He asserted that he would powerfully champion the Baptist and the Apostle Paul, along with Tauler and Kempis, and true Christianity: But he, having been warned in vain by the blessed Cluver, has already been solidly refuted by experience. It is a new and unheard-of thing that one thousand years should make up three years and nine months, for the sake of which fiction he assumed another [calculation] regarding the computation from the year 1517, when the Lutheran Reformation was instituted under that distinguished title. But what analogy, whether of proportion or of attribution, as they call it, what similarity is there between 1000 years and 45 days? What of that number of 3 years and 9 months, which makes 45, not days, not months, but what in the end? To what other number he might wish to compare it does not appear; to me, certainly, it is not known.

Furthermore, the Fanatics, the Anabaptists, with various errors resurrected from hell, in the city of Münster, as Sleidan testifies in book X, proclaimed an earthly kingdom of Christ in a book written under the title of 'Restitution,' in which only justice was to reign; some in Belgium, as Jansen reports in Conc. Evang. p. 842, dreamed that he himself was Christ the King even in Zion, not lacking in prodigies and revelations, as he boasted. They dreamed of a third age of the reborn, which they called the Holy Spirit's, and which was entirely holy and destined to last for a thousand years. I pass over for the present Nathan Ælian, the book of Mattenin, about which see Nucl. Histor. Meiger. §. 25, David Georg, the elder, Ezechiel Meth, Weigel, Nagel, Christoph, Andr, Christian, Simplic, Paul Felgenhauer, Angelus Maria, Johann Werner, Richard, his apostle of this century, about whom the theologians of Wittenberg and Jena, partly in the name of those of Lübeck, Hamburg, and Lüneburg, of the ministry, the blessed Dr. Nicolaus Hunnius, the blessed Dr. Theodor Thumm, the blessed Dr. Johann Müller, and B. Weber have dealt.

Adolph Held, in his Examination of the matter of Elias Praetorius, says that more than a thousand years, if the circumstances of the temple are estimated—the dimensions of which he reports St. John to designate from Ezekiel—constitute seven ages of the world, according to seven changes of the same, which he imagines regarding the whole substance: 1. from the creation of the world to Abraham. 2. from then to Christ. 3. to the last day; dreaming that the Genealogy of Christ in Matthew looks to this; because God changed his priesthood and kingdom in those times: which three great ones Heldius again subdivides regarding the second hour: 1. from Abraham to the Babylonian captivity, from this to Christ, and from then to the last day: having invented two new men: 1. who are regenerated from sinners to adoption through the Holy Spirit. 2. who, reborn from the just through the Spirit of life, are imitators of God. Heldius commemorates a certain Ludov. Frideric. Giffthoël, who, running about everywhere, calls himself King David the Second, who will avenge the Church against Babylon, just as Elias against the Priests of Baal.

Joh. Berckenthal reports of a certain person that he used a seal under this inscription: Priest according to the order of Melchizedek, and he brings in others dreaming of a fifth Monarchy, and many fanatics with Theophrastus and Caspar Schwenckfeld, namely Sebast. Franck, Dieterich Volckers, Cornhard, Jacob Behm, Val. Weigel, Paul Lautensack, El. Praetor., Frider. Brecheling, Antoinette Bourignon, Jac. Taube, the Labadists, and especially from Joh. Roth, he teaches concerning the bodily destruction of the Anti-Christ, that the time of the vengeance of God has come, that Babel must be judged by the mouth of God, and the sword of Elias must kill all Baal-priests, and take away the wickedness of the earth. A standard shall be raised in the year 1671 in the front part of the world in the city of Amsterdam, under which all scattered Jews shall be gathered. In the Netherlands a sovereign head shall rule, and thus continue a monarchical government, and thus Christ shall be exalted. Thence in the year 1674 an army is to be led out under some King, etc. Quirin Kuhlmann extols this fanatic to a wonderful degree in a book to which he gave the title New-Inspired Boehm, whom he says is the Angel flying through the sky with the eternal Gospel, who prophesied about himself and the Belgian Prophet Rhotius. Whom (I understand Boehm) he makes the Prophet of the seventh time, of the Monarchy of Jesus, calls him Luther against the Anti-Christ, and boasts that he was examined in Dresden in June 1624 by Hoe, Leiser, Baldwin, Meisner, and Gerhard, and he provokes us, Dr. Scherzer, myself, and Dr. Joh. Musaeus, to a response. I shall report only some chapters from the 150 prophecies and revelations approved by Boehm himself, and that in the author's own words, which are read in chapter XV: The very last time will soon break forth, and all mysteries will open themselves, because the restoration of all things draws near. All world-empires will fall as soon as it dawns at midnight. The Papacy, the Turkish realm, along with all sects and religions, will then attain their certain end. Thereafter, Moses and Elias shall appear again with Noah, and Elias's sign of fire shall be given to the world as a sign. The breaking of the great city of Babel, of confused Christendom, stands at the door; all sects shall soon be un-sected. In a short time, the Anti-Christ, together with the beast, the whore, and the false prophets, will be discovered and destroyed by a youth. A great King and ruler of the earth will be born a little after the noon of the sixth day; great heroes are around him, prophets prophesy of him, and his splendor goes from the sunrise to the sunset. The conversion of the Turks, Jews, and Heathens is to be expected immediately; one shepherd will gather the peoples into one flock. The mystery of the Jesus-Monarchy or Kingdom of God will be completed at seventeen o'clock, and there will be thereafter a tabernacle of God with men, etc. He boasts that he can resolve more than 1,000,000,000 new questions through 1,000 theosophical questions, of which not a single one could be solved by any of the theologians who follow the method of the schools without the Spirit of God. They are mere portents of words.

The aforementioned Adolph Held (to return to him) came to me in Wittenberg from Hamburg in previous years for the reason, as he testified, that he was persuaded that no one could inform him more correctly about his dogmas, whom I convinced with arguments from Scripture, so that he was reduced to silence; yet I rendered it most ambiguous by other merely topical arguments from the person of him, now a decrepit man of 60 years, an apostate from the apostles he had had, by the weakness of his judgment, ignorance of the sense of Scripture, and lack of skill in the art of disputing, without which he could convince no one, etc., and that he would hardly persuade the whole world that it would receive a seventh renovation from him: whom B. Müller's letters reported had renounced his errors in Altona near Hamburg before his analysis, confessing that he had been better informed by me from the Word of God. He invents sons of God who have arrived at the state of redemption from wrath, but are still spiritually under the Prince of the world, and outside the state of justification; he pretends that we know the mystery of the Holy Trinity through natural knowledge, and introduces certain new expressions; in a later MS confession offered to me, he speaks very inconveniently about the image of God, about renovation, and about the remission of sins regarding bodily things, etc.; but the former, which he had exhibited some years before the first advent, written out in types regarding the seven mutations of the world, teemed with satanic opinions, but which have now escaped my memory: they testified, however, if I remember correctly, that the author was addicted to chiliasm. The first change, as far as my memory still suffices, he assigned to the first age from the creation of the world to the flood; the second to the second, either to Abraham or to the Exodus; the third he extended as far as the Babylonian captivity, the fourth as far as Christ: the fifth, if I am not mistaken, to Luther: the sixth to himself, as a Prophet or Evangelist of the seventh universal change of all creatures. For he made all such: yet, when asked, he could not explain the others beyond the first and the last, regarding the remaining works of God besides man the microcosm, in whom, however, he was forced to acknowledge a change not substantial but accidental: finally restricting all those changes to the diverse administrations of the Priestly and Kingly office of Christ. This, if I remember correctly, was the sum of the opinions of the fanatic, who, as far as I can still recall to mind, indulged in his own speculations concerning the parts of man, and the interior and exterior man.

Letters from Hamburg recently announced that Elias Prætorius, whom we have also mentioned before, is now leaning toward a sounder opinion and is led by some repentance for his errors; provided that the repentance of this man, though late, be serious and true! He does indeed maintain the thousand years of the golden age, but he does not dare to affirm that worldly pleasures will have a place in them. He says, therefore, that he assigns spiritual happiness only to those blessed times: to which the scripture speaking of the calamity of the latest time is not opposed: inasmuch as it describes the calamities and wars and iniquity and impiety of men not reigning with Christ, but of those who are outside the Church, or looks to the times that are to follow the blessed age. But the voice of scripture is explicit concerning the latest times 1 Tim. IV. 1. According to which, sorrow, mourning, the cross, death, and what calamities do not remain for the faithful all the days of their life, Ps. XC. 10. Sir. XL. 1. seqq. 2 Tim. III. 12. Apoc. XXI. 4. Concerning the coming of the Lord and concerning ἀπισίᾳ throughout the whole earth: Do you think the Son of Man will find faith ON EARTH when he comes? Luke XVIII. 8. Which does not agree with the opinion concerning the conversion of both the Jews and the Gentiles, even if it seems to be proven by a certain reason not only by Praetorius and other fanatics, but also by many orthodox [theologians] and Fathers, Origen, Hilary, Ambrose, Jerome, Augustine, Chrysostom, Haymo, B. Aegidius Hunnius, Winckelmann, Mentzer, Hafenreffer, Baldwin, Gerhard, Meisner, Gravius, etc., as we have observed elsewhere.

But it is more correct that certain, and indeed a thousand years, are designated, as is evident from these things which will now follow, and thus they favor our opinion 1. The custom of the Apocalypse. For it is accustomed, when it employs numbers, to define a certain time. 2. The consistency of the explanation. For then Satan was truly bound, not absolutely, nor simply: but so that the Churches might not be prohibited or entirely removed among them: truly he was again released, by which Gentile persecutions [occurred]: because the Mohammedans are more correctly reckoned among the Gentiles than among the Christians, regarding doctrine and life, as far as the delights of the other age and polygamy, and other crimes of the Gentiles, the pagan ἀποθέωσιν of Mahomet, etc. If you say, how could Satan be considered bound, who raged so wonderfully under the Arian persecutions? Augustine's distinction in Ps. IX comes to aid. The first persecution of the Church, before, namely, Satan was bound, was violent, when Christians were bound to sacrifice with proscriptions, torments, and slaughters: the second was fraudulent, because it is carried out through heretics and false brethren: the third in the time of the Anti-Christ is both violent and fraudulent, having force in the empire, and deceit in miracles. That St. John speaks of the first, therefore, not of the second. And although the Anti-Christ also reigned within those thousand years (which Cornelius objects to this opinion), yet not all the Churches ceased to exist: For he himself sits in the Church, 2 Thess. II. He also objects to this: The Turkish empire is predicted to last for a short time, namely, only for an hour, a day, a month, and a year, that is, 390 years. But others establish angelic days from Daniel 45, and define the years as 1335 from the rise of the Anti-Christ, from which it will be necessary to assign the end, unless the days are shortened for the sake of the elect, about 1940. For some establish one beginning of the Anti-Christ, others another, so that it is not permitted to define anything ἀποτόμως here. 3. The opinion of the Chiliasts assumes a double falsehood, as Pareus admits; 1. That Satan had not yet been bound, so that he would no longer seduce the nations in Paganism, which is repugnant to History: 2. That after the ruin of the Papacy the world will not last for another thousand years, which is repugnant to the oracles concerning the abolishing of the Anti-Christ by the illustrious coming of the Lord, after which it seems absurd to me to establish a further thousand years of the world. He does not add the reasons why that seems absurd, so we add: 1. because scripture immediately joins the second coming of Christ, which the Chiliasts rashly and ἄτεχνεαφῆς imagine to be a double [event] with the destruction of the world, Matt. XXIV. 29, 30. 2 Thess.

1. 7. 8. 2. Pet. III. 10. 11. 12. 2. with the consummation of the age 1 Cor. 15, 23. Who, therefore, would the pious be who would still reign with Christ in this age for a thousand years after the coming of Christ? 3. With the last day of this age, and the very resurrection of the dead, which (bodily) scripture knows as only one, John 5, 28. c. 6, 38. 1 Thess. 4, 16. 4. With the final judgment, the creation of a new heaven and a new earth, the introduction of the saints into the new heaven and new earth, Matt. 25, 31. 2 Thess. 1, 7. seqq. 2 Tim. 4, 1. seqq. Is. 66, 22. 2 Pet. 3, 12. Ap. XII. 1. How, therefore, since the present earth has already fled, will Christ be able to reign in it with the saints for a thousand years? 4. He poses an Ἀντιλογία, as Pareus warns, in the opinion of the new Chiliasts, that before these thousand years the Pope, the Anti-Christ, will be cast into the lake of fire, and the Papacy will fall: And at the same time: that the Pope will gradually resume his strength over a thousand years, and after they have elapsed, will join himself with the Ethnic Kings to wage war against the Christians. But how can the Pope resume his strength while lying in the lake of fire? Thus he [Pareus] against his own companions in faith: who, if they object: It is not that the Pope himself cast into the lake will resume his strength; but someone else could be after him, who finally is abolished by the illustrious coming of Christ: Pareus retorts: This, however, is to play with a serious matter: And he warns: Let these explain themselves, whether they understand a partial or a total overthrow of the Papacy. If they understand a partial one, let them say that Satan was bound a hundred years ago, because a hundred years ago the Papacy began to fall in Germany and some kingdoms, as even Bellarmine admits: For, he says, from the time when, according to you, the Pope began to be the Anti-Christ, his empire not only did not grow, but always decreased more and more. If they understand a universal or total one, how will the beast gradually resume its strength, especially while lying in the lake of fire? 5. The Ἄτοπον with which the same [Pareus] presses them, namely that they say: That at the beginning of the thousand years the Martyrs are to bodily come to life again, and to reign with Christ for a thousand years, when the text speaks expressly of souls, not of the bodies of the martyrs: nor does it say that they revived or resurrected, but that they lived. 6. There is another absurdity, that they posit a double resurrection of the dead, one of the Martyrs after the ruin of the Papacy; the other of the rest of the dead after a thousand years of the reign of the Martyrs; which, in the judgment of Pareus, is foreign to the Catholic faith: I believe in the resurrection of the flesh, that is, of all the dead, which will be on the last day, and it is refuted by experience. For again, if they understand the ruin of the Papacy to be partial, since this has already happened a hundred years ago, they ought also to show that the first bodily resurrection of the martyrs has already taken place: If total, since this will happen only at the illustrious coming of the Lord, they cannot deny that the martyrs will then rise again with all others. He adds seventhly: I would like them to reconcile for me (for I cannot) what they posit, that after a thousand years from the overthrow of the Papacy Christ will come for judgment: and after those thousand years Gog and Magog will undertake to wage war against the Christians. But will this war really be undertaken after the return of Christ for the final judgment? Finally, 8. this opinion clearly agrees with the error of the Chiliasts, long since rejected by Christians, in that, contrary to the prophecy of the Apostle concerning the Antichrist being abolished only at the illustrious coming of the Lord, 2 Thess. 2:8, it grants a thousand additional years to the world after the Antichrist is abolished: and that, contrary to the scriptures concerning the resurrection of all the dead which will be on the last day, it introduces two particular resurrections: At least it differs in that it makes the millennial kingdom not earthly, as they did, but heavenly; although Augustine admits that there were also among the Chiliasts those who [expected] spiritual delights in that Sabbath for the saints would believe in the future through the presence of the Lord. All these things of Paraeus, which are deservedly opposed to his Venerable Parent in Christ (so he calls Piscator), are left to be dissolved by the new Chiliasts. We commit here the Cadmean brothers among themselves who stir up battles. That explanation concerning happiness, whether bodily or spiritual, not agreeing with the oracles describing the lot of the end time, is manifest. Lactantius also favors bodily pleasures, Inst. book VII, ch. 24.
