Then those who will be alive in their bodies will not die, but through those same thousand years will generate an infinite multitude, and their offspring will be holy and dear to God. But those who will be raised from the dead, they will preside over the living, like Judges: But some will be left for the victory of God, so that they may be triumphed over by the just and subjugated to perpetual servitude. He adds, moreover, the greatest fertility of the earth, the threats of animals and birds; and the Kings of the nations will come from the ends of the earth with gifts and offerings, so that they may adore and honor the great King, whose name will be famous and venerable to all nations that will be under heaven. You may find things similar in part to these in Cornelius a Lapide. But if those things are to be consistent with themselves, the times must be exquisitely distinguished. And shall we believe that Gog and Magog will presume to attack and finish off the saints who are already immortal with war? Or that the book of life, to be opened only at the final judgment, will be revealed in the particular resuscitation of the just Elect? Or are we to say that the new Jerusalem is seen descending from heaven having been inhabited for a thousand years, or that there will be camps without pain, without labor? Why also is only the resurrection of the Martyrs designated, when if the universal resuscitation of all men is included, those who worship the beast are also included? Why was mention made only of souls, if the resuscitation of bodies will happen then? How will that extreme security of the end time, so often asserted in the sacred writings, consist, if such spiritual happiness of the final age of the world, destined to last for a full thousand years, is asserted? See, if you please, concerning that, Matt. 24:12, 37; Luke 17:26, 18:8; 1 Tim. 4:1-2; 2 Tim. 3:1; 2 Thess. 2:8; 2 Pet. 3:3; Jude v. 18; 1 John 2:8, so that I may now pass over that it cannot be said that φανέρωσιν or ἐπιφάνειαν is the final advent of Christ, just as it is said more often in Luke 17:30; 1 Cor. 1:7; Col. 3:4; 2 Thess. 1:7, 2:8; 1 Tim. 6:14; 2 Tim. 4:1, 8; Tit. 1:13; 1 Pet. 1:7, 13, 4:13, 5:4; 1 John 2:28, 3:2; nor will the saints wait with pain for the advent of the Lord, or desire the crown, as having already received it before, Luke 21:24; Rom. 8:19, 2. Tim. 4:8, if they are already to have him present, who appeared a thousand years before and manifested himself? Those ancient millenarians arise 1000 years from the death of the Anti-Christ, and after the sixth millennium of the world they invent a seventh, in which the saints with Christ are in the highest delights, whether bodily or spiritual (which pleased Irenaeus and Augustine), which opinion P. Salas condemns as heretical. But Scripture not only makes the rewards of pious souls and holy men not bodily, but spiritual, not temporal, but eternal, Matt. V. 12; 2 Cor. IV. 17; Phil. III. 20. But it also simply denies that the kingdom of Christ is of this world, and teaches that the glory of the saints is still hidden here, John 18:36; Ps. 45:7; Rom. 8; Col. 3:3-4; Heb. 2:8, and that sin, death, and all evils are not to be abolished until the other life, 2 Pet. 3:12; 1 Cor. 15:24. Apoc. 21:4, and it hands down no other resurrection than the universal one, John 5:28, 6:39; 1 Cor. 15:22; 1 Thess. 4:16, and teaches that the crown of justice is to be expected, to be distributed on the παντοκριτικῷ day to all who love Christ, 2 Thess. 1:6; 2 Tim. 4:8; indeed, it predicts that persecutors and Martyrs will exist until the end of the world, Apoc. 20:9, and ascribes the beatitude to the souls of those beheaded for the Word of God, not to the martyrs only, Apoc. 6, so that there is no room for the opinion of Piscator, who interprets chiliasm concerning martyrs to be resurrected by Christ before the universal resurrection and to reign with him for a thousand years, with which the Socinian view in Matt. 1:63 agrees. For what Piscator urges in v. 4, the dead who did not come to life, has nothing to do with the matter, since they are opposed to the saints, and thus the impious are understood as spiritually dead, Matt. 8:22; John 5:25; Eph. 5:14; 1 Tim. 5:8. Apoc. 3:1, and the saints are described with those attributes of beatitude which are not of the Martyrs only, but of all the Elect, that the second death has no power over them, Apoc. 2:11, that they are Priests of God, Rom. 12:1; 1 Pet. 2:9; Apoc. 1:6, that they reign with Christ over the world, sin, and the Devil, John 4:5, 5:4, and that they will sit on the Throne of Christ, Apoc. 3:2.

They also understand the years definitely who begin them from the passion of Christ, whom Cornelius a Lapide names, Gregor. book 4, Mor. ch. 12; Lactant. book 7, Instit. ch. 4, 26; Ambros., August., Primasius, Beda, Andr. Vieg., Riber., and Perer. book 15, in Dan. they end in the Anti-Christ. The determination of 1000 years does not please B. Feurbornius, disp. 13, T. 3, Giess. in the appendix, p. 299. Gog and Magog seem to be the future leaders of the army of the Anti-Christ, who will come before the end of the world and before the resurrection, v. 7, and therefore these thousand years do not follow, but precede the Anti-Christ and the end of the world. Rashly, therefore, Pannonius, Joachimus, Seraphinus, and Bullinger understand these things concerning the peace of the Church to be fulfilled after the Anti-Christ, who is said to be killed and removed only by the advent of Christ. Whereas, on the contrary, they say that after the death of Elijah and Enoch, according to the Sibyl 350, there will still be time. Ubertinus, however, assigns a doubled number of 70 years, in which, having followed Joachim who posited that these thousand years of happiness would be free from all heresy, he deferred those years and established them before the Anti-Christ: But no century has been without heresy so far, nor will there be one, since the Anti-Christ, the worst of heretics, is to last until the end of the world. P. Galatinus also rashly, as Cornelius observes, counting these thousand years from the time of Christ, asserts that the principal part of them will be in the age of the Pastor or Angelic Pontiff of admirable humility, wisdom, and holiness, who will have twelve Apostles, whom S. Catherine of Siena and Rocellus of Blessed Amadeus promised. Brocardus, following Petrarch, assigns the beginning of these years to the year 313, in which Sylvester received opulent estates from Constantine the Great, which they call the Patrimony of Peter, and a voice was heard in the air: Today poison has been infused into the Church, as Nauclerus testifies in book II, generation. II. whence the end falls in the year 1375, in which the Evangelicals in Gaul and Belgium began to raise themselves. Some place the beginning of this time in the year of Christ 410, in which Rome was captured and plundered by Alaric, King of the Goths, and a great decline of the Roman Empire began to occur with the removal from the midst of τῷ κατέχοντι, 1 Thess. 2:7, so that the end is established in the year 1670, which experience has already refuted: Add that the end of the Anti-Christ is figured in the cited passage of the Apostle at the consummation of the world. What? That finally in the year of Christ 436, the Emperor Augustulus was ejected from Rome, and thus ὁ κατέχων was removed; whence also the beginning of others fixed in the year 331 is rendered doubtful. To others, and primarily to a certain Anonymous, it pleases to set the year 395 for the beginning and the year of Christ 1655 for the term, to fulfill the 1290 annual days of Daniel, because both the term from which and to which he produces 1685 years from the birth of Christ, from which 30 years are to be subtracted, which he had when he undertook the office, so that 1655 years emerge, to which an end will be brought for both the Anti-Christ and the whole world, citing Augustine, book 18 of The City of God, ch. 54, that the nations pretended that St. Peter taught that the Christian religion would last for 365 years. Which opinion, however, Augustine did not approve, whose judgment holds here as well. That year passed, which a fictitious divination promised, and deceived vanity believed. Others set the term of the days of Dan. 12:36 as the year 1666, fatal to the Anti-Christ, but without a solid foundation of scripture and the event of fulfillment. Those times saw not the end, but a new cruelty of the Anti-Christ in Hungary, the end of which is not yet foreseen. I pass over the fact that the time of the beginning is not certain even to the authors themselves, with some choosing the year 320, in which the dissipation of the Christian people ceased, and others the year 331, in which Constantine the Great transferred his seat to Rome, and setting the end in the persecution begun on account of the Gregorian Calendar, and other new Papal persecutions which were to last 45 years. Add that Constans the Emperor and Honorius still held the Roman seat, and that around the year 331 there is a great κρινόμενον.

It is a refutation of a false exposition that the Chiliasts take the thousand years in verse 4 properly and literally for a determined course of a thousand years. Whom Dn. D. Schindterus praises in his work on the Chiliastic kingdom. Cornelius a Lapide opposes the pleasure-seekers, and not without cause, with the passage of Matt. 22:30: In the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but shall be as the Angels of God. We add Rom. 14:17: The kingdom of God is not food and drink.

Concerning these thousand years, this is the opinion of the blessed Gravius: It seems to agree more with the historical fulfillment if we establish that the beginning of this millennium should be placed in the year of Christ 453, in which Attila, the most ferocious King of the Huns, after receiving a defeat on the Catalaunian plains, having been entreated by Leo, the Roman Bishop, departed from Italy and left the Western Empire entirely. Being asked the reason for his sudden departure, he replied: It was not the Pontiff who deterred me, but two old men, with flowing beards, of a form more terrible than human, threatening me with death with drawn swords unless I spared the suppliants. Then truly was the Gogitic Satan bound. For from that time, hindered by the power of Princes united as if by chains, he could not invade the Christian world toward the West. The end of this millennium, however, falls in the year of Christ 1453, in which Gog and Magog, i.e. The Turks occupied Constantinople, and having destroyed the empire of the East, they subjected all of Greece, Thrace, Bulgaria, Serbia, and the greatest part of Hungary to their tyranny. This Turkish power, by the just judgment of God, will remain in its vigor until the final Gogitic battle, in which, by the hand of Almighty God, it will be overcome and collapse.

The blessed Affelmann, in his Heptalogus of Questions, reduces the chiliasts to five classes: I. Those who write that Christ will return corporally before the last day and will establish such a kingdom on this earth. II. Those who restrict it more specifically to the land of Canaan, into which they say the Jews are to be led back. III. Those who claim the happiness of some millennium for their martyrs who are to be resurrected before the last day. IV. Those who understand the happiness spiritually and refer it to the Anti-Christ destroyed, the Turk extinguished, the heretics overthrown, the persecutions ceasing, and the Church being Catholicly Evangelical. V. Those who interpret it both spiritually and corporally, and promise us as much of it before the last judgment as there was in Paradise before the fall.

And after him he must be loosed for a little season) We said above at 1:9 that a short time is spoken of in the Prophets as even five hundred years. But there the comparison is made to the duration of the Jewish people, here to the duration of the world.

Lord Schindler, on page 64, understands the little season as 3 1/2 years. For 3 1/2 angelic days make just as many years, Apoc. 11. But what is predicted there is different. Those who confuse those with these show themselves to be too much of a stranger in the Apocalypse, says Pareus. For it concerns the burial of the witnesses, that their bodies are to be left unburied for 3 1/2 days. Nor is it necessary that angelic days be understood there, since they can be taken properly.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

Καὶ ἔδησεν ἀυτὸν χίλια ἔτη, καὶ ἔβαλεν ἀυτὸν εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον καὶ ἔκλεισε.] Transpositio & simul Ebræa loquu- tio, pro quo dicere liceat: Καὶ δήσοντα ἀυτὸν, καὶ βληθέντα εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον ἔκλεισεν εἰς χίλια ἔτη. Sic religatur & concluditur Dæmon, ne noceat Tob. VIII, 3. Apud Va- lerium Maximum VII, 6. est somnium de Dionysio ferreis catenis vincto ad Jovis solium, deinde soluto vinculis mul- tarum urbium cum exitio. Libertas autem hic intelligen- da illa ἐξουσία, de qua actum supra XIII, 3. Sævitiam suam in Christianos exercendi per idololatriam Roma- nam, sive per Principes idololatras: ideoque mille illo- rum annorum initium duci debet ab edicto Constantini, quod est apud Eusebium, in quo vincti Draconis est mentio. Romani autem Imperatores exemplum sequuti sunt Reges, alii citius, alii serius, sicut ante Imperato- rum sævitiam in Christianos imitati fuerunt. Ad mille annos felices referunt Judæi loca Danielis VII, 25. VIII, 14. ubi Jachiadem vide, Esa. XI, 6. & sequentibus. LX, 18. 22. LXV, 19. 20. Vide Justinum colloquio cum Try- phone. Anni mille felices per secundum Adamum re- spondent annis ferme mille, per quos duravit Adami prio- ris miseria.

Καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ἐπάνω ἀυτῶ.] Carcerem obsignavit, ne quis aperiret. Vid. Daniel. VI, 17. In Manuscripto: Καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ὀμμάτως ἀυτὸν.

Ἵνα μὴ πλανᾷ ἔτι τὰ ἔθνη.] Gentes nempe quæ Impe- rii Romani fuerunt. Ne deciperet nempe eas inflamman- das ad cædem piorum. Vide infra 7.

Ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη.] Tunc enim alia erit suscita- turus mala, de quibus infra 7.

De mille annis illis gravissimæ sunt concertatio- nes, quos definite totidem intelligunt chiliastæ vel millenarii, alii plerique indefinite: Numerum cer- tum & finitum pro incerto & indefinito accipientes. Illorum duplex datur classis.

Ad primam pertinent veteres inde ab ipso fere Apocalypseos initio a Papia nempe, quem Ire- neus, & Hieronymus auditorem S. Johannis Apo- stoli faciunt, sed ipso invito: qui sub initium com- mentationis suæ testatur, se nunquam audivisse san- ctos Apostolos: sed traditionem illam de mille an- nis a Presbyteris Apostolorum discipulis accepisse. Ni- mis vero credulum & parum judiciosum, fabulas multas pro veritate arripuisse, judicat Eusebius. Justinus tamen traditionem illam sequutus est Dial. cum Tryphone, nec non Irenæus l. V. Nepos Episc. Ægypt. refutatus a Dionys. Alex. apud Eu- seb. l. VII. c. 10. Tertullianus item l. III. contra Marc. Lactantius l. VII. Instit. c. 23. Victorinus Pictav. in Apocal. & quondam etiam Augustinus l. c. Qui vero postmodum mutavit sententiam, quia Papistæ Viegas, Ribera, Pererius, Cornelius a Lapi- de, Tirinus, observant Augustinum l. XX. de C. D. cap. 7. cum Ambrosio, Gregorio M. l. IV. Moral. cap. 12. mille annos de universo tempore regni Christi us- que ad Anti-Christum intelligere, id quod allegati Papistæ quoque approbant. Sed pertinent hi mille anni potius ad tempora inde a regimine Con- stanti M. sequuta, quæ postmodum excipiet bel- lum Gogiticum. Hieronymus vocat traditionem illam Judaicam δευτέρωσιν. Sequuti etiam di- cuntur Papiam Apollinarius, Suevus Coracion, nec traditionem illam damnare ausus fuit Hieronymus l. IV. in Jerem. cap. XIX. propterea quod multi Ec- clesiasticorum nostrorum & martyrum approbarint. Reprobavit eandem tamen ipse in cap. XXXVI. Ezech. & cap. VII. Dan. Cæterum aliter senten- tiam de terreno Christi regno post resurrectionem mille annorum, eoque carnalibus deliciis pleno asse- ruit Cerinthus, teste Eusebio l. III. H. E. cap. 25. & Dionysius Alexandr. aliter pii veteres: Missum fa- cientes illud somnium deliciarum corporearum, quod ex parte renovavit onus Ecclesiæ cum A- nabaptistis Monaster. & fanaticis nonnullis. Re- centiores vero videntur nihil cum somnio illo com- mercii habere velle, ut puta Johann. Piscator, Alstedius.

Porro indefinite explicant annos designatos alii de toto decursu temporum ab ascensione Christi usque ad diem novissimum, præeunte Augustino l. XX. de C. D. cap. 7. Cum quo tamen, ut ante monuimus, Beda, Anshelmus, & alii non in die novissimo ter- minum figunt, sed in adventu Anti-Christi. Non- nulli apud Lyranum de Papa Calixto Imperatorem Henricum V. ligante per excommunicationem decla- rarunt per annos 1000. id est, usque ad Anti-Chri- stum: Quem sensum reprobat, explicans de In- nocentio Fransisci & Dominici ordinis ad reprimen- dam potestatem Dæmonum confirmatores. Sed hæc explicatio æque inepta. Quam præclare fratres Ord. Minorum & Prædicatorum reprimant Draco- nem, vel ipsæ mutuæ eorum concertationes do- ceant. Joh. Viterb. in h. l. Sixto pollicetur vi- ctoriam hic prædictam de gente Saracenica Ann. 1481. Sed eum experientia confutavit. Uberti- nus de Casalis ligatum Satanam ait sub Constantino, solutum scrib Joh. XXII. An. 1315. quem mysticum Anti-Christum vocat. Sunt qui tempus infinitum per 1000. annos ipsam æternitatem intelligant. Quod non revicturi & cum Christo regnaturi im- pii, quamdiu sancti cum Christo regnabunt, h.e. in æternum. Ita Alph. a Castro l. III. contr, hær. Verb. Beatitudo hær. 2. per hosce annos denotare vult æternitatem beatorum in gaudio & gloria cœlesti.

At St. Johannes solutum post mille annos Gog & Magog congregaturum in prælium docet.

Aliam interpretationem affert B. Philipp. Ni- colai l. II. de regno CHRISTI · cap. 5. Martyres re- pudiato Papatu cum Christo vixisse spirituali vita in vera Dei cognitione per 1000. annos durante regno Papali, reliquos post revicturos, manifestato filio per- ditionis. Sed hæ explicationes, veriori propo- sita, facile in spongiam incumbent, ad quam pro- inde jam properamus.

Interpretatur autem B. Phil. Nicolai loco citato p. 225. de R. E. Hormisdâ alligante Imper. Justinum exhortatione ad Hæreticorum exterminationem Ma- humeturientium nempe Arianorum & Nestoriauo- rum. Sed cum ipse Pontif. hodie fert aut approbat Jesuitas Nestorianizantes? Annon ea parte obste- tricatur Draconi? Plerique mille annos definitè, & exactè intelligentes initium eorum ponunt Ann. Christi 73. quo Apostoli cursum suum in his terris consummarant, alii tempus regiminis Constantini M. illis finem assignantes in Papatu Gregorii VII. Hildebr. tyrannide valde celebris; quo tempore Saraceni etiam multas in Oriente vastarunt Eccle- sias, in anno 1300. circa quod tempus imperium Turcicum sub Otthomannis robur maximum ac- quisivit, occupata florentissima orbis parte, & tan- dem capta Constantinopoli sede Orientalis Imperii, quam etiamnum obtinet porta Otthomannica. Vid. Joh. Bapt. Nizar. apud Wolffium Lect. memor. Cent. XVI. p. 884. Quandoquidem Mahometici ma- nibus Christianorum eripuerunt Bithyniam, Cappa- dociam, Lyciam, Armeniam majorem & minorem, Cariam, Lydiam, Paphlagoniam, Phrygiam, Pontum, Pamphiliam, Galatiam, & in summa minorem Asiam universam (Turciam dictam) & cum Babylonia Æ- thiopiam. Adhæc perfidus iste Tyrannus transmisso mari Europam ingressus, adeoque Achaja, Attica, to- ta Thracia cum Imperio Constantinopolitano, Bæotia, Æolia, Peloponnenso, Morea, Epiro, Macedonia, Al- bania potitus, superatoque Bulgaria, Bosnia, Servia, Russia, Rhodi, Nigropontis, Belgradi, totiusq; ferme Dalmatiæ, Croatiæ, Sclavoniæ, Poloniæ, Ungariæ & Syriæ regnis; necdum imperii satur cuperet insuper Germaniam, Italiam, Galliam & Hispaniam invade- re, adeo ut se faciat appellari Imperatorem Imperato- rum, Regem Regum, Dominum Dominorum, & Do- minum Paradisi terrestris atque Hierosolymæ, Prin- cipem Principum & Subjugatorem Tartariæ, Persiæ, Indiarum & magni Cairi: ut insignis profecto fuerit ira Domini adversus miseros nos Christianos, qui per- misit, ut Turca tot Episcopatus totque Ecclesias è ma- nibus Christianorum extorserit, &, quod majoris est momenti, ipsam quoque terram sanctam, ubi Chri- stus sacrosanctum suum effudit sanguinem. Nec ab- surdum est dicere, quod per Satanæ à catenis libera- tionem post mille annos ab Angelo factam intelligi pos- sit Otthomannorum Mahumeticorum adventus. Un- de Johannes XX. Apoc. dicit, quod Angelus ligaverit Satanam ad mille annos, ne fideles perturbaret, & hoc factum est sub Constantino (ut multi periti ac do- cti viri opinantur) circa trecentesimum scilicet & vi- gesimum annum, qui majorem seditiosorum populo- rum, perversarumque gentium partem in statum sa- tis tolerabilem redegit, unde exacto post millenario ec- ce per Angelum, hoc est, voluntatem Divinam aliquo temporis spatio revinctus sit Satanas, & hoc contigit circa 1300. cum eruptione familiæ Otthomannicæ, ni- mirum ab Otthomanno Tartaro: quod quidem per exiguum tempus durabit, & postea Satanas denuo profligabitur. Unde beati illi prædicandi, qui patien- ter hactenus tulere Mahometicam istam & Ottho- mannicam persecutionem, cum dicat sacra scriptura: Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur. De Otthoman- nica hac fidelium persecutione ejusque præfixo quasi termino vaticinatus est Daniel cap. XII. dicendo (jux- ta genuinam Ebraicam expositionem) Beatus qui ex- pectat & pervenit usque ad dies mille trecentos trigin- taquinque. Quod autem hic dierum numerus de tempore adventus Otthomannorum intelligi debeat, resolutio (meo quidem judicio) hunc in modum fiet. Sermonem habens hoc loco Daniel de eorum beatitu- dine, qui ad dies pervenient 1335. stante eo, quod tum affligentur Christiani, tria circa hoc dictum veniunt consideranda, primo dierum numerus, secundo eo- rum qualitas, tertio eorum principium. Ad primum propositum dico, antiquos Interpretes diem pro anno accipere consuevisse, atque etiam pro multis annis: adeo 1335. totidem annos intelligere oporteat. Ad se- cundum loquendo de dierum ejusmodi aut annorum per dies istos intellectorum qualitate, utrum solares intelligendi sint, vel lunares anni, dico, (cum Prophe- ta hoc in loco de eorum, qui ad tempus illorum dierum sunt perventuri, beatitudine agat) intelligendos esse solares, quandoquidem anni bonis eventibus præfixi solares erant, lunares autem infaustis. Hæc ille. Consonat Ferdinandus Castrus l. 9. in Histor. Turc. p. II. c. 1. Cujus sententiæ quoque præ aliis sub- scribit B. Gerhardus disp. III. de nov. fanat. §. 15. Est & alia nova regni Chiliastici junctura in scri- pto P. E. Hosl. (forte P. Egardi Posaune) deli- neata: qui Angelum Satanam alligantem de Job. Arnd. veterem hominem in abyssum scripturæ perdi- tionis & gratiæ dejicientem, mille annos de trien- nio & novem mensibus accepit, & initium eorum ab Ann. 1625. fecit, quo revicturos in Spiritu Joh. Ba- ptistam & Paulum Apostolum cum Taulero & Kem- pisio, verumque Christianismum potenter propugna- turos asseruit: Sed qui nequicquam à B. Cluvero monitus, ab experientia solide jam confutatus est. Novum id & inauditum, mille annos tres annos cum novem mensibus conficere, cujus commenti causa aliud assumpsit de computo ab Anno. 1517. Luthe- rana Reformationis titulo insigni instituendo. Sed quænam est analogia sive proportionis sive attri- butionis, ut vocant, quænam similitudo 1000. an- norum, & 45. dierum inter se? quæ numeri istius 3. ann. & 9. mens. qui efficit 45. non dies, non menses, quid vero denique? Quem numerum cuinam alteri conferre velit, non apparet, mihi certe notum non est.

Cæterum Fanatici, Anabaptistæ variis erroribus ex orco resuscitatis in urbe Monasteriensi Sleidano l. X. teste libro sub titulo restitution. conscripto regnum Christi terrenum promulgarunt, in quo tan- tum justitia regnatura sit; Quidam in Belgio, re- ferente in Conc. Evang. Jansenio p. 842. se Chri- stum Regem etiam in Sion somniavit, non destitutus prodigiis & revelationibus ut jactitabat. Illi rena- tos tertii seculi, quod Spiritus S. vocabant, & pror- sus sanctum ac per mille annos duraturum so- mniabant. Taceo in præsenti Nathan. Ælian, li- bro Mattenin, de quo Nucl. Histor. Meiger. §. 25. David. Georg. superioris, Ezechiel. Meth. Weigel. Nagel. Christoph. Andr. Christian. Simplic. Paulum Felgenhawern, Angelum Mariam, Johannem Wer- ner. Richardum ejus Apostolum hujus seculi, de quibus Wittebergens. & Jenens. Theologi ex par- te nomine Lubec. Hamburg. Luneburg. Ministerii, B. D. Nicol. Hunnius, B. D. Theod. Thummius, B. D. Johann. Mullerus, B. Weberus egerunt.

Adolphus Held in Prüfung der Sache Eliæ Prætorii plures quam mille annos (ait) probabiliter, si æstimentur circumstantiæ templi, cujus dimen- sionem tradit S. Johannes ex Ezechiele designari, septem constituens mundi ætates, secundum se- ptem ejusdem, quas fingit, quoad totam substan- tiam mutationes, 1. a conditu mundi ad Abra- ham. 2. inde ad Christum. 3. ad novissimum diem; eo Genealogiam Christi apud Matthæum respicere somnians; quia Deus sacerdotium & regnum suum istis temporibus mutavit: quas tres magnas iterum subdividit Heldius quoad secun- dam horam 1. ab Abraham ad Babylonicam ca- ptivitatem, ab hac ad Christum, & inde ad no- vissimum diem: duos novos homines commentus 1. qui e peccatoribus ad ὑοθεσίαν per Spiritum S. regeniti sunt. 2. qui e justis per Spiritum vitæ renati imitatores Dei sunt. Commemorat Hel- dius quendam Ludov. Frideric. Giffthoël, qui cir- cumcursitans undiquaque se Regem Davidem se- cundum nuncupet, vindicaturum Ecclesiam contra Babylon, sicut Elias contra Sacerdotes Baal.

Joh. Berckenthal refert de quodam, quod sigil- lum sub hac ἐπιγραφῇ usurparit: Sacerdos juxta ordinem Melchisedech, & aliis quintam Monar- chiam somniantibus, adducitque fanaticos plurimos cum Theophrasto & Caspare Schwenckfeld. nimi- rum Sebast. Franck, Dieterich Volckers, Corn- hard, Jacob Behm, Val. Weigel. Paul Lautensack, El. Prætor. Frider. Brecheling, Athenette Bouri- gons, Jac. Taube Labedenistas, & imprimis e Joh. Roth de corporali excidio Anti - Christi do- cet, daß die Zeit von der Rache GOttes kom- men ist, daß Babel muß geurtheilet werden durch den Mund GOttes, und das Schwerdt Eliä alle Baals - Priester tödten muß, und die Bosheit der Erden wegnehmen. Eine Stan- dart werde aufgerichtet Anno 1671. in das vor- der Theil der Welt in der Stadt Amsterdam, worunter alle zerstreuete Jüden sollen versammlet werden. In Niederland soll ein Souverain Häupt regieren, und so eine Monarchiale Regierung fort- setzen, und so soll Christus erhoben werden. Inde Anno 1674. eductum iri exercitum sub Rege ali- quo &c. Fanaticum hunc mirum quantum ex- tollit Quirin Kuhlmann libro, cui titulum dedit Neu - Begeisterter Böhm, quem ait esse Ange- lum cum æterno Evangelio per cælum volantem, qui de se & Rhotio Propheta Belgico vaticinatus sit. Quem (Bohmium intelligo) Prophetam septimi temporis facit, Monarchiæ Jesu, Lutherum contra Anti-Christum dicit, jactitatque eum Anno 1624. M. Jun. ab Hoëo, Leisero, Balduino, Meisnero, Ger- hardo Dresdæ examinatum, nosque Dn. D. Scher- zerum, me, ac Dn. D. Joh. Musæum ad responsum provocat. Nonnulla capp. solum referam e Bohm ab ipso approbatis 150. vaticiniis & revelationi- bus, idque verbis autoris propriis, quæ cap. XV. leguntur: Die allerletzte Zeit wird bald anbre- chen, und eröffnen sich alle Verborgenheiten, weil die Wiederbringung aller Dinge herzu nahet. Alle Welt-Reiche werden fallen, so bald es in Mitter- nacht taget. Das Pabstthum, Türckenthum ne- benst allen Secten und Religionen erlangen als- denn ihre gewisse Endschafft. Darnach soll wieder erscheinen mit Noah Moses, Elias, und wird Elias Feuer - Zeichen der Welt zum Zeichen gege- ben. Die Zerbrechung der grossen Stadt Babel, der verwirrten Christenheit, stehet für der Thür, alle Secten sollen bald entsectet werden. Es wird in kurtzem der Anti-Christ samt dern Thiere, der Hu- ren und falschen Propheten von einem Jünglinge werden entdecket und erstrecket. Ein grosser König und Beherrscher des Erdreichs wird ein wenig über den Mittag des sechsten Tages gebohren, gros- se Helden sind um ihn, Propheten weissagen von ihm, und sein Glanz gehet vom Auffgang biß zum Niedergang. Die Türcken, Jüden und Heyden Bekehrung ist stracks zu erwarten, ein Hirte wird die Völcker in eine Heerde versammlen. Das Ge- heimniß der JEsus-Monarchi oder Reiches GOt- tes wird werden vollendet um sieben und ze- hen Uhr, und wird seyn darnach eine Hütte GOttes bey den Menschen, &c. Gloriatur se per 1000. Theosophicas quæstiones plures, quam 1000000000. novas expedire posse, quarum ne unica ab ullo Theologorum, qui scholarum me- thodum sine Spiritu Dei sectantur, solvi queat. Mera sunt verborum portenta.

Prædictus Adolph Held (ut ad illum revertamur) superioribus añis Hamburgo ad me Wittebergam ea, ut testabatur, de causa venit, quod persuasus es- set a nemine sese rectius de suis dogmatibus infor- mari posse, quem argumentis e scriptura convin- cebam, ut ad silentium redigeretur, aliis tamen me- re Topicis a persona ejus jam decrepitæ ætatis LX. annorum, ab Apostolis, quos habuerat, apostatis, in- firmitate judicii, ignorantia sensus scripturæ, impe- ritia artis disputandi, sine qua neminem convince- re possit &c. quæ totum orbem abs ipso septimam renovationem accepturum essa, vix persuasurus sit, maxime ambiguum reddebam: quem Altona prope Hamburgum ante ἀνάλυσιν erroribus suis renun- ciaffe, fassum se e Verbo Dei melius abs me infor- matum, B. Mülleri literæ retulerunt. Commini- scitur is filios Dei, qui ad statum redemptionis ex ira pervenere, sed adhuc spiritualiter sub Principe mundi sunt, & extra statum justificationis, per notitiam na- turalem nos mysterium S. Trinitatis cognoscere fin- git, & novas quasdam loquutiones invehit, in po- steriori MS. confessione mihi oblata de imagine Dei, de renovatione, de remissione peccatorum quoad cor- poralia &c. valde incommode loquitur, prior ve- ro quam sub primum adventum aliquot annis an- te de septem mutationibus mundi exhibuerat ty- pis exscripta, sataniticis scatebat opinionibus, sed quæ memoria jam exciderunt: chiliasmo autem, si recte recordor, Autorem addictum testabantur. Primam, quantum memoria adhuc sufficit, muta- tionem primæ assignabat ætati a mundi conditu ad diluvium; alteram secundæ sive ad Abrahamum, sive ad Exodum; tertiam usque ad captivitatem Babylonicam, quartam ad Christum usq́; extende- bat: quintam, ni fallor, ad Lutherum: sextam ad sese, Prophetam vel Evangelistam septima universa- lis mutationis creaturarum omnium. Tales enim omnes ille faciebat: nec explicare tamen, rogatus, poterat cæteras extra primam & ultimam, quoad reliqua Dei opera præter hominem microcosmum, in quo tamen mutationem non substantialem sed accidentatem agnoscere cogebatur: omnes illas mutationes denique restringens ad officii Chri- sti Sacerdotalis & Regii diversas administrationes. Hæc si recte memini erat summa opinionum fana- tici, qui de partibus hominis, de interiori & exte- riori homine, quantum adhuc animo recolere pos- sum, propriis indulgebat speculationibus.

Eliam Prætorium, cujus antea quoque mentio- nem fecimus, in saniorem jam propendere senten- tiam, & errorum suorum aliqua pœnitudine duci, literæ Hamburg. proxime nunciarunt; modo sera hujus hominis pœnitentia seria sit, & vera! Mille annos seculi aurei quidem tuetur, sed non affir- mare audet in illis voluptates mundanas locum ha- bituras. Felicitatem ergo spiritualem se tantum istis beatis temporibus assignare ait: cui non repugnet scriptura de calamitate novissimi temporis loquens: utpote quæ calamitates & bella ac iniquitatem & impietatem hominum non regnantium cum Chri- sto, sed eorum, qui extra Ecclesiam sunt, describat, vel tempora seculum beatum sequutura respiciat. Verum scripturæ vox diserta est de temporibus novissimis 1. Tim. IV. 1. Secundum quam omni- bus vitæ diebus fideles dolor, luctus, crux, mors & quæ non calamitates manent, Psal. XC. 10. Sir. XL. 1. seqq. 2. Tim. III. 12. Apoc. XXI. 4. De adven- tu Domini & de ἀπισίᾳ per universam terram: Num putas fidem inventurum filium hominis IN TERRA cum venerit? Luc. XIIX. 8. Quæ opi- nioni de conversione cum Judæorum tum gen- tium non convenire, etsi ea non Prætorio tantum fanaticisq; aliis, sed multis etiam orthodoxis ac Pa- tribus certa ratione probari videatur, Origeni, Hi- lario, Ambrosio, Hieronymo, Augustino, Chryso- stomo, Haymoni, B. Ægid. Hunno, Winckelman- no, Menzero, Hafenreffero, Balduino, Gerhardo, Meisnero, Gravio &c. quod alias observavimus.

Rectius autem certos, & mille quidem annos de- signari ex hisce patet, quæ jam sequentur, adeoque sententiæ nostræ favent 1. Apocalypseos consuetu- do. Solet enim illa, cum numeros adhibet, certum tempus definire. 2. Convenientia explicationis. Vere enim tum ligatus Satanas non absolute, nec id simpliciter: Sed ne inter eas prohiberentur aut tollerentur prorsus Ecclesiæ: vere iterum dimis- sus, qua persequutiones gentiles: quia Muham- medani rectius gentilibus accensentur, quam Chri- stianis, qua doctrinam & vitam, quantum ad deli- tias alterius seculi & polygamiam, aliaque scelera gentilium, ἀποθέωσιν Mahometi paganam &c. Si dicas, quomodo ligatus censeri potuit Satanas, qui sub persequutionibus Arianicis mirum quan- tum sæviit? Succurrit Augustini distinctio in Ps. IX. Prima Ecclesiæ persecutio, antequam scil. Sa- tanas ligaretur, fuit violenta, cum proscriptioni- bus, tormentis, cædibus Christiani ad sacrificium ligarentur: altera fuit fraudulenta, quia per hæ- reticos & falsos fratres agitur: tertia Anti-Christi tempore & violenta & fraudulenta est, vim ha- bens in imperio, dolum in miraculis. De prima itaque loqui S. Johannem, non de secunda. Etsi vero intra illos mille annos regnarit quoq; Anti- Christus, (quod huic sententiæ objicit Cornelius) non tamen Ecclesiæ omnes esse desierunt: Nam sedet ipse in Ecclesia, 2. Thess. II. Objicit & hoc: Modico tempore imperium Turcicum duraturum, scil. tantum ad horam, diem, mensem, & annum, id est, 390. annos prædicitur. Sed alii e Daniele 45. dies Angelicos constituunt, annosque definiunt 1335. ab ortu Anti-Christi, unde finem assignare oportebit, nisi propter electos dies decurtentur ann. 1940. cir- citer. Nam initium Anti-Christi alii aliud consti- tuunt, ut hic ἀποτόμως quid definire non liceat. 3. Assumitur Chiliastarum sententia geminum fal- sum fatente Pareo; 1. Satanam nondum fuisse liga- tum, ne amplius seduceret gentes in Paganismo, quod repugnat Historiæ: 2. post ruinam Papatus mundum non amplius mille annos adhuc duraturum, quod repugnat oraculis de abolendo Anti-Christo per illustrem adventum Domini, post quem porro mille annos mundi statuere absurdum mihi videtur. Non addit rationes, cur absurdum id videatur, nos ergo addimus: 1. quia scriptura conjungit im- mediate adventum Christi secundum, quem gemi- num temere & ἄτεχνεαφῆς Chiliastæ fingunt cum interitu mundi Matth. XXIV. 29. 30. 2. Thess.

1. 7. 8. 2. Petr. III. 10. 11. 12. 2. cum seculi consum- matione 1. Cor. 15, 23. Qui ergo mille annis cum Christo adhuc regnarent in hoc seculo pii post ad- ventum Christi? 3. Cum novissimo hujus seculi die, ipsaq; resurrectione mortuorum, quam (cor- poralem) non nisi unicam novit scriptura Joh. 5, 28. c. 6, 38. 1. Thess. 4, 16. 4. Cum extremo judicio, creatione cœli novi & terræ novæ, introductione in cælum novum & terram novam sanctorum Matth. 25, 31. 2. Thess. 1, 7. seqq. 2. Tim. 4, 1. seqq. Es. 66, 22. 2. Petr. 3, 12. Ap. XII. 1. Quomodo er- go, cum fugerit jam terra præsens, in illa Christus regnare poterit cum sanctis per mille annos? 4. Ἀντιλογία ponit, monente Pareo, Chiliastarum no- vorum sententia, ante hos mille Papam Anti- Chri- stum abjectum iri in stagnum ignis, & ruiturum Papatum: Et simul: Papam per mille annos paula- tim resumpturum vires, & illis elapsis sese cum Re- gibus Ethnicis conjuncturum ad bellum Christianis inferendum. Quomodo vero Papa resumat vires in stagno ignis jacens. Sic ille contra proprios fidei so- cios: qui si excipiant: Non quidem ille ipse Papa in stagnum abjectus resumet vires; poterit vero aliquis alius post eum esse, qui demum illustri adventu Chri- sti aboleatur: Regerit Pareus: Hoc vero est, ludere in re seria: Monetque: Hi se explicent, partialem an totalem eversionem Papatus intelligant. Si partia- lem intelligunt, dicant ante centum jam annos liga- tum esse Satanam, quia ante centum annos cæpit ruere Papatus in Germania & aliquot regnis, fa- tente etiam Bellarmino: Nam, inquit, ab eo tempo- re, quo per vos Papa Anti- Christus esse cæpit, non modo non crevit ejus imperium, sed semper magis ac magis decrevit. Si universalem seu totalem, quo- modo bestia paulatim resumet vires, maxime in sta- gno ignis jacens? 5. Ἄτοπον quo premit eos idem, quod nempe dicant: Quod in principio mille anno- rum Martyres sint corporaliter revicturi, & re- gnaturi cum Christo mille annos, cum textus expres- se loquatur de animabus, non de corporibus marty- rum: nec dicat quod revixerint aut resurrexerint, sed quod vixerint. 6. Aliud item ἄτοπον est, quod statuant duplicem resurrectionem mortuorum, unam Martyrum post ruinam Papatus; alteram reliquo- rum mortuorum post mille annos regni Martyrum; quod, judice Pareo, alienum est a fide Catholica: Cre- do resurrectionem carnis, hoc est, omnium mortuo- rum, futuram in novissimo die, & experientia refel- litur. Rursus enim si ruinam Papatus intelligunt par- tialem, cum hæc ante centum annos jam facta sit, etiam resurrectionem primam corporalem martyrum jam factam esse ostendere debent: Si totalem, cum hæc in illustri demum adventu Domini futura sit, etiam martyres tunc cum aliis omnibus resurrecturos esse negare non possunt. Addit septimo: Concilient mihi velim (ego enim non possum) quod statuunt, post mille annos ab everso Papatu Christum venturum esse ad judicium: & post mille illos annos Gog & Magog suscepturum esse bellum Christianis inferendum. An vero bellum hoc post reditum Christi ad judicium ex- tremum suspicietur? Denique 8. hæc opinio cum er- rore Chiliastarum a Christianis dudum exploso pla- ne convenit in eo, quod contra prophetiam Apostoli, de Anti- Christo illustri demum adventu Domini abolendo 2. Thess. 2, 8. post Anti- Christum abolitum mille insuper annos mundo tribuit: quodque contra scripturas de resurrectione omnium mortuorum fu- tura in novissimo die resurrectiones duas particula- res inducit: Saltem differt in eo, quod non terrenum, ut illi, sed cœleste regnum millenarium facit; quan- quam Augustinus fateatur, inter Chiliastas etiam fuisse, qui spirituales delitias in illo sabbatho sanctis futuras per Domini præsentiam crederent. Hæc omnia Paræus, quæ merito Parenti ejus in Christo Venerando (sic vocat Piscatorem) opponuntur, & novisChiliastis dissolvenda relinquuntur. Committimus hic fratres Cadmæos inter se qui prælia miscent. Illam de felicitate sive corporali,seu spirituali explicationem non convenire oraculis extremi temporis sortem describentibus in propatulo est. Voluptatibus corporeis favet etiam Lactantius l. VII. Instit. c. 24. Tum qui erunt in corporibus vivi non morientur, sed per eosdem mille annos infinitam multitudinem generabunt, & erit soboles eorum sancta & Deo chara. Qui autem ab inferis suscitabuntur, ii præerunt viventibus, velut Judices: Sed quosdam relinquentur in victoriam Dei, ut triumphentur a justis & subjugentur perpetuæ servituti. Addit insuper terræ fæcunditatem maximam, animalium, avium minas; & Reges gentium venient a finibus terræ cum donis ac muneribus, ut adorent & honorificent Regem magnum, cujus nomen erit præclarum ac venerabile universis nationibus, quæ sub cælo erunt. Quibus ex parte similia reperias apud Cornelium a Lapide. Ea vero si sibi constare debeant,tempora exquisite distinguenda erunt. Et num credemus Gog & Magog præsumpturos sanctos jam immortales bello aggredi & conficere? Aut librum vitæ in ultimo demum judicio aperiendum patefactum iri in particulari justorum Electorum resuscitatione? Aut novam Hierosolymam de cælo descendere visam mille annis jam habitatam dicturi sumus, aut castra sine dolore, sine labore futura? Cur etiam Martyrum tantum resurrectio designata, cum eorum qui bestiam venerantur, si omnium hominum universalis comprehensa resuscitatio? Cur animarum tantum mentio facta, si resuscitatio corporum tum fiet?Quomodo illa toties in sacris asserta novissimi temporis extrema securitas consistet, si tanta novissimæ ætatis mundi per integros mille annos duratura spiritualis felicitas asseratur? Vide sis de illa Matth. 24, 12. 37. Luc. 17, 26. c. 18, 8. 1. Tim. 4, 1. 2. 2. Tim. 3, 1. 2. Thess. 2, 8. 2. Petr. 3, 3. Jud. v. 18. 1. Joh. 2, 8. ut id jam prætermittam non dici posse φανέρωσιν vel ἐπιφάνειαν adventum Christi novissimum, quemadmodum sæpius dicitur Luc. 17, 30. 1. Cor. 1, 7. Col. 3, 4. 2. Thess. 1, 7. c. 2, 8. 1. Tim. 6, 14. 2. Tim. 4, 1. 8. Tit. 1, 13. 1. Petr. 1. 7. 13. c. 4, 13. c. 5, 4. 1. Joh. 2, 28. c. 3, 2. nec expectabunt adeo sancti cum dolore adventum Domini, aut desiderabunt coronam, utpote jam ante acceptam, Luc. 21, 24. Rom. 8, 19. 2. Tim. 4, 8. si jam ipsum habituri sunt præsentem, qui ante mille annos apparuerit, seque manifestarit? Illi antiqui millenarii ab Anti-Christi morte oriuntur 1000. annos, & post sextum mundi millenarium fingunt septimum, in quo sancti cum Christo in summis delitiis vel corporalibus vel spiritualibus (quod Irene & Augustino placuit) quam sententiam P. Salas ceu hæreticam damnat. Sed scriptura non modo præmia piarum animarum & sanctorum hominum non corporalia, sed spiritualia, non temporalia, sed æterna facit, Matth. V. 12. 2. Cor. IV. 17. Phil. III. 20. Sed & simpliciter negat, regnum Christi esse de hoc mundo, & gloriam sanctorum hic docet adhuc absconditam esse, Joh. 18. 36. Psal. 45, 7. Rom. 8. Col. 3, 3. 4. Ebr. 2, 8. nec nisi demum in altera vita abolenda esse peccatum, mortem & mala omnia, 2. Petr. 3, 12. 1. Cor. 15, 24. Apoc. 21, 4. nec aliam resurrectionem quam universalem tradit Joh. 5, 28. c. 6, 39. 1. Cor. 15, 22. 1. Thess. 4, 16. coronamque justitiæ expectandam, in die παντοκριτικῷ, omnibusque qui diligunt Chri- stum, distribuendam esse, docet 2. Thess. 1, 6. 2. Tim. 4, 8. imo ad finem usque mundi persecuto- res & Martyres futuros prædicit Apoc. 20, 9. & beatitudinem animabus decollatorum propter Ver- bum Dei, non martyribus tantum adscribit Apoc. 6. ut nec Piscatoris, chiliasmum interpretantis de marty- ribus, ante universalem resurrectionem a Christo resuscitandis, & per mille annos cum ipso regnatu- ris, opinioni locus sit, cui Sociniana in Matth. 1, 63. convenit. Quod enim Piscator v. 4. mortuos qui non revixerunt, urget, nil ad rem facit, quum op- ponantur illi sanctis, adeoque impii intelligantur spiritualiter mortui, Matth. 8, 22. Joh. 5, 25. Eph. 5, 14. 1. Tim. 5, 8. Apoc. 3, 1. sanctique describan- tur iis beatitudinis attributis, quæ non Martyrum solum sunt, sed omnium Electorum, quod mors secunda non habeat in eos potestatem, Apoc. 2, 11. quod sint Sacerdotes Dei Rom. 12, 1. 1. Petr. 2, 9. Ap. 1, 6. quod cum Christo regnent super mundum, peccatum, Diabolum Joh. 4. 5. c. 5, 4. inque Thro- no Christi sessuri sint, Apoc. 3, 2.

Definite annos etiam intelligunt, qui a passione Christi eos inchoant, quos nominat Cornelius a Lapide, Gregor. l. 4. Mor. c. 12. Lactant. l. 7. In- stit. c. 4, 26. Ambros. August. Primasius, Beda, Andr. Vieg. Riber. & Perer. l. 15. in Dan. finiunt in Anti- Christo. Non placet B. Feurbornio anno- rum 1000. determinatio disp. 13. T. 3. Giess. in ap- pend. p. 299. Gog & Magog videntur Duces futu- ri exercitus Anti-Christi, qui veniet ante finem mundi & ante resurrectionem v. 7. ideoque mille hi anni non sequuntur, sed præcedunt Anti - Chri- stum finemque mundi. Temere itaque Pannoni- us, Joachimus, Seraphinus & Bullinger hæc de pa- ce Ecclesiæ intelligunt implenda post Anti-Chri- stum, qui per adventum Christi demum interfici- endus, & tollendus dicitur. Quum contra illi, post mortem Eliæ, & Henochi ex Sibylla 350. adhuc fore ajant. Ubertinus vero duplicato numero ann. 70. affignet, in quo Joachimum hos mille felicitatis an- nos omni hæresi carituros statuentem sequutus, deferens annos illos ante Anti-Christum consti- tuit: Sed nullum hactenus seculum sine hæresi fuit, nec futurum est, quum Anti-Christus hæreticorum pessimus usque ad finem mundi duraturus sit. Te- mere etiam P. Galat. observante Cornelio, hos mille annos numerans a tempore Christi præcipuam eo- rum partem fore asserit ætate Pastoris vel Pontifi- cis Angelici admirandæ humilitatis, sapientiæ & sanctitatis XII. Apostolos habituri, quem promi- serit S. Catharinus Senens. & Rocel. B. Amadæi. Brocardus, Petrarcham sequutus principium ho- rum annorum assignat Ann. 313. quo Sylvester a Constantino M. opulenta prædia, quæ Patrimo- nium Petri vocant, & vox in aëre audita: Hodie venenum infusum est in Ecclesiam, teste Nauclero l. II. gener. II. unde finis incidit in ann. 1375. quo Evangelici in Gallia & Belgio sese cœperint eri- gere. Nonnulli initium hujus temporis collocant in annum Christi 410. quo Roma ab Alarico Go- thorum Rege capta ac direpta, & magna Impe- rii Romani inclinatio fieri cœpit sublato e me- dio τῷ κατέχοντι, 1. Thess. 2, 7. ut finis constitua- tur Anno 1670. quos jam refutavit experientia: Adde quod finis Anti-Christi figuratur in loco lau- dato Apostoli in consummatione seculi. Quid? quod demum Ann. Christi 436. Imper. Augustu- lus Roma ejectus, & sic ὁ κατέχων sublatus sit; unde etiam aliorum initium in ann. 331. fixum du- bium redditur. Aliis, & imprimis Anonymo cui- piam placet pro initio ann. 395. pro termino ann. Christi 1655. ad implendos Danielis 1290. dies an- nuos, quia uterque terminus a quo & ad quem producit 1685. annos a nativ. Christi quibus sub- trahendi 30. anni, quos habebat, quum aggredere- tur officium, ut prodeant anni 1655. quibus finis afferetur & Anti- Christo & mundo universo, ad- ducentes Augustinum l. XIIX. de civitate Dei c. 54. quod gentes prætenderint S. Petrum docuisse, Chri- stianam religionem 365. annis duraturam. Quam vero opinionem non probavit Augustinus, cujus sententia etiam hic obtinet. Annus iste transiit, quem Divinatio ficta promisit, & decepta vanitas cre- didit. Alii terminum dierum Dan. XII. 36. designa- tum constituunt ann. 1666. Anti-Christo fatalem, sed citra scripturæ fundamentum solidum, & com- plementi eventum. Non finem, sed novam, in Hungaria Anti-Christi M. sævitiem viderunt illa tempora, cujus nondum prospicitur terminus. Ta- ceo, quod nec Autoribus ipsis certum sit initii tem- pus, aliis ann. 320. quo cessavit dissipatio Christiani populi, aliis ann. 331. quo Constantinus M. sedem suam transtulerit Romam, eligentibus, & finem in persecutione ob Gregorian. Calendarium cœpta, novisque aliis Pontificiis persecutionibus 45. ann. duraturis constituentibus. Adde quod Constans Imper. & Honorius Romanam sedem adhuc ha- buerint, quodque circa ann. 331. magnum sit κρινόμενον.

Falsæ expositionis Elenchus est, quod mille an- nos vers. 4. Chiliastæ sumunt proprie & literaliter pro determinato mille annorum curriculo. Quos in eo laudat Dn. D. Schindterus in de regno Chi- liastico. Voluptuariis opponit, nec immerito Cor- nelius a Lapide locum Matth. XXII. 30. In resur- rectione neq; nubent neq; nubentur, sed erunt sicut Angeli Dei. Addimus Rom. XIV. 17. Regnum Dei non est cibus & potus.

De mille hisce annis B. Gravii hæc est sententia: Cum complemento historico magis convenire vi- detur, si statuamus initium hujus millenarii collo- candum esse in A. Christi 453. quo Attila Hunno- rum Rex truculentissimus post acceptam cladem in campis Catalaunicis exoratus a Leone Episcopo Ro- mano discessit ex Italia, atque Occidentale Impe- rium plane reliquit. Interrogatus causam subita- nei discessus: Respondit: Non Pontifex me deterruit, sed senes duo, demissa barba, specie supra humam terribili, districtis gladiis mihi minitantes mortem, nisi supplicibus parcerem. Tunc vere ligatus est Sa- tanas Gogiticus. Ab eo enim tempore virtute Prin- cipum catenatim quasi unitorum impeditus orbem Christianum Occidentem versus invadere non po- tuit. Finis autem hujus millenarii incidit in A. C. 1453. quo Gog & Magog, h. e. Turcæ occuparunt Constantinopolin, deletoque Orientis imperio to- tam Græciam, Thraciam, Bulgariam, Serviam & maximam Hungariæ partem suæ tyrannidi subje- cerunt. Hac potentia Turcica justo Dei judicio in suo vigore permanebit, usque ad ultimum prælium Gogiticum, quo Omnipotentis Dei manu superata corruet.

B. Affelmann. in Hept. Quæst. ad V. classes re- ducit chiliastas: I. Eorum est, qui Christum cor- poraliter ante diem novissimum rediturum scri- bunt, & in hac terra tale regnum instituturum. II. Qui specialius ad terram Canaan restringunt, in quam Judæos reducendos ajunt. III. Qui suis Mar- tyribus ante extremum diem resuscitandis mille- narii alicujus felicitatem vindicant. IV. Qui spiri- tualiter felicitatem intelligunt, eamque ad dele- tum Anti-Christum, extinctum Turcam, ever- sos hæreticos, cessantes persecutiones, & Eccle- siam Catholice Evangelicam referunt. V. Qui & spiritualiter, & corporaliter eam interpretantur, illamque tantam nobis, quanta ante lapsum in Pa- radiso fuit, ante extremum judicium pollicentur.

Καὶ μετὰ ἀυτὸν δεῖ λυθῆναι μικρὸν χρόνον) Diximus supra I. 9. exiguum tempus in Prophetis dici annos etiam quin- gentos. Sed ibi comparatio fit ad durationem populi Ju- daici, hic ad durationem mundi.

Modicum tempus intelligit Dominus Schindle- rus p. 64. de 3 1/2. annis. Nam 3 1/2. dies Angelici fa- ciunt totidem annos. Apoc. XI. Sed diversum est, quod ibi prædicitur. Qui illos cum istis confun- dunt, nimis se se hospites in Apocalypsi ostendunt, ait Pareus. Concernit enim humationem testium, quod corpora eorum per 3 1/2. dies inhumata relin- quenda sint. Nec necessum est, intelligantur illic dies Angelici, quum proprie accipi possint.

## 20:4
V. 4. And I saw thrones) Namely, as once in Daniel 7:9. And they sat upon them) Namely the same ones who are with Daniel, God and the Angels, as it were the chief Assessors of God, who countersign the decrees of God, Dan. 4:13. But Christ must be added here, by the nature of the New Testament, in the place between God and the Angels: which is sufficiently understood from the fact that it is below in 22:1 and 2. The Hebrews, however, often place verbs with the nominatives understood. But what is said here pertains to the following, as we know, done by the most just judgment of God, approved by the Angels, that a certain prerogative of resurrection was given to the martyrs, and their glory was not delayed until the universal judgment. What is said in this whole chapter was almost all in the traditions of the Jews, concerning two resurrections, concerning the thousand happy years between the two, concerning the war of Gog and Magog, about which can be seen Targum Megilla 11, 12. Aben-Ezra and Saadia on Daniel. Vayikra Rabbah ch. 28 and others. Jerome at the end of book 5 on Isaiah, at the beginning of book 15 on the same, and at the beginning of book 18, and on Ezekiel ch. 36. But it is shown here that the meanings are different than the Jews thought, as also concerning the new Jerusalem, which, not being well understood, gave many the occasion for rejecting the Apocalypse as the work of Cerinthus or another judaizer.

And the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the word of God) He understands those killed on account of the testimony concerning the things of Christ, and at the same time on account of his doctrine. A similar expression is in I. 29. VI. 9. in which place he had said 'the souls of those who had been slain,' for which here 'of those who had been beheaded,' namely, the more frequent species being put in place of the genus. For the punishment of the axe was most frequent among the Romans: therefore the Magistrate used to walk with axes. However, for 'beheaded' there is in the Manuscript 'those who had been warred against.' But I think the scribe wished to write 'those who had been enemies.' It is said well in Greek 'to be warred against,' those who are attacked by war. And we have already had 'to make war' for 'to persecute atrociously' several times, as XI. 7. XII. 17. XIII. 7.

And whoever did not worship the beast, nor his image, and did not receive the mark upon their forehead, and upon their hand) That 'and whoever' is as if you were to say, 'whoever may see,' as in Is. 62, 8. and elsewhere. He describes them first by positive acts, now also by negative ones. Not only did they bear testimony concerning the life, death, and resurrection of Christ, and spread his doctrine as widely as they could, but they also abstained from every act which would conflict with that doctrine, such as are still: to perform sacred rites to false Gods, to prostrate themselves before their images, to take marks on the forehead or hand. We have already seen several times before that 'to worship the beast' is to serve idolatry, and 'image' is singular in the sense of a multitude, and that by the species of 'mark' is understood the whole genus under which are both names expressed, and those signified by numbers. See above XII. But the fact that he says they abstained from these things is to be understood as occurring while they were nevertheless tempted by the hope of life and the fear of death and tortures.

Augustine denies that 'thrones' are spoken of regarding the last judgment. It is not to be thought here, he says in book XX of the City of God, ch. 9, that it is spoken of the last judgment, but the seats of the Overseers and the Overseers themselves are to be understood, by whom the Church is now governed. But in truth, the context teaches that it is not a matter of the Church hierarchy, but of the happiness of the pious and the punishment of the impious. Moreover, it is certain from Matt. XIX. 28 that the elders will also sit on Thrones in the final judgment.

Latin:

V. 4. Καὶ εἶδον Θρόνους) Nempe ut olim Daniel VII. 9. Καὶ ἐκάθισαν ἐπ᾿ ἀυτὸς) Nempe iidem, qui apud Danie- lem Deus & Angeli, præcipui velut Assessores Dei, qui De- creta Dei subsignant, Dan. IV. 13. Sed addendus hic ex natu- ra Novi Testamenti Christus medio inter Deum & Angelos loco : quod ipsum satis intelligitur ex eo, quod infra est XXII. 1. & 2. Ebræi autem sæpe verba ponunt subintelle- ctis nominativis. Quod vero hic dicitur ad sequentia per- tinet, ut novimus, factum justissimo Dei judicio, ab Ange- lis approbato, quod martyribus data est quædam præroga- tiva resurrectionis, nec dilata est illorum gloria, ad judicium usque universale. Quæ toto hoc capite dicuntur, fere omnia erant in Judæorum traditionibus, de duabus resurrectioni- bus, de mille annis felicibus inter utramque : de bello Gogi & Magogi, de quibus videri possunt Targum Megilla 11. 12. Aben - Esdra & Saadia ad Danielem. Vaiicra Rabba c. XXVIII. & alii. Hieronymus fine libri V. ad Esaiam, ini- tio libri XV. ad eundem, & initio libri XVIII. & ad Eze- chielis cap. XXXVI. Sed ostenditur hic sensus esse alios, quam Judæi putabant, ut & de novis Hierosolymis, quod non bene intellectum multis occasionem dedit Apocalypsin rejiciendi, tanquam opus Cerinthi aut alterius judaizantis.

Καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν πεπελεκισμένων διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησῦ, καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῦ Θεῦ) Intelligit interfectos pro- pter testimonium de rebus Christi, simulque ob doctrinam ipsius. Similis loquutio I. 29. VI. 9. quo loco dixerat ψυχὰς τῶν ἐσφαγμένων, pro quo hic τῶν πεπελε- κισμένων, nempe specie frequentiore posita vice generis. Fre- quentissimum enim apud Romanos securis supplicium : ideo Magistratus incedebat cum securibus. Pro πεπελεκισμένων tamen in Manuscripto est τῶν πεπολεμημένων. Sed puto scri- bam scribere voluisse πεπολεμίων. Dicitur bene Græce πολεμεῖσθαι, qui bello impetuntur. Et πόλεμον ποιεῖν pro atrociter persequi habuimus jam aliquoties ut XI. 7. XII. 17. XIII. 7.

Καὶ οἵτινες ὐ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ, ὔτε τῇ εἰκόνι ἀυτῦ, καὶ ὐκ ἔλαβον τὸ χάραγμα ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον ἀυτῶν, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα ἀυτῶν) Illud καὶ οἵτινες est quasi dicas, qui videat, ut Es. 62, 8. & alibi. Describit eos primum ex actibus positivis, nunc & negativis. Non tantum testimonium reddiderunt de Christi vita, morte & resurrectione, doctrinamque ejus sparse- runt quam latissime poterant, sed & abstinuerunt ab omni actu, qui cum ea doctrina pugnaret, quales adhuc sunt, sa- cra facere falsis Diis, ad eorum imagines procumbere, no- tas sumere in fronte aut manu. Jam ante aliquoties vidimus προσκυνεῖν τῷ θηρίῳ esse servire idololatriz, & εἰκόνι esse sin- gulare in sensu multitudinis, & per speciem χαράγματος in- telligi totum genus sub quo sunt & nomina expressa, & per numeros significata. Vide supra XII. Quod autem dicit eos ab his abstinuisse, intelligendum est, cum tamen spe vitæ & mortis & cruciatuum metu tentarentur.

Thronos etiam de ultimo judicio dici negat Au- gustinus. Non hic putandum est, inquit l. XX. de C. D. c. 9. de ultimo judicio dici, sed sedes Præpo- sitorum & ipsi Præpositi intelligendi sunt, per quos Ecclesia nunc gubernatur. Verum enim vero non de Ecclesia Hierarchia, sed de piorum felicitate, ac impiorum supplicio, agi contextus docet. Seniores autem in extremo judicio etiam sessuros in Thro- nis e Matth. XIX. 28. constat.

## 20:5
V. 5. And they lived) Souls which are in Sheol, in Hades, are not said to live, but only those which have been translated under the leaf of glory, as the Hebrews speak. Thus they call the most perfect state of souls before the universal resurrection. 'The abundant repentance of martyrs according to their action is a cleansing of sins with glory,' says Clement of Alexandria. Tertullian, however: 'That he may redeem the whole grace of God, that he may obtain every pardon from that compensation of his blood, for all sins are forgiven for this work.'

And they reigned with Christ a thousand years) Just as Christ reigns from heaven upon the earth, so do the martyrs under Christ, namely through the gifts of healings, which were observed at their memorials, and through the honor which the Churches openly held for them. Before the times of Constantine, it was neither safe to run to the monuments of the martyrs, and with Paganism flourishing, it could be feared that the honor of the martyrs might be seized by Pagans for the defense of their own superstition. But what is added, a thousand years, pertains to this, that we may know that after those thousand years the honor of the martyrs began to be diminished by many, namely by those who placed a part of piety in breaking the places dedicated to the memory of the martyrs, and in adding the ancient histories of healings to fables: for which things no slight occasion was given by those who invented false miracles, and who did not observe in the honor of the martyrs that measure which the ancient Church had observed.

And the rest of the dead) Besides the martyrs, that is, or if there are any whom the grace of God has equaled to the martyrs.

They did not live until the thousand years were finished) They did not live, that is, they remained, in Hades in that state which was appropriate to the life lived in the age. But when he says for a thousand years, it is to be understood as while those wars of Gog and Magog last, which extend beyond a thousand years.

This is the first resurrection) That lifting up of the martyrs into heaven can be called a resurrection, that is, תקומה. See Lam. IV. 63 and Heb. XI. 35.

Latin:

V. 5. Καὶ ἔζησαν) Animæ quæ sunt בשאול ἐν ἅδη non dicuntur ζῆν, sed eæ demum quæ translatæ sunt sub folium gloriæ, ut loquuntur Ebræi. Sic vocant perfectissi- mum statum animarum ante resurrectionem universalem. Μαρτύρων ἀδρόα κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν μετάνοια ἀποκάθαρσις ἁμαρ- τιῶν μετὰ δόξης, ait Clemens Alexandrinus. Tertullianus vero: Ut totam Dei gratiam redimat, ut omnem veniam ab ea compensatione sanguinis sui expediat, omnia enim huic operi delicta donantur.

Καὶ ἐβασίλευσαν μετὰ τῦ χρισῦ χίλια ἔτη) Sicut Christus ex coelo in terras regnat, sic & martyres sub Christo, nempe per dona sanationum, quæ conspiciebantur apud ipsorum memorias, & per honorem quem ipsis Ecclesiæ palam ha- buere. Ante tempora Constantini, neque tutum erat ad monumenta martyrum concurrere, & vigente Paganismo, metui poterat ne honor martyrum a Paganis in superstitio- nis suæ defensionem raperetur. Quod autem additur χίλια ἔτη, eo pertinet ut sciamus, post mille illos annos a multis imminui cœpisse honorem martyrum, ab iis scilicet qui pietatis partem in eo posuerunt, si loca martyrum me- moriæ dicata frangerent, & sanationum veteres Historias fabulis accenserent: quas ad res non levis occasio data est ab iis, qui falsa miracula comminiscebantur, quique in mar- tyrum honore non servabant eum modum, quem vetus Ec- clesia servaverat.

Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν νεκρῶν) Præter martyres scilicet, aut si quos Dei gratia martyribus æquavit.

Οὐκ ἔζησαν ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη) ἐκ ἔζησαν, id est, mansere, ἐν ᾅδε in eo statu qui congruens erat vitæ in seculo actæ. Cum autem dicit per mille annos, intelligendum est ut durantibus illis Gogi & Magogi bellis, quæ supra mille annos excurrunt.

Αὕτη ἡ ἀνάστασις πρώτη) illa martyrum in cœlum evectio potest ἀνάστασις dici, id est, תקומה. Vid. Lam. IV. 63. & Ebr. XI. 35.

## 20:6
V. 6. Blessed is the holy one, he who has a part in the first resurrection) This holy one, the same as one removed from all evil. For everything that is inviolable is called holy.

Over these the second death has no power) Mention of the second death is found in Onkelos at the end of Genesis, and Deut. 33, 16, and in Jonathan at Is. 22, 14, and passim among the Rabbis. We have said that the same is treated in the first and second chapters of Wisdom at those places; see what is above at II. 11 and below at XXI. 8.

But they shall be priests of God and of Christ) Just as God formerly heard the prayers of the Priests for the people: so now He hears the prayers of the Martyrs for the Church.

And they shall reign with him a thousand years) Everywhere on earth they shall be publicly honored, as Kings.

That word ἔζησαν, they lived, or as others say ἀνέζησαν, they lived again, is explained concerning the first resurrection, which is spiritual. The life, therefore, of those slain for Christ is understood as spiritual: nor is there need for it to be explained as a bodily resurrection, which is never divided into a first and second. Moreover, the same heavenly life follows in Apoc. XI. 12. The rest, spiritually dead, who did not rise in the first resurrection or regeneration, did not live again, but remained in spiritual death, ἕως, until, which can be explained as never, as in Matt. V. 25, c. XIII. 34. The discourse is about souls, as in v. 4. To whom life, or the first and spiritual resurrection, is appropriate, but not a bodily one. If the martyrs are to rise twice, they will therefore die twice: which is an ἀντίγραφον, Heb. IX. 27. For on the last day all are to rise, and therefore the martyrs also, John V. 28. Souls also have their death in impiety and sins, says Augustine, book XX de C. D. c. 6, according to which death they are dead, of whom the Lord says, 'Let the dead bury their own dead.' What in c. VI the souls of the slain ask for, that they obtain here. For the souls of the pious dead are not separated from the Church, which even now is the kingdom of Christ. Although, therefore, they are not yet with their bodies, their souls already reign with Him, while those thousand years run their course. But he commemorates the souls of the Martyrs for this reason only, because they especially reign as dead, who strove for the truth even unto death.

Latin:

V. 6. Μακάριος ὁ ἅγιος, ὁ ἔχων μέρος ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῇ πρώτῃ) Sanctus hic, idem quod semotus ab omni malo. Omne enim, quod inviolabile est sanctum dicitur.

Ἐπὶ τύτων ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος ὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν) Mortis secundæ mentio apud Onkelosum Genesis fine, & Deut. 33, 16. & apud Jonathanem Es. 22, 14. & passim apud Rab- binos. De eadem agi capite primo & secundo Sapientiæ diximus ad ea loca, vide quæ supra II. 11. & infra XXI. 8.

Ἀλλ’ ἔσονται ἱερεῖς τῦ Θεῦ καὶ τῦ χρισῦ) Sicut olim Deus preces Sacerdotum exaudiebat pro populo: Ita nunc preces Martyrum exaudit pro Ecclesia.

Καὶ βασιλεύσουσι μετ’ αὐτῦ χίλια ἔτη) Ubique in terris publice honorabuntur, ut Reges.

Illud ἔζησαν vixerunt, vel ut alii ἀνέζησαν revi- xerunt, de resurrectione prima explicatur, quæ spi- ritualis est. Vita ergo occisorum pro Christo spi- ritualis intelligitur: nec opus est explicetur de re- surrectione corporali: quæ nunquam distribuitur in primam & secundam. Sequitur autem eandem denique cælestis vita Apoc. XI. 12. Reliqui, spiritua- liter scilicet mortui, qui non resurrexerunt prima resurrectione seu regeneratione non revixerunt, sed manserunt in morte spirituali, ἕως donec expli- cari potest nunquam, ut Matth. V. 25. c. XIII. 34. de animabus sermo est, ut v. 4. Quibus convenit vita, vel resurrectio prima, & spiritualis, non autem corporalis. Si martyres duabus vicibus resurgent, duab. ergo vicibus morientur: Quod est ἀντί- γραφον, Ebr. IX. 27. In novissimo enim die resurre- cturi sunt omnes, adeoque & martyres Joh. V. 28. Habent & animæ mortem suam in impietate & pec- catis, ait Augustinus l. XX. de C. D. c. 6. secundum quam mortem mortui sunt, de quibus Dominus dicit, sine, mortui sepeliant mortuos suos. Quod c. VI. animæ occisorum petunt, id h. l. consequuntur. Ne- que enim piorum animæ mortuorum separantur ab Ecclesia, quæ etiam nunc est regnum Christi. Quamvis ergo cum suis corporibus nondum sint, jam tamen eorum animæ regnant cum illo, dum isti mille anni decurrunt. Sed ideo tantum Marty- rum animas commemorat, quia ipsi præcipue re- gnant mortui, qui usque ad mortem pro veritate certarunt.

## 20:7
V. 7. And when the thousand years are finished) Constantine's edict for the liberty of Christianity was given around the year of Christ 311. A thousand years later the Ottoman house arose, which brought the religion of Mahomet, a discovery of Satan, not into Persia or the shores of the Roman Empire, but into its innermost and most powerful parts, into Asia and Greece.

Satan shall be loosed out of his prison) He calls it prison, which he previously called the abyss. By these words is signified the restraint of Diabolical cruelty. He who sins, sets the Devil free from his bonds: it is in the book on the life and death of Moses. Thus, evils happened to the Church at the time when a most serious schism arose from ambition at Rome: and those were the morals which also gave occasion to the schisms that followed afterwards. Therefore, against the evils of former times, which only showed the virtue of Christians, we have seen many comforts brought. Against these, none, except the end of the age. For these are those times of which Christ speaks in Luke XVIII. 8, Matthew XXIV. 12.

Latin:

V. 7. Καὶ ὅταν τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη) Constantini edi- ctum pro Christianismi libertate datum fuit circa annum Christi CCCXI. Mille post annis orta est domus Otto- mannica, quæ non in Persidem aut oras Romani Impe- rii, sed in partes ejus intimas atque potissimas, in Asiam Græciamque invexit Mahumetis religionem, Satanæ re- pertum.

Λυθήσεται Σατανᾶς ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς αὐτοῦ) φυλακὴ vocat, quod antè ἄβυσσον. Sub quibus verbis significatur sævitiæ Diabolicæ coërcitio. Qui peccat, Diabolum vin- ctum liberat: est in libro de vita ac morte Mosis. Sic ma- illa Ecclesiæ evenere, quò tempore gravissimum schisma ex ambitione ortum est Romæ: & ii fuere mores qui & sequu- tis postea schismatibus occasionem dedere. Propterea ad- versus priorum temporum mala, quæ tantum Christiano rum ostendebant virtutem, multa allata vidimus solatia. Adversus hæc nulla, nisi finem seculi. Hæc enim sunt illa tempora, de quibus loquitur Christus Luc. XVIII. 8. Matth. XXIV. 12.

## 20:8
V. 8. And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four corners of the earth) that is, to incite to cruelty as above in 2. In the four corners, that is, from every part, Job I. 19, Ezekiel XLIII. 20, XLV. 19, above VII. 1. So also from the four winds, Mark XIII. 27, above VII.

Gog and Magog) From Ezekiel XXXVIII. & XXXIX., where we show at that place that the same is noted by a double name, namely Antiochus reigning in Asia and Syria. But most Rabbis refer all those things to the end of the world. The Apocalypse shows in that tradition, no less than in others, that something of truth underlies it. Here, therefore, by Gog is to be understood the Ottoman house, which first showed itself in that part of Asia which was once called Gygæa, and the Kings Gygæ or Gypidæ, that is, in Lydia and neighboring places. Thus also the Sibylline poems of the ancient Christians explain Gog as the Samphili and Lydians. By Magog, however, is understood here, not a city of Syria, but that nation from which the city of Syria itself received its name, as also Scythopolis, namely the Scythian nation: and Jerome says that the Jews of his time thought so regarding Ezekiel. Josephus: 'Magoges founded those who were named Magogites by him, but were called Scythians by them.'

To gather them together to the war) namely, to overthrow or occupy sacred buildings and the memorials of the martyrs.

Whose number is as the sand of the sea) Huge armies. That which is of a huge number is compared to sand, as we said in Gen. XXII. 17, XXXII. 12, XLI. 49. Thus Aristophanes said 'psammakosia' (sand-hundreds). In the Manuscript with Hebraism: 'Whose number of them'.

Latin:

V. 8. Καὶ ἐξελεύσεται πλανῆσαι τὰ ἔν ταῖς τέσσαρσι γω- νίαις τῆς γῆς) id est ad sævitiam excitare ut supra 2. In qua- tuor angulis, id est ab omni parte, Job. I. 19. Ezech. XLIII. 20. XLV. 19. supra VII. 1. Sic & a quatuor ventis Marci XIII. 27. supra VII.

Τὸν Γὼγ καὶ τὸν Μαγὼγ) Ex Ezechiele XXXVIII. & XXXIX. ubi eundem notari gemino nomine, Antiochum scilicet in Asia Syriaque regnantem, ad eum locum osten- dimns. At Rabbini plerique ea omnia referunt ad finem mundi. Ostendit Apocalypsis in ea traditione, non minus quam in aliis, aliquid subesse veri. Hic ergo per Gogum intelligenda domus Ottomannica, quæ primum in ea parte Asiæ se ostendit, quæ olim Gygæa dicta, & Reges Gygæ aut Gypidæ, id est in Lydia locisque vicinis. Sic & Sibyllina poëmata veterum Christianorum Gog exponunt Samphilos & Lydos. Per Magog autem hic intelligitur, non urbs Sy- riæ, sed ea gens, unde ipsa urbs Syriæ nomen accepit, ut & Scythopolis, nempe gens Scythica: & sic sensisse sui tem- poris Judæos ait ad Ezechielem Hieronymus. Josephus: Μαγώγης δὲ τὰς ὑπ' ἀυτᾶ Μαγώγας ὀνομασθέντας ᾤκισε. Σκύθας δὲ ὑπ' αὐτῶν προσαγορευομένυς.

Συναγαγεῖν αὐτὸς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον) nempe ad evertenda vel occupanda ædificia sacra, martyrumque memorias.

Ὧν ὁ ἀριθμὸς ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης) Ingentes exercitus. Quod numeri est ingentis arenæ comparatur, ut diximus Gen. XXII. 17. XXXII. 12. XLI. 49. Sic ψαμμακόσια dixit Aristophanes. In Manuscripto cum Ebraismo. Ὧν ὁ ἀριθμὸς ἀυτῶν.

## 20:9
V. 9. And they went up on the breadth of the earth) Those who held Asia extended their borders far and wide. Thus 'breadth of the land' in Isaiah VIII. 8. The past tense for the future, but as if present. 'They went up' is a military term, 1 Sam. 11.1, 1 Kings 20.1, Isaiah 36.

And they compassed the camp of the saints) They will enclose the camp of God on all sides with their camps, that is, those seven Churches to which this Apocalypse is especially dedicated. The expression is taken from Dan. 8.10, 'the host of heaven'. See above XIII. 6.

And the beloved city) They will also capture Constantinople, which the Greeks call the new Sion, not undeservedly. For there were excellent Bishops and Presbyters there, a religious populace: princes exceptionally Christian. Mahomet the second, Prince of the Ottoman stock, took the temple of this city, the most beautiful in the whole Christian world, called Sophia, away from the Christians and made it proper to Mahometanism in the year of Christ, as most learned men judge, 1453.

Brightman gathers here that the truth of the Gospel will reign among the nations for seven hundred years yet. But from a false hypothesis, namely that the thousand years of the loosing begin in the year 1300. Two machinations are attributed to the Dragon once loosed: 1. The seduction of the nations through the four corners of the earth to idolatry, which he will attempt more vehemently in the most recent time, because he knows that little time remains for him. 2. The stirring up of Gog and Magog to battle, of which Ezekiel 38 seq. speaks, who are not the northern nations shut up by Alexander the Great, of which Galat. lib. V. c. 12 and the Alcoran, Az. 20, 28, 31, nor the seven Kings who will defeat the Anti-Christ. For Gog and Magog are the assistants of the Anti-Christ. But of the Oriental Anti-Christ. Therefore, the Turkish war is looked to. Augustine, lib. XX. de C. D. c. XI: 'This will be,' he says, 'the most recent persecution, with the most recent judgment impending, which the holy Church will suffer in the whole world.' Namely, the whole city of Christ from the whole city of the Devil, however great each will be upon the earth Gog. If ba He seems to be the great-grandson of Ham, the first Prince in Arabia Felix, because Mahomet was born from there, and he is called such by others from the roof: because the Scythians are hamaxobioi, and it is known that the Northern Turks adhere to the Tartars. The Turks transferred to themselves all of Arabia and a great part of Africa, which is indicated under the name of Ethiopia and Libya. However, certain peoples are excepted, whom the Turks could not subjugate v. 41. But these alone shall be saved from his hand, Edom, and Moab, and the firstfruits of the children of Ammon. By Edom are understood the Latins, in the western part of the ancient Roman Empire; By the Moabites, the Muscovites. By the firstfruits of the children of Ammon, the Abyssinians. These have remained free from Turkish tyranny to this very day:

Regarding which, Dan. 11, 42. 43. The land of Egypt shall not escape, and he shall have dominion over the treasures of gold and silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt, he shall pass through Libya and Ethiopia. Which B. Gravius refers to the year 1516, in which Selim, Emperor of the Turks, conquered Campson Gauri, the Sultan of Egypt, and killed him in battle, and having occupied all of Syria and Egypt, he hung Campson's successor, Tornumbeius, the last of the Mamluk Sultans, before the palace after he had been vexed with all manner of torments and insults. In the year 1453, Mahomet II occupied Constantinople, having brought about an infinite slaughter of Christians. From that time, the Turks most miserably afflicted the Western provinces of the Christian world by land and sea. For although the Pope and the Pontifical Princes sometimes fought successfully against the Turks, they were nevertheless more often repulsed, not without significant slaughter and the loss of regions. In the year 1522, Solyman besieged and occupied Rhodes with a huge fleet. Not long after, he infested Hungary and occupied the Bishopric of Sirmium. In the year 1526, he defeated King Louis in a huge battle, in which Louis perished. In the year 1529, he besieged Vienna of Austria in vain with a huge army. In the year 1570, Selim fatigued Cyprus with a horrendous war and subjected it to the Turkish empire. How he brought Neuhäusel and other cities into his power in Hungary is in everyone's recent memory. The Prophet indicates the 'excellent land' as the Eastern empire, which, with its subject regions, was most famous throughout the world on account of its majesty and power, and especially for the innumerable churches founded by the Apostles themselves and their disciples.

Some dare to define the time of the battle, but this is mere rashness. There are those who determine the year 1621, in which the King of Poland, Sigismund III, and Prince Wladislaus gained a notable victory over the Turks by the grace of God, because that is the thousandth year from the year 620, from which the Turks count the years of Mahomet and his sect, and begin their Hegira. Others prefer the year 1630, because Christians deduce the beginning of the reign and sect of Mahomet from the year 630, in which Mahomet died, such as Theophanes, Cedrenus, Baronius, Bzovius, Spondanus, and others.

Some also prophesy about the place of the Gogic slaughter, but it is merely uncertain. The place of burial, says Gravius, is added as the city HAMONA, that is, 'multitude,' from the multitude of the buried, which is explained in the same verse as the 'valley of the multitude,' and indeed to the East of the sea. He refers to the slaughter of the Ammonites at the Dead Sea, which is called the Eastern Sea, Jos. 12, 3. D. Phil. Nicolai places the location at Constantinople. But because the terminus to which the Gogic incursion will mainly be directed is Germany and the mountains of Israel, that is, the Evangelical regions, from which in the last times the Word of God went forth as if to Zion: It seems that some city or place in Saxony on the Baltic Sea is indicated, which is commonly called the Eastern Sea, Ost-See. Perhaps the final and greatest slaughter and destruction of the Gogites will take place between Lübeck and Hamburg. However, he himself acknowledges the uncertainty, therefore he adds: 'But these uncertain things must be committed to divine disposition and omniscience.' Regarding the burning of the enemy weapons, he has this: 'The magnitude of this battle is exaggerated. For the scarcity of men after this battle will be stupendous in many places, so that the wood remaining from the weapons and chariots of the slain enemies may suffice for 7 years.'

PART II. THE CASTING OF THE DEVIL AND HIS WORSHIPPERS INTO THE LAKE OF FIRE.

And fire came down from heaven from God, and devoured them) Taken from the passage in Ezek. 38, 21 and 39, 6. The Prophets are accustomed to use the word 'fire' when they designate a swift end, as concerning the slaughter of Sennacherib, Isaiah 9, 5; 10, 6; 26, 11. Since this event has not yet occurred, an end to the Turkish kingdom is to be expected not unlike that which the armies of Sennacherib or Antiochus Epiphanes had.

Latin:

V. 9. Καὶ ἀνέβησαν ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς γῆς) Late suos ter- minos extenderunt illi qui Asiam tenebant. Sic πλάτος τῆς χώρας Es. VIII. 8. Præteritum pro futuro, sed quasi præsenti. Ἀνέβησαν est vox militaris 1. Sam, 11, 1. 1. Reg. 20, 1. Es. 36.

Καὶ ἐκύκλωσαν τὴν παρεμβολὴν τῶν ἁγίων) Undique in- cludent suis castris Dei castra, id est, septem illas Ecclesias, quibus præcipue dedicata est hæc Apocalypsis. Sumpta lo- cutio ex Dan. 8 10. צבא השמים. Vide supra XIII. 6.

Καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἠγαπημένην) Capient & Constantino- polin, quam Sionem novam dicunt Græci, non immerito. Nam egregii ibi fuere Episcopi & Presbyteri, plebs religio- sa: principes eximie Christiani. Hujus urbis ædem toto orbe Christiano pulcherrimam, dictam Sophiæ, Mahumetes secundus, Ottomannicæ stirpis Princeps, Christianis abla- tam Mahumetismo propriam fecit anno Christi, ut censent Viri Doctissimi, cIɔ cccc LIII.

Colligit hic Brightmannus, veritatem Evange- lii regnaturam inter gentes adhuc septingentis an- nis. Sed ex falsa hypothesi, mille nempe annos so- lutionis initium capere anno 1300. Duæ autem Dra- coni soluto tribuuntur molitiones, 1. seductio gen- tium per quatuor angulos terræ ad idololatriam, quam tentabit vehementius novissimo tempore, quia novit parum temporis sibi superesse. 2. Conci- tatio Gog & Magog ad prælium, de quo Ezech. 38. seq. qui non sunt gentes septentrionales ab Alexan- dro M. reclusæ, de quo Galat. l. V. c. 12. & Alcoran. Az. 20. 28. 31. nec septem Reges Anti-Christum ex- pugnaturi. Nam parastatæ sunt Gog & Magog Anti-Christi. Sed Anti-Christi Orientalis. Re- spicitur ergo bellum Turcicum. Augustinus l. XX. de C. D. c. XI. Hæc erit, inquit, novissima persecu- tio, novissimo imminente judicio, quam sancta Ec- clesia toto terrarum orbe patietur.
