To show to his servants, what must come to pass in haste.) And these things are repeated from the beginning of this book. Therefore he sent the Angel, so that through you those great things might be revealed to Christians, which are to exist within nearly two hundred and fifty years.

Behold I come quickly.) Here 'saying' is understood, as in Isa. 42, 14. Jer. 4, 10. ch. 6, 9. and elsewhere often among the Prophets. Saying that he will come shortly. God is said to come when he executes some great thing. See above 11, 16. especially where he delivers the pious. Ps. 80, 3. and 101, 2.

Latin:

V. 6. Καὶ λέγει μοί. Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιτοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί.) Nempe quæ dicta de splendore Ecclesiæ sub Principibus Christianis. Similis affirmatio supra 19, 9. λέγει μοι, nem- pe Angelus. Hic incipi debuit nova sectio.

Καὶ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν προφητῶν.) A quo omnia dona Prophetica ortum habent. Vide Ebr. 12, 9. Κύ- ριος hic valet יהוה

Ἀπέστειλε τὴν ἄγγελον ἀυτῶ.) Nempe tibi Johanni, ut supra.

Δεῖξαι τοῖς δέλοις ἀυτῶ, ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει.) Et hæc repetita ex libri hujus initio. Ideo Angelum misit, ut per te patefierent Christianis res illæ magnæ, quæ extituræ sunt intra annos ducentos ferme & quinquaginta.

Ἰδὲ ἔρχομαι ταχύ.) Hic subauditur λέγων, ut Esa. 42, 14. Jer. 4, 10. c. 6, 9. & alibi sæpe apud Prophetas. Dicens se brevi venturum. Venire Deus dicitur, cum magnum ali- quid exequitur. Vide supra II. 16. maxime ubi pios liberat. Ps. 80, 3. & 101, 2.

## 22:7
Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.) He who retains these things with a mindful heart, being about to have great comfort from it, while the time of the cross lasts. Above 1, 3.

Latin:

Μακάριος ὁ τηρῶν τὰς λόγες τῆς προφητείας τῶ βιβλίου τούτου.) Qui memori animo ista retinet, magnum inde solatium ha- biturus, durante crucis tempore. Supra 1, 3.

## 22:8
V. 8. And I John who hear and see these things.) 'Am' is understood, as is often the case among the Hebrews: and the Present for the immediate Past. John often in his works puts either his name or descriptions of his name in place of a Pronoun, as Thucydides and Virgil. See in the Gospel XIX, 35. XXI, 23.

And when I heard and saw.) Where I heard the words of the Angel, and saw all the forms which he showed to me.

I fell to worship before the feet of the Angel who was showing me these things.) So that I might bestow the highest honor I could upon the messenger of such great things. That 'before the feet' is construed with 'I fell', as above XIX, 10. In the manuscript it is 'at the feet'.

Latin:

V. 8. Κἀγὼ ἰωάννης ὁ ἀκούων καὶ βλέπων ταῦτα.) Subau- ditur sum, ut sæpe apud Ebræos: & Præsens pro Præterito proximo. Johannes sæpe in operibus suis aut nomen aut descriptiones nominis vice Pronominis ponit, ut Thucydi- des & Virgilius. Vide in Evangelio XIX, 35. XXI, 23.

Καὶ ὅτε ἤκουσα καὶ ἔβλεψα.) Ubi audivi verba Angeli, & vidi formas omnes, quas mihi monstravit.

Ἔπεσον προσκυνῆσαι ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν τοῦ Ἀγγέλου τοῦ δεικνύοντός μοι ταῦτα.) Ut honore, quem poteram, summo afficerem nuntium rerum tantarum. Illud ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν construitur cum ἔπεσον, ut supra XIX, 10. In manu- scripto est πρὸ ποδῶν.

## 22:9
V. 9. And he says to me: See that you do not. I am your fellow servant, and of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.) The same things as above; except that 'the prophets' is missing there, and for 'those who keep the words of this book' it is 'those who have the testimony of Jesus'. The name of the prophets is added here, because John did not entrust this book to everyone outside of those things which are in the Epistles to the seven Churches, but to a few, whom he knew to be both of great virtue and endowed with great gifts by God.

Latin:

V. 9. Καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή. Σύνδουλός σού εἰμι, καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν προφητῶν, καὶ τῶν τηρούντων τοὺς λόγους τοῦ βι- βλίου τούτου. τῷ Θεῷ προσκύνησον.) Eadem quæ supra; nisi quod deest ibi τῶν προφητῶν & pro τηρούντων τοὺς λόγους τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου est τῶν ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ. Propheta- rum nomen hic additur, quia non omnibus hunc librum extra ea quæ sunt in Epistolis ad septem Ecclesias, commisit Johannes, sed paucis, quos & magna esse virtute, & magnis a Deo donis præditos sciebat.

## 22:10
V. 10. And he says to me.) Here follows a Dialogue between the Lord Jesus and John, with the names of the persons not added, but which are easily understood from the words. Here Jesus begins to speak: You have a similar thing in Isa. VIII, XXVII. XLVIII. Jerem. V. VIII. IX. XV. XXII. near the end.

Do not seal the words of the prophecy of this book.) That is, do not enclose the book in an earthen vessel, as Jeremiah was ordered to do 32, 14. & Daniel 8, 26. c. 12, 9.

For the time is near.) That is, many things will happen shortly, as concerning Jewish affairs: concerning Domitian; and therefore the book must be at hand, so that it may be compared with the events.

Latin:

V. 10. Καὶ λέγει μοι.) Sequitur hic Dialogus inter Dom. Jesum & Johannem, non appositis personarum nominibus, sed quæ facile ex verbis subintelliguntur. Hic loqui inci- pit Jesus: Simile habes apud Esa. VIII, XXVII. XLVIII. Jerem. V. VIII. IX. XV. XXII. circa finem.

Μὴ σφραγίσῃς τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου.) Id est ne includas librum in testa, ut Jeremias jussus est fa- cere 32, 14. & Daniel 8, 26. c. 12, 9.

Ὅτι ὁ καιρὸς ἐγγύς ἐστιν.) Id est brevi multa evenient, ut de rebus Judaicis: de Domitiano; ideoque in promptu de- bet esse liber, ut cum eventibus comparetur.

## 22:11
V. 11. He who is unjust, let him be unjust still, and he who is filthy, let him be filthy still.) This is a concession, such as that: Go, follow Italy with the winds. Nor is it without its own force. For it signifies that no one is compelled by God. See this Apostle in the Gospel VI. 67. At the same time, understand that Christians ought not to be offended if idolaters rage. Those words, and he who is filthy, let him be filthy still, or as other books have, and he who is defiled, let him be defiled still, are absent in the Manuscript. They seem, however, to be retained, so that there may be a double antithesis: of injustice with justice, of filth with purity. And Cyprian reads this particle. By the name of filth, however, understand here all vices outside of injustice specifically so called. See James I, 20.

And he who is righteous, let him do righteousness still.) The Manuscript also has it thus. This Apostle said to do righteousness here, also in the epistle chapter II, 29. III, 7. Elsewhere for the same thing is to work righteousness, as Acts X, 35. Heb. XI, 33. or to perform, as James I, 20.

And he who is holy, let him be sanctified still.) That is, let him preserve holiness. Thus he is said to be made alive, who is preserved in life. For the most part in Scripture, justice is the beginning, holiness is progress into greater things. See what we have spoken beforehand in the epistle to the Romans. Just as what had preceded here just now were spoken figuratively by way of concession, so these are serious and salutary warnings.

These are to be understood not so much concerning the increase or continuation of justification or sanctification, as regards the words, and he who is righteous, let him do righteousness still, and he who is holy, let him be sanctified still (except as regards the latter warning), as concerning the preservation of justification, lest we fall from the same, which happens through heresy and sins against conscience, and thus apostasy from the faith: just as the particle properly is, let him be justified further, let him remain and persevere in the state of justification. Concerning which, the blessed Höpfner is worthy to be heard here, disp. on justification p. 869. The sense is perfectly consistent if these words are understood concerning perseverance: He who harms, or as it is in the Greek, acts unjustly, let him harm, or let him continue to act unjustly, or let him continue the guilt of injustice. Although, however, an increase of sanctification follows the continuation of it, it cannot nevertheless be inferred from that, that this is connoted by the word still, if the discourse is concerning justification before God; because the nature of justification before God, which consists in the total remission of all sins and the imputation of the whole obedience of Christ apprehended by faith by those who believe, done in an instant, is repugnant to it. Remission indeed can be renewed daily, because the mercies of the Lord are new every morning, Lam. III, 23, yet it cannot be increased or become greater. And therefore this little word will obtain a meaning common to both benefits and will be worth the same as further or more, as it is taken in c. XIII. 12. c. X. 6. and in this very chapter XXII. 3. etc.

Latin:

V. 11. Ὁ ἀδικῶν ἀδικησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ῥυπαρὸς ῥυπαρευθήτω ἔτι.) Est συγχώρησις qualis illa: I, sequere Italiam ventis. Nec caret illa sua vi. Significat enim neminem a Deo cogi. Vide hunc Apostolum in Evangelio VI. 67. Simul intelli- ge Christianos offendi non debere, si idololatræ sæviunt. Illa καὶ ὁ ῥυπαρὸς ῥυπαρευθήτω, aut ut alii libri habent; καὶ ὁ ῥυπῶν ῥυπωσάτω ἔτι, absunt in Manuscripto. Videntur tamen retinenda, ut duplex sit ἀντίθετον, injustitiæ cum ju- stitia, sordium cum puritate. Et legit hanc particulam Cy- prianus. Sordium autem nomine hic intellige vitia omnia extra injustitiam specialiter sic dictam. Vid. Jac. I, 20.

Καὶ ὁ δίκαιος δικαιοσύνην ποιησάτω ἔτι.) Sic habet & Manu- scriptus. Ποιεῖν δικαιοσύνην dixit hic Apostolus etiam episto- la cap. II, 29. III, 7. Alibi pro eodem est ἐργάζεσθαι δικαιο- σύνην, ut Act. X, 35. Ebr. XI, 33. aut κατεργάζεσθαι ut Jac. I, 20.

Καὶ ὁ ἅγιος ἁγιασθήτω ἔτι.) Id est sanctimoniam servet. Sic ζωοποιεῖσθαι dicitur, qui in vita servatur. Plerumque in Scriptura justitia est initium, sanctitas profectus in majora. Vide quæ proloquuti sumus in epistolam ad Ro- manos. Sicut quæ modo hic præcesserant, dicta sunt figura- te κατὰ συγχώρησιν, ita hæc seria & salutaria sunt monita.

Hæc non tam de incremento vel continuatione justificatio- nis vel sanctificationis, quod ad verba, & δίκαιος δικαιοσύνην ποιησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος ἁγιασθήτω ἔτι (nisi quod ad mo- nitum posterius) intelligenda, quam de justificationis conser- vatione, ne excidamus eadem, quod fit per hæresin & peccata contra conscientiam, adeoque ἀποστασίαν a fide: quemad- modum particula proprie est adhuc justificetur porro, ma- neat & perseveret in statu justificationis. Quo de dignus est, qui hic audiatur, B. Höpfnerus disp. de justif. p. 869. Optime sibi constat sensus, si de perseverantia intelligantur & hæc verba: Qui nocet, vel ut in Græco est, injuste agit, noceat, vel injuste agere pergat, aut reatum injustitiæ continuet. Quamvis autem sanctificationis continuationem sequatur in- crementum illius, non tamen inferri illinc potest, quod illud per vocabulum ἔτι connotetur, si de justificatione coram Deo sermo fit; quia natura justificationis coram Deo repugnat, quæ con- sistit in totali omnium peccatorum remissione, & totius obe- dientiæ Christi per fidem credentium apprehensæ, facta in in- stanti imputatione. Remissio quidem quotidie renovari potest, quia novæ quolibet mane misericordiæ Domini Thren. III, 23. non tamen augeri, vel major fieri. Ideoque hæc vocula commu- nem utrique beneficio significatum obtinebit ac idem valebit, quod ποῤῥώτερον porro vel amplius, uti sumitur c. XIII. 12. c. X. 6. & in hoc ipso cap. XXII. 3. &c.

## 22:12
V. 12. Behold, I come quickly) Namely, both to liberate Christians and to punish idolaters. For because the Christians of all times are one body, the good things of later ages also pertain to those now living. Many such things are also among the Prophets.

And my reward is with me.) That is, I bring the reward with me. A locution from Is. XL. 10. & LXII. 11.

To give to each according to his work.) So that I may both make the saints illustrious and destroy the idolaters.

He hints that the coming of Christ is imminent, and will approach sooner than the opinion of men. By which he will give to each according to his works, i.e., not according to merits; for he does not say because of works, but according to what his works will be. Concerning which Gregory the Great warned on Ps. 7 Penitential: It is one thing, he says, to render according to works, another to render according to the merits of works or on account of works. Compare similar passages Ps. 61, 13. Is. 40. (which passage seems to be referred to here) Matt. 16, 22. Luke 6, 38. Rom. 2, 5. 6. 1 Cor. 3, 8. Gal. 6, 8. Bellarmine, book II, on grace and free will, ch. 3, §. therefore the statement 1 Cor. 3, 8 is explained concerning the difference of degrees of glory in eternal life.

Latin:

V. 12. Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ταχὺ) Nempe tum ad liberandos Christianos, tum ad puniendos idololatras. Quia enim omnium temporum Christiani unum corpus sunt, bona etiam posteriorum ætatum ad nunc viventes pertinent. Talia multa etiam apud Prophetas.

Καὶ ὁ μισθός μου μετ' ἐμοῦ.) Id est mecum fero mercedem. Loquutio ex Es. XL. 10. & LXII. 11.

Ἀποδοῦναι ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτοῦ.) Ut & sanctos faciam illustres, & idololatras destruam.

Adventum Christi imminere, ac citius opinione hominum appropinquaturum, innuit. Quo dabit unicuique secundum opera sua, h. e. non juxta merita; Nec enim dicit propter ope- ra, sed prout erunt opera ejus. Quo de monuit Gregor. M. in- Ps. 7. Pœnit. Aliud est, inquiens, secundum opera reddere, aliud secundum merita operum vel propter opera reddere. Conf. loca similia Psalm. 61, 13. Es. 40. (qui locus hic respici videtur) Matth. 16, 22. Luc. 6, 38. Rom. 2, 5. 6. 1. Cor. 3, 8. Gal. 6, 8. Bellarminus l. II. de grat. & lib. arb. c. 3. §. itaq; dictum 1. Cor. 3, 8. explicat de differentia graduum gloriæ in vita æterna.

## 22:13
V. 13. I am the A. and the Ω. the beginning and the end.] That is, fulfilling promises: What had been attributed to GOD I, 8. and XXI, 6. is here attributed to Christ, as one who is the genuine image of the Father's faithfulness. Among Hermas, Christ is the old rock and the new gate. III, 9. Philo on dreams. The Word of God is the head and the end. See also 2 Cor. 1, 20.

the first and the last.] Above I, 18. I, being supreme in dignity, allowed myself to be reduced to the lowest lot. Do not therefore think it hard for yourselves, that which happened to me. I have been liberated, and the Church shall be liberated.

Latin:

V. 13. Ἐγὼ τὸ Α. κὶι τὸ Ω. ἀρχὴ κὰι τέλος.] Id est, implens promissa: Quod DEO tributum fuerat I, 8. & XXI, 6. hic Christo tribuitur, ut qui paternæ fidelitatis genuina sit imago. Apud Hermam Christus petra vetus & porta nova. III, 9. Philo de somniis.Ὁ λόγος Θεῦ κεφαλὴ κὰι τέλος. Vide & 2. Cor. 1, 20.

ὁ πρῶτος κὰι ὁ ἔσχατος.] Supra I, 18. Ego dignitate summus ad infimam sortem redigi me sum passus. Ne ergo vos durum vobis putetis, quod mihi evenit. Liberatus ego sum, & Ecclesia liberabitur.

## 22:14
Vers. 14. Blessed are those who do his commandments.] John speaks here to his readers, his, that is, Christ's, concerning whose precepts see Matt. 5, 19. John 14, 15. 21. 15, 10. 1 Cor. 14, 37. Just as we have placed the words here, Arethas and Cyprian also read. But in the Manuscript it is: Blessed are those who wash their robes: and thus the Latin reads, who for the sake of interpretation added in the blood of the Lamb, from those things which are above 7, 14, where see the statements.

Blessed, he says, are those who keep the commandments of the Lord: not indeed as the Papists pervert the meaning: blessed, because they keep the commandments. For the law was not given, which could give life, Gal. 3, 21.

That their authority may be over the tree of life.] That here is equivalent to because, as above 14, 13. Authority is right, as John I, 12. And there is a metonymy here. For the right to the tree of life is said for the right to obtain life through the tree, i.e., through the cross. See above 2, 7.

And that they may enter by the gates into the city.] Because such will be the case in the times of Constantine and afterwards: they will be able to see the splendor of the Church promised to the ancient Fathers, and to be participants of it. See above 21, 12. and the statements there.

It is prior to have a right to the tree of life, than to enter into the city in act through the gates. The angels were prohibiting Adam from it; but now they are stationed at the gates, so that they may bring in the faithful, Gen. 3, 24.

Latin:

Vers. 14. Μακάριοι οἱ ποιῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτῦ.] Johannes hic loquitur sua lecturis, αὐτῦ, id est, Christi, de cujus præceptis vide Matth. 5, 19. Joh. 14, 15. 21. 15, 10. 1. Cor. 14, 37. Ita ut hic verba posuimus, legerunt & Arethas, & Cyprianus. At in Manuscripto est: Μακάριοι οἱ πλύνοντες τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν: & sic legit Latinus, qui interpretandi causa addidit in sanguine Agni, ex iis, quæ supra 7, 14. ubi dicta vide.

Beati, inquit, qui servant mandata Domini: non vero ut Papistæ sensum pervertunt: beati, quia servant mandata. Non enim est data lex, quæ possit vivificare, Gal. 3, 21.

Ἴνα ἔσται ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς.] Ἴνα hic valet ὅτι, ut supra 14, 13. Ἐξουσία est jus, ut Joh. I, 12. Et est hic metonymia. Nam jus in lignum vitæ dicitur pro jure ad vitam adipiscendam per lignum, i. e. per crucem. Vide supra 2, 7.

Καὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν εἰσέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν πόλιν.] Quia tales erunt Constantini temporibus & postea: ii videre poterunt splendorem Ecclesiæ Patribus antiquis promissum, & ejus esse participes. Vide supra 21, 12. & ibi dicta.

Prius est habere jus ad lignum vitæ, quam actu per portas ingredi in civitatem. Angeli Adamum ab illo prohibebant; jam vero in portis constituuntur, ut fideles intromittant, Genef. 3, 24.

## 22:15
Vers. 15. Outside are the dogs.] Dogs are called here, those who are above the abominable XXI, 8. Thus certain Hebrews explain that which is in Deut. 23, 18.

And the sorcerers, and the fornicators, and the murderers, and the idolaters, and everyone who loves and does a lie.] Repeated from those things which are above 21, 8. Except that there it is and to all liars, for which doing a lie 21, 27. Those who are such, are either not admitted to baptism, or, if they were admitted before, they are excluded from the Church. Let the canons of both universal and particular synods, which have been approved by the universal ones, be seen concerning that matter.

Latin:

Vers. 15. Ἔξω οἱ κύνες.] Canes hic vocantur, qui supra ἐβδελυγμένοι XXI, 8. Sic Ebræi quidam exponunt id, quod est Deut. 23, 18.

Καὶ οἱ φαρμακοὶ, κὰι οἱ πόρνοι, κὰι οἱ φονεῖς, κὰι οἱ εἰδωλολάτραι, κὰι πᾶς ὁ φιλῶν, κὰι ποιῶν ψεῦδος.] Repetitum ex iis, quæ supra 21, 8. Nisi quod ibi κὰι πᾶσι τοῖς ψευδέσι, pro quo ποιῶν ψεῦδος 21, 27. Tales qui sunt, aut ad baptismum non admittuntur, aut, si ante admissi sunt, excluduntur ab Ecclesia. Videantur ea de re canones tum Synodorum universalium, tum particularium, quæ ab universalibus sunt approbatæ.

## 22:16
Vers. 16. I Jesus have sent my angel to testify to you these things in the Churches.] Here Jesus speaks again. To you, that is to John, and through John to the excellent men. In the Churches, that is, for the good of the Churches. Thus for which, that is, wherefore? Matt. 20, 58. In the Manuscript it is in the Churches.

I am the root and the offspring of David.] Here and is explanatory. For by the root is understood the shoot, by the shoot the progeny. See above V, 5. What wonder is it, if I subdue Kings? I am doing an ancestral deed. David did this among the Syrians, Idumeans, Moabites. Son of David is a designation of the Messiah, Matt. I, 1. IX, 27. XII, 28. Luke I, 32. and elsewhere.

The Star, the bright, the morning one.] Just as the star of Lucifer promises the day: So I [promise] that that splendor will come to the Church. Concerning the word πρωῖνὸς see above II, 28. Similitudes are taken from the same things, sometimes these, sometimes those.

Latin:

Vers. 16. Ἐγὼ Ἰησῦς ἔπεμψα τὸν ἄγγελόν με μαρτυρῆσαι ὑμῖν ταῦτα ἐπὶ ταῖς Ἐκκλησίαις.] Hic rursum Jesus loquitur. Vobis, id est Johanni, & per Johannem Viris eximiis. Ἐπὶ ταῖς Ἐκκλησίαις, id est, Ecclesiarum bono. Sic ἐφ’ ᾧ, id est, quamobrem? Matth. 20, 58. In Manuscripto est ἐν ταῖς Ἐκκλησίαις.

Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ῥίζα κὰι τὸ γένος τῦ Δαβίδ.] Hic κὰι est ἐξηγητικόν. Per radicem enim furculus intelligitur, per surculum progenies. Vide supra V, 5. Quid mirum est, si Reges Ego subigam? Facio rem avitam. Fecit hoc David in Syris, Idumæis, Moabitis. Filius Davidis notatio Messiæ, Matth. I, 1. IX, 27. XII, 28. Luc. I, 32. & alibi.

ὁ Ἀστὴρ, ὁ λαμπρὸς, ὁ πρωῖνός.] Sicut Luciferi sidus diem promittit: Ita ego splendorem illum eventurum Ecclesiæ. De voce πρωῖνὸς vide supra II, 28. Similitudines ab iisdem rebus sumuntur modo hæ, modo illæ.

## 22:17
Vers. 17. And the Spirit.] That is, men famous for prophetic gifts. See above 6. It is again the abstract for the concrete. Spirit for those who have the Spirit. Here John speaks again.

And the bride.] The others belonging to the Church.

They say come.] As if they were saying: May that day hasten, when we shall no longer be called fugitives from the light, when we shall no longer be accused of debaucheries and murdered infants. It seems that λέγουσιν is placed for λέγωσιν because of what follows.

And he who hears let him say come.] John excites all who will understand these things through others, that they may favor them with prayers. See above I, 3.

And he who thirsts let him come.] He who desires the contemplation of future things.

he who wishes let him take the water of life freely.] Just as perennial water refreshes a traveler in the heat: so these [refresh] those who are burning with the heat of prophecy. As if through the heat to quench thirst with a leaping stream of sweet water. Add the Greek epigrams about fountains on the road, and Psalm 36, 9. 10. and Isaiah 32, 2. ch. 49, 10. He says freely, because neither the Apostle himself asks anything for this benefit, nor were those to whom he had commended this book going to ask. See Matt. X, 8. The passage Eph. 55, 1 is referred to.

Latin:

Vers. 17. Καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα.] Id est, Viri Prophetici donis clari. Vide supra 6. Est abstractum rursus pro concreto. Spiritus pro habentibus Spiritum. Hic rursus Johannes loquitur.

Καὶ ἡ νύμφη.] Cæteri ad Ecclesiam pertinentes.

Λέγουσιν ἔρχε.] Quasi dicant: Illa dies propera, cum non amplius dicemur lucifugæ, cum non amplius de stupris & infantibus occisis accusabimur. Videtur λέγουσιν positum pro λέγωσιν ob sequentia.

Καὶ ὁ ἀκύων εἰπάτω ἔρχε.] Excitat Johannes omnes, qui per alios hæc intelligent, ut precibus faveant. Vide supra I, 3.

Καὶ ὁ διψῶν ἐρχέσθω.] Qui rerum futurarum cogitationem appetit.

ὁ θέλων λαβέτω ὕδωρ ζωῆς δωρεάν.] Sicut aqua perennis in æstu reficit viatorem: ita hæc prophetiæ æstuantes sub adversis. quale per æstum Dulcis aquæ saliente situm restingwere rivo. Adde epigrammata Græca de fontibus in via, & Psalm. 36, 9. 10. & Esaiam 32, 2. c. 49, 10. Gratis dicit, quia nec ipse Apostolus quicquam pro hoc beneficio postulat, nec illi, quibus hunc librum commendaveiat, erant postulaturi. Vide Matth. X, 8. Respicitur locus Ef. 55, 1.

## 22:18
Vers. 18. I testify to everyone who hears.] The Apostle adds a grave adjuration to those who will hear these things, that they do not change them in any part. A similar caution is found in Irenaeus; I adjure you who copy this book, by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by his glorious coming, in which he comes to judge the living and the dead, that you compare what you have copied, and correct it diligently according to this copy from which you copied, and that you likewise copy this oath and place it in the copy. Eusebius transcribed the same formula into his Chronicle, and Jerome from him into Latin. You have a similar one in Rufinus in the preface to the books of Origen translated by him, and in Valens of Antioch. The wickedness of Marcion and others, who falsified whole passages of the New Testament, shows that this care was not for nothing.

If anyone adds to these.) If anyone shall have added to this book of the Apocalypse.

May God add to him the seven plagues written in this book.) An elegant allusion in ἐπιθῇ and ἐπιθήσαι. Many Greek codices do not have that seven, just as the Latin does not. However, the plagues are to be understood as those which are in chapters eight, nine, ten, and eleven; and those which are in chapters 16, 17, 18, of which the former touch the Jews, the latter the Roman empire. It is the subjunctive ἐπιθήσαι of one praying, but not unjustly, for the sake of frightening. But in the Manuscript it is by way of prediction ἐπιθήσει and soon after ἀφελεῖ. And thus the Latin reads: and thus the words are cited in Arethas. See what we said at 2 Tim. 4, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 18. Μαρτυρῶ ἐγὼ παντὶ ἀκύοντι.] Addit Apostolus gravem obtestationem ad eos, qui hæc audient, ne ea aliqua ex parte immutent. Par ista cautio apud Irenæum; Ὁρκίζω σε τὸν μεταγραψάμενον τὸ βιβλίον τῦτο, κα- τὰ τῦ Κυρίε ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ, καὶ κατὰ τῆς ἐνδόξε πα- ρεσίας αὐτᾶ, ἧς ἔρχεται κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκρὲς, ἵνα ἀντιβάλῃς ὃ μετεγράψω, καὶ κατορθώσῃς κατὰ τὸ ἀντίγραφον τῦτο, ὅθεν μετεγράψω ἐπιμελῶς, καὶ τὸν ὅρκον τῦτον ὁμοίως μεταγράψῃς κὴ θήσῃς ἐν τῷ ἀντιγράφῳ. Eandem formulam transcripsit in Chroni- con suum Eusebius, & ex eo Latine Hieronymus. Similem habes apud Ruffinum præfatione in libros Origenis à se ver- sos, & apud Valentem Antiochenum. Non de nihilo fuisse hanc curam ostendit Marcionis & aliorum improbitas, qui tota loca Novi Testamenti falsarunt.

Ἐάν τις ἐπιθῇ ἐπ' αὐτά.) Si quis addiderit ad hunc Apoca- lypseos librum.

Ἐπιθήσαι ἐπ' αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς τὰς ἑπτὰ πληγὰς τὰς γεγραμμέ- νας ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ.) Elegans allusio in ἐπιθῇ & ἐπιθήσαι. Illud ἑπτὰ multi Græci codices non habent, ut nec Latinus. Intelligendæ autem plagæ, tum quæ sunt capitibus octavo, nono, decimo & undecimo; tum quæ capitibus 16. 17. 18. quarum illæ Judæos, hæ Romanum imperium tangunt. Est ἐπιθήσαι imprecantis, sed non injuste, terrendi causa. At in Manuscripto est prædictionis modo ἐπιθήσει & mox ἀφελεῖ. Et sic legit Latinus: & ita citantur verba apud Aretham. Vi- de quæ diximus ad 2. Tim. 4, 14.

## 22:19
Vers. 19. And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, may God take away his part from the tree of life.) May God cause or will cause that he not be a participant in the benefits which the cross of Christ has produced for us.

And from the holy city.) May He cause that he not be a citizen of the Church, may he be cast out as one who does a lie.

Of the things written in this book.) This refers both to the wood and to the city.

That the Johannine clause or adjuration is intended to refer to the whole of Scripture is evident, both from the homogeneous nature of the books of Scripture. For all are θεόπνευσοι (God-breathed), and therefore reject human additions; whence Adam Conzen, lib. 9, Politic. cap. 23, § 3: These things are to be accepted concerning the entire Christian economy of doctrine and the norm of believing, just as concerning the Apocalypse of John: since they were dictated by the same authority. Whoever changes these things corrects the Holy Spirit, whoever moderates the sentence of the supreme judge with human ingenuity denies divine wisdom. All are directed to the same end, eternal salvation, which it is granted to attain only by divine manifestation; the Scriptures alone are sufficient, therefore they stand in need of no addition. Holy Scripture is perfect, therefore it admits neither πρόσθεσιν (addition) nor ἀφαίρεσιν (subtraction). Let him show that it is written, says Tertullian against Hermogenes. the workshop of Hermogenes: if it is not written, let him fear that Woe destined for those who add or subtract. God permits nothing to be added to His word; if it is added, it is called anathema, Deut. 4:2, 12:32, Gal. 1:8-9. Nothing is to be taken away, because faith is like a chain, which, with one link loosened, collapses. He who shall break the least iota in the law shall be called least, i.e., nothing, i.e., shall be, in the kingdom of heaven, Matt. 5:19. Scotus acknowledges this, prod. sentent. q. 3, art. 3. Paulinus in the Council of Forum Julii: John, he says, the Apostle, under the designation of the book, has testified concerning the whole series of both Testaments. Andreas of Caesarea: A horrendous imprecation, he says, against the corrupters of the divine Scriptures. Likewise: He testifies to us who are listening, that we should not add or subtract anything, but that we should consider the idioms of the Scriptures much more worthy of faith and momentous than the Attic structure of speech and dialectical syllogisms.

Latin:

Vers. 19. Καὶ ἐάν τις ἀφέλῃ ἀπὸ τῶν λόγων τῶ βιβλίε τῆς προ- φητείας ταύτης, ἀφέλοι ὁ Θεὸς τὸ μέρος αὐτῦ ἀπὸ τῶ ξύλε τῆς ζωῆς.) Faciat aut faciet Deus, ne is particeps sit beneficio- rum, quæ crux Christi nobis peperit.

Καὶ ἐκ τῆς πόλεως τῆς ἁγίας ) Faciat ne sit ille civis Eccle- siæ, ejiciatur tanquam ποιῶν ψεῦδος.

Τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ.) Hoc refert tum ad li- gnum, tum ad urbem.

Ad totam scripturam clausulam, vel obtestationem Johan- neam velle referri patet, tum ex homogenea librorum scriptu- ræ natura. Omnes enim θεόπνευσοι, ideoq; humana addita- menta respuunt; unde Adam Conzen. l. 9. Politic. c. 23. §. 3. Hæc de universa doctrina Christiana œconomia & credendi nor- ma tam accipienda sunt, quam de Apocalypsi Johannis: quan- doquidem eadem autoritate dictata sint. Spiritum S. corrigit, quisquis ista mutat, divinam sapientiam negat, quisquis huma- no ingenio supremi judicis sententiam moderatur. Omnes ad eundem finem, salutem æternam, directi sunt, quem non nisi divina manifestatione consequi datur; Solæ scripturæ suffi- ciunt, proinde nulla additione indigent. Perfecta est Scriptu- ra S. idcirco nec πρόσθεσιν nec ἀφαίρεσιν admittit. Scriptum esse doceat, inquit Tertullianus adv. Hermog. Hermogenis offi- cina: si non est scriptum timeat Væ illud adjicientibus aut de- trahentibus destinatum. Nihil verbo suo addi permittit Deus, si addatur, anathema dicitur, Deut. IV, 2. XII, 32. Gal. I. 8. 9. Nihil demi, quia fides instar catenæ est, quæ una soluta ansu- la corruit. Qui minimum Jota in lege solverit, minimus, i. e. nullus vocabitur, i. e. erit, in regno cælorum, Matth. V, 19. A- gnoscit id Scotus prod. sentent. q. 3. art. 3. Paulinus in concil. Foro-Julienf. Johannes, inquit, Apostolus sub orsus libri appel- latione de tota utriusq; Testamenti serie contestatus est. Andr. Cæsariensis: Horrenda, ait, adversus corruptores divinarum scripturarum imprecatio. Item: Contestatur nobis audientibus, ut ne quid addamus aut detrahamus, sed scripturarum idioma- ta multo magis, quam Atticam orationis structuram & syllo- gismos dialecticos fide digna ac momentosa censeamus.

## 22:21
V. 21. The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the saints. Amen.) In the manuscript there is nothing else than 'the grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.' However, ὑμῖν (you) is understood, which the Latin added. Thus Paul, Rom. 16:24 and elsewhere. All will understand, both those who will read these things and those who will hear them as others recount them.

Latin:

V. 21. Ἡ χάρις τῦ Κυρίε Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ μετὰ πάντων τ' ἁγίων. Ἀμήν.) In Manuscripto nihil aliud est, quam ἡ χάρις τῦ Κυρίε Ἰησῦ μετὰ πάντων. Subauditur autem ὑμῖν vobis, quod adjecit Lati- nus. Sic Paulus Rom. 16, 24. & alibi. Omnes intelligent, tum qui legent hæc, tum qui aliis enarrantibus audient.
